englishMeaning: Feeling sick or nauseous while traveling in an airplane. Experiencing discomfort, nausea, or vomiting due to motion during air travel. This is a type of motion sickness specifically occurring on airplanes.
urduMeaning: ہوائی جہاز کی حرکت کے سبب جسم میں چکر، متلی یا قے کا احساس، جو خاص طور پر فضائی سفر کے دوران ہوتا ہے، ہوائی جہاز میں سفر کے دوران متلی یا بیماری محسوس کرنا
antonyms: Comfortable, Healthy, Untroubled, Well
synonyms: Nauseous in flight, Motion sick, Queasy, Travel sick
sindhiMeaning: هوائي جهاز جي حرڪت سبب ٿڪاوٽ، متلي يا الٽي جو احساس، جيڪو خاص طور تي جهاز ۾ ٿيڻ واري حرڪت سبب ٿيندو آهي، هوائي جهاز ۾ سفر دوران بيمار ٿيڻ
examples: She felt airsick after the turbulent flight. He always gets airsick on long journeys. The child became airsick during takeoff. They offered him medicine because he was airsick.

antonyms: Assurance, Guarantee, Commitment, Acceptance
englishMeaning: A statement that denies responsibility for something. An official statement intended to limit legal liability, clarify that the writer or speaker does not take responsibility for certain information, actions, or outcomes, or to caution the reader/listener about something.
examples: The website includes a disclaimer stating that it is not responsible for third-party content. He signed the contract after reading the disclaimer carefully. The email contained a disclaimer warning about confidential information. The product packaging had a disclaimer about potential side effects.
sindhiMeaning: زميوار نه ٿيڻ، دستبرداري، تياڳه، انڪار جو اعلان، بيخبريءَ جو اظهار
urduMeaning: بے تعلقی کا اظہار، ذمہ داری سے انکار کا بیان
synonyms: Waiver, Denial, Refusal, Caution, Notification

examples: The unfair decision discontended the workers. His harsh words discontended his friends. Continuous failure can discontend even a strong person. The sudden change in plans discontended the entire team.
synonyms: Displease, Dissatisfy, Upset, Disturb, Agitate
urduMeaning: ناراض یا غیر مطمئن کرنا، ناراض دل آزردہ کرنا، بے چین کرنا، اطمینان ختم کرنا، پریشان کرنایا غیر مطمئن کرنا، کسی کو ایسی حالت میں ڈالنا کہ وہ خوش یا مطمئن نہ رہے، دل میں بے چینی یا ناراضگی پیدا کرنا
sindhiMeaning: ناراض يا بي اطمينان ڪرڻ، بيچين ڪرڻ، دل ڏکائڻ، اطمينان ختم ڪرڻ، تڪليف ڏيڻ، ڪنهن کي اهڙي حالت ۾ آڻڻ جتي هو خوش نه هجي يا مطمئن نه هجي، دل ۾ بيچيني يا ناراضگي پيدا ڪرڻ
antonyms: Please, Satisfy, Comfort, Calm, Content
englishMeaning: To make someone unhappy or dissatisfied. To cause a feeling of dissatisfaction, unrest, or discontent in a person. It refers to disturbing someone’s peace of mind or making them unhappy with a situation.

antonyms: Content, Satisfaction, Gratified, Happiness, Satisfy, Patience
englishMeaning: To make someone dissatisfied or unhappy. A feeling of dissatisfaction or unhappiness with a situation, condition, or authority.
examples: The students were discontent with the new grading system. A discontent workforce can lower productivity. The manager’s unfair decision discontented the employees. Rising prices discontented many citizens. Public discontent grew after the government increased taxes. Workers showed their discontent by organizing a peaceful protest. Her constant complaints revealed her deep discontent with the job.
urduMeaning: ناخوش یا بے اطمینان کرنا، بے چینی، بے قناعی، بے قرار، غیر مطمئن، نا خوش، ناراضگی، بے اطمینانی، ناخوشی، بے قراری، عدم اطمینان، ناراض
sindhiMeaning: ناراض ڪرڻ ، ناخوشي، بي سڪوني، شڪايت، بي اطمينائي پيدا ڪرڻ، ناراضپو، ناراضگي، رنج، ناراض ، بي اطمينان، بيچيني
synonyms: Unhappiness, Dissatisfy, Regret, Uneasiness, Vexation

urduMeaning: اختلاف کرنا، ٹکرانا، متفق نہ ہونا؛ ہم آہنگ نہ ہونا، لوگوں یا خیالات کے درمیان تنازعہ یا عدم ہم آہنگی؛ ٹکراؤ والی آواز
antonyms: Agree, Match, Harmonize, Correspond, Fit, Harmony, Agreement, Concord, Peace, Unity
sindhiMeaning: اختلاف ڪرڻ، ٽڪراءُ ڪرڻ، ڪنهن سان يا ڪنهن شيءِ سان متفق نه ٿيڻ؛ هم آهنگي ۾ نه هجڻ، اختلاف، ٽڪراءُ
synonyms: Clash, Conflict, Disagree, Differ, Be incompatible, Disagreement, Strife, Tension, Friction, Disharmony
examples: His views discord with the company’s policy. The facts presented discord with her statement. Their actions discord with their promises. There was discord in the boardroom over the decision. Family discord can harm relationships. Political discord delayed the legislation.
englishMeaning: To disagree or clash. To be in conflict or disagreement with someone or something; to be out of harmony. Disagreement or conflict. A state of conflict, tension, or lack of harmony among people, ideas, or sounds.

sindhiMeaning: اختلافي، غير مشابه، اختلاف رکندڙ، جيڪو ميل نٿو کائي، غير مطابقت وارو، تضاد وارو، الڳ الڳ، غير موافق، بي ترتيب، بي هم آهنگ
englishMeaning: Not being in agreement or harmony. Showing a difference between two things that should be the same.
urduMeaning: متناقض ، متضاد، مختلف، فرق والا، مغائر ، بے آہنگ
antonyms: Accordant, Agreeing, Compatible, Concordant, Conformable (to), Congruent, Congruous, Consistent, Consonant, Correspondent (with or to), Harmonious, Nonconflicting
synonyms: Clashing, Conflicting, Disagreeing, Discordant, Incompatible, Incongruous, Inconsistent, Inconsonant, Inharmonious
examples: Discrepant results have been described by one group of scientists. These findings are discrepant with data from several other studies. In case discrepant documents are presented, we shall deduct USD 55.00 for each discrepant.

urduMeaning: علیحدہ الگ، جُدا، مجرَد، غیر ملتفی، ایسی چیز کو کہتے ہیں جو دوسری چیزوں سے واضح طور پر الگ ہو، جو مسلسل نہ ہو بلکہ الگ الگ حصوں میں موجود ہو
examples: The data was divided into discrete categories for analysis. Each discrete unit in the system performs a different function. The island ecosystem consists of several discrete habitats. In mathematics, integers are discrete numbers.
sindhiMeaning: هڪ ٻئي کان ڌار ڌار، غيرمسلسل، الڳ الڳ، جدا جدا، الڳ ٿيندڙ، منفرد، اُن شيءِ کي چيو وڃي ٿو جيڪا ٻين کان صاف الڳ هجي يا جدا هجي، اهڙيون شيون جيڪي پاڻ ۾ ڳنڍيل نه هجن
synonyms: Separate, Detached, Disconnected, Independent, Distinct
englishMeaning: Separate, distinct, or individually different. Something that is clearly separate or distinct from other things. It refers to items, units, or elements that are individually separate and not continuous or connected. In mathematics and science, it also describes values or data that exist as individual units rather than a continuous range.
antonyms: Attached, Connected, Joined, Linked, Continuous

englishMeaning: The state of being separated from the physical body. The idea of existing without a physical form, often spiritual or abstract. In literature/philosophy it may refer to detachment of mind, soul, or identity from the body.
sindhiMeaning: جسم کان جدا ٿيڻ، بي جسمي حالت، غير مادي هجڻ، جسم کان الڳ وجود رکڻ، روح جو جسم کان الڳ ٿيڻ، غير مادي حيثيت
synonyms: Separation, Detachment, Immateriality, Incorporeality
examples: Some religions describe death as the disembodiment of the soul from the body. Virtual reality creates a strange feeling of disembodiment, as if the body is left behind. The novel explores the disembodiment of consciousness in a digital world. Meditation can sometimes bring a sense of disembodiment from physical reality.
urduMeaning: روح کا جسم سے جدا ہونا، بے جسم ہونا، لا جسمی کیفیت، غیر مادی حالت، غیر جسمانی وجود
antonyms: Embodiment, Incarnation, Incorporation

sindhiMeaning: رسوا ڪرڻ، بدنام ڪرڻ، شرمنده ڪرڻ، بي عزتي، بدنامي، رسوائي، شرمندگي
synonyms: Shame, Dishonor
examples: The officer was disgraced for his corrupt actions. Cheating in exams disgraces the reputation of the school. He disgraced his family by lying in court. He was dismissed from the army in disgrace after being caught cheating. The scandal brought great disgrace to the politician’s family. Cheating in an exam is a disgrace to the student’s character.
antonyms: Honor, Respect
englishMeaning: To bring shame or dishonor upon someone or something. Loss of honor, respect, or reputation due to shameful action.
urduMeaning: رسوا کرنا، بدنام کرنا، ذلیل کرنا، دنامی، رسوائی، شرمندگی

antonyms: Certainly, Definitely, Without doubt
sindhiMeaning: جيتوڻيڪ، پر باوجود، ڪنهن ڳالهه کي قبول ڪرڻ سان گڏ ان جي ڪجهه حد يا رڪاوٽ ڏيکارڻ لاءِ
englishMeaning: Although, even though. Used to introduce a contrast or limitation in a statement. It connects two clauses, showing that the second clause modifies or reduces the force of the first clause. It is formal and mostly used in writing.
urduMeaning: حالانکہ، اگرچہ، کسی بات کے باوجود یا کسی محدودیت کو ظاہر کرنے کے لیے
examples: He finally agreed to join the project, albeit reluctantly. The movie was enjoyable, albeit a bit too long. She accepted the offer, albeit with some hesitation. The journey was exciting, albeit tiring.
synonyms: Although, Even though, Though, Notwithstanding

antonyms: Fix, Secure, Implant, Insert, Retain
urduMeaning: کسی چیز کو اس کی اصل جگہ سے زبردستی ہٹانا یا نکالنا، کسی شخص کو عہدہ یا مقام چھوڑنے پر مجبور کرنا
englishMeaning: To forcefully remove something that is fixed, stuck, or firmly positioned from its place, position, or situation. Can also refer to causing someone to leave a position or office.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ کي جڳهه مان زور ڀري هٽائڻ يا ڪڍڻ، ڪنهن ماڻهو کي پنهنجي جاءِ يا عهدو ڇڏڻ تي مجبور ڪرڻ
synonyms: Remove, Eject, Oust, Unseat, Extricate
examples: The storm dislodged several roof tiles. Protesters tried to dislodge the barricade. The dentist dislodged a piece of food stuck between my teeth. The new manager was able to dislodge the old leadership.

urduMeaning: دور کرنا، ختم کرنا، زائل کرنا، کسی چیز کو دور کرنا یا ختم کرنا خاص طور پر شک خوف یا غلط فہمی کو
antonyms: Create, Cause, Encourage, Spread, Build up
englishMeaning: To drive away, remove, or make something disappear (often doubt, fear, or a false idea). To get rid of something that is negative, unclear, or unwanted such as fear, doubt, myths, or darkness. It is often used for abstract things rather than physical objects.
synonyms: Remove, Eliminate, Clear, Drive away, Erase, Dissipate
sindhiMeaning: دفع ڪرڻ، دور ڪرڻ، هٺائڻ، ڪڍي ڇڏڻ، ختم ڪرڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ کي ختم ڪرڻ يا دور ڪرڻ خاص طور تي خوف شڪ يا غلط خيال کي ختم ڪرڻ
examples: The teacher tried to dispel the students’ doubts before the exam. His explanation helped dispel the confusion in the meeting. Sunlight began to dispel the morning fog. She spoke kindly to dispel his fears.

sindhiMeaning: جيڪو ضروري نه هجي، اُن شيءِ يا ماڻهو لاءِ چيو ويندو آهي جيڪو اهم نه هجي ۽ جنهن کان سواءِ به ڪم هلي سگهي
englishMeaning: Something that can be done without. A person, object, or thing that is not essential and can be removed, replaced, or ignored without causing serious problems or harm.
urduMeaning: غیر ضروری ، اُس چیز یا شخص کو کہتے ہیں جس کے بغیر بھی کام چل سکتا ہو اور جس کی کمی سے کوئی بڑا نقصان نہ ہو
antonyms: Essential, Indispensable, Necessary, Vital
examples: Extra staff were considered dispensable during the budget cuts. In an emergency, luxury items become dispensable. The manager felt that the outdated system was dispensable. Some rules are useful, but others are dispensable in practice.
synonyms: Unnecessary, Optional, Replaceable, Nonessential

urduMeaning: بغیر گزارا کرنا ، ختم کرنا ، فارغ کرنا، رعایت کرنا ، ( کسی قانون سے ) مستثنٰی کرنا ، قسم وغیرہ کی پابندی سے آزاد کرنا ، پابندی سے سبکدوش کرنا
englishMeaning: To do without. To stop using somebody/something because you no longer need them. To get rid of or do without something. To give up what is not strictly needed. Manage without, forgo, as in We can dispense with the extra help. To set aside.
antonyms: Adopt, Use, Continue, Hold, Keep, Note, Pay attention, Regard, Accept, Retain, Take
synonyms: Do away with, Abolish, Waive, Forgo, Dispose of, Discard
sindhiMeaning: بغير ڪم هلائڻ، بغير ڪم هلائڻو پئجي وڃڻ، ختم ڪرڻ، ڇڏي ڏيڻ، هٿ ڪڍي ڇڏڻ، نوڪري مان هٽائڻ، ضرورت نه سمجهڻ
examples: Debit cards dispense with the need for cash altogether. I think we can dispense with the formalities (= speak openly and naturally to each other). They've had to dispense with a lot of luxuries since Mike lost his job. Let’s dispense with the formalities and get right down to business. Electronic records can dispense with 80% of paper files and reduce the need for office space. The new chairman has said he will dispense with any directors who can't accept radical change.

antonyms: Essential, Indispensable, Necessary, Vital
synonyms: Unnecessary, Optional, Replaceable, Nonessential
urduMeaning: غیر ضروری ، اُس چیز یا شخص کو کہتے ہیں جس کے بغیر بھی کام چل سکتا ہو اور جس کی کمی سے کوئی بڑا نقصان نہ ہو
examples: Extra staff were considered dispensible during the budget cuts. In an emergency, luxury items become dispensible. The manager felt that the outdated system was dispensible. Some rules are useful, but others are dispensible in practice.
englishMeaning: Something that can be done without. A person, object, or thing that is not essential and can be removed, replaced, or ignored without causing serious problems or harm.
sindhiMeaning: جيڪو ضروري نه هجي، اُن شيءِ يا ماڻهو لاءِ چيو ويندو آهي جيڪو اهم نه هجي ۽ جنهن کان سواءِ به ڪم هلي سگهي

synonyms: Incline, Tend, Influence, Persuade, Prepare, Lead
examples: His kind nature disposes him to help others. The cool weather disposed us to go for a walk. Her upbringing disposed her to be respectful toward elders. The calm environment disposed him to study with focus. She is disposed to forgive him.
englishMeaning: To make someone likely or willing to behave in a particular way, or to have a certain attitude, feeling, or tendency toward something. It shows a natural inclination or readiness for a specific action or behavior.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کي ڪنهن خاص رويي عمل يا سوچ ڏانهن مائل ڪرڻ يا رجحان پيدا ڪرڻ، اهڙي حالت جنهن ۾ ماڻهو پاڻمرادو ڪنهن ڪم يا روئي ڏانهن لاڙو رکي
antonyms: Discourage, Disincline, Deter, Prevent, Restrain
urduMeaning: کسی شخص کو کسی خاص رویے یا عمل کی طرف مائل کرنا یا رجحان پیدا کرنا، ایسی کیفیت جس میں انسان خود بخود کسی بات یا کام کی طرف جھکاؤ محسوس کرے

antonyms: Discourage, Repel, Dissuade, Alienate, Deter
sindhiMeaning: مائل ڪرڻ، لاڙو پيدا ڪرڻ، ڪنهن کي ڪنهن ڳالهه ڏانهن راضي ڪرڻ، رجحان پيدا ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: مائل کرنا،رجحان پیدا کرنا، کسی شخص میں کسی خاص سوچ یا رویے کی طرف رجحان پیدا کرنا، راضی یا مائل کرنا، آمادہ کرنا
synonyms: Incline, Influence, Persuade, Attract, Prompt, Lead, Motivate
englishMeaning: To make someone likely or willing to think or feel in a particular way about someone or something, to influence a person’s attitude or tendency.
examples: I am not disposed toward taking unnecessary risks. His kindness disposed me toward trusting him. Her honesty disposed others toward respecting her opinion. The teacher’s patience disposed students toward liking the subject. Their generosity disposed the community toward supporting their cause.

He checked into the hotel under an alias. The writer published the novel under an alias. The criminal was arrested while using an alias. She created an email alias for professional work. The actor worked under an alias before becoming famous.
synonyms: Nickname, Pseudonym
englishMeaning: A false or alternative name used instead of a real name. Another name that a person uses instead of their real name. It is often used for privacy, safety, writing, acting, or sometimes to hide identity. In legal or criminal cases, it may refer to a false name used to avoid recognition. In technology, it can also mean an alternative name for a file or email address.
antonyms: Real name, Birth name, Original name, Legal name
urduMeaning: عرف، لقب ، عرف نامی، مشہور نام، کِسی اور نام سے مَعروف ، اِختِيار کَردَہ يا فَرضی نام
sindhiMeaning: اصلي نالي کان علاوھ، لقب، عرف، عام نالو، سڃاڻپ لاءِ ٻيو مشهور نالو، ٻيو نالو
ڪنهن کي بيچين يا پريشان ڪرڻ، پريشاني، بيچيني، ڳڻتي، دل جو سک نه هجڻ، بي آرامي، فڪر، دل جي اٿل پٿل، اضطراب
urduMeaning: کسی کو پریشان یا بے چین کرنا، بےچینی، پریشانی، ذہنی اضطراب، بے آرامی، فکر، گھبراہٹ، ذہنی بے سکونی
antonyms: Calm, Peace, Comfort, Ease, Tranquility, Reassurance, Contentment
englishMeaning: To make someone feel uneasy, troubled, or anxious. Worry, uneasiness, mental disturbance. A feeling of worry, restlessness, or lack of peace in the mind.
examples: News of war spread disquiet in the city. The news of the storm caused great disquiet among the villagers. She felt a sense of disquiet before the interview began. His rude tone seemed to disquiet everyone in the room. There was growing disquiet about the future of the company.
synonyms: Disturb, Trouble, Worry, Unsettle, Bother, Agitate, Uneasiness, Anxiety, Worry, Unrest, Disturbance, Agitation, Concern

englishMeaning: A long, formal, detailed discussion or essay on a subject. A long, careful, and formal examination or discussion of a topic. It is often written or spoken in an academic, scholarly, or serious style.
sindhiMeaning: مقالو، تفصيلي بحث، علمي گفتگو، تحقيقي لکڻي، شرح، وضاحت، ڪنهن موضوع مسئلي يا خيال تي ڊگهو سنجيده باقاعده ۽ تفصيلي بحث يا لکڻي جيڪا گهڻو ڪري علمي يا تحقيقي انداز ۾ هوندي آهي
antonyms: Summary, Outline, Brief note, Silence, Conciseness, Short remark
urduMeaning: مقالہ، تفصیلی بحث، علمی گفتگو، تحقیقی تحریر، تشریح، وضاحت، کسی موضوع مسئلے یا خیال پر طویل سنجیدہ منظم اور تفصیلی بحث یا تحریر جو عموماً علمی یا تحقیقی انداز میں ہوتی ہے
examples: The professor delivered a long disquisition on ancient philosophy. Her disquisition on climate change impressed the entire audience. The book contains a disquisition about the history of language. He wrote a thoughtful disquisition on moral responsibility.
synonyms: Treatise, Dissertation, Essay, Discussion, Analysis, Exposition, Commentary, Thesis
Disturb, Interrupt, Obstruct, Upset, Disorganize
englishMeaning: To interrupt or stop something from continuing normally. To cause disorder, disturbance, or interruption in a process, system, activity, or situation so that it cannot continue as planned or smoothly.
sindhiMeaning: بگاڙڻ، خلل وجهڻ، ڪنهن ڪم، نظام يا حالتن ۾ اهڙو خلل وجهڻ جو اهو صحيح نموني سان جاري نه رهي
examples: The heavy rain disrupted traffic across the city. Loud noise can disrupt students during exams. The strike disrupted public transportation services. Technical issues disrupted the online meeting.
urduMeaning: درہم برہم کرنا، خلل ڈالنا، کسی عمل، نظام یا سرگرمی میں ایسی مداخلت کرنا کہ وہ معمول کے مطابق جاری نہ رہ سکے
antonyms: Maintain, Continue, Support, Stabilize, Preserve

sindhiMeaning: ڦهلائڻ، پيغام کي هر طرف پهچائڻ عام ڪرڻ، ڄاڻ ۽ خبرن کي ماڻهن تائين وسيع نموني پهچائڻ، عام طور علم تحقيق يا معلومات کي ماڻهن ۾ پکيڙڻ لاءِ استعمال ٿيندو آهي
examples: The organization works to disseminate health information in rural areas. Scientists disseminate their research findings through journals and conferences. The government used social media to disseminate safety guidelines during the flood. Teachers help disseminate knowledge to students every day.
synonyms: Spread, Distribute, Circulate, Broadcast, Propagate, Publish
urduMeaning: پھیلانا، عام کرنا، معلومات خیالات یا خبروں کو وسیع پیمانے پر لوگوں تک پہنچانا، عام طور پر علم تحقیق یا پیغام کو زیادہ لوگوں تک پہنچانے کے لئے استعمال ہوتا ہے
englishMeaning: To spread information, ideas, knowledge, or news widely so many people can know about it. It is often used for sharing knowledge, research, or messages with a large audience.
antonyms: Suppress, Conceal, Hide, Withhold, Restrict

urduMeaning: نااتفاقی ، اختلاف رائے، رَنجِش ، پُھوٹ، اَن بَن، کسی گروہ ادارے یا برادری کے اندر شدید اختلاف پیدا ہو جائے اور اس کے نتیجے میں تنازع یا تقسیم ہو جائے
examples: Dissension within the committee delayed the final decision. The new policy created dissension among the employees. Political dissension weakened the unity of the party. Religious dissension led to conflict in the region.
synonyms: Disagreement, Conflict, Discord, Dispute, Division
englishMeaning: Disagreement that causes conflict among people. Conflict, division, or tension among members. The word is usually used when people who are expected to work together begin to oppose each other.
antonyms: Agreement, Harmony, Unity, Accord, Consensus
sindhiMeaning: اڻبڻ، جهيڙو، مخالفت، نفاق، تڪرار، ڪنهن گروهه اداري يا برادري ۾ سخت اختلاف پيدا ٿين ۽ انهن اختلافن سبب تڪرار يا ڦوٽ پيدا ٿئي

synonyms: Waste, Squandering, Extravagance, Decay, Disappearance
examples: His dissipation of family wealth left him bankrupt. The dissipation of heat from the engine prevents overheating. Years of dissipation affected his health badly. The dissipation of fog made the road visible again. Too much dissipation distracted him from his studies.
englishMeaning: A way of living focused too much on entertainment, drinking, or luxury, often leading to moral or physical weakness. A state in which attention is scattered and not focused on serious matters. The process of spreading something over a wide area until it loses strength or concentration. Gradual weakening of emotions, anger, fear, or excitement over time.
urduMeaning: فضول خرچی یا ضائع کرنا، آہستہ آہستہ ختم ہو جانا، عیش و عشرت میں زندگی گزارنے سے اخلاقی یا جسمانی کمزوری، ذہنی انتشار یا توجہ کا بٹ جانا، کسی چیز کا پھیل جانا اور طاقت کھو دینا، جذبات یا احساسات کا آہستہ آہستہ کم ہو جانا
antonyms: Conservation, Preservation, Saving, Accumulation, Retention
sindhiMeaning: فضول خرچي يا ضايع ڪرڻ، آهستي آهستي ختم ٿيڻ، جذبن يا احساسن جو آهستي آهستي گهٽجڻ، ذهن جو منتشر ٿيڻ يا ڌيان نه رهڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ جو پکڙجي وڃڻ ۽ طاقت وڃائڻ، عيش ۽ عشرت ۾ زندگي گذارڻ سبب اخلاقي يا جسماني ڪمزوري

englishMeaning: To persuade someone not to do something. To convince or advise someone against doing something, usually by giving reasons or warnings so that the person changes their mind. Dissuade is commonly used in formal or advisory situations where someone tries to stop another person from making a risky or unwise decision.
antonyms: Encourage, Persuade, Motivate, Urge, Influence
synonyms: Discourage, Deter, Persuade against, Advise against, Prevent
urduMeaning: کسی کو کسی کام سے روکنا یا باز رکھنا، کسی شخص کو کسی کام کے بارے میں سمجھا کر یا دلائل دے کر اس سے روکنا یا اس کا ارادہ بدل دینا، یہ لفظ زیادہ تر مشورے یا نصیحت کے موقع پر استعمال ہوتا ہے جب کسی کو نقصان دہ یا غلط کام سے روکا جائے
examples: I tried to dissuade him from quitting his job. The teacher dissuaded the students from cheating in the exam. Her friends dissuaded her from traveling alone at night. The doctor dissuaded him from smoking.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کي ڪنهن ڪم ڪرڻ کان روڪڻ يا منع ڪرڻ، ڪنهن ماڻهوءَ کي دليل ڏئي يا سمجهاڻي ڏئي ڪنهن ڪم ڪرڻ کان روڪڻ يا سندس ارادو بدلائڻ، هي لفظ اڪثر صلاح يا نصيحت ۾ استعمال ٿيندو آهي جڏهن ڪنهن کي غلط يا نقصان ڏيندڙ ڪم کان روڪيو وڃي

synonyms: Suffering, Anguish, Hardship, Trouble, Agony, Worry
examples: She was in deep distress after hearing the bad news. The ship sent a distress signal during the storm. Financial problems distressed him greatly. The abandoned animals were in distress.
englishMeaning: To put someone in a state of anxiety, sorrow, or difficulty. A state of extreme worry, sorrow, or physical discomfort caused by a difficult situation.
urduMeaning: پریشان کرنا، تکلیف دینا، تکلیف، غم، پریشانی، شدید ذہنی یا جسمانی اذیت، مشکل کی حالت
antonyms: Comfort, Relief, Ease, Happiness, Peace
sindhiMeaning: ڏک پهچائڻ، پريشان ڪرڻ، ڏک، تڪليف، ڏک، مصيبت، انتهائي فڪر، تڪليف يا مشڪل واري حالت

examples: His constant criticism alienated his coworkers. The new law alienated many citizens. She alienated her family by refusing to attend gatherings. Ignoring his friends alienated him from the group. Harsh government policies alienate minority communities. He alienated his land to his nephew.
englishMeaning: To make someone feel isolated or estranged. To cause someone to feel detached, unfriendly, or withdrawn, often by one’s actions, behavior, or attitude. To transfer ownership or rights of property to another person.
synonyms: Estrange, Isolate, Distance, Divide
urduMeaning: کسی کو الگ یا بیگانہ محسوس کروانا، کسی کو غیر دوست یا الگ محسوس کروانے کے لیے، اکثر اپنے اعمال یا رویے سے، منتقل کرنا، ملکیت کرنا، منتقل کرنا قبضے میں لینا
antonyms: Befriend, Unite, Reconcile, Connect
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کي ڌار ڪرڻ، پري ڪرڻ، ڪنهن کي اڪيلو، ڌار يا بي تعلق محسوس ڪرائڻ، اڪثر پنهنجي عمل يا رويي سبب، ڇني ڇڏڻ، وڪڻڻ، منتقل ڪرڻ، بدلي ڪرڻ

synonyms: Daily, Daytime, Day active, Everyday, Circadian
urduMeaning: دن میں سرگرم، دن سے متعلق، روزانہ ہونے والا، دن کے وقت سرگرم رہنے والا، روزانہ کے چکر سے متعلق
examples: Humans are mostly diurnal and sleep at night. The diurnal temperature changes were significant in the desert. Many birds have diurnal feeding habits. The scientist studied the diurnal cycle of plant growth.
sindhiMeaning: ڏينهن سان لاڳاپيل، ڏينهن دوران سرگرم، روزانو ٿيندڙ، ڏينهن جي وقت سرگرم رهندڙ جاندار، روزاني چڪر سان واسطو رکندڙ
englishMeaning: Active during the day or happening every day. Relating to the daytime. Occurring every day. Animals or plants active during daylight hours. Daily recurring cycle
antonyms: Nocturnal, Night active, Nightly

examples: The diversifiability of her investments allowed her to reduce potential losses. Diversifiability is key when constructing a balanced financial portfolio. Not all risks have high diversifiability; some are systemic. The company focused on diversifiability to enter multiple markets safely.
englishMeaning: The ability of an investment, asset, or risk to be diversified to reduce exposure. The characteristic of an investment, project, or financial portfolio that allows it to be spread across different assets, sectors, or regions to lower overall risk. It measures how effectively risks can be mitigated through diversification.
synonyms: Diversifiable nature, Spreadability, Risk-distribution potential, Portfolio flexibility
antonyms: Non-diversifiable, Concentrated, Undiversifiable, Inflexible
sindhiMeaning: ورهائجي سگهڻ جي صلاحيت، ڪنهن به سيڙپڪاري منصوبي يا مالي پورٽ فوليو جي اها خاصيت جيڪا ان کي مختلف اثاثن شعبن يا علائقن ۾ ورهائڻ جي اجازت ڏئي جيئن مجموعي خطري کي گهٽائي سگهجي
urduMeaning: تنوع پذیر ہونے کی صلاحیت، کسی سرمایہ کاری منصوبے یا مالیاتی پورٹ فولیو کی وہ خصوصیت جو اسے مختلف اثاثوں شعبوں یا علاقوں میں تقسیم کرنے کے قابل بناتی ہے تاکہ مجموعی خطرہ کم کیا جا سکے

synonyms: Diversifiable, Spreadable, Varied, Distributable, Allocable
examples: The risk in this portfolio is largely diversifiable. Diversifiable investments help protect against market fluctuations. By choosing diversifiable strategies, companies reduce financial exposure. Not all risks are diversifiable; some are inherent to the industry.
englishMeaning: Capable of being spread or varied to reduce risk or dependence. Something, especially investments, risks, or activities, that can be distributed among different options or categories to minimize potential loss or to create variety.
urduMeaning: قابلِ تقسیم یا متنوع بنانے کے قابل، کسی شے کو مختلف حصوں یا مواقع میں بانٹ کر خطرہ کم کرنا یا تنوع پیدا کرنا ممکن ہو، سرمایہ کاری کو مختلف شعبوں میں تقسیم کرنے سے نقصان کا امکان کم ہوتا ہے
antonyms: Non-diversifiable, Concentrated, Fixed, Undividable
sindhiMeaning: ورهايو وڃي سگهندڙ (ورڇ يا خطري کي گهٽائڻ لاءِ ورهائڻ جي قابل)، ڪنهن شيءِ کي مختلف حصن يا موقعن ۾ ورهائي سگهندڙ جيئن خطرو گهٽجي يا متنوعيت وڌي، سيڙپڪاري کي مختلف شعبن ۾ ورهائڻ سان نقصان جو امڪان گهٽجي ٿو

englishMeaning: The process of varying products, investments, or activities to reduce risk or expand opportunities. The act of introducing variety in business, finance, agriculture, or other areas to minimize risks, increase stability, and explore multiple growth opportunities. It can involve investing in different industries, creating new product lines, or spreading resources across sectors.
antonyms: Uniformity, Sameness, Concentration, Specialization
urduMeaning: تنوع، مختلف شعبوں یا سرگرمیوں میں پھیلاؤ، خطرہ کم کرنے یا مواقع بڑھانے کے لیے، مختلف شعبوں یا سرگرمیوں میں پھیلاؤ تاکہ خطرہ کم ہو، پیداوار یا کاروبار میں نئے مواقع پیدا کرنا، کسی ایک چیز پر انحصار کم کرنا اور متبادل راستے پیدا کرنا، فصلوں یا سرمایہ کاری میں ورائٹی بڑھانا
synonyms: Variation, Expansion, Assortment, Spread, Heterogeneity, Multiplicity
sindhiMeaning: ڦهلاءُ، ڪاروبار يا سيڙپڪاري ۾ خطرن کي گهٽائڻ لاءِ مختلف شعبن ۾ ورڇ يا پکيڙ، پيداوار يا سرگرمين ۾ نئون انداز آڻڻ، هڪ ئي شيءِ تي ڀروسو گهٽائڻ ۽ متبادل اختيار وڌائڻ، فصلن يا وسيلن جي ورائٽي وڌائڻ، مختلف شعبن يا سرگرمين ۾ ورڇ (خطرن کي گهٽائڻ لاءِ يا موقعن کي وڌائڻ لاءِ)
examples: The company pursued diversification by entering the renewable energy market. Farmers practiced diversification by growing multiple crops instead of relying on a single one. Diversification of investments can protect your savings from market fluctuations. The restaurant’s diversification into catering helped increase its revenue.

antonyms: Uniform, Limited, Narrow, Specialized, Monolithic
urduMeaning: متنوع، مختلف النوع، کئی قسموں والا، جس میں مختلف اقسام سرگرمیاں یا شعبے شامل ہوں، جیسے کاروبار سرمایہ کاری یا مہارتوں میں تنوع
englishMeaning: Varied or including many different types. Having a wide range of different elements, activities, or forms. It often implies variety in investments, skills, products, or experiences to reduce risk or broaden scope.
sindhiMeaning: مختلف قسمن وارو، گهڻ رخو، متنوع، جيڪو ڪيترن قسمن يا شعبن تي مشتمل هجي جهڙوڪ ڪاروبار سيڙپڪاري يا صلاحيتن ۾ تنوع پيدا ڪرڻ، طرحين طرحين جو
examples: The company has a diversified portfolio of products to serve different markets. She has a diversified skill set, including writing, coding, and graphic design. Farmers are encouraged to grow a diversified range of crops to reduce risk. The investment fund is diversified, with stocks from multiple industries.
synonyms: Varied, Assorted, Multifaceted, Mixed, Multidimensional

antonyms: Monopolizer, Standardizer, Concentrator, Restrictor
urduMeaning: متنوع بنانے والا، کوئی شخص یا چیز جو کسی نظام کاروبار سرمایہ کاری یا سرگرمی میں تنوع پیدا کرے خطرہ کم کرے یا دائرہ کار کو وسیع کرے، یہ لفظ مالیات کاروبار زراعت یا حکمت عملی میں استعمال ہوتا ہے
synonyms: Varier, Broadener, Innovator, Risk-spreader
sindhiMeaning: مختلف ڪندڙ، تبديلي آڻيندڙ، ڪو به شخص يا شيءِ جيڪا ڪا شيءِ مختلف بڻائي نواڻ آڻي يا خطري کي گھٽائي جيئن ڪاروبار ۾ نوان شعبا سيڙپڪاريءَ ۾ مختلف آپشنز يا منصوبابندي ۾ تبديليون
englishMeaning: Something or someone that makes things more varied or introduces variety. A person, company, or tool that adds variety, reduces risk, or broadens scope in a system, business, investment, or activity. It is often used in finance, business, agriculture, or strategy.
examples: The company acted as a diversifier by investing in multiple industries. Introducing new crops can be a diversifier for farmers facing climate risks. Mutual funds serve as diversifiers for investors. Technology has become a diversifier in traditional business models.

urduMeaning: ایسے پودے یا پودوں کے مجموعے کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے جن میں طرح طرح کے یا مختلف شکلوں کے پھول پائے جائیں، یہ لفظ زیادہ تر نباتیات اور ماحولیاتی مطالعات میں اس وقت استعمال ہوتا ہے جب کسی منظر یا ماحول میں پھولوں کی بہت زیادہ اقسام موجود ہوں کبھی کبھار اسے بطور استعارہ بھی استعمال کیا جاتا ہے جہاں پھولوں کی رنگا رنگی نمایاں ہو
sindhiMeaning: گلن جا مختلف قسمون يا مختلف شڪليون رکندڙ ٻوٽو يا گلن جي مجموعي کي چئبو آهي، هي لفظ اڪثر نباتيات ۽ ماحوليات ۾ استعمال ٿئي ٿو جتي گلن جي گهڻائي ۽ تنوع ڏيکارڻ مقصود هجي، ڪڏهن ڪڏهن ڪنهن به جاءَ يا منظر لاءِ استعاري طور ڪم اچي ٿو جتي گلن جو گهڻو تنوع موجود هجي
antonyms: Uniflorous, Single flowered, Uniform flowering, Monofloral
synonyms: Variflorous, Multifloral, Many flowered, Mixed flowering, Flower diverse
englishMeaning: Having flowers of many kinds or of different forms. Used for plants or vegetation that produce a variety of flowers differing in size, shape, color or type. It describes botanical diversity within one plant or within a group of plants. A description for ecosystems or habitats that show floral variation, often used in ecology and botany. It can also be applied metaphorically for anything showing wide floral variety.
examples: The garden looked diversiflorous with dozens of species blooming together. A diversiflorous meadow attracts more insects and birds. The scientist studied a rare diversiflorous shrub found in the valley. Their field became diversiflorous after years of careful restoration.

urduMeaning: متنوع پتیوں والا، ایسے پودے یا درخت کی خصوصیت جس کے پتے مختلف شکلوں یا اقسام کے ہوں، یہ اصطلاح عام طور پر نباتات یا باغبانی میں استعمال ہوتی ہے
sindhiMeaning: مختلف پنن وارو، اهڙي ٻوٽي يا وڻ جي وصف جنهن جا پن هڪجهڙا نه هوندا يعني مختلف شڪل يا قسم جا هوندا
antonyms: Uniform-leaved, Monophyllous, Simple-leaved
englishMeaning: Having leaves of different shapes or types. A plant or tree that bears more than one type of leaf, showing diversity in leaf forms or shapes. Often used in botany or horticulture.
examples: The garden featured a diversifoliate tree that attracted botanists. Diversifoliate plants can adapt better to different climates. She studied the diversifoliate patterns of the tropical forest. The new park included diversifoliate shrubs for ornamental purposes.
synonyms: Varied-leaved, Heterophyllous, Multi-leaved, Polymorphic leaves

antonyms: Uniform leaved, Monomorphic, Same shaped leaves
urduMeaning: ایسا پودا جس کے پتے ایک جیسے نہ ہوں بلکہ مختلف شکلوں کے ہوں، یہ لفظ زیادہ تر نباتات میں پتوں کی ساخت کے تنوع کو ظاہر کرنے کے لئے استعمال ہوتا ہے، کبھی کبھی ادبی انداز میں بھی کسی ایسی چیز کے لئے بولا جاتا ہے جس میں مختلف شکلیں یا انداز پائے جائیں
examples: The diversifolious shrub caught the botanist’s attention during the field survey. Many aquatic plants become diversifolious as they adapt to changing water levels. The tree looked unusual because its diversifolious leaves changed shape from branch to branch. Diversifolious species often thrive in regions with varied temperatures.
sindhiMeaning: اهڙو ٻوٽو جنهن جا پن هڪ جهڙا نه هجن پر مختلف شڪلن جا هجن، انهي لفظ جو استعمال گهڻائي پنن واري شڪل جي تنوع لاءِ ٿيندو آهي، ڪڏهن ڪڏهن تشبيهي طور پڻ استعمال ڪيو ويندو آهي جنهن ۾ ڪنهن شيءِ ۾ گهڻائي شڪلون يا انداز هجن
synonyms: Variable leaved, Heterophyllous, Mixed leaved, Shape varied leaves
englishMeaning: Having leaves of different shapes. A plant with leaves that are not uniform in shape but show noticeable variety. Used in botany to describe a plant that bears leaves of varied forms on the same stem or plant. It highlights natural variation in leaf shape due to growth stage, environment, or genetic traits. Used to emphasize natural diversity in leaf morphology within a single plant. Sometimes applied metaphorically in literature to describe anything showing mixed forms or patterns.

antonyms: Uniform, Homogeneous, Single shaped
englishMeaning: Shaped in various forms. Having mixed or different shapes. Something that appears in a variety of shapes, patterns or structures. It is used for objects, natural forms, designs or anything that does not follow a single uniform shape.
examples: The artist used diversiform patterns to make the painting more vibrant. Coral reefs have a diversiform structure that supports many species. The museum displayed diversiform pottery from ancient cultures. The landscape was diversiform with hills, plains and rocky cliffs.
urduMeaning: کئی شکلوں والا، مختلف صورتوں پر مشتمل، وہ چیز یا شکل جو ایک جیسی نہ ہو بلکہ کئی طرح کی صورتیں رکھتی ہو، مختلف ڈھانچوں یا شکلوں کا مجموعہ، اس لفظ کا استعمال ان چیزوں کے لئے بھی ہوتا ہے جو ساخت یا شکل میں بہت مختلف ہوں، مختلف انداز کی ظاہری صورتیں رکھنا
sindhiMeaning: گهڻ شڪلين وارو، مختلف صورتن ۾ موجود، اهي شيون يا صورتون جيڪي هڪ جهڙيون نه هجن بلڪه ڪيترين قسمن جي شڪلين ۾ هجن، مختلف بناوٽن يا صورتن جو مجموعو، اهو لفظ انهن شين لاءِ به استعمال ٿيندو آهي جيڪي بناوت يا صورت ۾ گهڻو فرق رکن ٿيون، مختلف طرح جون بناوتون رکڻ
synonyms: Variform, Multiform, Diverse, Manifold, Heterogeneous

englishMeaning: Feeling of isolation or separation. The state of being estranged, isolated, or detached from others, oneself, or society. It can occur emotionally, socially, legally, or culturally. It includes feelings of disconnection, lack of belonging, or loss of rights. The transfer of ownership, rights, or interest in property from one person to another, usually permanently.
urduMeaning: بیگانگی کا عمل یا حالت، کسی شخص کا معاشرے یا گروہ سے کٹا ہوا محسوس کرنا، اپنے احساسات یا خیالات سے دور محسوس کرنا، جائیداد یا حقوق کو کسی اور کے حوالے کرنا یا چھوڑ دینا، معاشرتی رویوں یا روایات سے الگ ہونا، انتقال ملکیت ، اِنتِقالِ جائيداد ، غَيرِيَت
antonyms: Connection, Attachment, Integration, Belonging
sindhiMeaning: دوري، اجنبي، ماڻهوءَ جو سماج يا گروپ سان ڪٽيل محسوس ڪرڻ، پنهنجي احساسن يا سوچن کان پاڻ کي ڌار محسوس ڪرڻ، ملڪيت يا حقن کي ڪنهن ٻئي کي منتقل ڪرڻ يا دستبرداري، معاشرتي رويي يا رواجن کان ڪٽجڻ، جائداد جي مٽاسٽا يا وڪرو، اڻ بڻ، انتقال جائيداد، جائداد جو وڪڻي ڇڏڻ
synonyms: Estrangement, Isolation, Detachment, Separation
examples: The new employee experienced alienation in the office because no one talked to him. Alienation from family can cause emotional stress. englishMeaning: Fit or safe to eat. Suitable for eating. Safe for human consumption. Non poisonous food item. Food grade. Something that can be eaten safely and is suitable for food. It may be raw or cooked but should not be harmful.
examples: These berries are edible but not very tasty. The leaves of this plant are edible after cooking. Make sure the mushrooms are edible before eating them. The oil is edible and safe for cooking.

sindhiMeaning: سکيا ڏيڻ يا اخلاقي سڌارو آڻڻ، شعور پيدا ڪرڻ، ڪنهن کي اهڙي ريت سيکارڻ يا سمجهائڻ جنهن سان سندس علم اخلاق يا سوچ ۾ بهتري اچي، اهو لفظ خاص طور تي ذهني ۽ اخلاقي ترقي لاءِ استعمال ٿيندو آهي
antonyms: Mislead, Corrupt, Confuse, Degrade, Misinform
urduMeaning: اخلاقی یا ذہنی طور بہتر بنانا، تعلیم دینا، شعور پیدا کرنا، کسی کو اس انداز میں سکھانا یا رہنمائی کرنا جس سے اس کے علم کردار یا اخلاق میں بہتری آئے، یہ لفظ زیادہ تر ذہنی اور اخلاقی ترقی کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے
examples: Good books can edify readers and broaden their minds. The teacher tries to edify students through real life examples. His speech was meant to edify the audience, not just entertain them. Religious teachings often aim to edify people morally.
englishMeaning: To teach or improve someone morally or intellectually. To instruct someone in a way that improves their knowledge, character, or moral values. It is often used for learning that uplifts a person’s thinking or behavior.
synonyms: Educate, Instruct, Enlighten, Improve, Uplift, Guide

sindhiMeaning: اثرائتو، ڪارائتو، مؤثر، اهڙي شيءِ جيڪا مطلوب نتيجو ڏئي يا ڪامياب ٿي، طريقو يا علاج جيڪو ڪم ڪري ٿو
synonyms: Effective, Successful, Powerful, Potent, Productive
examples: Meditation proved efficacious in reducing stress. The new policy was efficacious in improving productivity. Vaccines are efficacious in preventing diseases. Her persuasive speech was highly efficacious in winning support.
englishMeaning: Effective; producing the intended result. Something that works well or achieves the desired effect. It refers to a method, action, or remedy that is successful in producing a result.
antonyms: Ineffective, Useless, Unproductive, Powerless, Unsuccessful
urduMeaning: مؤثر، مفید، نتیجہ خیز، ایسا کام یا طریقہ جو مطلوبہ نتیجہ حاصل کرے، مؤثر اور کامیاب

examples: Soldiers have to swear allegiance to the Crown, The King. People of various party allegiances joined the campaign. He affirmed his allegiance to the president. She proudly recited the Oath of Allegiance. The students pledge allegiance (to the flag) at the beginning of the school day.
englishMeaning: Loyalty and support for a ruler, country, group, or belief. The act of binding yourself (intellectually or emotionally) to a course of action. A person’s continued support for a political party, religion, leader, etc.
synonyms: Adhesion, Attachment, Commitment, Constancy, Dedication, Devotedness, Devotion, Faith, Faithfulness, Fidelity, Piety
antonyms: Disloyalty, Faithlessness, Falseness, Falsity, Inconstancy, Infidelity, Perfidiousness, Perfidy, Treachery, Unfaithfulness
urduMeaning: وَفا داری ، اطاعت ، عقيدَت ، لَگَن ،حَکُومت يا اپنے حاکَم کے ساتھ وَفاداری، تابع داری، حاکمیت کو ماننا ، محکومی قبُول کرنا ، فرماں برداری
sindhiMeaning: فرمانبرداري، آڻ، نمڪ حلالي، تابعداري، وفاداري، بيعت، اطاعت، عقيدت، حاڪميت کي مڃڻ يا محڪومي قبول ڪرڻ، آڻ مڃڻ
مجسمو، پُتلو، نمائنده شڪل، علامتي شڪل، مجسمي يا ڪنهن شخص جي تصوير، جيڪا اڪثر ڪري احتجاج ۾ ساڙڻ لاءِ تيار ڪئي ويندي آهي
antonyms: Reality, Being, Entity, Living person
synonyms: Figure, Image, Representation, Dummy, Sculpture, Likeness, Idol
examples: Protesters burned an effigy of the corrupt leader in the city square. The museum displayed an effigy of the ancient king made of stone. During the festival, villagers carried an effigy of the demon before setting it on fire. The artist sculpted an effigy of the national hero to honor his bravery.
urduMeaning: کسی شخص کا مجسمہ یا پتلا جو اکثر احتجاج میں جلایا جاتا ہے یا یادگار کے طور پر بنایا جاتا ہے، عموماً کپڑے، مٹی یا لکڑی سے بنایا گیا کسی حقیقی شخص کا پتلا یا مجسمہ
englishMeaning: A model, statue, or image representing a person, often made to be burned or destroyed in protest or anger. It can also refer to a likeness or figure made to honor or criticize someone.

sindhiMeaning: مساوات پسند، سڀني لاءِ برابري جو حق رکڻ وارو
urduMeaning: مساوات پسند، ہر شخص کو برابر حقوق دینے والا
examples: The country aims to build an egalitarian society where everyone has equal access to education. She is known for her egalitarian views on workplace promotions. His policies reflect an egalitarian approach to healthcare. The organization promotes an egalitarian environment free from discrimination.
synonyms: Equalitarian, Fair-minded, Impartial, Just
englishMeaning: Supporting the principle that all people should have equal rights, opportunities, and treatment, regardless of gender, race, or social status
antonyms: Unequal, Elitist, Discriminatory, Biased

urduMeaning: برابری پسندی، سب کو مساوی حقوق اور مواقع فراہم کرنے کا نظریہ،
sindhiMeaning: مساوات پسندي، سڀني ماڻهن کي برابر حق ڏيڻ جي خيال
antonyms: Inequality, Discrimination, Elitism, Unfairness
synonyms: Equality, Fairness, Impartiality, Equal rights
englishMeaning: Belief in equality for all people in rights and opportunities.
examples: The new government promoted egalitarianism in education by ensuring equal access for all children. She supports egalitarianism and fights against discrimination in the workplace. The movement aims to establish egalitarianism in society by reducing wealth gaps. His philosophy of egalitarianism emphasizes equal opportunities regardless of social status.

englishMeaning: To encourage someone to do something, often foolish or risky. To push or provoke a person into doing an action, especially something they might not do on their own or something unwise.
examples: His friends egged him up to jump into the river. Do not egg her up to argue with the teacher. They egged the crowd up until the situation got out of control. He was egged up by his classmates to break the rules.
synonyms: Encourage, Incite, Urge, Provoke
antonyms: Discourage, Deter, Restrain, Calm
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کي اُڪساڻ، ڪنهن ماڻهو کي ڪنهن ڪم لاءِ ڀڙڪائڻ يا زور ڏيڻ، خاص طور تي اهڙو ڪم جيڪو خطري وارو يا غلط هجي
urduMeaning: اُکسانا ، کسی شخص کو کسی کام پر آمادہ کرنا، خاص طور پر ایسا کام جو ناسمجھی یا خطرے والا ہو

englishMeaning: A purple vegetable, also called aubergine, commonly used in cooking. A large, glossy, purple or sometimes white vegetable that belongs to the nightshade family. It is often used in dishes such as curries, stews, and roasted preparations.
antonyms: There are no antonyms
sindhiMeaning: بينگن، واڳڻ، انڊا واري وڻ جو ڀاڄي، هڪ ڳاڙهي ۽ گُهڙو ڀاڄي جيڪا سالن ترڪاري ۽ روسٽ ڪرڻ لاءِ استعمال ٿئي ٿي
synonyms: Aubergine, Brinjal, Solanum melongena
urduMeaning: بینگن (ایک بڑی، جامنی رنگ کی سبزی جو کھانے میں استعمال ہوتی ہے)
examples: I roasted eggplant with olive oil for dinner. Baba ghanoush is made from mashed eggplant. She added slices of eggplant to the curry. The farmer grew eggplants in his garden.

urduMeaning: خود غرض، اپنے آپ کو مرکز مان رکھنا، دوسروں کی نظر انداز کرنا، خود پسند اور خود مرکز شخص، جو زیادہ تر اپنے بارے میں سوچتا ہے اور دوسروں کے جذبات یا ضرورتوں کا خیال کم رکھتا ہے
antonyms: Altruistic, Selfless, Considerate, Empathetic, Humble
sindhiMeaning: خود غرض، پنهنجو خيال رکڻ ۽ ٻين کي نظرانداز ڪرڻ، خودمرڪز شخص، جيڪو رڳو پاڻ بابت سوچيندو آهي ۽ ٻين جي احساسن يا ضرورتن جو گهڻو خيال نٿو ڪري
synonyms: Self-centered, Selfish, Narcissistic, Self-absorbed, Self-involved
examples: His egocentric attitude made it hard for him to work in a team. She refused to listen to anyone because of her egocentric nature. The manager's egocentric decisions often harmed the employees. Children can be egocentric as they are learning to understand others’ feelings.
englishMeaning: Thinking only about oneself; self-centered. Someone tends to focus on their own needs, desires, and opinions, often ignoring the feelings or perspectives of others. It reflects an excessive preoccupation with oneself.

synonyms: Shocking, Outrageous, Appalling, Flagrant, Terrible
examples: The report highlighted egregious violations of human rights. His egregious error cost the company millions of dollars. The teacher punished the student for egregious misconduct. The court condemned the egregious abuse of power.
sindhiMeaning: اُن عملن يا غلطيُن لاءِ استعمال ٿيندو آهي جيڪي تمام خراب بيحد غلط يا اخلاقي حدن کان ٻاهر هجن ۽ ماڻهن کي سخت ناراض ڪن
urduMeaning: ایسے عمل یا غلطی کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے جو حد سے زیادہ بری ناقابلِ قبول یا انتہائی شرمناک ہو اور سب کو واضح طور پر غلط محسوس ہو
englishMeaning: Extremely bad, shocking, or unacceptable. Something that is remarkably bad or offensive. It is used for actions, mistakes, or behavior that clearly cross acceptable limits and cause strong disapproval.
antonyms: Minor, Acceptable, Reasonable, Justified, Proper

synonyms: Get rid of, Cancel, Reject, Remove, Dump
examples: The waiter said they had to eighty-six the soup because it was finished. The boss decided to eighty-six the new policy. They eighty-sixed him from the club for breaking the rules. Let’s eighty-six that idea and try something better.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ يا ماڻهو کي ختم ڪرڻ، رد ڪرڻ يا ڪڍي ڇڏڻ، سروس ڏيڻ کان انڪار ڪرڻ، جڏهن ڪا شيءِ گهربل نه رهي يا ختم ڪئي وڃي، هوٽلن ۾ کاڌي جي شيءِ ختم ٿيڻ لاءِ استعمال ٿيندو آهي، ڪنهن ماڻهو کي جڳهه مان ڪڍڻ لاءِ پڻ
englishMeaning: To get rid of, reject, cancel, or refuse service to someone or something. Used when something is no longer wanted or allowed. Often heard in restaurants when an item is unavailable. Can also refer to removing a person from a place or list. It is commonly used in informal American English, especially in restaurants and casual conversation.
antonyms: Keep, Accept, Approve, Allow
urduMeaning: کسی چیز یا شخص کو ختم یا نکال دینا، مسترد کرنا، سروس دینے سے انکار کرنا، جب کسی چیز کو ختم یا رد کر دیا جائے، ہوٹل میں کسی چیز کے ختم ہونے پر استعمال ہوتا ہے، کسی شخص کو جگہ سے نکالنے کے لیے بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے

synonyms: Detailed, Intricate, Complex, Thorough, Comprehensive, Expand, Explain
sindhiMeaning: وڌيڪ وضاحت ڪرڻ، تفصيل سان بيان ڪرڻ، تفصيلوار، مفصل، تفصيلي، پيچيده، سنڀاليل، مڪمل، گھڻي محنت سان ٺاھيل
urduMeaning: وضاحت کرنا، تفصیل سے بیان کرنا، تفصیلی طور پر مکمل کرنا، مفصل، پیچیدہ، باریک بینی سے تیار کیا ہوا
englishMeaning: To explain or describe in more detail. To provide more information or expand on an idea or statement. Detailed, complex, or carefully planned. Something that is intricate, carefully designed, or contains many details.
examples: She had prepared a elaborate meal. The scientist gave an elaborate explanation of the experiment. She wore an elaborate dress for the party. Could you elaborate on your idea so everyone understands? The architect presented an elaborate plan for the new building. He said he was resigning but did not elaborate on his reasons.
antonyms: Simple, Plain, Brief, Concise, Summarize

examples: The medicine helped alleviate his headache. Good sleep can alleviate stress and anxiety. The government took steps to alleviate poverty. Warm tea may alleviate a sore throat.
sindhiMeaning: تڪليف درد يا ڏک کي گهٽائڻ، ڪنهن به تڪليف درد پريشاني يا ڏکيائي کي مڪمل ختم ڪرڻ کان سواءِ گهٽ ڪرڻ ته جيئن ان کي برداشت ڪرڻ آسان ٿي وڃي
englishMeaning: To make pain, suffering, or difficulty less severe. To reduce the intensity of something unpleasant such as pain, stress, hardship, or problems. It does not completely remove the issue but makes it easier to tolerate or manage.
synonyms: Reduce, Ease, Relieve, Lessen, Mitigate, Diminish
antonyms: Worsen, Aggravate, Increase, Intensify, Exacerbate
urduMeaning: تکلیف درد یا مشکل کو کم کرنا، کسی درد تکلیف پریشانی یا مشکل کو مکمل ختم کیے بغیر کم کرنا تاکہ اسے برداشت کرنا آسان ہو جائے

sindhiMeaning: هڪ طبي ٽيسٽ جنهن ۾ سر تي لڳايل اليڪٽروڊن ذريعي دماغ جي برقي سرگرمي کي رڪارڊ ڪيو ويندو آهي، هي ٽيسٽ دماغي بيمارين جي سڃاڻپ لاءِ استعمال ٿئي ٿو
urduMeaning: ایک طبی طریقہ جس میں سر پر لگے الیکٹروڈز کے ذریعے دماغ کی برقی سرگرمی کو ریکارڈ کیا جاتا ہے، اس سے دماغی بیماریوں کی تشخیص میں مدد ملتی ہے
antonyms: There is no direct antonym
synonyms: EEG (Electroencephalogram test), Brain wave test, Neural activity recording, Brain electricity monitoring
englishMeaning: A medical test that records the electrical activity of the brain using small electrodes placed on the scalp. A diagnostic technique used in medicine and neuroscience to measure and record brain wave patterns. It helps doctors study brain function and detect conditions such as epilepsy, sleep disorders, brain injuries, and other neurological problems. The test works by detecting electrical signals produced by neurons in the brain and converting them into a visual graph called an electroencephalogram.
examples: The doctor ordered an electroencephalography test to check for epilepsy. Electroencephalography helps in studying brain wave patterns during sleep. The hospital used EEG to monitor the patient after a head injury. Electroencephalography revealed abnormal brain activity in the patient.

urduMeaning: کسی شخص سے جواب معلومات یا احساس حاصل کرنا، کسی شخص سے ردعمل یا جذبات ظاہر کروانا، چھپی ہوئی بات کو سامنے لانا، کسی بات کو ظاہر ہونے کا سبب بننا، کسی کو بولنے پر آمادہ کرنا یا معلومات نکالنا، کسی بات یا سوال کے ذریعے کسی سے کوئی ردعمل یا بات نکالنا
antonyms: Suppress, Hide, Conceal, Stifle
englishMeaning: To bring out a response, answer, fact, or feeling. To get or extract a reply, fact, reaction, or feeling from someone. To draw out information, emotions, or reactions from someone through asking, probing, encouraging, or causing something to be revealed.
examples: The committee said that draft must be circulated to elicit opinion of all stakeholders. I could elicit no response from him. Her tears elicit great sympathy from her audience. The teacher tried to elicit a clear answer from the students. His joke elicited laughter from everyone in the room. The survey was designed to elicit honest feedback.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن مان جواب احساس يا معلومات ڪڍرائڻ، ڪنهن مان ڪو ردعمل يا جذبو ظاهر ڪرائڻ، لڪل ڳالهه يا معلومات ٻاهر ڪڍرائڻ، ڪنهن ڳالهه کي ظاهر ٿيڻ لاءِ سبب بڻجڻ، ڪنهن کي ڳالهائڻ يا ٻڌائڻ تي آماده ڪرڻ، ڪنهن ڳالهه يا سوال جي ذريعي ڪنهن مان ڪا ڳالهه ظاهر ڪرائڻ
synonyms: Extract, Bring out, Draw out, Obtain, Invoke, Evoke, Prompt

sindhiMeaning: بهترين ۽ بااثر ماڻهو يا طبقو، اهڙا ماڻهو جيڪي ڪنهن شعبي ۾ تمام ماهر هجن، اهڙو طبقو جيڪو سماج يا رياست ۾ خاص اثر رکي، چونڊيل ۽ مٿانهون گروهه، تمام اعليٰ ۽ شان وارو درجو، اهڙو ننڍڙو طبقو يا ماڻهو جيڪي پنهنجي قابليت هنر علم حيثيت يا اثر جي ڪري ٻين کان مٿانهون سمجهيا وڃن
urduMeaning: بہترین اور بااثر لوگ یا طبقہ، وہ لوگ جو کسی شعبے میں اعلیٰ مہارت رکھتے ہوں، ایسا طاقتور طبقہ جو فیصلوں پر اثر رکھتا ہو، منتخب اور اعلیٰ درجے کا گروہ، بہت اعلیٰ معیار یا حیثیت رکھنے والا درجہ، ایسا چھوٹا طبقہ یا لوگ جو اپنی صلاحیت ہنر علم حیثیت یا اثر و رسوخ کی وجہ سے دوسروں سے بلند سمجھے جاتے ہیں
antonyms: Ordinary, Common, Average, Lower class, General public
englishMeaning: A group of people who are considered the best, most skilled, most powerful or most influential in a society or field. A small group of people who stand out because of their high ability, high status, special skills, wealth, education or influence. People who hold power or have superior talent in comparison to the general population.
synonyms: Top class, Superior, Exceptional, High ranking, Privileged group
examples: In these countries only the elite can afford the education of their children. Only the elite students were selected for the international program. She trained with an elite group of athletes. The country is run by a small political elite. He belongs to an elite team of researchers.

urduMeaning: واضع کرنا، آشکار کرنا،وضاحت سے بیان کرنا، سمجھانا
sindhiMeaning: کولي ٻڌائڻ، سمجھائن، واضح ڪرڻ، تشريح ڪرڻ
antonyms: Confuse, Obscure, Complicate, Mislead
synonyms: Clarify, Explain, Illuminate, Expound, Illustrate
examples: The professor tried to elucidate the complex theory for the students. Can you elucidate your point with an example? The report elucidates the reasons behind the recent economic changes. She wrote an article to elucidate the process of renewable energy production.
englishMeaning: To make something clear. To explain in detail so that it is easy to understand.

antonyms: Face, Confront, Meet, Encounter
examples: The thief managed to elude the police for several hours. The meaning of the poem eludes many students. Sleep has been eluding me for the past few nights. He tried to answer, but the right words eluded him.
sindhiMeaning: بچي وڃڻ يا چالاڪي سان پري ٿيڻ، پڪڙ کان بچي وڃڻ، حاصل ٿيڻ کان رهجي وڃڻ، ڪنهن کان يا ڪنهن صورتحال کان چالاڪي تيزي يا حڪمت عملي سان بچي وڃڻ، اهو ان حالت ۾ به استعمال ٿئي ٿو جڏهن ڪا ڳالهه سمجهه ۾ نه اچي يا ذهن ۾ نه اچي
urduMeaning: بچ نکلنا یا چالاکی سے دور ہونا ، کسی سے یا کسی حالت سے ہوشیاری تیزی یا حکمت کے ساتھ بچ نکلنا، یہ اس وقت بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے جب کوئی بات سمجھ میں نہ آئے یا ذہن میں نہ آئے
synonyms: Avoid, Escape, Evade, Dodge, Sidestep, Flee, Slip away
englishMeaning: To escape, avoid, or slip away from something or someone, often in a clever or quick way. To avoid being caught, understood, or achieved. It can be used for physical escape, avoiding a question or responsibility, or when an idea or memory cannot be grasped.

urduMeaning: بچ نکلنے یا بچنے کا عمل، کسی چیز سے چالاکی سے بچ نکلنا، گریز کرنا یا گرفت سے بچ جانا ہے، یہ اکثر ہوشیاری سے بچنے کے مفہوم میں استعمال ہوتا ہے
examples: The thief's elusion of the police surprised everyone. His elusion of responsibility caused problems for the team. The animal's quick elusion made it hard to track. Her clever elusion of the question made the audience curious.
synonyms: Evasion, Avoidance, Escape, Dodging, Circumvention
sindhiMeaning: بچي نڪرڻ يا پاسو ڪرڻ جو عمل، ڪنهن شيءِ کان هوشياري سان بچي نڪرڻ، پاسو ڪرڻ يا پڪڙ کان بچڻ، اهو اڪثر ذهانت سان بچڻ لاءِ استعمال ٿيندو آهي
antonyms: Capture, Confrontation, Acceptance, Facing, Submission
englishMeaning: The act of escaping, avoiding, or slipping away from something. The act of evading, escaping, or avoiding something such as a person, question, responsibility, or capture. It often implies clever or skillful avoidance.

Something hard to find, catch, understand, or achieve. A person, idea, or thing that is difficult to locate, define, or grasp. It may also refer to someone who avoids being caught or avoids giving clear answers.
urduMeaning: مشکل سے ملنے والا، گرفت میں نہ آنے والا، سمجھنے میں مشکل، چکمہ دینے والا، نظروں سے اوجھل رہنے والا، گرفت سے بچنے والا، حاصل کرنا مشکل، توجہ سے بچنے والا
sindhiMeaning: مشڪل سان هٿ ايندڙ، پڪڙ ۾ نه ايندڙ، سمجهڻ ۾ ڏکيو، لڪل رهندڙ، پڪڙ کان بچندڙ، ڏسڻ ۾ ناياب، حاصل ڪرڻ ۾ ڏکيو، هٿ نه ايندڙ، پڪڙ کان بچندڙ، هٿ نه ايندڙ، نظر کان لڪل، ڌيان کان بچندڙ، صحيح طرح بيان نه ٿي سگهندڙ
antonyms: Accessible, Approachable
synonyms: Evasive, Intangible, Fugitive
examples: The solution to the problem remained elusive. The criminal was elusive and avoided the police for months. Happiness sometimes feels elusive in busy life. She gave an elusive answer instead of speaking directly.

The government imposed an embargo on oil exports to the neighboring country. The United Nations lifted the embargo after peace agreements were signed. The company faced an embargo on its products due to safety concerns. The country decided to embargo all shipments until inspections were complete.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ملڪ ڪمپني يا شخص تي واپار سامان جي منتقلي يا سرگرميون سرڪاري طور تي روڪڻ يا پابندي لڳائڻ، واپار تي پابندي
englishMeaning: To impose a formal ban or restriction on the export, import, or transport of goods, or on communication or activities, usually for political, economic, or security reasons.
synonyms: Ban, Restriction, Prohibition, Blockade, Moratorium
antonyms: Permission, Approval, Free trade, Lift
urduMeaning: کسی ملک ادارے یا شخص پر تجارتی اشیاء آمد و رفت یا سرگرمیوں کو سرکاری طور پر روکنے یا پابندی لگانے کا عمل عموماً سیاسی یا اقتصادی وجوہات کی بنا پر، تجارتی پابندی

examples: Children often play hide and seek in the narrow alley behind the school. The small alley led to a hidden garden. Trash bins were lined up along the alley. He got lost while walking through the maze-like alleys of the old city.
sindhiMeaning: تنگ رستو، سوڙهي گهٽي، بند گهٽي، سوڙهو لنگهه، تنگ گلي، تنگ رستو جيڪو عمارتن جي وچ ۾ هجي، ماڻهن جي هلڻ لاءِ يا ڪاروباري/سروس لاءِ استعمال ٿيندو آهي
synonyms: Lane, Passage, Path, Corridor, Walkway
urduMeaning: تنگ راستہ، تنگ گلی، ایک تنگ راستہ جو عمارتوں کے درمیان ہوتا ہے، پیدل چلنے یا کچھ خدمات انجام دینے کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے
englishMeaning: A small, narrow lane or passage often found between or behind buildings. It can serve as a pedestrian path, service road, or shortcut. Some alleys may be quiet and residential, while others may be dark and commercial.
antonyms: Avenue, Boulevard, Street, Road

urduMeaning: جنگ کے لیے تیار کرنا، فوج یا دفاع کو لڑائی کے لیے منظم یا تیار کرنا، کسی جگہ کو حملے کے لیے مضبوط کرنا
antonyms: Retreat, Withdraw, Disorganize, Abandon
englishMeaning: To prepare or arrange for battle. To organize troops, fortifications, or defenses for fighting; to put into a state of readiness for combat or conflict.
synonyms: Fortify, Marshal, Deploy, Arrange
sindhiMeaning: جنگ لاءِ تيار ڪرڻ، فوج يا دفاع کي ترتيب ڏيڻ، فوج يا دفاع کي ترتيب ڏيڻ، جنگ لاءِ تيار ڪرڻ، ڪنهن جاءِ کي مضبوط ڪرڻ
examples: The general embattled his forces along the river. Villagers embattled their homes against the incoming storm. They embattled the city walls to withstand the attack. Leaders embattled their arguments in the debate.

synonyms: Insert, Fix, Implant, Ingrain, Integrate, Incorporate
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ کي ٻي شيءِ جي اندر مضبوطي سان لڳائڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ کي اهڙي طرح اندر لڳائڻ يا رکڻ جو اهو ان جو مستقل حصو بڻجي وڃي، هي لفظ خيالن نظامن يا ڊجيٽل مواد کي ويب سائيٽ يا دستاويز ۾ شامل ڪرڻ لاءِ به استعمال ٿيندو آهي
examples: The engineer embedded the metal rod in concrete for strength. Good values should be embedded in the education system. She embedded a video in her presentation to explain the topic. The journalist was embedded with the army during the operation.
englishMeaning: To fix something firmly inside another thing. To place, fix, or insert something deeply and firmly within another object, structure, idea, or system so that it becomes a permanent or natural part of it. It is also used for including media, data, or information within digital content such as a website or document.
urduMeaning: کسی چیز کو مضبوطی سے اندر جمانا یا شامل کرنا، کسی چیز کو دوسری چیز کے اندر اس طرح شامل یا نصب کرنا کہ وہ اس کا مستقل حصہ بن جائے، یہ لفظ خیالات کو نظام میں شامل کرنے یا ویب سائٹ میں ویڈیو اور کوڈ شامل کرنے کے لیے بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے
antonyms: Remove, Extract, Detach, Separate, Dislodge

englishMeaning: Decorative details, additions, or improvements that make something more beautiful, attractive, or impressive. It can also mean adding imaginative details to a story so it sounds more interesting than the original facts.
antonyms: Plainness, Simplicity, Bareness, Reduction
sindhiMeaning: اهڙو سينگار سجاوٽ يا اضافو جيڪو ڪنهن شيءِ کي وڌيڪ خوبصورت دلڪش يا متاثر ڪندڙ بڻائي، ڳالهه يا ڪهاڻي کي وڌيڪ دلچسپ بڻائڻ لاءِ حقيقتن ۾ اضافي تفصيل شامل ڪرڻ جو عمل
urduMeaning: ایسی سجاوٹ آرائش یا اضافہ جو کسی چیز کو زیادہ خوبصورت دلکش یا متاثر کن بنائے، یہ کسی کہانی یا بیان میں اضافی تفصیلات شامل کرنے کو بھی کہتے ہیں تاکہ وہ زیادہ دلچسپ لگے
examples: The dress had beautiful embellishments made with small pearls and beads. The writer added some embellishment to the story to make it more exciting. The palace walls were famous for their artistic embellishments. His speech contained a little embellishment, but the main idea was true.
synonyms: Decoration, Ornamentation, Adornment, Enhancement, Elaboration

sindhiMeaning: ڦٻائڻ، پيسا کائي وڃڻ، ڪنهن جي ذميواري هيٺ رکيل پيسا يا مال چوري ڪرڻ خاص ڪري نوڪري يا عهدو هئڻ دوران، غبن ڪرڻ، ذميواريءَ دوران مال يا پئسا ناجائز استعمال ڪرڻ، سرڪاري يا خانگي وسيلن جو غلط استعمال ڪرڻ، ڪنهن جي ملڪيت کي پنهنجو ڪرڻ يا لُٽي وٺڻ
antonyms: Give, Receive, Compensate, Pay, Reimburse, Return
examples: He was found guilty of embezzling $150 000 of public funds. She embezzled thousands of dollars from the charity. It was clear that funds were being embezzled but who could be doing it? He was caught embezzling money from his clients.
englishMeaning: To steal money or property from one’s organization or employer. To secretly take money or property entrusted to you, usually for personal use. It involves theft or misappropriation by someone in a position of trust, such as an employee, manager, or public official.
synonyms: Misappropriate, Misapply, Peculate, Misuse
urduMeaning: غبن کرنا ، خیانت کرنا ، خر دبرد کرنا ، چرالینا، فراڈ کرنا، رقم چو ری کرنا، کسی شخص کا اپنی تحویل میں دی جانے والی چیز کو ذاتی استعمال کے لیے دھوکے سے ہتھیا لینا

examples: She was found guilty of embezzlement. They were arrested for embezzlement of company funds. He's accused of tax evasion, embezzlement, and fraud. Their embezzlement bankrupted the firm. Their embezzlement bankrupted the firm.
sindhiMeaning: خيانت، غبن، تغلب، ڪپت، ٺڳي، پيسا کائڻ، ڪنهن جي ذميداري ۾ ڏنل پئسا يا ملڪيت کي چوري ڪرڻ يا غلط استعمال ڪرڻ جو عمل خاص طور تي نوڪريندڙ يا سرڪاري آفيسر طرفان
urduMeaning: دست برد ، غبن ، خیانت، دھوکہ، خورد برد، سرکاری یا ذمے دار اثاثوں کی چوری، اعتماد میں دی گئی چیز یا رقم کا ناجائز استعمال
synonyms: Misapplication, Misappropriation, Peculation, Fraud
englishMeaning: The act of stealing money that you are responsible for or that belongs to your employer. The crime of secretly taking money that is in your care or that belongs to an organization or business you work for.
antonyms: Compensation, Pay, Reimbursement, Return

synonyms: Symbol, Badge, Insignia, Mark, Token
englishMeaning: A symbol or sign that represents an idea, quality, group, or organization. A picture, design, object, or mark used to represent a particular meaning, value, nation, institution, or belief. It often appears on flags, badges, uniforms, and official documents to show identity or authority.
urduMeaning: نشان ، علامت، ایک خاص علامت نقش یا نشان ہوتا ہے جو کسی قوم تنظیم ادارے یا نظریے کی نمائندگی کرتا ہے، یہ اکثر جھنڈوں بیجز یونیفارم یا سرکاری دستاویزات پر شناخت کے طور پر استعمال ہوتا ہے
examples: The national flower became an emblem of the country's culture. The school uniform carried the emblem of the institution on the pocket. The dove is often used as an emblem of peace. The organization placed its emblem on every official document.
sindhiMeaning: علامت، نشاني، سڃاڻپ جو نشان، بيج، نمائندگي ڪندڙ تصوير، اهڙي تصوير نشاني يا ڊيزائن کي چوندا آهن جيڪا ڪنهن ملڪ تنظيم اداري يا خيال جي نمائندگي ڪري، اها عام طور تي جهنڊن بيجن يونيفارم يا سرڪاري دستاويزن تي سڃاڻپ طور استعمال ٿيندي آهي
antonyms: Reality, Substance, Actual object, Literal thing

urduMeaning: مظہر، مجسم صورت، پیکر، تشکیل، نمونہ، مثال
synonyms: Personification, Incarnation, Representation, Epitome, Manifestation
sindhiMeaning: مظهر، مجسم صورت، تجسيم، حقيقي صورت، نمائندگي، نمونو، مثال
examples: She is the embodiment of kindness and compassion. The leader became the embodiment of courage during the crisis. This painting is the embodiment of beauty and harmony. His actions were the very embodiment of honesty and integrity.
englishMeaning: A visible or living form of an abstract idea, quality, or feeling. A perfect representation of a particular trait or concept. Someone or something that shows a quality in its purest form.
antonyms: Abstraction, Disembodiment
Rivalry, Opposition, Conflict, Antagonism
urduMeaning: اتحاد، دو یا زیادہ فریقین کے درمیان باہمی تعاون یا مفاد کے لیے بنایا گیا معاہدہ، یہ سیاسی اقتصادی فوجی یا سماجی ہو سکتا ہے
sindhiMeaning: اتحاد، ٻن يا وڌيڪ ڌرين جو گڏجي ڪم ڪرڻ يا تعاون ڪرڻ جو معاهدو، اهو سياسي اقتصادي فوجي يا سماجي مقصدن لاءِ ٿي سگهي ٿو
examples: The two countries formed a military alliance to strengthen their defense. Several companies entered an alliance to develop new technology. She sought an alliance with local organizations to support her project. The political parties formed an alliance before the elections.
englishMeaning: A relationship formed between two or more parties to cooperate for specific purposes, such as political, economic, military, or social goals. It often involves trust and shared interests.
synonyms: Partnership, Coalition, Union, Association, Collaboration

antonyms: Hide, Conceal, Suppress, Separate, Exclude
synonyms: Represent, Express, Personify, Reflect, Incorporate
englishMeaning: To represent or show an idea or quality clearly. To give a visible or concrete form to an idea, feeling, quality, or principle. When someone or something embodies something, it perfectly represents or includes that quality in action or appearance.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن خاص خيال يا خوبي کي ظاهر ڪرڻ، ڪنهن خيال خوبي يا احساس کي عملي يا ظاهري صورت ۾ پيش ڪرڻ، يعني اهڙي نموني ظاهر ڪرڻ جو ماڻهو ان کي ڏسي يا سمجهي سگهي
examples: She embodies kindness through her actions. The constitution embodies the values of democracy. His work embodies years of experience and dedication. This project embodies our vision for the future.
urduMeaning: کسی خیال یا خوبی کی نمائندگی کرنا، کسی خیال اصول یا خوبی کو عملی یا ظاہری شکل میں پیش کرنا، یعنی کسی چیز یا شخص میں اس کا مکمل اظہار ہونا

synonyms: Hug, Clasp, Accept, Adopt, Welcome
englishMeaning: To hold someone closely with affection. To accept or adopt something willingly. To hug someone as a sign of love, comfort, or greeting. To accept an idea, belief, opportunity, or change with readiness and positivity. A hug or the act of holding someone closely in the arms.
examples: She embraced her friend after many years apart. The community embraced new technology to improve education. He decided to embrace the challenges of his new job. The policy embraces several ideas for environmental protection. She greeted her mother with a warm embrace. Their emotional embrace showed how much they missed each other.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کي پيار سان ڀاڪر پائڻ يا ڪنهن ڳالهه کي خوشي سان قبول ڪرڻ، ڪنهن کي محبت يا همدردي سان ڀاڪر ۾ وٺڻ، ڪنهن خيال تبديلي يا موقعي کي دل سان قبول ڪرڻ، ڀاڪر يا ڪنهن کي ٻانهن ۾ وٺڻ جو عمل
antonyms: Reject, Refuse, Avoid, Resist, Ignore
urduMeaning: کسی کو محبت سے گلے لگانا یا کسی خیال یا موقعے کو قبول کرنا، کسی شخص کو پیار یا تسلی کے طور پر گلے لگانا، کسی خیال تبدیلی یا موقعے کو خوشی سے قبول کرنا، گلے لگانے کا عمل

examples: Many people emigrate to Canada for better job opportunities. His family decided to emigrate after the economic crisis. She emigrated from Pakistan to Australia ten years ago. Thousands of workers emigrate every year in search of a stable future. He emigrated from Pakistan.
synonyms: Move abroad, Leave one’s country, Relocate overseas, Settle abroad
englishMeaning: To leave one’s own country to live permanently in another country. To move out of your native country with the intention of settling in a foreign country, usually for better living conditions, work, education, or safety.
antonyms: Immigrate, Return, Come back, Stay
urduMeaning: مستقل طور پر اپنا ملک چھوڑ کر کسی دوسرے ملک میں جا کر رہنا، بہتر زندگی، روزگار، تعلیم یا تحفظ کے لیے اپنا ملک چھوڑ کر مستقل طور پر کسی دوسرے ملک میں جا کر آباد ہو نا
sindhiMeaning: هميشه لاءِ پنهنجو ملڪ ڇڏي ٻئي ملڪ ۾ رهڻ وڃڻ، وزگار، تعليم، بهتر زندگي يا حفاظت لاءِ پنهنجو ملڪ ڇڏي هميشه لاءِ ٻئي ملڪ ۾ وڃي آباد ٿيڻ

synonyms: Migration, Relocation, Exodus, Departure, Outmigration
sindhiMeaning: اهو عمل جنهن ۾ ماڻهو پنهنجو اصل ملڪ ڇڏي ڪنهن ٻئي ملڪ ۾ مستقل طور رهڻ لاءِ منتقل ٿين، اهو اڪثر روزگار تعليم تحفظ يا بهتر زندگي لاءِ ڪيو ويندو آهي
examples: Emigration from rural areas increased due to lack of jobs. His emigration to Canada changed his family’s future. Economic hardship often leads to emigration. The government is studying the effects of emigration on the workforce.
urduMeaning: وہ عمل جس میں لوگ اپنے آبائی ملک کو چھوڑ کر کسی دوسرے ملک میں مستقل طور پر رہائش اختیار کرے، یہ عام طور پر بہتر روزگار تعلیم تحفظ یا معیارِ زندگی کے لیے ہوتا ہے
englishMeaning: The process in which people move out of their native country to settle in another country, usually for better employment, education, safety, or living conditions. The focus of the word is on leaving the home country.
antonyms: Immigration, Repatriation, Return, Resettlement at home
Loss, Debt, Penalty, Unpaid work, Expense
urduMeaning: تنخواہ، معاوضہ، الاؤنس یا کسی عہدے یا ملازمت سے حاصل ہونے والا مالی فائدہ، خدمات کا معاوضہ، ملازمت سے حاصل آمدنی، مالی فائدہ، سرکاری تنخواہ بمعہ الاؤنس
sindhiMeaning: اجورو، پگهار، نوڪري يا عهدو سنڀالڻ تي ملندڙ مالي فائدو يا الائونس، خدمت جو معاوضو، روزگار مان حاصل ٿيندڙ ڪمائي مالي فائدو، سرڪاري پگهار سان گڏ الائونس
englishMeaning: Payment or salary received for work or holding a position. Money, salary, allowance, or benefits earned from employment or office. It can include wages, bonuses, perks, or any financial gain from a job.
synonyms: Salary, Wage, Pay, Compensation, Remuneration, Allowance, Income
examples: The manager received a high emolument for his services. Government officials must declare their emoluments publicly. The job offers attractive emoluments and benefits. Her emolument increased after the promotion.

urduMeaning: ہمدردی ، احساسِ شراکت، کسی دوسرے شخص کے جذبات یا حالات کو سمجھنے اور ان کا احساس کرنے کی صلاحیت، جب آپ کسی کے دکھ یا خوشی کو اپنے دل میں محسوس کرتے ہیں
antonyms: Indifference, Cruelty, Apathy, Coldness, Harshness
englishMeaning: The ability to understand and share another person’s feelings, thoughts, or experiences. Feeling with someone rather than just for them, putting yourself in their place
sindhiMeaning: همدردي، احساس ڪرڻ جي صلاحيت، ٻين جي جذبن ۽ احساسن کي سمجهڻ ۽ محسوس ڪرڻ جي صلاحيت، جڏهن ڪو شخص ٻئي جي تڪليف خوشي يا حالتن کي پنهنجو سمجهي ساڻس گڏ محسوس ڪري
synonyms: Compassion, Understanding, Kindness, Sensitivity, Sympathy
examples: Her empathy for the poor made her volunteer at the shelter every weekend. A good leader shows empathy toward team members facing challenges. Teachers need empathy to understand their students’ emotional needs. He listened with empathy, offering comfort without judgment.

urduMeaning: کسی بات پر خاص زور، کسی خیال لفظ یا عمل پر زیادہ توجہ یا زور دینا تاکہ وہ بات نمایاں ہو جائے
examples: The teacher placed emphasis on good handwriting. He spoke with emphasis to make his point clear. The report gives emphasis to education improvement. She put emphasis on honesty in her speech.
synonyms: Stress, Importance, Focus, Attention, Highlight, Weight
englishMeaning: Special importance given to something. Giving extra attention, importance, or stress to a particular idea, word, or action so that it stands out clearly.
antonyms: Neglect, Disregard, Ignorance, Unimportance, Indifference
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ڳالهه تي خاص زور، ڪنهن خيال لفظ يا عمل تي وڌيڪ ڌيان يا زور ڏيڻ ته جيئن اها ڳالهه صاف ۽ اهم نظر اچي

antonyms: Ignore, Downplay, Minimize, Neglect, De-emphasize
urduMeaning: کسی بات پر خاص زور دینا، کسی بات کو نمایاں کرنا اہمیت دینا یا خاص طور پر زور دے کر بیان کرنا، نمایاں کرنا، اہمیت واضح کرنا، اہم سمجھنا یا وزن دینا
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ڳالهه تي خاص زور ڏيڻ، ڳالهه کي نمايان ڪرڻ اهميت ڏيکارڻ يا خاص طور زور ڏئي بيان ڪرڻ، نمايان ڪرڻ، اهميت ظاهر ڪرڻ، وزن ڏيڻ يا اهم سمجھڻ
examples: The teacher emphasized the importance of practice. He emphasized that honesty is the best policy. The report emphasizes safety measures. She emphasized her main point during the meeting.
synonyms: Stress, Highlight, Underline, Accentuate, Point out
englishMeaning: To give special importance to something. To give special attention. To highlight, stress, or make something more noticeable or important in speech or writing.

synonyms: Experiential, Experimental, Factual, Observational, Observed, Pragmatic, Provisional
englishMeaning: A person who relies solely on practical experience rather than on scientific principles. A person who practices medicine, treatment, or another skill based mainly on practical experience, not on established scientific principles or formal training.
