synonyms: Fear of words, Verbal anxiety, Speech phobia
examples: His logophobia made public speaking nearly impossible. She developed logophobia after being mocked for her vocabulary. Logophobia can interfere with daily communication significantly. The therapist worked with him to overcome his logophobia.
englishMeaning: An intense fear of words, particularly certain words, or a fear of speaking or expressing oneself verbally. It can also refer to a fear of the power or consequences of words.

synonyms: Fear of imperfection, Perfectionism disorder, Self-doubt phobia
sindhiMeaning: ناقص هجڻ يا ڪافي سٺو نه هجڻ جو خوف، اهڙو شخص هميشه غلطيون ڪرڻ يا پنهنجي اعليٰ معيار کي پورو نه ڪري سگهڻ کان ڊڄندو رهي ٿو
examples: Her atelophobia caused her to rewrite every email several times. Atelophobia often goes hand in hand with perfectionism. His atelophobia prevented him from submitting his work. She sought counselling to manage her atelophobia.
urduMeaning: ناقص ہونے یا کافی اچھا نہ ہونے کا خوف، اس فوبیا میں مبتلا شخص ہمیشہ غلطی کرنے یا اپنے اعلیٰ معیار پر پورا نہ اترنے سے ڈرتا رہتا ہے
englishMeaning: The fear of imperfection or of not being good enough. A person with atelophobia is constantly afraid of making mistakes or failing to meet their own high standards.
antonyms: Self-acceptance, Contentment, Confidence

sindhiMeaning: نين شين، تبديليءَ يا نون تجربن کان خوف، اهڙو شخص ڪجهه به نئون آزمائڻ کان ڊڄندو آهي
englishMeaning: The fear of new things, change, or novel experiences. A person with neophobia is reluctant or afraid to try anything new or unfamiliar.
antonyms: Neophilia (love of new things), Open-mindedness
synonyms: Fear of change, Misoneism, Resistance to novelty
urduMeaning: نئی چیزوں، تبدیلی یا نئے تجربات سے خوف، اس فوبیا میں مبتلا شخص کچھ بھی نیا آزمانے سے ڈرتا ہے
examples: His neophobia made it hard to adapt to new technology. Neophobia in children is often expressed as picky eating. Her neophobia kept her stuck in the same job for decades. The company's neophobia towards innovation led to its decline.

sindhiMeaning: نون تجربن يا تبديليءَ کان انتهائي خوف، جيڪو نيوفوبيا جهڙو آهي پر وڌيڪ شديد آهي
examples: Kainophobia prevented him from moving to a new city. Her kainophobia was triggered by the announcement of a new school curriculum. He struggled with kainophobia after returning from war. Kainophobia can make life in a rapidly changing world very difficult.
synonyms: Fear of novelty, Neophobia, Change aversion
antonyms: Adventurousness, Neophilia, Openness
englishMeaning: An extreme or irrational fear of novelty, newness, or change. Very similar to neophobia, it specifically relates to an overwhelming dread of anything new or different.
urduMeaning: نئے تجربات یا تبدیلی کا انتہائی خوف، جو نیوفوبیا سے ملتا جلتا لیکن زیادہ شدید ہے

antonyms: Comfort in crowds, Sociability
synonyms: Fear of crowds, Ochlophobia, Crowd anxiety
englishMeaning: An intense fear of crowds or densely populated places. A person with enochlophobia feels extreme anxiety, panic, or discomfort when surrounded by large groups of people.
examples: Her enochlophobia made it impossible to attend concerts. He experienced panic attacks due to enochlophobia at the market. Enochlophobia became worse for many people after the pandemic. She avoided shopping malls because of her enochlophobia.
urduMeaning: ہجوم یا بھیڑ والی جگہوں سے شدید خوف، اس فوبیا میں مبتلا شخص بھیڑ میں سخت اضطراب یا گھبراہٹ محسوس کرتا ہے
sindhiMeaning: ڀيڙ يا گهڻن ماڻهن واري جاءِ کان شديد خوف، اهڙو شخص ڀيڙ ۾ سخت پريشاني يا گهٻراهٽ محسوس ڪري ٿو

synonyms: Nosophobia, Hypochondria, Disease phobia
examples: His pathophobia led him to wash his hands dozens of times a day. She refused to leave home during flu season due to pathophobia. Pathophobia is closely related to hypochondria. His pathophobia worsened significantly after the pandemic.
urduMeaning: بیماری یا مرض میں مبتلا ہونے کا شدید اور غیر منطقی خوف، اس فوبیا میں مبتلا شخص ہمیشہ بیمار پڑنے کی فکر میں رہتا ہے
englishMeaning: An excessive and irrational fear of disease or suffering from illness. A person with pathophobia is constantly worried about contracting diseases even without any real medical evidence.
sindhiMeaning: بيماري يا مرض ۾ مبتلا ٿيڻ جو شديد ۽ غير منطقي خوف، اهڙو شخص هميشه بيمار ٿيڻ جي فڪر ۾ رهي ٿو
antonyms: Fearlessness, Medical confidence

englishMeaning: An intense fear of crowds, mobs, or large gatherings of people. Similar to enochlophobia but specifically focused on the fear of mobs and their potential danger.
antonyms: Comfort in crowds, Social ease
sindhiMeaning: ڀيڙ هجوم يا وڏي انگ ۾ ماڻهن کان شديد خوف، خاص طور انهن جي ممڪن خطري جي ڪري
synonyms: Fear of crowds, Ochlophobia, Enochlophobia
urduMeaning: ہجوم  مجمع یا بڑے اجتماع سے شدید خوف، خاص طور پر ان کے ممکنہ خطرے کی وجہ سے
examples: Her demophobia flared up at the political rally. He avoided city centres because of his demophobia. Demophobia became common after violent mob incidents. She felt her demophobia worsen at the overcrowded festival.

synonyms: Fear of travel, Travel anxiety, Dromomania aversion
urduMeaning: سفر کرنے یا راستے میں ہونے سے شدید اور غیر منطقی خوف، اس فوبیا میں مبتلا شخص کسی بھی طرح کے سفر سے گھبراتا ہے
examples: Her hodophobia meant she had never left her hometown. His hodophobia was triggered by a bad car accident. Hodophobia can severely limit a person's career opportunities. She turned down the job offer abroad due to her hodophobia.
sindhiMeaning: سفر ڪرڻ يا رستي ۾ هجڻ کان شديد ۽ غير منطقي خوف، اهڙو شخص ڪنهن به قسم جي سفر کان ڊڄندو آهي
englishMeaning: An intense and irrational fear of travel or of being in transit. A person with hodophobia may avoid any form of travel including road trips, flights, or even short journeys.
antonyms: Wanderlust, Love of travel, Dromomania
Road confidence, Traffic ease
urduMeaning: سڑکیں پار کرنے یا ٹریفک سے شدید خوف، اس فوبیا میں مبتلا شخص مصروف سڑکوں کے قریب یا پار کرتے وقت سخت اضطراب محسوس کرتا ہے
englishMeaning: An extreme fear of crossing streets or of roads and traffic. A person with dromophobia feels intense anxiety when near busy roads or when required to cross them.
examples: His dromophobia made commuting to work extremely stressful. She took long detours to avoid crossing busy roads due to dromophobia. Dromophobia can be treated with gradual exposure therapy. His dromophobia developed after he witnessed a road accident.
synonyms: Fear of crossing streets, Road anxiety, Traffic phobia
sindhiMeaning: رستا/ روڊ پار ڪرڻ يا ٽريفڪ کان شديد خوف، اهڙو شخص مصروف رستن جي ويجهو هجڻ تي سخت پريشاني محسوس ڪري ٿو

examples: She faced the tragedy with remarkable equanimity. His equanimity during the crisis inspired everyone around him. It takes great equanimity to remain calm during a storm. She accepted the criticism with equanimity and grace.
synonyms: Composure, Serenity, Calmness, Tranquillity, Poise
urduMeaning: ذہنی سکون اور متانت، خاص طور پر مشکل حالات میں جذباتی استحکام اور صبر و ضبط
antonyms: Anxiety, Agitation, Distress, Panic, Turmoil
sindhiMeaning: ذهني سڪون ۽ پُرسڪوني، خاص طور تڪليف يا دٻاءُ جي صورتحال ۾ جذباتي استحڪام ۽ صبر
englishMeaning: Mental calmness and composure, especially in difficult situations. The ability to remain emotionally stable and composed under pressure, stress, or adversity.

urduMeaning: عارضی طور پر معطل یا روکی ہوئی حالت، کسی معاملے کا وقتی طور پر موقوف ہونا
antonyms: Activity, Continuation, Progress, Action
synonyms: Suspension, Dormancy, Inactivity, Postponement, Hiatus
englishMeaning: A state of temporary suspension or inactivity; a condition of being held back or paused. Very similar to abeyance, referring to something temporarily set aside.
sindhiMeaning: عارضي طور تي معطل يا روڪيل حالت، جيئن ڪنهن معاملي کي وقتي طور تي پاسي رکيل هجي
examples: The project remained in abeyancy until new funds arrived. The law was held in abeyancy pending a court review. His plans fell into abeyancy during the pandemic. The committee kept the decision in abeyancy for six months.

The rival company upped the ante by cutting prices further. He upped the ante in the negotiation by threatening to walk out. The new offer upped the ante and forced a quick decision. She upped the ante by demanding a promotion along with the raise.
englishMeaning: To increase the stakes, demands, or risks in a situation. To raise the level of competition, expectation, or commitment in a negotiation or contest.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن معاملي ۾ شرط، گهرج يا خطري کي وڌائڻ، مقابلي يا گفتگو ۾ سطح کي اوچو ڪرڻ
synonyms: Raise the stakes, Increase pressure, Escalate, Intensify
antonyms: Lower the stakes, Back down, Reduce pressure
urduMeaning: کسی معاملے میں شرط، مطالبات یا خطرات بڑھانا، مقابلے یا گفتگو کی سطح کو بلند کرنا

antonyms: Active, Ongoing, In progress
urduMeaning: عارضی طور پر معطل یا روکے رکھنا، 'ابیئنس' کا قدیم یا کم استعمال شدہ روپ
englishMeaning: An archaic or rare form related to 'abeyance', meaning to hold in a state of suspension or temporary inactivity. Not commonly used in modern English.
examples: The matter was held in abey until further notice. The funds remained in abey for the entire fiscal year. The project was kept in abey pending approval. His appointment was left in abey by the committee.
sindhiMeaning: عارضي طور تي معطل يا روڪيل رکڻ، 'ابيئنس' جو پراڻو يا گهٽ استعمال ٿيندڙ روپ
synonyms: Suspended, Dormant, Held back, Paused

sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن بيڪار يا بي معنيٰ ڪم ڪرڻ جو مزاحيه اظهار، يا ڪنهن ڳالهه کي وڌاءِ چاءِ پيش ڪرڻ
examples: Trying to fix that old machine is like inflating a cow. He inflated the cow by turning a minor issue into a major scandal. Stop inflating the cow and focus on real problems. She had a habit of inflating the cow in every team meeting.
synonyms: Exaggerate, Blow out of proportion, Make a mountain of a molehill
urduMeaning: کسی بیکار یا بے معنی کام کے لیے طنزیہ اظہار، یا کسی بات کو بڑھا چڑھا کر پیش کرنا
antonyms: Understate, Minimise, Downplay
englishMeaning: A humorous or informal expression meaning to do something pointless, absurd, or unnecessarily complicated. It can also mean to exaggerate or blow something out of proportion.

examples: The project was held in abeyance due to lack of funds. The law remained in abeyance for several years. His ambitions fell into abeyance after the accident. The court kept the decision in abeyance pending appeal.
synonyms: Suspension, Postponement, Dormancy, Inactivity, Hiatus
englishMeaning: A state of temporary suspension or inactivity. When something is in abeyance, it is paused, delayed, or held back until a later time.
antonyms: Activity, Continuity, Progress, Resolution
urduMeaning: عارضی طور پر معطل یا روکی ہوئی حالت، جب کوئی معاملہ وقتی طور پر ملتوی یا موقوف کر دیا جائے
sindhiMeaning: عارضي طور تي معطل يا روڪيل حالت، جڏهن ڪو معاملو وقتي طور تي پاسي رکيو وڃي يا موخر ڪيو وڃي

urduMeaning: مطلوبہ رقم ادا کرنا، خاص طور جب دل نہ چاہے، مجبوری یا دباؤ میں پیسے دینا
synonyms: Pay up, Cough up, Fork out, Shell out, Contribute
sindhiMeaning: گهربل رقم ادا ڪرڻ، خاص طور جڏهن دل نه ٿي چاهي، پئسا يا وسيلا حوالي ڪرڻ
examples: Everyone had to pony up fifty dollars for the farewell party. He finally ponied up the money he owed after months of delay. The investors were asked to pony up more capital. She reluctantly ponied up for the repairs.
antonyms: Withhold, Refuse, Hold back
englishMeaning: To pay a required amount of money, especially when one is reluctant to do so. To hand over money or resources, often under obligation or pressure.

synonyms: Depressed, Gloomy, Down in the dumps, Dispirited, Low
examples: She has been in a funk ever since she lost her job. He spent the whole week in a funk after the breakup. Being in a funk is normal but it is important to seek help if it lasts long. The rainy weather put the whole office in a funk.
englishMeaning: To be in a depressed, unhappy, or unmotivated state. To feel low in mood or stuck in a period of gloom, sadness, or lack of energy.
urduMeaning: اداسی یا ذہنی دباؤ میں ہونا، غمگین یا بے ہمت محسوس کرنا، کچھ کرنے کو دل نہ کرنا
sindhiMeaning: اداسيءَ يا ذهني دٻاءُ ۾ هجڻ، غمگين يا بي همت محسوس ڪرڻ، ڪجهه ڪرڻ جو دل نه هجڻ
antonyms: Cheerful, Upbeat, Motivated, Elated, Energised

urduMeaning: ہر کام کو کامیاب یا منافع بخش بنانے کی فطری صلاحیت، یونانی داستان کے بادشاہ مائیڈاس کے حوالے سے جس کی چھوئی ہر چیز سونا بن جاتی تھی
antonyms: Midas curse, Failure, Bad luck, Misfortune
sindhiMeaning: هر ڪم کي ڪامياب يا منافعيبخش بڻائڻ جي قدرتي صلاحيت، يوناني ڏند ڪٿا جي بادشاهه مائيڊس جي حوالي سان جنهن جي هٿ لڳل شيءِ سون ٿي ويندي هئي
synonyms: Golden touch, Successful instinct, Business acumen, Magic formula
englishMeaning: The ability to make everything one does turn into a success or profit. Referring to the Greek myth of King Midas, who could turn everything he touched into gold.
examples: She has the Midas touch, every business she starts becomes profitable. His Midas touch turned the failing company into a market leader. Investors love working with him because of his Midas touch. The Midas touch of this director makes every film a blockbuster.

The concert last night was totally off the chain. Her performance in the final match was off the chain. The food at that new restaurant is off the chain. The party was off the chain, everyone had an amazing time.
synonyms: Outstanding, Incredible, Awesome, Wild, Exceptional
antonyms: Ordinary, Dull, Mediocre, Boring
urduMeaning: انتہائی شاندار، جوش سے بھرا یا توقع سے بڑھ کر، غیر رسمی زبان میں شاندار یا لاجواب
sindhiMeaning: انتهائي عمدو، جوش ڀريو يا توقع کان ٻاهر، غير رسمي زبان ۾ اسڙو يا ڪمال جو
englishMeaning: Exceptionally good, wild, exciting, or beyond expectations. Informal slang used to describe something that is extraordinary or outstanding.

Someone who finds peace, joy, inspiration, or fascination in sunsets and the colors of the sky during evening twilight. Such people often enjoy watching the sun go down, admiring the changing shades of orange, red, pink, purple, and gold, and appreciating the calm atmosphere that comes with dusk.
antonyms: Sun lover, Heliophile
sindhiMeaning: سج لهڻ جو شوقين، شام جي منظرن سان محبت ڪندڙ، غروبِ آفتاب جو دلدادو، شام جي قدرتي حسن جو قدر ڪندڙ، اهڙو شخص جيڪو سج لهڻ  شام جي وقت، ۽ آسمان جي خوبصورت رنگن کي ڏسڻ پسند ڪري ۽ انهن مان سڪون يا خوشي حاصل ڪري ٿو
urduMeaning: غروبِ آفتاب کا شوقین، شام کے مناظر کا دلدادہ، شام کی خوبصورتی سے محبت کرنے والا، ڈھلتی روشنی کا قدر دان،  ایسا شخص جو سورج کے غروب ہونے  شام کے دلکش مناظر اور آسمان کے بدلتے رنگوں کو پسند کرتا ہو اور ان سے سکون یا خوشی محسوس کرتا ہو
synonyms: Cloud lover, Overcast enthusiast
examples: She was an opacarophile who preferred rainy Sundays to sunny afternoons. The opacarophile felt most inspired under overcast skies. He described himself as an opacarophile who hated bright summer days. The opacarophile took photographs of dramatic cloudy landscapes.

urduMeaning: مسحور کر دینا، دل موہ لینا، بے حد متاثر کرنا، توجہ اپنی طرف کھینچ لینا، کسی شخص کو اس قدر متاثر  مسحور یا متوجہ کر دینا کہ وہ پوری طرح اس کی کشش یا دلچسپی میں کھو جائے
sindhiMeaning: مُتاثر ڪرڻ، موهي ڇڏڻ، دل کٽي وٺڻ، سحر ۾ آڻي ڇڏڻ، ڪنهن شخص کي ايترو متاثر يا موهي ڇڏڻ جو هو مڪمل طور تي ان جي دلڪشي  خوبصورتي  يا دلچسپي ۾ گم ٿي وڃي
englishMeaning: To capture the fascinated attention of someone. To hold someone spellbound or enchanted. It implies a sense of being enslaved by beauty or charm.
antonyms: Repel, Disgust, Bore, Release, Free
synonyms: Enchant, Captivate, Charm, Mesmerize, Hypnotize
examples: The magician's performance was enough to enthral the entire audience. She was enthralled by the breathtaking beauty of the Himalayan landscape. The ancient myths continue to enthral readers of all ages. His storytelling abilities could enthral anyone who sat by the campfire.

The circus performer's daring acts never fail to enthrall the young audience. She was completely enthralled by the vivid colors and intricate details of the painting. The speaker's eloquent words managed to enthrall every person in the crowded hall. The magical atmosphere of the ancient forest can enthrall any traveler.
englishMeaning: To capture the fascinated attention or interest of someone. To hold someone spellbound or to enslave mentally. It implies a state of being completely charmed or captivated by something beautiful or intense.
synonyms: Captivate, Fascinate, Enchant, Mesmerize, Charm, Spellbind
urduMeaning: مسحور کر دینا، دل موہ لینا، بے حد متاثر کرنا، توجہ اپنی طرف کھینچ لینا، کسی شخص کو اس قدر متاثر  مسحور یا متوجہ کر دینا کہ وہ پوری طرح اس کی کشش یا دلچسپی میں کھو جائے
antonyms: Bore, Disenchant, Repel, Tire, Weary, Disgust
sindhiMeaning: مُتاثر ڪرڻ، موهي ڇڏڻ، دل کٽي وٺڻ، سحر ۾ آڻي ڇڏڻ، ڪنهن شخص کي ايترو متاثر يا موهي ڇڏڻ جو هو مڪمل طور تي ان جي دلڪشي  خوبصورتي  يا دلچسپي ۾ گم ٿي وڃي

examples: The document serves to enumerate all the rights guaranteed to the citizens. She began to enumerate the many reasons why the project had failed. The census taker must enumerate every person living in the household. He paused to enumerate the various species of birds he had observed.
urduMeaning: شمار کرنا، گننا، فہرست بنانا، ایک ایک کر کے بتانا، تفصیل وار بتانا
synonyms: List, Itemize, Catalog, Count, Detail, Specify
antonyms: Conceal, Estimate, Guess, Generalize, Ignore, Suppress
sindhiMeaning: ڳڻڻ، شمار ڪرڻ، هڪ هڪ ڪري ٻڌائڻ، تفصيل سان بيان ڪرڻ، فهرست تيار ڪرڻ
englishMeaning: To mention a number of things one by one. To establish the number of something or to list items individually. It is often used in formal contexts to provide a detailed account or count of objects or reasons.

sindhiMeaning: عارضي، ٿورڙي وقت لاءِ، فاني، مٽجي ويندڙ، جلد گذرندڙ، بي بقا
synonyms: Transitory, Transient, Fleeting, Momentary, Brief, Evanescent
examples: The beauty of the sunset is ephemeral, lasting only a few precious minutes. Many internet trends are ephemeral and are forgotten within a few weeks. The ephemeral nature of fashion means that styles change every season. We must cherish these ephemeral moments of joy before they pass away.
englishMeaning: Lasting for a very short time. Short-lived or transitory in nature. It often describes things in nature like flowers or fleeting emotions that do not endure.
antonyms: Eternal, Permanent, Lasting, Perennial, Enduring, Perpetual
urduMeaning: عارضی، فانی، چند روزہ، تھوڑی دیر کا، ناپائیدار، مٹنے والا
مخنث، ہیجڑا، وہ اسم جو تذکیر و تانیث دونوں کے لیے بولا جائے، زنانہ، جِنسِ عام
antonyms: Masculine, Feminine, Virile, Manbound, Distinct, Sexed
synonyms: Androgynous, Effeminate, Genderless, Hermaphroditic, Neutered, Unisex
examples: The fashion designer focused on creating an epicene collection suitable for everyone. His epicene features made it difficult to determine his gender at a glance. The novel features an epicene protagonist who defies traditional gender roles. Some artists prefer an epicene aesthetic to challenge societal norms.
sindhiMeaning: مخنث، اڌ مرد اڌ عورت، عام جنس، هيجڙو، جنهن ۾ نر توڙي مادي جون نشانيون هجن
englishMeaning: Having characteristics of both sexes or neither sex. Often used to describe something that is effeminate or lacks a distinct gender identity. In linguistics, it refers to nouns that have one form for both masculine and feminine.

examples: She had an epiphany while reading the report and finally understood the problem. His travel experience led to an epiphany about what truly matters in life. During the meeting, the solution came to her as an epiphany. The teacher’s explanation gave the students an epiphany about the concept.
urduMeaning: اچانک سمجھ یا ادراک کا لمحہ، وہ لمحہ جب انسان کو اچانک کسی اہم حقیقت کی گہری سمجھ حاصل ہو جائے یا سوچ کا زاویہ بدل جائے، تجلی، وحی، انکشافِ حقیقت، نادیدہ حقیقت کا اچانک ادراک، ظہورِ قدسی
synonyms: Realization, Insight, Awakening, Revelation

examples: She is very affectionate toward her younger brother. The dog became more affectionate after being adopted. He wrote an affectionate letter to his mother. They shared an affectionate hug after a long time apart.
sindhiMeaning: پيار ۽ شفقت ڏيکاريندڙ، ان شخص يا رويي کي چئبو آهي جيڪو ٻين لاءِ پيار  شفقت ۽ نرمي ظاهر ڪري، اهڙو ماڻهو پنهنجي احساسن کي مهرباني ۽ محبت سان ظاهر ڪري ٿو

synonyms: Lovingly, Fondly, Tenderly, Warmly, Caring manner, Endearingly
examples: She smiled affectionately at her little brother. He spoke affectionately about his childhood memories. The teacher looked affectionately at her students after their success. The old couple held hands and looked affectionately at each other.
englishMeaning: In a way that shows love, care, warmth, or fond feelings toward someone. An action done with emotional warmth, tenderness, or deep liking. It is often used when someone speaks, looks at, or treats another person in a loving or caring manner. It shows positive emotional attachment, such as between family members, close friends, or loved ones.

antonyms: Coldness, Indifference, Hostility, Aloofness, Unkindness
englishMeaning: Affectionateness means the quality of being warm, loving, and showing care or tenderness toward others. urduMeaning: محبت اور شفقت سے بھرپور رویہ یا کیفیت، دوسروں کے لیے دل میں نرمی، پیار اور اپنائیت رکھنا، گرمجوشی اور ہمدردی کے ساتھ برتاؤ کرنا، ایسا مزاج یا عادت جس میں احساس اور محبت نمایاں ہو
synonyms: Affection, Warmth, Tenderness, Fondness, Lovingness, Carefulness
sindhiMeaning: محبت ۽ نرمي سان ڀريل رويو يا عادت، دل ۾ پيار ۽ شفقت رکڻ ۽ ان جو اظهار ڪرڻ، ٻين سان گرمجوشي، پنهنجائپ ۽ نرم دلي ڏيکارڻ، اهڙي طبيعت جنهن ۾ احساس ۽ همدردي وڌيڪ هجي

antonyms: Ailurophobia, Fear of cats, Cat aversion, Dislike of cats, Feline dislike
sindhiMeaning: ٻلين سان گهڻي محبت يا لڳاءُ، ان حالت کي چوندا آهن جنهن ۾ ماڻهو کي ٻلين سان گهري محبت ۽ لڳاءُ هوندو آهي، اهڙو ماڻهو ٻلين کي پسند ڪري ٿو انهن جو خيال رکي ٿو ۽ انهن سان وقت گذارڻ ۾ خوشي محسوس ڪري ٿو
urduMeaning: بلیوں سے شدید محبت یا لگاؤ، اس کیفیت کو کہتے ہیں جس میں کسی شخص کو بلیوں سے گہری محبت اور لگاؤ ہوتا ہے، ایسا شخص بلیوں کے ساتھ رہنا  ان کی دیکھ بھال کرنا اور ان کی موجودگی میں خوشی محسوس کرتا ہے
examples: Her ailurophilia is clear from the dozens of cats she has adopted. Due to his ailurophilia, he volunteers at an animal shelter every weekend. Ailurophilia often leads people to become passionate cat rescuers. She jokes that her ailurophilia is stronger than her love for anything else.
englishMeaning: Ailurophilia means a strong love or fondness for cats. An emotional attraction or deep affection toward cats. A person who has ailurophilia enjoys being around cats, caring for them, and often feels comforted or happy in their presence. It is not just liking cats, but a stronger emotional preference or passion for them.
synonyms: Cat love, Feline affection, Cat enthusiasm, Cat fondness

urduMeaning: الفاظ اور زبان سے شدید محبت یا دلچسپی، ایک ایسا رجحان جس میں انسان کو الفاظ  لغت اور زبان سے گہری محبت ہوتی ہے ایسے افراد نئے الفاظ سیکھنے  ان کے معانی اور استعمال سمجھنے اور زبان کے مطالعے میں دلچسپی رکھتے ہیں
antonyms: Logophobia, Fear or dislike of words, Indifference to language, Language apathy, Disinterest in vocabulary
synonyms: Word love, Lexical passion, Love of language, Verbal appreciation, Linguistic interest
englishMeaning: A strong love or fascination with words and language. An intense attraction toward words, vocabulary, and language in general. A person with logophilia enjoys learning new words, exploring their meanings, origins, and usage, and often finds pleasure in reading, writing, or studying languages.
sindhiMeaning: لفظن ۽ ٻولي سان گهري محبت يا دلچسپي، هڪ اهڙو جذبو جنهن ۾ ماڻهو لفظن  لغت ۽ ٻولي سان گهري محبت رکي، اهڙا ماڻهو نوان لفظ سکڻ  انهن جي معنى ۽ استعمال ڄاڻڻ ۽ ٻولين جي مطالعي ۾ خاص دلچسپي رکن ٿا
examples: Her logophilia made her spend hours reading dictionaries for fun. His logophilia is clear from the way he collects rare words. Logophilia often drives writers to explore language deeply. A teacher with logophilia can inspire students to love words.

englishMeaning: Related to vocabulary of a language. Connected with dictionary words and their meanings. Refers to word choice and word structure. Used in linguistics to describe word-level elements.
examples: The lexical meaning of the word changed over time. Students studied the lexical features of the text. The dictionary provides lexical information for each entry. Lexical analysis helps in understanding word usage in sentences.
synonyms: Word-based, Lexicological, Vocabulary-related, Verbal, Dictionary-related

antonyms: Grammatical, Structural, Functional, Syntactic

synonyms: Verbally, Vocabulary-wise, Word-wise, Terminologically, Semantically
urduMeaning: لغوی طور پر، الفاظ کے اعتبار سے، لفظی معنوں میں، لغت کے مطابق، الفاظ کے استعمال کے لحاظ سے، الفاظ   لغت  یا زبان میں الفاظ کے معنی اور استعمال کے حوالے سے ، یہ الفاظ کی سطح پر ہونے والی بات کو ظاہر کرتا ہے  نہ کہ صرف قواعد یا جملے کی ساخت کو

examples: The two words are lexically similar but have different meanings. The dictionary explains the term lexically and grammatically. English and German are lexically related in many ways. The sentence is lexically simple and easy to understand.

The professor recommended a historical lexicon for studying ancient languages. Medical students must become familiar with the lexicon of anatomy and physiology.
synonyms: Dictionary, Vocabulary, Wordbook, Glossary, Terminology, Word stock, Word list
urduMeaning: کسی زبان کے تمام الفاظ کا مجموعہ،  کسی شخص  گروہ یا شعبے کی مخصوص لفظیات، ایسی لغت جس میں الفاظ اور ان کے معانی درج ہوں، کسی خاص علم یا فن کے اصطلاحات کا ذخیرہ، کسی زبان  علم یا شعبے میں استعمال ہونے والے الفاظ کا مجموعہ یا ایسی کتاب جس میں الفاظ اور ان کے معانی درج ہوں

englishMeaning: The vocabulary of a language, a person, a group, or a subject. It can also mean a dictionary that contains words and their meanings. The complete set of words in a language. The vocabulary used by a particular person, profession, or field. A dictionary or reference book containing words and their meanings. The collection of terms associated with a specific subject or discipline.

urduMeaning: نحوی/ قواعدی/ جملے کی ساخت سے متعلق، الفاظ کی ترتیب سے متعلق/ زبان کی ساخت سے وابستہ، کے قواعد کے مطابق الفاظ اور جملوں کی ترتیب سے متعلق، اس چیز کو کہتے ہیں جو زبان میں الفاظ  فقروں اور جملوں کی درست ترتیب اور نحوی قواعد سے متعلق ہو، یہ جملوں کی ساخت اور ترتیب کے مطالعے سے وابستہ ہے
synonyms: Grammatical, Structural, Linguistic, Formal, Rule based, Sentence related
sindhiMeaning: نحوي/ گرامري/ جملي جي جوڙجڪ سان لاڳاپيل، لفظن جي ترتيب بابت ٻوليءَ جي ساخت سان واسطيدار، جي قاعدن موجب لفظن ۽ جملن جي ترتيب سان لاڳاپيل، اهڙي شيءِ جيڪا ٻوليءَ ۾ لفظن  فقرن ۽ جملن جي صحيح ترتيب ۽ نحوي قاعدن سان واسطو رکي، اهو جملن جي بناوت ۽ ساخت جو مطالعو ڪري ٿو
examples: The sentence contains several syntactic errors. Linguists study syntactic patterns in different languages. The software can identify syntactic mistakes in writing. Word order is an important syntactic feature of English.
englishMeaning: Related to syntax, the arrangement of words and phrases to form correct sentences in a language. It refers to the rules and structure governing how words are arranged in a sentence. It deals with sentence formation, word order, and grammatical relationships between words.
antonyms: Ungrammatical, Incorrect, Disordered, Unstructured, Ill formed, Irregular
Ungrammatically, Incorrectly, Improperly, Agrammatically, Illogically
synonyms: Grammatically, Structurally, Formally, Linguistically, According to grammar, In grammatical terms
sindhiMeaning: نحوي طور، گرامر جي لحاظ کان، جملي جي بناوت جي لحاظ کان، لفظن جي ترتيب مطابق، قاعدي موجب
examples: The sentence is syntactically correct but semantically confusing. The linguist analyzed the text syntactically to identify its grammatical structure. Although the words were familiar, they were not arranged syntactically. The software checks documents syntactically before processing them.

The structure and arrangement of words, phrases, and clauses in a sentence according to grammatical rules. It focuses on whether a sentence is correctly formed, regardless of its meaning.
urduMeaning: نحوی طور پر، گرامر کے لحاظ سے، جملے کی ساخت کے اعتبار سے، الفاظ کی ترتیب کے مطابق، قواعدِ نحو کے مطابق

englishMeaning: Sentence structure. Grammatical arrangement. Word order Language rules. Structural organization of expressions. Programming code rules. Set of rules that governs how words, phrases, clauses, or symbols are arranged to form correct sentences in a language or valid statements in a computer programming language.
antonyms: Disorder, Disorganization, Incorrect structure, Ungrammaticality, Chaos
sindhiMeaning: جملي جي بناوت، لفظن جي ترتيب گرامري جوڙجڪ، ٻولي جا قاعدا اظهار جي ترتيب، پروگرامنگ جا اصول، قاعدن جو مجموعو جيڪو ٻڌائي ته لفظن  جملن يا نشانين کي صحيح ترتيب سان ڪيئن رکجي ته جيئن صحيح مطلب وارو جملو يا پروگرام ٺهي
synonyms: Grammar, Sentence structure, Word order, Arrangement, Construction, Organization
examples: The teacher explained the syntax of English sentences to the students. Incorrect syntax can make a sentence difficult to understand. The programmer received an error because of a syntax mistake in the code. Learning syntax is essential for writing clear and correct language.
urduMeaning: جملے کی ساخت، الفاظ کی ترتیب، قواعدی تنظیم، زبان کے اصول، اظہار کی ساخت، پروگرامنگ کے قواعد، قواعد کا مجموعہ جو یہ طے کرتا ہے کہ الفاظ  فقروں یا علامات کو کس ترتیب سے رکھا جائے تاکہ درست جملہ یا پروگرام تشکیل پائے

englishMeaning: In a way that relates to meaning, interpretation, or the meaning of words, phrases, sentences, or symbols. Concerning meaning. In relation to interpretation. According to the intended sense. From a meaning-based perspective. With respect to significance or concept.
sindhiMeaning: معنوي طور، مفهوم جي لحاظ کان، مطلب جي اعتبار سان، معنيٰ سان لاڳاپيل نموني، مفهومي انداز ۾، معنيٰ يا مفهوم جي لحاظ کان، جڏهن ڪنهن لفظ  جملي  نشاني يا اظهار جي معنيٰ تي بحث ڪئي وڃي ته ان کي معنوي طور چيو ويندو آهي
antonyms: Syntactically, Formally, Literally, Meaninglessly, Superficially
urduMeaning: معنوی طور پر، مفہوم کے اعتبار سے، معنی کے لحاظ سے، مطلب کے مطابق، مفہومی انداز میں، معنی یا مفہوم کے اعتبار سے جب کسی لفظ  جملے  علامت یا اظہار کے معنی پر توجہ دی جائے تو اسے معنوی طور پر کہا جاتا ہے

synonyms: Meaningfully, Conceptually, Interpretively, Significantly, In terms of meaning

examples: The disagreement was mainly a semantic issue rather than a real conflict. Linguists study semantic relationships between words. The software checks for semantic errors in the code. There is a semantic difference between the two expressions.
urduMeaning: الفاظ کے معنی سے متعلق، زبان کی تشریح اور مفہوم سے وابستہ، رابطے اور سمجھ بوجھ کے معنی سے تعلق رکھنے والا، علامات اور نشانات کے مفہوم سے متعلق، کمپیوٹر سائنس میں کوڈ یا ڈیٹا کے مفہوم سے متعلق
synonyms: Meaningful, Interpretive, Linguistic, Conceptual, Significative, Denotative
englishMeaning: Related to the meaning of words. Concerned with interpretation of language. Connected with communication and understanding. Relating to symbols and their meanings. In computer science, relating to the meaning or behavior of code and data.
antonyms: Meaningless, Nonsensical, Illogical, Incoherent, Unintelligible
sindhiMeaning: لفظن جي معنيٰ سان لاڳاپيل، ٻولي جي مفهوم ۽ تشريح سان واسطيدار، سمجهڻ ۽ رابطي جي معنائن سان تعلق رکندڙ، نشانين ۽ علامتن جي مطلب سان لاڳاپيل، ڪمپيوٽر سائنس ۾ ڪوڊ يا ڊيٽا جي مفهوم سان واسطو رکندڙ

englishMeaning: Study of word meanings. Science of linguistic meaning. Analysis of semantic change. Investigation of how words acquire different senses. Examination of relationships between meanings of words. Study of meaning development in language. The branch of linguistics that studies the meanings of words and how meanings develop, change, and relate to one another.
sindhiMeaning: لفظن جي معنائن جو علم، معنائن جي تبديلي جو مطالعو، ٻوليءَ جي مفهوم جو جائزو، لفظن جي معنوي ارتقا جو علم، لفظ ۽ معنيٰ جي لاڳاپي جو مطالعو، لسانيات جي اها شاخ آهي جيڪا لفظن جي معنائن  انهن جي تبديلي ۽ ارتقا جو مطالعو ڪري ٿي
antonyms: There is no exact direct antonym
synonyms: Semantics, Lexical semantics, Meaning studies, Semantic analysis, Study of meaning
urduMeaning: الفاظ کے معانی کا علم، معنیات کا مطالعہ، الفاظ کے مفہوم کی تحقیق، معنوی تبدیلیوں کا جائزہ، لفظ اور معنی کے تعلق کا مطالعہ، لسانیات کی وہ شاخ ہے جو الفاظ کے معانی  ان کی تبدیلی اور ارتقا کا مطالعہ کرتی ہے
examples: Semasiology helps linguists understand how the meanings of words change over time. The researcher specialized in semasiology and semantic change. Semasiology examines why a single word may have several meanings. A study of semasiology can reveal the historical development of language.

sindhiMeaning: معنائن جو علم، لفظن جي مفهوم جي تشريح، ٻوليءَ ۾ مطلب سمجهڻ جو طريقو، نشانين ۽ انهن جي معنائن جو تعلق، لفظن ۽ جملن جي مفهوم جو مطالعو، معنيات/ لفظن ۽ ٻوليءَ جي معنائن جو علم
englishMeaning: The study of meaning in language, words, phrases, sentences, and symbols.  A branch of linguistics that deals with the meaning of words, phrases, sentences, and symbols. It helps explain how language conveys ideas, emotions, and information. Semantics examines both the literal meaning and the relationships between meanings.
synonyms: Meaning, Significance, Interpretation, Sense, Definition, Connotation, Implication, Semiology
examples: The argument was mostly about semantics rather than real differences. Linguistics students often study semantics to understand how language conveys meaning. The semantics of the contract caused confusion among the parties. Computers use semantic analysis to interpret the meaning of text.
urduMeaning: معنیات کا علم، الفاظ کے مفہوم کی تشریح، زبان میں معنی کو سمجھنے کا طریقہ، علامات اور ان کے معانی کا تعلق، الفاظ اور جملوں کے مفہوم کا مطالعہ، معنیات/ الفاظ، جملوں اور زبان کے معانی کا مطالعہ
antonyms: Nonsense, Meaninglessness, Gibberish, Absurdity, Incoherence
Agreement, Harmony, Praise, Compliment

urduMeaning: کسی کے خیالات یا عمل کے خلاف زوردار اور متنازعہ دلیل یا تنقید، وہ شخص جو متنازعہ بحث میں حصہ لے

examples: He was so gluttonous he ordered three full meals for himself. The gluttonous king held banquets every night. Her gluttonous habits led to serious health problems. The gluttonous child ate all the candy meant for the whole class.
urduMeaning: پیٹو، ضرورت سے زیادہ کھانے والا، کھانے یا کسی بھی چیز میں حد سے زیادہ لالچ رکھنے والا
englishMeaning: Having an excessively greedy approach to eating or consuming. Eating far more than necessary; marked by greed or excess in consumption.
synonyms: Greedy, Voracious, Ravenous, Insatiable, Piggish
antonyms: Abstemious, Moderate, Frugal, Temperate

urduMeaning: اٹلی کے آستی علاقے میں موسکاٹو انگوروں سے بنی میٹھی اور بلبلے دار سفید شراب، اپنے ہلکے، پھلوں والے ذائقے کے لیے مشہور ہے
antonyms: Dry wine, Still wine, Brut champagne
synonyms: Sparkling wine, Prosecco, Moscato d'Asti, Italian bubbly
englishMeaning: A sweet, sparkling Italian white wine made from Moscato Bianco grapes, produced in the Asti region of Piedmont, Italy. It is known for its light, fruity, and sweet flavour.
sindhiMeaning: اٽاليءَ جي آسٽي علائقي مان ٺهيل مٺي ۽ پڦ وارين اٽالوي اڇي شراب جو نالو، جيڪا موسڪاٽو انگورن مان ٺهندي آهي
examples: They toasted the new year with a bottle of Asti Spumante. Asti Spumante is a popular choice at Italian celebrations. The dessert was perfectly paired with a glass of Asti Spumante. She preferred Asti Spumante over drier sparkling wines.

synonyms: Warp, Twist, Misrepresent, Deform, Falsify
sindhiMeaning: شڪل يا معنيٰ بدلائڻ، غلط يا گمراهه ڪندڙ انداز ۾ پيش ڪرڻ، اصل صورت کي وڪڙائڻ
englishMeaning: To pull or twist out of shape; to give a misleading or false account of something. To change the original form, meaning, or nature of something in an inaccurate or deceptive way.
urduMeaning: شکل یا معنیٰ کو بگاڑنا، گمراہ کن انداز میں پیش کرنا، اصل حالت کو مسخ کرنا
examples: The mirror distorted their reflections in a funny way. The media often distorts facts to attract more viewers. Stress can distort your perception of reality. He distorted the truth to avoid taking blame.
antonyms: Clarify, Straighten, Correct, Represent accurately

urduMeaning: مرکز سے باہر کی طرف حرکت کرنا یا کرنے کا رجحان، اس قوت سے متعلق جو گردش کے دوران اشیاء کو باہر کی طرف دھکیلتی ہے
antonyms: Centripetal, Inward, Converging, Central
englishMeaning: Moving or tending to move away from a centre or axis. Relating to or using the force that pushes objects outward when they rotate around a central point.
sindhiMeaning: مرڪز کان ٻاهر ڌڪجڻ يا وڃڻ واري حرڪت، هن قوت سان لاڳاپيل جيڪا ڦرڻ وقت شين کي ٻاهر ڌڪيندي آهي
synonyms: Outward, Diverging, Radiating, Peripheral
examples: The centrifugal force threw the passenger outward on the curve. A centrifugal pump uses rotation to move fluid outward. The centrifugal effect can be felt on a spinning fairground ride. Washing machines use centrifugal force to dry clothes.

antonyms: Centripetal force, Inward force
sindhiMeaning: گول دائري ۾ ڦرندڙ شيءِ تي محسوس ٿيندڙ ظاهري قوت جيڪا شيءِ کي مرڪز کان ٻاهر ڌڪيندي لڳي ٿي، اها حقيقي نه پر محسوس ٿيندڙ قوت آهي
urduMeaning: گول راستے میں گھومتی شے پر محسوس ہونے والی ظاہری قوت جو شے کو مرکز سے باہر کی طرف دھکیلتی لگتی ہے، یہ ایک فرضی قوت ہے جو گھومتے ہوئے فریم میں محسوس ہوتی ہے
synonyms: Outward force, Rotational force, Apparent force
examples: Centrifugal force keeps water in a bucket when swung overhead. The centrifugal force in a washing machine spins out the water. Astronauts experience the effects of centrifugal force in training. The car's turn made him feel centrifugal force pushing him sideways.
englishMeaning: An apparent force felt by an object moving in a circular path that seems to push the object outward from the centre of the circle. It is a fictitious force observed in a rotating reference frame.

sindhiMeaning: ختم ٿي سگهڻ جوڳو، اهو وسيلو يا شيءِ جيڪا آخرڪار ختم ٿي سگهي ٿي، لامحدود نه
synonyms: Finite, Depletable, Limited, Consumable
examples: Oil is an exhaustible resource that will eventually run out. The company's exhaustible supply of materials caused production delays. Unlike solar energy, coal is exhaustible. Human patience, while great, is not inexhaustible.
urduMeaning: ختم ہو سکنے والا، وہ وسیلہ یا چیز جو آخرکار ختم ہو سکتی ہو، لامحدود نہیں
englishMeaning: Capable of being used up or depleted; not infinite in supply. Describing a resource or thing that can eventually run out.
antonyms: Inexhaustible, Infinite, Renewable, Unlimited
Centrifugal, Outward, Diverging
urduMeaning: مرکز کی طرف حرکت کرنا یا کرنے کا رجحان، اس قوت سے متعلق جو کسی چیز کو مرکز کی طرف کھینچ کر گھمانے پر مجبور کرتی ہے
sindhiMeaning: مرڪز ڏانهن ڇڪجڻ يا وڃڻ واري حرڪت، انهي قوت سان لاڳاپيل جيڪا شيءِ کي مرڪز ڏانهن ڇڪي ٿي
synonyms: Inward, Centre-directed, Converging
examples: Centripetal acceleration keeps the moon orbiting the earth. The string provides centripetal force when swinging a ball in a circle. Gravity acts as a centripetal force for planets orbiting the sun. The centripetal pull of the drain created a small whirlpool.
englishMeaning: Moving or tending to move toward a centre or axis. Relating to the force that makes an object follow a curved path by pulling it inward toward the centre of rotation.

sindhiMeaning: گول رستي تي هلندڙ شيءِ کي مرڪز ڏانهن ڇڪيندڙ اصلي قوت، جيڪا شيءِ کي ٻاهر نه نڪرڻ ڏيندي آهي
synonyms: Inward force, Centre-seeking force, Radial force
examples: Centripetal force keeps a car on a curved road without skidding. The tension in a string provides centripetal force for circular motion. Earth's gravity acts as centripetal force for the moon's orbit. The centripetal force decreases if the speed of rotation increases.
urduMeaning: گول راستے پر چلتی شے کو مرکز کی طرف کھینچنے والی اصل قوت جو اسے باہر نکلنے سے روکتی ہے
englishMeaning: The real inward force required to keep an object moving in a circular path. It acts toward the centre of the circle and prevents the object from flying outward.
antonyms: Centrifugal force, Outward force

sindhiMeaning: جانورن جي سيلن ۾ پائي ويندڙ هڪ ننڍڙي بيلناڪار جوڙجڪ جيڪا سيل ورهائڻ دوران ڪروموزومن کي الڳ ڪرڻ ۾ مدد ڪري ٿي
englishMeaning: A tiny cylindrical structure found in animal cells that plays a key role in cell division by organising the spindle fibres that separate chromosomes during mitosis.
antonyms: No antonym
synonyms: Cell organelle, Microtubule organiser, Centrosome component
urduMeaning: جانوروں کے خلیوں میں پائی جانے والی ایک چھوٹی بیلناکار ساخت جو خلیے کی تقسیم کے دوران کروموسوم الگ کرنے میں اہم کردار ادا کرتی ہے
examples: Centrioles are absent in the cells of higher plants. The centriole duplicates before cell division begins. Biologists studied the role of the centriole in cancer cell division. Each cell contains two centrioles forming the centrosome.

sindhiMeaning: هڪ مشين جيڪا تيز رفتار گهمڻ ذريعي مختلف کثافت وارين شين کي الڳ ڪري ٿي، لابارٽرين، دواسازيءَ ۽ صنعت ۾ وڏي پيماني تي استعمال ٿيندي آهي
antonyms: Mixer, Combiner, Blender
englishMeaning: A machine that uses centrifugal force to separate substances of different densities by spinning them rapidly. Widely used in laboratories, medicine, and industry.
examples: The laboratory used a centrifuge to separate blood plasma from cells. A centrifuge is essential for analysing urine samples. The dairy industry uses a centrifuge to separate cream from milk. Scientists used a high-speed centrifuge to isolate the virus.
urduMeaning: ایک مشین جو تیز گردش کے ذریعے مختلف کثافت والی چیزوں کو الگ کرتی ہے، لیبارٹریوں، طب اور صنعت میں بڑے پیمانے پر استعمال ہوتی ہے
synonyms: Separator, Spinner, Lab machine, Rotary separator
Moderate, Middle-of-the-road, Balanced, Nonpartisan
examples: The centrist candidate won support from both sides of the political spectrum. She described herself as a centrist who believed in practical solutions. The centrist party tried to bridge the gap between left and right. A centrist approach is often necessary to pass legislation in a divided parliament.
englishMeaning: A person who holds moderate political views, neither strongly left-wing nor strongly right-wing. Someone who supports compromise and balance between opposing political positions.
sindhiMeaning: اهو شخص جيڪو سياسي طور تي نه انتهائي کاٻي ڌر هجي نه ساڄي ڌر، پر وچ ۾ هجي، جيڪو اعتدال پسندي ۽ مصالحت جو حامي هجي
urduMeaning: وہ شخص جو سیاسی طور نہ انتہائی بائیں بازو ہو نہ دائیں بازو، بلکہ درمیان میں ہو، اعتدال پسندی اور سمجھوتے کا حامی
antonyms: Extremist, Radical, Far-left, Far-right
Fertile, Productive, Lush, Abundant, Fruitful
urduMeaning: بنجر، جہاں فصل یا پودے نہ اگیں، عورت یا مادہ جانور کا بچے نہ دینے کے قابل ہونا، مجازی طور پر خالی یا غیر نتیج خیز
englishMeaning: Too poor to produce vegetation or crops; (of a woman or female animal) unable to bear children. Also used figuratively to describe something empty, unproductive, or lacking results.
examples: The barren land produced nothing despite months of effort. The desert remained barren and lifeless for miles. She felt her creative life had become barren after years of routine. The barren hillside was eroded by years of overgrazing.
sindhiMeaning: بنجر، جتي فصل يا وڻ ٻوٽا نه ٿين، عورت يا مادي جانور لاءِ ٻار نه ڄڻڻ جي صلاحيت نه هجڻ، مجازي طور تي خالي يا بيڪار
synonyms: Sterile, Infertile, Desolate, Unproductive, Arid

examples: The bison once roamed freely across the American prairie. The vast prairie stretched to the horizon without a single tree. She grew up on a prairie farm in the Midwest of America. Prairie dogs build complex underground tunnel systems.
englishMeaning: A large, open area of flat or rolling grassland, especially in North America, with few trees. Known for its vast, treeless plains and rich biodiversity of grasses and wildlife.
urduMeaning: وسیع کھلے گھاس کے میدان، خاص طور پر شمالی امریکہ میں، کم درختوں والا اور گھاس سے بھرپور علاقہ
synonyms: Grassland, Plain, Savannah, Steppe, Meadow
antonyms: Forest, Jungle, Woodland, Desert
sindhiMeaning: وسيع کليل گاهه جو ميدان، خاص طور اتر آمريڪا ۾، گهٽ وڻن وارو ۽ گاهه سان ڀريل وسيع علائقو

urduMeaning: چراگاہ، وہ زمین جہاں گھاس اگتی ہو اور مویشی جیسے گائے، بھیڑ یا گھوڑے چرتے ہوں
antonyms: Desert, Barren land, Urban area
englishMeaning: Land covered with grass and other low plants suitable for grazing by livestock. An area where animals such as cows, sheep, or horses feed on growing grass.
examples: The cows grazed peacefully in the green pasture. He led the sheep to the new pasture at dawn. The rich pasture land supported hundreds of cattle. The farmer fenced off a new section of pasture for the horses.
synonyms: Meadow, Grazing land, Paddock, Field, Grassland
sindhiMeaning: گاهه جي چراگاهه، اهو زمين جو ٽڪرو جتي مال مويشي گاهه کائيندا آهن

examples: She was meticulous in her research and never missed a detail. The meticulous surgeon prepared every instrument before the operation. His meticulous notes helped him pass every exam with top marks. A meticulous approach is essential in forensic investigations.
synonyms: Careful, Precise, Thorough, Painstaking, Scrupulous
urduMeaning: ہر تفصیل کا خیال رکھنے والا، انتہائی محتاط اور درست، چھوٹی سے چھوٹی بات کو بھی سنجیدگی سے لینے والا
antonyms: Careless, Sloppy, Negligent, Hasty, Reckless
sindhiMeaning: هر تفصيل ڏانهن گهڻي توجهه ڏيڻ وارو، انتهائي محتاط ۽ درست، ننڍي کان ننڍي ڳالهه کي به سنجيدگي سان وٺڻ وارو
englishMeaning: Showing great attention to detail; very careful and precise. Taking extreme care to get every small detail right, often to the point of being thorough beyond what is expected.

antonyms: Edge, Periphery, Outskirts, Border
englishMeaning: The middle point or part of something; the central part of a group, place, or period of time. Often used in the phrase 'in the midst of' meaning surrounded by or in the middle of.
synonyms: Middle, Centre, Heart, Core, Thick
urduMeaning: وسط، درمیانی حصہ، کسی گروہ، جگہ یا وقت کا مرکزی حصہ، 'کے درمیان' یا 'کے بیچ' کے معنی میں استعمال ہوتا ہے
examples: She found herself in the midst of a heated argument. He stood in the midst of the crowd, searching for his friend. In the midst of the crisis, they remained calm. The bird nest was hidden in the midst of the dense forest.
sindhiMeaning: وچين حصو يا مرڪز، ڪنهن گروهه، جاءِ يا وقت جو درمياني حصو، 'ان جي وچ ۾' يا 'ان دوران' جي معنيٰ ۾ استعمال ٿيندو آهي

urduMeaning: شور و غوغا والا، ہنگامہ خیز، تبدیلیوں یا اضطراب سے بھرا، پُر آشوب
englishMeaning: Making or characterised by a loud, excited, or confused noise; involving a lot of change, disorder, or strong emotion. Very loud, disorderly, or turbulent.
antonyms: Calm, Peaceful, Quiet, Orderly, Tranquil
sindhiMeaning: شور شرابي وارو، ڌماچوکڙي وارو، تبديلين يا اضطراب سان ڀريل، طوفاني يا پُرآشوب،
synonyms: Turbulent, Chaotic, Stormy, Noisy, Disorderly
examples: The crowd gave a tumultuous welcome to the returning hero. She had a tumultuous relationship full of breakups and reunions. The country went through a tumultuous period after the revolution. The tumultuous storm lasted through the night.

antonyms: Dismiss, Repel, Ignore, Wave away, Reject
englishMeaning: To make a gesture with the hand or head to signal someone to come or follow. Also used figuratively to mean to attract or invite someone toward something.
examples: She beckoned him to come closer with a wave of her hand. The bright lights of the city beckoned the young man from his village. He beckoned to the waiter for another round of drinks. Adventure beckoned her to leave her comfortable life behind.
sindhiMeaning: هٿ يا مٿي سان اشارو ڪري ڪنهن کي سڏڻ يا پاڻ ڏانهن سڏڻ، مجازي طور ڪشش ڪرڻ يا ڏانهن کڻڻ
urduMeaning: ہاتھ یا سر کے اشارے سے کسی کو بلانا یا پاس آنے کو کہنا، مجازاً کسی کو اپنی طرف کھینچنا یا دعوت دینا
synonyms: Signal, Summon, Wave, Invite, Attract

sindhiMeaning: اتفاق سان ٿيل خوشگوار يا فائديمند واقعو، خوش قسمتيءَ سان ملندڙ ڪا سٺي شيءِ يا موقعو
urduMeaning: اتفاقاً ہونے والا خوشگوار یا فائدہ مند واقعہ، خوش قسمتی سے ملنے والا موقع یا چیز
englishMeaning: Occurring or discovered by chance in a happy or beneficial way. Describing a fortunate accident or a pleasant surprise that happens unexpectedly.
antonyms: Deliberate, Planned, Intentional, Unfortunate
synonyms: Fortuitous, Lucky, Accidental, Chance, Unexpected
examples: Their meeting was serendipitous, as neither had planned to be there. She made a serendipitous discovery while cleaning the attic. The serendipitous timing of his visit saved the company. It was serendipitous that both scientists were working on the same theory.

synonyms: Luck, Fortune, Happy chance, Fluke, Providence
englishMeaning: The occurrence of events that are pleasant or beneficial by chance rather than by planning. The faculty of finding something good or useful while not actively searching for it.
urduMeaning: اتفاق سے کچھ اچھا ملنا یا ہونا، خوش قسمت اتفاق، بغیر منصوبے کے کوئی اچھی چیز مل جانا
examples: Finding that old letter was pure serendipity. Serendipity brought the two future business partners together. Many great scientific discoveries are the result of serendipity. Their friendship began through serendipity at a train station.
antonyms: Misfortune, Bad luck, Design, Planning, Intention
sindhiMeaning: اتفاق سان ڪا سٺي شيءِ يا موقعو ملڻ، خوش قسمتيءَ جو اتفاق، بنا منصوبي جي ڪا سٺي ڳالهه ٿيڻ

antonyms: Include, Add, Insert, Mention, Incorporate
urduMeaning: کسی چیز کو چھوڑ دینا یا نظرانداز کرنا، جان بوجھ کر یا غلطی سے، وہ چیز شامل نہ کرنا جو ہونی چاہیے
synonyms: Exclude, Leave out, Skip, Drop, Neglect
englishMeaning: To leave out or exclude something, either accidentally or deliberately. To fail to include or mention something that should be present.
examples: She accidentally omitted her phone number on the form. He deliberately omitted the most important detail from his report. Don't omit the safety steps when assembling the equipment. The editor omitted three paragraphs from the final article.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ کي ڇڏڻ يا نظرانداز ڪرڻ، ارادي يا غلطيءَ سان، شامل ڪرڻ لازمي هجي پر نه ڪرڻ
اهو شخص جيڪو ڪنهن متن يا دستاويز تي وضاحتي نوٽ يا تبصرا لکي، تحريري مواد جي وضاحت لاءِ اضافي معلومات شامل ڪرڻ وارو
urduMeaning: وہ شخص جو کسی متن یا دستاویز پر وضاحتی نوٹس یا تبصرے لکھے، تحریری مواد کو واضح کرنے کے لیے اضافی معلومات شامل کرنے والا
synonyms: Commentator, Glossator, Editor, Reviewer, Critic
examples: The annotator added footnotes to explain the historical references. She worked as an annotator for a medical research database. A skilled annotator can greatly improve the usability of old manuscripts. The annotator highlighted all the key passages in the legal text.
englishMeaning: A person who adds explanatory notes, comments, or critical remarks to a text or document. Someone who annotates written material to provide additional context or clarity.
antonyms: Reader, Passive observer

synonyms: Commented, Glossed, Noted, Marked up, Explained
examples: She studied an annotated version of the novel for her exam. The annotated bibliography listed all sources with brief descriptions. He submitted an annotated copy of the contract to his lawyer. The annotated manuscript revealed new insights into the author's intentions.
sindhiMeaning: جنهن متن يا دستاويز تي وضاحتي نوٽ شامل ڪيا ويا هجن
antonyms: Unannotated, Plain, Unmarked
englishMeaning: Having been provided with critical or explanatory notes. A text that includes additional comments, definitions, or explanations added by an editor or scholar.
urduMeaning: وہ متن جس پر وضاحتی یا تنقیدی نوٹس شامل کیے گئے ہوں

synonyms: Enough, Adequate, Ample, Satisfactory, Competent
englishMeaning: Enough; adequate for a particular purpose or need. Having the right amount, neither too much nor too little.
examples: We have sufficient food to last a week. Is your income sufficient to cover all your expenses? A sufficient amount of sleep is crucial for good health. The evidence was not sufficient to convict him.
sindhiMeaning: ڪافي، جيترو گهربو اوترو، نه وڌيڪ نه گهٽ، ڪنهن ضرورت يا مقصد لاءِ پورو هجڻ
urduMeaning: کافی، ضرورت کے مطابق، نہ زیادہ نہ کم، کسی مقصد کے لیے کافی ہونا
antonyms: Insufficient, Inadequate, Deficient, Lacking, Wanting

examples: He apologised profusely for his rude behaviour. She was sweating profusely after the long run. The garden bloomed profusely after the heavy rains. He thanked her profusely for saving his life.
englishMeaning: In large quantities; abundantly and generously. Done or produced to an excessive or very great degree.
synonyms: Abundantly, Lavishly, Generously, Copiously, Extravagantly
urduMeaning: بہت زیادہ مقدار میں، وافر انداز میں، حد سے زیادہ
antonyms: Sparingly, Moderately, Barely, Insufficiently
sindhiMeaning: ڏاڍي ڪثرت سان، وافر انداز ۾، بي حد گهڻي مقدار ۾

antonyms: Descendant, Offspring, Successor, Heir
urduMeaning: وہ شخص یا چیز جس سے دوسرے نکلے ہوں، بزرگ آبا یا کسی خاندان، تحریک یا نوع کا بانی
synonyms: Ancestor, Forefather, Originator, Founder, Precursor
englishMeaning: A person or thing from which others are derived; an ancestor or originator. The first or earliest member of a lineage, movement, or type.
sindhiMeaning: اهو شخص يا شيءِ جنهن کان ٻيا نڪتل هجن، وڏو ڏاڏو يا بنياد رکڻ وارو
examples: He is considered the progenitor of the modern detective novel. The wolf is the progenitor of the domestic dog. She was the progenitor of a proud family of musicians. Darwin's work is the progenitor of modern evolutionary theory.

The king's progeny ruled the empire for generations. The scientist studied the progeny of the crossbred plants. Her novels are the progeny of years of research and experience. The progeny of the original settlers still live in that village.
englishMeaning: A person's children or descendants; the offspring of an animal or plant. Also used figuratively to mean the result or product of something.
synonyms: Offspring, Descendants, Children, Issue, Heirs
urduMeaning: اولاد، بچے یا نسل، جانور یا پودے کے بچے، مجازاً کسی چیز کا نتیجہ یا پیداوار
antonyms: Ancestors, Forebears, Predecessors, Progenitors
sindhiMeaning: اولاد، ٻار يا نسل، جانور يا ٻوٽي جا ٻچا، مجازي طور ڪنهن شيءِ جو نتيجو يا پيداوار
ڪنهن کي ڪجهه ڪرڻ جو سبب يا پريرڻا ڏيڻ، جوش ۽ لگن پيدا ڪرڻ
englishMeaning: To provide someone with a reason or incentive to act or behave in a certain way. To stimulate enthusiasm, drive, or interest in a person.
antonyms: Discourage, Demotivate, Deter, Dishearten, Suppress
synonyms: Inspire, Encourage, Stimulate, Drive, Prompt
urduMeaning: کسی کو کچھ کرنے کی وجہ یا ترغیب دینا، جوش اور لگن پیدا کرنا
examples: A good teacher knows how to motivate students to learn. She was motivated to succeed by her difficult childhood. His speech motivated thousands to take action. Nothing could motivate him to leave his comfortable routine.

synonyms: Progestogen, Female hormone, Steroid hormone

examples: Progesterone levels rise significantly during pregnancy. The doctor prescribed progesterone supplements after the miscarriage. Low progesterone can cause irregular menstrual cycles. Progesterone is used in some forms of contraception.
sindhiMeaning: اووري ۽ نالي ۾ پيدا ٿيندڙ هڪ اهم هارمون جيڪو عورت جي مهاوري چڪر ۽ حمل برقرار رکڻ ۾ ڪردار ادا ڪري ٿو
antonyms: Oestrogen (functionally opposing in some contexts), Testosterone
englishMeaning: A steroid hormone produced mainly in the ovaries and placenta that plays a key role in the menstrual cycle and maintaining pregnancy. Also used in hormone replacement therapy.

antonyms: Include, Bring in, Incorporate, Welcome
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کي يا ڪنهن شيءِ کي زوريءَ سان ٻاهر ڌڪڻ يا هٽائڻ

examples: He was shunted out of the committee without explanation. The new management shunted out the old-fashioned processes. She felt shunted out of the decision-making loop. The weak defender was shunted out by the aggressive forward.

synonyms: Push out, Sideline, Oust, Remove, Displace

sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کي يا ڪنهن شيءِ کي پاسي ڌڪڻ يا کيس گهٽ اهميت ڏيڻ

examples: The important issue was shunted aside during the meeting. She felt shunted aside when the new employee was given her role. The proposal was shunted aside by senior management. His concerns were shunted aside without discussion.
synonyms: Sideline, Bypass, Marginalise, Ignore, Overlook
englishMeaning: To push or move someone or something to the side; to treat as less important or to ignore.
antonyms: Prioritise, Address, Focus on, Highlight

sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کي يا ڪنهن شيءِ کي مختلف رخ ۾ موڙڻ يا مکيه رستي کان هٽائڻ
examples: The manager shunted off the complaint to a junior employee. He was shunted off to a remote branch as a form of punishment. The train was shunted off onto a side track. She felt shunted off every time she raised the issue.
urduMeaning: کسی کو یا کچھ کو مختلف سمت میں موڑنا یا مرکزی راستے سے ہٹانا
englishMeaning: To divert or send someone or something in a different direction, often to remove them from the main focus or path.
synonyms: Divert, Redirect, Deflect, Sideline, Transfer
antonyms: Engage, Direct, Include, Address
Pull out, Remove, Extract, Free
englishMeaning: To push or direct someone or something forcefully into a position or situation, often unwillingly.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کي يا ڪنهن شيءِ کي ڌڪي ڪري ڪنهن پوزيشن يا صورتحال ۾ وجهڻ
examples: He was shunted into a role he did not want. The car was shunted into the barrier at low speed. She was shunted into taking responsibility she never asked for. The funds were shunted into a separate account without notice.
synonyms: Push into, Force into, Direct into, Channel into
urduMeaning: کسی کو یا کچھ کو زبردستی کسی جگہ یا صورتحال میں دھکیلنا

englishMeaning: To move someone or something from place to place without clear purpose; to shuffle around without settling.
antonyms: Settle, Fix, Stabilise, Place permanently
examples: He was shunted around between departments for years. The documents were shunted around the office with no resolution. Children in unstable homes are often shunted around between relatives. She was shunted around four different schools in two years.
synonyms: Shuffle around, Transfer repeatedly, Move about, Redirect
urduMeaning: کسی کو یا کچھ کو بلا مقصد ایک جگہ سے دوسری جگہ منتقل کرتے رہنا
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کي يا ڪنهن شيءِ کي هڪ هنڌ کان ٻئي هنڌ بي مقصد موڙڻ يا گهمائڻ

englishMeaning: To push or send someone or something back to a previous position or place.
examples: The application was shunted back due to missing documents. He was shunted back to his original post after the restructuring. The train was shunted back to the station for repairs. Her ideas were shunted back every time she presented them.
synonyms: Send back, Return, Redirect, Push back, Reverse
antonyms: Move forward, Advance, Progress

urduMeaning: کسی کو یا کچھ کو پیچھے دھکیلنا یا پچھلی جگہ واپس بھیجنا

sindhiMeaning: اها مخصوص ڳالهه يا مسئلو جيڪو ڳالهٻولهه يا معاهدي ۾ رڪاوٽ بڻجي، مکيه اڙچڻ وارو نقطو
antonyms: Agreement, Resolution, Breakthrough, Consensus
englishMeaning: A specific issue or detail that prevents agreement or progress in a negotiation or discussion. The main obstacle or source of difficulty in reaching a solution.
urduMeaning: وہ مخصوص نکتہ یا مسئلہ جو کسی معاملے یا گفتگو میں پیشرفت روکے، بنیادی رکاوٹ
examples: The salary package became the main sticking point in negotiations. The sticking point in the deal was the ownership of intellectual property. Every other issue was resolved except for one sticking point. The peace talks collapsed over a single sticking point.
synonyms: Obstacle, Stumbling block, Bottleneck, Snag, Hurdle

englishMeaning: A false belief or impression that is firmly maintained despite being contradicted by reality or rational argument. A mistaken or misleading idea or belief.
synonyms: Illusion, Hallucination, Misconception, Fantasy, Fallacy
examples: He was under the delusion that everyone admired him. Her delusion that she was being followed led to her hospitalisation. The cult leader used delusion to control his followers. Living in delusion prevents personal growth.
urduMeaning: ایک غلط عقیدہ یا تصور جو حقیقت یا دلیل کے باوجود قائم رہے، وہم یا غلط فہمی
sindhiMeaning: هڪ غلط خيال يا يقين جيڪو حقيقت يا دليل جي باوجود برقرار رهي، وهم يا غلط فهمي
antonyms: Reality, Truth, Clarity, Fact, Awareness

synonyms: Peace, Harmony, Reconciliation, Unlikely alliance
urduMeaning: فطری دشمنوں کے درمیان امن اور ہم آہنگی کا بائبلی تصور، مارچ کے موسم کے بارے میں کہاوت میں بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے
examples: The peace agreement was celebrated as a lions and lambs moment. March came in like a lion and went out like a lamb this year. The coalition government was a rare lions and lambs arrangement. She described their unlikely friendship as a lions and lambs situation.
englishMeaning: Refers to the biblical idea of peace and harmony between natural enemies, inspired by Isaiah's prophecy. Also used in the saying 'March comes in like a lion and goes out like a lamb' meaning a rough start and peaceful end.
antonyms: Conflict, Enmity, War, Discord
sindhiMeaning: قدرتي دشمنن جي وچ ۾ امن ۽ هم آهنگيءَ جو بائبلي خيال، مارچ مهيني جي موسم جي تبديليءَ واري پهاڪي ۾ به استعمال ٿيندو آهي

synonyms: U-turn, Reversal, About-face, Turnaround, Backflip
examples: The government performed a volte face on its tax policy. His sudden volte face on the issue shocked his supporters. She executed a complete volte face after reading the new report. The prime minister's volte face on Brexit confused many voters.
sindhiMeaning: پنهنجي راءِ يا موقف ۾ مڪمل ۽ اوچتو تبديلي، خاص طور ڪنهن اهم معاملي تي
antonyms: Consistency, Steadfastness, Firmness, Resolve
urduMeaning: اپنی رائے، موقف یا پالیسی میں مکمل اور اچانک تبدیلی، خاص طور پر کسی اہم مسئلے پر یو ٹرن لینا
englishMeaning: A complete reversal of one's opinion, position, or policy. A sudden and unexpected change of attitude or direction, typically on a significant issue.

synonyms: Heir, Descendant, Offspring, Shoot, Graft
examples: He was the scion of a wealthy banking family. As the scion of a political dynasty, she entered parliament early. The gardener attached the scion to the rootstock carefully. She was the last scion of the royal bloodline.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن مشهور خاندان جو اولاد يا وارث، ٻوٽيءَ جي پيوند ڪاريءَ لاءِ ڪٽيل ٽاري

englishMeaning: A descendant of a notable family; the youngest member of a dynasty. Also refers to a shoot or twig cut from a plant and used in grafting.

englishMeaning: To think about something carefully and at length; to ponder or consider deeply. Also means to heat and spice wine or cider.
examples: She mulled over the job offer for several days. He sat quietly, mulling the decision in his mind. They enjoyed a cup of mulled wine by the fireplace. She needs time to mull before making a final choice.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ڳالهه تي ڊگهو سوچڻ يا غور ڪرڻ، وائن کي گرم ڪري مسالا ملائڻ
antonyms: Ignore, Dismiss, Decide hastily, Overlook
Indulgent, Gluttonous, Excessive, Self-gratifying
urduMeaning: کھانے پینے یا خواہشات میں پرہیزگار اور اعتدال پسند، خود پر قابو رکھنے والا
englishMeaning: Not self-indulgent, especially when eating and drinking; moderate and restrained in one's appetites. Choosing to consume little food or alcohol.
examples: He was abstemious in his diet, eating only plain food. Her abstemious lifestyle contributed to her long life. Being abstemious during Ramadan is a spiritual practice. The abstemious monk survived on very little food and water.
synonyms: Moderate, Temperate, Frugal, Restrained, Self-disciplined
sindhiMeaning: کاڌي پيتي يا خوشين ۾ پاڻ کي قابو ۾ رکڻ وارو، پرهيزگار، اعتدال پسند

englishMeaning: To think carefully and at length about something before making a decision. To consider all aspects of a situation or problem slowly and thoroughly.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن فيصلي کان اڳ ڪنهن ڳالهه تي ڊاهيءَ سان غور ڪرڻ، سڀ پاسا سوچڻ

antonyms: Rush, Decide hastily, Act impulsively
synonyms: Ponder, Deliberate, Consider, Reflect, Weigh up
examples: I need a few days to mull over your proposal. She mulled over the decision before accepting the new job. He mulled over every possible outcome before acting. Take your time and mull over all the options.

antonyms: Neutral, Balanced, Agreeable, Diplomatic, Conciliatory
englishMeaning: Relating to or involving strong controversy or argument; of the nature of a polemic. Aggressively challenging or attacking established opinions or doctrines.
sindhiMeaning: تڪراري يا متنازعه بحث سان لاڳاپيل، تکيرو يا جهيڙالو، قائم ٿيل خيالن تي زوردار حملو ڪندڙ
examples: His polemical writing earned him many critics and admirers. The book was a polemical attack on the pharmaceutical industry. She gave a polemical speech that divided the audience. The polemical tone of the article provoked widespread debate.
synonyms: Controversial, Argumentative, Combative, Provocative, Contentious
urduMeaning: متنازعہ بحث سے متعلق، تیز یا جھگڑالو، قائم عقیدوں کو چیلنج کرنے والا

synonyms: Anomaly, Deviation, Irregularity, Oddity, Divergence
sindhiMeaning: معمول يا توقع کان انحراف، غير معمولي واقعو يا رويو جيڪو عام معيار کان مختلف هجي
englishMeaning: A departure from what is normal, expected, or typical; an unusual occurrence or behaviour that differs significantly from the standard.
examples: His violent outburst was described as a one-time aberration. The scientist noted an aberration in the experimental results. Her low grade was an aberration; she usually excels. Racism is a moral aberration that must be challenged.
urduMeaning: معمول یا توقع سے انحراف، غیر معمولی واقعہ یا رویہ جو عام معیار سے بہت مختلف ہو
antonyms: Norm, Standard, Regularity, Conformity, Consistency

synonyms: Fake, Counterfeit, Fraudulent, Spurious, Sham

urduMeaning: جعلی، نقلی یا دھوکہ دہی والا، وہ جو اصلی لگے لیکن حقیقت میں نہ ہو
examples: The police discovered the bogus documents at the border. He made a bogus claim to receive the insurance money. The company was shut down for selling bogus medicines. She received a bogus job offer asking for personal information.
sindhiMeaning: جعلي، نقلي يا دوکيباز، اهو جيڪو اصلي لڳي پر اصل ۾ نه هجي
antonyms: Genuine, Authentic, Real, Legitimate, Valid

sindhiMeaning: اهو شخص جنهن جنسي تعلق نه قائم ڪيو هجي، مجازي طور ڪا اڻڇهيل، پاڪ يا پهريون ڀيرو استعمال ٿيندڙ شيءِ

antonyms: Used, Contaminated, Impure, Experienced, Defiled
synonyms: Pure, Untouched, Chaste, Pristine, Unspoiled
urduMeaning: وہ شخص جس نے جنسی تعلق نہ قائم کیا ہو، مجازاً کوئی اَن چھوئی، پاک یا پہلی بار استعمال ہونے والی چیز
examples: The expedition entered virgin territory never explored before. She poured virgin olive oil on the salad. The forest remained virgin, untouched by civilisation. The product was made from virgin materials for better quality.

urduMeaning: جنسی تعلق نہ قائم کرنے کی حالت، مجازاً پاکیزگی یا اَن چھوئی حالت
antonyms: Experience, Impurity, Defilement
sindhiMeaning: جنسي تعلق نه قائم ڪرڻ جي حالت، مجازي طور پاڪيزگي يا اڻ چهيل هجڻ
synonyms: Chastity, Purity, Celibacy, Innocence
englishMeaning: The state of never having had sexual intercourse. Also used figuratively to mean the quality of being pure, unspoiled, or unused.
examples: In many cultures, virginity is considered a matter of honour. The concept of virginity is complex and culturally defined. The mountain's virginity was lost once tourists arrived. She wrote about virginity as a social construct in her essay.

antonyms: Act impulsively, React without thought, Ignore
urduMeaning: گہرائی سے سوچنا یا غور کرنا، کسی مسئلے یا سوال پر طویل غور و فکر کرنا
examples: He cogitated for hours before making a decision. She cogitated deeply over the meaning of her dream. The philosopher would cogitate in silence for long periods. Take time to cogitate before you respond to the offer.
englishMeaning: To think deeply and carefully about something; to ponder or meditate at length over a question or problem.
synonyms: Ponder, Reflect, Contemplate, Meditate, Ruminate
sindhiMeaning: ڊاهيءَ سان سوچڻ يا غور ڪرڻ، ڪنهن مسئلي يا سوال تي ڊگهو سوچڻ

urduMeaning: گہری سوچ یا غور و فکر کا عمل، کسی معاملے پر طویل اور محتاط غور
sindhiMeaning: ڊاهيءَ سوچ يا غور جو عمل، ڪنهن معاملي تي ڊگهي ۽ محتاط سوچ
examples: After much cogitation, she arrived at a solution. His cogitation led him to a new theory in physics. Deep cogitation is the hallmark of great philosophers. She began her cogitation in the early morning silence.
synonyms: Reflection, Deliberation, Contemplation, Meditation, Thought
englishMeaning: The action of thinking deeply about something; deep, careful thought or deliberation.
antonyms: Impulsiveness, Rashness, Thoughtlessness

englishMeaning: To think deeply and unhappily about something for a long time; to dwell on worries or troubles repeatedly.
antonyms: Let go, Move on, Forget, Overlook, Accept
urduMeaning: کسی بات پر طویل عرصے تک اداسی سے سوچتے رہنا، پریشانیوں میں گھرے رہنا
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ڳالهه تي ڊگهو وقت اداسيءَ سان سوچندو رهڻ، پريشانين ۾ ٻڌل رهڻ
synonyms: Dwell on, Ruminate, Mope, Fret, Agonise
examples: He brooded over his failure for months. Don't brood over what you cannot change. She brooded over the argument long after it was resolved. Brooding over the past prevents you from moving forward.

englishMeaning: To strengthen or reinforce one's commitment to a risky or controversial action or decision, especially when facing opposition or doubt.
antonyms: Back down, Retreat, Concede, Surrender, Soften
sindhiMeaning: خطري يا متنازعه قدم تي پنهنجي عزم کي قائم رھڻ خاص طور مخالفت يا شڪ جي باوجود
urduMeaning: کسی خطرناک یا متنازعہ فیصلے پر اپنی وابستگی مضبوط کرنا  خاص طور مخالفت کے باوجود
synonyms: Intensify, Reinforce, Commit further, Escalate, Stand firm
examples: Instead of apologising, the politician decided to double down on his claims. She doubled down on her strategy despite the initial losses. He doubled down on his investment when the stocks dropped. The company doubled down on its controversial policy.

antonyms: Let go, Accept, Move on, Ignore
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ تي اداسيءَ ۽ فڪر سان ڊگهو سوچڻ
examples: He brooded on the injustice done to him. She brooded on her lost opportunities for years. Don't brood on things you cannot control. He brooded on the memory of his late father.
englishMeaning: To think long and unhappily about something; to fix the mind anxiously on a subject. Same as 'brood over'.
urduMeaning: کسی چیز پر اداسی اور فکر کے ساتھ طویل غور کرنا
synonyms: Dwell on, Ruminate, Ponder sadly, Mope, Worry

urduMeaning: کسی بات پر پریشانی یا اداسی کے ساتھ طویل وقت غور کرنا
