antonyms: Accept, Release, Forget, Overlook
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ڳالهه تي پريشانيءَ يا اداسيءَ سان ڊگهو وقت غور ڪرڻ
synonyms: Ponder sadly, Dwell on, Ruminate, Reflect, Agonise
examples: She brooded upon the mystery of his sudden disappearance. He brooded upon his mistakes until they consumed him. Do not brood upon what has already happened. She brooded upon the decision all week.

antonyms: Accept, Dismiss, Move on, Forget
synonyms: Worry about, Fret over, Obsess over, Ruminate, Mope
urduMeaning: کسی بات کے بارے میں مسلسل پریشانی کے ساتھ سوچنا یا اس میں گھرے رہنا
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ڳالهه بابت مسلسل پريشانيءَ سان سوچڻ يا انهي ۾ گهيريل رهڻ
englishMeaning: To think persistently and worriedly about something; to be preoccupied with anxious thoughts over a subject.
examples: He spent the evening brooding about the argument. She was brooding about whether she had made the right choice. Stop brooding about the past and focus on today. He was brooding about the unfair treatment he had received.

As an autophobe, she could not spend even an hour alone. His autophobe tendencies made relationships very difficult. The autophobe panicked whenever left alone at home. She sought help for her autophobe condition through therapy.
synonyms: Monophobe, One who fears solitude, Lonely fearing person
antonyms: Introvert, Recluse, Loner, Solitude-lover
englishMeaning: A person who fears loneliness or being alone; someone who has an irrational dread of being by themselves or isolated from others.
sindhiMeaning: اڪيلائيءَ کان ڊڄندڙ شخص، جيڪو پاڻ کي اڪيلو محسوس ڪرڻ کان شديد خوف رکي
urduMeaning: تنہائی سے ڈرنے والا شخص، جو خود کو اکیلا محسوس کرنے سے شدید خوف رکھتا ہو

examples: His Panglossian view of the economy ignored the poverty around him. She criticised the government's Panglossian attitude to climate change. A Panglossian outlook can prevent necessary action. His Panglossian speeches were comforting but ultimately misleading.
synonyms: Optimistic, Naive, Unrealistically positive, Rose-tinted
antonyms: Pessimistic, Realistic, Cynical, Critical
sindhiMeaning: حد کان وڌيڪ خوش بين، اهو سمجهڻ ته دنيا ۾ سڀ ڪجهه بهترين آهي، اصل مسئلن کي نظرانداز ڪندي، وولتيئر جي ناول جي ڪردار پانگلاس تان ورتل
englishMeaning: Excessively optimistic; believing that everything in the world is as good as it possibly can be, often ignoring real problems. Derived from Dr Pangloss in Voltaire's Candide.
urduMeaning: حد سے زیادہ پر امید، یہ سمجھنا کہ دنیا میں سب کچھ بہترین ہے، اصل مسائل کو نظرانداز کرتے ہوئے، وولٹیئر کے ناول کے کردار پینگلاس سے ماخوذ

antonyms: Rationalist, Logician, Philosopher, Thinker
sindhiMeaning: اهو شخص جيڪو عقل، منطق يا دليل کان نفرت رکي يا انهن تي اعتبار نه ڪري
synonyms: Anti-rationalist, Logic hater, Irrationalist
examples: The misologist rejected every rational explanation offered. His misologist views made intellectual discussion impossible. A misologist refuses to be swayed by logic or evidence. She described the anti-science movement as a gathering of misologists.
englishMeaning: A person who has a hatred or distrust of reason, logic, or rational argument. Someone who is opposed to reasoned discussion or intellectual debate.
urduMeaning: وہ شخص جو عقل، منطق یا دلیل سے نفرت رکھے یا ان پر بھروسہ نہ کرے

synonyms: Beard lover, Pogonophile
urduMeaning: داڑھیوں سے محبت رکھنے والا شخص یا داڑھی والے افراد کی طرف کشش رکھنے والا
examples: As a pagonophile, she always admired men with full beards. The pagonophile community celebrates the art of beard grooming. He was a proud pagonophile who grew his own beard for years. The beard festival was a gathering of pagonophiles.
antonyms: Clean-shaven preferrer
englishMeaning: A person who loves beards or is attracted to people with beards. Someone who has a fondness for facial hair, particularly beards.
sindhiMeaning: ڏاڙهن سان محبت رکندڙ شخص يا ڏاڙهي وارن ماڻهن ڏانهن ڪشش رکندڙ

examples: The sybarite spent his fortune on fine dining and travel. She was a sybarite who only wore the finest silk. The sybarite refused to stay anywhere without five-star amenities. His sybarite lifestyle left him bankrupt by forty.
sindhiMeaning: عيش ۽ آرام پسند شخص، جيڪو رڳو سهولتن ۽ لذتن ۾ ٻڏيل رهي
synonyms: Hedonist, Pleasure-seeker, Epicurean, Voluptuary, Sensualist
antonyms: Ascetic, Abstemious, Frugal, Austere, Spartan
urduMeaning: عیش پسند اور آرام طلب شخص، جو صرف آرام اور لذتوں میں ڈوبا رہے
englishMeaning: A person who is self-indulgent and devoted to luxury and pleasure; someone who lives only for comfort and sensual enjoyment.

sindhiMeaning: هڪ نادر يا پراڻو لفظ جنهن جي معنيٰ آهي خلاف هلڻ يا مقابلي ۾ هلڻ، جديد انگريزيءَ ۾ گهٽ استعمال ٿيندو آهي
synonyms: Oppose, Counter, Resist, Contradict, Challenge
englishMeaning: A rare or archaic term sometimes used to mean to ride against or in opposition; to counter-ride. Not widely used in modern English.
examples: The knight would contride against his enemy in the tournament. He seemed to contride every suggestion made by the team. She had a tendency to contride opinions she disagreed with. The faction would contride the policies of the ruling party.
antonyms: Support, Agree, Concur, Align
urduMeaning: ایک نادر یا قدیم لفظ جس کا مطلب مخالفت میں چلنا یا مقابلے میں آنا ہے، جدید انگریزی میں کم استعمال ہوتا ہے

examples: The dictator's myrmidons carried out every cruel order without hesitation. He was merely a myrmidon doing his master's dirty work. The police chief's myrmidons intimidated witnesses. History remembers those myrmidons as accessories to great crimes.
synonyms: Henchman, Stooge, Lackey, Follower, Minion
englishMeaning: A hired ruffian or unscrupulous person who carries out orders without question. Originally the name of a legendary warrior race who followed Achilles in Greek mythology.
sindhiMeaning: اهو شخص جيڪو بنا سوال جي حڪم بجا آڻي، گهڻو ڪري بد نيتي يا ظالماڻي ڪمن لاءِ، يونان ڏند ڪٿا ۾ اڪلز جي پٺيان هلندڙ جنگجوءَ جي قبيلي جو نالو
antonyms: Leader, Independent thinker, Rebel, Dissenter
urduMeaning: وہ شخص جو بغیر سوال کے احکامات بجا لائے، اکثر ظالمانہ کاموں کے لیے، یونانی داستان میں اکیلیس کے پیروکار جنگجو قبیلے کا نام
دوسروں کے معاملات میں دخل دینے والا، ناخواندہ مداخلت کرنے والا، ٹانگ اڑانے والا
sindhiMeaning: ٻين جي معاملن ۾ مداخلت ڪرڻ وارو، ناخوانده مهمان جهڙو ناڪ ٽوهيندڙ
englishMeaning: Having or showing a tendency to interfere in the affairs of others; intrusive and nosy in an unwelcome way.
antonyms: Non-interfering, Respectful, Unintrusive, Discrete
synonyms: Interfering, Intrusive, Nosy, Prying, Officious
examples: The meddlesome neighbour always interfered in family disputes. His meddlesome nature made him unpopular at work. She had to deal with a meddlesome colleague who reported everything. The meddlesome aunt tried to control every family decision.

antonyms: Simple, Plain-spoken, Modest, Understated, Clear
sindhiMeaning: شيخي ڀريل يا وڏيون وڏيون ڳالهيون ڪرڻ وارو، وڏيري زبان استعمال ڪندڙ
examples: The magniloquent speaker impressed the crowd but said very little. His magniloquent writing style hid a lack of real substance. She delivered a magniloquent speech at the award ceremony. The magniloquent professor made simple topics sound complex.
urduMeaning: شیخی بھری یا بلند آہنگ زبان استعمال کرنے والا، پر تکلف اور مغرورانہ انداز میں بولنے یا لکھنے والا
synonyms: Bombastic, Pompous, Grandiloquent, Pretentious, High-flown
englishMeaning: Using high-flown or bombastic language; speaking or writing in an impressive and elevated manner that may be overly grand or pompous.

examples: She developed androphobia after years of abuse. Her androphobia made it difficult to work in a male-dominated office. Androphobia is often linked to past trauma or violence. With therapy, she gradually overcame her androphobia.
synonyms: Fear of men, Male phobia
sindhiMeaning: مردن کان شديد ۽ غير منطقي خوف، اهڙو شخص مردن جي موجودگيءَ ۾ سخت پريشاني يا گهٻراهٽ محسوس ڪري ٿو
antonyms: Androphilia (attraction to men), Comfort with men
englishMeaning: An intense and irrational fear of men. A person with androphobia experiences extreme anxiety, discomfort, or panic in the presence of or when thinking about men.
urduMeaning: مردوں سے شدید اور غیر منطقی خوف، اس فوبیا میں مبتلا شخص مردوں کی موجودگی میں سخت اضطراب یا گھبراہٹ محسوس کرتا ہے

antonyms: Occasional, Reformed, Temporary, Changeable
urduMeaning: ایسی عادت یا رجحان جو اتنا پختہ ہو گیا ہو کہ تبدیل ہونے کا امکان نہ ہو، پرانی اور گہری جڑیں رکھنے والا
examples: He was an inveterate gambler who could not stop despite his losses. She was an inveterate reader, finishing a book every week. The inveterate liar was trusted by no one. His inveterate optimism kept him going through hard times.
englishMeaning: Having a habit or interest so firmly established that it is unlikely to change; long-established and deep-rooted.
synonyms: Habitual, Chronic, Deep-seated, Confirmed, Ingrained
sindhiMeaning: هڪ عادت يا رجحان جيڪو ايترو پختو ٿي ويو هجي جو شايد تبديل نه ٿئي، پراڻو ۽ پختو

examples: He thrust forward his hand for a handshake. The crisis thrust forward a new generation of leaders. She was thrust forward as the spokesperson without notice. The soldier thrust forward his bayonet in the training drill.
urduMeaning: کسی کو یا کچھ کو زبردستی آگے کی طرف دھکیلنا، مجازاً کسی کو نمایاں مقام دینا
synonyms: Push forward, Propel, Advance, Drive forward, Promote
englishMeaning: To push or move something or someone forcefully in a forward direction. Also used figuratively to mean to promote someone or something into prominence.
antonyms: Pull back, Restrain, Hold back, Retreat
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کي يا ڪنهن شيءِ کي زوريءَ سان اڳيان ڌڪڻ، مجازي طور ڪنهن کي نمايان ڪرڻ

englishMeaning: To force something onto someone without their choice or agreement; to impose something on a person.
synonyms: Impose on, Force on, Inflict on, Burden with, Foist on
examples: Leadership was thrust upon her when the director resigned. Responsibility was thrust upon him at a very young age. Fame was thrust upon the young actor overnight. The role of caretaker was thrust upon her without preparation.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن تي ڪا ذميواري يا شيءِ زوريءَ مڙهڻ، ان جي مرضيءَ کانسواءِ
antonyms: Offer freely, Choose voluntarily, Accept willingly
urduMeaning: کسی پر کوئی ذمہ داری یا چیز زبردستی ڈالنا، اس کی مرضی کے بغیر

examples: His exoneration came after twenty years in prison for a crime he didn't commit. The DNA evidence led to his exoneration. She celebrated her exoneration with tears of relief. The court ordered his exoneration after new evidence emerged.
englishMeaning: The official clearing of someone from blame or criminal charges. The act of declaring or proving that a person is not guilty.
urduMeaning: کسی شخص کو جرم یا الزام سے سرکاری طور بری کرنا یا بے گناہ قرار دینا
synonyms: Acquittal, Vindication, Absolution, Clearance, Pardon
antonyms: Conviction, Condemnation, Guilt, Blame, Accusation
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شخص کي ڏوهه يا الزام کان سرڪاري طور بري ڪرڻ يا بي گناهه قرار ڏيڻ

examples: His dismissal came as a shock to the entire team. The teacher's dismissal of the student's idea was discouraging. She received a dismissal letter on Monday morning. The court ordered the dismissal of all charges.
urduMeaning: کسی کو نوکری سے نکالنا یا کام سے فارغ کرنا، مجازاً کسی بات کو سنجیدگی سے نہ لینا
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کي ڪم تان ڪڍڻ يا موڪلڻ، نوڪريءَ جو خاتمو، مجازي طور ڪنهن ڳالهه کي اهميت نه ڏيڻ
synonyms: Termination, Discharge, Redundancy, Rejection, Sacking
antonyms: Appointment, Hiring, Acceptance, Retention, Employment
englishMeaning: The act of ordering or allowing someone to leave; the termination of someone's employment. Also means the act of treating something as unworthy of serious consideration.
The process of taking legal action; engaging in or being subject to a lawsuit in a court of law.
examples: The company faced costly litigation over its faulty products. He avoided litigation by settling the dispute out of court. Litigation can take years and cost millions of dollars. The two neighbours entered litigation over the boundary wall.
synonyms: Lawsuit, Legal action, Legal proceedings, Court case, Trial
sindhiMeaning: عدالتي ڪاروائي يا قانوني ڪيس هلائڻ جو عمل، عدالت ۾ مقدمي ۾ ملوث هجڻ
antonyms: Settlement, Agreement, Arbitration, Mediation, Resolution
urduMeaning: قانونی کارروائی یا مقدمہ بازی کا عمل، عدالت میں مقدمے میں ملوث ہونا

synonyms: Sue, Prosecute, Take to court, File a lawsuit, Contest legally
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن تڪرار کي عدالت ۾ وٺي وڃڻ، قانوني ڪاروائي شروع ڪرڻ
examples: He decided to litigate the case rather than accept the settlement. The company had to litigate to protect its patent rights. She was prepared to litigate if the insurer refused to pay. Some landlords choose to litigate rather than negotiate.
urduMeaning: کسی تنازعے کو عدالت میں لے جانا، قانونی کارروائی شروع کرنا
englishMeaning: To take a dispute or claim to a court of law; to engage in legal proceedings.
antonyms: Settle, Mediate, Resolve, Arbitrate, Negotiate

synonyms: Show-off, Exhibitionist, Braggart, Poser, Pretender
examples: The ostentateur arrived at the party in a gold-plated car. Her ostentateur behaviour made genuine friends hard to find. The ostentateur donated publicly to charities for recognition. He was dismissed as an ostentateur with nothing of real value.
englishMeaning: A French-derived term for one who is ostentatious; a person who makes a showy or pretentious display of wealth, knowledge, or achievement to impress others.
sindhiMeaning: دکاوو ڪندڙ شخص جيڪو پنهنجي دولت يا ڪاميابي ڏيکارڻ لاءِ نمائشي انداز اختيار ڪري
urduMeaning: دکھاوا کرنے والا شخص جو اپنی دولت، علم یا کامیابی کا نمائشی مظاہرہ دوسروں کو متاثر کرنے کے لیے کرے
antonyms: Modest person, Humble individual, Understatement

examples: As a festophile, she never missed a local or international festival. The festophile travelled across Europe just to attend its best music festivals. His festophile nature made him the life of every gathering. She was a true festophile who decorated her home for every holiday.
sindhiMeaning: ميلن، جشنن ۽ تهوارن سان محبت رکندڙ شخص، جيڪو هر قسم جي تهوار ۾ شرڪت ڪرڻ جو شوقين هجي
synonyms: Festival lover, Celebration enthusiast, Party lover
urduMeaning: تہواروں، میلوں اور جشنوں سے محبت رکھنے والا شخص، جو ہر طرح کے تہوار میں شرکت کرنے کا شوقین ہو
antonyms: Recluse, Homebody, Festival avoider
englishMeaning: A person who loves festivals, celebrations, and festive occasions. Someone who has a deep passion for attending or participating in festivals of all kinds.

To cut food, especially meat, into very small pieces. It can also mean to speak or act in an affected, overly careful, or delicate way. To chop food into very small pieces. To speak carefully or indirectly. Meat that has been cut or ground into very small pieces.
antonyms: Slice broadly, Leave whole, Dodge (when speaking)
synonyms: Chop, Dice, Hash, Grind, Cut finely
sindhiMeaning: بارڪ بارڪ ٽڪرا ڪرڻ، ڪُٽڻ يا قيمي جي صورت ۾ آڻڻ, (ڳالهائڻ ۾) بناوٽي نرمي يا نازڪ انداز سان ڳالهائڻ, گوشت يا ٻين شين کي تمام ننڍن ٽڪرن ۾ ڪٽڻ يا قيمي جي صورت ۾ آڻڻ, سڌي ڳالهه نه ڪرڻ, احتياط يا بناوٽي انداز سان ڳالهائڻ, بارڪ ڪٽيل يا پيٺل گوشت/ قيمو
urduMeaning: باریک باریک ٹکڑے کرنا، قیمہ بنانا, (بات چیت میں) بناوٹی نرمی یا نزاکت سے بات کرنا, گوشت یا دوسری اشیاء کو بہت باریک ٹکڑوں میں کاٹنا یا قیمہ بنانا, صاف اور براہ راست بات نہ کرنا، احتیاط یا بناوٹ کے ساتھ بات کرنا, باریک کٹا یا پسا ہوا گوشت/ قیمہ
examples: She minced the garlic and onions finely for the sauce. He minced across the room in his new shoes. The politician did not mince his words in the press conference. The chef minced the lamb to prepare the keema.

antonyms: Silence, Concealment, Secret agenda
synonyms: Declaration, Statement, Policy document, Platform, Proclamation
sindhiMeaning: منشور / اعلان نامو, ھڪڙو لکيل بيان جيڪو ڪنهن جماعت يا تنظيم جا اصول  نظريا ۽ مقصد واضع ڪري
urduMeaning: منشور, ایک ایسا تحریری بیان جس میں کسی فرد  جماعت یا تنظیم کے نظریات  مقاصد اور منصوبے واضح طور پر بیان کیے جائیں
englishMeaning: A public declaration of the intentions, policies, or views of an individual, group, or political party. Often issued before elections or major events to communicate key aims. A manifesto is like a written promise or plan that tells people what someone believes and what they will do in the future.
examples: The party released its manifesto one week before the election. His manifesto called for free education and universal healthcare. The artist published a manifesto outlining his creative philosophy. The environmental manifesto was signed by over a million people.

urduMeaning: ظاہر ہونا/ ظاہر, ظاہر کرنا, نمایاں ہونا/ نمایاں کرنا/ نمایاں, واضح ہونا/ واضح کرنا, آشکار ہونا/ آشکار کرنا/ آشکار, عیاں ہونا/ عیاں, کھل کر سامنے آنا, مسافروں کی فہرست/ سامان کی فہرست/ کارگو کی فہرست, بارنامہ, مال برداری کی تفصیلی فہرست
examples: Her talent was manifest from a very early age. The symptoms of the disease began to manifest after three days. The ship's manifest listed all the cargo on board. His anxiety manifested itself through constant nail-biting.
englishMeaning: To show something clearly or make something obvious. To make something visible or obvious, or to show a quality, feeling, or condition clearly. A document or list of cargo, passengers, or goods carried by a ship, aircraft, or vehicle. Clear, obvious, or easily noticed.
synonyms: Obvious, Clear, Evident, Apparent, Display
sindhiMeaning: ظاهر ٿيڻ/ ظاهر/ ظاهر ڪرڻ, پڌرو ٿيڻ/ پڌرو/ پڌرو ڪرڻ, واضح ٿيڻ/ واضح, نمايان ٿيڻ/ نمايان, عيان ٿيڻ/ عيان, چٽو ٿيڻ/ چٽو, ظاهر ڪري ڏيکارڻ, سڃاڻپ ۾ اچڻ, سامان جي فهرست/ مسافرن جي فهرست, مال برداري جي لسٽ/ بارنامو, ڪارگو فهرست
antonyms: Hidden, Concealed, Obscure, Latent, Vague

examples: She tried to mollify her angry customer with a full refund. He brought flowers to mollify his wife after their argument. The manager's kind words helped mollify the upset employee. Nothing seemed to mollify the protesting crowd.
urduMeaning: راضی کرنا، غصہ ٹھنڈا کرنا، نرم کرنا، دلجوئی کرنا, کسی کے غصے  ناراضی یا پریشانی کو کم کرنا، راضی کرنا یا کسی سخت صورتِ حال کو نرم بنانا, کشیدگی کم کرنا
synonyms: Appease, Pacify, Soothe, Calm, Placate
antonyms: Aggravate, Provoke, Irritate, Inflame, Antagonise
sindhiMeaning: پرچائڻ، نرم ڪرڻ، غصو گهٽائڻ، دلجوئي ڪرڻ, ڪنهن جي ڪاوڙ ناراضگي يا پريشاني کي گهٽائڻ، ڪنهن کي پرچائڻ يا ڪنهن شيءِ کي نرم ۽ گهٽ سخت بڻائڻ, تڪرار گهٽائڻ, راضي ڪرڻ
englishMeaning: To calm someone's anger, soften feelings, reduce severity, or make something less harsh. To make a person less angry, upset, or anxious. It can also mean reducing the severity, intensity, or harshness of a situation, statement, punishment, or condition.

synonyms: Shine, Lustre, Polish, Veneer, Sheen
englishMeaning: A smooth and shiny appearance on a surface. A brief explanation of a difficult word or passage. An attractive appearance that hides the truth. To give a surface a smooth and shiny finish.
urduMeaning: کسی چیز کو چمکدار بنانا, ظاہری خوبصورتی یا اچھا تاثر جو حقیقت کو چھپا دے, کسی لفظ یا عبارت کی مختصر تشریح, کسی چیز کی چمک یا دمک
examples: The new paint gave the furniture a high gloss finish. She tried to gloss over her mistake in the report. The glossy magazine covered glamour but glossed over real issues. The politician glossed over the corruption scandal in his speech.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ جي چمڪ يا آب, ڪنهن لفظ يا عبارت جي مختصر وضاحت, ظاهري سٺائي جيڪا حقيقت لڪائي, ڪنهن شيءِ کي چمڪدار بڻائڻ
antonyms: Dullness, Matte, Transparency, Frankness

synonyms: Humiliate, Degrade, Demean, Belittle, Disgrace
examples: He refused to abase himself before his rivals. The tyrant sought to abase those who opposed him. She would not abase her principles for anyone. The harsh criticism served only to abase his confidence. No one should abase another person to feel superior.
englishMeaning: To lower someone in rank, dignity, or social standing. To humiliate or degrade a person deeply, causing loss of self-respect. To bring down the status or prestige of oneself or another through words or actions. To reduce someone to a state of shame or inferiority. To demean or belittle in a public or private setting.
urduMeaning: ذلیل کرنا، بے عزت کرنا، پست کرنا، حقیر کرنا، رسوا کرنا، شرمندہ کرنا، توہین کرنا، گھٹانا، درجہ کم کرنا، بے آبرو کرنا
antonyms: Elevate, Exalt, Honor, Uplift, Dignify
sindhiMeaning: ذليل ڪرڻ، بي عزت ڪرڻ، رسوا ڪرڻ، پست ڪرڻ، حقير ڪرڻ، شرمندو ڪرڻ، ادنيٰ ڪرڻ، منهن ڪارو ڪرڻ، توهين ڪرڻ، گهٽائڻ

synonyms: Prior, Superior, Prelate, Head monk, Archimandrite

examples: The abbot welcomed the pilgrims to the monastery. The elderly abbot guided his monks with great wisdom. The new abbot introduced several reforms to daily life. He was elected abbot after many years of devoted service. The abbot granted permission for visitors to tour the grounds.

sindhiMeaning: لاش کي محفوظ رکڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ کي خراب ٿيڻ کان بچائڻ، ياد يا روايت کي زنده رکڻ، خوشبودار تيلن يا ڪيميائي مادّن سان سنڀالڻ، لاش کي خاص دوائن يا ڪيميائي مادّن سان محفوظ رکڻ ته جيئن اها جلدي خراب نه ٿئي، مجازي معنيٰ ۾ ڪنهن ياد يا عزت کي قائم رکڻ
antonyms: Decay, Decompose, Rot, Destroy, Corrupt, Neglect, Spoil, Deteriorate
englishMeaning: To preserve a corpse for funeral or scientific purposes. To protect something from decay or destruction. To keep a memory, tradition, or honor alive. To preserve by using oils, spices, or chemicals. To preserve a dead body by treating it with chemicals or other methods to slow decay. It can also mean to preserve or keep something in memory or honor.
urduMeaning: مردہ جسم کو محفوظ کرنا، کسی چیز کو خراب ہونے سے بچانا، یاد یا روایت کو قائم رکھنا، تیل  مصالحوں یا کیمیائی مادوں کے ذریعے حفاظت کرنا، کسی مردہ جسم کو کیمیائی طریقے سے محفوظ کرنا تاکہ وہ جلد خراب نہ ہو، مجازی طور پر کسی یاد یا عزت کو محفوظ رکھنا
synonyms: Preserve, Mummify, Treat, Protect, Conserve, Safeguard, Maintain, Keep
examples: The funeral home embalmed the body before the public viewing. Ancient Egyptians used special techniques to embalm their dead. The book embalms the memories of a forgotten generation. Historians strive to embalm important traditions through careful documentation.

urduMeaning: خشک کرنا، نمی ختم کرنا، پانی نکال دینا، سکھا دینا، مرجھا دینا، بے جان بنا دینا، تازگی ختم کرنا، بنجر یا خشک سالی کا شکار کرنا
antonyms: Moisten, Hydrate, Wet, Soak, Dampen, Saturate, Irrigate, Refresh, Rehydrate, Water
synonyms: Dry, Dehydrate, Evaporate, Wither, Shrivel, Parch, Bake, Drain, Scorch, Preserve by drying
englishMeaning: To dry something thoroughly by removing its moisture. It can refer to natural drying, artificial drying, or figuratively to describe something that has become lifeless, dull, or lacking energy or emotion.
sindhiMeaning: سُڪائڻ، نمي ختم ڪرڻ، بلڪل خشڪ ڪري ڇڏڻ، پاڻي ڪڍڻ، مرجھائي ڇڏڻ، بي جان بڻائڻ، تازگي ختم ڪرڻ، ويران يا بنجر بڻائڻ
examples: The hot desert wind quickly desiccated the plants. Scientists desiccate food samples before conducting certain laboratory tests. The intense heat desiccated the soil, making farming difficult. Months without rain desiccated the riverbed until it cracked.

synonyms: Decay, Decompose, Spoil, Perish, Deteriorate, Corrode, Molder, Putrefy
sindhiMeaning: سڙڻ،  ڳرڻ يا وقت سان خراب ٿي وڃڻ، هي لفظ ميون  ڪاٺ  پنن يا ٻين شين جي قدرتي خراب ٿيڻ لاءِ استعمال ٿيندو آهي، اهو اخلاقي يا اداري جي زوال لاءِ به استعمال ٿي سگهي ٿو
urduMeaning: سڑ جانا، گل جانا یا وقت کے ساتھ خراب ہو جانا، یہ لفظ پھلوں  سبزیوں  لکڑی یا دوسری نامیاتی چیزوں کے خراب ہونے کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے، مجازی طور پر یہ اخلاقی یا ادارہ جاتی زوال کے لیے بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے
antonyms: Preserve, Protect, Maintain, Restore, Repair, Freshen, Strengthen, Revive
englishMeaning: To decay, decompose, or become spoiled because of age, moisture, bacteria, or fungi. To weaken or deteriorate gradually. The process or state of decay or decomposition. A condition of corruption, decline, or moral decay.
examples: The apples began to rot after being left outside for a week. Constant moisture can cause wooden beams to rot. If food starts to rot, it should be thrown away immediately. Years of neglect allowed the old house to rot beyond repair.

antonyms: Mend, Repair, Fix, Restore, Heal, Rebuild, Unite, Join, Preserve, Strengthen
sindhiMeaning: چڪنا چور ڪرڻ، ٽڪرن ۾ ورهائي ڇڏڻ، اميدن کي ختم ڪري ڇڏڻ، اعتماد ٽوڙي ڇڏڻ، سڪون يا خاموشي ڀڃڻ، مڪمل تباهي آڻڻ
englishMeaning: To break into many fragments. To destroy emotionally or mentally. To ruin hopes, dreams, or expectations. To disturb complete peace or silence. To cause something to collapse suddenly. To scatter violently into pieces. The act or result of breaking into pieces.
synonyms: Break, Smash, Crush, Splinter, Fragment, Demolish, Ruin, Destroy, Burst, Crack
urduMeaning: چکنا چور کرنا، ٹکڑوں میں بکھیر دینا، امیدیں ختم کر دینا، اعتماد توڑ دینا، سکون یا خاموشی کو ختم کر دینا، مکمل تباہی پہنچانا
examples: The strong earthquake shattered the old windows. The unexpected news shattered her confidence. A loud explosion shattered the silence of the night. The glass vase fell from the table and shattered into tiny pieces.

urduMeaning: جھاڑی یا چھوٹا لکڑی دار پودا جو درخت سے چھوٹا ہوتا ہے اور جس کی کئی شاخیں زمین کے قریب سے نکلتی ہیں، ایک دائمی لکڑی دار پودا جو درخت سے چھوٹا ہوتا ہے، اس کی کئی شاخیں زمین کے قریب سے نکلتی ہیں جھاڑیاں باغات  پارکوں اور آرائش کے لیے استعمال کی جاتی ہیں
synonyms: Bush, Hedge, Thicket, Scrub, Underbrush, Woody plant
antonyms: Tree, Sapling, Herb, Grass
examples: The gardener planted a flowering shrub near the entrance gate. Birds often build their nests inside dense shrubs. The shrub grew quickly after the rainy season. We trimmed the shrubs to keep the garden neat and attractive.
sindhiMeaning: جَهاڙ يا ننڍو ڪاٺيءَ وارو ٻوٽو جيڪو وڻ کان ننڍو هوندو آهي ۽ ڪيترين ٽارين سان وڌندو آهي، دائمي ڪاٺيءَ وارو ٻوٽو جيڪو وڻ کان قد ۾ ننڍو هوندو آهي، ان جون ڪيتريون ٽاريون زمين جي ويجهو حصي مان نڪرنديون آهن، جهاڙ باغن  پارڪن ۽ سجاوٽ لاءِ وڏي پيماني تي پوکيا ويندا آهن
englishMeaning: A small to medium-sized woody plant that has several stems growing from its base and is shorter than a tree. A perennial woody plant that is smaller than a tree. It usually has multiple stems arising from the ground rather than a single trunk. Shrubs are commonly used in gardens, parks, and landscaping for decoration, privacy, and environmental benefits.

To mix into a liquid and become part of it. To end or break apart. To become incorporated into a liquid so that it forms a solution. To officially end or disband something like a group or partnership. To lose strength or intensity. A smooth transition where one image fades out while another fades in. A gradual blending or merging of one thing into another
antonyms: Solidify, Form, Build, Combine, Unite
synonyms: Melt, Disintegrate, Fade, Break up, Liquefy
sindhiMeaning: پگهرجڻ/ ٽٽڻ، ختم ٿيڻ/ ورهائجي وڃڻ، ڪنهن مايع ۾ ملي ڪري مڪمل طور شامل ٿي وڃڻ، آهستي آهستي ختم ٿي وڃڻ يا گم ٿي وڃڻ، ڪنهن اداري يا گروهه کي ختم ڪرڻ، حالت يا احساس جو ڪمزور ٿي وڃڻ، فلم يا وڊيو ۾ هڪ منظر جو آهستي ختم ٿي ٻئي ۾ تبديل ٿيڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ جو آهستي آهستي ٻي ۾ ملي وڃڻ
examples: Sugar dissolves quickly in hot tea. The fog began to dissolve as the sun rose. The company decided to dissolve the partnership. His anger slowly dissolved into sadness. The director used a dissolve to move between scenes. The film opens with a slow dissolve from black.
urduMeaning: پگھلن/ بکھر جاناا، گھل جانا/ تحلیل ہونا، کسی مائع میں حل ہو کر اس کا حصہ بن جانا، ختم ہو جانا یا آہستہ آہستہ غائب ہونا، کسی تنظیم یا ادارے کو ختم کر دینا، جذبات یا حالت کا کمزور پڑ جانا، فلم یا ویڈیو میں ایک منظر کا دھیرے دھیرے ختم ہو کر دوسرے میں تبدیل ہونا، کسی چیز کا آہستہ آہستہ دوسری میں مل جانا

englishMeaning: To spread out or scatter in different directions. To cause something to break up and go in different ways. To distribute over a wide area. To break up a group or crowd. To dissolve or scatter particles (like light, fog, smoke). To distribute things such as resources, people, or information. To vanish gradually by spreading out.
urduMeaning: منتشر ہونا، پھیل جانا، بکھر جانا، منتشر کرنا، کسی چیز یا لوگوں کا مختلف سمتوں میں پھیل جانا یا بکھر جانا
examples: The crowd began to disperse after the event ended. The teacher asked the students to disperse quietly. The sunlight dispersed through the clouds. Police used barriers to disperse the protesters.
sindhiMeaning: پکڙجي وڃڻ، ڇڄي وڃڻ، ورهائجي وڃڻ، منتشر ٿيڻ، جڏهن ڪا شيءِ يا ماڻهو مختلف طرفن ۾ پکڙجي وڃن يا الڳ الڳ ٿي وڃن
antonyms: Gather, Collect, Assemble, Unite, Concentrate
synonyms: Scatter, Spread, Dissolve, Distribute, Break up

antonyms: Appear, Emerge, Materialize, Arrive, Show up, Come into view, Surface, Reappear
synonyms: Disappear, Fade, Evaporate, Dissolve, Melt away, Go missing, Dematerialize, Fizzle out, Pass away, Die out
examples: The magician made the rabbit vanish inside the hat. The morning fog vanished as soon as the sun came out. The suspect vanished before the police could arrest him. My keys seem to vanish every time I am in a hurry. Her smile vanished the moment she heard the bad news.
urduMeaning: غائب ہونا، نظروں سے اوجھل ہونا، اچانک ختم ہو جانا، لاپتہ ہو جانا، بغیر کسی نشان کے چلے جانا
sindhiMeaning: غائب ٿيڻ، اوجهل ٿيڻ، نظرن کان پري ٿي وڃڻ، ختم ٿي وڃڻ، لوپ ٿي وڃڻ، اچانڪ ۽ مڪمل طور تي نظر نه اچڻ
englishMeaning: To disappear suddenly and completely from sight or existence. To cease to exist or be visible without any clear explanation. To go away quickly and entirely, leaving no trace behind. Often used when something or someone disappears in a way that is surprising, unexplained, or difficult to understand.

examples: The students assembled in the school hall for the morning assembly. The engineer assembled all the parts of the machine carefully. The general assembled his troops before the battle. It took him two hours to assemble the new bookshelf. Thousands of people assembled in the square to hear the speech.
sindhiMeaning: گڏ ڪرڻ، گڏجڻ، يڪجا ڪرڻ، ميڙ ڪرڻ، جوڙڻ، حصا ملائي مڪمل شيءِ ٺاهڻ، هڪ هنڌ گڏ ٿيڻ
urduMeaning: جمع کرنا، اکٹھا کرنا، یکجا کرنا، ملانا، جوڑنا، حصوں کو ملا کر مکمل چیز بنانا، ایک جگہ جمع ہونا
antonyms: Disperse, Scatter, Separate, Disassemble, Divide, Break apart, Dissolve, Dismiss
englishMeaning: To gather people or things together in one place for a common purpose. To fit or put the parts of something together to form a complete whole. To come together as a group. Used both for gathering people and for constructing or building something from separate components.
synonyms: Gather, Collect, Congregate, Convene, Muster, Unite, Compile, Put together, Join, Rally

examples: Fragments of broken glass were scattered across the floor. The archaeologist found a fragment of an ancient pottery bowl. The explosion fragmented the rock into dozens of pieces. Only a fragment of the original manuscript has survived. The mirror fragmented into hundreds of tiny pieces when it hit the ground.
synonyms: Piece, Shard, Chunk, Bit, Scrap, Splinter, Portion, Remnant, Slice, Particle
englishMeaning: A small piece broken off or separated from something larger. An incomplete or isolated portion of something. As a verb, to break or cause something to break into small pieces or parts. Often used to describe the remains of something that has been broken, damaged, or left incomplete.
sindhiMeaning: ٽڪرو، ڀڃيل حصو، ننڍو ٽڪرو، اڌورو حصو، ڪنهن وڏي شيءِ مان ڀڄي ويل حصو، ٽوٽل ٽڪرو
urduMeaning: ٹکڑا، ٹوٹا ہوا حصہ، چھوٹا ٹکڑا، ادھورا حصہ، کسی بڑی چیز کا کھنڈر، پارہ
antonyms: Whole, Complete, Entirety, Total, Unit, Mass, Unify, Join, Combine

examples: The corrosion on the iron gate was caused by years of exposure to rain. Engineers regularly inspect pipelines for signs of corrosion. The corrosion of public trust in the government took many years. Salt water accelerates the corrosion of metal parts in ships. The bridge was declared unsafe due to severe corrosion of its steel beams.
antonyms: Preservation, Protection, Strengthening, Restoration, Maintenance, Conservation
sindhiMeaning: زنگ لڳڻ، زنگ آلودگي، ڪيميائي عمل سان ڌاتو يا مواد جو ڪمزور ٿيڻ ۽ خراب ٿيڻ، آهستي آهستي گهسجڻ يا خراب ٿيڻ جو عمل
englishMeaning: The gradual destruction or wearing away of a material, especially metal, caused by a chemical reaction with its environment such as moisture, air, or acid. The process by which a substance is slowly broken down and damaged over time. It is also used figuratively to describe the slow weakening or destruction of something such as trust, values, or institutions.
urduMeaning: زنگ، کٹاؤ، زنگ آلودگی، کسی دھات یا مواد کا کیمیائی عمل سے آہستہ آہستہ تباہ ہونا، گھسنا، بوسیدہ ہونے کا عمل
synonyms: Rust, Decay, Deterioration, Erosion, Oxidation, Degradation, Wear, Disintegration, Rotting

urduMeaning: خرابی، سڑاند، ضائع ہونے کا عمل، کھانے یا مال کا بگڑ جانا، گلنا سڑنا، نقصان
sindhiMeaning: خرابي، خراب ٿيڻ جو عمل، سڙڻ، گنداڻ، کاڌي شين جو خراب ٿيڻ، نقصان، ضياعت
examples: Proper refrigeration helps reduce food spoilage significantly. The supermarket suffered heavy losses due to spoilage of fresh produce. Spoilage of the cargo during transportation caused major financial damage. Farmers in hot climates face the constant problem of spoilage. The company introduced better packaging to minimise spoilage during shipping.
englishMeaning: The process by which food, goods, or materials become damaged, rotten, or unfit for use due to the action of bacteria, mold, time, or improper storage. The loss or waste resulting from decay or damage. It can also refer to the amount of material wasted or rendered unusable during a production or storage process.
synonyms: Decay, Decomposition, Rotting, Deterioration, Putrefaction, Wastage, Contamination, Damage, Ruin
antonyms: Preservation, Freshness, Conservation, Protection, Storage, Maintenance

synonyms: Revealer, Blabbermouth, Detractor, Disruptor, Ruiner, Blighter, Deflector, Aerofoil
englishMeaning: A person or thing that spoils or ruins something. Someone who reveals important plot details of a film, book, or show before others have had the chance to experience it. A device fitted to a vehicle, especially a racing car or aircraft, to improve aerodynamic performance by reducing drag or increasing stability. It can also refer to a candidate in an election who has little chance of winning but takes votes away from a stronger candidate.
antonyms: Keeper of secrets, Secret keeper, Supporter, Promoter, Enhancer, Improver
examples: He posted a spoiler about the film's ending before most people had seen it. The aerodynamic spoiler on the racing car helps keep it stable at high speeds. Please do not post any spoilers in the comment section. The third-party candidate acted as a spoiler in the election by drawing votes away from both major parties. She was furious when her friend revealed a major spoiler about the series finale.
sindhiMeaning: خراب ڪندڙ، ڳجهه ظاهر ڪندڙ، وڏي خبر ٻڌائيندڙ جيڪو مزو خراب ڪري، گاڏيءَ تي هوا روڪيندڙ پر، ووٽ ورهائيندڙ اميدوار
urduMeaning: برباد کرنے والا، فلم یا کہانی کا اہم راز پہلے بتانے والا، گاڑی پر ہوا کو کنٹرول کرنے والا آلہ، الیکشن میں ووٹ تقسیم کرنے والا امیدوار
خراب ہوا، بگڑا ہوا، ناقابل استعمال، حد سے زیادہ لاڈ پیار میں خراب ہوا بچہ، ضائع شدہ
sindhiMeaning: خراب ٿيل، بگڙيل، ناقابل استعمال ٿيل، وڌيڪ لاڊ لڏ ۾ وڌايل، بچو جيڪو حد کان وڌيڪ خراب ٿي ويو هجي
examples: The milk was spoilt because it had been left out of the fridge overnight. He was a spoilt child who always demanded whatever he wanted. The heavy rain spoilt our picnic completely. The spoilt food had to be thrown away immediately. Her spoilt behaviour made it difficult for others to get along with her.
antonyms: Fresh, Preserved, Unspoiled, Well-behaved, Disciplined, Intact, Undamaged
englishMeaning: Damaged, ruined, or made unfit for use or enjoyment. Used to describe a child who has been given too much by parents and has developed selfish or demanding behaviour. Also used in British English as the past tense and past participle of the verb spoil. Something that has been harmed, wasted, or impaired in quality or condition.
synonyms: Ruined, Damaged, Pampered, Indulged, Overindulged, Rotten, Contaminated, Impaired, Marred

urduMeaning: خراب ہوا، سڑا ہوا، فاسد، ناقابل استعمال، حد سے زیادہ نازنین بنایا ہوا بچہ، ضائع شدہ
sindhiMeaning: خراب ٿيل، سڙيل، بگڙيل، حد کان وڌيڪ نازبرداري سان خراب ڪيل، کاڌي جي شيءِ جيڪا پراڻي ٿي خراب ٿي وڃي
examples: The spoiled meat had a foul smell and had to be discarded. Growing up as the only child, he was somewhat spoiled by his parents. The fresh vegetables we bought yesterday are already spoiled. She realised the trip had been spoiled by the constant arguments. A spoiled child often struggles to adapt to the demands of adult life.
antonyms: Fresh, Unspoiled, Well-mannered, Disciplined, Intact, Preserved, Wholesome
englishMeaning: Damaged, decayed, or no longer fit for use. Used to describe food that has gone bad and is no longer safe to eat. Also used to describe a child who has been excessively indulged and has become selfish or demanding as a result. In American English, it is the preferred past tense and past participle of spoil.
synonyms: Rotten, Bad, Decayed, Pampered, Indulged, Ruined, Corrupted, Tainted, Marred, Overindulged

antonyms: Dehydrate, Dry, Desiccate, Parch, Drain, Deplete, Wither
englishMeaning: To cause a person, animal, or substance to absorb or be supplied with water or moisture. To restore or maintain the water balance in the body or a substance. A compound containing water molecules chemically combined in a definite ratio. To keep the body adequately supplied with fluids to maintain health and proper function.
synonyms: Moisturise, Water, Soak, Saturate, Replenish, Quench, Nourish, Refresh
urduMeaning: پانی پلانا، نمی دینا، جسم میں پانی کی کمی پوری کرنا، تر کرنا، سیراب کرنا
examples: Doctors advised the athlete to hydrate well before and after the race. You should hydrate your skin daily using a good moisturiser. It is important to hydrate yourself by drinking plenty of water in hot weather. The plant needs to be hydrated regularly during the dry season. She drank several glasses of water to hydrate herself after the long walk.
sindhiMeaning: پاڻي پيارڻ، رطوبت ڏيڻ، نمي ڀرڻ، جسم ۾ پاڻي جي گهٽتائي پوري ڪرڻ، ترٻيل ڪرڻ

antonyms: Moist, Wet, Hydrated, Saturated, Lush, Fresh, Juicy, Damp
englishMeaning: Completely dried out or dehydrated, often as a result of the removal of moisture. Used to describe food that has been dried as a method of preservation. Also used figuratively to describe something that is dry, lifeless, or lacking in vitality or interest. Having had all moisture removed from it, either naturally or artificially.
sindhiMeaning: مڪمل طور سکيل، خشڪ ٿيل، سڪايل، نمي کان خالي، خشڪ ۽ بيجان، پاڻي کان محروم
synonyms: Dried, Dehydrated, Parched, Shrivelled, Withered, Arid, Bone-dry, Moisture-free, Mummified
urduMeaning: مکمل طور خشک، سکھایا ہوا، نمی سے محروم، خشک و بے جان، پانی کے بغیر، خشک کیا ہوا
examples: The expedition team carried desiccated food because it was light and had a long shelf life. The desiccated landscape stretched for miles without a single green plant. Desiccated coconut is widely used in baking and cooking. The ancient mummy was found in a perfectly desiccated state. The prolonged drought left the farmland desiccated and infertile.

synonyms: Drying, Dehydration, Evaporation, Withering, Parching, Drainage, Aridity, Drought
antonyms: Hydration, Moistening, Saturation, Irrigation, Flooding, Dampening, Wetting
urduMeaning: مکمل خشکی، پانی کا مکمل خاتمہ، سکھانے کا عمل، نمی ختم ہونے کی حالت، قحط سالی
sindhiMeaning: مڪمل خشڪي، پاڻي جو مڪمل ختم ٿيڻ، سڪائڻ جو عمل، نمي ختم ٿيڻ جي حالت، خشڪي
englishMeaning: The process of completely drying out or removing all moisture from something. The state of being extremely dry or having all moisture removed. Used in science to describe the removal of water from a substance for preservation or analysis. Also used in ecology to describe the drying up of environments such as lakes, soil, or vegetation.
examples: The desiccation of the Aral Sea is considered one of the worst environmental disasters in history. Scientists use desiccation to preserve biological samples in laboratories. The desiccation of the soil made farming almost impossible in the affected region. Prolonged heat waves can lead to the desiccation of rivers and wetlands. The desiccation of the seeds was necessary before storing them for long-term use.

antonyms: Dry, Encourage, Enliven, Intensify, Heighten, Inspire, Stimulate, Invigorate
synonyms: Moisten, Wet, Dull, Reduce, Lessen, Suppress, Discourage, Muffle, Subdue, Restrain

synonyms: Geeky, Studious, Bookish, Brainy, Scholarly, Intellectual, Wonkish

Used to describe a person, style, hobby, or activity that reflects the qualities typical of a nerd, often in a humorous or affectionate way.

antonyms: Disconnection, Separation, Division, Periphery, Outskirts
synonyms: Connection, Link, Center, Hub, Junction, Network, Bond, Tie, Core, Focal point

urduMeaning: ربط، تعلق، گٹھ جوڑ، مرکز، ایسا نقطہ جہاں کئی چیزیں یا لوگ آپس میں ملیں، ایسا مرکز جہاں مختلف سرگرمیاں  خیالات یا مفادات جمع ہوں، جوڑنے والی کڑی
sindhiMeaning: ڳانڍاپو، تعلق، ڪڙي، ميلاپ، اهڙو مرڪز جتي ڪيتريون ئي شيون يا ماڻهو ملن، اهڙي جڳهه يا نقطو جتي مختلف سرگرميون  خيال يا مفاد گڏ ٿين، ڳنڍڻ وارو نقطو
examples: Dubai has become a major nexus for international trade. There is a clear nexus between poverty and lack of education. The city is the nexus of political and cultural activity in the region. Investigators uncovered a nexus between the smugglers and corrupt officials. The university serves as a nexus for research and innovation.

synonyms: Miser, Skinflint, Cheapskate, Penny-pincher, Scrooge, Hoarder
englishMeaning: A person who is extremely unwilling to spend money or share resources. A stingy or miserly individual. Someone who hoards possessions and avoids generosity even when capable of giving. A person known for excessive thriftiness to the point of meanness.
antonyms: Spendthrift, Philanthropist, Donor, Squanderer, Generous person
sindhiMeaning: ڪنجوس، بخيل، تنگ دل، گهٽ خرچ ڪندڙ، اهڙو ماڻهو جيڪو پئسو يا شيون ٻين سان وراهڻ کان لنوائي، ڏاڍو ڪفايتي ماڻهو جيڪو فضول ته ڇا ضرورت تي به خرچ نه ڪري
examples: He is such a niggard that he refuses to buy new shoes even when his old ones are torn. The old niggard would not give a single coin to charity. People avoided inviting him because he was known as a niggard. Despite his wealth, he lived like a niggard in a tiny room. The niggard counted every rupee before spending it.
urduMeaning: کنجوس، بخیل، تنگ دل، کم خرچ کرنے والا، ایسا شخص جو پیسہ یا چیزیں دوسروں کے ساتھ بانٹنے سے گریز کرے، حد سے زیادہ کفایت شعار جو ضرورت پر بھی خرچ نہ کرے

englishMeaning: Unwilling to give or spend money, time, or effort. Extremely stingy or miserly in nature. Provided in a very small or inadequate amount. Used to describe a person, attitude, or amount that reflects excessive meanness or lack of generosity.
antonyms: Generous, Lavish, Liberal, Bountiful, Munificent, Plentiful
sindhiMeaning: ڪنجوسي وارو، بخيلانه، تنگ دلي سان، تمام ٿورو، گهٽ ۽ ناڪافي، اهڙو رويو يا مقدار جيڪو ڪنجوسي ظاهر ڪري، خرچ ڪرڻ کان پاسو ڪرڻ وارو
synonyms: Stingy, Miserly, Mean, Tight-fisted, Parsimonious, Frugal, Sparing, Scanty
urduMeaning: کنجوسانہ، بخیلانہ، تنگ دلی سے، بہت کم، ناکافی مقدار میں، ایسا رویہ یا مقدار جو کنجوسی ظاہر کرے، خرچ کرنے سے گریز کرنے والا
examples: He gave a niggardly tip to the waiter despite the excellent service. The company offered a niggardly raise to its hardworking employees. She is known for her niggardly attitude towards charity. Their niggardly donation barely covered the cost of one meal. The host served a niggardly portion of food to the guests.

urduMeaning: رات کی چڑیل، رات کی بدروح، ایسی مافوق الفطرت عورت یا بھوت جسے لوگ نیند میں آنے والے ڈراؤنے خواب یا سانس گھٹنے کا سبب سمجھتے ہیں، رات کے وقت ستانے والی بدروح، خوفناک رات کا وجود
examples: Old tales speak of a night hag that sits on the chest of sleepers. He woke up screaming, claiming a night hag had visited him. In the poem, the night hag rides the storm across the dark sky. Villagers believed a night hag was responsible for the children's bad dreams. The novel describes a terrifying night hag haunting the lonely castle.
englishMeaning: A female demon or evil spirit believed in folklore to visit people during sleep and cause nightmares or a feeling of suffocation. A frightening figure associated with sleep paralysis in old superstitions. In literary use, a witch or wicked supernatural woman of the night. Sometimes used figuratively to describe a terrifying or oppressive presence experienced at night.
sindhiMeaning: رات جي ڏائڻ، رات جي بدروح، اهڙي مافوق الفطرت عورت يا ڀوت جنهن کي ماڻهو ننڊ ۾ ايندڙ خوفناڪ خواب يا ساهه گهٽجڻ جو سبب سمجهن، رات جي وقت تنگ ڪندڙ بدروح، خوفناڪ رات وارو وجود
synonyms: Witch, Demoness, Hag, Specter, Phantom, Ghoul, Succubus
antonyms: Angel, Fairy, Guardian spirit, Benevolent being

synonyms: Conceptualism, Anti-realism, Particularism, Terminism
englishMeaning: A philosophical doctrine which holds that general or abstract terms and universal concepts exist only as names and have no independent reality. The belief that only individual objects are real and that classes or categories are merely mental constructs. A theory opposing the view that universals possess true existence outside the mind. An important position in medieval and modern philosophy concerning the nature of reality and language.
antonyms: Realism, Platonism, Universalism, Idealism
urduMeaning: نام پرستی، وہ فلسفیانہ نظریہ جو کہتا ہے کہ عمومی یا تجریدی تصورات صرف نام ہیں اور ان کا کوئی خود مختار وجود نہیں، صرف انفرادی اشیاء حقیقی ہیں اور اقسام و درجات محض ذہنی تخلیق ہیں، کلیات کے وجود کا انکار کرنے والا فلسفیانہ نظریہ
sindhiMeaning: نام پرستي، اهو فلسفياڻو نظريو جيڪو چوي ٿو ته عام يا تجريدي تصورات صرف نالا آهن ۽ انهن جو ڪو خود مختيار وجود ڪونهي، صرف انفرادي شيون حقيقي آهن ۽ ذيلي درجا ذهني تخليق آهن، ڪليتن جي وجود کان انڪار وارو فلسفياڻو نظريو
examples: Nominalism challenged the medieval belief in the real existence of universals. William of Ockham is regarded as a leading figure of nominalism. The debate between realism and nominalism shaped medieval philosophy. Modern nominalism continues to influence theories of language and logic. The professor explained nominalism with simple everyday examples.

englishMeaning: Famous or well known, especially for something bad or unpleasant. Widely recognized for negative qualities, behavior, or reputation. Infamous and known by many people for wrongdoing, crime, or misconduct. Used to describe persons, places, or things that have gained widespread attention due to undesirable traits or actions.
examples: The area is notorious for its high crime rate. He is a notorious liar and no one trusts him anymore. The gang leader was notorious throughout the country. The hotel is notorious for its poor service. She became notorious after the scandal was exposed in the media.
antonyms: Reputable, Respected, Honorable, Unknown, Esteemed, Virtuous
sindhiMeaning: بدنام، مشهور خراب ڪمن جي ڪري، عام طور خراب ڪمن لاءِ سڃاتل، اهڙو شخص يا جڳهه جيڪو بڇڙي شهرت رکي، عوام ۾ ڪنهن خراب عادت يا ڪم سبب مشهور
synonyms: Infamous, Disreputable, Ill-famed, Scandalous, Disgraceful, Dishonorable, Well-known
urduMeaning: بدنام، خراب کاموں کی وجہ سے مشہور، عام طور پر منفی عادات یا اعمال کی بنا پر پہچانا جانے والا، ایسا شخص یا جگہ جو بری شہرت رکھے، کسی غلط کام کی وجہ سے عوام میں مشہور

englishMeaning: The food and other substances necessary for growth, health, and good condition. The act or process of providing or receiving the things needed to live and develop. Something that supports life, energy, or strength, whether physical, mental, or emotional. Used to refer to anything that helps a living being or a thing grow, develop, or remain healthy.
antonyms: Starvation, Malnutrition, Deprivation, Hunger, Famine
synonyms: Food, Nutrition, Sustenance, Diet, Nutriment, Subsistence, Provisions
urduMeaning: غذا، خوراک، پرورش، پرورش کا سامان، ایسی چیز جو جسم  دماغ یا روح کو طاقت اور صحت بخشے، ایسی چیز جو بچوں  پودوں یا جانوروں کی نشوونما میں مدد دے، پالنے والی چیز
sindhiMeaning: غذا، خوراڪ، پرورش، پرورش جو سامان، اهڙي شي جيڪا جسم، دماغ يا روح کي طاقت ۽ صحت بخشي، اهڙي شي جيڪا ٻارن، ٻوٽن يا جانورن جي واڌ ويجهه ۾ مدد ڪري، پاليندڙ شي
examples: A balanced diet provides proper nourishment to the body. Plants draw nourishment from the soil through their roots. Books are a source of nourishment for the mind. Mother's love gives emotional nourishment to a child. Without enough nourishment, animals cannot survive in the wild.

antonyms: Harmless, Safe, Healthy, Beneficial, Wholesome, Innocuous
synonyms: Harmful, Poisonous, Toxic, Injurious, Pernicious, Damaging, Deleterious, Unhealthy
englishMeaning: Harmful, poisonous, or very unpleasant. Causing damage or injury to health, life, or the environment. Morally harmful or corrupting in influence. Used to describe gases, substances, fumes, ideas, or atmospheres that are dangerous, unhealthy, or destructive in nature.
urduMeaning: زہریلا، نقصان دہ، مضر صحت، تکلیف دہ، ایسی چیز جو صحت  زندگی یا ماحول کے لیے نقصان دہ ہو، اخلاقی طور پر برا اثر ڈالنے والی، خطرناک اور بدبودار
sindhiMeaning: زهريلو، نقصانڪار، مضر صحت، تڪليف ڏيندڙ، اهڙي شي جيڪا صحت، زندگي يا ماحول لاءِ نقصانڪار هجي، اخلاقي طور خراب اثر وجهندڙ، خطرناڪ ۽ بدبودار
examples: The factory releases noxious fumes into the air. Noxious chemicals were leaking from the broken container. The room was filled with a noxious smell. Children should be kept away from noxious substances. He warned them against the noxious influence of bad company.

synonyms: Criticism, Censure, Abuse, Vilification, Defamation, Disgrace, Reproach, Slander
englishMeaning: Strong public criticism, blame, or verbal attack. The condition of being discredited or disgraced due to widespread condemnation. Harsh and abusive language directed at someone or something. Public shame or loss of reputation resulting from criticism.
antonyms: Praise, Honor, Approval, Respect, Commendation, Glory, Acclaim
examples: The minister faced public obloquy after the scandal was exposed. The writer's controversial book brought him obloquy from religious groups. He bore the obloquy of his enemies with patience and dignity. The leader's actions invited obloquy from every section of society. Despite the obloquy, she continued her work without fear.
urduMeaning: بدنامی، عوامی ملامت، سخت تنقید، گالم گلوچ، ذلت، رسوائی، عوام کی طرف سے لعن طعن، کسی کی شہرت کو نقصان پہنچانے والی سخت بیان بازی
sindhiMeaning: بدنامي، عوامي ملامت، سخت تنقيد، گاريون، ذلت، رسوائي، عوامي طرفان لعن طعن، ڪنهن جي شهرت کي نقصان پهچائيندڙ سخت بيانبازي

sindhiMeaning: جنون، خبط، گهرو شوق، ڌيان جو ڪنهن هڪ شي تي ڄمي وڃڻ، ڪنهن خيال، ماڻهو يا ڪم جي پٺيان لڳڻ، ذهن مان نه نڪرندڙ سوچ، اهڙي گهري دلچسپي جيڪا ٻيون سڀ ڳالهيون وسارائي ڇڏي
examples: His obsession with cricket affected his studies. She has an unusual obsession with collecting old coins. Cleanliness has become an obsession for him. The detective's obsession with the case finally led him to the truth. Social media has turned into an obsession for many young people.
englishMeaning: A continual and excessive preoccupation of the mind with a particular idea, feeling, person, or activity. A strong and uncontrollable desire or interest that dominates a person's thoughts. A persistent thought, image, or impulse that a person cannot easily get rid of. In psychology, a fixed idea that often causes distress and influences behavior.
antonyms: Indifference, Disinterest, Apathy, Detachment, Unconcern
synonyms: Fixation, Mania, Preoccupation, Passion, Compulsion, Fascination, Infatuation

antonyms: Love, Affection, Admiration, Approval, Esteem, Liking
sindhiMeaning: نفرت، ڌڪار، عوامي ڌڪار، بدنامي، عام ماڻهن جي شديد ناپسنديده راءِ، ڪنهن خراب ڪم سبب پيدا ٿيندڙ نفرت، عوام ۾ پيدا ٿيندڙ ڌڪار جو احساس
urduMeaning: نفرت، عوامی نفرت، بدنامی، عام لوگوں کی شدید ناپسندیدگی، کسی برے کام کی وجہ سے پیدا ہونے والی نفرت، عوام میں پھیلی ہوئی شدید مذمت کا احساس
synonyms: Hatred, Loathing, Detestation, Abhorrence, Disgrace, Contempt, Antipathy
englishMeaning: Widespread hatred or strong dislike directed at a person or action regarded as wrong or evil. General disgust or contempt felt towards someone. The disgrace or unpopularity resulting from a hated act. Used especially in formal contexts to describe intense public condemnation.
examples: The dictator earned the odium of the entire nation. The cruel act brought lasting odium upon the perpetrators. He has suffered great odium for his unjust decisions. The traitor lived the rest of his life in odium. Their corrupt practices invited the odium of the public.

sindhiMeaning: ڪڏهن ڪڏهن، وقت بوقت، رک رک ڪري، ٿوري ٿوري دير کان پوءِ، لاڳيتو نه پر ٽوڙي ٽوڙي ٿيندڙ، ڪجهه دير لاءِ بند ٿيندڙ ۽ وري شروع ٿيندڙ
urduMeaning: کبھی کبھار، وقتاً فوقتاً، رک رک کر، تھوڑی تھوڑی دیر بعد، مسلسل نہیں بلکہ ٹوٹ ٹوٹ کر ہونے والا، کچھ دیر کے لیے بند ہو کر دوبارہ شروع ہونے والا
examples: It rained off and on throughout the day. They have been dating off and on for two years. I worked on the project off and on for several months. He visits his hometown off and on. The machine has been giving trouble off and on this week.
englishMeaning: Happening occasionally rather than continuously. Starting and stopping at irregular intervals. From time to time or now and then. Used to describe an action, event, or condition that occurs intermittently over a period of time.
antonyms: Continuously, Constantly, Steadily, Regularly, Always, Uninterruptedly
synonyms: Intermittently, Occasionally, Sporadically, Periodically, Now and then, From time to time

examples: It is admitted on all hands that he is the best player in the team. On all hands, people praised her courage and honesty. The proposal was welcomed on all hands by the members. On all hands, the city was surrounded by mountains. His leadership is appreciated on all hands.
urduMeaning: ہر طرف سے، ہر سمت سے، چاروں طرف سے، سب کی جانب سے، عام طور پر، سب کی رائے میں، ہر شخص کی طرف سے، ایسی بات جس پر سب متفق ہوں
antonyms: Nowhere, By none, From one side, Partially, Locally
englishMeaning: From every side or direction. By everyone or from all people. Universally acknowledged or agreed upon. From all quarters or sources. Used to indicate that something is admitted, accepted, or experienced by all parties involved.
sindhiMeaning: هر طرف کان، هر هنڌان، سڀني پاسن کان، عام طور تي، سڀني جي راءِ ۾، هر ڪنهن طرفان، چوڌاري، سڀئي ماڻهو جنهن ڳالهه تي متفق هجن
synonyms: Everywhere, Universally, From all sides, From every quarter, By all, Generally

antonyms: Continuously, Constantly, Always, Steadily, Regularly
sindhiMeaning: ڪڏهن ڪڏهن، وقت بوقت، رک رک ڪري، ٽوڙي ٽوڙي، لاڳيتو نه پر وقفي وقفي سان ٿيندڙ، ڪڏهن هلندڙ ۽ ڪڏهن بند ٿيندڙ
synonyms: Intermittently, Sporadically, Occasionally, Periodically, From time to time, Off and on
englishMeaning: Occurring at irregular intervals rather than continuously. Starting, stopping, and starting again over a period of time. Intermittently or from time to time. Used to describe relationships, weather, conditions, or activities that happen with breaks in between.
examples: It snowed on and off all night. They have been friends on and off for many years. He has been studying medicine on and off due to financial issues. The fan keeps working on and off. I have known him on and off since college.
urduMeaning: کبھی کبھار، وقفے وقفے سے، رک رک کر، مسلسل نہیں بلکہ ٹوٹ ٹوٹ کر ہونے والا، کبھی چلنے اور کبھی بند ہونے والا، وقتاً فوقتاً
وجودی، وجودیت سے متعلق، وجود کے فلسفے سے متعلق، حقیقت اور ہستی کے مطالعے سے تعلق رکھنے والا، ایسے مباحث جو اشیاء کے اصل وجود اور ماہیت سے متعلق ہوں، فلسفے کی شاخ آنٹولوجی سے متعلق
synonyms: Metaphysical, Existential, Philosophical, Essential, Theoretical
antonyms: Empirical, Material, Concrete, Physical, Tangible
examples: The book deals with ontological questions about human existence. Philosophers have long debated the ontological status of numbers. His argument is based on an ontological assumption about reality. The ontological proof of God's existence is a famous philosophical concept. The thesis examines the ontological nature of consciousness.
englishMeaning: Relating to the philosophical study of the nature of being, existence, or reality. Concerned with what exists and the categories of being. Pertaining to ontology as a branch of metaphysics. Used in philosophical, theological, and scientific discussions about the fundamental nature of things.
sindhiMeaning: وجوديت سان لاڳاپيل، وجود جي فلسفي بابت، حقيقت ۽ هستيءَ جي مطالعي سان واسطو رکندڙ، اهڙا بحث جيڪي شين جي اصل وجود ۽ ماهيت بابت هجن، فلسفي جي شاخ آنٽولاجي سان لاڳاپيل

englishMeaning: The branch of philosophy that studies the nature of being, existence, and reality. The systematic study of what exists and how things can be categorized. In computer science, a formal representation of knowledge through a set of concepts and the relationships between them. A theory concerning the fundamental categories of reality.
synonyms: Metaphysics, Philosophy of being, Existential study, Cosmology
sindhiMeaning: وجوديات، علم الوجود، فلسفي جي اها شاخ جيڪا هستي ۽ حقيقت جو مطالعو ڪندي آهي، ڪمپيوٽر سائنس ۾ تصورن ۽ انهن جي وچ ۾ رشتن جي رسمي نمائندگي، شين جي بنيادي ماهيت بابت نظريو
urduMeaning: وجودیات، علم الوجود، فلسفے کی وہ شاخ جو ہستی اور حقیقت کا مطالعہ کرتی ہے، کمپیوٹر سائنس میں تصورات اور ان کے باہمی تعلقات کی رسمی نمائندگی، اشیاء کی بنیادی ماہیت سے متعلق نظریہ
antonyms: Empiricism, Materialism, Phenomenology
examples: Aristotle's writings laid the foundation for modern ontology. Ontology asks what it means for something to exist. The course covers both metaphysics and ontology in detail. In artificial intelligence, ontology helps machines understand information. His research focuses on the ontology of social institutions.

Doctors sometimes prescribe an opiate to relieve severe pain. Karl Marx famously called religion the opiate of the masses. Television has become an opiate for many idle minds. The opiate made the patient drift into a deep sleep. Misuse of opiates can lead to serious addiction.
antonyms: Stimulant, Tonic, Energizer, Antidote
synonyms: Narcotic, Sedative, Tranquilizer, Anodyne, Soporific, Drug
englishMeaning: A drug derived from opium or having effects similar to opium, used to relieve pain or induce sleep. A narcotic substance that produces drowsiness or numbness. Anything that soothes the mind, dulls the senses, or makes a person less aware of unpleasant realities. Figuratively, something that calms emotions or distracts from problems.
urduMeaning: افیمی دوا، نیند لانے والی دوا، درد کم کرنے والی نشہ آور دوا، ایسی چیز جو حواس کو سن کر دے یا ذہن کو سست کر دے، استعارے کے طور پر ایسی چیز جو لوگوں کو حقیقت سے غافل کر دے
sindhiMeaning: آفيمي دوا، ننڊ آڻيندڙ دوا، درد گهٽائيندڙ نشيلي دوا، اهڙي شي جيڪا حواسن کي بي حس ڪري يا ذهن کي سُست ڪري، استعاري طور اهڙي شي جيڪا ماڻهن کي حقيقت کان غافل ڪري ڇڏي

antonyms: Antidote, Stimulant, Remedy, Tonic
englishMeaning: A reddish-brown addictive drug prepared from the juice of the opium poppy, used as a narcotic and in medicine to relieve pain. A powerful substance that causes sleep, dulls the senses, and can lead to addiction. Figuratively, anything that creates a state of unawareness, illusion, or false comfort and prevents people from facing reality.
synonyms: Narcotic, Drug, Poppy juice, Sedative, Soporific
urduMeaning: افیون، نیند لانے والی نشہ آور چیز، پوست کے پودے سے حاصل ہونے والا خطرناک نشہ، درد کم کرنے والی مگر عادت ڈالنے والی دوا، استعارے کے طور پر ایسی چیز جو انسان کو حقیقت سے بے خبر کر دے
sindhiMeaning: آفيم، ننڊ آڻيندڙ نشيلي شي، پوست جي ٻوٽي مان نڪرندڙ هڪ خطرناڪ نشو، درد گهٽائيندڙ پر عادت پيدا ڪندڙ دوا، استعاري طور اهڙي شي جيڪا ماڻهن کي حقيقت کان بي خبر ڪري ڇڏي
examples: The smuggling of opium is a serious crime in many countries. Opium was once widely used as a medicine to ease pain. Long-term use of opium can destroy a person's health. He compared the addictive entertainment to opium for the mind. The police seized a large quantity of opium near the border.

antonyms: Pessimism, Despair, Hopelessness, Cynicism, Gloom, Negativity
englishMeaning: A hopeful and positive attitude towards life and the future. The belief that good things will happen and that problems can be overcome. A tendency to expect the best possible outcome in any situation. In philosophy, the doctrine that this world is the best of all possible worlds and that good ultimately prevails over evil.
urduMeaning: امید، خوش امیدی، مثبت سوچ، یہ یقین کہ آئندہ سب کچھ اچھا ہوگا، مشکلات میں بھی امید رکھنے کا رویہ، فلسفے کا وہ نظریہ کہ دنیا میں خیر شر پر غالب رہتا ہے
synonyms: Hopefulness, Positivity, Confidence, Cheerfulness, Buoyancy, Idealism
examples: His optimism inspired everyone around him during the crisis. There is a sense of optimism about the country's economic future. She faced her illness with great courage and optimism. Despite repeated failures, his optimism never faded. The new policy has created optimism among the youth.
sindhiMeaning: اميد، خوش اميدي، مثبت سوچ، اها سوچ ته آئنده سڀ ڪجهه چڱو ٿيندو، مشڪلاتن ۾ به اميد رکڻ جو رويو، فلسفي جو اهو نظريو ته دنيا ۾ خير شر تي غالب آهي
اميد پرست، مثبت سوچ رکندڙ شخص، اهڙو ماڻهو جيڪو هميشه چڱي نتيجي جي اميد رکي، مشڪلاتن ۾ به اميد نه ڇڏيندڙ، فلسفي ۾ اهو شخص جيڪو خير جي غالب اچڻ تي يقين رکي
examples: He is a born optimist and never loses hope. An optimist sees opportunity in every difficulty. She remained an optimist throughout her long illness. The young entrepreneur is an optimist about the future of technology. Only a true optimist could have started a business in such hard times.
urduMeaning: امید پرست، مثبت سوچ رکھنے والا شخص، ایسا شخص جو ہمیشہ اچھے نتیجے کی توقع رکھے، مشکلات میں بھی امید نہ چھوڑنے والا، فلسفے میں وہ شخص جو خیر کی فتح پر یقین رکھے
synonyms: Idealist, Dreamer, Believer, Hopeful person, Positive thinker
antonyms: Pessimist, Cynic, Defeatist, Doubter, Skeptic
englishMeaning: A person who tends to expect favorable or good outcomes from situations. Someone who maintains a hopeful and positive attitude even in difficult circumstances. A person who believes in the goodness of life and the possibility of success. In philosophy, one who holds the doctrine that good ultimately triumphs over evil.

antonyms: Pessimistic, Gloomy, Hopeless, Negative, Cynical, Despondent
englishMeaning: Having or showing a hopeful and confident view about the future. Believing that good things will happen or that something will succeed. Expecting positive outcomes despite challenges or uncertainty. Used to describe a person, attitude, prediction, or feeling that is full of hope and confidence.
synonyms: Hopeful, Positive, Confident, Cheerful, Buoyant, Sanguine, Upbeat
sindhiMeaning: اميد ڀريو، مثبت سوچ وارو، خوش اميدي رکندڙ، چڱي نتيجي جي اميد ڪندڙ، اهڙو رويو جنهن ۾ مشڪلاتن جي باوجود اميد قائم رهي، خوشگوار نتيجي جي توقع رکندڙ
urduMeaning: پر امید، مثبت سوچ والا، خوش امید، اچھے نتیجے کی توقع رکھنے والا، ایسا رویہ جس میں مشکلات کے باوجود امید قائم رہے، خوشگوار انجام کی توقع رکھنے والا
examples: She is optimistic about her chances of getting the job. The doctor was optimistic about the patient's recovery. Despite the setbacks, the team remained optimistic. He gave an optimistic forecast for next year's economy. The students are optimistic about their final results.

synonyms: Improve, Enhance, Perfect, Maximize, Refine, Streamline, Boost
englishMeaning: To make the best or most effective use of a situation, resource, or opportunity. To improve something so that it works as efficiently as possible. In technology, to adjust a system, design, or program to achieve maximum performance. To rearrange or fine-tune for the best possible result.
antonyms: Worsen, Reduce, Weaken, Hinder, Spoil, Minimize
sindhiMeaning: بهترين بڻائڻ، بهتر ڪرڻ، وڌ ۾ وڌ فائدو حاصل ڪرڻ، ڪنهن شي يا عمل کي تمام موثر بڻائڻ، ٽيڪنالاجي ۾ ڪنهن سسٽم يا پروگرام جي ڪارڪردگي بهتر ڪرڻ، بهترين نتيجي لاءِ ترتيب ڏيڻ
examples: The company is trying to optimize its production process. We must optimize our resources to reduce costs. Engineers worked hard to optimize the website's speed. Athletes optimize their performance through proper training and diet. The new software helps businesses optimize their workflow.
urduMeaning: بہترین بنانا، بہتر کرنا، زیادہ سے زیادہ فائدہ حاصل کرنا، کسی چیز یا عمل کو نہایت مؤثر بنانا، ٹیکنالوجی میں کسی نظام یا پروگرام کی کارکردگی بہتر کرنا، بہترین نتیجے کے لیے ترتیب دینا

sindhiMeaning: ڪڍي ڇڏڻ، عهدي تان هٽائڻ، زبردستي ڪڍڻ، ڌڪي ڪڍڻ، ڪنهن کي طاقت يا عهدي تان لاهي ڇڏڻ، قبضو هٽائڻ، ڪنهن جي جاءِ تي پاڻ قابض ٿيڻ
urduMeaning: نکالنا، عہدے سے ہٹانا، زبردستی نکالنا، باہر کرنا، کسی کو طاقت یا عہدے سے ہٹا دینا، قبضہ ختم کرنا، کسی کی جگہ خود قابض ہو جانا
examples: The party tried to oust the prime minister through a vote of no confidence. He was ousted from the club for breaking the rules. The young player ousted the senior captain from the team. Rebels managed to oust the dictator from power. The court has the authority to oust an unfit guardian.
englishMeaning: To remove someone forcibly from a position of power, office, or property. To drive out, expel, or dispossess. To take the place of another by force or authority. Often used in political, legal, or competitive contexts to describe sudden removal or replacement.
antonyms: Appoint, Install, Reinstate, Admit, Welcome, Restore
synonyms: Remove, Expel, Dismiss, Overthrow, Eject, Banish, Depose, Displace
Removed, Expelled, Dismissed, Overthrown, Deposed, Banished, Displaced
sindhiMeaning: ڪڍيل، عهدي تان لاٿل، زبردستي ڪڍيو ويل، ڌڪي ڪڍيو ويل، اهڙو شخص جنهن کي طاقت يا عهدي تان لاهي ڇڏيو ويو هجي، جنهن جي جاءِ تي ٻيو ڪو قابض ٿي ويو هجي
antonyms: Appointed, Installed, Reinstated, Restored, Welcomed
examples: The ousted leader fled the country to seek asylum. The ousted manager later started his own business. Several ousted ministers spoke against the government. The ousted king was never allowed to return. The ousted captain remained a loyal member of the team.
urduMeaning: نکالا گیا، عہدے سے ہٹایا گیا، زبردستی نکالا گیا، باہر کیا گیا، ایسا شخص جسے طاقت یا عہدے سے ہٹا دیا گیا ہو، جس کی جگہ کوئی دوسرا قابض ہو گیا ہو
englishMeaning: Removed forcibly from a position, office, or place. Driven out or expelled, often by political action, public pressure, or competition. Replaced by someone else against one's will. Used to describe leaders, officials, or persons who have lost their position through removal.

antonyms: Confined, Bedridden, Indoors, Inactive, Stationary, Housebound
urduMeaning: گھر سے باہر سرگرم، چلتا پھرتا، گھومتا پھرتا، صحتیاب ہو کر گھر سے باہر نکلنا، روزمرہ کے کاموں کے لیے باہر گھومنا، چاق چوبند ہو کر باہر آنا جانا
synonyms: Active, Mobile, Moving around, On the move, Travelling, Up and about
englishMeaning: Moving around outside, especially after being indoors due to illness or rest. Active and engaged in normal outdoor activities. Going from place to place rather than staying at home. Used to describe a person who is out walking, traveling, or going about daily life after recovery or during a busy day.
sindhiMeaning: گهر کان ٻاهر سرگرم، چرپر ۾، گهمندو ڦرندو، صحتياب ٿي گهر کان ٻاهر نڪرڻ، روزمره جي ڪمن لاءِ ٻاهر گهمڻ، چاق چوبند ٿي ٻاهر هلڻ چلڻ
examples: She is finally out and about after her long illness. We were out and about all day exploring the new city. My grandfather is still out and about at the age of eighty. He likes to be out and about on weekends. Despite the cold weather, people were out and about in the streets.

urduMeaning: مکمل، خالص، پورا پورا، بالکل، سراسر، ہر لحاظ سے، کامل، جس میں کوئی کمی یا شک نہ ہو، اندر باہر یکساں
englishMeaning: Complete, thorough, or absolute in nature. Used to emphasize that someone or something is exactly what is described, with no doubt or exception. Through and through. Used especially before nouns to stress the extreme or undeniable quality of a person, thing, or action.
synonyms: Complete, Total, Absolute, Utter, Thorough, Downright, Sheer, Unqualified
antonyms: Partial, Incomplete, Doubtful, Limited, Qualified, Half-hearted
sindhiMeaning: مڪمل، خالص، پورو پورو، بلڪل، سراسر، هر لحاظ کان، ڪامل، جنهن ۾ ڪابه گهٽتائي يا شڪ نه هجي، اندر ٻاهر هڪجهڙو
examples: He is an out and out liar and cannot be trusted. The match was an out and out victory for the home team. She is an out and out professional in her field. It was an out and out lie from beginning to end. The film turned out to be an out and out success at the box office.

synonyms: Blackout, Interruption, Stoppage, Breakdown, Failure, Shutdown, Disruption
sindhiMeaning: بندش، تعطل، بجلي  پاڻي يا انٽرنيٽ جي بندي جو وقفو، ڪنهن سهولت جو عارضي طور بند ٿيڻ، سسٽم جي ڪم نه ڪرڻ جو دور، خرابي سبب خدمت جو معطل ٿيڻ
antonyms: Service, Supply, Restoration, Continuation, Functioning
englishMeaning: A period when a service, especially the supply of electricity, water, or internet, is not available. A temporary interruption or failure in the normal operation of a system or utility. The act of being out of use due to technical or other reasons. Commonly used in the context of power, network, or communication breakdowns.
examples: A sudden power outage left the entire city in darkness. The internet outage disrupted business activities for hours. There was a brief water outage in the area this morning. The company apologized for the service outage. Engineers worked all night to fix the network outage.
urduMeaning: بندش، تعطل، بجلی  پانی یا انٹرنیٹ کی بندش کا وقفہ، کسی سہولت کا عارضی طور پر بند ہونا، نظام کے کام نہ کرنے کا دور، خرابی کے باعث خدمت کا معطل ہونا

examples: They traveled deep into the Australian outback on their adventure trip. Life in the outback can be tough and challenging. The outback is famous for its red soil and unique wildlife. He grew up on a cattle station in the outback. Tourists from around the world visit the outback every year.
synonyms: Bush, Wilderness, Backcountry, Hinterland, Remote area, Wilds
urduMeaning: آسٹریلیا کا دور دراز اور ویران اندرونی علاقہ، شہروں اور ساحلوں سے دور صحرائی اور جنگلی خطہ، اندرونی ملک کے غیر آباد میدان، ایسے علاقے جہاں آبادی بہت کم ہو اور سہولیات نہ ہوں، آسٹریلیا کے بیابانی خطے
englishMeaning: The remote, dry, and sparsely populated inland regions of Australia, far from cities and the coast. The vast wilderness area characterized by deserts, bushland, and isolated settlements. Used to refer to any wild and remote country area, especially in Australia. Often associated with adventure, ranching, and indigenous culture.
sindhiMeaning: آسٽريليا جو پري ۽ ويران علائقو، شهرن کان پري واريارو ۽ بياباني علائقو، اندرين ملڪ جا ويران ميدان، اهڙا علائقا جتي آبادي تمام گهٽ هجي ۽ ساوڪ نه هجي، آسٽريليا جا بياباني پٽ
antonyms: City, Urban area, Metropolis, Coast, Town

examples: The engineers studied the feasibility of building a bridge over the river. A feasibility report must be submitted before the project starts. The committee doubted the feasibility of the new education plan. We are conducting a feasibility study for the proposed solar power plant. The feasibility of the idea depends on the available budget.
englishMeaning: The state or quality of being possible, practical, or able to be done successfully. The likelihood that a plan, idea, or project can be carried out effectively. An assessment of whether something can be achieved given available resources, time, and conditions. Often used in business and engineering studies to evaluate proposed projects before implementation.
antonyms: Impracticality, Impossibility, Inviability, Unworkability
urduMeaning: ممکن ہونا، قابل عمل ہونا، کسی منصوبے کے عملی طور پر ممکن ہونے کی حالت، یہ جائزہ کہ کوئی کام ہو سکتا ہے یا نہیں، کسی تجویز کے قابل عمل ہونے کی کیفیت، امکانیت
synonyms: Practicality, Possibility, Viability, Workability, Practicability, Achievability
sindhiMeaning: ممڪن هجڻ، عمل ۾ اچڻ جي صلاحيت، ڪنهن منصوبي جي قابل عمل هجڻ جي حالت، اهو جائزو ته ڪو ڪم ٿي سگهي ٿو يا نه، ڪنهن رٿا جي عملي طور تي ٿي سگهڻ جي ڪيفيت، ممڪنيت

synonyms: Possible, Practical, Viable, Workable, Achievable, Realistic, Doable
antonyms: Impossible, Impractical, Unworkable, Unrealistic, Unachievable
sindhiMeaning: ممڪن، قابل عمل، عملي طور تي ٿي سگهڻ جوڳو، اهڙو منصوبو يا رٿا جيڪا حقيقت ۾ پوري ٿي سگهي، ڪارگر ۽ مناسب، اهڙو ڪم جيڪو موجوده حالتن ۾ ٿي سگهندو هجي
urduMeaning: ممکن، قابل عمل، عملی طور پر ہو سکنے والا، ایسا منصوبہ یا تجویز جو حقیقت میں پوری ہو سکے، کارگر اور مناسب، ایسا کام جو موجودہ حالات میں کیا جا سکے
examples: Is it feasible to complete this project within a month? The plan seems feasible if we get enough funding. Solar power is now a feasible alternative to conventional energy. We must find a feasible solution to the traffic problem. The proposal is feasible but requires careful planning.
englishMeaning: Capable of being done, accomplished, or carried out successfully. Possible to do easily or conveniently under the given circumstances. Likely to work or to be effective in practice. Reasonable and likely to succeed. Used for plans, ideas, solutions, or projects that can realistically be put into practice.

synonyms: Aigai, Ancient Macedonian capital, Archaeological site
sindhiMeaning: ورگينا، اتر يونان جو هڪ قديم شهر، جنهن کي اڳي ايگائي چيو ويندو هو، مقدونيا جي بادشاهت جي پهرين راڄڌاني، شاهي قبرن جي ڪري مشهور، خاص طور بادشاهه فلپ ٻئي جي قبر، يونيسڪو طرفان عالمي ورثو قرار ڏنل آثار قديمه وارو هنڌ
antonyms: Modern city, Contemporary settlement
englishMeaning: An ancient city in northern Greece, historically known as Aigai, which served as the first capital of the Kingdom of Macedonia. The site is famous for the royal tombs, including that believed to be of King Philip II, father of Alexander the Great. A UNESCO World Heritage Site renowned for its archaeological treasures and the symbol known as the Vergina Sun.
urduMeaning: ورجینا، شمالی یونان کا ایک قدیم شہر، جسے پہلے ایگائی کہا جاتا تھا، مقدونیہ کی سلطنت کا پہلا دار الحکومت، شاہی مقبروں کے باعث مشہور، خاص طور پر بادشاہ فلپ دوم کا مقبرہ، یونیسکو کی جانب سے عالمی ورثہ قرار دیا گیا آثار قدیمہ کا مقام
examples: Vergina is famous for the royal tombs of ancient Macedonian kings. The Vergina Sun is an important symbol of ancient Greek culture. Tourists visit Vergina to see the museum built around the royal tombs. The discovery of the tomb at Vergina was a major archaeological breakthrough. Vergina was once the capital of the Macedonian kingdom.

antonyms: Lengthy, Wordy, Verbose, Long-winded, Detailed, Rambling
synonyms: Brief, Short, Succinct, Terse, Compact, Pithy, To the point, Summary
urduMeaning: مختصر، جامع، تھوڑے میں بہت کچھ، صاف اور سیدھی بات، ایسی تحریر یا تقریر جو کم لفظوں میں مکمل بات بیان کرے، غیر ضروری تفصیل سے پاک، نقطے پر آنے والا
englishMeaning: Giving a lot of information clearly and in a few words. Brief but comprehensive in expression. Short, clear, and to the point. Free from unnecessary detail or wordiness. Used to describe writing, speech, statements, or explanations that convey meaning efficiently without losing essential information.
sindhiMeaning: مختصر، جامع، ٿوري ۾ گهڻو، صاف ۽ سڌي ڳالهه، اهڙي تحرير يا تقرير جيڪا ٿورن لفظن ۾ پوري ڳالهه بيان ڪري، اضافي تفصيل کان پاڪ، نقطي تي پهچڻ وارو
examples: Please give me a concise summary of the report. His speech was concise yet very powerful. The teacher praised the student for his concise answer. A concise definition is easier to remember than a long one. The book is a concise guide to modern grammar.

synonyms: Perfume Fragrance Aroma Scent Resin, Enrage Anger Infuriate Irritate Provoke
sindhiMeaning: لوبان، خوشبو ڏيندڙ ساڙڻ واري شيءِ, غصي ۾ آڻڻ/ ڪاوڙائڻ, عبادت يا رسم ۾ ساڙڻ لاءِ خوشبودار مواد, پاڪيزگي ۽ روحانيت جي نشاني, ڪنهن کي سخت ڪاوڙائڻ
antonyms: Calm Soothe Please Pacify, Stench Odor (unpleasant) Foul smell
examples: The temple was filled with the sweet smell of incense. She lit incense to create a peaceful atmosphere at home. His rude comments incensed the entire team. The decision to cancel the event incensed many people.
englishMeaning: To make someone very angry or enrage them. A substance that produces a pleasant smell when burned, often used in religious, spiritual, or cultural practices. A fragrant material made from plant resins, oils, or powders used in rituals. Symbol of purification, meditation, or spirituality. Something that creates a calming or sacred atmosphere. Emotionally, it can describe provoking strong anger when used as a verb.
urduMeaning: لوبان، بخور، خوشبودار جلانے والی چیز, غصہ دلانا، سخت ناراض کرنا, عبادات میں استعمال ہونے والا خوشبودار دھواں, روحانی سکون یا پاکیزگی کی علامت, کسی کو شدید غصہ دلانے کا عمل

sindhiMeaning: ملائڻ، الحاق ڪرڻ، ڳنڍڻ، شامل ڪرڻ، ڪنهن علائقي يا عمارت کي قانوني يا زوري طريقي سان ڪنهن وڏي يونٽ ۾ شامل ڪرڻ، اضافي عمارت يا حصو
englishMeaning: To officially add or attach a territory, building, or room to a larger existing one. To incorporate land or property into a bigger unit by legal or forceful means. An additional structure or section attached to a main building. To seize control of another country or territory and make it part of one's own state.
examples: The government moved to annex the disputed territory after years of negotiation. The hotel built an annex to accommodate more guests during the busy season. The country attempted to annex the neighboring region, which caused international outrage. The library's annex housed a rare book collection not available in the main building. The new annex was used as additional office space for the expanding company.
antonyms: Detach, Separate, Release, Surrender, Cede
urduMeaning: ملانا، الحاق کرنا، شامل کرنا، اضافی حصہ، قبضہ کرنا، کسی علاقے یا عمارت کو قانونی یا طاقت کے ذریعے کسی بڑے ملک یا ادارے میں شامل کر لینا
synonyms: Attach, Incorporate, Acquire, Append, Seize

examples: The annexation of the region triggered widespread international protests. Historical annexation often resulted in the suppression of local culture and language. He felt that the scandalous rumors would defile his family’s honorable name. No one should be allowed to defile such a sacred place of worship.

To spend the winter in a dormant or inactive state, as some animals do. It involves a significant drop in body temperature and metabolic rate to conserve energy. Figuratively, it can mean to remain inactive or in seclusion for an extended period.
examples: Bears typically hibernate in caves during the coldest months of the year. Some species of bats hibernate in clusters to maintain warmth. The software project had to hibernate for a few months due to a lack of funding. During the blizzard, many villagers chose to hibernate in their homes with plenty of food.

synonyms: Cluster, Crowd, Gather, Bunch, Throng, Congregate

examples: He dismissed the entire story as nothing but pure humbug. The old merchant was known to be a humbug who cheated his customers. 'Bah! Humbug!' shouted the character when asked about the holiday spirit. Don't listen to his excuses, it is all a load of humbug.

The researchers formulated a hypothesis to explain the unusual weather patterns. Our initial hypothesis was proven wrong after the first round of experiments. You must provide evidence to support your hypothesis during the science fair. A scientific hypothesis must be testable and falsifiable.

antonyms: Fact, Proof, Certainty, Reality, Truth
urduMeaning: مفروضہ، قیاس، گمان، فرضی نظریہ، تخمینہ، احتمال، تصور کنا

examples: Scientists hypothesize that the new drug will significantly reduce symptoms. Researchers often hypothesize about the long-term effects of climate change. It is difficult to hypothesize without having access to the primary data. She began to hypothesize why the ancient civilization suddenly disappeared.
sindhiMeaning: فرض ڪرڻ، قياس ڪرڻ، گمان ڪرڻ، انگ اٽڪل ڪرڻ، خيال آرائي ڪرڻ پيش ڪرڻ، نظريو قائم ڪرڻ
synonyms: Speculate, Theorize, Surmise, Suppose, Postulate

antonyms: Prove, Verify, Establish, Confirm, Demonstrate
