examples: The bird will regurgitate food for its babies to eat. Some students just regurgitate facts during exams without understanding them. I cannot digest milk and often regurgitate it. The speaker seemed to merely regurgitate political speech points. He felt so sick that he began to regurgitate his dinner.
urduMeaning: اگلنا، قے کرنا، الٹی کرنا، واپس نکالنا، نگلی ہوئی چیز کو منہ میں واپس لانا، بغیر سمجھے سنی سنائی باتوں کو دہرانے کا عمل
antonyms: Swallow, Digest, Ingest, Absorb, Compress, Retain, Understand

synonyms: Persistent, Determined, Stubborn, Resolute, Unyielding, Steadfast, Firm, Unwavering, Dogged
examples: The tenacious athlete refused to let her injury stop her from competing. You must be tenacious to succeed in this highly competitive industry. He holds a tenacious belief in the power of free speech. The lawyer made a tenacious defense of her client in court. We admired his tenacious grip on the slippery rope.
sindhiMeaning: ثابت قدم، پرعزم، پڪو، ارادي جو مضبوط، همت نه هارڻ وارو، ڏکيائين جي باوجود ڪم ۾ لڳل رهڻ ۽ هار نه مڃڻ واري خاصيت
urduMeaning: ثابت قدم، پرعزم، پکا، مضبوط، ضدی، ڈٹا رہنے والا، کسی چیز کو مضبوطی سے پکڑنے یا مشکلات کے باوجود ہار نہ ماننے والی طبعیت
antonyms: Irresolute, Yielding, Weak, Surrendering, Wavering, Fickle, Quitting
englishMeaning: Tending to keep a firm hold of something or clinging closely. It describes a person who is very determined, persistent, and unwilling to give up despite difficulties. It illustrates a strong will and unyielding nature.

synonyms: Selflessness, Compassion, Generosity, Philanthropy, Benevolence, Charity, Kindness
examples: Her entire life was a testament to selfless altruism. Many charitable organizations rely on the altruism of their donors. True altruism means helping others without wanting anything in return. The millionaire showed great altruism by giving away his fortune. Animals sometimes exhibit altruism toward members of their group.
englishMeaning: The selfless concern for the well-being and happiness of others. It involves acting out of a desire to help people, often at one's own expense. This moral practice emphasizes kindness, generosity, and compassion without expecting anything in return.
sindhiMeaning: ايثار، قرباني، بنا غرض جي خدمت، ٻين جو ڀلو چاهڻ، همدردي، پنهنجي ذاتي فائدي جي پرواهه ڪرڻ کانسواءِ ٻين جي ڀلائي ۽ مدد ڪرڻ جو جذبو
antonyms: Selfishness, Greed, Egoism, Self-centeredness, Narcissism, Avarice
urduMeaning: ایثار، قربانی، بے لوث خدمت، ہمدردی، دوسروں کی بھلائی کا جذبہ، بغیر کسی ذاتی غرض کے دوسروں کی مدد اور خوشی کے لیے کام کرنے کی خوبی

synonyms: Sleeplessness, Wakefulness, Restlessness, Sleep Disorder, Indisposition
examples: She has been taking medication to treat her severe insomnia. Stress and caffeine are two common causes of chronic insomnia. Suffering from insomnia made him irritable during the working hours. He tried meditating every night to find relief from his insomnia. The doctor suggested reading a book before bed to fight insomnia.
sindhiMeaning: اوجاڳو، ننڊ نه اچڻ جي بيماري، بي خوابي، رات جو ننڊ نه پون يا ننڊ ڦٽي وڃڻ واري طبي حالت جنهن سان جسماني ٿڪاوٽ پيدا ٿئي ٿي
urduMeaning: بے خوابی، نیند نہ آنے کی بیماری، جاگتے رہنا، رات بیداری، رات کو نیند نہ آنے یا بار بار آنکھ کھل جانے کی طبی حالت جسے انسان کو شدید تھکاوٹ محسوس ہوتی ہے
antonyms: Sleepiness, Somnolence, Lethargy, Rest, Drowsiness, Slumber
englishMeaning: A sleep disorder characterized by a persistent difficulty in falling asleep or staying asleep. It often leads to waking up feeling unrefreshed and feeling extremely tired during the day. It is usually caused by stress, anxiety, or underlying health issues.

examples: His severe asthma prevents him from playing intense sports in winter. The pollution in the city triggered a sudden asthma attack. She always carries an inhaler to manage her childhood asthma. Children with asthma need to strictly avoid dusty environments. Cold weather can severely worsen the symptoms of asthma.
urduMeaning: دمہ، سانس کی بیماری، تنگی تنفس، ایک دائمی بیماری جس میں سانس کی نالیاں تنگ اور سوج جاتی ہیں جس سے سانس لینے میں دشواری ہوتی ہے
synonyms: Breathlessness, Wheezing, Respiratory Disorder, Bronchospasm, Shortness Of Breath, Lung Disease
englishMeaning: A chronic respiratory condition that causes the airways to narrow, swell, and produce extra mucus. It leads to difficulty in breathing, wheezing, coughing, and shortness of breath. The severity of the condition can vary greatly from person to person.
antonyms: Healthy Lungs, Normal Breathing, Respiratory Health, Unrestricted Airflow, Clear Airways
sindhiMeaning: دم، ساهه جي بيماري، دمہ، هوا جي نالين ۾ سوڄ ۽ تنگي سبب ساهه جي تڪليف ٿيڻ، جنهن سان کنگهه ۽ سهڪو ٿيندو آهي
اوري، خسرو، رت جا داڻا، هڪ متعدي وائرس واري بيماري جنهن ۾ بخار، کنگهه ۽ سڄي جسم تي ڳاڙها داڻا نڪري پوندا آهن
examples: The child developed a high fever and the characteristic rash of measles. Many countries have successfully eradicated measles through mass vaccination programs. Measles is highly contagious and spreads easily through coughing and sneezing. Before the vaccine, measles was a very common childhood illness. The doctor immediately isolated the patient suspected of having measles.
synonyms: Rubeola, Viral Infection, Infectious Disease, Rash, Contagion, Childhood Illness
antonyms: Complete Immunity, Good Health, Wellness, Disease-free State, Immunity
urduMeaning: خسرہ، سرخے، ایک انتہائی متعدی وائرل بیماری، جس میں تیز بخار کے ساتھ جسم پر سرخ دانے اور خارش نکل آتی ہے جو عموماً بچوں کو متاثر کرتی ہے
englishMeaning: A highly contagious infectious disease caused by a virus. It is characterized by fever, a runny nose, cough, and a widespread red rash on the skin. It primarily affects children but can be prevented through vaccination.

synonyms: Spasm, Contraction, Twinge, Pang, Kink, Convulsion, Stitch
examples: He suffered a painful cramp in his leg during the marathon. Swimmers are advised not to eat right before swimming to avoid a stomach cramp. The cold water gave her a sudden muscle cramp. Dehydration is known to cause a severe muscle cramp. She massaged her foot to relieve the debilitating cramp.
sindhiMeaning: سٽ، وٽ، تڪليف ده ڇڪتائي، مشڪن جو سور، جسم جي مشڪن يا پٺن ۾ اوچتو پيدا ٿيندڙ تڪليف ده ڇڪتاڻ جنهن ڪري حرڪت ڏکي ٿي وڃي
englishMeaning: A sudden, painful, and involuntary contraction of one or more muscles. It often occurs after intense exercise, dehydration, or keeping a muscle in the same position for a long time. It restricts movement temporarily until the muscle relaxes.
urduMeaning: اکڑن، کھنچاؤ، پٹھوں کا درد، اینٹھن، پٹھوں کا اچانک اور تکلیف دہ طور پر سکڑ جانا، جس سے حرکت کرنے میں عارضی تکلیف ہوتی ہے
antonyms: Relaxation, Comfort, Relief, Ease, Flexibility, Stretching

urduMeaning: غذائی قلت، ناقص خوراک، کمزوری، سوکھا پن، مناسب متوازن خوراک کی کمی یا زیادتی کے باعث پیدا ہونے والی کمزوری اور جسمانی خرابی کی حالت
englishMeaning: A condition resulting from an unbalanced diet in which certain nutrients are lacking, in excess, or in the wrong proportions. It can lead to poor health, weight loss, stunted growth, and weakness. It affects both physical and mental development.
antonyms: Nourishment, Proper Nutrition, Healthy Diet, Well-fed Condition, Sustenance, Satiety
examples: Millions of children in the famine-struck region suffer from severe malnutrition. The hospital treated the rescued animals for dehydration and malnutrition. A poor diet consisting only of junk food can lead to malnutrition. Educating mothers about balanced diets helped reduce child malnutrition. Prolonged malnutrition severely stunted the physical growth of the orphans.
synonyms: Undernourishment, Starvation, Diet Deficiency, Emaciation, Famine, Nutritional Deficit
sindhiMeaning: غذائي قلت، ناقص خوراڪ، ڪمزوري، کاڌي جي کوٽ، جسم کي مناسب ۽ متوازن خوراڪ نه ملڻ جي ڪري پيدا ٿيندڙ ڪمزوري ۽ بيماري واري حالت

examples: Dyslexia makes it incredibly challenging for him to spell words correctly. The teacher used special learning methods to assist students with dyslexia. Despite her dyslexia, she became a highly successful and prolific writer. Early intervention can greatly improve reading skills in children with dyslexia. Dyslexia has absolutely nothing to do with a person's level of intelligence.
synonyms: Learning Disorder, Word Blindness, Reading Difficulty, Learning Disability, Cognitive Condition, Processing Problem
antonyms: High Literacy, Reading Fluency, Hyperlexia, Excellent Comprehension, Spelling Proficiency
urduMeaning: ڈسلیکسیا، پڑھنے لکھنے کی دشواری، حروف کی پہچان کا مسئلہ، ایک ذہنی یا اعصابی حالت جس میں حروف تہجی کو سمجھنے اور پڑھنے لکھنے میں دقت پیش آتی ہے مگر اسکا تعلق ذہانت سے نہیں ہوتا
englishMeaning: A specific learning difficulty that primarily affects reading, spelling, and writing skills. It is a neurological difference that causes difficulty in processing language and recognizing word patterns. It does not affect a person's general intelligence.
sindhiMeaning: پڙهڻ ۽ لکڻ جي معذوري، لفظن کي سڃاڻڻ جي تڪليف، هڪ دماغي يا اعصابي حالت جنهن ۾ ماڻهوءَ کي اکرن سڃاڻڻ ۽ لکڻ پڙهڻ ۾ ڏکيائي پيش اچي ٿي پر اهو ذهانت جو مسئلو ناهي

englishMeaning: A medical condition characterized by a deficiency of red blood cells or hemoglobin in the blood. It results in reduced oxygen flow to the body's organs, causing symptoms like fatigue, paleness, and weakness. It is often caused by an iron deficiency.
urduMeaning: خون کی کمی، انیمیا، جسم میں خون کے سرخ خلیوں یا ہیموگلوبن کی غیر معمولی کمی، جس کی وجہ سے مریض کو تھکاوٹ اور کمزوری محسوس ہوتی ہے
antonyms: Vitality, High Hemoglobin, Robustness, Full-bloodedness, Good Health, Vigor
sindhiMeaning: رت جي کوٽ، انيميا، پيلاڻ، جسم ۾ رت جي ڳاڙهن جزن يا هيموگلوبن جي کوٽ، جنهن سبب ماڻهو ٿڪاوٽ ۽ ڪمزوري جو شڪار ٿي پوندو آهي
synonyms: Blood Deficiency, Iron Deficiency, Weakness, Paleness, Hemoglobin Deficiency, Blood Disorder
examples: Her constant fatigue and paleness were eventually diagnosed as severe anaemia. Eating iron-rich foods like spinach and liver can help prevent anaemia. The doctor prescribed a daily iron supplement to treat his anaemia. Heavy blood loss during the surgery resulted in temporary anaemia. Pregnant women are routinely checked and tested for signs of anaemia.

urduMeaning: گٹھیا، جوڑوں کا درد، وجع المفاصل، بادی، جوڑوں، پٹھوں یا ہڈیوں کی سوجن اور درد کی ایک عام حالت جس میں حرکت کرنے میں تکلیف ہوتی ہے
synonyms: Joint Pain, Arthritis, Inflammation, Joint Stiffness, Osteoarthritis, Gout
examples: The cold, damp weather always causes a sharp flare-up of his rheumatism. My grandmother takes special medication daily to cope with her rheumatism. Rheumatism makes his joints overly stiff and remarkably painful in the mornings. Exercise and physical therapy greatly help manage the symptoms of rheumatism. He wore thick woolen clothing to stop the cold from aggravating his rheumatism.
englishMeaning: A non-specific medical term used to describe any disease or painful condition of the joints, muscles, or fibrous tissue. It is characterized by inflammation, stiffness, and pain in the affected areas. It commonly refers to forms of arthritis and autoimmune conditions.
sindhiMeaning: سنڌن جو سور، واءُ، گٺيا، جوڙن جو درد، سنڌن يا پٺن ۾ سور ۽ سڄڻ جي حالت، جنهن سان اٿڻ ويهڻ ۽ هلڻ ۾ ڏکيائي ٿيندي آهي
antonyms: Joint Flexibility, Nimbleness, Suppleness, Mobility, Agility, Healthy Joints

englishMeaning: A neurological disorder marked by sudden, recurrent episodes of sensory disturbance, loss of consciousness, or convulsions. It is associated with abnormal electrical activity in the brain. The seizures vary in intensity and frequency among affected individuals.
synonyms: Seizures, Convulsions, Neurological Disorder, Fits, Falling Sickness, Spasms
examples: She takes medication to successfully control the seizures caused by her epilepsy. The flashing strobe lights at the concert triggered his epilepsy. Epilepsy is a complex neurological disorder that requires careful medical management. Children diagnosed with epilepsy can still lead perfectly normal and active lives. He wears a medical alert bracelet in case an attack of epilepsy occurs.
urduMeaning: مرگی، دورہ پڑنا، غشی، ایک اعصابی بیماری جس میں دماغی خلیوں کی غیر معمولی برقی سرگرمی کی وجہ سے مریض کو بار بار دورے پڑتے ہیں اور بے ہوشی طاری ہو سکتی ہے
sindhiMeaning: مرگهي، دورو پوڻ، غشي، دماغ ۾ بجلي جي غير معمولي سرگرمي جي ڪري پيدا ٿيندڙ اعصابي بيماري، جنهن ۾ ماڻهوءَ کي اوچتو دورا پوندا آهن
antonyms: Neurological Stability, Uninterrupted Consciousness, Health, Normalcy, Composure, Stillness

synonyms: Head Trauma, Brain Injury, Head Knock, Shock, Stun, Blow
englishMeaning: A mild traumatic brain injury caused by a bump, blow, or jolt to the head. It alters the way the brain functions temporarily, leading to headaches, confusion, dizziness, and memory problems. Rest and observation are the primary treatments.
urduMeaning: دماغی چوٹ، سر کی چوٹ، دماغی صدمہ، چکر آنا، سر پر زور دار چوٹ لگنے کی وجہ سے دماغ کو پہنچنے والا عارضی نقصان، جس سے چکر اور سردرد ہو سکتا ہے
examples: The football player sustained a severe concussion after a clash of heads. You should stay awake and be monitored closely if you have a concussion. Symptoms of a concussion can include terrible headaches, dizziness, and extreme nausea. She wore a helmet to protect herself from a potential concussion while cycling. The doctors told him to heavily limit screen time to recover from the concussion.
sindhiMeaning: دماغي ڌڪ، سري جو ڌڪ، دماغ جو هلجي وڃڻ، مٿي ۾ زوردار ڌڪ يا ڌوٻو لڳڻ سبب دماغ جي ڪم ڪرڻ ۾ پيدا ٿيندڙ عارضي خلل ۽ تڪليف جو احساس
antonyms: Mental Clarity, Brain Health, Cognitive Normalcy, Lucidity, Invulnerability, Safety

urduMeaning: بھوک کا مر جانا، غذا سے جان بوجھ کر پرہیز، اینوریکسیا، وزن بڑھنے کے خوف سے کھانا پینا چھوڑ دینے کی نفسیاتی اور جسمانی بیماری، جس سے انسان انتہائی کمزور ہو جاتا ہے
synonyms: Eating Disorder, Starvation, Appetite Loss, Malnourishment, Fasting, Emaciation
sindhiMeaning: بک جو مري وڃڻ، کائڻ پيئڻ ڇڏي ڏيڻ جي بيماري، وزن وڌڻ جي خوف سبب گهٽ کائڻ جي نفسياتي حالت جنهن ڪري انسان حد کان وڌيڪ ڪمزور ٿي ويندو آهي
examples: Anorexia is a dangerous eating disorder that primarily affects young women. She successfully recovered from anorexia after months of intense psychological therapy. People suffering from anorexia often have a completely distorted image of their bodies. The clinic specializes in treating eating disorders like bulimia and anorexia. Extreme weight loss and a refusal to eat are main symptoms of anorexia.
englishMeaning: An eating disorder characterized by an abnormally low body weight, an intense fear of gaining weight, and a distorted perception of weight. People with this condition often severely restrict their food intake. It requires medical and psychological treatment for recovery.
antonyms: Healthy Appetite, Hearty Eating, Gluttony, Overeating, Nourishment, Corpulence

synonyms: Absurd, Ridiculous, Preposterous, Foolish, Laughable, Bizarre, Nonsensical, Crazy
sindhiMeaning: بيکاري، کل جوڳو، احمقانه، واهيات، اهڙي ڳالهه يا حقيقت جيڪا ايتري غير معقول ۽ بيوقوفيءَ تي ٻڌل هجي جو کل اچي وڃي يا اها مذاق لڳي
examples: It was completely ludicrous to suggest that we could finish the project in one day. He looked absolutely ludicrous wearing that gigantic, brightly colored hat. The new company policy imposing a dress code for remote workers is ludicrous. They charged a ludicrous amount of money for a small cup of coffee. The explanation she provided for being late was frankly ludicrous.
urduMeaning: مضحکہ خیز، بے ہودہ، احمقانہ، ہنسنے کے قابل، کوئی ایسی بات یا صورتحال جو اتنی بے وقوفانہ اور غیر معقول ہو کہ اس پر ہنسی آ جائے
englishMeaning: Something that is so foolish, unreasonable, or out of place as to be amusing or completely ridiculous. It describes actions, ideas, or situations that defy logic and provoke mocking laughter. It represents ultimate absurdity.
antonyms: Reasonable, Sensible, Logical, Serious, Practical, Rational, Sound

examples: His reckless driving eventually resulted in a terrible and costly accident. It is reckless to make large financial investments without doing proper research. The company showed a reckless disregard for the safety of its employees. She deeply regretted her reckless decision to quit her job without a backup plan. Reckless behavior on the mountain can easily endanger the lives of other climbers.
synonyms: Careless, Rash, Irresponsible, Hasty, Thoughtless, Foolhardy, Imprudent, Daring
antonyms: Cautious, Careful, Prudent, Thoughtful, Responsible, Safe, Mindful
urduMeaning: لاپرواہ، بے باک، غیر محتاط، عاقبت نا اندیش، نتائج کی پرواہ کیے بغیر جلدی اور دلیری سے کام کرنے والا، خطرے کو نظر انداز کرنے والا رویہ
sindhiMeaning: لاپرواهه، بي ڌيان، نتيجن جي پرواهه نه ڪندڙ، اٻهرو، انجام کان بي پرواهه ٿي جلدبازي ۽ خطري سان ڀريل قدم کڻڻ واري خاصيت يا روين
englishMeaning: Acting or doing something without thinking or caring about the potential consequences of the action. It describes behavior that is rash, careless, and dangerous to oneself or others. It shows a complete disregard for safety precautions.

sindhiMeaning: ڌاتوءَ جو ڪچرو، ٻارڻ جي رک، گند، گپ، برائي ڪرڻ، لوهه يا ڌاتو ڳارڻ جي عمل ۾ نڪري ويندڙ بيڪار مادو، ڪنهن تي سخت تنقيد ڪرڻ يا گلا ڪرڻ
englishMeaning: Stony waste matter separated from metals during the smelting or refining of ore. In a colloquial sense, it is used to describe harsh criticism or verbal abuse. It also broadly denotes worthless matter left over from a process.
antonyms: Pure Metal, Jewel, Treasure, Praise, Compliment, Commend, Flatter, Support
synonyms: Refuse, Scum, Waste, Dross, Criticize, Insult, Mock, Disparage, Trash
urduMeaning: دھات کا فضلہ، کچ دھات کی گندگی، کوئلے کی راکھ، سخت تنقید کرنا، دھات پگھلانے کے عمل میں بچ جانے والا کچرا، یا عام بول چال میں کسی کی سخت برائی کرنا
examples: The factory produced mountains of black slag during the intensive smelting process. In the interview, she refused to publicly slag off her former employers. The heavy slag is carefully separated from the pure molten metal. It is not professional to constantly slag your coworkers behind their backs. The road was reinforced using layers of cooling industrial slag.

The furnace required constant monitoring to prevent improper slagging of the metal. She was severely reprimanded for openly slagging off the company's new policies. The continuous slagging severely affected the morale of the entire office team. Slagging off the competition might make you look extremely desperate. Proper slagging ensures that the extracted iron is incredibly pure.
synonyms: Criticizing, Mocking, Insulting, Bad-mouthing, Disparaging, Ridiculing, Trash-talking
englishMeaning: The process of producing stony waste from metals, or the accumulation of slag. In informal use, it means severely criticizing, mocking, or verbally attacking someone. It conveys continuous disparagement or ridicule.
sindhiMeaning: بي عزتي ڪرڻ، تنقيد ڪرڻ، چٿرون ڪرڻ، سخت گلا ڪرڻ، ڌاتوءَ مان گند ڪڍڻ جو عمل، ڪنهن ماڻهوءَ تي گهري تنقيد ۽ خوار ڪرڻ وارو عمل
antonyms: Praising, Complimenting, Flattering, Commending, Supporting, Encouraging, Respecting
urduMeaning: کچرا نکالنے کا عمل، پھبکیر، سخت نکتہ چینی، مذاق اڑانا، تنقید، کسی شخص کی لگاتار اور شدید انداز میں برائی، نکتہ چینی یا مذاق اڑانے کا عمل

synonyms: Extortionate, Exorbitant, Outrageous, Excessive, Unreasonable, Greedy, Exploitative
urduMeaning: سود خوری سے متعلق، بھاری سود کا، سود در سود، ایسا مالی لین دین یا شخصی رویہ جس میں ناجائز اور بہت زیادہ سود وصول کر کے منافع کمایا جائے
examples: The loan shark charged usurious interest rates that trapped people in debt forever. The new financial regulations strictly prohibit banks from imposing usurious fees. They were forced to blindly accept the usurious terms because they were desperate. Legal action was rightfully taken against the company for its usurious lending practices. Usurious contracts exploit vulnerable individuals during times of financial crisis.
englishMeaning: Pertaining to the practice of lending money at unreasonably high or illegally exorbitant rates of interest. It describes financial transactions or individuals that exploit borrowers for excessive profit. It demonstrates extreme greed and financial exploitation.
sindhiMeaning: وياج خوري، ڳرو وياج، ناجائز منافعو، پئسن جي ڏيتي ليتي ۾ تمام گهڻو ۽ غيرقانوني حد تائين وياج وٺڻ واري عمل ۽ روين کي ظاهر ڪري ٿو
antonyms: Fair, Reasonable, Just, Equitable, Moderate, Cheap, Generous

englishMeaning: Cancel or postpone the punishment of someone, especially someone condemned to death. It also means a temporary relief or rest from something unpleasant or challenging. It gives someone extra time to find a solution or enjoy a brief break from hardship.
antonyms: Punishment, Conviction, Penalty, Condemnation, Continuation, Execution, Aggravation
urduMeaning: سزا میں تاخیر، مہلت، عارضی راحت، پناہ، موت یا کسی سخت سزا کو عارضی طور پر ٹال دینا، یا کسی مشکل وقت اور پریشانی سے ملنے والی تھوڑی دیر کی آزادی
synonyms: Respite, Delay, Adjournment, Pardon, Postponement, Relief, Amnesty, Break
examples: The rain offered a brief but welcome reprieve from the extremely sweltering heat. The condemned prisoner was remarkably granted a last-minute reprieve by the governor. We have a temporary reprieve before the next large project officially begins. The medicine provided a quick reprieve from his nagging back pain. The sudden cancellation of the exam was a wonderful reprieve for the busy students.
sindhiMeaning: سزا ۾ مهلت، معافي، ملتوي ڪرڻ، عارضي سک، ڪنهن مجرم جي سزا روڪڻ يا مهلت ڏيڻ، خراب حالتن يا تڪليف کان ملندڙ ٿوري دير جو آرام ۽ راحت

antonyms: Unmixed Ingredient, Element, Truth, Fact, Reality, Certainty
englishMeaning: A mixture of various ingredients or elements. It can be a strange or unusual drink or soup made by mixing multiple things. Figuratively, it refers to an elaborate story, plan, or excuse that has been invented to deceive someone.
urduMeaning: آمیزہ، مرکب، من گھڑت کہانی، بہانہ، مختلف چیزوں کو ملا کر بنائی گئی مشروب یا دوائی، یا دھوکہ دینے کے لیے گھڑی گئی کوئی جھوٹی کہانی اور منصوبہ
sindhiMeaning: آريز، ملاوت، من گهڙت ڪهاڻي، ٺاهه، مختلف شين جي ملاوٽ سان ٺهيل مشروب يا دوا، يا ڪنهن کي دوکو ڏيڻ لاءِ سوچي سمجهي ٺاهيل ڪوڙي آکاڻي
examples: She drank a strange herbal concoction to help cure her persistent cold. The bartender served a fiery green concoction that smelled of strong mint. His ridiculous excuse was nothing more than a poorly planned verbal concoction. The chef's newest culinary concoction is proving incredibly popular with the guests. I poured the strange concoction down the drain because it tasted awful.
synonyms: Mixture, Blend, Brew, Preparation, Fabrication, Invention, Tale, Brew, Combo

sindhiMeaning: تيار ڪرڻ، گڏ ڪرڻ، ڳنڍي جوڙي ٺاهڻ، من گهڙت ڳالهه ٺاهڻ، مختلف شيون ملائي خوراڪ يا پيئڻ جي شيءِ ٺاهڻ، يا دوکو ڏيڻ لاءِ ڪا ڪوڙي ڳالهه يا منصوبو جوڙڻ
antonyms: Destroy, Demolish, Tell Truth, Replicate, Ruin, Dismantle, Copy
englishMeaning: To make a dish or meal by combining various ingredients in an original way. It also means to create or invent a story, excuse, or plan, usually to deceive someone or avoid punishment. It suggests using imagination and craftiness to fabricate something.
urduMeaning: بنانا، ترکیب دینا، گھڑنا، جھوٹا بہانہ بنانا، مختلف اجزاء کو ملا کر کوئی نئی چیز تیار کرنا، یا لوگوں کو بیوقوف بنانے کے لیے کوئی جھوٹی ترکیب یا کہانی بنانا
examples: We had to quickly concoct a reasonable excuse for being so incredibly late. He managed to concoct a delicious meal using only the leftover ingredients. The criminals tried to concoct a clever scheme to rob the downtown bank. The children excitedly decided to concoct a magical potion in their backyard. The imaginative writer could effortlessly concoct thrilling stories about space adventures.
synonyms: Invent, Fabricate, Make Up, Create, Formulate, Devise, Hatch, Prepare

antonyms: Migration, Relocation, Departure, Flight, Exodus, Journey, Permanent Residence
urduMeaning: عارضی قیام، پڑاؤ، کچھ دیر کا ٹھہراؤ، سفر کے دوران کسی جگہ پر عارضی طور پر قیام کرنا یا ٹھہرنا، جسے مستقل رہائش کی بجائے مختصر دورانیہ سمجھا جائے
englishMeaning: A temporary stay at a place away from one's home. It refers to a brief period of living or residing in a specific location for travel, work, or resting. It marks a short-term visit rather than a permanent settlement.
sindhiMeaning: عارضي قيام، ٿوري وقت لاءِ ٽڪڻ، مسافري دوران ترسڻ، سفر دوران ڪنهن هنڌ هلي عارضي طور رهڻ، جنهن جو مقصد مستقل رهائش جي جاءِ تي ٿورو وقت گذارڻ هجي
examples: My brief sojourn in the picturesque village completely refreshed my weary spirit. After a short sojourn in Japan, he vividly wrote a famous travel book. Their lovely summer sojourn at the lake house was filled with pure joy. Her delightful Parisian sojourn ended quite abruptly due to a family emergency. He took a restful sojourn to the mountains to write his deeply emotional novel.
synonyms: Stay, Visit, Stopover, Vacation, Holiday, Break, Rest, Residency
Credible, Reasonable, Probable, Believable, Logical, Likely, Persuasive, Rational
englishMeaning: Seeming reasonable, probable, or likely to be true. It describes an argument, statement, or excuse that is convincingly presented and makes logical sense. It indicates something that can be believed, although it may not necessarily be proven.
examples: The detective urgently needed a plausible explanation for the suspect's sudden disappearance. Her bold excuse for missing the important meeting simply wasn't very plausible. It seems completely plausible that the heavy rain caused the terrible accident. He presented a plausible business plan that easily impressed the wealthy investors. A plausible theory must be fully supported by solid and undeniable evidence.
sindhiMeaning: يقين جوڳو، قابل اعتبار، معقول، ظاهري طرح سچو لڳندڙ، ڪا اهڙي ڳالهه، دليل يا بهانو جيڪو ٻڌڻ ۾ سچو لڳي ۽ جنهن تي آسانيءَ سان اعتبار ڪري سگهجي
antonyms: Implausible, Unlikely, Impossible, Unbelievable, Absurd, Irrational
urduMeaning: قرین قیاس، قابلِ اعتبار، بظاہر درست، معقول، کوئی ایسا عذر، دلیل یا بیان جو سننے میں سچا اور منطقی لگے، جسے بآسانی تسلیم کیا جا سکے
اچانک گراوٹ، مندی، مندی کا رجحان، ڈھلک کر بیٹھنا، قیمتوں، تجارت یا معیشت میں اچانک بڑی کمی آنا، تھکاوٹ یا مایوسی کی حالت میں نڈھال ہو کر گرنا یا بیٹھ جانا
antonyms: Rise, Boom, Ascent, Surge, Increase, Growth, Improvement, Recovery
synonyms: Decline, Drop, Crash, Tumble, Collapse, Plunge, Deteriorate, Fall
englishMeaning: A sudden or severe fall in prices, values, or sales. It also means to sit, lean, or fall heavily and limply, often due to exhaustion or despair. It denotes a rapid deterioration in economic conditions or personal posture.
sindhiMeaning: ڪاروباري مندي، اوچتو ڪِري پوڻ، اگهه ڪرڻ، لڙڪي ويهڻ، واپار يا شين جي قيمتن ۾ اوچتو وڏي گهٽتائي اچڻ، ٿڪ يا مايوسيءَ سبب ڪامپو ۽ جهڪي ويهڻ
examples: The company experienced a severe financial slump during the last business quarter. He dragged himself to the couch and allowed his tired body to slump heavily. The sudden slump in housing prices worried many independent real estate investors. Players often experience a massive slump in performance during a long, grueling season. She tends to slump her shoulders forward whenever she feels sad or defeated.

synonyms: Dash, Rush, Sprint, Shoot, Fly, Bound, Arrow, Missile, Projectile
englishMeaning: A small pointed missile that can be thrown or fired. As an action, it means to move or run somewhere suddenly and rapidly. It illustrates a sudden, quick, and sharp movement across a short distance.
examples: She suddenly watched a small rabbit dart quickly across the narrow road. He threw a pointed dart perfectly into the central bullseye of the heavy board. The suspicious guard saw a dark shadow dart stealthily behind the large building. Whenever the heavy doorbell rings, my anxious cat will dart under the old bed. He cast a sharp, angry dart with his eyes towards his noisy neighbors.
urduMeaning: نیزہ، تیر، چھوٹی برچھی، تیزی سے بھاگنا، اڑان بھرنا، ایک چھوٹا نوک دار ہتھیار جو پھینکا جائے، یا اچانک اور انتہائی تیز رفتاری سے کسی طرف جھپٹنا یا حرکت کرنا
sindhiMeaning: ننڍو تير، ڀالو، تيزيءَ سان نڪري وڃڻ، تکو اڏامڻ، هڪ ننڍو نوڪدار هٿيار جنهن کي اڇلايو وڃي، يا اوچتو ئي تمام تيزيءَ سان ڪنهن طرف ڊوڙي يا هلي وڃڻ
antonyms: Dawdle, Stroll, Amble, Walk, Creep, Linger, Snail, Delay

sindhiMeaning: پڇتاءُ ڪرڻ، افسوس ڪرڻ، ارمان ڪرڻ، ڏک ٿيڻ، پنهنجي ڪنهن پراڻي غلطي يا عمل تي سخت پڇتاءُ ۽ ڏک محسوس ڪرڻ، اها تمنا ڪرڻ ته ڪاش ائين نه ٿئي ها
antonyms: Rejoice, Celebrate, Praise, Enjoy, Delight, Be Glad, Appreciate
synonyms: Regret, Lament, Mourn, Repent, Deplore, Grieve, Sorrow, Bemoan
englishMeaning: To bitterly regret something one has done or allowed to happen. It involves a feeling of deep sorrow, repentance, and wishing that a past situation had been different. It denotes carrying a burden of remorse for a past mistake.
urduMeaning: پچھتانا، افسوس کرنا، ندامت، ملال کرنا، کسی گزشتہ عمل یا غلطی پر گہرا افسوس اور پچھتاوا محسوس کرنا اور یہ چاہنا کہ کاش وہ کام نہ کیا ہوتا
examples: He will certainly rue the day he arrogantly insulted his best friend. I deeply rue my hasty decision to quit that excellent job without a plan. You will live to rue this deeply tragic and foolish mistake. She came to bitterly rue the missed opportunity to travel the entire world. They secretly rue the harsh, unforgiving words spoken in the extreme heat of anger.

synonyms: Anger, Resentment, Outrage, Fury, Wrath, Annoyance, Displeasure, Irritation
urduMeaning: غصہ، خفگی، طیش، برہمی، کسی نامناسب، غیر منصفانہ یا توہین آمیز سلوک پر پیدا ہونے والا غصہ اور خفگی، حق تلفی پر محسوس ہونے والا شدید رنج
examples: Her sheer indignance at being rudely ignored was entirely visible on her flushed face. The massive crowd expressed growing indignance over the new, incredibly unfair tax laws. He wrote intensely about his fierce indignance regarding global human rights violations. The customer stormed out of the bright store in a huff of pure indignance. An undeniable feeling of deep indignance fueled their passionate and vocal protests.
sindhiMeaning: ڪاوڙ، ناراضگي، ڪروڌ، غصو، ڪنهن اڻبرابري يا ناانصافي واري رويي سبب پيدا ٿيندڙ شديد ڪاوڙ ۽ بيزاري جنهن ۾ ماڻهو پنهنجي عزت مجروح ٿيندي محسوس ڪري
englishMeaning: Anger or annoyance provoked by what is perceived as unfair treatment. It is a feeling of righteous frustration when one encounters injustice, disrespect, or wrongful accusation. It represents an offended sense of dignity or justice.
antonyms: Delight, Pleasure, Calmness, Satisfaction, Contentment, Happiness, Joy, Approval

englishMeaning: A sculpture of a person's head, shoulders, and chest. It also refers to a period of economic difficulty, a police raid, or the act of breaking something. To break, smash, or arrest someone.
synonyms: Sculpture, Statue, Raid, Arrest, Break, Shatter, Failure, Flop
examples: A beautifully carved marble bust of the famous emperor sits elegantly in the library. The police executed a massive drug bust at the abandoned coastal warehouse. During the painful economic bust, many long-standing businesses were forcibly closed forever. He bravely promised he would bust the heavy lock if nobody could quickly find the key. This grand new festival project turned out to be a complete and utter financial bust.
urduMeaning: مجسمہ، معاشی زوال، چھاپہ مار کر گرفتار کرنا، توڑنا، کندھوں اور سر پر مشتمل کسی شخص کا مجسمہ، اچانک معاشی تنگی، پولیس کا چھاپہ مارنا یا کسی چیز کو توڑ دینا
sindhiMeaning: مجسمو، ڇاپو هڻڻ، معاشي بحران، ڀڃڻ يا ٽوڙڻ، مٿي ۽ ڪلهن تائين ٺهيل شڪل يا مورتي، پوليس جو ڇاپو، اوچتو ٿيندڙ نقصان يا ڪنهن شيءِ کي تباهه ڪرڻ
antonyms: Success, Boom, Triumph, Mend, Fix, Build, Create, Achievement

urduMeaning: مرغی کی آواز، کڑکڑاہٹ، زبان سے ہمدردی یا ناپسندیدگی کا اظہار کرنا، مرغی کی مخصوص آواز نکالنا، یا انسانوں کا زبان تالو سے ٹکرا کر افسوس، ناپسندیدگی یا ہمدردی کے لیے آواز نکالنا
englishMeaning: The characteristic short, guttural sound made by a hen. It also describes a similar sound made by a person using their tongue to express sympathy, concern, or disapproval. It conveys a motherly or reprimanding maternal attitude.
synonyms: Chuckle, Cackle, Gobble, Squawk, Tsk, Murmur, Sound, Clutter
examples: The mother hen began to softly cluck to gather her fuzzy little chicks. Aunt Mary would always cluck her tongue whenever we made a messy mistake. We heard the gentle cluck of the lively chickens from the old wooden barn. He offered a sympathetic cluck when I described my terrible morning commute. The loud, sudden cluck warned the noisy flock of an approaching predatory danger.
sindhiMeaning: ڪڙڪڙ ڪرڻ، ڪڪڙ جي آواز، افسوس يا همدردي ۾ زبان سان آواز ڪڍڻ، ڪڪڙ جو مخصوص آواز جيڪو اها ڪڍندي آهي، ماڻهن پاران افسوس يا چڙ ڏيکارڻ لاءِ مخصوص زبان جو آواز
antonyms: Silence, Quietness, Roar, Shout, Yell, Scream, Howl
Apathy, Gloom, Depression, Lethargy, Dullness, Melancholy, Despair, Sadness
englishMeaning: The quality of being full of energy, excitement, and cheerfulness. It refers to a lively, enthusiastic, and joyful state of being, often visible in a person's bubbly behavior. It can also describe the lush and abundant growth of plants.
examples: The lively children bounded into the bright room with enormous, unmatched exuberance. Nothing could possibly dampen the sheer youthful exuberance of the joyful winning team. Her natural warmth and daily exuberance invariably make her incredibly fun to be around. The spring garden burst into vibrant life with an overwhelming, colorful exuberance. He delivered the energetic speech with an enormous amount of passion and loud exuberance.
urduMeaning: جوش، خروش، شادمانی، فراوانی، بے پناہ خوشی اور توانائی کا اظہار، زندہ دلی اور پرجوش کیفیت جو انسان کی باتوں اور رویے سے ظاہر ہو، پودوں کی سرسبز افزائش
sindhiMeaning: جوش، جذبو، خوشي ۽ شادماني، گهڻائي، توانائي، ماڻهوءَ ۾ حد کان وڌيڪ خوشي ۽ جذبي سان ڀرپور حالت جيڪا سندس کل مک هجڻ مان ظاهر ٿئي
synonyms: Enthusiasm, Energy, Ebullience, Cheerfulness, Buoyancy, Vitality, Joy, Liveliness

sindhiMeaning: جشن، زبردست خوشي، سرشاري، فتح جي خوشي، ڪنهن وڏي ڪاميابي يا فتح جي نتيجي ۾ پيدا ٿيندڙ بي انتها خوشي ۽ جشن ملهائڻ واري حالت
antonyms: Sorrow, Grief, Misery, Sadness, Mourning, Depression, Woe, Despondency
urduMeaning: شادمانی، جشن کی کیفیت، بے پناہ خوشی، فتح کی خوشی، کسی بڑی کامیابی، فتح یا بہت اچھی خبر ملنے پر انتہائی خوشی، مسرت اور جشن منانے کی کیفیت
synonyms: Triumph, Exultation, Joyfulness, Celebration, Elation, Happiness, Rejoicing, Ecstasy
englishMeaning: A feeling of supreme triumph and excessive happiness. It is typically a reaction to a great success, victory, or milestone achievement. It involves openly expressing great joy and celebration with others.
examples: The entire crowded stadium erupted in deafening jubilance as the final whistle blew. Her bright face completely radiated undeniable jubilance when she saw the fantastic test results. The grand streets were totally filled with the loud jubilance of the celebrating citizens. Such immense jubilance naturally follows a incredibly long, difficult, and fought-for victory. No one could ignore the wild jubilance of the happy athletes embracing each other.

sindhiMeaning: گدگد ڪرڻ، گهڻو خوش ڪرڻ، جوش ڏيارڻ، مگن ڪرڻ، ڪنهن کي تمام گهڻو خوش ۽ پرجوش ڪري ڇڏڻ جنهن سان هو فخر ۽ خوشيءَ جي انتها تي پهچي وڃي
examples: Winning the highly prestigious national award will absolutely elate any serious young artist. The completely unexpected arrival of her dear friend never failed to deeply elate her. Outstanding critical reviews for his new book will surely elate the incredibly nervous author. They successfully tried to totally elate the disappointed crowd with an incredibly energetic musical performance. Such wonderful community news is entirely guaranteed to quickly elate everyone in the entire town.
synonyms: Thrill, Exhilarate, Overjoy, Delight, Gladden, Excite, Uplift, Cheer
englishMeaning: To make someone practically burst with happiness and pride. It refers to filling an individual with intense joy, high spirits, and a sense of triumphant fulfillment. It elevates a person's mood to its highest levels.
antonyms: Depress, Disappoint, Sadden, Bring Down, Discourage, Deflate, Dishearten, Upset
urduMeaning: بے حد خوش کرنا، پھولے نہ سمانا، پرجوش کرنا، مسرور کرنا، کسی کی خوشی اور فخر کو بڑھانا، کسی کو اتنا خوش کر دینا کہ وہ اپنے آپ پر فخر محسوس کرے اور اس کا موڈ بہت بلند ہو جائے

examples: The news of her promotion overjoyed the entire family. His safe return from the war overjoyed his parents. The surprise gift overjoyed the little child. Winning the championship overjoyed the whole team. The reunion with her old friend overjoyed her completely.
sindhiMeaning: بيحد خوش ڪرڻ، انتهائي خوشي ڏيڻ، گهڻي مسرت پهچائڻ، خوشيءَ سان ڀرپور ڪرڻ، دل خوش ڪري ڇڏڻ، حد کان وڌيڪ خوش ڪرڻ، بيحد مسرور ڪرڻ
synonyms: Delight, Thrill, Elate, Please greatly, Enrapture, Gladden, Exhilarate, Cheer, Enchant
antonyms: Sadden, Depress, Distress, Disappoint, Upset, Grieve, Dishearten, Dismay
urduMeaning: بے حد خوش کرنا، نہایت مسرور کرنا، انتہائی خوشی دینا، خوشی سے سرشار کر دینا، حد سے زیادہ خوش کرنا، دل کو خوشیوں سے بھر دینا، بہت زیادہ مسرت پہنچانا
englishMeaning: To make someone extremely happy, delighted, or filled with joy. To fill a person with intense pleasure or great happiness. To cause feelings of overwhelming gladness, delight, or satisfaction. It is usually used when a piece of good news, an event, or a gesture brings extraordinary happiness that goes beyond ordinary pleasure.

synonyms: Rejoice, Celebrate, Triumph, Glory, Revel, Delight, Jubilate, Crow
englishMeaning: To show or feel great joy, triumph, or happiness, especially because of a success or victory. To rejoice openly and energetically. To be jubilant. To express delight in a lively or proud manner, often after defeating someone or achieving something significant.
examples: The fans exulted when their team won the final match. She exulted in her unexpected victory. The soldiers exulted over their hard-won triumph. He exulted at the news of his promotion. The crowd exulted as the champion crossed the finish line.
urduMeaning: خوشی سے جھومنا، فتح پر نازاں ہونا، فخر سے خوشی کا اظہار کرنا، شادمان ہونا، کامیابی پر بے حد مسرور ہونا، جشن منانا، خوشی سے سرشار ہونا
sindhiMeaning: خوشيءَ مان جهومڻ، فتح تي خوش ٿيڻ، فخر سان خوشي جو اظهار ڪرڻ، خوشيءَ ۾ نچڻ، ڪاميابيءَ تي بيحد خوش ٿيڻ، جشن ملهائڻ، خوشيءَ سان ٻُرڻ
antonyms: Mourn, Lament, Grieve, Despair, Sorrow, Sulk

examples: She felt euphoric after receiving the scholarship. The team was euphoric after winning the championship. He was in a euphoric mood on his wedding day. The fans were euphoric when their favourite singer came on stage. The euphoric crowd cheered for hours.
urduMeaning: بے حد خوش، نہایت مسرور، خوشی میں سرشار، جوش و خروش سے بھرپور، حد سے زیادہ شادمان، انتہائی پُرجوش، وجد کی کیفیت میں
synonyms: Elated, Jubilant, Ecstatic, Overjoyed, Thrilled, Exhilarated, Blissful, Rapturous
englishMeaning: Feeling or expressing intense happiness, excitement, or well-being. Extremely elated or cheerful. Filled with a sense of joy that is sometimes exaggerated or unrealistic. Describes a state of overwhelming delight, often following a great success, achievement, or pleasant experience.
sindhiMeaning: بيحد خوش، انتهائي مسرور، خوشيءَ ۾ ٻڏل، جوش ۽ خوشيءَ سان ڀرپور، حد کان وڌيڪ شادمان، بيحد پُرجوش، سرور واري ڪيفيت ۾
antonyms: Depressed, Miserable, Sad, Despondent, Gloomy, Melancholic, Dejected

synonyms: Soothe, Relieve, Calm, Ease, Mitigate, Alleviate, Pacify, Allay, Quench, Quell
urduMeaning: کم کرنا، تسلی دینا، تکلیف کو ہلکا کرنا، غم یا غصے کو ٹھنڈا کرنا، خوف کم کرنا، اطمینان دلانا، بھوک یا پیاس بجھانا، دل کو سکون پہنچانا
examples: He tried to assuage her grief with kind words. The government took steps to assuage public anger over the new law. A cold drink helped assuage his thirst. Nothing could assuage the mother's sorrow. The manager attempted to assuage the concerns of the worried employees.
englishMeaning: To make an unpleasant feeling less intense or severe. To soothe, calm, or relieve pain, anger, grief, fear, or worry. To satisfy hunger, thirst, or desire. To ease or lessen distress. It is often used in formal contexts when emotions or physical discomfort are reduced or softened.
antonyms: Aggravate, Worsen, Intensify, Provoke, Inflame, Exacerbate, Increase
sindhiMeaning: گهٽائڻ، تسلي ڏيڻ، آرام پهچائڻ، ڏک يا ڏاکڙي کي گهٽائڻ، خوف يا غصو ٿڌو ڪرڻ، تشفي ڏيڻ، بک يا اڃ مٽائڻ، دل کي راحت ڏيڻ

englishMeaning: A sudden short attack or raid, especially into enemy territory. A brief attempt or venture into a new activity, field, or area. A short trip made for a specific purpose, such as obtaining something. It can describe both a military incursion and a person's first attempt at something unfamiliar.
synonyms: Raid, Incursion, Attack, Sortie, Venture, Expedition, Excursion, Invasion
sindhiMeaning: اوچتو حملو، مختصر ڪاهه، ڌاڙو، نئين ميدان ۾ پهرين ڪوشش، ٿوري وقت لاءِ ڪنهن نئين شعبي ۾ قدم رکڻ، مختصر مهم، حملو ڪرڻ يا ڪجهه حاصل ڪرڻ لاءِ ٿوري وقت لاءِ وڃڻ
examples: The soldiers made a quick foray into enemy territory. Her first foray into politics was surprisingly successful. He made a brief foray into the world of acting. The company's foray into the smartphone market failed. They made a foray into the forest to collect firewood.
urduMeaning: اچانک حملہ، مختصر یلغار، چھاپہ، نئے میدان میں پہلی کوشش، تھوڑے وقت کے لیے کسی نئے شعبے میں قدم رکھنا، مختصر مہم، کسی چیز کے حصول کے لیے مختصر سفر
antonyms: Retreat, Withdrawal, Stay, Inaction

examples: The army repelled the enemy's incursion across the border. There were repeated incursions into the protected wildlife area. The incursion of foreign goods threatened the local industry. The general warned of further military incursions. The journalist criticized the incursion into people's private lives.
sindhiMeaning: حملو، چڙهائي، ڪاهه، ڌاڙو، ٻئي جي علائقي ۾ زبردستي داخل ٿيڻ، اڻ گهربل مداخلت، اوچتو ۽ سخت حملو، ڪنهن جاءِ تي زوريءَ گهڙي اچڻ
synonyms: Invasion, Raid, Attack, Intrusion, Encroachment, Foray, Inroad, Infiltration
urduMeaning: حملہ، یلغار، چڑھائی، دراندازی، دوسرے کے علاقے میں زبردستی داخل ہونا، ناپسندیدہ مداخلت، اچانک اور سخت حملہ، کسی جگہ زبردستی گھس آنا
antonyms: Retreat, Withdrawal, Evacuation, Departure
englishMeaning: A sudden invasion or attack into another's territory. An act of entering a place, especially in a way that is unwanted or harmful. An unwelcome intrusion into a domain, situation, or area. It is often used for military advances, but also for any forceful entry where someone is not welcome.

synonyms: Onslaught, Assault, Offensive, Lightning attack, Bombardment, Strike, Campaign
sindhiMeaning: تيز رفتار ۽ زبردست فوجي حملو، اوچتو ۽ سخت ڪاهه، طوفاني حملو، تيزيءَ سان ڪاميابي حاصل ڪرڻ واري مهم، هڪدم ۽ زبردست ڪارروائي
englishMeaning: An intense, swift, and overwhelming military attack designed to defeat the enemy quickly using fast-moving forces. Any sudden, forceful, and concentrated effort or campaign aimed at achieving rapid results. The word originated in the German military strategy of World War II but is now used broadly for any rapid and powerful offensive.
examples: The German army used blitzkrieg tactics during World War II. The company launched a marketing blitzkrieg to capture the market. The opposition faced a political blitzkrieg from the ruling party. The team's blitzkrieg in the first half secured them the victory. Their blitzkrieg of questions left the witness confused.
urduMeaning: تیز رفتار اور زبردست فوجی حملہ، اچانک اور شدید یلغار، طوفانی حملہ، تیزی سے کامیابی حاصل کرنے والی مہم، فوری اور بھرپور کارروائی
antonyms: Retreat, Withdrawal, Defence, Truce, Ceasefire

synonyms: Overturn, Topple, Invert, Capsize, Tip over, Disrupt, Unsettle, Defeat
urduMeaning: الٹا کرنا، اوپر نیچے کرنا، اُلٹ دینا، ترتیب بگاڑ دینا، حالات بدل دینا، اچانک شکست دینا، کسی نظام یا چیز کو درہم برہم کر دینا
examples: He accidentally upended the glass of water on the table. The new technology upended the entire industry. The underdog team upended the champions in a stunning match. The scandal upended his political career. She upended the basket to empty the fruits.
englishMeaning: To turn something upside down. To overturn, invert, or flip. To disrupt or completely change a situation, system, or order of things. To defeat someone unexpectedly. It is used both literally for physically turning objects over and figuratively for upsetting plans, expectations, or norms.
antonyms: Right, Stabilize, Maintain, Preserve, Uphold
sindhiMeaning: اونڌو ڪرڻ، مٿاهون هيٺ ڪرڻ، اُٿلائي ڇڏڻ، ترتيب خراب ڪرڻ، حالتون مٽائي ڇڏڻ، اوچتو شڪست ڏيڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ يا نظام کي درهم برهم ڪرڻ

englishMeaning: To laugh in a quiet, partly hidden, or disrespectful way. To give a smothered or sly laugh, often at someone else's misfortune, mistake, or embarrassment. To laugh secretly or rudely. It usually carries a sense of mockery or amusement at another's expense.
urduMeaning: دبی دبی ہنسی ہنسنا، مذاق میں ہنسنا، طنزیہ ہنسی، چھپ کر ہنسنا، کسی پر تمسخر کے ساتھ ہنسنا، ہونٹوں میں ہنسنا، چوری چوری ہنسنا
examples: The students snickered when the teacher mispronounced the name. He snickered behind his hand at her old-fashioned dress. They snickered at his clumsy attempt to dance. Stop snickering and pay attention to the lecture. The boys snickered as the principal slipped on the wet floor.
synonyms: Giggle, Titter, Chuckle, Snigger, Smirk, Sneer, Chortle
antonyms: Cry, Weep, Sob, Frown, Sulk
sindhiMeaning: دٻيل کِل کلڻ، مذاق ۾ کلڻ، طنزيه کِل، ڳجهي طرح کلڻ، ٻئي تي مسخريءَ سان کلڻ، چپن ۾ ئي مرڪڻ، چوريءَ کلڻ

antonyms: Order, Arrange, Organize, Stroll, Walk slowly
sindhiMeaning: تڪڙ ۾ چڙهڻ، هٿ پير هلائي وڃڻ، ڊوڙ ڊوڙ ۾ پهچڻ، ڪجهه حاصل ڪرڻ لاءِ ڌِڪا ڌُڪي ڪرڻ، شيون گڏ ملائي پريشان ڪرڻ، آنا ڦينٽڻ، سگنل خراب ڪرڻ
englishMeaning: To move or climb quickly using hands and feet, especially in a hurried or awkward way. To struggle or compete eagerly with others to get or do something. To mix things together in a disordered manner. To cook eggs by beating and stirring them in a pan. To make a radio or telephone signal unintelligible.
examples: The children scrambled up the rocks to reach the top. Reporters scrambled to get the first interview. She scrambled the eggs for breakfast. Soldiers scrambled to their positions when the alarm sounded. The transmission was scrambled to keep it secret.
urduMeaning: تیزی سے چڑھنا، ہاتھ پاؤں مار کر جانا، جلدی میں پہنچنا، کچھ حاصل کرنے کے لیے دھکم پیل کرنا، چیزوں کو الٹ پلٹ کرنا، انڈے پھینٹ کر پکانا، سگنل خراب کرنا
synonyms: Clamber, Climb, Hurry, Rush, Struggle, Jostle, Mix, Jumble

examples: The lion was prowling through the tall grass. Thieves prowl the streets at night. A strange man was seen prowling around the house. The cat prowled silently behind the mouse. Reporters prowled the corridors waiting for the politician.
synonyms: Lurk, Roam, Sneak, Stalk, Skulk, Slink, Hunt, Patrol
antonyms: Rest, Stay, Remain, Sit still
englishMeaning: To move about quietly and secretly, especially while hunting or searching for something. To roam stealthily, often with harmful or suspicious intent. To wander like a predator looking for prey or opportunity. The word is used for both animals and people who move silently in search of something.
urduMeaning: چوری چوری گھومنا، شکار کی تلاش میں آہستہ چلنا، چھپ کر پھرنا، تاک میں رہنا، خاموشی سے کسی جگہ گھومتے رہنا، شکاری کی طرح تلاش کرنا
sindhiMeaning: چوريءَ چوريءَ گهمڻ، شڪار جي ڳولا ۾ آهستي هلڻ، لڪي گهمڻ، چوريءَ سان تاڙ ۾ ويهڻ، خاموشيءَ سان ڪنهن جاءِ تي گهمندو رهڻ، شڪاري وانگر ڳولا ڪرڻ

synonyms: Strengthen, Support, Bolster, Fortify, Consolidate, Boost, Underpin, Toughen
sindhiMeaning: مضبوط ڪرڻ، تقويت ڏيڻ، حمايت وڌائڻ، اضافي مدد ڏيڻ، ڪنهن خيال يا روش کي مضبوط بنائڻ، فوجي مدد موڪلڻ، يقين پختو ڪرڻ، بنيادن کي مضبوط ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: مضبوط کرنا، تقویت دینا، حمایت بڑھانا، اضافی مدد فراہم کرنا، کسی خیال یا رویے کو مزید پختہ کرنا، فوجی کمک بھیجنا، یقین کو پختہ کرنا، بنیادوں کو مستحکم کرنا
examples: The walls were reinforced with steel bars. His success only reinforced her belief in hard work. The army sent troops to reinforce the border. Parents should reinforce good behaviour with praise. The new evidence reinforced the prosecution's case.
englishMeaning: To make something stronger by adding extra support, material, or effort. To strengthen a feeling, idea, or behaviour by providing additional evidence or encouragement. To send more soldiers or supplies to support a military operation. It is used in physical, emotional, and military contexts.
antonyms: Weaken, Undermine, Reduce, Diminish, Soften, Erode

synonyms: Disgrace, Dishonour, Shame, Humiliation, Infamy, Embarrassment, Stigma, Discredit
sindhiMeaning: بدنامي، رسوائي، شرمندگي، عزت جو نقصان، عوام جي اڳيان ذلت، بي عزتي، ساک کي ٿيل گهرو نقصان، شرم ۽ بدنامي واري حالت
examples: He suffered the ignominy of being dismissed from his post. The team faced the ignominy of defeat by a much weaker side. She could not bear the ignominy of public failure. The scandal brought ignominy upon the whole family. He resigned to avoid further ignominy.
urduMeaning: بدنامی، رسوائی، شرمندگی، ذلت، عوام کے سامنے بے عزتی، عزت کا نقصان، ساکھ کو شدید نقصان پہنچنے کی حالت، رسوا کن صورتحال
englishMeaning: Public shame, disgrace, or dishonour, especially as a result of bad behaviour or a serious failure. A state of severe humiliation in front of others. A deeply embarrassing situation that damages one's reputation. The word is formal and usually used for serious, lasting disgrace rather than minor embarrassment.
antonyms: Honour, Glory, Respect, Dignity, Esteem, Reputation, Pride
Disagreement, Dispute, Conflict, Quarrel, Discord
sindhiMeaning: ثالثي، فيصلو ڪرائڻ، تڪرار جي حل لاءِ ٽئين غير جانبدار ماڻهوءَ جو فيصلو، عدالت کان ٻاهر تڪرار جو حل، پنچائت، صلح صفائي جو رسمي طريقو
urduMeaning: ثالثی، فیصلہ کرانا، تنازعے کے حل کے لیے غیر جانبدار تیسرے فریق کا فیصلہ، عدالت سے باہر تنازعہ حل کرنا، پنچایت، صلح صفائی کا رسمی طریقہ
examples: The two countries agreed to settle the dispute through arbitration. The labour union demanded arbitration in the wage dispute. The contract included a clause for compulsory arbitration. International arbitration helped end the long conflict. The arbitration ruling was accepted by both companies.
englishMeaning: The process of settling a dispute between two parties by referring it to a neutral third person or panel whose decision is usually binding. A formal method of resolving disagreements outside the court system. It is commonly used in labour disputes, business conflicts, and international issues.
synonyms: Mediation, Adjudication, Negotiation, Conciliation, Settlement, Judgement, Reconciliation

englishMeaning: Extremely serious, urgent, or terrible. Causing great fear, anxiety, or distress. Describing a situation that is very bad and likely to get worse if not addressed. Used for warnings, consequences, needs, or conditions that are critical and demand immediate attention.
antonyms: Mild, Trivial, Minor, Good, Favourable, Pleasant, Safe
synonyms: Terrible, Severe, Grave, Critical, Desperate, Urgent, Serious, Disastrous, Calamitous
sindhiMeaning: تمام سخت، خوفناڪ، ڏکيو، اشد ضرورت وارو، انتهائي سنگين، خطرناڪ، تمام برو، تشويش ڏيندڙ، فوري ڪارروائي گهرندڙ
urduMeaning: نہایت سنگین، خوفناک، شدید، اشد ضرورت والا، انتہائی برا، خطرناک، تشویشناک، فوری توجہ کا متقاضی، بدترین
examples: The country is facing dire economic conditions. He gave a dire warning about climate change. The flood victims are in dire need of food and shelter. Failure to act now could have dire consequences. The patient is in a dire state and needs immediate surgery.

urduMeaning: اثر و رسوخ، طاقت، اختیار، سیاسی یا سماجی اثر، فیصلوں پر اثر ڈالنے کی صلاحیت، زوردار ضرب، تھپڑ، رعب داب
englishMeaning: Influence or power, especially in politics, business, or society. The ability to affect decisions or events. A heavy blow or hit with the hand or a hard object. In informal usage, it refers to authority or pull that a person uses to get things done.
antonyms: Weakness, Insignificance, Powerlessness, Caress, Pat
synonyms: Influence, Power, Authority, Pull, Weight, Sway, Strike, Blow
sindhiMeaning: اثر و رسوخ، طاقت، اختيار، سياسي يا سماجي اثر، فيصلن تي اثر وجهڻ جي صلاحيت، زوردار ڌڪ، چماٽ، رعب رسوخ
examples: He used his political clout to get the project approved. The company has enormous clout in the global market. She gave the ball a hefty clout with the bat. Wealthy donors carry a lot of clout in elections. His clout in the industry helped him secure the deal.

sindhiMeaning: ٻن حصن ۾ ورهائڻ، ٻه شاخون ٿيڻ، ٻن طرفن ۾ جدا ٿيڻ، ٻه ڀاڱا ڪرڻ، ٻن رستن ۾ ورهائجڻ، ٻن قسمن ۾ تقسيم ڪرڻ
synonyms: Divide, Split, Fork, Separate, Branch, Part, Cleave
urduMeaning: دو حصوں میں تقسیم کرنا، دو شاخیں ہونا، دو سمتوں میں جدا ہونا، دو ٹکڑے کرنا، دو راستوں میں بٹ جانا، دو اقسام میں منقسم کرنا
examples: The road bifurcates near the old bridge. The committee decided to bifurcate the project into two phases. The river bifurcates into two streams further north. The court ordered to bifurcate the trial. The province was bifurcated for better administration.
englishMeaning: To divide or split something into two branches, parts, or directions. To fork into two separate paths or streams. To cause a single thing to separate into two distinct sections. It is commonly used in geography, biology, law, and any context where a single entity divides into two.
antonyms: Unite, Merge, Combine, Join, Consolidate, Connect

sindhiMeaning: منصوبو ناڪام بڻائڻ، ڪوششون برباد ڪرڻ، اميدون ٽوڙي ڇڏڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ کي ناڪام ڪرڻ، جهاز کي ارادي طور ٻوڙڻ، رٿا کي ناس ڪرڻ، اميدن تي پاڻي ڦيرائڻ
examples: The sudden rain scuppered our picnic plans. His careless remark scuppered the business deal. Lack of funding scuppered the project. The captain ordered the crew to scupper the ship before surrender. The scandal scuppered his chances of becoming president.
synonyms: Ruin, Wreck, Sabotage, Destroy, Foil, Thwart, Sink, Spoil
englishMeaning: To prevent something from happening or succeeding. To ruin, spoil, or destroy plans, hopes, or efforts. In naval usage, to deliberately sink one's own ship. The word is mostly British and informal, used when something causes a plan or chance to fail completely.
antonyms: Help, Support, Promote, Encourage, Aid, Save, Rescue
urduMeaning: منصوبہ ناکام بنانا، کوششیں برباد کرنا، امیدیں توڑ دینا، کسی چیز کو ناکام کرنا، جہاز کو جان بوجھ کر ڈبونا، منصوبے کو خراب کرنا، امیدوں پر پانی پھیرنا

antonyms: Solution, Order, Clarity, Agreement, Resolution, Simplicity
examples: The government found itself in a diplomatic imbroglio with its neighbour. The political imbroglio lasted for several months. He got entangled in a legal imbroglio over his property. The company's financial imbroglio damaged its reputation. Reporters covered every detail of the celebrity imbroglio.
sindhiMeaning: پيچيده ۽ پريشان ڪندڙ صورتحال، الجهيل معاملو، تڪراري ۽ شرمناڪ حالت، گُتل مسئلو، سياسي يا سماجي گهڙمس، اهڙو معاملو جنهن ۾ ڪيترائي ڌر شامل هجن
urduMeaning: پیچیدہ اور پریشان کن صورتحال، الجھا ہوا معاملہ، تنازعہ اور شرمناک حالت، گنجلک مسئلہ، سیاسی یا سماجی الجھن، ایسا معاملہ جس میں کئی فریق ملوث ہوں
englishMeaning: A complicated, confusing, or embarrassing situation, especially one involving disagreement, misunderstanding, or scandal. A messy or entangled state of affairs that is difficult to resolve. The word is often used in political, diplomatic, or personal contexts where many parties and issues are tangled together.
synonyms: Predicament, Quagmire, Mess, Entanglement, Complication, Scandal, Dispute, Confusion

englishMeaning: To pull a plant out of the ground along with its roots. To force someone to leave their home, country, or settled place. To remove something completely from its established position. It is used both literally for plants and figuratively for displacing people, customs, or systems.
antonyms: Plant, Root, Settle, Establish, Restore, Preserve
urduMeaning: جڑ سے اکھاڑنا، پودے کو جڑ سمیت نکالنا، گھر یا وطن سے بے دخل کرنا، کسی کو اپنی جگہ سے ہٹانا، کسی رسم یا نظام کو بنیاد سمیت ختم کرنا، بے گھر کرنا
sindhiMeaning: پاڙ پٽڻ، جڙ سميت اکوڙي ڇڏڻ، گهر يا وطن مان ڪڍي ڇڏڻ، ڪنهن کي پنهنجي جاءِ تان هٽائي ڇڏڻ، ڪنهن رواج يا نظام کي بنياد سميت ختم ڪرڻ، بي گهر ڪرڻ
synonyms: Eradicate, Displace, Remove, Eliminate, Pull up, Banish, Dislodge, Exile
examples: The storm uprooted hundreds of trees in the area. War uprooted thousands of families from their homes. The new policy aims to uproot corruption from society. They had to uproot themselves and move to another city. Reformers worked hard to uproot outdated customs.

synonyms: Execute, Carry out, Apply, Enforce, Perform, Fulfil, Tool, Instrument
examples: The government will implement the new tax policy next year. The school implemented several safety measures after the incident. Farmers use modern implements for cultivation. It is easier to plan than to implement. The company implemented the software across all branches.
englishMeaning: To put a plan, decision, agreement, or policy into action. To carry out, execute, or fulfil something formally. A tool, instrument, or piece of equipment used for a particular purpose. It is widely used in administrative, technical, and everyday contexts.
antonyms: Ignore, Neglect, Cancel, Abandon, Reject, Withhold
sindhiMeaning: لاڳو ڪرڻ، عمل ۾ آڻڻ، ڪنهن منصوبي يا فيصلي تي عمل ڪرڻ، نافذ ڪرڻ، مڪمل ڪرڻ، اوزار، آلو، ڪم ڪرڻ جو سامان
urduMeaning: نافذ کرنا، عمل میں لانا، کسی منصوبے یا فیصلے پر عمل کرنا، اطلاق کرنا، مکمل کرنا، اوزار، آلہ، کام کرنے کا سامان

antonyms: Arrogant, Boastful, Proud, Conceited, Showy, Immodest, Vain, Excessive
englishMeaning: Not boastful or arrogant about one's abilities or achievements. Humble in attitude and behaviour. Limited in size, amount, or importance. Decent and not showy in dress or manner. The word can describe a person's character as well as quantities or appearances that are moderate.
sindhiMeaning: عاجز، نمر، شرميلو، گهٽ ۽ مناسب، نه دکاوي وارو، شائسته، حياءَ وارو، معمولي، محتاط لباس وارو، گهٽ ۾ گهٽ ضرورت رکندڙ
examples: Despite his fame, he remains a modest man. She received a modest income from her small business. He gave a modest answer when praised. The house was modest but comfortable. She always dressed in a modest manner.
urduMeaning: عاجز، منکسر المزاج، شرمیلا، کم اور مناسب، نمائش سے دور، شائستہ، باحیا، معمولی، سادہ لباس والا، کم خواہشات والا
synonyms: Humble, Unassuming, Reserved, Simple, Moderate, Decent, Plain, Unpretentious

antonyms: Honesty, Integrity, Lawfulness, Righteousness, Probity
englishMeaning: Wrongdoing or misconduct, especially by a public official or person in a position of trust. Illegal or dishonest behaviour while performing official duties. An unlawful act that causes harm to others. The word is formal and most often used in legal, governmental, or corporate contexts.
examples: The minister was dismissed for malfeasance in office. The auditor uncovered serious malfeasance in the department. He was charged with malfeasance and misuse of public funds. Several officers were investigated for malfeasance. The committee took strict action against corporate malfeasance.

sindhiMeaning: بدعنواني، عهدي جو غلط استعمال، سرڪاري عملدار جي طرفان غير قانوني عمل، خيانت، غلط ڪاريون، فرض ۾ بدنيتي، اختيارن جو ناجائز استعمال
synonyms: Misconduct, Wrongdoing, Corruption, Misbehaviour, Dishonesty, Impropriety, Misdeed

englishMeaning: A clever, cunning, and shrewd way of thinking. A mind that is quick, sly, and capable of outsmarting others. A person with a foxy mind is intelligent and tricky, often using craftiness to achieve goals. The expression highlights cleverness mixed with a touch of slyness.
antonyms: Naive mind, Simple mind, Innocent mind, Gullible mind, Dull mind
urduMeaning: چالاک ذہن، تیز اور ہوشیار دماغ، شاطر سوچ، عقل اور مکاری سے بھرپور ذہن، دوسروں کو چالاکی سے مات دینے والا دماغ، تیز فہم اور تدبیر باز سوچ

sindhiMeaning: چالاڪ دماغ، تيز ۽ هوشيار ذهن، شاطر سوچ، عقل ۽ مڪاريءَ سان ڀرپور دماغ، ٻين کي چالاڪيءَ سان مات ڏيندڙ سوچ، تيز فهم ۽ ترڪيب باز ذهن
examples: He has a foxy mind and always finds a way out of trouble. With his foxy mind, he easily outsmarted his opponents in the deal. A politician with a foxy mind is hard to defeat. urduMeaning: طرفداری، جانبداری، ناانصافی کے ساتھ کسی فرد یا گروہ کو ترجیح دینا، اقربا پروری، ناجائز پسندیدگی، انصاف کے خلاف رویہ، بے جا حمایت
sindhiMeaning: طرفداري، پاسداري، ناانصافي سان هڪ فرد يا گروهه کي ترجيح ڏيڻ، جانبداري، اقربا پروري، ناجائز پسنديدگي، انصاف جي ابتڙ سلوڪ
englishMeaning: The practice of giving unfair preference to one person or group over others. Treating someone better than others without a valid reason. Showing partiality, often based on personal liking, relationship, or bias. It is generally viewed negatively, especially in workplaces, families, and institutions where fairness is expected.
examples: The teacher was accused of favoritism by the students. Favoritism in promotions has damaged the company's morale. Parents should avoid favoritism among their children. The manager's favoritism caused resentment in the team. Many believe favoritism is widespread in government appointments.
synonyms: Partiality, Bias, Preference, Nepotism, Discrimination, Prejudice, One-sidedness

sindhiMeaning: بنا ڊپ، بي خوف رهڻ، سختيءَ ۾ به ثابت قدم رهڻ، ڪنهن مشڪل تي پوئتي نه هٽڻ، همت سان مقابلو ڪرڻ، نه ڊڄڻ، جرئت سان بيهڻ
antonyms: Hesitant, Cowardly, Fearful, Wavering, Weak, Timid, Faint-hearted
urduMeaning: بنا گھبرائے، بے خوف رہنا، مشکل میں بھی ثابت قدم رہنا، چیلنج پر پیچھے نہ ہٹنا، ہمت سے مقابلہ کرنا، نہ ڈرنا، جرات سے کھڑا رہنا
synonyms: Steadfast, Resolute, Fearless, Unwavering, Determined, Brave, Firm, Bold
englishMeaning: Not to show fear, hesitation, or weakness in the face of danger, difficulty, or pain. To remain firm, brave, and steady when others might shrink. To describe courageous and unwavering behaviour.
examples: He stood unflinching in the face of harsh criticism. The soldiers remained unflinching under heavy fire. She gave an unflinching reply to the difficult question. His unflinching loyalty impressed everyone. The reporter delivered an unflinching account of the war.

He did not flinch when the doctor gave him the injection. She flinched at the loud sound of the explosion. The boxer never flinched, no matter how hard the punch. He didn't flinch from telling the truth, even when it hurt. She flinched at the sight of blood.

sindhiMeaning: ڊپ کان پوئتي هٽڻ، اوچتو سُسي وڃڻ، درد يا خوف کان سُور ڀرين، گهٻرائڻ، همت هارجڻ، ڪا ڏکي ڳالهه ڏسي پوئتي هٽڻ، چهرو سُسائڻ
englishMeaning: To make a sudden small movement because of pain, fear, or surprise. To shrink or pull back from something unpleasant or frightening. To show reluctance to face difficulty or duty. It can describe both a physical reaction and an emotional unwillingness.
urduMeaning: ڈر کر پیچھے ہٹنا، اچانک سکڑ جانا، درد یا خوف سے کانپنا، گھبرانا، ہمت ہارنا، کسی مشکل کو دیکھ کر پیچھے ہٹنا، چہرہ بگاڑنا

englishMeaning: The condition of having one's hair stand on end, especially due to cold, fear, or strong emotion. The medical term for goose bumps. A reaction of the skin in which tiny bumps appear and hair rises. It can occur from chills, excitement, or intense emotional experiences.

examples: The horror movie caused horripilation throughout my body. The sudden cold breeze led to horripilation on her arms. He felt horripilation while listening to the national anthem. Fear gripped him and horripilation spread over his skin. The story of the haunted house gave the children horripilation.
sindhiMeaning: وارن جو کڙو ٿيڻ، جسم تي ڏڪار نڪرڻ، ڊپ يا سرديءَ کان جسم تي رونڍا نڪرڻ، جذباتي حالت ۾ کل جا وار ڪانڊارجي وڃڻ، رونگٽا کڙا ٿيڻ

synonyms: Burdensome, Heavy, Demanding, Taxing, Arduous, Difficult, Strenuous, Oppressive
englishMeaning: Involving a great amount of effort, difficulty, or responsibility. Burdensome, troublesome, or oppressive. Describing a task, duty, or condition that is heavy and hard to bear. The word is formal and often used in legal, professional, or moral contexts.
urduMeaning: دشوار، بوجھل، تھکا دینے والا، ذمہ داری بھرا، بہت محنت طلب کام، مشکل اور سخت، سخت فرض، تکلیف دہ شرط
examples: The new manager found his duties extremely onerous. The contract included several onerous conditions. Looking after a large family is an onerous responsibility. He was relieved of his onerous tasks after the reform. Paying back the loan became an onerous burden.
sindhiMeaning: ڏکيو، بار وارو، ٿڪائيندڙ، ذميواري وارو، گهڻي محنت گهرندڙ ڪم، مشڪل ۽ بوجهل، سخت فرض، تڪليف ڏيندڙ شرط

englishMeaning: To cause severe and widespread damage or destruction to a place, thing, or system. To devastate, ruin, or lay waste. To plunder violently. The destructive effects of something such as war, disease, or time. It is often used for both natural disasters and human actions.
examples: The earthquake ravaged the entire town. War has ravaged the country for years. The disease has ravaged the population. Time has ravaged the once beautiful palace. The forest fire ravaged thousands of acres.
sindhiMeaning: تباهه ڪرڻ، برباد ڪرڻ، ويران ڪرڻ، ڦرلٽ ڪرڻ، شديد نقصان پهچائڻ، مڪمل طور تباهه ڪرڻ، جنگ، بيماري يا وقت جو ويراني ڏيندڙ اثر

englishMeaning: Spreading or growing in an uncontrolled and widespread way, especially something undesirable. Existing or happening on a large scale without restraint. Used for diseases, crime, corruption, weeds, and similar negative things that flourish without being checked.

sindhiMeaning: بي قابو، بي حساب پکڙيل، عام، شدت سان وڌندڙ، روڪ کان سواءِ پکڙيل، گهڻو پکڙيل، بي لگام، آزاديءَ سان وڌندڙ خراب شيءِ
examples: Corruption is rampant in the department. Crime was rampant in the city before the new police chief took charge. Weeds were rampant in the neglected garden. Rumours about the merger were rampant in the office. Inflation has been rampant for the past two years.
urduMeaning: بے قابو، بے حساب پھیلا ہوا، عام، شدت سے بڑھنے والا، روک ٹوک کے بغیر پھیلا ہوا، حد سے بڑھا ہوا، بے لگام، آزادی سے بڑھنے والی بُری چیز

Complete, Comprehensive, Exhaustive, Total, Absolute, Detailed, Full, Meticulous
examples: The police conducted a thoroughgoing investigation into the case. The reform required a thoroughgoing change in the system. He is a thoroughgoing professional. The book offers a thoroughgoing analysis of the topic. The committee carried out a thoroughgoing review of the policy.

examples: Her nyctophilia made her feel most productive after midnight. People with nyctophilia often enjoy stargazing. His nyctophilia led him to become a night photographer. englishMeaning: A strong preference or love for the night and darkness. antonyms: Nyctophobia, Fear of darkness, Photophilia, Love of light

Used to describe a person who looks dejected, sullen, or downcast, often without speaking much, usually because of disappointment or worry. It can also describe an atmosphere or expression that feels heavy and joyless.

examples: The mendacious witness misled the entire court. His mendacious claims were quickly exposed by the journalists. She accused him of being a mendacious and manipulative politician. The report was full of mendacious statements about the company. We cannot trust such a mendacious source of information.

antonyms: Truthful, Honest, Sincere, Candid, Frank, Genuine, Trustworthy, Reliable, Straightforward
urduMeaning: جھوٹا، جھوٹ بولنے والا، جھوٹ پر مبنی، فریبی، دغاباز، ناقابلِ اعتبار، عادتاً جھوٹ بولنے والا، جھوٹے بیانات دینے والا، کذاب
بڑھانا، عظیم بنانا، خود کو بڑا ظاہر کرنا، شان و شوکت بڑھانا، طاقت یا دولت میں اضافہ کرنا، حقیقت سے زیادہ اہم دکھانا، مبالغہ آرائی کرنا، اپنی تعریف بڑھا چڑھا کر بیان کرنا، بلند کرنا

antonyms: Diminish, Belittle, Reduce, Lessen, Downplay, Understate, Humble, Degrade, Shrink
sindhiMeaning: وڌائڻ، عظيم بڻائڻ، پاڻ کي وڏو ڏيکارڻ، شان مان وڌائڻ، طاقت يا دولت وڌائڻ، حقيقت کان وڌيڪ اهم ڏيکارڻ، مبالغو ڪرڻ، پنهنجي تعريف وڌائي ڪرڻ، بلند ڪرڻ
englishMeaning: To increase the power, status, or wealth of. To make something appear greater than it really is. To enhance the reputation of beyond what is justified by the facts. To exaggerate. urduMeaning: سانولا، گہرے رنگ والا، سیاہ فام، سانولی رنگت والا، دھوپ میں پکا ہوا چہرہ رکھنے والا، گہری رنگت والا، گندمی رنگ سے بھی گہرا

englishMeaning: Having a dark complexion. Dark-skinned. Tanned. Having a dark or sun-browned face. It is usually applied to the face and is mostly used in literary or descriptive writing.
antonyms: Fair, Pale, Light-skinned, White, Pallid, Fair-complexioned

englishMeaning: To forbid by law. To officially prohibit something. To ban. To denounce or condemn. To outlaw a person, group, or activity. When an authority such as a government, court, or organization formally forbids an activity, group, book, or substance, often with legal punishment for those who break the ban.
antonyms: Allow, Permit, Authorize, Sanction, Approve, Endorse, License, Tolerate
synonyms: Forbid, Ban, Prohibit, Outlaw, Disallow, Bar, Embargo, Veto, Condemn, Interdict

examples: The government has proscribed several extremist organizations. Smoking is proscribed in all public buildings. The book was proscribed by the regime for political reasons. Many religious texts proscribe the consumption of alcohol. The new law proscribes the import of these chemicals.

englishMeaning: To claim the right to have or do something before anyone else. To call dibs on something. An informal British expression used, especially by children, to reserve something for oneself. It is used to quickly stake a claim on an object, seat, or task so that others cannot take it. It is a casual and playful word.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ تي پهرين دعويٰ ڪرڻ، اها منهنجي آهي چوڻ، اڳواٽ پاڻ لاءِ مخصوص ڪرڻ، حق جتائڻ، ٻارن وارو غير رسمي لفظ جنهن سان ڪا شيءِ پاڻ لاءِ رکڻ جو اعلان ڪجي

urduMeaning: کسی چیز پر پہلے دعویٰ کرنا، یہ میری ہے کہہ کر مخصوص کرنا، پہلے سے اپنے لیے رکھ لینا، حق جتانا، بچوں کا غیر رسمی لفظ جس سے کوئی چیز اپنے لیے محفوظ کر لی جائے
