sindhiMeaning: بدمعاش، غنڊو، اوباش، گنڊو، جرائم پيشه نوجوان، گينگ جو ميمبر، تشدد ڪندڙ شخص، دادا گير، شرپسند، قانون شڪن
synonyms: Thug, Gangster, Criminal, Ruffian, Hooligan, Tough, Mobster, Delinquent, Brute, Lout
examples: A gang of hoodlums attacked the shopkeeper at night. The police arrested several hoodlums during the raid. He grew up in a neighborhood plagued by hoodlums. The film portrays the life of a young hoodlum in the city. The hoodlums smashed the windows of the parked cars.
englishMeaning: A violent criminal. A gangster. A tough and aggressive young man involved in crime or violence. A member of a gang of street thugs. A person who behaves in a rough, lawless, and threatening way, often as part of a group, and is associated with petty crime, vandalism, or organized criminal activity.

The act of secretly watching a place by police or detectives. Surveillance of a location over a period of time to gather evidence or catch a suspect. A period of continuous observation, often from a hidden position, usually conducted by law enforcement to monitor the activities of a person or building suspected of criminal involvement.
antonyms: Inattention, Neglect, Disregard, Ignoring, Oversight
sindhiMeaning: ڳجهي نگراني، پوليس يا جاسوسن پاران ڪنهن جاءِ تي لڪل نظر رکڻ، نگراني وارو آپريشن، شڪي ماڻهوءَ يا جاءِ جي خفيه نگراني، گهات لائڻ، تاڙ ۾ رهڻ، خفيه طور ڏسڻ ۽ معلومات گڏ ڪرڻ
examples: The detectives organized a stakeout outside the suspect's apartment. The police were on a stakeout for three nights before making the arrest. Officers conducted a stakeout to monitor the drug dealers' activities. The stakeout finally produced enough evidence to charge the gang. They sat in an unmarked van during the long stakeout.
urduMeaning: خفیہ نگرانی، پولیس یا جاسوسوں کی طرف سے کسی جگہ پر چھپ کر نظر رکھنا، نگرانی کا آپریشن، مشتبہ شخص یا جگہ کی خفیہ نگرانی، گھات لگانا، تاک میں رہنا، چھپ کر دیکھنا اور معلومات اکٹھی کرنا
synonyms: Surveillance, Watch, Observation, Vigil, Lookout, Reconnaissance, Monitoring, Shadowing

examples: His mugshot appeared on the front page of every newspaper. The police released the mugshots of all five suspects. She was embarrassed when her mugshot was shared online. The detective compared the witness's description with several mugshots. After the arrest, the officer took his fingerprints and mugshot.
urduMeaning: پولیس کی کھینچی ہوئی تصویر، گرفتاری کے بعد ملزم کے چہرے کی تصویر، پولیس ریکارڈ کے لیے لی گئی شناختی تصویر، مجرم کی شناخت کے لیے کھینچی گئی تصویر، چہرے کی قریبی تصویر، شناختی فوٹو
sindhiMeaning: پوليس وارو فوٽو، گرفتاريءَ بعد ملزم جي چهري جو فوٽو، پوليس رڪارڊ لاءِ ورتل تصوير، مجرم جي سڃاڻپ لاءِ ورتل فوٽو، چهري جو ويجهو فوٽو، شناختي تصوير
synonyms: Police photo, Booking photo, Identification photo, Portrait, Snapshot, Headshot
antonyms: Anonymity, Concealment
englishMeaning: A photograph of a person's face taken by the police after that person has been arrested. A police photograph showing the front and side view of a suspect or criminal. An official photograph kept in police records for identification purposes. Informally, it can also refer to any close-up photograph of a person's face.

antonyms: Yield, Surrender, Give in, Submit, Collapse, Succumb, Break, Give up
urduMeaning: مقابلہ کرنا، برداشت کرنا، سہنا، مقابلہ میں ڈٹ جانا، دباؤ یا حملے کا سامنا کرنا، نہ ٹوٹنا، نہ جھکنا، مضبوطی سے قائم رہنا، مشکلات کا سامنا کرنا، صبر سے جھیلنا
synonyms: Resist, Endure, Bear, Tolerate, Survive, Stand up to, Weather, Hold out, Defy, Brave
sindhiMeaning: مقابلو ڪرڻ، برداشت ڪرڻ، سهڻ، مقابلي ۾ ڪامياب رهڻ، جهيڙي يا دٻاءَ کي برداشت ڪرڻ، نه ٽٽڻ، نه جهڪڻ، مضبوطيءَ سان قائم رهڻ، مشڪلاتن سامهون بيهڻ، صبر سان منهن ڏيڻ
englishMeaning: To resist successfully. To endure. To remain undamaged or unaffected by something. To stand up against attack, pressure, or force without giving way. To bear or tolerate difficult conditions. Used for people, materials, or structures that are strong enough not to be defeated, broken, or harmed by the opposing force, pressure, weather, or hardship they face.
examples: These houses are built to withstand strong earthquakes. The soldiers withstood the enemy attack for many hours. She had to withstand a lot of criticism for her decision. This material can withstand very high temperatures. He could not withstand the pressure and finally resigned.

antonyms: Honest, Straightforward, Sincere, Open, Ethical, Principled, Upright, Honourable, Trustworthy
englishMeaning: Cunning and deceitful, especially in politics or in seeking power. Using clever but dishonest methods. Sly. Manipulative. Unscrupulous. Used to describe a person or behaviour that is willing to use any means, including lies, tricks, or unethical actions, in order to achieve personal goals, especially political or professional success. It comes from the Italian writer Niccolò Machiavelli.
urduMeaning: مکار، چالاک، سیاسی چالبازی کرنے والا، مفاد کے لیے ہر حد سے گزر جانے والا، فریبی، چالبازی سے مقصد حاصل کرنے والا، دو رخا، اخلاق سے بے نیاز، اقتدار کے لیے کچھ بھی کر گزرنے والا
examples: He used Machiavellian tactics to remove his rivals from the company. The novel describes the Machiavellian schemes of a corrupt minister. Her Machiavellian behavior shocked even her closest friends. Some leaders are admired for their Machiavellian skill in politics. He saw a Machiavellian plot behind every appointment.
sindhiMeaning: مڪار، چالباز، سياسي چالبازي وارو، مفاد لاءِ هر حد تائين وڃڻ وارو، فريبي، چالبازيءَ سان مقصد حاصل ڪرڻ وارو، ٻه منهون، اخلاقن کي پاسي ڪندڙ، طاقت لاءِ ڪجهه به ڪرڻ وارو
synonyms: Cunning, Crafty, Sly, Devious, Scheming, Manipulative, Unscrupulous, Deceitful, Underhanded, Calculating
Fair, Impartial, Unbiased, Just, Equitable, Balanced, Objective, Neutral, Nonpartisan, Disinterested
englishMeaning: Fair and impartial. Treating all people or sides equally. Not favouring one side over another. Just. Balanced. Used to describe a person, judgment, treatment, or decision that is fair and shows no bias or favouritism toward any individual, group, or point of view, especially in matters of dispute, judgement, or competition.
examples: The judge is known for his evenhanded approach to every case. The newspaper provided an evenhanded report on the political dispute. As a teacher, she is firm but always evenhanded with her students. We need an evenhanded mediator to resolve this conflict. The committee gave an evenhanded review of all the proposals.
sindhiMeaning: انصاف وارو، غير جانبدار، سڀني سان هڪجهڙو سلوڪ ڪندڙ، طرفداري نه ڪندڙ، منصف مزاج، برابري وارو، ٻنهي پاسن کي يڪسان درجو ڏيندڙ، صحيح فيصلو ڪندڙ، غير متعصب
urduMeaning: منصف، غیر جانبدار، سب کے ساتھ یکساں سلوک کرنے والا، طرفداری نہ کرنے والا، انصاف پسند، برابری کرنے والا، دونوں فریقوں کو یکساں اہمیت دینے والا، صحیح فیصلہ کرنے والا، غیر متعصب
antonyms: Biased, Partial, Unfair, Prejudiced, One-sided, Partisan, Unjust, Discriminatory

synonyms: Upstart, Nouveau riche, Social climber, Arriviste, Newcomer, Self-made man, Johnny-come-lately
examples: He was dismissed as a mere parvenu by the old aristocratic families. The novel mocks the manners of a wealthy parvenu trying to enter high society. Many old families looked down on him as a parvenu. The parvenu spent lavishly to gain social acceptance. She refused to be treated as a parvenu in their circle.
urduMeaning: نوکیسہ، نیا امیر، نیا اعلیٰ طبقے میں شامل ہونے والا، اعلیٰ طبقے میں نیا آیا ہوا لیکن اصل قبولیت سے محروم، نیا مالدار جو اعلیٰ طبقے کی تہذیب نہ رکھتا ہو، دکھاوے والا نوکیسہ
englishMeaning: A person who has recently become rich or socially important but is not fully accepted by others of that class. A social climber. A newly rich person who is considered to lack the manners or culture of the established upper class. Often used in a disapproving way to suggest pretension and lack of refinement.
antonyms: Aristocrat, Blue blood, Old money, Patrician, Noble, Long-established
sindhiMeaning: نئون امير، نئون اوچي طبقي ۾ شامل ٿيندڙ، اوچي طبقي ۾ نئون آيل پر اصل قبوليت نه ماڻيندڙ، نئون مالدار جيڪو اصل اوچي طبقي وارن وانگر تهذيب نه رکي، ڏيک ويک وارو نئون امير

urduMeaning: نگلنا، حلق سے نیچے اُتارنا، پیٹ میں اُتارنا، گھونٹ بھرنا، کسی بات کو بغیر سوال کے مان لینا، کسی جھوٹی یا کڑوی بات کو قبول کر لینا، جذبات کو دبا لینا، ابابیل (پرندہ)
antonyms: Spit out, Reject, Disbelieve, Question, Disgorge, Eject, Refuse
synonyms: Gulp, Devour, Ingest, Consume, Engulf, Accept, Believe, Endure, Suppress
englishMeaning: To cause food or drink to pass from the mouth into the stomach. To make a movement in the throat as if doing this, especially because of nervousness or strong emotion. To accept or believe something without questioning, especially something untrue or unpleasant. To suppress or hold back feelings. A small migratory bird with a forked tail and long pointed wings.
examples: He swallowed the medicine with a glass of water. She swallowed hard before answering the difficult question. I cannot swallow such an obvious lie. He had to swallow his pride and apologize to her. A swallow built its nest under the roof of our old house.
sindhiMeaning: ڳڙڪائڻ، نڙيءَ کان هيٺ لاهڻ، پيٽ ۾ لاهڻ، ڳل ۾ گهٽ ڪرڻ، نگلڻ، ڪنهن ڳالهه تي بنا سوال جواب جي يقين ڪري وٺڻ، ڪنهن ڪوڙي يا ڪؤڙي ڳالهه کي قبول ڪري وٺڻ، احساسن کي روڪڻ، ابابيل (پکي)

antonyms: Law-abiding, Responsible, Dutiful, Conscientious, Obedient, Reliable, Punctual, Upright
synonyms: Offender, Criminal, Wrongdoer, Lawbreaker, Hooligan, Negligent, Defaulter, Truant, Miscreant
sindhiMeaning: مجرم، خاص ڪري نوجوان مجرم، قانون شڪن، فرض کان غافل، ذميواري ادا نه ڪرڻ وارو، ضابطي جي خلاف هلندڙ، بقايا ادا نه ڪندڙ، بدچلن نوجوان، بگڙيل، اخلاقي طور تي خراب
urduMeaning: مجرم، خاص طور پر نوجوان مجرم، قانون شکن، فرض سے غافل، ذمہ داری ادا نہ کرنے والا، ضوابط کی خلاف ورزی کرنے والا، بقایا ادا نہ کرنے والا، بدچلن نوجوان، بگڑا ہوا، اخلاقی طور پر خراب
englishMeaning: A person, especially a young one, who behaves in an illegal or antisocial way. Failing in one's duty. Guilty of a minor crime or misdeed. Overdue in payment. A young offender. Behaviour, accounts, or duties that are neglected, unpaid, or in violation of the law.
examples: The school has started a special program for juvenile delinquents. He was a delinquent in his teens but later turned his life around. The bank sent a notice about her delinquent account. They were delinquent in paying their taxes for two years. Several delinquents were caught vandalizing the public park.

He has become very uppity since his promotion. She gave me an uppity look when I asked the question. Don't get uppity with your elders. The customer was rude and uppity with the waiter. I can't stand his uppity attitude in meetings.
synonyms: Arrogant, Snobbish, Haughty, Conceited, Stuck-up, Self-important, Pompous, Cocky, Pretentious
englishMeaning: Behaving as if one is more important than one really is. Arrogant. Self-important. Snobbish. Acting in a way that shows you think you are superior to others. Informally used in a disapproving way to describe someone, especially of lower or junior status, who behaves with too much pride, attitude, or independence.
urduMeaning: بڑائی جتانے والا، مغرور، خود پسند، اپنے آپ کو دوسروں سے بڑا سمجھنے والا، تکبر کرنے والا، نخرے دکھانے والا، چھوٹے درجے کا ہو کر بھی مغرور ہونے والا، اکڑ دکھانے والا، گستاخ
antonyms: Humble, Modest, Down-to-earth, Unassuming, Polite, Respectful, Meek
sindhiMeaning: وڏ ماڻهپ ڏيکاريندڙ، مغرور، ٿلهي ٿلهي ڳالهائيندڙ، پاڻ کي ٻين کان وڌيڪ سمجهندڙ، تکبر وارو، نخرا ڪندڙ، ٿوري درجي وارو پر مغرور ٿيندڙ، اڏول، گستاخ

englishMeaning: A thing presented or offered to God or a god. A religious offering. The act of making such an offering. A charitable gift or donation to a religious institution. Used especially in religious contexts for sacrifices, gifts, or acts of devotion offered to a deity, including bread and wine in the Christian Eucharist.
urduMeaning: نذرانہ، چڑھاوا، خدا یا دیوتا کے نام پر پیش کی گئی چیز، مذہبی نذرانہ، عبادت گاہ میں پیش کیا گیا تحفہ، صدقہ، خیرات، عقیدت کے طور پر پیش کی گئی چیز
antonyms: Withholding, Refusal, Denial, Retention
synonyms: Offering, Sacrifice, Donation, Tribute, Gift, Contribution, Dedication, Presentation
sindhiMeaning: نذرانو، چڙهاوو، خدا يا ديوتا جي نالي تي پيش ڪيل شيءِ، مذهبي نذرانو، عبادتگاهه ۾ پيش ڪيل تحفو، صدقو، خيرات، عقيدت جي نشاني طور پيش ڪيل شيءِ
examples: The priests received many oblations from the worshippers. Bread and wine are offered as oblations in the church. Devotees brought flowers and fruits as oblations to the temple. The ancient text describes the proper way of making oblations. Their oblation was accepted with great respect.

sindhiMeaning: درگاهه، مزار، مقدس جاءِ، عبادت گاهه، ولي يا بزرگ جي قبر تي ٺهيل جاءِ، تبرڪات رکڻ جي جاءِ، عقيدت جو مرڪز، زيارت گاهه
urduMeaning: درگاہ، مزار، مقدس جگہ، عبادت گاہ، بزرگ یا ولی کی قبر پر بنی ہوئی جگہ، تبرکات رکھنے کا مقام، عقیدت کا مرکز، زیارت گاہ
antonyms: Profane place, Secular site, Ordinary building
synonyms: Sanctuary, Temple, Tomb, Mausoleum, Memorial, Holy place, Altar, Reliquary
examples: Thousands of devotees visit the shrine every year. The old shrine stands on top of the hill. She lit a candle at the shrine of her favorite saint. The room was kept as a shrine to his late mother's memory. The new shrine was built in honor of the great poet.
englishMeaning: A place regarded as holy because of its associations with a divine being, a saint, or a sacred event. A building or structure built in honor of a holy person. A container or receptacle for sacred relics. A place where people come to worship, pray, or pay respect. It can also refer informally to a place dedicated to a person or thing one greatly admires.

examples: Let's have a quickie coffee before the meeting starts. Can I ask you a quickie before you go? They got married in a quickie ceremony at the courthouse. I just need a quickie answer; it's not a long discussion. The journalist wrote a quickie article to meet the deadline.
sindhiMeaning: تڪڙي ڪم، جلدي ٿيندڙ ڳالهه، ٿوري وقت ۾ ٿيل ڪم، تڪڙو شراب جو دور، تڪڙي ملاقات، تڪڙو سوال يا ڪم، مختصر ۽ تڪڙو عمل، غير رسمي تڪڙي ڳالهه
synonyms: Brief moment, Short task, Fast one, Speedy job, Rapid affair, Snap, Flash
antonyms: Lengthy affair, Long process, Prolonged activity, Drawn-out task
urduMeaning: جلدی کیا گیا کام، تیز کام، تھوڑے وقت میں ہونے والی بات، جلدی کا پیگ، جلدی کی ملاقات، جلدی سوال یا کام، مختصر اور تیز عمل، غیر رسمی تیز بات
englishMeaning: Something done or made quickly. A short, hurried activity. A quick drink, meeting, question, or task that takes very little time. Informally, a brief act of sexual intercourse. Used in casual speech to describe anything that is brief, fast, and informal in nature.

examples: The officer placed handcuffs on the suspect and led him to the car. The thief was led away in handcuffs. New regulations have handcuffed small businesses. The judge ordered that the prisoner be handcuffed during the trial. He felt handcuffed by the strict rules of his job.
englishMeaning: A pair of lockable linked metal rings used by the police to fasten a prisoner's wrists together. To put handcuffs on someone. To restrain or limit the freedom or ability of a person to act. Figuratively, anything that prevents someone from doing what they want or need to do.
synonyms: Manacle, Shackle, Restrain, Bind, Fetter, Chain, Cuff, Restrict, Hamper
sindhiMeaning: هٿڪڙي، لوهي ڪڙا جيڪي مجرم جي هٿن ۾ پوليس وجهي، هٿڪڙي وجهڻ، گرفتار ڪرڻ، آزاديءَ کي محدود ڪرڻ، روڪڻ، ڪنهن کي عمل کان روڪڻ، بند ڪرڻ، پابند ڪرڻ
antonyms: Free, Release, Unshackle, Liberate, Loosen, Unbind, Unchain
urduMeaning: ہتھکڑی، لوہے کے کڑے جو پولیس مجرم کے ہاتھوں میں ڈالتی ہے، ہتھکڑی لگانا، گرفتار کرنا، آزادی کو محدود کرنا، روکنا، کسی کو عمل سے روکنا، بند کرنا، پابند کرنا

examples: Can you enlighten me about the new company policy? The teacher tried to enlighten the students on the importance of honesty. His lecture enlightened the audience on environmental issues. She wrote the book to enlighten people about mental health. Travel can enlighten one's view of the world.
urduMeaning: روشن خیال بنانا، علم دینا، سمجھانا، آگاہ کرنا، جہالت یا غلط فہمی سے آزاد کرنا، روحانی آگاہی دینا، ذہن کھولنا، حقیقت سمجھانا، تعلیم دینا، رہنمائی کرنا
synonyms: Inform, Educate, Instruct, Illuminate, Teach, Clarify, Explain, Awaken, Edify, Apprise
antonyms: Confuse, Mislead, Mystify, Bewilder, Obscure, Deceive, Befuddle, Keep in the dark
englishMeaning: To give someone greater knowledge or understanding about a subject or situation. To inform. To explain. To free someone from ignorance, prejudice, or false belief. To give spiritual insight. Used both for sharing information that clarifies something and for the deeper sense of gaining wisdom or spiritual awareness.
sindhiMeaning: روشن ضمير بڻائڻ، علم ڏيڻ، سمجهائڻ، آگاهه ڪرڻ، جهالت يا غلط فهميءَ کان آزاد ڪرڻ، روحاني آگاهي ڏيڻ، ذهن کوليو، حقيقت سمجهائڻ، تعليم ڏيڻ، رهنمائي ڪرڻ

englishMeaning: Ordinary. Average. Not special or unusual in any way. Lacking distinction. Used to describe people, things, products, or experiences that are common, standard, and have nothing remarkable or impressive about them. It often carries a slightly negative or dismissive tone, suggesting that the subject is unimpressive.
antonyms: Exceptional, Extraordinary, Remarkable, Unique, Outstanding, Special, Distinctive, Rare
urduMeaning: عام، معمولی، عام درجے کا، کوئی خاص نہیں، کسی خاصیت کے بغیر، روزمرہ کا، عام قسم کا، غیر معیاری نہیں مگر اعلیٰ بھی نہیں، سادہ، بغیر کسی نیا پن کے
examples: The hotel we stayed in was just a run of the mill place. He is not a star player; he is a run of the mill performer. The movie has a run of the mill story with no surprises. This is a run of the mill restaurant with average food. Her writing style is interesting and not at all run of the mill.
synonyms: Ordinary, Average, Common, Standard, Mediocre, Unremarkable, Typical, Everyday, Mundane, Routine
sindhiMeaning: عام، معمولي، عام درجي جو، خاص نه، بنا ڪنهن خاصيت جي، روزمره وارو، عام قسم جو، اعليٰ نه، سادو، بنا ڪنهن نواڻ جي

urduMeaning: حیوانی، جانوروں جیسا، وحشی، بنیادی جسمانی خواہشات پر مبنی، ابتدائی، فطری، عقل کے بجائے جذبے پر چلنے والا، جنگلی، بے قابو، جذباتی اور بے لگام
sindhiMeaning: جانورن جهڙو، حيواني، وحشي، بنيادي خواهشن تي هلندڙ، ابتدائي، فطري، عقل کان وڌيڪ جذبي تي هلندڙ، جهنگلي، بي ضابطو، جذباتي ۽ بي قابو
antonyms: Civilized, Refined, Cultured, Rational, Restrained, Humane, Gentle, Disciplined
synonyms: Bestial, Brutal, Wild, Savage, Primitive, Instinctive, Feral, Beastly, Untamed
examples: He let out an animalistic roar when he won the match. The crowd was driven by an almost animalistic excitement. There was something animalistic in the way he attacked his food. The film shows the animalistic side of human nature. Their fight was savage and animalistic.
englishMeaning: Characteristic of or resembling an animal. Driven by basic physical urges rather than reason. Wild. Primitive. Instinctive. Used to describe behaviour, sounds, or feelings that are seen as belonging more to animals than to civilized humans, often involving aggression, passion, fear, or raw physical desire.

synonyms: Torment, Torture, Agonize, Distress, Afflict, Pain, Rack, Anguish, Harrow

englishMeaning: A small, mischievous, and often grotesque creature from folklore, typically depicted as malevolent or troublesome. A mythical being commonly portrayed in fairy tales and fantasy fiction as living underground or in hidden places. Used to describe a person, especially in a playful or insulting way, who behaves in a sly or troublesome manner. A creature often associated with trickery, greed, or minor mischief in stories and games.
examples: In the story, a mischievous goblin guarded the entrance to the cave.  The video game featured armies of goblins attacking the player's castle.  Children love stories about goblins hiding treasure in dark forests.  The illustration depicted the goblin as small, green, and sharp-toothed.  Local folklore warned travelers about goblins lurking near the old bridge.

antonyms: Angel, Fairy godmother, Hero, Guardian, Benevolent spirit
sindhiMeaning: بدروح، شيطان جهڙو ننڍڙو مخلوق جو لوڪ ڪهاڻين ۾ شرارتي ۽ خطرناڪ ڏيکاريو ويندو آهي، فينٽسي ڪهاڻين جو ڪردار

synonyms: Intuition, Impulse, Inclination, Reflex, Gut feeling
englishMeaning: An innate, natural tendency or impulse that prompts behavior without the need for conscious thought or learning. A natural ability or capacity to know or do something without prior instruction or experience. A strong, often automatic feeling that something is true or that a particular action should be taken. The inherent behavior patterns seen in animals that drive survival-related actions such as feeding, reproduction, or self-defense.
sindhiMeaning: فطري جذبو، پيدائشي بصيرت، بنا سوچ سمجهه جي خود بخود ٿيندڙ عمل يا احساس، جانورن ۽ انسانن جي فطري رويو
examples: Her instinct told her something was wrong even before she saw the damage.  Animals rely on instinct to find food and avoid predators.  His first instinct was to call for help immediately.  Maternal instinct often drives mothers to protect their children at all costs.  Experienced pilots develop strong instincts for handling emergencies.
urduMeaning: فطری جذبہ، پیدائشی بصیرت، بغیر سوچے سمجھے خود بخود ہونے والا عمل یا احساس، جانوروں اور انسانوں کا فطری رویہ
antonyms: Reason, Logic, Deliberation, Calculation, Analysis

synonyms: Worn, Tattered, Ragged, Strained, Threadbare
examples: The old rope was frayed and looked dangerous to use for climbing.  Months of stress had left his nerves completely frayed.  She noticed the frayed edges of the antique tablecloth.  Their friendship became frayed after the heated argument.  The frayed cable needed to be replaced before it caused an accident.
sindhiMeaning: ڦاٿل، ڪپڙي يا رسي جون چيونون ڍري ٿي ويون، ٿڪل، رشتن يا اعصاب جو دباءُ سبب ڪمزور ٿيڻ، استعمال سبب خراب ٿيل
englishMeaning: Having threads or fibers worn away or loosened at the edge of fabric, rope, or material due to wear or rubbing. Showing signs of strain, exhaustion, or breakdown, especially in relationships, emotions, or nerves. Worn down through repeated use or stress, often to the point of damage. Used to describe something that is becoming weak, unraveled, or close to breaking.
urduMeaning: پھٹا ہوا، کپڑے یا رسی کے تار ڈھیلے ہو جانا، تھکا ہوا، تعلقات یا اعصاب کا دباؤ کی وجہ سے کمزور ہونا، استعمال کی وجہ سے خراب ہونا
antonyms: Intact, Smooth, New, Sturdy, Unworn
Strengthen, Mend, Repair, Calm, Resolve
sindhiMeaning: ڦٽڻ، ڪناري کان ڍري ٿيڻ، تڪرار يا جنگ جو منظر، اعصاب يا رشتن جو ڪمزور ٿيڻ، جوش سان جنگ يا مقابلي ۾ شامل ٿيڻ
synonyms: Unravel, Wear, Strain, Conflict, Struggle
urduMeaning: پھٹنا، کنارے سے ڈھیلا ہونا، تنازعہ یا لڑائی کا منظر، اعصاب یا تعلقات کا کمزور ہونا، جوش سے لڑائی یا مقابلے میں شامل ہونا
examples: The edges of the carpet began to fray after years of foot traffic.  Tempers began to fray as the negotiations dragged on for hours.  Several new candidates have entered the political fray ahead of the election.  Her patience started to fray after the third delay.  The two companies were drawn into a bitter legal fray over the contract.
englishMeaning: To cause fabric, rope, or material to become worn or unravel at the edges through rubbing or use. A situation involving conflict, argument, or competitive struggle, especially one that is intense or chaotic. To become weakened, strained, or damaged, especially in relation to nerves, emotions, or relationships. To enter into or join a fight, conflict, or competitive struggle.

antonyms: Blush, Flush, Redden, Darken, Color
urduMeaning: رنگ اڑ جانا، زرد پڑ جانا، خوف سے پیلا ہونا، سبزیوں کو ہلکا ابالنا
sindhiMeaning: پيلو پوڻ، رنگ اڏارڻ، ڦٽي وڃڻ، ڊپ کان پيلو ٿيڻ، ڀاڄين کي ٿوري دير لاءِ اٻارڻ
examples: He blanched visibly and stumbled back when he heard the terrible news. You always need to blanch the fresh tomatoes briefly before peeling them for the sauce. Her expression blanched with pure terror as the shadow moved deliberately across the dark room. The bitter cold winter air rapidly blanched the sensitive tips of his weary fingers.
englishMeaning: To make white or pale by extracting color. To grow suddenly pale from shock, fear, or a strong negative emotion. To briefly boil food, especially vegetables, in water or steam to shrink them or carefully remove their skins.
synonyms: Pale, Whiten, Drain, Fade, Scald

englishMeaning: To give again. To restore something to its former state or rightful owner. To return or replenish what was taken away or lost.
examples: The king decided to reuter the stolen lands to the poor peasants. We must effectively reuter the missing funds to their original accounts. The charity hopes to reuter dignity and hope to the homeless population. He solemnly promised to reuter the ancient artifact to the museum.

urduMeaning: دوبارہ دینا, بحال کرنا, واپس کرنا, لوٹانا
antonyms: Take, Steal, Confiscate, Remove, Withhold
sindhiMeaning: ٻيهر ڏيڻ, بحال ڪرڻ, واپس ڏيڻ, موٽائڻ, اڳوڻي حالت ۾ آڻڻ

synonyms: Organize, Harmonize, Synchronize, Integrate, Match, Align
sindhiMeaning: هم آهنگ ڪرڻ، ٺيڪ ڪرڻ، گڏجائي ڪم ڪرڻ، ترتيب ڏيڻ، پتو، هم رتبو

To securely negotiate with others in order to happily work together effectively. A distinct set of reliable numbers used to specify the exact geographical location of a specific point.
antonyms: Disorganize, Confuse, Disrupt, Scatter, Mismatch

examples: The chef prepared a gourmet meal for the special guests. She enjoys shopping at gourmet food stores for rare ingredients. He considers himself a gourmet and loves trying new restaurants. The hotel offers gourmet dining options for its affluent visitors.

examples: The new legislation attempts to unprecedent years of standing common law. The supreme court chose to unprecedent the older ruling in favor of modern logic. synonyms: Annul, Nullify, Overturn, Undo, Invalidate
englishMeaning: To remove or destroy a precedent. To act without any prior example or to undo an established norm. To make something unprecedented by stripping away its historical justification or legal basis standing.

synonyms: Insult, Offense, Indignity, Slur, Outrage, Disrespect, Humiliation, Slight, Snub, Provocation

urduMeaning: نقد رقم حاصل کرنا، حصص یا اثاثے بیچ کر پیسے لینا، اکاؤنٹ سے رقم نکالنا، سرمایہ کاری ختم کرنا، جوئے میں جیتی ہوئی رقم لینا، کاروبار سے باہر نکل آنا
englishMeaning: To exchange chips, shares, or assets for cash, especially after gambling or investment. To withdraw money from an account, investment, or pension. To sell one's holdings to take profits. Informally, to take money out and end one's involvement in something. In slang, sometimes used to mean dying.
synonyms: Withdraw, Liquidate, Encash, Redeem, Sell off, Convert, Realise

antonyms: Praised, Commended, Caressed, Stroked, Whispered, Soothed
urduMeaning: کھٹکھٹایا، ہلکی مگر تیز ضرب لگائی، دروازے پر دستک دی، سخت لہجے میں کہا، ڈانٹا، ریپ گیت گایا، تنقید کی
englishMeaning: Past tense of 'rap'. Struck something sharply with a quick, light blow. Knocked sharply on a door or surface to attract attention. Spoke sharply, suddenly, or in a critical manner. Performed rap music by speaking rhythmically over a beat. Informally, criticised or rebuked someone.
examples: She rapped on the door three times before entering. The teacher rapped the desk with his ruler to get attention. The minister was rapped by the press for his careless remarks. The young artist rapped on stage in front of a huge crowd. He rapped out his orders in a sharp voice.
sindhiMeaning: کڙڪايو، تيز ۽ هلڪو ڌڪ هنيو، دروازي تي ٺڪاءُ سان دستڪ ڏني، سخت لفظن ۾ ڳالهايو، ڊاٽ پلٽ ڪئي، ريپ گيت ڳايو، تڪراريو
synonyms: Knocked, Tapped, Struck, Hit, Criticised, Rebuked, Chanted

sindhiMeaning: پنهنجي غلطي جو اقرار ڪرڻ, سچ ڳالهه ظاهر ڪرڻ, لڪيل حقيقت ٻڌائڻ, پنهنجي ذميواري قبول ڪرڻ, ڪنهن ڳالهه کي ايمانداري سان مڃڻ, ڍال جي وچ ۾ افقي ويڪرو پٽو (هيرالڊري ۾)
examples: He finally fessed up about breaking the window. If you made the mistake, just fess and apologize. She decided to fess up before anyone found out the truth. The child fessed to taking the last cookie. The knight's shield displayed a fess in gold. A red fess crossed the center of the coat of arms.
englishMeaning: To confess to doing something wrong. To admit the truth honestly. To reveal a secret or hidden fact. To acknowledge responsibility for a mistake. To tell someone what really happened.  A wide horizontal stripe across the middle of a heraldic shield.
urduMeaning: اپنی غلطی کا اعتراف کرنا, سچ بات مان لینا, چھپی ہوئی حقیقت ظاہر کرنا, اپنی ذمہ داری قبول کرنا, ایمانداری سے حقیقت بیان کرنا, علمِ نشان میں ڈھال کے درمیان ایک چوڑی افقی پٹی
synonyms: Confess, Admit, Acknowledge, Reveal, Disclose, Own up, Come clean, Tell the truth, Declare, Avow
antonyms: Deny, Conceal, Hide, Withhold, Cover up, Disguise, Suppress, Reject, Refuse, Lie
Returning, Restoring, Giving back, Protection, Safeguarding, Honesty
sindhiMeaning: چوري، گهر ۾ گهڙي چوري ڪرڻ، ڌاڙو، رات جو لڪي چوريءَ لاءِ گهر ۾ گهڙڻ، نقب زني، ڪنهن جي ملڪيت ۾ غير قانوني داخلا
examples: There has been a sharp rise in burglary cases in the city. The police arrested two men for the burglary at the jewellery shop. Their house was the target of a burglary last week. He was sentenced to five years in prison for burglary. The insurance policy covers loss caused by burglary.
synonyms: Theft, Robbery, Housebreaking, Break-in, Larceny, Stealing, Looting
englishMeaning: The crime of illegally entering a building, usually a house or shop, with the intention of stealing. The act of breaking into premises to commit theft or another serious offence. A criminal offence in which a person enters another's property unlawfully. Housebreaking for the purpose of robbery.
urduMeaning: چوری، نقب زنی، گھر میں گھس کر چوری کرنا، ڈاکہ، کسی عمارت میں غیر قانونی داخلہ، رات کے وقت چوری کی واردات
سسلی سے متعلق، سسلی جزیرے کا باشندہ، سسلی کی زبان یا بولی، سسلی کی ثقافت یا کھانوں سے متعلق، اطالوی جزیرے سسلی کا فرد
antonyms: Non-Sicilian, Mainland, Foreign, Unrelated
synonyms: Of Sicily, Mediterranean, Italian (regional), Islander
englishMeaning: Relating to Sicily, the largest island in the Mediterranean Sea, situated to the south of mainland Italy. A native or inhabitant of Sicily. The dialect or language spoken in Sicily. Often used in reference to Sicilian culture, cuisine, or the famous Sicilian Mafia.
examples: He is proud of his Sicilian heritage. The restaurant serves authentic Sicilian dishes. She is studying the Sicilian dialect for her thesis. Many famous films have been made about Sicilian families. The Sicilian coastline is one of the most beautiful in Europe.
sindhiMeaning: سسليءَ سان لاڳاپيل، سسلي ٻيٽ جو رهواسي، سسلي ٻيٽ جي زبان يا ٻولي، سسلي جي ثقافت يا کاڌي سان واسطو، اطالوي ٻيٽ سسلي جو فرد

urduMeaning: کسی چیز یا شخص کے خیال میں کھویا ہوا، ذہن پر چھایا ہوا، کسی سوچ یا خواہش کا غلام، انتہائی شوقین، دیوانہ، کسی پر مکمل طور پر جذب
englishMeaning: Completely preoccupied with someone or something to an unhealthy degree. Constantly thinking about a particular person, idea, or activity so that one cannot focus on anything else. Dominated or filled with a continuous and overpowering thought, desire, or emotion. Strongly attached to or fixated on something.
antonyms: Indifferent, Uninterested, Detached, Unconcerned, Apathetic, Disinterested
synonyms: Preoccupied, Fixated, Consumed, Infatuated, Gripped, Possessed, Engrossed, Hooked
examples: She is obsessed with cleanliness and washes her hands constantly. He became obsessed with the idea of becoming a famous singer. Many teenagers are obsessed with social media these days. The detective was obsessed with solving the old murder case. He is completely obsessed with football.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ڳالهه يا شخص جي خيال ۾ کوئجي وڃڻ، ذهن تي حاوي ٿيل، ڪنهن سوچ يا خواهش جو غلام بڻجي وڃڻ، ڌيان هڪ ئي شيءِ تي مرڪوز هجڻ، ديوانگيءَ جي حد تائين شوقين

synonyms: Messenger, Precursor, Harbinger, Forerunner, Sign, Omen, Announce, Proclaim
examples: The blooming of crocuses is a herald of spring. The article heralded a new era in cancer research. The king's herald announced the royal decree to the townspeople. Dark clouds on the horizon often herald an approaching storm. He was heralded as the greatest writer of his generation.
englishMeaning: An official messenger bringing news. A person or thing viewed as a sign that something is about to happen. To be a sign that something is about to happen; to announce or acclaim.
urduMeaning: قاصد، نقیب، منادی کرنے والا، پیش خیمہ، کسی چیز کی آمد کا اعلان کرنا
sindhiMeaning: پيشرو، قاصد، نياپو آڻيندڙ، اعلان ڪندڙ، اطلاع ڏيندڙ، ڪنهن شيءِ جي اچڻ جو نشان
antonyms: Conceal, Hide, Suppress, Withhold, Keep secret

englishMeaning: To involve something as a necessary or inevitable part or consequence. To impose, involve, or imply as a necessary accompaniment or result.
antonyms: Exclude, Omit, Preclude, Forgo, Waive, Obviate
urduMeaning: مستلزم ہونا، لازم کرنا، ضروری ہونا، شامل ہونا، تقاضا کرنا
synonyms: Involve, Necessitate, Require, Demand, Incur, Imply, Cause, Result in
sindhiMeaning: ضروري هجڻ، لازمي هجڻ، نتيجي طور پيدا ٿيڻ، شامل هجڻ، تقاضا ڪرڻ
examples: The project will entail considerable expense and effort. A leadership position entails a great deal of responsibility. His decision to move abroad would entail leaving his friends and family behind. What does the new job actually entail? The journey entailed a long and tiring bus ride through the mountains.

englishMeaning: Lacking cilia or hair-like projections on the surface of a cell or organism.  A scientific term used mainly in biology and zoology to describe a cell, tissue, or organism that does not have cilia, which are tiny hair-like structures used for movement or for moving fluids across a surface.
urduMeaning: بغیر سیلیا (بال نما باریک ساختوں) والا، جس میں سیلیا موجود نہ ہوں, حیاتیات میں استعمال ہونے والی اصطلاح ہے جو ایسے خلیے  بافت یا جاندار کو ظاہر کرتی ہے جس میں سیلیا یعنی باریک بال نما ساختیں موجود نہ ہوں
antonyms: Ciliated, Hairy, Flagellated (in some biological contexts, though flagella and cilia are different structures) Bearing cilia
sindhiMeaning: بغير سيليا (وارن جهڙين ننڍين بناوتن) وارو، جنهن ۾ سيليا موجود نه هجن, حياتيات ۾ استعمال ٿيندڙ اصطلاح آهي جيڪو اهڙي سيل  عضوي يا جاندار لاءِ استعمال ٿيندو آهي جنهن ۾ سيليا يعني ننڍڙا وارن جهڙا حصا موجود نه هجن
synonyms: Non-ciliated, Cilia-free, Devoid of cilia, Without cilia, Unciliated
examples: The researcher identified an aciliate cell under the microscope. Some microorganisms are naturally aciliate and rely on other methods of movement. The specimen appeared aciliate, showing no visible hair-like structures. Scientists compared the aciliate organism with closely related ciliated species.

urduMeaning: راضی کرنا، منانا، صلح کرانا، تسلی دینا، میل ملاپ کرنا, ناراضی دور کرنا, کسی ناراض یا مخالف شخص کو راضی کرنا  اس کی ناراضی کم کرنا  یا اختلاف ختم کرکے صلح اور اچھے تعلقات قائم کرنا, یہ کام نرمی  سمجھداری یا مصالحت کے ذریعے کیا جاتا ہے
antonyms: Provoke, Alienate, Antagonize, Incite, Irritate
synonyms: Appease, Placate, Pacify, Mollify, Reconcile, Soothe
englishMeaning: To stop someone from being angry or intensely discontented. To sincerely act as a capable mediator or neutral peacemaker. To proactively overcome the deep distrust or bitter hostility of someone. To tactfully win over or gracefully gain goodwill through intentionally pleasing, kind acts.
sindhiMeaning: پرچائڻ، راضي ڪرڻ، صلح ڪرائڻ، ٺاهه ڪرائڻ، دلجاءِ ڏيڻ, ناراضگي ختم ڪرڻ, ڪنهن ناراض يا ڏکيل ماڻهو کي پرچائڻ  راضي ڪرڻ  يا اختلاف ختم ڪري صلح ۽ هم آهنگي پيدا ڪرڻ, اهو عمل نرمي  سمجهداري يا مناسب رعايت ذريعي ڪيو ويندو آهي
examples: The experienced duty manager tried frantically to conciliate the incredibly angry customer by quickly offering a full cash refund. He actively made a deeply genuine attempt to eventually conciliate with his stubbornly estranged younger brother. Her perfectly calm words effectively helped to peacefully conciliate the bitterly opposing factions in the heated live debate. The skilled foreign diplomat's main noble goal was to properly conciliate the hostile rival nations and permanently prevent a devastating war.

englishMeaning: A generous reward. A payment offered for capturing a person or animal or for completing a task. A plentiful supply or abundance of something. Generosity freely given. Historically, money paid by a government to encourage recruitment or production.
urduMeaning: انعام، صلہ، اجر، فراوانی، کثرت، سخاوت، کسی شخص کو پکڑنے یا کوئی خاص کام مکمل کرنے پر دی جانے والی رقم، کسی نعمت یا پیداوار کی بہت زیادہ اور وافر مقدار
antonyms: Penalty, Punishment, Scarcity, Shortage, Lack, Dearth, Meagerness
synonyms: Reward, Prize, Premium, Bonus, Payment, Abundance, Plenty, Profusion, Generosity
sindhiMeaning: انعام، اجورو، فراواني، گهڻائي، سخاوت، ڪنهن شخص کي پڪڙڻ يا ڪو خاص ڪم پورو ڪرڻ تي ڏنو ويندڙ انعام، ڪنهن نعمت يا پيداوار جي تمام وڏي ۽ ڀرپور مقدار
examples: The police offered a bounty for information leading to the fugitive's arrest. The garden provided a rich bounty of fresh vegetables. We shared the autumn bounty with our neighbors. Her family was grateful for nature's bounty. The company paid a bounty to employees who recruited skilled workers.

His sudden apology was merely a ploy to regain her trust. The discount was a clever marketing ploy. She recognized the question as a ploy to distract her from the main issue. The team used a defensive ploy to slow the game. Pretending to leave was part of his negotiating ploy.
synonyms: Tactic, Strategy, Maneuver, Scheme, Ruse, Trick, Device, Stratagem, Gambit
antonyms: Honesty, Candor, Frankness, Directness, Sincerity, Openness
englishMeaning: A cunning plan or action designed to gain an advantage. A deliberate tactic used to distract, persuade, deceive, or outmaneuver someone. A strategic move in a game, argument, negotiation, or competitive situation.
urduMeaning: چال، تدبیر، حکمتِ عملی، حربہ، فریب، فائدہ حاصل کرنے یا کسی کو بھٹکانے، قائل کرنے یا دھوکا دینے کے لیے جان بوجھ کر اختیار کیا گیا منصوبہ یا قدم
sindhiMeaning: چال، ترڪيب، حڪمت عملي، اٽڪل، فريب، فائدو حاصل ڪرڻ يا ڪنهن کي ڌيان هٽائڻ، قائل ڪرڻ يا دوکو ڏيڻ لاءِ ڄاڻي واڻي اختيار ڪيل منصوبو يا قدم

examples: The child is finicky about vegetables. This old printer is finicky and jams unless the paper is perfectly aligned. She is finicky about the quality of her coffee. The recipe is finicky, so measure every ingredient carefully. Our cat can be extremely finicky at mealtimes.
synonyms: Fussy, Fastidious, Particular, Picky, Choosy, Exacting, Persnickety, Delicate, Temperamental
antonyms: Easygoing, Undemanding, Uncritical, Flexible, Accommodating, Indiscriminate
englishMeaning: Hard to please. Excessively particular about small details. Requiring careful handling or precise conditions to work properly. Fussy about food, appearance, quality, or procedure.
sindhiMeaning: نخريلو، ڏکيو راضي ٿيندڙ، تمام چونڊ ڪندڙ، ننڍين ڳالهين بابت حد کان وڌيڪ خاص خيال رکندڙ، اهڙي شيءِ جيڪا صحيح ڪم ڪرڻ لاءِ تمام احتياط يا مخصوص حالتون گهري
urduMeaning: نخریلا، مشکل سے راضی ہونے والا، بہت چنندہ، معمولی تفصیلات کے بارے میں حد سے زیادہ محتاط، ایسی چیز جسے درست کام کرنے کے لیے خاص دیکھ بھال یا مخصوص حالات درکار ہوں

synonyms: Revenge, Vindicate, Retaliate for, Requite, Redress, Get even for
englishMeaning: To punish or harm someone in return for an injury or wrong. To obtain justice or satisfaction on behalf of oneself or another person. To retaliate for a defeat, insult, or injustice.
sindhiMeaning: بدلو وٺڻ، انتقام وٺڻ، ڪنهن ظلم يا نقصان جي عيوض سزا ڏيڻ، پنهنجي يا ٻئي ڪنهن سان ٿيل ناانصافي جو حساب وٺي انصاف يا تسلي حاصل ڪرڻ
examples: She vowed to avenge her brother's death. The team avenged last year's defeat with a decisive victory. He wanted to avenge the insult but chose to remain calm. The hero returns to avenge the villagers who were attacked. Justice, not anger, should guide anyone seeking to avenge a wrong.
urduMeaning: بدلہ لینا، انتقام لینا، کسی ظلم یا نقصان کے عوض سزا دینا، اپنے یا کسی دوسرے کے ساتھ ہونے والی ناانصافی کا حساب لے کر انصاف یا تسلی حاصل کرنا
antonyms: Forgive, Pardon, Excuse, Overlook, Absolve, Reconcile

sindhiMeaning: اختيار جو دائرو، ذميواري جو ميدان، عمل جي حد، ڪنهن شخص يا اداري جي اختيار، ڄاڻ يا سرگرمي هيٺ ايندڙ معاملا، ڪنهن قانون يا عهدي جي لاڳو ٿيڻ جي حد
urduMeaning: دائرۂ اختیار، ذمہ داری کا میدان، حدودِ کار، کسی شخص یا ادارے کے اختیار، علم یا سرگرمی میں آنے والے معاملات، کسی قانون یا عہدے کے اطلاق کی حد
antonyms: Exclusion, Limitation, Restriction, Irrelevance, Outside authority
englishMeaning: The range of authority, responsibility, knowledge, or activity covered by a person or organization. The scope within which something operates or is considered. The matters that a law, document, or official position applies to.
synonyms: Scope, Range, Province, Domain, Remit, Jurisdiction, Authority, Ambit, Sphere
examples: Budget approval falls within the committee's purview. Medical advice is outside my professional purview. The new regulations broaden the agency's purview. Hiring decisions are under the purview of the human resources director. The court examined whether the dispute came within its purview.

sindhiMeaning: صفائي ڪندڙ، عمارت جو سنڀاليندڙ، چوڪيدار، اهڙو ملازم جيڪو اسڪول، آفيس يا ٻي عمارت جي صفائي، معمولي مرمت، حفاظت ۽ روزاني سار سنڀال ڪري
antonyms: Occupant, Tenant, Visitor, Litterer, Vandal
urduMeaning: صفائی کرنے والا، عمارت کا نگران، چوکیدار، ایسا ملازم جو اسکول، دفتر یا دوسری عمارت کی صفائی، معمولی مرمت، حفاظت اور روزمرہ دیکھ بھال کرے
englishMeaning: A person employed to clean and maintain a building. A caretaker responsible for minor repairs, security, heating, supplies, and general upkeep. In some varieties of English, a doorkeeper or building custodian.
examples: The janitor cleaned the classrooms after the students left. We asked the janitor to repair the broken door handle. The building's janitor keeps the hallways spotless. A janitor unlocked the gym early in the morning. She worked as a school janitor for twenty years.
synonyms: Custodian, Caretaker, Cleaner, Maintenance worker, Porter, Building superintendent

sindhiMeaning: کنيل، کڻي ويل، برداشت ڪيل، سهيل، سهارو ڏنل، پيدا ڪيل، جنم ڏنل، هوا، پاڻي، رت يا جيتن وسيلي پکڙيل، خرچ يا ذميواري طور قبول ڪيل، هي لفظ بيئر فعل جو ماضي وارو مڪمل روپ آهي
urduMeaning: اٹھایا گیا، لے جایا گیا، برداشت کیا گیا، سہارا دیا گیا، پیدا کیا گیا، جنم دیا گیا، ہوا، پانی، خون یا کیڑوں کے ذریعے پھیلایا گیا، خرچ یا ذمہ داری کے طور پر قبول کیا گیا، یہ بیئر فعل کی ماضی کی تکمیلی شکل ہے
synonyms: Carried, Transported, Supported, Sustained, Endured, Tolerated, Produced, Conveyed, Paid
examples: The cost will be borne by the company. She had borne the hardship with remarkable courage. The injured climber was borne down the mountain on a stretcher. Mosquito-borne diseases are common in tropical regions. The trees had borne fruit earlier than expected.
englishMeaning: Carried or transported. Supported or sustained. Endured or tolerated. Produced or given birth to. Carried or spread by a particular agent such as air, water, insects, or blood. Accepted or paid as a cost or responsibility. The past participle of bear and normally used with an auxiliary verb.
antonyms: Dropped, Abandoned, Rejected, Avoided, Resisted, Unendured

sindhiMeaning: ذمواري، فرض، بار، ڪنهن ڳالهه کي ثابت ڪرڻ، سمجهائڻ يا ڪم پورو ڪرڻ جي ذميواري جيڪا ڪنهن خاص شخص يا ڌر تي هجي
examples: The onus is on the applicant to provide accurate documents. In court, the onus of proof lies with the prosecution. Parents should not place the entire onus on teachers. The new policy puts the onus on companies to protect customer data. He accepted the onus of resolving the dispute.
englishMeaning: A duty or responsibility. The burden of proving, explaining, or accomplishing something. An obligation placed on a particular person or group.
synonyms: Burden, Responsibility, Duty, Obligation, Liability, Charge, Load
antonyms: Freedom, Exemption, Immunity, Release, Relief, Discharge
urduMeaning: ذمہ داری، فرض، بوجھ، کسی بات کو ثابت کرنے، سمجھانے یا کام مکمل کرنے کی ذمہ داری جو کسی خاص شخص یا فریق پر عائد ہو

sindhiMeaning: ساراهه جوڳو، واکاڻ لائق، قابلِ تعريف، اهڙو عمل، ڪوشش يا رويو جيڪو سٺائي، همت يا اعليٰ معيار سبب تعريف ۽ عزت جو مستحق هجي
examples: Her commitment to helping the poor is commendable. The firefighters showed commendable courage. He made a commendable effort despite limited resources. The students maintained a commendable level of discipline. Your honesty in admitting the mistake was commendable.
englishMeaning: Deserving praise or approval. Worthy of admiration because of good conduct, effort, courage, or quality. Meeting a high moral or practical standard.
synonyms: Praiseworthy, Admirable, Laudable, Meritorious, Exemplary, Creditworthy, Worthy
antonyms: Blameworthy, Disgraceful, Deplorable, Shameful, Reprehensible, Unworthy

گودام، ذخیرہ، ڈپو، بس یا ریلوے اسٹیشن، سامان، ایندھن یا گاڑیاں رکھنے اور تقسیم کرنے کی جگہ، فوجی سامان یا رسد محفوظ کرنے کا مرکز
examples: The bus leaves the depot at six every morning. Food supplies were stored in a central depot. The army established a fuel depot near the base. Damaged trains are repaired at the maintenance depot. Please deliver the equipment to the regional depot.
sindhiMeaning: گودام، ذخيرو، ڊپو، بس يا ريلوي اسٽيشن، سامان، ٻارڻ يا گاڏيون رکڻ ۽ ورهائڻ جي جاءِ، فوجي سامان يا رسد محفوظ ڪرڻ جو مرڪز
englishMeaning: A place where goods, equipment, fuel, or vehicles are stored. A station or terminal for buses, trains, or other transport. A military storehouse or supply center. A place from which workers, vehicles, or supplies are dispatched.
synonyms: Warehouse, Storehouse, Repository, Terminal, Station, Yard, Base, Storage facility
antonyms: Destination, Outlet, Retail shop, Disposal site, Emptiness

englishMeaning: A British nobleman ranking below an earl and above a baron. A member of the European nobility holding a rank corresponding to that title. Historically, an official who acted as a deputy to a count.
antonyms: Commoner, Peasant, Subject, Non-noble
urduMeaning: وائکاؤنٹ، برطانوی امرا میں ارل سے نیچے اور بیرن سے اوپر درجے کا شخص، یورپی اشرافیہ میں اسی درجے کا لقب رکھنے والا، تاریخی طور پر کاؤنٹ کا نائب
synonyms: Nobleman, Peer, Aristocrat, Lord, Dignitary, Count's deputy
sindhiMeaning: وائڪائونٽ، برطانوي اميرن ۾ ارل کان هيٺ ۽ بيرن کان مٿي درجي وارو شخص، يورپي اميرن ۾ ساڳئي درجي جو لقب رکندڙ، تاريخي طور ڪائونٽ جو نائب
examples: The viscount inherited the title from his father. A viscount ranks above a baron in the British peerage. The novel tells the story of a young viscount. The viscount attended the ceremony with other members of the nobility. Historically, the viscount administered land on behalf of the count.

sindhiMeaning: نائب، مددگار، قائم مقام، نمائندو، ڪنهن اعليٰ آفيسر جي بدران يا سندس طرفان ڪم ڪندڙ شخص، اداري ۾ ٻئي نمبر جو ذميوار، شيرف هيٺ ڪم ڪندڙ پوليس اهلڪار
antonyms: Principal, Chief, Superior, Leader, Commander, Head
synonyms: Assistant, Substitute, Representative, Delegate, Vice, Second-in-command, Agent, Lieutenant
urduMeaning: نائب، معاون، قائم مقام، نمائندہ، کسی اعلیٰ افسر کی جگہ یا اس کی طرف سے کام کرنے والا شخص، ادارے میں دوسرے درجے کا ذمہ دار، شیرف کے ماتحت کام کرنے والا اہلکار
englishMeaning: A person appointed to act on behalf of a superior. The second-in-command in an organization or office. An elected representative in some legislatures. A law-enforcement officer who works under a sheriff. Acting as a substitute or assistant to a senior official.
examples: The deputy director chaired the meeting in her absence. A sheriff's deputy arrived at the scene. Each region elected a deputy to the national assembly. He serves as deputy head of the department. The manager appointed a deputy to handle daily operations.

synonyms: Legacy, Inheritance, Birthright, Tradition, Culture, Ancestry, Patrimony, Estate, Lineage, Bequest
sindhiMeaning: ورثو / ثقافتي ورثو، ابن ڏاڏن کان مليل ثقافت  ٻولي  رسمون  فنون ۽ قدر، تاريخي عمارتون  ماڳ ۽ يادگار جيڪي ماضي جي نمائندگي ڪن، خانداني روايتون  عقيدا  نسل ۽ مليل ملڪيت، قدرتي وسيلا  ٻيل  جهنگلي جيوت ۽ ماحولياتي نظام جيڪي ايندڙ نسلن لاءِ محفوظ رکيا وڃن، روايتون  ثقافت  تاريخ  رسمون  قدرون يا ملڪيتون جيڪي هڪ نسل کان ٻئي نسل تائين منتقل ٿينديون آهن
englishMeaning: The traditions, culture, history, values, property, or achievements that are passed down from previous generations. Traditions, customs, language, arts, and values inherited from ancestors. Historical monuments, buildings, and sites that represent the past. Family traditions, beliefs, ancestry, and inherited property. Natural resources, landscapes, forests, wildlife, and ecosystems preserved for future generations.
examples: The ancient fort is an important part of our national heritage. She is proud of her cultural heritage and traditional customs. The museum helps preserve the heritage of the region. Children should learn about their heritage to understand their roots.
urduMeaning: ورثہ / ثقافتی ورثہ، آباؤ اجداد سے ملنے والی ثقافت  زبان  رسم و رواج  فنون اور اقدار، تاریخی عمارتیں  مقامات اور یادگاریں جو ماضی کی نمائندگی کرتی ہیں، خاندانی روایات  عقائد  نسل اور وراثت میں ملنے والی جائیداد، قدرتی وسائل  جنگلات  جنگلی حیات اور ماحولیاتی نظام جو آئندہ نسلوں کے لیے محفوظ کیے جائیں، وہ روایات  ثقافت  تاریخ  اقدار یا جائیداد جو ایک نسل سے دوسری نسل تک منتقل ہوتی ہیں
antonyms: Loss, Disinheritance, Forgetfulness, Modernity (in some cultural contexts), Separation, Alienation, Abandonment, Deprivation

examples: The court's ruling set an important legal precedent. There is no precedent for canceling the election in these circumstances. We should not create a dangerous precedent by ignoring the rules. Earlier cases provided a useful precedent for the judge. Her appointment established a precedent for greater inclusion.
urduMeaning: سابقہ مثال، نظیر، عدالتی فیصلہ، ایسا پہلے کا واقعہ یا فیصلہ جو ملتی جلتی صورتِ حال میں رہنمائی کرے، ایسا قائم شدہ طریقہ جو آئندہ عمل کی بنیاد بنے
synonyms: Example, Model, Pattern, Guide, Prior case, Authority, Standard, Antecedent
englishMeaning: An earlier event or decision used as an example or guide in a similar situation. A previous legal judgment that influences later cases. An established practice or pattern that may justify similar action in the future. Something that comes before another thing in time, order, or importance.
antonyms: Subsequent case, Exception, Departure, Innovation, Anomaly
sindhiMeaning: اڳوڻو مثال، نظير، عدالتي فيصلو، اهڙو اڳ ۾ ٿيل واقعو يا فيصلو جيڪو ساڳي صورتحال ۾ رهنمائي ڪري، اهڙو رواج يا طريقو جيڪو مستقبل جي عمل لاءِ بنياد بڻجي

antonyms: Agreement, Breakthrough, Resolution, Progress, Settlement, Compromise
englishMeaning: A situation in which no progress or agreement is possible because opposing sides are equally strong or unwilling to compromise. A complete standstill in negotiations or decision-making. In computing, a condition in which processes wait indefinitely for one another's resources. To bring or come to such a standstill.
examples: Negotiations ended in deadlock after both sides rejected the proposal. The committee remained deadlocked over the budget. A compromise finally broke the political deadlock. Poor resource management can cause a deadlock in the program. The tied vote left the council in a deadlock.
synonyms: Stalemate, Impasse, Standstill, Gridlock, Tie, Logjam, Standoff, Draw
sindhiMeaning: تعطل، بند گهٽي، فيصلو نه ٿيڻ، اهڙي صورتحال جنهن ۾ مخالف ڌريون برابر طاقتور هجن يا سمجهوتو نه ڪن ۽ اڳڀرائي ممڪن نه رهي، ڪمپيوٽر ۾ عملن جو هڪ ٻئي جي وسيلن لاءِ اڻڄاتل وقت تائين انتظار
urduMeaning: تعطل، بند گلی، فیصلہ نہ ہو پانا، ایسی صورتِ حال جس میں مخالف فریق برابر طاقت رکھتے ہوں یا سمجھوتہ نہ کریں اور پیش رفت ممکن نہ رہے، کمپیوٹر میں عملوں کا ایک دوسرے کے وسائل کا غیر معینہ انتظار

synonyms: Signal, Gesture, Nod, Summons, Call, Brook, Stream, Rivulet
urduMeaning: اشارہ، بلاوا، حکم کا اشارہ، خاص طور پر کسی کے ہر حکم پر حاضر رہنے کے محاورے میں استعمال ہونے والا لفظ، چھوٹی ندی یا نالا خصوصاً شمالی انگلستان میں
examples: He expected his assistants to be at his beck and call. I cannot remain at your beck and call all weekend. A narrow beck flowed behind the cottage. Wildflowers grew along the banks of the beck. At the king's beck, the servant stepped forward.
sindhiMeaning: اشارو، سڏ، حڪم جو اشارو، خاص طور ڪنهن جي هر حڪم تي حاضر رهڻ واري محاوري ۾ استعمال ٿيندڙ لفظ، ننڍو وهڪرو يا ندي خاص ڪري اتر انگلينڊ ۾
antonyms: Dismissal, Refusal, Rejection, Release, River, Torrent
englishMeaning: A gesture or signal of command, chiefly used in the phrase at someone's beck and call. A small stream or brook, especially in northern England. Historically, a nod or motion used to summon someone.

synonyms: Long live, Support, Hail, Hurrah for, In favor of, Endorse
sindhiMeaning: زنده باد، حمايت جو نعرو، ڪنهن شخص، جماعت يا مقصد جي ڪاميابي ۽ واڌاري لاءِ جوش يا منظوري ظاهر ڪرڻ، اڳئين فعل سان گڏ اچڻ تي برداشت ڪرڻ يا ساٿ ڏيڻ جي معنيٰ به سياق موجب ٿي سگهي ٿي
examples: Up with freedom and justice for everyone! The crowd shouted, “Up with the workers!” Up with anyone who has the courage to speak the truth! I will not put up with such rude behavior. She walks quickly, but I can still keep up with her.
englishMeaning: An exclamation expressing support, approval, or enthusiasm for a person, group, or cause. Used to urge that someone or something should rise, succeed, or be promoted. In ordinary combinations, able or willing to tolerate or participate in something, especially in phrases such as put up with or keep up with, though the exact meaning depends on the preceding verb.
urduMeaning: زندہ باد، حمایت کا نعرہ، کسی شخص، جماعت یا مقصد کی کامیابی اور ترقی کے لیے جوش یا منظوری ظاہر کرنا، پہلے فعل کے ساتھ آنے پر برداشت کرنے یا ساتھ دینے کا مفہوم بھی سیاق کے مطابق ہو سکتا ہے
antonyms: Down with, Oppose, Reject, Condemn, Away with

synonyms: Away with, Abolish, Oppose, Reject, Overthrow, End, In agreement with
examples: The protesters shouted, “Down with corruption!” Down with laws that deny people equal rights! The crowd raised banners saying, “Down with tyranny!” I'm down with your plan if everyone agrees. She came down with the flu after the trip.
urduMeaning: مردہ باد، ختم کرو، سخت مخالفت یا ناپسندیدگی کا نعرہ، کسی شخص، نظام یا پالیسی کو ہٹانے یا ختم کرنے کا مطالبہ، غیر رسمی استعمال میں کسی بات سے راضی یا اس میں شامل ہونا
antonyms: Up with, Support, Uphold, Preserve, Endorse, Opposed to
englishMeaning: An exclamation demanding the removal, defeat, or end of a person, system, policy, or practice. Used to express strong opposition or disapproval. Informally, in be down with, willing to accept, understand, or participate in something. Also used literally for movement or position toward a lower place when the context requires it.
sindhiMeaning: مردا باد، ختم ڪريو، سخت مخالفت يا ناپسنديدگي جو نعرو، ڪنهن شخص، نظام يا پاليسي کي هٽائڻ يا ختم ڪرڻ جو مطالبو، غير رسمي استعمال ۾ ڪنهن ڳالهه سان راضي يا شامل ٿيڻ

antonyms: Cooperative, Peaceful, Conciliatory, Harmonious, Noncompetitive, Antagonistic, Inhibitory
urduMeaning: جھگڑالو، مسابقتی، تنازعی، جدوجہد یا مقابلے سے متعلق، حیاتیات میں جانوروں کے درمیان دھمکی، حملہ، دفاع، پسپائی یا اطاعت والا رویہ، ایسا مادہ جو حیاتیاتی رسیپٹر کو فعال کرے
englishMeaning: Combative or argumentative. Relating to competition, struggle, or conflict. In biology and animal behavior, involving threat, aggression, defense, avoidance, submission, or fighting between individuals. Relating to an agonist that activates a receptor or produces a biological response.
examples: The debate became increasingly agonistic as neither speaker would compromise. The deer displayed agonistic behavior during the breeding season. Researchers recorded both aggressive and submissive agonistic signals. The drug has an agonistic effect on the receptor. An agonistic political culture can make cooperation difficult.
sindhiMeaning: جهيڙالو، مقابلي وارو، تڪراري، جدوجهد يا مقابلي سان لاڳاپيل، حياتيات ۾ جانورن وچ ۾ ڌمڪي، حملو، بچاءُ، پوئتي هٽڻ يا تابعداري وارو رويو، دوا يا مادو جيڪو حياتياتي رسيپٽر کي سرگرم ڪري
synonyms: Combative, Competitive, Contentious, Adversarial, Aggressive, Conflictual, Struggling, Agonist-related

examples: He donated his fortune to expiate the wrongs of his past. She tried to expiate her guilt by helping the family she had harmed. The ritual was intended to expiate the community's sins. No apology can fully expiate such deliberate cruelty. He accepted the penalty as a way to expiate his offense.
synonyms: Atone for, Make amends for, Redeem, Absolve, Recompense, Rectify, Repair, Purge
sindhiMeaning: ڪفارو ڏيڻ، گناهه يا ڏوهه جو ازالو ڪرڻ، معافي، سزا، قرباني يا سڌاري واري عمل وسيلي پنهنجي غلطي جو بار گهٽائڻ ۽ تلافي ڪرڻ
antonyms: Commit, Offend, Sin, Aggravate, Compound, Persist in
englishMeaning: To make amends for guilt, wrongdoing, or sin. To atone for an offense through punishment, sacrifice, apology, or corrective action. To extinguish or remove guilt by accepting consequences and making reparation.
urduMeaning: کفارہ دینا، گناہ یا جرم کا ازالہ کرنا، معافی، سزا، قربانی یا اصلاحی عمل کے ذریعے اپنی غلطی کا بوجھ کم کرنا اور تلافی کرنا

synonyms: Scornful, Disdainful, Derisive, Disrespectful, Sneering, Supercilious, Insulting, Dismissive
sindhiMeaning: حقارت ڀريو، توهين آميز، نفرت ۽ بي عزتي ڏيکاريندڙ، ڪنهن شخص يا شيءِ کي گهٽ، بي قدر يا ڌيان جي لائق نه سمجهڻ وارو رويو
examples: She gave him a contemptuous glance and walked away. His contemptuous remarks offended the entire team. The critic was contemptuous of the amateur performance. He laughed in a contemptuous manner. Such a contemptuous attitude makes respectful discussion impossible.
englishMeaning: Showing contempt or deep disrespect. Expressing the belief that someone or something is worthless, inferior, or undeserving of consideration. Scornful in manner, speech, or appearance.
urduMeaning: تحقیر آمیز، توہین بھرا، نفرت اور بے عزتی ظاہر کرنے والا، کسی شخص یا چیز کو کمتر، بے قدر یا توجہ کے لائق نہ سمجھنے والا رویہ
antonyms: Respectful, Admiring, Appreciative, Courteous, Considerate, Reverent

urduMeaning: تمسخر آمیز، حقارت بھرا، توہین آمیز، کسی شخص یا چیز کو بے قدر یا کمتر سمجھ کر کھلے طور پر مذاق، نفرت یا بے عزتی ظاہر کرنے والا
sindhiMeaning: ٺٺولي ڪندڙ، حقارت وارو، توهين ڀريو، ڪنهن شخص يا شيءِ کي بي قدر يا گهٽ سمجهي کليل نموني مذاق، نفرت يا بي عزتي ڏيکاريندڙ
antonyms: Respectful, Admiring, Approving, Appreciative, Complimentary, Reverent
synonyms: Contemptuous, Disdainful, Derisive, Mocking, Sneering, Supercilious, Disparaging
englishMeaning: Showing open contempt or strong disrespect. Mocking or rejecting someone or something as worthless or inferior. Characterized by derision, disdain, or a proud lack of respect.
examples: He was scornful of their attempts to solve the problem. She responded with a scornful smile. The audience gave the dishonest speaker a scornful reception. His scornful tone made the young employee feel small. They rejected the proposal with scornful laughter.

antonyms: Fast, Dine alone, Isolate, Withdraw, Quarrel, Separate
englishMeaning: To feast or dine together. To share food and drink in friendly company. To live or socialize together harmoniously. A rare and literary verb connected with convivial gathering.
synonyms: Feast, Dine together, Banquet, Socialize, Convivialize, Gather, Live together
urduMeaning: مل کر کھانا کھانا، اکٹھے دعوت کرنا، دوستوں کے ساتھ کھانا پینا بانٹنا، خوش گوار انداز میں ساتھ رہنا یا میل جول کرنا، یہ ایک نادر ادبی فعل ہے
sindhiMeaning: گڏجي ماني کائڻ، گڏ دعوت ڪرڻ، دوستاڻن ماڻهن سان کاڌو ۽ پيئڻ ونڊڻ، خوشگوار نموني گڏ رهڻ يا ميل جول ڪرڻ، هي هڪ ناياب ادبي فعل آهي
examples: The travelers convived at a long table after the journey. Friends gathered to convive and exchange stories. The villagers convived peacefully during the harvest festival. The author describes artists who worked and convived in the same house. We convived late into the evening over a simple meal.

antonyms: Retain, Hold, Please, Calm, Soothe, Save, Conserve
urduMeaning: پیشاب کرنا، پیشاب، یہ فحش اور عامیانہ لفظ ہے، کسی کو سخت ناراض کرنا، وقت یا پیسہ ضائع کرنا، مختلف غیر رسمی محاوروں میں تحقیر یا زور ظاہر کرنے کے لیے استعمال ہونے والا لفظ
englishMeaning: A vulgar term meaning to urinate. Urine, expressed vulgarly. To annoy or anger someone, especially in the phrase piss someone off. To waste time or resources, especially in phrases such as piss about or piss away. Used in several informal expressions of dismissal, emphasis, or poor quality and may be offensive.
examples: The drunk man stopped in an alley to piss. The rude comment really pissed her off. He pissed away his savings on reckless bets. Stop pissing about and finish the work. The vulgar word “piss” should be avoided in formal conversation.
synonyms: Urinate, Pee, Micturate, Annoy, Anger, Irritate, Squander, Waste
sindhiMeaning: پيشاب ڪرڻ، پيشاب، هي بي ادبي ۽ عاميانه لفظ آهي، ڪنهن کي سخت ناراض ڪرڻ، وقت يا پئسو اجايو وڃائڻ، مختلف غير رسمي اصطلاحن ۾ نفرت يا زور ظاهر ڪرڻ لاءِ استعمال ٿيندڙ لفظ

antonyms: Developed, Flourishing, Thriving, Full-grown, Mature, Unhindered, Robust
urduMeaning: نشوونما رکی ہوئی، چھوٹا رہ جانے والا، نامکمل طور پر بڑھا ہوا، کمزور، ایسا جسم، پودا یا صلاحیت جس کی معمول کی ترقی غذا کی کمی، بیماری یا خراب حالات کے باعث رک گئی ہو
examples: Poor nutrition left many of the plants stunted. The disease had stunted his physical growth. Lack of investment resulted in stunted economic development. The stunted tree produced very little fruit. Constant criticism can lead to stunted emotional growth.
sindhiMeaning: واڌ ويجهه روڪيل، ننڍو رهجي ويل، اڻپورو وڌيل، ڪمزور، اهڙو جسم، ٻوٽو يا صلاحيت جنهن جي عام واڌ خوراڪ، بيماري يا خراب حالتن سبب رڪجي وئي هجي
synonyms: Underdeveloped, Dwarfed, Retarded, Arrested, Hindered, Restricted, Suppressed, Undersized
englishMeaning: Prevented from growing or developing normally. Abnormally short, small, weak, or underdeveloped. Limited in intellectual, emotional, social, or economic development. The past tense and past participle of stunt, meaning to hinder growth or progress.
Green with abundant vegetation. Covered in fresh grass, plants, or foliage. Lush and fertile in appearance. Figuratively, inexperienced, youthful, or fresh, though this sense is less common.
antonyms: Barren, Arid, Dry, Parched, Leafless, Withered, Desolate
urduMeaning: سرسبز، ہریالی سے بھرپور، گھنے پودوں یا تازہ پتوں سے ڈھکا ہوا، زرخیز اور شاداب، مجازی طور پر ناتجربہ کار یا جوان اور تازہ
sindhiMeaning: سرسبز، ساوڪ سان ڀرپور، گهاٽن ٻوٽن يا تازن پنن سان ڍڪيل، زرخيز ۽ شاداب، مجازي طور ناتجربيڪار يا جوان ۽ تازو
synonyms: Green, Lush, Leafy, Flourishing, Fertile, Grassy, Luxuriant, Fresh
