englishMeaning: Without a point, spine, or sharp projection. In botany and zoology, used to describe a plant, leaf, seed, or animal part that is blunt and lacks an awn, bristle, or sharp tip. Smooth-ended and not pointed. A technical adjective used mainly in scientific descriptions of plants and insects.
examples: The botanist described the leaf as muticous and smooth-edged. Many grass species have muticous seeds that lack awns. The insect's wings appeared muticous under the microscope. This variety of wheat is preferred for being muticous and easy to handle. The specimen was identified by its muticous tip.
synonyms: Blunt, Pointless, Awnless, Unarmed, Smooth, Rounded
urduMeaning: بغیر نوک کے، بغیر کانٹے کے، بغیر تیز سرے کے، ایسا پودا پتہ یا جزو جس کا کنارا یا سرا تیز یا نوکیلا نہ ہو، گول یا کند کنارے والا، نباتاتی و حیاتیاتی اصطلاح

sindhiMeaning: بدنام ڪرڻ، الزام تراشي ڪرڻ، تهمت لڳائڻ، ڪنهن جي عزت تي حملو ڪرڻ، ڪوڙا الزام هڻڻ، چغلي ڪرڻ، مذهبي رسم ۾ پاڻي ڇٽڪارڻ
urduMeaning: بدنام کرنا، الزام تراشی کرنا، تہمت لگانا، کسی کی عزت پر حملہ کرنا، جھوٹے الزامات لگانا، غیبت کرنا، مذہبی رسم میں پانی چھڑکنا
antonyms: Praise, Compliment, Honour, Commend, Glorify, Respect, Extol
synonyms: Defame, Slander, Malign, Vilify, Smear, Denigrate, Disparage, Calumniate, Sprinkle
englishMeaning: To attack the reputation of someone by making false or damaging statements. To spread harmful rumours or accusations about a person. To slander, defame, or speak ill of someone. To sprinkle, especially with holy water in a religious ceremony. To criticize unfairly with the aim of harming honour.
examples: It is wrong to asperse someone without solid evidence. The politician tried to asperse his rival before the elections. She refused to asperse her former colleagues in the interview. Critics aspersed the writer for his controversial novel. The priest aspersed the congregation with holy water.

urduMeaning: گنگنانا، بھنبھنانا، شہد کی مکھی جیسی آواز نکالنا، بند ہونٹوں سے کوئی دھن گانا، کسی جگہ کا سرگرمی سے بھرپور ہونا، مشین یا مجمع کی ہلکی مسلسل آواز
synonyms: Buzz, Drone, Murmur, Croon, Sing, Whir, Purr, Bustle, Throb
examples: She likes to hum her favourite songs while cooking. The bees were humming softly in the garden. The whole market was humming with activity in the morning. You can hear the fridge humming in the quiet room. He hummed a tune as he walked down the street.
sindhiMeaning: گنگنائڻ، ڀنڀوڙڻ، مکيءَ وانگر آواز ڪڍڻ، بند چپن سان ڪا ڌن ڳائڻ، ڪنهن جاءِ جو سرگرميءَ سان ڀرپور هجڻ، مشين يا ميڙ جو هلڪو لڳاتار آواز
englishMeaning: To make a low, continuous sound similar to that of a bee. To sing a tune with closed lips, without using words. To be full of activity, energy, or busy movement. To produce a steady murmuring noise, especially from machines or crowds. To emit a soft and even sound.
antonyms: Silence, Quiet, Stillness, Hush, Stop, Calm

sindhiMeaning: رد ڪرڻ، منسوخ ڪرڻ، ختم ڪرڻ، دٻائڻ، بغاوت يا فساد کي ڪچلڻ، ڪنهن فيصلي يا حڪم کي قانوني طور تي ختم ڪرڻ، افواهن کي روڪڻ
antonyms: Approve, Validate, Confirm, Uphold, Support, Encourage, Allow, Permit
synonyms: Annul, Overturn, Revoke, Reject, Suppress, Crush, Cancel, Nullify, Squash, Subdue
urduMeaning: رد کرنا، منسوخ کرنا، ختم کرنا، دبا دینا، بغاوت یا فساد کو کچل دینا، کسی فیصلے یا حکم کو قانونی طور پر ختم کرنا، افواہوں کو روکنا
englishMeaning: To officially reject, cancel, or annul a decision, verdict, or law by legal authority. To put an end to something forcefully, especially a rebellion, rumour, or protest. To suppress or crush completely. To reject a proposal or suggestion firmly. To stop something from spreading or continuing.
examples: The high court decided to quash the lower court's verdict. The government used the army to quash the rebellion. He issued a statement to quash the rumours about his resignation. The committee voted to quash the new proposal. Police acted quickly to quash the violent protest.

antonyms: Subtle, Hidden, Concealed, Secret, Discreet, Minor, Slight, Unnoticeable
englishMeaning: Clearly and openly bad, shocking, or wrong. Done in a very obvious way without any attempt to hide it. Outrageously noticeable, especially when referring to wrongdoing or violation of rules. Boldly offensive or scandalous. Used for behaviour, actions, or violations that are impossible to ignore.
examples: The referee punished the player for a flagrant foul. This is a flagrant violation of human rights. His flagrant disregard for the rules shocked everyone. The company was fined for flagrant misuse of public funds. She told a flagrant lie in front of the whole class.
sindhiMeaning: کلي طور تي خراب، چٽي پٽي طرح غلط، پڌرو ۽ شرمناڪ، ظاهر ظهور برو ڪم ڪرڻ وارو، اهڙي حرڪت جيڪا لڪائڻ جي ڪوشش بنا ڪئي وڃي، صريح خلاف ورزي ڪندڙ
synonyms: Blatant, Glaring, Obvious, Outrageous, Brazen, Shameless, Conspicuous, Egregious, Open
urduMeaning: کھلم کھلا برا، صریح، واضح طور پر غلط، شرمناک حد تک ظاہر، ایسا عمل جو چھپانے کی کوشش کے بغیر کیا جائے، صریح خلاف ورزی کرنے والا

englishMeaning: The belief that direct knowledge of God, spiritual truth, or ultimate reality can be attained through personal experience, intuition, or meditation rather than through reasoning. A spiritual practice focused on union with the divine. Vague or obscure thinking that is hard to understand. The doctrines and practices of mystics.
sindhiMeaning: تصوف، روحانيت، باطني علم، خدا يا حقيقت سان روحاني ميلاپ جو يقين، اهڙو تجربو جيڪو عقل کان مٿي روح جي ذريعي حاصل ٿئي، صوفياڻو نظريو
antonyms: Rationalism, Materialism, Realism, Atheism, Skepticism, Worldliness
synonyms: Spirituality, Sufism, Esotericism, Occultism, Transcendentalism, Contemplation, Divinity
urduMeaning: تصوف، روحانیت، باطنی علم، خدا یا حقیقت سے روحانی ملاپ کا یقین، ایسا تجربہ جو عقل سے بالاتر روح کے ذریعے حاصل ہو، صوفیانہ نظریہ
examples: He wrote a book on the mysticism of the great Sufi poets. Mysticism plays an important role in many world religions. She turned to mysticism after years of restless searching. The painting reflects the deep mysticism of the East. Many philosophers have explored the connection between mysticism and reality.

sindhiMeaning: وڏي دل وارو، سخي، فراخدل، معاف ڪرڻ وارو، دشمن سان به مهرباني ڪندڙ، اعليٰ ظرف وارو، ننڍين ڳالهين کي نظرانداز ڪندڙ، شريف النفس
antonyms: Selfish, Mean, Stingy, Petty, Vindictive, Resentful, Small-minded, Greedy
urduMeaning: بڑے دل والا، سخی، فراخدل، معاف کرنے والا، دشمن سے بھی مہربانی کرنے والا، اعلیٰ ظرف رکھنے والا، چھوٹی باتوں کو نظر انداز کرنے والا، شریف النفس
synonyms: Generous, Noble, Forgiving, Big-hearted, Charitable, Bountiful, Gracious, Liberal, Kindhearted
englishMeaning: Very generous, kind, and forgiving, especially towards an enemy, rival, or weaker person. Having a noble and large-hearted nature. Showing greatness of mind by overlooking insults, injuries, or petty matters. Willing to give more than is necessary or expected. Showing a high-minded and noble character.
examples: The king was magnanimous in his treatment of the defeated enemy. It was magnanimous of her to forgive him after such a betrayal. He made a magnanimous donation to the orphanage. The winner was magnanimous in his victory speech. Only a truly magnanimous person can rise above petty disputes.

englishMeaning: An extremely handsome young man. A man whose physical beauty attracts admiration. In Greek mythology, a beautiful youth loved by the goddess Aphrodite. A symbol of male beauty and youthful charm. Sometimes used humorously for a man who is overly proud of his looks.
antonyms: Ugly man, Unattractive person, Plain, Homely, Unsightly
urduMeaning: نہایت خوبصورت نوجوان، حسین مرد، خوبصورت جوان، یونانی دیومالا میں ایک حسین نوجوان جس سے محبت کی دیوی محبت کرتی تھی، مردانہ حسن کی علامت
sindhiMeaning: نهايت سهڻو نوجوان، حسين مرد، خوبصورت جوان، يوناني ديو مالا ۾ هڪ حسين نوجوان جنهن سان محبت جي ديوي محبت ڪندي هئي، مرداڻي حسن جو علامتي نالو
examples: He looked like an Adonis in his wedding photographs. The actor is regarded as the Adonis of the film industry. She admired the young Adonis sitting in the cafe. The painting depicts Adonis surrounded by goddesses. Not every handsome man can be called an Adonis.
synonyms: Handsome man, Beau, Heartthrob, Hunk, Charmer, Beauty, Youthful idol

englishMeaning: A firm warning, scolding, or piece of advice given to correct a person's behaviour. A gentle but serious reproof. A caution against doing something wrong or dangerous. Counsel intended to remind someone of their duty. Mild rebuke combined with guidance for improvement.
synonyms: Warning, Reprimand, Reproof, Caution, Rebuke, Counsel, Advice, Censure, Scolding
sindhiMeaning: نصيحت، تنبيهه، خبرداري، ٻاجهاري ملامت، اهڙي صلاح جيڪا غلطي کان روڪڻ لاءِ ڏني وڃي، هلڪي سرزنش سان گڏ هدايت، احتياط ڪرڻ جي تاڪيد
examples: The teacher's admonition helped the student to improve his behaviour. He ignored his father's admonition and faced serious trouble. The judge delivered a stern admonition to the young offender. Her gentle admonition was enough to stop the children from quarrelling. The book is full of moral admonitions for young readers.
urduMeaning: نصیحت، تنبیہ، خبرداری، ہلکی سرزنش، ایسی صلاح جو غلطی سے روکنے کے لیے دی جائے، نرم ڈانٹ کے ساتھ ہدایت، احتیاط کی تاکید
antonyms: Praise, Approval, Compliment, Encouragement, Commendation, Applause

sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن جانور جي پٺيءَ تي چڙهيل سخت خول، ڪڇون، ڪيڪڙي يا چنگي جو سخت ٻاهريون پوش، حفاظتي خول، علامتي طور تي ماڻهوءَ جو جذباتي حفاظتي حصار
examples: The turtle quickly pulled its head inside its carapace. A crab's carapace protects it from predators in the sea. Scientists studied the patterns on the ancient carapace. She had built an emotional carapace to hide her pain. The fossil showed a perfectly preserved carapace.
synonyms: Shell, Shield, Armour, Casing, Covering, Exoskeleton, Crust
urduMeaning: کسی جانور کی پشت پر چڑھا ہوا سخت خول، کچھوے کیکڑے یا جھینگے کا سخت بیرونی غلاف، حفاظتی خول، علامتی طور پر انسان کا جذباتی حفاظتی حصار
antonyms: Softness, Vulnerability, Bareness, Exposure, Openness
englishMeaning: The hard, protective upper shell that covers the back of certain animals such as turtles, crabs, and lobsters. A bony or chitinous outer covering that shields the body from injury. Figuratively, an emotional or psychological shield that protects a person from being hurt. A defensive outer layer.

synonyms: Fossil, Prehistoric arthropod, Ancient sea creature, Palaeozoic invertebrate
sindhiMeaning: هڪ قسم جو سامونڊي جيو جيڪو ڪروڙين سال اڳ موجود هو ۽ هاڻي معدوم ٿي چڪو آهي، ٽن حصن ۾ ورهايل جسم وارو ننڍڙو سامونڊي جانور، قديم زماني جو ڄاتل سڃاتل فاسل
examples: The museum displayed a perfectly preserved trilobite fossil. Trilobites lived in ancient oceans millions of years ago. Scientists study the trilobite to learn about early marine life. He found a small trilobite while exploring the rocky beach. The trilobite is one of the most successful early life forms.
urduMeaning: ایک قسم کا سمندری جاندار جو کروڑوں سال پہلے موجود تھا اور اب معدوم ہو چکا ہے، تین حصوں میں منقسم جسم والا چھوٹا سمندری جانور، قدیم زمانے کا معروف فوسل
antonyms: Modern creature, Living organism, Contemporary species
englishMeaning: An extinct marine arthropod that lived in the seas of the Palaeozoic era. A small, oval-shaped sea creature whose body was divided into three lobes lengthwise. One of the earliest known groups of animals with hard shells. A common fossil studied to understand prehistoric life and ancient oceans.

urduMeaning: معدوم، ختم شدہ، ناپید، ایسی چیز یا جانور جس کا وجود ختم ہو چکا ہو، ایسی زبان رسم یا خاندان جس کا سلسلہ ختم ہو چکا ہو، ایسا آتش فشاں جو دوبارہ نہ پھٹے
sindhiMeaning: معدوم، ختم ٿيل، ناپيد، اهڙي شيءِ يا جانور جو وجود ختم ٿي چڪو هجي، اهڙي ٻولي رسم يا خاندان جنهن جو سلسلو ختم ٿي چڪو هجي، اهڙو آتش فشان جيڪو وري نه ڦاٽي
synonyms: Vanished, Wiped out, Gone, Dead, Defunct, Obsolete, Lost, Perished
examples: Dinosaurs became extinct millions of years ago. Many animal species are at risk of becoming extinct due to climate change. Latin is now considered an extinct language in daily use. The volcano on the island has been extinct for centuries. Several old customs are nearly extinct in modern society.
englishMeaning: No longer existing or living on the earth. Having died out as a species or group. No longer in use, active, or practised, as a custom, language, or tradition. Of a volcano: no longer capable of erupting. Of a family, title, or organization: ended and gone forever.
antonyms: Living, Surviving, Existing, Active, Thriving, Alive, Present, Flourishing

sindhiMeaning: ڀاڻ، گوبر، ڍڳن ۽ گهوڙن جو فضلو جيڪو زمين کي زرخيز بنائڻ لاءِ ڪتب آندو وڃي، قدرتي ڀاڻ، فصلن کي ڀرپور بنائڻ وارو نامياتي مادو، زمين ۾ ڀاڻ وجهڻ
antonyms: Poison, Pollutant, Sterilizer, Toxin, Barren matter
englishMeaning: Animal dung, especially that of cattle or horses, used to fertilize the soil and make crops grow better. Any natural substance applied to land to enrich it. To spread fertilizer or dung on land in order to improve its fertility. Decayed organic matter used in farming and gardening.
examples: Farmers spread manure on the fields before sowing the seeds. Cow manure is considered an excellent natural fertilizer. The garden needs fresh manure to produce healthy vegetables. He uses organic manure instead of chemical fertilizers. They manure the land twice a year for better crops.
synonyms: Fertilizer, Dung, Compost, Muck, Humus, Excrement, Nutrient
urduMeaning: کھاد، گوبر، گائے اور گھوڑے کا فضلہ جو زمین کو زرخیز بنانے کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے، قدرتی کھاد، فصلوں کو بہتر بنانے والا نامیاتی مادہ، زمین میں کھاد ڈالنا

englishMeaning: To take air into the lungs and let it out again through the nose or mouth. To live or be alive. To say something softly or in a whispering manner. To allow fresh air to enter or pass through something. To pause and relax for a short time after stress or effort.
antonyms: Suffocate, Choke, Hold breath, Die, Stifle
urduMeaning: سانس لینا، سانس لینا اور چھوڑنا، زندہ ہونا، آہستہ آواز میں کچھ کہنا، تازہ ہوا کو اندر آنے دینا، تھوڑی دیر کے لیے سستانا اور آرام کرنا
sindhiMeaning: ساهه کڻڻ، ساهه کڻڻ ۽ ڇڏڻ، جيئرو هجڻ، ڌيمي آواز ۾ ڪجهه چوڻ، تازي هوا اندر داخل ٿيڻ ڏيڻ، ٿوري دير لاءِ سستائڻ ۽ آرام ڪرڻ
synonyms: Inhale, Exhale, Respire, Pant, Sigh, Whisper, Live, Murmur
examples: It is hard to breathe at such a high altitude. Open the windows so the room can breathe. She breathed a few soft words into his ear. After the exam, the students could finally breathe again. Plants breathe in carbon dioxide and release oxygen.

sindhiMeaning: لڳاتار، بنا روڪ، بنا وقفي وارو، جيڪو هلندو ئي رهي، اڻ کٽ، اهڙو شور يا عمل جيڪو ختم ئي نه ٿئي، مسلسل ۽ ڪڏهن ڪڏهن ڏکوئيندڙ
urduMeaning: مسلسل، بلا وقفہ، بغیر رکے، جو رکے بغیر چلتا رہے، نہ ختم ہونے والا، ایسا شور یا عمل جو ختم ہی نہ ہو، مسلسل اور بسا اوقات تنگ کرنے والا
synonyms: Continuous, Constant, Endless, Unceasing, Nonstop, Perpetual, Relentless, Persistent
examples: The incessant noise of traffic kept him awake all night. We are tired of his incessant complaints about everything. The incessant rain caused heavy floods in the city. Her incessant questions began to irritate the teacher. He worked with incessant effort to complete the project on time.
englishMeaning: Continuing without pause or interruption. Going on for a long time without stopping. Constant, endless, and often annoying. Used for sounds, actions, or activities that do not stop even for a short while. Persistent and unending in nature.
antonyms: Intermittent, Occasional, Brief, Stopping, Periodic, Temporary, Interrupted
Masculine, Feminine, Fertile, Reproductive, Biased, Partial
englishMeaning: Belonging to the gender that is neither masculine nor feminine, especially in grammar. Having no developed sexual organs, or being sexually undeveloped, as in some insects. To remove the reproductive organs of an animal so that it cannot produce young. Neither one side nor the other; neutral. A neutered animal.
urduMeaning: نہ نر نہ مادہ، صنف سے آزاد، گرامر کی اصطلاح میں صنف بے طرف، کسی جانور کے تناسلی اعضا نکال دینا تاکہ وہ بچے پیدا نہ کر سکے، غیر جانبدار، نہ ایک طرف نہ دوسری طرف
sindhiMeaning: نه نر نه مادي، صنف کان آجو، گراميٽڪل اصطلاح ۾ صنفِ بي طرف، ڪنهن جانور جا تناسلي عضوا ڪڍي ڇڏڻ ته جيئن اهو ٻچا نه ڄڻي، غير جانبدار، نه هڪ طرف نه ٻيءَ طرف
synonyms: Sexless, Asexual, Neutral, Impartial, Sterilize, Castrate, Spay, Genderless
examples: In English grammar, the word 'it' is often used as a neuter pronoun. The vet advised them to neuter the male cat. Many pet owners choose to neuter their dogs to control the population. The country tried to remain neuter during the conflict. Worker bees are neuter and cannot reproduce.

antonyms: Safe, Secure, Harmless, Risk-free, Protected, Stable, Sheltered
urduMeaning: خطرناک، پُرخطر، جوکم بھرا، نقصان دہ، خوفناک، خطرات سے بھرپور، جان لیوا، ایسی صورتحال یا کام جس میں نقصان اور تباہی کا شدید امکان ہو
synonyms: Dangerous, Hazardous, Risky, Treacherous, Unsafe, Precarious, Threatening, Life-threatening
sindhiMeaning: خطرناڪ، پُرخطر، جوکم وارو، نقصانڪار، خوفناڪ، خطرن سان ڀريل، جان جوکم ۾ وجهندڙ، اهڙي حالت يا ڪم جنهن ۾ نقصان ۽ تباهي جو وڏو امڪان هجي
englishMeaning: Full of danger or risk. Hazardous. Highly dangerous. Involving serious threat to life, safety, or well-being. Risky and uncertain in outcome. Used to describe situations, journeys, conditions, or actions that carry a high likelihood of harm, injury, loss, or failure.
examples: The climbers began a perilous ascent of the icy mountain. Driving on these narrow roads at night is perilous. The country is going through a perilous economic situation. Sailors faced a perilous journey across the stormy sea. Ignoring safety warnings can be perilous for workers.

antonyms: Decide, Resolve, Determine, Commit, Persist, Stand firm
sindhiMeaning: هٻڪڻ، دوڌو هجڻ، فيصلو ڪرڻ ۾ دير ڪرڻ، راءِ بدلائيندو رهڻ، ٻن خيالن جي وچ ۾ جهولڻ، پڪو فيصلو نه ڪري سگهڻ، شڪ ۾ پيل هجڻ
urduMeaning: ہچکچانا، تذبذب میں رہنا، فیصلہ کرنے میں ہچکچاہٹ، رائے بدلتے رہنا، دو خیالات کے درمیان جھولنا، غیر یقینی کا شکار ہونا، پختہ فیصلہ نہ کر سکنا
examples: He continued to vacillate between accepting and rejecting the job offer. The committee vacillated for weeks before announcing its decision. She tends to vacillate whenever she has to make important choices. Investors vacillate when the market becomes unstable. The leader was criticized for vacillating during the crisis.
englishMeaning: To keep changing one’s opinions, decisions, or actions. To waver between different choices. To be indecisive or hesitant. To swing back and forth between options. To show uncertainty or lack of firmness in deciding what to do, often resulting in delay or confusion.
synonyms: Waver, Hesitate, Dither, Fluctuate, Oscillate, Shilly-shally, Falter, Equivocate
Irreversible, Unfixable, Permanent, Irremediable, Incurable, Beyond repair
urduMeaning: ناقابلِ تلافی، جس کی مرمت ممکن نہ ہو، جسے درست نہ کیا جا سکے، مستقل نقصان والا، ایسا نقصان جس کی بھرپائی ممکن نہ ہو
sindhiMeaning: جنهن جي مرمت ممڪن نه هجي، نه سُڌرڻ جوڳو، نه ٺيڪ ٿيڻ جوڳو، اڻ ٺاهيندڙ، مستقل نقصان وارو، اهڙو نقصان جنهن جي تلافي ممڪن نه هجي
examples: The earthquake caused irreparable damage to the ancient buildings. His careless words did irreparable harm to their friendship. The factory suffered an irreparable loss in the fire. Pollution is causing irreparable damage to the environment. The accident left him with an irreparable injury.
antonyms: Repairable, Fixable, Reversible, Curable, Remediable, Restorable
englishMeaning: Impossible to repair, restore, or put right. Beyond recovery or fixing. Permanent and lasting in nature. Causing damage that cannot be undone. Used for harm, loss, or injury that is so severe that no remedy, compensation, or correction can fully restore the original state.

examples: There was great jubilation in the city after the team won the championship. The announcement of independence was met with national jubilation. His face showed jubilation when he received the award. The crowd erupted in jubilation as the results were declared. Jubilation filled the hall when the project was finally approved.
synonyms: Joy, Exultation, Celebration, Rejoicing, Elation, Delight, Triumph, Glee
sindhiMeaning: خوشي، جشن، شاديءَ جو اظهار، فتح جي خوشي، وڏي خوشي جو احساس، مسرت، خوشيءَ مان جهومڻ، ڪاميابي تي ملهايل جشن
antonyms: Sadness, Sorrow, Grief, Misery, Mourning, Despair, Gloom
englishMeaning: A feeling of great happiness, joy, and triumph. Public expression of celebration and delight. Exultation over success or victory. A state of rejoicing. The strong emotion of happiness shown openly when something very pleasing, successful, or long-awaited happens.
urduMeaning: خوشی، جشن، مسرت، فتح کی خوشی، بے حد خوشی کا اظہار، شادمانی، کامیابی پر منایا جانے والا جشن، دلی مسرت کا برملا اظہار

sindhiMeaning: قدر گهٽجڻ، قيمت ۾ ڪمي اچڻ، گهٽائڻ، گهٽ سمجهڻ، ڪنهن جي عزت يا اهميت کي گهٽائڻ، ڪا شيءِ جنهن جي قيمت وقت سان گهٽبي وڃي
antonyms: Appreciate, Increase, Rise, Value, Praise, Upgrade, Enhance
synonyms: Devalue, Reduce, Decline, Diminish, Belittle, Disparage, Downgrade
englishMeaning: To decrease in value over time. To lose worth. To reduce the price or value of something. To belittle, undervalue, or speak of with disrespect. Used in finance for assets losing value, and in general speech for making something seem less important or worthy.
examples: New cars depreciate quickly within the first few years. The value of the currency continues to depreciate against the dollar. He should not depreciate the efforts of his hardworking team. Machinery tends to depreciate as it grows older. Critics often depreciate the work of young writers.
urduMeaning: قدر گھٹنا، قیمت میں کمی آنا، کم کرنا، کم تر سمجھنا، کسی کی اہمیت یا قدر کو گھٹانا، ایسی چیز جس کی مالیت وقت کے ساتھ کم ہوتی جائے
کم ہونا، گھٹنا، کم کرنا، آہستہ آہستہ کمی آنا، اہمیت یا طاقت میں کمی، کسی کی قدر یا عزت کو کم کرنا
sindhiMeaning: گهٽجڻ، ننڍو ٿيڻ، ڪم ٿيڻ، گهٽائڻ، آهستي آهستي ڪمي اچڻ، اهميت يا طاقت ۾ گهٽتائي، ڪنهن جي قدر يا عزت کي گهٽائڻ
antonyms: Increase, Grow, Expand, Enlarge, Rise, Augment, Intensify
synonyms: Decrease, Reduce, Lessen, Shrink, Decline, Dwindle, Abate, Wane
examples: The supply of clean water is rapidly diminishing in many regions. Her enthusiasm did not diminish despite many setbacks. Loud arguments only diminish the respect between family members. The pain began to diminish after taking the medicine. Modern technology has diminished the need for manual labor.
englishMeaning: To make or become smaller, fewer, or less in size, amount, importance, or intensity. To reduce gradually. To lessen the reputation or value of someone or something. Used both for physical reduction and for decline in significance, power, or quality.

urduMeaning: ضروری بنانا، لازم کر دینا، مجبور کرنا، کسی بات کو ناگزیر بنا دینا، ایسی صورتحال پیدا کرنا جس کی وجہ سے کوئی کام ضروری ہو جائے
examples: Heavy rains may necessitate the closure of several roads. The illness necessitated immediate hospital treatment. Rapid growth in users will necessitate an upgrade of the system. Security concerns necessitated stricter checking at the airport. The new project necessitates additional staff and funding.
englishMeaning: To make something necessary or unavoidable. To require as a result of circumstances. To compel or oblige action. To create a need for something to be done. Used when a particular situation forces or demands that a certain step, action, or response must take place.
synonyms: Require, Demand, Compel, Oblige, Force, Entail, Call for
antonyms: Avoid, Prevent, Hinder, Block, Discourage, Stop
sindhiMeaning: ضروري بڻائڻ، لازمي ڪرڻ، مجبور ڪرڻ، ڪا ڳالهه ضروري بڻائي ڇڏڻ، اهڙي صورتحال پيدا ڪرڻ جنهن سبب ڪو ڪم لازمي ٿي پوي

examples: He gave a sheepish smile after forgetting her name. She looked sheepish when the teacher caught her copying. The boy admitted his mistake with a sheepish expression. He felt sheepish for arriving so late to the meeting. There was a sheepish grin on his face as he apologized.
urduMeaning: شرمندہ، خفت زدہ، جھینپا ہوا، شرمیلا، اپنی غلطی پر شرمسار، ہلکی شرمندگی والا، ایسا انداز جو اپنی حماقت پر کسی کو محسوس ہو
synonyms: Embarrassed, Bashful, Shy, Ashamed, Awkward, Timid, Self-conscious
sindhiMeaning: شرمسار، شرمائيندڙ، نهٺو، جهڪيل، پنهنجي غلطي تي شرمايل، نينڊ ۾، هلڪي شرمندگي وارو، اهڙو ماڻهو جيڪو پنهنجي ڪم تي جهيپ محسوس ڪري
antonyms: Bold, Confident, Shameless, Brazen, Assured, Unabashed
englishMeaning: Showing embarrassment from shame or a feeling of having done something silly, foolish, or wrong. Looking shy, awkward, or apologetic. Resembling the timid manner of a sheep. Used to describe a person’s expression, smile, or behavior when they feel mildly guilty or self-conscious.

synonyms: Modern, Current, Present-day, Up-to-date, Recent, Latest, Concurrent
urduMeaning: ہم عصر، ہم زمانہ، موجودہ دور کا، جدید، عہدِ حاضر کا، ایک ہی وقت میں موجود، آج کل کا، نیا اور جدید انداز کا
examples: She is one of the most respected contemporary writers in the country. The museum displays both classical and contemporary art. Shakespeare and Marlowe were contemporaries. The house is built in a contemporary style with large glass windows. Many contemporary issues were discussed at the conference.
sindhiMeaning: همعصر، هم وقت، موجوده دور جو، جديد، اڄوڪو، ساڳئي زماني جو، اهو ماڻهو يا شيءِ جيڪا ساڳئي وقت ۾ موجود هجي
englishMeaning: Belonging to or occurring in the present time. Modern. Living or existing at the same time as someone or something else. Up-to-date in style, design, or thinking. Used both for things of the current era and for people or events from the same historical period.
antonyms: Ancient, Old, Outdated, Past, Former, Obsolete, Traditional

synonyms: Bubble, Swelling, Boil, Sore, Bulge, Vesicle
examples: Tight shoes can cause painful blisters on the feet. A blister formed on his hand after working in the garden. The hot iron left a blister on her finger. Sunburn often leads to blisters on exposed skin. Old paint on the wall began to blister in the sun.
sindhiMeaning: ڦُلڪو، ڦولڙي، چمڙي تي پاڻيءَ سان ڀريل سُڄ، جلڻ يا رڳڙ سبب پيدا ٿيندڙ ننڍو ڦولڙو، رنگ يا ڌاتوءَ جي مٿاڇري تي ڦوڪ پيدا ٿيڻ
antonyms: Smoothness, Flatness, Healing
englishMeaning: A small swelling on the skin filled with fluid, usually caused by burning, rubbing, or infection. A raised bubble-like spot on a surface such as paint or metal. To develop blisters or to cause blisters to form due to heat, friction, or pressure.
urduMeaning: چھالا، آبلہ، جلد پر پانی سے بھرا ہوا ابھار، جلنے یا رگڑ سے بننے والا چھوٹا چھالا، رنگ یا دھات کی سطح پر بلبلے کا بننا

englishMeaning: Showing or feeling hesitancy. Uncertain about how to act or proceed. Lacking firmness of decision or purpose. Wavering and indecisive. Used to describe a person who finds it difficult to make up their mind or to stick to a chosen plan of action.
antonyms: Resolute, Determined, Decisive, Firm, Steadfast, Strong-willed
synonyms: Hesitant, Indecisive, Wavering, Uncertain, Doubtful, Vacillating, Weak-willed
urduMeaning: دو دل، متذبذب، کمزور ارادے والا، فیصلہ کرنے میں ہچکچانے والا، غیر پختہ، ایسا شخص جو پختہ فیصلہ نہ کر سکے
examples: His irresolute attitude cost the team a clear victory. She felt irresolute about leaving her hometown. An irresolute leader cannot inspire confidence in others. He stood irresolute at the doorway, unsure whether to enter. The committee remained irresolute on the matter for months.
sindhiMeaning: دوڌي، هٻڪندڙ، فيصلو ڪرڻ ۾ ڪمزور، غير پڪو، ڪمزور ارادي وارو، اهڙو ماڻهو جيڪو پڪو فيصلو نه ڪري سگهي
سست، ڍلو، بي حال، ٿڪل ٿڪل، ڪمزور، ڍرو، نرم ۽ آرامده انداز وارو، حرڪت يا انداز جنهن ۾ زور ۽ تيزي نه هجي
urduMeaning: سست، کاہل، ڈھیلا، بے حال، تھکا ہوا، نرم اور سست رفتار، کمزور، ایسی حرکت یا انداز جس میں جوش اور تیزی نہ ہو
examples: She gave him a languid smile from across the room. The hot afternoon made everyone feel languid. He walked with a languid step toward the river. There was a languid atmosphere in the village by noon. The patient looked pale and languid after the long illness.
synonyms: Sluggish, Listless, Lethargic, Weary, Drowsy, Slow, Relaxed, Feeble
englishMeaning: Lacking energy, spirit, or vigor. Slow and relaxed in a pleasant way. Showing weakness or weariness. Lazy and unhurried in manner. Used to describe movement, atmosphere, or a person who appears tired, gentle, soft, or lacking enthusiasm and liveliness.
antonyms: Energetic, Lively, Active, Vigorous, Brisk, Spirited, Alert
Talkative, Chatty, Loquacious, Communicative, Garrulous, Outgoing
englishMeaning: Reserved or uncommunicative in speech. Saying little. Preferring silence over conversation. Habitually quiet and not inclined to talk much. Used to describe a person whose nature is to remain silent, speak briefly, or avoid sharing thoughts and feelings openly with others.
examples: He is a taciturn man who rarely shares his feelings. The taciturn old farmer answered only with a nod. She felt uneasy with his taciturn behavior during dinner. Despite being taciturn, he was deeply respected by everyone. The new officer was taciturn but very observant.
urduMeaning: کم گو، خاموش طبع، کم بولنے والا، خاموشی پسند، ایسا شخص جو زیادہ بات نہ کرے اور خاموش رہنا پسند کرے
synonyms: Quiet, Reserved, Silent, Reticent, Withdrawn, Uncommunicative, Tight-lipped
sindhiMeaning: گهٽ ڳالهائيندڙ، خاموش طبيعت، چپ چاپ رهندڙ، گهٽ گفتگو ڪرڻ وارو، اهڙو ماڻهو جيڪو زياده نه ڳالهائي ۽ خاموشي پسند ڪري

antonyms: Moderate, Skeptic, Cynic, Apathetic person, Indifferent person
sindhiMeaning: انتها پسند، جنوني، ڪنهن نظريي يا مذهب جو سخت پيروڪار، حد کان وڌيڪ جوش وارو، اهڙو ماڻهو جيڪو ڪنهن خيال يا عقيدي تي ٻين کي به مڃائڻ جي ضد ۾ هجي
examples: He was a political zealot who never accepted other views. Religious zealots often misinterpret the true message of faith. The reformer was called a zealot by his opponents. A zealot can sometimes do more harm than good to a cause. She is a zealot when it comes to environmental protection.
urduMeaning: متعصب، جنونی، انتہاپسند، کسی نظریے یا مذہب کا شدید پیروکار، حد سے زیادہ جوش رکھنے والا، ایسا شخص جو اپنے عقیدے میں سختی اور عدم برداشت دکھائے
synonyms: Fanatic, Extremist, Devotee, Enthusiast, Militant, Bigot
englishMeaning: A person who is fanatically devoted to a cause, belief, religion, or political ideal. An extreme enthusiast. Someone who supports a viewpoint with uncompromising and often intolerant passion. The term is often used in a negative sense for excessive or aggressive devotion.

antonyms: Humane, Kind, Gentle, Civilized, Merciful, Compassionate
englishMeaning: Resembling a beast in nature or behavior. Savage, brutal, or cruel. Lacking human qualities of kindness or compassion. Used to describe acts, behavior, or instincts that are extremely violent, inhumane, or animal-like, especially involving cruelty toward others.
synonyms: Brutal, Savage, Beastly, Inhuman, Barbaric, Cruel, Ferocious
sindhiMeaning: حيواني، وحشي، ظالم، جانورن جهڙو، بي رحم، انسانيت کان خالي، اهڙو رويو يا عمل جيڪو بيحد ظالماڻو ۽ جانورن جيان هجي
urduMeaning: حیوانی، وحشی، درندہ صفت، ظالم، بے رحم، انسانیت سے عاری، ایسا رویہ یا عمل جو نہایت ظالمانہ اور جانوروں جیسا ہو
examples: The villagers were shocked by the bestial attack on the travelers. War often brings out the bestial side of human nature. The criminal was punished for his bestial behavior. Such bestial cruelty has no place in a civilized society. The film depicted the bestial conditions of the prisoners.

antonyms: Smooth, Flat, Even, Plain, Level
sindhiMeaning: لهرئون لهر، ڪنڊائتو، ڌارن واري سطح وارو، چادر يا ڪاغذ جي مٿاڇري تي ٺهيل لهرون، اهڙي شيءِ جنهن جي مٿاڇري تي ابتدائي لهرون ۽ گهرايون هجن
examples: The roof of the shed was made of corrugated iron sheets. Goods were packed safely in strong corrugated boxes. They walked along the corrugated metal walls of the warehouse. Corrugated pipes are often used in drainage systems. The old man’s forehead was wrinkled and corrugated with age.
urduMeaning: لہریا، چنٹ دار، نالی دار، ایسی سطح جس پر لہریں یا تہیں بنی ہوں، عام طور پر چادر، گتے یا پائپ کی سطح پر بنی ہوئی لہریں
synonyms: Ridged, Grooved, Furrowed, Wrinkled, Crinkled, Folded, Channeled
englishMeaning: Shaped into alternating parallel ridges and grooves. Having a wavy or ridged surface. Folded into a series of regular curves or lines. Commonly used for materials like iron sheets, cardboard, or pipes whose surface is shaped this way for added strength and flexibility.

A soft, round, flat-crowned cap, usually made of woven or felted wool, without a peak or brim. Often worn tilted to one side. Commonly associated with artists, soldiers, and certain national costumes. Used as both fashion wear and as part of military uniforms.
sindhiMeaning: هڪ قسم جي گول، نرم ۽ سپاٽ ٽوپي جنهن کي ڪناري نه هوندي آهي، اڪثر سپاهين، فنڪارن ۽ فيشن وارن جي پاران پاتي ويندي آهي، اڪثر هڪ پاسي جهڪائي پاتي ويندي آهي
antonyms: No common antonym
urduMeaning: ایک قسم کی نرم، گول اور چپٹی ٹوپی جس کا کنارا نہیں ہوتا، اکثر فوجی، فنکار اور فیشن پسند لوگ پہنتے ہیں، عام طور پر ایک طرف جھکا کر پہنی جاتی ہے
examples: The artist wore a black beret while painting. French soldiers are often seen wearing green berets. She matched her red beret with a white coat. The boy looked smart in his school beret. Berets are part of the official uniform of many army units.
synonyms: Cap, Hat, Headgear, Bonnet

sindhiMeaning: برداشت، صبر، سهپ، ڊگهي عرصي تائين مشڪل برداشت ڪرڻ جي طاقت، جسماني يا ذهني قوت، تڪليفن کي سهڻ جي صلاحيت
englishMeaning: The ability to withstand hardship, pain, stress, or prolonged effort without giving up. Lasting strength and patience. The power of bearing difficulty over time. Used both for physical stamina in sports or work and for mental and emotional capacity to face challenges.
antonyms: Weakness, Frailty, Surrender, Fatigue, Impatience
synonyms: Stamina, Patience, Perseverance, Tolerance, Fortitude, Resilience, Persistence
examples: Marathon running requires great physical endurance. Her endurance during the long illness inspired everyone. Soldiers are trained to build mental and physical endurance. The endurance of the workers in harsh weather was admirable. Success often depends on hard work and endurance.
urduMeaning: برداشت، صبر، قوتِ برداشت، طویل عرصے تک مشکل کو برداشت کرنے کی طاقت، جسمانی یا ذہنی قوت، تکالیف کو سہنے کی صلاحیت

antonyms: Original, Fresh, Novel, Innovative, Unique, Creative, New
sindhiMeaning: گهڻو استعمال ٿيل، فرسوده، عام ۽ بي اثر ٿي ويل، جنهن ۾ نواڻ نه هجي، اهڙو جملو يا خيال جيڪو ايترو ته استعمال ٿي چڪو هجي جو دلچسپي نه رکي
synonyms: Clichéd, Trite, Overused, Stale, Banal, Worn-out, Unoriginal
examples: The speech was full of hackneyed phrases and lacked originality. Many writers avoid such hackneyed expressions in their novels. The film’s plot felt hackneyed and predictable. He used the same hackneyed argument again. Hackneyed slogans no longer impress modern voters.
englishMeaning: Lacking originality or freshness due to overuse. Overly familiar through repetition. Stale, clichéd, or commonplace. Used to describe phrases, ideas, expressions, plots, or themes that have been used so often that they no longer feel interesting, creative, or effective.
urduMeaning: فرسودہ، پامال، گھِسا پٹا، بہت زیادہ استعمال شدہ، ایسا جملہ یا خیال جو اتنا دہرایا جا چکا ہو کہ اپنی تازگی اور تاثیر کھو چکا ہو

englishMeaning: The theory, philosophy, and science of law. The study of the principles on which legal systems are built. A particular system or body of law of a country or area. The branch of knowledge dealing with the interpretation, application, and development of legal rules.
synonyms: Law, Legal theory, Legal science, Legal philosophy, Fiqh, Code of law
urduMeaning: علمِ قانون، فقہ، قانون کا فلسفہ، قانونی اصولوں کا مطالعہ، قانونی نظام کی تشریح، عدالتی فیصلوں کا علم
examples: He is studying jurisprudence at a well-known university. Islamic jurisprudence has a long and rich history. Modern jurisprudence covers human rights and constitutional law. The judge is well versed in international jurisprudence. Students of law must understand the basics of jurisprudence.
antonyms: No direct antonym
sindhiMeaning: قانون جو علم، فقه، قانون جو فلسفو، قانون جي اصولن جو مطالعو، قانوني نظام جي سمجهاڻي، عدالتي فيصلن جو علم
فرقيوار، فرقي وارو، ڪنهن خاص فرقي يا گروهه سان وابسته، تنگ نظر، فرقيواري سوچ وارو، اهڙو تڪرار جيڪو مذهبي يا گروهي اختلاف تي ٻڌل هجي
synonyms: Partisan, Factional, Denominational, Bigoted, Narrow-minded, Parochial
examples: The country has suffered from years of sectarian violence. Sectarian politics has weakened national unity. The government banned sectarian hate speech in the media. Leaders should rise above sectarian interests. Sectarian conflicts often have deep historical roots.
urduMeaning: فرقہ وارانہ، فرقہ پرست، کسی خاص فرقے یا گروہ سے وابستہ، تنگ نظر، ایسا تنازعہ جو مذہبی یا گروہی اختلاف پر مبنی ہو
englishMeaning: Relating to or supporting a particular religious, political, or social sect. Narrow-minded loyalty to one group over others. Often involving prejudice, hatred, or violence between different sects. Used to describe conflicts, attitudes, or actions based on rigid group identity.
antonyms: Nonsectarian, Tolerant, Open-minded, Inclusive, Broad-minded, Universal

examples: The empire reached its zenith during his rule. She was at the zenith of her career when she retired. The sun was almost at its zenith by noon. The team’s performance touched its zenith last season. Their popularity reached its zenith after the new album’s release.
urduMeaning: عروج، بلندی، چوٹی، آسمان کا سب سے اونچا نقطہ، کامیابی یا طاقت کی انتہا، کسی کی زندگی یا کیریئر کا بہترین دور
synonyms: Peak, Summit, Apex, Climax, Pinnacle, Top, Acme, Height
antonyms: Nadir, Bottom, Low point, Base, Foot, Depth
englishMeaning: The highest point reached by a celestial or other object. The peak or culmination of success, power, or development. The point in the sky directly above an observer. Used figuratively to describe the most successful or glorious moment in someone’s life or career.
sindhiMeaning: چوٽي، عروج، بلندي، آسمان جو سڀ کان مٿيون نقطو، ڪاميابي يا طاقت جي اوچائي، ڪنهن جي زندگي يا ڪيريئر جو بهترين دور

antonyms: Strong, Sturdy, Solid, Durable, Robust, Firm, Convincing
englishMeaning: Thin, weak, and easily broken or torn. Lacking strength, durability, or solidity. Not strong enough to be reliable. Used both for physical objects of poor quality and for arguments, excuses, or evidence that are weak, unconvincing, or unlikely to be believed.
sindhiMeaning: ڪمزور، نازڪ، پتلو، جلدي ڀڄندڙ، غير معياري، ڪمزور دليل وارو، اهڙي شيءِ جيڪا مضبوط نه هجي ۽ آسانيءَ سان ڀڄي پوي
urduMeaning: کمزور، نازک، پتلا، جلد ٹوٹنے والا، غیر معیاری، کمزور دلیل والا، ایسی چیز جو مضبوط نہ ہو اور آسانی سے ٹوٹ جائے
examples: The house was made of flimsy wooden planks. She gave a flimsy excuse for being late again. The evidence presented in court was too flimsy to convict him. He wore a flimsy shirt on the cold winter day. The roof was so flimsy that it leaked during the rain.
synonyms: Weak, Fragile, Frail, Thin, Insubstantial, Feeble, Unconvincing

examples: I haven’t the foggiest idea where she has gone. He hadn’t the foggiest clue about the answer. Don’t ask me, I haven’t the foggiest. She had not the foggiest notion of what was happening in the office. They hadn’t the foggiest about the new rules.
synonyms: Slightest, Faintest, Vaguest, Remotest, Smallest
sindhiMeaning: اهڙي جاءِ يا وقت جتي سڀ کان وڌيڪ ڪوهيڙو هجي, خيالن، ڳالهين يا حالتن لاءِ استعمال ٿيندو آهي جيڪي سمجهڻ ڏکيا هجن, هن محاوري جو مطلب آهي ته ڪنهن ڳالهه جي بلڪل به خبر نه هجڻ
englishMeaning: (superlative of foggy) Describes a place or time with the thickest or heaviest fog. Describes ideas, memories, explanations, or situations that are extremely unclear. The phrase "not the foggiest" means having absolutely no knowledge or understanding.
urduMeaning: کسی ایسی جگہ یا وقت کے لیے جہاں دھند بہت زیادہ ہو, کسی خیال، وضاحت یا صورتحال کے لیے جو سمجھنے میں بہت مشکل ہو, اس محاورے کا مطلب ہے کہ کسی بات کا بالکل بھی علم نہ ہونا
antonyms: Clearest, Strongest, Definite, Certain, Sure
No specific antonym
urduMeaning: لمبی پٹی، لمبا تسمہ، چمڑے یا کپڑے کی لمبی پٹی جو بیگ، کیمرے، گھڑی یا دیگر اشیاء کے ساتھ لگی ہوتی ہے تاکہ انہیں کندھے پر یا لٹکا کر استعمال کیا جا سکے
sindhiMeaning: ڊگهي پٽي، ڊگهو تسمو، ڊگهي چمڙي يا ڪپڙي جي پٽي جا ٿيلهي، ڪئميرا، گهڙي يا ٻين شين سان لڳل هجي ته جيئن انهن کي ٽنگي يا ڪلهي تي رکي سگهجي
examples: The bag had a long strap that could be worn across the shoulder. She adjusted the long strap of her camera before the trip. The traveler tightened the long strap of his backpack. A long strap is more comfortable for carrying heavy items. The watch came with a long strap suitable for larger wrists.
synonyms: Belt, Band, Strip, Sling, Cord, Loop, Thong
englishMeaning: A long, narrow piece of leather, cloth, plastic, or other flexible material used for fastening, carrying, hanging, or holding something. Often attached to bags, watches, cameras, or belts to allow them to be worn on the shoulder, around the body, or hung from an object.

antonyms: Innocence, Lawfulness, Compliance, Defence, Protection, Compliment, Praise, Approval
englishMeaning: A breach of a law or rule; an illegal act. A crime or violation of legal or moral standards. Something that causes hurt feelings, anger, displeasure, or resentment in another person. The act of attacking or being on the attacking side in a conflict, game, or sport. Any action that offends someone or breaks accepted norms of behaviour, conduct, or law.
urduMeaning: جرم، قصور، خطا، قانون کی خلاف ورزی، ناجائز یا غیر قانونی فعل، کسی کی دل آزاری، ناراضگی، بے عزتی، ایسا عمل جو کسی کو تکلیف یا غصہ دلائے، حملہ کرنے والا پہلو، کسی کھیل یا جنگ میں حملہ آور فریق
sindhiMeaning: ڏوهه، جرم، خلاف ورزي، قانون شڪني، ڪا غلط يا ناجائز حرڪت، ڪنهن جي دل آزاري، ناراضگي جو سبب بڻجڻ، بي عزتي، اهڙو عمل جيڪو ڪنهن کي ناراض يا تڪليف ڏئي، حملي وارو پاسو، ڪنهن راند يا جنگ ۾ حملي ڪندڙ ڌر
examples: Driving without a licence is a serious offence in this country. He apologised at once so as not to cause any offence. The minister resigned after being charged with a criminal offence. She took offence at his careless remark about her work. Our team has a strong offence but a weak defence.
synonyms: Crime, Wrongdoing, Violation, Misdemeanour, Transgression, Insult, Affront, Outrage, Attack, Assault

antonyms: Ignore, Disregard, Forget, Dismiss, Discouragement, Hindrance
synonyms: Ponder, Reflect, Meditate, Contemplate, Think, Ruminate, Inspiration, Stimulus, Source of ideas
urduMeaning: گہری سوچ میں ڈوبنا، غور و فکر کرنا، سوچنا، خیالوں میں کھو جانا، سوچتے ہوئے کچھ کہنا، تخلیقی الہام کا ذریعہ، فنکار یا ادیب کے لیے تحریک دینے والی شخصیت، یونانی دیومالا میں نو دیویوں میں سے کوئی ایک جو علم و فن کی سرپرست تھی
sindhiMeaning: گهري سوچ ۾ پئجڻ، خيالن ۾ گم ٿيڻ، سوچڻ ويچارڻ، غور ڪرڻ، ڌيان سان ڪجهه چوڻ، تخليقي تحريڪ جو ذريعو، فنڪار يا اديب لاءِ الهام ڏيندڙ، يوناني ڏند ڪٿا ۾ نون ديوين مان ڪا هڪ جيڪا فن ۽ علم جو سرچشمو هئي
englishMeaning: To think about something deeply and at length, often in a quiet or thoughtful way. To ponder, reflect, or meditate. To say something in a thoughtful manner. A source of inspiration, especially for an artist, writer, or musician. In Greek mythology, one of the nine goddesses who inspired learning and the arts.
examples: She sat by the window and began to muse about her childhood. The poet found his muse in the quiet mountains of the north. He mused that life was full of unexpected turns. The artist often mused over his unfinished paintings for hours. Many writers consider nature their greatest muse.

antonyms: Calm, Soothe, Reassure, Comfort, Relax, Compose
urduMeaning: اچانک ڈرا دینا، چونکا دینا، ہڑبڑا دینا، یکدم حیران کر دینا، اچانک خوف زدہ کر دینا، کسی غیر متوقع آواز یا منظر سے چونکا دینا، ایکدم بدک جانا
sindhiMeaning: اوچتو ڊيڄارڻ، ڇرڪائڻ، اچانڪ حيران ڪرڻ، ايڪدم جهٻڪائڻ، ڊپ ۾ وجهڻ، اوچتي آواز يا حرڪت سان چوڪس ڪرڻ، ايڪدم ٽپ ڏياري ڇڏڻ، حيرت ۾ وجهڻ
englishMeaning: To cause a person or animal to feel sudden shock, surprise, or fright. To make someone jump or react quickly because of an unexpected event, sound, or sight. To be alarmed or astonished suddenly. The effect is usually short, sharp, and unexpected rather than deeply frightening.
examples: The loud thunderclap startled the children in the garden. She was startled by the sudden ring of the telephone at midnight. A deer can be easily startled by any movement in the bushes. His sudden appearance at the door startled everyone in the room. The news of his promotion startled even his closest friends.
synonyms: Surprise, Shock, Frighten, Alarm, Scare, Astonish, Jolt, Stun, Astound

antonyms: Stare, Gaze, Study, Examine, Scrutinise, Inspect
sindhiMeaning: هلڪي نظر وجهڻ، تڪڙي نگاهه ڦيرائڻ، اک ڦيرائي ڏسڻ، ٿوري وقت لاءِ ڏسڻ، سرسري طور ڏسڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ کي تڪڙي طرح پڙهڻ، ڪنهن سان ٽڪرائجي پاسي ڦرڻ، هڪ مختصر نظر
englishMeaning: To take a quick or brief look at something or someone. A rapid, short look. To read or examine something hurriedly. To strike something lightly and bounce off at an angle. A brief direct look that lasts only a moment.
examples: She glanced at her watch and realised she was late. He glanced over the newspaper headlines during breakfast. The two friends exchanged a quick glance and smiled. The ball glanced off the bat and went past the wicketkeeper. A single glance at the painting was enough to impress the visitors.
synonyms: Look, Peek, Peep, Glimpse, Skim, Scan, Browse, Brush, Graze
urduMeaning: اچٹتی نظر ڈالنا، سرسری طور پر دیکھنا، ایک نظر ڈالنا، جلدی سے دیکھنا، کسی چیز کو تیزی سے پڑھنا، کسی چیز سے ٹکرا کر پھسل جانا، مختصر نگاہ

englishMeaning: A strong feeling of active interest, excitement, or eagerness about something that you like or enjoy. Intense and eager enjoyment, interest, or approval. The energy and willingness with which a person approaches a task, idea, or activity. A subject or activity that arouses such interest.
antonyms: Apathy, Indifference, Boredom, Disinterest, Reluctance, Lethargy, Coolness
synonyms: Eagerness, Passion, Zeal, Keenness, Excitement, Fervour, Zest, Ardour, Interest
urduMeaning: جوش، ولولہ، شوق، گرمجوشی، دلچسپی، لگن، کسی کام کے لیے دلی رغبت، اندرونی جذبہ، توانائی اور سرگرمی، کسی موضوع میں شدید رغبت
examples: The students greeted the new teacher with great enthusiasm. He talked about his project with so much enthusiasm that everyone wanted to join. Her enthusiasm for music began when she was only six years old. The audience cheered the players with unmatched enthusiasm. Despite many failures, he never lost his enthusiasm for learning.
sindhiMeaning: جوش، ولولو، اتساه، شوق، چاهت، گرم جوشي، ڪنهن ڪم لاءِ گهري دلچسپي ۽ سرگرمي، چاهه سان ڪجهه ڪرڻ جي خواهش، اندروني جذبو، اتساه ۽ توانائي
بدنامي، بد شهرت، خراب ناماچار، ڪنهن غلط ڪم سبب مشهور ٿيڻ، رسوائي، عام ماڻهن ۾ خراب طور سڃاتو وڃڻ، عوامي بدنامي
englishMeaning: The state of being famous or well known for something bad or unpleasant. Wide reputation, usually of an unfavourable kind. The condition of being notorious. Public attention received because of misconduct, scandal, crime, or other negative actions rather than for good achievements.
urduMeaning: بدنامی، بد شہرت، رسوائی، کسی برے کام کی وجہ سے مشہور ہونا، عوامی سطح پر منفی شہرت، عام لوگوں میں برے انداز میں جانا پہچانا جانا
antonyms: Fame, Honour, Repute, Esteem, Respect, Prestige, Good name
synonyms: Infamy, Disrepute, Disgrace, Ill repute, Bad reputation, Scandal, Dishonour
examples: The gangster gained notoriety for his violent crimes across the city. The scandal brought instant notoriety to the once respected minister. She achieved notoriety after the controversial interview was broadcast. The street is famous for its notoriety as a centre of illegal trade. His notoriety made it difficult for him to find honest work.

synonyms: Crucial, Critical, Central, Key, Vital, Decisive, Essential, Fundamental, Important
examples: Education plays a pivotal role in the progress of any nation. Her pivotal performance helped the team win the championship. The treaty was a pivotal moment in the history of the region. He held a pivotal position in the company for over a decade. The witness gave pivotal evidence that changed the course of the trial.
urduMeaning: کلیدی، مرکزی، انتہائی اہم، فیصلہ کن، بنیادی حیثیت رکھنے والا، ایسا موڑ یا شخص جس پر کامیابی یا ناکامی کا دار و مدار ہو، محور کی مانند اہم
englishMeaning: Of crucial importance in relation to the development or success of something. Acting like a pivot on which other things turn or depend. Central, key, or vital. A pivotal moment, decision, person, or event is one that has a major influence on what happens afterwards.
sindhiMeaning: مرڪزي، انتهائي اهم، ڪليدي، فيصلي ڪن، جنهن تي ٻيون ڳالهيون دارومدار رکن، بنيادي حيثيت رکندڙ، اهڙو موقعو يا ماڻهو جنهن تي ڪاميابي يا ناڪامي جو دارومدار هجي
antonyms: Unimportant, Minor, Trivial, Insignificant, Peripheral, Secondary, Negligible
Conceal, Hide, Withhold, Keep secret, Suppress, Cover up, Hush up
englishMeaning: To make known or reveal private, secret, or confidential information. To disclose something that was previously hidden or unknown. To tell people about something which should have been kept secret. Often used in the context of names, sources, plans, or sensitive details.
urduMeaning: راز فاش کرنا، بھید کھولنا، چھپی ہوئی بات بتانا، انکشاف کرنا، خفیہ معلومات ظاہر کرنا، پوشیدہ بات ظاہر کر دینا، رازداری توڑنا
examples: The journalist refused to divulge the name of his source. She would not divulge the details of the secret meeting to anyone. Company employees are not allowed to divulge confidential client information. He finally divulged the truth after years of silence. The witness was forced to divulge what he had seen that night.
sindhiMeaning: راز فاش ڪرڻ، ڳجهه ظاهر ڪرڻ، لڪل ڳالهه ٻڌائڻ، انڪشاف ڪرڻ، ڄاڻ پڌري ڪرڻ، خفيه معلومات ٻين تائين پهچائڻ، رازداري ٽوڙڻ
synonyms: Reveal, Disclose, Tell, Expose, Uncover, Make known, Confess, Communicate, Leak

antonyms: River, Sea, Ocean, Lake, Flood, Torrent
urduMeaning: چھوٹی ندی، چھوٹا نالا، پانی کی پتلی دھار، چشمہ، آنسوؤں یا خون کی باریک دھار، چھوٹی بہتی ہوئی دھارا، چھوٹا سا بہاؤ
englishMeaning: A very small stream of water; a tiny brook. A narrow flow of liquid, especially water, blood, or tears, that moves in a thin line. A small natural watercourse, smaller than a river or stream. Often used in literary descriptions of landscapes.
examples: A clear rivulet ran through the green meadow behind our house. Children love to play in the shallow rivulet during the summer. After the rain, tiny rivulets formed along the dusty road. A rivulet of sweat trickled down his forehead as he worked. The rivulet eventually joined a larger river in the valley.
sindhiMeaning: ننڍڙي ندي، ننڍڙو نالو، پاڻيءَ جو سنهڙو وهڪرو، چشمو، پاڻيءَ جي سنهي ڌار، ڳوڙهن يا رت جي سنهي ڌارا، ننڍڙي وهندڙ ڌارا
synonyms: Stream, Brook, Creek, Streamlet, Runnel, Rill, Trickle

antonyms: Cursed, Unholy, Desecrated, Profane, Disrespected, Ordinary, Common
englishMeaning: Regarded as holy, sacred, or greatly respected. Honoured and revered because of long history, religious importance, or deep tradition. Consecrated or made holy through religious ceremony. Used to describe places, names, traditions, or memories that are treated with great respect.
examples: The mosque is a hallowed place for the people of this town. He spoke of his teacher with hallowed respect. Cricket has a hallowed tradition at this historic ground. Their names are written in the hallowed pages of history. The hallowed silence of the library should never be broken.
sindhiMeaning: مقدس، پاڪ، پوڄا جوڳو، عزت وارو، احترام جوڳو، ديني لحاظ کان پاڪ ڪيل، ڊگهي وقت کان عزت وارو ٿيل، روايتي طور تي معزز
urduMeaning: مقدس، پاک، قابل احترام، متبرک، تقدیس یافتہ، مذہبی طور پر پاک کیا گیا، روایتی طور پر معزز، عقیدت کے ساتھ یاد رکھا جانے والا
synonyms: Sacred, Holy, Sanctified, Consecrated, Blessed, Revered, Venerated, Honoured

antonyms: Services, Liabilities, Worthless items
examples: Oil and gas are among the most important commodities in the world market. Prices of basic commodities have risen sharply this year. Farmers sell their commodities directly to wholesalers. The country exports several agricultural commodities to Europe. Honest information has become one of the most valuable commodities of our age.
englishMeaning: Raw materials or primary agricultural products that can be bought and sold, such as oil, wheat, cotton, or gold. Useful or valuable things. Articles of trade or commerce, especially products as opposed to services. Goods that have economic value and can be exchanged in markets.
sindhiMeaning: واپاري شيون، اجناس، خام مال، خريد و فروخت جون شيون، مارڪيٽ ۾ وڪرو ٿيندڙ شيون، زرعي پيداوار، قيمتي ۽ ڪارآمد شيون، تجارتي مال
urduMeaning: اجناس، تجارتی اشیاء، خام مال، خرید و فروخت کی چیزیں، منڈی میں بکنے والی اشیاء، زرعی پیداوار، قیمتی اور کارآمد چیزیں، سامانِ تجارت
synonyms: Goods, Products, Wares, Merchandise, Articles, Stock, Produce, Items

sindhiMeaning: بچاءُ، مدافعت، بيمارين کان حفاظت، جسم جي اندروني قوت جيڪا بيمارين کي روڪي، قانوني تحفظ، سزا کان آزادي، ڪنهن ذميواري کان رعايت
examples: Vaccines help the body build immunity against dangerous diseases. The witness was given immunity from prosecution in exchange for his testimony. Diplomats often enjoy immunity from local laws while serving abroad. Regular exercise and good food strengthen the body's immunity. No one has complete immunity from criticism in public life.
synonyms: Resistance, Protection, Exemption, Freedom, Safeguard, Privilege, Impunity
antonyms: Susceptibility, Vulnerability, Liability, Exposure, Weakness, Responsibility
urduMeaning: مدافعت، قوتِ مدافعت، بیماریوں سے بچاؤ، جسم کی اندرونی طاقت جو بیماریوں کا مقابلہ کرے، قانونی تحفظ، سزا سے استثنیٰ، کسی ذمہ داری سے چھوٹ
englishMeaning: The ability of the body to resist a particular infection or toxin through the action of specific antibodies or white blood cells. Protection or exemption from something, especially an obligation, penalty, or duty. In law, freedom from prosecution or legal action granted to a person. Resistance to something unpleasant.

sindhiMeaning: تائيد ڪرڻ، حمايت ڪرڻ، منظوري ڏيڻ، پٺڀرائي ڪرڻ، چيڪ يا دستاويز جي پٺيءَ تي صحيح ڪرڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ يا اميدوار جي عوامي طور سفارش ڪرڻ، ڊرائيونگ لائسنس تي ڏوهه جو اندراج ڪرڻ
synonyms: Support, Approve, Back, Recommend, Sanction, Sign, Authorise, Advocate, Champion
englishMeaning: To declare one's public approval or support of something or someone. To sign the back of a cheque or bill in order to make it payable to another person or to cash it. To recommend a product, service, or candidate, especially in advertising or politics. To add a note to an official document, such as a driving licence, recording a penalty.
examples: Several famous athletes endorse this brand of sports shoes. The committee unanimously endorsed the new education policy. Please endorse the cheque before depositing it in the bank. The party leader refused to endorse the controversial candidate. His licence was endorsed after the traffic offence.
urduMeaning: توثیق کرنا، تائید کرنا، حمایت کرنا، منظوری دینا، چیک یا دستاویز کی پشت پر دستخط کرنا، کسی پروڈکٹ یا امیدوار کی عوامی سفارش کرنا، لائسنس پر جرم درج کرنا
antonyms: Oppose, Reject, Disapprove, Denounce, Condemn, Veto, Repudiate
Keep, Retain, Hold on to, Embrace, Adopt, Continue
sindhiMeaning: کاهي، نالي، نيڪال جو نالو، آبپاشي لاءِ کوٽيل کاهي، ڇڏي ڏيڻ، ترڪ ڪرڻ، اڇلائي ڇڏڻ، طياري کي پاڻيءَ تي زبردستي لاهڻ، ڪنهن کي اوچتو ڇڏي وڃڻ
englishMeaning: A long narrow channel dug in the ground, typically used for drainage or irrigation along the side of a road or field. To get rid of something or someone that is no longer wanted. To make a forced landing of an aircraft on water. In informal use, to leave a class, meeting, or person abruptly.
examples: The car skidded off the road and landed in a deep ditch. Farmers dig ditches to bring water to their fields. He decided to ditch his old phone and buy a new one. The pilot had to ditch the plane in the sea after engine failure. She ditched her friends and went home early.
urduMeaning: خندق، نالی، نکاسی کا نالہ، آبپاشی کے لیے کھودی گئی نالی، چھوڑ دینا، ترک کر دینا، پھینک دینا، طیارے کو پانی پر زبردستی اتارنا، کسی کو اچانک چھوڑ دینا
synonyms: Trench, Channel, Drain, Gutter, Furrow, Abandon, Discard, Dump, Scrap, Leave

antonyms: Peaceful, Easygoing, Amicable, Conciliatory, Cooperative, Agreeable
urduMeaning: مقدمہ باز، عدالت بازی کا شوقین، جلد قانونی کارروائی کرنے والا، جھگڑالو، چھوٹی چھوٹی بات پر عدالت جانے کا رجحان رکھنے والا، قانونی نزاع پسند
sindhiMeaning: مقدمي بازي جو شوقين، مقدما هلائيندڙ، عدالت ۾ وڃڻ جو رجحان رکندڙ، جهيڙي جهٽي وارو، قانوني ڪارروائي ڪرڻ ۾ تڪڙو، ڪورٽن ۾ گهٽي گهٽي تي وڃڻ وارو
examples: He has a litigious nature and sues anyone who annoys him. The company was caught in a long and litigious battle with its rivals. America is often described as a litigious society. Their litigious neighbour took them to court over the boundary wall. Doctors today work in an increasingly litigious environment.
englishMeaning: Tending to go to law to settle disputes; overly eager or quick to take legal action. Concerned with lawsuits and legal proceedings. Showing a strong inclination to argue or quarrel. A litigious person or society frequently resorts to courts even over minor disagreements.
synonyms: Argumentative, Contentious, Quarrelsome, Disputatious, Legalistic

examples: The professor gave a lucid explanation of the difficult theory. Despite his high fever, he had a few lucid moments in the afternoon. Her writing is lucid and a pleasure to read. The water in the lake was so lucid that we could see the bottom. He presented a lucid argument that convinced the entire committee.
urduMeaning: واضح، صاف، روشن، آسانی سے سمجھ میں آنے والا، صاف ذہن والا، شفاف، ہوش و حواس میں، صاف بیانی والا، روشن خیال
sindhiMeaning: صاف، چٽو، واضح، آسانيءَ سان سمجهه ۾ ايندڙ، چٽي ذهن وارو، روشن، شفاف، ذهني طور تي صاف ۽ هوشيار، صاف بياني وارو
englishMeaning: Expressed clearly and easy to understand. Showing the ability to think clearly, especially in the middle of confusion or illness. Bright, shining, or transparent. A lucid explanation, writing, or person is clear and free from confusion.
synonyms: Clear, Comprehensible, Intelligible, Understandable, Coherent, Transparent, Plain, Articulate

antonyms: Sanity, Lucidity, Calmness, Composure, Clear-headedness, Reason

englishMeaning: Clever and skilful, especially in handling difficult situations. Skilled. Dexterous. Expert. Quick and able in thought or action. Showing great ability in using the hands or the mind. Used for people who manage tasks, problems, or challenges with intelligence and ease.

englishMeaning: To damage something severely, especially by cutting or tearing off parts of it. To injure a person or animal badly by removing or destroying body parts. To disfigure. examples: The accident mutilated his right arm beyond recognition. Vandals mutilated the ancient statue in the museum. Wild animals had mutilated the body of the deer. Censors mutilated the film by cutting out important scenes. It is a crime to mutilate currency notes in any country.

The crowd vociferated loudly when the referee made an unfair decision. She vociferated her support for the cause at the public meeting. examples: The young pianist showed a prodigious talent at the age of six. The company made a prodigious profit in the last financial year. englishMeaning: Showing little emotion or interest. Calm and unexcitable. Impassive. Unemotional. Not easily moved by feelings or surprises. Used to describe a person whose face or behaviour does not reveal their thoughts or reactions, sometimes appearing dull or indifferent.
