Her orgulous behaviour cost her many true friends. Such an orgulous attitude is rarely appreciated in modern society.
englishMeaning: Excessively proud, haughty, or arrogant. Showing great pride and self-importance. Disdainful in manner. An old or literary word used to describe someone who behaves in a proud and superior way, often looking down on others. It carries a slightly negative tone.
sindhiMeaning: مغرور، وڏائي ڪندڙ، گهمنڊي، فخر مان ڀريل، پاڻ کي ٻين کان مٿاهون سمجهندڙ، آڪڙ وارو، نخريلو، شيخي خور، فخر سان ٻين کي حقير سمجهڻ وارو، انا پرست
urduMeaning: مغرور، متکبر، گھمنڈی، فخر سے بھرا ہوا، اپنے آپ کو دوسروں سے برتر سمجھنے والا، اکڑ والا، نخرے باز، شیخی خور، فخر سے دوسروں کو حقیر سمجھنے والا، خود پسند
antonyms: Humble, Modest, Meek, Unassuming, Self-effacing, Down-to-earth, Polite, Gracious

urduMeaning: دھمکانا، رعب جمانا، ڈرانا، اونچی آواز میں بات کر کے دباؤ ڈالنا، گالیاں دے کر ڈرانا، زبردستی کرنا، حکم چلانا، دوسروں کو تنگ کرنا، دھونس دینا، ڈانٹ ڈپٹ کرنا
synonyms: Bully, Intimidate, Threaten, Browbeat, Harass, Domineer, Badger, Pressurize, Coerce, Pester
sindhiMeaning: ڌمڪائڻ، ڌونس ڌاڙي ڏيڻ، رعب ڄمائڻ، گهٻرائڻ، اوچي آواز ۾ ڳالهائي دٻاءَ هيٺ آڻڻ، گاريون ڏئي ڊيڄارڻ، زبردستي ڪرڻ، حڪم هلائڻ، ٻين کي تنگ ڪرڻ، دٻاءُ وجهڻ
examples: The senior employee used to hector the new staff members constantly. He hectored his younger brother into doing all the housework. The coach hectored the players for their poor performance. She refused to be hectored by anyone, no matter how powerful. The boss tried to hector everyone in the meeting, but no one listened.
antonyms: Encourage, Support, Comfort, Help, Assist, Praise, Soothe, Coax
englishMeaning: To talk to someone in a bullying, threatening, or aggressive way. To intimidate by loud and persistent harassment. To bully. To pressurize someone through harsh words. Used to describe a person who tries to control or frighten others by speaking in a domineering, boastful, or scolding manner.

urduMeaning: مبلغ، مذہب کی تبلیغ کرنے والا، دین کا پرچار کرنے والا، عیسائیت یا کسی اور مذہب کی تبلیغ کے لیے بھیجا گیا شخص، بیرونِ ملک مذہب پھیلانے، تعلیم دینے یا لوگوں کی مدد کرنے جانے والا، کسی نظریے یا مقصد کا پُرجوش پرچارک، مشن سے متعلق
antonyms: Atheist, Disbeliever, Skeptic, Convert, Follower
sindhiMeaning: مبلغ، مذهب جي تبليغ ڪندڙ، دين جو پرچار ڪندڙ، عيسائيت يا ٻئي مذهب جي تبليغ لاءِ موڪليل شخص، ڌارئين ملڪ ۾ مذهب پکيڙڻ، تعليم ڏيڻ يا ماڻهن جي مدد ڪرڻ ويندڙ، ڪنهن نظريي يا مقصد جو پرجوش پرچارڪ، مشن سان لاڳاپيل
synonyms: Evangelist, Preacher, Apostle, Proselytizer, Crusader, Propagandist, Promoter, Campaigner
examples: The missionary spent twenty years teaching in remote African villages. She worked as a medical missionary in rural India. The young missionary devoted his life to spreading his faith. They built a school and a hospital during their missionary work. He had an almost missionary zeal for protecting the environment.
englishMeaning: A person sent on a religious mission to promote a faith and convert others to it. A person who works to spread Christianity or another religion, often in a foreign country. Someone who travels to teach religion, provide education, or help people in poor or remote areas as part of religious service. A person who is very enthusiastic and dedicated to spreading a particular belief, cause, or idea. Relating to or characteristic of a religious mission or its workers.

sindhiMeaning: قرباني ڏيڻ، ڪا قيمتي شيءِ ڪنهن وڏي مقصد لاءِ ترڪ ڪرڻ، ڪنهن وڏي ڀلائي خاطر نقصان برداشت ڪرڻ، الله جي راهه ۾ جانور ذبح ڪرڻ، نذرانو ڏيڻ، پنهنجي ذاتي فائدي کي ٻين لاءِ قربان ڪرڻ، بي لوث ايثار
synonyms: Forgo, Give up, Surrender, Relinquish, Offer, Forfeit, Renounce, Immolate
examples: Parents often sacrifice their own comfort for their children. The soldiers made the ultimate sacrifice for their country. Muslims sacrifice animals during Eid al-Adha. She sacrificed her career to take care of her family. He had to sacrifice his queen to win the chess match.
urduMeaning: قربانی دینا، کوئی قیمتی چیز کسی بڑے مقصد کے لیے چھوڑ دینا، کسی بڑی بھلائی کی خاطر نقصان برداشت کرنا، اللہ کی راہ میں جانور ذبح کرنا، نذرانہ دینا، اپنے ذاتی فائدے کو دوسروں کے لیے قربان کر دینا، بے لوث ایثار
antonyms: Keep, Retain, Hold on to, Gain, Preserve, Acquire
englishMeaning: To give up something valuable or important for the sake of something else considered more worthwhile. The act of offering something to a deity, especially the killing of an animal or person as a religious ritual. A loss or something given up in order to gain or achieve a greater purpose. To sell or give away something at a loss. In games, to deliberately give up a piece or advantage to gain a better position. An act of selfless giving for the benefit of others.

sindhiMeaning: خيرات، صدقو، غريبن ۽ مسڪينن کي ڏنل مال يا پئسا، محتاجن کي مدد طور ڏنل شيءِ، رحم ۽ همدردي ۾ ضرورتمندن کي ڏنل عطيو، دين جي حڪم تحت غريبن جي مدد ڪرڻ
antonyms: Greed, Withholding, Hoarding, Selfishness
synonyms: Charity, Donation, Offering, Handout, Contribution, Gift, Aid, Relief
englishMeaning: Money, food, or other donations given to poor and needy people as an act of charity. Charitable giving as a religious or moral duty. Help or relief given out of compassion to those in need. Voluntary donations made to support the poor, often associated with religious practice.
urduMeaning: خیرات، صدقہ، زکوٰۃ، غریبوں اور مسکینوں کو دیا جانے والا مال یا رقم، محتاجوں کو بطورِ مدد دی جانے والی چیز، رحم اور ہمدردی میں ضرورت مندوں کو دیا گیا عطیہ، دین کے حکم کے تحت غریبوں کی مدد
examples: He gave alms to the beggars outside the mosque. Giving alms to the poor is an important act of charity in Islam. The wealthy man distributed alms during the festival. She always keeps some coins to give as alms. Collecting alms for the needy was part of their religious duty.

sindhiMeaning: تمام گهٽ، ٿورو، محدود، انتهائي گهٽ، معمولي، ٿورو ڪلائن، محدود مقدار
englishMeaning: Very small in amount or size; insufficient. Something extremely limited, scanty, or meager. Often used to describe resources, quantities, or space that are barely adequate or almost negligible.
antonyms: Ample, Abundant, Sufficient, Generous, Plentiful
urduMeaning: نہایت کم، محدود، قلیل، انتہائی محدود، مختصر مقدار
synonyms: Tiny, Scanty, Meager, Insufficient, Minimal, Slender
examples: The evidence against him was exiguous, making the case weak. She lived on an exiguous income, barely covering her expenses. The exiguous rainfall this year has affected crops severely. His knowledge of the subject was exiguous, but he tried to answer confidently.

antonyms: Condemnation, Blame, Punishment, Guilt, Penalty, Accusation
synonyms: Forgiveness, Pardon, Acquittal, Remission, Exoneration, Clearance, Mercy, Redemption
englishMeaning: Formal release from guilt, obligation, or punishment. The act of forgiving someone for their sins, especially the religious forgiveness pronounced by a priest. Freedom from blame or responsibility. A declaration that a person is forgiven and free from the consequences of wrongdoing. The state of being pardoned or cleared of sin.
urduMeaning: گناہوں سے نجات، بخشش، معافی، الزام یا سزا سے آزادی، گناہوں کی رسمی معافی، قصور سے بری ہونا، خطا معاف ہونے کا اعلان، پاک اور بے گناہ ہونے کی حالت
examples: The priest granted absolution to the repentant man. She sought absolution for the mistakes of her past. He felt a sense of absolution after confessing the truth. The court's decision gave him absolution from all charges. Many people seek spiritual absolution through prayer.
sindhiMeaning: گناهن کان نجات، بخشش، معافي، الزام يا سزا کان آزادي، گناهن جي رسمي معافي، قصور کان بري ٿيڻ، خطا معاف ٿيڻ جو اعلان، پاڪ ۽ بيگناهه ٿيڻ جي حالت
مضبوطي، پختگي، مستقل مزاجي، فيصلي يا راءِ ۾ ثابت قدمي، سختي، ڪنهن شيءِ جي سخت ۽ ٺوس هجڻ، ڪردار جي مضبوطي، دٻاءُ ۾ نه جهڪڻ جي حالت، عزم ۽ استقلال
urduMeaning: مضبوطی، پختگی، استقلال، فیصلے یا رائے میں ثابت قدمی، سختی، کسی چیز کا سخت اور ٹھوس ہونا، کردار کی مضبوطی، دباؤ میں نہ جھکنے کی حالت، عزم اور استقامت
englishMeaning: The quality of being strong, solid, and not easily moved or changed. Determination and steadiness in decisions, opinions, or actions. The physical hardness or solidity of an object. Strength and stability of character or will. The state of being resolute and not yielding to pressure.
antonyms: Weakness, Softness, Flexibility, Hesitation, Instability, Indecision
synonyms: Strength, Steadiness, Resolve, Determination, Solidity, Stability, Hardness, Sternness
examples: She handled the difficult situation with great firmness. The firmness of his decision impressed everyone. He spoke with calm firmness and did not change his stance. The firmness of the mattress provided good support for the back. The teacher maintained firmness while remaining kind to the students.

antonyms: Truth, Vindication, Proof, Fair charge, Exoneration, Honest claim
englishMeaning: The act of wrongly attributing a fault, crime, or bad quality to someone without justification. A baseless accusation or charge made against a person. Falsely blaming someone for something they did not do. An untrue statement that damages someone's reputation by charging them with wrongdoing.
sindhiMeaning: ڪوڙو الزام، بي بنياد تهمت، ڪنهن تي ناحق ڏوهه يا برائي مڙهڻ، بنا ثبوت ڪنهن تي الزام لڳائڻ، ڪنهن کي اهڙي ڪم لاءِ موردِ الزام ٺهرائڻ جيڪو هن نه ڪيو هجي، عزت کي نقصان پهچائيندڙ ڪوڙي ڳالهه
examples: He was deeply hurt by the false imputation against his honesty. The false imputation ruined her reputation in the community. The court dismissed the case as a false imputation. Making a false imputation about someone can lead to legal action. He filed a complaint over the false imputation of theft.
urduMeaning: جھوٹا الزام، بے بنیاد تہمت، کسی پر ناحق جرم یا برائی تھوپنا، بغیر ثبوت کسی پر الزام لگانا، کسی کو ایسے کام کا ذمہ دار ٹھہرانا جو اس نے نہ کیا ہو، عزت کو نقصان پہنچانے والی جھوٹی بات
synonyms: False accusation, Slander, Defamation, Calumny, Libel, Aspersion, Smear, Allegation

urduMeaning: الزام، تہمت، کسی پر جرم یا غلطی عائد کرنے کا دعویٰ، کسی کو قصوروار ٹھہرانا، الزام لگانے یا لگنے کا عمل، کسی کے خلاف رسمی طور پر جرم کا دعویٰ کرنا
sindhiMeaning: الزام، تهمت، ڪنهن تي ڏوهه يا غلطي مڙهڻ جو دعويٰ، ڪنهن کي قصوروار ٺهرائڻ، الزام لڳائڻ يا لڳجڻ جو عمل، ڪنهن جي خلاف رسمي طور تي ڏوهه جو دعويٰ ڪرڻ
antonyms: Defense, Denial, Exoneration, Acquittal, Vindication, Praise
synonyms: Charge, Allegation, Indictment, Blame, Complaint, Claim, Imputation, Denunciation
englishMeaning: A charge or claim that someone has done something wrong or illegal. A statement blaming a person for a fault, crime, or offense. The act of accusing or being accused. An assertion that a person is guilty of misconduct, often made formally.
examples: The accusation against him was never proven in court. She denied the accusation of cheating in the exam. Making a serious accusation requires solid evidence. The accusations damaged his political career. He responded calmly to the false accusation.

antonyms: Night prayer, Evening prayer, Noon prayer
sindhiMeaning: فجر جي نماز، صبح سوير سج اڀرڻ کان اڳ پڙهي ويندڙ فرض نماز، اسلام ۾ پنجن نمازن مان پهرين نماز، صبح جي شروعات ۾ پڙهي ويندڙ عبادت، سج اڀرڻ کان اڳ ڪيل بندگي
examples: He wakes up early every day to offer the dawn prayer. The mosque was full of worshippers for the dawn prayer. Offering the dawn prayer requires waking up before sunrise. She felt peaceful after completing the dawn prayer. The call for the dawn prayer echoed across the quiet town.
urduMeaning: فجر کی نماز، صبح سویرے سورج نکلنے سے پہلے پڑھی جانے والی فرض نماز، اسلام میں پانچ نمازوں میں سے پہلی نماز، صبح کے آغاز میں ادا کی جانے والی عبادت، طلوعِ آفتاب سے پہلے کی جانے والی بندگی
englishMeaning: The early morning obligatory prayer offered before sunrise, known as Fajr in Islam. The first of the five daily Muslim prayers, performed at dawn. A prayer said at the break of day. The act of worship carried out in the early hours before the sun rises.
synonyms: Fajr, Morning prayer, Daybreak prayer, Sunrise prayer

antonyms: Dawn prayer, Night prayer, Evening prayer
urduMeaning: ظہر کی نماز، دوپہر کے وقت سورج ڈھلنے کے بعد پڑھی جانے والی فرض نماز، اسلام میں پانچ نمازوں میں سے دوسری نماز، دوپہر کے وقت ادا کی جانے والی عبادت، زوالِ آفتاب کے بعد کی جانے والی بندگی
examples: He offers the noon prayer during his lunch break. The workers gathered at the mosque for the noon prayer. The noon prayer is performed after midday. She paused her work to perform the noon prayer. People rushed to the mosque when the noon prayer was called.
sindhiMeaning: ظهر جي نماز، منجهند جو سج لهڻ شروع ٿيڻ کان پوءِ پڙهي ويندڙ فرض نماز، اسلام ۾ پنجن نمازن مان ٻي نماز، منجهند جي وقت ڪيل عبادت، سج لاهي شروع ٿيڻ کان پوءِ ڪيل بندگي
englishMeaning: The midday obligatory prayer offered after the sun passes its highest point, known as Zuhr in Islam. The second of the five daily Muslim prayers, performed in the early afternoon. A prayer said around midday. The act of worship carried out after the sun begins to decline.
synonyms: Zuhr, Midday prayer, Afternoon prayer

sindhiMeaning: الزام/ نسبت/ منسوب ڪرڻ، ذميواري مقرر ڪرڻ/ بدنيتي جو الزام، ڪنهن ڳالهه کي ڪنهن سان وابسته ڪرڻ/ گناهه يا ثواب کي منسوب ڪرڻ، اڻپوري انگن اکرن کي اندازي سان مڪمل ڪرڻ، ڪنهن تي الزام لڳائڻ، ڪنهن عمل يا ڳالهه جي ذميواري مڙهڻ، ڪنهن خاص خوبي  خامي  نيت يا عمل کي ڪنهن سان منسوب ڪرڻ، اهو الزام صحيح به ٿي سگهي ٿو ۽ غلط به، قانون  شماريات  مالي معاملن ۽ مذهبي اصطلاحن ۾ به هن لفظ جا مختلف فني مطلب آهن
antonyms: Exoneration, Vindication, Acquittal, Absolution, Praise, Commendation, Approval, Innocence, Disproof, Denial, Refutation, Justification
englishMeaning: The act of attributing, assigning, or ascribing a quality, action, fault, responsibility, motive, or characteristic to someone or something, whether rightly or wrongly. The process of saying that a person is responsible for something, especially something negative such as blame, guilt, wrongdoing, or bad intentions. It can also mean assigning a value, quality, cause, or characteristic to a person, object, or situation based on evidence, assumption, or judgment. In fields such as law, statistics, finance, and theology, the word has specialized meanings involving attribution or assignment.
synonyms: Attribution, Ascription, Assignment, Accusation, Allegation, Blame, Charge, Responsibility, Insinuation, Inference, Attribution of fault, Implied accusation, Allocation, Crediting, Estimation
urduMeaning: الزام لگانا/ منسوب کرنا/ نسبت دینا، ذمہ داری عائد کرنا/ قصور ٹھہرانا/ بد نیتی منسوب کرنا/کسی صفت یا عمل کو کسی سے وابستہ کرنا، نامکمل اعداد و شمار کو اندازے سے مکمل کرنا، کسی شخص پر کسی عمل  قصور  نیت  صفت یا ذمہ داری کو منسوب کرنا، یہ نسبت درست بھی ہو سکتی ہے اور غلط بھی، عام طور پر یہ لفظ الزام یا قصور عائد کرنے کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے  لیکن قانون  شماریات  مالیات اور مذہبی تعلیمات میں اس کے مخصوص فنی معنی بھی ہیں
examples: The imputation of fraud damaged his professional reputation, even though no evidence was found. She rejected the imputation that her decision was influenced by personal interests. In statistics, imputation is used to estimate missing values in a dataset. The court carefully considered whether the imputation of liability was legally justified.

The manager refused to impute dishonest motives to the employee without evidence. Many people impute the company's success to its strong leadership. It is unfair to impute every mistake to a single person. Historians should not impute modern values to people who lived centuries ago.
englishMeaning: To blame someone for something. To credit someone with something. To attribute a cause or motive. To assign responsibility. To regard something as belonging to someone. It is commonly used when blaming, praising, or assigning responsibility.
synonyms: Attribute, Ascribe, Assign, Credit, Accredit, Attach, Lay upon, Blame, Charge, Associate, Connect, Refer, Trace, Pin on, Fasten upon
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن تي الزام رکڻ، ڪنهن ڏانهن نسبت ڪرڻ، ڪنهن کي ذميوار قرار ڏيڻ، ڪنهن جي نالي سان منسوب ڪرڻ، نسبت ڪرڻ، منسوب ڪرڻ، الزام ڏيڻ، ذميواري مڙهڻ، سبب قرار ڏيڻ، ڪنهن جي کاتي ۾ وجهڻ، ڏوهه لڳائڻ
urduMeaning: الزام دینا، منسوب کرنا، ذمہ دار ٹھہرانا، نسبت کرنا، الزام عائد کرنا، نسبت دینا، ذمہ داری ڈالنا، قصور وار قرار دینا، کسی کے کھاتے میں ڈالنا، کسی کی طرف منسوب کرنا، سبب ٹھہرانا
antonyms: Exonerate, Acquit, Absolve, Clear, Excuse, Exculpate, Disassociate, Dissociate, Detach, Separate, Remove responsibility, Vindicate

synonyms: Asr, Late afternoon prayer, Twilight prayer
sindhiMeaning: عصر جي نماز، شام کان اڳ منجهند لهڻ کان پوءِ پڙهي ويندڙ فرض نماز، اسلام ۾ پنجن نمازن مان هڪ نماز، شام جي وقت ڪيل عبادت، سج لهڻ کان اڳ ڪيل بندگي
urduMeaning: عصر کی نماز، شام سے پہلے سہ پہر کے وقت پڑھی جانے والی فرض نماز، اسلام میں پانچ نمازوں میں سے ایک نماز، شام کے وقت ادا کی جانے والی عبادت، غروبِ آفتاب سے پہلے کی جانے والی بندگی
examples: He reached home in time for the evening prayer. The evening prayer is offered before the sun goes down. They gathered in the mosque for the evening prayer. She finished her tasks and went for the evening prayer. The evening prayer brought a sense of calm after a busy day.
englishMeaning: The prayer offered in the late afternoon before sunset, known as Asr in Islam. One of the five daily Muslim prayers, performed in the latter part of the day. A prayer said in the evening hours. An act of worship carried out before the sun sets.
antonyms: Dawn prayer, Noon prayer, Night prayer

examples: They broke their fast and then offered the dusk prayer. The dusk prayer is performed soon after sunset. He hurried to the mosque for the dusk prayer. The family gathered together for the dusk prayer. The call for the dusk prayer was heard as the sky turned orange.
synonyms: Maghrib, Sunset prayer, Twilight prayer
sindhiMeaning: مغرب جي نماز، سج لهڻ کان پوءِ سِگهوئي پڙهي ويندڙ فرض نماز، اسلام ۾ پنجن نمازن مان هڪ نماز، شام جو اونداهي ٿيڻ وقت ڪيل عبادت، سج لهڻ سان ئي ادا ڪيل بندگي
urduMeaning: مغرب کی نماز، سورج غروب ہونے کے فوراً بعد پڑھی جانے والی فرض نماز، اسلام میں پانچ نمازوں میں سے ایک نماز، شام کو اندھیرا ہونے کے وقت ادا کی جانے والی عبادت، غروبِ آفتاب کے ساتھ ہی کی جانے والی بندگی
antonyms: Dawn prayer, Noon prayer, Night prayer
englishMeaning: The prayer offered just after sunset, known as Maghrib in Islam. One of the five daily Muslim prayers, performed at dusk when the sun has set. A prayer said at twilight. An act of worship carried out immediately after the sun disappears below the horizon.

examples: He offers the night prayer before going to bed. The night prayer is the last prayer of the day. They went to the mosque for the night prayer. She recited extra verses during the night prayer. The streets were quiet after the night prayer was over.
englishMeaning: The prayer offered after nightfall, known as Isha in Islam. The last of the five daily Muslim prayers, performed when the sky is fully dark. A prayer said at night. An act of worship carried out in the late evening after twilight has ended.
sindhiMeaning: عشاءَ جي نماز، رات جي شروعات ۾ پڙهي ويندڙ فرض نماز، اسلام ۾ پنجن نمازن مان آخري نماز، آسمان مڪمل اونداهو ٿيڻ کان پوءِ ڪيل عبادت، رات جو دير سان ادا ڪيل بندگي
synonyms: Isha, Late prayer, Nightfall prayer
antonyms: Dawn prayer, Noon prayer, Evening prayer
urduMeaning: عشاء کی نماز، رات کے آغاز میں پڑھی جانے والی فرض نماز، اسلام میں پانچ نمازوں میں سے آخری نماز، آسمان مکمل تاریک ہونے کے بعد کی جانے والی عبادت، رات کو دیر سے ادا کی جانے والی بندگی

synonyms: Fard prayer, Compulsory prayer, Mandatory prayer, Required worship
examples: The five daily prayers are obligatory prayers for every Muslim. He never misses his obligatory prayers. Performing the obligatory prayer on time is highly rewarded. Children are taught to offer obligatory prayers from a young age. The obligatory prayer must be performed even while traveling.
sindhiMeaning: فرض نماز، اها نماز جيڪا هر مؤمن تي لازمي آهي، اهڙي عبادت جيڪا بنا ڪنهن جائز عذر جي ڇڏي نه ٿي سگهجي، روزانو لازمي نمازون جيڪي هر بالغ مسلمان تي فرض آهن، دين ۾ ضروري سمجهي ويندڙ عبادت جو فرض
englishMeaning: A prayer that is compulsory and must be performed by a believer, known as Fard in Islam. A required act of worship that cannot be skipped without a valid reason. The mandatory daily prayers that every adult Muslim is bound to offer. A duty of worship considered essential in religion.
urduMeaning: فرض نماز، وہ نماز جو ہر مومن پر لازمی ہے، ایسی عبادت جو بغیر کسی جائز عذر کے چھوڑی نہیں جا سکتی، روزانہ کی لازمی نمازیں جو ہر بالغ مسلمان پر فرض ہیں، دین میں ضروری سمجھی جانے والی عبادت کا فریضہ
antonyms: Optional prayer, Voluntary prayer, Nafl prayer

examples: He offers optional prayers at night for extra blessings. Optional prayers are not compulsory but are highly encouraged. She performs optional prayers after the obligatory ones. Many worshippers stay back to offer optional prayers. Offering optional prayers shows extra devotion to God.
synonyms: Nafl prayer, Voluntary prayer, Supererogatory prayer, Additional prayer
urduMeaning: نفل نماز، وہ نماز جو اختیاری ہے اور فرض نہیں، اضافی ثواب کے لیے فرض نمازوں سے زیادہ پڑھی جانے والی عبادت، ایسی نماز جو مومن اپنی مرضی اور عقیدت سے پڑھے، شوق اور ایمان سے کی جانے والی اضافی عبادت
englishMeaning: A prayer that is voluntary and not compulsory, known as Nafl in Islam. An additional act of worship offered for extra reward beyond the required prayers. A non-mandatory prayer that a believer may perform out of devotion. Supererogatory worship performed by choice.
sindhiMeaning: نفل نماز، اها نماز جيڪا اختياري آهي ۽ فرض نه آهي، اضافي ثواب لاءِ فرض نمازن کان وڌيڪ پڙهي ويندڙ عبادت، اهڙي نماز جيڪا مؤمن پنهنجي مرضي ۽ عقيدت سان پڙهي، شوق ۽ ايمان سان ڪيل اضافي عبادت
antonyms: Obligatory prayer, Compulsory prayer, Fard prayer

englishMeaning: A small rug or mat used by Muslims to pray on, keeping the place of worship clean. A piece of fabric, often decorated, on which a person kneels and prostrates during prayer. A portable mat reserved for offering prayers. A clean sheet or carpet used specifically for worship.
antonyms: No Antonym
synonyms: Prayer rug, Janamaz, Musalla, Worship mat
urduMeaning: جائے نماز، مصلیٰ، وہ چھوٹی چٹائی جس پر مسلمان نماز پڑھتے ہیں، ایسا کپڑا یا قالین جس پر نمازی جھک کر سجدہ کرتا ہے، نماز کے لیے مخصوص پاک بچھونا، عبادت کے لیے استعمال ہونے والی صاف چادر یا قالین
examples: She laid out her prayer mat facing the direction of the Kaaba. He always carries a prayer mat when he travels. The prayer mat had a beautiful floral design. They rolled up their prayer mats after the prayer. A clean prayer mat is kept ready in the corner of the room.
sindhiMeaning: جانماز، مصلو، اها ننڍي وڇاڻي جنهن تي مسلمان نماز پڙهن ٿا، اهڙو ڪپڙو يا غاليچو جنهن تي نمازي جهڪي ۽ سجدو ڪري، نماز لاءِ مخصوص پاڪ وڇاڻو، عبادت لاءِ استعمال ٿيندڙ صاف چادر يا غاليچو

urduMeaning: کلمہ پڑھنا، ایمان کا اقرار کرنا، شہادت دینا، اللہ کی وحدانیت اور اس کے رسول کی رسالت کا اعلان کرنا، زبان سے عقیدے کا اظہار کرنا، دین کے بنیادی اقرار کے الفاظ کہنا
antonyms: Deny faith, Disbelieve, Renounce belief, Apostatize
englishMeaning: To declare one's faith by reciting the statement of belief, especially the Islamic declaration of faith (Kalima/Shahada). To formally proclaim belief in the oneness of God and His messenger. To utter the words that affirm one's religion. To express a formal statement of religious belief.
sindhiMeaning: ڪلمو پڙهڻ، ايمان جو اقرار ڪرڻ، شهادت ڏيڻ، الله جي وحدانيت ۽ سندس رسول جي رسالت جو اعلان ڪرڻ، زبان سان عقيدي جو اظهار ڪرڻ، دين جي بنيادي اقرار جا لفظ چوڻ
synonyms: Recite the Kalima, Declare the Shahada, Profess faith, Affirm belief, Bear witness
examples: The new convert said the creed in front of the congregation. He said the creed with deep sincerity and faith. To enter the religion, one must say the creed. They asked him to say the creed aloud. Saying the creed is the first pillar of faith in Islam.

sindhiMeaning: روزو ڇڏڻ، روزو نه رکڻ، روزي کان دستبردار ٿيڻ، ڪنهن جائز عذر جهڙوڪ بيماري يا سفر سبب روزو نه رکڻ، روزي رکڻ کان پاسو ڪرڻ، عام طور رکيو ويندڙ روزو ترڪ ڪرڻ
antonyms: Keep a fast, Observe a fast, Maintain fasting, Complete a fast
urduMeaning: روزہ چھوڑنا، روزہ نہ رکھنا، روزے سے دستبردار ہونا، کسی جائز عذر مثلاً بیماری یا سفر کی وجہ سے روزہ نہ رکھنا، روزہ رکھنے سے گریز کرنا، عام طور پر رکھے جانے والے روزے کو ترک کرنا
englishMeaning: To give up or skip a fast, choosing not to observe it. To break or not keep a religious fast, sometimes due to a valid reason such as illness or travel. To deliberately abstain from fasting. To leave out the act of fasting that one would normally perform.
examples: She had to forgo the fast because she was unwell. Travelers are allowed to forgo the fast and make it up later. He decided not to forgo the fast despite the long journey. Patients may forgo the fast on a doctor's advice. They were warned not to forgo the fast without a valid reason.
synonyms: Skip a fast, Break a fast, Omit fasting, Abstain from fasting, Give up fasting
Recite the azan, Give the call to prayer, Announce the azan, Proclaim the call
examples: The muezzin called out the azan from the minaret. He calls out the azan five times a day. The boy learned how to call out the azan beautifully. They waited for someone to call out the azan before praying. The man called out the azan as the sun began to set.
urduMeaning: اذان دینا، نماز کے وقت کا بلند آواز میں اعلان کرنا، اذان پکار کر مسلمانوں کو عبادت کے لیے بلانا، نماز کے لیے بندوں کو بلانے کا عوامی اعلان کرنا، مسجد سے ہر نماز سے پہلے روایتی پکار دینا
sindhiMeaning: اذان ڏيڻ، نماز جي وقت جو بلند آواز ۾ اعلان ڪرڻ، اذان پڪاري مسلمانن کي عبادت لاءِ سڏڻ، نماز لاءِ بندن کي گهرائڻ جو عوامي اعلان ڪرڻ، مسجد مان هر نماز کان اڳ روايتي سڏ ڏيڻ
antonyms: No Antonym
englishMeaning: To loudly proclaim the Islamic call to prayer that announces the time for prayer. To recite the azan aloud, inviting Muslims to gather for worship. To make the public announcement summoning believers to prayer. To deliver the traditional call from the mosque before each prayer.

To divide, distribute, or calculate something proportionally according to a share, time, or rate. To allocate an amount in proportion to the relevant period or usage. To adjust a charge or payment so it reflects only the part that applies. To split costs or benefits fairly based on proportion.
sindhiMeaning: تناسب سان ورهائڻ، حصي يا وقت جي مطابق رقم جوڙڻ، استعمال يا مدت جي نسبت سان ادائگي مقرر ڪرڻ، چارج کي ايتري حد تائين ترتيب ڏيڻ جيترو لاڳو ٿئي، خرچ يا فائدو منصفاڻي تناسب سان ورهائڻ
antonyms: Lump together, Charge in full, Combine, Withhold
urduMeaning: تناسب سے تقسیم کرنا، حصے یا وقت کے مطابق رقم کا حساب لگانا، استعمال یا مدت کی نسبت سے ادائیگی مقرر کرنا، چارج کو اتنی حد تک ترتیب دینا جتنا لاگو ہو، خرچ یا فائدہ منصفانہ تناسب سے تقسیم کرنا
examples: The company will prorate the rent for the half month. Your salary will be prorated based on the days you worked. The refund was prorated according to the unused period. They decided to prorate the charges among all the users. The bill was prorated to reflect the actual usage.
synonyms: Apportion, Allocate, Distribute proportionally, Divide, Share out, Assign

examples: His job application received a turndown from the company. The turndown of her proposal disappointed the whole team. They were surprised by the sudden turndown of the deal. The hotel offers a turndown service every evening. The turndown of the collar gave the shirt a neat look.
englishMeaning: A refusal or rejection of an offer, request, or application. The act of declining or not accepting something. A folding down of a part of something, such as a collar or a bedcover. A service in hotels where the bed is prepared for sleeping in the evening.
synonyms: Rejection, Refusal, Denial, Decline, Rebuff, Dismissal, No
sindhiMeaning: رد ڪرڻ، انڪار، ڪنهن آڇ، درخواست يا گذارش کي قبول نه ڪرڻ، نه مڃڻ يا ٺڪرائڻ جو عمل، ڪنهن شيءِ جي حصي کي هيٺ موڙڻ جهڙوڪ ڪالر يا بسترو، هوٽلن ۾ شام جو بستر سمهڻ لاءِ تيار ڪرڻ جي خدمت
urduMeaning: رد کرنا، انکار، کسی پیشکش، درخواست یا گزارش کو قبول نہ کرنا، نہ ماننا یا ٹھکرانے کا عمل، کسی چیز کے حصے کو نیچے موڑنا جیسے کالر یا بستر، ہوٹلوں میں شام کو بستر سونے کے لیے تیار کرنے کی خدمت
antonyms: Acceptance, Approval, Consent, Agreement, Offer
Calm, Soothe, Please, Pacify, Appease, Comfort, Delight
sindhiMeaning: سخت ناراض ڪرڻ، ڪاوڙائڻ، ڪنهن کي بيحد ڪاوڙ ۾ آڻڻ، شديد غصو پيدا ڪرڻ، ڪنهن کي تمام گهڻو تنگ يا چڙائڻ، ڪاوڙ ۽ بيزاري جو سخت احساس پيدا ڪرڻ
examples: His rude behavior never fails to infuriate his colleagues. The unfair decision infuriated the entire crowd. It infuriates me when people break their promises. The constant delays infuriated the passengers. Her careless attitude infuriated the manager.
urduMeaning: سخت ناراض کرنا، غصہ دلانا، کسی کو انتہائی غصے میں لانا، شدید طیش پیدا کرنا، کسی کو بہت زیادہ تنگ یا برہم کرنا، غصے اور جھنجھلاہٹ کا شدید احساس پیدا کرنا
englishMeaning: To make someone extremely angry. To provoke intense rage or fury in a person. To irritate or annoy someone greatly. To cause a strong feeling of anger and frustration.
synonyms: Enrage, Anger, Madden, Provoke, Exasperate, Incense, Irritate, Aggravate
Thin, Lean, Slim, Slender, Bony, Lanky, Scrawny, Gaunt
sindhiMeaning: سنهڙو، ڏٻرو، تمام پتلو، جسم تي تمام گهٽ گوشت يا چرٻي وارو، جسم سان چنبڙيل تنگ ڪپڙا، گهٽ چرٻي سان ٺهيل کاڌو يا مشروب، غير رسمي طور تي ڳجهي يا اندروني خبر
englishMeaning: Very thin or lean, often unusually so. Having little flesh or fat on the body. Fitting very closely to the body, as in tight clothing. Made with reduced fat, as in certain drinks or foods. Informal term for confidential or inside information.
urduMeaning: دبلا، پتلا، بہت لاغر، جسم پر بہت کم گوشت یا چربی والا، جسم سے چپکنے والے تنگ کپڑے، کم چکنائی سے بنا کھانا یا مشروب، غیر رسمی طور پر خفیہ یا اندرونی خبر
examples: He was a tall, skinny boy with long legs. She wore a pair of skinny jeans to the party. The skinny cat looked like it needed a good meal. He ordered a skinny latte with no sugar. Tell me the skinny on what happened at the meeting.
antonyms: Fat, Plump, Chubby, Overweight, Stout, Heavy

examples: The old legal term levance referred to the rising of cattle. Levance and couchancy described livestock that lay down and rose on the land. The word levance is rarely used in modern English. Scholars studied the meaning of levance in ancient property law. The concept of levance appeared in old grazing rights.
sindhiMeaning: اُٿڻ، بلند ٿيڻ، آرام مان اُٿڻ جو عمل، خاص طور تي مال جي اُٿي بيهڻ جي حالت، قديم قانوني اصطلاح ۾ ڍورن جي اُٿڻ جي ڪيفيت، مٿي کڄڻ يا اُڀرڻ جي حالت، هڪ نادر يا متروڪ لفظ جيڪو اُٿڻ ڏانهن اشارو ڪري
synonyms: Rising, Getting up, Ascent, Uprising, Elevation
antonyms: Couchancy, Lying down, Resting, Sitting, Descent
urduMeaning: اٹھنا، بلند ہونا، آرام سے اٹھنے کا عمل، خاص طور پر مویشیوں کے اٹھ کھڑے ہونے کی حالت، قدیم قانونی اصطلاح میں جانوروں کے اٹھنے کی کیفیت، اوپر اٹھنے یا ابھرنے کی حالت، ایک نادر یا متروک لفظ جو اٹھنے کی طرف اشارہ کرتا ہے
englishMeaning: The act of rising or getting up. The condition of cattle or livestock rising from rest, traditionally paired with couchancy in legal contexts of trespass. The state of being raised or lifted up. An obsolete or rare term referring to the act of rising.

A peculiar or unusual habit, behavior, or feature of a person. A strange or unexpected twist or turn of events. A small distinctive trait that makes someone or something unique. A sudden curve, flourish, or change. A clever or odd peculiarity in nature or design.
antonyms: Normality, Conformity, Regularity, Standard, Conventionality
urduMeaning: عجیب عادت، انوکی خصلت، کسی شخص کا نرالا مزاج یا انداز، واقعات کا اچانک اور غیر متوقع موڑ، چھوٹی منفرد خصوصیت جو کسی کو خاص بناتی ہے، اچانک موڑ یا تبدیلی، فطرت یا ساخت میں کوئی انوکی بات
examples: Talking to himself was one of his strange quirks. By a quirk of fate, they met again after many years. Every person has their own little quirks. The old house had many charming quirks. A quirk in the system caused the unexpected error.
sindhiMeaning: عجيب عادت، انوکي خصلت، ڪنهن شخص جي نرالي طبيعت يا انداز، واقعن جو اوچتو ۽ غير متوقع موڙ، ننڍڙي منفرد خصوصيت جيڪا ڪنهن کي خاص بڻائي، اوچتو موڙ يا تبديلي، فطرت يا بناوت ۾ ڪا انوکي ڳالهه
synonyms: Peculiarity, Idiosyncrasy, Eccentricity, Oddity, Trait, Foible, Mannerism, Twist
Cauldron, Pot, Kettle, Vat, Boiler, Vessel, Hotbed, Melting pot
examples: The witches stirred a bubbling caldron in the old fairy tale. Soup was cooking slowly in a huge iron caldron over the fire. The city has become a caldron of political unrest. His mind was a caldron of conflicting emotions after the news. Workers poured the molten metal from the caldron into the moulds.
englishMeaning: A large metal pot or kettle used for cooking or boiling something over an open fire. A big deep round vessel, usually made of iron, with a handle at the top, used for heating or boiling liquids. (Figuratively) A situation or place of intense feelings, conflict, activity, or change. A state in which strong emotions, ideas, or forces are mixed together. Also spelled 'cauldron'.
sindhiMeaning: وڏي ديڳ، وڏو ديڳڙو، لوهي وڏو ٿانءُ جنهن ۾ ڪجهه گرم يا اُٻاريو ويندو آهي، مجازي طور تي شديد جذبن، تڪرارن يا تبديليءَ جو ماحول، اٿل پٿل وارو ماحول، جذبن جي اٿل پٿل وارو ماحول
urduMeaning: بڑی دیگ، بڑی کڑاہی، لوہے کا بڑا برتن جس میں آگ پر کوئی چیز پکائی یا اُبالی جاتی ہے، مجازی طور پر شدید جذبات، کشمکش یا ہلچل کی فضا، جوش و خروش اور ہنگامہ خیز ماحول
antonyms: Calm, Stillness, Tranquillity, Peace, Quietness

englishMeaning: The quality of being impudent. Rude, bold, or disrespectful behaviour, especially towards someone who deserves respect. Shameless boldness or cheekiness in speech or conduct. Lack of modesty, manners, or proper respect. An older or less common form of the word 'impudence'.
antonyms: Politeness, Respect, Courtesy, Humility, Modesty, Manners, Civility
synonyms: Impudence, Insolence, Cheek, Audacity, Rudeness, Boldness, Disrespect, Effrontery, Brazenness
sindhiMeaning: بي شرمي، بي ادبي، گستاخي، بي حيائي، ڍٽائي، بدلحاظي، اخلاقي حدن جي پرواه نه ڪرڻ وارو رويو، وڏن جو احترام نه ڪرڻ، بي باڪاڻه ۽ ڪوڙ ڳالهائڻ يا هلڻ جي عادت
examples: His impudency in front of the teacher shocked the whole class. She replied with such impudency that even her friends felt embarrassed. The manager would not tolerate any kind of impudency from his staff. His impudency towards the elders cost him their respect. Such impudency in a court of law is unacceptable.
urduMeaning: بے شرمی، بے ادبی، گستاخی، بے حیائی، ڈھٹائی، بدلحاظی، اخلاقی حدود کی پرواہ نہ کرنے والا رویہ، بزرگوں کا احترام نہ کرنا، بے باکانہ اور بے جھجک بات کرنے یا چلنے کی عادت

englishMeaning: Rude and disrespectful behaviour or speech. The act of showing a lack of respect, especially towards someone in authority. Offensive or arrogant attitude that hurts or insults others. Bold and shameless behaviour that ignores the feelings or position of others.
antonyms: Politeness, Respect, Courtesy, Humility, Civility, Deference, Manners
examples: The student was punished for his insolence towards the teacher. She could not bear the insolence of the new employee. His insolence in front of the guests embarrassed the whole family. The officer was suspended for his insolence to a senior. I will not tolerate such insolence in my house.
synonyms: Impudence, Rudeness, Disrespect, Arrogance, Cheek, Audacity, Effrontery, Impertinence, Contempt
sindhiMeaning: گستاخي، بي ادبي، بدتميزي، بي شرمي، حاڪم يا وڏي جي بي عزتي ڪرڻ، تڪبر سان ڀريل رويو، توهين آميز ڳالهائڻ يا هلت، ٻين جي عزت جو خيال نه رکڻ
urduMeaning: گستاخی، بے ادبی، بدتمیزی، بے شرمی، کسی بڑے یا صاحبِ اختیار کی توہین کرنا، تکبر سے بھرا رویہ، توہین آمیز انداز میں بات یا برتاؤ، دوسروں کی عزت کا خیال نہ رکھنا

synonyms: Insolence, Impudence, Arrogance, Rudeness, Disrespect, Audacity, Effrontery, Haughtiness
sindhiMeaning: گستاخي، بي ادبي، بدتميزي، تڪبر، بي شرمي، وڏن جي بي عزتي ڪرڻ، هٺيلي ۽ اڍنگي رويي جو اظهار، احترام نه ڪرڻ جي عادت
englishMeaning: An old and rarely used form of the word 'insolence'. The state or quality of being insolent. Rude, arrogant, and disrespectful behaviour. Shameless boldness in attitude or speech, especially towards those who deserve respect.
examples: The king would not tolerate the insolency of his courtiers. Her insolency towards the elders surprised everyone present. He spoke with an air of insolency that annoyed the audience. The old writer used the word 'insolency' in his classic novel. Such insolency from a junior officer is unacceptable.
urduMeaning: گستاخی، بے ادبی، بدتمیزی، تکبر، بے شرمی، بڑوں کی توہین کرنا، مغرورانہ اور بے ادبانہ رویہ، احترام نہ کرنے کی عادت
antonyms: Humility, Politeness, Respect, Courtesy, Modesty, Civility

englishMeaning: The meat of a young calf, used as food. Tender pale-coloured meat obtained from calves, usually less than a few months old. A type of red meat often used in European and continental dishes.
synonyms: Calf meat, Calf's flesh
sindhiMeaning: گابي جو گوشت، نوجوان گابي جو نرم گوشت، ننڍي وهيءَ واري گابي جو گوشت جيڪو کاڌي ۾ ڪتب ايندو آهي، يورپي کاڌن ۾ استعمال ٿيندڙ هلڪي رنگ جو نرم گوشت
examples: The chef prepared a delicious veal cutlet for the guests. Veal is considered a delicacy in many European countries. She ordered roasted veal with mushroom sauce at the restaurant. The recipe calls for thin slices of tender veal. Some people avoid eating veal for ethical reasons.
antonyms: Beef, Mutton, Pork (as alternative meats)
urduMeaning: بچھڑے کا گوشت، نوجوان بچھڑے کا نرم گوشت، چھوٹی عمر کے بچھڑے کا گوشت جو خوراک کے طور پر کھایا جاتا ہے، یورپی کھانوں میں استعمال ہونے والا ہلکے رنگ کا نرم گوشت

antonyms: Defendant, Respondent, Disclaimer, Donor, Giver
urduMeaning: دعویدار، مدعی، حق طلب کرنے والا شخص، کسی جائیداد، رقم یا حق کا دعویٰ کرنے والا، عدالت یا قانونی طور پر دعویٰ پیش کرنے والا شخص
englishMeaning: A person who claims or demands something as a right, especially money, property, or a title. Someone who formally states that something belongs to them or that they deserve something. A person who makes a legal or official claim, for example in court or for insurance or compensation.
sindhiMeaning: دعويدار، دعويٰ ڪندڙ، حقدار ٿيڻ جي دعويٰ ڪندڙ ماڻهو، ڪنهن ملڪيت، رقم يا حق جي طلب ڪندڙ، عدالت ۾ يا قانوني طور تي دعويٰ پيش ڪندڙ شخص
examples: The court will hear the claimant's case next week. There are several claimants to the late king's throne. The insurance company asked the claimant to submit all documents. Only one claimant turned up to receive the prize money. Each claimant must prove his right to the property.
synonyms: Petitioner, Applicant, Plaintiff, Suitor, Litigant, Demander, Pretender

examples: He was just a callow youth when he joined the army. The manager did not trust the callow new recruits with such an important task. Her callow remarks showed she had little experience of the world. As a callow writer, he made many mistakes in his early work. The nest was full of callow chicks waiting for their mother.
synonyms: Inexperienced, Immature, Naive, Green, Raw, Juvenile, Unfledged, Young, Unsophisticated
englishMeaning: Young, inexperienced, and lacking in maturity or judgement. Not yet fully developed or wise because of young age. (Of a bird) Young and without feathers, not yet able to fly. Used to describe people, especially young men, who are immature in behaviour or thinking.
sindhiMeaning: ناتجربيڪار، ناپختو، نادان، نوجوان ۽ بي عقل، اَڻ سکيو، اڃا تائين سمجهه ۽ تجربو نه رکندڙ، (پکيءَ لاءِ) اڃا کنڀ نه نڪتل، ننڍي وهيءَ جو ۽ غير سنجيده
antonyms: Mature, Experienced, Worldly, Seasoned, Adult, Sophisticated, Wise
urduMeaning: ناتجربہ کار، ناپختہ، نادان، نوجوان اور بے عقل، اَن سیکھا، ابھی تک سمجھ اور تجربہ نہ رکھنے والا، (پرندے کے لیے) ابھی پر نہ نکلے ہوئے، کم عمر اور غیر سنجیدہ

examples: The butter had turned rancid after being left out in the heat. There was a rancid smell coming from the kitchen. Do not use this oil; it has gone rancid. He gave a rancid laugh that made everyone uncomfortable. The room was filled with the rancid odour of old grease.
sindhiMeaning: خراب ٿيل، باسي، بدبودار، (تيل يا گيهه لاءِ) خراب ٿيل ۽ بدبوءَ وارو، سَڙيل ۽ ناپسنديده ذائقي وارو، مجازي طور تي بڇڙو، ناپسنديده يا اخلاقي طور تي خراب
synonyms: Stale, Spoiled, Rotten, Off, Sour, Putrid, Foul, Rank, Rotten-smelling
englishMeaning: (Of food, especially fats or oils) Smelling or tasting unpleasant because it is no longer fresh. Spoiled, stale, or gone bad with a strong, sour, or disgusting smell. (Figuratively) Unpleasant, offensive, or morally bad.
antonyms: Fresh, Sweet, Pure, Fragrant, Wholesome, Pleasant, Edible
urduMeaning: خراب شدہ، باسی، بدبودار، (تیل یا گھی کے لیے) خراب ہو چکا اور بدبو والا، سڑا ہوا اور ناپسندیدہ ذائقے والا، مجازی طور پر برا، ناپسندیدہ یا اخلاقی طور پر خراب

synonyms: Cancerous, Deadly, Fatal, Harmful, Virulent, Evil, Vicious, Spiteful, Hostile, Malicious
englishMeaning: (Of a disease, especially a tumour) Very harmful, dangerous, and likely to cause death if not treated; cancerous. (Of a person or behaviour) Full of hatred, evil, or strong desire to harm others. Showing intense ill will or wishing serious harm to others.
examples: The doctors confirmed that the tumour was malignant. She has a malignant form of cancer that requires immediate treatment. He gave her a malignant look full of hatred. There were malignant rumours spreading about the new manager. His malignant intentions were soon exposed.
sindhiMeaning: نقصانڪار، خطرناڪ، (بيماري لاءِ) ڪينسر وارو ۽ موتمار، تيزيءَ سان وڌندڙ ۽ جان لاءِ خطرناڪ، (ماڻهوءَ لاءِ) بدنيت، ڪينو رکندڙ، نقصان رساڻ جي خواهش وارو، شيطاني سوچ وارو
urduMeaning: نقصان دہ، خطرناک، (بیماری کے لیے) سرطانی اور جان لیوا، تیزی سے بڑھنے والا اور جان کے لیے خطرناک، (شخص کے لیے) بدنیت، کینہ پرور، نقصان پہنچانے کی خواہش رکھنے والا، شیطانی سوچ والا
antonyms: Benign, Harmless, Healthy, Kind, Friendly, Benevolent, Curable
Fall short, Lag behind, Fail, Underperform, Lose, Trail
sindhiMeaning: اڳتي نڪري وڃڻ، ٻين کان وڌي وڃڻ، بهتر ثابت ٿيڻ، حد کان وڌي وڃڻ، توقعن کان وڌيڪ ڪارڪردگي ڏيکارڻ، مات ڏيڻ، فوقيت حاصل ڪرڻ، ڀيٽ ۾ بهتر هجڻ
englishMeaning: To go beyond or do better than something or someone else. To be greater, higher, or more excellent than another in quality, degree, or performance. To exceed expectations or limits. To outdo or excel in a particular area.
urduMeaning: آگے نکل جانا، دوسروں سے بڑھ جانا، بہتر ثابت ہونا، حد سے تجاوز کرنا، توقعات سے بڑھ کر کارکردگی دکھانا، مات دینا، فوقیت حاصل کرنا، مقابلے میں بہتر ہونا
examples: Her performance surpassed all our expectations. He has surpassed his elder brother in academic achievements. This year's profits surpassed those of last year. The new model surpasses the older one in speed and efficiency. No other player in the team can surpass his record.
synonyms: Exceed, Outdo, Excel, Outshine, Outstrip, Beat, Transcend, Overtake, Eclipse
Spoiled, Damaged, Ruined, Blemished, Tarnished, Disfigured, Impaired, Harmed
sindhiMeaning: خراب ٿيل، بگڙيل، بدنما ٿيل، ڪنهن خرابيءَ سبب اصلي حسن يا قيمت وڃائي ويٺل، داغدار، نقصان رسيل، ڪنهن غلطي يا واقعي سبب ناقص ٿي ويل
examples: The beautiful painting was marred by a deep scratch in the middle. Their wedding day was marred by sudden heavy rain. His face was marred by an old scar. The match was marred by the poor behaviour of the spectators. A small mistake marred his otherwise excellent performance.
urduMeaning: خراب شدہ، بگڑا ہوا، بدنما کیا گیا، کسی خرابی کی وجہ سے اصل حسن یا قیمت کھو دینے والا، داغدار، نقصان زدہ، کسی غلطی یا واقعے کی وجہ سے ناقص ہو جانے والا
englishMeaning: Spoiled, damaged, or made less perfect by something unpleasant. Having lost beauty, quality, or value because of a flaw, mistake, or unwanted event. Past form of the verb 'mar', meaning to spoil or impair.
antonyms: Improved, Enhanced, Perfected, Repaired, Restored, Beautified

examples: He is a really nice guy and everyone likes him. Hey guys, are you ready to leave? That guy at the door is asking for you. The campers tied the tent with strong guys. Some guy called for you while you were out.
englishMeaning: A man or boy, used in an informal way. (In plural 'guys') People of any gender, used to address a group informally. A rope, chain, or wire used to hold something firmly in place, such as a tent or pole. (Old use) A strange-looking person.
urduMeaning: آدمی، لڑکا، نوجوان، (غیر رسمی طور پر) مرد یا لڑکا، (جمع میں) لوگ، ٹولی، گروہ، (دوسرا مطلب) رسی یا تار جو خیمے یا ستون کو مضبوط کرنے کے لیے باندھی جاتی ہے
synonyms: Man, Fellow, Chap, Bloke, Dude, Boy, Lad, (for rope) Cable, Cord, Stay
antonyms: Woman, Lady, Girl
sindhiMeaning: ماڻهو، نوجوان، ڇوڪرو، (غير رسمي طور) مرد يا ڇوڪرو، (ٻه وچن ۾) ماڻهو، ٽولي، گروهه، (ٻيو مطلب) رسي يا تار جيڪا تنبوءَ يا ٿنڀ کي مضبوط ڪرڻ لاءِ ٻَڌي ويندي آهي

antonyms: Heterosexual, Straight, Sad, Gloomy, Dull, Dreary, Sombre
sindhiMeaning: هم جنس پرست، (مرد لاءِ خاص طور) پنهنجي ساڳئي جنس ڏانهن جنسي ڪشش رکندڙ، (پراڻي استعمال ۾) خوش، شاد، خوشمزاج، چرچائي، چمڪدار ۽ وڻندڙ، رنگين ۽ پُرڪشش
examples: He has been openly gay since his college days. The couple recently got married in a small gay wedding ceremony. The children were in a gay mood at the picnic. The streets were decorated with gay lights for the festival. She wore a gay floral dress to the party.
englishMeaning: Homosexual; sexually or romantically attracted to people of the same sex, especially used of men. (Old use) Happy, cheerful, lively, and full of fun. Bright and attractive in appearance, especially of colours or decorations.
synonyms: Homosexual, (old) Cheerful, Merry, Happy, Joyful, Lively, Bright, Colourful, Vivid
urduMeaning: ہم جنس پرست، (خاص طور پر مرد کے لیے) اپنی ہی جنس کی طرف جنسی کشش رکھنے والا، (پرانے استعمال میں) خوش، شاد، خوش مزاج، شگفتہ، چمکدار اور دلکش، رنگین اور پرکشش

examples: The poor villagers depend on simple food for their daily sustenance. Water is essential for the sustenance of all living beings. Her faith provided her with spiritual sustenance during hard times. The charity provides sustenance to hundreds of homeless people. Farming is the main source of sustenance in this region.
synonyms: Nourishment, Food, Nutrition, Subsistence, Maintenance, Support, Livelihood, Provision
sindhiMeaning: خوراڪ، رزق، گذر سفر جو سامان، زندگي قائم رکڻ لاءِ ضروري کاڌو ۽ پاڻي، پرورش، سهارو، ڪنهن شيءِ کي قائم رکڻ يا جاري رکڻ جو ذريعو، روحاني يا جذباتي سهارو
urduMeaning: خوراک، رزق، گزر بسر کا سامان، زندگی قائم رکھنے کے لیے ضروری کھانا اور پانی، پرورش، سہارا، کسی چیز کو قائم رکھنے یا جاری رکھنے کا ذریعہ، روحانی یا جذباتی سہارا
englishMeaning: Food and drink that is needed to live and stay healthy. Nourishment that keeps a person, animal, or plant alive. The act of supporting, maintaining, or keeping something going. Something that gives strength, support, or encouragement.
antonyms: Starvation, Deprivation, Hunger, Neglect, Abandonment

englishMeaning: The curved path that a moving object follows through space, such as a bullet, missile, or thrown ball. The route or course something takes through the air under the action of forces like gravity. (Figuratively) The path or progress of development that someone or something follows over time, for example a career or an event.
antonyms: Stagnation, Standstill, Inactivity
sindhiMeaning: گولي يا ميزائل جي اڏام جو رستو، اڇلايل شيءِ جي هوا ۾ ٺهيل گول رستو، ڪنهن متحرڪ شيءِ جي رفتار جو رخ، (مجازي معنيٰ ۾) ڪنهن جي ڪيريئر يا واقعي جي ترقي ۽ سفر جو طريقو
urduMeaning: گولی یا میزائل کی پرواز کا راستہ، پھینکی گئی چیز کا ہوا میں بننے والا خمدار راستہ، کسی متحرک چیز کی رفتار کا رخ، (مجازی معنوں میں) کسی کے کیریئر یا واقعے کی ترقی اور سفر کا انداز
examples: Scientists carefully calculated the trajectory of the missile. The trajectory of the ball took it just over the boundary. His career has followed an upward trajectory ever since college. The trajectory of the country's economy is worrying experts. Engineers studied the trajectory of the satellite before launching it.
synonyms: Path, Course, Route, Flight path, Arc, Curve, Direction, Progression

antonyms: Bearish, Pessimistic, Negative, Doubtful, Cautious, Gloomy, Uncertain
urduMeaning: اُمید بھرا، پُراعتماد، مستقبل کے بارے میں مثبت سوچ رکھنے والا، (مالیاتی زبان میں) اسٹاک مارکیٹ میں قیمتوں کے بڑھنے کی توقع رکھنے والا، جارحانہ، زوردار اور اعتماد سے بھرا ہوا رویہ
examples: Investors remain bullish about the future of the technology sector. The CEO sounded very bullish during the annual meeting. The market is bullish after the latest economic report. He took a bullish stance in the negotiations. Analysts are bullish on the company's new product line.
englishMeaning: Feeling confident and hopeful about something, especially about success or improvement in the future. (In finance) Showing expectations that prices in the stock market will rise. Aggressive, forceful, and confident in attitude or behaviour.
synonyms: Optimistic, Confident, Positive, Hopeful, Assured, Buoyant, Upbeat, Aggressive
sindhiMeaning: اميد ڀريو، پُراعتماد، مستقبل بابت مثبت سوچ رکندڙ، (مالياتي ٻولي ۾) اسٽاڪ مارڪيٽ ۾ قيمتن جي وڌڻ جي اميد رکندڙ، جارحاڻو، زوردار ۽ اعتماد سان ڀريل رويو

synonyms: Sad, Lonely, Miserable, Wretched, Desolate, Abandoned, Hopeless, Pitiful, Deserted
examples: The little boy looked forlorn at the railway station. She gave him a forlorn smile as he walked away. The old house stood forlorn at the end of the street. They made one last forlorn attempt to save the project. He felt forlorn after his best friend moved to another city.
englishMeaning: Sad, lonely, and unhappy, especially because of being left alone or abandoned. Looking pitiful and miserable. (Of a place) Empty, deserted, and giving a feeling of sadness. (Of hope or attempt) Unlikely to succeed; almost hopeless.
urduMeaning: اُداس، تنہا، بے یار و مددگار، چھوڑا ہوا، ویران، دکھ میں ڈوبا ہوا، قابلِ رحم لگنے والا، (جگہ کے لیے) سنسان اور اُداس کر دینے والی، (اُمید کے لیے) بہت کم اُمید والی، تقریباً بے سود کوشش
sindhiMeaning: اُداس، اڪيلو، بي يار و مددگار، ڇڏيل، ويران، ڏک ۾ ٻڏل، رحم جوڳو لڳندڙ، (جاءِ لاءِ) سُنسان ۽ اُداس ڪندڙ، (اُميد لاءِ) تمام گهٽ اميد واري، تقريباً بي سود ڪوشش
antonyms: Happy, Cheerful, Hopeful, Joyful, Content, Lively, Optimistic

synonyms: Pessimistic, Negative, Downbeat, Gloomy, Doubtful, Skeptical, Cautious, Declining, Weak, Downward looking
englishMeaning: Expecting the price of stocks, currencies, commodities, or other assets to decrease. Having a pessimistic opinion about future business or economic conditions. Showing a lack of confidence in growth or success. Indicating downward market movement or declining value. Describing investors who believe selling is better than buying because prices are likely to fall. Having a negative outlook toward a company, industry, economy, or investment.
examples: Many investors became bearish after the company reported weak earnings. The analyst remains bearish about the stock market this year. Rising inflation has created a bearish outlook for the economy. Traders adopted a bearish strategy because they expected prices to decline.
sindhiMeaning: منڊي جي قيمتن ۾ گهٽتائي جي اميد رکندڙ، منفي سوچ رکندڙ، نااميد يا مايوس رويو رکندڙ، اهڙو جيڪو سمجهي ته شيئر يا مارڪيٽ هيٺ ويندي، واپار يا معيشت بابت گهٽتائي جي اڳڪٿي ڪندڙ، اهڙي حالت يا سوچ کي چيو ويندو آهي جنهن ۾ ماڻهو سمجهي ٿو ته مارڪيٽ  شيئرن يا ڪنهن شيءِ جي قيمت گهٽجندي
urduMeaning: مندی کی توقع رکھنے والا، منفی سوچ رکھنے والا، مایوس کن نقطۂ نظر رکھنے والا، ایسا جو قیمتوں میں کمی کی پیش گوئی کرے، شیئر مارکیٹ میں گراوٹ کی توقع رکھنے والا، اس سوچ یا رویے کو کہتے ہیں جس میں یہ توقع ہو کہ قیمتیں  مارکیٹ یا کاروبار نیچے جائے گا
antonyms: Bullish, Optimistic, Positive, Hopeful, Confident, Encouraging, Upbeat, Favorable, Rising, Strong

sindhiMeaning: وڙهڻ، جهيڙو ڪرڻ، تڪرار ڪرڻ، زباني جنگ ڪرڻ، اُچي آواز ۾ بحث ڪرڻ، تيز ۽ ڪاوڙ ڀري بحث ۾ پوڻ، گاريون يا تيز لفظ هلائڻ
englishMeaning: To argue, quarrel, or dispute noisily with another person. To have a heated verbal exchange or angry discussion. To engage in a loud or bitter argument, usually in public.
antonyms: Agree, Concur, Reconcile, Settle, Make peace, Harmonize
urduMeaning: لڑنا، جھگڑا کرنا، تکرار کرنا، زبانی جنگ کرنا، اونچی آواز میں بحث کرنا، تیز اور غصے بھری بحث میں پڑنا، تلخ کلامی کرنا
examples: The two neighbours began to altercate over the boundary wall. He altercated with the shopkeeper about the price of the item. They altercated for nearly an hour without any result. It is not wise to altercate in public places. The brothers altercated bitterly over their late father's property.
synonyms: Quarrel, Argue, Dispute, Wrangle, Bicker, Squabble, Fight, Clash, Row

sindhiMeaning: جهيڙو، تڪرار، زباني جنگ، ڪاوڙ ڀريو بحث، اڳيان پويان لفظ، ٻن يا وڌيڪ ماڻهن جي وچ ۾ تيز ۽ گرم بحث، اهڙو جهيڙو جيڪو ڪڏهن ڪڏهن مار ڪٽ تائين به وڃي سگهي ٿو
synonyms: Quarrel, Argument, Dispute, Row, Squabble, Wrangle, Clash, Confrontation, Brawl
examples: There was a loud altercation between the driver and the passenger. The meeting ended in a bitter altercation between the two members. Police arrived quickly to stop the altercation in the market. A small misunderstanding led to a serious altercation. He was injured during an altercation outside the restaurant.
antonyms: Agreement, Harmony, Peace, Accord, Reconciliation, Understanding
englishMeaning: A noisy argument, quarrel, or angry dispute, especially in public. A heated exchange of words between two or more people. A short but intense disagreement that may sometimes lead to a fight.
urduMeaning: جھگڑا، تکرار، زبانی جنگ، غصے بھری بحث، تلخ کلامی، دو یا زائد افراد کے درمیان تیز اور گرم بحث، ایسا جھگڑا جو کبھی کبھی مار پیٹ تک بھی پہنچ سکتا ہے

antonyms: (For woman) Gentle woman, Sweet-tempered lady, Calm person, Mild person
examples: A shrew is often mistaken for a small mouse in the garden. Shrews have a very fast heartbeat and are always hungry. His wife was such a shrew that no one liked to visit them. Shakespeare wrote a famous play called 'The Taming of the Shrew'. Neighbours called her a shrew because she fought with everyone.
englishMeaning: A small mouse-like animal with a long pointed nose, small ears, and soft fur, which feeds mainly on insects. A bad-tempered, scolding, and quarrelsome woman who often nags others. (Used in literature) An aggressive and ill-tempered female.
sindhiMeaning: هڪ ننڍڙو چُوهي جهڙو جانور جنهن جي نڪ ڊگهي ۽ تيز هوندي آهي، جيڪو خاص طور تي ڪيڙا کائي ٿو، (مجازي معنيٰ ۾) ڪاوڙيل، جهيڙاڪ ۽ گاريون ڏيندڙ عورت، تيز زبان واري ۽ بدمزاج زال
urduMeaning: ایک چھوٹا چوہے جیسا جانور جس کی ناک لمبی اور نوکیلی ہوتی ہے، جو زیادہ تر کیڑے کھاتا ہے، (مجازی معنوں میں) جھگڑالو، بدمزاج اور گالیاں دینے والی عورت، تیز زبان والی اور لڑاکا عورت
synonyms: (Animal) Mole-like rodent, (Woman) Nag, Scold, Termagant, Virago, Harridan, Vixen
Clever, Sharp, Astute, Smart, Wise, Cunning, Perceptive, Sagacious, Intelligent, Crafty
sindhiMeaning: هوشيار، چالاڪ، ذهين، تيز فهم، عقلمند، تجربيڪار، (خاص طور تي ڪاروبار ۽ پئسي جي معاملن ۾) سياڻو، حالتن کي جلدي سمجهي صحيح فيصلو ڪندڙ، دور انديش
examples: She is a shrewd businesswoman who knows how to make a profit. He made a shrewd guess about the company's future. The shrewd lawyer easily won the difficult case. With his shrewd judgement, he avoided a serious loss. Voters are shrewd enough to recognize false promises.
urduMeaning: ہوشیار، چالاک، ذہین، تیز فہم، عقلمند، تجربہ کار، (خاص طور پر کاروبار اور پیسے کے معاملات میں) دانا، حالات کو جلدی سمجھ کر درست فیصلہ کرنے والا، دور اندیش
englishMeaning: Having or showing sharp powers of judgement; clever and good at understanding situations quickly, especially in matters of money or business. Cunning and practical in dealing with people. Mentally sharp, wise, and astute in decision-making.
antonyms: Foolish, Stupid, Naive, Dull, Gullible, Unwise, Simple, Dim-witted

englishMeaning: Practical knowledge, understanding, and good judgement, especially in a particular field. Shrewd, well-informed, and able to make sensible decisions, especially in business, politics, or technology. To know or understand something.
antonyms: Ignorance, Inexperience, Foolishness, Naivety, Dullness, Stupidity
urduMeaning: آگاہی، سمجھ بوجھ، تجربے سے حاصل ہونے والی عقل، عملی علم، (صفت کے طور پر) ہوشیار، باخبر، صحیح فیصلہ کرنے کی صلاحیت رکھنے والا، (کاروبار یا ٹیکنالوجی میں) ماہر اور دانا، (غیر رسمی طور پر) سمجھنا یا جاننا
sindhiMeaning: ڄاڻ، سمجهه، تجربيڪاريءَ مان حاصل ٿيل عقل، عملي ڄاڻ، (صفت طور) هوشيار، باخبر، صحيح فيصلو ڪرڻ جي صلاحيت رکندڙ، (ڪاروبار يا ٽيڪنالاجي ۾) ماهر ۽ سياڻو، (غير رسمي طور) سمجهڻ يا ڄاڻڻ
synonyms: Know-how, Common sense, Shrewdness, Intelligence, Expertise, Insight, Astuteness, Smartness
examples: She has a lot of political savvy and knows how to win supporters. You need real business savvy to succeed in this market. He is a tech-savvy young man who can fix any computer problem. Do you savvy what I am trying to tell you?. Her financial savvy saved the company from bankruptcy.

In ancient times, some rulers ordered criminals to behead prisoners as a form of punishment. The story describes a knight who was ordered to behead a dangerous enemy. The documentary explains how beheading was used as a method of execution in certain historical periods. The company decided to behead the leadership team by removing several top executives. This is a figurative use of the word.
sindhiMeaning: سر قلم ڪرڻ، ڪنهن ماڻهو يا جانور جو سر ڌڙ کان ڌار ڪرڻ، سزا يا قتل طور سر ڪٽڻ، جنگ يا تشدد دوران ڪنڌ ڌار ڪرڻ، مجازي معنيٰ ۾ ڪنهن اداري يا گروهه جي اڳواڻ کي هٽائڻ، اڳواڻ کي هٽائڻ (مجازي معنيٰ)
englishMeaning: To cut off someone's head. To execute a person by removing the head. To kill by decapitation. To remove the head of an animal. Figuratively, to remove the leader or chief of a group or organization. To cut off the head of a person or animal, usually as a form of execution, punishment, murder, or in violent situations.
synonyms: Decapitate, Execute, Kill, Slay, Sever the head, Chop off the head, Put to death, Remove the head
antonyms: Spare, Save, Protect, Preserve, Rescue, Revive, Defend, Guard
urduMeaning: سر قلم کرنا، کسی شخص یا جانور کا سر جسم سے الگ کرنا، سزا یا قتل کے طور پر گردن کاٹ دینا، جنگ یا تشدد کے دوران سر کاٹ دینا، مجازی طور پر کسی ادارے یا گروہ کے سربراہ کو ہٹا دینا، کسی تنظیم کے سربراہ کو ہٹا دینا (مجازی معنی)
چمکتا ہوا، جگمگاتا ہوا، روشنی سے بھرپور، (بات چیت یا کارکردگی کے لیے) ذہین، چست، دلچسپ اور مزیدار، کمال کا اور پرکشش، تیز ذہانت اور مزاح سے بھرپور
antonyms: Dull, Boring, Tedious, Dim, Lifeless, Uninspiring, Lacklustre
englishMeaning: Sparkling, shining brightly with flashes of light. Brilliantly clever, lively, witty, or interesting, especially in speech or performance. Very impressive and exciting in an intellectual or entertaining way.
sindhiMeaning: چمڪندڙ، جرڪندڙ، روشنيءَ سان ڀريل، (ڳالهائڻ يا ڪارڪردگي لاءِ) ذهين، چست، دلچسپ ۽ مزيدار، ڪمال جو ۽ پُرڪشش، تيز ذهانت ۽ مزاح سان ڀريل
synonyms: Sparkling, Glittering, Shining, Brilliant, Dazzling, Witty, Lively, Stimulating, Fascinating
examples: She wore a scintillating diamond necklace at the party. The speaker gave a scintillating speech that impressed everyone. It was a scintillating performance by the young actress. We had a scintillating conversation about literature and life. The lake looked scintillating under the morning sun.

synonyms: Sparkle, Shine, Glitter, Twinkle, Flash, Gleam, Dazzle, Shimmer
urduMeaning: چمکنا، جگمگانا، چنگاریاں اڑانا، تیز روشنی سے جگمگانا، (بات چیت میں) ذہانت اور ظرافت سے دوسروں کو متاثر کرنا، شاندار کارکردگی دکھانا، چست اور دلچسپ ہو کر سامنے آنا
sindhiMeaning: چمڪڻ، جرڪڻ، چڻنگون اڇلائڻ، تيز روشنيءَ سان جرڪڻ، (ڳالهائڻ ۾) ذهانت ۽ ظرافت سان ٻين کي متاثر ڪرڻ، شاندار ڪارڪردگي ڏيکارڻ، چست ۽ دلچسپ ٿي ظاهر ٿيڻ
examples: The stars scintillate brightly in the clear night sky. Her jewellery scintillated under the bright lights of the hall. The young writer scintillates whenever he talks about poetry. The actress continues to scintillate on stage even after twenty years. Diamonds scintillate beautifully in sunlight.
englishMeaning: To give off sparks or flashes of light; to shine brightly with sparkling light. To be brilliantly clever, witty, or lively in conversation or performance. To impress others with intelligence, charm, or skill.
antonyms: Dim, Darken, Dull, Fade, Bore, Tarnish

examples: We could hear the echo of our voices in the empty hall. The mountains sent back a clear echo of his shout. His latest speech was just an echo of his earlier ideas. The new policy is an echo of the old one. Her words echoed in my mind for days.
urduMeaning: بازگشت، گونج، آواز کا دیوار، پہاڑ یا غار سے ٹکرا کر دوبارہ سنائی دینا، ایک ہی آواز کا دہرایا جانا، (مجازی معنوں میں) کسی دوسرے کی رائے، خیال یا الفاظ کا دہرایا جانا، کسی گزری ہوئی بات کا اثر یا نشانی، (فعل کے طور پر) آواز یا بات کو دہرانا
synonyms: Reverberation, Repetition, Resonance, Reflection, Imitation, Repeat, Reproduce, Mirror
antonyms: Silence, Originality, Quiet, Stillness, Uniqueness
sindhiMeaning: بازگشت، گونج، آواز جو ڀت، جبل يا غار سان ٽڪرائي وري ٻڌجڻ، ساڳيءَ آواز جو ورجاءُ، (مجازي معنيٰ ۾) ڪنهن ٻئي جي راءِ، خيال يا لفظن جو ورجاءُ، ڪنهن گذريل ڳالهه جو اثر يا نشاني، (فعل طور) آواز يا ڳالهه کي دهرائڻ
englishMeaning: A sound that is heard again because it is reflected from a surface such as a wall, mountain, or cave. The repetition of a sound caused by reflection of sound waves. (Figuratively) A repetition or imitation of someone else's opinions, words, ideas, or style. A trace or sign that something still exists or has an influence. To repeat a sound or to express the same opinion as someone else.

examples: The carpenter used a metal template to cut identical pieces of wood. Please use this template to design the new brochure. He created a template for the monthly progress report. The website offers free templates for resumes and cover letters. Teachers were given a template to prepare the question papers.
urduMeaning: نمونہ، خاکہ، ماڈل، پہلے سے تیار شدہ ڈھانچہ، ایسی چیز جسے رہنما یا اصل نمونہ بنا کر دوسری چیزیں بنائی جائیں، (کمپیوٹر میں) پہلے سے تیار شدہ فائل یا ڈیزائن جو دستاویز یا ویب پیج بنانے میں مدد دے
sindhiMeaning: نمونو، خاڪو، ماڊل، اڳواٽ تيار ڪيل ڍانچو، ڪا اهڙي شيءِ جنهن کي گائيڊ يا اصل نمونو بڻائي ٻيون شيون ٺاهيون وڃن، (ڪمپيوٽر ۾) اڳواٽ تيار ڪيل فائيل يا ڊيزائن جيڪا ڊاڪيومينٽ يا ويب پيج ٺاهڻ ۾ مدد ڏئي
synonyms: Pattern, Model, Mould, Guide, Blueprint, Framework, Prototype, Format, Layout
antonyms: Original, One-off, Unique creation, Custom design
englishMeaning: A shaped piece of metal, plastic, paper, or other material used as a pattern or guide for making something accurately. A ready-made model, design, or document that can be used as a starting point and filled in or modified for a particular purpose. (In computing) A pre-designed file or layout that helps create documents, web pages, or presentations quickly.

synonyms: Rebellion, Revolt, Uprising, Mutiny, Insurgency, Revolution, Sedition, Coup, Riot
urduMeaning: بغاوت، حکومت کے خلاف مسلح بغاوت، اقتدار یا اختیار کے خلاف منظم بغاوت، سرکشی، علمِ بغاوت بلند کرنا، عوامی شورش، ریاست کے خلاف مسلح مزاحمت، حکمرانوں کی قانونی حیثیت کو مسترد کرتے ہوئے کھلی مخالفت
examples: The government quickly moved to crush the armed insurrection in the northern provinces. Several leaders were arrested for plotting an insurrection against the king. The failed insurrection left hundreds of people dead and the city in ruins. Historians still debate whether the uprising should be called a revolution or merely an insurrection. The soldiers refused to fire on civilians during the brief insurrection.
sindhiMeaning: بغاوت، سرڪار خلاف هٿياربند بغاوت، حڪومت يا اختيار رکندڙن خلاف منظم اُٿل پُٿل، سرڪشي، علم بغاوت بلند ڪرڻ، عوامي بغاوت، رياست خلاف هٿياربند مزاحمت، حڪمرانن جي قانوني حيثيت کي رد ڪندي ڪيل کلم کلا مخالفت
englishMeaning: A violent uprising against an established government or authority. An organized act of rebellion or revolt by a group of people against those in power. An armed resistance, mutiny, or insurgency intended to overthrow a ruling system. A serious public disturbance involving open defiance of laws, leaders, or institutions. It is usually carried out by citizens or factions who reject the legitimacy of the current rulers.
antonyms: Obedience, Submission, Compliance, Loyalty, Allegiance, Order, Peace, Surrender

englishMeaning: A flat surface or table over which business is conducted in a shop, bank, or kitchen. A small disc or token used in board games for keeping score or marking positions. A device that automatically counts or records the number of times something happens. To speak or act in opposition to something. To oppose, respond to, or nullify the effect of an action, argument, or attack. In the opposite direction to something; contrary to.
synonyms: Oppose, Resist, Rebut, Refute, Respond, Desk, Table, Token, Reverse, Against
sindhiMeaning: ڪائونٽر، دڪان يا بئنڪ ۾ ليڻ ڏيڻ وارو ميز، رانديءَ ۾ استعمال ٿيندڙ نشانو يا ٽوڪن، ڳڻپ ڪندڙ اوزار، مخالفت ڪرڻ، جواب ڏيڻ، اُبتڙ ڪرڻ، ڪنهن حملي يا دليل کي رد ڪرڻ، ابتڙ، اُبتي طرف، خلاف
examples: She placed the groceries on the counter and waited for the cashier. The bank teller called the next customer to the counter. He used a small counter to keep track of the votes. The boxer threw a quick counter to his opponent's punch. Their argument runs counter to all the available evidence.
urduMeaning: کاؤنٹر، دکان یا بینک میں لین دین کی میز، کھیل میں استعمال ہونے والا نشان یا ٹوکن، گننے والا آلہ، مخالفت کرنا، جواب دینا، توڑ کرنا، کسی حملے یا دلیل کا جواب دینا، اُلٹا، مخالف سمت میں، برعکس
antonyms: Support, Agree, Confirm, Accept, Endorse, Aid, Assist, Same direction

urduMeaning: نیند بھرا، اونگھا ہوا، غنودگی والا، سست، نیند لانے والا، نیم خوابیدہ، خاموش اور سست ماحول والا، سستی میں ڈوبا ہوا، آدھی نیند میں، نیند کی کیفیت میں
antonyms: Alert, Awake, Active, Lively, Energetic, Vigilant, Wakeful, Sharp
synonyms: Sleepy, Drowsy, Sluggish, Lethargic, Dozy, Soporific, Languid, Torpid
examples: The warm afternoon sun made the entire class feel somnolent. He spoke in a low, somnolent voice that nearly put the children to sleep. The small village wore a somnolent look in the heat of summer. After the heavy lunch, a somnolent silence settled over the room. She felt somnolent after taking the strong cold medicine.
sindhiMeaning: ننڊاکڙو، اوجهراٽيل، ننڊ ۾ پيل جهڙو، ستل جهڙو، ستائيندڙ، سستيءَ وارو، ننڊ آڻيندڙ، خاموش ۽ سست ماحول وارو، چست نه پر سست، ننڊ جو شڪار
englishMeaning: Feeling sleepy, drowsy, or inclined to sleep. Causing or tending to cause sleep. Half-asleep or in a state of dullness and inactivity. Lacking energy or alertness, as if about to fall asleep. Often used to describe places, sounds, or atmospheres that have a quiet, sleep-inducing quality.

antonyms: Thoughtlessness, Inattention, Carelessness, Distraction, Neglect, Impulsiveness
sindhiMeaning: گهري سوچ، غور و فڪر، ڌيان سان سوچڻ، تفڪر، مراقبو، ڪنهن ڳالهه تي گهري ويچار ڪرڻ، خاموش ويچار، ڪا شيءِ ڌيان سان ڏسڻ، اڳتي جو ارادو يا منصوبو
urduMeaning: گہری سوچ، غور و فکر، تفکر، مراقبہ، ذہنی توجہ، کسی بات پر گہرائی سے سوچنا، خاموش غور، کسی چیز کو غور سے دیکھنا، آئندہ کا ارادہ یا منصوبہ
examples: She sat by the window in quiet contemplation of the falling rain. After much contemplation, he finally decided to accept the job offer. The monk spent hours in deep contemplation every morning. The painting invites the viewer into a moment of peaceful contemplation. The new policy is still under contemplation by the board.
englishMeaning: The act of thinking deeply and seriously about something. Long, careful consideration of an idea, subject, or possibility. A state of quiet reflection, meditation, or spiritual focus. The act of looking at or observing something thoughtfully. The intention or expectation of doing something in the future.
synonyms: Reflection, Meditation, Thought, Consideration, Pondering, Rumination, Musing, Deliberation
Thoughtful, Reflective, Meditative, Pensive, Pondering, Studious, Introspective
englishMeaning: Involving or given to deep, serious thought. Thoughtful, reflective, or meditative in nature. Showing a calm and quiet attitude of careful consideration. Relating to religious or spiritual meditation. A person who spends much time in thought or prayer.
examples: He gave her a long, contemplative look before answering the question. She is a quiet, contemplative woman who enjoys reading and writing poetry. The old man sat in a contemplative mood beside the river. They lead a contemplative life in the mountain monastery. His contemplative essays explore the meaning of human suffering.
urduMeaning: غور و فکر کرنے والا، سوچنے والا، تفکر آمیز، مراقبہ کرنے والا، خاموش اور سنجیدہ سوچ والا، ذہنی توجہ والا، روحانی مراقبے سے متعلق، گہری سوچ رکھنے والا شخص
sindhiMeaning: غور ڪندڙ، سوچيندڙ، ويچار وارو، مراقبي وارو، خاموش ۽ غور سان سوچيندڙ، ڌيان مگن، تفڪر ڪندڙ، روحاني مراقبي سان لاڳاپيل، ڳوڙهي سوچ رکندڙ شخص
antonyms: Thoughtless, Impulsive, Rash, Inattentive, Frivolous, Shallow

examples: The irony of the situation was that the fire station itself caught fire. She used heavy irony when she called the rainy, cold day 'perfect weather'. There is a bitter irony in losing your job at a company you helped to build. The novel is filled with irony and dark humour. It is an irony of history that the peace treaty led to another war.
urduMeaning: طنز، چوٹ، ایسا اندازِ بیان جس میں معنی الٹا ہو، ایسی صورتِ حال جو توقع کے برعکس ہو، ادبی تکنیک جس میں ظاہری اور اصل مفہوم مختلف ہوں، عجیب اتفاق، الٹی بات، ستم ظریفی
synonyms: Sarcasm, Mockery, Satire, Paradox, Incongruity, Wit, Ridicule
englishMeaning: The expression of meaning by using language that normally signifies the opposite, typically for humorous or emphatic effect. A situation, event, or outcome that is strange or amusing because it is the opposite of what was expected. A literary technique in which the intended meaning is different from, or opposite to, the literal meaning. A state of affairs that seems deliberately contrary to what one expects.
antonyms: Sincerity, Seriousness, Straightforwardness, Honesty, Directness
sindhiMeaning: طنز، چوٽ، ڳالهائڻ جو اهڙو انداز جنهن ۾ معنى ابتڙ هجي، ڪا اهڙي صورتحال جا توقع جي خلاف هجي، ادب ۾ اهڙي ٽيڪنڪ جنهن ۾ ظاهري معنى ۽ اصل معنى مختلف هجن، عجيب اتفاق، الٽي ڳالهه
ڪنهن ڏوهه يا غلط ڪم ۾ شراڪت، ڏوهه ۾ ساٿ، ڳجهي ڀائيواري، ڪنهن غلط ڪم ۾ گڏ هجڻ، خاموش حمايت، ڪنهن جرم ۾ شامل هجڻ، گناهه ۾ ساٿي ٿيڻ، شراڪتِ جرم
antonyms: Innocence, Non-involvement, Opposition, Resistance, Ignorance
englishMeaning: The state of being involved with others in an illegal activity or wrongdoing. Partnership or association in a crime, plot, or wrongful act. Secret cooperation or agreement in doing something wrong or unlawful. A shared responsibility or guilt in a harmful action. Silent acceptance or support of someone else's bad behaviour.
examples: He was accused of complicity in the murder of the businessman. Her silence was seen by many as complicity with the corrupt officials. The report exposed the bank's complicity in the money laundering scheme. Several officers were charged with complicity in the cover-up. By doing nothing, the neighbours showed a clear complicity in the abuse.
urduMeaning: کسی جرم یا غلط کام میں شراکت، جرم میں ساتھ دینا، خفیہ ملی بھگت، کسی غلط کام میں شریک ہونا، خاموش حمایت، جرم میں شامل ہونا، گناہ میں ساتھ دینا، شراکتِ جرم
synonyms: Collusion, Conspiracy, Involvement, Participation, Connivance, Partnership, Collaboration

antonyms: Bore, Annoy, Displease, Disgust, Tire, Weary, Disappoint
urduMeaning: خوش کرنا، تفریح فراہم کرنا، دلچسپ کہانیاں سنا کر لطف اندوز کرنا، شاندار کھانے سے مہمان نوازی کرنا، کسی کو خوشی اور مزہ دینا، خاطر تواضع کرنا، دل بہلانا، شاندار ضیافت کرنا
sindhiMeaning: خوش ڪرڻ، تفريح فراهم ڪرڻ، دلچسپ ڪهاڻيون ٻڌائي لطف ڏيڻ، شاندار طعام سان مهماني ڪرڻ، ڪنهن کي خوشي ۽ مزو ڏيڻ، شاندار دعوت ڪرڻ، خوب خاطر تواضع ڪرڻ، دل وندرائڻ
examples: Grandfather used to regale us with stories of his adventures at sea. The host regaled the guests with a sumptuous five-course dinner. sindhiMeaning: ڪاٺ، شيشي يا ڌاتوءَ جو ننڍڙو تکو ٽڪرو، ڪرچ، ڇيپر، ٽُڪرو، ڪاٺ جو چُڀندڙ ننڍڙو ٽُڪرو، ڀُري ٽڪرا ٽڪرا ٿيڻ، ڦاٽي ٽڪرا ٿيڻ، ڪنهن وڏي شيءِ تان لهي پيل تکي ڇيپر، جماعت يا گروهه مان الڳ ٿيل ننڍو ڌڙو
examples: He got a tiny splinter of wood stuck in his finger while moving the old furniture. The vase shattered into countless splinters when it fell on the marble floor. The old wooden bench has begun to splinter and needs to be replaced. A small splinter group broke away from the main political party last year. She used tweezers to carefully remove the splinter from her child's foot.

synonyms: Scalpel, Surgical knife, Blade, Bistoury, Cutter

englishMeaning: A small, sharp, pointed, two-edged surgical knife used by doctors to make small cuts in the skin, lance boils, or open veins. A pointed surgical instrument. A small, sharp medical blade traditionally used for bloodletting, draining abscesses, or piercing the skin for minor surgical procedures and modern diagnostic tests.
antonyms: Suture, Bandage, Dressing, Plaster
examples: The surgeon used a sterilised lancet to drain the small abscess on the patient's arm. In earlier times, a lancet was commonly used for bloodletting to treat various illnesses. The medical student learned how to handle a lancet safely during her surgical training.
urduMeaning: نشتر، آپریشن میں استعمال ہونے والا چھوٹا تیز دو دھاری چاقو، ڈاکٹروں کا استعمال کردہ تیز جراحی آلہ، پھوڑے یا زخم چیرنے والا اوزار، گاتھک طرز تعمیر میں تیز نوک دار محراب یا کھڑکی

antonyms: Chalice, Cup, Goblet

urduMeaning: عیسائی عبادت گاہوں میں مقدس روٹی یا ویفر رکھنے کے لیے استعمال ہونے والی چھوٹی گول پلیٹ، عموماً سونے یا چاندی کی بنی ہوئی مقدس طشتری، عشائے ربانی کی رسم میں استعمال ہونے والا تبرک شدہ ٹھالا
synonyms: Plate, Disc, Communion plate, Salver, Dish
examples: The priest carefully placed the consecrated bread on the golden paten during the Mass. The church's antique silver paten is displayed in the parish museum on special occasions. synonyms: Sanctified, Hallowed, Blessed, Sacred, Holy, Dedicated, Devoted, Ordained
antonyms: Desecrated, Defiled, Profaned, Unholy, Cursed, Polluted, Disrespected
sindhiMeaning: متبرڪ ڪيل، پاڪ ڪيل، مقدس بڻايل، خدا جي عبادت لاءِ مخصوص ڪيل، ڪنهن مذهبي مقصد لاءِ وقف ڪيل، ڪنهن خاص مقصد لاءِ پنهنجو پاڻ کي ارپڻ ڪيل، تبرڪ ٿيل

englishMeaning: Declared or made sacred, holy, or set apart for a religious or sacred purpose. Officially dedicated to the service or worship of God. Devoted entirely to a particular cause or aim. synonyms: Defiled, Profaned, Violated, Dishonoured, Polluted, Vandalised, Blasphemed, Disrespected

synonyms: Holy Communion, Lord's Supper, Mass, Sacrament, Blessed Sacrament, Communion

synonyms: Bit, Bridle, Curb (related), Grab, Seize, Snatch, Pinch, Pocket, Nab

sindhiMeaning: گهوڙي جي وات ۾ وجهڻ وارو سادو لغام، گهوڙي کي ضابطي ۾ رکڻ لاءِ استعمال ٿيندڙ ٻن ڀاڱن وارو لغام، ڪا شيءِ جلدي ۽ هوشياريءَ سان حاصل ڪرڻ، ٻين کان اڳ ۾ ڪا شيءِ جهٽي وٺڻ، جلدي ۾ هٿ ڪرڻ

Spraining your joints repeatedly can lead to long-term weakness if not treated properly.
sindhiMeaning: جوڙ ۾ موچ اچڻ، اوچتو مروڙ يا ڇڪ سبب جوڙ کي زخمي ڪرڻ جو عمل، ٽخن، ٻانهن يا گوڏي کي مروڙي زخمي ڪرڻ، رڳن کي ڇڪڻ سان تڪليف ڏيڻ، موچ کارائڻ، جوڙ جي رڳن کي نقصان رسائڻ جو عمل

synonyms: Cross-shaped, Crossed, Cruciform, Intersecting

synonyms: Twist, Wrench, Strain, Pull, Injury, Tear, Tweak

antonyms: Heal, Recovery, Strengthen, Restore, Mend
examples: She suffered a painful sprain in her ankle after slipping on the wet floor. The doctor told him that it was only a mild sprain and would heal within a week. englishMeaning: A tool with adjustable jaws used for gripping and turning nuts, bolts, or pipes. To pull or twist something suddenly and violently. A sudden, violent twist or pull. synonyms: Stringy, Threadlike, Sinewy, Tough, Woody, Veined, Stranded
