The salesman's blarney eventually convinced her to buy a product she did not need.  People say that kissing the Blarney Stone grants you the gift of blarney.  Despite knowing it was blarney, she found herself charmed by his words.

urduMeaning: خون بہنا، زخم سے خون نکلنا، وسائل یا پیسوں کا آہستہ آہستہ ضائع ہونا، پرنٹنگ میں تصویر کا صفحے کے کنارے تک پھیلنا
examples: The wound on his hand continued to bleed despite the pressure applied.  The prolonged legal battle caused the company to bleed money for years.  First aid training teaches you how to stop a wound from bleeding.  The design required the image to bleed off the edge of the page.  Her heart bled for the families who had lost everything in the disaster.
antonyms: Heal, Clot, Restore, Replenish, Gain
englishMeaning: To lose blood from the body as a result of injury, illness, or a medical procedure. To draw blood from a person or animal, either medically or as a result of harm. To gradually lose money, resources, or vitality over time, especially in a slow and damaging way. Used in printing to describe an image or color that extends to the very edge of a page with no margin.
sindhiMeaning: رت وهڻ، خون وهڻ، زخم کان رت نڪرڻ، وسيلن يا پيسن جو آهستي آهستي ضائع ٿيڻ، پرنٽنگ ۾ تصوير جو صفحي جي ڪناري تائين وڌڻ
synonyms: Hemorrhage, Ooze, Drain, Seep, Lose

englishMeaning: A plant disease, especially one caused by fungi or bacteria, that causes plants to wither, decay, or die. Something that has a severely damaging or destructive effect on a person, place, or situation. To cause harm, damage, or ruin to something, preventing it from developing or thriving. Urban blight refers to the deterioration of buildings and neighborhoods in a city.
examples: The potato blight of the 1840s caused widespread famine across Ireland.  Urban blight had left many buildings in the neighborhood abandoned and decaying.  Unemployment can blight an entire community for generations.  The disease blighted his career at the very moment it was reaching its peak.  Scientists developed new crop varieties resistant to the devastating wheat blight.
synonyms: Disease, Decay, Ruin, Curse, Deterioration
urduMeaning: فصل یا پودوں کی بیماری جس سے وہ مرجھائیں یا خراب ہوں، کسی جگہ یا حالت پر تباہی یا تنزلی، نقصان پہنچانا یا برباد کرنا
antonyms: Blessing, Flourishing, Growth, Improvement, Prosperity
sindhiMeaning: فصل يا ٻوٽن جي بيماري جنهن سبب اهي مرجهائجن يا خراب ٿين، ڪنهن جاءِ يا حالت تي تباهي يا تنزلي، نقصان پهچائڻ يا برباد ڪرڻ

antonyms: Sober, Unaffected, Defended, Protected, Calm
urduMeaning: تیز اور اچانک حملے سے تباہ، بہت زیادہ نشے میں چور، کام یا سرگرمی سے مغلوب، دوسری جنگ عظیم میں جرمن ہوائی بمباری کا نشانہ
synonyms: Bombed, Overwhelmed, Devastated, Intoxicated, Hammered
englishMeaning: Overwhelmed or defeated by a sudden and powerful attack. Very drunk or heavily intoxicated. Subjected to a blitz, especially the German aerial bombing campaigns of the Second World War. Completely overwhelmed with work, activity, or a sudden rush of something.
sindhiMeaning: تيز ۽ اچانڪ حملي سبب تباهه ٿيل، تمام گهڻو نشي ۾ مست، ڪم يا سرگرمي سبب مغلوب ٿيل، ٻيهين عالمي جنگ ۾ جرمن هوائي بمباري جو شڪار
examples: The city was blitzed during the Second World War and had to be rebuilt.  He came home completely blitzed after the office party.  The team was blitzed in the first half of the match.  She was blitzed with emails the moment she returned from her holiday.  The enemy positions were blitzed before the ground troops advanced.

Eating too quickly can cause your stomach to bloat uncomfortably.  The bureaucracy had bloated over the years with unnecessary administrative layers.  The software update caused the file size to bloat significantly.  He suffered from bloat after eating a large meal late at night.  The company's costs began to bloat as management kept hiring without oversight.
englishMeaning: To cause something to swell or expand, especially with gas or liquid, in an unpleasant or uncomfortable way. To become swollen or puffed up in size, often due to gas, water retention, or excess food. Used figuratively to describe something becoming unnecessarily large, excessive, or inefficient. A condition in which the body or stomach becomes swollen and distended.
sindhiMeaning: سُجڻ، ڦُلڻ، گئس يا پاڻي سبب پيٽ يا جسم جو سُڄي وڃڻ، حد کان وڌيڪ وڌي ٿيڻ، ناضروري طور تي وڏو ٿيڻ
synonyms: Swell, Puff up, Expand, Distend, Enlarge
urduMeaning: سوجنا، پھولنا، گیس یا پانی سے پیٹ یا جسم کا سوج جانا، حد سے زیادہ بڑھ جانا، غیر ضروری طور پر بڑا ہو جانا
antonyms: Shrink, Deflate, Reduce, Contract, Slim down

synonyms: Siege, Embargo, Barricade, Obstruction, Encirclement
sindhiMeaning: ناڪابندي، محاصرو، ڪنهن جاءِ تي سامان يا ماڻهن جي اچ وڃ روڪڻ، فوجي يا معاشي پابندي، بندرگاهه يا شهر کي سيل ڪرڻ
antonyms: Opening, Access, Supply route, Clearance, Freedom of movement
urduMeaning: ناکہ بندی، محاصرہ، کسی جگہ پر سامان یا لوگوں کی آمدورفت روکنا، فوجی یا معاشی پابندی، بندرگاہ یا شہر کو سیل کرنا
examples: The naval blockade prevented food and medicine from reaching the besieged city.  Economic sanctions were paired with a trade blockade to increase pressure on the regime.  Protesters formed a human blockade outside the government building.  The country attempted to break the blockade by sending supply ships.  The blockade of the port lasted for several months and caused severe shortages.
englishMeaning: A military or economic measure that prevents goods, people, or communication from entering or leaving a place. The act of sealing off an area, port, or city to prevent movement in or out. To obstruct or seal off a place in order to prevent the passage of supplies, reinforcements, or people. A situation in which access to a place is deliberately cut off as a form of pressure or siege.

synonyms: Idiot, Fool, Dolt, Dimwit, Dunce
englishMeaning: An informal or insulting term for a very stupid or dull-witted person. Someone who is slow to understand or incapable of intelligent thought. A foolish person who acts without thinking or lacks common sense. Used to express frustration at someone's stupidity or obtuseness.
sindhiMeaning: بيوقوف، احمق، سُست ذهن، ڪُنڊ، اهڙو شخص جيڪو سوچڻ يا سمجهڻ جي صلاحيت نه رکندو هجي
antonyms: Genius, Intellectual, Scholar, Sage, Bright mind
examples: Don't be such a blockhead and think before you act.  He called himself a blockhead for forgetting the anniversary.  Only a complete blockhead would ignore such clear warning signs.  She muttered under her breath that her colleague was a total blockhead.  The cartoon featured a lovable blockhead as its main character.
urduMeaning: بیوقوف، احمق، سست ذہن، اکھڑ، ایسا شخص جو سوچنے یا سمجھنے کی صلاحیت نہ رکھتا ہو

englishMeaning: Having light-colored or golden-yellow hair, used especially to describe a person or their hair. A person with fair or light-colored hair. Light or pale in color, used to describe wood, beer, or other materials with a similar golden hue. Often spelled blonde when referring specifically to a female person.
sindhiMeaning: سونهري يا هلڪي رنگ جا وار رکندڙ، هلڪي رنگ جا وار، سونهري يا هلڪي رنگ وارو شخص، لکڙي يا ٻين شين لاءِ به هلڪي رنگ جي وصف طور استعمال
synonyms: Fair-haired, Golden-haired, Light-haired, Flaxen, Platinum
antonyms: Dark-haired, Brunette, Black-haired, Dark, Raven-haired
urduMeaning: سنہری یا ہلکے رنگ کے بال رکھنے والا، ہلکے رنگ کے بال، سنہری یا ہلکے رنگ والا شخص، لکڑی یا دیگر اشیاء کے لیے بھی ہلکے رنگ کی صفت کے طور پر استعمال
examples: She had naturally blond hair that darkened slightly as she grew older.  The child in the photograph had bright blond curls and blue eyes.  The furniture was made from pale blond wood imported from Scandinavia.  He dyed his hair blond before the summer holiday.  The blond actor was immediately recognizable from across the room.

synonyms: Flower, Bloom, Flourish, Thrive, Develop
antonyms: Wither, Fade, Decline, Shrivel, Die
englishMeaning: The flower or mass of flowers on a fruit tree or other plant, especially before the fruit has formed. To produce flowers or bloom, especially said of fruit trees in spring. To develop, grow, or flourish in a positive and pleasing way, especially used of a person, relationship, or talent. A state of flowering or fresh, promising development.
sindhiMeaning: گُل، ٻوٽي يا وڻ تي آيل گُل، ڦُلڻ، ترقي ڪرڻ، ڪنهن جي صلاحيتن يا رشتي جو خوبصورتيءَ سان اڀرڻ، وسنتي موسم ۾ ميوي جي وڻن جو کِلڻ
urduMeaning: پھول، پودے یا درخت پر آیا ہوا پھول، کھلنا، ترقی کرنا، کسی کی صلاحیتوں یا رشتے کا خوبصورتی سے ابھرنا، موسم بہار میں پھلوں کے درختوں کا کھلنا
examples: The cherry trees came into blossom in early April, drawing large crowds to the park.  Their friendship gradually blossomed into a lasting and deep romance.  The young singer has blossomed into one of the most talented performers of her generation.  Spring blossom filled the orchard with color and fragrance.  With encouragement and practice, his confidence began to blossom.

synonyms: Strike, Hit, Impact, Shock, Gust
antonyms: Caress, Relief, Comfort, Calm, Benefit
examples: He struck the nail with a single blow of the hammer.  The unexpected resignation was a serious blow to the company's leadership.  She blew out all the candles on her birthday cake in one blow.  A strong wind blew through the valley overnight.  Losing the contract was a devastating blow to their plans.
urduMeaning: ضرب، مار، سخت ہاتھ یا ہتھیار کی وار، منہ سے زور سے ہوا نکالنا، ہوا چلنا، اچانک صدمہ یا تکلیف دینے والی خبر
englishMeaning: A hard hit or strike delivered by a fist, weapon, or object. An act of breathing out through the mouth with force. A sudden event or piece of news that causes shock, distress, or a significant setback. The movement of air, especially wind.
sindhiMeaning: ضرب، مار، سخت هٿ يا هٿيار جو وار، منهن مان زور سان هوا ڪڍڻ، هوا هلڻ، اوچتو صدمو يا تڪليف ڏيندڙ خبر

examples: The two boxers exchanged blows in the center of the ring.  The storm blows fiercely across the open countryside every winter.  The athlete suffered multiple blows to the head during the match.  The business received several blows in quick succession that year.  She blows out her birthday candles and makes a wish every year.
urduMeaning: وار کی جمع، کئی ضربوں یا وارون کا ذکر، ہوا چلنے کا فعل حال، باہمی ضربوں کا تبادلہ، ہوا چلتی ہے/پھونک مارتا ہے، ضربیں یا چوٹیں مارتا ہے، صدمے یا دھچکے، زور سے مارنا یا ضرب لگانا، چوٹیں/ ضربیں/ دھکے
synonyms: Strikes, Hits, Punches, Impacts, Gusts
antonyms: Caresses, Comforts, Reliefs, Benefits, Calms
englishMeaning: The plural form of blow, referring to multiple hits, strikes, or impacts. Third-person singular present tense form of the verb blow, meaning wind or air moves or someone exhales with force. Refers to multiple setbacks or shocks occurring in succession. The exchange of punches or hits between two or more parties.
sindhiMeaning: هوا هلائي ٿو / هوا لڳي ٿي، ڦوڪ ڏئي ٿو، ڌڪ هڻي ٿو، صدما يا جهٽڪا، زور سان ڌڪ هڻڻ، ڌڪ/ ضربون، اوچتي مشڪلاتون، وات مان هوا ڪڍڻ يا ڦوڪ ڏيڻ، هوا جو هلڻ يا ڪنهن طرف وهڻ

antonyms: Honest person, Straight talker, Sincere person, Transparent individual, Truth-teller
urduMeaning: دھوکہ دینے والا، کوڑی اعتماد سے اپنی حیثیت یا صلاحیت کا غلط تاثر دینے والا، بلفنگ کرنے والا شخص
synonyms: Deceiver, Pretender, Impostor, Faker, Blusterer
sindhiMeaning: ٺڳ، ڌوڪيباز، ڪوڙي اعتماد سان پنهنجي حيثيت يا صلاحيت جو غلط تاثر ڏيندڙ، بلفنگ ڪندڙ شخص
englishMeaning: A person who bluffs, meaning someone who deliberately misleads others about their abilities, intentions, or situation. Someone who pretends to have knowledge, skill, or confidence they do not actually possess. A person who uses bold or deceptive talk to create a false impression. Someone who frequently uses bluffing as a tactic in negotiation, games, or social situations.
examples: Everyone at the poker table knew he was a notorious bluffer.  As a negotiator, he was considered a skilled bluffer who rarely showed his true hand.  She was a convincing bluffer who had fooled almost everyone in the room.  The bluffer was eventually exposed when pressed for real evidence.  Being a good bluffer requires confidence and the ability to read other people.

urduMeaning: دھوکہ دینا، جو طاقت یا علم نہیں اس کا دکھاوا کرنا، جوئے یا مذاکرات میں اپنی حیثیت بڑھا کر دکھانا، جھوٹا تاثر قائم کرنا
examples: He was clearly bluffing when he claimed to have already received a better offer.  Bluffing is a core skill in competitive poker.  The suspect was bluffing when he said he had an alibi for that evening.  She realized he was bluffing only after she called his bluff.  Bluffing in negotiations can sometimes backfire badly if the other side calls it out.
englishMeaning: The act of deliberately misleading others by pretending to have greater strength, knowledge, or resources than one actually possesses. Feigning confidence or capability in order to intimidate, deceive, or gain an advantage. A tactic used in card games, negotiations, or confrontations to create a false impression. Pretending something is true in order to manipulate another person's response.
synonyms: Deceiving, Feigning, Pretending, Faking, Misleading
antonyms: Being honest, Telling the truth, Revealing, Disclosing, Admitting
sindhiMeaning: ڌوڪو ڏيڻ، جيڪا طاقت يا ڄاڻ نه آهي ان جو ڏيکاءُ ڪرڻ، جوا يا گفت شنيد ۾ پنهنجي حيثيت وڌيڪ ڏيکارڻ، ڪوڙو تاثر قائم ڪرڻ
شرم سان منهن ڳاڙهو ٿيڻ، لڄ سبب گالون جو ڳاڙها ٿيڻ، هلڪو گلابي رنگ، چهري کي رنگ ڏيڻ جو ميڪ اپ
synonyms: Redden, Flush, Color, Glow, Go pink
urduMeaning: شرم سے منہ لال ہونا، لجاتے ہوئے گالوں کا سرخ ہونا، ہلکا گلابی رنگ، چہرے کو رنگ دینے کا میک اپ
antonyms: Pale, Whiten, Blanch, Bold face, Remain unmoved
examples: She blushed deeply when he paid her an unexpected compliment.  The child blushed with embarrassment when the whole class laughed.  At first blush, the proposal seemed quite reasonable.  She applied a soft blush to her cheeks before the event.  He could not help but blush when he realized his mistake in front of everyone.
englishMeaning: To become red in the face due to embarrassment, shyness, shame, or modesty. A reddening of the face caused by strong emotion, usually embarrassment or pleasure. A pink or reddish color, often used in cosmetics to describe a makeup product used to add color to the cheeks. To feel embarrassed or ashamed about something.

examples: His bluster in the meeting convinced no one of his actual ability.  The manager blustered about consequences but never followed through.  Strong winds blustered through the coastal town all night.  Despite all his bluster, he backed down the moment he was challenged directly.  She was not intimidated by his bluster and calmly continued with her proposal.
urduMeaning: للکارنا، گرجنا، بڑی بڑی باتوں سے دوسروں کو ڈرانا، کھوکھلی دھمکیاں دینا، تیز ہوا کا زور سے چلنا، اکڑ سے بات کرنا
sindhiMeaning: ڦوڪائڻ، گرجڻ، وڏن وڏن ڳالهين سان ٻين کي ڊيڄارڻ، کوکليون ڌمڪيون ڏيڻ، تيز هوا جو زور سان هلڻ، آڪڙ سان ڳالهائڻ
synonyms: Bluff, Rant, Swagger, Bravado, Bombast
antonyms: Calm speech, Quiet delivery, Modesty, Humility, Understatement
englishMeaning: Loud, aggressive, or threatening talk with little real substance or follow-through. To talk in a boisterous, arrogant, or threatening manner without having the ability to back up the words. Of wind or weather, to blow loudly and with violent gusts. To behave or speak in a noisy, self-important, or blustering manner.

sindhiMeaning: سفري جهاز، ٽرين يا هوائي جهاز ۾ چڙهي ويل، ڪاٺ جي تختن سان بند ڪيل، ادائيگي تي رهائش يا کاڌي جي سهولت وارو
synonyms: Embarked, Sealed, Covered, Entered, Lodged
antonyms: Disembarked, Opened, Unsealed, Exited, Departed
examples: By the time they arrived, everyone had already boarded the flight.  The windows of the old house were boarded up after it was abandoned.  He boarded the ship just minutes before it departed from the harbor.  The students boarded at a small guesthouse near the university.  Several shops in the town had been boarded following the storm damage.
englishMeaning: Past tense of board, meaning to get on or enter a vehicle such as a ship, train, or aircraft. Having wooden boards nailed or fixed across openings, doors, or windows, typically to secure an abandoned or damaged building. Referring to accommodation or meals provided in exchange for payment at a boarding house or school.
urduMeaning: سفری جہاز، ٹرین یا ہوائی جہاز میں چڑھ گئے، لکڑی کے تختوں سے بند کیا گیا، ادائیگی پر رہائش یا کھانے کی سہولت والا

englishMeaning: Noisy, energetic, and cheerfully rough or exuberant in behavior. Full of energy, excitement, and enthusiasm, often in a way that seems unruly or unrestrained. Used to describe a person, group, or event that is lively and loud in an uninhibited way. Of weather or the sea, wild, stormy, and tempestuous.
synonyms: Rowdy, Noisy, Lively, Exuberant, Raucous
antonyms: Quiet, Calm, Subdued, Reserved, Peaceful
urduMeaning: شور شرابے والا، بے قابو انداز میں خوشی سے شور مچانے والا، توانا اور بے قابو سرگرمی والا، ہنگامہ خیز
sindhiMeaning: شور شرابي وارو، ڌاڳيل ۽ جوشيلو، بي قابو انداز ۾ خوشيءَ سان شور مچائيندڙ، توانا ۽ اڻ روڪيل سرگرمي وارو
examples: The boisterous children ran through the corridors despite repeated warnings to walk quietly.  A boisterous crowd of fans greeted the team at the airport.  Their boisterous laughter could be heard from the other end of the building.  The normally boisterous market was unusually quiet on that cold morning.  He had a boisterous personality that made him popular at social gatherings.

urduMeaning: چبائے ہوئے کھانے کی چھوٹی گولی جو نگلنے کے لیے تیار ہو، دوا کی ایک بڑی خوراک جو ایک ہی بار دی جائے، نگلنے کے قابل لقمہ
examples: The speech-language therapist assessed how the patient formed a bolus before swallowing.  The doctor administered a bolus of medication directly into the intravenous line.  Difficulty forming a bolus is a common symptom of certain neurological conditions.  A bolus dose of the antibiotic was given at the start of the treatment.  The nurse explained the difference between a bolus injection and a slow infusion.
englishMeaning: A small rounded mass of chewed food ready to be swallowed. A soft mass of food or medicine prepared for swallowing in one portion. In medicine, a single large dose of a drug administered quickly, especially by injection. A rounded lump of any substance that is treated as a single unit.
synonyms: Lump, Mass, Dose, Mouthful, Morsel
antonyms: Powder, Liquid, Dissolved dose, Drip, Gradual infusion
sindhiMeaning: چٻاٽيل کاڌي جو ننڍڙو گولو جيڪو نگرڻ لاءِ تيار هجي، دوا جي هڪ وڏي خوراڪ جيڪا هڪ ئي ڀيري ڏني وڃي، نگرڻ جوڳو لڪيو

examples: She ate every last morsel on her plate. The dog waited patiently for a morsel of food. He enjoyed every morsel of the delicious cake. Not a single morsel was left after the feast.
englishMeaning: A small piece or bite of food. It can also mean a small amount of something, especially something pleasant or desirable. A very small portion of food that can be eaten in one bite. It is often used in a gentle or descriptive way, especially when talking about tasty food. In a broader sense, it can also mean a small piece of anything, such as information, pleasure, or experience.
urduMeaning: لُقمہ (کھانے کا چھوٹا سا حصہ جو ایک بار میں کھایا جائے)، بہت چھوٹا ٹکڑا، ذرا سا حصہ، تھوڑی سی مقدار (کسی چیز کی بھی ہو سکتی ہے), کھانے کا ایک چھوٹا سا لقمہ، معلومات کا تھوڑا سا حصہ
synonyms: Bite, Piece, Mouthful, Fragment, Scrap
sindhiMeaning: لقمو (کاڌي جو ننڍڙو حصو جيڪو هڪ ئي دفعو ۾ کائجي)، ننڍڙو ٽڪرو، ٿورو حصو، ڪا به شيءِ جو تمام ٿورو مقدار, ماني جو ننڍڙو لقمو، ڪا شيءِ جو ٿورو حصو
antonyms: Whole, Portion, Bulk, Entirety, Meal

synonyms: Pomposity, Bluster, Grandiloquence, Hot air, Rhetoric
englishMeaning: High-sounding, inflated language that is full of exaggeration and self-importance but contains little real meaning or substance. Speech or writing that impresses through its grand-sounding words but is ultimately empty or insincere. Pompous or overly elaborate talk intended to impress but often coming across as ridiculous. Inflated language used to make something sound more important or impressive than it really is.
antonyms: Simplicity, Understatement, Directness, Clarity, Plainness
examples: The speech was pure bombast with very little of any real policy substance.  Critics dismissed the minister's announcement as empty bombast.  His writing was often criticized for its bombast and lack of clarity.  Behind all the bombast, there was actually very little being offered.  She cut through the bombast and asked directly what the plan actually was.
sindhiMeaning: لفاظي، بلند بانگ پر خالي ڳالهيون، شيخي خوري، وڏن وڏن لفظن ۾ ڳالهائڻ پر مقصد ڪجهه نه، خودساختي اهميت وارو انداز
urduMeaning: لفاظی، بلند بانگ مگر خالی باتیں، شیخی خوری، بڑے بڑے الفاظ میں بولنا مگر مقصد کچھ نہیں، خود ساختہ اہمیت والا انداز

antonyms: Bad faith, Deception, Fraud, Insincerity, Pretence
englishMeaning: A Latin phrase meaning in good faith, used to express sincere and honest intention. The genuine and honest intentions or qualifications of a person. Evidence or proof of a person's good faith, honesty, trustworthiness, or legitimacy. Credentials or evidence used to establish that someone's motives or qualifications are genuine and can be trusted.
synonyms: Good faith, Credentials, Authenticity, Legitimacy, Sincerity
urduMeaning: نیک نیتی، اصل ارادے، ایمانداری اور سچائی کا ثبوت، کسی کی اہلیت یا نیت کی سچائی کے ثبوت، لاطینی اصطلاح سے ماخوذ جس کا مطلب نیک نیتی سے ہے
sindhiMeaning: نيڪ نيتي، اصل ارادا، ايمانداري ۽ سچائي جو ثبوت، ڪنهن جي قابليت يا نيت جي سچائي جا ثبوت، لاطيني اصطلاح مان ورتل جنهن جو مطلب نيڪ نيتيءَ سان آهي
examples: The charity was asked to provide its bona fides before receiving government funding.  He questioned the bona fides of the organization offering such unusually high returns.  Her bona fides as a human rights lawyer were beyond question.  The investigator was asked to verify the bona fides of the new business partner.  Establishing your bona fides early in a negotiation can help build trust quickly.

englishMeaning: Crazy. Mad. Insane. Wildly enthusiastic or excited. Behaving in a foolish or absurd way. An informal word used to describe someone or something that seems completely irrational, eccentric, or out of control. It can also describe a situation that is chaotic, ridiculous, or extremely unusual. Often used humorously in everyday conversation rather than as a serious medical or psychological term.
urduMeaning: پاگل، دیوانہ، بے وقوف، سرپھرا، خبطی، کسی چیز کے لیے انتہائی جنونی، حواس باختہ، عجیب اور غیر معقول حرکات کرنے والا، مذاقاً کسی کو پاگل یا سنکی کہنے کے لیے استعمال ہونے والا غیر رسمی لفظ
examples: He went bonkers when he heard the good news. The kids drove their mother bonkers all afternoon. That idea sounds completely bonkers to me. The crowd went bonkers at the concert. She is bonkers about classic cars.
antonyms: Sane, Sensible, Rational, Calm, Composed, Level-headed, Reasonable
synonyms: Crazy, Mad, Insane, Nuts, Wild, Daft, Loony, Mental, Off one's head, Wacky
sindhiMeaning: چريو، چرچو، پاگل، ديوانو، احمق، بيوقوف، ڪنهن شيءِ تي بيحد جنوني، حواس وڃائي ويٺل، عجيب ۽ بي ترتيب رويي وارو، مذاق ۾ ڪنهن کي چريو يا بيوقوف چوڻ لاءِ استعمال ٿيندڙ لفظ

urduMeaning: ناپسندیدگی کا آواز نکالنا، ہوٹ کرنا، چڑانا، کسی کو شور مچا کر مخالفت کرنا، اچانک ”بُو“ کہہ کر کسی کو ڈرانا، طنزیہ آواز، (غیر رسمی طور پر) محبوب یا قریبی ساتھی کے لیے پیار بھرا لفظ
englishMeaning: A sound made to express disapproval, contempt, or to startle someone. To shout 'boo' at a performer, speaker, or team to show that you do not like them. A sudden exclamation used to frighten or surprise a person, often as a joke. Used as a noun for the sound itself and as a verb for the act of making it. In informal American English, it is also used as an affectionate term for a boyfriend, girlfriend, or close loved one.
antonyms: Cheer, Applaud, Clap, Praise, Acclaim, Encourage, Hail
synonyms: Hiss, Jeer, Hoot, Heckle, Mock, Catcall, Sneer, Deride
examples: The audience began to boo the politician during his speech. He jumped out from behind the door and shouted 'Boo!' to scare his sister. The crowd booed loudly when the referee made the wrong decision. Don't boo the players; they are trying their best. She called him her boo on social media.
sindhiMeaning: ناپسنديءَ جو آواز ڪڍڻ، چِڙائڻ، شور مچائي ڪنهن جي مخالفت ڪرڻ، ڪنهن کي ڊيڄارڻ لاءِ اوچتو ”بُو“ چوڻ، طنزيه آواز، اوچتو ٻاڦ ڪڍي ڊيڄارڻ، (غير رسمي طور) محبوب يا پيارو ساٿي

antonyms: Water, Soft drink, Juice, Non-alcoholic beverage, Abstinence, Sobriety
synonyms: Alcohol, Liquor, Spirits, Drink, Hooch, Grog, Tipple
sindhiMeaning: شراب، مَڌ، نشيدار مشروب، شراب پيئڻ، گهڻي شراب نوشي ڪرڻ، عام ڳالهائڻ ۾ شراب لاءِ استعمال ٿيندڙ لفظ، نشي وارو مشروب پيئڻ
urduMeaning: شراب، مے، نشہ آور مشروب، شراب پینا، بہت زیادہ شراب نوشی کرنا، عام بول چال میں شراب کے لیے استعمال ہونے والا لفظ، نشہ آور مشروبات کا استعمال
englishMeaning: Alcoholic drink. Liquor. To drink large quantities of alcohol. An informal word for any alcoholic beverage such as beer, wine, whisky, or spirits. To consume alcohol heavily, usually at a party or social gathering. The word is casual and often used in everyday conversation rather than in formal writing.
examples: They brought plenty of booze to the party. He spent all his money on booze and cigarettes. The guests boozed until late at night. Try not to booze too much before the meeting tomorrow. There was no booze allowed at the wedding.

sindhiMeaning: اوڌر وٺڻ، قرض وٺڻ، ڪجهه وقت لاءِ استعمال لاءِ وٺڻ ۽ پوءِ موٽائڻ، ڪنهن جي شيءِ عارضي طور وٺڻ، پئسو يا رقم قرض طور وٺڻ، ڪنهن ٻولي يا ثقافت مان لفظ يا خيال اخذ ڪرڻ
examples: Can I borrow your pen for a minute? She borrowed a book from the library yesterday. They had to borrow money from the bank to buy a new house. English has borrowed many words from French and Latin. He borrowed his brother's car for the weekend.
englishMeaning: To take and use something that belongs to someone else with the intention of returning it. To receive money from a person, bank, or institution that must be paid back, usually with interest. To take a word, idea, or custom from another language or culture and use it as one's own. The opposite of lend. The act of using something temporarily without claiming permanent ownership.
urduMeaning: ادھار لینا، قرض لینا، کسی کی چیز کچھ وقت کے لیے استعمال کے واسطے لینا اور پھر واپس کرنا، رقم بطور قرض حاصل کرنا، کسی دوسری زبان یا ثقافت سے لفظ یا خیال اخذ کرنا
antonyms: Lend, Return, Give, Repay, Own, Provide, Grant
synonyms: Take on loan, Loan, Adopt, Take, Acquire temporarily, Obtain, Use, Receive on credit

antonyms: Pebble, Grain, Sand, Dust, Speck, Particle
sindhiMeaning: وڏو گول پٿر، ڳورو ۽ ڳنڍيدار پٿر، اهو وڏو پٿر جيڪو پاڻيءَ يا موسم سان لسو ٿي ويو هجي، جبلن، ندين ۽ ڪناري وارن علائقن ۾ ملندڙ وڏو پٿر، گهٽ يا وڏي صورت ۾ ڳورو پٿر
urduMeaning: بڑا گول پتھر، بھاری اور وزنی چٹان، وہ بڑا پتھر جو پانی یا موسم سے ہموار ہو چکا ہو، پہاڑوں، دریاؤں اور ساحلی علاقوں میں پایا جانے والا بڑا پتھر، علامتی طور پر بھاری بوجھ
synonyms: Rock, Stone, Crag, Megalith, Slab, Pebble (small), Outcrop
englishMeaning: A large, rounded rock, especially one that has been worn smooth by water or weather. A massive stone, usually too big to be lifted easily, that lies on the surface of the ground or in a river. Boulders are larger than ordinary stones and are often found in mountains, valleys, rivers, and along coastlines. The word is also used figuratively to describe something heavy or burdensome.
examples: A huge boulder blocked the mountain road after the landslide. Children climbed over the smooth boulders by the river. The boulder rolled down the hill and crashed into the trees. Workers used machines to move the giant boulder. The path was covered with rocks and boulders.

urduMeaning: کشادہ سڑک، چوڑی شاہراہ، دونوں طرف درختوں سے سجی ہوئی بڑی گلی، شہر کی شاندار اور وسیع سڑک، وہ بڑی شاہراہ جس کے دونوں جانب عمارتیں، دکانیں یا تفریحی مقامات ہوں
sindhiMeaning: ويڪرو پڪو رستو، وڏو شاهراهي رستو، ٻنهي پاسي وڻن سان سينگاريل وڏي گهٽي، شهر جو شاندار ۽ وسيع رستو، مرڪزي وڏي شاهراهه جنهن جي ٻنهي پاسي عمارتون يا دڪان هجن
antonyms: Alley, Lane, Path, Track, Footpath, Narrow street
synonyms: Avenue, Street, Road, Promenade, Thoroughfare, Highway, Parade
englishMeaning: A wide street in a city or town, usually lined with trees on both sides. A broad avenue, often considered grand or important, that may feature shops, restaurants, monuments, or fashionable buildings. Boulevards are typically found in major cities and are designed for both traffic and pedestrians. The term originally comes from French and refers to a fortified rampart that was later turned into a public road.
examples: We walked along the famous boulevard in Paris. The hotel is located on a busy boulevard near the city center. Tall palm trees lined the entire boulevard. A parade was held on the main boulevard yesterday. Their new house overlooks a quiet, tree-lined boulevard.

englishMeaning: A boundary or limit. A small stream or brook, especially one that flows from a spring. A goal or destination, often used in a literary or poetic sense. An archaic or literary word that can mean either a physical boundary, a small watercourse, or the final point of a journey. Famously used by Shakespeare in 'Hamlet' to refer to the undiscovered country from which no traveller returns.
synonyms: Boundary, Limit, Goal, Destination, Stream, Brook, Frontier, End
antonyms: Beginning, Start, Origin, Source, Infinity, Boundlessness
urduMeaning: حد، سرحد، منزل، مقصد، انتہا، چھوٹی ندی یا چشمہ، ادبی یا شعری لفظ جس کا مطلب حد، منزل یا چھوٹی پانی کی گزرگاہ ہے، آخری مقام یا ٹھکانہ
examples: Death is the bourne from which no traveller returns. The little bourne flowed gently through the meadow. They reached the bourne of their long journey at sunset. His ambition knew no bourne. The old map marked the bourne between the two estates.
sindhiMeaning: حد، سرحد، منزل، مقصد، انتها، ننڍي ندي يا چشمو، ادبي يا شعري لفظ جنهن جو مطلب حد، منزل يا ننڍڙي وهڪري وارو پاڻي آهي، آخري مقام يا ٺڪاڻو

antonyms: Lively, Alert, Quick, Energetic, Sharp, Sprightly, Animated
sindhiMeaning: ڳئون يا ڍڳن سان لاڳاپيل، ڍور ڍڳا واري قسم جو، سست، بي حس، ڍڳي وانگر ست ۽ بي تاثر، حيواني علم ۾ ڳئون، ڍڳو، مينهن وغيره لاءِ استعمال ٿيندڙ صفت، علامتي طور سست ۽ بيوقوف انسان
synonyms: Cow-like, Cattle-related, Sluggish, Dull, Stolid, Slow, Phlegmatic
urduMeaning: گائے سے متعلق، گائے بیل کی نسل کا، سست، بے حس، گائے کی مانند کاہل اور بے تاثر، حیاتیات میں گائے، بیل، بھینس وغیرہ کے لیے استعمال ہونے والی صفت، علامتی طور پر سست اور کند ذہن انسان
examples: Bovine diseases can spread quickly if cattle are not vaccinated. The farm specializes in bovine health and breeding. He stared at the screen with a bovine expression. Bovine milk is the most common type consumed worldwide. Scientists studied the bovine immune system in detail.
englishMeaning: Relating to or resembling cattle. Connected with cows, bulls, oxen, or buffaloes. Slow-moving, dull, or stolid in manner, like a cow. In biology and zoology it describes animals of the cattle family. Also used figuratively to describe a person who appears sluggish, expressionless, or lacking in intelligence or emotion.

synonyms: Bending, Stooping, Inclining, Nodding, Saluting, Yielding, Curtsying
englishMeaning: Bending the upper body or head forward as a sign of respect, greeting, agreement, or submission. The act of inclining the body in front of a person, audience, or sacred object. Used in formal greetings, religious ceremonies, theatrical performances, and martial arts. Can also refer to the act of playing a stringed musical instrument with a bow, or bending under pressure or weight.
sindhiMeaning: جهڪڻ، تعظيم ۾ سر نوائڻ، عزت يا احترام طور جسم اڳتي جهڪائڻ، سلام ۾ جهڪڻ، تابعداريءَ جو اظهار، ساز وڄائڻ ۾ ڪمان جو استعمال، دٻاءُ يا بار جي ڪري جهڪي پوڻ
antonyms: Standing straight, Rising, Lifting, Resisting, Defying, Standing upright
urduMeaning: جھکنا، تعظیم میں سر جھکانا، احترام یا عزت کے طور پر جسم آگے کو جھکانا، سلام میں جھکنا، فرمانبرداری کا اظہار، ساز بجانے میں کمان کا استعمال، دباؤ یا بوجھ کے باعث جھک جانا
examples: Bowing is a common form of greeting in Japan. The actor was bowing to the audience after the performance. He kept bowing his head out of respect for the elder. Bowing under the weight of the heavy bag, he walked slowly. She practiced bowing techniques for her violin lesson.

synonyms: Arches, Curves, Knots, Ribbons, Salutes, Prows, Fronts
sindhiMeaning: ڪمانون، تير ڇوڙڻ وارا اوزار، فيتي يا ڪپڙي مان ٺاهيل سينگار جا ڳنڍا، تعظيم ۾ جهڪڻ جا عمل، ٻيڙين يا جهازن جا اڳيان حصا، وائلن وغيره وڄائڻ لاءِ ڪمانون
englishMeaning: Plural of bow. Curved weapons used for shooting arrows. Decorative knots tied from ribbon or string, often used on gifts or in hair. Acts of bending the body forward as a sign of respect or greeting. The front parts of ships or boats. Long, thin sticks with horsehair stretched along them, used to play stringed instruments such as the violin or cello.
antonyms: Sterns (of a ship), Straight lines, Backs, Rears
urduMeaning: کمانیں، تیر چلانے والے ہتھیار، فیتے یا ربن سے بنی سجاوٹی گرہیں، عزت میں جھکنے کے عمل، کشتیوں اور جہازوں کے اگلے حصے، وائلن وغیرہ بجانے کے لیے استعمال ہونے والی کمانیں
examples: The hunters carried bows and arrows into the forest. She tied colorful bows on all the gift boxes. The performers gave three bows to the cheering audience. Waves crashed against the bows of the fishing boats. The violinists tightened their bows before the concert.

The little boy laughed and pointed at the bowwow in the garden. We could hear the bowwow of the neighbor's dog all night. She bought a tiny bowwow as a pet for her daughter. The puppy let out a soft bowwow when it saw the stranger. 'Look at the bowwow!' the child shouted happily.
englishMeaning: An imitation of the barking sound made by a dog. A childish or informal word for a dog. Used especially by or with young children to refer to dogs in a friendly way. It can be used as a noun for the dog itself or as an interjection imitating its bark. The word reflects how the sound of a dog's bark is represented in English onomatopoeia.
sindhiMeaning: ڪتي جي ڀُونڪڻ جو آواز، ٻارن جي ٻوليءَ ۾ ڪتي لاءِ پيار وارو لفظ، ڪتو، ”ڀؤ ڀؤ“ آواز ڪرڻ، ٻاراڻي زبان ۾ ڪتو يا ان جو آواز
urduMeaning: کتے کے بھونکنے کی آواز، بچوں کی زبان میں کتے کے لیے پیار بھرا لفظ، کتا، ”بھؤ بھؤ“ کی آواز نکالنا، بچوں والی زبان میں کتا یا اس کی آواز
synonyms: Bark, Woof, Yap, Yelp, Doggy, Puppy, Hound
antonyms: Silence, Quiet, Hush, Stillness
Weaken, Loosen, Release, Relax, Detach, Unprepare
synonyms: Support, Prop, Reinforce, Strengthen, Steady, Pair, Couple, Prepare
urduMeaning: سہارا، ٹیک، مضبوطی کے لیے لگائی جانے والی پٹی یا آلہ، جوڑا، دو ایک جیسی چیزیں خاص طور پر شکار شدہ پرندے یا جانور، اپنے آپ کو کسی مشکل کے لیے تیار کرنا، مضبوط کرنا، دانتوں کو سیدھا کرنے والا تار
englishMeaning: A device used to support, strengthen, or hold something firmly in place. A pair of two similar things, especially birds or animals. To prepare oneself mentally or physically for something difficult or unpleasant. To make stronger by adding a support. In dentistry, a wire device worn to straighten the teeth. Also used to describe a pair of suspenders that hold up trousers.
examples: He wore a brace on his knee after the injury. The pilot told the passengers to brace for landing. She got a brace fitted to straighten her teeth. They shot a brace of pheasants during the hunt. Wooden braces were used to support the roof.
sindhiMeaning: ٽيڪ، سهارو، مضبوطيءَ لاءِ لڳايل پٽي يا اوزار، جوڙو، ٻه ساڳيون شيون خاص ڪري شڪار ٿيل پکي يا جانور، پاڻ کي ڪنهن ڏکيائيءَ لاءِ تيار ڪرڻ، مضبوط ڪرڻ، ڏندن کي سڌو ڪرڻ وارو تار وارو اوزار

urduMeaning: ہتھیار لہرانا، تلوار یا چاقو وغیرہ غصے میں ہلانا، کسی چیز کو دکھاتے ہوئے گھمانا، دھمکی یا جوش میں کوئی چیز لہرانا، فخر یا غصے میں کوئی چیز نمایاں طور پر دکھانا
antonyms: Hide, Conceal, Sheathe, Lower, Withhold, Cover
englishMeaning: To wave or swing something, especially a weapon, in a threatening or excited way. To display something boldly or aggressively in order to impress, threaten, or attract attention. Usually used when a person shows a sword, knife, gun, or other object by moving it through the air. Can also be used figuratively for showing off documents, awards, or ideas.
synonyms: Wave, Flourish, Swing, Wield, Shake, Display, Flaunt, Exhibit
sindhiMeaning: هٿيار لهرائڻ، تلوار يا ڪاتي وغيره وير ۾ هلائڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ کي ڏيکاريندي گهمائڻ، ڌمڪي يا جوش ۾ ڪا شيءِ لهرائڻ، فخريه يا غصي ۾ ڪا شيءِ ڏيکارڻ
examples: He brandished a sword at the intruder. The protester brandished a banner above the crowd. The robber brandished a knife and demanded money. She brandished her award proudly in front of her friends. The soldier brandished his rifle to scare away the attackers.

synonyms: Rascal, Imp, Scamp, Mischief-maker, Spoiled child, Urchin, Troublemaker
antonyms: Angel, Well-behaved child, Darling, Sweetheart, Obedient child
examples: That child is such a spoiled brat. Stop behaving like a brat and listen to your mother. The little brat threw his food on the floor. He grew up as an army brat, moving from city to city. She loves her nephew, even though he is a cheeky brat.
sindhiMeaning: بدتميز ٻار، بگڙيل ٻار، شرارتي ۽ ضدي ٻار، ٻيارَ، چِڙچِڙو ٻار، عام طور تي ناپسنديءَ سان استعمال ٿيندڙ لفظ، فوجي يا ڪنهن خاص پيشي واري جو ٻار به سڏيو ويندو آهي
englishMeaning: A badly behaved or annoying child. A spoiled, rude, or unruly young person. Often used in a disapproving or affectionate way to describe a child who acts in a selfish or troublesome manner. Can also refer informally to the child of a person in a particular profession, such as an 'army brat'. The word is usually used in casual or humorous speech.
urduMeaning: بدتمیز بچہ، بگڑا ہوا بچہ، شرارتی اور ضدی بچہ، چڑچڑا بچہ، عام طور پر ناپسندیدگی کے ساتھ استعمال ہونے والا لفظ، فوجی یا کسی خاص پیشے والے کا بچہ بھی کہلاتا ہے

examples: The soldier was honored for his bravery in battle. Her bravery in speaking out inspired many others. It takes great bravery to admit one's mistakes. The firefighters showed remarkable bravery during the rescue. Children learn about bravery from stories of real heroes.
synonyms: Courage, Valor, Heroism, Fearlessness, Boldness, Gallantry, Daring, Pluck
sindhiMeaning: بهادري، دليري، جرئت، همت، خوف کان سواءِ خطري يا تڪليف کي منهن ڏيڻ جي صلاحيت، نڊرتا، جانبازي، شجاعت، دلير عمل
englishMeaning: Courageous behavior or character. The quality of being brave. The ability to face danger, difficulty, fear, or pain without showing fear. A noble and admirable quality shown by people who act with strength of mind in challenging situations. Bravery is often praised in soldiers, firefighters, doctors, and ordinary people who perform heroic acts.
urduMeaning: بہادری، دلیری، جرات، ہمت، خوف کے بغیر خطرے یا مشکل کا سامنا کرنے کی صلاحیت، نڈر پن، جانبازی، شجاعت، دلیرانہ عمل
antonyms: Cowardice, Fear, Timidity, Weakness, Faintheartedness, Cravenness

sindhiMeaning: ڇاتي، سيني جو حصو، عورت جي ڇاتيءَ جو حصو جنهن مان کير پيدا ٿئي، سيني وارو حصو، جذبن جو مرڪز، پکيءَ جي اڳيون حصو، دليريءَ سان ڪنهن شيءِ کي منهن ڏيڻ
examples: Mothers are encouraged to breastfeed their babies. He felt a sudden pain in his breast. The chef prepared a delicious chicken breast for dinner. She held the child gently to her breast. The swimmer breasted the waves with great strength.
urduMeaning: چھاتی، سینے کا حصہ، عورت کی چھاتی جس سے دودھ پیدا ہوتا ہے، سینہ، جذبات کا مرکز، پرندے کے سینے کا حصہ، دلیری سے کسی چیز کا سامنا کرنا
englishMeaning: One of the two soft, rounded parts on the upper front of a woman's body that can produce milk. The front part of the chest in humans and animals. The seat of emotions, used in literary expressions such as 'a feeling in one's breast'. The part of a bird that covers the front of its body. To face or move forward against something with courage.
synonyms: Chest, Bosom, Bust, Heart, Front, Torso, Pectoral
antonyms: Back, Rear, Behind, Spine

sindhiMeaning: نسل، قسم، جانورن يا ٻوٽن جي خاص قسم، نسل پيدا ڪرڻ، اولاد پيدا ڪرڻ، پرورش ڪرڻ، ڪنهن مقصد لاءِ جانور يا ٻوٽا پالڻ، ڪنهن جذبي يا حالت کي پيدا ڪرڻ
englishMeaning: To produce young animals or plants through reproduction. A particular type or kind of animal or plant. To raise animals or plants for a specific purpose, such as appearance, behavior, or productivity. To cause a feeling, condition, or situation to develop. Often used both literally about animals and figuratively about ideas, emotions, or social problems.
examples: This farm breeds horses for racing. Poverty often breeds crime and frustration. The Labrador is a very friendly breed of dog. Scientists are trying to breed a disease-resistant variety of wheat. Familiarity is said to breed contempt.
antonyms: Destroy, Kill, Prevent, Stop, Eliminate, Suppress
synonyms: Reproduce, Multiply, Produce, Rear, Raise, Generate, Create, Cultivate
urduMeaning: نسل، قسم، جانوروں یا پودوں کی خاص قسم، نسل پیدا کرنا، اولاد پیدا کرنا، پرورش کرنا، کسی مقصد کے لیے جانور یا پودے پالنا، کسی جذبے یا کیفیت کو جنم دینا

examples: She brewed a fresh pot of tea for the guests. This company has been brewing beer for over a hundred years. A storm is brewing on the horizon. Trouble was brewing between the two rival groups. He sat quietly, sipping his morning brew.
englishMeaning: To make beer, ale, or other drinks by mixing, boiling, and fermenting ingredients. To prepare tea or coffee by mixing it with hot water. To be in the process of developing, especially something unpleasant such as a storm or trouble. A drink made by brewing, especially beer or tea. To plan or plot something secretly.
sindhiMeaning: ٺاهڻ، شراب يا بيئر ٺاهڻ، چانهه يا ڪافي ٺاهڻ، ڪا مصيبت يا طوفان پيدا ٿيڻ ۾ هجڻ، ڪا سازش رٿڻ، ٺهيل مشروب خاص ڪري بيئر يا چانهه
urduMeaning: بنانا، شراب یا بیئر بنانا، چائے یا کافی بنانا، کوئی مصیبت یا طوفان پیدا ہونے کے قریب ہونا، خفیہ طور پر کوئی منصوبہ بنانا، تیار کیا گیا مشروب خاص طور پر بیئر یا چائے
synonyms: Prepare, Make, Ferment, Boil, Concoct, Mix, Develop, Plot
antonyms: Drink, Consume, Dismantle, Resolve, Calm, Settle

englishMeaning: A strong regional accent, especially an Irish or Scottish one, when speaking English. A type of strong, sturdy leather shoe with decorative perforations along the seams. The word can describe a way of speaking that clearly shows a person's regional origin, or a classic style of formal shoe popular in both men's and women's fashion.
examples: He spoke English with a thick Irish brogue. You can recognize him by his Scottish brogue. She bought a pair of brown leather brogues for the office. His brogue made him sound charming and unique. The shop sells handmade brogues in many colors.
urduMeaning: خاص علاقائی لہجہ خاص طور پر آئرش یا اسکاٹش، زبان میں علاقائی تلفظ، چمڑے کے مضبوط جوتے جن پر سوراخوں والے ڈیزائن ہوں، روایتی رسمی جوتا
antonyms: Standard accent, Neutral speech, Sandals, Slippers
sindhiMeaning: خاص علائقائي لهجو خاص ڪري آئرش يا اسڪاٽش، ٻوليءَ ۾ علائقائي اچار، مضبوط چمڙي جا جُتا جن تي سوراخن وارا نمونا هجن، روايتي رسمي بوٽ
synonyms: Accent, Dialect, Intonation, Inflection, Pronunciation, Shoe, Footwear

antonyms: Original thought, Insight, Novelty, Fresh idea, Profundity
urduMeaning: گھسا پٹا یا فرسودہ جملہ، عام اور بے معنی تسلی آمیز بات، کیمیا میں برومائیڈ مرکب جو پہلے نیند آور دوا کے طور پر استعمال ہوتا تھا، سست یا بور کرنے والا گفتگو کرنے والا شخص
sindhiMeaning: رواجي يا ٿڪل جملو، عام ۽ بي معنيٰ تسلي وارو جملو، ڪيميائي اصطلاح ۾ برومائيڊ مرڪب جيڪو اڳي خواب آور دوا طور استعمال ٿيندو هو، سست يا بور ڪندڙ ڳالهائيندڙ ماڻهو
englishMeaning: A commonplace or unoriginal remark, especially one intended to soothe or please. A trite, dull, or boring statement. In chemistry, a compound of bromine with another element or group, formerly used as a sedative. A person who is conventional, dull, or tiresome in conversation. The word can be used both literally in chemistry and figuratively in language.
synonyms: Cliché, Platitude, Truism, Commonplace, Banality, Stereotype
examples: His speech was full of bromides and offered no real advice. 'Time heals all wounds' is an old bromide. Doctors once prescribed bromides to calm nervous patients. She found the lecture full of dull bromides. Avoid bromides if you want your writing to sound fresh.

englishMeaning: A thin soup made by boiling meat, fish, or vegetables in water. The liquid in which meat, fish, or vegetables have been cooked. A nutritious clear liquid often used as a base for soups, stews, and sauces. Considered comforting and healthy, especially for those who are sick or recovering. Sometimes used figuratively to refer to a mixture of different elements.
urduMeaning: شوربہ، رس، گوشت یا سبزیوں کو پانی میں ابال کر بنایا گیا پتلا سوپ، وہ پانی جس میں گوشت یا سبزیاں پکائی گئی ہوں، طاقت بخش اور صحت مند مائع، بیماروں کے لیے مفید سوپ
examples: She made a warm chicken broth for her sick son. Add the noodles to the boiling broth and stir well. A good broth is the foundation of many delicious soups. The cook simmered the bones for hours to prepare the broth. He drank a bowl of vegetable broth before dinner.
sindhiMeaning: شوربو، رس، گوشت يا ڀاڄين کي پاڻيءَ ۾ ٻاڙي ٺاهيل پتلو سوپ، اهو پاڻي جنهن ۾ گوشت يا ڀاڄيون پچايون ويون هجن، طاقتور ۽ تندرستيءَ بخش پاڻي، بيمارن لاءِ مفيد سوپ
antonyms: Solid food, Stew (thick), Paste, Dry food
synonyms: Soup, Stock, Bouillon, Consommé, Liquor, Decoction

examples: The preacher condemned all forms of brothelry in his sermon. Old laws were passed to prevent brothelry in the town. The novel describes the brothelry of the corrupt nobles. He was ashamed of the brothelry that had taken over the district. Such brothelry has no place in a respectable society.
antonyms: Chastity, Morality, Decency, Virtue, Purity, Modesty
englishMeaning: Behavior or activities associated with a brothel. Lewd, immoral, or vulgar conduct. An archaic word used to describe shameful or indecent practices and the people involved in them. Rarely used in modern English, the term carries strong moral disapproval and refers broadly to debauchery, prostitution, or scandalous behavior.
urduMeaning: بدکاری، عیاشی، فحاشی، چکلے سے متعلق سرگرمیاں، اخلاقی طور پر مذموم عمل، بدچلنی، شرمناک حرکات، پرانی انگریزی میں بدکاری یا فحش پیشے کے لیے استعمال ہونے والا لفظ
sindhiMeaning: بدڪاري، عياشي، فحاشي، چڪلي وارا ڪم، اخلاقي طور بدنام عمل، بداخلاقي، شرمناڪ حرڪتون، پراڻي انگريزيءَ ۾ بدڪاريءَ يا فحش ڌنڌي لاءِ استعمال ٿيندڙ لفظ
synonyms: Debauchery, Lewdness, Immorality, Vice, Prostitution, Indecency, Licentiousness

sindhiMeaning: جهيڙا، اختلاف، ناراضگيون، دوستن يا ويجهن ماڻهن جي وچ ۾ جهڳڙا، رشتن ۾ ٿيندڙ ننڍا تڪرار، بدمزگيون، غلط فهميون
urduMeaning: جھگڑے، اختلافات، ناراضگیاں، دوستوں یا قریبی لوگوں کے درمیان تنازعات، تعلقات میں پیدا ہونے والی چھوٹی کشیدگیاں، بدمزگیاں، غلط فہمیاں
examples: Their friendship survived many small brouilles over the years. The diplomat tried to settle the brouilles between the two nations. Old brouilles were forgotten at the family reunion. Such brouilles often arise from simple misunderstandings. The letters reveal the brouilles between the famous writers.
englishMeaning: Quarrels, disagreements, or fallings-out between people. A French-origin word used in English to describe states of conflict, estrangement, or misunderstanding, often between friends, lovers, or allies. The term suggests minor disputes that disturb a previously good relationship and may or may not be easily resolved.
synonyms: Quarrels, Disputes, Disagreements, Tiffs, Spats, Misunderstandings, Estrangements
antonyms: Reconciliations, Agreements, Friendships, Peace, Harmony, Accord

examples: She wiped the sweat from her brow with a cloth. He raised his brow in surprise at the news. A deep frown appeared on his brow. They camped on the brow of the hill overlooking the valley. The old man's brow was wrinkled with worry.
englishMeaning: The forehead. The arch of hair above each eye, also called the eyebrow. The upper edge or projecting part of something such as a hill or cliff. Used figuratively to refer to facial expressions that show thought, worry, or anger, as in 'a furrowed brow'. A literary and poetic word often used to describe a person's appearance or mood.
synonyms: Forehead, Eyebrow, Temple, Crest, Top, Ridge, Edge
sindhiMeaning: پيشاني، اَبرو، اکين مٿان وارن وارو حصو، ٽڪريءَ يا چوٽيءَ جو مٿيون ڪنارو، فڪرمنديءَ يا ڪاوڙ جو اظهار، چهري جو مٿيون حصو
antonyms: Base, Bottom, Chin, Foot (of a hill), Valley
urduMeaning: پیشانی، ابرو، آنکھوں کے اوپر بالوں والا حصہ، پہاڑی یا چٹان کا اوپری کنارہ، فکر مندی یا غصے کا اظہار، چہرے کا اوپری حصہ

englishMeaning: A color produced by mixing red, yellow, and black, similar to that of wood, soil, or chocolate. Having this color. To cook food until it turns brown on the outside. To become brown, especially due to sunlight or heat. Used to describe skin, hair, eyes, or objects of this color. Also a common family name in English-speaking countries.
antonyms: White, Pale, Light, Bleached, Colorless, Pallid
synonyms: Tan, Beige, Chestnut, Khaki, Coffee-colored, Bronze, Hazel, Chocolate
sindhiMeaning: ناسي رنگ، خاڪي، ڀورو رنگ، ڪپڙي، چمڙي يا کاڌي جو ناسي ٿيڻ، کاڌو پچائي ناسي رنگ ڏيارڻ، اس ۾ چمڙي جو ڪارو ٿيڻ، ناسي رنگ وارو
examples: She has beautiful brown eyes and dark hair. The leaves turned brown in autumn. Brown the onions in oil before adding the meat. He wore a brown suit to the meeting. The bread should be golden brown when fully baked.
urduMeaning: بھورا رنگ، خاکی، براؤن رنگ، کپڑے، جلد یا کھانے کا بھورا ہونا، کھانا پکا کر بھورا رنگ دینا، دھوپ سے جلد کا سانولا ہونا، بھورا رنگ والا

synonyms: Cruel, Savage, Ruthless, Merciless, Harsh, Inhuman, Barbaric, Vicious
sindhiMeaning: ظالم، سفاڪ، بي رحم، سخت، بي درد، تشدد وارو، انتهائي ڪرڙو، انساني همدرديءَ کان خالي، سخت ۽ ايذاءُ ڏيندڙ، ڪنهن سان رحم نه ڪندڙ
antonyms: Kind, Gentle, Merciful, Humane, Compassionate, Mild, Tender
englishMeaning: Extremely cruel, violent, or harsh. Without mercy or pity. Direct and unpleasant in a way that may hurt others' feelings. Used to describe people, actions, conditions, or experiences that involve severe physical or emotional harm. Can also describe weather, criticism, or competition that is very difficult to endure.
examples: The dictator was known for his brutal treatment of opponents. They survived a brutal winter in the mountains. He gave her a brutal but honest answer. The match was a brutal contest from start to finish. Brutal attacks on civilians shocked the world.
urduMeaning: ظالم، سفاک، بے رحم، سخت، بے درد، تشدد آمیز، انتہائی سخت، انسانی ہمدردی سے خالی، تکلیف دہ، کسی پر رحم نہ کرنے والا

synonyms: Cruelty, Savagery, Ruthlessness, Inhumanity, Barbarity, Viciousness, Harshness
sindhiMeaning: ظلم، سفاڪي، بي رحمي، تشدد، ڪرڙائي، انساني همدرديءَ کان خالي عمل، ڏاڍايون، ايذائيندڙ سلوڪ، خاص ڪري طاقتور ماڻهن يا ادارن طرفان ظلم
englishMeaning: Cruel, violent, and harsh treatment of others. The quality of being brutal. Acts of physical or emotional cruelty, often performed without mercy. Used to describe the behavior of individuals, groups, regimes, or systems that inflict severe suffering. Often appears in discussions of war, crime, oppression, and human rights abuses.
antonyms: Kindness, Mercy, Compassion, Humanity, Gentleness, Tenderness
examples: The world condemned the brutality of the regime. Witnesses described the brutality of the attack in shocking detail. Police brutality became a major issue in the country. The novel exposes the brutality of war on ordinary people. Such brutality has no justification under any circumstances.
urduMeaning: ظلم، سفاکی، بے رحمی، تشدد، سختی، انسانی ہمدردی سے خالی عمل، زیادتیاں، تکلیف دہ سلوک، خاص طور پر طاقتور لوگوں یا اداروں کی جانب سے ظلم
وزن، حجم، مقدار، کسی چیز کا بڑا حصہ، اکثریت، تھوک، تھوک میں خریدنا یا بیچنا، کسی چیز کو بڑا ظاہر کرنا، کسی بڑی مقدار کی چیز
synonyms: Mass, Volume, Size, Majority, Greater part, Quantity, Weight, Body
sindhiMeaning: وزن، حجم، ماپ، ڪنهن شيءِ جو وڏو حصو، اڪثريت، گهڻائي، ٿوڪ ۾ خريد ڪرڻ يا وڪڻڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ کي وڏو ڏيکارڻ، ڪنهن وڏي مقدار جي شيءِ
antonyms: Minority, Small amount, Fraction, Bit, Portion, Fragment
examples: The bulk of the work has already been completed. The company buys rice in bulk to save money. The huge bulk of the ship appeared on the horizon. Most of the bulk of his fortune was donated to charity. Heavy clothes can bulk up your appearance in winter.
englishMeaning: The mass, size, or volume of something, especially when large. The greater or main part of something. Large quantity, as in buying or selling in bulk. To make something appear larger or more important than it is. Used in commerce, science, and everyday speech to describe quantity or physical mass, and also figuratively for the major share of a group or thing.

examples: The news bulletin announced the prime minister’s visit. The hospital issued a daily bulletin about the patient’s condition. Students receive a weekly bulletin from the university. A special bulletin was broadcast after the earthquake. The company publishes a monthly bulletin for its employees.
urduMeaning: مختصر سرکاری اطلاع، تازہ خبر، اعلان نامہ، خبرنامہ، نشریہ، ادارے کی جانب سے جاری کردہ مختصر رپورٹ، ریڈیو یا ٹی وی پر پیش کی جانے والی تازہ خبروں کا خلاصہ، کسی اہم معاملے سے متعلق سرکاری اعلان
sindhiMeaning: مختصر سرڪاري اطلاع، تازي خبر، اعلان نامو، خبرنامو، نشريو، اداري طرفان جاري ٿيل مختصر رپورٽ، ريڊيو يا ٽي وي تي پيش ڪيل تازي خبرن جو خلاصو، ڪنهن اهم معاملي بابت سرڪاري اعلان
englishMeaning: A short official statement or broadcast giving the latest news or information. A regular printed report or newsletter issued by an organization, institution, or group. A brief news item announced on radio, television, or other media to inform the public about current events. An official announcement made by an authority concerning an important matter such as health, security, or weather.
synonyms: Announcement, Report, Statement, Notice, Communiqué, Newsletter, Briefing, Dispatch, News flash
antonyms: Concealment, Suppression, Silence, Secret, Withholding
Truth, Sense, Wisdom, Reality, Attend, Appear
synonyms: Berth, Cot, Bed, Nonsense, Rubbish, Hogwash, Drivel, Skip, Truant
urduMeaning: تنگ بستر، دیوار سے لگا ہوا پلنگ، جہاز یا ریل گاڑی میں سونے کی جگہ، فضول بات، بے معنی یا بیہودہ گفتگو، اسکول یا کام سے غیر حاضر ہونا، چھپ کر بھاگ جانا
sindhiMeaning: تنگ بستر، ڀت سان لڳل پلنگ، جهاز يا ريل گاڏي ۾ سمهڻ جي جاءِ، بيوقوفي ڀري ڳالهه، بيڪار يا اجائي بڪواس، اسڪول يا ڪم تان غير حاضر رهڻ، لِڪي وڃڻ
englishMeaning: A narrow bed, especially one built like a shelf into a wall, on a ship, train, or in a dormitory. Foolish, insincere, or nonsensical talk; humbug. To sleep in a bunk or to occupy a sleeping place for the night. (Informal) To run away from school, duty, or an obligation without permission.
examples: The children climbed into their bunks and fell asleep. Don’t talk such bunk; nobody believes you. The sailors bunked together below deck. He decided to bunk school and go to the cinema. We had to bunk down in the office during the storm.

englishMeaning: A reinforced underground shelter, typically used in wartime to protect people from bombs, shells, or other attacks. A large container or compartment for storing fuel, coal, or other materials, especially on a ship. A sand-filled hollow or hazard on a golf course. To place fuel or supplies in a bunker, or to find oneself in a difficult and seemingly hopeless situation.
examples: The soldiers took cover in the underground bunker. The ship’s fuel bunker was filled before the long voyage. His golf ball landed in the bunker near the green. During the air raid, families rushed into the nearest bunker. The general directed the operation from his command bunker.
antonyms: Open ground, Exposed area, Surface
urduMeaning: زمین دوز پناہ گاہ، جنگ کے دوران تحفظ کے لیے بنائی گئی خفیہ جگہ، ایندھن یا کوئلے کا بڑا ذخیرہ خانہ، جہاز میں ایندھن رکھنے کی جگہ، گالف کے میدان میں ریت سے بھرا گڑھا، مشکل صورتِ حال میں پھنس جانا
sindhiMeaning: زمين دوز پناهه گاهه، جنگي محاذ تي تحفظ لاءِ ٺاهيل خفيه جاءِ، ٻارڻ يا ڪوئلي جو وڏو ذخيرو ڪرڻ وارو خانو، جهاز ۾ ٻارڻ رکڻ جي جاءِ، گالف جي ميدان ۾ واريءَ سان ڀريل کڏ، ڏکيءَ صورتحال ۾ ڦاسي وڃڻ
synonyms: Shelter, Dugout, Refuge, Hideout, Stronghold, Bin, Container

examples: The minister’s speech was full of bunkum and empty promises. Don’t believe everything he says — most of it is bunkum. Voters are tired of political bunkum before every election. She dismissed the rumours as utter bunkum. His explanation sounded like complete bunkum to the experts.
sindhiMeaning: بيوقوفيءَ ڀري ڳالهه، فضول بڪواس، بي معنيٰ تقرير، اجائي ۽ نمائشي گفتگو، خاص ڪري سياستدانن جي عوام کي خوش ڪرڻ واري ڳالهه، ٺلهي ۽ بي بنياد ڳالهه
antonyms: Truth, Sense, Fact, Wisdom, Sincerity, Reality
synonyms: Nonsense, Rubbish, Drivel, Humbug, Twaddle, Claptrap, Balderdash, Hogwash
englishMeaning: Insincere or foolish talk; nonsense. Empty or pretentious speech, especially that made by politicians to please an audience rather than to convey real meaning. Words that sound impressive but actually contain no truth, sense, or value. A statement intended to deceive or flatter rather than to inform.
urduMeaning: فضول بات، بے معنی گفتگو، بے ہودہ تقریر، خالی اور نمائشی باتیں، خاص طور پر سیاستدانوں کی عوام کو خوش کرنے والی باتیں، کھوکھلی اور بے بنیاد گفتگو

examples: The buoyancy of the boat kept it afloat in rough seas. Salt water increases the buoyancy of swimmers. Despite many setbacks, she maintained her natural buoyancy of spirit. The buoyancy of the housing market surprised the analysts. Children show a remarkable buoyancy after disappointment.
englishMeaning: The ability or tendency of an object to float in a liquid or gas. The upward force exerted by a fluid that opposes the weight of an immersed object. A cheerful, optimistic, and resilient quality of mind that allows a person to recover quickly from difficulties. The ability of an economy, market, or price to rise or recover quickly after a fall.
synonyms: Floatation, Lightness, Cheerfulness, Optimism, Resilience, Liveliness, Vivacity

englishMeaning: A homogeneous, non-crystalline substance consisting of large molecules or ultramicroscopic particles of one substance dispersed through a second substance. Colloids include gels, sols, and emulsions; the particles do not settle and cannot be separated by ordinary filtering or centrifuging. In a colloidal system, the dispersed phase is spread evenly throughout the continuous phase. The particles in a colloid are larger than molecules but small enough that they remain suspended rather than settling out. Colloids are very common in everyday life and include materials like milk, fog, and paint. The stability of colloids is often due to the electrostatic repulsion between the dispersed particles. Many biological fluids, such as blood, are colloidal suspensions.

englishMeaning: To become unusable through long use. To make someone extremely tired. To exhaust completely. To use something until it is no longer effective. examples: My old shoes have finally worn out after years of use. Looking after three small children wears her out by the evening. The long journey wore the travellers out completely. The carpet in the hallway has worn out in several places. Constant night shifts can wear a person out very quickly.

synonyms: Erode, Grind down, Reduce, Weaken, Exhaust, Break down, Diminish, Overcome

Remain, Endure, Last, Persist, Be preserved, Stay intact
englishMeaning: To slowly disappear or be removed through constant rubbing or use. To gradually erode. To be reduced little by little over a long period. To fade through time. synonyms: Erode, Fade, Vanish, Diminish, Wash away, Crumble, Disappear, Decay

englishMeaning: In golf, "dormie" is a term used to describe a situation in match play where a player or team is leading by as many holes as there are holes remaining to be played. For example, if there are three holes left and a player is up by three holes, they are dormie. This means the leading player cannot lose the match, as their opponent would need to win all remaining holes just to tie. The leading player only needs to halve one more hole to win the match outright. Essentially, being dormie signifies that the leading player has secured at least a tie, and often the win, barring any exceptional comebacks.
examples: After sinking a crucial putt on the 15th hole, she was dormie, leading by three holes with only three to play. The tension mounted as the underdog found himself dormie with only two holes remaining, needing to win both to tie. The commentator announced that the favorite player was dormie, making his victory almost certain. Despite being dormie, he played cautiously, not wanting to give his opponent any chance of a comeback.

englishMeaning: Dormin is a plant hormone, also known as abscisic acid, that plays a crucial role in plant growth and development. It is primarily involved in regulating stress responses, such as drought and cold tolerance. Dormin also promotes dormancy in seeds and buds, ensuring their survival during unfavorable conditions. Furthermore, it influences processes like leaf senescence and fruit ripening. Its multifaceted functions make it a vital regulator in the plant kingdom.
examples: Scientists are studying dormin to understand its role in drought resistance. The application of dormin can induce dormancy in plant seeds. Dormin levels in the plant increase significantly under stress conditions. The discovery of dormin has revolutionized our understanding of plant growth. Farmers sometimes use synthetic dormin to control crop development.

urduMeaning: امراضِ نسواں کا علم، عورتوں کی بیماریوں کا علم، خواتین کے تولیدی نظام کی صحت کا شعبہ، طب کی وہ شاخ جس میں عورتوں کا علاج ہوتا ہے، گائناکالوجی

sindhiMeaning: عورتن جي بيمارين جو علم، امراضِ نسواں، عورتن جي توليدي نظام جي صحت جو شعبو، طب جي اها شاخ جنهن ۾ عورتن جي بيمارين جو علاج ٿئي، گائناڪالاجي

The phrase can also imply a sudden, forceful departure from something.

The children love to jump around in the bouncy castle. He tends to jump around from topic to topic during his presentations. When the music started, everyone began to jump around energetically. synonyms: Begin, Start, Commence, Undertake, Embark, Initiate, Plunge, Dive, Jump, Erupt

examples: The opposition party decided to launch against the government's new policies. They plan to launch a full-scale legal challenge against the company. The politician used his speech to launch on a scathing critique of his opponent's policies. We are excited to launch on this journey of discovery together. englishMeaning: To plunge headfirst into water or to descend rapidly. It can also refer to an act of sudden and deep involvement in an activity or situation. Figuratively, it implies intense focus or a quick, often downwards, movement in price or value.
antonyms: Ascend, Rise, Emerge, Surface, Float, Climb, Soar
sindhiMeaning: غوطه هڻڻ، پاڻي ۾ ٽپو ڏيڻ، لوڏو کائڻ، هيٺ لهڻ، اونهو وڃڻ، ڪنهن ڪم ۾ پاڻ کي ڦاسائڻ، اندر گهڙڻ، ٽوپو هڻڻ، ترڻ، غريق ٿيڻ، تيزي سان گهٽجڻ
examples: She decided to dive into the ocean despite the cold water. The stock market took a dive after the unexpected news. He watched the pelican dive for fish. We need to dive deeper into the data to find the root cause. The swimmer prepared to dive off the high board.
urduMeaning: غوطہ لگانا، پانی میں چھلانگ لگانا، ڈبکی لگانا، تیزی سے نیچے اترنا، سر کے بل کودنا، کسی کام میں پوری طرح شامل ہونا، اندر گھسنا، قیمت کا تیزی سے گرنا، گہرائی میں جانا

examples: When the project was announced, she was eager to dive in and take on the most challenging tasks. The children couldn't wait to dive in to the swimming pool on such a hot day. Don't be afraid to dive in; the water's fine once you get used to it. After a long discussion, everyone was ready to dive in and implement the new strategy. Let's not overthink it, just dive in and see what happens.
sindhiMeaning: شروعات ڪرڻ، اندر ٽپو ڏيڻ، پاڻي ۾ ٽپڻ، پاڻ کي ڪنهن ڪم ۾ مشغول ڪرڻ، پرجوش ٿي شروع ڪرڻ، ڪم ۾ گهڙي پوڻ، ڪنهن نئين سرگرمي يا منصوبي ۾ چستيءَ سان شامل ٿيڻ، دل سان ڪم ڪرڻ
synonyms: Engage, Plunge, Immerse, Commence, Undertake, Participate, Embark, Tackle, Start, Begin
urduMeaning: شروع کرنا، سرگرمی سے حصہ لینا، پانی میں غوطہ لگانا، بھرپور انداز میں مشغول ہونا، جوش و خروش سے آغاز کرنا، کسی کام میں لگ جانا، نیا پروجیکٹ شروع کرنا، دل و جان سے کسی کام میں کود پڑنا
englishMeaning: To 'dive in' means to enthusiastically and fully immerse oneself in an activity or task, often without hesitation. It implies a readiness to start something with vigor and commitment. It can also literally refer to jumping into water, but its more common idiomatic use is about beginning a new project or challenge with great enthusiasm and energy.
antonyms: Withdraw, Retreat, Hesitate, Abstain, Disengage, Postpone, Avoid, Shy away
Avoid, Neglect, Skim Over, Withdraw From, Hold Back, Disengage, Procrastinate
synonyms: Plunge Into, Immerse Oneself, Delve Into, Engage In, Get Stuck Into, Become Absorbed, Undertake Enthusiastically, Embark On, Tackle Vigorously, Commit Fully
urduMeaning: مکمل طور پر کسی چیز میں شامل ہونا، گہرائی میں اترنا، لگ جانا، بہت زیادہ دھیان دینا، پوری دل سے کام کرنا، گہرا مطالعہ کرنا، کسی کام میں خود کو پوری طرح مشغول کرنا، جوش و خروش سے کسی کام کا آغاز کرنا، پوری طرح سے لگ جانا، کامل مشغولیت
examples: She decided to dive into learning a new language during her sabbatical. He dove into the project with such enthusiasm that he forgot about the time. Let's dive into the details of the financial report. The students were encouraged to dive into the research topic. He will dive into the role with his characteristic passion.
englishMeaning: To fully immerse oneself into an activity or subject with great enthusiasm and focus. This idiom suggests a profound engagement, often implying a quick and deep involvement rather than a gradual approach. It can also mean to begin a task or exploration with intensity and commitment.
sindhiMeaning: مڪمل طور تي پاڻ کي ڪنهن شيءِ ۾ شامل ڪرڻ، گهاڙهو ٿيڻ، لڳي پيئڻ، گهڻو ڌيان ڏيڻ، پوري دل سان ڪم ڪرڻ، اونهو اڀياس ڪرڻ، ڪنهن ڪم ۾ پاڻ کي لوڙهي ڇڏڻ، جوش سان ڪنهن ڪم ۾ شامل ٿيڻ يا شروع ڪرڻ، پوري طرح لڳي وڃڻ، مڪمل طور تي وٺي ويهڻ

synonyms: Re-engage, Resume, Rejoin, Recommence, Return to, Get back into, Pick up again, Plunge back into, Immerse oneself again in
antonyms: Withdraw from, Discontinue, Abandon, Quit, Stop, Detach from, Give up
sindhiMeaning: وري مڙڻ، وري شامل ٿيڻ، وري شروع ڪرڻ، وري واپس وڃڻ، ٻيهر دلچسپي وٺڻ، ٻيهر هٿ وجهڻ، پوئتي موٽڻ، نئين سر شروع ڪرڻ، وري ان ۾ لڳي پوڻ، اڳ وانگر شروع ڪرڻ
englishMeaning: To re-engage with something after a period of absence or a break. It implies a renewed and often enthusiastic return to an activity, task, or situation. This phrase suggests picking up where one left off, often with a sense of excitement or dedication.
urduMeaning: دوبارہ کسی کام میں شامل ہونا، دوبارہ کسی چیز کی طرف لوٹنا، نئی سرے سے آغاز کرنا، پھر سے دلچسپی لینا، کسی کام میں دوبارہ لگنا، واپس جانا، از سر نو شروع کرنا، کسی سرگرمی میں دوبارہ مصروف ہونا، اس میں پھر سے شامل ہو جانا
examples: After a long vacation, I'm ready to dive back into my work. She took a break from painting, but now she's eager to dive back into her art. Even after a minor setback, he was determined to dive back into his studies. Let's dive back into the discussion where we left off. The team is excited to dive back into training after their win.

englishMeaning: To plunge suddenly from a height into water, usually headfirst. This action implies a deliberate and often vigorous descent, distinguishing it from merely falling into water. It can also metaphorically refer to a sudden and rapid decrease or fall in some quantity or value.
synonyms: Plunge, Jump, Leap, Spring, Dive, Descend, Drop, Submerge, Immense
antonyms: Ascend, Rise, Emerge, Float, Clamber Up, Scale
sindhiMeaning: پاڻي ۾ ٽپو ڏيڻ، اونچائي تان پاڻي ۾ ٽپي پوڻ، ٽوپي ڏيڻ، لوڙهڻ، لاهڻ، گهڙڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ جو اوچتو گهٽجڻ، هيٺ ڪرڻ، ڳوڙهڻ
examples: She decided to dive off the high cliff into the clear blue ocean. The children loved to dive off the side of the swimming pool. He watched the stock prices dive off after the announcement. The birds would dive off the branches to catch fish. Be careful when you dive off that unstable platform.
urduMeaning: پانی میں چھلانگ لگانا، اونچائی سے پانی میں کودنا، غوطہ لگانا، ڈبکی لگانا، تیزی سے نیچے آنا، کسی چیز کا اچانک کم ہونا، تیزی سے کمی آنا

synonyms: Plunge, Submerge, Descend, Dip, Duck, Plunge In, Fathom, Delve, Probe, Explore
antonyms: Ascend, Emerge, Surface, Rise, Float, Climb Up
examples: The submarine prepared to dive down to the ocean floor. The reporter decided to dive down into the archives to find more information. We watched the pelican dive down to catch a fish. Let's dive down into the details of this proposal. The engineers will dive down into the system's code to find the bug.
englishMeaning: To descend quickly or plunge headfirst into water or another medium. It can also metaphorically mean to delve deeply into a topic or investigate something thoroughly. This phrasal verb often implies a rapid and focused movement either physically or intellectually.
sindhiMeaning: هيٺ لهڻ، هيٺ ترڻ، گهاٽائي پيدا ڪرڻ، ڳُنهن ۾ لهڻ، گَهُرائي ۾ ترڻ، جانچڻ، تفصيل ۾ وڃڻ، ڌيان سان ڳولڻ، غور ڪرڻ، ڳوڙهائي سان ڇانڻ، اونهائي ۾ لهڻ
urduMeaning: نیچے اترنا، غوطہ لگانا، ڈوب جانا، گہرائی میں جانا، کسی موضوع کی تہہ تک پہنچنا، تفصیل سے جانچنا، تحقیق کرنا، گہرائی میں اترنا، باریکی سے جائزہ لینا، غور کرنا

examples: The children loved to dive under the waves at the beach. He had to dive under the table to escape the falling debris. The submarine can dive under the polar ice cap. She would often dive under her blanket when she heard strange noises. The swimmer quickly dove under the surface to retrieve the lost item.
englishMeaning: To go beneath the surface of water or another medium. It implies a deliberate and often quick movement to submerge oneself or something. The phrase can be used literally for swimming or figuratively for escaping a situation or hiding from view.
sindhiMeaning: پاڻي هيٺ وڃڻ، لڪڻ، ٽوپي هڻڻ، غوطو هڻڻ، پاڻي ۾ هيٺ وڃڻ، هيٺ لڪڻ، ڦاڙيون کڻڻ، غائب ٿيڻ، لڪي وڃڻ، مٿي کان هيٺ گهڙڻ
synonyms: Submerge, Plunge, Dip, Descend, Go Under, Sink, Immerse, Duck, Penetrate, Snoop
urduMeaning: پانی کے نیچے جانا، غوطہ لگانا، چھپ جانا، ڈبکی لگانا، زیر آب جانا، غائب ہو جانا، نظروں سے اوجھل ہونا، چھپنے کے لیے نیچے جانا
antonyms: Emerge, Surface, Rise, Float, Ascend, Appear, Come Up

urduMeaning: غوطہ لگانا، میں سے گزرنا، چھلانگ لگانا، تیزی سے پار کرنا، اندر جانا، تیزی سے عبور کرنا، ڈوب کر گزرنا، تیراکی کرتے ہوئے نکلنا، کسی چیز میں سے گزرنا، تحقیق کرنا
examples: The submarine was able to dive through the narrow underwater passage. We had to dive through a pile of old documents to find the key report. The swimmer will dive through the ring of fire as part of the stunt. Scientists often dive through vast amounts of data to uncover new patterns in research. The small boat managed to dive through the crashing waves during the storm.
sindhiMeaning: گھڙي وڃڻ، ترسڻ، تيزي سان پار ڪرڻ، ڇوڙي نڪرڻ، ويهڻ، گوتا کوڙڻ، تري وڃڻ، تري نڪرڻ، وچان لنگھڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ مان گذرڻ، ڍُڪي وڃڻ
synonyms: Plunge Through, Submerge Through, Immense Through, Penetrate Through, Pass Through, Go Through, Navigate Through, Traverse Through, Burrow Through, Pierce Through
englishMeaning: To dive through something means to quickly move or pass through an opening, a body of water, or an obstacle. It often implies a swift, immersive, or even challenging passage. This phrase can be used literally, referring to plunging into water, or metaphorically, indicating a rapid progression through information or a difficult situation.
antonyms: Avoid, Bypass, Circumnavigate, Detour, Skirt, Emerge From, Withdraw From

sindhiMeaning: اکر اچارڻ، لفظ جا اکر ترتيب سان چوڻ يا لکڻ، حرف بحرف ٻڌائڻ، ڪنهن ڳالهه جو سبب ٿيڻ، نشاندهي ڪرڻ، اشارو ڏيڻ، ڪنهن نتيجي جو سبب بڻجڻ، ٿوري عرصي جو دور، وقفو، مدت، جادو، منتر، ٽوڻو، ڪشش، موهه
examples: Can you spell your full name for the registration form? The dark clouds spell trouble for our picnic plans. She had a brief spell of dizziness after standing up too quickly. The wizard cast a spell to protect the village from harm. He worked at the company for a long spell before moving abroad.
urduMeaning: ہجے کرنا، کسی لفظ کے حروف کو ترتیب سے کہنا یا لکھنا، حرف بحرف بتانا، کسی بات کی نشاندہی کرنا، اشارہ دینا، کسی نتیجے کا سبب بننا، تھوڑے عرصے کا دورانیہ، وقفہ، مدت، جادو، منتر، ٹونا، کشش، سحر
antonyms: Misspell, Confuse, Obscure, Hide, Continuity, Permanence
englishMeaning: To say or write the letters of a word in correct order. To form a word with letters in proper sequence. To signify or indicate something, especially something bad. To bring about a particular result. To be a sign of something that is going to happen. A short period of time during which something lasts. A continuous course or period of an activity. A state of being under a magical influence. Words supposed to have magical power. A strong attraction or fascination that someone or something has.
synonyms: Indicate, Signify, Mean, Denote, Suggest, Period, Interval, Stretch, Charm, Incantation, Bewitchment

sindhiMeaning: تفصيل سان سمجهائڻ، چٽو ڪري ٻڌائڻ، هڪ هڪ اکر ٻڌائڻ، صاف لفظن ۾ بيان ڪرڻ، واضح ڪرڻ، تفصيل سان سمجهائي ڏيڻ، چٽائي سان بيان ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: تفصیل سے واضح کرنا، صاف لفظوں میں بیان کرنا، حرف بہ حرف بتانا، ایک ایک بات کھول کر بیان کرنا، تفصیل سے سمجھانا، ہر بات کھول کر بیان کرنا، واضح طور پر بتانا
synonyms: Clarify, Explain, Detail, Specify, Elaborate, Make clear, State, Define
englishMeaning: To explain something clearly and in detail so that there is no doubt about the meaning. To say or write the letters of a word one by one. To make something completely clear and easy to understand. To state precisely what is required or expected. To describe in a thorough and step-by-step manner.
antonyms: Confuse, Obscure, Hide, Conceal, Imply, Hint, Suggest
examples: The teacher asked the student to spell out the difficult word slowly. The manager spelled out the new policy in detail during the meeting. I had to spell out exactly what I expected from the team. The contract spells out the duties of both parties. She spelled out the reasons behind her decision in a long letter.

sindhiMeaning: حق ڇڏڻ جو دستاويز، ڪنهن حق يا دعويٰ کان دستبرداري جو رسمي اعلان، حق کان هٿ کڻڻ جو لکت ۾ اقرار، رعايتي اجازت نامو، استثنيٰ، ڪنهن قاعدي يا شرط کان معافي
synonyms: Relinquishment, Renunciation, Surrender, Exemption, Dispensation, Concession, Release
antonyms: Claim, Insistence, Demand, Imposition, Enforcement, Retention
urduMeaning: دستبرداری، کسی حق یا دعوے سے دستبرداری کا تحریری بیان، اپنے کسی قانونی حق سے رضاکارانہ دستبرداری، کسی قاعدے یا شرط سے استثنیٰ کا رسمی اجازت نامہ، چھوٹ، رعایت
examples: All players had to sign a waiver before participating in the tournament. The university granted him a tuition fee waiver due to his financial situation. She signed a waiver giving up her right to sue the company. The bank offered a waiver of late payment charges this month. Visitors must sign a waiver before entering the adventure park.
englishMeaning: An official statement saying that a right or claim has been given up. A document showing that someone has agreed to give up a legal right. The act of giving up a right, claim, or privilege voluntarily. A formal written agreement of surrender of a right. Permission to ignore or break a rule in a particular case.

synonyms: Relinquish, Surrender, Forgo, Renounce, Give up, Abandon, Forfeit
antonyms: Claim, Demand, Insist, Enforce, Impose, Retain
examples: The judge agreed to waive the court fee for the poor applicant. The company decided to waive the joining fee for new members. He waived his right to remain silent and answered every question. The university waived the entrance test for top students. The hotel waived the cancellation charges as a gesture of goodwill.
englishMeaning: To voluntarily give up a right, claim, or privilege. To choose not to insist on something one is entitled to. To officially decide not to apply a rule or charge. To refrain from enforcing a regulation. To set aside or postpone the use of a right.
sindhiMeaning: حق ڇڏڻ، ڪنهن حق يا دعويٰ کان دستبردار ٿيڻ، رعايت ڏيڻ، ڪنهن قاعدي يا شرط کي معاف ڪرڻ، ڪنهن چارج يا فيس کان معافي ڏيڻ، نظرانداز ڪرڻ

examples: The groom looked very handsome in his traditional wedding outfit. She spends an hour every morning to groom her long hair carefully. The manager is grooming his assistant to take over the department. The trainer groomed the horse before the race. Parents groom their children to face the challenges of life.
urduMeaning: دولہا، شادی کرنے والا مرد، گھوڑوں کی دیکھ بھال کرنے والا شخص، سائیس، جانوروں خاص طور پر گھوڑوں کو صاف اور سنوارنا، کسی کو کسی خاص کام یا عہدے کے لیے تیار کرنا، تربیت دینا، سنوارنا، آراستہ کرنا
sindhiMeaning: گهوٽ، شادي ڪندڙ مرد، ماڻهو جيڪو گهوڙن جي سار سنڀال ڪري، گهوڙن جو نوڪر، جانورن کي صاف ڪرڻ ۽ سنوارڻ، ڪنهن کي ڪنهن خاص ڪم لاءِ تيار ڪرڻ، تربيت ڏيڻ، سنوارڻ، ٺاهڻ، تيار ڪرڻ
synonyms: Bridegroom, Train, Prepare, Tidy, Brush, Coach, Mentor, Tutor, Smarten
antonyms: Bride, Neglect, Disregard, Ignore, Untidy, Dishevel
englishMeaning: A man on his wedding day or just before and after the event. A person who looks after horses, especially in a stable. To brush and clean an animal, especially a horse. To prepare or train someone for a particular role, position, or job. To make oneself neat and tidy in appearance. To carefully prepare someone over time for a future responsibility.

sindhiMeaning: ڪنوار، شادي ڪندڙ عورت، نئين شادي ٿيل عورت، گهوٽ جي گهرواري، شادي جي ڏينهن واري عورت
examples: The bride wore a beautiful red dress on her wedding day. Everyone praised the bride for her grace and elegance. The bride and groom cut the wedding cake together. The bride was escorted to the stage by her father. Photographs of the bride were taken before the ceremony began.
