urduMeaning: دلہن، شادی کرنے والی عورت، نئی شادی شدہ عورت، دولہا کی شریکِ حیات، شادی کے دن کی عورت
synonyms: Wife-to-be, Newlywed, Spouse, Fiancée
englishMeaning: A woman on her wedding day or just before and after the event. A woman who is about to get married or has just got married. A female partner in a marriage ceremony. The female counterpart of the groom in a wedding.

examples: She looked stunning in her white bridal gown. The bridal shop has a wide collection of wedding dresses. The bridal suite was beautifully decorated with flowers. The bridal procession moved slowly toward the venue. Her bridal jewellery was passed down from her grandmother.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنوار سان لاڳاپيل، شادي سان لاڳاپيل، شاديءَ جو، ڪنوار جو، شاديءَ جي تقريب سان واسطو رکندڙ، ڪنوار جي استعمال جو
antonyms: Single, Unwed, Divorced
englishMeaning: Relating to a bride or a wedding. Belonging to or used by a bride. Connected with the ceremony or celebration of marriage. Suitable for a wedding. Associated with the period around a wedding.
urduMeaning: دلہن سے متعلق، شادی سے متعلق، شادی کا، دلہن کا، شادی کی تقریب سے تعلق رکھنے والا، دلہن کے استعمال کا
synonyms: Wedding, Nuptial, Marital, Matrimonial, Conjugal

urduMeaning: غلط، خطا پر مبنی، نادرست، غلط معلومات پر مبنی، حقیقت کے خلاف، خامی والا، درست نہیں، فکری غلطی والا
examples: The report was based on erroneous data and had to be revised. He held an erroneous belief about the company's financial position. Her erroneous assumptions led to a wrong conclusion. The newspaper apologized for publishing erroneous information. Erroneous calculations caused a major loss to the firm.
englishMeaning: Wrong or based on incorrect information. Containing or characterized by error. Mistaken in judgement or opinion. Not accurate or correct. Resulting from a mistake or a faulty assumption.
antonyms: Correct, Accurate, Right, True, Valid, Precise
sindhiMeaning: غلط، ڀُل وارو، نادرست، حقيقت کان پري، خاميءَ تي ٻڌل، غلط معلومات تي مبني، صحيح نه، ڀُل ٿيل
synonyms: Incorrect, Wrong, Inaccurate, Mistaken, False, Faulty, Flawed, Untrue

examples: Smoking in public places contravenes the new health regulations. His actions contravene the terms of the contract. The new policy contravenes basic human rights. Building without permission contravenes municipal laws. Their statement contravenes the official version of events.
urduMeaning: قانون یا قاعدے کی خلاف ورزی کرنا، حکم یا معاہدے کے خلاف عمل کرنا، مخالفت کرنا، رد کرنا، اصول کے برعکس چلنا، انکار کرنا
synonyms: Violate, Breach, Break, Infringe, Defy, Disobey, Oppose, Contradict
antonyms: Obey, Comply, Follow, Observe, Uphold, Respect, Support
englishMeaning: To act against an established law, rule, or agreement. To violate a regulation or order. To go against or be in conflict with something. To deny the truth of a statement. To oppose or contradict openly.
sindhiMeaning: قانون يا قاعدي جي ڀڃڪڙي ڪرڻ، خلاف ورزي ڪرڻ، حڪم يا معاهدي جي خلاف عمل ڪرڻ، مخالفت ڪرڻ، رد ڪرڻ، انڪار ڪرڻ، اصول جي ابتڙ هلڻ

synonyms: Heat-producing, Calorific, Metabolic, Warming, Energy-releasing
urduMeaning: حرارت پیدا کرنے والا، گرمی پیدا کرنے والا، جسم میں حرارت بڑھانے والا، میٹابولزم تیز کرنے والا، حرارت سے متعلق، حرارت ساز

According to legend, Hercules completed twelve impossible labours to prove his strength. The wrestler was so muscular that everyone called him a modern-day Hercules. sindhiMeaning: يوناني ۽ رومن ديو مالا جو هڪ مشهور سورمو جيڪو پنهنجي بي مثال طاقت ۽ بهادريءَ لاءِ مشهور هو، نهايت طاقتور ماڻهو، پهلوان، ديو جهڙو زورآور انسان، اهڙو شخص جيڪو ڏکيا ڪم آسانيءَ سان ڪري سگهي
antonyms: Weakling, Coward, Feeble person
synonyms: Strongman, Titan, Giant, Superman, Hero, Champion, Powerhouse
urduMeaning: یونانی اور رومی دیومالا کا ایک مشہور سورما جو اپنی غیر معمولی طاقت اور بہادری کے لیے جانا جاتا ہے، نہایت طاقتور شخص، پہلوان، دیو جیسا زبردست انسان، ایسا شخص جو مشکل ترین کام آسانی سے کر لے
englishMeaning: A hero of ancient Greek and Roman mythology famous for his extraordinary physical strength and courage. The son of the god Jupiter (Zeus) and a mortal woman, known for performing twelve nearly impossible tasks called the Labours of Hercules. Figuratively, a person of unusual strength, power, or great achievement. The name is often used to describe anyone who is exceptionally strong or who completes very difficult work.

antonyms: Acquired, Learned, Earned, Non-hereditary, Environmental
synonyms: Inherited, Genetic, Inborn, Innate, Ancestral, Family, Inheritable, Transmitted
englishMeaning: Passed down from parents to children through the genes. Relating to qualities, diseases, or features that are inherited biologically from one's ancestors. Also used for titles, positions, or property that are passed from one generation to the next by right of birth rather than by choice or election. Anything that is transmitted by inheritance, whether physical, social, or legal.
urduMeaning: موروثی، آبائی، نسل در نسل منتقل ہونے والا، والدین سے اولاد کو ملنے والا، خاندانی، وراثت میں ملنے والا، ایسی چیز یا خصوصیت جو باپ دادا سے اولاد کو منتقل ہو، خاندانی سلسلے میں چلنے والا
sindhiMeaning: وراثتي، ابن جدي، نسل در نسل ملندڙ، ماءُ پيءُ کان اولاد ڏانهن منتقل ٿيندڙ، خانداني، ورثي ۾ ملندڙ، اهڙي شيءِ يا خصوصيت جيڪا پيءُ ڏاڏي کان اولاد کي ملي، خانداني سلسلي ۾ هلندڙ
examples: Diabetes can sometimes be a hereditary disease that runs in families. The king's throne was hereditary and passed to his eldest son. Eye colour and height are largely hereditary traits. He inherited the hereditary title of lord from his late father. Doctors believe that certain types of cancer have a hereditary link.

urduMeaning: وراثت، موروثیت، نسل در نسل خصوصیات کا منتقل ہونا، والدین سے اولاد کو خصوصیات اور خوبیوں کا منتقل ہونا، خاندانی ورثہ، جینیاتی وراثت، آبائی خصوصیات
synonyms: Inheritance, Genetics, Lineage, Ancestry, Descent, Genealogy, Bloodline
antonyms: Environment, Upbringing, Nurture, Acquisition
englishMeaning: The biological process by which physical and mental characteristics are passed from parents to their children through genes. The sum of qualities and traits that a person inherits from their ancestors. The transmission of features such as appearance, intelligence, temperament, and certain diseases from one generation to the next. In a broader sense, the natural inheritance of qualities that shapes an individual's identity.
examples: Scientists study heredity to understand how traits pass from parents to children. Both heredity and environment shape a child's personality. Heredity plays an important role in determining a person's height. Some diseases are caused by heredity rather than by lifestyle. The professor gave an interesting lecture on the laws of heredity.
sindhiMeaning: وراثت، نسل در نسل خصوصيتن جو منتقل ٿيڻ، ماءُ پيءُ کان اولاد ڏانهن صفتن ۽ خاصيتن جو منتقل ٿيڻ، خاندان مان ملندڙ خاصيتون، جينياتي ورثو، ابن جدي خصوصيتون

synonyms: Bisexual, Androgynous, Intersex, Dual-sexed, Gynandromorphic
antonyms: Unisexual, Single-sexed, Male, Female
urduMeaning: دو جنسی، نر مادہ، ایسا جاندار یا پودا جس میں نر اور مادہ دونوں کی خصوصیات موجود ہوں، دونوں اصناف کی خصوصیات رکھنے والا، مخنث، ایسا جسم جس میں دونوں جنسوں کے اعضا موجود ہوں
englishMeaning: Having both male and female reproductive organs in the same individual. Relating to an organism, plant, or animal that possesses characteristics of both sexes. In biology, used to describe species in which a single individual can produce both eggs and sperm. Figuratively, it may describe something that combines two opposing qualities or natures.
sindhiMeaning: ٻنهي جنسن وارو، نر مادي، اهڙو جاندار يا ٻوٽو جنهن ۾ نر ۽ ماديءَ ٻنهي جون خاصيتون موجود هجن، ٻنهي صنفن جون خاصيتون رکندڙ، خنثي، اهڙو جسم جنهن ۾ ٻنهي جنسن جا اعضاءَ هجن
examples: Earthworms are hermaphroditic creatures that have both male and female organs. Many flowering plants are hermaphroditic in nature. The biologist explained how hermaphroditic species reproduce. Some species of fish are hermaphroditic and can change their sex when needed. The painting showed a strange hermaphroditic figure standing in the moonlight.

englishMeaning: To cut or chop something, especially wood or stone, with heavy blows using an axe, sword, or other sharp tool. To shape, form, or carve something by cutting. To strike repeatedly to break or fell something. Figuratively, to stick to, conform to, or follow a particular rule, principle, or course strictly.
urduMeaning: کاٹنا، کلہاڑی سے کاٹنا، لکڑی یا پتھر کو کاٹ کر شکل دینا، تراشنا، چھیلنا، گھڑنا، کسی اصول یا راستے پر سختی سے قائم رہنا، پابندی سے عمل کرنا
synonyms: Chop, Cut, Hack, Carve, Shape, Fell, Sculpt, Trim, Cleave
antonyms: Join, Attach, Build, Mend, Connect, Construct
examples: The lumberjacks began to hew the huge oak tree with their sharp axes. He had to hew a path through the thick jungle. The sculptor carefully hewed the statue out of a single block of marble. antonyms: Activity, Wakefulness, Liveliness, Alertness, Action, Animation
synonyms: Dormancy, Sleep, Inactivity, Torpor, Slumber, Rest, Stagnation, Sluggishness
englishMeaning: A state of deep sleep or inactivity in which certain animals spend the winter months in order to survive cold weather and lack of food. During hibernation, the animal's body temperature, heart rate, and breathing slow down to save energy. Figuratively, a period during which a person, activity, or organisation becomes inactive or dormant for a long time.
sindhiMeaning: سياري جي ننڊ، سرديءَ ۾ ڪجهه جانورن جو گهڻي عرصي تائين ننڊ ۾ هليو وڃڻ، خاموش رهڻ جو دور، غير فعال حالت، گهڻي وقت تائين سست يا بيڪار رهڻ جي حالت، سرما خوابي

examples: Bears go into hibernation during the long cold winter months. Frogs and snakes also undergo hibernation to survive freezing temperatures. The company was in hibernation for several years before its sudden revival. After months of hibernation, the political party became active again before the elections. Scientists study how animals slow their heartbeat during hibernation.

antonyms: (No direct antonym)
synonyms: Rosemallow, Shoeflower, China rose, Mallow, Rose of Sharon
sindhiMeaning: گڙهل جو گل، اهڙو ٻوٽو جنهن جا گل وڏا، خوبصورت ۽ گهڻ رنگ هوندا آهن، گرم علائقن جو هڪ زينتي ٻوٽو، گڙهل، گهڻ پنکڙين وارو گل، جوڙي گل

urduMeaning: گڑہل کا پھول، گڑہل کا پودا، ایک گرم خطے کا خوبصورت پودا جس کے پھول بڑے اور رنگین ہوتے ہیں، زینتی پودا جو سرخ  گلابی  پیلے یا سفید پھول دیتا ہے، چائے اور دوا میں استعمال ہونے والا پھول

synonyms: High priest, Bishop, Patriarch, Prelate, Chief, Leader, Dignitary, Ruler

antonyms: Subordinate, Follower, Layman, Underling, Disciple
englishMeaning: A person who holds a high or chief position in a hierarchy, especially in a religious order such as a high priest, bishop, archbishop, or patriarch. A leader who occupies a position of authority over others in any ranked organisation. By extension, any influential or ruling figure in a structured group or institution.
examples: The hierarch led the prayers at the grand cathedral. Each hierarch of the church was invited to the special meeting. Only a senior hierarch had the authority to make such an important decision. The young priest hoped to one day become a hierarch of his order. The hierarchs gathered to elect a new spiritual leader.

antonyms: Help, Aid, Assist, Encourage, Promote, Facilitate, Support, Advance, Speed up

examples: Heavy rain hindered the rescue operation in the flooded village. Lack of funds hindered the progress of the new school project. Do not let fear hinder you from following your dreams. The fallen tree on the road hindered the traffic for hours. Constant interruptions hindered her from completing the report on time.
englishMeaning: To create difficulty or to delay the progress of someone or something. To prevent or obstruct an action, movement, or development. To stand in the way of something happening as quickly or as smoothly as it should. To slow down or interfere with a process, plan, or person. The word is used both physically (blocking the way) and figuratively (obstructing progress or success).

examples: Lack of proper roads is a major hindrance to development in the village. He completed his studies without any hindrance from his family. The bad weather proved to be a serious hindrance to the climbers. Old laws are sometimes a hindrance to economic growth. She refused to be a hindrance to her friend's career.

antonyms: Help, Aid, Assistance, Support, Advantage, Encouragement, Boost
urduMeaning: رکاوٹ، آڑ، روک، خلل، حرج، ایسی چیز یا صورت حال جو کام میں مشکل پیدا کرے، دشواری، آگے بڑھنے میں رکاوٹ، روک ٹوک، بندش
englishMeaning: Something that makes it difficult for someone or something to make progress or to act freely. An obstacle, barrier, or difficulty that delays, prevents, or interferes with an action, plan, or movement. The act of hindering or the state of being hindered. Anything that comes in the way of success, work, or development.

synonyms: Backcountry, Interior, Outback, Countryside, Inland, Backwoods, Remote area, Inner region
englishMeaning: The remote or less developed areas of a country, located away from the coast, major cities, or main rivers. Figuratively, an unknown, unexplored, or undeveloped area of knowledge, experience, or thought.
antonyms: Coast, Seaside, Metropolis, City, Urban area, Downtown, Centre
examples: Karachi serves as the main port for the entire industrial hinterland of Pakistan. The road network in the hinterland needs urgent improvement. examples: During the crisis, many people began to hoard food and water at home. The miser used to hoard every coin he earned. Archaeologists discovered a huge hoard of ancient gold coins. urduMeaning: ذخیرہ کرنا، جمع کرنا، چھپا کر رکھنا، بڑی مقدار میں چیزیں جمع کرنا، خزانہ چھپانا، جمع پونجی اکٹھی کرنا، ذخیرہ، چھپا ہوا خزانہ، جمع کیا ہوا سامان، قیمتی اشیاء چھپا کر رکھنا
englishMeaning: To collect and store away large amounts of money, food, valuable items, or supplies, often secretly and for future use. englishMeaning: A trick or act of deception in which someone makes others believe that something false is true. sindhiMeaning: دوکو، فريب، ٺڳي، جعلي خبر، ٺڳ ٻول، اهڙي ڪوڙي ڳالهه جنهن کي سچ ڪري ٻين کي يقين ڏياريو وڃي، مذاق طور تي ڪيل دوکو، فراڊ، دغا، فريب ڏيڻ، ٺڳڻ
examples: The news about the alien landing turned out to be a complete hoax. He played a cruel hoax on his younger brother. The bomb threat was a hoax made by a college student. antonyms: Ladies, Gentlewomen, Respectable women, Decent women

examples: The word hobags is considered highly offensive and should be avoided in polite conversation. Many people complained when the rapper used the word hobags in his song. He is so short and shy that his friends jokingly call him a hobbit. A hobbit's home is usually a cosy hole in the ground full of comfort.

englishMeaning: An imaginary creature created by the British writer J. R. R. Tolkien in his famous novels The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings. Figuratively, the word is sometimes used to describe a short, gentle, home-loving person.
antonyms: Giant, Ogre, Titan, Colossus
synonyms: Halfling, Fairy creature, Imaginary being, Dwarf-like character

antonyms: Avoid, Shun, Ignore, Snub, Withdraw, Disassociate, Keep away
englishMeaning: To spend time with someone in a friendly or informal way, especially with people of higher social rank, wealth, or status. To mix or associate socially with important or influential people. To chat, drink, or socialise on familiar terms with others. Sometimes used with a slight hint of disapproval when someone tries to gain favour by mixing with the elite.
urduMeaning: اعلیٰ لوگوں کے ساتھ دوستانہ تعلقات رکھنا، امیر  بااثر یا اہم لوگوں کے ساتھ گھل مل کر بیٹھنا، بے تکلفانہ میل جول رکھنا، خاص لوگوں سے میل ملاپ بڑھانا، اونچے طبقے میں اٹھنا بیٹھنا
sindhiMeaning: اعليٰ ماڻهن سان دوستاڻو لاڳاپو رکڻ، بزرگن، اميرن يا اهم ماڻهن سان ملي جلي ويهڻ، گهرائي وارو ميل جول رکڻ، خاص ماڻهن سان ميل ميلاپ رکڻ، گڏجي ٻهلڻ، ميل جول وڌائڻ
synonyms: Mingle, Mix, Socialise, Associate, Fraternise, Consort, Rub shoulders, Chat, Network
examples: He loves to hobnob with film stars at every party he attends. She often hobnobs with politicians and businessmen at charity events. As a journalist, he had the chance to hobnob with world leaders. The young actor was seen hobnobbing with famous directors at the festival. People criticised the minister for hobnobbing with wealthy industrialists.

urduMeaning: چوپایوں کی پچھلی ٹانگ کا جوڑ، گٹھنے کا جوڑ، گھوڑے یا گائے کی پچھلی ٹانگ کا درمیانی جوڑ، سور کی پچھلی ٹانگ کا گوشت، کوئی قیمتی چیز گروی رکھنا، رہن رکھنا، قرض میں ڈوبا ہونا، گروی رکھی ہوئی چیز
sindhiMeaning: جانورن جي پوئين ٽنگ جو جوڙ، ٿوهي، گهوڙي يا ڍڳي جي پوئين ٽنگ جو وچيون جوڙ، سور جي پوئين ٽنگ جو گوشت، ڪا قيمتي شيءِ گروي رکڻ، رهن ڪرڻ، قرض هيٺ هجڻ، گروي شيءِ
examples: The horse injured its hock while jumping over the fence. She slowly cooked the ham hock with vegetables and herbs. He had to hock his watch to pay the rent. The family was deep in hock after the long illness of their father. The vet examined the hock of the lame cow carefully.
antonyms: Redeem, Reclaim, Buy back, Clear (debt)
englishMeaning: The joint in the back leg of a four-legged animal such as a horse, cow, or dog, equivalent to the human ankle. A cut of meat taken from the leg of a pig (ham hock) or other animal. As a verb (informal), to pawn something, that is, to leave a valuable item with a pawnbroker in exchange for money. Also used in the phrase 'in hock' meaning in debt.
synonyms: Joint, Ankle (animal), Pawn, Pledge, Mortgage, Debt, Cut of meat

examples: The old hogman lived in a small hut near the pig farm. As a hogman, his job was to feed and look after the pigs every day. The hogman drove his herd of pigs to the village market. In the old days, every village had its own hogman. The novel described the simple life of a poor hogman in the countryside.
sindhiMeaning: سؤرن جو پاليندڙ، ڇيلي پاليندڙ، سؤر جو واپاري، سؤر چاريندڙ، سؤرن کي بازار تائين پهچائيندڙ ماڻهو، پراڻي انگريزيءَ ۾ سؤرن جو رکوالو يا چرواهو
englishMeaning: A man who keeps, rears, looks after, or deals in pigs (hogs); a swineherd or pig farmer. The word is now rare and is mostly found in older English texts. In some old dialects, it also refers to a person who drives pigs to market. (Not to be confused with 'Hogmanay', which is the Scottish word for New Year's Eve.)
urduMeaning: سور پالنے والا، سور چرانے والا، سور کا تاجر، سوروں کا چرواہا، سوروں کو منڈی تک لے جانے والا شخص، قدیم انگریزی میں سور پالنے والا کسان یا چرواہا
synonyms: Swineherd, Pig farmer, Pigman, Herder, Stockman
antonyms: Vegetarian farmer, Pig buyer, Customer

urduMeaning: عزت، احترام، تعظیم، خراج عقیدت، خراج تحسین، کسی کی عظمت یا خدمات کا اعتراف کرنا، عقیدت پیش کرنا، نذرانہ، وفاداری کا اعلان، باوقار سلامی
examples: The whole nation paid homage to the brave martyrs of the war. The poet wrote a beautiful poem in homage to his mother. Thousands of people gathered to pay homage to the late leader. The film is a homage to the golden age of cinema. Soldiers stood silently in homage at the war memorial.
englishMeaning: Special respect, honour, or admiration shown publicly for a person, achievement, work of art, or memory. A formal act, ceremony, speech, or tribute paid in recognition of someone's greatness, service, or sacrifice. In old feudal times, a public ceremony in which a vassal swore loyalty to his lord. A sincere expression of devotion, reverence, or tribute.
antonyms: Disrespect, Dishonour, Contempt, Insult, Scorn, Disregard, Disloyalty
sindhiMeaning: عزت، احترام، تعظيم، خراج عقيدت، ڪنهن جي عظمت يا خدمتن جو احترام ڪرڻ، عقيدت پيش ڪرڻ، نذرانو، تابعداريءَ جو اعلان، عزت ڀري سلامي، خراج تحسين
synonyms: Tribute, Respect, Honour, Reverence, Praise, Admiration, Devotion, Loyalty, Salute

englishMeaning: Cloth that is woven or spun at home, usually plain, simple, and coarse in texture. Made of such cloth. By extension, anything that is simple, plain, unsophisticated, and lacking in fancy style; especially used for ideas, advice, philosophy, or wisdom that is straightforward and based on common sense rather than on formal learning.
examples: She wore a long homespun dress made by her grandmother. His grandfather often shared bits of homespun wisdom at the dinner table. The villagers wore simple homespun clothes throughout the winter. The speech was full of homespun humour that made everyone laugh. The cottage had a warm, homespun atmosphere that made guests feel at home.
antonyms: Sophisticated, Refined, Factory-made, Elaborate, Polished, Elegant, Fancy, Urban
sindhiMeaning: گهر ۾ ڪتيل، گهر جو ٺهيل ڪپڙو، گهرو، سادو، عام، اهڙو ڪپڙو جيڪو گهر ۾ سٽڻ ۽ اڻڻ سان تيار ٿئي، سادگي وارو، بي ٺاٺ، ڳوٺاڻو، عام فهم ۽ سادي عقل تي ٻڌل ڳالهه يا صلاح
urduMeaning: گھر میں بنا ہوا، گھریلو، سادہ، گھر میں کاتے اور بُنے ہوئے کپڑے سے بنا، گھریلو دستکاری کا، سادگی والا، بے تکلف، دیہاتی، عام فہم اور سادہ عقل پر مبنی بات یا مشورہ
synonyms: Handmade, Homemade, Simple, Plain, Rustic, Unsophisticated, Folksy, Domestic, Coarse

antonyms: Heterogeneous, Mixed, Diverse, Varied, Different, Unlike, Assorted
synonyms: Uniform, Similar, Identical, Alike, Consistent, Same, Comparable, Unvarying
englishMeaning: Of the same kind, type, or nature throughout. Consisting of parts or elements that are all alike or similar in character, quality, or composition. Uniform in structure, appearance, or thought. Used in science to describe a substance or mixture that has the same composition throughout, and in society to describe a group whose members share similar features such as race, religion, or culture.
sindhiMeaning: هڪجهڙو، يڪسان، هڪ ئي قسم جو، هڪ جنس وارو، اهڙي شيءِ يا گروهه جنهن جا سڀ حصا ساڳيا هجن، يڪرنگ، يڪساني وارو، هڪجنسي، ساڳيءَ خاصيت وارو
examples: The class was made up of a homogeneous group of engineering students. Milk and water do not form a truly homogeneous mixture without mixing. The society in that small town is very homogeneous in its traditions. The company prefers a homogeneous team to ensure smooth coordination. The surface of the metal sheet was perfectly smooth and homogeneous.
urduMeaning: یکساں، ہم جنس، ایک ہی قسم کا، یک رنگ، ایسی چیز یا گروہ جس کے تمام اجزاء ایک جیسے ہوں، ہم نوع، ایک خاصیت والا، یکسانیت رکھنے والا، یک سطحی

synonyms: Similar, Corresponding, Equivalent, Matching, Parallel, Analogous, Comparable
sindhiMeaning: هڪجهڙو ساخت وارو، ساڳيءَ بنياد وارو، اصل ۾ ساڳيءَ هڪجهڙائي وارو، ساڳئي خاندان جا ٻه شيون جيڪي ساخت ۾ هڪجهڙا هجن، مشابهه، هم ساخت، هم اصل، ساڳيءَ ترتيب ۾ هجڻ
antonyms: Different, Dissimilar, Unrelated, Distinct, Heterologous, Unlike
examples: The wings of a bird and the arms of a human are homologous structures. Scientists study homologous organs to understand evolution. Methane and ethane are part of a homologous series of compounds. The two languages share many homologous words from a common root. The two committees have homologous functions in their respective organisations.
urduMeaning: ہم رتبہ، ہم ساخت، ایک جیسی ساخت یا اصل رکھنے والا، ایسی چیزیں جو بنیادی طور پر ایک جیسی ہوں مگر کام مختلف کرتی ہوں، مشابہ، ہم اصل، ہم خاندان، ایک ہی ترتیب میں
englishMeaning: Having the same relation, relative position, value, or structure. In biology, used for body parts of different species that have a common evolutionary origin, even though they may now perform different functions, such as the human arm and a whale's flipper. In chemistry, used for compounds belonging to the same series with similar properties. In general, corresponding or matching in nature.

examples: The university awarded him an honorary doctorate for his services to literature. She was appointed as the honorary president of the women's welfare society. He works as the honorary secretary of the local sports club. The retired general was given an honorary rank in the new force. Several writers received honorary memberships of the literary academy.
englishMeaning: Given as an honour or mark of respect rather than for actual work, qualifications, or payment. Used for titles, degrees, memberships, or positions awarded to a person in recognition of their achievements, services, or status. Such positions usually carry no salary, formal duties, or active responsibilities and are mainly symbolic in nature.
synonyms: Titular, Nominal, Ceremonial, Symbolic, Token, Unpaid, Complimentary
sindhiMeaning: اعزازي، شاندار، عزت طور تي ڏنل، بنا تنخواهه واري عهدي وارو، اهڙو لقب يا عهدو جيڪو ڪنهن جي خدمتن جي اعتراف ۾ ڏنو وڃي، رسمي طور ڏنل اعزاز، عزت لاءِ ڏنل عهدو يا سند
urduMeaning: اعزازی، رسمی، باعزت طور پر دیا گیا، بغیر تنخواہ کے عہدہ، ایسا خطاب یا عہدہ جو کسی کی خدمات کے اعتراف میں دیا جائے، علامتی طور پر دیا گیا اعزاز، اعزاز کے طور پر عطا کیا گیا منصب یا سند
antonyms: Paid, Salaried, Working, Professional, Substantive, Earned

urduMeaning: کھر، سم، گھوڑے یا گائے وغیرہ کے پاؤں کا سخت حصہ، چوپایوں کے پاؤں کا سخت ڈھکن، جانور کے کھر، پیدل چلنا، لات مارنا، تیزی سے پیدل جانا، کھر والا حصہ
examples: The blacksmith carefully cleaned the horse's hoof before fitting a new shoe. The cattle's hooves left deep marks in the muddy field. The deer's hoof was injured by a sharp stone. We had to hoof it all the way to the next village. The farmer noticed an infection in one of the cow's hooves.
sindhiMeaning: کر، سنب، گهوڙي يا ڍڳي وغيره جي پيرن جو سخت حصو، چوپائي مال جي پيرن جا کر، جانور جا سنب، پيرين پنڌ هلڻ، لت هڻڻ، تکيءَ رفتار سان پنڌ ڪرڻ، سنبن وارو حصو
englishMeaning: The hard, horny covering at the end of the foot of certain mammals such as horses, cows, goats, sheep, deer, and camels, on which the animal stands and walks. As a verb (informal), to walk, kick, or travel on foot. The word is also used in expressions like 'on the hoof', meaning while moving, or 'hoof it', meaning to walk briskly.
synonyms: Foot (of animal), Trotter, Pad, Cloven foot
antonyms: Paw, Claw, Hand (human), Talon

examples: A hornet flew into the room and frightened the children. He was stung by a hornet while working in the garden. Their constant complaints stirred up a hornet's nest in the office. The angry old man was as fierce as a hornet. Hornets build their large grey nests under the roof of old buildings.
sindhiMeaning: وڏي قسم جو ڊنگ، زرد ڪاراڙي ڊنگ، اهڙي وڏي ڊنگ جنهن جو ڏنگ سخت ۽ دردناڪ هوندو آهي، ڪاراڙي ڊنگ، چڙ وارو يا خطرناڪ ماڻهو، اهڙو ماڻهو جنهن کي ڇيڙڻ خطري کان خالي نه هجي، ڊنگ مکيءَ جو خاندان
urduMeaning: بھڑ، بڑی قسم کی بھڑ، زہریلی بھڑ، ایسی بڑی بھڑ جس کا ڈنک سخت اور تکلیف دہ ہو، تند خو اور خطرناک شخص، ایسا شخص جسے چھیڑنا خطرے سے خالی نہ ہو، بھڑوں کے خاندان کا ایک کیڑا
synonyms: Wasp, Stinger, Yellow jacket, Bee, Insect, Sting insect
antonyms: Friendly creature, Harmless insect, Peaceful person, Gentle person
englishMeaning: A large, powerful kind of social wasp with a painful sting, usually brown, yellow, or red in colour, that lives in big paper nests and is known for its aggressive behaviour when disturbed. Figuratively, used to describe an angry, irritable, or dangerous person. The phrase 'stir up a hornets' nest' means to cause a sudden and dangerous reaction.

sindhiMeaning: ڊيڄارڻ، دهشت ۾ وجهڻ، خوفزده ڪرڻ، سخت ڊپ ۾ وجهڻ، صدمي ۾ وجهڻ، نفرت ۽ خوف پيدا ڪرڻ، ڪنهن جا هوش اڏائي ڇڏڻ، انتهائي پريشان ۽ ڇرڪايل ڪرڻ
examples: The terrible news of the accident horrified the entire family. The cruel treatment of the prisoners horrified the world. Scenes of the war continue to horrify viewers even today. His rude behaviour horrified all the guests at the dinner. The teacher was horrified by the children's poor exam results.
urduMeaning: خوفزدہ کرنا، ہول دلانا، دہشت زدہ کرنا، سخت ڈر میں مبتلا کرنا، صدمے میں ڈالنا، نفرت اور خوف پیدا کرنا، ہوش اڑا دینا، انتہائی پریشان اور حیران کر دینا
antonyms: Comfort, Reassure, Please, Delight, Soothe, Calm, Encourage, Cheer
synonyms: Terrify, Frighten, Shock, Appal, Dismay, Scare, Petrify, Disturb, Sicken, Alarm
englishMeaning: To fill someone with deep fear, terror, shock, disgust, or great horror. To cause a strong feeling of dread, alarm, or moral outrage. To shock someone so much that they are unable to react normally. Often used when a sight, news, act, or behaviour is so terrible that it disturbs people emotionally or morally.

The friendly, generous, and warm reception, welcome, and treatment of guests, visitors, or strangers. The quality or practice of being hospitable, kind, and welcoming. The business or industry concerned with providing food, drink, accommodation, and entertainment to guests, including hotels, restaurants, and resorts. A polite way of showing care, respect, and good manners towards others.
examples: Sindhi people are famous all over the world for their warm hospitality. The hotel is known for its excellent hospitality and friendly service. Many young people now study hospitality management as a career. We will always remember the hospitality of our hosts in the village. Her hospitality made every guest feel like a member of the family.
urduMeaning: مہمان نوازی، مہمان داری، خوش اخلاقی، مہمانوں کا پرتپاک استقبال اور خدمت، عزت اور پیار سے مہمان کی خاطر تواضع کرنا، ہوٹلوں اور ریستورانوں کا شعبہ، آنے جانے والوں سے اچھا سلوک
synonyms: Welcome, Warmth, Friendliness, Generosity, Kindness, Cordiality, Reception, Entertainment
antonyms: Hostility, Unfriendliness, Inhospitality, Coldness, Rudeness, Neglect, Indifference
sindhiMeaning: مهمان نوازي، مهمان داري، خوش اخلاقي، مهمان جو پرتپاڪ آڌر ڀاءُ ڪرڻ، عزت ۽ پيار سان مهمان جي خدمت ڪرڻ، هوٽلون، ريسٽورنٽ وغيره جو شعبو، ايندڙ ويندڙ سان سهڻو سلوڪ ڪرڻ

englishMeaning: To send or admit a person to a hospital for medical care, observation, or treatment. To place under hospital care because of illness, injury, or surgery. The word is mainly used in formal, medical, or news contexts when a patient needs continuous treatment that cannot be given at home.
antonyms: Discharge, Release, Send home, Cure, Heal, Recover
synonyms: Admit, Confine to hospital, Treat, Institutionalise, Place under care
sindhiMeaning: اسپتال ۾ داخل ڪرڻ، اسپتال موڪلڻ، علاج لاءِ اسپتال ۾ رکڻ، ڪنهن مريض کي علاج ڪرائڻ لاءِ اسپتال ۾ داخل ڪرائڻ، اسپتال ۾ بستري ڪرڻ، شفاخاني ۾ داخلا ڏيارڻ
examples: Doctors decided to hospitalize the patient after his condition got worse. The injured workers were immediately hospitalized after the accident. Her father had to be hospitalized for surgery last week. During the epidemic, hundreds of people were hospitalized in a single day. He was hospitalized for high fever and weakness for three days.
urduMeaning: اسپتال میں داخل کرنا، اسپتال بھیجنا، علاج کے لیے اسپتال میں رکھنا، کسی مریض کو علاج کرانے کے لیے اسپتال میں داخل کرانا، اسپتال میں زیر علاج کرنا، شفا خانے میں داخلہ دلوانا
سرائے، مسافر خانہ، قدیم زمانے کا مہمان خانہ، ایسی جگہ جہاں مسافروں کو کھانا اور رات گزارنے کی سہولت ملتی تھی، گھوڑوں کے اصطبل سمیت سرائے، پرانا ہوٹل، رہائشی مسافر گاہ (متروک لفظ)
synonyms: Inn, Lodging, Hostelry, Guest house, Tavern, Caravanserai, Motel, Hostel
antonyms: Home, Residence, Private house, Mansion, Palace
examples: The weary travellers reached the old hostry just before sunset. Long ago, every main road had a hostry for caravans and traders. The poet described a quiet hostry standing beside the river. They spent the cold night at a small hostry near the mountain pass. Few hostries from that era still survive today.
englishMeaning: An old or rare English word meaning an inn, lodging, or place where travellers could find food and shelter for the night, including a stable for their horses. A hostelry; a guest house. The word is now archaic and is rarely used in modern English except in literature, history, or old poetry.
sindhiMeaning: مسافر خانو، سراءِ، مسافرن جي رهائش وارو پراڻو هنڌ، اهڙي جاءِ جتي مسافر رات گذارن ۽ کاڌو حاصل ڪن، گهوڙن لاءِ تنبيلي سان گڏ سراءِ، پراڻو هوٽل، رهائشي مسافر گاهه (پراڻو لفظ)

antonyms: Healthy meal, Home-cooked food, Modest behaviour, Humble act
sindhiMeaning: هاٽ ڊاگ، گرم سوسيج وارو ڊبل روٽيءَ جو رول، گرم سوسيج روٽيءَ ۾ وجهي تيار ڪيل کاڌو، فاسٽ فوڊ جو هڪ مشهور کاڌو، ڏيکاء ڪرڻ، چالاڪيءَ سان ڪرتب ڏيکارڻ، خوشيءَ جو اظهار
synonyms: Frankfurter, Sausage roll, Wiener, Bun sausage, Fast food, Show-off (verb)
urduMeaning: ہاٹ ڈاگ، ایک قسم کا فاسٹ فوڈ جس میں گرم ساسیج کو لمبے بن میں رکھا جاتا ہے، گرم ساسیج اور روٹی پر مبنی مقبول امریکی کھانا، دکھاوا کرنا، کرتب دکھانا، خوشی کا اظہار کرنا، تعجب اور خوشی کا کلمہ
englishMeaning: A long, soft bread roll filled with a hot cooked sausage, usually served with mustard, ketchup, onions, or other toppings; a very popular fast food, especially in the United States. As a verb (informal), to show off or perform daring tricks, especially in skiing, surfing, or other sports. As an exclamation, used to express excitement or delight.
examples: He ordered a hotdog with extra mustard and onions. Hotdogs are a popular snack at American baseball games. The skier began to hotdog down the slope to impress the crowd. They sold hundreds of hotdogs at the football stadium. Hotdog! We finally won the match.

urduMeaning: شکاری کتا، شکار کا کتا، ایسا کتا جو سونگھ کر شکار کا پیچھا کرے، پیچھا کرنا، تنگ کرنا، مسلسل پریشان کرنا، کسی کے پیچھے پڑ جانا، کمینہ شخص، ذلیل آدمی، دھمکانا اور ہراساں کرنا
antonyms: Help, Comfort, Console, Leave alone, Protect, Encourage, Assist
synonyms: Dog, Pursue, Chase, Harass, Pester, Trail, Persecute, Track, Bother, Bloodhound
englishMeaning: A type of dog used in hunting, known for its strong sense of smell and ability to track or chase animals such as foxes, hares, or deer. As a verb, to chase, pursue, or follow someone persistently, often in a troubling or annoying way. To harass someone constantly with questions, demands, or threats. Also used to describe a despicable or contemptible person.
sindhiMeaning: شڪاري ڪتو، شڪار جو ڪتو، اهڙو ڪتو جيڪو سونگهي شڪار جو پيڇو ڪري، پيڇو ڪرڻ، تنگ ڪرڻ، لاڳيتو پريشان ڪرڻ، ڪنهن جي پٺيان لڳڻ، نڌرو ماڻهو، ذليل شخص، ڌمڪائڻ ۽ تنگ ڪرڻ
examples: The hunter trained his hounds to track foxes in the forest. Reporters continued to hound the actress wherever she went. Creditors began to hound him for the unpaid loans. The old hound followed its master loyally everywhere. He was hounded out of office by constant criticism.

synonyms: Wail, Cry, Yell, Scream, Roar, Bawl, Bellow, Shriek, Whine
englishMeaning: To make a long, loud, mournful cry, as that of a wolf, dog, or wind. To cry out loudly in pain, anger, sorrow, or laughter. A long, loud cry or wail. Used both literally for animals and the wind, and figuratively for human cries or strong expressions of feeling such as a howl of protest or a howl of laughter.
antonyms: Whisper, Murmur, Hush, Silence, Mutter, Be quiet
urduMeaning: چیخنا، رونا، چلانا، کتے یا بھیڑیے کا رونا، ہوا کا تیز شور کرنا، درد  غصے یا خوشی میں چیخنا، طویل اور بلند آواز میں رونا، شور و غل، چیخ و پکار
examples: The wolves began to howl as the full moon rose over the mountains. The strong wind howled through the empty streets all night. The child started to howl when his toy broke. There was a howl of laughter from the back of the classroom. The crowd let out a loud howl of protest against the new law.
sindhiMeaning: رڙ ڪرڻ، ڪتي يا بگهڙ جو روئڻ، اوناڙ، اوڇنگار، اوڙڪ، ڊگهي ۽ زوردار رڙ ڪرڻ، هوا جو شور ڪرڻ، درد، خوشي يا غم ۾ رڙيون ڪرڻ، ڌاڙ، چيخ پڪار

examples: The huckster shouted loudly to attract customers in the busy market. He worked for years as a huckster selling fruits from a cart. People are tired of TV hucksters making false promises. The huckster tried to sell us a fake watch at a high price. Politicians sometimes act like hucksters during election campaigns.
englishMeaning: A person who sells small goods or articles in the street or from door to door, especially in a noisy or pushy way. A pedlar or hawker. A person who uses aggressive, dishonest, or showy methods to sell, advertise, or promote something. As a verb, to sell goods or advertise products in a pushy, noisy, or sometimes dishonest way.
sindhiMeaning: ڦيري وارو، گهٽين ۾ سامان وڪڻندڙ، دڪاندار جنهن جو رويو زوريءَ وڪڻڻ وارو هجي، چالاڪ ۽ ٺڳيءَ سان وڪرو ڪندڙ، نقلي اشتهار ٺاهيندڙ، گهر گهر سامان وڪڻندڙ، نوسربازي سان وڪرو ڪندڙ
urduMeaning: چھابڑی والا، پھیری والا، گلیوں میں سامان بیچنے والا، گھر گھر سامان فروخت کرنے والا، چالاکی اور دھوکے سے بیچنے والا، اشتہار بازی کر کے بیچنے والا، شور مچا کر بیچنے والا تاجر، خوانچہ فروش
antonyms: Customer, Buyer, Honest seller, Purchaser, Consumer, Client
synonyms: Hawker, Pedlar, Vendor, Street seller, Trader, Salesperson, Promoter, Tout

examples: The sky turned a beautiful golden hue at sunset. Her dress was of a soft pinkish hue. Leaders of every political hue attended the meeting. The painting was full of warm hues of red and orange. There was a great hue and cry over the new tax policy.
sindhiMeaning: رنگ، رنگت، رنگ جو ڪو خاص شيڊ، روپ، ڪنهن شيءِ جو ظاهري رنگ يا روپ، ماحول جو رنگ، ڪردار جو روپ، 'هيو ائنڊ ڪراءِ': گهڻن ماڻهن جي شور سان احتجاج ڪرڻ، عوامي شور غل
englishMeaning: A particular shade, tint, or variety of a colour. The attribute of colour by which one may distinguish red from blue, yellow from green, etc. In a wider sense, any aspect, character, or quality of something, as in the phrase 'political hue'. Also occurs in the old phrase 'hue and cry', meaning a loud public protest or noisy outcry.
synonyms: Colour, Shade, Tint, Tone, Tinge, Cast, Complexion, Nuance
urduMeaning: رنگ، رنگت، رنگ کا کوئی خاص شیڈ، روپ، کسی چیز کا ظاہری رنگ یا روپ، نوعیت، کردار کا رنگ، 'ہیو اینڈ کرائی': بلند آواز سے عوامی احتجاج، شور و غوغا، چیخ و پکار
antonyms: Colourlessness, Paleness, Whiteness, Blankness, Drabness

englishMeaning: Showing kindness, mercy, sympathy, and compassion towards people and animals. Treating others with care, gentleness, and respect, especially those who are weak, suffering, or in need. Marked by understanding and consideration of others' pain and feelings. Also used for actions, laws, or methods that avoid causing unnecessary pain or cruelty.
examples: She is known for her humane treatment of stray animals. The new law promotes more humane conditions in prisons. Doctors should always behave in a humane manner with their patients. He is a kind and humane person who helps the poor every day. The organisation works for the humane treatment of all living beings.
urduMeaning: رحمدل، مہربان، انسان دوست، ہمدردی والا، دوسروں اور جانوروں سے نرمی اور رحمدلی سے پیش آنے والا، ظالم نہ ہو بلکہ شفیق ہو، دوسروں کی تکلیف محسوس کرنے والا، انسانیت پسند، رحم کرنے والا
synonyms: Kind, Compassionate, Merciful, Sympathetic, Tender, Gentle, Benevolent, Considerate, Charitable
antonyms: Cruel, Inhumane, Brutal, Heartless, Merciless, Harsh, Savage, Ruthless
sindhiMeaning: رحمدل، مهربان، انسان دوست، انساني همدرديءَ وارو، ٻين ۽ جانورن سان نرم ۽ رحمدلانه برتاءُ ڪندڙ، ظالم نه پر شفقت ڀريو، ٻين جي تڪليف کي محسوس ڪندڙ، انسانيت پسند، رحم وارو، شفيق

antonyms: Dry, Arid, Parched, Crisp, Cool, Fresh, Bone-dry
sindhiMeaning: گهميل، نم وارو، ٿڌي گرم، ڄاٽي وارو، اهڙو موسم جنهن ۾ هوا ۾ گهڻي گهام يا نمي هجي، سخت گهام وارو، ٻوسٽ وارو، نم آلوده، گهام وارو ماحول
englishMeaning: Containing a high level of moisture, water vapour, or dampness in the air. Used to describe weather, climate, or atmosphere that feels wet, sticky, and uncomfortable, especially when combined with heat. Marked by a damp and sultry feeling caused by too much moisture in the surrounding air.
urduMeaning: مرطوب، نم آلود، حبس والا، گرم اور نم موسم، ایسی فضا جس میں ہوا میں نمی زیادہ ہو، حبس بھرا، گھٹن والا، چپچپا موسم، نمی والا ماحول، گرمی اور نمی سے بھرپور
synonyms: Damp, Moist, Muggy, Sticky, Sultry, Wet, Steamy, Clammy
examples: The weather in Karachi is usually hot and humid during the summer. It was a humid evening, and everyone was sweating in the room. Plants like ferns grow well in humid conditions. The humid air made it difficult to breathe inside the closed hall. Coastal areas tend to be more humid than inland regions.

urduMeaning: شکار کرنا، جانوروں کا شکار، تلاش کرنا، کھوج لگانا، ڈھونڈنا، شکار کا عمل، کسی چیز یا شخص کو ڈھونڈنا، مجرم کا پیچھا کرنا، تلاش کا کام، کھوج کا عمل، چھان بین کرنا
examples: Ancient people used to hunt wild animals for food and clothing. The police are still hunting for the missing child. She spent the whole morning hunting for her lost ring. The hunt for the dangerous criminal lasted several weeks. He went on a hunt for a good job after finishing his studies.
sindhiMeaning: شڪار ڪرڻ، جانورن جو شڪار، ڳولها ڪرڻ، تلاش ڪرڻ، تيز ڳولا، شڪار جو عمل، ڪنهن شيءِ يا ماڻهوءَ کي ڳولڻ، چور يا ڏوهاريءَ جي پٺيان لڳڻ، ڳولا مهم، تلاشيءَ جو عمل
englishMeaning: To chase and try to kill or catch wild animals or birds for food, sport, or profit. To search carefully and thoroughly for someone or something that is hidden, lost, or hard to find. The act of hunting, a search, or an organised chase. Used both literally for animals and figuratively for looking for jobs, criminals, information, or objects.
synonyms: Chase, Pursue, Search, Track, Seek, Look for, Stalk, Trail, Quest
antonyms: Find, Discover, Release, Free, Leave alone, Stop, Give up

englishMeaning: A small wooden cage or box-like enclosure, usually with wire mesh on one side, used for keeping pet animals such as rabbits, guinea pigs, or chickens. A piece of furniture similar to a cupboard or sideboard, often with open shelves on top and closed cabinets below, used for storing and displaying dishes. Informally, a small, simple, or untidy room or house.
examples: He built a small wooden hutch for his pet rabbits in the garden. The chickens were kept safe inside a large hutch at night. She placed her best plates on the top shelf of the hutch. They lived in a tiny hutch on the outskirts of the city. The carpenter is making a new hutch for the kitchen.
urduMeaning: خرگوش یا چھوٹے جانوروں کے رہنے کا لکڑی کا چھوٹا پنجرا، خرگوش کا پنجرا، اوپر کھلے خانوں اور نیچے بند الماری والا فرنیچر جو برتن رکھنے کے کام آئے، چھوٹا اور ابتر کمرہ، چھوٹا سا گھر، کوٹھری
sindhiMeaning: خرگوش، ڪڪڙ يا ٻين ننڍڙن جانورن لاءِ ڪاٺ جي ننڍڙي پنجري، خرگوش جو پڃرو، اسٽور لاءِ استعمال ٿيندڙ خاص فرنيچر، ٿانون وارو ڪٻاٽ، ننڍڙو ۽ ابتر گهر، ننڍڙي ڪوٺڙي، پڃرو
synonyms: Cage, Pen, Coop, Enclosure, Cabinet, Cupboard, Sideboard, Box, Shanty
antonyms: Open field, Pasture, Outdoors, Wilderness, Mansion, Palace

synonyms: Cleanliness, Sanitation, Sterility, Purity, Healthfulness, Disinfection, Tidiness
urduMeaning: صفائی، صحت کی حفاظت کے لیے صفائی رکھنا، جسمانی اور ماحولیاتی صفائی، ایسے اعمال جن سے جسم  گھر اور ماحول صاف رہے اور بیماریاں نہ پھیلیں، حفظانِ صحت، صفائی کے اصولوں پر عمل
antonyms: Dirtiness, Filth, Uncleanliness, Pollution, Squalor, Contamination, Untidiness
sindhiMeaning: صفائي، صحت جي حفاظت لاءِ صفائي رکڻ، جسماني ۽ ماحولياتي صفائي، اهڙا عمل جن سان جسم، گهر ۽ ماحول صاف رهي ۽ بيماريون نه ٿين، حفظان صحت، صفائيءَ جي اصولن جي پيروي ڪرڻ
englishMeaning: The practice of keeping oneself, one's surroundings, and one's food clean in order to stay healthy and prevent the spread of disease. The set of conditions or activities, such as washing hands, bathing, brushing teeth, cleaning the house, and safe food handling, that help maintain good health. The branch of science concerned with the protection of health through cleanliness.
examples: Good personal hygiene helps in preventing many diseases. Children should be taught the importance of hygiene from an early age. The hospital follows strict hygiene rules in every ward. Poor hygiene in restaurants can cause food poisoning. Regular hand washing is the simplest rule of hygiene.

antonyms: Curse, Insult, Lament, Dirge, Mockery, Blasphemy
synonyms: Anthem, Psalm, Chant, Song of praise, Devotional song, Carol, Ode, Paean
englishMeaning: A religious song or poem of praise, usually addressed to God or a deity, sung in a place of worship by a congregation. A song expressing strong feelings of devotion, gratitude, or admiration. By extension, any song or expression that strongly praises a person, an idea, or a thing. As a verb, to praise or celebrate someone or something in song.
sindhiMeaning: حمد، مذهبي گيت، ڀڄن، خدا جي حمد ۽ ثنا، عبادت گاهه ۾ گڏجي ڳايو ويندڙ مذهبي گيت، تعريف ڀريو گيت، ڪنهن جي عظمت بيان ڪرڻ وارو گيت، خدا جي تعريف، عقيدت ڀريو نظم
examples: The congregation sang a beautiful hymn at the end of the service. She loves to listen to old hymns on Sunday mornings. The poet wrote a hymn in praise of nature and its beauty. The national anthem is a hymn of love for the country. The children's choir hymned the glory of their teacher.
urduMeaning: حمد، مذہبی گیت، بھجن، خدا کی تعریف، عبادت گاہ میں مل کر گایا جانے والا مذہبی گیت، تعریفی نغمہ، کسی کی عظمت بیان کرنے والا گیت، خدا کی ثنا، عقیدت بھرا نظم

synonyms: Ice mass, Floating ice, Berg, Ice mountain, Glacier fragment, Frozen mass
englishMeaning: A very large mass of floating ice that has broken away from a glacier or an ice sheet and drifts in cold ocean waters; only about one-tenth of an iceberg is visible above the surface while the rest lies hidden underwater. Figuratively, the phrase 'tip of the iceberg' is used to describe a small visible part of a much bigger hidden problem or situation. Also used for an emotionally cold or unfeeling person.
antonyms: Warm water, Tropical sea, Warmth, Warm-hearted person, Friendly soul
urduMeaning: برفانی تودہ، سمندر میں تیرتا ہوا بہت بڑا برف کا ٹکڑا جو گلیشیئر سے ٹوٹ کر الگ ہوا ہو، ایسا برف کا تودہ جس کا بیشتر حصہ پانی کے نیچے ہوتا ہے، کسی بڑے پوشیدہ مسئلے کا چھوٹا حصہ، احساس میں ٹھنڈا اور بے حس شخص
examples: The Titanic sank after striking a huge iceberg in the North Atlantic. Climate change is causing more icebergs to break away from the polar ice. What we see is only the tip of the iceberg of the country's economic problems. From the air, the iceberg looked like a floating white mountain. He was so cold and silent that his colleagues called him an iceberg.
sindhiMeaning: برفاني ٽڪرو، تمام وڏي برف جو ٽڪرو جيڪو سمنڊ ۾ تڙي ٿو، گليشيئر مان ٽٽل برف جو وڏو ٽڪرو، 'برفاني چوٽي' جو محاورو وڏي مسئلي جو معمولي حصو، احساس ۾ ٿڌو ماڻهو، بي حس انسان

antonyms: Anonymity, Unknown, Disguise, Concealment, Pseudonym, Mask
synonyms: Name, Code, Label, Marker, Tag, ID, Sign, Indicator, Designator
urduMeaning: شناخت کنندہ، شناختی نشانی، نام  نمبر یا کوڈ جو کسی چیز یا شخص کو الگ پہچاننے کے لیے استعمال ہو، شناختی علامت، کمپیوٹر میں کسی فائل  صارف یا ریکارڈ کا منفرد کوڈ، پہچان کا ذریعہ
englishMeaning: A name, label, number, sign, or any piece of information that is used to identify, recognise, or distinguish one person, object, or thing from another. In computing and databases, a unique string or code used to refer to a specific record, file, variable, or user, such as a username, ID number, or product code. Anything that serves as a mark of identity.
sindhiMeaning: سڃاڻپ ڏيندڙ، سڃاڻپ نشاني، نالو، انگ يا ڪوڊ جيڪو ڪنهن شيءِ يا ماڻهوءَ کي الڳ سڃاڻڻ لاءِ ڪم اچي، شناختي نشان، ڪمپيوٽر ۾ ڪنهن فائل، يوزر يا رڪارڊ جو منفرد ڪوڊ، شناخت ڪندڙ
examples: Each student is given a unique identifier at the time of admission. In the database, the employee ID acts as the main identifier for every worker. Your email address is often used as an identifier on online platforms. Fingerprints are a reliable identifier of a person. The product is marked with a special barcode identifier on its box.

antonyms: Secondary, Caused, Symptomatic, Traceable
sindhiMeaning: اڻڄاتل سبب سان ٿيندڙ بيماري، جنهن جو ڪو معلوم سبب نه هجي، طب ۾ بي سبب بيماري لاءِ استعمال
englishMeaning: Relating to a disease or condition that arises spontaneously or from an unknown cause. Not caused by any identifiable or previously existing disease. Used in medicine to describe conditions with no known origin.
synonyms: Unknown-cause, Spontaneous, Self-originated, Primary, Essential
urduMeaning: نامعلوم سبب سے پیدا ہونے والی بیماری، جس کا کوئی معلوم سبب نہ ہو، طب میں ایسی حالت جس کا ماخذ نامعلوم ہو
examples: The patient was diagnosed with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis after all known causes were ruled out. Idiopathic epilepsy accounts for a large proportion of seizure disorders in children. Doctors classified her condition as idiopathic because no underlying cause could be identified. He was told his hearing loss was idiopathic and could not be traced to any specific event. The research team is studying idiopathic cases to better understand the mechanisms of the disease.

sindhiMeaning: ذليل، رسوا، شرمناڪ، بدنام ڪندڙ، عار آڻيندڙ، شرم ۽ ذلت ڀريو
examples: The general suffered an ignominious defeat and was forced to surrender in front of his own troops. His ignominious behaviour at the ceremony shocked everyone who was present. The politician resigned after a series of ignominious scandals tarnished his reputation beyond repair. She refused to accept such an ignominious outcome after years of hard work and dedication. The team's ignominious performance in the final match was widely criticised in the press.
englishMeaning: Deserving or causing public shame, disgrace, or humiliation. Bringing dishonour or great embarrassment. Extremely shameful or degrading in nature.
antonyms: Honourable, Glorious, Distinguished, Praiseworthy, Dignified
urduMeaning: ذلت آمیز، شرمناک، رسوا کن، بدنامی لانے والا، عار آور، انتہائی شرمناک
synonyms: Shameful, Disgraceful, Humiliating, Dishonourable, Degrading, Inglorious

examples: He was ignominiously removed from his position following the investigation. The army retreated ignominiously after suffering heavy losses in the first engagement. She was ignominiously dismissed from the competition for breaking the rules. The team was ignominiously knocked out of the tournament in the very first round. He had to walk away ignominiously after the crowd booed him off the stage.
sindhiMeaning: ذليل طريقي سان، شرمناڪ انداز ۾، بدنامي سان، رسوائيءَ سان
synonyms: Shamefully, Disgracefully, Dishonourably, Humiliatingly, Degradingly
urduMeaning: ذلت آمیز طریقے سے، شرمناک انداز میں، بدنامی کے ساتھ، رسوائی سے
antonyms: Honourably, Gloriously, Proudly, Respectably
englishMeaning: In a shameful, disgraceful, or humiliating manner. In a way that brings dishonour or public embarrassment. Done in a degrading or undignified way.

synonyms: Disregard, Overlook, Neglect, Dismiss, Snub, Pay no attention to, Turn a blind eye to
urduMeaning: نظرانداز کرنا، توجہ نہ دینا، دیکھ کر بھی نہ دیکھنا، اہمیت نہ دینا، ان دیکھا کرنا
sindhiMeaning: نظرانداز ڪرڻ، ڌيان نه ڏيڻ، ڏسندي به نه ڏسڻ، اهميت نه ڏيڻ، اڻ ڏٺو ڪرڻ
antonyms: Notice, Acknowledge, Regard, Attend to, Heed, Recognise
examples: She chose to ignore his rude comment and continued with her presentation calmly. The government cannot afford to ignore the warnings issued by the environmental scientists. He tried to ignore the pain in his shoulder and carry on with the match. Please do not ignore the safety guidelines posted on the walls of the laboratory. The teacher asked the students not to ignore any question in the examination paper.
englishMeaning: To deliberately pay no attention to something or someone. To disregard or refuse to take notice of a person, fact, or situation. To treat something as if it does not exist or does not matter.

sindhiMeaning: ناجائز، غير قانوني، حرام، ممنوع، سماجي يا قانوني طور تي نه مڃيل
antonyms: Legal, Lawful, Permitted, Authorized, Legitimate, Sanctioned
urduMeaning: ناجائز، غیر قانونی، حرام، ممنوع، سماجی یا قانونی طور پر ناقابلِ قبول
englishMeaning: Forbidden by law, rules, or custom. Not permitted or sanctioned by accepted standards or norms. Illegal or unlawful in nature. Something done in secret because it is socially or legally unacceptable.
synonyms: Illegal, Unlawful, Forbidden, Prohibited, Banned, Criminal, Unauthorized
examples: The authorities seized a large quantity of illicit drugs at the border checkpoint. He was arrested for his involvement in an illicit trading network. The investigation revealed illicit financial transactions worth millions of dollars. She knew that accepting the offer would be illicit and could cost her the job. Illicit activities such as smuggling continue to pose a serious challenge to law enforcement agencies.

The street lamps were switched on to illuminate the road during the heavy fog. Her detailed explanation helped to illuminate the complexities of the new tax policy. The documentary was designed to illuminate the struggles faced by refugees around the world. Candles were placed along the path to illuminate the garden during the evening celebration.
synonyms: Light up, Brighten, Clarify, Enlighten, Explain, Elucidate, Shed light on
englishMeaning: To light up or make bright with light. To make something clearer or easier to understand. To enlighten or inform someone. To decorate a manuscript or text with coloured illustrations. To shed light on a topic, idea, or problem.
urduMeaning: روشن کرنا، چمکانا، واضح کرنا، سمجھانا، ذہن کو روشنی دینا، تصویروں سے سجانا
sindhiMeaning: روشن ڪرڻ، چمڪائڻ، واضح ڪرڻ، سمجهائڻ، ذهن کي روشني ڏيڻ، تصويرن سان سينگارڻ
antonyms: Darken, Obscure, Confuse, Cloud, Dim, Mystify

examples: The illumination of the cathedral on Christmas Eve was a truly breathtaking sight. She experienced a sudden illumination after reading the philosopher's work for the first time. The illumination of medieval manuscripts was a painstaking art that took years to perfect. Adequate illumination in the workplace is essential for the health and productivity of all employees.
antonyms: Darkness, Obscurity, Confusion, Ignorance, Dimness

englishMeaning: The quality or state of not being interested or curious; a lack of concern or engagement. Uninterestedness refers to an absence of personal involvement, enthusiasm, or attraction towards a subject, person, or activity. It is often characterized by apathy or a sense of detachment.
sindhiMeaning: عدم دلچسپي، بي رغبتي، لاپرواهي، بي ڌياني، ڪنهن ڪم، شخص يا شيءِ ۾ دلچسپي نه هجڻ جي حالت، دل نه لڳڻ
examples: His uninterestedness in the family business was a great disappointment to his father. The teacher noticed the student's uninterestedness and tried a new way to explain the lesson. She feigned uninterestedness, but her eyes gave away her deep curiosity. The politician's speech was met with a wave of public uninterestedness. Her air of calm uninterestedness was just a mask for her anxiety.
antonyms: Interest, Enthusiasm, Curiosity, Concern, Engagement, Eagerness, Fascination, Attentiveness
synonyms: Apathy, Indifference, Detachment, Aloofness, Heedlessness, Unconcern, Listlessness, Disregard, Incuriosity

examples: The new salon on the corner is a unisex establishment. Many modern fragrances are unisex, appealing to both men and women. He prefers to shop for unisex clothing because he likes the looser fit. The university is installing more unisex restrooms in its new buildings.
englishMeaning: Suitable for both sexes; not gender-specific. The term refers to things like clothing, hairstyles, or facilities that are designed to be used or worn by both males and females. This approach promotes inclusivity and breaks away from traditional gender roles in fashion and design.
synonyms: Gender-neutral, Androgynous, Coed, Shared, Common, Universal, For all
urduMeaning: دونوں جنسوں کے لیے، مرد و زن کے لیے یکساں، مشترکہ، ایسی کوئی چیز جو مرد اور عورت دونوں استعمال کر سکیں
sindhiMeaning: ٻنهي جنسن لاءِ، مردن ۽ عورتن لاءِ يڪسان، گڏيل، اهڙي شيءِ جيڪا مرد ۽ عورت ٻئي استعمال ڪري سگهن

synonyms: Untie, Unfasten, Unbind, Release, Detach, Loosen, Set free, Unmoor

englishMeaning: To untie or unfasten. To release something from its bindings, such as ropes or straps. This term is often used when talking about cargo on a ship, truck, or other vehicle.
antonyms: Lash, Fasten, Tie, Secure, Bind, Strap, Hitch
examples: The sailors began to unlash the cargo as soon as the ship docked. He had to unlash the spare tire from the roof rack. Before setting up camp, they unlashed the tents and supplies from the pack mules. They carefully unlashed the fragile statue from its crate.
urduMeaning: کھولنا، رسی یا بندھن کھولنا، آزاد کرنا، کسی بندھی ہوئی چیز کو کھولنا، خاص طور پر جہاز یا گاڑی سے سامان کی رسیاں ہٹانا

englishMeaning: To release or open a latch. To undo the fastening of a door, gate, or window by lifting or moving its latch. This action allows the object to be opened.
urduMeaning: کُنڈی کھولنا، چٹخنی کھولنا، اٹکا ہٹانا، دروازے یا کھڑکی کو کھولنے کے لیے اس کا لاک ہٹانا
examples: She heard a key turn in the lock and then the sound of the door unlatching. Please unlatch the gate so I can bring the car into the driveway. He reached over to unlatch the window, letting in a cool breeze. The child was just tall enough to unlatch the back door and run outside.
sindhiMeaning: ڪُنڊو کولڻ، چٽڪڻي کولڻ، ڪڙو کولڻ، ڪنهن دروازي يا دريءَ جو اٽڪاءُ هٽائڻ تہ جيئن اُها کُلي سگهي
antonyms: Latch, Fasten, Lock, Bolt, Secure, Close, Bar, Shut
synonyms: Unfasten, Open, Unhook, Unbolt, Release, Unlock, Unbar, Unclasp

sindhiMeaning: بغير معاوضي جي، بنا اجوري، رضاڪاراڻو، مفت، اھڙو ڪم جنھن جي پگھار يا پئسا نہ ملن
antonyms: Paid, Remunerated, Compensated, Salaried, Lucrative, Professional, Stipendiary
urduMeaning: بغیر معاوضے کے، بلا اجرت، رضاکارانہ، جس کے پیسے نہ ملیں، مفت میں کیا گیا کام
synonyms: Unpaid, Voluntary, Uncompensated, Gratuitous, Honorary, Pro bono, Unsalaried, Wageless
englishMeaning: Not paid; voluntary. Describes work, an activity, or a position for which no payment or other financial reward is given. This type of labor is often performed to gain experience, support a cause, or fulfill a civic duty.
examples: Many internships at non-profits are unremunerated, offering experience instead of a salary. He served on the board for ten years in an unremunerated capacity. A great deal of unremunerated work, such as childcare and housework, contributes significantly to the economy. The community garden is maintained by a team of unremunerated volunteers.

antonyms: Inferior, Common, Mediocre, Ordinary, Surpassed, Matched, Rivalled
englishMeaning: Better than everyone or everything of the same type. Having no equal, match, or competition. It describes something so superior in quality, skill, or achievement that nothing else can compare to it.
synonyms: Unequalled, Unparalleled, Incomparable, Matchless, Peerless, Supreme, Surpassing, Second-to-none
urduMeaning: بے مثال، بے نظیر، لاجواب، یکتا، جس کا کوئی مقابل نہ ہو، اپنی مثال آپ
sindhiMeaning: بي مثال، لاجواب، اڪيلو، جنهن جو ڪو ثاني نه هجي، اهڙو جو ڪو ٻيو سندس مقابلو نه ڪري سگهي
examples: The beauty of the valley is unrivalled. He has an unrivalled knowledge of local history. The company has an unrivalled reputation for quality. Her performance in the final was simply unrivalled. The museum boasts an unrivalled collection of ancient artifacts.

antonyms: Tarnished, Stained, Blemished, Marred, Sullied, Damaged, Corrupted
englishMeaning: Not spoiled or stained; clean and bright. Referring to a reputation, character, or record that is free from any blame or criticism. Something that is pure, perfect, and in its original pristine condition.
sindhiMeaning: بي داغ، صاف، بي عيب، جنهن تي ڪو بہ داغ يا نشان نہ هجي، اهڙي شهرت يا ڪردار جيڪو هر قسم جي الزام کان پاڪ هجي، اڻ ميرو، اجرو
synonyms: Unblemished, Pristine, Immaculate, Flawless, Spotless, Unsullied, Unstained, Perfect, Pure

examples: She left the company with an untarnished reputation. The silver trophy remained untarnished even after fifty years. He was a man of untarnished integrity. Despite the political turmoil, his record as a leader remained untarnished. They wanted to preserve the untarnished beauty of the national park.

antonyms: Tarnishable, Corruptible, Stainable, Perishable, Blemished, Corroding, Fading, Degradable
englishMeaning: Resistant to losing luster or becoming discolored. It describes a material that does not easily corrode or stain. Figuratively, it means remaining pure, spotless, or unblemished in reputation or character.
urduMeaning: بے داغ رہنے والا، جس کا رنگ خراب نہ ہو، اپنی چمک برقرار رکھنے والا، بے عیب، جس کی ساکھ پر کوئی حرف نہ آئے
synonyms: Stainless, Incorruptible, Unblemished, Unstained, Imperishable, Enduring, Ever-bright, Pure, Spotless
sindhiMeaning: جنهن جو رنگ خراب نه ٿئي، نه مرجهائجندڙ، بي داغ رهڻ وارو، جنهن جي ساک کي نقصان نه پهچي، هميشه چمڪدار ۽ صاف رهندڙ
examples: The company markets its new cutlery as having an untarnishing finish, even after years of use. He maintained an untarnishing reputation for honesty throughout his long political career. Her untarnishing integrity made her the ideal candidate to lead the ethics committee. Platinum is valued for its beauty and untarnishing quality. The hero's legacy remained untarnishing, inspiring generations to come.

She worked patiently to untwine the tangled necklace chains. The two vines had grown so tightly together they were impossible to untwine. It can be difficult to untwine fact from fiction in his stories. He gently untwined his fingers from hers.
englishMeaning: To separate strands that are twisted or woven together. To unwind or disentangle from a tangled or coiled state. This can refer to physically separating items like ropes and vines, or metaphorically separating complex ideas, relationships, or legal issues.
synonyms: Disentangle, Unravel, Unwind, Untwist, Uncoil, Unbraid, Separate, Disengage
sindhiMeaning: ويڙهه کولڻ، اُڪلڻ، ڇوڙڻ، هڪ ٻئي ۾ مليل يا وٽيل شين کي جدا ڪرڻ، ڳنڍ کولڻ
urduMeaning: بل کھولنا، سُلجھانا، اُلجھی ہوئی چیزوں کو الگ کرنا، ایک دوسرے میں لپٹی ہوئی ڈوریوں یا تاروں کو جُدا کرنا
antonyms: Entwine, Twist, Weave, Braid, Tangle, Interlace, Entangle, Knit

synonyms: Reveal, Expose, Disclose, Uncover, Present, Launch, Announce, Display, Divulge
urduMeaning: نقاب کشائی کرنا، رونمائی کرنا، ظاہر کرنا، کسی نئی چیز یا منصوبے کو پہلی بار عوام کے سامنے لانا، پردہ اٹھانا، بے نقاب کرنا
antonyms: Conceal, Hide, Cover, Veil, Shroud, Mask, Obscure, Suppress
sindhiMeaning: پردو هٽائڻ، ظاهر ڪرڻ، رونمائي ڪرڻ، ڪنهن نئين شيءِ يا منصوبي کي عوام جي سامهون پيش ڪرڻ، نقاب ڪشادگي ڪرڻ، فاش ڪرڻ
englishMeaning: To remove a veil or covering from something, especially as part of a ceremony. To make something secret or previously unknown public for the first time. It is often used for new products, plans, or works of art being shown to the world.
examples: The company will unveil its new smartphone next week. The mayor is scheduled to unveil the new statue in the town square. They plan to unveil their strategy at the annual meeting. The investigation unveiled a widespread conspiracy.

The civil war caused a massive social upheaval in the country. Her father's sudden death led to a great emotional upheaval in her life. The industrial revolution was a period of great technological and economic upheaval. The family is going through a bit of an upheaval since they decided to move.
urduMeaning: اتھل پتھل، انقلاب، ہنگامہ، بہت بڑی تبدیلی، انتشار، معاشرتی یا سیاسی خلفشار، زیر و زبر
englishMeaning: A violent or sudden change or disruption to something. A major disturbance or radical change. It refers to a great shift, especially one that causes significant conflict, confusion, or suffering in society, politics, or one's personal life. The term can also describe a geological process involving the upward displacement of the earth's crust.
synonyms: Disruption, Turmoil, Disturbance, Revolution, Cataclysm, Commotion, Disorder, Tumult, Ferment
sindhiMeaning: اٿل پٿل، وڏو انقلاب، ڀڃ ڊاهه، هنگامه، سخت بيچيني جي حالت، وڏي تبديلي يا خرابي، سماجي يا سياسي انتشار
antonyms: Stability, Calm, Peace, Tranquility, Order, Harmony, Serenity

englishMeaning: Suave, courteous, and refined in manner. Especially of a man, being sophisticated, worldly, and polished. An urbane person is notably polite and elegant and is comfortable in social situations, often with a witty or charming demeanor.
sindhiMeaning: مهذب، شائسته، خوش اخلاق، نفيس، سڌريل، شهري آدابن کان واقف، اهڙو ماڻهو جنهن جو وهنوار ۽ گفتگو ڏاڍي سُلجھيل ۽ دلڪش هجي
examples: The host was an urbane and witty man who made all his guests feel comfortable. He maintained an urbane charm even when faced with difficult questions. Her urbane conversation was a delight at the formal dinner party. The diplomat was known for his urbane manner and skillful negotiation.
antonyms: Uncouth, Boorish, Crude, Unrefined, Unsophisticated, Provincial, Rude
urduMeaning: مہذب، شائستہ، خوش اخلاق، نفاست پسند، وضعدار، شہری آداب سے واقف شخص، جس کا انداز پُرکشش اور سلجھا ہوا ہو
synonyms: Sophisticated, Suave, Debonair, Cultured, Polished, Refined, Civilized, Courteous, Elegant

examples: The moneylender was condemned for his practice of usure. Ancient laws were enacted to prevent the poor from falling victim to usure. He considered any interest on a loan to be a form of usure. The medieval church taught that usure was a sin against one's neighbor.
sindhiMeaning: سود خوري، وياج خوري، رِبا، ناجائز وياج، تمام گهڻو وياج وٺڻ جو عمل، وڌيڪ اگهه تي قرض ڏيڻ
antonyms: Charity, Benevolence, Aid, Philanthropy, Fair lending, Altruism, Generosity

englishMeaning: An archaic term for usury. The practice of lending money at unreasonably high rates of interest. It refers to charging an exorbitant or illegally high amount of interest on a loan. Historically, usure meant charging any interest at all, which was forbidden by several religions.
synonyms: Usury, Exploitation, Extortion, Gouging, Predatory lending, Profiteering, Sharking

englishMeaning: Practiced usury; lent money at excessively high interest rates. This refers to the act of charging an exorbitant or unlawfully high rate of interest on a loan. Historically, it describes an exploitative financial practice. A moneylender who has 'usured' has preyed on the desperate for financial gain.
examples: The corrupt moneylender usured the poor farmer, charging him an interest rate that was impossible to repay. He had usured his way to immense wealth by preying on the financial desperation of others. Ancient laws strictly forbade merchants who usured their clients. The desperate man felt he had been usured into a debt he could never escape.
urduMeaning: سود خوری کی، بہت زیادہ شرح پر قرض دیا، ناجائز منافع خوری کی، سودی کاروبار کیا
antonyms: Aided, Assisted, Donated, Gifted, Subsidized, Supported, Helped
synonyms: Exploited, Extorted, Overcharged, Gouged, Fleeced, Swindled, Profiteered
sindhiMeaning: سود خوري ڪئي، وياج تي پئسا ڏنا، تمام گهڻي ۽ غير قانوني وياج جي شرح تي قرض فراهم ڪيو، ناجائز منافعو ورتو

urduMeaning: غاصب، ناجائز قابض، زبردستی اقتدار پر قبضہ کرنے والا، حق چھیننے والا
sindhiMeaning: غاصب، ناجائز قبضو ڪندڙ، زبردستي تخت يا اختيار تي ويهڻ وارو، حق کسيندڙ
examples: The prince declared his uncle a usurper for seizing the throne after the king's death. Many viewed the military leader as a usurper, not a legitimate ruler. She fought to reclaim her company from the usurper who had ousted her through corporate intrigue. The usurper's reign was marked by fear and instability.
antonyms: Rightful Heir, Legitimate Ruler, Lawful Sovereign, Successor, Incumbent, Appointee
synonyms: Autocrat, Dictator, Tyrant, Supplanter, Infringer, Intruder, Pretender, Encroacher
englishMeaning: A person who takes a position of power illegally or by force. One who wrongfully seizes and holds the place of another. The term is often used for someone who takes a throne or high office without a rightful claim.

A spoken word, statement, or vocal sound. The action of saying or expressing something aloud. An utterance is the smallest unit of speech, representing a complete thought or expression, bounded by silence.
antonyms: Silence, Quiet, Taciturnity, Muteness, Reticence, Inarticulateness, Unspoken thought
urduMeaning: کلام، بول، کہی ہوئی بات، بیان، گفتگو، لفظ، اظہارِ خیال
sindhiMeaning: چَوڻ، ڳالھ، ٻول، لفظ، اظھار، واتان نڪتل ڪا ڳالھ يا آواز
synonyms: Statement, Remark, Articulation, Pronouncement, Declaration, Expression, Comment, Speech
examples: Her every utterance was carefully analyzed by the press. The baby's first utterance sounded like 'mama'. The politician's public utterances were often controversial. A simple nod can be as meaningful as a verbal utterance.
They journeyed to the uttermost parts of the continent. She trusted him to the uttermost. He exerted his strength to the uttermost to win the race. This is a matter of the uttermost importance.
englishMeaning: Most extreme; farthest or most remote. It signifies the greatest possible degree or extent. This can refer to a physical distance, such as the outermost point of a region, or to an abstract concept, like the highest level of effort or importance.
synonyms: Utmost, Extreme, Farthest, Ultimate, Maximum, Supreme, Furthest, Greatest, Final
sindhiMeaning: انتها، حد، پوري ۾ پورو، وڌ کان وڌ، سڀ کان ڏور، پري ۾ پري، آخري حد تائين، پنهنجي وس کان وڌيڪ
urduMeaning: انتہائی، بعید ترین، آخری حد، زیادہ سے زیادہ، حد درجہ، انتہا کا، اپنی پوری بساط بھر
antonyms: Nearest, Closest, Innermost, Minimum, Least, Central, Initial
Fullness, Substance, Meaningfulness, Intelligence, Profundity, Content, Significance
englishMeaning: Total emptiness; a void. A lack of thought, intelligence, or serious purpose. This term can describe a literal empty space or a metaphorical one, such as the absence of meaningful content or ideas. It is often used to criticize the intellectual or spiritual emptiness of a person, conversation, or work of art.
synonyms: Emptiness, Void, Inanity, Blankness, Hollowness, Shallowness, Mindlessness, Nothingness
urduMeaning: خلا، خالی پن، بے معنویت، ذہنی خالی پن، بے فکری، بے عقلی یہ لفظ کسی خالی جگہ یا سوچ، عقل اور ذہانت کی کمی کو ظاہر کرتا ہے، اکثر کسی چیز کے سطحی یا بے معنی ہونے پر تنقید کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے
sindhiMeaning: خال، خلا، خالي جاءِ، سوچ ۽ فهم جي کوٽ، بي عقلي، بي فڪري، ذهني خالي پن، بي معنيٰ هجڻ هي لفظ جسماني خال يا ذهني خالي پن، يعني سوچ، فهم يا معنيٰ جي کوٽ کي ظاهر ڪري ٿو
examples: The vacuity of his stare suggested he wasn't paying attention. She was struck by the intellectual vacuity of the film's plot. He filled the vacuity of his lonely days with endless television. There's a certain vacuity in modern pop culture that many critics lament. The vast vacuity of space is both terrifying and beautiful.

englishMeaning: To check or prove the validity or accuracy of something. To make something legally or officially acceptable. It can also mean to recognize, confirm, or affirm that a person or their feelings are worthwhile and legitimate.
examples: You need to validate your parking ticket at the machine before you leave. The research findings validate the new theory. It's important for a therapist to validate their client's feelings. The software will validate the data before processing it.
sindhiMeaning: تصديق ڪرڻ، پڪ ڪرڻ، جائز قرار ڏيڻ، صحيح ثابت ڪرڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ جي درستگي يا سچائي کي پرکڻ، قانوني طور تي منظور ڪرڻ، ڪنهن شخص جي احساسن يا خيالن کي اهميت ڏيڻ ۽ انهن کي تسليم ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: تصدیق کرنا، توثیق کرنا، جانچ پڑتال کرنا، جائز قرار دینا، کسی چیز کی درستگی کو پرکھنا اور ثابت کرنا، قانونی طور پر منظور کرنا، کسی شخص کے جذبات یا رائے کو تسلیم کرنا اور اہمیت دینا
antonyms: Invalidate, Disprove, Refute, Contradict, Annul, Cancel, Reject
synonyms: Confirm, Verify, Authenticate, Endorse, Substantiate, Corroborate, Ratify, Approve, Justify

urduMeaning: بہادری، شجاعت، دلیری، جوانمردی، خطرے کے مقابلے میں دکھائی جانے والی جرأت اور ہمت، میدانِ جنگ کی بہادری
examples: The soldiers received medals for the valor they displayed in combat. She showed remarkable valor by rescuing the child from the burning house. His valor on the battlefield was legendary. The epic poem recounts the valor of ancient heroes. It takes valor to admit when you are wrong.
sindhiMeaning: بهادري، سورهيائي، شجاعت، جرئت، خاص طور تي جنگ جي ميدان ۾ ڏيکاريل همت ۽ جرئت، جوانمردي، خطري کان نه ڊڄڻ واري حالت
synonyms: Courage, Bravery, Gallantry, Heroism, Fearlessness, Boldness, Intrepidity, Prowess, Mettle
antonyms: Cowardice, Fear, Timidity, Pusillanimity, Spinelessness, Irresolution, Faintheartedness
englishMeaning: Great courage in the face of danger, especially in battle. Valor is the quality of a person who is not afraid of difficult or dangerous situations. This term often describes the exceptional bravery and boldness shown by a soldier during a conflict.

sindhiMeaning: رَت پيئندڙ پِشاچ، آدم خور، هڪ خيالي مخلوق جيڪا رات جو قبر مان نڪري جيئرن ماڻهن جو رت پيئندي آهي، رَت چوسيندڙ، ظالم شخص، لُٽيرو ماڻهو
urduMeaning: خون آشام، پشاچ، آدم خور بھوت، ایک خیالی مخلوق جو رات کو قبر سے نکل کر زندہ انسانوں کا خون پیتی ہے، استحصال کرنے والا شخص، ظالم، لٹیرا
englishMeaning: A corpse supposed to leave its grave at night to drink the blood of living people. In folklore, a vampire is an undead creature that subsists by feeding on the blood of the living. Figuratively, it refers to a person who preys ruthlessly on others, like an exploiter or extortionist. It can also refer to a vampire bat.
examples: Bram Stoker's Dracula is the most famous vampire in literature. According to legend, a vampire cannot enter a home unless invited. He called the loan shark a ruthless vampire for preying on the needy. The movie was about a group of teenagers who discover a vampire living in their town. Vampire bats are native to the Americas.
antonyms: Mortal, Human, Victim, Prey, Angel, Protector, Benefactor
