examples: She bought a pair of brown suede shoes for the winter. His suede jacket looked stylish and comfortable. Clean your suede bag carefully to avoid damaging the material. The sofa was covered with soft suede, making it feel luxurious.
urduMeaning: نرم مخملی چمڑا، فیشن اور لباس میں استعمال ہونے والا چمڑا، جوتوں اور فرنیچر کے لیے اعلیٰ معیار کا چمڑا، نرم اور خوبصورت ساخت والا چمڑا
synonyms: Soft leather, Nubuck (similar but not identical), Velvety leather, Leather, Fine leather
antonyms: Patent leather, Glossy leather, Synthetic leather, Plastic material, Vinyl
englishMeaning: A type of soft leather made from the inner side of an animal's skin. It has a smooth, velvety surface and is commonly used for shoes, jackets, bags, gloves, and furniture.  A luxurious type of leather produced from the underside of animal hides, usually from lamb, goat, calf, or deer. It has a soft, fuzzy texture instead of the shiny finish found on regular leather. Suede is valued for its comfort, elegant appearance, and flexibility, but it requires careful maintenance because it stains and absorbs water easily.

sindhiMeaning: لاشعور، اَڻ سجاڳ ذهن، ذهن جو اهو حصو جنهن جي ماڻهوءَ کي پوري ڄاڻ نه هوندي آهي پر جيڪو سوچن، جذبن ۽ رويي تي اثر انداز ٿيندو آهي، ذهن جو اندريون حصو، اُهو جيڪو شعور کان هيٺ هجي
examples: Many of our fears come from the subconscious mind. Dreams often reveal our subconscious thoughts and desires. He had a subconscious fear of failure. Advertisements try to influence the subconscious of viewers. Her subconscious was troubled by the accident she had witnessed.
urduMeaning: لاشعور، تحت الشعور، ذہن کا وہ حصہ جس کا انسان کو مکمل شعور نہیں ہوتا لیکن جو اس کے خیالات، جذبات اور رویے پر اثر انداز ہوتا ہے، ذہن کا اندرونی حصہ، شعور سے نیچے کا
synonyms: Unconscious, Instinctive, Innate, Hidden, Inner, Involuntary, Latent
antonyms: Conscious, Aware, Deliberate, Intentional, Known, Recognised
englishMeaning: The part of the mind that we are not fully aware of but which influences our thoughts, feelings, and behaviour. Existing or operating in the mind without one's awareness. Related to mental activities that happen below the level of conscious thought.

examples: She subconsciously touched her hair whenever she felt nervous. He subconsciously copied his father's way of talking. People subconsciously judge others by their appearance. She was subconsciously afraid of the dark. He subconsciously chose the same restaurant every time.
sindhiMeaning: لاشعوري طور تي، اَڻ سجاڳ ذهن سان، ڄاڻڻ کان سواءِ، بغير ڄاڻ يا سوچ جي، اندروني طور تي، بنا ارادي جي، دل جي اڻ لڀندڙ ڪنڊ کان
englishMeaning: In a way that is not fully conscious. Without being aware of it. Done or felt in the deeper part of the mind that we do not fully notice. Acting from inner feelings, memories, or instincts without deliberate thought.
synonyms: Unconsciously, Instinctively, Unknowingly, Involuntarily, Automatically, Unwittingly
urduMeaning: لاشعوری طور پر، تحت الشعور میں، جانے بغیر، بغیر شعور کے، اندرونی طور پر، بلا ارادہ، ذہن کے پوشیدہ گوشے سے
antonyms: Consciously, Deliberately, Knowingly, Intentionally, Purposely

synonyms: Evolving star, Intermediate star
englishMeaning: In astronomy, a star that is brighter than a normal main-sequence star of the same temperature but not as bright as a true giant star. A star in the stage of evolution between the main sequence and the giant phase, larger and more luminous than the Sun but smaller than a giant.
antonyms: Dwarf, Main-sequence star, Giant, Supergiant
urduMeaning: فلکیات میں ایسا ستارہ جو عام مرکزی تسلسل کے ستارے سے زیادہ روشن ہو مگر جائنٹ ستارے سے چھوٹا ہو، درمیانے درجے کا بڑا ستارہ، ستارے کی زندگی کی درمیانی منزل
examples: Procyon is a well-known example of a subgiant star. Astronomers study subgiants to understand how stars evolve. A subgiant is larger than the Sun but smaller than a giant. The telescope helped scientists identify a new subgiant in the galaxy. Our own Sun will one day become a subgiant.
sindhiMeaning: فلڪيات ۾ اهڙو ستارو جيڪو عام سج جهڙي ستاري کان وڏو ۽ روشن هجي پر جيائنٽ ستاري کان ننڍو، وچين درجي جو وڏو ستارو، ستاري جي زندگيءَ جي وچ واري منزل

examples: The prisoners were forced to live in subhuman conditions. Scientists study subhuman primates to understand evolution. His subhuman treatment of the workers shocked everyone. Slavery reduced people to a subhuman status. The story described the villain as a subhuman monster.
sindhiMeaning: غير انساني، انسان جي درجي کان گهٽ، پستيءَ وارو، وحشي، جانورن جهڙو، هڪ اهڙو جاندار جيڪو انسان جهڙو هجي پر انسان نه، ذليل يا هيڻي درجي وارو، ظالماڻو
synonyms: Bestial, Brutal, Animalistic, Inhuman, Barbaric, Primitive, Degraded
antonyms: Human, Humane, Civilised, Refined, Cultured, Dignified, Superior
urduMeaning: غیر انسانی، انسان کے درجے سے کم، پست، وحشیانہ، جانوروں جیسا، ایک ایسا جاندار جو انسان جیسا ہو مگر انسان نہ ہو، ذلیل یا کم درجے کا، ظالمانہ
englishMeaning: Below the level of human beings in behaviour, ability, or living conditions. Relating to creatures that resemble humans but are not fully human. Sometimes used unkindly or offensively to describe cruel, brutal, or degraded behaviour. In science, referring to primates and animals close to humans in development.

examples: She was too submissive to argue with her strict father. A good soldier must be submissive to the orders of his officers. His submissive nature made others take advantage of him. The dog rolled over in a submissive pose. She had a quiet and submissive manner in front of the elders.
sindhiMeaning: تابعدار، فرمانبردار، عاجز، اطاعت گذار، حڪم مڃيندڙ، ذليل، سِر جهُڪائيندڙ، جيڪو مخالفت نه ڪري، آڻميل، ماتحت رهڻ وارو
englishMeaning: Ready to obey or yield to others without resistance. Willing to accept the authority or control of another. Meek, humble, and unassertive. Showing a tendency to give in to the wishes or demands of others rather than to assert one's own.
urduMeaning: تابعدار، فرمانبردار، مطیع، عاجز، حکم ماننے والا، جھکنے والا، جو مخالفت نہ کرے، سرنگوں، ماتحت رہنے والا
synonyms: Obedient, Compliant, Meek, Yielding, Docile, Passive, Humble, Deferential
antonyms: Rebellious, Defiant, Assertive, Dominant, Disobedient, Stubborn, Resistant

urduMeaning: بعد کا، بعد میں آنے والا، بعد میں ہونے والا، پیرو، اگلا، آئندہ، وہ جو کسی اور چیز کے بعد آئے، بعد کا واقعہ
englishMeaning: Coming after something in time or order. Following something else. Happening or existing later. Used to describe events, actions, or things that occur after a particular point or event.
examples: Subsequent events proved that his warning was correct. The first meeting went well, but subsequent ones were less successful. Details will be shared in a subsequent email. Her subsequent behaviour showed she had learnt her lesson. All subsequent editions of the book include new photographs.
sindhiMeaning: بعد وارو، پوءِ ايندڙ، پُٺيان ايندڙ، ايندڙ، آئندي جو، ٻئي نمبر تي ايندڙ، جيڪو ڪنهن ٻي شيءِ کان پوءِ اچي، بعد ۾ ٿيندڙ
antonyms: Previous, Earlier, Prior, Preceding, Former, Antecedent
synonyms: Following, Later, Next, Ensuing, Succeeding, Successive, After
Afterwards, Later, Then, Thereafter, Following, Next
sindhiMeaning: ان کان پوءِ، بعد ۾، پوءِ، ايندڙ وقت ۾، ٻي ڀيري، پُٺيان، اڳتي هلي، ڪجهه وقت پوءِ
antonyms: Previously, Earlier, Before, Beforehand, Formerly
examples: He was arrested and subsequently released on bail. The report was drafted first and subsequently approved by the committee. She joined the team in January and subsequently became its captain. The building was damaged in the earthquake and subsequently rebuilt. He fell ill and subsequently had to leave the job.
englishMeaning: Afterwards. At a later time. In the period following something. Used to indicate that something happened after another event or action.
urduMeaning: بعد ازاں، بعد میں، اس کے بعد، پھر، آئندہ، آگے چل کر، کچھ عرصے بعد

englishMeaning: Too willing to obey other people. Serving as a means to help achieve a purpose. Ready to do what other people want without questioning. Excessively obedient, often in a way that lacks dignity or self-respect.
examples: He refused to be subservient to his rude boss. Personal interests should be subservient to the good of the nation. Her subservient attitude annoyed her friends. The old system kept the peasants subservient to the landlords. In the film, the servant is shown as always subservient to the family.
antonyms: Dominant, Rebellious, Defiant, Independent, Assertive, Rude, Bold
urduMeaning: تابعدار، ماتحت، خدمت گزار، حد سے زیادہ فرمانبردار، غلامانہ رویہ رکھنے والا، دوسرے کے مقصد کے لیے استعمال ہونے والا، دوسرے کی خواہش کا غلام
synonyms: Obedient, Submissive, Servile, Compliant, Docile, Deferential, Meek
sindhiMeaning: تابعدار، ماتحت، هيٺاهون، غلاماڻو رويو رکندڙ، وڌيڪ فرمانبردار، خدمتگار، ٻئي جي مقصد لاءِ استعمال ٿيندڙ، ٻئي جي خواهش جو غلام، اطاعت گذار
گذارو، پيٽ گذر، روزي، جيئڻ لاءِ گهربل شيون، بقا، جيون گذارڻ جو ذريعو، ٿوري ۾ گذارو ڪرڻ، معمولي روزگار، جياپي جو ذريعو
antonyms: Luxury, Abundance, Wealth, Prosperity, Excess, Comfort
urduMeaning: گزارا، بقا، روزی، زندگی گزارنے کے لیے ضروری چیزیں، معیشت، جینے کا سہارا، تھوڑے میں گزارا، معمولی روزگار، جیون بسر کا ذریعہ
synonyms: Livelihood, Survival, Sustenance, Living, Maintenance, Support, Existence
englishMeaning: The state of having what one needs to stay alive, especially food and shelter. The means of supporting life. A minimum level of existence. The ability to continue living on very little. Basic livelihood.
examples: Many farmers in the area live at a subsistence level. Fishing provides the main means of subsistence for the villagers. The government promised support for those who could not earn their subsistence. The poor family struggled for daily subsistence. Subsistence farming is common in remote hilly regions.

urduMeaning: معیاری نہ، معیار سے کم، خراب معیار کا، کم درجے کا، عام سے کمتر، ناقص، ہلکی قسم کا، کمتر قدر والا
synonyms: Inferior, Poor, Second-rate, Low-quality, Deficient, Unsatisfactory, Shoddy
sindhiMeaning: معياري نه، معيار کان گهٽ، خراب معيار جو، ٿوري درجي جو، نچلي درجي جو، عام کان گهٽيا، ناقص، هلڪي قسم جو، ڪم قدر وارو
antonyms: Superior, High-quality, Excellent, First-rate, Standard, Satisfactory, Premium
englishMeaning: Below the usual or required standard. Not as good as it should be. Of lower quality than expected. Failing to meet accepted norms in quality, condition, or performance.
examples: The building was demolished because of substandard construction. Many people live in substandard housing in the city outskirts. The company was fined for selling substandard products. His work has been substandard for the past few months. Substandard food was found in the storeroom during the inspection.

urduMeaning: بدل، متبادل، نائب، جانشین، دوسرے کی جگہ رکھنا یا آنا، کسی کی جگہ دوسرا رکھنا، متبادل چیز، جگہ بھرنے والا، عارضی طور پر کام کرنے والا
sindhiMeaning: بدل، عيوضي، نائب، جاءِ نشين، ٻئي جي جاءِ تي رکڻ يا اچڻ، متبادل، ڪنهن جي جاءِ تي ٻيو رکڻ، جاءِ ڀرڻ وارو، ڪم هلائيندڙ
examples: You can substitute honey for sugar in this recipe. The teacher was absent, so a substitute took the class. Butter is a good substitute for oil in baking. He came on as a substitute in the second half. There is no substitute for hard work.
antonyms: Original, Real, Regular, Permanent, Genuine
synonyms: Replacement, Alternative, Stand-in, Deputy, Proxy, Surrogate, Reserve
englishMeaning: A person or thing that takes the place of another. To use one thing in place of another. To replace someone or something with a different one. A player who takes another's place in a game. Something used instead of what is usually used.

examples: He used subterfuge to enter the meeting without an invitation. The spy relied on subterfuge to gather secret information. She obtained the money through subterfuge. Politicians sometimes use subterfuge to hide the truth. The children invented a subterfuge to skip school.
urduMeaning: چالبازی، فریب، بہانہ، حیلہ، مکاری، دھوکہ، ہاتھ کی صفائی، جھوٹ سے کام نکالنا، ایسا طریقہ جس سے سچ چھپایا جائے
sindhiMeaning: چالبازي، ٺڳي، بهانو، حيلو، فريب، مڪر، هٿ چراند، ڪوڙ سان ڪم ڪڍڻ، دوکو، حيلي بازي، اهڙو طريقو جنهن سان سچ لڪايو وڃي
antonyms: Honesty, Truthfulness, Openness, Sincerity, Frankness, Candour
synonyms: Deception, Trickery, Deceit, Ruse, Ploy, Fraud, Cunning, Guile
englishMeaning: A trick or dishonest way used to achieve a goal or to escape a difficult situation. Deception used to hide the truth or to gain an advantage. A clever plan or action designed to deceive.

examples: The ancient alchemical texts often refer to a subtile essence that pervades all matter. She possessed a subtile mind that could easily dismantle the most complex philosophical ideas. The chef used a subtile blend of spices that enhanced rather than overpowered the meat. He employed a subtile strategy to outmaneuver his opponents without them noticing. There was a subtile difference in the texture of the two fabrics that only an expert could detect.
urduMeaning: لطیف، باریک، نازک، دقیق، پیچیدہ، نفیس، پراسرار، شاطر، چالاک، سمجھنے میں مشکل
synonyms: Fine, Delicate, Elusive, Refined, Acute, Astute, Cunning, Shrewd, Tenuous, Rarefied
englishMeaning: Having a comparatively fine, delicate, or thin physical layer or structure. Difficult to perceive or grasp completely due to extreme delicacy, faintness, or elusiveness. Characterized by intellectual cleverness, shrewdness, or cunning in a way that is not immediately obvious. Manifesting fine distinctions or delicate sensitivity in thought, argument, or analysis. Operating in a hidden, insidious, or highly refined manner without drawing attention. Known historically to describe something thinly composed or rarefied, such as a subtile gas or ether.
sindhiMeaning: باريڪ، لطيف، نازڪ، نفيس، ڏاهو، اونهو، ڳجهو، پرکڻ ۾ ڏکيو، هلڪو، چالاڪ، عيار
antonyms: Coarse, Dense, Thick, Obvious, Blatant, Clumsy, Unrefined, Heavy

synonyms: Outskirts, Neighbourhood, Township, Residential area, Outlying district, Locality
englishMeaning: A residential area or district on the outer edge of a city or large town. A place where people live outside the busy city centre. An outlying part of a town that is mainly residential and quieter than the centre.
urduMeaning: شہر کا مضافاتی علاقہ، شہر کے کنارے پر رہائشی علاقہ، شہر کے باہر کا محلہ، شہری کنارے کا علاقہ، شہر کے قریب کی آبادی، شہر کی حد سے باہر کی بستی
antonyms: City centre, Downtown, Urban core, Metropolis, Countryside
sindhiMeaning: شهر جي ڪنڊ يا ٻاهرين حد وارو علائقو، شهر جا مضافات، شهر جو ٻاهريون رهائشي علائقو، مضافاتي علائقو، شهر جي پاسي وارو رهائشي علائقو، شهري ڪناري جو علائقو
examples: They moved to a quiet suburb of Karachi last year. Property prices in the suburb are lower than in the city centre. Many people commute daily from the suburbs to work in the city. The new school was built in a growing suburb. Life in the suburb is peaceful and family friendly.

antonyms: Support, Loyalty, Obedience, Defence, Preservation, Strengthening, Allegiance
synonyms: Overthrow, Sabotage, Undermining, Rebellion, Insurrection, Corruption, Weakening
englishMeaning: The act of trying to destroy or weaken a government, system, or authority, often from within. Secret action to overthrow or damage an established order. The undermining of the power, authority, or principles of an institution.
sindhiMeaning: اُٿل پُٿل، بغاوت، ڪنهن حڪومت يا نظام کي تباهه ڪرڻ جي ڪوشش، حڪومت خلاف سازش، حڪومت جو تختو اُپٽڻ جي ڪوشش، خفيه طور تي نظام کي ڪمزور ڪرڻ، انتشار پکيڙڻ
urduMeaning: تخریب، بغاوت، کسی حکومت یا نظام کو کمزور یا ختم کرنے کی کوشش، حکومت کے خلاف سازش، تختہ الٹنے کی کوشش، خفیہ طور پر نظام کو ناکارہ بنانا
examples: He was arrested on charges of subversion against the state. The government took strict action against acts of subversion. Foreign powers were accused of subversion of the peaceful nation. The book was banned for promoting subversion of religious values. Subversion of the rules cannot be allowed in any organisation.

englishMeaning: To try to destroy or damage a government, system, or set of beliefs. To secretly weaken the authority or power of something. To overturn or overthrow. To undermine the principles or effectiveness of an established institution.
synonyms: Overthrow, Undermine, Destabilise, Sabotage, Weaken, Corrupt, Ruin
antonyms: Support, Strengthen, Uphold, Preserve, Defend, Reinforce, Maintain
urduMeaning: تختہ الٹنا، تخریب کرنا، کسی نظام یا حکومت کو کمزور کرنا، برباد کرنا، جڑیں ہلانا، اصولوں کو نقصان پہنچانا، خفیہ طور پر خراب کرنا
examples: They tried to subvert the government through false propaganda. Corruption can subvert the entire justice system. His writings were said to subvert the moral values of the youth. The general was accused of trying to subvert democracy. Small lies can slowly subvert trust in a relationship.
sindhiMeaning: اُٿل پُٿل ڪرڻ، ڪنهن نظام يا حڪومت کي ڪمزور ڪرڻ، تباهه ڪرڻ، تختو اُپٽڻ، پاڙون هلائڻ، اصولن کي نقصان پهچائڻ، خفيه طور خراب ڪرڻ

antonyms: Predecessor, Ancestor, Forerunner, Founder, Precursor
synonyms: Heir, Follower, Replacement, Descendant, Inheritor, Next in line
englishMeaning: A person or thing that comes after another and takes their position, job, or role. Someone who inherits a title, office, or property. Something that replaces an earlier version of the same kind.
sindhiMeaning: جاءِ نشين، پُٺيان ايندڙ، وارث، جاٿ لهندڙ، ڪنهن جي جاءِ تي ايندڙ شخص، عهدو سنڀاليندڙ، اڳوڻي جو نائب، جاءِ ڀرڻ وارو
examples: His son was named as his successor in the family business. The king had no successor to inherit the throne. The new model is a worthy successor to the previous one. She was appointed successor to the retiring principal. Every leader must prepare a capable successor.
urduMeaning: جانشین، وارث، بعد میں آنے والا، کسی کی جگہ لینے والا، عہدہ سنبھالنے والا، سابقہ کا قائم مقام، جگہ لینے والا

examples: His sudden departure surprised everyone at the office. A sudden storm ruined our picnic plans. She felt a sudden pain in her chest. There was a sudden silence in the room. The sudden change in weather caught the farmers off guard.
sindhiMeaning: اوچتو، اچانڪ، هڪدم، بنا اطلاع جي، ايڪدم، ذري گهڙيءَ ۾، فوري، جيڪو گهڻي ڀاڱي بغير ڪنهن پيشگي خبر جي ٿئي، اُڏامندو
urduMeaning: اچانک، ناگہاں، دفعتاً، یکایک، بغیر اطلاع کے، فوری، ایسا جو بغیر پیشگی خبر کے ہو، بلا خبر، غیر متوقع
antonyms: Gradual, Slow, Expected, Anticipated, Predictable, Planned, Steady
synonyms: Abrupt, Unexpected, Immediate, Quick, Swift, Instant, Unforeseen, Startling
englishMeaning: Happening or coming quickly and without warning. Occurring unexpectedly. Done, made, or occurring without prior notice or preparation. Abrupt in nature.

The right to vote in political elections. The exercise of such a right. In older usage, a short prayer or plea, especially one offered in a religious service. The system by which people choose their representatives through voting.
urduMeaning: حقِ رائے دہی، ووٹ دینے کا حق، ووٹ، انتخابات میں شرکت کا اختیار، عوامی رائے، (پرانی معنیٰ) مختصر دعا، سفارش
examples: Women had to fight for many years to win suffrage. Universal suffrage means that all adult citizens have the right to vote. The reform gave suffrage to millions of new voters. He wrote a famous book on the history of women's suffrage. Suffrage is a basic feature of democracy.
antonyms: Disenfranchisement, Denial, Suppression, Voicelessness
sindhiMeaning: ووٽ ڏيڻ جو حق، راءِ ڏيڻ جو حق، چونڊ ۾ حصو وٺڻ جو اختيار، عوامي راءِ، ووٽ، (پراڻي معنيٰ) مختصر دعا، سفارش

englishMeaning: Characterized by strong and turbulent emotions. Extremely stormy or violent, as of weather. Full of anger, excitement, or intense conflict. Very heated and unpredictable in nature or behavior.
examples: Their marriage was tempestuous from the very beginning. A tempestuous wind blew across the coast all night. She had a tempestuous relationship with her business partner. The meeting turned into a tempestuous debate over the new policy. He is known for his tempestuous temper and sudden outbursts.
urduMeaning: طوفانی، شدید، پرجوش، جذباتی طور پر ہنگامہ خیز، سخت جھگڑالو، غصے اور جوش سے بھرپور، تیز موسم والا، غیر متوقع اور ہنگامی
synonyms: Stormy, Turbulent, Wild, Violent, Fierce, Furious, Passionate, Volatile, Tumultuous

englishMeaning: A building used for religious worship, especially in non-Christian faiths such as Hinduism, Buddhism, and Sikhism. A place regarded as being occupied by a god or gods. The flat area on each side of the forehead. The side piece of a pair of spectacles.
sindhiMeaning: مندر، پوڄا جو هنڌ، عبادت گاهه، ديوتائن جو گهر، ڪنارو جبين، مٿي جي پاسي وارو حصو، عينڪ جي پاسي واري ڏانڊي
antonyms: Marketplace, Battlefield, Wilderness; (Figurative) Profane place
synonyms: Shrine, Sanctuary, Place of worship, Church, Mosque, House of God; (Anatomy) Side of forehead
urduMeaning: مندر، عبادت گاہ، پوجا کا مقام، دیوتاؤں کا گھر، پیشانی کے اطراف کا حصہ، کنپٹی، عینک کی کمانی کا پہلو
examples: The ancient temple attracts thousands of pilgrims every year. He bowed his head as he entered the temple. She felt a sudden pain in her temple. The old temple was built more than a thousand years ago. He gently rubbed his temples to ease the headache.

The offer of a free trip tempted her to sign the contract. Do not tempt him with sweets before dinner. The delicious smell of food tempted us to enter the restaurant. He was tempted to accept the bribe but refused. Don't tempt fate by driving in this storm.
synonyms: Entice, Lure, Attract, Seduce, Persuade, Coax, Allure, Invite, Provoke
englishMeaning: To try to persuade someone to do something, especially something wrong or unwise. To attract someone by offering something desirable. To arouse a desire in someone. To risk provoking, as in 'tempt fate'.
urduMeaning: لالچ دینا، ورغلانا، بہکانا، دل میں خواہش پیدا کرنا، ترغیب دینا، آزمائش میں ڈالنا، مائل کرنا، اکسانا
sindhiMeaning: لالچ ڏيڻ، ورغلائڻ، بهڪائڻ، دل ۾ خواهش پيدا ڪرڻ، ڪنهن ڪم لاءِ راغب ڪرڻ، آزمائش ۾ وجهڻ، لالچائڻ، ڀڙڪائڻ
antonyms: Repel, Discourage, Deter, Dissuade, Warn, Put off, Repulse

sindhiMeaning: ورغلائيندڙ، لالچ ڏيندڙ، آزمائش ۾ وجهندڙ، بهڪائيندڙ شخص، غلط ڪم ڏانهن ڇڪيندڙ، شيطان (خاص طور تي مذهبي حوالي سان)
antonyms: Protector, Guide, Advisor, Deterrent, Saint, Preserver
synonyms: Seducer, Enticer, Deceiver, Beguiler, Corrupter, Devil, Satan, Lure
englishMeaning: A person or thing that tempts, especially to do wrong. One who entices someone into evil or unwise action. In religious texts, often used as a name for the Devil or Satan.
examples: He proved to be a dangerous tempter for the young boys. The tempter offered him money in exchange for silence. In the story, the tempter appears as a friendly stranger. She refused to listen to the tempter's promises. According to the Bible, the Tempter deceived Adam and Eve.
urduMeaning: ورغلانے والا، لالچ دینے والا، آزمائش میں ڈالنے والا، بہکانے والا، بُرے کام کی طرف مائل کرنے والا، شیطان (خصوصاً مذہبی حوالے سے)
ورغلانے والی عورت، دل موہ لینے والی، حسین اور دلکش عورت، مردوں کو مائل کرنے والی، فتنہ انگیز عورت، دل فریب عورت
antonyms: Nun, Puritan, Prude, Repeller, Innocent, Modest woman
sindhiMeaning: ورغلائيندڙ عورت، دل ڦسائيندڙ عورت، حسين ۽ لالچائيندڙ عورت، مردن کي ڇڪيندڙ عورت، دلبر عورت، فتنه انگيز عورت
englishMeaning: A woman who tempts or attracts someone, especially into sexual or immoral behavior. A seductive or alluring female. A woman who deliberately entices others.
examples: In the film, she plays the role of a mysterious temptress. He described her as a dangerous temptress with a charming smile. The novel's temptress leads the hero into serious trouble. She was often unfairly labeled as a temptress by her critics. The painting shows a temptress in a red gown.
synonyms: Seductress, Enchantress, Siren, Flirt, Coquette, Vamp, Charmer

antonyms: Confidently, Definitely, Firmly, Boldly, Decisively, Certainly, Assuredly
urduMeaning: غیر یقینی طور پر، جھجک کر، احتیاط سے، آزمائشی طور پر، عارضی طور پر، بغیر حتمی فیصلے کے، شک اور احتیاط کے ساتھ
englishMeaning: In a way that is not certain or definite. Hesitantly and with caution. As a first attempt that may be changed later. Provisionally, subject to confirmation.
synonyms: Hesitantly, Cautiously, Provisionally, Uncertainly, Warily, Timidly, Doubtfully
sindhiMeaning: غير يقيني نموني، جهجهڪ سان، احتياط سان، آزمائشي طور، عارضي طور، بغير حتمي فيصلي جي، شڪ ۽ احتياط سان
examples: The meeting has been tentatively scheduled for next Monday. She tentatively agreed to join the project team. He tentatively stepped forward to speak. The date of the wedding was fixed tentatively for December. They tentatively suggested a new price for the product.

sindhiMeaning: اصطلاحات، ڪنهن خاص علم يا شعبي ۾ استعمال ٿيندڙ خاص لفظ، اصطلاحي زبان، فني لفظن جو مجموعو، خاص شعبي جي لغت
examples: Medical terminology can be very difficult for beginners. He is well-versed in legal terminology. The book explains scientific terminology in simple language. Different fields have their own specific terminology. Students should learn the correct terminology of their subject.
urduMeaning: اصطلاحات، کسی خاص علم یا شعبے میں استعمال ہونے والے مخصوص الفاظ، اصطلاحی زبان، فنی الفاظ کا مجموعہ، خاص شعبے کی لغت
englishMeaning: The body of terms used in a particular subject, profession, or field of study. The special language and vocabulary of a specialized area. The system of technical terms and their usage.
synonyms: Vocabulary, Jargon, Nomenclature, Language, Lexicon, Terms, Wording, Phraseology
antonyms: Common speech, Everyday language, Plain words, Layman's terms

examples: Frogs are amphibious, while lizards are largely terrestrial animals. The book compares terrestrial and marine ecosystems. Most terrestrial channels are still popular in rural areas. Scientists have long searched for extra-terrestrial life. The terrestrial climate varies greatly from region to region.
englishMeaning: Relating to or existing on the earth or land. Living on or in the ground, as opposed to in water, air, or trees. Of or belonging to this world rather than heaven or outer space. Broadcasting from stations on the ground rather than by satellite.
synonyms: Earthly, Earthbound, Worldly, Land, Ground, Mundane, Global
sindhiMeaning: زميني، ڌرتيءَ سان لاڳاپيل، خشڪيءَ تي رهندڙ، دنيوي، هن دنيا سان تعلق رکندڙ، ڌرتيءَ جو، سيٽلائيٽ کان علاوه زميني نشرياتي
antonyms: Celestial, Heavenly, Aquatic, Marine, Aerial, Extraterrestrial
urduMeaning: زمینی، زمین سے تعلق رکھنے والا، خشکی پر رہنے والا، دنیاوی، اس دنیا کا، ارضی، سیٹلائٹ کے بجائے زمینی نشریاتی

englishMeaning: A small, active breed of dog originally bred to hunt small animals in burrows. A brave and energetic dog of various small breeds. Figuratively, a person who is persistent and tenacious.
antonyms: Cat, Feline, (Figurative) Quitter, Slacker
sindhiMeaning: هڪ ننڍي قسم جو شڪاري ڪتو، جيڪو ننڍا جانور شڪار ڪرڻ لاءِ پاليو ويندو آهي، سرگرم ۽ بهادر ننڍڙو ڪتو، جفاڪش شخص لاءِ به استعمال
urduMeaning: ایک چھوٹی نسل کا شکاری کتا جو چھوٹے جانوروں کے شکار کے لیے پالا جاتا ہے، پھرتیلا اور بہادر چھوٹا کتا، مجازاً محنتی اور ثابت قدم شخص
examples: He keeps a small terrier as a pet at home. The terrier chased the rat into the field. Yorkshire terriers are very popular family dogs. She is a real terrier when it comes to finishing her work. The farmer's terrier barked all night at the intruders.
synonyms: Dog, Hound, Pup, Canine, Hunting dog

antonyms: Comfort, Calm, Reassure, Soothe, Encourage, Relax, Please
sindhiMeaning: خوف ۾ وجهڻ، ڊيڄارڻ، سخت ڊپ ڏيڻ، دهشت وجهڻ، دل ڏاري وجهڻ، سخت خوفزده ڪرڻ
synonyms: Frighten, Scare, Horrify, Alarm, Panic, Petrify, Shock, Startle, Intimidate
examples: The loud thunder began to terrify the little children. The idea of speaking in public terrifies her. Horror movies used to terrify me as a child. The sudden fire terrified everyone in the building. Do not terrify the poor animal by shouting at it.
englishMeaning: To cause someone to feel extreme fear. To frighten severely. To fill with terror or dread. To scare intensely.
urduMeaning: دہشت زدہ کرنا، شدید خوف میں مبتلا کرنا، ڈرا دینا، خوف طاری کرنا، دل دہلا دینا، حواس باختہ کر دینا

synonyms: Regional, Local, Provincial, Protective, Possessive, Jurisdictional, Geographic
sindhiMeaning: علائقائي، ڪنهن علائقي سان لاڳاپيل، پنهنجي حد جي حفاظت ڪندڙ، پنهنجي ملڪيت جي حفاظت ۾ سخت، ملڪي حدن سان تعلق رکندڙ
examples: The country protects its territorial waters with a strong navy. Dogs can become very territorial when strangers enter the house. There is an old territorial dispute between the two nations. He is quite territorial about his desk at the office. Many animals are naturally territorial by instinct.
urduMeaning: علاقائی، کسی علاقے سے متعلق، اپنی حدود کی حفاظت کرنے والا، اپنی ملکیت کے بارے میں حساس، ملکی حدود سے متعلق
englishMeaning: Relating to the ownership of an area of land or sea. Showing strong defensive attitudes toward one's area, possessions, or rights. Belonging to a particular territory. Relating to a country's land or waters.
antonyms: International, Global, Universal, Shared, Communal, Neutral

englishMeaning: A person's will, especially the part dealing with personal property. Something that serves as clear evidence or proof of a specified fact or quality. Either of the two main divisions of the Christian Bible (Old Testament and New Testament).
antonyms: Denial, Contradiction, Disproof, Refutation
urduMeaning: وصیت نامہ، وصیت، شہادت، واضح ثبوت، کسی بات کا کھلا ثبوت، بائبل کے دو بڑے حصوں میں سے ایک (پرانا یا نیا عہد نامہ)
sindhiMeaning: وصيت نامو، وصيت، شاهدي، ثبوت، ڪنهن ڳالهه جو کليل ثبوت، بائيبل جو ٻن مکيه حصن مان هڪ (پراڻو يا نئون عهد نامو)
examples: His success is a testament to his hard work and dedication. She wrote her last will and testament before the operation. The building stands as a testament to fine craftsmanship. He often read the New Testament in the evenings. Her calm behavior is a testament to her strong character.
synonyms: Proof, Evidence, Witness, Tribute, Demonstration, Will, Legacy

antonyms: Criticism, Complaint, Denunciation, Rejection, Condemnation, Dispraise
sindhiMeaning: توثيقي بيان، سفارشي خط، ڪنهن جي خوبين جي تعريف ۾ لکيل بيان، ڪنهن جي شخصيت يا لياقت جي شاهدي، عزت ۽ قدرداني جو اظهار
examples: The company website is full of customer testimonials. His former boss wrote him an excellent testimonial. The team organized a testimonial match in honor of the retiring player. She read the testimonial aloud at the farewell party. The book contains testimonials from famous scientists.

synonyms: Recommendation, Reference, Endorsement, Tribute, Commendation, Certificate, Praise
englishMeaning: A formal statement testifying to someone's character and qualifications. A public expression of appreciation or admiration. A written or spoken recommendation given by a customer or user. An event held to honor someone.

synonyms: Evidence, Statement, Deposition, Witness, Affidavit, Proof, Attestation, Declaration
examples: The witness gave her testimony before the judge. His life is a living testimony to the power of faith. The lawyer challenged the testimony of the main witness. Her achievements are a testimony to years of hard work. Several people offered testimony in support of the accused.
urduMeaning: شہادت، گواہی، عدالت میں حلف اٹھا کر دیا گیا بیان، ثبوت، کسی بات کا واضح ثبوت، مذہبی سیاق میں ذاتی تجربے کا اظہار
sindhiMeaning: شاهدي، گواهي، عدالت ۾ قسم کڻي ڏنل بيان، ثبوت، ڪنهن ڳالهه جو کليل ثبوت، مذهبي حوالي سان ذاتي تجربي جو اظهار
englishMeaning: A formal written or spoken statement, especially one given in a court of law. Evidence or proof provided by the existence or appearance of something. A public declaration of a personal experience or belief, especially in a religious context.

examples: The thatcher climbed onto the roof to begin his work. Only a skilled thatcher can produce such a neat finish. The village thatcher has been working for over forty years. She hired a thatcher to repair the old cottage roof. The thatcher explained how long the new roof would last.

antonyms: Roof breaker, Demolisher, Wrecker

antonyms: Naturally, Simply, Plainly, Modestly, Quietly, Undramatically, Subtly
sindhiMeaning: ناٽڪي انداز ۾، مبالغي سان، ڊرامائي طور تي، ڏيکاءَ لاءِ، جذباتي ۽ نمائشي نموني، اسٽيج جي انداز ۾
urduMeaning: ڈرامائی انداز میں، مبالغہ آرائی کے ساتھ، تھیٹر کے انداز میں، نمائشی طور پر، جذباتی اور دکھاوے کے ساتھ، اسٹیج کے انداز میں

englishMeaning: In a way that is exaggerated for dramatic effect. In a manner suited to the theatre. In a showy, expressive, or overly dramatic style.
synonyms: Dramatically, Showily, Ostentatiously, Melodramatically, Expressively, Extravagantly

antonyms: Partially, Incompletely, Superficially, Carelessly, Hastily, Slightly, Barely
sindhiMeaning: چڱيءَ طرح، پوريءَ ريت، مڪمل نموني، غور سان، هر لحاظ کان، مڪمل طور، هر پهلوءَ سان چڱي طرح، احتياط ۽ پوري ڌيان سان
urduMeaning: اچھی طرح، مکمل طور پر، پوری طرح، ہر لحاظ سے، تسلی بخش انداز میں، تفصیل سے، غور سے، احتیاط کے ساتھ
englishMeaning: In a complete and careful way; leaving nothing undone. Very much; to a great degree. In every respect; entirely. With attention to every detail.
examples: Please read the instructions thoroughly before starting the exam. She thoroughly enjoyed her holiday in the mountains. The room was thoroughly cleaned before the guests arrived. He thoroughly investigated every detail of the case. I am thoroughly convinced of his honesty.
synonyms: Completely, Fully, Entirely, Wholly, Totally, Carefully, Meticulously, Utterly, Absolutely

antonyms: Single, Halved, Reduced, One-fold, Diminished
englishMeaning: Three times as great or as numerous. Consisting of three parts, elements, or aspects. Multiplied by three. Having three components.
sindhiMeaning: ٽيڻ، ٽي ڀيرا، ٽن حصن تي مشتمل، ٽيڻ وڌيڪ، ٽن پاسن وارو، ٽي درجا
examples: The population of the city has increased threefold in twenty years. His plan has a threefold purpose: education, health, and jobs. Profits grew threefold after the new product was launched. The threefold benefits of exercise include strength, stamina, and health. She achieved a threefold rise in her business income.
urduMeaning: تین گنا، تہرا، تین حصوں پر مشتمل، تین گنا زیادہ، تین پہلوؤں والا، تین درجے

antonyms: Ode of joy, Celebration, Hymn of praise, Anthem, Song of joy
urduMeaning: مرثیہ، سوگ کا گیت، کسی مرحوم کی یاد میں لکھی گئی نظم، غم و اندوہ کا گیت، ماتمی کلام، نوحہ
examples: The poet wrote a moving threnody for his late friend. A soft threnody was played at the funeral service. Her novel ends with a threnody for the lost city. The composer's most famous work is a threnody for the war dead. He recited a heartfelt threnody in memory of his mother.

englishMeaning: A song, hymn, or poem of mourning composed or performed as a memorial to a dead person. A lament or elegy expressing grief and sorrow.
synonyms: Elegy, Lament, Dirge, Requiem, Mourning song, Funeral hymn, Ode of grief

sindhiMeaning: بيحد خوش، جذبات ۾ آيل، سرشار، خوشيءَ ۾ ڀرپور، جوش ۾ آيل، نهايت مسرور، جذباتي طور تي خوش
synonyms: Delighted, Excited, Overjoyed, Elated, Pleased, Ecstatic, Enchanted, Exhilarated
urduMeaning: بہت خوش، جذبات میں آیا ہوا، سرشار، فرطِ مسرت میں مبتلا، پرجوش، نہایت خوش، جوش و خروش سے بھرا ہوا
antonyms: Disappointed, Displeased, Bored, Sad, Depressed, Unhappy, Indifferent
englishMeaning: Extremely pleased, excited, or delighted about something. Filled with a sudden feeling of intense joy or excitement. Very happy because of a pleasant surprise or achievement.

urduMeaning: دھڑکنا، پھڑکنا، درد سے ٹیس اٹھنا، دل کا تیز دھڑکنا، رگ کا پھڑکنا، تیز نبض، شدت سے دھڑکن ہونا
sindhiMeaning: ڦڙڪڻ، تيزيءَ سان ڌڙڪڻ، درد ۾ ڦڙڪڻ، دل جو زور سان ڌڙڪڻ، رڳ جو ڦڙڪڻ، ڌڙڪ، تيز نبض
antonyms: Be still, Calm, Rest, Ease, Stop, Cease, Steady

synonyms: Pulse, Beat, Pound, Thump, Pulsate, Palpitate, Ache, Vibrate
examples: Her heart began to throb with excitement. His head throbbed painfully after the long journey. The wound on his hand throbbed all night. She could feel the throb of the drums during the parade. A dull throb of pain returned to his back.

antonyms: Individual, Few, Handful, Emptiness, Solitude, Scatter
sindhiMeaning: ميڙ، هجوم، ماڻهن جي وڏي ڀيڙ، انبوهه، گڏ ٿي هڪ هنڌ جمع ٿيڻ، ٽچرو، پيدل ماڻهن جو رش

examples: A huge throng gathered outside the palace to see the king. Fans thronged the stadium hours before the match. The market was thronging with shoppers on the eve of Eid. A throng of children surrounded the ice-cream vendor. Pilgrims throng to the holy city every year.
synonyms: Crowd, Multitude, Mob, Horde, Swarm, Mass, Assembly, Gathering
englishMeaning: A large, densely packed crowd of people or animals. To gather in large numbers in a particular place. To crowd or press together. A great multitude assembled in one place.

examples: The shopkeeper was attacked by a group of thugs at night. Police arrested the thug who had been terrorizing the neighborhood. He behaves like a thug whenever he loses his temper. A gang of thugs robbed the passengers on the highway. The film is based on the story of an old-time thug.

englishMeaning: An involuntary quivering movement or a slight shake, often resulting from physical weakness or emotional stress. In a geological context, it refers to a minor earthquake or a series of vibrations in the earth's crust. It can also describe a slight variation in a musical tone or pitch. Medically, it is a rhythmic, purposeless contraction of muscles. The term generally suggests a movement that is less violent than a full-scale quake or convulsion.
urduMeaning: لرزش، تھرتھراہٹ، جھٹکا، زلزلے کا ہلکا جھٹکا، جسم میں ہونے والی ہلکی کپکپی
examples: The doctor noticed a slight tremor in the patient's right hand. Several small tremors were felt in the region following the main earthquake. A tremor of excitement ran through the crowd as the celebrity appeared. The elderly man's voice had a noticeable tremor when he spoke of the past. Tiny tremors on the water's surface suggested that fish were feeding nearby.
synonyms: Shake, Vibration, Quiver, Shudder, Spasm, Quake, Throb, Flutter, Ripple, Twitch

sindhiMeaning: مصيبت، ڏکيو وقت، آفت، سخت آزمائش، اهنج، تڪليف جنهن ۾ صبر جو امتحان هجي، ڏاکڙو، ايذاءُ، ڪٺن گهڙي جنهن مان گذرڻ مشڪل هجي
synonyms: Suffering, Hardship, Adversity, Affliction, Misery, Woe, Ordeal, Trial, Distress, Pain
examples: The family faced great tribulation after the sudden loss of their home. Every leader must find the strength to guide others through times of tribulation. Faith is often tested most severely during periods of deep tribulation.
englishMeaning: A state of great trouble, suffering, or distress that often feels overwhelming. It refers to severe trials or afflictions that test a person's endurance and spirit. In a historical or religious context, it often denotes a period of great suffering before a divine intervention. The term describes the intense pressure or hardship one faces in life's most difficult moments. It is commonly used to describe deep personal sorrow or collective hardship during a crisis.
urduMeaning: مصیبت، آزمائش، سخت تکليف، دکھ، آفت، رنج و ملال، شديد پریشانی جنهن ۾ انسان صبر و استقلال سے کام لے، ابتلا، دکھ بھرا وقت
antonyms: Joy, Happiness, Peace, Comfort, Prosperity, Success, Relief, Contentment

synonyms: Jog, Run, Scuttle, Scurry, Scamper, Canter, Amble, Hike, Dash, Pace
sindhiMeaning: کڙڪو، سنبڙ تڪڙو هلڻ، گهوڙي جي ساهي جهڙي چال، تڪڙو قدم کڻڻ، ننڍن قدمن سان ڊوڙڻ، تڪڙي هل چال

The act of moving at this particular speed or a period of such movement.
urduMeaning: دُلکی چلنا، تیز قدم چلنا، سبک رفتاری، گھوڑے کی ایک خاص چال جس میں وہ قدم تیزی سے اٹھاتا ہے، تیزی سے جانا

Attendant, Regular, Diligent, Studious, Reliable, Present, Constant, Faithful
englishMeaning: A student who stays away from school without leave or explanation. It refers to anyone who shirks their duty or neglects their responsibilities by being absent. In a broader sense, it refers to an idle or lazy person who avoids work.
sindhiMeaning: ڀڄڻو، اسڪول مان ڀڄي ويندڙ شاگرد، پنهنجي فرض کان لنوايندڙ، غير حاضر رهندڙ ٻار، ڪم چور، آواره گرد

synonyms: Absentee, Shirker, Slacker, Vagrant, Runaway, Idler, Absent, Delinquent, Stray, Nonparticipant
examples: The school counselor called the parents to discuss the student's truant behavior. Several truants were seen hanging out at the mall during school hours. synonyms: Defiant, Aggressive, Belligerent, Pugnacious, Hostile, Combative, Surly, Fierce, Quarrelsome, Antagonistic

sindhiMeaning: ويڙهاڪ، جهڳڙو ڪندڙ، مڇريل، وحشي، سخت گير، خونخوار، لڙائيءَ لاءِ تيار رهندڙ، ظالم، بي رحم طبيعت وارو
urduMeaning: لڑاکا، جھگڑالو، سرکش، وحشی، تند خو، لڑنے مرنے پر تیار رہنے والا، درندہ صفت، کٹھور، نہایت جارحانہ مزاج رکھنے والا

synonyms: Fall, Topple, Plumb, Drop, Plump, Roll, Spill, Cascade, Flop, Slump
sindhiMeaning: ڪرڻ، قلابازي کائڻ، ٿيڙ کائڻ، لڙهڻ، مٿان کان هيٺ ڪرڻ، مٿي کان پيرن تائين ڪلابازي
examples: The toddler took a clumsy tumble but quickly got back up and laughed. Stock prices began to tumble as soon as the news of the scandal broke. urduMeaning: گرنا، ٹھوکر کھانا، قلابازی کھانا، نیچے آنا، ڈھیر ہونا، مندی آنا، تیزی سے گرنا

sindhiMeaning: تدفين، مٽيءَ جي ڍير يا قبر ۾ پورڻ، قبر بڻائڻ جو عمل، مائت کي دفن ڪرڻ
antonyms: Exhumation, Disinterment, Unearthing, Resurrection, Exposure, Leveling
synonyms: Burial, Interment, Entombment, Sepulture, Inhumation, Funeral, Deposition, Grave-making
englishMeaning: The act of placing a body in a grave or a tomb. The process of burying someone or the state of being interred. This term is often found in historical or poetic descriptions of funerals and ancient burial rites.
examples: The ancient king's tumulation was marked by a massive stone monument. Archaeologists studied the site of the tumulation to learn about the tribe's customs. The process of tumulation in that culture involved placing gold with the deceased. After the battle, the soldiers were honored with a collective tumulation. Historical records describe the solemn tumulation of the fallen hero.

englishMeaning: A vast, flat, treeless Arctic region of Europe, Asia, and North America in which the subsoil is permanently frozen. The environment is characterized by extremely cold temperatures, little precipitation, and a short growing season. Vegetation typically consists of mosses, lichens, herbs, and small shrubs. antonyms: Tropics, Jungle, Desert, Rainforest, Savannah, Grassland
sindhiMeaning: برفاڻو پٽ، اتر قطب جي هڪ وڏي بي وڻ واري پٽي، ڄميل زمين وارو علائقو جتي وڻ نه ٿين

synonyms: Steppe, Heath, Arctic plain, Frozen waste, Permafrost region, Barren land, Treeless plain, Moorland
examples: The permafrost of the tundra makes it impossible for deep-rooted trees to grow. Arctic foxes are well-adapted to the harsh conditions of the snowy tundra. Explorers faced sub-zero temperatures while crossing the vast Siberian tundra.

antonyms: Discordant, Cacophonous, Inharmonious, Harsh, Piercing, Monotonous, Unmusical, Jangled

synonyms: Melodious, Musical, Tuneful, Harmonic, Dulcet, Euphonious, Lyrical, Mellifluous, Sweet-sounding, Rhythmic

In literary contexts, it conveys a sense of lyrical beauty.

antonyms: Separate, Unweave, Disentangle, Detach, Divide
examples: The craftsman interlaced strips of leather to create the strong and flexible belt. The branches of the two old trees had grown to interlace overhead, forming a natural arch. Traditional basket weavers interlace natural fibres with great skill and precision.

synonyms: Weave, Entwine, Intertwine, Blend, Mesh, Braid, Interweave

examples: The interlocutors in the peace talks agreed to suspend hostilities for a period of thirty days. She found it difficult to concentrate when her interlocutors kept interrupting each other. antonyms: Listeners, Observers, Silent parties
englishMeaning: People who take part in a dialogue or conversation. Those who speak or engage in discussions during formal or informal exchanges. Participants in an interview, negotiation, or formal discussion.

antonyms: Member, Insider, Invited guest, Welcomed participant

examples: She felt like an interloper at the family gathering she had not been formally invited to attend. The interloper had managed to gain access to the restricted area without any authorisation. synonyms: Intruder, Trespasser, Meddler, Outsider, Unwanted visitor, Uninvited guest
sindhiMeaning: اڻ گهريل، ناحق وچ ۾ پوندڙ، ٻاهريون ماڻهو، جيڪو اتي نه هجڻ گهرجي

antonyms: Separate, Divide, Isolate, Segregate, Distinguish
examples: Guests from all over the world were invited to intermingle at the international reception. The two rivers intermingle before flowing together into the sea. antonyms: Typically male, Typically female, Binary sex
englishMeaning: Describing a person born with reproductive or sexual anatomy, chromosomes, or hormones that do not fit typical definitions of male or female. Relating to a natural biological variation in sex characteristics. A term used to describe people whose bodies do not fit neatly into the binary male or female categories.
examples: Many intersex people report that they were not adequately informed about their condition during childhood. The organisation works to protect the rights of intersex individuals in healthcare settings. Intersex variations occur naturally and are more common than most people realise. She identified as intersex and spoke openly about her experiences to raise awareness. Medical professionals are increasingly moving away from unnecessary surgeries on intersex infants.
synonyms: Biologically variant, Ambiguous sex, Non-binary biological

examples: The teacher had to intervene when the disagreement between the two students began to escalate. The government decided to intervene in the market to stabilise prices for essential goods. antonyms: Stay out, Ignore, Withdraw, Abstain, Keep away

antonyms: Extrovert, Behaviourist, Empiricist
sindhiMeaning: خودنظريي جو پرچارڪ، پنهنجي ذهني حالتن جو مطالعو ڪندڙ، نفسيات ۾ خود مشاهدي جو حامي

examples: As an introspectionist, she believed that understanding oneself was the first step toward understanding others. synonyms: Quack remedy, Patent medicine, Cure-all, Panacea, Snake oil
antonyms: Proven remedy, Medicine, Treatment, Cure
urduMeaning: جادوئی دوا، آزمائش نہ کی گئی اور بے ثبوت دوا، نیم حکیم دوا

antonyms: Ordinary, Unknown, Insignificant, Unremarkable, Obscure
sindhiMeaning: قابل ذڪر، مشهور، اهم، نمايان، قابل توجه
urduMeaning: قابلِ ذکر، مشہور، اہم، نمایاں، قابلِ توجہ
englishMeaning: Worthy of attention or notice; remarkable. A famous or important person. Deserving to be noted or known, especially for particular achievements. Something or someone that stands out for its significance.
examples: The conference was attended by several notable figures from the worlds of science and politics. His most notable achievement was winning the international prize for research in renewable energy. There was a notable improvement in the patient's condition after the new course of treatment began. She is a notable figure in the history of women's rights and is remembered for her courage. The notable exceptions to the rule were discussed in detail in the final chapter of the report.
synonyms: Remarkable, Distinguished, Famous, Prominent, Significant, Noteworthy

antonyms: Obscurely, Praiseworthily, Admirably, Anonymously
englishMeaning: In a way that is famous or well known, especially for a bad quality or action. Used to emphasise that something is widely known, usually for a negative reason. In a manner that is clearly and widely recognised, often unfavourably.
examples: The region is notoriously difficult to access in winter due to the extreme weather conditions. He was notoriously unreliable and rarely completed any task on time. The city is notoriously expensive to live in compared to other major European capitals. The company was notoriously slow in responding to customer complaints and regularly lost business. She was notoriously secretive about her private life and never gave personal interviews.
urduMeaning: بدنامی سے، مشہور برائی سے، سب کو معلوم خرابی سے
synonyms: Infamously, Famously (negatively), Scandalously, Markedly
sindhiMeaning: بدنامي سان، مشهور برائيءَ سان، سڀني کي معلوم خرابيءَ سان

synonyms: Invalidity, Voidance, Nothingness, Worthlessness, Non-existence
englishMeaning: The state of being legally void, invalid, or of no effect. Something that is of no legal force or validity. The condition of having no value, existence, or significance. In law, a declaration that something such as a marriage is invalid.
examples: The court granted a nullity of the marriage on the grounds that one party had been underage at the time. The contract was declared a nullity after it was found to have been signed under duress. He sought a legal nullity of the agreement after discovering it contained several fraudulent clauses. The nullity of the election result was announced following evidence of widespread irregularities. Her contribution to the debate was a complete nullity and had no influence on the final decision.
urduMeaning: بطلان، غیر قانونی ہونا، ناکارگی، کسی چیز کا قانونی طور کالعدم ہونا
sindhiMeaning: بطلان، غير قانوني هجڻ، ناڪارگي، ڪنهن شيءِ جو قانوني طور ڪالعدم هجڻ
antonyms: Validity, Legality, Effect, Existence, Substance
Genius, Intellectual, Clever person, Bright individual
urduMeaning: بیوقوف، احمق، کند ذہن آدمی
synonyms: Fool, Blockhead, Dunce, Dimwit, Idiot, Simpleton
sindhiMeaning: بيوقوف، احمق، ڪند ذهن ماڻهو
examples: Only a numbskull would ignore the weather warnings and go hiking in those conditions. She muttered under her breath that the driver was a complete numbskull for missing the obvious turn. He was called a numbskull by his classmates for repeatedly forgetting to bring the homework. The manager had little patience for numbskulls who failed to follow even the simplest instructions. Do not be such a numbskull — the answer is written clearly on the board for everyone to see.
englishMeaning: A stupid or foolish person. Someone who lacks intelligence or good sense. An informal and mildly insulting term for a dull-witted individual.

antonyms: Few, Scarce, Rare, Limited, Insufficient
urduMeaning: بہت سے، کئی، بے شمار، بڑی تعداد میں
sindhiMeaning: گهڻا، ڪيترائي، بيشمار، وڏي تعداد ۾
examples: She received numerous applications for the position from highly qualified candidates. Numerous studies have confirmed the health benefits of regular physical exercise. He had made numerous attempts to contact the company before finally receiving a reply. The region is home to numerous species of rare and endangered wildlife. They had discussed the topic on numerous occasions without ever reaching a firm conclusion.
englishMeaning: Great in number; many. Consisting of a large number of people or things. More than can be easily counted or specified.
synonyms: Many, Multiple, Several, Various, Countless, Abundant, Plentiful

sindhiMeaning: روحاني، پاڪ، الاهي حضوريءَ جو احساس ڏياريندڙ، عظمت ڀريو
antonyms: Mundane, Ordinary, Secular, Earthly, Trivial
englishMeaning: Having a strong sense of the presence of a divinity; spiritual and awe-inspiring. Mysterious and filling one with a sense of the presence of something greater than oneself. Related to or evoking a sense of the divine or the sacred.
urduMeaning: روحانی، پاک، الٰہی حضوری کا احساس دلانے والا، عظمت بھرا
synonyms: Sacred, Divine, Spiritual, Awe-inspiring, Transcendent, Mystical
examples: The ancient forest had a numinous quality that silenced even the most talkative of visitors. She felt a numinous presence in the old cathedral that she could not explain in rational terms. The philosopher described the experience of the numinous as central to all genuine religious feeling. His poetry often explored the numinous aspects of everyday life and the natural world. The silence at the summit of the mountain was so complete it felt almost numinous.

englishMeaning: A woman who is a member of a religious community, typically living under vows of poverty, chastity, and obedience. A member of a female religious order devoted to contemplation or active work. A woman who has devoted her life to religious service and communal spiritual life.
sindhiMeaning: راهبه، مذهبي برادريءَ ۾ رهندڙ عورت، خدمت ۽ عبادت لاءِ پاڻ کي وقف ڪيل عورت
synonyms: Sister, Religious woman, Monastic, Abbess (senior)
examples: The nun spent over forty years teaching children at the school attached to the convent. She felt a calling to become a nun and entered the religious order at the age of twenty-one. The visiting nun spoke to the students about the importance of compassion and service to others. The documentary followed a group of nuns as they went about their daily routines of prayer and community work. A senior nun was elected to lead the convent for the next five years.
urduMeaning: راہبہ، مذہبی برادری میں رہنے والی عورت، خدمت اور عبادت کے لیے خود کو وقف کرنے والی عورت
antonyms: Layperson, Secular woman

urduMeaning: پرورش کرنا، پالنا پوسنا، ترقی کے لیے مدد کرنا، خیال رکھنا
examples: A nurturing environment in early childhood has a lasting impact on a person's emotional development. She was known for her nurturing approach to leadership, always encouraging her team to grow. The programme was designed to focus on nurturing young talent in the performing arts. He credited his parents' nurturing support with giving him the confidence to pursue his ambitions. Nurturing strong relationships within a team is one of the most important responsibilities of a good manager.
englishMeaning: Caring for and encouraging the growth and development of someone or something. Providing support, love, and guidance to help something or someone flourish. The process of bringing up, fostering, and developing an individual or idea.
synonyms: Caring, Fostering, Supporting, Encouraging, Developing, Nourishing
antonyms: Neglecting, Stifling, Hindering, Suppressing, Ignoring
sindhiMeaning: پرورش ڪرڻ، پالڻ پوسڻ، ترقي لاءِ مدد ڪرڻ، خيال رکڻ

synonyms: Paddle, Scull, Blade, Row
englishMeaning: A long pole with a flat blade used to row a boat through water. Something that resembles an oar in shape or function. To row or propel a boat using oars.
examples: He gripped the oar tightly and pulled hard as the boat struggled against the current. One of the oars slipped from her hand and had to be retrieved from the water quickly. The wooden oar had been used by fishermen in the village for generations. They took turns with the oar to row the heavy boat across the wide lake. She snapped an oar accidentally on the rocks during the kayaking competition.
urduMeaning: پتوار، کشتی کو چلانے والی لاٹھی، کشتی کو کھینچنے کا آلہ
sindhiMeaning: پتوار، ٻيڙي کي هلائڻ وارو لٺ، ٻيڙيءَ کي ڇڪڻ وارو اوزار
antonyms: Motor, Engine, Sail
Desert, Wasteland, Barren place, Hostile environment
englishMeaning: A fertile spot in a desert where water is found, often with trees and vegetation. A pleasant or peaceful area or period in the middle of a difficult, troubled, or hectic situation. A place of comfort, calm, or safety surrounded by hardship or unpleasantness.
urduMeaning: صحرا میں پانی کی جگہ، نخلستان، مشکل صورتحال میں سکون کی جگہ
synonyms: Haven, Refuge, Sanctuary, Fertile spot, Retreat, Safe haven
examples: The weary travellers finally reached the oasis after three days of walking through the scorching desert. Her small garden was an oasis of calm in the middle of the noisy and crowded city. The library served as an oasis of quiet for students who needed to concentrate on their work. An oasis of green appeared unexpectedly in the middle of the otherwise barren landscape. She described their friendship as an oasis during what had been one of the most difficult years of her life.
sindhiMeaning: صحرا ۾ پاڻيءَ جي جڳهه، نخلستان، ڏکيءَ صورتحال ۾ سڪون جي هنڌ

antonyms: Soften, Yield, Relent, Melt, Submit, Give in, Weaken
urduMeaning: دل سخت کرنا، ضدی ہو جانا، ہٹ دھرم ہونا، سنگدل ہو جانا، احساسات میں سختی لانا، کسی کی بات نہ ماننا، اپنے موقف پر ڈٹ جانا، جذبات کو سخت کر لینا
englishMeaning: To harden. To make stubborn or unyielding. To become hardened in feelings, attitude, or heart. To resist persuasion or softening of emotions. An archaic verb form related to 'obdurate', used when a person becomes emotionally hardened, stubborn, or unmoved by appeals, suffering, or persuasion.
sindhiMeaning: دل سخت ڪرڻ، ضدي ٿيڻ، اڙٻنگ ٿيڻ، سخت دل ٿيڻ، نه مڃڻ وارو ٿيڻ، احساسن ۾ سختي اچڻ، ڪنهن جي ڳالهه نه مڃڻ، هٺ ڌرمي اختيار ڪرڻ، جذبن کي سخت ڪرڻ
examples: Years of hardship obdured his heart against pity. She obdured herself before delivering the harsh decision. The tyrant obdured his mind against every plea for mercy. Suffering had obdured him to the cries of the poor. He tried not to obdure his feelings despite repeated betrayals.
synonyms: Harden, Stiffen, Toughen, Steel, Indurate, Make stubborn, Fortify
Bow, Homage, Reverence, Respect, Deference, Salutation, Genuflection, Submission, Curtsy
examples: The villagers made obeisance to the king as he entered the palace. She bowed in obeisance before the holy shrine. The soldiers paid obeisance to their commander with a sharp salute. Pilgrims offered obeisance at the temple's altar. He refused to make obeisance to the new dictator.
urduMeaning: تعظیم، ادب و احترام سے جھکنا، سجدہ، سلام، عقیدت کا اظہار، فرمانبرداری، اطاعت، کسی بڑے کے سامنے ادب سے جھکنا، تعظیمی سلام، عقیدت مندانہ جھکاؤ
englishMeaning: A gesture of respect, submission, or reverence such as a bow or curtsy. Deep respect or homage shown to someone of higher rank or authority. The act of showing deference or acknowledging another's superiority. A formal expression of obedience or loyalty. A respectful salutation made by bending the body or lowering the head before kings, elders, or sacred figures.
sindhiMeaning: تعظيم، احترام جو اظهار، جهڪڻ، سلام ڪرڻ، ادب ۽ احترام سان جهڪي سلام ڪرڻ، اطاعت ڪرڻ، فرمانبرداري جو اظهار، ڪنهن وڏي يا بزرگ آڏو عاجزي ڏيکارڻ، تابعداري، نمستي وانگر احترام جو اشارو
antonyms: Disrespect, Defiance, Disregard, Insolence, Rebellion, Contempt, Disobedience

examples: The newspaper printed a short obit for the famous poet. His obit appeared in the morning edition. The family arranged an obit at the local church. She wrote a moving obit for her late mentor. Readers were saddened by the obit of the beloved singer.
urduMeaning: وفات کا اعلان، اخبار میں شائع وفات کی خبر، تعزیتی نوٹس، مرثیہ، یادگاری تقریب، برسی کا ذکر، مرحوم کی مختصر سوانح، خبرِ رحلت
englishMeaning: A published notice of a person's death, often with a short biography. An obituary. A memorial service or ceremony held for someone who has died. The anniversary of a person's death observed with prayers or rites. A brief announcement in a newspaper or online about someone's passing.
synonyms: Obituary, Death notice, Eulogy, Necrology, Memorial, In memoriam
antonyms: Birth announcement, Nativity notice, Celebration of life beginning
sindhiMeaning: وفات جو اعلان، اخبار ۾ ڇپيل وفات جي خبر، ڪنهن جي موت جو نوٽيس، تعزيتي اعلان، مرثيو، ياد گاري تقريب، ورسي جو ذڪر، مرحوم جي مختصر سوانح
مدار سان لاڳاپيل، گردشي مدار جو، چوڌاري گردش ڪندڙ، اکين جي خاني سان لاڳاپيل، ڌرتيءَ يا سيارن جي گردشي رستي سان واسطو رکندڙ، چڪرائتي مدار جو
englishMeaning: Relating to an orbit. Pertaining to the curved path of a planet, satellite, or object around another body in space. Relating to the eye socket in anatomy. Concerning circular or elliptical motion around a center. (Variant spelling of 'orbital'.)
urduMeaning: مدار سے متعلق، گردشی مدار کا، کسی شے کے گرد گھومنے والے راستے سے متعلق، آنکھ کے خانے سے متعلق، سیاروں یا سیٹلائٹ کے مدار سے متعلق، چکر دار راستے کا
antonyms: Linear, Straight, Stationary, Fixed, Non-rotational
synonyms: Orbital, Circular, Revolving, Rotational, Cyclic, Planetary
examples: The satellite was placed in a stable obital path around the earth. Scientists calculated the obital speed of the new probe. The doctor examined the obital region near the patient's eye. The moon's obital motion affects the tides. Engineers adjusted the obital position of the telescope.

sindhiMeaning: وفات جي اعلان سان لاڳاپيل، تعزيتي، مرثياتي، ياد گاريءَ سان واسطو رکندڙ، مرحومن جي ياد ۾ لکيل يا چيل، وفات جي خبر سان منسوب، برسي يا ورسي سان لاڳاپيل
antonyms: Celebratory, Festive, Joyful, Natal, Congratulatory
urduMeaning: وفات کے اعلان سے متعلق، تعزیتی، مرثیاتی، یادگاری تحریر سے متعلق، مرحومین کی یاد سے منسوب، خبرِ رحلت سے وابستہ، برسی سے متعلق
synonyms: Obituary, Commemorative, Memorial, Funereal, Elegiac, Mournful
examples: The magazine devoted an obitual column to fallen soldiers. She wrote an obitual tribute for her grandfather. The obitual notice was published in several newspapers. They held an obitual gathering on the first anniversary of his death. The obitual section of the journal honored departed scholars.
englishMeaning: Relating to an obituary or death notice. Concerning the announcement, remembrance, or commemoration of a person's death. Pertaining to memorial writings, funeral rites, or anniversaries of death. Used to describe writings, ceremonies, or references associated with obituaries.

synonyms: Elongated, Rectangular, Elliptical, Oval, Stretched, Lengthened, Rectangle-shaped
examples: The dining table had an oblong shape that seated ten people. She drew an oblong on the chalkboard to illustrate the concept. The platter was oblong rather than round. An oblong window let light into the long corridor. The bakery sold oblong loaves of fresh bread.
sindhiMeaning: ڊگهيرو، ڊگهو ۽ سوڙهو، آيتاڪار، ڊگهيرڙي شڪل وارو، ڊگهو چورس، انڊاڪار، ڊگهيرڙو گول، هڪ طرف ڊگهو ٿيل، آئتاڪار شڪل
urduMeaning: مستطیل، لمبوترا، بیضوی، آئتاکار، لمبا اور تنگ، چوکور سے لمبا، انڈے کی شکل کا، ایک طرف کھنچا ہوا، مستطیل نما
antonyms: Square, Round, Circular, Spherical, Equilateral
englishMeaning: Having an elongated rectangular or oval shape. Longer than it is wide. A shape that is rectangular with unequal adjacent sides. Of a figure or object that deviates from a perfect square or circle by being stretched in one direction. Used as both a noun (the shape itself) and an adjective (describing such a shape).

examples: The politician faced an obloquial campaign launched by his rivals. The article contained obloquial remarks aimed at damaging her reputation. Such obloquial language has no place in academic debate. He ignored the obloquial comments and continued his work. The newspaper apologized for its obloquial coverage of the scandal.
sindhiMeaning: بدنامي وارو، بدگوئيءَ سان واسطو رکندڙ، سخت تنقيدي، گلا چوڻ وارو، بدنام ڪندڙ، عيب جوئي وارو، بهتان تراشيءَ وارو، رسوا ڪندڙ، بدگو
englishMeaning: Relating to obloquy. Expressing strong public criticism, blame, or abuse. Defamatory, slanderous, or disgracing in nature. Characterized by harsh verbal censure or shame brought upon a person's reputation. Used to describe language, writings, or remarks that bring disgrace or ill repute.
synonyms: Defamatory, Slanderous, Disparaging, Abusive, Censorious, Reproachful, Vituperative, Calumnious
antonyms: Praising, Complimentary, Laudatory, Flattering, Respectful, Honoring
urduMeaning: بدنامی سے متعلق، بدگوئی پر مبنی، سخت تنقیدی، رسوا کن، بہتان آمیز، عیب جوئی والا، توہین آمیز، بدنام کرنے والا، ہتکِ عزت سے متعلق

sindhiMeaning: تمام ناگوار نموني، بيزار ڪندڙ انداز ۾، چڙائيندڙ نموني، اڻوڻندڙ طريقي سان، بدتميزيءَ سان، رکائيءَ سان، گستاخيءَ سان، نفرت انگيز انداز ۾
antonyms: Pleasantly, Politely, Agreeably, Charmingly, Respectfully, Courteously, Graciously
urduMeaning: نہایت ناگوار طریقے سے، تنگ کرنے والے انداز میں، چڑانے والے طور پر، گستاخی سے، بدتمیزی سے، ناخوشگوار انداز میں، بیزار کن طریقے سے، قابلِ نفرت انداز میں
synonyms: Rudely, Offensively, Annoyingly, Disagreeably, Insufferably, Disrespectfully, Boorishly, Insolently
examples: He behaved obnoxiously at the dinner party and embarrassed his friends. She laughed obnoxiously during the quiet ceremony. The drunk man spoke obnoxiously to the waiter. Children were running obnoxiously through the library. He boasted obnoxiously about his promotion in front of everyone.
englishMeaning: In an extremely unpleasant or offensive manner. In a way that is highly annoying, rude, or objectionable. So as to cause strong dislike or irritation in others. In a loud, arrogant, or socially unacceptable way. Used to describe behavior, speech, or actions that are openly disagreeable.

urduMeaning: گالیاں، فحش الفاظ، بے ہودہ کلمات، نازیبا باتیں، بدتمیزی والے جملے، اخلاق سوز الفاظ، گندے کلمات، بے حیائی والی باتیں، توہین آمیز الفاظ

englishMeaning: Offensive, indecent, or vulgar words or expressions. Profane language or curse words. Acts, images, or remarks that are morally offensive or sexually explicit. Things considered shocking or disgusting to public decency. The plural form of 'obscenity', referring to multiple instances of indecent speech or behavior.
examples: He shouted obscenities at the referee after the foul. The walls were covered with obscenities written by vandals. She was shocked by the obscenities heard in the film. The driver yelled obscenities during the traffic jam. The book was banned for containing obscenities and graphic content.
sindhiMeaning: گارگند، گاريون، بيهودا لفظ، فحش ڳالهيون، بيشرميءَ وارا لفظ، نازيبا ڳالهيون، اخلاق سوز ڪلام، بدتميزيءَ وارا جملا، گندا لفظ
synonyms: Profanities, Curses, Vulgarities, Swear words, Indecencies, Abuses, Expletives, Foul language

sindhiMeaning: خوشامدي، چاپلوس، حد کان وڌيڪ تابعداريءَ وارو، مفاد لاءِ جهڪندڙ، چمچاگيري ڪندڙ، نقلي عاجزي ڏيکاريندڙ، ٻين کي راضي ڪرڻ لاءِ ذليل ٿيندڙ، خوشامدي طبيعت وارو
synonyms: Servile, Fawning, Sycophantic, Flattering, Toadying, Ingratiating, Submissive, Grovelling, Cringing
englishMeaning: Excessively eager to please or obey others. Showing servile flattery or fawning behavior. Overly submissive in a way that seems insincere. Behaving with exaggerated respect to gain favor. Used to describe people who flatter or serve superiors in a way considered dishonest or self-serving.
examples: The obsequious clerk bowed repeatedly to impress the manager. His obsequious smile irritated everyone in the meeting. She disliked the obsequious tone of the salesman. The minister was surrounded by obsequious advisers. He gave an obsequious nod whenever the boss spoke.
antonyms: Assertive, Independent, Dignified, Bold, Confident, Defiant, Self-respecting, Domineering
urduMeaning: خوشامدی، چاپلوس، چمچہ، حد سے زیادہ فرمانبردار، مفاد کے لیے جھکنے والا، جھوٹی عاجزی دکھانے والا، خوشامدانہ، چاپلوسانہ، چمچہ گیری کرنے والا

examples: Typewriters have become obsolete in the age of computers. Many traditional jobs are becoming obsolete due to automation. The factory was shut down because its machinery was completely obsolete. His ideas about education are now considered obsolete. Floppy disks are an obsolete form of data storage.
englishMeaning: No longer in use. Out of date. Outdated. Discarded as no longer useful. Replaced by something newer. Belonging to an earlier time. Something that is no longer produced or used because it has been replaced by a newer or more efficient version. It refers to ideas, methods, technologies, words, or objects that have lost their value, relevance, or usefulness with the passage of time.
synonyms: Outdated, Antiquated, Old-fashioned, Out of date, Archaic, Disused, Defunct, Superseded, Passé, Outmoded
antonyms: Modern, Current, New, Up-to-date, Fashionable, Fresh, Latest, Contemporary, Trendy
urduMeaning: متروک، فرسودہ، پرانا، ناکارہ، استعمال سے باہر، دورِ حاضر سے مطابقت نہ رکھنے والا، ایسی چیز یا خیال جو اب استعمال میں نہ ہو کیونکہ اُس کی جگہ کوئی نئی اور بہتر چیز لے چکی ہے
sindhiMeaning: متروڪ، پراڻو ٿيل، استعمال مان نڪتل، فرسوده، ناڪار آمد، وقت گذرڪو، اهڙي شيءِ يا خيال جيڪو هاڻي ڪم نه ٿو اچي ڇو ته ان جي جاءِ تي ڪا نئين ۽ بهتر شيءِ آيل آهي

sindhiMeaning: گوڙ ڪندڙ، شور مچائيندڙ، بي قابو، بدمست، حڪم نه مڃيندڙ، اڙٻنگ، اهڙو ماڻهو جيڪو گوڙ ڪندو ۽ ضابطي ۾ نه ايندو، خاص طور تي ٻارن لاءِ استعمال ٿيندڙ لفظ
englishMeaning: Noisy and difficult to control. Loud and unruly. Aggressively boisterous. Resisting authority or restraint. Behaving in a noisy and uncontrolled way. It is usually used to describe people, especially children or crowds, who are loud, rowdy, and refuse to obey rules or instructions.

englishMeaning: The front or main side of something, especially a coin or medal. The opposite or counterpart of a fact or truth. The side of a coin bearing the head or principal design. urduMeaning: اگلا رخ، سامنے کا حصہ، سکے یا تمغے کا مرکزی رخ، کسی شے کا سامنے والا یا اہم پہلو، کسی حقیقت کا اُلٹ یا دوسرا رخ

examples: The obverse of the coin shows the portrait of the queen. Poverty is often the obverse of wealth in unequal societies. He examined the obverse of the medal carefully under the light. The obverse side of the document contained the official seal. Joy and sorrow are the obverse of each other in human life.

It was obvious that he was lying about the incident. The answer to the question is quite obvious. There are obvious reasons for the company's decision to expand. She had an obvious talent for music from a young age. The mistake in the report was so obvious that everyone noticed it.

englishMeaning: Easily seen or understood. Clear. Plain. Evident. Apparent. Self-evident. Not difficult to perceive or recognize. antonyms: Hidden, Obscure, Unclear, Ambiguous, Vague, Concealed, Subtle, Imperceptible
urduMeaning: ظاہر، واضح، صاف، نمایاں، کھلا ہوا، عیاں، ایسی بات جو بغیر کسی وضاحت کے سمجھ میں آ جائے، آسانی سے دکھائی یا سمجھ میں آنے والی

synonyms: Hash, Hashtag, Pound sign, Number sign, Hash mark
examples: Please press the octothorpe key after entering your account number. The octothorpe is widely known today as the hashtag symbol on social media. englishMeaning: The symbol (#). The hash sign. The pound sign on a telephone keypad. A typographical symbol consisting of two horizontal and two vertical lines crossing each other. urduMeaning: نفرت انگیز، قابلِ نفرت، گھناؤنا، مکروہ، بے حد ناپسندیدہ، ایسی چیز یا فعل جس سے شدید کراہت محسوس ہو، ڈھٹائی بھرا، نفرت کے قابل
antonyms: Lovely, Pleasant, Delightful, Agreeable, Charming, Likeable, Admirable, Attractive
englishMeaning: Extremely unpleasant. Repulsive. Hateful. Disgusting. Detestable. Deserving of hatred. Causing strong dislike or disgust. It is used to describe people, actions, behaviour, or things that are so offensive or evil that they provoke strong feelings of hatred and revulsion.

sindhiMeaning: نفرت انگيز، ڪراهت ڀريو، گهنائتو، بڇڙو، نهايت ناپسنديده، اهڙي شيءِ يا عمل جنهن کان سخت نفرت ٿئي، ڌڪاريل، باعث ڪراهت

examples: The menu listed oeuf en cocotte as the chef's special. She ordered an oeuf mayonnaise as a starter at the French café. In French cuisine, oeuf is used in many classic recipes. The word oeuf simply means egg in English. He learned that 'oeuf' is pronounced almost like 'uhf' in French.

antonyms: (No direct antonyms)

antonyms: Origin, Source, Root, Parent body, Main stem
synonyms: Branch, Subsidiary, Spin-off, Outgrowth, Derivative, Byproduct, Extension, Side branch, Descendant

englishMeaning: A branch that grows from the main stem of a plant. Something that develops from something larger or earlier. A subsidiary or derivative of something. A side branch. sindhiMeaning: شاخ، ٽاري، ڪنهن وڏي شيءِ مان نڪتل ننڍي شاخ يا حصو، ڪنهن وڏي اداري يا تنظيم مان نڪتل ذيلي اداره، نسل جي شاخ، ڪنهن اصل شيءِ مان جنم وٺندڙ نئون حصو
examples: The new company is an offshoot of a much larger international corporation. Jazz is considered an offshoot of African American musical traditions. The gardener cut away the small offshoots from the main branch. This research project is an offshoot of our earlier study on climate change. The political party began as an offshoot of a larger reform movement.

synonyms: Musical drama, Lyric drama, Operetta, Music drama, Sung drama
examples: We attended a beautiful opera at the Sydney Opera House last summer. She has been training to become a professional opera singer for ten years. englishMeaning: A dramatic musical work in which the text is sung with orchestral accompaniment. A theatrical performance combining music, singing, and acting. The art form of staged sung drama. antonyms: Easy, Effortless, Simple, Lazy, Idle, Light, Undemanding

examples: Translating the ancient manuscript was an operose task that took many years. The scientist undertook the operose work of cataloguing every species in the region. synonyms: Laborious, Tedious, Arduous, Toilsome, Hardworking, Industrious, Painstaking, Strenuous, Demanding

synonyms: Balance, Manage, Handle, Manipulate, Alternate, Combine, Coordinate, Toss
examples: The circus artist can juggle five balls at once. She has to juggle her job, studies, and family life every day. Working mothers often juggle multiple responsibilities. urduMeaning: ہوا میں کئی چیزیں ایک ساتھ اچھال کر پکڑنا, ایک ہی وقت میں کئی کاموں یا ذمہ داریوں کو سنبھالنا, مختلف مطالبات میں توازن قائم کرنا, اعداد و شمار یا حقائق میں ہیرا پھیری کرنا, بازیگری کرنا
sindhiMeaning: هوا ۾ ڪيتريون ئي شيون هڪ ئي وقت اڇلائي جهلڻ, ڪيترن ئي ڪمن يا ذميوارين کي هڪ ئي وقت سنڀالڻ, هڪ ئي وقت گهڻن معاملن ۾ توازن رکڻ, انگن اکرن يا حقيقتن سان ٺڳيءَ لاءِ هٿ چراند ڪرڻ, بارَ کيڏڻ

The act or process of deriving logical conclusions from known or assumed facts. Something that is inferred rather than directly stated. An opinion or judgment formed by considering available information.
examples: The detective drew an inference from the fingerprints found at the scene. Her silence led me to the inference that she was upset. Scientists make inferences based on experimental data. The inference from the report is that sales are declining. His inference proved to be correct.
synonyms: Deduction, Conclusion, Reasoning, Assumption, Presumption, Interpretation, Judgment, Surmise
urduMeaning: نتیجہ، اندازہ، قیاس، استنباط، دلائل و شواہد کی بنیاد پر اخذ کیا گیا نتیجہ، منطقی طور پر نکالا گیا مطلب، کسی بات سے سمجھی جانے والی چیز

synonyms: Leap, Spring, Hop, Bound, Vault, Skip, Surge, Rise, Increase
sindhiMeaning: ٽپو ڏيڻ، ٽپ ڏيڻ، اڇل ڏيڻ، اوچتو مٿي اڇلجڻ، اوچتو وڌي وڃڻ، هراس مان اڇل کائڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ مٿان ٽپي وڃڻ، اڇل، ٽپو، اوچتو اڀار

sindhiMeaning: روانو ڪرڻ، شروع ڪرڻ، متعارف ڪرائڻ، راڪيٽ يا ميزائل خلا ۾ ڇڏڻ، ٻيڙي پاڻيءَ ۾ لاهڻ، ڪنهن مهم يا منصوبي جي شروعات ڪرڻ، پيش ڪرڻ، آغاز
synonyms: Begin, Start, Introduce, Initiate, Inaugurate, Kick off, Set in motion, Unveil, Fire, Propel

antonyms: End, Finish, Conclude, Stop, Halt, Terminate, Withdraw
urduMeaning: روانہ کرنا، شروع کرنا، متعارف کرانا، راکٹ یا میزائل داغنا، کشتی کو پانی میں اتارنا، کسی مہم یا منصوبے کا آغاز کرنا، پیش کرنا، ابتدا

urduMeaning: جلدی سے باہر نکل جانا، تیزی سے تیار کرنا یا شائع کرنا، عجلت میں کہیں جانا، جلدی میں کسی جگہ سے روانہ ہونا

antonyms: Amble, Stroll, Delay, Linger, Ignore, Stay away
Delay, Slow down, Take time, Deliberate, Postpone, Linger

englishMeaning: To do something very quickly, often without proper care. To pass a bill, law, or decision through an official process quickly. To move through a place at high speed.

antonyms: Linger, Delay, Stay, Remain, Wait, Proceed slowly
