sindhiMeaning: تڪڙو موٽي اچڻ، جلدي واپس وڃڻ، ڪنهن ضروري ڪم سبب تڪڙي واپسي ڪرڻ، جلدي ۾ اڳوڻي جاءِ تي موٽڻ
examples: He rushed back home when he heard about the fire. She rushed back to the office to collect her bag. The soldiers rushed back to defend the border. I rushed back as soon as I got your call. Memories rushed back when she saw the old photo.
synonyms: Hurry back, Hasten back, Return quickly, Dash back, Speed back

antonyms: Relax, Rest, Slow down, Take it easy, Stay still
urduMeaning: ایک جگہ سے دوسری جگہ جلدی جلدی بھاگنا، بہت سے کام ایک ساتھ کرنے کی کوشش میں مصروف رہنا، بھاگ دوڑ کرنا
sindhiMeaning: هڪ هنڌ کان ٻئي هنڌ تڪڙ ۾ ڊوڙڻ، ڪيترائي ڪم هڪ ئي وقت ۾ ڪرڻ جي ڪوشش ڪرڻ، تڪڙ ۾ مشغول رهڻ
examples: She was rushing around the kitchen preparing dinner. I have been rushing around all day trying to finish my errands. Do not rush around too much or you will get tired. He rushes around the office all morning. Parents often rush around before school starts.
synonyms: Bustle, Scurry, Dash about, Hurry about, Scramble, Run around
englishMeaning: To move quickly from one place to another trying to do many things. To be very busy in a hurried and often disorganized way.

sindhiMeaning: ٻين جو انتظار ڪرڻ کان سواءِ اڳتي هليو وڃڻ، بنا سوچ ويچار جي تڪڙو اڳتي وڌڻ، ٻين کان اڳتي نڪري وڃڻ
antonyms: Lag behind, Hesitate, Wait, Stop, Delay, Fall back
englishMeaning: To move forward quickly without waiting for others. To proceed with something too quickly, without careful thought. To make faster progress than others.
examples: Do not rush ahead with the plan before consulting the team. He rushed ahead of the group and got lost. She rushed ahead in her career at a young age. The runner rushed ahead of his competitors. Let us not rush ahead without proper preparation.
synonyms: Press on, Push forward, Forge ahead, Advance quickly, Hurry on
urduMeaning: دوسروں کا انتظار کیے بغیر آگے بڑھ جانا، بغیر سوچے تیزی سے آگے بڑھنا، دوسروں سے پہلے آگے نکل جانا

examples: I will rush round to your house after work. She rushed round to see if her friend was all right. He rushes round the shops during his lunch break. Can you rush round with the medicine, please? Mum rushed round tidying up before the guests arrived.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن سان تڪڙي ملاقات لاءِ وڃڻ، ٿوري وقت لاءِ جلدي پهچڻ، ڪنهن جاءِ تي تڪڙ ۾ گهمي پھمي ڪم ڪرڻ
synonyms: Pop round, Nip round, Dash round, Hurry round, Come over quickly
urduMeaning: کسی سے مختصر ملاقات کے لیے جلدی جانا، تھوڑی دیر کے لیے فوراً پہنچنا، کسی جگہ پر عجلت میں گھومنا
antonyms: Delay, Take time, Stay put, Linger, Postpone visit
englishMeaning: To visit someone or somewhere quickly, especially for a short time. To move hurriedly around a place doing many things.

examples: She jumped at the chance to study abroad. He jumped at the offer of a promotion. Any student would jump at such a scholarship. I would jump at the opportunity to work with him. They jumped at the suggestion of a weekend trip.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن موقعي کي بنا دير جي قبول ڪرڻ، وڏي شوق سان ڪنهن پيشڪش کي فوراً وٺڻ، ڪنهن آڇ تي جلدي راضي ٿي وڃڻ
urduMeaning: کسی موقع کو بغیر دیر کے قبول کر لینا، پیشکش کو فوراً اور خوشی سے قبول کرنا، کسی بات پر جلدی سے آمادہ ہو جانا
synonyms: Accept eagerly, Grab, Seize, Snatch, Welcome, Embrace
antonyms: Refuse, Reject, Decline, Hesitate, Turn down, Ignore
englishMeaning: To accept an opportunity, offer, or chance eagerly and without hesitation. To take advantage of something immediately when it is offered.

sindhiMeaning: تڪڙو ڪنهن جاءِ يا گاڏيءَ ۾ چڙهڻ، ڳالهه ٻولهه يا سرگرميءَ ۾ اوچتو شامل ٿيڻ، بنا دير مدد لاءِ اڳتي وڌڻ
synonyms: Join in, Enter, Interject, Chime in, Hop in, Step in
examples: Jump in, I will give you a lift home. He jumped in whenever there was a chance to speak. Feel free to jump in if you have any questions. She jumped in to defend her brother. The teacher jumped in to explain the point.
urduMeaning: جلدی سے کسی جگہ یا گاڑی میں سوار ہونا، اچانک گفتگو یا سرگرمی میں شامل ہو جانا، بلاجھجک کسی معاملے میں کود پڑنا
antonyms: Stay out, Withdraw, Keep quiet, Hold back, Exit, Refrain
englishMeaning: To enter a place or vehicle quickly. To join a conversation or activity suddenly. To become involved in a situation without hesitation, often to help.

synonyms: Plunge into, Dive into, Embark on, Throw oneself into, Start eagerly
urduMeaning: پورے جوش کے ساتھ کوئی کام شروع کرنا، کسی سرگرمی میں فوراً شامل ہو جانا، پانی وغیرہ میں چھلانگ لگا کر داخل ہونا
examples: She jumped into her new job with great enthusiasm. The children jumped into the swimming pool. Do not jump into a business without proper research. He jumped into the debate confidently. They jumped into action as soon as the alarm rang.
englishMeaning: To begin doing something with great energy and enthusiasm. To become involved in an activity or situation very quickly. To enter something such as water by leaping in.
sindhiMeaning: وڏي جوش سان ڪو ڪم شروع ڪرڻ، ڪنهن سرگرمي ۾ تڪڙو شامل ٿيڻ، پاڻي وغيره ۾ ٽپو ڏيئي داخل ٿيڻ
antonyms: Hesitate, Delay, Withdraw, Avoid, Step back

examples: The boss jumped on him for being late again. She jumped on the new business idea immediately. He jumped on the bus just as it was leaving. Critics jumped on the minister for his careless remarks. Investors jumped on the opportunity to buy shares.
synonyms: Attack, Criticize, Reprimand, Pounce on, Seize on, Board
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن جي غلطي تي تڪڙو ۽ سخت نڪتيچيني ڪرڻ، فوراً ڪنهن موقعي مان فائدو وٺڻ، هلندڙ گاڏيءَ يا شيءِ تي چڙهڻ
englishMeaning: To criticize someone quickly and severely for something they have said or done. To take immediate advantage of an opportunity. To get onto a moving vehicle or object.
antonyms: Praise, Ignore, Overlook, Support, Defend, Miss out
urduMeaning: کسی کی بات پر فوراً اور سختی سے تنقید کرنا، کسی موقع سے فوراً فائدہ اٹھانا، چلتی گاڑی یا چیز پر سوار ہو جانا

antonyms: Blend in, Stay hidden, Remain inside, Go unnoticed, Enter
sindhiMeaning: تڪڙو ٽپو ڏيئي ٻاهر نڪرڻ، تمام گهڻو نمايان لڳڻ، اوچتو ظاهر ٿي ڪنهن کي حيران ڪري ڇڏڻ
synonyms: Leap out, Spring out, Stand out, Catch the eye, Emerge suddenly
examples: He jumped out of the car and ran into the house. Her red dress really jumped out at the party. The mistake jumped out at me as soon as I read the page. A cat jumped out from behind the bush. His name jumped out from the list of winners.
englishMeaning: To leave a place or vehicle quickly by leaping. To be very noticeable or striking. To appear suddenly and surprise someone.
urduMeaning: چھلانگ لگا کر جلدی باہر نکلنا، بہت نمایاں دکھائی دینا، اچانک ظاہر ہو کر حیران کر دینا

englishMeaning: To leap across or above something in order to get to the other side. To skip or omit a step, section, or part.
antonyms: Crawl under, Go around, Stop, Include, Follow step by step
examples: The horse jumped over the fence gracefully. He jumped over the puddle to keep his shoes dry. She jumped over the introduction and started with chapter two. The dog jumped over the wall easily. You should not jump over important safety steps.
synonyms: Leap over, Vault, Hurdle, Spring over, Bound over, Skip
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ مٿان ٽپي ٻئي پاسي پهچڻ، ڪنهن مرحلي يا حصي کي ڇڏي اڳتي وڌڻ
urduMeaning: کسی چیز کے اوپر سے پھلانگنا، کسی مرحلے یا حصے کو چھوڑ کر آگے بڑھنا

sindhiMeaning: ٽپو ڏيئي ڪنهن شيءِ مان لنگهي وڃڻ، ڪنهن کي راضي ڪرڻ يا مقصد حاصل ڪرڻ لاءِ ڏکيا ڪم ڪرڻ
englishMeaning: To pass through something by leaping. Used often in the idiom to indicate doing many difficult tasks to please someone or achieve something.
antonyms: Avoid, Bypass, Skip, Refuse
synonyms: Leap through, Pass through, Endure, Comply with
urduMeaning: چھلانگ لگا کر کسی چیز میں سے گزر جانا، کسی کو راضی کرنے یا مقصد حاصل کرنے کے لیے مشکل کام کرنا
examples: The tiger jumped through the ring of fire. Applicants had to jump through many stages of testing. The dog was trained to jump through a hoop. She had to jump through a lot to get the visa. They made him jump through several procedures.

antonyms: Relax, Do the minimum, Refuse, Take it easy, Give up
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن مقصد لاءِ ڪيتريون ئي ڏکيون ۽ چڙ چڙ ڀريون ڪارروايون ڀوڳڻ، ڪنهن کي راضي ڪرڻ لاءِ وڏيون ڪوششون ڪرڻ، هڪ کان پوءِ ٻي شرط پوري ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: کسی مقصد کے حصول کے لیے کئی مشکل اور تکلیف دہ مراحل سے گزرنا، کسی کو خوش کرنے کے لیے بہت زیادہ کوشش کرنا، ایک کے بعد ایک شرط پوری کرنا
examples: I had to jump through hoops to get my documents verified. Employees are forced to jump through hoops for a small pay rise. She jumped through hoops to please her boss. Getting a bank loan makes you jump through hoops. Do not make customers jump through hoops for a simple refund.
synonyms: Go to great lengths, Struggle, Bend over backwards, Make great efforts
englishMeaning: To go through a long series of difficult or annoying tasks or procedures in order to achieve something or please someone. To make great efforts, often unnecessarily, to satisfy a demand.

sindhiMeaning: پنهنجي راءِ ڏيڻ، خيال ظاهر ڪرڻ، ڪنهن معاملي تي سوچ سمجهي راءِ بيان ڪرڻ، رسمي انداز سان نظريو پيش ڪرڻ
synonyms: State, Comment, Remark, Declare, Express, Assert, Observe
examples: The judge opined that the evidence was insufficient. Many critics opined that the film was overrated. He opined on the current political situation. She opined that the plan needed more work. Experts opined about the future of the economy.
antonyms: Withhold, Stay silent, Refrain, Listen, Question
englishMeaning: To hold and state as one’s opinion. To express a view or belief about something. To say what one thinks in a formal or considered way.
urduMeaning: اپنی رائے دینا، خیال ظاہر کرنا، کسی معاملے پر سوچ سمجھ کر رائے بیان کرنا، رسمی انداز میں نقطہ نظر پیش کرنا

synonyms: Wharf, Dock, Pier, Jetty, Landing, Berth
sindhiMeaning: ٻيڙين جي لهڻ چڙهڻ لاءِ پاڻيءَ جي ڪناري تي ٺهيل پڪو ڦٽو، بندرگاهه جو ڪناري وارو حصو جتي مسافر ۽ سامان لاٿو ۽ چاڙهيو وڃي
examples: The ship was tied up at the quay. Fishermen were unloading their catch on the quay. Tourists strolled along the busy quay. Cargo was stacked neatly on the quay. The old quay has been renovated for public use.
antonyms: Open sea, Deep water, Middle of the sea
urduMeaning: کشتیوں کے لنگر انداز ہونے کے لیے پانی کے کنارے بنا ہوا پختہ پلیٹ فارم، بندرگاہ کا وہ حصہ جہاں مسافر اور سامان اتارا اور چڑھایا جاتا ہے
englishMeaning: A stone or metal platform beside water where boats and ships are loaded and unloaded. A landing place built parallel to the waterway for handling passengers and cargo.

antonyms: Open sea, Middle of the ocean, Deep water
examples: The cargo ship was anchored at the wharf. Workers loaded goods onto the wharf. The old wharf is a popular tourist spot. Fish were brought to the wharf every morning. The wharf was busy with activity all day.
englishMeaning: A structure built on the shore of a harbour or on the bank of a river where ships may dock to load and unload cargo or passengers.
synonyms: Quay, Pier, Dock, Jetty, Landing stage, Berth
sindhiMeaning: بندرگاهه جي ڪناري تي ٺهيل جاءِ جتي ٻيڙيون سامان يا مسافر لاهڻ چاڙهڻ لاءِ لنگر انداز ٿين، ٻيڙين جو ڦٽو
urduMeaning: بندرگاہ کے کنارے یا دریا کے کنارے بنی ہوئی وہ عمارت جہاں جہاز سامان یا مسافر اتارنے چڑھانے کے لیے ٹھہرتے ہیں، گھاٹ
پانی میں بنایا ہوا لکڑی یا پتھر کا چھوٹا پلیٹ فارم جہاں کشتیاں لنگر انداز ہو سکیں، بندرگاہ کی حفاظت کے لیے پانی میں اُبھری ہوئی تعمیر
englishMeaning: A landing stage or small pier at which boats can dock. A structure that projects from the land into the water to protect a harbour or influence a current.
examples: The boat was tied to the wooden jetty. We walked along the jetty to see the sunset. A new jetty has been built for the ferry service. Children were fishing from the jetty. The storm damaged the jetty badly.
synonyms: Pier, Wharf, Dock, Quay, Breakwater, Landing
sindhiMeaning: پاڻيءَ ۾ اُڀاريل ڪاٺ يا پٿر جو ننڍو ڦٽو جتي ٻيڙيون بيهي سگهن، بندرگاهه جي حفاظت لاءِ زمين کان پاڻيءَ ۾ اڀريل جوڙو
antonyms: Open water, Deep sea, Bay without structure

englishMeaning: To take away an amount or part from a total. To subtract a sum, especially from wages, taxes, or a bill.
urduMeaning: کل رقم میں سے کچھ منہا کرنا، تنخواہ، ٹیکس یا بل سے رقم کاٹنا، کم کرنا
antonyms: Add, Include, Increase, Insert, Sum up, Attach
synonyms: Subtract, Take away, Withhold, Remove, Discount, Minus
examples: The employer will deduct tax from your salary. Please deduct the discount from the total bill. Ten marks were deducted for late submission. They deducted the loan installment automatically. Charges will be deducted from your account each month.
sindhiMeaning: ڪل مان ڪا رقم يا حصو گهٽائڻ، پگهار، ٽيڪس يا بل مان رقم ڪپڻ، منها ڪرڻ

synonyms: Toilet, Lavatory, Loo, Privy, Outhouse, Restroom
urduMeaning: برطانوی غیر رسمی لفظ جو بیت الخلا خصوصاً باہر بنے ہوئے پیخانے کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے، ٹوائلٹ
examples: He went out to the netty at the back of the house. The old cottage still had a netty in the yard. Grandfather told stories about using the netty in winter. The netty was small but clean. Locals still call the toilet a netty in that region.
sindhiMeaning: برطانوي غير رسمي لفظ، ٻاهرين جاءِ تي ٺهيل بيت الخلاءَ لاءِ ڪم ايندڙ اصطلاح، پيخانو، ٽوائلٽ
englishMeaning: British informal term for a toilet, especially an outside one. In dialect use, a small outbuilding used as a lavatory.
antonyms: Living room, Bedroom, Kitchen, Main house

sindhiMeaning: پاڻ کي يا ڪنهن شيءِ کي ٻئي ماڻهو، گروهه يا خيال کان الڳ ڪرڻ، تعلق ٽوڙڻ، پاڻ کي ڌار ڪرڻ، لاڳاپا ختم ڪرڻ
synonyms: Separate, Detach, Distance, Disconnect, Sever, Break away
englishMeaning: To separate or disconnect oneself or something from another person, group, or idea. To break the connection or association between things. To distance oneself from someone or something.
examples: He tried to disassociate himself from the corrupt group. The company disassociated itself from the controversial advertisement. She wants to disassociate her name from the scandal. It is hard to disassociate the singer from her famous song. The party disassociated itself from the extremist views.
antonyms: Associate, Join, Connect, Link, Unite, Involve
urduMeaning: خود کو یا کسی چیز کو دوسرے شخص، گروہ یا خیال سے علیحدہ کرنا، تعلق توڑنا، خود کو دور رکھنا، رشتہ ختم کرنا
کسی کے شرمناک یا غلط رویے پر سخت عوامی تنقید اور رسوائی، بدنامی، شرمندگی، سخت مذمت، ذلت
antonyms: Praise, Honour, Approval, Admiration, Respect, Esteem
synonyms: Disgrace, Shame, Condemnation, Contempt, Scorn, Reproach, Infamy
examples: The minister faced public opprobrium after the scandal. The team suffered opprobrium for their poor performance. His actions brought opprobrium upon his family. The policy was met with widespread opprobrium. Few can withstand the opprobrium of the entire community.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن جي بري ڪم سبب سخت عوامي تنقيد ۽ رسوائي، شرمساري، بدنامي، سخت مذمت، بيعزتي
englishMeaning: Harsh criticism or public disgrace directed at someone because of shameful or wrong behaviour. Public shame or contempt. Strong condemnation.

synonyms: Best, Ideal, Perfect, Prime, Finest, Most favourable
examples: The optimal temperature for this plant is around 25 degrees. We must find the optimal solution to the problem. This is the optimal time to invest in property. The engine runs at optimal efficiency. Doctors recommend an optimal diet for good health.
urduMeaning: بہترین، سب سے مناسب، مقررہ حالات میں سب سے موزوں، سب سے اچھا، بہترین نتیجہ دینے والا
englishMeaning: Best or most favourable, especially under a set of conditions. Most desirable or satisfactory. Producing the best possible result.
sindhiMeaning: بهترين، سڀ کان مناسب، مقرر حالتن ۾ سڀ کان سٺو، تمام گهڻو موزون، بهتر نتيجو ڏيندڙ
antonyms: Worst, Poor, Suboptimal, Inferior, Bad, Unsuitable

englishMeaning: The action of making the best or most effective use of a situation, resource, or process. The process of adjusting a system to make it as efficient as possible.
synonyms: Improvement, Enhancement, Refinement, Streamlining, Perfecting
examples: Website optimization improves search engine ranking. The company focuses on the optimization of production costs. Route optimization saves time and fuel. Optimization of resources is essential for growth. The team worked on the optimization of the algorithm.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن حالت، وسيلي يا عمل جو بهترين استعمال ڪرڻ جو عمل، سسٽم کي وڌ ۾ وڌ ڪارگر بڻائڻ، بهتري آڻڻ
antonyms: Deterioration, Worsening, Neglect, Waste, Inefficiency
urduMeaning: کسی صورتحال، وسائل یا عمل کا بہترین استعمال کرنے کا عمل، نظام کو زیادہ سے زیادہ کارگر بنانا، بہتری لانا

examples: She has a passel of children to look after. The farmer owns a passel of cattle. There was a passel of complaints about the service. A whole passel of tourists arrived at the hotel. He brought a passel of gifts for everyone.
urduMeaning: لوگوں یا چیزوں کا بڑا مجمع، خاصی تعداد، غیر رسمی طور پر بڑی مقدار کے لیے استعمال ہونے والا لفظ، جھمگٹا
englishMeaning: A large group or number of people or things. An informal term for a considerable quantity.
synonyms: Bunch, Group, Crowd, Multitude, Heap, Lot, Bundle
antonyms: Few, Handful, Scarcity, Small number, Individual
sindhiMeaning: ماڻهن يا شين جو وڏو انبوهه، ڪافي مقدار، غير رسمي طور تي وڏي تعداد لاءِ ڪم ايندڙ لفظ، ڪٽڪ

examples: The hostages survived a terrible ordeal. Going through surgery was a painful ordeal. She spoke about her ordeal in a calm voice. The long court case became an ordeal for the family. Losing his job was an emotional ordeal.
sindhiMeaning: تمام ڏکي، تڪليف ڏيندڙ ۽ ڊگهي تجربي واري صورتحال، آزمائش، سخت امتحان، مصيبت جو دور، تڪليف ڀريو وقت
synonyms: Trial, Tribulation, Suffering, Hardship, Torment, Trauma, Nightmare
urduMeaning: بہت تکلیف دہ، مشکل اور طویل تجربہ، سخت آزمائش، کڑی امتحان، مصیبت کا دور، اذیت ناک وقت
antonyms: Pleasure, Comfort, Ease, Enjoyment, Delight, Relief
englishMeaning: A very unpleasant, painful, or difficult experience that lasts for a long time. A severe test of character or endurance. A painful or trying experience.

antonyms: Abscissa, X-coordinate, Disarrange, Disorder
englishMeaning: In mathematics, the y-coordinate of a point on a graph, measured parallel to the vertical axis. As a verb, to arrange in a proper order or to ordain.
synonyms: Y-coordinate, Vertical value, Ordain, Arrange, Order
urduMeaning: ریاضی میں، گراف پر کسی نقطے کا y محور کے متوازی فاصلہ، عمودی محور کے متوازی پیمائش، ترتیب دینا
sindhiMeaning: رياضيءَ ۾، گراف تي ڪنهن نقطي جو y محور جي نسبت واريو انگ، عمودي محور جي متوازي پيمائش، ترتيب ڏيڻ
examples: The ordinate of the point is five. Plot the abscissa and the ordinate carefully. Every point on the graph has an abscissa and an ordinate. The ordinate axis shows the temperature values. He learned how to read the ordinate of each point.

synonyms: Natural, Biological, Living, Chemical-free, Pure, Wholesome
sindhiMeaning: جاندار شين سان لاڳاپيل، ڪيميائي ڀاڻن ۽ دوائن کان سواءِ پيدا ٿيندڙ، جسماني عضون سان تعلق رکندڙ، فطري طور تي ترقي ڪندڙ
examples: She prefers organic vegetables and fruits. Organic farming is becoming popular worldwide. The soil is rich in organic matter. There has been an organic growth in the company. Organic compounds contain carbon atoms.
urduMeaning: جانداروں سے متعلق، کیمیائی کھادوں اور کیڑے مار ادویات کے بغیر تیار کردہ، جسمانی اعضاء سے متعلق، فطری طور پر بڑھنے والا
englishMeaning: Relating to or derived from living matter. Produced or involving production without the use of chemical fertilizers, pesticides, or artificial chemicals. Relating to bodily organs. Developing naturally.
antonyms: Inorganic, Artificial, Synthetic, Chemical, Processed
Plain, Simple, Functional, Practical, Utilitarian
sindhiMeaning: سينگار جي مقصد لاءِ ٺهيل، عملي ڪم بجاءِ سونهن وڌائڻ لاءِ استعمال ٿيندڙ، سينگاري، آرائشي
englishMeaning: Serving as decoration rather than for a practical purpose. Designed to make something more attractive. Relating to ornaments.
urduMeaning: سجاوٹ کے مقصد کے لیے بنایا گیا، عملی استعمال کے بجائے خوبصورتی بڑھانے والا، آرائشی، زیبائشی
synonyms: Decorative, Fancy, Adorning, Embellishing, Attractive
examples: The garden is full of ornamental plants. She wore an ornamental hairpin. Ornamental fish are kept in aquariums. The palace has beautiful ornamental gates. The vase is purely ornamental, not for use.

urduMeaning: وہ بچہ جس کے والدین فوت ہو چکے ہوں، یتیم، بے سہارا، سرپرستی سے محروم، کسی کو یتیم بنانا
synonyms: Waif, Foundling, Parentless child, Abandoned child
examples: The orphan was raised by his kind uncle. War left many children as orphans. She donates every month to an orphan charity. The accident orphaned three young children. Society must protect every orphan.
sindhiMeaning: اهو ٻار جنهن جا مائٽ مري ويا هجن، يتيم، بي سهارو، سرپرستيءَ کان محروم، ڪنهن کي يتيم بڻائڻ
englishMeaning: A child whose parents are dead. A person or thing lacking support, protection, or care. To make a child an orphan by causing the death of the parents.
antonyms: Cared-for child, Adopted, Protected, Nurtured
Family home, Private home, Household
englishMeaning: A residential institution for the care and education of orphans. A home where orphan children are looked after.
sindhiMeaning: يتيمن جي رهائش، تعليم ۽ سنڀال لاءِ قائم ڪيل ادارو، يتيم خانو، يتيم ٻارن جو گهر
examples: The orphanage takes care of over a hundred children. She volunteers at a local orphanage every weekend. The government funds several orphanages in the city. The orphanage arranged education for all the children. Donations to the orphanage are always welcome.
synonyms: Children’s home, Foundling home, Shelter, Refuge, Institution
urduMeaning: یتیموں کی رہائش، تعلیم اور دیکھ بھال کے لیے قائم کیا گیا ادارہ، یتیم خانہ، یتیم بچوں کا گھر

antonyms: Steadiness, Stability, Constancy, Fixity, Firmness
sindhiMeaning: پينڊولم وانگر باقاعدي رفتار سان اڳتي پوئتي حرڪت، مختلف حالتن يا رايي جي وچ ۾ لهر چڙهاءُ، وائبريشن، لڏپلاڻ
englishMeaning: Movement back and forth in a regular rhythm, like that of a pendulum. Fluctuation between different states, opinions, or values. A single swing or vibration.
synonyms: Swing, Vibration, Fluctuation, Wavering, Sway, Variation
urduMeaning: پینڈولم کی طرح باقاعدہ رفتار سے آگے پیچھے حرکت، مختلف حالتوں یا آراء کے درمیان اتار چڑھاؤ، ارتعاش، جھولنا
examples: The oscillation of the pendulum is smooth and steady. There is a constant oscillation in market prices. The oscillation of the bridge worried the engineers. Sound is produced by the oscillation of air particles. His oscillation between the two options confused everyone.

sindhiMeaning: هڏي ۾ تبديل ٿيڻ، هڏيون بڻجي وڃڻ، سخت ۽ ناقابل تبديل ٿي وڃڻ، سوچ يا رويي ۾ اٽل ٿيڻ
antonyms: Soften, Loosen, Adapt, Change, Evolve, Flex
examples: Cartilage gradually ossifies into bone as a child grows. Old ideas can ossify if they are never challenged. The institution has ossified over the years. His views on the matter have ossified with time. Rules can ossify and lose their usefulness.
urduMeaning: ہڈی میں تبدیل ہو جانا، ہڈیاں بن جانا، سخت اور ناقابلِ تبدیل ہو جانا، سوچ یا رویے میں جامد ہو جانا
englishMeaning: To turn into bone or bony tissue. To become rigid, fixed, or unable to change, especially in attitudes, ideas, or systems.
synonyms: Harden, Solidify, Stiffen, Fossilize, Set, Freeze

antonyms: Ahh (relief), Phew, Yay
examples: Ouch, that really hurt! Ouch, I did not expect the water to be so hot. He said ouch when he stubbed his toe. Ouch, that comment was a bit harsh. She cried ouch as the needle touched her arm.
englishMeaning: An exclamation used to express sudden pain or displeasure. A word used to show that something hurts or is unpleasant.
sindhiMeaning: اوچتي درد يا ناخوشگواريءَ جو اظهار ڪندڙ لفظ، ”آخ“، ”هاءِ“، تڪليف جي وقت واتان نڪرندڙ آواز
urduMeaning: اچانک درد یا ناگواری کے اظہار کے لیے استعمال ہونے والا لفظ، ”آہ“، ”اُف“، تکلیف کے وقت نکلنے والی آواز
synonyms: Ow, Ah, Ay, Yow, Yikes
Friendly, Sociable, Extroverted, Warm, Departing, Leaving, Retiring
examples: She has an outgoing personality and many friends. The outgoing president gave a farewell speech. Outgoing calls are recorded for quality purposes. He is more outgoing than his shy brother. The outgoing team wished the new members good luck.
englishMeaning: Friendly, sociable, and enjoying being with other people. Leaving a position, place, or job. Going out or departing.
antonyms: Shy, Reserved, Introverted, Withdrawn, Incoming, Arriving
sindhiMeaning: خوش مزاج، ملنسار، ٻين سان گڏجڻ پسند ڪندڙ، عهدو يا نوڪري ڇڏيندڙ، وڃڻ وارو، رخصت ٿيندڙ
urduMeaning: خوش مزاج، ملنسار، دوسروں سے ملنے جلنے کا شوقین، عہدہ یا نوکری چھوڑنے والا، جانے والا، رخصت ہونے والا

synonyms: Exceed, Surpass, Overshadow, Dominate, Prevail over, Override
examples: The benefits of this plan outweigh the risks. Her achievements far outweigh her mistakes. Practical experience often outweighs theoretical knowledge. The advantages outweigh the disadvantages in this case. Duty outweighed his personal wishes.
englishMeaning: To be greater in weight, value, importance, or influence than something else. To exceed in significance or effect.
antonyms: Fall short, Be less, Underweigh, Be inferior, Yield to
urduMeaning: وزن، اہمیت، قیمت یا اثر میں کسی دوسری چیز سے بڑھ کر ہونا، فائدہ یا اہمیت نقصان سے زیادہ ہونا
sindhiMeaning: وزن، اهميت، قدر يا اثر ۾ ٻي ڪنهن شيءِ کان وڌيڪ هجڻ، فائدو يا اهميت نقصان کان وڌيڪ هجڻ

englishMeaning: To examine something thoroughly and make any necessary changes or repairs. To reform or improve a system completely. A thorough examination and repair. To overtake.
urduMeaning: کسی چیز کا مکمل معائنہ کر کے ضروری مرمت یا تبدیلی کرنا، نظام میں وسیع اصلاح کرنا، مکمل جانچ پڑتال، آگے نکل جانا
antonyms: Neglect, Damage, Break, Leave alone, Preserve as is
synonyms: Renovate, Repair, Refurbish, Reform, Revamp, Restore, Modernize
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ جو مڪمل معائنو ڪري ضروري مرمت يا تبديلي ڪرڻ، سسٽم ۾ وڏي بهتري آڻڻ، مڪمل جانچ، اڳتي نڪري وڃڻ
examples: The engine needs a complete overhaul. The government plans to overhaul the tax system. After a full overhaul, the car ran smoothly. Their strategy requires a serious overhaul. The leader promised to overhaul the education sector.

antonyms: Leave on time, Depart early, Cut short, Withdraw promptly
urduMeaning: مقررہ یا مناسب وقت سے زیادہ ٹھہرنا، ویزا یا میزبانی کی مدت سے زیادہ قیام کرنا
englishMeaning: To stay somewhere longer than is expected, wanted, or allowed. To remain past the permitted time, especially regarding a visa or a visit.
synonyms: Outstay, Linger, Remain too long, Stay beyond limit
sindhiMeaning: مقرر يا مناسب وقت کان وڌيڪ ترسي پوڻ، ويزا يا مهماني جي مدت کان وڌيڪ رهي پوڻ
examples: Do not overstay your welcome at anyone’s house. He was fined for overstaying his visa. Guests should not overstay after dinner. She overstayed her leave and got a warning. Tourists who overstay may face legal action.

antonyms: Understate, Downplay, Relieve, Ease, Underemphasize
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ڳالهه تي حد کان وڌيڪ زور ڏيڻ، ڪنهن ماڻهوءَ يا شيءِ تي بيحد دٻاءُ وجهڻ، وڌاءُ ڪرڻ
synonyms: Overemphasize, Exaggerate, Overburden, Strain, Overload
englishMeaning: To place too much emphasis on something. To subject someone or something to excessive stress or strain.
examples: Do not overstress the importance of grades over learning. It is easy to overstress workers with tight deadlines. Teachers should not overstress a single topic. Overstressed machinery breaks down more often. He tends to overstress minor mistakes.
urduMeaning: کسی بات پر ضرورت سے زیادہ زور دینا، کسی شخص یا چیز پر حد سے زیادہ دباؤ ڈالنا، مبالغہ کرنا

examples: There was overt hostility between the two leaders. The company faced overt criticism from customers. She showed overt support for the movement. Overt discrimination is against the law. His overt behaviour left no room for doubt.
sindhiMeaning: کليل طور تي، ظاهر، صاف نظر ايندڙ، نه لڪل، عوامي طور تي پڌرو، بغير ڍڪ وارو
synonyms: Open, Public, Visible, Undisguised, Obvious, Plain, Manifest
antonyms: Covert, Hidden, Secret, Concealed, Private, Disguised
urduMeaning: کھلم کھلا، ظاہر، صاف دکھائی دینے والا، غیر خفیہ، عوامی طور پر واضح، بغیر پردے کے
englishMeaning: Done or shown openly, without any attempt to hide it. Clearly visible, not secret or hidden. Public and undisguised.

synonyms: Calm, Soothe, Appease, Placate, Quiet, Settle, Conciliate
englishMeaning: To calm a person or group that is angry, upset, or violent. To bring peace to a country or area where there is fighting. To soothe or appease.
urduMeaning: غصے یا پریشان شخص یا گروہ کو پرسکون کرنا، کسی علاقے میں امن قائم کرنا، تسلی دینا، دلاسا دینا، راضی کرنا
examples: The mother tried to pacify the crying child. The government sent troops to pacify the region. He raised his hand to pacify the crowd. She could not pacify her angry friend. Sweet words often pacify difficult customers.
sindhiMeaning: ڪاوڙيل يا پريشان ماڻهوءَ کي ماٺ ڪرائڻ، ڪنهن علائقي ۾ امن قائم ڪرڻ، تسلي ڏيڻ، دلجاءِ ڪرائڻ، راضي ڪرڻ
antonyms: Anger, Enrage, Provoke, Agitate, Excite, Inflame

urduMeaning: رنگ برنگے لباسوں میں لوگوں کے جلوس پر مشتمل عوامی تفریح جو اکثر تاریخی مناظر پیش کرتی ہے، حسن کا مقابلہ، شاندار مظاہرہ، جلوس
synonyms: Show, Parade, Procession, Spectacle, Display, Ceremony, Contest
examples: The children performed a Christmas pageant at school. She won the beauty pageant last year. The town holds a historical pageant every summer. The wedding was a grand pageant of colour and music. A pageant was arranged for Independence Day.
sindhiMeaning: رنگ برنگي پوشاڪن ۾ ماڻهن جي جلوس واري عوامي تفريح جيڪا اڪثر تاريخي منظر ڏيکاري، خوبصورتيءَ جو مقابلو، پُرشان مظاهرو، جلوس
englishMeaning: A public entertainment consisting of a procession of people in elaborate, colourful costumes, often depicting scenes from history. A show, especially a beauty competition.
antonyms: Silence, Simplicity, Ordinary event, Plain gathering

examples: There was a lot of palaver about the small change in rules. I do not have time for all this palaver. After much palaver, they finally agreed. The palaver in the meeting achieved nothing. Do not create palaver over such a trivial issue.
urduMeaning: بے مقصد اور طویل گفتگو، فضول بحث و مباحثہ، معمولی بات پر غیر ضروری ہنگامہ، بیکار باتیں کرنا
englishMeaning: Prolonged and idle discussion. Unnecessary fuss or bother about something. To talk unproductively and at length.
synonyms: Fuss, Chatter, Prattle, Bother, Nonsense, Talk, Discussion
antonyms: Silence, Brevity, Conciseness, Action, Efficiency
sindhiMeaning: بيڪار ۽ ڊگهي بحث مباحثو، بيڪار جي ڪٿ ڪٿا، ڪنهن ننڍي معاملي تي وڌاءُ، جهڳڙو، فضول ڳالهيون ڪرڻ

examples: She felt a sudden pang of hunger. He experienced a pang of guilt after lying. A pang of jealousy crossed her face. The old memory brought a pang of sadness. He felt a sharp pang in his chest.
sindhiMeaning: اوچتي تيز درد يا جذباتي تڪليف، افسوس، پڇتاءَ يا بک جو اوچتو شديد احساس، سور جي جهاٽ
synonyms: Twinge, Ache, Stab, Pain, Prick, Sting, Spasm
urduMeaning: اچانک تیز درد یا جذباتی تکلیف، افسوس، ندامت یا بھوک کا فوری شدید احساس، درد کی لہر
antonyms: Comfort, Relief, Pleasure, Ease, Contentment, Joy
englishMeaning: A sudden sharp pain or painful emotion. A brief but strong feeling of an unpleasant or distressing emotion such as guilt, regret, or hunger.
The action of forgiving or being forgiven for an error or offence. To forgive a person for a mistake or crime. An official cancellation of the legal consequences of a crime.
sindhiMeaning: معافي، بخشش، ڪنهن غلطي يا ڏوهه لاءِ معاف ڪرڻ، سرڪاري طور تي ڏوهه جي سزا کي معاف ڪرڻ، مافي وٺڻ يا ڏيڻ
synonyms: Forgive, Excuse, Absolve, Acquit, Overlook, Reprieve, Exonerate
examples: I beg your pardon for interrupting you. The president granted him a full pardon. She asked pardon from her parents. Pardon me for being late. Please pardon my rude behaviour.
antonyms: Punish, Condemn, Blame, Convict, Sentence, Penalize
urduMeaning: معافی، بخشش، کسی غلطی یا جرم پر معاف کر دینا، سرکاری طور پر سزا معاف کر دینا، درگزر کرنا

sindhiMeaning: ننڍي فائدي يا رقم کي وڏي ڪاميابيءَ يا قدر ۾ تبديل ڪرڻ، جوا ۾ هڪ شرط جي جيت کي ٻي شرط تي هلائڻ، اثاثي کي وڌائڻ
examples: He parlayed his small savings into a large fortune. She parlayed her acting skills into a successful career. The company parlayed a single product into a global brand. He parlayed his internship into a permanent job. Investors parlay early gains into bigger profits.
englishMeaning: To use a small initial advantage or amount to gain something of much greater value. In gambling, to let the winnings from one bet ride on another.
urduMeaning: چھوٹے فائدے یا رقم کو بڑی کامیابی میں بدل دینا، جوئے میں ایک شرط کی جیت کو اگلی شرط پر لگا دینا، سرمائے کو بڑھانا
synonyms: Leverage, Convert, Transform, Exploit, Build up, Increase
antonyms: Waste, Squander, Lose, Diminish, Reduce

synonyms: Deflect, Ward off, Fend off, Block, Evade, Avoid, Dodge
examples: The swordsman parried his opponent’s attack. She parried every difficult question at the press conference. He parried the blow with his shield. The minister parried the criticism cleverly. She parried his advances politely.
urduMeaning: ہتھیار یا وار کو روکنا یا موڑنا، کسی سوال یا معاملے سے چالاکی سے بچ نکلنا، دفاع کرنا
sindhiMeaning: هٿيار يا وار کي روڪڻ يا ڦيرائڻ، ڪنهن سوال يا معاملي کان هوشياريءَ سان بچي وڃڻ، دفاع ڪرڻ
englishMeaning: To ward off a weapon or blow, especially with a countermove. To skillfully avoid answering a question or dealing with an issue.
antonyms: Attack, Strike, Confront, Accept, Face, Answer directly

urduMeaning: بیماری پیدا کرنے والے جراثیم، وائرس یا مائیکرو آرگنزم، بیماری کا سبب بننے والا عنصر
examples: The scientists identified a new pathogen in the samples. Washing hands helps stop the spread of pathogens. This pathogen can cause serious respiratory illness. Vaccines protect us against many pathogens. The lab studies dangerous pathogens under strict safety rules.
englishMeaning: A bacterium, virus, or other microorganism that can cause disease. Any agent that produces illness in a host organism.
synonyms: Germ, Virus, Bacterium, Microbe, Infection agent, Contaminant
sindhiMeaning: بيماري پيدا ڪندڙ جراثيم، وائرس يا مائڪرو آرگنزم، بيماريءَ جو سبب بڻجندڙ عنصر
antonyms: Antibody, Antigen (opposite context), Cure, Vaccine

synonyms: Sick person, Case, Calm, Tolerant, Enduring, Composed, Uncomplaining
examples: The doctor examined every patient carefully. Teachers must be patient with slow learners. She is a very patient listener. The patient recovered quickly after surgery. Be patient, help is on the way.
englishMeaning: A person receiving or registered to receive medical treatment. Able to accept or tolerate delays, problems, or suffering without becoming annoyed or anxious.
sindhiMeaning: طبي علاج وٺندڙ ماڻهو، مريض، صبر ڪندڙ، جيڪو تڪليف يا دير کي بنا چڙ چڙ برداشت ڪري
antonyms: Impatient, Restless, Intolerant, Irritable, Doctor, Healthy person
urduMeaning: طبی علاج حاصل کرنے والا شخص، مریض، صبر کرنے والا، جو مشکلات یا تاخیر بغیر غصے کے برداشت کرے

antonyms: Abundance, Plenty, Surplus, Excess, Sufficiency, Wealth
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ جو ٿورو يا اڻپورو مقدار، کوٽ، ڪمي، اڻاٺ، قلت
synonyms: Scarcity, Shortage, Lack, Dearth, Insufficiency, Rarity
englishMeaning: The presence of something in only small or insufficient quantities. Scarcity or lack of something.
urduMeaning: کسی چیز کی بہت کم یا ناکافی مقدار، کمی، قلت، فقدان، نایابی
examples: There is a paucity of clean drinking water in the village. The report highlights a paucity of skilled workers. A paucity of evidence weakened the case. Scientists complained about the paucity of funding. The paucity of information made planning difficult.

englishMeaning: The foot of an animal that has claws or nails, such as a cat, dog, or bear. To touch or handle something in a rough, awkward, or unwelcome way.
urduMeaning: بلی، کتے یا ریچھ جیسے جانور کا پنجہ، ناخن والا پاؤں، کسی چیز کو بھونڈے یا ناپسندیدہ انداز میں چھونا
sindhiMeaning: ٻلي، ڪتي يا رڇ جهڙي جانور جو پنجو، ننهن وارو پير، ڪنهن کي بيڊرنگ يا اڻ وڻندڙ نموني هٿ لائڻ
antonyms: Release, Let go, Ignore, Untouch
synonyms: Foot, Claw, Hand (informal), Handle, Touch, Grope
examples: The cat licked its paw clean. The dog gave me its paw to shake. The bear reached with a huge paw. Do not paw the exhibits in the museum. Please stop pawing at me.

urduMeaning: کسانوں، چھوٹے زمینداروں اور زرعی مزدوروں کا طبقہ، خاص طور پر روایتی معاشروں میں زراعت سے وابستہ لوگوں کی جماعت، کسان طبقہ
englishMeaning: Peasants considered as a group or class. The body of small farmers and agricultural labourers in a country, especially in traditional societies.
synonyms: Farmers, Rural folk, Country people, Tillers, Serfs
examples: The peasantry suffered under the old landlord system. Land reforms helped uplift the peasantry. Novels of that era often depict the life of the peasantry. The peasantry played a key role in the revolution. Education among the peasantry is improving.
sindhiMeaning: هارين، ڏتڙيل زميندارن ۽ زرعي مزدورن جو گروهه، عام طور تي روايتي معاشرن ۾ زراعت سان جڙيل ماڻهن جو طبقو، هاري طبقو
antonyms: Nobility, Aristocracy, Elite, Gentry, Ruling class
Honesty, Integrity, Fair dealing, Trustworthiness
urduMeaning: امانت میں رکھی گئی رقم، خاص طور پر سرکاری پیسے کی چوری یا خرد برد، مالی خیانت، بدعنوانی
englishMeaning: The act of embezzling or stealing money, especially public funds, entrusted to one’s care.
sindhiMeaning: امانت ۾ رکيل رقم، خاص طور تي سرڪاري پئسي جي چوري يا خردبرد، مالي بددياتي، بدعنواني
examples: The officer was dismissed for peculation. Peculation of public funds is a serious crime. An audit revealed peculation in the department. He was jailed for peculation of charity money. Strict rules were introduced to prevent peculation.
synonyms: Embezzlement, Misappropriation, Theft, Fraud, Corruption
Embezzler, Thief, Fraudster, Swindler, Cheat

englishMeaning: A network of paths and hedges designed as a puzzle through which one has to find a way. A confusing labyrinth. A confusing mass of information or complicated situation.
urduMeaning: بھول بھلیاں، پیچ در پیچ راستہ، مشکل راستہ، پیچیدہ صورتحال، الجھا ہوا معاملہ، مغالطہ آمیز ماحول، گمراہ کن راستہ

englishMeaning: An alcoholic drink made by fermenting honey with water, sometimes with fruits, spices, grains, or hops. A meadow. A traditional drink dating from ancient times.
examples: The tavern served mead in wooden cups. Vikings were known for drinking mead. The cows grazed in the green mead. Homemade mead can take months to ferment. He offered his guests a glass of mead.
synonyms: Honey wine, Fermented honey drink, Meadow, Pasture, Grassland

englishMeaning: The usual time at which a meal is eaten. Breakfast, lunch, or dinner time. Any scheduled time for eating.
antonyms: Fasting period, Non eating hours
synonyms: Dinnertime, Lunchtime, Breakfast time, Suppertime, Feeding time

examples: The family gathers together at mealtime. Mealtime is a good time for conversation. Please wash your hands before mealtime. Mealtime is strictly at seven in the evening. Children look forward to mealtime.
urduMeaning: کھانے کا وقت، ناشتہ، دوپہر یا رات کے کھانے کا وقت، طعام کا مقررہ وقت، وقت طعام، دستر خوان کا وقت

antonyms: Straight path, Direct route, Focus, Go straight
sindhiMeaning: ٺلهو ڦرڻ گهرڻ، ڪا صاف رستي کان هٽي وچڙيل واٽ وٺڻ، درياءَ جو موڙ وارو وهڪرو، بيمقصد گهمڻ، وچڙيل نموني ڳالهائڻ
urduMeaning: ٹیڑھے میڑھے چلنا، بے مقصد گھومنا، دریا کا خمدار بہاؤ، سست روی سے چلنا، بھٹکنا، بلا مقصد بات کرنا، پیچیدہ راستہ اختیار کرنا
englishMeaning: To follow a winding course. To wander aimlessly. A curve or bend in a river or road. Rambling in speech or writing.
examples: The river meanders through the valley. Tourists meandered through the market. Her speech meandered from topic to topic. We meandered along the country lane. The path meanders around old oak trees.

urduMeaning: دوران، اسی دوران، اسی وقت میں، ادھر، ادھر ادھر، اسی اثنا میں، اسی عرصے میں، ساتھ ساتھ
synonyms: Meantime, Simultaneously, Concurrently, At the same time, In the interim
examples: She cooked dinner. Meanwhile, he set the table. Meanwhile, the situation abroad grew worse. Meanwhile, the children played in the yard. He waited at the station. Meanwhile, the bus was delayed. Meanwhile, everyone else had finished their work.
englishMeaning: At the same time. In the intervening period. Meanwhile is used to describe events that happen at the same time or during the same period as another event.
sindhiMeaning: دوران، ايتري ۾، ساڳي وقت، ساڳئي وقت تي، ٻئي پاسي، اوچتو، انهيءَ عرصي دوران
antonyms: Afterwards, Later, Subsequently, Before, Earlier

sindhiMeaning: معمولي پڻو، اوسط درجي، خاص نه هجڻ، درميانو معيار، عام حيثيت جو ماڻهو، بي مثال نه هجڻ، بيهودو معيار
urduMeaning: معمولی پن، اوسط درجہ، خاص نہ ہونا، درمیانی معیار، عام حیثیت کا شخص، غیر معیاری کارکردگی، بے کیفی، عام سطح کی صلاحیت
antonyms: Excellence, Distinction, Superiority, Brilliance, Greatness, Mastery
englishMeaning: The quality or state of being average or ordinary. Lack of high quality or excellence. A person of only average ability.
examples: He was tired of the mediocrity of his job. She refused to settle for mediocrity in her work. The film was dismissed as mere mediocrity. Their team suffered from years of mediocrity. Do not accept mediocrity in your studies.

antonyms: Punishment, Penalty, Deprivation, Loss, Forfeit
englishMeaning: A deserved share or reward. A well earned recognition or portion. An archaic word for wages or recompense.
sindhiMeaning: حقدار جو حصو، انعام، محنت جو معاوضو، لائق اجر، منصفانه بدلو، پراڻو لفظ جيڪو معاوضي لاءِ استعمال ٿئي
examples: He received the meed of his hard work. Every soldier deserves the meed of praise. Poets often speak of the meed of glory. She earned the meed of her efforts. The knight received a meed of gold.
synonyms: Reward, Recompense, Prize, Share, Due, Payment, Recognition
urduMeaning: مستحق حصہ، انعام، محنت کا معاوضہ، جائز اجر، منصفانہ بدلہ، پرانا لفظ جو معاوضے کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے، جزائے کار

synonyms: Humble, Docile, Gentle, Mild, Submissive, Compliant, Modest, Quiet
urduMeaning: نرم دل، حلیم، اکسانے پر نہ لڑنے والا، بردبار، فرمانبردار، سادہ، عاجز، خاکسار، بے زبان، بردار، نم مزاج
examples: The meek child rarely spoke in class. Blessed are the meek, according to the Bible. Her meek nature made her easy to work with. He gave a meek reply to the harsh question. Do not mistake her meek manner for weakness.
englishMeaning: Quiet, gentle, and easily imposed on. Submissive. Humble in disposition or behavior. Not proud or self assertive.
sindhiMeaning: نرم، حليم، اکيلو، بردبار، خاڪسار، فرمانبردار، سادو، بي زبان، هيٺانهون، بي غصو
antonyms: Arrogant, Bold, Aggressive, Assertive, Proud, Defiant, Overbearing

antonyms: Cortisol, Wake hormone, Stimulant hormone

examples: Doctors prescribed melatonin to help him sleep. Melatonin levels rise at night. Travelers use melatonin to overcome jet lag. Sunlight affects melatonin production. Melatonin is sold as a sleep aid.
englishMeaning: A hormone produced by the pineal gland that regulates sleep and wakefulness. A dietary supplement used to promote sleep. A substance influencing circadian rhythms.
urduMeaning: نیند کا ہارمون، پائنیل غدود سے خارج ہونے والا ہارمون، نیند کو منظم کرنے والا مادہ، نیند لانے والی دوا، جسم کی حیاتیاتی گھڑی کو کنٹرول کرنے والا

urduMeaning: سُر، دھن، راگ، خوش کن آواز، موسیقی کا مرکزی سُر، گیت کی دھن، آواز کی مٹھاس، ترنم، آہنگ
sindhiMeaning: سُر، راڳ، مٺو آواز، موسيقيءَ جو مکيه سُر، گيت جو مکيه رخ، آواز جي مٺاڻ، ڌن، سازن جو تال ميل

examples: The dog growled menacingly. He raised his hand menacingly. The clouds gathered menacingly over the town. She stared menacingly at her rival. The tiger crept menacingly toward its prey.

antonyms: Menarche, Puberty, Reproductive age, Fertility

englishMeaning: Material made of a network of wire or thread. Openings or spaces in a net. To fit or work together. To become entangled. A complex situation.
examples: The window was covered with a fine mesh. The gears must mesh smoothly. Their ideas meshed perfectly. She got caught in the mesh of lies. Wire mesh kept the birds out of the garden.
urduMeaning: جالی، جال، تاروں یا دھاگوں کا جال، آپس میں ملنا، اچھی طرح کام کرنا، پھنس جانا، ہم آہنگ ہونا، پیچیدہ صورتحال، تعاون کرنا
antonyms: Separate, Clash, Disconnect, Solid surface, Diverge, Conflict
sindhiMeaning: جالو، ڄاري، تارن يا ڌاڳن جو ڄارو، ڀيڙا ٿيڻ، سٺي نموني ڪم ڪرڻ، ڦاسي وڃڻ، لڳ ڀڳ ٿيڻ، پيچيده صورتحال

synonyms: Isolate, Segregate, Seclude, Confiscate, Seize, Appropriate, Expropriate, Hide, Conceal, Separate
antonyms: Integrate, Mingle, Socialize, Release, Free, Return, Restore, Unify

englishMeaning: A conclusion or statement that logically follows from the previous argument or statement. A logical consequence. An inference that follows from a set of premises.
antonyms: Non sequitur, Irrelevance, Inconsequence, Disconnection, Unrelatedness, Premise, Assumption

urduMeaning: وحشت، بربریت، جنگلی پن، شدید یا ظالمانہ ہونے کا معیار، انتہائی ظلم، بربریت یا تشدد کا ایک عمل یہ تہذیب اور ہمدردی کی مکمل کمی کو ظاہر کرتا ہے
antonyms: Civilization, Gentleness, Humanity, Kindness, Mildness, Benevolence, Compassion, Decency
englishMeaning: The quality of being fierce or cruel. The condition of being primitive or uncivilized. An act of extreme cruelty, brutality, or violence. It suggests a complete lack of civilization and compassion.
sindhiMeaning: وحشت، بربريت، جهنگلي پڻو، تيز يا ظالم هجڻ جو معيار، انتهائي ظلم، بربريت يا تشدد جو ڪم اهو تهذيب ۽ شفقت جي مڪمل کوٽ کي ظاهر ڪري ٿو
examples: The war was marked by acts of unimaginable savagery. The film depicted the savagery of life in the wild. The savagery of the attack shocked the nation. There was a primitive savagery in his determination to win. He condemned the savagery of the regime.
synonyms: Brutality, Ferocity, Barbarity, Cruelty, Viciousness, Barbarism, Fierceness, Atrocity, Inhumanity
Rescuer, Liberator, Redeemer, Deliverer, Guardian, Protector, Champion, Defender, Good Samaritan
sindhiMeaning: بچائيندڙ, نجات ڏيندڙ، ڇڏائيندڙ، محافظ، پناهه ڏيندڙ، هڪ شخص جيڪو ڪنهن کي خطري يا مشڪل کان بچائيندو آهي
urduMeaning: بچانے والا، نجات دہندہ، چھڑانے والا، محافظ، پناہ دینے والا، ایک شخص جو کسی کو خطرے یا مشکل سے بچاتا ہے

antonyms: Destroyer, Oppressor, Adversary, Antagonist, Enemy, Foe, Captor

englishMeaning: To enjoy or appreciate something completely. To taste good food or drink and enjoy it completely. To relish a memory or experience.
antonyms: Dislike, Hate, Detest, Loathe, Abhor, Despise, Reject
sindhiMeaning: ذائقو وٺڻ، لطف اندوز ٿيڻ، مزو وٺڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ جو پورو پورو مزو وٺڻ يا ان جي تعريف ڪرڻ
synonyms: Relish, Enjoy, Appreciate, Delight in, Revel in, Cherish, Treasure, Bask in, Luxuriate in
urduMeaning: ذائقہ لینا، لطف اندوز ہونا، مزہ لینا، کسی چیز کا پورا پورا مزہ لینا یا اس کی تعریف کرنا
examples: She savored every moment of her vacation. He savored the taste of the fine wine. I want to savor this victory. Let's savor the beautiful sunset.
The surgeon made a precise incision with a scalpel. A scalpel must be sterilized before use. He held the scalpel steady. The artist used a scalpel for detailed paper cutting.

urduMeaning: جراحی کا چاقو، نشتر، جراح کا چھرا، ایک چھوٹا اور انتہائی تیز چاقو جو ایک سرجن استعمال کرتا ہے

antonyms: Blunt object, Mallet, Hammer, Club, Paddle, Spatula
sindhiMeaning: چاقو، جراحي وارو ننڍڙو چاقو، آپريشن جو اوزار، هڪ ننڍڙو ۽ انتهائي تيز چاقو جيڪو سرجن استعمال ڪندو آهي

englishMeaning: A disgraceful or discreditable action or event. An action or event regarded as morally or legally wrong, causing general public outrage. It often involves allegations of wrongdoing that damage a reputation.
antonyms: Praise, Honor, Glory, Acclaim, Credit, Esteem, Commendation
examples: The political scandal dominated the headlines for weeks. The company was rocked by a financial scandal. She was at the center of a huge scandal. The scandal led to the minister's resignation.
urduMeaning: اسکینڈل، بدنامی، رسوائی، بہتان، ایک ایسا عمل یا واقعہ جو اخلاقی یا قانونی طور پر غلط سمجھا جائے اور عام لوگوں میں غم و غصے کا سبب بنے
sindhiMeaning: بدنامي، رسوائي، تهمت، اهڙو عمل يا واقعو جيڪو اخلاقي يا قانوني طور تي غلط سمجهيو وڃي ۽ عام ماڻهن ۾ غم ۽ غصي جو سبب بڻجي
synonyms: Disgrace, Outrage, Dishonor, Reproach, Uproar, Offense, Sensation, Controversy, Exposé, Affair

urduMeaning: بدنام کرنا، رسوا کرنا، کسی کو بے عزتی والے عمل سے صدمہ یا خوفزدہ کرنا
synonyms: Shock, Appall, Outrage, Offend, Horrify, Disgust, Repulse, Mortify, Disgrace
sindhiMeaning: بدنام ڪرڻ، رسوا ڪرڻ، ڪنهن کي بي عزتي واري عمل سان صدمو يا خوفزده ڪرڻ
examples: The celebrity's behavior scandalized the public. Their affair scandalized the small town. He was scandalized by her lack of manners. The revealing photos were intended to scandalize her conservative family.
englishMeaning: To shock or horrify someone by a disgraceful action. To offend the moral feelings of someone. It means to cause a scandal or to bring disgrace upon someone or something.
antonyms: Please, Delight, Charm, Impress, Flatter, Soothe, Honor
Pale, Ashen, White, Colorless, Dull, Muted, Green, Cyan
examples: She wore a stunning scarlet dress to the gala. The autumn leaves turned a beautiful scarlet hue before falling. His face went scarlet with embarrassment after the mistake. Historically, the robes of cardinals were dyed a deep scarlet.
englishMeaning: A brilliant red color. A type of bright red cloth, often associated with luxury or official uniforms. Symbolically, it can represent sin, passion, or courage.
urduMeaning: گہرا سرخ رنگ، قرمزی، شنگرفی، ایک قسم کا چمکدار سرخ کپڑا، گناہ یا برائی کی علامت
sindhiMeaning: ڳاڙهو، گهرو لال رنگ، قرمزي، شنگرفي، هڪ قسم جو روشن لال ڪپڙو، گناهه يا برائي جي علامت
synonyms: Crimson, Ruby, Vermilion, Cherry, Cardinal Red, Bright Red, Fiery Red, Blood Red, Carmine

englishMeaning: Pleasure derived by someone from another person's misfortune. A feeling of joy or satisfaction when one sees or hears about the troubles of others. It is a complex emotion, often felt towards a rival or someone disliked.
sindhiMeaning: ٻئي جي تڪليف مان خوشي، غير جي نقصان تي خوشي، ٻئي جي بدحالي تي خوش ٿيڻ جو احساس
antonyms: Compassion, Sympathy, Pity, Empathy, Commiseration, Benevolence, Mercy
synonyms: Malicious Joy, Gloating, Epicaricacy, Sadistic Pleasure, Malevolent Glee, Triumph, Vicious Satisfaction
urduMeaning: دوسروں کی تکلیف سے خوشی، غیر کے نقصان پر خوشی، دوسرے کی بدحالی پر خوش ہونے کا احساس
examples: He couldn't help but feel a touch of schadenfreude when his arrogant boss was fired. Social media comments were full of schadenfreude after the influencer's public apology. She felt a guilty sense of schadenfreude watching her competitor stumble during the race. To feel schadenfreude is a common, if not particularly noble, human emotion.

antonyms: Release, Statement, Announcement, Common Knowledge, Public Record, Official Report
sindhiMeaning: چمچو، ڊوئي، ڪَرڇو، خاص خبر، اڳواٽ خبر، کڻڻ، خبر جيڪا ٻين کان اڳ ڏني وڃي
englishMeaning: A utensil resembling a spoon, with a short handle and a deep bowl. A piece of exclusive news published or broadcast before one's rivals. The quantity of material taken up by a scoop. The act of picking something up in a swift, continuous movement.
examples: Use the metal scoop to measure the coffee beans. The journalist received an anonymous tip and got the biggest scoop of her career. Can I have one scoop of vanilla and one of chocolate? The crane will scoop up the debris from the construction site.
synonyms: Ladle, Shovel, Spoon, Dipper, Exclusive, Revelation, Exposé, Inside Story, Beat
urduMeaning: چمچہ، ڈوئی، کرچھا، خصوصی خبر، سب سے پہلے شائع ہونے والی خبر، اٹھانا، خبر جو دوسروں سے پہلے دی جائے

examples: She looked at him with utter scorn when he lied. The determined artist scorned the critics' negative reviews and continued her work. His offer of a bribe was met with scorn. They poured scorn on his revolutionary ideas, only to adopt them years later.
synonyms: Contempt, Derision, Disdain, Mockery, Sneering, Disrespect, Contemptuousness, Disparagement, Revulsion
urduMeaning: نفرت، حقارت، بے عزتی، کم نظر سے دیکھنا، نفرت کرنا، حقارت سے دیکھنا، بے عزت کرنا
englishMeaning: The feeling or expression of contempt or derision. Open disrespect for someone or something. To reject, refuse, or dismiss something with contempt. It implies a strong sense of superiority over the object of contempt.
antonyms: Admiration, Respect, Approval, Praise, Esteem, Veneration, Honor, Adoration
sindhiMeaning: نفرت، حقارت، بي عزتي، گهٽ نظر سان ڏسڻ، نفرت ڪرڻ، حقارت سان ڏسڻ، بي عزت ڪرڻ

synonyms: Transfer, Assignment, Deployment, Relocation, Posting, Loan, Detachment
examples: She is on a six-month secondment to our marketing department. The secondment gave him valuable experience in a different field. He applied for a secondment to the company's international branch. The agreement outlines the terms of his secondment.
englishMeaning: The temporary transfer of an employee to another position or organization. A period of time when an employee is sent to work elsewhere to gain new skills or experience. This is a common practice in large corporations and government bodies for professional development.
urduMeaning: عارضی منتقلی، دوسرے محکمے میں عارضی طور پر جانا، کسی ملازم کو دوسرے محکمے یا تنظیم میں عارضی طور پر بھیجنے کا عمل
antonyms: Permanence, Retention, Stagnation, Inactivity, Stasis, Fixity

urduMeaning: رطوبت، اخراج، تراوش، کسی خلیے، غدود یا عضو سے مادے کے پیدا ہونے اور خارج ہونے کا عمل
englishMeaning: The process by which substances are produced and discharged from a cell, gland, or organ. A substance that is secreted. In biology, it refers to the movement of material from one point to another, such as a hormone into the blood. It can also refer to the act of concealing something.
sindhiMeaning: رطوبت، نڪرڻ، خارج ٿيڻ، ڪنهن جيو گھرڙي، غدود يا عضوي مان مادي جو نڪرڻ ۽ خارج ٿيڻ جو عمل
antonyms: Absorption, Ingestion, Assimilation, Intake, Revelation, Disclosure
synonyms: Discharge, Emission, Excretion, Oozing, Exudation, Issuance, Production, Concealment
examples: The secretion of hormones is essential for bodily functions. The plant has a sticky secretion that traps insects. This gland is responsible for the secretion of saliva. The police were investigating the secretion of illegal funds.

englishMeaning: Capable of being cut smoothly with a knife. Relating to a mineral that can be cut into thin shavings. This property is characteristic of certain soft minerals like gypsum or talc.
examples: Gold is a sectile metal that can be easily shaped. The geologist identified the mineral as sectile. Unlike brittle minerals, sectile ones do not crumble when cut. Talc is known for being very soft and sectile.
synonyms: Cuttable, Carvable, Malleable, Pliant, Soft, Workable, Ductile
urduMeaning: نرم، کاٹنے کے قابل، وہ چیز جسے چاقو سے آسانی سے کاٹا جا سکے

sindhiMeaning: نرم، ڪٽڻ لائق، اها شيءِ جنهن کي چاقو سان آسانيءَ سان ڪٽي سگهجي

synonyms: Division, Zone, Area, District, Region, Sphere, Field, Branch, Category, Department
urduMeaning: شعبہ، حصہ، علاقہ، ایک دائرے کا وہ حصہ جو دو ریڈیس اور ان کے درمیان قوس سے گھرا ہو
examples: The financial sector is a critical component of the economy. A new military sector was established along the border. The city was divided into several administrative sectors. She works in the public sector.

examples: The plant's leaves looked unhealthy and scurfy. His skin became dry and scurfy in the winter. The old book had a scurfy, disintegrating leather cover. A scurfy scalp needs immediate and special treatment. The unpolished wood had a scurfy texture.

antonyms: Smooth, Clean, Clear, Sleek, Polished, Glossy, Unblemished
Fact, Truth, Reality, Certainty, News, Report, Evidence, Proof

englishMeaning: Rumor or gossip. An informal term often used in nautical or military contexts. A drinking fountain on a ship, which traditionally served as a place for sailors to gather and chat.
synonyms: Gossip, Rumor, Hearsay, Tattle, Idle talk, Chatter, Canard, Grapevine, Whispers, Report
examples: The scuttlebutt around the office is that the CEO is resigning. I don't pay much attention to scuttlebutt; I prefer facts. What's the latest scuttlebutt from the naval base?. The crew exchanged scuttlebutt while on their break. She heard the scuttlebutt about the surprise party.

He had a scrupulous regard for the truth. The research was carried out with scrupulous attention to detail. She is scrupulous in her work. He is too scrupulous to take advantage of the situation. The scrupulous accountant would not let even a penny go unaccounted for.
urduMeaning: محتاط، باریک بین، ایماندار، دیانت دار، فرض شناس، خبردار وہ شخص جو اخلاقی اصولوں کی سختی سے پابندی کرتا ہے اور ضمیر کے خلاف کوئی کام نہیں کرتا
synonyms: Meticulous, Conscientious, Thorough, Principled, Honest, Upright, Righteous, Moral, Careful, Fastidious

antonyms: Unscrupulous, Careless, Negligent, Dishonest, Unprincipled, Lax, Remiss
englishMeaning: Diligent, thorough, and extremely attentive to details. Very careful and precise. Having or showing a strict regard for what one considers right; principled. Very concerned to avoid doing wrong.
A layer of impure matter on the surface of a liquid. A worthless or contemptible person or group of people. This informal term expresses strong disdain.
urduMeaning: میل، گندگی، جھاگ، فضول لوگ، گھٹیا انسان، معاشرے کے ناسور مائع کی سطح پر جمع ہونے والی گندگی کی تہہ
examples: He skimmed the scum off the jam as it cooled. The pond was covered with a thick layer of green scum. They considered him the scum of the earth. The politician referred to the protestors as scum. She felt like scum after her mistake.
synonyms: Froth, Film, Dregs, Residue, Rabble, Riffraff, Trash, Refuse, Dross, Offscouring
antonyms: Elite, Cream, Gentry, Aristocracy, Nobility, Flower, Finest

synonyms: Random, Wholesale, Haphazard, Thoughtless, Undiscriminating, Careless, Reckless
examples: The police warned against the indiscriminate use of fireworks in crowded areas. Indiscriminate cutting of trees can seriously damage the environment. She avoids the indiscriminate sharing of personal information on social media. The disease spread because of the indiscriminate movement of infected animals.
urduMeaning: بغیر سوچ سمجھ یا امتیاز کے، اندھا دھند، بلا تفریق سب پر لاگو ہونے والا, ایسے عمل  فیصلے یا رویے کو کہتے ہیں جو بغیر کسی امتیاز  انتخاب یا غور و فکر کے کیا جائے, اس کا مطلب ہے ہر شخص یا ہر چیز کے ساتھ ایک جیسا برتاؤ کرنا  چاہے وہ مناسب ہو یا نہ ہو, یہ لفظ اکثر منفی مفہوم میں استعمال ہوتا ہے
englishMeaning: Done without careful judgment, selection, or distinction. Affecting or including everyone or everything without considering differences. Actions, behavior, or decisions made without careful choice, judgment, or discrimination. It refers to treating all people or things the same regardless of differences, quality, suitability, or consequences. The word is often used negatively to describe careless, random, excessive, or uncontrolled actions.
sindhiMeaning: بغير چونڊ يا فرق ڪرڻ جي، اندھاڌند، بنا سوچ ويچار جي سڀني تي لاڳو ٿيندڙ, ان عمل  فيصلي يا رويي کي چيو ويندو آهي جيڪو بغير فرق ڪرڻ  چونڊ ڪرڻ يا سوچ ويچار جي ڪيو وڃي, اهڙو عمل جيڪو سڀني ماڻهن يا شين سان هڪجهڙو ورتاءُ ڪري  ڀلي اهي مناسب هجن يا نه, هي لفظ گهڻو ڪري منفي معنيٰ ۾ استعمال ٿيندو آهي
antonyms: Selective, Discriminating, Careful, Judicious, Deliberate, Targeted
Selectively, Carefully, Deliberately, Discriminately, Purposefully
englishMeaning: Without making careful choices or distinctions. In a random, uncontrolled, or impartial manner. Doing something without selecting carefully, without considering differences, or without proper judgment. It often describes actions that affect everyone or everything equally, whether appropriate or not. Depending on the context, it may carry a negative meaning (carelessly or recklessly) or a neutral meaning (equally without favoritism).
sindhiMeaning: بي امتيازيءَ سان، بنا فرق ڪرڻ جي، بنا چونڊ جي، اندھا ڌند، بي پرواهي سان، بي سوچي سمجهي، سڀني سان هڪجهڙو سلوڪ ڪندي، بنا سڃاڻپ جي، بي ترتيب نموني، هر طرف، بنا انصاف واري چونڊ جي
examples: The storm damaged houses indiscriminately across the entire village. He spent money indiscriminately without thinking about the future. The disease spread indiscriminately among people of all ages. Do not use pesticides indiscriminately because they can harm helpful insects.
urduMeaning: بلا امتیاز، بغیر فرق کیے، اندھا دھند، لاپرواہی سے، بغیر سوچے سمجھے، بغیر انتخاب کے، یکساں طور پر، بے ترتیب انداز میں، بغیر مناسب فیصلہ کیے، سب پر برابر اثر انداز ہوتے ہوئے
synonyms: Randomly, Haphazardly, Carelessly, Without distinction, Recklessly, Blindly

englishMeaning: The best, most favorable, or most effective level, condition, or amount for achieving a desired result. The ideal or most advantageous condition, level, quantity, or degree at which something works best or produces the greatest benefit. It describes the perfect balance between too little and too much.
antonyms: Worst, Poor, Inferior, Unsuitable, Inappropriate, Inefficient, Unfavorable, Harmful, Deficient, Imperfect, Inadequate, Substandard

urduMeaning: شروع سے، بالکل ابتدا سے، پہلے ہی مرحلے سے، بنیادی سطح سے، کسی چیز کو ازسر نو یا آغاز سے شروع کرنا

englishMeaning: A Latin phrase meaning to whose benefit. Used to ask who gains from a particular action or event. A principle used in law to identify the beneficiary of a crime or act. Questioning who profits from a certain situation. Investigating the motive behind an act by examining who benefits.
urduMeaning: کس کے فائدے میں، کس کو فائدہ پہنچتا ہے، کسی کام سے کس کو فائدہ ہوتا ہے، کس کے مفاد میں ہے، فائدہ اٹھانے والے شخص کی نشاندہی کرنا
examples: In every investigation, we must ask cui bono. Cui bono is a key question in criminal cases. The lawyer applied the principle of cui bono to find the real culprit. Cui bono often reveals hidden motives behind events.
synonyms: Who benefits, For whose advantage, To whose profit, Beneficiary question
antonyms: Selfless act, Without motive, No gain
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن جي فائدي لاءِ، ڪنهن کي نفعو پهچي ٿو، ڪنهن ڪم مان ڪنهن کي فائدو رسي ٿو، ڪنهن جي مفاد ۾ آهي، فائدي واري شخص جي نشاندهي

englishMeaning: A classical or authoritative passage often quoted as the best example on a subject. A standard reference or original text on a particular topic. A well-known passage considered the finest illustration of an idea. A definitive source used to explain or support a concept. The most cited or respected example in literature or study.

urduMeaning: اس حد تک کہ بیزاری پیدا ہو جائے، حد سے زیادہ دہرانا، اتنی دیر تک کہ لوگ تنگ آ جائیں، بار بار وہی بات کرنا، اکتاہٹ کی حد تک

urduMeaning: بے وقوفانہ یا بے معنی بات، بالکل جھوٹی یا مضحکہ خیز بات، بے کار اور بے بنیاد بیان، فضول اور بے مقصد گفتگو، بکواس یا جھوٹا دعویٰ
