examples: He was diagnosed with contact dermatitis after using the soap. Dermatitis can be treated with proper medication. Cold weather often worsens dermatitis symptoms. She consulted a dermatologist about her dermatitis.
sindhiMeaning: چمڙيءَ جي سوز، جنهن سبب لالاڻ  چڪ ۽ سُڄَ ٿئي، الرجي، ڪيميائي شين يا چڙ جي ڪري ٿيندڙ چمڙيءَ جي بيماري، مختلف قسم جي چمڙيءَ جي دانن جو عام نالو

antonyms: Dry skin, Healthy skin, Clear complexion
englishMeaning: A skin condition marked by excessive oil production from the sebaceous glands. A disorder that causes greasy, scaly patches on the scalp or face. Overactivity of oil glands leading to dandruff, redness, and irritation.
synonyms: Oily skin, Seborrheic dermatitis, Greasiness, Skin disorder
sindhiMeaning: چمڙيءَ جي بيماري جنهن ۾ تيل جا غدود گهڻو تيل پيدا ڪن، مٿي يا منهن تي چڪٽيدار ۽ ذرن وارا نشان ٿيڻ، تيل جي گهڻي پيداوار جي ڪري لالاڻ ۽ چڙ ٿيڻ
urduMeaning: جلد کی وہ حالت جس میں چکنائی پیدا کرنے والے غدود زیادہ تیل خارج کرتے ہیں، سر یا چہرے پر چکنے اور کھردرے دھبے پیدا کرنے والا مرض، تیل کی زیادتی سے سرخی، خارش اور خشکی پیدا ہونا
examples: Seborrhea is common in both infants and adults. The doctor prescribed a medicated shampoo for seborrhea. Seborrhea often affects the scalp and face. Stress can worsen the symptoms of seborrhea.

synonyms: Peeling, Scrubbing, Shedding, Cleansing, Renewal
antonyms: Buildup, Accumulation, Retention, Growth
urduMeaning: جلد کی سطح سے مردہ خلیوں کو ہٹانے کا عمل، جلد کی بیرونی تہہ کا قدرتی طور پر جھڑ جانا، جلد کو صاف اور تروتازہ کرنے والا خوبصورتی کا علاج، پتھروں  درختوں کی چھال یا جلد کا تہہ در تہہ اترنا
examples: Regular exfoliation makes the skin smoother and brighter. The spa offers a full-body exfoliation treatment. Exfoliation helps remove dry and dead skin cells. Geologists study the exfoliation of large rocks.
englishMeaning: The process of removing dead cells from the surface of the skin. The natural shedding of the outer layer of skin. A cosmetic treatment that cleanses and renews the skin. The peeling off of rock, bark, or skin in layers.
sindhiMeaning: چمڙيءَ جي مٿاڇري تان مئل ذرن کي هٽائڻ جو عمل، چمڙيءَ جي ٻاهرين تهه جو قدرتي طور تي لهي وڃڻ، چمڙيءَ کي صاف ۽ نئون ڪرڻ وارو حسن جو علاج، پٿرن  ٿڙ يا چمڙيءَ جي تهن جو لهڻ

synonyms: Legality, Legitimacy, Validity, Justice, Righteousness, Compliance
antonyms: Unlawfulness, Illegality, Injustice, Wrongdoing, Corruption, Crime
englishMeaning: The quality of being in accordance with the law. The state of being legal, permitted, or justified by rules. Respect for and obedience to the laws of a society.
examples: The judge questioned the lawfulness of the arrest. Citizens must respect the lawfulness of the government. The lawfulness of his actions was widely praised. The report examined the lawfulness of the new policy.
sindhiMeaning: قانون مطابق هجڻ جي حالت، قانوني ۽ جائز هجڻ جي خاصيت، قانون جو احترام ۽ فرمانبرداري
urduMeaning: قانون کے مطابق ہونے کی حالت، جائز اور قانونی ہونے کی خصوصیت، قانون کا احترام اور اطاعت

synonyms: Rebellious, Insubordinate, Disobedient, Resistant, Bold, Challenging, Insolent
antonyms: Obedient, Submissive, Compliant, Respectful, Yielding, Meek
englishMeaning: Openly resisting or refusing to obey authority. Showing bold disobedience or challenge. Displaying a strong and fearless attitude against control. Refusing to accept rules, orders, or opposition.
urduMeaning: اختیار کی کھلی مخالفت کرنے والا، حکم عدولی کرنے والا، بےخوف اور جرأت مندانہ رویہ رکھنے والا، قواعد یا احکامات ماننے سے انکار کرنے والا
sindhiMeaning: اختيار جي مخالفت ڪندڙ، کليل نافرماني ڪندڙ، دلير ۽ بيباڪ انداز سان مقابلو ڪندڙ، قاعدن يا حڪمن کي مڃڻ کان انڪار ڪندڙ
examples: The defiant child refused to listen to his parents. She gave a defiant look to the officer. The protesters remained defiant despite the warnings. His defiant tone shocked the audience.

antonyms: Loyal, Obedient, Peaceful, Compliant, Law-abiding, Submissive
synonyms: Rebellious, Revolutionary, Mutinous, Seditious, Insurgent, Uprising
sindhiMeaning: بغاوت يا حڪومت خلاف اٿاءَ سان تعلق رکندڙ، بغاوت جي حوصلا افزائي ڪندڙ، مسلح مخالفت وارو، بغاوت ۾ حصو وٺندڙ شخص
examples: The government banned all insurrectionary activities. The book described the insurrectionary movements of the century. He was accused of making insurrectionary speeches. The insurrectionary forces gathered in the mountains.
englishMeaning: Relating to or involving a revolt against authority. Encouraging or supporting an uprising. Characterized by rebellion or armed resistance. Someone who takes part in an insurrection.
urduMeaning: بغاوت یا حکومت کے خلاف اٹھ کھڑے ہونے سے متعلق، بغاوت کی حوصلہ افزائی کرنے والا، مسلح مزاحمت پر مبنی، بغاوت میں شریک شخص

examples: His provocative remarks upset many people. The film raised provocative questions about society. She wore a provocative dress to the party. The article had a provocative title to attract readers.
englishMeaning: Causing anger, excitement, or strong reaction. Intended to stimulate discussion or thought. Deliberately arousing sexual interest or attention. Challenging accepted norms in a bold way.
urduMeaning: غصہ، جوش یا شدید ردعمل پیدا کرنے والا، سوچ یا بحث کو ابھارنے والا، جان بوجھ کر جنسی توجہ حاصل کرنے والا، عام روایات کو چیلنج کرنے والا
sindhiMeaning: ڪاوڙ، جوش يا سخت ردعمل پيدا ڪندڙ، سوچ يا بحث کي اڀاريندڙ، جان بوجهه ڪري جنسي دلچسپي وڌائيندڙ، عام قدرن کي چيلينج ڪندڙ
synonyms: Stimulating, Inflammatory, Challenging, Inciting, Alluring, Suggestive, Controversial
antonyms: Soothing, Calming, Dull, Uninteresting, Peaceful, Pacifying

synonyms: Inflammatory, Provocative, Combustible, Fiery, Seditious, Explosive, Arsonist
urduMeaning: آگ لگانے یا دھماکہ کرنے کے لیے تیار کیا گیا، جھگڑا، غصہ یا تشدد بھڑکانے والا، جان بوجھ کر آگ لگانے والا شخص، آگ لگانے والا بم یا آلہ
antonyms: Noun, Adjective
examples: The rebels used incendiary bombs during the attack. His incendiary speech provoked violent reactions. The police arrested the incendiary responsible for the fire. The article had an incendiary tone.
sindhiMeaning: باهه لڳائڻ يا ڌماڪي لاءِ ٺهيل، جھڳڙو، ڪاوڙ يا تشدد پيدا ڪندڙ، جان بوجهه ڪري باهه لڳائيندڙ شخص، باهه لڳائيندڙ بم يا شيءِ
englishMeaning: Designed to cause fires or explosions. Tending to stir up conflict, anger, or violence. A person who starts fires deliberately. A bomb or device intended to ignite fires.

synonyms: Rebellious, Defiant, Insubordinate, Insurgent, Disobedient, Seditious
antonyms: Loyal, Obedient, Submissive, Compliant, Faithful, Disciplined
englishMeaning: Refusing to obey the orders of a person in authority, especially in the military. Showing rebellious feelings or behavior. Involved in or inclined toward mutiny. Openly disloyal or resistant.
sindhiMeaning: اختيار وارن جي حڪم کي مڃڻ کان انڪار ڪندڙ  خاص ڪري فوج ۾، بغاوت جي رويي وارو، بغاوت ڏانهن مائل، کليل نافرمان
examples: The mutinous sailors took control of the ship. His mutinous behavior led to his dismissal. The soldiers grew mutinous after months without pay. She gave her boss a mutinous look.
urduMeaning: اختیار والوں کے حکم کی خلاف ورزی کرنے والا  خاص طور پر فوج میں، بغاوت پر آمادہ رویہ رکھنے والا، بغاوت میں شامل یا مائل، کھلا نافرمان

englishMeaning: Willing to comply with orders, rules, or requests. Showing respect and submission to authority. Following instructions without resistance. Dutiful and well-behaved.
sindhiMeaning: حڪمن، قاعدن يا درخواستن تي عمل ڪندڙ، اختيار جو احترام ۽ فرمانبرداري ڏيکاريندڙ، بغير مخالفت جي هدايتن تي عمل ڪندڙ، فرض شناس ۽ سٺي رويي وارو
examples: He was an obedient student who followed every rule. Her dog is well trained and obedient. Obedient children make parenting easier. The soldiers remained obedient to their commander.
antonyms: Disobedient, Rebellious, Defiant, Unruly, Insubordinate, Mutinous
urduMeaning: احکامات، قواعد یا درخواستوں پر عمل کرنے والا، اختیار کا احترام اور تابعداری کرنے والا، بغیر مزاحمت کے ہدایات پر عمل کرنے والا، فرض شناس اور خوش اخلاق
synonyms: Compliant, Submissive, Dutiful, Respectful, Loyal, Well-behaved, Docile

examples: Her parents were very supportive of her career. He wore a supportive brace for his knee. Friends should always be supportive of one another. The manager was supportive during the difficult project.
englishMeaning: Providing encouragement, help, or emotional assistance. Willing to give aid or approval in difficult times. Serving to hold or strengthen something. Showing kindness and understanding to others.
synonyms: Encouraging, Helpful, Caring, Reassuring, Understanding, Nurturing, Sustaining
sindhiMeaning: حوصلا افزائي، مدد يا جذباتي سهارو ڏيندڙ، ڏکئي وقت ۾ مدد يا رضامندي ڏيندڙ، ڪنهن شيءِ کي سهارو ڏيندڙ يا مضبوط ڪندڙ، ٻين لاءِ مهرباني ۽ سمجهه ڏيکاريندڙ
urduMeaning: حوصلہ افزائی، مدد یا جذباتی سہارا فراہم کرنے والا، مشکل وقت میں مدد کرنے کو تیار، کسی چیز کو سہارا یا تقویت دینے والا، دوسروں کے لیے مہربان اور ہمدرد
antonyms: Unsupportive, Discouraging, Hostile, Indifferent, Neglectful, Uncaring

englishMeaning: A hasty tidying of the house between the time you see a visitor and the time they knock on the door. To quickly clean or straighten up a place in a rush. A rushed and last-minute cleaning effort before guests arrive.
synonyms: Tidy-up, Cleanup, Sprucing, Straighten, Hurried cleaning
antonyms: Mess, Disorder, Clutter, Untidiness, Neglect
sindhiMeaning: مهمان جي اچڻ کان اڳ گهر کي تڪڙ ۾ صاف ڪرڻ، تڪڙ ۾ گهر يا ڪمرو سنڀالڻ، مهمانن جي اچڻ کان اڳ آخري وقت ۾ صفائي ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: مہمان کے دروازے پر پہنچنے سے پہلے گھر کو جلدی جلدی صاف کرنا، جلدی میں کمرہ یا گھر سمیٹنا، مہمانوں کی آمد سے قبل آخری لمحے کی صفائی
examples: She did a quick scurryfunge before her mother-in-law arrived. We had to scurryfunge the living room when guests came unexpectedly. A good scurryfunge can hide a lot of mess in minutes. He is an expert at the last-minute scurryfunge.

synonyms: Another matter, Separate issue, Different story, Unrelated topic, Whole new ballgame
antonyms: Same thing, Similar matter, Identical situation, Same story
urduMeaning: بالکل مختلف بات یا معاملہ، جو زیر بحث موضوع سے متعلق نہ ہو، ایسا مسئلہ جو الگ طریقے سے حل کرنا پڑے، ایک بالکل جداگانہ معاملہ
examples: Managing a small shop is one thing, but running a company is a different kettle of fish. Playing football is fun, but coaching is a different kettle of fish. Writing a poem is easy for her, but writing a novel is a different kettle of fish. I can cook simple meals, but baking cakes is a different kettle of fish.
sindhiMeaning: بلڪل ٻي ڳالهه يا صورتحال، جيڪا موضوع سان لاڳاپيل نه هجي، اهڙو مسئلو جيڪو مختلف انداز سان حل ٿئي، هڪ الڳ ۽ مختلف معاملو
englishMeaning: A completely different matter or situation from the one being discussed. Something that is not related to or comparable with what has just been mentioned. An entirely separate issue that must be handled differently.

synonyms: Squirm, Wriggle, Twitch, Fiddle, Wiggle, Shuffle, Stir, Jiggle, Fuss
englishMeaning: To make small, quick movements with your hands, feet, or body, especially because you are nervous, bored, or restless. To move restlessly or uneasily. To play or fiddle with something absentmindedly. A person who fidgets. A small movement caused by restlessness or nervousness.
antonyms: Relax, Rest, Settle, Calm, Compose, Still, Steady
examples: The child began to fidget during the long lecture. She fidgeted nervously with her pen while waiting for the results. Please stop fidgeting and sit still. He is such a fidget that he can never stay in one place.
sindhiMeaning: بيچينيءَ ۾ ٿوري ٿوري  چرپر ڪرڻ، هٿن يا پيرن سان بيچين انداز ۾ چرڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ سان بي ڌياني ۾ کيڏڻ، بيچينيءَ سبب مسلسل چرپر ڪندڙ ماڻهو، بي آراميءَ ۽ ناچاڪيءَ جي حالت
urduMeaning: بے چینی سے چھوٹی چھوٹی حرکتیں کرنا، ہاتھ پاؤں کو بار بار ہلانا، کسی چیز سے بلا وجہ کھیلنا، بے قراری میں ادھر ادھر ہونا، مسلسل حرکت کرنے والا شخص
جسم کو بل دینا یا مروڑنا، بے چینی یا شرمندگی سے حرکت کرنا، ذہنی الجھن محسوس کرنا، کیڑے کی طرح بل کھانا، پیچ و تاب کھانے کی حرکت
antonyms: Relax, Rest, Settle, Stay still, Compose
synonyms: Wriggle, Writhe, Twist, Fidget, Wiggle, Flinch, Shift
sindhiMeaning: جسم کي مروڙڻ يا وٽ کائڻ، بيچينيءَ يا شرمندگيءَ سبب چرپر ڪرڻ، ذهني بي آرامي محسوس ڪرڻ، ڪينئون وانگر وٽ کائڻ، مروڙ واري چرپر
englishMeaning: To twist and turn the body with small quick movements, especially due to nervousness, discomfort, or embarrassment. To feel or show mental discomfort or awkwardness. To wriggle like a worm. A wriggling movement.
examples: The child squirmed in his seat during the boring lesson. She squirmed with embarrassment when her secret was revealed. The worm squirmed on the wet ground. He tried to squirm out of answering the difficult question.
She twisted the wire around the pole. He twisted his ankle while playing football. The reporter twisted his words to create a scandal. The story had an unexpected twist at the end.
urduMeaning: کسی چیز کو موڑنا یا بل دینا، دو یا زیادہ چیزوں کو آپس میں لپیٹنا، الفاظ یا حقائق کا مطلب بدل دینا، بل یا موڑ، کہانی یا صورتحال میں غیر متوقع تبدیلی
englishMeaning: To bend, turn, or rotate something into a different shape or direction. To wind two or more things together. To distort the meaning of words or facts. An act of twisting or a twisted shape. An unexpected change or development in a story or situation.
antonyms: Straighten, Untwist, Unwind, Align, Level
synonyms: Turn, Bend, Coil, Wind, Curl, Distort, Warp, Rotate, Spin
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ کي وٽ ڏيڻ يا مروڙڻ، ٻن يا وڌيڪ شين کي پاڻ ۾ وٽڻ، ڳالهه جو مطلب مروڙي بيان ڪرڻ، وٽ يا مروڙ، ڪهاڻيءَ يا حالت ۾ اوچتو تبديلي
بيچينيءَ سان، بغير آرام جي، بي صبريءَ ۽ اضطراب سان، ذهني سڪون کان سواءِ، مسلسل چرپر ڪندي
englishMeaning: In a manner showing an inability to remain still or calm. With anxiety, impatience, or unease. In a way that lacks rest or peace of mind. Constantly moving or acting without settling.
examples: He paced restlessly around the room waiting for the news. She slept restlessly throughout the stormy night. The children waited restlessly for the show to begin. He shifted restlessly in his chair during the meeting.
antonyms: Calmly, Peacefully, Restfully, Quietly, Serenely
urduMeaning: بے چینی سے، بغیر آرام کے، بے صبری اور اضطراب کے ساتھ، ذہنی سکون کے بغیر، مسلسل حرکت کرتے ہوئے
synonyms: Uneasily, Anxiously, Impatiently, Nervously, Fitfully

sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کي ڏنڊي يا چهبڪ سان سخت مارڻ، راند يا مقابلي ۾ بري طرح شڪست ڏيڻ، هٿ پير زور سان هلائڻ، ڪنهن مسئلي تي تفصيل سان بحث ڪري نتيجي تي پهچڻ، سخت مار يا ڦٿڪڻ جي حالت
examples: The farmer thrashed the wheat to separate the grain. Our team thrashed the opponents by a huge margin. The fish thrashed about in the net. The committee thrashed out the details of the new policy.
antonyms: Praise, Reward, Lose, Surrender, Rest, Still
urduMeaning: کسی کو ڈنڈے یا کوڑے سے شدید پیٹنا، کھیل یا مقابلے میں بری طرح شکست دینا، ہاتھ پاؤں کو زور سے مارنا یا چلانا، کسی مسئلے پر تفصیل سے بحث کر کے حل نکالنا، شدید مار یا تڑپنے کی حالت
englishMeaning: To beat someone or something violently, especially with a stick or whip. To defeat someone thoroughly in a game or contest. To move wildly or violently, especially arms and legs. To discuss a problem in detail until a solution is reached. A violent movement or beating.
synonyms: Beat, Whip, Flog, Batter, Pound, Defeat, Trounce, Flail, Wriggle

antonyms: Optionally, Voluntarily, Willingly, By choice
synonyms: Necessarily, Unavoidably, Inevitably, Compulsorily, Willy-nilly
sindhiMeaning: لازمي طور، مجبوريءَ سبب، ضرورت جي تحت، حالتن جي زور تي، ناگزير طور
urduMeaning: لازمی طور پر، مجبوراً، حالات کے دباؤ کی وجہ سے، ضرورتاً، ناگزیر طور پر
examples: The road was blocked, so he perforce had to take another route. She perforce accepted the decision of the committee. Being the only doctor available, he perforce attended to every patient. The heavy rain perforce delayed our journey.
englishMeaning: By necessity or force of circumstances. Unavoidably or inevitably. Because circumstances make it so. As a matter of compulsion rather than choice.

sindhiMeaning: ڪو، آيا، ڇا، ٻن ڳالهين مان ڪهڙي، شڪ يا چونڊ ظاهر ڪرڻ لاءِ استعمال ٿيندڙ لفظ
synonyms: If, In case, Either
urduMeaning: آیا، کیا، خواہ، دو باتوں میں سے کوئی ایک، شک یا انتخاب ظاہر کرنے کے لیے استعمال ہونے والا لفظ
antonyms: Certainly, Definitely, Surely
englishMeaning: Used to introduce alternatives or express a doubt or choice between possibilities. Expressing an inquiry or investigation into two alternatives. Used before or between choices. Regardless of which of two possibilities.
examples: I don't know whether he will come or not. She asked whether the shop was open. Whether you agree or not, the decision stands. He couldn't decide whether to stay or leave.

synonyms: Later, Subsequently, After, Thereafter, Then
antonyms: Before, Previously, Earlier, Beforehand
sindhiMeaning: پوءِ، بعد ۾، ان کان پوءِ، بعد ۾ ٿيندڙ وقت ۾، ڪنهن واقعي کان پوءِ
examples: We had dinner and went for a walk afterward. She apologized to him afterward. He felt very tired afterward. They discussed the matter and left afterward.
urduMeaning: بعد میں، اس کے بعد، پھر، بعد ازاں، کسی واقعے کے بعد
englishMeaning: At a later or subsequent time. After the event or time mentioned. Later on. Following something that has happened.

sindhiMeaning: لڳاتار، بنا وقفي جي، مسلسل، بغير ركاوٽ جي، هڪ ئي رفتار سان
examples: It has been raining continuously for three days. The machine works continuously without stopping. He talked continuously for two hours. She has been studying continuously since morning.
englishMeaning: Without interruption or pause. In an unbroken or uninterrupted manner. Steadily and constantly over a period of time. Without stopping or breaking.
urduMeaning: لگاتار، بلا تعطل، مسلسل، بغیر رکے، ایک ہی رفتار سے
antonyms: Intermittently, Occasionally, Sporadically, Rarely
synonyms: Constantly, Nonstop, Endlessly, Perpetually, Unceasingly, Steadily

englishMeaning: Care taken to avoid danger or mistakes. A warning against possible danger or trouble. Prudence in handling risky matters. To warn someone against something. A formal warning given by authority.
examples: You should exercise caution while driving in the fog. The doctor cautioned him against smoking. A word of caution before you sign the contract. The police officer gave him a caution for speeding.
sindhiMeaning: احتياط، خبرداري، خطري کان بچڻ لاءِ ڌيان، ڪنهن کي خبردار ڪرڻ، سرڪاري چتاءُ
antonyms: Recklessness, Carelessness, Rashness, Negligence, Boldness
synonyms: Care, Warning, Wariness, Prudence, Vigilance, Alertness, Heed
urduMeaning: احتیاط، ہوشیاری، خطرے سے بچنے کی کوشش، کسی کو خبردار کرنا، سرکاری تنبیہ

sindhiMeaning: احتياط سان، خبردار ٿي، ڌيان سان، هوشياريءَ سان، پرهيز ڪندي
examples: He walked cautiously across the icy road. She cautiously opened the old wooden door. The soldier moved cautiously through the forest. He cautiously answered the tricky question.
urduMeaning: احتیاط سے، ہوشیاری سے، خبرداری کے ساتھ، سوچ سمجھ کر، دھیان سے
synonyms: Carefully, Warily, Prudently, Vigilantly, Attentively
antonyms: Recklessly, Carelessly, Rashly, Hastily
englishMeaning: In a careful, watchful, and attentive manner. With care and attention to avoid danger or mistakes. Prudently. In a way that shows caution.

sindhiMeaning: بيوقوفيءَ جون ڳالهيون، بيهودو ۽ بي معنيٰ گفتگو، اجايون ڳالهيون، بيوقوفيءَ سان ڳالهائڻ
examples: Stop that twaddle and get back to work. The article was full of political twaddle. He twaddled on for hours about nothing important. I have no time to listen to such twaddle.
antonyms: Sense, Wisdom, Reason, Truth, Fact
synonyms: Nonsense, Rubbish, Drivel, Balderdash, Gibberish, Baloney
englishMeaning: Silly or trivial talk or writing. Nonsense or foolish speech. Meaningless chatter. To talk in a foolish or empty manner.
urduMeaning: فضول باتیں، بےہودہ اور بےمعنی گفتگو، بکواس، احمقانہ باتیں کرنا
بےہودہ باتیں، بےمعنی گفتگو، احمقانہ کلام، فضول اور کھوکھلی باتیں
examples: His speech was pure balderdash from start to finish. Don't believe that balderdash he told you. The old man dismissed the theory as balderdash. She was tired of listening to his balderdash.
englishMeaning: Senseless, meaningless talk or writing. Nonsense. Foolish or absurd statements. Empty or worthless words.
sindhiMeaning: بيهوده ڳالهيون، بي معنيٰ گفتگو، بيوقوفيءَ ڀريون ڳالهيون، اجايون ڪوريون ڳالهيون
synonyms: Nonsense, Rubbish, Twaddle, Drivel, Baloney, Gibberish
antonyms: Sense, Truth, Wisdom, Reality, Fact

examples: The novel was complete drivel and I couldn't finish it. Stop drivelling and speak sensibly. The baby drivelled all over his bib. I refuse to listen to such drivel anymore.
sindhiMeaning: بيوقوفيءَ جون ڳالهيون، اجايون ڳالهيون، وات مان ڳاڙهاٽيءَ يا لعاب جو وهڻ، بي معنيٰ گفتگو ڪرڻ
synonyms: Nonsense, Rubbish, Twaddle, Balderdash, Slobber, Dribble
englishMeaning: Silly or meaningless talk or writing. Saliva running from the mouth. To let saliva flow from the mouth. To talk foolishly or childishly.
antonyms: Sense, Wisdom, Reason, Truth
urduMeaning: بیوقوفانہ باتیں، فضول گفتگو، منہ سے رال ٹپکنا، بےمعنی باتیں کرنا

synonyms: Nonsense, Rubbish, Twaddle, Balderdash, Hogwash
englishMeaning: Foolish or deceptive talk. Nonsense. Something considered untrue or exaggerated. A type of sausage (also 'bologna').
antonyms: Truth, Fact, Reality, Sense
examples: That story about winning the lottery is a load of baloney. Don't feed me that baloney; tell me the truth. His excuses were pure baloney. She made a sandwich with baloney and cheese.
sindhiMeaning: بيوقوفيءَ جون ڳالهيون، ڪوڙيون ۽ مبالغه آميز ڳالهيون، اجايون ڳالهيون، هڪ قسم جو سوسيج
urduMeaning: بےہودہ باتیں، جھوٹی اور مبالغہ آمیز باتیں، بکواس، ایک قسم کا ساسیج

sindhiMeaning: ڪچرو، بيڪار شيون، بيوقوفيءَ ڀريون ڳالهيون، ڪنهن شيءِ کي بي قدرو سمجهڻ يا سختيءَ سان تنقيد ڪرڻ، خراب معيار جي شيءِ
urduMeaning: کچرا، فضلہ، بےمعنی باتیں، ناقص یا بےکار چیز، کسی کو سخت تنقید کا نشانہ بنانا
synonyms: Garbage, Trash, Waste, Nonsense, Refuse, Litter, Junk
antonyms: Sense, Truth, Treasure, Valuables, Wisdom
examples: Please throw the rubbish in the bin. Don't talk such rubbish in front of the guests. The film was absolute rubbish. Critics rubbished the government's new plan.
englishMeaning: Waste material or garbage. Worthless or foolish talk, ideas, or writing. Something of very poor quality. To criticize severely or dismiss as worthless.

urduMeaning: الفاظ سے بھرا ہوا، طویل گفتگو کرنے والا، ضرورت سے زیادہ الفاظ استعمال کرنے والا، دراز نفس، لمبی چوڑی تحریر
sindhiMeaning: لفظن سان ڀريل، ڊگهيون ڳالهيون ڪندڙ، گهڻڳالهائو، ضرورت کان وڌيڪ لفظ استعمال ڪندڙ، ڊگهي ۽ اجائي تحرير
examples: His essays are often too wordy and hard to follow. She gave a wordy explanation instead of a simple answer. The report is wordy but lacks substance. Editors dislike wordy writing.
synonyms: Verbose, Long-winded, Prolix, Rambling, Talkative, Diffuse
antonyms: Concise, Brief, Terse, Succinct, Pithy
englishMeaning: Using or containing too many words. Verbose. Expressed in more words than necessary. Long-winded in speech or writing.

urduMeaning: باتونی، بہت زیادہ باتیں کرنے والا، فضول باتیں کرنے والا، بلاوجہ بولنے والا
englishMeaning: Talkative in a chatty way, especially about unimportant matters. Fond of talking a lot. Excessively communicative.
examples: My gabby neighbor kept me on the phone for an hour. He becomes gabby after a cup of tea. She is friendly but a bit gabby at parties. The gabby tour guide entertained everyone with stories.
sindhiMeaning: گهڻ ڳالهائو، بلا ضرورت ڳالهائيندڙ، چٽ چٽ ڪندڙ، اجايون ڳالهيون ڪندڙ
antonyms: Quiet, Silent, Reserved, Taciturn, Reticent
synonyms: Talkative, Chatty, Loquacious, Garrulous, Verbose

englishMeaning: Willing, ready, or able to talk or share information. Relating to communication. Open and expressive in conveying thoughts or feelings.
synonyms: Talkative, Expressive, Open, Forthcoming, Articulate, Sociable
urduMeaning: بات چیت کرنے والا، معلومات کا تبادلہ کرنے والا، اپنے خیالات کا اظہار کرنے والا، ملنسار، رابطہ رکھنے والا
antonyms: Reserved, Silent, Uncommunicative, Withdrawn, Secretive
examples: She is friendly and very communicative with her students. He was not communicative about his personal life. Good teachers need to be communicative. Modern technology has made us more communicative.
sindhiMeaning: ڳالهه ٻولهه ڪندڙ، معلومات ورهائيندڙ، کليل انداز ۾ ڳالهائيندڙ، رابطي وارو، پنهنجا خيال چٽيءَ ريت پيش ڪندڙ

antonyms: Listener, Silent person, Introvert
synonyms: Chatterer, Babbler, Chatterbox, Gossip, Blabbermouth
englishMeaning: A person who talks a lot in a foolish or childish way. Someone who chatters about unimportant things. A talkative child.
sindhiMeaning: بيوقوفيءَ سان گهڻو ڳالهائيندڙ، ٻاراڻي انداز ۾ چٽ چٽ ڪندڙ، اجايون ڳالهيون ڪندڙ ماڻهو
urduMeaning: بےمقصد باتیں کرنے والا، بچگانہ انداز میں بولنے والا، فضول باتیں کرنے والا شخص
examples: The prattler kept everyone amused at the dinner table. Don't be such a prattler; listen for a change. The little prattler asked a hundred questions. He is a harmless prattler who means no offense.

urduMeaning: منظور کرنا، عطا کرنا، درخواست قبول کرنا، کسی بات کو تسلیم کرنا، ادارے یا حکومت کی طرف سے دی گئی رقم، قانونی طور پر منتقل کرنا
examples: The government granted him a scholarship for higher studies. She was granted permission to leave early. I grant that you have a valid point. The university offers research grants to students.
sindhiMeaning: منظور ڪرڻ، عطا ڪرڻ، ڪنهن جي درخواست تسليم ڪرڻ، ڪا ڳالهه صحيح مڃڻ، ادارو يا حڪومت پاران خاص مقصد لاءِ ڏنل رقم، قانوني طور منتقل ڪرڻ
synonyms: Award, Give, Bestow, Allow, Permit, Concede, Admit, Confer
antonyms: Deny, Refuse, Reject, Withhold, Disallow
englishMeaning: To agree to give or allow something requested. To admit or accept that something is true. A sum of money given by an organization or government for a specific purpose. To transfer legally.

synonyms: Pass, Surpass, Outstrip, Outdo, Exceed, Overhaul, Catch up
urduMeaning: آگے نکل جانا، کسی کو پکڑ کر پیچھے چھوڑ دینا، تعداد یا اہمیت میں بڑھ جانا، اچانک کسی کیفیت کا آ جانا، پیچھے چھوڑ دینا
sindhiMeaning: اڳي وڃڻ، ڪنهن کي پڪڙي پار ڪرڻ، تعداد يا اهميت ۾ اڳتي نڪري وڃڻ، اوچتو ڪنهن حالت جو گهيرو ٿيڻ، ڪنهن کان وڌي وڃڻ
antonyms: Follow, Trail, Lag, Fall behind
englishMeaning: To catch up with and pass someone or something moving in the same direction. To become greater in number or importance than something else. To come upon suddenly, as an event or emotion. To surpass or exceed.
examples: The red car overtook us on the highway. India has overtaken many countries in software exports. He was overtaken by grief after the news. Online sales have overtaken traditional retail.
She always tries to outdo her classmates in exams. The chef outdid himself with tonight's dinner. He worked hard to outdo his previous record. They tried to outdo each other in generosity.
urduMeaning: کسی سے بہتر کام کر دکھانا، مات دینا، کارکردگی میں پیچھے چھوڑ دینا، بازی لے جانا
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کان بهتر ڪم ڪري ڏيکارڻ، ڪنهن کي پوئتي ڇڏي اڳتي وڃڻ، ڪارڪردگيءَ ۾ ٻين کان اڳرو ٿيڻ
synonyms: Surpass, Exceed, Outshine, Overtake, Beat, Outstrip
englishMeaning: To do better than someone or something. To surpass in performance or achievement. To exceed in action or effort.
antonyms: Fail, Lag, Fall short, Underperform

synonyms: Surpass, Exceed, Outrun, Overtake, Outdo, Outpace
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کان اڳيان نڪري وڃڻ، ڊوڙ ۾ پوئتي ڇڏڻ، مقدار يا معيار ۾ ٻين کان وڌيڪ ٿيڻ، اڳرائي ماڻڻ
antonyms: Lag, Trail, Fall behind, Follow
urduMeaning: کسی سے آگے نکل جانا، دوڑ میں پیچھے چھوڑ دینا، مقدار یا معیار میں بڑھ جانا، سبقت لے جانا
examples: Demand has outstripped supply in the housing market. She outstripped her rivals in the final lap. His achievements outstripped everyone's expectations. Modern technology has outstripped old methods.
englishMeaning: To go faster than or beyond someone or something. To exceed or surpass in performance, quantity, or degree. To leave behind in a race or competition.

synonyms: Exceed, Transgress, Violate, Infringe, Overreach
antonyms: Respect, Observe, Comply, Obey, Follow
sindhiMeaning: حد کان ٻاهر وڃڻ، اختيار کان وڌيڪ ڪم ڪرڻ، مقرر ٿيل حدون ٽوڙڻ، قاعدن جي خلاف ورزي ڪرڻ
englishMeaning: To go beyond an accepted limit or boundary. To exceed proper behavior, authority, or rules. To transgress.
urduMeaning: حد سے تجاوز کرنا، اختیار سے بڑھ کر کام کرنا، مقررہ حدود پار کرنا، قواعد کی خلاف ورزی کرنا
examples: He overstepped his authority by firing the employee. Don't overstep the boundaries of politeness. The officer was punished for overstepping the rules. She felt he had overstepped by asking personal questions.

synonyms: Misconduct, Offense, Crime, Sin, Malpractice, Transgression, Misdeed
antonyms: Righteousness, Honesty, Virtue, Innocence, Goodness
examples: The company was cleared of any wrongdoing after the inquiry. He denied all charges of wrongdoing. Any wrongdoing will be strictly punished. The investigation revealed serious wrongdoing.
englishMeaning: Illegal or dishonest behavior. An act that is morally wrong or against the law. Misconduct or bad actions. Any act that violates ethical or legal standards.
urduMeaning: غلط کام، غیر قانونی یا بد دیانتی پر مبنی عمل، اخلاقی یا قانونی اصولوں کی خلاف ورزی، بد کرداری
sindhiMeaning: غلط ڪم، غير قانوني يا بي ايماني وارو ڪم، اخلاقي يا قانوني اصولن جي خلاف عمل، بدڪاري

antonyms: End with, Conclude with, Finish with
urduMeaning: کسی چیز سے شروعات کرنا، پہلے جزو کے طور پر استعمال کرنا، ابتدا کسی خاص نقطے سے کرنا
synonyms: Start with, Commence with, Open with, Initiate with
englishMeaning: To start something with a particular element or point. To have as the first part or step. To use as an initial item.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ڳالهه سان شروعات ڪرڻ، پهرين شيءِ طور استعمال ڪرڻ، ابتدا ڪنهن خاص نقطي کان ڪرڻ
examples: Let's begin with a short prayer. The book begins with an interesting quotation. We shall begin with chapter one. Every good speech begins with a strong opening line.

urduMeaning: کسی خاص عمل سے آغاز کرنا، پہلا قدم کے طور پر کوئی کام کرنا
examples: Let us begin by introducing ourselves. He began by thanking the audience. She began by explaining the rules. I will begin by summarizing the main points.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن خاص عمل سان شروعات ڪرڻ، پهرين قدم طور ڪو ڪم ڪرڻ
antonyms: Finish by, End by, Conclude by
synonyms: Start by, Commence by, Initiate by
englishMeaning: To start by doing a particular action. To take a specific action as the first step.
To start work on a particular task or project. To commence something on a specific day or subject.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ڪم يا منصوبي تي ڪم شروع ڪرڻ، ڪنهن خاص ڏينهن يا موضوع تي ابتدا ڪرڻ
examples: He began on his new novel last month. The workers began on the new road today. She began on her homework immediately. They begin on the project next week.
urduMeaning: کسی کام یا منصوبے پر کام شروع کرنا، کسی خاص دن یا موضوع پر آغاز کرنا
antonyms: Finish, Stop, Abandon
synonyms: Start on, Commence on, Embark on

antonyms: End as, Retire as
synonyms: Start as, Commence as, Originate as
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن حيثيت يا ڪردار سان شروعات ڪرڻ، ابتدا ۾ ڪنهن خاص روپ ۾ هجڻ
urduMeaning: کسی خاص کردار یا حیثیت سے شروعات کرنا، ابتدا میں کسی خاص شکل میں ہونا
englishMeaning: To start in a particular role, form, or capacity. To have a specified beginning or origin.
examples: He began as a clerk and rose to become a manager. She began as a volunteer at the hospital. The company began as a small family business. He began as a poet before writing novels.
The lecture will begin at nine o'clock. Charity begins at home. The race begins at the school gate. Our tour begins at the museum entrance.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن خاص جاءِ يا وقت کان شروع ٿيڻ، ابتدائي نقطي کان شروعات ڪرڻ
antonyms: End at, Finish at, Stop at
englishMeaning: To start at a specific place, time, or point. To have a starting location or moment.
synonyms: Start at, Commence at, Open at
urduMeaning: کسی خاص جگہ یا وقت سے شروع ہونا، ابتدائی مقام سے آغاز کرنا

sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن خاص جاءِ يا وقت کان شروع ڪرڻ، ابتدائي نقطي کان ابتدا ڪرڻ
synonyms: Start from, Commence from, Originate from
urduMeaning: کسی خاص جگہ یا وقت سے آغاز کرنا، ابتدائی نقطے سے شروعات کرنا
antonyms: End at, Finish at
examples: The story begins from his childhood days. Let us begin from page ten. Their friendship began from college. Counting begins from one.
englishMeaning: To start from a particular point, place, or time. To have origin in a specified source.

antonyms: Stop, Finish, End, Quit
synonyms: Restart, Resume, Recommence, Renew
urduMeaning: دوبارہ شروع کرنا، پھر سے آغاز کرنا، نئے سرے سے شروع کرنا
sindhiMeaning: ٻيهر شروعات ڪرڻ، نئين سر ابتدا ڪرڻ، وري شروع ڪرڻ
englishMeaning: To start something once more after stopping. To restart or resume from the beginning.
examples: After the interruption, the speaker had to begin again. Let's begin again from where we left off. She erased the drawing and began again. The teacher asked us to begin again from the top.
The mistake was too big; he had to begin over. She decided to begin over with a fresh page. If it fails, we will begin over. He wanted to begin over and correct his errors.
antonyms: Continue, Finish, Complete
urduMeaning: بالکل شروع سے دوبارہ کرنا، نئے سرے سے شروع کرنا، غلطی کے بعد دوبارہ آغاز کرنا
sindhiMeaning: بلڪل شروع کان وري ڪرڻ، نئين سر شروع ڪرڻ، غلطي کان پوءِ ٻيهر ابتدا ڪرڻ
synonyms: Restart, Redo, Recommence, Start afresh
englishMeaning: To start something completely from the beginning again, especially after a mistake. To redo from scratch.

antonyms: Heal, Forgive, Forget, Move on, Let go
englishMeaning: To bring back painful memories or feelings from the past. To revive past hurts or conflicts. To cause someone to feel emotional pain again by discussing past events.
sindhiMeaning: پراڻن زخمن کي تازو ڪرڻ، گذريل درد يا تڪليف کي وري ياد ڏيارڻ، پراڻن جهيڙن يا رنجشن کي وري اڀارڻ
synonyms: Revive pain, Rekindle sorrow, Bring back memories, Stir up the past
examples: Talking about the accident might reopen old wounds. Please don't reopen old wounds by mentioning that argument. The film reopened old wounds for many war survivors. His questions reopened old wounds between the brothers.
urduMeaning: پرانے زخم ہرے کرنا، گزری ہوئی تکلیف یا رنجش کو دوبارہ یاد دلانا، پرانے جھگڑوں کو پھر سے چھیڑنا

englishMeaning: To deliberately cause problems, arguments, or unrest. To provoke conflict or difficulty among people.
sindhiMeaning: جهڳڙو پيدا ڪرڻ، فساد کي هوا ڏيڻ، ماڻهن ۾ جان بوجهه سان مسئلا پيدا ڪرڻ، بدامني پکيڙڻ
examples: He always tries to stir up trouble in the office. Don't stir up trouble by spreading rumors. Some politicians stir up trouble for personal gain. Her comments only stirred up trouble in the family.
urduMeaning: جھگڑا کھڑا کرنا، فساد بھڑکانا، جان بوجھ کر مسائل پیدا کرنا، بدامنی پھیلانا
antonyms: Calm, Pacify, Reconcile, Soothe, Settle
synonyms: Provoke, Incite, Instigate, Agitate, Cause conflict

examples: Why do you always dig up the past during arguments? Let bygones be bygones and stop digging up the past. Reporters love to dig up the past of celebrities. Digging up the past won't solve our current problems.
englishMeaning: To bring up old memories, events, or issues that were forgotten or buried. To revisit painful or unpleasant past matters.
urduMeaning: ماضی کو کھود کر باہر نکالنا، گزرے ہوئے واقعات کو پھر سے چھیڑنا، بھولے بسرے یا دفن مسائل کو تازہ کرنا
antonyms: Forget, Move on, Let go, Bury the past
synonyms: Revive memories, Reopen old wounds, Bring up old issues, Rehash
sindhiMeaning: پراڻي وقت جون ڳالهيون کوٽي ٻاهر ڪڍڻ، گذريل واقعن کي وري اٿارڻ، وسريل يا دفن ٿيل مسئلن کي وري تازو ڪرڻ

englishMeaning: To mention or discuss problems or matters from the past that were previously resolved or forgotten. To raise past disputes again.
examples: Please don't bring up old issues during the family dinner. Every argument turns bad when he brings up old issues. Bringing up old issues will not help us move forward. She promised not to bring up old issues again.
urduMeaning: پرانے مسائل کو دوبارہ اٹھانا، پہلے حل شدہ باتوں کو پھر سے چھیڑنا، گزرے تنازعات کا ذکر کرنا
sindhiMeaning: پراڻن مسئلن کي وري اٿارڻ، اڳ حل ٿيل ڳالهين کي ٻيهر ياد ڪرڻ، گذريل تڪرارن جو ذڪر ڪرڻ
antonyms: Forget, Let go, Move on, Forgive
synonyms: Revive disputes, Rehash, Dig up the past, Reopen old wounds

sindhiMeaning: باهه کي ڀڙڪائڻ، جهيڙي يا ڪاوڙ کي وڌائڻ، ڪنهن مسئلي کي وڌيڪ خراب ڪرڻ، جذبن کي وڌيڪ ڀڙڪائڻ
urduMeaning: آگ کو ہوا دینا، جھگڑے یا غصے کو بڑھانا، کسی مسئلے کو مزید خراب کرنا، جذبات کو بھڑکانا
antonyms: Calm, Pacify, Soothe, Cool down, Ease
synonyms: Incite, Provoke, Aggravate, Intensify, Inflame
examples: His speech only fanned the flames of protest. Don't fan the flames by taking sides in their quarrel. The media fanned the flames of controversy. Her sarcastic remarks fanned the flames of his anger.
englishMeaning: To make a difficult situation, argument, or emotion worse. To intensify anger, conflict, or excitement.

sindhiMeaning: خطرناڪ يا طاقتور ماڻهوءَ کي نه ڇيڙيو، اجائي جهيڙي کان پاسو ڪريو، ڪاوڙيل ماڻهوءَ کي وڌيڪ نه ڀڙڪايو
examples: He is in a bad mood today, so don't poke the bear. I warned him not to poke the bear by mentioning the topic. When the boss is angry, don't poke the bear. She learned the hard way not to poke the bear.
synonyms: Let sleeping dogs lie, Leave well enough alone, Avoid trouble
englishMeaning: A warning not to provoke or annoy someone who is dangerous, powerful, or easily angered. Advice to avoid stirring up trouble unnecessarily.
urduMeaning: خطرناک یا طاقتور شخص کو مت چھیڑو، غیر ضروری جھگڑے سے بچو، غصے والے شخص کو مزید مت اکساؤ
antonyms: Provoke, Instigate, Challenge, Confront

examples: The plan is working, so leave well enough alone. Don't reorganize the office; leave well enough alone. She should have left well enough alone instead of complaining. Sometimes the best action is to leave well enough alone.
sindhiMeaning: جيڪا حالت ٺيڪ آهي، ان کي نه ڇيڙيو، بلاوجه دخل نه ڏيو، صحيح ڪم کي وڌيڪ خراب نه ڪريو
synonyms: Let it be, Don't meddle, Don't poke the bear, Let sleeping dogs lie
englishMeaning: To not interfere with a situation that is already satisfactory. To avoid making changes that might cause problems.
antonyms: Interfere, Meddle, Disturb, Tamper
urduMeaning: جو حالت ٹھیک ہے اسے مت چھیڑو، بلاوجہ دخل مت دو، اچھی چیز کو خراب مت کرو

examples: Fenugreek is commonly used in Indian and Pakistani cuisine. My mother adds fenugreek seeds to lentil curry. Fenugreek is believed to have many health benefits. She grows fresh fenugreek leaves in her kitchen garden.
englishMeaning: An aromatic plant of the pea family, whose seeds and leaves are widely used as a spice and herbal medicine. A common ingredient in South Asian cooking, known as 'methi'.
sindhiMeaning: ميٺي، ميٿي جو ٻوٽو، هڪ خوشبودار ٻوٽو جنهن جا ٻج ۽ پن مصالحن ۽ دوا طور استعمال ٿيندا آهن
synonyms: Methi, Trigonella, Herb, Spice
antonyms: (No direct antonym)
urduMeaning: میتھی، ایک خوشبودار پودا جس کے بیج اور پتے مصالحہ اور دوا کے طور پر استعمال ہوتے ہیں، جنوبی ایشیائی کھانوں کا اہم جزو

synonyms: Cluster bean, Guar, Legume
englishMeaning: A genus of leguminous plants, best known for the species Cyamopsis tetragonoloba, also called cluster bean or 'guar'. Widely grown in South Asia for food and industrial gum.
examples: Cyamopsis tetragonoloba is commonly known as cluster bean. Farmers in Rajasthan grow Cyamopsis for its gum. Cyamopsis seeds are a valuable export commodity. Research on Cyamopsis has increased due to its industrial uses.
urduMeaning: گوار کا پودا، ایک قسم کا پھلی دار پودا جس سے گوار حاصل ہوتا ہے، جو خوراک اور صنعتی مقاصد کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے

urduMeaning: حکومت یا مشورے کے لیے منتخب یا نامزد افراد کا گروہ، مشاورت کے لیے جمع ہونے والی جماعت، مقامی حکومت کا ادارہ جو شہر یا قصبے کے امور دیکھتا ہے، مشورے یا بحث کے لیے رسمی اجلاس
antonyms: Individual, Dictator, Autocracy, Single ruler
sindhiMeaning: صلاح مشوري يا حڪومت هلائڻ لاءِ چونڊيل يا مقرر ٿيل ماڻهن جو گروهه، صلاح مشوري لاءِ گڏ ٿيل ماڻهن جي جماعت، مقامي حڪومت جو ادارو جيڪو شهر يا ڳوٺ جا ڪم سنڀاليندو آهي، رسمي گڏجاڻي جيڪا بحث يا صلاح لاءِ ٿئي
synonyms: Committee, Board, Assembly, Cabinet, Panel, Congress, Senate, Convention, Body
examples: The city council approved the new road project. She was elected to the student council last year. A council of ministers advises the president. The council meets every Monday to discuss local issues.
englishMeaning: A group of people elected or appointed to make decisions or give advice on matters of governance or administration. An assembly of persons called together for consultation, deliberation, or advice. A local governing body responsible for public services in a town or city. A formal meeting for discussion or consultation.

antonyms: Whole, Mass, Freedom, Openness, Exterior
urduMeaning: جاندار کا سب سے چھوٹا بنیادی حصہ، جیل کا چھوٹا کمرہ جہاں قیدی بند ہو یا راہب رہتا ہو، کسی بڑے ڈھانچے میں چھوٹا خانہ، بجلی پیدا کرنے والا کیمیائی آلہ، کسی بڑی سیاسی یا دہشت گرد تنظیم کا چھوٹا گروپ
examples: The human body is made up of trillions of cells. The prisoner was locked in a small cell. He replaced the battery cells in his flashlight. Police uncovered a secret cell operating in the city.
sindhiMeaning: جاندار جو سڀ کان ننڍڙو بنيادي حصو، جيل جو ننڍڙو ڪمرو جتي قيدي بند رهي ٿو يا راهب رهي ٿو، ڪنهن وڏي جوڙجڪ ۾ ننڍڙو خانو، بجلي پيدا ڪندڙ ڪيميائي آلو، ڪنهن وڏي سياسي يا ڏهشتگرد تنظيم جو ننڍڙو گروهه
englishMeaning: The smallest structural and functional unit of a living organism. A small room in which a prisoner is locked up or a monk lives. A small compartment or enclosed space in a larger structure. A device that produces electricity through chemical reactions. A small group of people forming part of a larger political or terrorist organization.
synonyms: Compartment, Chamber, Room, Unit, Cubicle, Enclosure, Group, Faction

urduMeaning: تقریباً، لگ بھگ، کم و بیش، اندازاً، بالکل نہیں لیکن قریب قریب، معقول حد تک، تقریباً یکساں
antonyms: Exactly, Precisely, Completely, Entirely, Absolutely
sindhiMeaning: لڳ ڀڳ، تقريباً، ٿورو گهڻو، اٽڪل، بلڪل نه پر اٽڪل، لڳ ڀڳ ساڳيو، مناسب حد تائين
examples: The work is more or less finished. They arrived more or less at the same time. His answer was more or less correct. The two products are more or less the same.
synonyms: Approximately, Roughly, Nearly, Almost, About, Practically, Virtually
englishMeaning: Approximately or about a certain amount. Almost completely or nearly so. To a moderate or reasonable extent. Roughly, without being exact. Practically the same as.

antonyms: Individual, One person, Order, Calm, Peace, Discipline
sindhiMeaning: وڏو بيقابو ميڙ ماڻهن جو، گوڙ ڪندڙ يا فسادي هجوم، هڪ جماعت جيڪا گڏجي غلط ڪم ڪري، منظم ڏوهارين جو گروهه، ڪنهن جي چوڌاري بيقابو انداز ۾ گڏ ٿيڻ
synonyms: Crowd, Horde, Throng, Rabble, Gang, Swarm, Multitude, Mass, Pack
urduMeaning: بڑا بے قابو ہجوم، شور مچانے والا یا فسادی گروہ، مل کر غلط کام کرنے والی جماعت، منظم مجرموں یا غنڈوں کا گروہ، کسی کے گرد بے ترتیب انداز میں جمع ہو جانا
englishMeaning: A large disorderly crowd of people, often noisy and out of control. A gathering of people intent on causing trouble or violence. A group of people acting together, usually in an aggressive or unlawful way. An organized group of criminals or gangsters. To crowd around someone in an unruly way.
examples: An angry mob gathered outside the courthouse. The mob attacked the police vehicles during the protest. Fans mobbed the famous actor at the airport. The mob was finally dispersed by the security forces.

urduMeaning: جو دکھائی نہ دے، پوشیدہ یا آنکھ سے اوجھل، غیر مرئی، جو نظر نہ آئے، آنکھوں سے چھپا ہوا، کسی طرح بھی دیکھا نہ جا سکنے والا
sindhiMeaning: جيڪو ڏسي نه سگهجي، لڪل يا اک کان اوجهل، غيرمرئي، جيڪو نظر نه اچي، ڏسڻ ۾ نه ايندڙ، ڪنهن به طرح نظر کان اوٽ
antonyms: Visible, Seen, Apparent, Noticeable, Obvious, Perceptible, Evident
synonyms: Unseen, Hidden, Concealed, Imperceptible, Undetectable, Obscured, Veiled
examples: The wind is invisible but powerful. She felt invisible in a room full of strangers. Germs are invisible to the naked eye. He wished he could become invisible for a day.
englishMeaning: Unable to be seen, either because it is hidden or because it does not physically exist. Not perceptible by the eye. Concealed from view or hidden from sight. Not noticeable or recognized by others. Impossible to detect visually.

examples: Her red dress made her conspicuous in the crowd. He was conspicuous by his absence at the meeting. The tall building is conspicuous from a distance. His bravery was conspicuous during the emergency.
synonyms: Noticeable, Prominent, Obvious, Striking, Visible, Evident, Remarkable, Outstanding
antonyms: Inconspicuous, Hidden, Concealed, Unnoticeable, Obscure, Invisible, Subtle
sindhiMeaning: چٽو نظر ايندڙ، نمايان، اکين ۾ چڀندڙ، اهڙو جيڪو آسانيءَ سان نظر اچي وڃي، غير معمولي هئڻ ڪري توجهه ڇڪائيندڙ، ظاهر ظهور
englishMeaning: Clearly visible and attracting attention. Standing out so as to be easily seen or noticed. Attracting notice or attention because of being unusual or remarkable. Obvious to the eye or mind.
urduMeaning: نمایاں، صاف نظر آنے والا، آنکھوں میں کھٹکنے والا، جو بآسانی نظر آ جائے، غیر معمولی ہونے کی وجہ سے توجہ کھینچنے والا، ظاہر و باہر

examples: I can't tell you the exact figure off-hand. His off-hand reply upset the customer. She spoke in an off-hand manner about the accident. He gave an off-hand answer without thinking.
englishMeaning: Done or said without previous thought or preparation. In a casual or careless manner. Without warmth, politeness, or interest. Immediately, without checking or consulting anything.
synonyms: Casual, Impromptu, Unprepared, Spontaneous, Curt, Careless, Brusque, Extempore
antonyms: Planned, Prepared, Deliberate, Careful, Considered, Polite, Formal
sindhiMeaning: بغير سوچ سمجھ جي، اڻ رٿيل، لاپرواهي سان، سرسري نموني ۾، بغير ادب يا دلچسپي جي، بلاتيار، بنا ڪنهن حوالي جي جواب ڏيڻ
urduMeaning: بغیر سوچے سمجھے، غیر رسمی، لاپرواہی سے، سرسری انداز میں، بغیر ادب یا دلچسپی کے، بلا تیاری، فوراً بغیر کسی حوالے کے
اپنے کام یا فرض کو پوری ایمانداری اور خوبی سے کرنے والا، ضمیر کا پابند، ذمہ دار، دیانتدار، محنتی اور اصولوں کا پابند، اخلاقی اصولوں کے مطابق چلنے والا
antonyms: Careless, Negligent, Irresponsible, Lazy, Unreliable, Reckless, Dishonest
synonyms: Diligent, Careful, Honest, Responsible, Meticulous, Scrupulous, Dutiful, Hardworking, Principled
englishMeaning: Wishing to do one's work or duty well and thoroughly. Guided by or in accordance with one's sense of right and wrong. Careful, honest, and hardworking. Governed by a strict sense of duty or moral principles.
examples: She is a conscientious worker who never misses a deadline. Conscientious students always complete their homework on time. He is very conscientious about his responsibilities. A conscientious teacher inspires her students to do their best.
sindhiMeaning: پنهنجي ڪم يا فرض کي پوري ايمانداري ۽ خوبيءَ سان ڪرڻ وارو، ضمير جو پابند، ذميوار، ديانتدار، محنتي ۽ اصولن جو پابند، اخلاقي اصولن مطابق هلندڙ

examples: He filed a lawsuit for defamation against the newspaper. Spreading false rumors is a form of defamation. The politician accused his rival of defamation. Defamation cases can lead to heavy fines in court.
urduMeaning: کسی کی عزت کو جھوٹے الزامات سے نقصان پہنچانا، جھوٹ بول یا لکھ کر کسی کی شہرت خراب کرنا، بدنامی، تہمت، کسی کے کردار پر غلط الزام لگانا
synonyms: Slander, Libel, Calumny, Character assassination, Vilification, Smear, Aspersion, Disparagement
antonyms: Praise, Compliment, Commendation, Approval, Honor, Respect, Vindication
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن جي عزت کي ڪوڙن الزامن سان نقصان پهچائڻ، ڪوڙ ڳالهائي يا لکي ڪنهن جي شهرت خراب ڪرڻ، بدنامي، تهمت، ڪنهن جي ڪردار تي غلط الزام
englishMeaning: The act of damaging the good reputation of someone through false statements. Communication of false information that harms another person's character. Slander or libel that lowers a person's standing in society. A false statement, spoken or written, that injures someone's reputation.

examples: Keep your phone at hand in case of emergency. The examination is at hand, so study seriously. Help was at hand when the accident occurred. All the tools you need are at hand.
englishMeaning: Close by, within easy reach. Available or ready for use when needed. About to happen very soon. Near in time or place.
synonyms: Nearby, Close, Available, Handy, Accessible, Imminent, Approaching, Ready
urduMeaning: قریب، ہاتھ میں، آسانی سے پہنچ میں، جلد ہونے والا، وقت یا جگہ کے لحاظ سے قریب، تیار اور موجود
sindhiMeaning: ويجهو، ھٿ وٽ، آسانيءَ سان پهچ ۾، جلد ٿيڻ وارو، وقت يا جاءِ جي لحاظ کان ويجهو، تيار ۽ موجود
antonyms: Far, Distant, Remote, Unavailable, Away, Absent

sindhiMeaning: پيشانيءَ جو صاف حصو جيڪو ابرو جي وچ ۾ ۽ نڪ جي مٿان هوندو آهي، دماغ جي هڏي جو اُهو حصو جيڪو ابرو جي وچ ۾ صاف هوندو آهي، طبي ۽ حياتياتي مطالعن ۾ استعمال ٿيندڙ اصطلاح
englishMeaning: The smooth area of the forehead located between the eyebrows and above the nose. The flat surface of bone between the brow ridges. An anatomical landmark used in medical and biological studies.
antonyms: (No direct antonym; anatomical term)
synonyms: Brow, Forehead area, Interbrow, Frontal bone
urduMeaning: پیشانی کا ہموار حصہ جو ابرو کے درمیان اور ناک کے اوپر ہوتا ہے، ابرو کے درمیان ہڈی کا چپٹا حصہ، طبی اور حیاتیاتی مطالعے میں استعمال ہونے والا اصطلاح
examples: The doctor examined the patient's glabella carefully. The glabella is often used as a reference point in facial measurements. Wrinkles between the eyebrows appear on the glabella. Anthropologists study the shape of the glabella to identify skulls.

synonyms: Practical, Realistic, Sensible, Humble, Modest, Grounded, Unpretentious, Genuine
examples: Despite his fame, he remains down to earth. She is a very down-to-earth person, always kind and humble. I like him because he is so down to earth. Down-to-earth people are usually good listeners.
sindhiMeaning: عملي، حقيقت پسند، سادو ۽ مصنوعيت کان پاڪ، مغرور يا وڏائي وارو نه، خلوص وارو ۽ حقيقت ۾ رهندڙ، انسانن سان سولائيءَ سان ملڻ وارو
antonyms: Arrogant, Proud, Pretentious, Unrealistic, Snobbish, Impractical, Haughty
urduMeaning: عملی، حقیقت پسند، سادہ اور بناوٹ سے پاک، مغرور یا متکبر نہیں، خلوص والا اور حقیقت میں رہنے والا، لوگوں سے آسانی سے ملنے والا
englishMeaning: Practical, sensible, and realistic in behavior. Not proud, arrogant, or pretentious. Simple, natural, and easy to talk to. Honest and grounded in real life.

examples: She is very considerate of her elderly parents. It was considerate of him to bring an extra umbrella. A considerate leader listens to everyone's opinion. Please be considerate of your neighbors and keep the noise down.
englishMeaning: Careful not to inconvenience or hurt others. Showing kind awareness of and regard for the feelings of others. Thoughtful and mindful in behavior. Sympathetic and caring toward others.
synonyms: Thoughtful, Kind, Caring, Sympathetic, Attentive, Mindful, Polite, Compassionate
urduMeaning: دوسروں کے جذبات کا خیال رکھنے والا، مہربان، سوچ سمجھ کر چلنے والا، ہمدرد، دوسروں کو تکلیف نہ دینے والا، خیال رکھنے والا اور شفیق
antonyms: Inconsiderate, Selfish, Thoughtless, Rude, Unkind, Careless, Uncaring
sindhiMeaning: ٻين جي جذبن جو خيال رکندڙ، مهربان، سوچ سمجھ سان هلندڙ، همدرد، ٻين کي تڪليف نه ڏيڻ وارو، خيال رکندڙ ۽ ھمدرد

urduMeaning: شرمیلا، جھجک والا، لوگوں کے سامنے شرمانے والا، اپنے بارے میں زیادہ سوچنے والا، سماجی مواقع پر جھینپنے والا، سنجیدہ اور خاموش
synonyms: Shy, Timid, Modest, Reserved, Coy, Diffident, Meek, Reticent
sindhiMeaning: شرميلو، جهجهڪ وارو، ماڻهن سامهون شرمائيندڙ، پنهنجي باري ۾ گهڻو سوچيندڙ، سماجي حالتن ۾ ڊڄندڙ، جهڪ ۽ ماٺو
englishMeaning: Shy and easily embarrassed in the company of others. Reluctant to speak or act because of self-consciousness. Timid and modest, especially in social situations. Lacking confidence in front of people.
examples: The bashful boy hid behind his mother. She gave a bashful smile when he complimented her. He is too bashful to speak in front of a crowd. Her bashful nature makes her seem quiet at first.
antonyms: Bold, Confident, Outgoing, Extroverted, Brazen, Assertive, Shameless
Refined flour, Maida, Fine flour
urduMeaning: سوجی، گندم سے بنایا گیا موٹا آٹا، پاستا، حلوہ اور میٹھے پکوان بنانے کے لیے استعمال ہونے والی، گندم کے دانوں سے تیار کردہ غذائی جزو
synonyms: Sooji, Rava, Wheat middlings, Farina, Durum flour
