examples: My grandmother makes delicious semolina pudding. Semolina is the main ingredient in traditional pasta. She prepared halwa using semolina and sugar. Semolina gives a slightly grainy texture to bread.

sindhiMeaning: منع ڪرڻ، روڪڻ، ڪنهن ڪم ڪرڻ کان جھلڻ، حڪم ڏيڻ ته نه ڪر، ڪنهن ڪم جي اجازت نه ڏيڻ، ممنوع قرار ڏيڻ
antonyms: Allow, Permit, Approve, Authorize, Consent, Sanction, Enable
examples: The teacher forbade the students from using mobile phones in class. Smoking is strictly forbidden in this area. My parents forbid me to stay out late. God forbid such a tragedy should happen again.
urduMeaning: منع کرنا، روکنا، کسی کام سے باز رکھنا، حکم دینا کہ نہ کرو، کسی کام کی اجازت نہ دینا، ممنوع قرار دینا
synonyms: Prohibit, Ban, Disallow, Prevent, Bar, Outlaw, Restrict, Veto
englishMeaning: To order someone not to do something. To officially refuse to allow. To make a rule against something. To prevent or hinder an action.

examples: Be careful not to squash the tomatoes in your bag. The government squashed the rebellion quickly. He drank a glass of lemon squash after the match. She loves cooking butter squash soup in winter. My brother plays squash every weekend.
englishMeaning: To crush or squeeze something so that it becomes flat or shapeless. To suppress or put an end to something forcefully. A soft drink made from fruit juice, sugar, and water. A type of vegetable belonging to the gourd family. A racket sport played by two players in an enclosed court.
synonyms: Crush, Flatten, Compress, Mash, Suppress, Quell, Pulp, Squeeze
urduMeaning: کچلنا، دبا کر بے شکل کرنا، کسی چیز کو زبردستی ختم کرنا، پھلوں سے بنایا گیا میٹھا مشروب، ایک قسم کی سبزی، بند کورٹ میں دو کھلاڑیوں کی کھیلی جانے والی ریکٹ گیم
antonyms: Expand, Stretch, Encourage, Release, Support, Inflate
sindhiMeaning: چيڀاٽڻ، دٻائي پٽيءَ ڪرڻ، ڪنهن ڪم کي زور سان ختم ڪرڻ، ميوي مان تيار ٿيل مٺو پيئڻ وارو مواد، هڪ قسم جي ڀاڄي، بند ڪورٽ ۾ ٻن رانديگرن جي کيڏي ويندڙ راند
جادو ٽوڻو، ڪارو علم، جادوگريءَ ذريعي شيطاني قوتون استعمال ڪرڻ، منتر ۽ ڦيڻن سان ماڻهن تي اثر ڪرڻ، ديويائي يا مافوق الفطرت قوتن جو استعمال
englishMeaning: The practice of magic, especially black magic, using supernatural powers. The use of spells and charms often associated with evil spirits. The art or exercise of magical powers by a witch. Supernatural or mystical influence attributed to sorcerers.
urduMeaning: جادو ٹونا، کالا علم، جادوگری کے ذریعے شیطانی قوتیں استعمال کرنا، منتر اور ٹوٹکوں سے لوگوں پر اثر ڈالنا، مافوق الفطرت یا ماورائی قوتوں کا استعمال
antonyms: Reality, Science, Reason, Logic, Fact
examples: In ancient times, many innocent women were accused of witchcraft. She was fascinated by stories about witchcraft. The novel explores the mysterious world of witchcraft. Some cultures still believe in the power of witchcraft.
synonyms: Sorcery, Magic, Wizardry, Enchantment, Occultism, Necromancy, Voodoo, Spellcraft

urduMeaning: یاد دلانا، جذبات یا احساسات کو بیدار کرنا، روحوں یا یادوں کو بلانا، ماضی کا خیال تازہ کرنا، کسی چیز کے ذریعے احساس پیدا کرنا
sindhiMeaning: ياد ڏيارڻ، جذبن يا احساسن کي بيدار ڪرڻ، روحن يا يادن کي سڏڻ، ماضيءَ جو خيال تازو ڪرڻ، ڪنهن شئي ذريعي احساس پيدا ڪرڻ
antonyms: Suppress, Silence, Ignore, Forget, Repress, Stifle
synonyms: Evoke, Summon, Recall, Awaken, Arouse, Bring forth, Elicit, Conjure
englishMeaning: To call forth or summon a spirit, memory, or feeling. To bring back to mind by association. To arouse or evoke a particular emotion or reaction. To recall something from the past.
examples: The old song evocated memories of her childhood. His words evocated deep emotions in the audience. The photograph evocated a sense of nostalgia. The perfume evocated her mother's presence.

sindhiMeaning: دل ۽ ذهن ۾ يادون يا احساس تازا ڪندڙ، اثرائتو، جذبات جاڳائيندڙ، ماضيءَ جا منظر ياد ڏياريندڙ، ذهن ۾ چٽي تصوير پيدا ڪندڙ
urduMeaning: دل و دماغ میں یادیں یا احساسات تازہ کرنے والا، اثر انگیز، جذبات کو بیدار کرنے والا، ماضی کے مناظر یاد دلانے والا، ذہن میں واضح تصویر پیدا کرنے والا
examples: The novel contains many evocative descriptions of village life. Her painting is deeply evocative and moving. The music was evocative of a peaceful summer evening. His speech was evocative and inspired the audience.
synonyms: Suggestive, Reminiscent, Expressive, Vivid, Moving, Poignant, Stirring, Emotive
antonyms: Unemotional, Dull, Cold, Bland, Uninspiring, Emotionless
englishMeaning: Bringing strong images, memories, or feelings to mind. Tending to arouse thoughts or emotions vividly. Powerful in producing a mental picture or recollection. Suggestive or reminiscent of something.

sindhiMeaning: جادوگرياڻي، ڏائڻ، اهڙي عورت جنهن وٽ ديوي يا شيطاني قوتون هجن، منتر پڙهي جادو ڪندڙ عورت، لوڪ ڪهاڻين جي جادوگرياڻي، ڪنهن بدذات عورت لاءِ لفظ
antonyms: Angel, Saint, Nun, Innocent
synonyms: Sorceress, Enchantress, Magician, Wizardess, Hag, Crone
urduMeaning: جادوگرنی، ڈائن، ایسی عورت جس کے پاس دیوی یا شیطانی قوتیں ہوں، منتر پڑھ کر جادو کرنے والی عورت، لوک کہانیوں کی جادوگرنی، کسی بری عورت کے لیے استعمال ہونے والا لفظ
englishMeaning: A woman thought to have magical powers, especially evil ones. A female sorcerer or practitioner of witchcraft. In folklore, a woman who uses spells and charms. A term sometimes used disapprovingly for an unpleasant woman.
examples: The story is about a witch who lives in the forest. She dressed up as a witch for Halloween. In old times, women accused of being witches were punished. The witch cast a spell on the prince.

sindhiMeaning: هڪ گرم ۽ مٽيءَ سان ڀريل اڀرندي هوا جيڪا اسپين جي بحيره روم واري ساحل تي لڳندي آهي خاص طور تي اونهاري ۾، خشڪ ۽ تڪليف ڏيندڙ هوا، مقامي اسپيني موسمي هوا جو نالو
antonyms: Cool breeze, Cold wind, Zephyr, Northerly wind
urduMeaning: ایک گرم اور گرد آلود مشرقی ہوا جو اسپین کے بحیرہ روم کے ساحل پر چلتی ہے خاص طور پر گرمیوں میں، خشک اور تکلیف دہ ہوا، مقامی اسپینی موسمی ہوا کا نام
examples: The solano made the afternoon unbearably hot. Farmers dread the solano during harvest time. Many people suffer headaches when the solano blows. The solano brought clouds of dust into the town.
englishMeaning: A hot, dust-laden easterly wind that blows on the Mediterranean coast of Spain, especially during summer. A dry, oppressive wind causing discomfort and health problems. A local Spanish term for a specific seasonal wind.
synonyms: Sirocco, Hot wind, Levanter, Easterly wind

englishMeaning: To press, fold, and stretch dough with the hands to make it smooth. To massage a part of the body firmly with the hands. To work a substance into a soft mass by pressing and squeezing. To manipulate or shape by squeezing.
antonyms: Loosen, Release, Leave, Stiffen, Harden
urduMeaning: آٹا گوندھنا، ہاتھوں سے دبا کر اور موڑ کر نرم کرنا، جسم کا مساج کرنا، کسی مواد کو دبا کر نرم بنانا، ہاتھوں سے دبا کر کسی چیز کو شکل دینا
sindhiMeaning: اٽو گنڍڻ، هٿن سان دٻائي ۽ ورائي نرم ڪرڻ، جسم جو مساج ڪرڻ، ڪنهن مواد کي دٻائي نرم بنائڻ، هٿن سان دٻائي ڪنهن شئي کي شڪل ڏيڻ
examples: She kneaded the dough for ten minutes before baking. The masseur kneaded the muscles of his back. Knead the clay until it becomes soft and pliable. Grandmother kneads flour every morning to make fresh bread.
synonyms: Massage, Press, Squeeze, Work, Manipulate, Mold, Pummel, Rub

englishMeaning: A close friend or companion. Someone with whom one spends a lot of friendly time. Bait consisting of chopped fish thrown into the water to attract fish. To be friendly or intimate with someone.
antonyms: Enemy, Foe, Stranger, Rival, Adversary
urduMeaning: قریبی دوست، ساتھی، ایسا شخص جس سے بہت گہری دوستی ہو، مچھلی کو پھنسانے کے لیے پانی میں ڈالا جانے والا چارہ، کسی سے دوستی کرنا یا میل جول رکھنا
examples: He has been my chum since childhood. She invited her old chums to the party. The fishermen used chum to attract sharks. They chummed together during their college days.
synonyms: Friend, Buddy, Pal, Companion, Comrade, Mate, Fellow
sindhiMeaning: ويجهو دوست، ساٿي، اهڙو ماڻهو جنهن سان تمام گهڻي دوستي هجي، مڇيءَ کي ڦاسائڻ لاءِ پاڻيءَ ۾ اڇلايل مڇيءَ جو مواد، ڪنهن سان دوستي رکڻ يا هلي ملي رهڻ

examples: God is often described as omniscient and all-powerful. The novel is written from an omniscient point of view. No human being can be truly omniscient. The omniscient narrator revealed the thoughts of every character.
synonyms: All-knowing, All-wise, Wise, Cognizant, Aware, Sagacious
englishMeaning: Having complete or unlimited knowledge, awareness, or understanding. Knowing everything, past, present, and future. All-knowing, especially used as an attribute of God. A narrator in literature who knows all characters' thoughts and actions.
sindhiMeaning: سڀ ڄاڻندڙ، هر شئي جو علم رکندڙ، خدا لاءِ استعمال ٿيندڙ صفت، ماضي  حال ۽ مستقبل جو علم رکندڙ، اهڙو راوي جيڪو سڀني ڪردارن جي سوچن کي ڄاڻندو هجي
antonyms: Ignorant, Unaware, Unknowing, Uninformed, Clueless
urduMeaning: سب کچھ جاننے والا، ہر چیز کا علم رکھنے والا، خدا کی صفت کے طور پر استعمال ہونے والا لفظ، ماضی  حال اور مستقبل کا علم رکھنے والا، ایسا راوی جو تمام کرداروں کے خیالات جانتا ہو

sindhiMeaning: خدا جي وجود تي ايمان رکندڙ شخص، هڪ ذاتي، خالق ۽ فعال خدا تي ايمان رکندڙ، خدا پرست، الحاد جي مخالف نظريو رکندڙ، مذهبي عقيدي جو ماننده
urduMeaning: خدا کے وجود پر یقین رکھنے والا شخص، ایک ذاتی، خالق اور فعال خدا کو ماننے والا، خدا پرست، الحاد کے مخالف نظریہ رکھنے والا، مذہبی عقیدے کا ماننے والا
englishMeaning: A person who believes in the existence of a god or gods. Someone who believes in a personal, active, and creator God. A believer in the divine as opposed to an atheist. An adherent of theism as a philosophical or religious belief.
antonyms: Atheist, Nonbeliever, Skeptic, Agnostic, Infidel
synonyms: Believer, Deist, Monotheist, Devotee, Faithful, Godly person
examples: A theist believes that God created the universe. Many philosophers are theists in their outlook. She was raised as a theist in a religious family. Theists and atheists often engage in deep debates.

englishMeaning: A person who can endure pain or hardship without showing feelings or complaining. Enduring difficulty calmly and patiently. A follower of the ancient Greek philosophy of Stoicism, teaching self-control and calmness. Unemotional and indifferent to pleasure or pain.
examples: He remained stoic even after losing everything. Her stoic attitude helped her survive the crisis. The soldier faced the pain with stoic silence. She listened to the bad news with a stoic expression.
synonyms: Patient, Calm, Composed, Impassive, Unemotional, Enduring, Resilient, Philosophical
antonyms: Emotional, Expressive, Sensitive, Restless, Excitable, Complaining, Weak
sindhiMeaning: صبر ڪندڙ، تڪليف ۾ به پرسڪون رهندڙ شخص، جيڪو درد يا مصيبت ۾ شڪايت نه ڪري، پراڻي يوناني فلسفي اسٽوئزم جو ماننده، جذبن کان بيپرواهه، برداشت وارو
urduMeaning: صبر کرنے والا، تکلیف میں بھی پرسکون رہنے والا، جو درد یا مصیبت میں شکایت نہ کرے، قدیم یونانی فلسفے اسٹوئزم کا ماننے والا، جذبات سے بے پروا، برداشت والا

examples: The library keeps a detailed catalogue of every book in its collection. She flipped through the clothing catalogue looking for a winter coat. Researchers must catalogue each specimen before storing it. The museum has begun to catalogue its ancient artifacts online.
synonyms: List, Register, Directory, Index, Inventory, Record, Roster, Schedule, Brochure, Compendium
urduMeaning: اشیاء کی مکمل فہرست جو ترتیب سے اور تفصیل کے ساتھ بنائی گئی ہو، کتابوں یا اشیاء کی فہرست جو لائبریری یا عجائب گھر میں رکھی جاتی ہے، فروخت کے لیے اشیاء کی کتابچہ یا فہرست، اشیاء کو ترتیب سے درج کرنا، رجسٹر میں اندراج کرنا
englishMeaning: A complete list of items, typically arranged systematically and often with descriptions. A publication or booklet containing details of goods, products, or services for sale. A list of books, works of art, or other items in a library, museum, or collection. To make a systematic list of items. To enter something in a register or record.
antonyms: Disorder, Disarrange, Jumble, Confusion, Miscellany, Chaos, Muddle
sindhiMeaning: شين جي مڪمل فهرست جيڪا ترتيبوار ۽ تفصيل سان ٺاهيل هجي، ڪتابن يا شين جي فهرست جيڪا لائبريري يا عجائب گهر ۾ رکيل هجي، وڪري لاءِ رکيل شين جو ڪتابچو يا فهرست، شين کي ترتيبوار درج ڪرڻ يا فهرست ٺاهڻ، رجسٽر ۾ داخل ڪرڻ

examples: The doctor's handwriting on the prescription was completely illegible. His signature was so illegible that the clerk asked him to sign again. The old manuscript had become illegible over the centuries. Please rewrite this note, as your writing is illegible.
sindhiMeaning: جيڪو پڙهي نه سگهجي، صاف نه هجڻ سبب پڙهڻ ۾ ڏکيو، خراب لکائي جي ڪري ناقابل فهم، مِٽيل يا ڦِڪو ٿيل لکت جيڪو سمجهي نه سگهجي
englishMeaning: Not clear enough to be read. Impossible or very difficult to decipher due to poor handwriting or damage. Unreadable because of faded, smudged, or unclear text. Writing that cannot be understood or made out.
synonyms: Unreadable, Indecipherable, Unintelligible, Unclear, Scrawled, Faint, Obscure, Muddled
antonyms: Legible, Readable, Clear, Distinct, Neat, Decipherable, Plain, Intelligible
urduMeaning: جو پڑھا نہ جا سکے، ناقابلِ فہم تحریر، خراب لکھائی کی وجہ سے سمجھ میں نہ آنے والا، مٹا ہوا یا دھندلا لکھا ہوا متن جو واضح نہ ہو

antonyms: Literate, Educated, Learned, Scholarly, Cultured, Knowledgeable, Well-read
synonyms: Uneducated, Unlettered, Unschooled, Ignorant, Untaught, Unread, Uninformed
sindhiMeaning: جيڪو پڙهي لکي نه سگهي، اڻ پڙهيل، ڪنهن خاص موضوع ۾ ڄاڻ نه رکندڙ، جاهل يا اڻ ڄاڻ، اهڙو ماڻهو جيڪو تعليم کان محروم هجي
urduMeaning: جو پڑھ لکھ نہ سکے، اَن پڑھ، کسی مخصوص موضوع میں معلومات سے عاری، جاہل یا ناواقف، وہ شخص جو تعلیم سے محروم ہو
englishMeaning: Unable to read or write. Lacking education or knowledge in a particular subject. Ignorant or uneducated in general matters. A person who cannot read or write.
examples: Many adults in rural areas remain illiterate due to lack of schools. He was computer illiterate and needed help sending emails. The government launched a campaign to help illiterate citizens learn to read. She felt illiterate in matters of finance and sought advice.

antonyms: Hard work, Toil, Drudgery, Labor, Grind, Chore, Burden
sindhiMeaning: اهڙي نوڪري جنهن ۾ ڪم گهٽ يا نه هجي پر پگهار ملي، بغير ذميواريءَ واري عهدو، آسان ۽ آرام واري نوڪري جيڪا صرف فائدي لاءِ رکيل هجي، مذهبي عهدو جنهن ۾ ڪا خاص خدمت نه هجي
englishMeaning: A position or job that requires little or no work but usually provides a salary or benefits. An office or role that offers pay without responsibility. A comfortable and undemanding post held mainly for its rewards. A church benefice without pastoral duties.
urduMeaning: ایسا عہدہ یا نوکری جس میں کام کم یا نہ ہو مگر تنخواہ ملے، بغیر ذمہ داری کا منصب، آسان اور آرام دہ ملازمت جو صرف فائدے کے لیے ہو، مذہبی عہدہ جس میں کوئی خاص خدمت شامل نہ ہو
examples: The advisory role turned out to be a sinecure with almost no actual duties. Critics claimed the appointment was a political sinecure. He was rewarded for his loyalty with a comfortable sinecure. Many considered the honorary chairmanship a mere sinecure.
synonyms: Cushy job, Easy job, Soft job, Gravy, Plum, Featherbed

examples: He is an incorrigible liar who never tells the truth. Their son proved to be an incorrigible troublemaker. She is an incorrigible optimist despite all her hardships. The teacher finally gave up on the incorrigible student.
sindhiMeaning: جنهن کي سڌاري نه سگهجي، هميشه لاءِ بگڙيل، اهڙي عادت وارو جيڪو ڪڏهن به نه سڌرندو، اصلاح جي ناقابل، اهڙو شخص جنهن جون خرابيون درست نه ٿي سگهن
synonyms: Unreformable, Hopeless, Hardened, Inveterate, Irredeemable, Stubborn, Obstinate, Confirmed
urduMeaning: جس کی اصلاح ممکن نہ ہو، ناقابلِ اصلاح، ایسا شخص جس کی عادت درست نہ ہو سکے، ضدی اور بگڑا ہوا، وہ شخص جس کی خامیاں ٹھیک نہ کی جا سکیں
englishMeaning: Impossible to correct, reform, or improve. Firmly rooted in bad habits or behavior that cannot be changed. Beyond correction or discipline. A person whose faults cannot be reformed.
antonyms: Corrigible, Reformable, Repentant, Amenable, Docile, Manageable, Yielding

englishMeaning: Capable of being corrected, reformed, or improved. Open to correction or amendment. Willing to accept advice or discipline. Able to be set right.
synonyms: Reformable, Amenable, Tractable, Docile, Manageable, Compliant, Improvable
examples: The young offender was considered corrigible by the counselor. His behavior is corrigible with the right guidance. She is a corrigible student who accepts feedback willingly. The report described the flaws as minor and corrigible.
urduMeaning: جس کی اصلاح ممکن ہو، درست کیے جانے کے قابل، نصیحت قبول کرنے والا، اصلاح پذیر، ایسا شخص جو اپنی غلطی مان کر سدھر جائے
sindhiMeaning: جيڪو سڌاري سگهجي، درست ٿيڻ جي قابل، نصيحت قبول ڪندڙ، اصلاح لائق، اهڙو شخص جيڪو پنهنجي غلطي مڃي سڌارجي وڃي
antonyms: Incorrigible, Unreformable, Stubborn, Hopeless, Obstinate, Hardened

sindhiMeaning: جهڳڙي کان پوءِ ٻيهر دوستي قائم ڪرڻ، صلح ڪرڻ ۽ اختلاف ختم ڪرڻ، خراب ٿيل رشتو درست ڪرڻ، ڪنهن سان ٻيهر ٺاهه ڪرڻ، ناراضگي دور ڪري ٻيهر ملڻ
antonyms: Quarrel, Fall out, Fight, Argue, Break up, Dispute, Feud
urduMeaning: جھگڑے کے بعد دوبارہ صلح کرنا، تنازعہ ختم کر کے تعلق بحال کرنا، بگڑا ہوا رشتہ ٹھیک کرنا، کسی سے دوبارہ میل ملاپ کرنا، ناراضگی دور کر کے تعلقات بہتر بنانا
synonyms: Reconcile, Make up, Make peace, Settle, Resolve, Bury the hatchet, Mend fences
examples: After weeks of silence, the two friends finally patched things up. They argued at dinner but managed to patch things up before leaving. He hopes to patch things up with his brother soon. The couple decided to patch things up for the sake of their children.
englishMeaning: To restore a friendly relationship after a disagreement or quarrel. To resolve a dispute and make peace. To fix or repair a damaged situation. To reconcile with someone after a fight.

synonyms: Partners, Associates, Supporters, Confederates, Collaborators, Friends, Comrades, Companions
englishMeaning: People, groups, or countries that cooperate with each other for a common purpose. Nations joined together by a formal agreement, especially in war. Supporters who help or assist in a struggle or cause. Friends who provide help and back up during difficulties.
examples: Britain and the United States were close allies during the war. She found strong allies among her colleagues at work. The two nations remained allies for decades. Political allies helped him win the election.
sindhiMeaning: اهڙا ماڻهو  گروهه يا ملڪ جيڪي گڏجي ڪم ڪن، جنگ ۾ گڏيل معاهدي وارا ملڪ، حمايت ڪندڙ يا مددگار، ڪنهن مقصد ۾ ساٿ ڏيندڙ، دوست جيڪي مصيبت ۾ ساٿ ڏين
urduMeaning: وہ لوگ  گروہ یا ممالک جو مشترکہ مقصد کے لیے مل کر کام کریں، جنگ میں معاہدے کے تحت متحد ممالک، حمایتی یا مددگار، کسی مقصد میں ساتھ دینے والے، دوست جو مشکل میں کام آئیں
antonyms: Enemies, Foes, Rivals, Opponents, Adversaries, Antagonists

examples: I have a sweet tooth, so I can't resist chocolate cake. My grandmother has a sweet tooth and always keeps candy at home. He admits he has a sweet tooth and eats dessert every night. Children usually have a sweet tooth from a very young age.
englishMeaning: To have a strong liking or fondness for sweet foods such as cakes and chocolate. To particularly enjoy sugary or dessert items. To crave sweets or sugary treats regularly. To be inclined toward eating sweets.
synonyms: Fond of sweets, Sugar lover, Dessert lover, Candy lover
antonyms: Dislike sweets, Sugar-averse, Savory preference
urduMeaning: میٹھے کا شوقین ہونا، مٹھائیوں کا رسیا ہونا، کیک اور چاکلیٹ وغیرہ پسند کرنا، ہر وقت میٹھے کی طلب ہونا، میٹھی چیزوں کی طرف رجحان رکھنا
sindhiMeaning: مٺاين جو گهڻو شوق هجڻ، مٺي شين پسند ڪرڻ، ڪيڪ چاڪليٽ ۽ مٺايون کائڻ جي عادت هجڻ، هر وقت مٺي جي طلب رهڻ، مٺي شين طرف رجحان رکڻ

englishMeaning: To help or assist someone with a task. To offer physical or practical help. To applaud or clap for someone as a sign of appreciation. To provide support in an activity or job.
antonyms: Hinder, Ignore, Obstruct, Refuse, Boo, Discourage
synonyms: Help, Assist, Aid, Support, Lend a hand, Applaud, Clap
examples: Could you give me a hand with these bags? Let's give the performers a big hand for their wonderful show. He kindly gave her a hand moving the furniture. Please give me a hand setting up the chairs.
urduMeaning: کسی کی مدد کرنا، کام میں ہاتھ بٹانا، کسی کی تعریف میں تالیاں بجانا، عملی طور پر سہارا دینا، تعاون فراہم کرنا
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن جي مدد ڪرڻ، ڪنهن ڪم ۾ هٿ ونڊائڻ، ڪنهن جي ساراهه ۾ تاڙيون وڄائڻ، عملي طور سهارو ڏيڻ، ڪنهن سان تعاون ڪرڻ
جاءِ جاءِ تي گهمڻ ڦرڻ، ملڪ ملڪ ۾ سفر ڪرڻ، پيرين پنڌ گهمڻ، مختلف علائقن ۾ سير سفر ڪرڻ، ڊگهو ۽ گهمندڙ سفر ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: جگہ جگہ گھومنا پھرنا، مختلف ممالک یا علاقوں میں سفر کرنا، پیدل سیر کرنا، لمبا اور گھومتا پھرتا سفر کرنا، سیر و سیاحت کرنا
antonyms: Stay, Settle, Remain, Rest, Halt, Abide
examples: He spent his youth peregrinating across Europe. They peregrinated through the countryside for weeks. Poets often peregrinate in search of inspiration. She loves to peregrinate whenever she gets a chance.
englishMeaning: To travel or wander from place to place, especially on foot. To journey through various regions or countries. To roam widely, often for pleasure or exploration. To make a long, meandering trip.
synonyms: Travel, Wander, Roam, Journey, Rove, Trek, Meander, Traverse

englishMeaning: To consider something carefully before making a decision. To reflect on a matter thoughtfully. To ponder or weigh options before acting. To review a situation mentally.
synonyms: Consider, Ponder, Reflect, Contemplate, Mull over, Deliberate, Weigh, Ruminate
examples: Please think over my offer before you reply. He needs time to think over the proposal. I'll think it over and let you know tomorrow. She thought over her options carefully before deciding.
urduMeaning: غور کرنا، کسی معاملے پر سوچ بچار کرنا، فیصلے سے پہلے اچھی طرح غور کرنا، ذہنی طور پر تولنا، دوبارہ سوچنا
sindhiMeaning: غور ڪرڻ، ڪنهن معاملي تي سوچ ويچار ڪرڻ، فيصلي کان اڳ چڱي طرح سوچڻ، ذهني طور تي تور تڪ ڪرڻ، ٻيهر سوچڻ
antonyms: Ignore, Dismiss, Overlook, Neglect, Disregard
Ignore, Neglect, Disregard, Overlook, Be careless
urduMeaning: ہوشیار رہنا، خبردار رہنا، کسی خطرے سے بچنے کے لیے چوکنا رہنا، کسی چیز کی نگرانی کرنا، احتیاط کرنے کا اشارہ دینا
sindhiMeaning: خبردار رهڻ، هوشيار ٿيڻ، ڪنهن خطري کان بچڻ لاءِ چوڪس رهڻ، ڪنهن شئي جي نظرداري ڪرڻ، احتياط ڪرڻ جو اشارو ڏيڻ
englishMeaning: To be careful or alert, especially to avoid danger. To keep an eye out for something or someone. To be on guard against a possible threat. Used as a warning to someone to be cautious.
synonyms: Beware, Be careful, Be alert, Look out, Take care, Mind, Be cautious
examples: Watch out! There's a car coming. You should watch out for pickpockets in crowded markets. Watch out for slippery floors after mopping. Parents told the children to watch out while crossing the road.

urduMeaning: لکھ لینا، کاغذ پر درج کرنا، معلومات کو تحریری شکل دینا، یادداشت بنانا، حسابات میں کسی اثاثے کی قیمت کم کر کے درج کرنا
antonyms: Erase, Delete, Forget, Ignore, Omit
englishMeaning: To record something on paper or in writing. To make a written note of information. To put thoughts, ideas, or details into written form. To officially reduce the value of an asset in accounting.
examples: Please write down your address here. She wrote down every word the professor said. Don't forget to write down the phone number. The company had to write down the value of its old equipment.
synonyms: Note, Record, Jot down, Inscribe, Register, Log, Document
sindhiMeaning: لکي ڇڏڻ، ڪاغذ تي درج ڪرڻ، ڳالهين يا معلومات کي لکت ۾ آڻڻ، يادداشت ٺاهڻ، حساب ڪتاب ۾ قيمت گهٽائي درج ڪرڻ
الٽي ڪرڻ، پيٽ جي شئي منهن ذريعي ٻاهر ڪڍڻ، ڪا شئي جلدي مٿي ڪرڻ، جلدي جلدي ڪا اڏاوت ڪرڻ، نوڪري يا ڪم ڇڏي ڏيڻ
antonyms: Swallow, Digest, Keep, Retain, Continue
englishMeaning: To vomit or expel the contents of the stomach through the mouth. To raise or lift something quickly. To construct or build hastily. To abandon or give up something, such as a job.
urduMeaning: قے کرنا، پیٹ کی چیز منہ کے ذریعے باہر نکالنا، کسی چیز کو تیزی سے اوپر اٹھانا، جلد بازی میں کوئی عمارت بنانا، نوکری یا کام چھوڑ دینا
synonyms: Vomit, Puke, Regurgitate, Retch, Bring up, Abandon, Quit
examples: The child threw up after eating too much cake. He threw up his hands in frustration. Builders threw up new houses within weeks. She threw up her job to start a business.

englishMeaning: A person or animal that sets the pace in a race. A horse trained to move both legs on one side together. A person who walks back and forth, especially when anxious. A device that regulates rhythm, such as a heart pacemaker.
synonyms: Pacesetter, Leader, Trotter, Pacemaker
examples: The pacer helped the runner maintain a steady speed. The pacer horse won several races last year. He became a nervous pacer while waiting for the results. Her heart pacer keeps her rhythm normal.
sindhiMeaning: اهڙو شخص يا جانور جيڪو ڊوڙ ۾ رفتار مقرر ڪري، هڪ خاص چال هلندڙ گهوڙو، پريشانيءَ ۾ اڳتي پوئتي گهمندڙ ماڻهو، دل جي رفتار قائم رکندڙ اوزار
antonyms: Follower, Laggard, Straggler
urduMeaning: دوڑ میں رفتار مقرر کرنے والا شخص یا گھوڑا، ایک خاص چال چلنے والا گھوڑا، بےچینی میں آگے پیچھے چلنے والا شخص، دل کی دھڑکن قابو کرنے والا آلہ

synonyms: Flat, Even, Smooth, Stage, Degree, Rank, Grade, Balance, Equalize, Honest
examples: The water reached the level of the window. She has reached a high level of expertise. Please level the ground before laying tiles. He was completely level with me about his mistakes. The next level of the game is very challenging.
englishMeaning: A horizontal position or line. A particular height or amount. A specific stage or degree in a scale or process. To make flat or even. Honest or straightforward in dealings.
urduMeaning: افقی حالت یا سطح، کسی چیز کی بلندی یا مقدار، کسی درجے یا مرحلے کا مقام، برابر یا ہموار کرنا، سیدھی اور کھری بات کرنا
sindhiMeaning: افقي حالت يا سطح، ڪنهن شئي جي اوچائي يا مقدار، ڪنهن مرحلي يا درجي جو مقام، برابر يا هموار ڪرڻ، سچائي سان ڳالهائڻ
antonyms: Uneven, Sloping, Rough, Bumpy, Dishonest, Unequal
Stench, Reek, Stink, Nothing
englishMeaning: A brief or faint smell carried in the air. A quick puff or breath of air, smoke, or vapor. A slight trace or hint of something. To catch a slight smell of something.
examples: I caught a whiff of fresh bread as I passed the bakery. There was a whiff of smoke coming from the kitchen. She sensed a whiff of trouble in his voice. He whiffed the perfume and smiled.
synonyms: Scent, Smell, Aroma, Odor, Trace, Hint, Puff, Breath
sindhiMeaning: هلڪي بوءِ جيڪا هوا ۾ اچي، هوا يا دونهين جو مختصر جهوٽو، ڪنهن شئي جو معمولي اشارو يا نشان، هلڪو مهڪار محسوس ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: ہلکی سی بو جو ہوا میں آئے، ہوا یا دھوئیں کا مختصر جھونکا، کسی چیز کا معمولی اشارہ یا سراغ، ہلکی سی مہک محسوس کرنا
بند ناک سے آواز کے ساتھ سانس لینا، بار بار سونگھنا، رونے یا زکام کی حالت میں ناک سڑکنا، ہلکی سونگھنے کی آواز نکالنا
antonyms: Breathe clearly, Exhale calmly
englishMeaning: To breathe noisily through a partially blocked nose. To sniff repeatedly, especially when crying or having a cold. To make a soft snorting sound while smelling something. A snuffling sound or breath.
sindhiMeaning: بند نڪ سان آواز ڪري ساهه کڻڻ، بار بار نڪ سونگهڻ، روئڻ يا ٿڌ جي حالت ۾ نڪ سُڙڪڻ، هلڪو سُڙڪڻ جو آواز ڪرڻ
examples: The child snuffled quietly after crying. The dog snuffled around the bushes looking for its toy. She had a bad cold and snuffled all night. He snuffled through the pages of his old diary.
synonyms: Sniff, Snuff, Snort, Snivel, Wheeze
Wonderful, Marvelous, Amazing, Incredible, Superb, Splendid, Terrific, Fantastic, Legendary, Mythical
urduMeaning: شاندار، حیرت انگیز، نہایت خوبصورت، افسانوی یا داستانی، حد سے زیادہ
sindhiMeaning: شاندار، حيرت انگيز، بيحد سٺو، ڪهاڻين ۽ داستانن سان تعلق رکندڙ، حد کان وڌيڪ
examples: She looked absolutely fabulous in her new dress. We had a fabulous time on our holiday. The book tells fabulous tales of ancient heroes. He earned a fabulous amount of money last year.
englishMeaning: Extraordinarily good, wonderful, or impressive. Almost unbelievable in nature. Relating to legend or fable. Very great in extent or degree.
antonyms: Ordinary, Terrible, Poor, Awful, Dull, Unimpressive, Real

examples: The bride looked radiant on her wedding day. The sun was radiant in the clear blue sky. She gave him a radiant smile. His face was radiant with pride when his son graduated.
sindhiMeaning: چمڪندڙ، روشني وکيرندڙ، خوشيءَ ۽ صحت سان چهرو ٻرندڙ، گرمي يا طاقت ڏيندڙ، اميد ۽ محبت سان ڀرپور
englishMeaning: Sending out light or shining brightly. Showing great happiness, joy, or health. Emitting warmth, energy, or a strong feeling. Full of hope or love.
synonyms: Bright, Shining, Glowing, Luminous, Brilliant, Beaming, Sparkling, Dazzling
antonyms: Dull, Dark, Gloomy, Dim, Sad, Cloudy, Lifeless
urduMeaning: چمکدار، روشنی بکھیرنے والا، خوشی اور صحت سے دمکتا چہرہ، گرمی یا توانائی خارج کرنے والا، امید اور محبت سے بھرا ہوا

englishMeaning: Having a full, rounded, and slightly fat shape. Pleasantly chubby or well-filled. To make or become fuller and rounder. To drop or fall heavily and suddenly.
urduMeaning: موٹا اور گول جسم والا، صحت مند اور بھرا ہوا، کسی چیز کو بھر کر پھلانا، کسی چیز کا دھڑام سے گر جانا
antonyms: Thin, Slim, Skinny, Slender, Lean, Bony, Gaunt
synonyms: Chubby, Round, Fleshy, Full, Stout, Buxom, Padded, Fat
examples: She had plump rosy cheeks as a child. The chef used plump juicy tomatoes for the salad. She plumped up the pillows before guests arrived. He plumped down onto the sofa exhausted.
sindhiMeaning: ٿلهو ۽ گول جسم وارو، صحتمند ۽ ڀريل، ڪا شئي وڌائي يا ڦوڪي ڀرڻ، ڪا شئي دم ڪري ڪري پوڻ

examples: The painting depicted a bosomy woman in traditional attire. The dress was designed for a bosomy figure. She was tall and bosomy, with an elegant walk. The character in the novel was described as bosomy and charming.
englishMeaning: Having large or prominent breasts. Full-figured, especially in the chest area. Curvaceous with a well-developed bust.
synonyms: Buxom, Busty, Curvaceous, Full-bosomed, Voluptuous
urduMeaning: بھرے سینے والی، بھرپور جسم والی عورت، ابھرے سینے والی
antonyms: Flat-chested, Slender, Slim, Small-busted
sindhiMeaning: وڏي سيني واري، ڀرپور جسم واري عورت، اڀريل سيني واري

antonyms: Plump, Fat, Fleshy, Chubby, Stout, Rounded
sindhiMeaning: هڏن وارو، بيحد سنهو جو هڏا ظاهر هجن، هڏن سان ڀرپور جهڙوڪ مڇي، هڏي جهڙي سختي وارو
synonyms: Skinny, Thin, Gaunt, Lean, Scrawny, Skeletal, Emaciated
urduMeaning: ہڈیلا، بہت دبلا کہ ہڈیاں نظر آئیں، ہڈیوں سے بھرپور جیسے مچھلی، ہڈی جیسا سخت
examples: The dog looked hungry and bony. She had long bony fingers. The fish was too bony to eat comfortably. His bony frame surprised the doctor.
englishMeaning: Having prominent or visible bones. Very thin, so that bones can be seen or felt. Containing many bones, as in fish. Resembling bone in shape or hardness.

synonyms: Sharp, Pointed, Bony, Gaunt, Jagged, Cornered, Edged
urduMeaning: تیز کونوں والا، دبلا اور ہڈیلا چہرہ جس میں خدوخال نمایاں ہوں، زاویے کے حساب سے ماپا جانے والا، اکڑا ہوا یا بےڈھب حرکت والا
englishMeaning: Having sharp angles or corners. Lean and bony, with prominent features. Measured by angles rather than distance. Stiff or awkward in movement.
sindhiMeaning: تِکن ڪنڊن وارو، ٿلهاڻ کان سواءِ چهرو جنهن ۾ هڏا نمايان هجن، زاويي جي بنياد تي ماپيو ويندڙ، بيڊولي هلندڙ يا سخت
examples: The building has a very angular modern design. He had an angular face with sharp cheekbones. Physics students learn about angular velocity. Her movements were stiff and angular on stage.
antonyms: Rounded, Curved, Smooth, Plump, Soft, Flowing

synonyms: Impartial, Objective, Neutral, Unbiased, Calm, Cool, Detached, Fair
englishMeaning: Not influenced by strong emotion; calm and impartial. Able to judge or act objectively without bias. Free from personal feelings or prejudice. Cool-headed and rational.
examples: The judge gave a dispassionate ruling on the sensitive case. Scientists must remain dispassionate when analyzing data. He offered a dispassionate view of the political situation. Her dispassionate tone calmed everyone in the room.
sindhiMeaning: جذبن کان آجو، بي طرف ۽ پرسڪون، انصاف سان فيصلو ڪندڙ، ذاتي راءِ کان بچيل، ٿڌي دماغ سان سوچيندڙ
urduMeaning: جذبات سے پاک، غیر جانبدار اور پرسکون، معروضی فیصلہ کرنے والا، ذاتی رائے سے آزاد، ٹھنڈے دماغ سے سوچنے والا
antonyms: Emotional, Biased, Prejudiced, Partial, Passionate, Excited

examples: The insipidity of the soup disappointed the guests. Critics complained about the insipidity of the film's dialogue. Her writing suffered from insipidity and lacked emotion. The insipidity of the meeting made everyone yawn.
englishMeaning: The quality of lacking flavor, taste, or excitement. Dullness or lack of interest. A state of being uninteresting or unstimulating. Blandness in food, speech, or personality.
urduMeaning: بے ذائقہ پن، بے مزگی، دلچسپی سے عاری ہونا، پھیکی حالت، کھانے  گفتگو یا شخصیت میں کشش کی کمی
synonyms: Blandness, Dullness, Tastelessness, Vapidity, Flatness, Monotony, Boredom
sindhiMeaning: ڪا مزي جي کوٽ، بي ذائقگي، ڪا شئي جيڪا دلچسپ نه هجي، ماٺاٽ يا خشڪي جي حالت، کاڌي  ڳالهائڻ يا شخصيت ۾ بيرنگي
antonyms: Flavor, Excitement, Zest, Spice, Interest, Liveliness, Vibrancy
Ignore, Disregard, Overlook, Loosen, Detach
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شئي تي مسلسل ڌيان ڏيڻ، ڪنهن خيال ۾ کپي وڃڻ، ڪا شئي مضبوطي سان قائم ڪرڻ، ڪنهن ماڻهو يا خيال سان اڻ صحتمند لڳاءَ ٿيڻ، هڪ ئي جاءِ تي نظر ڄمائي ڏسڻ
examples: She tends to fixate on small mistakes. Please don't fixate on the past. The child fixated on the shiny toy in the window. Investigators fixated on one suspect from the start.
synonyms: Obsess, Focus, Concentrate, Fasten, Stare, Preoccupy, Dwell
urduMeaning: کسی چیز پر مسلسل توجہ مرکوز کرنا، کسی خیال میں کھو جانا، کسی چیز کو مضبوطی سے جمانا، کسی شخص یا خیال سے غیر صحت مند لگاؤ ہو جانا، ایک جگہ نظریں جما کر دیکھنا
englishMeaning: To focus one's attention or thoughts obsessively on something. To fasten or make stable. To become emotionally attached to a person or idea in an unhealthy way. To stare fixedly at something.

antonyms: Reduce, Shrink, Diminish, Minimize, Downplay, Lessen
examples: The microscope magnifies tiny cells for study. He tends to magnify his problems unnecessarily. The mirror magnified her reflection. The hymn magnifies the greatness of God.
englishMeaning: To make something appear larger, especially using a lens or microscope. To increase the size, importance, or effect of something. To exaggerate or overstate a problem or feeling. To praise or glorify.
urduMeaning: کسی چیز کو بڑا کر کے دکھانا، عدسے یا خوردبین سے بڑا کرنا، بات کو بڑھا چڑھا کر پیش کرنا، کسی چیز کی اہمیت بڑھانا، تعریف یا حمد کرنا
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شئي کي وڏو ڪري ڏيکارڻ، عدسي يا خوردبين سان وڏو ڪرڻ، ڪا ڳالهه وڌائي پيش ڪرڻ، ڪنهن شئي جي اهميت وڌائڻ، ساراهه يا تعريف ڪرڻ
synonyms: Enlarge, Expand, Increase, Amplify, Exaggerate, Boost, Intensify, Glorify

antonyms: Crawl, Amateur, Novice, Beginner, Slow
synonyms: Zoom, Dash, Speed, Rush, Expert, Genius, Prodigy, Ace
urduMeaning: تیزی سے گزر جانا، کسی کام کا ماہر شخص، تیز رفتاری سے سنسناہٹ کی آواز کرنا، ایک حیرت انگیز کامیابی
englishMeaning: To move very quickly, often with a rushing sound. A person who is exceptionally skilled at something. To make a hissing or humming sound while moving fast. A quick or impressive achievement.
examples: Cars whizzed past on the highway. He is a whiz at solving math problems. The arrow whizzed through the air. She finished the puzzle in a whiz.
sindhiMeaning: تيزيءَ سان لنگهي وڃڻ، ڪنهن ڪم ۾ ماهر ماڻهو، تيز رفتاريءَ سان آواز ڪرڻ، هڪ حيرت انگيز ڪاميابي

antonyms: Distract, Ignore, Scatter, Disperse, Neglect
sindhiMeaning: ڌيان جو مرڪز، روشنيءَ يا آواز جو ملڻ وارو نقطو، ڪنهن ڪم يا موضوع تي ڌيان ڏيڻ، عدسي کي صاف تصوير لاءِ ترتيب ڏيڻ، مرڪزي نقطو
urduMeaning: توجہ کا مرکز، روشنی یا آواز کے ملنے کا مقام، کسی موضوع یا کام پر توجہ دینا، عدسے کو واضح تصویر کے لیے ترتیب دینا، مرکزی نقطہ
englishMeaning: The center of interest, attention, or activity. The point at which rays of light or sound meet. To concentrate on a particular subject or task. To adjust a lens to produce a clear image.
examples: She lost her focus during the meeting. The camera lens was not in focus. He needs to focus on his studies. The focus of the report is climate change.
synonyms: Concentrate, Center, Aim, Direct, Attention, Spotlight, Hub, Emphasis

englishMeaning: To move slowly on hands and knees or with the body close to the ground. To move very slowly, like a car in heavy traffic. To be full of insects, worms, or unpleasant things. A slow rate of movement or a swimming stroke.
examples: The baby learned to crawl at seven months. Traffic was crawling due to the accident. The old kitchen was crawling with ants. She won the medal in the front crawl race.
synonyms: Creep, Slither, Inch, Drag, Slog, Trudge
sindhiMeaning: هٿن ۽ گوڏن تي رِڙهڻ، تمام آهستي هلڻ، ڪنهن جاءِ تي جيتن جو ڀرجي وڃڻ، تير جو تير هلڻ، تيراڪي جو هڪ انداز
antonyms: Run, Rush, Speed, Sprint, Race, Fly
urduMeaning: ہاتھوں اور گھٹنوں کے بل چلنا، بہت آہستہ چلنا، کسی جگہ کیڑوں مکوڑوں سے بھرا ہونا، سست رفتاری سے حرکت کرنا، تیراکی کا ایک انداز

antonyms: Wrong, Incorrect, Inaccurate, False, Imprecise, Faulty, Erroneous
sindhiMeaning: بلڪل درست، غلطي کان آجو، ماپ يا بيان ۾ صحيح، حقيقتن تي مبني، نشاني تي پهچندڙ
urduMeaning: بالکل درست، غلطیوں سے پاک، پیمائش یا بیان میں صحیح، حقائق پر مبنی، نشانے پر لگنے والا
examples: The report gives an accurate account of the incident. Her watch is very accurate. We need accurate measurements before cutting the wood. The archer's aim was accurate.
synonyms: Correct, Exact, Precise, Right, True, Faithful, Reliable, Truthful
englishMeaning: Correct in all details and free from errors. Precise and exact in measurement or description. Careful and truthful in reporting or reflecting facts. Hitting the intended target or mark.

urduMeaning: پیدل چلنے کا راستہ، کسی منزل تک لے جانے والا راستہ، کسی مقصد کے حصول کے لیے اقدامات کا سلسلہ، حیاتیاتی کیمیائی عمل کی ترتیب
sindhiMeaning: پيرين هلڻ جو رستو، ڪنهن مقصد ڏانهن وٺي ويندڙ رستو، ڪنهن ڪاميابيءَ لاءِ اختيار ڪيل قدم، حياتياتي ڪيميائي عمل جو سلسلو
examples: A narrow pathway led through the garden. Education is a pathway to success. The company outlined a clear pathway for career growth. Scientists studied the pathway of the disease in the body.
synonyms: Path, Route, Track, Trail, Way, Road, Course, Passage
englishMeaning: A path or track laid down for walking or made by regular use. A route or course leading to a particular goal or destination. A series of steps or actions to achieve something. A sequence of chemical reactions in biology.
antonyms: Obstacle, Barrier, Dead end, Blockage

examples: Public officials must act with honesty and accountability. There is a growing demand for greater accountability in government. The manager takes full accountability for the team's performance. Teachers share accountability for their students' progress.
synonyms: Responsibility, Answerability, Liability, Obligation, Duty, Trustworthiness, Reliability
urduMeaning: جواب دہی، ذمہ داری، اپنے اعمال کا حساب دینے کی پابندی، جوابدہ ہونے کا احساس، اپنے فیصلوں کی ذمہ داری قبول کرنا، کام کا حساب کتاب دینے کی مجبوری
antonyms: Irresponsibility, Unaccountability, Immunity, Exemption, Negligence, Unreliability
sindhiMeaning: جوابداري، ذميواري، پنهنجن عملن جو حساب ڏيڻ جي پابندي، جوابدهي جو احساس، پنهنجن فيصلن جي ذميواري کڻڻ، ڪم جو حساب ڪتاب ڏيڻ جي مجبوري
englishMeaning: The fact or condition of being responsible for one's actions and decisions. The obligation to explain, justify, and take responsibility for what one does. A willingness to accept blame or credit for outcomes. The quality of being answerable to someone for a duty or task. A system in which people are required to report on their work and accept its consequences.

examples: He received a small increment in his monthly salary. The temperature rises in tiny increments each hour. Every yearly increment brought him closer to his goal. The software updates come in regular increments.
urduMeaning: اضافہ، بڑھوتری، تنخواہ میں باقاعدہ تھوڑا تھوڑا اضافہ، درجہ بدرجہ بڑھنا، مقرر مقدار میں اضافہ
antonyms: Decrease, Reduction, Decrement, Loss, Cut, Diminution
Departure, Resignation, Abdication, Withdrawal, Loss, Decrease
examples: The queen's accession to the throne was celebrated nationwide. The library announced several new accessions this month. The country signed the accession to the trade agreement. His accession to power surprised everyone.
urduMeaning: تخت نشینی، عہدے پر فائز ہونا، کسی معاہدے میں شامل ہونا، اضافہ، مجموعے میں نئی چیز کا شامل ہونا
englishMeaning: The attainment or acquisition of a position of rank or power. A new item added to a collection. Formal acceptance or agreement to a treaty. The act of joining an organization or country. An increase or addition to something.
sindhiMeaning: تخت نشيني، عهدي تي فائز ٿيڻ، ڪنهن معاهدي ۾ شامل ٿيڻ، اضافو، مجموعي ۾ نئين شيءِ شامل ٿيڻ
synonyms: Ascension, Attainment, Assumption, Addition, Acquisition, Joining, Increase

sindhiMeaning: وڏو ڪرڻ، ڦهلاءُ، واڌارو، تصوير جو وڏو نسخو، جسم جي ڪنهن حصي جو وڌي وڃڻ
antonyms: Reduction, Contraction, Decrease, Shrinkage, Compression, Diminution
urduMeaning: بڑا کرنا، پھیلاؤ، اضافہ، تصویر کا بڑا نسخہ، جسم کے کسی حصے کا بڑھ جانا

synonyms: Expansion, Extension, Increase, Growth, Development, Amplification, Broadening
englishMeaning: The act of making something bigger in size or amount. A photographic print that is larger than the negative. An extension or expansion of something. An increase in scope, importance, or range. Growth in physical size of a body part or organ.

synonyms: Expand, Increase, Extend, Broaden, Widen, Amplify, Magnify, Grow
sindhiMeaning: وڏو ڪرڻ، ڦهلائڻ، وسيع ڪرڻ، تفصيل سان بيان ڪرڻ، تصوير وڏي ڪرڻ
examples: They plan to enlarge the school building next year. He asked her to enlarge on her previous statement. We can enlarge the picture for better viewing. Reading widely helps enlarge one's understanding of the world.
urduMeaning: بڑا کرنا، پھیلانا، وسیع کرنا، تفصیل سے بیان کرنا، تصویر بڑی کرنا
antonyms: Reduce, Shrink, Contract, Decrease, Diminish, Compress, Narrow
englishMeaning: To make or become bigger in size or amount. To expand the scope of something. To describe something in greater detail. To increase the capacity or importance of something. To reproduce a photograph on a larger scale.

synonyms: Increase, Extension, Supplement, Attachment, Annex, Inclusion, Expansion
examples: The new player is a valuable addition to the team. Children learn addition in their early classes. They built an addition to their house last summer. In addition to English, she speaks three other languages.
englishMeaning: The process of adding something to something else. A person or thing added to an existing group. The mathematical operation of combining numbers to find their sum. An extra part built onto a building. An increase resulting from being added.
sindhiMeaning: اضافو، ملائڻ، جمع ڪرڻ، حساب ۾ عددن جو جوڙ، عمارت ۾ نئون حصو، ڪنهن گروهه ۾ نئون فرد
antonyms: Subtraction, Removal, Reduction, Deduction, Loss, Decrease
urduMeaning: اضافہ، ملانا، جمع کرنا، حساب میں عدد جوڑنا، عمارت میں نیا حصہ، کسی گروہ میں نیا فرد

synonyms: Abolition, Termination, Cancellation, Annulment, Elimination, Removal, Repeal
englishMeaning: The act of officially ending a law, system, or practice. The formal cancellation of something established. The termination of an institution or custom. The action of putting an end to something. The removal of something by authority.

sindhiMeaning: خاتمو، ختم ڪرڻ، رواج يا قانون کي منسوخ ڪرڻ، سرڪاري طور تي ختم ڪرڻ، مڪمل طور خاتمو ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: خاتمہ، ختم کرنا، رواج یا قانون کو منسوخ کرنا، سرکاری طور پر ختم کرنا، مکمل طور پر خاتمہ کرنا
antonyms: Establishment, Creation, Introduction, Institution, Enactment, Preservation

sindhiMeaning: منسوخي، رد ڪرڻ، قانون يا معاهدي جو سرڪاري طور تي ختم ٿيڻ، ڪنهن حق کي ختم ڪرڻ، رواج ختم ڪرڻ
examples: The abrogation of the treaty caused political tension. Parliament voted for the abrogation of the outdated law. The abrogation of these rights sparked strong protests. Both nations agreed to the abrogation of the old agreement.
englishMeaning: The formal repeal or cancellation of a law, agreement, or right. The act of ending something formally or officially. Cancellation of a treaty or contract by mutual consent or authority. The revocation of a rule or decision. The nullification of an existing arrangement.
synonyms: Repeal, Cancellation, Annulment, Revocation, Nullification, Abolition, Termination
urduMeaning: منسوخی، رد کرنا، قانون یا معاہدے کا سرکاری طور پر ختم ہونا، کسی حق کو ختم کرنا، رواج ختم کرنا
antonyms: Enactment, Establishment, Confirmation, Ratification, Approval, Institution

examples: The curtailment of expenses helped the company survive. Citizens protested against the curtailment of their rights. There has been a curtailment of public transport services. The curtailment of working hours pleased many employees.
synonyms: Reduction, Cutback, Decrease, Limitation, Restriction, Shortening, Diminution
sindhiMeaning: گھٽتائي، ڪٽوتي، محدود ڪرڻ، خرچ يا حقن ۾ گھٽتائي، وقت يا سرگرمي کي ننڍو ڪرڻ

englishMeaning: The act of reducing or limiting something. A cutback in the size, amount, or extent of something. A shortening of duration or activity. The imposition of restrictions on something. A decrease or restriction imposed upon rights or freedoms.

synonyms: Inn, Pub, Bar, Public house, Alehouse, Saloon, Roadhouse, Taproom, Drinking place, Hostelry
sindhiMeaning: شراب يا مشروبات وڪرو ٿيڻ واري جاءِ، اهڙو سرائو يا عوامي گهر جتي کاڌو يا رهائش به ملي سگهي، ننڍو روايتي شراب خانو، مسافرن يا مقامي ماڻهن جي گڏجڻ جي جاءِ
antonyms: School, Mosque, Church, Office, Workplace, Home, Abstinence, Sobriety, Private house
englishMeaning: A place where alcoholic drinks are sold and people can sit and drink. An inn or public house that may also provide food or lodging. A small traditional bar or drinking house. A social meeting place where travelers or local people gather.
urduMeaning: شراب یا مشروبات فروخت ہونے کی جگہ، ایسا سرائے یا عوامی گھر جہاں کھانا یا رہائش بھی مل سکتی ہو، چھوٹا روایتی شراب خانہ، مسافروں یا مقامی لوگوں کے جمع ہونے کی جگہ

antonyms: Later, Subsequent, Following, Future, Next, Afterward, Junior, Inferior, Posterior
examples: Please tell us about any prior experience you have. The meeting was canceled because of a prior commitment. The report refers to events from the prior year. The prior welcomed the visitors to the monastery.
englishMeaning: Existing or happening before something else in time, order, or importance. Earlier or previous. More important or having precedence in a particular situation. A senior monk who ranks below an abbot. The head of a priory.
sindhiMeaning: اڳ ۾ ٿيندڙ يا موجود، اڳوڻو يا پهريون، ڪنهن ڪم کان اڳ وارو، اهميت يا ترتيب ۾ اڳرائي رکندڙ، خانقاهه جو نائب يا سربراهه راهب
urduMeaning: پہلے ہونے والا یا موجود، سابقہ یا پچھلا، کسی کام سے پہلے کا، اہمیت یا ترتیب میں مقدم، خانقاہ کا نائب یا سربراہ راہب
synonyms: Earlier, Previous, Former, Preceding, Antecedent, Past, Advance, Preliminary, Senior, Superior

antonyms: Layperson, Secular person, Parishioner, Commoner, Follower, Noncleric, Subordinate

englishMeaning: A high-ranking member of the Christian clergy. A bishop, archbishop, or other senior church official. A religious leader with authority over a diocese or church community. A dignitary in an ecclesiastical hierarchy.
synonyms: Bishop, Archbishop, Cleric, Churchman, Ecclesiastic, Cardinal, Abbot, Monsignor, Church leader, Dignitary
examples: The prelate addressed the congregation after the ceremony. Several prelates attended the council meeting. The old cathedral was restored under the guidance of a respected prelate. The prelate spoke carefully about peace and charity.
urduMeaning: عیسائی مذہبی ادارے کا اعلیٰ عہدیدار، بشپ یا آرچ بشپ جیسا بڑا پادری، کلیسا یا مذہبی علاقے کا بااختیار رہنما، مذہبی درجہ بندی میں بڑا شخص
مشرقی عیسائی کلیساؤں میں بڑا راہب یا پادری، خانقاہ یا کئی خانقاہوں کا سربراہ، اہم خانقاہی رہنما کے لیے اعزازی لقب، بعض روایات میں عام ایبٹ سے بلند مذہبی عہدیدار
synonyms: Abbot, Senior monk, Prior, Monastic superior, Cleric, Priest, Prelate, Ecclesiastic, Religious leader
sindhiMeaning: اوڀر عيسائي گرجائن ۾ وڏو راهب يا پادري، خانقاهه يا ڪيترين خانقاهن جو سربراهه، اهم خانقاهي اڳواڻ لاءِ اعزازي لقب، ڪجهه روايتن ۾ عام ايبٽ کان مٿانهون مذهبي عهديدار
examples: The archimandrite led the prayers in the monastery chapel. Visitors asked the archimandrite about the history of the community. The title of archimandrite is respected in many Eastern churches. An archimandrite supervised several monks and novices.
antonyms: Novice, Layperson, Junior monk, Secular person, Follower, Subordinate, Common member
englishMeaning: A senior priest or monk in some Eastern Christian churches. The head of a monastery or group of monasteries. An honorary title given to an important monastic leader. A church official ranking above an ordinary abbot in certain traditions.

sindhiMeaning: درجي يا عهدي ۾ هيٺ، ڪنهن جي ماتحت ڪم ڪندڙ، گهٽ اهم، ماتحت ماڻهو، ڪنهن شيءِ کي ٻي شيءِ کان گهٽ اهم رکڻ

synonyms: Inferior, Junior, Lower-ranking, Dependent, Secondary, Lesser, Assistant, Underling, Subject, Subaltern
urduMeaning: درجے یا عہدے میں کم، کسی کے ماتحت کام کرنے والا، کم اہم، ماتحت شخص، کسی چیز کو دوسری چیز سے کم اہم رکھنا

examples: Every subordinate must understand the new safety rules. The manager listened carefully to her subordinate's concerns. In this plan, personal interest is subordinate to public duty. The committee decided to subordinate minor issues to the main goal.

antonyms: Accept, Claim, Keep, Maintain, Embrace, Support, Acknowledge, Retain, Defend, Adopt
sindhiMeaning: حق لقب يا دعويٰ ڇڏي ڏيڻ، عقيدي عادت يا طريقي کي رد ڪرڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ جي حمايت يا قبوليت کان انڪار ڪرڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ کي ڇڏڻ جو کليل اعلان ڪرڻ
englishMeaning: To formally give up a claim, right, title, or position. To reject or disown a belief, habit, or way of life. To refuse to continue supporting or accepting something. To declare publicly that one will abandon something.
urduMeaning: حق لقب یا دعویٰ چھوڑ دینا، عقیدے عادت یا طریقے کو رد کرنا، کسی چیز کی حمایت یا قبولیت سے انکار کرنا، کسی چیز کو چھوڑنے کا کھلا اعلان کرنا
examples: She decided to renounce her claim to the property. The leader refused to renounce violence at first. He renounced his old habits after becoming ill. The prince was forced to renounce the throne.
synonyms: Abandon, Give up, Reject, Disown, Repudiate, Relinquish, Surrender, Forswear, Abdicate, Forsake
Quit, Step down, Leave, Retire, Abdicate, Relinquish, Surrender, Withdraw, Submit, Accept
sindhiMeaning: نوڪري عهدي يا ذميواري تان رسمي طور دستبردار ٿيڻ، رضاڪارانه طور عهدي ڇڏڻ، مجبوري حالت کي صبر سان قبول ڪرڻ، پاڻ کي ڪنهن فيصلي يا حالت حوالي ڪرڻ

englishMeaning: To formally leave a job, office, or position. To give up a responsibility or post voluntarily. To accept an unpleasant situation calmly because it cannot be changed. To submit oneself to a condition or decision.

antonyms: Chest, Back, Head, Limbs, Thorax, Pelvis, Extremity
urduMeaning: سینے اور کولہے کے درمیان جسمانی حصہ، پیٹ کا علاقہ جہاں معدہ آنتیں جگر اور دوسرے اعضا ہوتے ہیں، کیڑوں میں پچھلا جسمانی حصہ، انسانوں اور جانوروں کے دھڑ کا اہم خانہ

synonyms: Belly, Stomach area, Midsection, Tummy, Paunch, Trunk, Body cavity, Gut, Abdominal region
englishMeaning: The part of the body between the chest and the pelvis. The belly area containing the stomach, intestines, liver, and other organs. The posterior body section of many insects and other arthropods. A major cavity of the trunk in humans and animals.
examples: The doctor examined the patient's abdomen for swelling. Pain in the lower abdomen should not be ignored. The insect has stripes across its abdomen. Strong muscles help protect the abdomen.

sindhiMeaning: معدو جتي کاڌو هضم ٿيڻ شروع ٿئي، پيٽ يا اڳيون وچ وارو جسماني حصو، بک يا کاڌي جي خواهش، مشڪل ڪم برداشت ڪرڻ جي همت، ڪنهن ناپسند شيءِ کي سهي وڃڻ
antonyms: Back, Chest, Disgust, Weakness, Cowardice, Refuse, Reject, Loathe, Avoid

synonyms: Belly, Abdomen, Tummy, Gut, Appetite, Digestion, Courage, Nerve, Endure, Tolerate
englishMeaning: The organ in the body where food is stored and partly digested. The front part of the body around the abdomen. A person's appetite or desire for food. The courage or willingness to face something unpleasant. To tolerate or endure something difficult.

The injury affected several bones in his spine. The title was printed on the spine of the book. Some desert plants have sharp spines instead of leaves. She showed real spine during the difficult negotiations.

synonyms: Backbone, Vertebral column, Backbone structure, Support, Shaft, Ridge, Thorn, Prickle, Courage, Resolve
urduMeaning: کمر کی ہڈیوں کی قطار، ریڑھ کی ہڈی، کتاب یا پتے کا درمیانی سہارا، پودے یا جانور کا نوکیلا کانٹا، ہمت ثابت قدمی یا اخلاقی طاقت
sindhiMeaning: پٺيءَ جي هڏين جي قطار، ريڙهه جي هڏي، ڪتاب يا پن جي وچ وارو سهارو، ٻوٽي يا جانور جو نوڪدار ڪنڊو، همت ثابت قدمي يا اخلاقي طاقت

examples: The patient needed a spinal examination after the accident. A spinal injury can affect movement and feeling. The surgeon discussed the risks of spinal anesthesia. The hospital ordered a scan of the spinal column.
urduMeaning: ریڑھ کی ہڈی سے متعلق، اسپائنل کارڈ سے وابستہ، ریڑھ کی ہڈی کے قریب یا اسے متاثر کرنے والا، ریڑھ میں دی جانے والی بے ہوشی یا انجیکشن کے لیے مختصر لفظ

sindhiMeaning: ريڙهه جي هڏي سان لاڳاپيل، اسپائنل ڪارڊ سان واسطو رکندڙ، ريڙهه جي هڏي ڀرسان يا ان کي متاثر ڪندڙ، ريڙهه ۾ لڳندڙ بيهوشي يا انجڪشن لاءِ مختصر لفظ

synonyms: Neck-related, Cervix-related, Nuchal, Vertebral, Medical, Uterine, Spinal

sindhiMeaning: ڳچيءَ سان لاڳاپيل، رحم جي سروڪس سان لاڳاپيل، ڳچيءَ واري ريڙهه جي حصي سان واسطو رکندڙ، طبي اصطلاح ۾ ڳچي يا سروڪس جي بناوتن بابت

englishMeaning: Relating to the neck. Relating to the cervix of the uterus. Located in or affecting the neck region of the spine. Used in medical terms for structures in the neck or cervix.

antonyms: Spinal, Cervical, Caudal, Peripheral, Abdominal, External
urduMeaning: کھوپڑی یا سر سے متعلق، کرینیم سے وابستہ، کھوپڑی کے اندر یا قریب موجود، دماغ یا دماغ سے نکلنے والے اعصاب سے متعلق
englishMeaning: Relating to the skull. Relating to the cranium or head. Located inside or near the skull. Connected with the brain or nerves that arise from the brain.

sindhiMeaning: کوپڙي يا مٿي سان لاڳاپيل، ڪرينيئم سان واسطو رکندڙ، کوپڙي اندر يا ڀرسان موجود، دماغ يا دماغ مان نڪرندڙ عصبن سان لاڳاپيل
synonyms: Skull-related, Head-related, Cerebral, Cephalic, Intracranial, Neurological, Cranial-bone

synonyms: Grab, Grasp, Catch, Snatch, Capture, Confiscate, Take, Occupy, Arrest, Exploit
sindhiMeaning: اوچتو ۽ مضبوطي سان پڪڙڻ، زور يا قانوني اختيار سان قبضو ڪرڻ، موقعو جلدي وٺڻ، ڪنهن تي اوچتو اثر ڪرڻ، مال يا شين کي ضبط ڪرڻ
antonyms: Release, Free, Let go, Surrender, Give, Lose, Miss, Return, Liberate, Yield
urduMeaning: اچانک اور مضبوطی سے پکڑنا، زور یا قانونی اختیار سے قبضہ کرنا، موقعہ فوراً حاصل کرنا، کسی پر اچانک اثر کرنا، مال یا چیزوں کو ضبط کرنا

antonyms: Release, Free, Rescue, Liberate, Return, Protect, Save, Let go
englishMeaning: To take a person away illegally by force or deception. To abduct someone and hold them captive. To seize a person for ransom, pressure, or another unlawful purpose. The act of unlawfully carrying someone away.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ماڻهو کي زور يا ٺڳي سان غيرقانوني طور کڻي وڃڻ، اغوا ڪري قيد رکڻ، ڀنگ دٻاءُ يا ناجائز مقصد لاءِ ماڻهو پڪڙڻ، اغوا جو عمل
examples: The criminals planned to kidnap a wealthy businessman. Police rescued the child before the kidnappers could leave the city. The story is about a plot to kidnap a scientist. They were arrested for trying to kidnap a witness.
urduMeaning: کسی شخص کو زور یا دھوکے سے غیر قانونی طور پر لے جانا، اغوا کرکے قید رکھنا، تاوان دباؤ یا ناجائز مقصد کے لیے شخص کو پکڑنا، اغوا کا عمل
synonyms: Abduct, Seize, Carry off, Snatch, Capture, Detain, Take hostage, Hijack, Hold captive

sindhiMeaning: عام يا روزمره، غير خاص يا غير معمولي نه، اوسط معيار يا درجي وارو، چرچ يا قانوني اداري ۾ معمولي اختيار رکندڙ شخص، پراڻي استعمال ۾ مقرر قيمت وارو کاڌو
antonyms: Exceptional, Unusual, Rare, Extraordinary, Special, Remarkable, Strange, Unique, Outstanding
englishMeaning: Normal, usual, or common. Not special, rare, or exceptional. Of average quality or rank. A person with regular authority in a church or legal office. A fixed meal provided at a set price in older usage.
synonyms: Common, Usual, Normal, Regular, Average, Plain, Routine, Everyday, Typical, Unremarkable
urduMeaning: عام یا روزمرہ، غیر خاص یا غیر معمولی نہیں، اوسط معیار یا درجے کا، کلیسا یا قانونی ادارے میں معمول کا اختیار رکھنے والا شخص، پرانے استعمال میں مقرر قیمت والا کھانا
examples: It was an ordinary day at the office. The box looked ordinary, but it contained rare documents. Ordinary people often suffer most during a crisis. The judge served as the ordinary in that jurisdiction.

sindhiMeaning: غير معمولي طور سٺو يا اثرائتو، عام کان الڳ، ناياب يا گهٽ ملندڙ، قاعدي کان استثنا، خاص حالتن يا خوبين سبب خاص ڌيان جو محتاج
synonyms: Outstanding, Remarkable, Extraordinary, Unusual, Rare, Excellent, Superior, Special, Notable, Unique
urduMeaning: غیر معمولی طور پر اچھا یا متاثر کن، عام سے الگ، نایاب یا کم ملنے والا، قاعدے سے استثنا، خاص حالات یا خوبیوں کی وجہ سے خاص توجہ کا محتاج
examples: She has exceptional talent for languages. The school gives extra support to children with exceptional needs. This was an exceptional case and required special approval. His performance in the final match was exceptional.
englishMeaning: Unusually good or impressive. Not typical or ordinary. Rare or uncommon. Forming an exception to a rule or general pattern. Needing special treatment because of unusual qualities or circumstances.
antonyms: Ordinary, Common, Average, Usual, Normal, Typical, Mediocre, Regular, Unremarkable
Normal, Regular, Typical, Usual, Standard, Expected, Consistent, Ordinary, Conventional
urduMeaning: عام یا متوقع سے مختلف، ایسا غیر معمولی یا بے قاعدہ جس کی وضاحت مشکل ہو، معمول کے قاعدے یا نمونے سے نہ ملنے والا، اردگرد کے حقائق سے غیر موافق
examples: The lab reported an anomalous result in one sample. Scientists studied the anomalous weather pattern carefully. His behavior seemed anomalous for such a quiet student. The accountant found an anomalous entry in the records.
synonyms: Abnormal, Irregular, Unusual, Atypical, Odd, Strange, Deviant, Exceptional, Inconsistent, Peculiar
englishMeaning: Different from what is normal or expected. Irregular or unusual in a way that is difficult to explain. Not fitting the usual rule, pattern, or classification. Abnormal or inconsistent with surrounding facts.
sindhiMeaning: عام يا متوقع کان مختلف، اهڙو غيرمعمولي يا بيقاعده جيڪو سمجهائڻ ڏکيو هجي، معمول جي قاعدي يا نموني سان نه ملندڙ، ڀرپاسي حقيقتن سان غير موافق

antonyms: Convergence, Agreement, Similarity, Unity, Consistency, Meeting, Harmony, Parallelism, Accord
examples: There was a clear divergence between the two reports. The divergence of opinions made agreement difficult. Scientists measured the divergence of the two species over time. A sudden divergence in the data caught the analyst's attention.
englishMeaning: The act of moving or developing in different directions. A difference between two things that were expected to be similar. A departure from a common path, opinion, or standard. In mathematics or science, a measure or pattern of spreading apart.
sindhiMeaning: مختلف رخن ۾ وڃڻ يا وڌڻ جو عمل، ٻه ساڳيون سمجهيون ويندڙ شيون وچ ۾ فرق، عام رستي راءِ يا معيار کان هٽڻ، رياضي يا سائنس ۾ پکڙجڻ يا الڳ ٿيڻ جو اندازو
synonyms: Difference, Deviation, Separation, Variation, Disagreement, Departure, Split, Disparity, Gap, Forking
urduMeaning: مختلف سمتوں میں جانے یا بڑھنے کا عمل، دو مماثل سمجھی جانے والی چیزوں کے درمیان فرق، عام راستے رائے یا معیار سے ہٹنا، ریاضی یا سائنس میں پھیلنے یا الگ ہونے کا اندازہ
کسی کام میں وقفہ یا تعطل، سلسلے یا ریکارڈ میں خلا، کام پڑھائی یا کارکردگی سے عارضی غیر حاضری، جسمانی ساخت میں سوراخ یا راستہ
synonyms: Pause, Break, Gap, Interval, Interruption, Lapse, Rest, Suspension, Recess, Opening
examples: The band returned after a two-year hiatus. There is a long hiatus in the historical record. She took a short hiatus from social media. The doctor explained the meaning of a hiatus in the diaphragm.
englishMeaning: A pause, break, or interruption in an activity. A gap in a sequence, record, or series. A temporary absence from work, study, or performance. In anatomy, an opening or passage in an organ or body structure.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ڪم ۾ وقفو يا ٽٽڻ، سلسلي يا رڪارڊ ۾ خال، ڪم پڙهائي يا ڪارڪردگي کان عارضي غيرحاضري، جسماني بناوت ۾ سوراخ يا گذرگاهه
antonyms: Continuation, Continuity, Flow, Resumption, Connection, Closure, Permanence, Uninterrupted activity

englishMeaning: Showing calm seriousness and self-respect. Noble, honorable, and worthy of respect. Formal or stately in manner or appearance. Made to seem important, respectable, or honorable.
synonyms: Noble, Respectable, Honorable, Stately, Graceful, Decent, Serious, Composed, Majestic, Elevated
urduMeaning: وقار اور خود عزتی ظاہر کرنے والا، عزت کے قابل اور شریف، انداز یا صورت میں سنجیدہ اور باوقار، کسی کو اہم یا معزز بنایا ہوا
sindhiMeaning: وقار ۽ خود عزتي ڏيکاريندڙ، عزت لائق ۽ شريف، انداز يا صورت ۾ سنجيده ۽ باوقار، ڪنهن کي اهم يا معزز بڻايل
examples: She gave a dignified response to the criticism. The old building has a dignified simplicity. He remained dignified even after the defeat. The ceremony dignified the achievements of the volunteers.
antonyms: Undignified, Shameful, Vulgar, Disgraceful, Silly, Crude, Low, Humiliating, Base

synonyms: Unhappy, Sad, Wretched, Depressed, Gloomy, Poor, Awful, Pitiful, Distressed, Dejected
examples: He felt miserable after hearing the bad news. The refugees lived in miserable conditions. We had a miserable journey through the storm. She offered him a miserable amount for the hard work.
urduMeaning: بہت اداس یا دکھی، تکلیف یا دکھ پیدا کرنے والا، معیار یا حالت میں بہت خراب، بہت کم یا ناکافی، قابل رحم یا بدحال
englishMeaning: Very unhappy or depressed. Causing discomfort, suffering, or unhappiness. Very poor in quality or condition. Extremely small, inadequate, or mean. Wretched or pitiable.
antonyms: Happy, Cheerful, Comfortable, Pleasant, Joyful, Excellent, Fortunate, Content, Satisfied
sindhiMeaning: تمام اداس يا ڏکيو، تڪليف يا ڏک پيدا ڪندڙ، معيار يا حالت ۾ تمام خراب، تمام ٿورو يا ناڪافي، رحم جوڳو يا بدحال

examples: The farmer stopped to unyoke the oxen at sunset. The reform aimed to unyoke workers from unfair rules. After the plowing was finished, he unyoked the horses. The treaty helped unyoke the region from foreign control.
synonyms: Release, Free, Unharness, Detach, Separate, Liberate, Disengage, Untie, Unbind, Emancipate
antonyms: Yoke, Bind, Harness, Attach, Join, Enslave, Fasten, Tie, Restrain, Connect
urduMeaning: جانوروں سے جوا اتارنا، بوجھ پابندی یا قابو سے آزاد کرنا، کام کے لیے جوڑے گئے جانوروں یا لوگوں کو جدا کرنا، خدمت یا ظلم سے چھڑانا
englishMeaning: To remove a yoke from animals. To release from a burden, restraint, or control. To separate animals or people that were joined together for work. To free someone from service or oppression.
sindhiMeaning: جانورن تان جوءِ يا جوا هٽائڻ، بار پابندي يا ڪنٽرول کان آزاد ڪرڻ، گڏ ڪم لاءِ ٻڌل جانورن يا ماڻهن کي جدا ڪرڻ، خدمت يا ظلم کان ڇڏائڻ

englishMeaning: To tie or fasten something tightly. To hold things together. To make someone legally or morally obligated. To restrict or limit someone's freedom. A difficult or troublesome situation. The edge or covering that holds pages together.
urduMeaning: مضبوطی سے باندھنا یا جکڑنا، چیزوں کو اکٹھا رکھنا، قانونی یا اخلاقی طور پابند کرنا، آزادی محدود کرنا، مشکل یا پریشان کن حالت، کتاب کے صفحات کو جوڑنے والا کنارہ یا جلد
antonyms: Untie, Release, Free, Loosen, Detach, Separate, Liberate, Unbind, Disconnect, Unfasten
synonyms: Tie, Fasten, Secure, Attach, Join, Bond, Obligate, Restrict, Constrain, Connect
sindhiMeaning: مضبوطي سان ٻڌڻ يا جڪڙڻ، شين کي گڏ رکڻ، قانوني يا اخلاقي طور پابند ڪرڻ، آزادي محدود ڪرڻ، ڏکي يا پريشان ڪندڙ حالت، ڪتاب جا ورق گڏ رکڻ وارو ڪنارو يا جلد
examples: Please bind the papers with a clip. The agreement will bind both companies for five years. Fear can bind people more strongly than rules. He found himself in a bind when both meetings started at once.

englishMeaning: A wooden frame placed over the necks of animals so they can pull together. A device or harness that joins animals for work. A burden, control, or oppressive authority. To join, link, or harness together. To force someone into service or control.
antonyms: Freedom, Liberty, Release, Independence, Unyoke, Detach, Separate, Liberation, Relief
sindhiMeaning: جانورن جي ڳچين تي رکيل ڪاٺي جو فريم، گڏ ڪم لاءِ جانورن کي جوڙڻ وارو اوزار، بار ڪنٽرول يا ظلم واري حڪمراني، گڏ ڪرڻ يا جوتڻ، ڪنهن کي خدمت يا ڪنٽرول ۾ آڻڻ
urduMeaning: جانوروں کی گردنوں پر رکھا جانے والا لکڑی کا فریم، کام کے لیے جانوروں کو جوڑنے والا آلہ، بوجھ قابو یا ظالمانہ حکمرانی، جوڑنا یا جوتنا، کسی کو خدمت یا قابو میں لانا
synonyms: Harness, Collar, Frame, Coupling, Bond, Burden, Oppression, Link, Join, Enslave
examples: The oxen pulled the cart under a heavy yoke. The people struggled to throw off the yoke of tyranny. The farmer yoked two animals before sunrise. The plan would yoke local schools to a national testing system.

antonyms: Free, Liberate, Emancipate, Release, Rescue, Unyoke, Empower, Deliver, Set free
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کي غلام بڻائڻ، آزادي کسي زبردستي ڪم يا فرمانبرداري ڪرائڻ، مڪمل ڪنٽرول ڪرڻ، عادت خواهش نظام يا طاقت جو محتاج بڻائڻ
examples: The invaders tried to enslave the defeated population. Debt can enslave families for generations. No society has the right to enslave another people. Addiction may enslave a person slowly and silently.
urduMeaning: کسی کو غلام بنانا، آزادی چھین کر زبردستی کام یا اطاعت کرانا، مکمل قابو کرنا، عادت خواہش نظام یا طاقت کا محتاج بنانا
englishMeaning: To make someone a slave. To take away a person's freedom and force them to work or obey. To control someone completely. To make someone dependent on a habit, desire, system, or power.
synonyms: Subjugate, Oppress, Dominate, Captivate, Control, Subject, Bond, Tyrannize, Exploit, Imprison
Abandon, Desert, Leave, Renounce, Give up, Quit, Reject, Disown, Relinquish, Betray
urduMeaning: کسی شخص یا چیز کو چھوڑ دینا، شخص جگہ فرض یا عقیدے سے مکمل دستبردار ہونا، عادت عمل یا طریقے کو ترک کرنا، ضرورت کے وقت کسی کو اکیلا چھوڑ دینا
examples: He promised never to forsake his family. She chose to forsake luxury and live simply. Many villagers had to forsake their homes during the flood. A true friend will not forsake you in trouble.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ماڻهو يا شيءِ کي ڇڏي ڏيڻ، شخص جڳهه فرض يا عقيدي کان مڪمل دستبردار ٿيڻ، عادت عمل يا طريقي کي ترڪ ڪرڻ، ضرورت جي وقت ڪنهن کي اڪيلو ڇڏڻ
englishMeaning: To abandon someone or something. To leave a person, place, duty, or belief entirely. To give up or renounce a habit, practice, or way of life. To desert someone in a time of need.
antonyms: Keep, Support, Stay, Retain, Embrace, Adopt, Protect, Maintain, Cherish, Stand by

examples: The boat came alongside the dock. She worked alongside experienced nurses during training. The new policy was introduced alongside other reforms. Place the chart alongside the explanation for clarity.
urduMeaning: برابر یا پہلو میں، کسی کے ساتھ، اسی وقت، تعاون یا موازنہ میں کسی چیز کے ساتھ
synonyms: Beside, Next to, By, Near, Along with, Together with, Adjacent to, Parallel to, With, Beside by side
antonyms: Away from, Apart from, Separate from, Opposite, Distant from, Without, Aside from
englishMeaning: Next to or by the side of someone or something. Together with another person or thing. At the same time as something else. In cooperation or comparison with someone or something.
sindhiMeaning: ڀرسان يا پاسي ۾، ڪنهن سان گڏ، ساڳئي وقت، تعاون يا ڀيٽ ۾ ڪنهن شيءِ سان گڏ

antonyms: Opening, Drainage, Depression, Hollow, Normal tissue, Absence, Flatness
englishMeaning: A closed sac or pouch in the body containing fluid, air, or other material. An abnormal growth under the skin or inside an organ. A protective capsule formed by some parasites or microorganisms. A medically defined swelling that may be harmless or require treatment.
examples: The doctor said the lump was a harmless cyst. A small cyst developed under her skin. Some cysts disappear without surgery. The scan showed a cyst near the kidney.
sindhiMeaning: جسم ۾ پاڻي هوا يا ٻئي مواد سان ڀريل بند ٿيل ٿيلهڙو، چمڙي هيٺ يا عضوي اندر غيرمعمولي واڌ، ڪجهه جراثيم يا پيراسائٽس جو حفاظتي خول، طبي سوڄ جيڪا بي ضرر يا علاج لائق ٿي سگهي
urduMeaning: جسم میں پانی ہوا یا دوسرے مواد سے بھرا بند تھیلا، جلد کے نیچے یا عضو کے اندر غیر معمولی بڑھوتری، بعض جراثیم یا طفیلیوں کا حفاظتی خول، طبی سوجن جو بے ضرر یا علاج طلب ہو سکتی ہے
synonyms: Sac, Pouch, Capsule, Lump, Swelling, Growth, Blister, Vesicle, Nodule, Encapsulation

sindhiMeaning: چمڙي تي پپ سان ڀريل ننڍو اڀريل داڻو، پمپل جهڙي سڙيل سوڄ، انفيڪشن خارش يا سوزش سبب چمڙي جو زخم، ڳاڙهي پيلي گاڙهي رطوبت وارو ننڍو ڦوڪڻو
antonyms: Clear skin, Healthy skin, Smoothness, Healing, Flat skin, Absence of infection
urduMeaning: جلد پر پیپ سے بھرا چھوٹا ابھرا دانہ، پمپل جیسی سوزش والی سوجن، انفیکشن خارش یا سوزش سے جلد کا زخم، گاڑھے زردی مائل مادے والا چھوٹا چھالا
synonyms: Pimple, Boil, Blister, Abscess, Spot, Lesion, Papule, Sore, Blemish, Inflamed bump
examples: A pustule appeared on his chin overnight. The nurse cleaned the pustule carefully. Some skin infections cause clusters of pustules. Do not squeeze a pustule without medical advice.
englishMeaning: A small raised spot on the skin filled with pus. A pimple-like inflamed swelling. A skin lesion caused by infection, irritation, or inflammation. A small blister containing thick yellowish fluid.

antonyms: Expansion, Enlargement, Full version, Extension, Elaboration, Increase, Complete text, Amplification
urduMeaning: کتاب تقریر یا متن کا مختصر نسخہ، اصل مطلب رکھتے ہوئے مختصر کرنے کا عمل، کسی چیز میں کمی یا حد بندی، لمبی تحریر کی خلاصہ شدہ شکل
englishMeaning: A shortened version of a book, speech, or text. The act of making something shorter while keeping the main meaning. A reduction or limitation of something. A condensed form of a longer work.
examples: The teacher assigned an abridgment of the novel. The editor prepared an abridgment for younger readers. Some critics objected to the abridgment of civil rights. This version is an abridgment, not the complete text.
sindhiMeaning: ڪتاب تقرير يا متن جو مختصر نسخو، اصلي مطلب رکندي مختصر ڪرڻ جو عمل، ڪنهن شيءِ ۾ گهٽتائي يا حدبندي، ڊگهي تحرير جو خلاصو روپ
synonyms: Summary, Condensation, Shortening, Abbreviation, Digest, Abstract, Reduction, Epitome, Synopsis, Cut

englishMeaning: To shorten a book, speech, or piece of writing. To reduce something while keeping its main sense. To limit or restrict a right, freedom, or privilege. To condense a longer work into a shorter form.
antonyms: Expand, Extend, Lengthen, Enlarge, Amplify, Elaborate, Increase, Develop, Widen
sindhiMeaning: ڪتاب تقرير يا تحرير کي مختصر ڪرڻ، اصل مطلب رکندي گهٽائڻ، حق آزادي يا رعايت کي محدود ڪرڻ، ڊگهي ڪم کي ننڍي صورت ۾ آڻڻ
examples: The publisher asked the author to abridge the manuscript. Laws should not abridge basic freedoms without strong reasons. The editor abridged the lecture for radio. This edition abridges the original story but keeps the main plot.
synonyms: Shorten, Condense, Reduce, Abbreviate, Summarize, Cut, Compress, Curtail, Truncate, Limit
urduMeaning: کتاب تقریر یا تحریر کو مختصر کرنا، اصل مطلب رکھتے ہوئے کم کرنا، حق آزادی یا رعایت کو محدود کرنا، لمبے کام کو مختصر شکل میں لانا

sindhiMeaning: سوچ احساس يا مطلب جي وڏي گهرائي، گهرو ۽ سنجيده خيال، ذهني بصيرت يا فڪري گهرائي، عميق هجڻ جي خوبي، حقيقي يا علامتي وڏي گهرائي
englishMeaning: Great depth of thought, feeling, or meaning. A deep or serious idea. Intellectual depth or insight. The quality of being profound. Great depth in a physical or figurative sense.
urduMeaning: سوچ احساس یا معنی کی بڑی گہرائی، گہرا اور سنجیدہ خیال، ذہنی بصیرت یا فکری گہرائی، عمیق ہونے کی خوبی، حقیقی یا علامتی بڑی گہرائی
antonyms: Shallowness, Superficiality, Triviality, Simplicity, Lightness, Emptiness, Folly, Insignificance
synonyms: Depth, Insight, Wisdom, Seriousness, Gravity, Deepness, Significance, Thoughtfulness, Sagacity, Meaningfulness
examples: The profundity of her words moved the audience. He did not understand the profundity of the problem at first. The poem has beauty as well as profundity. Scientists were struck by the profundity of the discovery.

The excuse sounded ridiculous to everyone in the room. It is ridiculous to spend so much money on a broken machine. She wore a ridiculous hat to make the children laugh. The rules became ridiculous when nobody could follow them.
urduMeaning: بہت بے وقوفانہ یا غیر معقول، عجیب ہونے کی وجہ سے ہنسی یا مذاق کے قابل، بالکل نامناسب حد سے بڑھا ہوا یا غیر منطقی، سنجیدگی سے لینا مشکل
