examples: She was a true nefelibata, always lost in her poetic dreams. The artist called himself a nefelibata who ignored trends. Only a nefelibata could imagine such a magical world. His writing shows the free spirit of a nefelibata.
synonyms: Dreamer, Visionary, Idealist, Romantic, Free spirit, Nonconformist, Daydreamer
urduMeaning: خوابوں اور خیالوں کی دنیا میں رہنے والا شخص، سماج کے اصولوں سے آزاد، تصور پسند، روایات سے بغاوت کرنے والا، خیالی دنیا کا باسی، بادلوں پر چلنے والا
antonyms: Realist, Pragmatist, Conformist, Materialist, Conventionalist
sindhiMeaning: خوابن ۽ خيالن جي دنيا ۾ رهندڙ ماڻهو، سماج جي قاعدن کان آجو، تصور پرست، رواج کان بغاوت ڪندڙ، خيالي دنيا جو رهاڪو، بادلن تي هلندڙ

urduMeaning: کام بگاڑ دینا، اچھا موقع کھو دینا، غلطی سے ناکام ہو جانا، اچھا موقع ضائع کر دینا، سب کچھ تباہ کر دینا
sindhiMeaning: ڪم خراب ڪري ڇڏڻ، سٺو موقعو وڃائي ڇڏڻ، غلطي سبب ناڪام ٿيڻ، ڪامياب موقعو گم ڪرڻ، سڀ ڪجهه برباد ڪرڻ
examples: Don't blow it, this is your best chance to get the job. He worked hard for months but blew it in the final interview. She was ahead in the race but blew it in the last lap. If you blow it now, you may not get another chance.
synonyms: Fail, Botch, Ruin, Mess up, Bungle, Spoil, Fumble, Waste
englishMeaning: To fail badly at something, especially through carelessness. To lose a good opportunity by making a mistake. To ruin one's chance of success. To perform very poorly when it matters most. To waste something valuable through poor judgment.
antonyms: Succeed, Achieve, Win, Nail it, Excel, Accomplish, Master
Succeed, Triumph, Prosper, Flourish, Thrive, Win
urduMeaning: بری طرح ناکام ہونا، دیکھتے ہی دیکھتے تباہ ہو جانا، اچانک اور واضح طور پر شکست کھا جانا، منصوبہ برباد ہو جانا، عزت خاک میں مل جانا
sindhiMeaning: شديد ناڪامي سان ختم ٿيڻ، ڏسندي ڏسندي تباه ٿي وڃڻ، اوچتو ۽ نمايان طور تي هارائجي وڃڻ، برباد ٿيڻ، عزت خاڪ ۾ ملي وڃڻ
examples: His political career went down in flames after the scandal. The startup went down in flames within a year. Their plans went down in flames due to poor planning. He fought bravely but went down in flames.
englishMeaning: To fail suddenly and dramatically. To end in a spectacular disaster. To be defeated completely and publicly. To collapse in a very visible way. To ruin one's plans or reputation in a dramatic manner.
synonyms: Fail, Collapse, Crash, Crumble, Perish, Flop, Sink, Falter

examples: We argued for hours but got nowhere. Without proper planning, you will get nowhere in life. The negotiations got nowhere after two days. She tried her best but got nowhere with the project.
urduMeaning: کوئی ترقی نہ کرنا، کوشش کے باوجود کچھ حاصل نہ کرنا، مقصد تک نہ پہنچنا، وہیں کا وہیں رہ جانا، کامیاب نہ ہونا
sindhiMeaning: ڪا ترقي نه ڪرڻ، ڪوشش جي باوجود ڪجهه به حاصل نه ڪرڻ، مقصد تائين نه پهچڻ، ساڳي هنڌ رهجي وڃڻ، ڪامياب نه ٿيڻ
synonyms: Fail, Stall, Stagnate, Falter, Flounder, Halt, Struggle
antonyms: Advance, Progress, Succeed, Achieve, Prosper, Move forward
englishMeaning: To make no progress at all. To achieve nothing despite effort. To fail to reach a goal or agreement. To end up in the same situation as before. To have no success in an attempt.

synonyms: Complete, Detailed, Comprehensive, Exhaustive, Careful, Meticulous, Painstaking, Rigorous
examples: The police conducted a thorough investigation of the case. She is a thorough professional in her field. He gave the room a thorough cleaning before guests arrived. Our teacher provided a thorough explanation of the topic.
sindhiMeaning: مڪمل، هر پهلوءَ کان پورو، محتاط، تفصيلي، غور سان ڪم ڪندڙ، مڪمل طور تي، پورو پورو
englishMeaning: Complete with regard to every detail. Careful and accurate in performing a task. Absolute and unmitigated in nature. Painstaking and methodical in approach. Not superficial or partial.
urduMeaning: مکمل، ہر پہلو سے پورا، محتاط، تفصیلی، غور و فکر سے کام کرنے والا، مکمل طور پر، جامع
antonyms: Incomplete, Superficial, Careless, Partial, Cursory, Sloppy, Hasty

synonyms: Demonstration, Sample, Trial, Preview, Example, Presentation, Showing
sindhiMeaning: مظاهرو، ڪنهن شيءِ جي ڪم ڪرڻ جو ڏيکاءُ، نموني وارو ريڪارڊنگ، آزمائشي نسخو، پروڊڪٽ جي وضاحت ڪرڻ، مثال طور ڏيکارڻ
urduMeaning: مظاہرہ، کسی چیز کے کام کرنے کا نمونہ دکھانا، نمونہ ریکارڈنگ، آزمائشی نسخہ، پروڈکٹ کی وضاحت، مثال کے طور پر دکھانا
examples: The salesman gave us a quick demo of the new phone. She recorded a demo to send to record labels. You can try the free demo before buying the software. Let me demo how this machine works.
englishMeaning: A demonstration of how something works or what it can do. A sample recording made to showcase a musician's ability. A trial version of software or a product. A short display of a product's features for promotion. To show or explain how something functions.
antonyms: Actual, Final version, Full product, Concealment
Elite, Aristocracy, Rulers, Nobility, Final versions
urduMeaning: عام لوگ، عوام، قدیم یونانی ریاست کے شہری، متعدد مظاہرے یا نمونے، جمہوریت میں طاقت کا سرچشمہ، عوام الناس
examples: In ancient Athens the demos held real political power. The band released several demos before their first album. The company shared free demos of its new software. True democracy respects the will of the demos.
englishMeaning: The common people of an ancient Greek state. The populace or ordinary citizens as a political unit. More than one demonstration or sample. Plural form of demo, referring to trial versions or samples. The people considered as the source of political power in a democracy.
sindhiMeaning: عام ماڻهو، عوام، قديم يوناني رياست جا شهري، ڪيترائي مظاهرا يا نمونا، جمهوريت جو بنيادي عنصر، عوام الناس
synonyms: People, Populace, Citizens, Public, Masses, Community, Samples, Trials

urduMeaning: لمبا اور واقعات سے بھرپور سفر، مہم جوئی سے بھرا سفر، روحانی یا فکری تلاش، ہومر کی مشہور یونانی رزمیہ نظم، طویل مہماتی سفر
synonyms: Journey, Voyage, Adventure, Expedition, Quest, Trek, Pilgrimage, Wandering
examples: His life has been an odyssey of struggles and triumphs. The book describes an odyssey across seven countries. Their space mission was a real odyssey. Writing this novel was an emotional odyssey for her.
sindhiMeaning: ڊگهو ۽ واقعن سان ڀريل سفر، ڪيترن مهم جوئين وارو سفر، روحاني يا فڪري ڊگهي کوجنا، هومر جو مشهور يوناني رزميه، سفرِ زندگي
antonyms: Stagnation, Rest, Halt, Standstill, Idleness
englishMeaning: A long and eventful journey or experience. A series of wanderings or adventures. A lengthy adventurous voyage. A long spiritual or intellectual quest. A great Greek epic poem by Homer describing such a journey.

urduMeaning: مہم، کسی خاص مقصد کے لیے کیا جانے والا سفر، تحقیق یا دریافت کا سفر، تیزی سے کام کرنا، مہم پر جانے والا گروہ، فوجی مہم
examples: They joined an expedition to the North Pole. The scientific expedition discovered a new species. He led an expedition into the deep jungle. The mail was delivered with great expedition.
synonyms: Journey, Voyage, Trip, Mission, Quest, Trek, Exploration, Tour, Speed
sindhiMeaning: مهم، ڪنهن خاص مقصد لاءِ ڪيل سفر، تحقيق يا کوجنا وارو سفر، تڪڙ سان ڪم ڪرڻ، مهم تي ويندڙ ٽولو، فوجي مهم
englishMeaning: A journey undertaken by a group of people with a particular purpose, especially exploration. A short trip made for a specific reason. Promptness or speed in doing something. The group of people making such a journey. A military mission sent to a distant place.
antonyms: Delay, Stagnation, Rest, Halt, Sluggishness

englishMeaning: A journey to a sacred place for religious reasons. A trip made to a place that is special or important to someone. A long journey involving a search for meaning or moral significance. A visit to a holy site as an act of devotion. Any journey undertaken for a deeply personal reason.
urduMeaning: زیارت، مذہبی مقصد کے لیے مقدس مقام کا سفر، حج، روحانی مقصد سے کیا جانے والا سفر، کسی بامعنی مقصد کے لیے طویل سفر، عبادت کی نیت سے سفر
antonyms: Stay, Rest, Halt, Idleness, Homecoming
sindhiMeaning: زيارت، مذهبي مقصد لاءِ مقدس هنڌ جو سفر، حج، روحاني مقصد سان ڪيل سفر، ڪنهن معنيٰ ڀرئي مقصد لاءِ ڊگهو سفر، عبادت جي نيت سان يڪر رخي سفر
examples: Every year millions of Muslims go on pilgrimage to Mecca. She made a pilgrimage to her grandfather's birthplace. The old church is a popular place of pilgrimage. Their trip felt like a spiritual pilgrimage.
synonyms: Journey, Voyage, Trip, Expedition, Quest, Visitation, Hajj, Tour

antonyms: Stay, Rest, Settlement, Halt, Idleness
urduMeaning: سفر کرنا، خاص طور پر پیدل سفر، عام سفر، ایک جگہ سے دوسری جگہ جانا، راستے پر چلنے کا عمل، مسافرت
englishMeaning: The act of traveling, especially on foot. A journey or trip made by an ordinary traveler. Passage from one place to another. The experience or process of traveling along a road. Movement across a distance as part of a journey.
examples: His life of wayfare took him across many lands. The old man spoke of his years of wayfare with joy. Wayfare in ancient times was full of dangers. She loved the simple joy of wayfare on country roads.
synonyms: Travel, Journey, Voyage, Trip, Passage, Trek, Roaming
sindhiMeaning: سفر ڪرڻ، خاص ڪري پيدل سفر، عام سفر، هڪ هنڌ کان ٻئي هنڌ وڃڻ، رستي تي هلڻ جو عمل، مسافري

examples: An old wayfarer stopped at the inn to rest for the night. The wayfarer walked with a small bag on his back. Many wayfarers cross this mountain pass every year. She felt like a lonely wayfarer in a strange city.
synonyms: Traveler, Wanderer, Pilgrim, Roamer, Voyager, Trekker, Nomad, Rover
sindhiMeaning: مسافر، پيدل سفر ڪندڙ، گهمندڙ، اڻ ڄاڻ رستن جو مسافر، سفر ڪندڙ شخص، پيرين پنڌ ويندڙ
antonyms: Resident, Settler, Local, Native, Homebody
urduMeaning: مسافر، پیدل سفر کرنے والا، گھومنے پھرنے والا، اجنبی راستوں کا مسافر، سفر کرنے والا شخص، راہ گیر
englishMeaning: A person who travels, especially on foot. A traveler or wanderer. Someone who is on a journey through unfamiliar places. A pilgrim or roamer moving from place to place. A person who spends much of their life traveling.

synonyms: Trip, Voyage, Expedition, Trek, Tour, Passage, Excursion, Odyssey
examples: They set out on a long journey across the country. Life is a journey full of ups and downs. Her journey to success was inspiring. The journey by train takes about six hours.
englishMeaning: An act of traveling from one place to another. A long and often difficult process of personal change and development. The distance covered or time taken in traveling. A trip made for a particular purpose. The passage or progress from one stage to another.
sindhiMeaning: سفر، هڪ هنڌ کان ٻئي هنڌ وڃڻ، زندگيءَ جو ڊگهو تجربو، ذاتي ترقيءَ جو عمل، سفر جو فاصلو يا وقت، مسافري
urduMeaning: سفر، ایک جگہ سے دوسری جگہ جانا، زندگی کا لمبا تجربہ، ذاتی ترقی کا سفر، سفر کا فاصلہ یا وقت، مسافت
antonyms: Stay, Rest, Halt, Arrival, Settlement

synonyms: Hike, Journey, Expedition, March, Walk, Trip, Voyage, Trudge
englishMeaning: A long and difficult journey, especially on foot. A journey involving hardship or adventure. To travel slowly and with effort over a difficult terrain. A migration of people or animals over a long distance. A hike undertaken for recreation or exploration.
examples: They made a long trek through the Himalayas. The daily trek to school was tiring for the children. Our trek across the desert took two weeks. We plan to trek up the mountain next summer.
urduMeaning: لمبا اور مشکل سفر، خاص طور پر پیدل، محنت سے کیا گیا سفر، پہاڑوں پر پیدل چلنا، مہم جوئی سفر، لوگوں یا جانوروں کی ہجرت
sindhiMeaning: ڊگهو ۽ ڏکيو سفر، خاص ڪري پيدل، محنت سان ڪيل سفر، پهاڙي علائقن ۾ گهمڻ، مهم جوئي وارو سفر، ماڻهن يا جانورن جي هجرت
antonyms: Rest, Stay, Halt, Idleness, Standstill
Deviation, Detour, Obstruction, Standstill
englishMeaning: A way or course taken to get from one place to another. A regular line of travel or delivery. A method or means of achieving something. The path chosen for a journey. To send or direct along a particular course.
urduMeaning: راستہ، ایک جگہ سے دوسری جگہ جانے کا طریقہ، کسی مقصد کے لیے اختیار کیا گیا طریقہ، مقررہ راستہ، کسی چیز کو مخصوص راستے پر بھیجنا
examples: We took the shortest route to the airport. The bus follows the same route every day. Hard work is the surest route to success. Please route the package through Karachi.
sindhiMeaning: رستو، هڪ هنڌ کان ٻئي هنڌ وڃڻ جو طريقو، ڪنهن مقصد لاءِ اختيار ڪيل طريقو، مقرر رستو، ڪنهن شيءِ کي مقرر رستي تي موڪلڻ
synonyms: Path, Way, Course, Road, Track, Passage, Direction, Line

sindhiMeaning: گاڏيءَ ۾ لڳل اهو اوزار جيڪو طي ڪيل مفاصلو ماپي، ميل ماپيندڙ، فاصلو ٻڌائيندڙ آلو، سفر جو فاصلو ريڪارڊ ڪندڙ
englishMeaning: An instrument for measuring the distance traveled by a vehicle. A device that records the total mileage of a car. A mechanical or digital tool showing distance covered. A gauge fitted in vehicles to track journey length. Any instrument for measuring distance in motion.
antonyms: Speedometer (measures speed, not distance)
synonyms: Mileometer, Distance meter, Gauge, Meter, Measuring device
urduMeaning: گاڑی میں لگا وہ آلہ جو طے کیا گیا فاصلہ ناپتا ہے، میل شمار کرنے والا آلہ، فاصلہ بتانے والا میٹر، سفر کا فاصلہ ریکارڈ کرنے والا
examples: The odometer showed that the car had done 80,000 miles. He checked the odometer before selling the car. A faulty odometer can hide a vehicle's true mileage. The mechanic reset the odometer during repairs.

englishMeaning: The place to which someone or something is going or being sent. The end point of a journey. The purpose for which something is intended. A popular place that people travel to. The ultimate goal or aim of an action.
urduMeaning: منزل، وہ جگہ جہاں کوئی جا رہا ہو یا بھیجا جا رہا ہو، سفر کا آخری مقام، مقصد، مشہور سیاحتی مقام، آخری ہدف
antonyms: Origin, Start, Source, Departure point, Beginning
synonyms: Goal, Target, End, Terminus, Aim, Objective, Stop, Endpoint
sindhiMeaning: منزل، اهو هنڌ جتي ڪو ماڻهو يا شيءِ وڃي رهي هجي، سفر جو آخري هنڌ، مقصد، مشهور گهمڻ جو هنڌ، آخري نشانو
examples: Our final destination was a small village in the mountains. Dubai is a popular tourist destination. The package reached its destination on time. Hard work will take you to your destination in life.
His sudden departure surprised the whole family. The train departure is scheduled at 6 AM. Her new film is a departure from her usual style. They watched the departure of the ship from the harbor.
synonyms: Leaving, Exit, Start, Farewell, Withdrawal, Deviation, Divergence
antonyms: Arrival, Return, Coming, Entry, Homecoming
englishMeaning: The act of leaving a place, especially to start a journey. A deviation from an accepted or usual course. The action of leaving a job or position. The starting point of a train, bus, or flight. A new or different way of doing something.
sindhiMeaning: روانگي، ڪنهن هنڌ ڇڏي وڃڻ، سفر جي شروعات، عام روش کان هٽڻ، نوڪري ڇڏڻ، نئون طريقو اختيار ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: روانگی، کسی جگہ سے چلے جانا، سفر کا آغاز، عام روش سے ہٹنا، نوکری چھوڑنا، نیا طریقہ اختیار کرنا

antonyms: Departure, Leaving, Exit, Withdrawal, Absence
sindhiMeaning: پهچڻ، ڪنهن هنڌ اچڻ جو عمل، تازو آيل ماڻهو يا شيءِ، ڪنهن نئين شيءِ جو منظر عام تي اچڻ، منزل تي پهچڻ، نتيجي تي پهچڻ
englishMeaning: The act of coming to or reaching a place. A person or thing that has come or been brought to a place. The moment when someone or something begins to exist or be used. The appearance of something new in a particular field. The reaching of a conclusion or decision.
urduMeaning: آمد، کسی جگہ پہنچنے کا عمل، نیا آنے والا شخص یا چیز، کسی نئی چیز کا وجود میں آنا، منزل پر پہنچنا، کسی نتیجے پر پہنچنا
examples: We are waiting for the arrival of the train. Her arrival brought great joy to the family. The arrival of the internet changed our lives. A new arrival in the neighborhood was warmly welcomed.
synonyms: Coming, Entrance, Appearance, Approach, Advent, Landing, Reaching

sindhiMeaning: ڀڻ ڀڻ، مکين يا مشين جو مسلسل هلڪو آواز، جوش يا ولولو، اڏامندڙ خبر، ڀڻڪو، بجليءَ جي گهنٽيءَ سان سڏڻ
synonyms: Hum, Murmur, Drone, Rumor, Excitement, Whisper, Ring
examples: There was a loud buzz of bees near the flowers. A buzz of excitement filled the stadium. There is a buzz that the company will launch a new product. Please buzz me when the guest arrives.
englishMeaning: A low, continuous humming sound made by insects or machines. A feeling of excitement, energy, or pleasant intoxication. A rumor or piece of news that is spreading quickly. To make a low humming sound. To call someone using a buzzer or intercom.
antonyms: Silence, Quiet, Calm, Stillness, Hush
urduMeaning: بھنبھناہٹ، مکھیوں یا مشین کی مسلسل ہلکی آواز، جوش و خروش، اڑتی ہوئی خبر، سرگوشی، بجلی کی گھنٹی سے بلانا

antonyms: Silent, Quiet, Still, Calm, Dull, Lifeless, Boring, Inactive, Peaceful, Motionless
urduMeaning: مکھی کی طرح گنگناہٹ کی آواز نکالنے والا، سرگرمی اور چہل پہل سے بھرپور، جوش و خروش سے معمور، تیزی سے پھیلنے والی افواہیں یا باتیں، ہلکے نشے کی کیفیت میں، سنسناہٹ یا لہر محسوس کرنا
sindhiMeaning: ماکيءَ جي مکين وانگر گنگناهٽ جو آواز ڪندڙ، سرگرم ۽ چهل پهل سان ڀريل، جوش ۽ خوشيءَ سان ڀرپور، تيزيءَ سان پکڙيل ڳالهيون يا افواهون، ٿورو نشي واري حالت ۾، ٿرٿراهٽ يا لهرن جو محسوس ٿيڻ
synonyms: Humming, Droning, Whirring, Murmuring, Vibrating, Bustling, Lively, Active, Thriving, Exciting, Thrilling
examples: The bees were buzzing around the garden all afternoon. The city was buzzing with excitement before the festival. She felt her phone buzzing in her pocket. The office was buzzing with rumors about the new manager.
englishMeaning: Making a low, continuous humming or vibrating sound like that of a bee. Filled with lively activity, excitement, or energy. Feeling a sense of thrill, excitement, or pleasant tingling. Spreading quickly through talk, rumor, or gossip. Slightly intoxicated or lightheaded.

Dishonest, deceitful, or unprincipled behavior. A trick or act performed by a dishonest person. Cunning or roguish conduct intended to cheat others. The quality of being a knave or scoundrel. Mischievous or fraudulent dealings.
urduMeaning: بے ایمانی اور دھوکہ دہی کا عمل، فریب یا چال بازی، ٹھگی اور مکاری، بدمعاشی و شرارت، دغا بازی پر مبنی حرکت
antonyms: Honesty, Integrity, Sincerity, Truthfulness, Uprightness, Fairness, Virtue, Trustworthiness, Loyalty
synonyms: Dishonesty, Trickery, Deceit, Fraud, Roguery, Mischief, Cheating, Villainy, Chicanery, Duplicity
examples: His knavery was finally exposed when the documents were reviewed. The old story warns readers against the knavery of dishonest merchants. She could not tolerate the knavery of her business partner. Such knavery has no place in a fair society.
sindhiMeaning: بي ايماني ۽ فريب واري ڪار، ٺڳيءَ جو ڪم يا چال، دوکو ڏيڻ جي عادت، بدمعاشي ۽ چالاڪي، بدنيتيءَ سان ڪيل ڪم

englishMeaning: In spite of the fact that; although. Used to introduce a contrast or unexpected element. However; nevertheless. Even if; whether or not. Used to soften a statement or add a qualifying remark.

englishMeaning: To surprise someone greatly. To astonish or amaze a person so much that they are speechless. To shock or overwhelm with something unexpected. To leave someone stunned and unable to react.
synonyms: Astonish, Amaze, Astound, Stun, Shock, Stagger, Dumbfound, Bewilder, Surprise
urduMeaning: سخت حیران کر دینا، ششدر کر دینا، ایسا چونکا دینا کہ بولنے کے قابل نہ رہے، دنگ کر دینا
sindhiMeaning: ڏاڍو حيران ڪري ڇڏڻ، اچرج ۾ وجهي ڇڏڻ، اهڙو صدمو ڏيڻ جو ماڻهو ڳالهائي نه سگهي، ششدر ڪري ڇڏڻ
examples: The news of his sudden promotion will flabbergast everyone. Her sharp reply flabbergasted the entire audience. The magician's trick flabbergasted the children. The final result flabbergasted the whole team.

sindhiMeaning: سخت حيران، اچرج ۾ پيل، ڳالهائڻ کان قاصر ٿي ويل، ششدر ٿيل
examples: I was flabbergasted when I saw my old friend after twenty years. She looked flabbergasted at the surprise party. He was flabbergasted by the amount of the electricity bill. The teacher was flabbergasted by the student's rude reply.
urduMeaning: سخت حیران، ششدر، دنگ رہ گیا، بولنے سے قاصر، حیرت زدہ
englishMeaning: Extremely surprised or shocked. Stunned into silence by something unexpected. Amazed and unable to think clearly. Overwhelmed with astonishment.
synonyms: Astonished, Amazed, Stunned, Shocked, Astounded, Speechless, Dumbfounded, Bewildered
antonyms: Unimpressed, Calm, Composed, Indifferent, Unmoved, Unsurprised

sindhiMeaning: لوهه جو ڪم ڪندڙ ڪاريگر، لوهار، اهو ماڻهو جيڪو لوهه کي گرم ڪري اوزار يا نعل ٺاهي، بھٽيءَ ۾ لوهه ڪٽي شيون ٺاهيندڙ ڪاريگر
synonyms: Ironsmith, Ironworker, Forger, Smith, Metalworker, Farrier
antonyms: Customer, Client, Unskilled worker
examples: The village blacksmith made horseshoes for the farmers. My grandfather worked as a blacksmith all his life. The blacksmith heated the iron rod until it turned red. A skilled blacksmith can shape almost anything from iron.
englishMeaning: A person whose work is making and repairing things from iron by heating and hammering the metal. A craftsman who forges tools, horseshoes, gates, and other iron objects. A skilled worker who shapes hot metal on an anvil. An artisan working with iron in a forge.
urduMeaning: لوہار، لوہے کا کام کرنے والا کاریگر، وہ شخص جو لوہے کو گرم کر کے اوزار یا نعل بناتا ہے، بھٹی پر لوہے کی چیزیں بنانے والا ہنر مند
عجیب و غریب، مسخرہ پن والا، بھولا بھالا اور احمقانہ، مذاقیہ انداز والا، غیر سنجیدہ اور کھلنڈرا
sindhiMeaning: عجيب، مسخريءَ وارو، بيوقوفيءَ وارو پر پيارو، مذاقيه انداز وارو، سنجيده نه هجڻ وارو
examples: He made a goofy face to make the baby laugh. She wore a goofy hat to the party. My little brother has a goofy sense of humor. Stop being so goofy and finish your homework.
antonyms: Serious, Sensible, Sober, Wise, Solemn, Grave, Mature
englishMeaning: Silly, foolish, or slightly ridiculous in a harmless way. Behaving in a funny or awkward manner. Having a strange or amusing appearance. Not serious; playful and lighthearted.
synonyms: Silly, Foolish, Zany, Wacky, Daffy, Loony, Absurd, Ridiculous, Comical

examples: He felt unworthy of such a great honor. Such behavior is unworthy of a leader. She thought herself unworthy of his love. His actions were unworthy of a man of his position.
englishMeaning: Not deserving respect, attention, or praise. Not good enough for a particular purpose, position, or person. Lacking the qualities needed to be worthy. Behaving in a way that is beneath one's standards or dignity.
antonyms: Worthy, Deserving, Fit, Suitable, Qualified, Honorable, Meritorious, Respectable
sindhiMeaning: لائق نه هجڻ، نااهل، عزت جي قابل نه، ڪنهن ڪم يا مقام لاءِ موزون نه، پنهنجي مرتبي جي خلاف عمل ڪندڙ
urduMeaning: نااہل، لائق نہ ہونا، عزت یا توجہ کے قابل نہیں، کسی مقام یا کام کے قابل نہ، اپنے مرتبے کے خلاف رویہ رکھنے والا
synonyms: Undeserving, Unfit, Inadequate, Unsuitable, Inferior, Unqualified, Disgraceful, Dishonorable

sindhiMeaning: لائق، ڪنهن شيءِ جي قابل، عزت جي لائق، ڪنهن ڪم لاءِ موزون، وڏي مرتبي وارو شخص
examples: He is a worthy candidate for the leadership role. This cause is worthy of our full support. She proved herself a worthy opponent in the debate. The village elders are considered worthies of the community.
antonyms: Unworthy, Undeserving, Unfit, Dishonorable, Disgraceful, Inferior, Unsuitable
englishMeaning: Deserving respect, attention, or admiration. Having qualities that make someone or something good enough for a particular purpose. Suitable for a specified role, action, or reward. A person of great merit or importance.
urduMeaning: لائق، قابل، عزت و احترام کے قابل، کسی کام کے قابل، معتبر شخص، اہل
synonyms: Deserving, Meritorious, Honorable, Admirable, Respectable, Commendable, Praiseworthy, Suitable
Scribble, Sketch, Scrawl, Draw, Scrabble, Squiggle
sindhiMeaning: بغير ڌيان جي ڪا لڪير يا شڪل ٺاهڻ، وقت وڃائيندي هلندي ڪجهه ڊرا ڪرڻ، لاپرواهيءَ سان ٺاهيل خاڪو، وقت وڃائڻ، شوق طور سادي شڪل ٺاهڻ
antonyms: Concentrate, Focus, Pay attention, Work seriously
urduMeaning: بغیر توجہ کے کچھ لکیریں یا شکلیں بنانا، لاپرواہی سے بنایا گیا خاکہ، وقت گزاری کے لیے کچھ بنانا، شوقیہ سادہ خاکہ، بلا سوچے سمجھے تصویر بنانا
examples: He often doodles in the margins of his notebook during meetings. Her page was covered with tiny doodles of flowers and stars. Stop doodling and pay attention to the lecture. The child made a colorful doodle on the wall.
englishMeaning: To draw simple pictures or patterns absent-mindedly, especially while thinking about something else. A rough drawing or scribble made without much attention. To waste time doing nothing in particular. A simple sketch made for fun rather than seriously.

sindhiMeaning: مٺائيون ٺاهيندڙ يا وڪڻندڙ ماڻهو، حلوائي، ڪيڪ ۽ چاڪليٽ ٺاهيندڙ ڪاريگر، مٺائيءَ جي دڪاندار، شيرين شيون ٺاهيندڙ فنڪار
antonyms: Consumer, Customer, Buyer
englishMeaning: A person or business that makes or sells sweets, chocolates, and other sugar-based products. A skilled maker of cakes, pastries, and candies. A shopkeeper whose main goods are sweets and confectionery. An artisan specializing in fancy sugar work and desserts.
synonyms: Sweet maker, Candy maker, Pastry chef, Chocolatier, Baker, Sweetmeat seller
examples: The confectioner prepared a beautiful wedding cake. We bought a box of chocolates from the local confectioner. She learned the art of baking from a French confectioner. The confectioner's shop is famous for its handmade sweets.
urduMeaning: مٹھائی بنانے یا بیچنے والا، حلوائی، کیک اور چاکلیٹ بنانے والا ماہر، مٹھائی کی دکان کا مالک، قندی اشیاء بنانے والا کاریگر

antonyms: Shoe wearer, Customer
synonyms: Shoemaker, Bootmaker, Shoe repairer, Leatherworker, Mender
sindhiMeaning: موچي، بوٽ ٺاهيندڙ يا مرمت ڪندڙ ماڻهو، چمڙي جو ڪاريگر، آمريڪا ۾ ميوي سان ٺهيل هڪ قسم جو ميٺاڻو، اٻاڻڪو ڪاريگر
examples: The cobbler repaired my old shoes for a very small fee. My grandfather was a skilled cobbler in his village. She made a delicious peach cobbler for dessert. The cobbler sat outside the shop with his tools.
englishMeaning: A person whose job is to mend or make shoes. A shoemaker who works with leather and simple tools. A deep-dish fruit dessert with a thick crust, popular in America. A clumsy or unskilled worker (informal, older use).
urduMeaning: موچی، جوتے بنانے یا مرمت کرنے والا، چمڑے کا کاریگر، پھلوں سے بنی ایک قسم کی امریکی مٹھائی، اناڑی کاریگر
کباڑی، پرانے لوہے اور کباڑ کا تاجر، وہ شخص جو ضائع شدہ یا پرانی اشیاء خرید کر بیچتا ہے، ری سائیکلنگ کے کاروبار کا درمیانی تاجر، استعمال شدہ سامان کا سوداگر
englishMeaning: A person or business that buys and sells scrap metal, old materials, or discarded items. A trader who collects, sorts, and resells waste metal, paper, or plastic. A middleman in the recycling and salvage trade. A merchant dealing in used or broken goods.
antonyms: Manufacturer, Producer, Wholesaler of new goods, Retailer
synonyms: Junk dealer, Junkman, Salvage merchant, Rag-and-bone man, Recycler, Waste trader
examples: The scrap dealer bought all the old iron from our workshop. He earns his living as a scrap dealer in the city. A scrap dealer came to the neighborhood collecting newspapers. The scrap dealer weighed the metal before paying us.
sindhiMeaning: ڪباڙي، پراڻي لوهه ۽ ڪباڙ جو واپاري، اهو شخص جيڪو گهٽ قيمت ۾ پراڻيون شيون خريد ڪري وڪڻي، ريسائيڪلنگ جي واپار ۾ وچولو، ٽٽل ۽ استعمال ٿيل شين جو تاجر
سونارو، سون جو ڪم ڪندڙ ڪاريگر، سون جا زيور ٺاهيندڙ ۽ مرمت ڪندڙ، قيمتي ڌاتن جو فنڪار، زيور ساز
synonyms: Jeweler, Ornament maker, Metalsmith, Artisan, Silversmith (related)
urduMeaning: سنار، سونے کا کام کرنے والا کاریگر، سونے کے زیورات بنانے اور مرمت کرنے والا، قیمتی دھاتوں کا ماہر کاریگر، زیور ساز
antonyms: Customer, Buyer, Consumer
examples: The goldsmith crafted a beautiful necklace for the bride. She took her old bangles to the goldsmith to be redesigned. The goldsmith weighed the gold carefully before starting the work. His family has been working as goldsmiths for generations.
englishMeaning: A person who makes objects and jewelry from gold and other precious metals. A skilled craftsman who designs, shapes, and repairs gold ornaments. An artisan who works with fine metals to create decorative or valuable items. A jeweler specializing in gold work.

sindhiMeaning: موسيقيءَ جي هڪ خاص طرز جتي هڪ ئي ڌن ڪيترن حصن ۾ ورجائجي ٿي، ذهني حالت جنهن ۾ ماڻهو پنهنجي سڃاڻپ وساري ڀڄي وڃي، عارضي ذهني الجهاءُ يا خواب جهڙي ڪيفيت، مختلف شين جو پيچيده ميلاپ
examples: Bach is famous for his beautiful fugues. The patient suffered a fugue and could not remember his own name. She composed a fugue for the piano and violin. He wandered for two days in a state of fugue before he was found.
antonyms: Awareness, Consciousness, Clarity, Simplicity
englishMeaning: A musical composition in which one or more themes are introduced by one part and then repeated and developed by others in complex patterns. A state of mind in which a person temporarily loses their sense of identity and memory, often wandering away from home. A period of confused or dreamlike behavior. Any complicated interweaving of different elements.
synonyms: Composition, Musical piece, Trance, Amnesia, Blackout, Dissociation, Reverie
urduMeaning: موسیقی کی ایک پیچیدہ ترتیب جس میں ایک ہی دھن مختلف حصوں میں دہرائی جاتی ہے، ذہنی حالت جس میں شخص اپنی شناخت اور یادداشت کھو دیتا ہے اور بھٹکنے لگتا ہے، عارضی ذہنی الجھاؤ یا خواب جیسی کیفیت، پیچیدہ ملاپ

englishMeaning: Feeling sure about one's own abilities, decisions, or qualities. Certain that something will happen or be the case. Showing self-assurance in behavior or speech. Trusting firmly in someone or something.
examples: She is confident that she will pass the exam. He gave a confident speech in front of the audience. I am confident in your ability to handle this project. The team looks confident before the final match.
sindhiMeaning: پُر يقين، پنهنجي صلاحيتن تي ڀروسو رکندڙ، پڪ رکندڙ، خود اعتماد، ٻئي تي ڀروسو رکندڙ
synonyms: Self-assured, Sure, Certain, Positive, Assured, Optimistic, Bold, Poised
antonyms: Unsure, Doubtful, Uncertain, Nervous, Shy, Hesitant, Insecure, Timid
urduMeaning: پُراعتماد، اپنی صلاحیتوں پر بھروسا رکھنے والا، یقین رکھنے والا، خود اعتماد، کسی بات پر پکا یقین رکھنے والا
رازدار، وہ دوست جس سے راز کی باتیں کہی جائیں، قریبی اور قابل اعتماد ساتھی، ذاتی جذبات بانٹنے کے لیے قابل بھروسا شخص، معتبر مشیر
examples: She is my closest friend and my only confidant. He needed a confidant to share his worries. The queen chose her old nurse as her confidant. Every leader needs a loyal confidant beside him.
sindhiMeaning: رازدار دوست، اهو ماڻهو جنهن کي پنهنجا راز ٻڌائجن، ويجهو ۽ ڀروسي وارو ساٿي، ذاتي جذبا ونڊڻ لاءِ ڀروسو رکيل شخص، معتبر مشير
englishMeaning: A person to whom secrets or private matters are told. A close friend one can trust completely. Someone in whom one confides personal thoughts and feelings. A trusted companion or advisor.
synonyms: Close friend, Trusted friend, Intimate, Companion, Confidante, Advisor, Bosom friend
antonyms: Stranger, Enemy, Rival, Foe, Adversary, Acquaintance

sindhiMeaning: اعتماد، پاڻ تي ڀروسو، ڪنهن شيءِ يا شخص تي يقين، رازداري وارو ڀروسو، خفيه ڳالهه
englishMeaning: The feeling of trust in one's own abilities, qualities, or judgment. A firm belief that something will happen as expected. Trust placed in another person. Information told in secret.
examples: She spoke with great confidence during the interview. I have full confidence in his honesty. He told me the news in confidence. Winning the match gave the players new confidence.
urduMeaning: اعتماد، اپنے آپ پر بھروسا، کسی بات یا شخص پر یقین، رازداری، خفیہ بات
antonyms: Doubt, Distrust, Uncertainty, Insecurity, Shyness, Fear, Suspicion
synonyms: Self-assurance, Trust, Faith, Belief, Certainty, Poise, Assurance, Reliance

examples: This report is strictly confidential and must not be shared. She spoke in a confidential tone. The two friends had a confidential conversation in the corner. All medical records are kept confidential.
sindhiMeaning: رازدارانه، ڳجهه ۾ رکڻ جوڳو، صرف چند ماڻهن سان ونڊڻ لاءِ، ذاتي ۽ ڳجهي معلومات وارو، خانگي معاملن سان لاڳاپيل
antonyms: Public, Open, Known, Disclosed, Published, Common, Unrestricted
englishMeaning: Intended to be kept secret and shared with only a few people. Entrusted with private information. Spoken or written in a private, trusting manner. Relating to matters that must not be disclosed publicly.
urduMeaning: خفیہ، رازدارانہ، صرف چند لوگوں تک محدود، نجی معلومات پر مبنی، عوام کے سامنے نہ لانے کے لائق
synonyms: Secret, Private, Classified, Restricted, Hush-hush, Personal, Undisclosed
Assign, Commit, Consign, Delegate, Charge, Confide, Hand over, Trust
antonyms: Withhold, Withdraw, Distrust, Deny, Retain, Take back, Doubt
sindhiMeaning: ڀروسي سان ڪنهن کي ڪا ذميواري سونپڻ، اعتماد ڪري ڪم يا شيءِ حوالي ڪرڻ، اهم ڪم ڪنهن جي حوالي ڪرڻ، ڪنهن کي پنهنجي شيءِ يا فرض جي سنڀال ڏيڻ
englishMeaning: To give someone the responsibility of doing something or taking care of something. To place trust in a person by handing over an important task or item. To assign a duty to someone with confidence. To commit something to another's care.
examples: They entrusted the project to the most experienced engineer. She entrusted her savings to her elder brother. The family entrusted the child to a kind nanny. He was entrusted with the safety of the entire team.
urduMeaning: کسی کو کوئی ذمہ داری سونپنا، اعتماد کے ساتھ کوئی کام یا چیز حوالے کرنا، بھروسے پر اہم کام دینا، کسی کی نگہداشت میں کچھ دینا

synonyms: Genius, Wonder, Wunderkind, Talent, Marvel, Sensation, Whiz, Phenomenon
sindhiMeaning: غير معمولي ذهانت وارو ٻار، ننڍي عمر ۾ عظيم ڪاريگريءَ وارو، غير معمولي صلاحيت رکندڙ شخص، ڪا حيرت انگيز شيءِ، ڪا مثالي مثال
antonyms: Dunce, Amateur, Beginner, Fool, Underachiever, Mediocrity
examples: Mozart was a musical prodigy who composed his first piece at the age of five. The young chess prodigy defeated several grandmasters. She is considered a prodigy in mathematics. The invention was regarded as a prodigy of modern science.
urduMeaning: غیر معمولی ذہانت والا بچہ، کم عمری میں غیر معمولی صلاحیت رکھنے والا، حیرت انگیز فرد، انوکھی چیز، کسی خوبی کی نمایاں مثال
englishMeaning: A young person with exceptional abilities or talents. A person who is very unusually skilled or intelligent. A remarkable or amazing thing. An extraordinary example of a quality.

antonyms: Boring information, Dull fact, Trivial detail, Uninteresting news
synonyms: Gossip, Scandal, Tidbit, Titillating fact, Rumor, Inside story, Scoop
englishMeaning: An interesting, exciting, or scandalous piece of information, often about someone's private life. A rich or entertaining bit of gossip. A colorful and vivid part of a story. An eagerly awaited piece of news.
sindhiMeaning: مزيدار يا دلچسپ ڳجهي خبر، ڪنهن جي ذاتي زندگيءَ بابت چٽيل معلومات، شوق سان ٻڌي سگهجندڙ ڳالهه، دلچسپ افواهه، رنگين ۽ زنده باب
urduMeaning: دلچسپ اور چٹپٹی خبر، کسی کی نجی زندگی کے بارے میں مزیدار معلومات، شوق سے سننے والی بات، رنگین اور جاندار حصہ، اہم افواہ
examples: She loves to share the juicy details of every wedding she attends. The reporter uncovered some juicy details about the scandal. Don't leave out the juicy details of your trip. Everyone was waiting to hear the juicy details of the meeting.

urduMeaning: جو حق کسی سے چھینا نہ جا سکے، ناقابل انتقال، پیدائشی حق، فرد سے علیحدہ نہ ہو سکنے والا، دائمی اور مستقل
sindhiMeaning: جيڪو حق کسي نه سگهجي، جيڪو منتقل يا ختم نه ٿي سگهي، پيدائشي حق، ماڻهوءَ کان جدا نه ٿيندڙ، دائمي ۽ مضبوط
examples: Freedom of speech is an inalienable right. The constitution protects the inalienable rights of citizens. Life and liberty are considered inalienable. These rights are inalienable and cannot be surrendered.
antonyms: Alienable, Transferable, Removable, Conditional, Negotiable, Revocable
englishMeaning: Unable to be taken away from or given up by the person who has them. Belonging to someone by right and impossible to transfer or remove. Absolute and permanent, especially regarding rights. Impossible to separate from a person or thing.
synonyms: Absolute, Nontransferable, Inviolable, Sacred, Basic, Unassailable, Fundamental

urduMeaning: جانبدارانہ، ایک مخصوص رائے یا نظریے کی حمایت کرنے والا، غیر جانبدار نہ، کسی نظریے کو ابھارنے والا، متعصبانہ
englishMeaning: Expressing or promoting a particular opinion, cause, or point of view, especially in a biased way. Not neutral or objective; deliberately favoring one side. Written or spoken in a manner intended to persuade rather than inform. Marked by a strong intentional bias.
examples: The article was tendentious and lacked balanced reporting. His speech was clearly tendentious in favor of the ruling party. She wrote a tendentious book on the war. Their tendentious views made the debate unfair.
antonyms: Impartial, Unbiased, Neutral, Fair, Objective, Balanced, Even-handed
sindhiMeaning: طرفدارانه، هڪ خاص راءِ يا نظريي جي حق ۾ لڙيل، غير جانبدار نه، ٻين کي قائل ڪرڻ لاءِ لکيل يا چيل، جانبدار نظرين وارو
synonyms: Biased, Partisan, One-sided, Prejudiced, Slanted, Opinionated, Colored, Loaded
Unacceptable, Impermissible, Disallowed, Prohibited, Barred, Unallowable, Invalid
sindhiMeaning: جيڪو قبول نه ٿي سگهي، عدالت ۾ ثبوت طور نه مڃيل، اصولن جي خلاف، ناقابل تسليم، جنهن کي شامل نه ڪري سگهجي
antonyms: Admissible, Acceptable, Permissible, Allowed, Valid, Legitimate
englishMeaning: Not allowed or accepted, especially in a court of law. Not acceptable as evidence or argument. Not permitted according to rules or standards. Something that cannot be considered or included.
examples: The judge ruled the evidence inadmissible in court. His statement was inadmissible because it was hearsay. Such behavior is inadmissible in a professional environment. The document was declared inadmissible by the committee.
urduMeaning: ناقابل قبول، عدالت میں بطور ثبوت مسترد شدہ، قواعد کے خلاف، جو تسلیم نہ ہو سکے، ناقابل شمولیت

examples: The school is inadequately equipped for so many students. He was inadequately prepared for the interview. The problem was inadequately explained by the teacher. Their claims were inadequately supported by evidence.
urduMeaning: ناکافی طور پر، اَدھورے انداز میں، مطلوبہ معیار سے کم، ناقص طور پر، ضرورت سے کم مقدار یا معیار میں

englishMeaning: To make someone sad or dispirited. To cast down in spirits. To cause loss of hope or courage. To depress emotionally. To lower someone’s mood or confidence.

examples: The government tried to rein in inflation. He needs to rein in his temper. The manager reined in the spending of the team. Parents should rein in their children’s screen time.
sindhiMeaning: قابو ڪرڻ، ڪنهن ڪم يا جذبن کي روڪڻ، حد ۾ رکڻ، ڪنٽرول ڪرڻ، رفتار گهٽائڻ
antonyms: Release, Free, Unleash, Encourage, Loosen
urduMeaning: قابو میں رکھنا، کسی چیز یا جذبات کو روکنا، حد میں رکھنا، کنٹرول کرنا، رفتار کم کرنا
synonyms: Control, Restrain, Curb, Check, Limit, Hold back, Contain
englishMeaning: To control or restrain something. To bring under limit or check. To slow down or stop an activity. To hold back emotions or actions. To keep something under control.
To reduce or restrain something, especially spending or activity. To pull back or slow down. To hold back progress or effort. To limit or moderate. To decrease intensity of an action.
examples: The company reined back its expenses this year. He reined back his enthusiasm during the meeting. The government reined back public spending. She reined back her ambitions temporarily.
urduMeaning: کم کرنا، روکنا، خرچ یا سرگرمی کو محدود کرنا، پیچھے ہٹانا، شدت کو کم کرنا
antonyms: Increase, Expand, Boost, Extend, Encourage
synonyms: Reduce, Restrain, Curtail, Slow, Limit, Moderate, Check
sindhiMeaning: گهٽ ڪرڻ، روڪڻ، خرچ يا سرگرمي کي محدود ڪرڻ، پوئتي ڇڪڻ، رفتار يا زور گهٽائڻ

antonyms: Restrict, Limit, Control, Restrain, Supervise
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کي مڪمل آزادي ڏيڻ، ڪنهن کي پنهنجي مرضي مطابق ڪم ڪرڻ جي اجازت ڏيڻ، مڪمل اختيار ڏيڻ، ڪنهن تي ڀروسو ڪري آزاد ڪرڻ، بغير ڪنهن روڪ جي اجازت ڏيڻ
synonyms: Grant freedom, Allow liberty, Give authority, Let loose, Empower
englishMeaning: To allow someone complete freedom to act as they wish. To let a person make their own decisions without restriction. To give full authority or control to someone. To permit someone unrestricted action. To trust someone with independent decisions.
urduMeaning: کسی کو مکمل آزادی دینا، اپنی مرضی سے کام کرنے کی اجازت دینا، مکمل اختیار سونپنا، بلا روک ٹوک اجازت دینا، بھروسا کر کے آزاد چھوڑ دینا
examples: The director gave the artist free rein over the design. Parents should not give children free rein all the time. She was given free rein to manage the project. The coach gave free rein to the players during practice.

englishMeaning: To control something or someone strictly. To manage with strict discipline. To carefully limit or restrict. To maintain firm control over a situation. To keep something under close supervision.
urduMeaning: سختی سے قابو میں رکھنا، سخت نظم و ضبط کے تحت چلانا، کڑی نگرانی میں رکھنا، سخت پابندی کے تحت رکھنا، مضبوطی سے کنٹرول کرنا
antonyms: Loosen, Free, Release, Ignore, Neglect
synonyms: Control strictly, Restrain, Supervise closely, Manage firmly, Regulate
sindhiMeaning: سخت ڪنٽرول ۾ رکڻ، سخت نظم ۽ ضبط سان هلائڻ، ڪنهن کي ڪڙي نگرانيءَ ۾ رکڻ، سخت پابندي هيٺ رکڻ، مضبوطيءَ سان قابو ڪرڻ
examples: The manager keeps a tight rein on the office expenses. Parents should keep a tight rein on their teenagers. She keeps a tight rein on her emotions in public. The government keeps a tight rein on the media.

antonyms: Relinquish, Surrender, Give up, Step down, Withdraw
englishMeaning: To take control or leadership of something. To assume authority or responsibility. To become the person in charge. To start managing a group or task. To take over from another leader.
synonyms: Take control, Assume power, Lead, Take charge, Take command
sindhiMeaning: قيادت سنڀالڻ، ڪنهن ڪم يا اداري جو ڪنٽرول وٺڻ، ذميواري قبول ڪرڻ، حاڪم يا سردار بڻجڻ، ڪنهن ٻئي کان اقتدار وٺڻ
examples: After his father retired, he took the reins of the business. She took the reins of the team when the captain was injured. The new president will take the reins next month. He is ready to take the reins of leadership.
urduMeaning: قیادت سنبھالنا، کسی کام یا ادارے کا کنٹرول لینا، ذمہ داری قبول کرنا، سربراہ بننا، کسی سے اختیار لینا

synonyms: Transfer power, Pass control, Delegate, Surrender leadership, Cede authority
antonyms: Take control, Retain, Hold on, Keep, Assume
urduMeaning: کنٹرول یا قیادت کسی اور کے سپرد کرنا، اختیار منتقل کرنا، ذمہ داری کسی دوسرے کو دینا، اقتدار سونپنا، سربراہی چھوڑ دینا
examples: The CEO handed over the reins to his successor. She handed over the reins of the project to her deputy. After many years, the coach handed over the reins to a younger man. He is preparing to hand over the reins of the family business.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنٽرول يا قيادت ٻئي کي حوالي ڪرڻ، اختيار سونپڻ، ذميواري ٻئي کي ڏيڻ، اقتدار منتقل ڪرڻ، ڪنهن ٻئي کي سربراهه بڻائڻ
englishMeaning: To give control or leadership to someone else. To transfer authority or responsibility. To pass management to another person. To relinquish one’s position of power. To let another person take charge.

sindhiMeaning: وڌيڪ آزادي ڏيڻ، ڪنٽرول کي ڍلو ڪرڻ، سخت نگراني گهٽائڻ، پابنديون گهٽ ڪرڻ، ماڻهن کي پنهنجي مرضي سان ڪم ڪرڻ ڏيڻ
examples: Parents should loosen the reins as their children grow up. The manager loosened the reins to boost creativity. The government loosened the reins on trade regulations. She decided to loosen the reins on her team’s work hours.
urduMeaning: زیادہ آزادی دینا، کنٹرول کو نرم کرنا، سخت نگرانی کم کرنا، پابندیاں کم کرنا، اپنی مرضی سے کام کرنے دینا
synonyms: Relax control, Ease restrictions, Grant freedom, Free up, Slacken
antonyms: Tighten, Restrict, Control, Restrain, Discipline
englishMeaning: To give someone more freedom or flexibility. To relax control over a person or situation. To reduce strict supervision. To allow more independence. To ease restrictions previously imposed.

sindhiMeaning: سڌارڻ جو عمل، ڪنهن غلطي کي درست ڪرڻ، اصلاح ڪرڻ، ڪا خرابي درست ڪرڻ، غلطي جي درستي
urduMeaning: درست کرنے کا عمل، کسی غلطی کو ٹھیک کرنا، اصلاح، خرابی کی درستی، خامی کو دور کرنا
synonyms: Correction, Amendment, Adjustment, Improvement, Repair, Remedy
englishMeaning: The act of correcting something that is wrong. The process of making right. Adjustment or improvement of a fault. Amendment of an error or mistake. Correction of an inaccuracy or defect.
antonyms: Damage, Error, Mistake, Fault, Deterioration
examples: The rectification of the error took several days. He demanded the rectification of the injustice. Rectification of the accounts is necessary before the audit. The company promised the quick rectification of faults.

antonyms: Initial attempt, First try, Early effort, Beginning
synonyms: Final attempt, Desperate try, Last resort, Ultimate effort, Final push
urduMeaning: آخری کوشش، مایوسی کی حالت میں کی جانے والی حتمی کوشش، تمام کوششیں ناکام ہونے کے بعد آخری جدوجہد، ہار ماننے سے پہلے آخری کاوش، مجبوری میں کی گئی حتمی کوشش
englishMeaning: A final attempt made after all others have failed. A desperate try to achieve something at the last moment. An ultimate effort in a hopeless situation. A final push to succeed. A last try before giving up.
examples: They made a last-ditch effort to save the company. In a last-ditch effort, doctors performed an emergency surgery. The team’s last-ditch effort helped them win the match. He made a last-ditch effort to convince her to stay.
sindhiMeaning: آخري ڪوشش، مايوسي جي وقت ۾ ڪيل آخري ڪوشش، سڀ ڪوششون ناڪام ٿيڻ کان پوءِ آخري حل، هارائڻ کان اڳ آخري جدوجهد، انتهائي مجبوري ۾ ڪيل ڪوشش

antonyms: Initial, First, Early, Preliminary
sindhiMeaning: آخري، مايوسي وارو، حتمي، انتهائي مجبوري ۾ ڪيل، آخري وقت جو
synonyms: Final, Desperate, Ultimate, Eleventh-hour, Do-or-die
urduMeaning: آخری، مایوسانہ، حتمی، انتہائی مجبوری میں کیا گیا، آخری وقت پر کیا گیا
englishMeaning: Made as a final desperate effort. Done at the last possible moment. Relating to a last attempt to avoid failure. Used to describe a final resort. Employed when no other option remains.
examples: They made a last-ditch attempt to reach an agreement. The soldiers put up a last-ditch defense. The doctor tried a last-ditch treatment. It was a last-ditch move to save the sinking business.

antonyms: Clarity, Clear speech, Fluency, Articulation
sindhiMeaning: اهڙي ڳالهائڻ جي عادت جنهن ۾ س کي ٿ وانگر اچاريو ويندو آهي، ٻاراڻي انداز ۾ ڳالهائڻ، ڳالهائڻ ۾ خرابي، هلڪي ٻولي وارو عيب، آواز جو ناقص اچار
synonyms: Stammer, Stutter, Speech defect, Mumble, Slur
urduMeaning: ایسی گفتگو کی عادت جس میں س کو تھ کی طرح بولا جائے، بچگانہ انداز میں بولنا، بولنے میں نقص، معمولی گفتگو کا عیب، الفاظ کا ناقص تلفظ
englishMeaning: A speech defect in which the sound s is pronounced like th. To speak with such a defect. To say something in a soft or childish way. A slight speech impediment. The act of pronouncing sibilant sounds imperfectly.
examples: The little boy speaks with a slight lisp. She had a lisp that made her sound charming. He lisped his words shyly. The child began to lisp her first sentences.

sindhiMeaning: ڪنجوس، بخيل، پيسو خرچ ڪرڻ ۾ سستي ڪندڙ، تمام گهڻي بچت ڪندڙ، خرچ ۾ سخت
examples: He is too parsimonious to buy new clothes. Her parsimonious habits allowed her to save a fortune. The manager was parsimonious with praise. They lived a parsimonious lifestyle despite being wealthy.
englishMeaning: Extremely unwilling to spend money or use resources. Very careful about spending. Miserly or stingy. Frugal to an excessive degree. Sparing in the use of anything.
synonyms: Stingy, Miserly, Frugal, Thrifty, Tightfisted, Sparing, Penny-pinching
urduMeaning: کنجوس، بخیل، پیسہ خرچ کرنے میں پیچھے ہٹنے والا، حد سے زیادہ بچت کرنے والا، خرچ میں سختی برتنے والا
antonyms: Generous, Extravagant, Lavish, Wasteful, Liberal, Spendthrift

examples: He paid a fancy price for the antique clock. The painting was sold at a fancy price at the auction. Tourists often pay fancy prices for souvenirs. She refused to pay such a fancy price for a bag.
sindhiMeaning: تمام گهڻي قيمت، عام کان وڌيڪ اگهه، شاندار يا مهانگو اگهه، وڌايل قيمت، شاهاڻي يا خاص شيءِ جو مهانگو اگهه
synonyms: High price, Exorbitant cost, Steep price, Premium cost, Inflated price
englishMeaning: An unusually high or excessive price. A price much higher than normal. A cost that reflects luxury or exclusivity. An inflated or exaggerated price. A price paid for something rare or fashionable.
urduMeaning: بہت زیادہ قیمت، عام سے کہیں زیادہ دام، پرتعیش یا مہنگا نرخ، بڑھایا ہوا نرخ، نایاب یا فیشن ایبل چیز کی مہنگی قیمت
antonyms: Bargain, Cheap price, Low cost, Discount, Reasonable price

examples: My aunt is a real backseat driver during long trips. Nobody likes a backseat driver in the office. Stop being a backseat driver and let me focus. He acts like a backseat driver in every meeting.
englishMeaning: A passenger who gives unwanted advice to the driver. A person who interferes in matters that are not their responsibility. Someone who criticizes without doing the work themselves. An observer who tells others how to act. A person offering unsolicited direction.
sindhiMeaning: اهو ماڻهو جيڪو ڊرائيور کي بنا پڇيا صلاحون ڏئي، ٻين جي معاملن ۾ مداخلت ڪندڙ، بغير ذميواريءَ جي صلاحون ڏيندڙ، تنقيد ڪندڙ پر خود ڪم نه ڪندڙ، بي ڪار نصيحتون ڪندڙ
urduMeaning: وہ شخص جو ڈرائیور کو بن مانگے مشورے دے، دوسروں کے معاملات میں دخل دینے والا، ذمہ داری کے بغیر مشورے دینے والا، تنقید کرنے والا لیکن خود کام نہ کرنے والا، غیر ضروری ہدایات دینے والا
synonyms: Meddler, Interferer, Kibitzer, Nag, Critic, Busybody
antonyms: Silent observer, Non-interferer, Passive passenger, Supporter

englishMeaning: A person who prefers to stay at home rather than go out. Someone who enjoys domestic life. A person who feels most comfortable in their home. An individual who avoids social gatherings. A stay-at-home type.
examples: She is a homebody who loves reading in her room. He became a homebody after retirement. Homebodies enjoy cooking and watching movies at home. Being a homebody, she rarely attends parties.
antonyms: Socialite, Adventurer, Traveler, Extrovert, Outgoer
sindhiMeaning: گهر ۾ رهڻ پسند ڪندڙ ماڻهو، جيڪو ٻاهر گهمڻ کان بچي، گهرو زندگي پسند ڪندڙ، گهر ۾ آرام محسوس ڪندڙ، محفلن کان پري رهندڙ
urduMeaning: گھر میں رہنے کا شوقین شخص، جو باہر جانے سے گریز کرے، گھریلو زندگی پسند کرنے والا، گھر میں سکون محسوس کرنے والا، محفلوں سے دور رہنے والا
synonyms: Stay-at-home, Introvert, Homelover, Domestic person

examples: He is so tight fisted that he never buys gifts. Her tight fisted nature annoys her friends. The tight fisted boss refused to give bonuses. Being tight fisted, he saves every penny.
antonyms: Generous, Charitable, Lavish, Openhanded, Spendthrift
englishMeaning: Very unwilling to spend money. Extremely stingy or miserly. Careful with money to an excessive degree. Reluctant to share resources. Mean in financial matters.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنجوس، بخيل، پيسا خرچ ڪرڻ ۾ سست، هٿ ڇڏائيندڙ نه، خرچ ۾ سختي ڪندڙ
urduMeaning: کنجوس، بخیل، پیسہ خرچ کرنے میں ہچکچانے والا، خرچ میں سختی برتنے والا، ہاتھ کھول کر خرچ نہ کرنے والا
synonyms: Stingy, Miserly, Parsimonious, Frugal, Penny-pinching, Cheap

examples: Don’t be such a worrywart; everything will be fine. My mother is a worrywart about our safety. He is a worrywart who checks the door lock ten times. She calls herself a worrywart about small things.
sindhiMeaning: بيحد پريشان ٿيڻ وارو ماڻهو، ننڍي ڳالهه تي به فڪر ڪندڙ، مستقل پريشان رهندڙ، وڌيڪ سوچيندڙ، هر وقت ڳڻتيءَ ۾ رهندڙ
antonyms: Optimist, Carefree person, Calm person, Easygoing individual
englishMeaning: A person who worries excessively about small or unlikely problems. Someone who is habitually anxious. A person who frets over minor issues. An individual prone to overthinking. A chronic worrier.
synonyms: Worrier, Fretter, Fusspot, Alarmist, Overthinker
urduMeaning: چھوٹی چھوٹی باتوں پر پریشان ہونے والا شخص، ہر وقت فکر مند رہنے والا، ضرورت سے زیادہ سوچنے والا، حد سے زیادہ حساس، پریشانیوں میں گھِرا رہنے والا

antonyms: Modesty, Simplicity, Humility, Authenticity, Sincerity
englishMeaning: A false or superficial display of grandeur. Outward show without real substance. Artificial magnificence or pride. Empty grandeur made only for appearance. A hollow display of splendor.
synonyms: False grandeur, Superficial display, Empty show, Ostentation, Pretense
sindhiMeaning: نمائشي شان و شوڪت، ظاهري چمڪ دمڪ بغير حقيقت جي، ٺاهيل شان، بنا اصليت جي شاهاڻو مظاهرو، خالي شان و شوڪت
urduMeaning: دکھاوے کی شان و شوکت، ظاہری چمک دمک بغیر حقیقت کے، بناوٹی شان، بغیر اصل کے شاہانہ مظاہرہ، کھوکھلی شان
examples: The king’s ceremony was full of painted pomp. Beneath the painted pomp lay a poor and unhappy court. Their wedding was nothing but painted pomp. History is full of rulers who loved painted pomp.

synonyms: Fool, Simpleton, Idiot, Dreamer, Daydreamer, Blockhead, Dolt, Nitwit, Ninny
antonyms: Genius, Sage, Scholar, Intellectual, Wise person, Thinker, Expert
urduMeaning: بیوقوف یا کند ذہن شخص، خواب دیکھنے والا یا خیالوں میں کھویا ہوا آدمی، سادہ لوح یا احمق شخص، ذہنی طور پر کمزور آدمی، بے کار وقت ضائع کرنے والا شخص
examples: Stop being such a mooncalf and finish your homework. He stood there like a mooncalf, staring at the sky. The teacher called him a mooncalf for forgetting his books again. Only a mooncalf would believe such a ridiculous story.
englishMeaning: A foolish or absent-minded person. Someone who behaves in a silly, dreamy, or thoughtless way. A person who wastes time daydreaming instead of paying attention. An old-fashioned word for a simpleton or fool. A born fool or a person considered mentally slow.
sindhiMeaning: بيوقوف يا سست الذهن شخص، خواب ڏسندڙ يا خيالن ۾ گم رهندڙ ماڻهو، سادو يا احمق ماڻهو، ذهني طور تي ڪمزور شخص، بيڪار وقت ضايع ڪندڙ ماڻهو

examples: Their ear-kissing during the meeting made everyone suspicious. The couple exchanged an ear-kissing moment at the party. She was annoyed by their constant ear-kissing behind her back. The politicians were seen ear-kissing before the vote.
urduMeaning: کان میں سرگوشی کرنا یا راز کہنا، کان چومنا محبت اور پیار کے اظہار کے طور پر، خفیہ اور قریبی گفتگو، کسی سے چھپ کر کھسر پھسر کرنا، محبت کا ایک نرم اور قریبی اظہار
sindhiMeaning: ڪنن ۾ ڀڻڪڻ يا راز ٻڌائڻ، پيار ۽ محبت جو اظهار ڪن کي چمي ڏيڻ سان، ڳجهي ۽ ويجهي ڳالهه ٻولهه، ڪنهن سان لڪ ۾ سرگوشي ڪرڻ، محبت جي هڪ نرم ۽ ويجهي حرڪت
synonyms: Whispering, Murmuring, Confiding, Nuzzling, Caressing, Cuddling
antonyms: Shouting, Announcing, Proclaiming, Broadcasting, Ignoring, Distancing
englishMeaning: The act of whispering something secretly into someone's ear. A gesture of showing affection or intimacy by kissing the ear. A close, private conversation held in a low voice. Speaking to someone in a very confidential manner. A romantic or affectionate touch of the lips to the ear.

sindhiMeaning: انتهائي ڪاوڙيل، وحشي بيل جيان غضبناڪ، بي قابو ڪاوڙ ۾ ورتل، پاڻ تي ضابطو وڃائي ويهڻ جي حد تائين ناراض، حسد يا دوکي ڪري چريو ٿيل
examples: He was horn-mad when he heard about the betrayal. She became horn-mad after losing all her savings. The manager was horn-mad at the team's careless mistake. Do not go near him now, he is completely horn-mad.
antonyms: Calm, Composed, Peaceful, Content, Pleased, Tranquil, Serene
urduMeaning: انتہائی غصے میں، جنگلی بیل کی طرح برہم، بے قابو غصے میں مبتلا، ہوش و ہواس کھو دینے کی حد تک ناراض، حسد یا دھوکے کی وجہ سے پاگل ہونا
englishMeaning: Extremely angry or furious, like a bull ready to attack. In a state of raging madness or uncontrolled fury. So angry that one loses all reason or self-control. Wildly enraged, especially over jealousy or betrayal. Driven to fury, often in an old-fashioned literary sense.
synonyms: Furious, Enraged, Livid, Raging, Incensed, Infuriated, Wrathful
Rude, Uncivil, Impolite, Boorish, Vulgar, Coarse, Uncouth, Discourteous
antonyms: Polite, Refined, Well-mannered, Cultured, Civil, Courteous, Gentle
englishMeaning: To raise or bring up someone with poor manners or bad behavior. To fail to teach proper etiquette or values. Rude, impolite, or lacking good upbringing. Behavior showing a lack of refinement or good manners. A person who has not been taught proper conduct.
sindhiMeaning: خراب تربيت ڏيڻ يا بدتميز بڻائڻ، بداخلاق يا بي ادب ماڻهو، سٺا آداب نه سيکارڻ، بي تهذيبيءَ سان پيش اچڻ، ننڍي هوندي کان غلط عادتون سيکارڻ
urduMeaning: بری تربیت دینا یا بد اخلاق بنانا، بدتمیز یا بے ادب شخص، اچھے آداب نہ سکھانا، بد تہذیبی کا مظاہرہ کرنا، بچپن سے غلط عادات سکھانا
examples: It is a shame to ill-breed a child in such a rough environment. His ill-breed manners embarrassed his parents. Do not ill-breed your children by ignoring their behavior. She was clearly an ill-breed guest at the formal dinner.

urduMeaning: سفر کے دوران کچھ دیر کے لیے کہیں رک جانا، دو پروازوں کے درمیان مختصر توقف کرنا، کسی کام کو بعد کے لیے ملتوی کرنا، سفر کا مختصر وقفہ، کسی چیز کو کسی کے اوپر بچھانا
synonyms: Stop, Halt, Pause, Break, Stopover, Postpone, Delay, Defer
antonyms: Continue, Proceed, Advance, Hasten, Rush, Depart
sindhiMeaning: سفر دوران ٿوري وقت لاءِ ڪٿي رهجي پوڻ، ٻن پرواز جي وچ ۾ مختصر توقف ڪرڻ، ڪنهن ڪم کي پوءِ لاءِ ملتوي ڪرڻ، سفر جو مختصر وقفو، ڪنهن شيءِ کي ڪنهن جي مٿان وڇائڻ
englishMeaning: To stop or stay somewhere for a short time during a journey. To make a temporary halt between two parts of a trip. To postpone or delay something to a later time. A short break in a journey, especially between flights. To spread something flat over a surface.
examples: We had to lay over in Dubai for six hours. The pilot decided to lay over the flight due to bad weather. Let us lay over this discussion until tomorrow. Passengers can rest in the lounge during a long lay over.

synonyms: Busybody, Meddler, Snoop, Prier, Gossip, Interferer, Eavesdropper
englishMeaning: A person who is overly curious about other people's private matters. Someone who interferes in things that do not concern them. An inquisitive individual who asks too many personal questions. A meddler who cannot mind their own business. A prying or intrusive person.
antonyms: Discreet person, Reserved person, Private person, Uninvolved person, Respectful person
sindhiMeaning: ٻين جي ذاتي معاملن ۾ حد کان وڌيڪ چوپچوپ ڪندڙ، بيجا مداخلت ڪندڙ ماڻهو، وڌيڪ سوال پڇندڙ، ٻين جي ڪمن ۾ ٽنگ اڙائيندڙ، پرائي معاملي ۾ گهڙي پوندڙ
examples: Do not be such a nosy parker and mind your own business. Our neighbor is a real nosy parker who watches everyone. She hated how her aunt acted like a nosy parker at family events. The nosy parker kept asking about my salary.
urduMeaning: دوسروں کے ذاتی معاملات میں حد سے زیادہ دلچسپی لینے والا، بلا وجہ مداخلت کرنے والا شخص، بہت زیادہ سوالات کرنے والا، دوسروں کے کاموں میں ٹانگ اڑانے والا، پرائے معاملے میں دخل دینے والا

examples: The new intern is a real eager beaver at the office. Our teacher praised the eager beaver students in class. He is such an eager beaver that he arrives an hour early. The team needs an eager beaver like her to succeed.
sindhiMeaning: تمام گهڻو محنتي ۽ جوش سان ڀريل ماڻهو، هر ڪم لاءِ تيار رهندڙ شخص، حد کان وڌيڪ سرگرم ۽ محنتي، ذميواري نڀائڻ لاءِ سدائين تيار، هر معاملي ۾ اڳتي وڌي ڪم ڪندڙ
englishMeaning: A person who is very enthusiastic and hardworking. Someone who is always ready to do more than what is required. An overly keen and diligent worker or student. A person full of energy and willingness to please. Someone excessively eager to start or complete tasks.
synonyms: Enthusiast, Go-getter, Hard worker, Zealot, Workaholic, Keener, Achiever
antonyms: Slacker, Loafer, Idler, Sluggard, Lazybones, Procrastinator
urduMeaning: بہت زیادہ محنتی اور پرجوش شخص، ہر کام کے لیے تیار رہنے والا، حد سے زیادہ سرگرم اور محنتی، ذمہ داری نبھانے کے لیے ہمیشہ تیار، ہر معاملے میں آگے بڑھ کر کام کرنے والا

englishMeaning: A person who imitates or copies another person's actions, style, or ideas. Someone who mimics others without originality. A child's word for one who copies. Describing behavior that closely follows another's example. An imitator who lacks creativity of their own.
examples: Stop being a copycat and think of your own ideas. His little brother is such a copycat. The company was accused of copycat marketing tactics. She called her friend a copycat for wearing the same dress.
antonyms: Originator, Innovator, Creator, Inventor, Pioneer, Leader
sindhiMeaning: ٻين جي نقل ڪندڙ ماڻهو، بغير سوچ سمجھ جي نقل ڪندڙ، ٻين جي عادتن ۽ انداز کي هوبهو اپنائيندڙ، پنهنجي پاڻ ۾ اصليت نه رکندڙ، ٻارن جي زبان ۾ نقل ڪندڙ کي چوندا آهن
urduMeaning: دوسروں کی نقل کرنے والا شخص، بغیر سوچے سمجھے نقل کرنے والا، دوسروں کے انداز اور طرزِ عمل کو ہوبہو اپنانے والا، اپنی اصلیت نہ رکھنے والا، بچوں کی زبان میں نقل کرنے والے کو کہا جاتا ہے
synonyms: Imitator, Mimic, Follower, Impersonator, Plagiarist, Duplicator, Aper

englishMeaning: A person who is very clumsy or careless in a delicate situation. Someone whose rough behavior causes damage or upset. A person lacking tact and grace when handling sensitive matters. Behavior that is destructive or reckless in refined surroundings. Anyone who moves or acts without care for what might break.
sindhiMeaning: نازڪ صورتحال ۾ بيحد بي احتياط ماڻهو، بي ڊول ۽ ڀڃ ڊاهه ڪندڙ شخص، سنجيده معاملن ۾ بي هوش هلندڙ، اهڙو ماڻهو جيڪو نازڪ ماحول ۾ نقصان ڪري، بي پرواهيءَ سان هلندڙ
urduMeaning: نازک صورتحال میں بہت بے احتیاط شخص، بھدا اور توڑ پھوڑ کرنے والا آدمی، سنجیدہ معاملات میں بغیر سوچے چلنے والا، ایسا شخص جو نازک ماحول میں نقصان پہنچائے، بے پروائی سے حرکت کرنے والا
antonyms: Diplomat, Tactful person, Careful person, Graceful person, Delicate person
synonyms: Clumsy person, Blunderer, Klutz, Oaf, Bungler, Tactless person
examples: He handled the situation like a bull in a china shop. Do not send him to the meeting, he is a bull in a china shop. She entered the discussion like a bull in a china shop and upset everyone. The child ran through the museum like a bull in a china shop.

My mother is a busy bee around the house every morning. She is such a busy bee that she never takes a break. The office is full of busy bees before the deadline. Even on holidays, he is a busy bee in his garden.
sindhiMeaning: هميشه مصروف ۽ محنتي ماڻهو، لڳاتار ڪم ڪندڙ شخص، وڏي محنتي ۽ متحرڪ فرد، اهڙو ماڻهو جيڪو خالي نه ٿو ويهي، پنهنجي محنت ۽ چستيءَ لاءِ ساراهيو ويندڙ
urduMeaning: ہمیشہ مصروف اور محنتی شخص، مسلسل کام کرنے والا آدمی، بہت محنتی اور متحرک فرد، ایسا شخص جو خالی نہیں بیٹھتا، اپنی محنت اور چستی کے لیے سراہا جانے والا
englishMeaning: A person who is always working hard and staying active. Someone who is constantly occupied with many tasks. A hardworking and industrious individual. A person who cannot sit still and keeps busy. Someone admired for their productivity and energy.
synonyms: Hard worker, Workaholic, Go-getter, Achiever, Doer, Hustler
antonyms: Idler, Loafer, Slacker, Lazybones, Sluggard, Procrastinator

sindhiMeaning: جلدي ڊڄي ويندڙ ماڻهو، بيجا احتياط ڪندڙ شخص، ڊڄڻو يا بزدل فرد، نوان ڪم ڪرڻ کان ڊڄندڙ، ٻارن جي زبان ۾ ڊڄڻي کي چوندا آهن
examples: Do not be such a scaredy cat and jump into the pool. My brother is a scaredy cat when it comes to horror films. She called him a scaredy cat for refusing to ride the roller coaster. He is a scaredy cat about visiting the dentist.
antonyms: Brave person, Hero, Daredevil, Bold person, Courageous person, Warrior
englishMeaning: A person who is easily frightened or overly cautious. Someone who avoids risk or adventure out of fear. A timid or cowardly individual, often used playfully. A person who is afraid to try new things. A childish term for a fearful person.
urduMeaning: جلدی ڈر جانے والا شخص، ضرورت سے زیادہ محتاط آدمی، بزدل یا ڈرپوک فرد، نئی چیزیں آزمانے سے ڈرنے والا، بچوں کی زبان میں ڈرپوک کو کہا جاتا ہے
synonyms: Coward, Chicken, Wimp, Timid person, Fraidy-cat, Faint-heart

antonyms: Honest person, Sincere friend, Trustworthy person, Genuine soul, Loyal companion
synonyms: Deceiver, Impostor, Fraud, Hypocrite, Traitor, Pretender, Betrayer
sindhiMeaning: خطرناڪ ماڻهو جيڪو معصوم ٿي ڏيکاري، نيڪ چهري ۾ لڪل بدنيت شخص، فريبي جيڪو اصل روپ لڪائيندو آهي، مٿان مٺو پر اندران خطرناڪ، ظاهر ۾ سٺو پر اندران بڇڙو انسان
englishMeaning: A dangerous person who pretends to be harmless or friendly. Someone who hides evil intentions behind a kind appearance. A deceiver who disguises their true nature. A person whose outward behavior is misleading. Anyone who seems trustworthy but is secretly a threat.
urduMeaning: خطرناک شخص جو معصوم بن کر پیش آئے، اچھے چہرے میں چھپا ہوا بدنیت شخص، فریبی جو اپنی اصل حقیقت چھپاتا ہے، اوپر سے میٹھا مگر اندر سے خطرناک، ظاہری طور پر اچھا مگر اندر سے برا انسان
examples: Beware of him, he is a wolf in sheep's clothing. The kind stranger turned out to be a wolf in sheep's clothing. Many con artists are wolves in sheep's clothing. She did not know her new friend was a wolf in sheep's clothing.

antonyms: Fair court, Legitimate court, Just tribunal, Impartial hearing, Lawful trial
synonyms: Mock trial, Sham court, Show trial, Farce, Unjust tribunal
englishMeaning: An unfair or unofficial court that ignores proper legal procedures. A trial in which the outcome is decided in advance. A mock or illegitimate legal proceeding. A court that disregards justice and fairness. Any judgment given without a fair hearing.
sindhiMeaning: غير منصفانه يا غير قانوني عدالت، اڳ ۾ فيصلو ٿيل مقدمو، جعلي يا نقلي عدالتي ڪارروائي، انصاف نه ڏيندڙ عدالت، بغير ٻڌڻي جي فيصلو ڪندڙ عدالت
examples: The trial was nothing but a kangaroo court. Human rights groups condemned the kangaroo court proceedings. He said the disciplinary hearing was a kangaroo court. Many dictators use kangaroo courts to silence opponents.
urduMeaning: غیر منصفانہ یا غیر قانونی عدالت، جس کا فیصلہ پہلے سے طے ہو، نقلی یا جعلی عدالتی کارروائی، انصاف نہ کرنے والی عدالت، بغیر سنے فیصلہ سنانے والی عدالت

sindhiMeaning: وڌيڪ معلومات لاءِ ڳنڍيل رهڻ، ايندڙ اپڊيٽ يا خبر جو انتظار ڪرڻ، ڏسندڙن يا ٻڌندڙن کي متوجه رهڻ جو چوڻ، چينل سان جڙيل رهڻ، جلد ايندڙ شيءِ لاءِ تيار رهڻ
antonyms: Tune out, Ignore, Disconnect, Leave, Switch off
urduMeaning: مزید معلومات کے لیے جڑے رہنا، آنے والی اپڈیٹ یا خبر کا انتظار کرنا، ناظرین یا سامعین کو متوجہ رہنے کا کہنا، چینل سے منسلک رہنا، جلد آنے والی چیز کے لیے تیار رہنا
synonyms: Keep watching, Keep listening, Wait, Remain alert, Follow along
englishMeaning: To keep watching or listening for more information. To remain attentive for upcoming news or updates. Used to tell the audience to wait for what comes next. To stay connected to a channel or source. A phrase meaning to be ready for something coming soon.
examples: Stay tuned for our next big announcement. Stay tuned to this channel for live updates. We have exciting news coming up, so stay tuned. Stay tuned after the break for the final results.

antonyms: Belittle, Criticize, Demean, Disparage, Undervalue, Degrade
synonyms: Idolize, Worship, Glorify, Exalt, Adore, Revere, Praise
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کي حد کان وڌيڪ عزت يا احترام ڏيڻ، ڪنهن کي مڪمل يا ڀلو سمجهڻ، حقيقت کان وڌيڪ آدرش بڻائڻ، ڪنهن کي عيبن کان مٿي سمجهڻ، ڪنهن کي عزت سان اوچو مقام ڏيڻ
urduMeaning: کسی کو حد سے زیادہ عزت یا احترام دینا، کسی کو مکمل یا برتر سمجھنا، حقیقت سے بڑھ کر مثالی بنانا، کسی کو عیبوں سے بالاتر سمجھنا، کسی کو بہت اونچا مقام دینا
examples: She tends to place her father on a pedestal. Do not place any leader on a pedestal without questioning them. He placed his teacher on a pedestal for years. Fans often place celebrities on a pedestal.
englishMeaning: To admire or respect someone greatly, often too much. To treat a person as if they are perfect or superior. To idealize someone beyond reality. To hold someone in unusually high regard. To honor someone as flawless or beyond criticism.

sindhiMeaning: پيار ۽ سڪون سان ڊگهي ڳالهه ٻولهه ڪرڻ، دوستن سان بي تڪلف گفتگو ڪرڻ، گپ شپ يا خوش گپي ڪرڻ، هلڪي ڦلڪي ڳالهين ۾ وقت گذارڻ، آرام سان ويهي ڳالهيون ڪرڻ
englishMeaning: To have a long, relaxed conversation with someone. To chat in a friendly and informal way. To gossip or share stories with friends. To discuss unimportant matters casually. To spend time talking pleasantly.
synonyms: Chat, Gossip, Converse, Talk, Natter, Chitchat, Yak
antonyms: Be silent, Stay quiet, Ignore, Remain speechless, Say nothing
urduMeaning: آرام سے لمبی گفتگو کرنا، دوستوں کے ساتھ بے تکلف بات چیت کرنا، گپ شپ یا خوش گپیاں کرنا، ہلکی پھلکی باتوں میں وقت گزارنا، سکون سے بیٹھ کر باتیں کرنا
examples: We sat on the porch and chewed the fat for hours. Grandpa loves to chew the fat with his old friends. Let us chew the fat over a cup of tea. They often chew the fat during lunch breaks.

You cannot rest on your laurels forever. Great athletes never rest on their laurels. He warned the team not to rest on their laurels after winning. Companies that rest on their laurels lose their market.
synonyms: Relax, Coast, Be complacent, Stagnate, Idle, Slack off
sindhiMeaning: پراڻي ڪاميابيءَ تي ڀروسو ڪرڻ، اڳوڻي ڪاميابيءَ سبب سست ٿي وڃڻ، هدف حاصل ڪرڻ بعد ڪوشش ڇڏي ڏيڻ، اڳئين حاصلات تي مطمئن ٿي وڃڻ، نئين محنت نه ڪرڻ
englishMeaning: To rely on past successes instead of making new efforts. To become complacent because of previous achievements. To stop trying after reaching a certain goal. To be satisfied with what one has already accomplished. To take pride in old victories without progressing.
antonyms: Strive, Persevere, Progress, Advance, Improve, Push forward
urduMeaning: پرانی کامیابی پر بھروسا کرنا، سابقہ کامیابی کی وجہ سے سست ہو جانا، مقصد حاصل کرنے کے بعد کوشش چھوڑ دینا، پچھلی کامیابیوں پر مطمئن ہو جانا، نئی محنت نہ کرنا

examples: It is a case of monkey see, monkey do with young children. He learned bad habits from his brother, monkey see, monkey do. In this office it is often monkey see, monkey do. The trend spread quickly, monkey see, monkey do.
urduMeaning: بغیر سمجھے نقل کرنا، دوسروں کو دیکھ کر ویسا ہی عمل کرنا، بے سوچی نقل کا رجحان، خاص طور پر بچوں کی اندھی نقل، صرف دوسروں کو دیکھ کر کام کرنا
englishMeaning: A phrase describing how people copy others without understanding. Used when someone imitates an action without thinking. The tendency to mimic behavior seen in others. Blind imitation, especially by children. Doing something just because others are doing it.
synonyms: Imitation, Mimicry, Copying, Aping, Emulation
sindhiMeaning: بغير سمجهه جي نقل ڪرڻ، ٻين کي ڏسي هوبهو عمل ڪرڻ، بي سوچ نقل جو رجحان، خاص ڪري ٻارن جي انڌي نقل، صرف ٻين کي ڏسي ڪم ڪرڻ
antonyms: Originality, Creativity, Innovation, Independence, Uniqueness

synonyms: Destined, Fated, Preordained, Predestined, Meant to be, Inevitable
englishMeaning: Something believed to be destined or predetermined by fate. An event that seems to be meant to happen. A romantic idea of a predestined relationship. A situation that appears to be arranged by destiny. Fate that cannot be avoided or changed.
urduMeaning: قسمت میں لکھا ہونا، پہلے سے مقرر شدہ واقعہ، محبت کا ایسا رشتہ جو نصیب سے جڑا ہو، ایسی صورتحال جو قدرت کی طرف سے طے شدہ لگے، ایسی تقدیر جو بدلی نہ جا سکے
sindhiMeaning: قسمت ۾ لکيل هجڻ، اڳ ۾ مقرر ٿيل واقعو، محبت جو رشتو جيڪو نصيب سان جڙيل هجي، اهڙي صورتحال جيڪا قدرت طرفان مقرر لڳي، اهڙي تقدير جنهن کي بدلائي نه سگهجي
antonyms: Accidental, Unplanned, Coincidental, Random, Avoidable
examples: Their meeting felt as if it was written in the stars. She believed their marriage was written in the stars. Success in this project seems written in the stars. Some say our friendship was written in the stars.

englishMeaning: To avoid someone or something completely. To stay away from a person, place, or situation. To keep a safe distance from possible trouble. To not get involved in a certain matter. To purposely avoid contact or interaction.
synonyms: Avoid, Shun, Evade, Dodge, Bypass, Sidestep, Escape
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ يا شخص کان مڪمل پاسو ڪرڻ، پري رهڻ، مصيبت کان بچڻ لاءِ فاصلو رکڻ، ڪنهن معاملي ۾ نه اچڻ، ڄاڻي واڻي پاسو ڪرڻ
antonyms: Approach, Confront, Face, Engage, Meet, Encounter
urduMeaning: کسی چیز یا شخص سے مکمل پرہیز کرنا، دور رہنا، مصیبت سے بچنے کے لیے فاصلہ رکھنا، کسی معاملے میں شامل نہ ہونا، جان بوجھ کر گریز کرنا
examples: Steer clear of that dangerous neighborhood at night. I always steer clear of arguments at work. Doctors advise us to steer clear of fatty foods. She learned to steer clear of toxic people.

englishMeaning: A comfortable but restrictive situation. A life of luxury that lacks true freedom. A pleasant environment where one still feels trapped. Wealth or privilege that comes with hidden limitations. A beautiful yet confining condition.
antonyms: True freedom, Liberty, Independence, Openness, Freedom of movement
synonyms: Golden prison, Luxurious confinement, Comfortable trap, Restricted luxury
sindhiMeaning: ٺاهوڪي پر پابنديءَ واري صورتحال، عيش وارو زندگي جيڪا حقيقي آزادي نه ڏئي، خوشگوار ماحول ۾ به قيد جو احساس، دولت جيڪا لڪل پابندين سان اچي، خوبصورت پر بند حال
urduMeaning: خوبصورت مگر پابندی والی صورتحال، عیش و آرام کی زندگی جو حقیقی آزادی نہ دے، خوشگوار ماحول میں بھی قید کا احساس، ایسی دولت جس کے ساتھ چھپی ہوئی پابندیاں ہوں، خوبصورت مگر بند حالت
examples: She lived in a gilded cage as a princess. His job pays well but feels like a gilded cage. Many celebrities describe fame as a gilded cage. The mansion was beautiful but felt like a gilded cage to her.

urduMeaning: کانوں کے لیے خوشگوار آواز یا خبر، ایسے الفاظ جو دل کو بھائیں، سننے والے کو خوش کر دینے والا جملہ، ہر وہ آواز جو خوشی دے، خوشی سے سنی جانے والی خبر
examples: Her promotion news was music to her ears. His apology was music to my ears. The sound of rain is music to a farmer's ears. Their laughter was music to their mother's ears.
englishMeaning: Something very pleasant or delightful to hear. Words or news that bring great joy. A statement that satisfies or pleases the listener. Any sound that gives happiness to the hearer. Information that is welcomed warmly.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنن لاءِ خوشگوار آواز يا خبر، اهڙا لفظ جيڪي دل کي وڻن، ٻڌندڙ کي راضي ڪندڙ جملو، هر اهو آواز جيڪو خوشي بخشي، خوشيءَ سان ٻڌل خبر
synonyms: Delightful, Pleasing, Welcome, Joyful, Gratifying, Heartwarming
