synonyms: Strange, Weird, Eccentric, Unconventional, Quirky, Unusual, Bizarre
sindhiMeaning: غير معمولي، عجيب يا انوکو، حيرت انگيز يا اڻ ٿيندڙ، وڏي تخليقي يا غير روايتي، عام سوچ کان مختلف، دلچسپ ۽ عجيب انداز وارو
englishMeaning: Unusual, strange, or eccentric. Something surprising or unexpected. Very creative or unconventional. Not what people would normally think or do. Wild and imaginative in a quirky way.
antonyms: Normal, Ordinary, Conventional, Typical, Standard, Predictable
examples: His ideas are always a bit off the wall. She wore an off the wall outfit to the party. The movie has an off the wall sense of humor. He gave an off the wall answer to the simple question.
urduMeaning: غیر معمولی، عجیب یا انوکھا، حیران کن یا غیر متوقع، بہت تخلیقی یا غیر روایتی، عام سوچ سے مختلف، دلچسپ اور نرالا انداز والا

synonyms: Neat, Tidy, Orderly, Organized, Spotless, Immaculate, Well-arranged
antonyms: Messy, Disorderly, Chaotic, Cluttered, Untidy, Disorganized
examples: Her room was in apple-pie order before the guests arrived. He keeps his desk in apple-pie order. The soldiers left the barracks in apple-pie order. My grandmother's kitchen is always in apple-pie order.
englishMeaning: Perfectly arranged and neatly organized. Kept in very good and tidy condition. Everything in its proper place. Extremely well ordered and clean. In a state of complete neatness.
urduMeaning: بالکل صاف ستھرا اور منظم، ہر چیز اپنی جگہ پر، بہت اچھی طرح ترتیب دیا گیا، صاف ستھرا اور مرتب، مکمل نظم و ضبط میں
sindhiMeaning: بلڪل صاف سٿرو ۽ منظم، هر شيءِ پنهنجي جاءِ تي، تمام سٺي طرح رٿيل، صاف سٿرو ۽ ترتيبوار، مڪمل نظم و ضبط ۾

examples: Winning the award was a feather in her cap. This promotion is a real feather in his cap. Publishing a book is a feather in any writer's cap. The championship was another feather in the team's cap.
sindhiMeaning: فخر جوڳي ڪاميابي، خاص عزت يا حاصلات، اهم ڪاميابي جيڪا سڃاڻپ ڏي، ذاتي فتح جيڪا رڪارڊ ۾ شامل ٿئي، محنت سان حاصل ٿيل امتياز
synonyms: Achievement, Honor, Accomplishment, Success, Triumph, Distinction, Merit
urduMeaning: قابلِ فخر کامیابی، خاص اعزاز یا حصول، اہم کامیابی جو پہچان دلائے، ذاتی فتح جو ریکارڈ میں شامل ہو، محنت سے حاصل کیا گیا امتیاز
englishMeaning: An achievement to be proud of. A special honor or accomplishment. A notable success that brings recognition. A personal victory added to one's record. A distinction earned through effort.
antonyms: Failure, Setback, Disgrace, Shame, Loss, Defeat

englishMeaning: To follow someone's example or behavior. To learn from another person's actions. To imitate a good habit or method. To use someone else's approach as a model. To copy a successful person's way of doing things.
examples: You should take a leaf out of your sister's book. I decided to take a leaf out of his book and start exercising. Teachers should take a leaf out of her book on patience. Let us take a leaf out of their book on teamwork.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ٻئي جي مثال تي عمل ڪرڻ، ڪنهن جي عملن مان سبق سکڻ، سٺي عادت يا طريقي کي اپنائڻ، ٻئي جي طريقي کي پنهنجي لاءِ نمونو بڻائڻ، ڪامياب ماڻهوءَ جي نقل ڪرڻ
word: Take a leaf out of someone's book
synonyms: Imitate, Emulate, Follow, Copy, Model, Adopt
antonyms: Ignore, Reject, Disregard, Oppose, Differ, Resist
urduMeaning: کسی دوسرے کی مثال پر عمل کرنا، کسی کے اعمال سے سبق سیکھنا، اچھی عادت یا طریقہ اپنانا، دوسرے کے طریقے کو اپنے لیے نمونہ بنانا، کامیاب شخص کی نقل کرنا

synonyms: Ruined, Deteriorated, Declined, Spoiled, Decayed, Worsened
antonyms: Improved, Flourished, Thrived, Prospered, Restored, Renewed
sindhiMeaning: خراب يا برباد ٿي وڃڻ، زوال جو شڪار ٿيڻ، سٺي حالت مان نڪري خراب ٿيڻ، بي پرواهيءَ سبب خراب ٿيل، وقت سان گڏ خراب ٿي ويل
examples: The old house has completely gone to pot. His health has gone to pot since the accident. The business went to pot after the manager left. The garden has gone to pot due to neglect.
englishMeaning: Ruined or in very poor condition. Fallen into disrepair or decline. No longer working well or looking good. Deteriorated because of neglect. Something that has become worse over time.
urduMeaning: خراب یا برباد ہو جانا، زوال کا شکار ہو جانا، اچھی حالت سے نکل کر خراب ہو جانا، بے توجہی کی وجہ سے خراب ہو جانا، وقت کے ساتھ بگڑ جانا

antonyms: Never, Not at all, Timely, Punctual, Immediate
synonyms: Eventually, At last, Finally, In the end, Belatedly
urduMeaning: دیر سے کرنا نہ کرنے سے بہتر ہے، دیر سے کیا گیا کام بھی قیمتی ہوتا ہے، دیر سے آنے کو خوش دلی سے قبول کرنے کا انداز، کام کی اہمیت کو ظاہر کرنا، دیر کے باوجود کام مکمل کرنے کی ترغیب
englishMeaning: It is better to do something late than not do it at all. Late action is preferable to no action. Even delayed effort has value. Encouragement to complete a task despite the delay. A phrase used to accept a late arrival kindly.
sindhiMeaning: دير سان ڪرڻ  نه ڪرڻ کان بهتر آهي، دير سان ڪيل عمل به قيمتي آهي، دير سان اچڻ کي قبول ڪرڻ جو انداز، ڪم جي اهميت کي واضح ڪرڻ، دير باوجود ڪم مڪمل ڪرڻ لاءِ همٿ
examples: You finally started studying, better late than never. She apologized after years, but better late than never. He joined the class late, better late than never. Better late than never, they finally acknowledged the mistake.

Do not worry about slow progress, Rome wasn't built in a day. She reminded him that Rome wasn't built in a day. Learning a language takes time, Rome wasn't built in a day. Building a business is hard, Rome wasn't built in a day.
word: Rome wasn't built in a day
synonyms: Patience needed, Takes time, Gradual, Slow progress, Step by step
sindhiMeaning: وڏا ڪم وقت ۽ صبر گهرن ٿا، وڏا منصوبا جلدي ۾ مڪمل نه ٿيندا آهن، ڪاميابي جلدي نه ملندي، ترقيءَ لاءِ صبر ضروري آهي، اهم شيون وقت سان بڻجن ٿيون
antonyms: Instant, Immediate, Quick, Sudden, Rushed, Overnight
urduMeaning: بڑے کام وقت اور صبر مانگتے ہیں، بڑے منصوبے جلدی مکمل نہیں ہوتے، کامیابی فوراً حاصل نہیں ہوتی، ترقی کے لیے صبر ضروری ہے، اہم چیزیں وقت کے ساتھ بنتی ہیں
englishMeaning: Great achievements take time and cannot be rushed. Big projects require patience and effort. A reminder that success does not come instantly. Encouragement to be patient with progress. Important things need time to develop.

antonyms: Lose-lose, One-sided, Unfair deal, Zero-sum, Disadvantageous
englishMeaning: A situation in which everyone involved benefits. An outcome that is good for all parties. A deal or arrangement where no one loses. A positive result for both sides. A mutually beneficial condition.
synonyms: Mutual benefit, Beneficial deal, Fair outcome, Advantageous, Profitable for all
urduMeaning: ایسی صورتحال جس میں سب کو فائدہ ہو، دونوں فریقین کے لیے فائدہ مند نتیجہ، ایسا معاملہ جس میں کوئی نقصان میں نہ ہو، دونوں طرف کے لیے اچھا نتیجہ، ایک دوسرے کو فائدہ پہنچانے والی صورتحال
sindhiMeaning: اهڙي صورتحال جنهن ۾ سڀ فائدو حاصل ڪن، ٻنهي طرفن لاءِ فائدي وارو نتيجو، اهڙو معاملو جنهن ۾ ڪوبه نقصان ۾ نه رهي، ٻنهي فريقن لاءِ سٺو نتيجو، هڪ ٻئي کي فائدو ڏيندڙ صورتحال
examples: The new agreement is a win-win situation for both companies. Sharing resources created a win-win situation. This deal offers a win-win situation for buyers and sellers. Cooperation led to a true win-win situation.

englishMeaning: To unfairly change the rules or expectations of a task. To make it harder for someone to succeed by shifting the criteria. To alter targets after progress has been made. To keep changing what is required. To act unfairly by adjusting standards.
synonyms: Change rules, Shift targets, Alter criteria, Redefine, Modify unfairly
antonyms: Keep promises, Stay consistent, Honor rules, Maintain standards, Be fair
urduMeaning: قواعد یا شرائط بدل کر مشکل پیدا کرنا، کام کے دوران مقصد تبدیل کرنا، کامیابی کو مشکل بنانے کے لیے معیار بدلنا، ہر بار نئے مطالبات کرنا، غیر منصفانہ طور پر حد تبدیل کرنا
sindhiMeaning: قاعدا يا شرطون بدلائي ڏکيائي پيدا ڪرڻ، ڪم جي وچ ۾ مقصد تبديل ڪرڻ، ڪاميابيءَ کي مشڪل بڻائڻ لاءِ معيار بدلائڻ، هر دفعي نوان مطالبا ڪرڻ، غير منصفاڻي طور تي حد بدلائڻ
examples: Every time we finish a task, he moves the goalposts. Do not move the goalposts once the project starts. The company keeps moving the goalposts on employee bonuses. It is unfair to move the goalposts after the agreement.

englishMeaning: The most important fact or point of a matter. The final result or conclusion of something. The essential truth after everything is considered. A summary of the key issue. The main financial result of a business.
antonyms: Trivial detail, Minor point, Side issue, Irrelevant matter
synonyms: Main point, Conclusion, Result, Essence, Final outcome, Key issue
urduMeaning: سب سے اہم نکتہ یا حقیقت، حتمی نتیجہ یا فیصلہ، سب کچھ کے بعد کی بنیادی سچائی، اہم معاملے کا خلاصہ، کاروبار کا حتمی مالی نتیجہ
sindhiMeaning: اهم ترين نڪتو يا حقيقت، آخري نتيجو يا فيصلو، سڀ ڪجهه بعد جي بنيادي سچائي، مکيه معاملي جو خلاصو، ڪاروبار جو حتمي مالي نتيجو
examples: The bottom line is that we must reduce expenses. She explained the bottom line of the report clearly. The bottom line for any company is profit. Ignore the details and focus on the bottom line.
He cannot walk, let alone run. She has no time for lunch, let alone dinner. The child cannot read, let alone write. We do not own a car, let alone a house.
urduMeaning: دوسری چیزوں کا ذکر تو دور، زیادہ اہم یا مشکل چیز کا ذکر تو الگ، دو چیزوں کے درمیان فرق ظاہر کرنا، کسی بات پر زور دینا، پہلے کی منفی بات کو مضبوط کرنا
englishMeaning: Used to say that something is even less likely or possible. Not to mention something more important or difficult. Used to compare two things where the second is more extreme. To emphasize that something is beyond consideration. Used to strengthen a previous negative statement.
synonyms: Much less, Not to mention, Never mind, Besides, In addition
antonyms: Including, As well as, Also, Even, Together with
sindhiMeaning: ٻين شين جو ذڪر ته پري، وڌيڪ اهم يا ڏکي شيءِ جو ذڪر ته پاسي، ٻن شين جي وچ ۾ فرق ظاهر ڪرڻ، ڪنهن ڳالهه کي وڌيڪ زور ڏيڻ، اڳوڻي نفي واري جملي کي مضبوط ڪرڻ

synonyms: Stay silent, Hold back, Refrain, Keep quiet, Restrain speech
englishMeaning: To stop yourself from saying something you might regret. To keep quiet even when tempted to speak. To hold back words that could cause trouble. To restrain oneself from speaking out. To avoid making a hurtful or inappropriate comment.
antonyms: Speak up, Blurt out, Voice, Express, Retort
urduMeaning: کہنے سے خود کو روک لینا، کچھ بولنے سے باز رہنا، ناراضگی یا نقصان سے بچنے کے لیے خاموش رہنا، جذبات کو دبا کر رکھنا، ناپسندیدہ بات سے گریز کرنا
examples: I had to bite my tongue during the meeting. She bit her tongue to avoid an argument. Sometimes it is better to bite your tongue than reply. He bit his tongue when his boss criticized him unfairly.
sindhiMeaning: ڳالهائڻ کان رڪجي وڃڻ، ڪجهه چوڻ کان پاڻ کي روڪڻ، ناراضگي يا نقصان کان بچڻ لاءِ خاموش رهڻ، جذبات کي دٻائي رکڻ، ناپسنديده جملي کان پاسو ڪرڻ

examples: He loves to blow his own trumpet at every meeting. Modest people rarely blow their own trumpet. Stop blowing your own trumpet and let the results speak. It is time to blow your own trumpet a little.
urduMeaning: اپنی تعریف خود کرنا، اپنی صلاحیتوں یا کامیابیوں پر فخر جتانا، عوام میں اپنی تعریف کرنا، کامیابیوں کی طرف توجہ دلانا، بلند آواز سے خود کو پیش کرنا
sindhiMeaning: پنهنجي تعريف پاڻ ڪرڻ، پنهنجي صلاحيتن يا ڪاميابين تي فخر ڪرڻ، عوام ۾ پاڻ کي ساراهڻ، ڪاميابين ڏانهن ڌيان ڇڪائڻ، بلند آواز سان پاڻ کي پيش ڪرڻ
synonyms: Boast, Brag, Show off, Self-promote, Gloat, Crow
englishMeaning: To boast about your own abilities or achievements. To praise yourself publicly. To draw attention to your own success. To speak proudly of what you have done. To promote one's own accomplishments loudly.
antonyms: Be humble, Be modest, Downplay, Understate, Stay quiet

sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن مسئلي جو سامهون تڏهن ڪرڻ جڏهن اهو حقيقت ۾ پيش اچي، اڳواٽ پريشان نه ٿيڻ، وقت پوڻ تي معاملي کي منهن ڏيڻ، اڳتي جي ڳالهه اڳتي ڏسبي، مستقبل جي مشڪلات جي فڪر ۾ نه پوڻ
examples: Don't worry about the interview now; we'll cross that bridge when we come to it. If the payment gets delayed, we'll cross that bridge when we come to it. She refused to plan for problems that might never happen and said they'd cross that bridge when they came to it. Let's finish today's work first and cross that bridge when we come to it.
englishMeaning: To deal with a problem only when it actually arises. To postpone worrying about a possible difficulty until it truly happens. Used to advise someone not to worry about future problems in advance. A phrase encouraging patience and focus on present matters. To handle a situation as it comes, rather than anticipating trouble.
word: Cross that bridge when you come to it
antonyms: Plan ahead, Anticipate, Prepare in advance, Worry beforehand, Preempt, Foresee, Prearrange
urduMeaning: کسی مسئلے کا سامنا اُس وقت کرنا جب وہ حقیقتاً پیش آئے، پہلے سے پریشان نہ ہونا، وقت آنے پر معاملہ نمٹانا، آگے کی بات آگے دیکھی جائے گی، مستقبل کی مشکلات کی فکر میں نہ پڑنا
synonyms: Deal with it later, Handle it when it happens, Face it in time, Wait and see, Take one step at a time, Postpone worry, Address later

sindhiMeaning: پنهنجي ئي ڪيل ڪم جو مزو چکڻ، جهڙو ڪم پاڻ ٻين سان ڪيو ٿي، اهو ئي ورتاءُ پاڻ سان ٿيڻ، پنهنجن ڪرتوتن جو بدلو ملڻ، جيئن ڪيو تيئن ڀوڳڻ
synonyms: Poetic justice, Just deserts, Payback, Retaliation, Karma, Comeuppance, Retribution, Tit for tat
word: Get taste of your own medicine
englishMeaning: To receive the same unpleasant treatment that one has given to others. To experience the same bad behavior one has shown to someone else. A situation in which a person is treated unkindly in the way they treated others. Used when someone finally faces the consequences of their own actions. To be repaid in kind for one's unfair conduct.
antonyms: Forgiveness, Mercy, Pardon, Reward, Kindness, Compassion, Amnesty
urduMeaning: اپنے ہی کیے کا مزہ چکھنا، جیسا سلوک دوسروں سے کیا وہی اپنے ساتھ ہونا، اپنے کرتوتوں کا بدلہ ملنا، جیسا کرو گے ویسا بھرو گے، اپنی ہی چال میں پھنسنا
examples: He always mocked others, and today he got a taste of his own medicine. When she was ignored by her friends, she finally got a taste of her own medicine. The bully got a taste of his own medicine when a bigger boy pushed him. It felt satisfying to see him get a taste of his own medicine.

urduMeaning: طویل عرصے کے بعد، وقت گزرنے پر، آخرکار، مستقبل میں، بالآخر
examples: Studying hard now will help you in the long run. Eating healthy food benefits your body in the long run. In the long run, honesty always pays off. Small daily savings can make a big difference in the long run.
englishMeaning: Over an extended period of time. Eventually, after a long period. Considering the future rather than the immediate present. Used to describe an outcome that becomes clear only after time passes. In the end, when everything is finally taken into account.
sindhiMeaning: ڊگهي عرصي بعد، وقت گذرڻ سان، آخرڪار، مستقبل ۾، نيٺ ڪري
synonyms: Eventually, Ultimately, In time, Over time, In the end, Sooner or later, Finally, In due course
antonyms: Immediately, Instantly, Right away, In the short term, At once, Momentarily, Presently

synonyms: Honor a promise, Fulfill, Stay true, Be reliable, Follow through, Stand by, Deliver, Commit
englishMeaning: To do what one has promised to do. To fulfill a promise or commitment. To remain true to a spoken agreement. Being reliable and honest about what one says. Not breaking a promise, no matter the circumstances.
antonyms: Break a promise, Betray, Renege, Backtrack, Deceive, Fail, Lie
examples: He always keeps his word, no matter how difficult the task is. She promised to help and kept her word. A true leader must keep his word to gain trust. If you keep your word, people will respect you.
urduMeaning: اپنے وعدے پر قائم رہنا، بات کا پکا ہونا، وعدہ پورا کرنا، زبان کا پاس رکھنا، اپنی بات نبھانا
sindhiMeaning: پنهنجي واعدي تي قائم رهڻ، ڳالهه پاڙڻ، وچن نڀائڻ، زبان جو پڪو رهڻ، قول پورو ڪرڻ
اڌ رات جو وقت جڏهن جادو يا روحاني شيون ٿيڻ جو چوندا آهن، ڀوتاٽ وارو وقت، اونداهي ۽ پراسرار گهڙي، رات جو ٻارهين وڳي جو وقت، ڊيڄاريندڙ گهڙي
examples: Ghost stories always come alive during the witching hour. She woke up at the witching hour to a strange noise. Legends say spirits roam freely at the witching hour. The old house feels haunted around the witching hour.
urduMeaning: آدھی رات کا وہ وقت جب جادو یا مافوق الفطرت واقعات ہونے کا خیال کیا جاتا ہے، بھوت پریت کا وقت، پُراسرار اور تاریک گھڑی، رات بارہ بجے کا وقت، ڈراؤنی ساعت
antonyms: Daytime, Daylight, Noon, Morning, Dawn, Sunrise, Broad daylight
englishMeaning: The time late at night when supernatural events are said to occur, traditionally midnight. A time associated with witches, ghosts, and magic. A period considered dark, mysterious, or eerie. Figuratively, a critical or difficult time of day, especially late at night. A moment when things feel strange or unsettling.
synonyms: Midnight, Dead of night, Small hours, Twilight, Nighttime, Dark hour, Ghostly hour

englishMeaning: A town that has been completely abandoned by its inhabitants. A once populated place now empty and silent. A location that feels deserted or lifeless. A place that used to be busy but is now nearly empty. Figuratively, any area that seems unusually quiet.
examples: After the mines closed, the settlement became a ghost town. The streets were empty and the market looked like a ghost town. Once a busy port, the area is now a ghost town. During the lockdown, the entire city felt like a ghost town.
urduMeaning: ویران شہر، ایسا شہر جو مکینوں نے چھوڑ دیا ہو، خالی اور سنسان جگہ، بے آباد بستی، جہاں کوئی چہل پہل نہ ہو
synonyms: Deserted town, Abandoned place, Empty settlement, Wasteland, Uninhabited area, Ruin, Ghostly place
antonyms: Bustling city, Populated town, Lively place, Metropolis, Crowded area, Thriving town

sindhiMeaning: اڌ رات جي اونداهي وقت ۾، رات جي سانت واري گهڙي ۾، جڏهن سڀ سُتل هجن، لڪ ڇپ ۾ رات جو، اونداهي ۽ خاموش رات ۾

synonyms: Midnight, Dead of night, Late at night, Nighttime, Small hours, Witching hour, Wee hours

urduMeaning: مصروف انسان کو آرام نصیب نہیں، کام میں لگے رہنا، ہر وقت مصروف رہنا، تھکاوٹ کے باوجود کام کرنا، مسلسل مشغولیت

Often said jokingly about ongoing duties or responsibilities. A reminder that work continues even when one is tired.

examples: As soon as I finished cooking, the phone rang; no rest for the wicked! She sighed and said, 'No rest for the wicked,' before starting another task. No rest for the wicked, he laughed, picking up more files. With guests arriving soon, it seems there's no rest for the wicked.

antonyms: Give up, Surrender, Back down, Yield, Be discouraged, Stop, Quit
urduMeaning: کتے بھونکتے رہتے ہیں مگر قافلہ چلتا رہتا ہے، تنقید کرنے والوں کی پرواہ نہ کرنا، اپنی منزل کی طرف بڑھتے رہنا، لوگوں کی باتوں کو نظرانداز کرنا، کام جاری رکھنا چاہے کوئی کچھ بھی کہے

synonyms: Declining, Decreasing, Fading, Diminishing, Weakening, Dwindling, Ebbing, Shrinking
sindhiMeaning: گهٽجندڙ، ڪمزور ٿيندڙ، ختم ٿيندڙ، آهستي آهستي زوال پذير، اهم ٻاڏائيندڙ

sindhiMeaning: دير رات تائين، اڌ رات کان به پوءِ، رات جو گهڻي دير تائين، جاڳي جاڳي وقت گذارڻ، وقت جي پرواهه ڪرڻ کان سواءِ

synonyms: Incompatible, Mismatched, Clashing, Opposite, Contrasting, Discordant, At odds

examples: He asked a few questions to test the water before proposing the idea. Let's test the water before launching the product. She tested the water by discussing the plan with her manager first. Before investing, test the water carefully.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ڪم کي آزمائڻ، حالت جانچڻ، راءِ معلوم ڪرڻ، اڳتي وڌڻ کان اڳ جاچ ڪرڻ، ماحول ڏسڻ

synonyms: Probe, Check, Assess, Explore, Gauge, Try out, Feel out, Sound out

englishMeaning: To try something carefully before fully committing to it. To find out people's opinions before taking action. To check a situation before making a decision. To make a small effort to see how something will be received. To gather information before proceeding.

A phrase used to describe an obvious or undeniable fact. Something so clear that it does not need to be explained. Used sarcastically to comment on stating the obvious. A truth known to everyone. Refers to universally accepted knowledge.
sindhiMeaning: بلڪل ظاهر ڳالهه، هر ڪنهن کي خبر واري حقيقت، جيڪا ڳالهه ٻڌائڻ جي ضرورت ئي نه هجي، پڌرو سچ، سڀ کي معلوم ڳالهه
examples: Saying he is smart is like saying water is wet. Of course she got the job; water is wet. Telling me that the sun is hot is like saying water is wet. Everyone knows he studies hard; water is wet.

sindhiMeaning: دماغ وڃائي ويهڻ، مٿي جو خراب ٿيڻ، عقل گم ڪري ڇڏڻ، چريو ٿي پوڻ، سوچ ۽ سمجهه گم ڪرڻ

sindhiMeaning: پنهنجن سوچن کي سنڀالڻ، دماغ کي ٺيڪ ڪرڻ، خود کي سنڀالي وٺڻ، پنهنجي هوش ۾ اچڻ، دل ۽ دماغ کي پُر سڪون ڪرڻ
synonyms: Compose yourself, Pull yourself together, Regain focus, Calm down, Get a grip, Steady yourself

synonyms: Sane, Sensible, Clear-minded, Sharp, Alert, Rational, Sound
Crazy, Confused, Irrational, Silly, Unstable, Foolish, Mad
sindhiMeaning: مڪمل هوش حواس نه هجڻ، دماغي طرح ٺيڪ نه هجڻ، عقل جو ٿورو گهٽ هجڻ، سمجهه ۾ ڪمي، چريو نظر اچڻ

synonyms: Genuine, Sincere, Real, Heartfelt, True, Honest, Authentic, Frank

examples: He turned out to be a deadbeat who never paid his rent. Her ex-husband was a deadbeat father. The company sued several deadbeat clients. Don't lend him money he's a known deadbeat.
sindhiMeaning: قرض نه ڏيندڙ ماڻهو، سست ۽ نڪمو شخص، ذميواريءَ کان ڀڄندڙ، ٻين تي گذارو ڪندڙ، بيڪار ماڻهو

urduMeaning: قرض نہ چکانے والا شخص، سست اور نکما آدمی، ذمہ داری سے بھاگنے والا، دوسروں پر گزارا کرنے والا، بیکار شخص

englishMeaning: The act or state of being unable to breathe, often leading to death. Death or distress caused by lack of oxygen. A feeling of being oppressed or overwhelmed. The prevention of normal growth or expression.

sindhiMeaning: اڳواٽ ڄاڻندڙ، مستقبل جو اڳواٽ اندازو لڳائيندڙ، ڏورانديش، بصيرت رکندڙ، غيبي ڄاڻ رکندڙ

examples: His prescient warnings about the market crash proved correct. She was prescient in choosing that career path. The novel offers a prescient view of modern technology. His prescient advice saved the company.

examples: The snake's venom can be fatal without treatment. He spoke about his rival with pure venom. Her words were full of venom and anger. Scientists study venom to develop new medicines.
antonyms: Antidote, Kindness, Love, Goodwill, Sweetness, Affection, Benevolence

synonyms: Poison, Toxin, Malice, Spite, Bitterness, Hatred, Rancor, Hostility

urduMeaning: زہریلا، زہر رکھنے والا، کینہ پرور، نفرت بھرا، نقصان دہ، تلخ لہجے والا
englishMeaning: Producing or containing venom capable of causing injury or death. Full of malice, spite, or extreme hostility. Expressing intense bitterness or hatred. Dangerous and harmful in a poisonous manner.
antonyms: Harmless, Nontoxic, Kind, Friendly, Loving, Benign, Gentle

examples: They moved into a spacious new apartment. The hotel offers spacious rooms with a view. The car has a spacious interior for long trips. We enjoyed dinner in a spacious dining hall.

synonyms: Delicate, Elegant, Fine, Pretty, Graceful, Refined, Petite

sindhiMeaning: اجازت ڏيندڙ، نرم، سختي نه ڪندڙ، ڇوٽ ڏيندڙ، وڏي حد تائين آزادي ڏيندڙ

synonyms: Idler, Lazy, Sluggard, Loafer, Inactive, Do-nothing, Indolent

synonyms: Say sorry, Beg pardon, Express regret, Atone, Repent, Make amends

synonyms: Cocky, Arrogant, Presumptuous, Brash, Bold, Smug, Self-assured
englishMeaning: Excessively confident in one's own abilities or judgment. Having more self-assurance than is warranted. Feeling too sure of success, often leading to mistakes.

examples: He was overconfident and failed the exam. The team became overconfident after their easy wins. Do not be overconfident about your abilities. Her overconfident attitude annoyed her colleagues.

antonyms: Fact, Proof, Certainty, Humility, Modesty, Reality
synonyms: Assumption, Supposition, Belief, Guess, Boldness, Arrogance, Impudence
sindhiMeaning: بغير ثبوت جي فرض ڪرڻ، اڳواٽ اندازو، بي ادبي، حد کان وڌي وڃڻ، پاڻ سيتي فرض ڪرڻ
englishMeaning: An idea or belief taken to be true without proof. Bold or arrogant behavior that goes beyond what is appropriate. An assumption based on probability. The act of taking something for granted.
examples: There is a presumption of innocence until proven guilty. His presumption in speaking to the boss surprised us. The report is based on the presumption that prices will rise. Do not act on mere presumption.
urduMeaning: بغیر ثبوت کے فرض کرنا، پیشگی اندازہ، گستاخی، حد سے تجاوز، خود سے فرض کر لینا

antonyms: Respect, Appreciate, Repay, Honor, Refrain
synonyms: Take advantage of, Exploit, Impose upon, Trade on, Overuse

synonyms: Take advantage of, Exploit, Impose upon, Trade on
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن جي رحمدلي  دوستي يا سٺي رويي جو ناجائز فائدو وٺڻ، ٻئي جي نرميءَ تي وڌيڪ ڀاڙڻ
examples: He often presumes upon his uncle's wealth. She presumed upon their long friendship to borrow money. Do not presume upon my good nature. Some employees presume upon the manager's leniency.

synonyms: Assumed, Supposed, Likely, Probable, Expected, Apparent
antonyms: Proven, Confirmed, Certain, Definite, Verified

sindhiMeaning: گمان تي ٻڌل، ظاهري طور تي درست، اندازي مطابق مڃيل، غالب امڪان وارو
urduMeaning: قیاس پر مبنی، بظاہر درست، اندازے کے مطابق تسلیم شدہ، غالب امکان والا
examples: He is the presumptive winner of the election. The prince is the presumptive heir to the throne. Presumptive evidence supports the theory. She is the presumptive nominee of the party.

antonyms: Critic, Opponent, Attacker, Detractor, Adversary
synonyms: Defender, Advocate, Supporter, Champion, Justifier, Proponent
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ڳالهه  عقيدي يا ادارو جي دفاع ڪندڙ، وضاحت ڏيندڙ، حمايت ۾ دليل ڏيندڙ، صفائي پيش ڪندڙ
urduMeaning: کسی نظریے  عقیدے یا ادارے کا دفاع کرنے والا، وضاحت پیش کرنے والا، حمایت میں دلائل دینے والا، صفائی پیش کرنے والا
englishMeaning: A person who offers arguments in defense of something controversial. A speaker or writer who defends a belief, doctrine, or institution. One who justifies or explains an idea, often against criticism.
examples: He is a well-known apologist for free market economics. The writer became an apologist for the government's policies. She is an apologist of modern art. Many apologists have defended the ancient traditions.

sindhiMeaning: انتهائي ڪاوڙ ۾ ڀريل، غصي کان ڳاڙهو ٿي ويل، ڪاوڙ کان بي ڪنٽرول ٿيندڙ، فالج سان لاڳاپيل يا ان جو شڪار، اهڙي ڪاوڙ جيڪا ماڻهوءَ کي لفظ چوڻ کان روڪي ڇڏي، شديد جذباتي بگاڙ ۾ ورتل
englishMeaning: Overcome with extreme anger and unable to control it. Furious to the point of being nearly speechless or physically shaking. Relating to or suffering from apoplexy, an old medical term for a stroke. Showing signs of intense rage such as a flushed face and raised voice. Extremely enraged or incensed in a way that seems almost uncontrollable.
examples: He was apoplectic when he saw the damage to his car. The manager became apoplectic after hearing the excuse. She turned apoplectic with rage at the unfair decision. The old doctor described the patient's condition as apoplectic.
synonyms: Furious, Enraged, Livid, Incensed, Irate, Fuming, Wrathful, Infuriated, Raging, Seething
antonyms: Calm, Composed, Peaceful, Serene, Content, Pleased, Relaxed, Unruffled, Placid, Tranquil
urduMeaning: غصے سے بھرا ہوا، انتہائی ناراض اور بے قابو، غصے سے چہرہ سرخ ہو جانے والا، فالج سے متعلق یا اس کا شکار، اتنا غصہ کہ بولنا مشکل ہو جائے، شدید جذباتی ہیجان میں مبتلا

synonyms: Stroke, Seizure, Fit, Rage, Fury, Frenzy, Paroxysm, Attack, Convulsion, Outburst
urduMeaning: فالج، دماغ کی رگ پھٹنے سے اچانک بے ہوشی، شدید غصہ جو انسان کو مفلوج کر دے، اچانک صدمہ یا ہیجان، اسٹروک کے لیے پرانا طبی نام، انتہائی غضب کی کیفیت
antonyms: Calmness, Composure, Health, Serenity, Recovery, Peace, Stability, Wellness, Tranquility, Ease
examples: The old man died of apoplexy in his sleep. His face turned red as if he were about to have apoplexy. She nearly had apoplexy when she saw the phone bill. Doctors once called every sudden collapse apoplexy.
sindhiMeaning: فالج، دماغ ۾ رت جي رڳ ڦاٽڻ سبب ٿيندڙ اوچتو بيهوشي، شديد ڪاوڙ جيڪا ماڻهوءَ کي بيوس ڪري ڇڏي، اوچتو صدمو يا هيجان، طبي طور تي اسٽروڪ لاءِ پراڻو نالو، انتهائي غضب جي حالت
englishMeaning: An old-fashioned medical term for a stroke caused by bleeding in the brain. Sudden loss of consciousness and paralysis due to a ruptured blood vessel. A state of extreme anger or excitement that seems to overwhelm a person. Great rage or shock that leaves someone almost incapacitated. Any condition marked by sudden collapse or violent emotion.

antonyms: Proudly, Boldly, Confidently, Defiantly, Shamelessly, Unrepentantly, Arrogantly, Brazenly, Assertively, Boastfully
synonyms: Regretfully, Remorsefully, Sorrowfully, Humbly, Penitently, Sheepishly, Contritely, Ruefully, Meekly, Shamefacedly
englishMeaning: In a way that shows regret or asks for forgiveness. With a tone or manner expressing that one is sorry. In a humble and remorseful manner. While admitting fault or expressing embarrassment. In a way that seeks to excuse or explain a mistake politely.
urduMeaning: معافی مانگتے ہوئے، افسوس کے ساتھ، ندامت کے انداز میں، شرمندگی سے، عاجزی اور پشیمانی سے، غلطی تسلیم کرتے ہوئے، نرم اور معذرت خواہانہ لہجے میں
sindhiMeaning: معافي گهرندي، افسوس سان، ندامت واري انداز ۾، شرمساري سان، عاجزي ۽ پشيمانيءَ سان ڳالهائيندي، ڏوهه قبول ڪندي، نرم ۽ معذرت واري لهجي ۾
examples: He smiled apologetically after arriving late to the meeting. She apologetically explained that the item was out of stock. The child looked apologetically at his mother after breaking the vase. He coughed apologetically before interrupting the conversation.

antonyms: Insignificance, Smallness, Limitation, Narrowness, Sameness, Uniformity, Flatness, Simplicity, Restriction, Triviality
englishMeaning: A measurable extent such as length, width, height, or depth. An aspect or feature of a situation or problem. The size or scope of something. In physics, one of the fundamental coordinates needed to describe a point in space or time. A particular way of looking at or considering something.
urduMeaning: پیمائش، لمبائی چوڑائی یا اونچائی، کسی چیز کا حجم یا وسعت، کسی معاملے کا پہلو یا رخ، طبیعیات میں مکان یا وقت کا محور، کسی مسئلے کی وسعت یا اہمیت، جہت
synonyms: Measurement, Size, Extent, Scope, Aspect, Facet, Feature, Proportion, Magnitude, Scale
sindhiMeaning: ماپ، طول، عرض يا اونهائي، ڪنهن شيءِ جو حجم يا وسعت، ڪنهن معاملي جو پاسو يا رخ، طبيعيات ۾ خلا يا وقت جو محور، ڪنهن مسئلي جي وسعت يا اهميت، جهت
examples: The room's dimensions are perfect for a small office. This discovery adds a new dimension to the research. We must consider every dimension of the problem before deciding. Time is often called the fourth dimension.

urduMeaning: پیمائش سے متعلق، لمبائی چوڑائی یا اونچائی والا، تین جہتی یا کسی بھی سمت والا، حجم یا شکل سے تعلق رکھنے والا، گہرائی اور وسعت ظاہر کرنے والا، جیومیٹری سے متعلق
synonyms: Spatial, Measurable, Geometric, Voluminous, Proportional, Structural, Physical, Metric, Sizable, Extensive
antonyms: Flat, Two-dimensional, Shapeless, Immeasurable, Formless, Insubstantial, Abstract, Unmeasured, Planar, Simple
sindhiMeaning: ماپ سان لاڳاپيل، طول عرض يا اونهائيءَ وارو، ٽي طرفو يا ڪنهن به جهت وارو، حجم يا شڪل سان تعلق رکندڙ، اونهائي ۽ گهرائي ڏيکاريندڙ، جيوميٽري سان واسطو رکندڙ
examples: The engineer studied the dimensional properties of the new material. Modern films often use three-dimensional imaging. The dimensional analysis helped solve the physics problem. Her artwork has a strong dimensional quality.
englishMeaning: Relating to measurements such as length, width, or height. Having a specified number of dimensions, as in three-dimensional. Concerning the size, shape, or extent of something. Adding depth or complexity to something. Used to describe objects that appear to have volume rather than being flat.

antonyms: Lovable, Admirable, Pleasant, Delightful, Adorable, Likable, Charming, Agreeable, Respectable, Wonderful
synonyms: Hateful, Loathsome, Abominable, Despicable, Repulsive, Odious, Contemptible, Vile, Disgusting, Repugnant
urduMeaning: قابل نفرت، ناپسندیدہ، بہت ہی برا اور ناگوار، ایسا جو کسی کو پسند نہ آئے، بیزار کرنے والا، اخلاقی طور پر گھناؤنا، انتہائی ناپسندیدہ
sindhiMeaning: نفرت جوڳو، ڌڪار جوڳو، ڏاڍو خراب ۽ ناپسنديده، اهڙو جيڪو ڪنهن کي به وڻي نه سگهي، بيزار ڪندڙ، اخلاقي طور تي گندو، انتهائي ناپسند ڪرڻ جهڙو
englishMeaning: Deserving intense dislike or hatred. Extremely unpleasant or offensive. Worthy of being despised or loathed. Morally repulsive or disgusting. So bad in nature that no one can bear it.
examples: His detestable behavior at the party shocked everyone. Cheating in exams is a detestable act. She found his lies absolutely detestable. The dictator's detestable crimes were condemned worldwide.

antonyms: Random, Probabilistic, Uncertain, Indeterminate, Free, Chance, Unpredictable, Arbitrary, Spontaneous, Stochastic
englishMeaning: Relating to the belief that every event is caused by previous events. Predictable because outcomes are completely determined by prior conditions. In science, describing a system whose future state is fully fixed by its current state. Not involving chance or free will. Following strict cause-and-effect reasoning.
urduMeaning: جبریت پسند، ایسا نظریہ جو کہے ہر عمل پہلے اسباب کا نتیجہ ہے، پہلے سے طے شدہ، ایسا نظام جس کا نتیجہ پہلے سے معلوم ہو، بغیر اتفاق یا آزادی کے، سبب و نتیجہ کے اصول پر مبنی
synonyms: Predetermined, Fixed, Causal, Predictable, Fated, Inevitable, Preordained, Certain, Mechanistic, Fatalistic
sindhiMeaning: اهڙو نظريو جيڪو چوي ٿو ته هر ڪم پهرين سببن جي ڪري ٿئي ٿو، اڳواٽ طي ٿيل، جبريت وارو، اهڙو نظام جنهن جو نتيجو اڳ ۾ ئي معلوم هجي، بنا اتفاق يا آزاديءَ جي، سبب ۽ نتيجي واري اصول تي ٻڌل
examples: Classical physics is based on a deterministic view of the universe. His deterministic approach left no room for chance. The model uses deterministic equations to predict outcomes. Some philosophers reject a deterministic explanation of human behavior.

synonyms: Fatalism, Predestination, Causality, Necessity, Predeterminism, Inevitability, Destiny, Fate, Preordination, Mechanism
urduMeaning: جبریت، وہ فلسفہ جو کہے ہر واقعہ پہلے اسباب کا نتیجہ ہے، آزاد ارادے کی نفی، تقدیر پرستی، یہ عقیدہ کہ ہر کام پہلے سے طے شدہ ہے، فطری قوانین کا نظریہ
englishMeaning: The philosophical belief that all events are caused by earlier events and natural laws. The idea that free will does not exist because everything is predetermined. A doctrine holding that human actions are the result of prior causes. In science, the view that identical conditions always produce identical results. The theory that the future is fixed by the past.
antonyms: Free will, Choice, Randomness, Chance, Indeterminism, Liberty, Freedom, Spontaneity, Autonomy, Uncertainty
examples: Determinism argues that free will is only an illusion. Scientific determinism suggests that everything follows natural laws. Many philosophers have debated the truth of determinism. Cultural determinism claims that behavior is shaped by society.
sindhiMeaning: اهو فلسفياڻو نظريو جيڪو چوي ٿو ته هر واقعو پهرين سببن جي ڪري ٿئي ٿو، جبريت، آزاد ارادي جي نفي، تقدير پرستي، اهو عقيدو ته سڀ ڪم اڳ ۾ ئي مقرر ٿيل آهن، فطرتي قانونن جو نظريو

synonyms: Resolutely, Firmly, Steadfastly, Purposefully, Doggedly, Persistently, Tenaciously, Decisively, Unwaveringly, Stubbornly
urduMeaning: پختہ ارادے سے، مضبوط عزم کے ساتھ، بغیر ہمت ہارے، ثابت قدمی سے، پکی نیت کے ساتھ، مضبوط انداز میں، پوری توجہ سے
englishMeaning: In a firm and unwavering way. With strong resolve and purpose. Showing great determination to achieve a goal. In a manner that refuses to give up. Steadily and with clear intention.
antonyms: Hesitantly, Weakly, Indecisively, Reluctantly, Uncertainly, Timidly, Half-heartedly, Waveringly, Feebly, Passively
examples: She worked determinedly to finish the project on time. He walked determinedly toward the finish line. The team fought determinedly until the last minute. She spoke determinedly about her plans for the future.
sindhiMeaning: پختي ارادي سان، مضبوط عزم سان، بنا هارجي، ثابت قدميءَ سان، پڪي نيت سان، اڏول انداز ۾، پوري توجهه سان

examples: He carried a torch through the dark cave. The Olympic torch was lit at the opening ceremony. Vandals torched the abandoned building last night. The teacher is like a torch that guides students.
urduMeaning: بیٹری والی ٹارچ، ہاتھ کی روشنی دینے والا آلہ، مشعل، جلتی ہوئی لکڑی، کسی چیز کو آگ لگانا، روشنی اور رہنمائی کی علامت، امید یا علم کی نشانی
englishMeaning: A portable light usually powered by batteries. A stick with burning material at one end used for light or as a weapon. To deliberately set something on fire. A symbol of guidance, learning, or freedom. In some cultures, a source of enlightenment or hope.
synonyms: Flashlight, Lamp, Light, Flare, Beacon, Lantern, Firebrand, Brand, Burner, Ignitor
antonyms: Darkness, Extinguisher, Shadow, Gloom, Blackness, Dimness, Obscurity, Nightfall, Douse, Cover
sindhiMeaning: بيٽري وارو ٽارچ، هٿ وارو روشني ڏيندڙ اوزار، ٻرندڙ لڪڙي جا ڪاٺ سان ٻڌل، مشعل، ڪنهن شيءِ کي باهه لڳائڻ، روشني ۽ رهنمائيءَ جو نشان، اميد يا علم جو علامتي اظهار
خوف کان پوئتي هٽي وڃڻ، همت هارڻ، ڪم ڪرڻ کان انڪار ڪري ڇڏڻ، ڊپ سبب ارادو بدلائڻ، بزدلي ڏيکارڻ، آخري وقت تي پيڇو ڪرڻ، پنهنجي ڳالهه کان مڪرڻ
examples: He was ready to jump but chickened out at the last second. Don't chicken out now, we have come too far. She chickened out of giving the speech in front of the class. I hope he doesn't chicken out of the fight.
urduMeaning: ڈر کر پیچھے ہٹ جانا، ہمت ہار دینا، کام کرنے سے انکار کر دینا، بزدلی دکھانا، آخری وقت میں ارادہ بدل لینا، اپنی بات سے پھر جانا، ڈر کی وجہ سے پیچھے ہٹنا
antonyms: Persist, Persevere, Continue, Face, Confront, Dare, Brave, Endure, Proceed, Commit
englishMeaning: To decide not to do something because of fear at the last moment. To back out of a plan due to nervousness or cowardice. To lose courage and avoid a challenge. To withdraw from a commitment because of fear. To become too scared to follow through with an action.
synonyms: Back out, Withdraw, Retreat, Give up, Quit, Flinch, Recoil, Cop out, Bail, Falter

englishMeaning: A system of sending messages using flags held in different positions. A visual signaling method used especially at sea or on railways. A device with movable arms or lights for giving signals. In computing, a variable used to control access to a shared resource. To send a message using such a system.
examples: Sailors used semaphore to communicate between ships. The railway operator worked the semaphore at the crossing. Scouts learn how to signal using semaphore flags. In computing, a semaphore controls access to shared memory.
antonyms: Silence, Concealment, Ignorance, Hiding, Muteness, Confusion, Miscommunication, Void, Nothingness, Obscurity
synonyms: Signal, Flag, Sign, Indicator, Beacon, Marker, Gesture, Cue, Notification, Symbol
urduMeaning: جھنڈوں کے ذریعے پیغام بھیجنے کا نظام، اشاراتی نظام، ریلوے یا بحری جہازوں کا سگنل، کمپیوٹر میں کنٹرول کا خاص متغیر، اشاروں سے بات پہنچانا، اشارے دینے کا آلہ
sindhiMeaning: جهنڊن ذريعي پيغام موڪلڻ جو طريقو، اشاراتي نظام، ريل جي پٽڙين تي هلندڙ سگنل ڏيندڙ آلو، بحري جهازن جو رابطي وارو اشارو، ڪمپيوٽر ۾ هڪ خاص ڪنٽرول متغير، اشاري وسيلي ڳالهه پهچائڻ
انتهائي غريب، مفلس، ڪنجوس، لالچي، پيسا خرچ ڪرڻ کان ڪيٻائيندڙ، بخيل، غربت جي حالت ۾ رهندڙ، تنگدست
examples: The penurious old man refused to buy new clothes. Their penurious lifestyle surprised their wealthy neighbors. He was too penurious to help even his own family. Years of unemployment left them in a penurious state.
urduMeaning: انتہائی غریب، مفلس، کنجوس، پیسے خرچ کرنے سے کترانے والا، بخیل، غربت کی حالت میں رہنے والا، تنگدست
synonyms: Poor, Impoverished, Destitute, Needy, Miserly, Stingy, Frugal, Parsimonious, Tightfisted, Poverty-stricken
antonyms: Wealthy, Rich, Generous, Prosperous, Affluent, Lavish, Bountiful, Charitable, Munificent, Well-off
englishMeaning: Extremely poor and living in want. Unwilling to spend money, miserly. Marked by extreme poverty or scarcity. Reluctant to share resources with others. Showing a stingy or miserly nature.

urduMeaning: دھوکہ دینا، ٹھگنا، پیسے ہڑپ کرنا، فراڈ کر کے مال حاصل کرنا، قرض ادا نہ کرنا، حق مارنا، جعل سازی کرنا
sindhiMeaning: ٺڳي ڪرڻ، دوکو ڏيڻ، پيسا هڙپ ڪرڻ، فراڊ ڪري ڪنهن کان پيسا وٺي ڀڄي وڃڻ، قرض نه ڏيڻ، حق مارڻ، هٿ ڪٽي وڃڻ
englishMeaning: To cheat someone out of money or property. To defraud or deceive a person, especially for financial gain. To avoid paying a debt owed to someone. To trick someone by dishonest means. To swindle or con.
examples: The con artist tried to bilk elderly people out of their savings. He was accused of bilking the company of thousands of dollars. She managed to bilk her partners with a fake investment scheme. Don't let strangers bilk you with false promises.
antonyms: Compensate, Repay, Reimburse, Refund, Pay, Honor, Reward, Satisfy, Restore, Give back
synonyms: Cheat, Defraud, Swindle, Con, Deceive, Trick, Fleece, Dupe, Scam, Rip off

antonyms: Husband, Married man, Spouse, Groom, Partner, Wedded, Companion, Consort, Mate, Attached
sindhiMeaning: ڪنوارو مرد، غير شادي شده، يونيورسٽيءَ جي پهرين ڊگريءَ رکندڙ، بيچلر ڊگري وارو، آزاد رهندڙ نوجوان، اڪيلو رهندڙ مرد
synonyms: Unmarried man, Single, Celibate, Stag, Graduate, Unwed, Free man, Lone man, Single guy, Suitor
englishMeaning: An unmarried man. A person who holds a first university degree. A young knight serving under another's banner in medieval times. A man of any age who has never married. In some contexts, an independent single male living alone.
urduMeaning: کنوارا مرد، غیر شادی شدہ، یونیورسٹی کی پہلی ڈگری رکھنے والا، بیچلر ڈگری کا حامل، آزاد رہنے والا نوجوان، تنہا رہنے والا مرد
examples: He remained a bachelor throughout his life. She earned a bachelor's degree in economics. The bachelor lived alone in a small apartment. Many of his friends were still bachelors in their thirties.

sindhiMeaning: خوبصورت عورت، سهڻي ۽ دلڪش ڇوڪري، محفل جي سڀ کان سهڻي عورت، حسينه، ناز نخري واري نوجوان، ادا جي حسن جي مالڪ
examples: She was the belle of the ball in her beautiful gown. Every belle in the town admired the new dress design. The belle smiled gracefully at her guests. The young belle became famous for her charm.
urduMeaning: خوبصورت عورت، حسینہ، دلکش لڑکی، محفل کی سب سے خوبصورت خاتون، نازک اندام حسینہ، حسن و ادا کی مالک نوجوان خاتون
antonyms: Hag, Crone, Ugly woman, Plain Jane, Frump, Witch, Wallflower, Beast, Eyesore, Simpleton
englishMeaning: A beautiful and charming woman, especially the most admired at a social event. A pretty and popular young lady. A woman known for her elegance and attractiveness. A term used historically for a well-dressed lady of society. Any female considered outstandingly lovely.
synonyms: Beauty, Charmer, Lovely, Damsel, Maiden, Stunner, Goddess, Lady, Miss, Sweetheart
Sea-man, Triton, Sea-god, Aquatic being, Water-man, Sea creature, Poseidon-like figure, Neptune, Mythic swimmer, Male mermaid
antonyms: Human, Landsman, Mortal, Earthling, Land-dweller, Ordinary man, Real person, Non-mythical being, Terrestrial, Reality
examples: Children love stories about a friendly merman living in the ocean. In the film, the merman rescued a drowning sailor. Ancient sailors claimed to have seen a merman near the rocks. The book describes a kingdom ruled by a wise merman.

sindhiMeaning: افسانوي سامونڊي مخلوق جنهن جو مٿيون حصو مرد ۽ هيٺيون مڇيءَ جو هجي، مرد جل پري، سمنڊ جو ديو، مِرمين، ڪهاڻين ۾ ذڪر ٿيل نر جل مخلوق

urduMeaning: دستہ، ٹیم، گروہ، منظم جماعت، فوجی دستہ، پولیس کا خصوصی دستہ، منتخب کھیلوں کی ٹیم، کام کرنے والی ٹیم، دوستوں کا گروپ
examples: The bomb disposal squad arrived quickly at the scene. The coach announced the starting squad for the championship match. A military squad was sent to patrol the borders. She went to the mall to hang out with her squad.
antonyms: Individual, Single, Solo, Loner, One, Person, Independent, Outsider
sindhiMeaning: دستو، جٿو، ٽيم، منظم گروهه، فوجي دستو، پوليس جو خاص دستو، چونڊيل راندين جي ٽيم، ڪم ڪندڙ ٽولي، دوستن جو گروهه
synonyms: Team, Crew, Gang, Troop, Unit, Band, Group, Company, Force, Platoon

antonyms: Irregular, Informal, Random, Unconventional, Lexical, Main, Tonal
urduMeaning: طریقہ یا انداز سے متعلق، قواعد میں معاون افعال سے متعلق، موسیقی کے مخصوص انداز سے متعلق، امکان یا ضرورت سے متعلق، بیچ کے درخت کے ریشے سے بنا ہوا کپڑا
synonyms: Methodical, Formal, Stylistic, Functional, Procedural, Auxiliary, Helping, Rayon, Viscose, Lyocell
englishMeaning: Related to mode, manner, or form. Related to modal verbs in grammar. In music, based on a musical mode. In logic or philosophy, related to possibility, necessity, or probability. A type of fabric made partly or wholly from regenerated beech tree cellulose.
sindhiMeaning: طريقي يا انداز سان لاڳاپيل، گرامر ۾ معاون فعل سان لاڳاپيل، موسيقي جي راڳي انداز سان لاڳاپيل، امڪان يا ضرورت سان لاڳاپيل، بيچ جي وڻ جي فائبر مان ٺهيل ڪپڙو
examples: You should learn how modal verbs are used in English grammar. The singer performed a beautiful modal melody. The jacket is made from soft modal fabric. The philosopher discussed modal logic in his lecture. Can, could, may, might, must, shall, should, will and would are all modal verbs.

englishMeaning: A source of many unexpected troubles or difficulties. Something that seems harmless at first but releases countless problems once it is opened or started. An action or decision that creates complications which cannot be undone. In Greek mythology, the container that Pandora opened, releasing all the evils into the world.
urduMeaning: مصیبتوں کا پٹارا، ایسا کام جو شروع ہوتے ہی بے شمار مسائل پیدا کر دے، بظاہر بے ضرر مگر حقیقت میں خطرناک معاملہ، ایسا فیصلہ جس کے نتائج واپس نہ ہو سکیں، یونانی دیومالائی کہانی کا وہ صندوق جس سے تمام برائیاں نکلیں
antonyms: Blessing, Remedy, Solution, Relief, Safeguard, Simplicity, Order, Calm
synonyms: Can of worms, Hornet's nest, Minefield, Source of trouble, Complication, Quagmire, Trigger, Floodgate
sindhiMeaning: مصيبتن جو دروازو، اهڙو ڪم جيڪو شروع ٿيڻ کان پوءِ بيشمار مسئلا پيدا ڪري، مٿاڇري تي بي ضرر پر حقيقت ۾ خطرناڪ معاملو، اهڙو فيصلو جنهن کي واپس نه ٿو ڪري سگهجي، يوناني آکاڻي ۾ اهو دٻو جنهن مان سڀ برايون نڪتيون
examples: Investigating the old accounts opened a Pandora's box of financial problems. He warned that changing the law could open a Pandora's box. Her simple question turned out to be a Pandora's box for the whole family. The report opened a Pandora's box of complaints against the department.

urduMeaning: کسی مضبوط شخص یا چیز کی چھوٹی مگر خطرناک کمزوری، وہ واحد نقطہ جہاں سے شکست ممکن ہو، پوشیدہ خامی جو سب کچھ تباہ کر دے، یونانی دیومالا میں اکلیز کی ایڑی جو اس کی واحد کمزوری تھی
examples: Overconfidence has always been his Achilles' heel. Poor defence is the Achilles' heel of this otherwise strong team. Her impatience proved to be the Achilles' heel of an excellent plan. The weak battery is the Achilles' heel of this smartphone.
englishMeaning: A small but serious weakness in a person or thing that is otherwise strong. A single vulnerable point that can cause complete failure. A hidden flaw that makes someone easy to defeat. In Greek mythology, the only part of the hero Achilles' body where he could be wounded.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن مضبوط شيءِ يا ماڻهوءَ ۾ لڪل ننڍڙي پر خطرناڪ ڪمزوري، اهو نقطو جتان ماڻهو آسانيءَ سان شڪست کائي سگهي، لڪل خامي جيڪا سڄي ڪم کي تباهه ڪري ڇڏي، يوناني ڪهاڻيءَ ۾ اکليز جي کڙي جيڪا سندس واحد ڪمزوري هئي
antonyms: Strength, Strong point, Advantage, Forte, Asset, Merit, Power, Invulnerability
synonyms: Weak point, Vulnerability, Weakness, Flaw, Soft spot, Shortcoming, Frailty, Drawback

examples: Rebuilding the bridge in one month was a Herculean task. She made a Herculean effort to finish her thesis on time. The rescue workers showed Herculean strength during the flood. Cleaning the entire warehouse alone proved Herculean.
englishMeaning: Requiring very great strength, effort, or determination. Extremely difficult and demanding. Unusually large or powerful in size or force. Relating to Hercules, the hero of Greek mythology famous for his enormous strength.
synonyms: Arduous, Gruelling, Strenuous, Formidable, Mighty, Colossal, Demanding, Laborious, Tough
sindhiMeaning: تمام گهڻي طاقت يا محنت جي ضرورت وارو، انتهائي ڏکيو ۽ مشڪل ڪم، غير معمولي طاقتور يا وڏو، هرڪيوليز جهڙو زبردست طاقت وارو
antonyms: Easy, Simple, Effortless, Light, Trivial, Manageable, Undemanding, Weak
urduMeaning: بہت زیادہ طاقت یا محنت کا متقاضی، انتہائی مشکل اور کٹھن، غیر معمولی طور پر طاقتور یا بڑا، ہرکیولیس جیسی زبردست قوت والا

antonyms: Confuse, Obscure, Complicate, Hide, Conceal, Mystify, Cloud, Muddle
synonyms: Clarify, Explain, Illuminate, Elucidate, Reveal, Explicate, Shed light on, Clear up
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ڳالهه کي واضح ڪرڻ، نئين معلومات ڏئي معاملو سمجهائڻ، لڪل حقيقتون ظاهر ڪرڻ، ڪنهن واقعي جو سبب يا مطلب سمجهائڻ
urduMeaning: کسی بات کو واضح کرنا، نئی معلومات فراہم کر کے معاملہ سمجھانا، پوشیدہ حقائق ظاہر کرنا، کسی واقعے کی وجہ یا مطلب واضح کرنا
examples: The new documents throw light on the causes of the accident. Can you throw light on why the meeting was cancelled? Her research throws light on an ignored period of history. The witness threw light on what happened that night.
englishMeaning: To make something clearer or easier to understand. To provide new information that explains a situation. To reveal facts that were previously hidden or confusing. To help explain the cause or meaning of an event.

sindhiMeaning: وڏي رقم کٽڻ، اوچتو وڏي ڪاميابي يا خوش نصيبي ملڻ، بلڪل اهو ئي ملي وڃڻ جيڪو گهربل هو، ننڍي ڪوشش مان وڏو فائدو حاصل ڪرڻ
examples: He hit the jackpot when his small business went international. She hit the jackpot with her very first novel. They hit the jackpot by buying that land before the prices rose. We hit the jackpot when we found this flat at such a low rent.
antonyms: Lose out, Fail, Miss out, Come up empty, Suffer loss, Flop, Bomb, Fall short
urduMeaning: بڑی رقم جیت جانا، اچانک زبردست کامیابی یا خوش قسمتی ملنا، بالکل مطلوبہ چیز مل جانا، معمولی کوشش سے بڑا فائدہ حاصل کرنا
englishMeaning: To win a large amount of money, especially suddenly. To have great and unexpected success or good luck. To find exactly what one needs or wants. To gain a very large reward from a small effort or chance.
synonyms: Strike gold, Strike it rich, Win big, Succeed, Prosper, Luck out, Score, Triumph

sindhiMeaning: سٺي نتيجي جي اميد ڪرڻ، ڪنهن لاءِ خير جي دعا يا سٺي نصيب جي خواهش ڪرڻ، نتيجي جو انتظار ڪندي اميد رکڻ، خوش نصيبيءَ لاءِ آڱريون هڪ ٻئي مٿان رکڻ جو اشارو
synonyms: Hope for the best, Wish for luck, Pray, Stay hopeful, Cross one's fingers, Await hopefully
urduMeaning: اچھے نتیجے کی امید رکھنا، کسی کے لیے نیک خواہش یا خوش قسمتی مانگنا، نتیجے کے انتظار میں پُرامید رہنا، خوش قسمتی کے لیے انگلیاں ایک دوسرے پر رکھنے کا اشارہ
englishMeaning: To hope strongly that something good will happen. To wish for good luck for oneself or someone else. To express hopeful anticipation while waiting for a result. A superstitious gesture of crossing one finger over another to bring good fortune.
antonyms: Despair, Give up, Lose hope, Doubt, Expect the worst, Resign
examples: Keep your fingers crossed for my interview tomorrow. We are keeping our fingers crossed that the weather stays clear. She kept her fingers crossed while the results were announced. Let's keep our fingers crossed and hope for the best.

sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کي جلدي ۽ مڪمل طور محبت ۾ مبتلا ڪرڻ، پنهنجي دلڪشيءَ سان ڪنهن کي بيحد متاثر ڪرڻ، ڪنهن کي جوش ۽ واکاڻ سان مغلوب ڪري ڇڏڻ، ڪنهن کي اوچتو زمين تان کڻي وٺڻ
englishMeaning: To make someone fall in love very quickly and completely. To impress or charm a person so much that they lose all resistance. To overwhelm someone with excitement or admiration. To lift someone physically off the ground in a sudden movement.
examples: He swept her off her feet within a few weeks of meeting. Her performance swept the audience off their feet. The charming guide swept the tourists off their feet. He lifted the child and swept her off her feet playfully.
urduMeaning: کسی کو بہت جلد اور مکمل طور پر محبت میں مبتلا کر دینا، اپنی دلکشی سے کسی کو بے حد متاثر کرنا، جوش اور تعریف سے کسی کو مغلوب کر دینا، کسی کو اچانک زمین سے اٹھا لینا
antonyms: Repel, Bore, Disgust, Put off, Disappoint, Alienate, Underwhelm
synonyms: Enchant, Captivate, Charm, Enthral, Bowl over, Dazzle, Win over, Fascinate

sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن سان گڏ هليو وڃڻ، خاص طور تي بنا دعوت جي ساڻ ٿي وڃڻ، ڪنهن جي پٺيان پٺيان هلڻ، اهڙو ماڻهو جيڪو هميشه ٻين سان گڏ لڳو رهي
examples: Do you mind if I tag along to the market? My younger brother always tags along when I meet my friends. She tagged along with the team to the tournament. He was happy to tag along rather than stay at home.
antonyms: Lead, Stay behind, Leave, Separate, Depart, Go alone, Withdraw
urduMeaning: کسی کے ساتھ چل پڑنا، خاص طور پر بغیر بلائے ساتھ ہو لینا، کسی کے پیچھے پیچھے چلنا، ایسا شخص جو ہمیشہ دوسروں کے ساتھ لگا رہے
englishMeaning: To go somewhere with someone, especially without being invited. To accompany another person as a companion or follower. To follow closely behind a group or individual. A person who habitually follows others around.
synonyms: Accompany, Follow, Join, Trail, Come along, Shadow, Attend, Go with

englishMeaning: To share interesting gossip or private information. To reveal the details of a secret or scandal. To tell someone the latest news about people they know. An informal invitation to disclose everything one knows about a situation.
urduMeaning: دلچسپ یا خفیہ خبر سنانا، کسی راز یا اسکینڈل کی تفصیل بتانا، جان پہچان والوں کی تازہ خبریں سنانا، سب کچھ کھول کر بتانے کی غیر رسمی فرمائش
examples: Come on, spill the tea about last night's party. She finally spilled the tea about her new job. Everyone gathered around her to hear her spill the tea. He refused to spill the tea about his friend's engagement.
antonyms: Keep quiet, Withhold, Conceal, Hide, Keep a secret, Hold back, Stay silent
sindhiMeaning: ڳجهي يا دلچسپ خبر ٻڌائڻ، ڪنهن راز يا اسڪينڊل جا تفصيل ظاهر ڪرڻ، ماڻهن بابت تازيون خبرون ٻڌائڻ، سڀ ڪجهه کولي ٻڌائڻ جي غير رسمي گذارش
synonyms: Gossip, Dish the dirt, Reveal, Disclose, Divulge, Blab, Tell all, Let slip

antonyms: Closed, Shut, Sealed, Locked, Fastened, Bolted
urduMeaning: تھوڑا سا کھلا، پوری طرح بند نہیں، دروازے یا کھڑکی کا نیم وا ہونا، ہلکا سا کھلا ہوا، جان بوجھ کر تھوڑا کھلا چھوڑا ہوا
synonyms: Half-open, Partly open, Unclosed, Open, Unlatched, Gaping slightly
sindhiMeaning: ٿورو کليل، پورو بند نه ٿيل، دروازي يا دري جو اڌ کليل هجڻ، ٿوري وٿي سان کليل، ڄاڻي واڻي ٿورو کليل ڇڏيل
englishMeaning: Slightly open, not fully closed. Partly open, as of a door or window. In a position that leaves a small gap. Left open just a little, often on purpose.
examples: She left the door ajar so the cat could come in. The window was ajar and cold air filled the room. He noticed the gate standing ajar late at night. Please keep the door ajar while the paint dries.
The suspect had a solid alibi for the night of the robbery. Her colleagues confirmed his alibi. He always has an alibi for arriving late. The lawyer alibied his client with security footage.
sindhiMeaning: اهو ثبوت ته ڏوهه وقت ماڻهو ڪنهن ٻئي هنڌ موجود هو، غيرحاضريءَ جو دعويٰ يا ثبوت، الزام کان بچڻ لاءِ بهانو، ڪنهن جي بچاءَ لاءِ عذر پيش ڪرڻ
