examples: Everyone in the office knew he was a brown noser. She refused to become a brown noser just to get promoted. The team disliked the brown noser who agreed with every order. Being a brown noser rarely earns real respect.
englishMeaning: A person who flatters others, especially superiors, to gain advantage. Someone who behaves in an insincerely obedient way to win favour. An offensive informal term for a shameless flatterer.
urduMeaning: وہ شخص جو فائدے کے لیے دوسروں، خاص طور پر افسروں کی خوشامد کرے، فائدہ حاصل کرنے کے لیے جھوٹی فرمانبرداری دکھانے والا، بے شرم چاپلوس کے لیے استعمال ہونے والا غیر رسمی اور طنزیہ لفظ
antonyms: Critic, Straight talker, Independent thinker, Dissenter, Honest person, Rebel

synonyms: Internet troll, Online ranter, Armchair critic, Troll, Cyberbully, Loudmouth
urduMeaning: وہ شخص جو انٹرنیٹ پر جارحانہ یا گالم گلوچ والے تبصرے کرے مگر حقیقی زندگی میں سامنا کرنے سے کترائے، آن لائن بہادر لیکن آمنے سامنے خاموش رہنے والا، انٹرنیٹ پر بکواس کرنے والے کے لیے طنزیہ غیر رسمی لفظ
sindhiMeaning: اهو ماڻهو جيڪو انٽرنيٽ تي سخت يا گاريون ڏيندڙ تبصرا ڪري پر حقيقي زندگيءَ ۾ ٽڪراءَ کان لهرائي، آن لائين بهادر پر آمهون سامهون خاموش رهندڙ، انٽرنيٽ تي بڪواس ڪندڙ لاءِ ٽوڪ وارو غير رسمي لفظ
examples: He is just a keyboard warrior who never speaks up in meetings. The post attracted dozens of keyboard warriors within an hour. Keyboard warriors filled the comment section with insults. Ignore the keyboard warriors and focus on real feedback.
englishMeaning: A person who makes aggressive or abusive comments online while avoiding confrontation in real life. Someone who argues bravely on the internet but is passive in person. An informal, disapproving term for an internet ranter.
antonyms: Peacemaker, Quiet observer, Real-life activist, Diplomat, Supporter, Encourager

sindhiMeaning: بهادر ۽ تجربيڪار جنگجو، خاص ڪري پراڻي دور جو، جنگ ۾ وڙهندڙ سپاهي، ڪنهن مقصد يا نظريي لاءِ ثابت قدميءَ سان وڙهندڙ ماڻهو، مشڪلاتن جو دليريءَ سان مقابلو ڪندڙ
englishMeaning: A brave and experienced fighter, especially in past times. A soldier engaged in war or battle. A person who fights determinedly for a cause or belief. Someone who shows great courage in facing hardship.
urduMeaning: بہادر اور تجربہ کار جنگجو، خاص طور پر قدیم زمانے کا، جنگ میں لڑنے والا سپاہی، کسی مقصد یا نظریے کے لیے ثابت قدمی سے لڑنے والا شخص، مشکلات کا دلیری سے سامنا کرنے والا
antonyms: Pacifist, Civilian, Coward, Peacemaker, Bystander, Deserter
synonyms: Fighter, Soldier, Combatant, Champion, Crusader, Militant, Hero, Campaigner
examples: The ancient warrior was buried with his sword and shield. She is a tireless warrior for children's education. The old warrior told stories of long-forgotten battles. Cancer patients are often called warriors for their courage.

antonyms: Supporter, Optimist, Believer, Advocate, Enthusiast, Backer, Cheerleader
sindhiMeaning: اهو ماڻهو جيڪو هميشه شڪ يا مخالفت ظاهر ڪري، خيالن تي تنقيد ڪري ناڪاميءَ جي اڳڪٿي ڪندڙ، ڪنهن تجويز جي خلاف ووٽ ڏيندڙ يا ڳالهائيندڙ
englishMeaning: A person who habitually expresses doubt or opposition. Someone who criticises ideas and predicts failure. A person who votes or speaks against a proposal.
urduMeaning: وہ شخص جو ہمیشہ شک یا مخالفت ظاہر کرے، خیالات پر تنقید کر کے ناکامی کی پیش گوئی کرنے والا، کسی تجویز کے خلاف ووٹ دینے یا بولنے والا
examples: The naysayers said the project would never succeed. She ignored the naysayers and opened her own shop. Every new invention faces its share of naysayers. He answered the naysayers with solid results.
synonyms: Critic, Pessimist, Doubter, Skeptic, Detractor, Cynic, Opponent, Faultfinder

urduMeaning: وہ شخص جو چھوٹی اور غیر اہم باتوں میں نقص نکالے، معمولی باتوں پر حد سے زیادہ تنقید کرنے والا، چھوٹی چھوٹی باتوں میں سختی سے درستی کا مطالبہ کرنے والا
englishMeaning: A person who finds fault with small and unimportant details. Someone who criticises trivial matters excessively. A person who insists on petty accuracy.
sindhiMeaning: اهو ماڻهو جيڪو ننڍين ۽ غير اهم ڳالهين ۾ نقص ڪڍي، معمولي ڳالهين تي حد کان وڌيڪ تنقيد ڪندڙ، ننڍڙين ڳالهين ۾ سختيءَ سان درستگي گهرندڙ
antonyms: Easygoing person, Tolerant person, Big-picture thinker, Approver, Praiser
synonyms: Faultfinder, Pedant, Quibbler, Hair-splitter, Perfectionist, Carper, Critic
examples: The editor was a nitpicker who questioned every comma. Nobody enjoys working with a constant nitpicker. He is such a nitpicker about spelling mistakes. A nitpicker can slow down a whole meeting.

englishMeaning: A person who speaks quietly and unclearly. Someone whose words are hard to understand because they are not spoken distinctly. A person who mutters under their breath.
antonyms: Orator, Clear speaker, Announcer, Articulate speaker, Shouter
sindhiMeaning: اهو ماڻهو جيڪو ماٺ ۽ نامعلوم انداز ۾ ڳالهائي، جنهن جا لفظ صاف نه هجڻ ڪري سمجهه ۾ نه اچن، پنهنجو پاڻ سان دل ئي دل ۾ ڀڻڪندڙ
urduMeaning: وہ شخص جو دھیمی اور غیر واضح آواز میں بولے، جس کے الفاظ صاف نہ ہونے کی وجہ سے سمجھ نہ آئیں، اپنے آپ سے زیرِ لب بڑبڑانے والا
synonyms: Mutterer, Murmurer, Whisperer, Grumbler, Muffled speaker
examples: The teacher asked the mumbler to speak up. He is a natural mumbler, especially on the phone. As a mumbler, he often had to repeat himself. Listeners complained that the presenter was a hopeless mumbler.

englishMeaning: Unwilling to speak or reveal information. Keeping silent about something deliberately. Showing determination or disapproval by pressing the lips together.
antonyms: Talkative, Open, Forthcoming, Chatty, Communicative, Frank, Expressive
urduMeaning: بولنے یا معلومات ظاہر کرنے سے گریز کرنے والا، کسی بات کے بارے میں جان بوجھ کر خاموش رہنے والا، ہونٹ بھینچ کر ناراضی یا پختہ ارادہ ظاہر کرنے والا
examples: The company remained tight lipped about the merger. He stayed tight lipped throughout the interview. She gave a tight lipped smile and said nothing. Officials were tight lipped when asked about the report.
synonyms: Silent, Reticent, Secretive, Reserved, Uncommunicative, Guarded, Discreet, Taciturn
sindhiMeaning: ڳالهائڻ يا ڳجهه ظاهر ڪرڻ کان انڪار ڪندڙ، ڪنهن ڳالهه بابت ڄاڻي واڻي خاموش رهندڙ، چپ ڀيڪوڙي ناراضگي يا پختو ارادو ظاهر ڪندڙ

urduMeaning: وہ شخص جو پیسہ خرچ کرنے سے بہت گریز کرے، کنجوس یا بخیل شخص کے لیے غیر رسمی لفظ، حد سے زیادہ اور گھٹیا انداز میں پیسہ بچانے والا
synonyms: Miser, Skinflint, Cheapskate, Penny-pincher, Scrooge, Niggard, Hoarder
examples: He is such a tightwad that he never buys a round of tea. The tightwad refused to tip the waiter. Don't be a tightwad on your own birthday. Her uncle had a reputation as the family tightwad.
englishMeaning: A person who is very unwilling to spend money. An informal term for a stingy or miserly person. Someone who saves money in an extreme and mean way.
sindhiMeaning: اهو ماڻهو جيڪو پئسا خرچ ڪرڻ کان تمام گهڻو ڪيٻائي، ڪنجوس يا بخيل ماڻهوءَ لاءِ غير رسمي لفظ، حد کان وڌيڪ ۽ ڪميڻي انداز ۾ پئسا بچائيندڙ
antonyms: Spender, Big spender, Philanthropist, Generous person, Giver, Squanderer

englishMeaning: Unwilling to give or spend money. Mean and ungenerous in financial matters. Holding on to resources tightly.
antonyms: Generous, Openhanded, Liberal, Charitable, Lavish, Bountiful, Giving
urduMeaning: پیسہ دینے یا خرچ کرنے سے گریز کرنے والا، مالی معاملات میں کنجوس اور بخیل، وسائل کو سختی سے تھامے رکھنے والا
examples: Her close-fisted landlord refused to repair the roof. He was close-fisted with money but generous with advice. The company is close-fisted when it comes to bonuses. People found him too close-fisted to invite anywhere.
synonyms: Stingy, Miserly, Tight-fisted, Parsimonious, Mean, Frugal, Ungenerous, Grasping
sindhiMeaning: پئسا ڏيڻ يا خرچ ڪرڻ کان لهرائيندڙ، مالي معاملن ۾ ڪنجوس ۽ بخيل، وسيلن کي سختيءَ سان جهليندڙ

examples: He went fishing with his old army buddy. Each new student is given a buddy for the first week. Hey buddy, you dropped your wallet. The two boys buddied up during the summer camp.
synonyms: Friend, Pal, Mate, Companion, Comrade, Chum, Partner, Sidekick
englishMeaning: A close friend or companion. A partner assigned to work with or look after someone. An informal way of addressing a man, sometimes friendly and sometimes unfriendly. To become friendly with someone, as in buddy up.
sindhiMeaning: ويجهو دوست يا ساٿي، اهو ساٿي جيڪو گڏ ڪم ڪرڻ يا خيال رکڻ لاءِ مقرر ڪيو وڃي، ڪنهن مرد کي سڏڻ جو غير رسمي انداز جيڪو ڪڏهن دوستاڻو ته ڪڏهن ٽوڪ وارو هوندو آهي، ڪنهن سان دوستي ڪرڻ
antonyms: Enemy, Stranger, Rival, Foe, Opponent, Adversary
urduMeaning: قریبی دوست یا ساتھی، وہ ساتھی جو مل کر کام کرنے یا خیال رکھنے کے لیے مقرر کیا جائے، کسی مرد کو مخاطب کرنے کا غیر رسمی انداز جو کبھی دوستانہ اور کبھی طنزیہ ہوتا ہے، کسی سے دوستی کر لینا

antonyms: Socialite, Party-goer, Traveller, Extrovert, Adventurer, Nightlifer
sindhiMeaning: اهو ماڻهو جيڪو ٻاهر وڃڻ بدران گهر ۾ رهڻ پسند ڪري، خاموش گهريلو زندگي پسند ڪندڙ ۽ محفلن کان پري رهندڙ، اهو ساٿي جنهن سان گڏ گهر ۾ وقت گذاريو وڃي
englishMeaning: A person who prefers staying at home rather than going out. Someone who enjoys quiet domestic life and avoids socialising. A friend or companion with whom one shares a home or stays in.
examples: She is a home buddy who spends weekends reading. My brother is a home buddy and rarely goes to parties. As a home buddy, he turned his living room into a studio. They became home buddies during the long rainy season.
synonyms: Homebody, Stay-at-home, Housebound person, Introvert, Domestic type, Recluse
urduMeaning: وہ شخص جو باہر جانے کے بجائے گھر میں رہنا پسند کرے، پرسکون گھریلو زندگی پسند کرنے والا اور محفلوں سے دور رہنے والا، وہ ساتھی جس کے ساتھ گھر میں وقت گزارا جائے

synonyms: Cowardly, Timid, Fearful, Faint-hearted, Spineless, Craven, Nervous, Gutless
sindhiMeaning: جلدي ڊڄي ويندڙ ۽ همت کان خالي، ڊڄڻو ۽ خطرو کڻڻ کان ڪيٻائيندڙ، خطري يا مشڪل سامهون بزدل
examples: He was too chicken hearted to complain about the mistake. Don't be chicken hearted; just tell her the truth. The chicken hearted soldier fled at the first shot. She called him chicken hearted for avoiding the interview.
englishMeaning: Easily frightened and lacking courage. Timid and unwilling to take risks. Cowardly in the face of danger or difficulty.
antonyms: Brave, Courageous, Bold, Fearless, Daring, Valiant, Heroic, Gutsy
urduMeaning: جلدی ڈر جانے والا اور ہمت سے عاری، بزدل اور خطرہ مول لینے سے گریز کرنے والا، خطرے یا مشکل کے سامنے بودا

examples: The police promised to end the thuggery on the city streets. Local shopkeepers complained about the thuggery of a small gang. Such thuggery has no place in a peaceful society. The report described years of political thuggery in the region.
englishMeaning: Violent, brutal, or criminal behaviour, especially by gangs or organised groups. The use of physical force and intimidation to frighten or control other people. Rough, lawless conduct that shows no respect for order or human dignity. Acts of bullying and street violence carried out openly and repeatedly.
synonyms: Violence, Brutality, Hooliganism, Ruffianism, Gangsterism, Bullying, Lawlessness, Savagery, Rowdyism
antonyms: Peacefulness, Civility, Kindness, Gentleness, Lawfulness, Order, Politeness, Nonviolence
sindhiMeaning: تشدد، ظلم ۽ ڏاڍ وارو عمل، خاص ڪري ٽولين پاران ڪيل ڏنگائي ۽ ڏاڍ، ماڻهن کي ڊيڄارڻ ۽ قابو ڪرڻ لاءِ طاقت جو استعمال، قانون شڪني ۽ بدمعاشي، گنڊا گيري ۽ ڏاڍ وارو رويو
urduMeaning: غنڈہ گردی، تشدد اور بدمعاشی، خاص طور پر گروہوں کی جانب سے کیا جانے والا پرتشدد رویہ، لوگوں کو ڈرانے اور دبانے کے لیے طاقت کا استعمال، قانون شکنی اور دہشت پھیلانے والا عمل

sindhiMeaning: غير قانوني ۽ فراڊ وارو ڌنڌو ڪري پئسا ڪمائڻ، ڌمڪين، رشوت يا ٺڳي ذريعي مال حاصل ڪرڻ، منظم ڏوهه ذريعي ڪيل ڪاروبار، جائز ڪاروبار جي آڙ ۾ ڪيل غير قانوني ڪم
urduMeaning: غیر قانونی اور فریب پر مبنی کاروبار سے پیسہ کمانا، بھتہ خوری، رشوت یا دھوکہ دہی کے ذریعے مال حاصل کرنا، منظم جرائم پر مبنی کاروبار، جائز کاروبار کی آڑ میں کیے جانے والے غیر قانونی کام
antonyms: Honesty, Integrity, Fair dealing, Lawfulness, Transparency, Legitimacy
synonyms: Extortion, Fraud, Organised crime, Graft, Corruption, Blackmail, Swindling, Profiteering
examples: He was arrested on charges of racketeering and money laundering. The gang was accused of racketeering in the construction industry. Federal agents spent two years investigating the racketeering network. Racketeering damages honest businesses and public trust.
englishMeaning: The act of running a dishonest or illegal business scheme for profit. Obtaining money through fraud, extortion, bribery, or organised crime. A pattern of criminal activity carried out repeatedly by an organised group. Illegal dealings that are disguised as a legitimate business.

sindhiMeaning: گوڙ، بدنظمي ۽ ڏنگائي وارو رويو، خاص ڪري عوامي جاءِ تي، رڙيون ڪري يا جھيڙو ڪري امن خراب ڪرڻ، بي قابو ۽ بي ترتيب حرڪتون ڪرڻ جي عادت، ميڙ پاران پيدا ڪيل بدامني
antonyms: Orderliness, Discipline, Calmness, Politeness, Quietness, Decorum, Restraint
urduMeaning: شور شرابہ، بدنظمی اور ہلڑ بازی، خاص طور پر عوامی مقامات پر، چیخنے یا لڑنے سے امن خراب کرنا، بے قابو اور غیر مہذب رویہ اختیار کرنے کی عادت، ہجوم کی جانب سے پیدا کی گئی بدامنی
examples: Rowdyism at the stadium forced the referee to stop the match. The teacher warned the students against rowdyism during the trip. Police were called to control rowdyism outside the hall. Their rowdyism spoiled an otherwise pleasant evening.
synonyms: Hooliganism, Disorder, Unruliness, Boisterousness, Ruckus, Mayhem, Uproar, Turbulence
englishMeaning: Noisy, rough, and disorderly behaviour, especially in a public place. Conduct that disturbs peace through shouting, fighting, or wild activity. The habit of behaving in an unruly and uncontrolled manner in groups. Public disorder created by excited or aggressive crowds.

synonyms: I don't know, No idea, Search me, Who knows, I'm clueless, Your guess is as good as mine
examples: How did he pass the test without studying? Beats me. Beats me why she left the job so suddenly. When I asked about the missing keys, he just said, Beats me. Beats me how they finished the work so quickly.
sindhiMeaning: ڪا خبر نه آهي، مون کي ڪجهه سمجهه ۾ نٿو اچي، هي ڳالهه منهنجي سمجهه کان ٻاهر آهي، خبر ناهي ڇو ٿيو، مان بلڪل حيران آهيان
englishMeaning: An informal way of saying that you do not know the answer to something. Used to express complete puzzlement about a question or situation. A casual admission that something is beyond your understanding. Said when you cannot explain why something has happened.
antonyms: I know, I understand, I'm certain, That's clear to me, Obviously
urduMeaning: مجھے نہیں معلوم، میری سمجھ میں نہیں آتا، یہ بات میری سمجھ سے باہر ہے، خدا جانے ایسا کیوں ہوا، میں حیران ہوں

examples: Don't answer now; sleep on it and tell me tomorrow. I decided to sleep on it before signing the contract. She slept on it and changed her mind by morning. It is always wise to sleep on it before making a big purchase.
synonyms: Think it over, Mull over, Consider, Reflect on, Take time, Deliberate, Weigh up
urduMeaning: کسی فیصلے کو اگلے دن تک ٹال دینا تاکہ اچھی طرح سوچا جا سکے، جواب دینے سے پہلے سوچنے کے لیے وقت لینا، جلد بازی سے بچنے کے لیے ٹھنڈے دل سے غور کرنا، رات گزار کر فیصلہ کرنا
antonyms: Decide at once, Rush, Act impulsively, Answer immediately, Jump in
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن فيصلي کي سڀاڻي تائين ملتوي ڪرڻ ته چڱي طرح سوچي سگهجي، جواب ڏيڻ کان اڳ سوچڻ لاءِ وقت وٺڻ، جلدبازي کان بچڻ لاءِ ٺهراءُ ٿڌي دل سان ڪرڻ، رات گذارڻ کان پوءِ فيصلو ڪرڻ
englishMeaning: To delay a decision until the next day so you can think more clearly. To take extra time before giving an answer to something important. To postpone judgement in order to reflect calmly and avoid mistakes. To let time pass so that your feelings settle before you choose.

synonyms: Botch, Bungle, Mess up, Spoil, Ruin, Blunder, Mishandle, Fumble
examples: I hope I don't screw up the presentation tomorrow. He screwed up the order and sent the wrong parcel. She screwed up the letter and threw it in the bin. He screwed up his eyes against the bright sunlight.
sindhiMeaning: ڪم خراب ڪري ڇڏڻ، وڏي غلطي ڪرڻ، ڪنهن ڪم کي ايترو خراب نموني ڪرڻ جو ناڪام ٿي وڃي، ڪاغذ وغيره کي مروڙي گڏ ڪرڻ، منهن يا اکيون گھنڊ وجهي سيڪوڙڻ
englishMeaning: To make a serious mistake and spoil something. To handle a task so badly that it fails. To twist or crumple something tightly, such as paper. To tighten the eyes or face into a wrinkled expression.
antonyms: Succeed, Perfect, Manage well, Accomplish, Handle properly, Excel
urduMeaning: کام بگاڑ دینا، سنگین غلطی کرنا، کسی کام کو اس قدر خراب انداز میں کرنا کہ ناکام ہو جائے، کاغذ وغیرہ کو مروڑ کر گولا بنانا، آنکھیں یا چہرہ سکیڑنا

synonyms: Blunder, Mistake, Mess, Botch, Error, Fiasco, Mix-up, Bungle
englishMeaning: A serious mistake or badly handled situation. A failure caused by carelessness or poor judgement. An informal word for a person who often makes mistakes. A muddle or mess created by someone's error.
examples: The delay was caused by an administrative screw-up. It was a small screw-up, but the client noticed it. He apologised for the screw-up in the accounts. Losing the file was a major screw-up on my part.
urduMeaning: سنگین غلطی یا بگڑا ہوا کام، لاپرواہی کے باعث ہونے والی ناکامی، ایسا شخص جو بار بار غلطیاں کرے، غلطی سے پیدا ہونے والی گڑبڑ
sindhiMeaning: وڏي غلطي يا خراب ڪيل ڪم، لاپرواهي سبب ٿيل ناڪامي، اهڙو ماڻهو جيڪو گھڻيون غلطيون ڪري، غلطي سبب پيدا ٿيل گڙٻڙ
antonyms: Success, Achievement, Triumph, Accuracy, Perfection, Accomplishment

examples: We subscribe to two daily newspapers at home. Thousands of people subscribe to her cooking channel. I do not subscribe to the view that money brings happiness. Both partners subscribed to the agreement in front of a witness.

englishMeaning: Relating to or showing a difference between two or more things. A difference in amount, rate, or quality between comparable items. A gear system in a vehicle that lets wheels turn at different speeds. In mathematics, relating to very small differences or rates of change.

sindhiMeaning: فرق ڏيکاريندڙ يا فرق سان لاڳاپيل، ٻن شين جي وچ ۾ مقدار، شرح يا معيار جو فرق، گاڏي جو اهو گيئر نظام جيڪو ڦيٿن کي مختلف رفتار تي ڦيرائي، حسابي لحاظ کان تمام ننڍي تبديلي سان واسطو رکندڙ

antonyms: Patient, Layperson, Non-specialist

examples: The cardiologist advised him to reduce salt and fat. She was referred to a cardiologist after her chest pain. A cardiologist examined the patient's heart rhythm carefully. My uncle visits his cardiologist every three months.

antonyms: Patient, Layperson, Non-specialist
sindhiMeaning: گڙدن جو ماهر ڊاڪٽر، گڙدن جي بيمارين ۽ ناڪامي جو علاج ڪندڙ ماهر، ڊائيلاسز ۽ گڙدي جي مَنتقلي جي سنڀال ڪندڙ ماهر، نيفرالاجي جو ماهر طبيب

examples: The nephrologist put him on regular dialysis. A nephrologist should review these kidney test reports. She became a nephrologist after years of study. The nephrologist explained the risks of the transplant.
urduMeaning: گردوں کا ماہر ڈاکٹر، گردوں کی بیماریوں اور ناکامی کا علاج کرنے والا ماہر، ڈائیلاسز اور گردے کی پیوندکاری کی دیکھ بھال کرنے والا ماہر، نیفرولوجی کا ماہر طبیب

englishMeaning: A doctor who specialises in bones, joints, muscles, and ligaments. A surgeon who treats fractures, deformities, and spinal problems. A specialist who performs joint replacement and bone surgery. A physician trained in the branch of medicine called orthopaedics.
urduMeaning: ہڈیوں، جوڑوں اور پٹھوں کا ماہر ڈاکٹر، ٹوٹی ہڈیوں، ٹیڑھ پن اور ریڑھ کی ہڈی کے مسائل کا علاج کرنے والا سرجن، جوڑ بدلنے اور ہڈیوں کے آپریشن کرنے والا ماہر، آرتھوپیڈکس کا ماہر طبیب

englishMeaning: A doctor who specialises in mental, emotional, and behavioural disorders. A medical expert who diagnoses and treats depression, anxiety, and psychosis. A specialist who can prescribe medicines as well as recommend therapy. A physician trained in the branch of medicine called psychiatry.
urduMeaning: ذہنی، جذباتی اور رویے کی بیماریوں کا ماہر ڈاکٹر، ڈپریشن، بے چینی اور ذہنی امراض کی تشخیص اور علاج کرنے والا ماہر، دوا تجویز کرنے اور تھراپی کا مشورہ دینے والا ماہر، نفسیاتی امراض کا ماہر طبیب

examples: Public sentiment has turned against the new tax. I share your sentiments about the decision. The letter was full of warm sentiment. Market sentiment improved after the announcement.
englishMeaning: A view, opinion, or attitude about something. A feeling or emotion, especially a tender one. General feeling or mood shared by a group of people. Exaggerated or delicate emotion expressed in words.
sindhiMeaning: راءِ، خيال، نظريو، احساس يا جذبو، نرم جذبو، ماڻهن جي عام سوچ يا مزاج، لفظن ۾ ظاهر ڪيل جذبو

englishMeaning: In a way that gives moral advice in a short, self-important manner. In a manner full of brief, weighty sayings or maxims.
examples: He spoke sententiously about the duties of youth. The old man nodded sententiously and quoted a proverb. She sententiously reminded us to save money. The article ends rather sententiously.
antonyms: Modestly, Casually, Lightly, Humbly, Informally
urduMeaning: نصیحت آمیز انداز میں، مختصر اور بامعنی طور پر، خود کو دانا ظاہر کرتے ہوئے، ضرب الامثال کے انداز میں بولتے ہوئے
synonyms: Moralistically, Pompously, Preachily, Pithily, Solemnly, Self-righteously
sindhiMeaning: نصيحت واري ڍنگ سان، مختصر ۽ وزنائتي انداز ۾، پاڻ کي داناءُ ظاهر ڪندي، ضرب المثلن واري نموني ڳالهائيندي

synonyms: Moralistic, Pompous, Preachy, Pithy, Aphoristic, Self-righteous, Terse
antonyms: Humble, Modest, Rambling, Verbose, Casual, Unpretentious
urduMeaning: نصیحت کرنے والا، خود کو دانا سمجھنے والا، کم الفاظ میں زیادہ مطلب بیان کرنے والا، ضرب الامثال سے بھرپور کلام
sindhiMeaning: نصيحت ڪندڙ، پاڻ کي داناءُ سمجهندڙ، ٿورن لفظن ۾ گهڻو مطلب بيان ڪندڙ، ضرب المثلن سان ڀرپور ڳالهائيندڙ
englishMeaning: Given to moralizing in a pompous or self-satisfied way. Full of short, pithy sayings that sound wise. Expressing much meaning in few words.
examples: His sententious remarks annoyed the younger staff. The essay is short but sententious. She disliked his sententious tone. A sententious style can quickly tire the reader.

sindhiMeaning: جذبن تي هلندڙ ماڻهو، نرم دل شخص، جلد جذباتي ٿي ويندڙ، ماضيءَ جي يادن ۾ گم رهندڙ
urduMeaning: جذبات پر چلنے والا شخص، نرم دل انسان، جلد جذباتی ہو جانے والا، ماضی کی یادوں میں کھویا رہنے والا
examples: He is a sentimentalist who keeps every old letter. Only a sentimentalist would call those days perfect. She admits to being something of a sentimentalist. The poet was a romantic and a sentimentalist.
antonyms: Realist, Pragmatist, Cynic, Rationalist, Materialist
englishMeaning: A person who is guided by feelings rather than reason. Someone who is easily moved by tender emotions or nostalgia, sometimes excessively.
synonyms: Romantic, Dreamer, Idealist, Softie, Nostalgic, Emotionalist

sindhiMeaning: سزا ٻڌائيندڙ، فيصلو ڪندڙ جج يا مئجسٽريٽ، عدالت ۾ سزا جو اعلان ڪندڙ شخص
examples: The sentencer must consider all the circumstances of the case. Guidelines help every sentencer apply the law consistently. As sentencer, the judge explained her reasons in open court. The sentencer reduced the term because of the guilty plea.
antonyms: Defendant, Accused, Offender, Pardoner, Acquitter
urduMeaning: سزا سنانے والا، فیصلہ کرنے والا جج یا مجسٹریٹ، عدالت میں سزا کا اعلان کرنے والا شخص
synonyms: Judge, Magistrate, Adjudicator, Arbiter, Justice, Decider
englishMeaning: A person, especially a judge or magistrate, who passes a sentence on a convicted offender. One who decides and pronounces the punishment in a court of law.

antonyms: Non-geographical, Abstract, Placeless, Unrelated, Theoretical
sindhiMeaning: جاگرافيءَ سان لاڳاپيل، ڪنهن علائقي جي زميني بناوت، محل وقوع، موسم يا آبادي سان تعلق رکندڙ
synonyms: Topographical, Regional, Territorial, Spatial, Physical, Locational, Environmental
englishMeaning: Relating to geography or to the physical features of an area. Concerned with the location, land, climate, or population of a place.
examples: The region has great geographical importance. Geographical barriers made travel difficult. The survey covers a wide geographical area. Rainfall varies according to geographical conditions.
urduMeaning: جغرافیہ سے متعلق، کسی علاقے کی زمینی ساخت، محلِ وقوع، موسم یا آبادی سے تعلق رکھنے والا

antonyms: Abstractly, Theoretically, Non-spatially, Culturally
synonyms: Regionally, Territorially, Spatially, Locationally, Topographically, Physically
englishMeaning: In terms of geography or physical location. According to the arrangement of places on the earth's surface.
sindhiMeaning: جاگرافيائي لحاظ کان، محل وقوع جي حساب سان، زمين تي جڳهه جي بناوت مطابق
examples: The two towns are geographically close but culturally different. Geographically, the province is mostly desert. The team is geographically spread across four countries. Rainfall is geographically uneven in the region.
urduMeaning: جغرافیائی اعتبار سے، محلِ وقوع کے لحاظ سے، زمین پر مقام کی ترتیب کے مطابق
جغرافیائی، جغرافیہ سے متعلق، کسی علاقے کی حدود، ساخت یا مقام سے وابستہ، زمین پر محلِ وقوع پر مبنی
examples: The company divides its sales into geographic regions. Geographic data is stored in a digital map. The island's geographic isolation protected its wildlife. Prices differ by geographic area.
sindhiMeaning: جاگرافيائي، جاگرافيءَ سان واسطو رکندڙ، ڪنهن علائقي جي حدن، بناوت يا جڳهه سان لاڳاپيل، زمين تي محل وقوع تي ٻڌل
antonyms: Non-geographic, Abstract, Placeless, Theoretical
synonyms: Geographical, Regional, Territorial, Spatial, Physical, Locational
englishMeaning: Relating to geography; describing the physical features, boundaries, or location of an area. Based on position on the earth's surface.

sindhiMeaning: جاگرافي، ڌرتيءَ جي سطح، ان جي بناوت، موسم، وسيلن ۽ آبادي جو مطالعو، ڪنهن هنڌ جي زميني بناوت ۽ خاصيتون، ڪنهن شيءِ جي عام ترتيب
examples: She teaches geography at a secondary school. The geography of the valley makes farming difficult. We studied the geography of South Asia this term. He explained the geography of the political parties.
antonyms: Astronomy, Abstraction, Placelessness, Disorder
urduMeaning: جغرافیہ، زمین کی سطح، اس کی ساخت، موسم، وسائل اور آبادی کا مطالعہ، کسی جگہ کی زمینی ساخت اور خصوصیات، کسی چیز کی عمومی ترتیب
synonyms: Topography, Terrain, Landscape, Earth science, Physical features, Layout, Environment
englishMeaning: The study of the earth's surface, its physical features, climate, resources, and populations. The physical layout and characteristics of a particular place. The general arrangement or structure of something.
Relating to geology; concerning the structure of the earth, its rocks, and their history. Occurring over very long periods of time, as in the formation of rocks and landforms.
examples: A geological survey was carried out before drilling. These cliffs are of great geological interest. Mountains form over geological time. Geological faults run beneath the city.
antonyms: Biological, Atmospheric, Artificial, Man-made, Chemical
urduMeaning: ارضیاتی، زمین کی ساخت، چٹانوں اور ان کی تاریخ سے متعلق، بہت طویل عرصے میں ہونے والی زمینی تبدیلیوں سے وابستہ
synonyms: Earth-related, Rock-related, Mineralogical, Tectonic, Terrestrial, Stratigraphic
sindhiMeaning: ارضياتي، زمين جي بناوت، پٿرن ۽ انهن جي تاريخ سان لاڳاپيل، تمام ڊگهي عرصي ۾ ٿيندڙ زميني تبديلين سان تعلق رکندڙ

englishMeaning: From the point of view of geology. In terms of the earth's structure, rocks, or long-term physical processes.
examples: Geologically, the region is still very young. The area is geologically unstable. The two ranges are geologically related. Geologically speaking, the change happened quickly.
antonyms: Biologically, Chemically, Artificially, Atmospherically
synonyms: Structurally, Terrestrially, Tectonically, Mineralogically, Physically
urduMeaning: ارضیاتی اعتبار سے، زمین کی ساخت اور چٹانوں کے لحاظ سے، طویل زمینی مدت کے پیمانے پر
sindhiMeaning: ارضياتي لحاظ کان، زمين جي بناوت ۽ پٿرن جي حساب سان، ڊگهي زميني عرصي جي پيماني تي

synonyms: Positioning, Location tracking, GPS location, Place identification, Mapping, Coordinates
antonyms: Anonymity, Concealment, Untraceability, Location hiding
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ماڻهوءَ، ڊوائيس يا شيءِ جي حقيقي زميني جڳهه معلوم ڪرڻ، محل وقوع جي نشاندهي، ويڪرائي ۽ ڊيگهه جي ماپ تي ٻڌل مقام جي ڄاڻ
examples: The app uses geolocation to find nearby restaurants. Please allow geolocation access in your browser. Geolocation data helped the rescue team reach the hikers. Some websites restrict content by geolocation.
urduMeaning: کسی شخص، آلے یا چیز کے حقیقی زمینی مقام کی نشاندہی، محلِ وقوع کا تعین، طول و عرض بلد پر مبنی مقام کی معلومات
englishMeaning: The identification of the real-world geographic position of a person, device, or object. The data that describes such a position, usually as latitude and longitude.
A mass of rocks, gravel, and soil carried and deposited by a glacier. A ridge or mound of such material left behind when a glacier melts.
synonyms: Debris, Till, Glacial deposit, Ridge, Mound, Drift, Rubble
urduMeaning: گلیشیئر کے ساتھ بہہ کر آنے والے پتھروں، بجری اور مٹی کا ڈھیر، برف پگھلنے کے بعد چھوڑا گیا پتھروں کا ٹیلہ
antonyms: Bedrock, Plain, Hollow, Basin, Solid ground
examples: A long moraine marks the edge of the ancient glacier. The lake is held back by a natural moraine. Climbers crossed the loose moraine slowly. Geologists dated the moraine to the last ice age.
sindhiMeaning: برفاني گليشيئر سان گڏ لڏي ايندڙ پٿرن، ڪنڪر ۽ مٽيءَ جو ڍير، گليشيئر جي پگهرڻ بعد ڇڏيل مٽيءَ ۽ پٿرن جو ڍڳو

antonyms: Stable, Calm, Minor, Insignificant, Steady, Slight
synonyms: Earthquake-related, Tectonic, Vibrational, Tremor-related, Momentous, Earth-shaking, Dramatic
urduMeaning: زلزلے سے متعلق، زمین کی لرزش سے تعلق رکھنے والا، زلزلہ ناپنے والا، نہایت بڑا اور اچانک تبدیلی لانے والا (اثر)
sindhiMeaning: زلزلي سان لاڳاپيل، ڌرتيءَ جي لرزش سان تعلق رکندڙ، زلزلي جي ماپ ڪندڙ، تمام وڏو ۽ اوچتو تبديلي آڻيندڙ (اثر)
examples: The building was designed to resist seismic activity. Seismic waves were recorded far from the epicentre. The election brought a seismic shift in policy. Engineers studied the seismic risk of the valley.
englishMeaning: Relating to earthquakes or vibrations of the earth's crust. Caused by or measuring such vibrations. Very great in size or effect; causing sudden and dramatic change.

urduMeaning: ایک موٹا اور مضبوط کپڑا جس کی سطح مخمل جیسی ہوتی ہے، قالین اور کرسیوں کے غلاف کے لیے استعمال ہونے والا کپڑا، بس اور ٹرین کی نشستوں کا کپڑا
examples: The train seats were covered in blue moquette. Moquette wears well in busy public spaces. She chose a patterned moquette for the armchairs. The old bus still has its original moquette.
englishMeaning: A thick, hard-wearing fabric with a velvet-like pile, used for carpets and upholstery. Material of this kind commonly used to cover seats in buses and trains.
sindhiMeaning: هڪ ٿلهو ۽ مضبوط ڪپڙو جنهن جي مٿاڇري مخمل جهڙي ٿيندي آهي، قالين ۽ ڪرسين جي غلاف لاءِ استعمال ٿيندڙ ڪپڙو، بس ۽ ٽرين جي سيٽن جو ڪپڙو
antonyms: Leather, Plastic, Bare surface, Thin cloth
synonyms: Upholstery fabric, Velvet cloth, Pile fabric, Plush, Carpeting, Textile

examples: Water flows down the headrace to the turbine. The old mill's headrace has been restored. Silt had blocked the headrace after the flood. Engineers widened the headrace to increase power output.
synonyms: Millrace, Channel, Conduit, Flume, Watercourse, Feeder canal
sindhiMeaning: اهو نار يا پائيپ جيڪو پاڻي کي چڪي، ٽربائن يا واٽر ويل تائين پهچائي، پاڻيءَ جي مٿئين وهڪري وارو حصو
antonyms: Tailrace, Outlet, Drain, Discharge channel
urduMeaning: وہ نالی یا پائپ جو پانی کو چکی، ٹربائن یا واٹر وہیل تک پہنچاتا ہے، پانی کے بالائی بہاؤ کا حصہ
englishMeaning: The channel or pipe that carries water to a water wheel, mill, or turbine. The upstream part of a watercourse leading to the point where the water is used.

sindhiMeaning: باقاعده افتتاح ڪرڻ، ڪنهن نئين ڪم يا دور جي شروعات ڪرڻ، تقريب سان نئين عمارت يا خدمت جو آغاز ڪرڻ، ڪنهن کي عهدي جو حلف ڏيارڻ
englishMeaning: To formally begin or introduce a new project, policy, or period. To open a new building or service with a formal ceremony. To admit someone formally to an official position or office.
urduMeaning: باقاعدہ افتتاح کرنا، کسی نئے کام یا دور کا آغاز کرنا، تقریب کے ساتھ نئی عمارت یا سروس کا افتتاح کرنا، کسی کو عہدے کا حلف دلانا
synonyms: Launch, Initiate, Open, Begin, Institute, Establish, Commence, Install, Introduce
antonyms: Close, End, Terminate, Conclude, Finish, Dissolve, Remove
examples: The mayor will inaugurate the new hospital next week. His victory inaugurated a period of reform. The president was inaugurated in a simple ceremony. They inaugurated the bus service on Monday.

urduMeaning: افتتاحی، کسی چیز کے آغاز سے متعلق، پہلی بار ہونے والا، افتتاحی تقریب سے وابستہ، افتتاحی تقریر
examples: The team won its inaugural match of the season. She gave a short inaugural address. The inaugural issue of the magazine sold out. Guests attended the inaugural dinner.
sindhiMeaning: افتتاحي، ڪنهن شيءِ جي شروعات سان لاڳاپيل، پهرين ڀيري ٿيندڙ، افتتاحي تقريب سان تعلق رکندڙ، افتتاحي تقرير
synonyms: First, Opening, Initial, Introductory, Maiden, Founding, Launching
antonyms: Final, Closing, Last, Concluding, Farewell
englishMeaning: Marking the beginning of something, especially an official term or series. Relating to a formal opening ceremony. A speech given at such a ceremony.

urduMeaning: افتتاح، کسی کام یا عمارت کا باقاعدہ آغاز، حلف برداری کی تقریب، نئے دور یا نظام کا آغاز
examples: The inauguration of the bridge drew a large crowd. Thousands watched the president's inauguration. Rain delayed the inauguration of the new park. The inauguration marked a new chapter for the university.
antonyms: Closure, Termination, Ending, Conclusion, Dismissal
sindhiMeaning: افتتاح، ڪنهن ڪم يا عمارت جي باقاعده شروعات، حلف برداري جي تقريب، نئين دور يا نظام جو آغاز
synonyms: Opening, Launch, Initiation, Commencement, Installation, Induction, Dedication
englishMeaning: The formal beginning or opening of something, marked by a ceremony. The ceremony at which a person is admitted to an official position. The start of a new period or system.

sindhiMeaning: مناسب، موزون، صورتحال مطابق درست، ڪنهن جي شيءِ بنا اجازت پنهنجي استعمال ۾ آڻڻ، مخصوص مقصد لاءِ رقم يا وسيلا مقرر ڪرڻ
synonyms: Suitable, Proper, Fitting, Apt, Relevant, Seize, Confiscate, Allocate, Assign, Earmark
antonyms: Inappropriate, Unsuitable, Improper, Irrelevant, Return, Restore, Withhold, Release
englishMeaning: Suitable, proper, or correct for a particular situation. To take something for one's own use, often without permission. To set aside money or resources for a specific purpose.
examples: Please wear appropriate clothing for the interview. His remarks were not appropriate for a formal meeting. The government appropriated the land for a new road. Parliament appropriated funds for flood relief.
urduMeaning: مناسب، موزوں، حالات کے مطابق درست، کسی کی چیز بغیر اجازت اپنے استعمال میں لانا، مخصوص مقصد کے لیے رقم یا وسائل مختص کرنا

sindhiMeaning: غير مناسب, اڻ سڌريل, بي موقعو, جيڪو موزون نه هجي, نامناسب, ناجائز
urduMeaning: نامناسب, غیر موزوں, بے جا, جو محل کے مطابق نہ ہو, ناگوار, غیر شائستہ
englishMeaning: Not suitable or proper in the circumstances. Lacking in propriety or socially acceptable standards. Unsuited for a particular purpose or person. Not appropriate or relevant to the situation at hand. Something that is socially or morally unacceptable or improper. Acting in a way that is not considered right or fit for a specific occasion.
examples: His jokes were completely inappropriate for a formal dinner. The manager took action after reports of inappropriate behavior in the office. It would be inappropriate to comment on the case while it is still in court. The heavy coat was inappropriate for the scorching summer heat.
antonyms: Appropriate, Suitable, Proper, Fitting, Decent, Relevant, Apt, Correct, Right, Commensurate
synonyms: Unsuitable, Improper, Unfitting, Inapt, Incorrect, Unbecoming, Undue, Wrong, Indecent, Irrelevant, Malapropos, Incongruous, Unseemly

sindhiMeaning: تبديل ٿيڻ, لاهي چاڙهي اچڻ, گهٽ وڌ ٿيڻ, لڏڻ يا لوڏن ۾ هجڻ, غير مستقل هجڻ, لهرن وانگر مٿي هيٺ ٿيڻ
antonyms: Stabilize, Persist, Remain, Stay, Settle, Continue, Endure, Hold, Fix, Stand, Freeze, Stagnate
urduMeaning: تبدیل ہونا, اتار چڑھاؤ آنا, کمی بیشی ہونا, متزلزل ہونا, ڈانواں ڈول ہونا, لہرانا یا تھرتھرانا
englishMeaning: To change or vary irregularly and continuously. To rise and fall in number, amount, or intensity. To shift back and forth in a way that is unpredictable or uncertain. To experience frequent and often sudden changes between different levels or states. To waver or vacillate between different opinions or courses of action.
synonyms: Vary, Waver, Oscillate, Vacillate, Shift, Alter, Undulate, Seesaw, Swerve, Change, Sway, Flutter, Ebb, Flow
examples: The stock market prices continue to fluctuate based on global economic news. During the storm, the temperature began to fluctuate wildly between warm and cold. Public opinion on the new policy tends to fluctuate depending on the latest media reports. Her moods fluctuate so much that it is difficult to know how she will react today.

The government decided to subsidize public transportation to encourage people to leave their cars at home. Many local farms would go out of business if the state did not subsidize their crop production. Large corporations often subsidize child care costs for their employees as a benefit. The housing program is designed to subsidize rent for low-income families in the city.
urduMeaning: مالی امداد دینا, اعانت کرنا, مدد دینا, سرکاری طور پر مالی مدد فراہم کرنا, قیمت کم کرنے کے لیے رقم دینا, رعایت دینا
synonyms: Fund, Finance, Sponsor, Support, Underwrite, Back, Aid, Assist, Endow, Promote, Grant, Contribute, Help, Sustain
sindhiMeaning: مالي مدد ڪرڻ, ناڻي جي مدد ڏيڻ, رعايت ڏيڻ, مالي مدد ذريعي قيمتون گهٽائڻ, امداد ڏيڻ, سرڪاري مدد ڏيڻ
englishMeaning: To support an organization or activity financially. To pay part of the cost of producing something to keep the selling price low. To provide a grant or contribution of money to help another person or entity. To reduce the cost of a service or product for the consumer through government or external funding. To promote the growth of an industry through financial incentives.
antonyms: Defund, Tax, Penalize, Withdraw, Charge, Confiscate, Deplete, Extract, Withhold, Starve, Undermine, Burden

examples: The government decided to subsidise public transport to reduce traffic congestion. Many local councils subsidise arts programs to ensure they remain accessible to everyone. Farmers are often able to subsidise their income with government grants during droughts. The company agreed to subsidise the employees' gym memberships as part of a wellness initiative.
englishMeaning: To support an organization or activity financially. To pay part of the cost of something to keep the price low. To aid or promote with public money or a government grant. To provide financial assistance to reduce the burden on the consumer. To supplement the cost of a service or product through external funding. To maintain a particular activity by providing economic help.
urduMeaning: مالی مدد دینا, رعایت دینا, امدادی رقم دینا, خرچ برداشت کرنا, سستا کرنا, حکومتی امداد فراہم کرنا
synonyms: Fund, Sponsor, Finance, Support, Underwrite, Aid, Assist, Endow, Back, Help, Contribute, Promote, Sustain, Voucher
sindhiMeaning: مالي مدد ڪرڻ, رعايت ڏيڻ, امداد ڏيڻ, سرڪاري مدد فراهم ڪرڻ, خرچ ۾ ڀاڱي ڀائيوار ٿيڻ, گهٽ قيمت تي سهولت ڏيڻ
antonyms: Tax, Charge, Withhold, Withdraw, Penalize, Defund, Obstruct, Hinder, Forfeit, Discourage

A system of springs and shock absorbers that supports a vehicle on its wheels. A mixture in which solid particles float in a liquid without dissolving. englishMeaning: To an unusually great degree; extremely. In a way that is much better than the normal standard. Only in rare or special cases, as an exception to the usual rule. Remarkably or outstandingly, in a manner that stands out from others.

examples: There is a diversion in place because of roadworks. The magician used a clever diversion to fool the audience. Reading is his favourite evening diversion. The army created a diversion to hide its main advance.
sindhiMeaning: رخ تبديل ڪرڻ جو عمل، متبادل رستو جڏهن اصل رستو بند هجي، ڌيان ٻي طرف ڇڪڻ واري شيءِ، وندر يا دل وندرائڻ جو ذريعو، ڦيرو
englishMeaning: The act of changing the direction or course of something. An alternative route used when the usual road is closed. Something that takes a person's attention away from the main matter. An activity done for enjoyment or amusement.
synonyms: Detour, Deviation, Redirection, Distraction, Deflection, Amusement, Entertainment, Pastime, Digression, Sidetrack, Recreation
urduMeaning: رخ تبدیل کرنے کا عمل، متبادل راستہ جب اصل راستہ بند ہو، توجہ ہٹانے والی چیز، تفریح یا دل بہلاوا، انحراف

urduMeaning: حکمتِ عملی سے متعلق، طویل مدتی منصوبہ بندی والا، سوچ سمجھ کر کیا گیا، جنگی یا کاروباری لحاظ سے اہم، فائدہ مند جگہ پر رکھا گیا

examples: The general explained the strategical value of the hills. Their strategical planning gave them a clear advantage. He wrote a book on strategical thinking in business. The move had strategical as well as political significance.
englishMeaning: Relating to strategy; an older and less common form of the word strategic. Concerned with overall planning rather than immediate details. Important for carrying out a long-term plan. Done according to a carefully prepared method.
urduMeaning: حکمتِ عملی سے متعلق، اسٹریٹجک کی پرانی اور کم مستعمل شکل، مجموعی منصوبہ بندی سے متعلق، طویل منصوبے کے لیے اہم، سوچے سمجھے طریقے کے مطابق
sindhiMeaning: حڪمت عملي سان تعلق رکندڙ، اسٽريٽجڪ جو پراڻو ۽ گهٽ استعمال ٿيندڙ روپ، مجموعي منصوبابندي سان لاڳاپيل، ڊگهي منصوبي لاءِ اهم، سوچيل طريقي مطابق ڪيل

synonyms: Tactically, Deliberately, Carefully, Purposefully, Systematically, Cleverly, Methodically, Advantageously, Prudently, Shrewdly
sindhiMeaning: حڪمت عملي سان، سوچي سمجهي منصوبي مطابق، وڌ ۾ وڌ فائدي واري جاءِ تي، ڊگهي نتيجن کي نظر ۾ رکندي، جنگي يا ڪاروباري حڪمت عملي جي لحاظ کان
englishMeaning: In a way that relates to a carefully prepared plan for achieving an aim. In a position or manner that offers the greatest advantage. With careful thought about long-term results. In terms of military or business strategy.
examples: The cameras are strategically placed around the building. She strategically avoided answering the difficult question. The country is strategically located between two major markets. The firm strategically invested in renewable energy.

urduMeaning: جنگی سامان، اسلحہ اور گولہ بارود، بم اور گولوں کا ذخیرہ، فوج کو اسلحہ فراہم کرنا، دفاع یا حملے کے لیے درکار سامان

urduMeaning: پیچ کے ذریعے کسی چیز کو مضبوطی سے جوڑنا یا کسنا، ڈھکن یا والو گھما کر سخت کرنا، دباؤ ڈال کر کسی سے قیمت کم کرانا یا سخت شرائط منوانا، کسی چیز کو سختی سے محدود کرنا
englishMeaning: To fasten or fix something firmly in place using screws. To tighten something by turning it, such as a lid or valve. To force someone to reduce a price or accept harder terms through pressure. To restrict or limit something severely.
synonyms: Fasten, Tighten, Secure, Fix, Bolt, Clamp, Restrict, Pressure, Squeeze
antonyms: Unscrew, Loosen, Release, Free, Detach, Relax, Slacken, Open
sindhiMeaning: پيچ يا اسڪرو سان ڪا شيءِ مضبوطيءَ سان جوڙڻ يا هڻڻ، ڍڪڻ يا والو گهمائي سخت ڪرڻ، دٻاءُ وجهي ڪنهن کان قيمت گهٽ ڪرائڻ يا سخت شرط مڃائڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ کي سختيءَ سان محدود ڪرڻ

examples: Police are cracking down on drunk driving this month. The school has decided to crack down on latecomers. Authorities cracked down hard on illegal construction. The bank is cracking down on fraudulent transactions.
sindhiMeaning: غير قانوني يا ناپسنديده عملن کي روڪڻ لاءِ سخت ڪارروائي ڪرڻ، قانون يا ضابطن تي اڳ کان وڌيڪ سختيءَ سان عمل ڪرائڻ، ضابطا ٽوڙيندڙن سان سختيءَ سان پيش اچڻ
synonyms: Clamp down, Suppress, Repress, Curb, Restrain, Punish, Discipline, Tighten up, Stamp out
urduMeaning: غیر قانونی یا ناپسندیدہ رویے کو روکنے کے لیے سخت کارروائی کرنا، قوانین یا ضوابط پر پہلے سے زیادہ سختی سے عمل کرانا، قانون توڑنے والوں سے سختی سے نمٹنا
antonyms: Tolerate, Permit, Allow, Overlook, Ignore, Relax, Encourage, Condone
englishMeaning: To take strong and severe action to stop or punish illegal or unacceptable behaviour. To enforce rules or laws much more strictly than before. To deal firmly with people who are breaking regulations.

examples: The factory closed down after fifty years of production. They had to close down the shop because of rising costs. Inspectors closed down the restaurant for poor hygiene. The station closes down at midnight.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ڪاروبار يا ادارې جو مستقل طور تي بند ٿي وڃڻ، ڪنهن جاءِ يا سهولت کي بند ڪرڻ، ڪنهن اداري يا سرگرميءَ کي زوريءَ بند ڪرائڻ، نشريات جو ڏينهن جي پڇاڙيءَ تي بند ٿيڻ
englishMeaning: To stop operating permanently, especially a business or institution. To shut a place or service so that it no longer functions. To force an organisation or activity to cease. Of broadcasting, to end transmission for the day.
urduMeaning: کسی کاروبار یا ادارے کا مستقل طور پر بند ہو جانا، کسی جگہ یا سہولت کو بند کر دینا، کسی ادارے یا سرگرمی کو زبردستی بند کرانا، نشریات کا دن کے اختتام پر ختم ہونا
antonyms: Open, Launch, Start, Establish, Reopen, Begin, Expand, Operate
synonyms: Shut down, Cease, Terminate, Wind up, Fold, Discontinue, Liquidate, Halt, Suspend

urduMeaning: اوپر سے نیچے آنا یا گرنا، قیمت، سطح یا مقدار میں کمی آنا، کسی ایک فریق کے حق میں فیصلہ دینا، پرانی نسلوں سے ورثے میں چلا آنا، کسی بیماری میں مبتلا ہو جانا
synonyms: Descend, Drop, Fall, Decrease, Decline, Lower, Diminish, Land, Sink
englishMeaning: To move or fall from a higher position to a lower one. To decrease in price, level, or amount. To reach a decision or state an opinion in favour of one side. To be passed on from earlier generations or times. To become ill with a particular disease.
antonyms: Rise, Ascend, Climb, Increase, Go up, Soar, Escalate, Mount
examples: Please come down from the ladder before you fall. House prices have come down slightly this year. The committee came down in favour of the new proposal. I think I am coming down with a cold.
sindhiMeaning: مٿان کان هيٺ اچڻ يا ڪرڻ، قيمت، سطح يا مقدار ۾ گهٽتائي اچڻ، ڪنهن هڪ پاسي جي حق ۾ فيصلو ڏيڻ، اڳين نسلن کان ورثي ۾ هلي اچڻ، ڪنهن بيماريءَ ۾ مبتلا ٿيڻ
پنهنجي شيءِ وڪڻي ان کان سستي يا ننڍي شيءِ خريد ڪرڻ، خاص ڪري گهر يا گاڏي بدلائي گهٽ قيمت واري وٺڻ، خريدارن جو مهانگين شين بدران سستيون شيون وٺڻ شروع ڪرڻ
antonyms: Trade up, Upgrade, Splurge, Expand, Improve, Enlarge, Invest
englishMeaning: To buy or sell something in order to move to a cheaper or smaller item than the one owned before. To exchange a possession for one of lower value, especially a house or car. Of consumers, to switch to less expensive brands or products.
synonyms: Downgrade, Downsize, Economize, Cut back, Exchange, Substitute, Reduce, Switch
urduMeaning: اپنی چیز بیچ کر اس سے سستی یا چھوٹی چیز خریدنا، خاص طور پر گھر یا گاڑی بدل کر کم قیمت والی لینا، صارفین کا مہنگی اشیاء کے بجائے سستی اشیاء خریدنا شروع کرنا
examples: After retirement they decided to trade down to a smaller house. Many shoppers trade down to cheaper brands during a recession. He traded down from a luxury car to a compact model. Families are trading down as household budgets shrink.

antonyms: Abandon, Release, Ignore, Lose, Give up, Free, Overlook, Retreat
englishMeaning: To pursue someone or something until you catch them. To search hard for something until you find it. To make persistent efforts to obtain information, payment, or an answer from someone.
urduMeaning: کسی کے پیچھے بھاگ کر اسے پکڑنا، کسی چیز کو ڈھونڈ نکالنے تک محنت کرنا، معلومات، رقم یا جواب حاصل کرنے کے لیے بار بار کوشش کرنا
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن جي پٺيان ڊوڙي ان کي پڪڙڻ، ڪا شيءِ ڳولي لهڻ تائين محنت ڪرڻ، معلومات، رقم يا جواب حاصل ڪرڻ لاءِ بار بار ڪوشش ڪرڻ
synonyms: Pursue, Track down, Hunt down, Catch, Follow, Trace, Locate, Capture, Seek out
examples: The officer chased down the thief on foot. It took me hours to chase down the missing file. She is still chasing down the unpaid invoices. Reporters chased down every lead in the story.

sindhiMeaning: رگبيءَ ۾ راند ٻيهر شروع ڪرڻ لاءِ مخالف رانديگرن سان گڏجي اسڪرم ٺاهڻ، بال جي چوڌاري رانديگرن جو جهڪي گڏجي بيهڻ، غير رسمي طور تي ڪنهن معاملي تي بحث لاءِ ويجهو گڏ ٿيڻ
examples: The two packs scrummed down near the halfway line. The referee ordered the teams to scrum down again. Both sides scrummed down for the final play of the match. The staff scrummed down in the corner to finalise the plan.
englishMeaning: In rugby, to form a scrum with the opposing forwards in order to restart play. To crouch and bind together as a pack of players around the ball. Informally, to gather closely together in a tight group to discuss or deal with something.
antonyms: Disperse, Scatter, Separate, Break up, Spread out, Disband
synonyms: Pack down, Bind, Huddle, Group, Cluster, Assemble, Gather, Crouch
urduMeaning: رگبی میں کھیل دوبارہ شروع کرنے کے لیے مخالف کھلاڑیوں کے ساتھ اسکرم بنانا، گیند کے گرد کھلاڑیوں کا جھک کر آپس میں جڑ کر کھڑا ہونا، غیر رسمی طور پر کسی معاملے پر بات کرنے کے لیے قریب اکٹھا ہونا
الفاظ سے متعلق، خواہ بولے گئے ہوں یا لکھے گئے، تحریری کے بجائے زبانی، جیسے زبانی معاہدہ، گرامر میں فعل سے متعلق یا فعل سے بنا ہوا، فعل سے بننے والا لفظ یا فقرہ، کسی کو کہے گئے سخت الفاظ یا گالم گلوچ
englishMeaning: Relating to or consisting of words, whether spoken or written. Spoken rather than written, as in a verbal agreement. In grammar, relating to a verb or derived from a verb. A word or phrase formed from a verb, such as a gerund, participle, or infinitive. Informal insults or abuse directed at someone.
synonyms: Spoken, Oral, Unwritten, Linguistic, Lexical, Word-based, Vocal, Expressed, Stated
sindhiMeaning: لفظن سان لاڳاپيل، چاهي ڳالهايل هجن يا لکيل، لکت بدران زباني، جيئن زباني معاهدو، گرامر ۾ فعل سان لاڳاپيل يا فعل مان ٺهيل، فعل مان ٺهيل لفظ يا جملو، ڪنهن کي چيل سخت لفظ يا گارگند
antonyms: Written, Nonverbal, Silent, Documented, Unspoken, Physical, Gestural
examples: They had only a verbal agreement, with nothing in writing. Her verbal skills are excellent for a child of her age. The teacher explained the verbal forms of the sentence. He received a verbal warning from his manager.

She found the job through a recruitment agency. The agency is responsible for monitoring air quality. Students should be given more agency over their own learning. The change was brought about through the agency of local volunteers.
urduMeaning: ایسا ادارہ یا کاروبار جو دوسروں کی جانب سے کوئی خدمت فراہم کرے، حکومت کا کوئی خاص محکمہ یا ادارہ، کسی شخص کی اپنی مرضی سے عمل کرنے اور فیصلے کرنے کی صلاحیت، وہ ذریعہ جس سے کوئی کام انجام پائے، کسی بڑی کمپنی کی نمائندگی کرنے والا دفتر یا شاخ
sindhiMeaning: اهڙو ادارو يا ڪاروبار جيڪو ٻين جي طرفان ڪا خدمت مهيا ڪري، حڪومت جو ڪو خاص کاتو يا ادارو، ڪنهن ماڻهوءَ جي پنهنجي مرضيءَ سان عمل ڪرڻ ۽ فيصلا ڪرڻ جي صلاحيت، اهو ذريعو جنهن سان ڪو ڪم پورو ٿئي، ڪنهن وڏي ڪمپنيءَ جي نمائندگي ڪندڙ آفيس يا شاخ
synonyms: Organisation, Bureau, Office, Firm, Department, Body, Authority, Instrumentality, Means, Autonomy
englishMeaning: A business or organisation that provides a particular service on behalf of others. A department or body of government responsible for a specific area of work. The capacity of a person to act independently and make their own choices. The means or process by which something is achieved or caused. An office or branch that represents a larger company.
antonyms: Helplessness, Powerlessness, Dependence, Inaction, Passivity, Constraint, Headquarters

examples: Air pollution in the city has reached dangerous levels. Factories are the main source of water pollution in this river. Noise pollution makes it difficult to sleep near the highway. The government introduced new rules to reduce pollution.
synonyms: Contamination, Impurity, Filth, Toxicity, Smog, Waste, Defilement, Dirtiness, Poisoning
antonyms: Purity, Cleanliness, Purification, Freshness, Sanitation, Conservation, Decontamination
sindhiMeaning: هوا، پاڻي يا زمين ۾ نقصانڪار يا زهريلن مادن جي موجودگي، ماحول کي گندو ۽ غير محفوظ بڻائڻ جو عمل، اهي نقصانڪار مادا جيڪي قدرتي ماحول کي خراب ڪن، آواز يا روشنيءَ جهڙي اڻ گهربل خلل جيڪو ماحول کي متاثر ڪري
urduMeaning: ہوا، پانی یا زمین میں نقصان دہ یا زہریلے مادوں کی موجودگی، ماحول کو گندا اور غیر محفوظ بنانے کا عمل، وہ مضر مادے جو قدرتی ماحول کو نقصان پہنچائیں، آواز یا روشنی جیسی غیر ضروری خلل جو ماحول کو متاثر کرے
englishMeaning: The presence of harmful or poisonous substances in the air, water, or land. The act or process of making the environment dirty and unsafe. The harmful substances themselves that damage the natural world. Unwanted disturbance of any kind, such as noise or light, that harms the surroundings.

sindhiMeaning: لفظن يا ٻئي ڪنهن ذريعي سان خيال، جذبو يا راءِ بيان ڪرڻ، رويي، چهري يا اشارن ذريعي ڪا ڳالهه ظاهر ڪرڻ، تيز رفتار ۽ گهٽ اسٽاپن واري گاڏي يا خدمت، چٽو ۽ واضح طور تي بيان ڪيل، تيز هلندڙ ريل، بس يا ترسيل جي خدمت، ڪنهن شيءِ مان رس يا کير نچوڙي ڪڍڻ
synonyms: Convey, Articulate, State, Communicate, Utter, Voice, Rapid, Fast, Explicit, Direct
antonyms: Suppress, Withhold, Conceal, Hide, Repress, Slow, Local, Implied, Vague
urduMeaning: الفاظ یا کسی اور ذریعے سے خیال، جذبہ یا رائے بیان کرنا، رویے، چہرے یا اشاروں سے کوئی بات ظاہر کرنا، تیز رفتار اور کم اسٹاپ والی گاڑی یا سروس، واضح اور صریح طور پر بیان کیا گیا، تیز چلنے والی ٹرین، بس یا ترسیل کی سروس، کسی چیز سے رس یا دودھ نچوڑ کر نکالنا
englishMeaning: To convey a thought, feeling, or opinion in words or by other means. To show or reveal something through behaviour, looks, or signs. Operating at high speed with few or no stops, as of a train or service. Clearly and definitely stated, leaving no room for doubt. A fast train, bus, or delivery service that stops rarely. To squeeze out liquid, especially milk or juice.
examples: She struggled to express her feelings in front of the class. He expressed his gratitude in a short speech. We took the express to the airport to save time. The parcel was sent by express delivery.

synonyms: Maritime, Oceanic, Nautical, Naval, Seafaring, Aquatic, Saltwater, Seagoing, Soldier
antonyms: Terrestrial, Inland, Freshwater, Land-based, Continental, Civilian, Aerial
englishMeaning: Relating to the sea or ocean and the life found in it. Connected with shipping, sailing, or naval affairs. A soldier trained to serve on land and at sea, especially a member of the marines. The shipping fleet of a country considered collectively.
urduMeaning: سمندر یا سمندری حیات سے متعلق، جہاز رانی، کشتیوں یا بحری امور سے تعلق رکھنے والا، ایسا سپاہی جو خشکی اور سمندر دونوں پر لڑنے کی تربیت رکھتا ہو، کسی ملک کا مجموعی بحری بیڑا
sindhiMeaning: سمنڊ يا سامونڊي حياتيءَ سان لاڳاپيل، جهازراني، ٻيڙين يا بحري معاملن سان تعلق رکندڙ، اهڙو سپاهي جيڪو زمين ۽ سمنڊ ٻنهي تي وڙهڻ لاءِ تربيت يافته هجي، ڪنهن ملڪ جو مجموعي بحري ٻيڙو
examples: Plastic waste is a serious threat to marine life. She is studying marine biology at university. A marine engineer inspected the damaged hull. His brother served as a marine for eight years.

urduMeaning: بادشاہ، ملکہ یا شاہی خاندان سے متعلق، شاہی شان کے لائق، شاندار اور پرشوکت، ایسے ادارے کے نام میں استعمال ہونے والا جسے بادشاہ کی سرپرستی حاصل ہو، شاہی خاندان کا کوئی فرد، غیر رسمی طور پر مکمل یا انتہائی
examples: The royal family attended the opening ceremony. They were given a royal welcome at the airport. The Royal Society funds scientific research. Several royals were present at the wedding.
englishMeaning: Belonging to or connected with a king, queen, or member of a ruling family. Suitable for or worthy of a monarch; splendid and impressive. Used in the names of organisations under the patronage of a monarch. A member of a royal family. Informally, complete or utter, as in a royal mess.
sindhiMeaning: بادشاهه، راڻي يا شاهي خاندان سان لاڳاپيل، شاهي شان جي لائق، شاندار ۽ پرشوڪت، اهڙي اداري جي نالي ۾ استعمال ٿيندڙ جنهن کي بادشاهه جي سرپرستي حاصل هجي، شاهي خاندان جو ڪو فرد، غير رسمي طور تي مڪمل يا انتهائي
synonyms: Regal, Majestic, Imperial, Kingly, Queenly, Sovereign, Princely, Noble, Splendid, Monarch
antonyms: Common, Ordinary, Plebeian, Humble, Lowly, Modest, Civilian, Republican

englishMeaning: A strong feeling such as love, anger, joy, fear, or sadness. The part of a person's character that involves feeling rather than reason. An instinctive state of mind arising from circumstances, mood, or relationships. Strong feeling expressed in speech, writing, or behaviour.
examples: She spoke about her childhood with great emotion. Fear is a powerful emotion that can affect our decisions. He tried to hide his emotions during the meeting. Music has the ability to stir deep emotions.
urduMeaning: کوئی شدید احساس جیسے محبت، غصہ، خوشی، خوف یا غم، انسان کی شخصیت کا وہ حصہ جو عقل کے بجائے احساس پر مبنی ہو، حالات، موڈ یا رشتوں سے پیدا ہونے والی فطری کیفیت، بات چیت، تحریر یا رویے میں ظاہر ہونے والا شدید جذبہ
antonyms: Indifference, Apathy, Reason, Logic, Coldness, Detachment, Calmness, Numbness
synonyms: Feeling, Sentiment, Passion, Affection, Mood, Sensation, Ardour, Reaction, Warmth
sindhiMeaning: ڪو شديد احساس جهڙوڪ محبت، ڪاوڙ، خوشي، ڊپ يا ڏک، انسان جي شخصيت جو اهو حصو جيڪو عقل بدران احساس تي ٻڌل هجي، حالتن، موڊ يا رشتن سبب پيدا ٿيندڙ فطري ڪيفيت، ڳالهائڻ، لکڻ يا رويي ۾ ظاهر ٿيندڙ شديد جذبو

englishMeaning: Relating to a person's feelings and emotions. Easily affected by feelings and inclined to show them openly. Arousing or expressing strong feelings in others. Involving or based on emotion rather than reason or facts.
synonyms: Sentimental, Passionate, Sensitive, Feeling, Moving, Touching, Tender, Demonstrative, Affective
sindhiMeaning: انسان جي جذبن ۽ احساسن سان لاڳاپيل، جلد جذباتي ٿي پوندڙ ۽ احساس کليل نموني ظاهر ڪندڙ، ٻين ۾ شديد جذبا پيدا ڪندڙ، عقل يا حقيقتن بدران جذبن تي ٻڌل
antonyms: Rational, Unemotional, Detached, Cold, Indifferent, Logical, Impassive, Objective
examples: The film tells an emotional story about a lost family. She became emotional while thanking her teachers. Children need emotional support as much as physical care. Try not to make an emotional decision about the offer.
urduMeaning: انسان کے جذبات و احساسات سے متعلق، جلد جذباتی ہو جانے والا اور احساسات کھل کر ظاہر کرنے والا، دوسروں میں شدید جذبات پیدا کرنے والا، عقل یا حقائق کے بجائے جذبات پر مبنی

examples: The young actor emoted beautifully in the final scene. He tends to emote whenever he talks about his childhood. Some singers emote more with their faces than their voices. She emoted so strongly that the audience wept.
antonyms: Suppress, Repress, Hide, Conceal, Restrain, Understate, Withhold
sindhiMeaning: جذبن کي چٽي ۽ اڪثر مبالغي واري انداز ۾ ظاهر ڪرڻ، خاص ڪري اداڪاري دوران احساس کليل نموني پيش ڪرڻ، ڊرامائي انداز ۾ پنهنجن جذبن جو اظهار ڪرڻ
englishMeaning: To show emotion in a clear and often exaggerated way. To express feelings openly, especially while acting or performing. To talk about one's feelings in a dramatic manner.
urduMeaning: جذبات کو واضح اور اکثر مبالغہ آمیز انداز میں ظاہر کرنا، خاص طور پر اداکاری کے دوران احساسات کھل کر پیش کرنا، ڈرامائی انداز میں اپنے جذبات کا اظہار کرنا
synonyms: Express, Emotionalize, Dramatize, Perform, Gesture, Convey, Display, Act, Show

englishMeaning: A conversation between two or more people. The spoken or written exchange of words in a book, play, or film. A discussion between groups or countries aimed at solving a problem or reaching agreement. In computing, a small window that appears on screen to give or request information.

sindhiMeaning: ٿلهو ۽ ڪارو هيٺاهون ڪڪر جيڪو مسلسل مينهن يا برف وسائي، لڳاتار برسات سان لاڳاپيل ڪڪرن جو قسم، سڄي آسمان کي ڍڪيندڙ بي شڪل برساتي ڪڪر، موسمياتي علم ۾ برسات آڻيندڙ ڪڪر جو هڪ قسم
urduMeaning: موٹا اور سیاہ نچلی سطح کا بادل جو مسلسل بارش یا برف برسائے، لگاتار بارش سے وابستہ بادلوں کی قسم، پورے آسمان کو ڈھانپنے والا بے شکل بارشی بادل، موسمیات میں بارش لانے والے بادل کی ایک قسم
antonyms: Clear sky, Cirrus, Sunshine, Blue sky, Cloudlessness, Fair weather, Dry spell, Bright sky, Openness, Drought

urduMeaning: کتاب کے آخر میں دی گئی فہرست جس میں موضوعات اور صفحہ نمبر ہوں، کسی چیز کی سطح یا تبدیلی ظاہر کرنے والا عدد، کسی حالت کی نشانی یا اشارہ، معلومات کو ترتیب سے فہرست میں لانا، اجرت یا قیمت کو مہنگائی سے منسلک کرنا

A sign or indicator of a particular condition or trend. To arrange information in a systematic list. To link a value such as wages to a measure such as inflation.

sindhiMeaning: ڪتاب جي آخر ۾ ڏنل فهرست جنهن ۾ عنوان ۽ صفحن جا نمبر هجن، ڪنهن شيءِ جي سطح يا تبديلي ڏيکاريندڙ انگ، ڪنهن حالت جي نشاني يا اشارو، ڄاڻ کي ترتيب سان فهرست ۾ آڻڻ، اجرت يا قيمت کي مهانگائي سان ڳنڍڻ

She pointed at the map with her index finger. He tapped the screen gently with his index finger. The doctor asked him to touch his nose with his index finger. A cut on his index finger made typing painful.
synonyms: Forefinger, First finger, Pointer, Digit, Pointing finger, Second digit, Trigger finger, Finger, Forefinger digit, Hand digit
antonyms: Thumb, Little finger, Ring finger, Middle finger, Toe, Palm, Wrist, Knuckle, Nail, Heel of hand

urduMeaning: انگوٹھے کے ساتھ والی انگلی جو اشارہ کرنے کے لیے استعمال ہوتی ہے، ہاتھ کی پہلی انگلی، شہادت کی انگلی، انسانی ہاتھ کی دوسری انگلی

urduMeaning: کسی کو کھلا چیلنج دینا، مقابلے کے لیے للکارنا، مخالفت کا اعلان کر کے جواب طلب کرنا، اصل میں دستانہ پھینک کر دوبدو مقابلے کا چیلنج دینا

A difficult ordeal in which a person faces criticism or danger from several sides. Historically, a military punishment in which a person ran between two rows of men who struck him.

Stay calm, Keep cool, Compose oneself, Relax, Tolerate, Endure, Settle, Accept, Restrain, Soothe
urduMeaning: اچانک غصے میں آ کر بے قابو ہو جانا، معمولی بات پر ہنگامہ کرنا، لوگوں کے سامنے سخت پریشان یا مشتعل ہو جانا، برطانوی غیر رسمی محاورہ جس کا مطلب ہے واویلا مچانا
englishMeaning: To suddenly lose one's temper and behave in an uncontrolled way. To have a tantrum or emotional outburst, often over something minor. To become extremely upset or agitated in public. An informal British expression for making a fuss.
sindhiMeaning: اوچتو ڪاوڙ ۾ اچي بي قابو ٿي وڃڻ، ننڍي ڳالهه تي هنگامو ڪرڻ، عام ماڻهن اڳيان تمام گهڻو پريشان يا مشتعل ٿيڻ، برطانوي غير رسمي محاورو جنهن جو مطلب آهي فساد مچائڻ

antonyms: Be careful, Play safe, Hesitate, Take precautions, Hold back, Beware, Deliberate, Restrain, Avoid risk, Proceed cautiously
urduMeaning: خطرات کی پرواہ کیے بغیر بے احتیاطی سے کام کرنا، احتیاط چھوڑ کر جرات سے قدم اٹھانا، نقصان کے خطرے کے باوجود موقع لینا، دانائی چھوڑ کر دلیری سے کام کرنا
synonyms: Take a risk, Gamble, Chance it, Be reckless, Plunge in, Dare, Venture, Act boldly, Go for broke, Abandon restraint
examples: He threw caution to the wind and invested all his savings in the venture. They threw caution to the wind and set off without a map. She threw caution to the wind and told her boss exactly what she thought. For once, let us throw caution to the wind and enjoy the evening.

urduMeaning: کسی خیال یا منصوبے پر تنقید کر کے حوصلہ توڑنا، کسی کا جوش یا امید ختم کرنا، شک ظاہر کر کے تجویز کو خراب کرنا، کسی بات کے جوش کو ٹھنڈا کر دینا

sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن سان هٿن سان وڙهڻ، مُڪن سان مقابلو ڪرڻ، جهيڙي ۾ پوڻ، جهڳڙو هٿن سان نبيرڻ، غير رسمي انداز ۾ لڙڻ لاءِ تيار ٿيڻ

examples: The two men were ready to throw hands outside the stadium. Instead of throwing hands, they finally sat down and talked. Security guards separated the fans before they could throw hands. He warned that anyone throwing hands would be removed from the club.

synonyms: Thin, Emaciated, Haggard, Bony, Skeletal, Drawn, Wasted, Lean, Scrawny, Bleak
sindhiMeaning: تمام سنهو ۽ هڏائون، عام طور بيماري بک يا پريشاني سبب، ڦڪو ۽ ٿڪل شڪل وارو، اهڙي جاءِ جيڪا ويران ۽ اداس لڳي، سخت ۽ اجڙيل ڏيک وارو

sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن مسئلي کي رڳو گهڻا پئسا خرچ ڪري حل ڪرڻ جي ڪوشش، بغير منصوبابندي جي وڏي رقم لڳائڻ، سوچ ۽ محنت جي بدران پئسو استعمال ڪرڻ، جلد حل جي اميد تي کليل خرچ ڪرڻ

examples: The gauntness of his face shocked his old friends. Years of famine had left a gauntness in every village. There was a striking gauntness about the abandoned factory. Doctors noted the gauntness typical of long malnutrition.

word: Have your nose in a book

urduMeaning: زوردار آواز کے ساتھ پھٹ جانا، اچانک اور تیزی سے بڑھ جانا، اچانک شدید غصے یا جذبات میں بھڑک اٹھنا، کسی نظریے یا غلط فہمی کو مکمل طور پر غلط ثابت کرنا
