ڪنهن خاص شيءِ سان ڪجهه ملائڻ يا شامل ڪرڻ، اڳ ۾ مڪمل ٿيل شيءِ سان اضافي حصو  شرط يا رقم ڳنڍڻ، ڪنهن لکڻي يا منصوبي جي آخر ۾ ڪا ڳالهه يا شق شامل ڪرڻ، هڪ شيءِ کي ٻي سان هلڪي طرح لڳائڻ
synonyms: Attach to, Add to, Append to, Affix to, Annex to, Fasten to, Join to, Connect to, Stick to
examples: They tacked an extra fee onto the final bill. She tacked a personal message onto the official report. The builder tacked a small porch onto the front of the house. Do not tack new rules onto an agreement people have already signed.
urduMeaning: کسی خاص چیز کے ساتھ کچھ جوڑنا یا شامل کرنا، پہلے سے مکمل چیز کے ساتھ اضافی حصہ  شرط یا رقم لگانا، کسی تحریر یا منصوبے کے آخر میں کوئی بات یا شق شامل کرنا، ایک چیز کو دوسری کے ساتھ ہلکے سے لگانا
englishMeaning: To attach or add something to a particular thing. To join an extra part, condition, or amount to something already complete. To append a remark, clause, or item to the end of a text or plan. To fix one object loosely onto another.
antonyms: Detach from, Remove from, Separate from, Delete from, Take off, Exclude from, Disconnect from

sindhiMeaning: اهو رانديگر جيڪو بال کڻندڙ مخالف کي روڪي، اهو شخص جيڪو ٻئي کي پڪڙي يا ڪيرائي روڪي، اهو ماڻهو جيڪو ڪنهن مسئلي يا ڏکئي ڪم کي همت سان منهن ڏئي، اهو شخص جيڪو ڪنهن سان سڌو مقابلو يا سامهون ٿئي
antonyms: Runner, Attacker, Striker, Evader, Dodger, Avoider, Bystander, Spectator
englishMeaning: A player who stops an opponent carrying the ball in sports such as rugby or football. A person who brings down or seizes another to stop their movement. Someone who deals with a problem or difficult task with determination. A person who confronts or challenges another directly.
synonyms: Defender, Stopper, Blocker, Interceptor, Challenger, Opponent, Marker, Grappler, Confronter
urduMeaning: وہ کھلاڑی جو گیند لے جانے والے مخالف کو روکے، وہ شخص جو دوسرے کو پکڑ کر یا گرا کر روک دے، وہ شخص جو کسی مسئلے یا مشکل کام کا ہمت سے سامنا کرے، وہ شخص جو کسی کا براہِ راست مقابلہ کرے
examples: He is the strongest tackler in the entire team. The tackler brought the runner down near the goal line. Two tacklers failed to stop the fast winger. She is a fearless tackler of social problems in her community.

sindhiMeaning: سستو ۽ خراب معيار وارو خاص ڪري عمارتن ۽ سامان جي حوالي سان، بنا ڪنهن انفراديت جي هڪجهڙو ۽ بيزار ڪندڙ نموني ٺهيل، اهي مضافاتي گهر جيڪي سڀ هڪجهڙا ۽ بي مزو لڳن، سستي اڏاوت ۾ استعمال ٿيندڙ گهٽ معيار وارو مواد
antonyms: Sturdy, Durable, Elegant, Well-made, Distinctive, High-quality, Unique, Solid, Refined
urduMeaning: سستا اور کم معیار کا خاص طور پر عمارتوں اور سامان کے حوالے سے، بغیر کسی انفرادیت کے یکساں اور بے کیف انداز میں بنا ہوا، وہ مضافاتی مکانات جو سب ایک جیسے اور بے کشش لگیں، سستی تعمیر میں استعمال ہونے والا گھٹیا مواد
examples: Rows of ticky-tacky houses lined the new suburb. The furniture was ticky-tacky and fell apart within months. He criticised the ticky-tacky design of the shopping centre. They built the huts out of ticky-tacky wood and plastic.
englishMeaning: Cheap and poor in quality, especially of buildings and materials. Made in a dull, repetitive way with no character or individuality. Describing suburban houses that all look boringly the same. Shoddy material used in cheap construction.
synonyms: Cheap, Shoddy, Flimsy, Inferior, Tawdry, Tacky, Mass-produced, Uniform, Low-grade, Substandard

sindhiMeaning: برطانوي گهوڙ دوڙ جي ميدان تي شرط لڳائيندڙ جو مددگار جيڪو هٿن جي اشارن سان شرط جا اگهه ٻڌائي، اهو ماڻهو جيڪو شرطن جي بدلجندڙ ريٽن جي خبر هڪ کان ٻئي تائين پهچائي، اهو شخص جيڪو ميڙ ۾ خاموش اشارن سان ڳالهه ٻولهه ڪري، اهو پراڻو پيشو جيڪو هاڻي موبائل ٽيڪنالاجي سبب ختم ٿي ويو آهي
examples: The tic-tac man stood on a box waving both arms. Old photographs show a tic-tac man signalling across the racecourse. Bookmakers relied on a tic-tac man before mobile phones arrived. He worked as a tic-tac man for more than twenty years.
synonyms: Signaller, Bookmaker's assistant, Odds signaller, Racecourse signaller, Betting assistant, Gesturer, Course worker
englishMeaning: A bookmaker's assistant at a British racecourse who signals betting odds using hand movements. A person who passes information about changing odds between bookmakers. Someone who communicates silently with gestures across a crowd at races. An old occupation now largely replaced by mobile technology.
urduMeaning: برطانوی ریس کورس پر بک میکر کا مددگار جو ہاتھوں کے اشاروں سے شرط کے نرخ بتاتا ہے، وہ شخص جو بدلتے ہوئے نرخوں کی اطلاع ایک سے دوسرے تک پہنچائے، وہ شخص جو ہجوم میں خاموش اشاروں سے بات چیت کرے، وہ پرانا پیشہ جو اب موبائل ٹیکنالوجی کے باعث تقریباً ختم ہو چکا ہے
antonyms: Punter, Bettor, Spectator, Jockey, Trainer, Onlooker

sindhiMeaning: هڪ سادي راند جنهن ۾ ٻه رانديگر نون خانن واري جدول ۾ ايڪس يا او لکندا آهن، اها راند جيڪا پنهنجا ٽي نشان هڪ سڌي لڪير ۾ رکڻ سان کٽجي ٿي، ٻارن جي پينسل ۽ ڪاغذ واري راند جنهن کي ناٽس اينڊ ڪراسز به چئبو آهي، ڪا اهڙي صورتحال جيڪا محدود چالن واري سادي مقابلي جهڙي هجي
urduMeaning: ایک سادہ کھیل جس میں دو کھلاڑی نو خانوں کے جدول میں ایکس یا او لکھتے ہیں، وہ کھیل جو اپنے تین نشان ایک سیدھی لکیر میں رکھنے سے جیتا جاتا ہے، بچوں کا پنسل اور کاغذ والا کھیل جسے ناٹس اینڈ کراسز بھی کہتے ہیں، ایسی صورتحال جو محدود چالوں والے سادہ مقابلے جیسی ہو
synonyms: Noughts and crosses, Grid game, Paper game, Board game, Pastime, Puzzle game, Two-player game
englishMeaning: A simple game in which two players mark X or O in a grid of nine squares. A game won by placing three of one's own marks in a straight line. A children's pencil-and-paper pastime also known as noughts and crosses. Any situation described as a simple contest with limited possible moves.
examples: The children played tic-tac-toe while waiting for the bus. He drew a tic-tac-toe grid on the back of his notebook. Almost every game of tic-tac-toe between adults ends in a draw. She wrote a simple computer program to play tic-tac-toe.
antonyms: Chess, Complex game, Sport, Work, Study, Serious contest

englishMeaning: Relating to or affected by the rise and fall of the sea. Describing water, land, or a river that is influenced by tides. Rising and falling regularly like the tide. Very large or powerful in movement, as in a tidal wave of change.
antonyms: Inland, Landlocked, Still, Stagnant, Motionless, Non-tidal, Freshwater, Calm
synonyms: Marine, Coastal, Oceanic, Estuarine, Ebbing, Flowing, Sea-related, Rising, Surging
sindhiMeaning: سمنڊ جي جوار ڀاٽا سان لاڳاپيل يا ان کان متاثر، اهو پاڻي  زمين يا درياءُ جيڪو جوار ڀاٽا کان اثر وٺي، جوار ڀاٽا وانگر باقاعدي چڙهڻ ۽ لهڻ وارو، تمام وڏي يا طاقتور حرڪت وارو جيئن تبديليءَ جي زبردست لهر
examples: The tidal currents near the harbour are very strong. Birds feed on the tidal mudflats every morning. A tidal power station has been built along the coast. A tidal wave of protest followed the announcement.
urduMeaning: سمندر کے مد و جزر سے متعلق یا اس سے متاثر، وہ پانی  زمین یا دریا جو مد و جزر سے متاثر ہو، مد و جزر کی طرح باقاعدگی سے چڑھنے اور اترنے والا، بہت بڑی یا طاقتور حرکت والا جیسے تبدیلی کی زبردست لہر
کسی کو کوئی چیز حاصل کرنے یا کام کرنے کا حق دینا، کسی کو سرکاری طور پر کسی سہولت یا دعوے کا حقدار بنانا، کتاب  فلم یا کسی تخلیق کو عنوان یا نام دینا، کسی کو کوئی درجہ یا اعزازی لقب دینا
englishMeaning: To give someone the right to have or do something. To qualify a person officially for a benefit, service, or claim. To give a title or name to a book, film, or piece of work. To give a person a rank or honourable title.
examples: This ticket entitles you to free entry for one day. Full-time employees are entitled to paid annual leave. He entitled his first novel The Long Road Home. The king entitled him a lord for his loyal service.
synonyms: Authorise, Empower, Qualify, Permit, Allow, Enable, Name, Title, Call, Designate, License, Warrant
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کي ڪا شيءِ حاصل ڪرڻ يا ڪم ڪرڻ جو حق ڏيڻ، ڪنهن کي سرڪاري طور تي ڪنهن سهولت يا دعويٰ جو حقدار بڻائڻ، ڪتاب  فلم يا ڪنهن ڪم کي نالو يا عنوان ڏيڻ، ڪنهن کي ڪو درجو يا عزت وارو لقب ڏيڻ
antonyms: Deny, Forbid, Disqualify, Prohibit, Prevent, Refuse, Bar, Exclude, Withhold
Denial, Prohibition, Disqualification, Forfeiture, Duty, Obligation, Restriction, Refusal
examples: Every worker has a holiday entitlement of twenty days. She checked her pension entitlement before retiring. His sense of entitlement annoyed his colleagues. The government reduced spending on welfare entitlements.
englishMeaning: The legal or moral right to receive or do something. An amount or benefit that a person is officially allowed to have. The belief that one deserves special treatment or privileges. A government payment or service that citizens have a right to claim.
synonyms: Right, Claim, Privilege, Allowance, Benefit, Due, Prerogative, Permission, Quota, Provision
urduMeaning: کوئی چیز حاصل کرنے یا کام کرنے کا قانونی یا اخلاقی حق، وہ رقم یا سہولت جو کسی کو سرکاری طور پر ملنے کی اجازت ہو، یہ سوچ کہ اسے خاص رعایت یا مراعات ملنی چاہئیں، حکومت کی جانب سے دی جانے والی ادائیگی یا سہولت جو شہریوں کا حق ہو
sindhiMeaning: ڪا شيءِ حاصل ڪرڻ يا ڪم ڪرڻ جو قانوني يا اخلاقي حق، اها رقم يا سهولت جيڪا ڪنهن کي سرڪاري طور تي ملڻ جي اجازت هجي، اهو خيال ته پاڻ کي خاص رعايت يا اهميت ملڻ گهرجي، حڪومت پاران ڏنل اها ادائگي يا سهولت جيڪا شهرين جو حق هجي

urduMeaning: کوئی چیز حاصل کرنے یا کام کرنے کا سرکاری حق رکھنے والا، وہ شخص جو سمجھے کہ اسے دوسروں سے زیادہ رعایت ملنی چاہیے، کسی کتاب یا فلم کو دیا گیا خاص عنوان رکھنے والا، باقاعدہ طور پر کوئی درجہ  اعزاز یا حق دیا گیا
examples: You are entitled to a full refund within thirty days. Only registered voters are entitled to take part. He behaves like a spoilt and entitled child. She read a poem entitled Hope in the Morning.
sindhiMeaning: ڪا شيءِ حاصل ڪرڻ يا ڪم ڪرڻ جو سرڪاري حق رکندڙ، اهو ماڻهو جيڪو سمجهي ته کيس ٻين کان وڌيڪ رعايت ملڻ گهرجي، ڪنهن ڪتاب يا فلم کي ڏنل خاص عنوان وارو، رسمي طور تي ڪو درجو  اعزاز يا حق ڏنل
englishMeaning: Having the official right to receive or do something. Believing that one deserves special privileges or better treatment than others. Given a particular title or name, as of a book or film. Formally granted a rank, honour, or claim.
synonyms: Eligible, Qualified, Authorised, Permitted, Licensed, Privileged, Deserving, Named, Titled, Called
antonyms: Ineligible, Unqualified, Barred, Disqualified, Unauthorised, Humble, Modest, Undeserving, Nameless

sindhiMeaning: مئل جسم کي قبر يا مقبري ۾ رکڻ، ڪنهن کي مٽيءَ  برف يا ملبي هيٺان مڪمل طور دفن ڪرڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ کي اهڙي طرح بند ڪرڻ جو اها نڪري يا نظر اچي نه سگهي، ڪنهن شيءِ کي دفن ٿيل وانگر لڪائي يا محفوظ ڪري رکڻ
antonyms: Exhume, Unearth, Dig up, Disinter, Release, Free, Uncover, Expose, Reveal
urduMeaning: مردہ جسم کو قبر یا مقبرے میں رکھنا، کسی کو مٹی  برف یا ملبے کے نیچے مکمل طور پر دفن کر دینا، کسی چیز کو اس طرح بند کرنا کہ وہ نکل یا دکھائی نہ دے سکے، کسی چیز کو دفن شدہ کی طرح چھپا کر محفوظ رکھنا
synonyms: Bury, Inter, Lay to rest, Inhume, Enclose, Encase, Cover, Trap, Immure, Sepulchre
examples: The pharaoh was entombed with gold and precious jewels. Two climbers were entombed by the sudden avalanche. The old village lies entombed beneath the reservoir. His memories remained entombed in silence for years.
englishMeaning: To place a dead body in a tomb or grave. To bury someone or something completely under earth, snow, or rubble. To trap or enclose something so that it cannot escape or be seen. To preserve or hide something as if buried away.

examples: The museum has a large entomological collection. She published an entomological study of desert beetles. Entomological evidence helped the police fix the time of death. He attended an entomological conference in Germany.
urduMeaning: حشرات کے سائنسی مطالعے سے متعلق، کیڑوں  ان کی درجہ بندی اور عادات کے بارے میں، حشرات کی تحقیق  ذخائر یا انجمنوں سے متعلق، وہ طریقے یا شواہد جو حشرات کے مطالعے پر مبنی ہوں
sindhiMeaning: حشرات جي سائنسي مطالعي سان لاڳاپيل، حشرن  انهن جي درجه بندي ۽ عادتن بابت، حشرات جي تحقيق  ذخيرن يا انجمنن سان لاڳاپيل، اهي طريقا يا ثبوت جيڪي حشرات جي مطالعي تي ٻڌل هجن
synonyms: Insect-related, Zoological, Biological, Scientific, Taxonomic, Ecological, Naturalistic, Bug-related
antonyms: Botanical, Ornithological, Non-scientific, Unrelated, Mineralogical, Astronomical
englishMeaning: Relating to the scientific study of insects. Concerning insects, their classification, and their behaviour. Connected with research, collections, or societies devoted to insects. Used to describe methods or evidence based on the study of insects.

urduMeaning: اس طرح کہ حشرات کے مطالعے سے متعلق ہو، حشرات کی سائنس کے نقطہ نظر سے، علمِ حشرات کے طریقوں یا معلومات کو استعمال کرتے ہوئے، کیڑوں اور ان کی درجہ بندی یا عادات کے حوالے سے
synonyms: Scientifically, Zoologically, Biologically, Taxonomically, Technically, Ecologically, Academically
examples: Entomologically speaking, this specimen is extremely rare. The site was examined entomologically by two experts. The samples were entomologically identified as house flies. Entomologically, the region is still poorly explored.
sindhiMeaning: اهڙي طرح جو حشرات جي مطالعي سان لاڳاپيل هجي، حشرات جي سائنس جي نقطه نظر کان، حشرات جي علم جي طريقن يا ڄاڻ کي استعمال ڪندي، حشرن ۽ انهن جي درجه بندي يا عادتن جي حوالي سان
antonyms: Botanically, Unscientifically, Casually, Superficially, Astronomically, Chemically
englishMeaning: In a way that relates to the study of insects. From the point of view of insect science. Using methods or knowledge drawn from entomology. In terms of insects and their classification or behaviour.

antonyms: Botanist, Ornithologist, Amateur, Layperson, Novice, Geologist, Astronomer
sindhiMeaning: اهو سائنسدان جيڪو حشرات جو مطالعو ڪري، حشرن جي درجه بندي  حياتيات ۽ عادتن جو ماهر، اهو ماهر جيڪو تحقيق  زراعت يا جرم جي تحقيقات لاءِ حشرات جي سڃاڻپ ڪري، اهو ماڻهو جيڪو حشرات جا نمونا گڏ ڪري ۽ جاچي
examples: The entomologist spent years studying honeybee colonies. A forensic entomologist helped solve the murder case. She became an entomologist after visiting a butterfly farm. Entomologists warn that insect numbers are falling fast.
englishMeaning: A scientist who studies insects. An expert in the classification, biology, and behaviour of insects. A specialist who identifies insects for research, agriculture, or criminal investigations. A person who collects and examines insect specimens.
urduMeaning: وہ سائنسدان جو حشرات کا مطالعہ کرتا ہے، کیڑوں کی درجہ بندی  حیاتیات اور عادات کا ماہر، وہ ماہر جو تحقیق  زراعت یا جرائم کی تفتیش کے لیے حشرات کی شناخت کرے، وہ شخص جو حشرات کے نمونے جمع کرے اور جانچے
synonyms: Insect scientist, Bug expert, Zoologist, Biologist, Naturalist, Researcher, Specialist, Taxonomist

englishMeaning: The branch of zoology that deals with the scientific study of insects. The study of insect life, structure, classification, and behaviour. A field of science applied in agriculture, medicine, and forensic investigation. Knowledge concerning insects as a group of animals.
antonyms: Botany, Ornithology, Geology, Astronomy, Chemistry, Ignorance, Superstition
sindhiMeaning: علم حيوانات جي اها شاخ جيڪا حشرات جي سائنسي مطالعي سان تعلق رکي، حشرن جي زندگي  بناوت  درجه بندي ۽ عادتن جو مطالعو، سائنس جو اهو شعبو جيڪو زراعت  طب ۽ جرم جي تحقيقات ۾ ڪم اچي، حشرات جي باري ۾ حاصل ڪيل علم
examples: He studied entomology at an agricultural university. Forensic entomology can help estimate the time of death. Her interest in entomology began with a book about ants. Modern entomology relies heavily on genetic analysis.
synonyms: Insect science, Zoology, Biology, Natural science, Life science, Taxonomy, Bug study, Research field
urduMeaning: علمِ حیوانات کی وہ شاخ جو حشرات کے سائنسی مطالعے سے تعلق رکھتی ہے، کیڑوں کی زندگی  ساخت  درجہ بندی اور عادات کا مطالعہ، سائنس کا وہ شعبہ جو زراعت  طب اور جرائم کی تفتیش میں کام آتا ہے، حشرات کے بارے میں حاصل کیا گیا علم

englishMeaning: A group of people who travel with and attend to an important person. The assistants, advisers, and followers who surround a famous figure. A circle of companions who accompany someone in public. The people or surroundings closely associated with a person.
examples: The singer arrived with a large entourage of assistants. His entourage waited outside the conference hall. The president travelled with an entourage of security officers. She dislikes moving anywhere with a noisy entourage.
synonyms: Retinue, Followers, Attendants, Company, Escort, Staff, Suite, Court, Companions, Associates
sindhiMeaning: ماڻهن جو اهو ٽولو جيڪو ڪنهن اهم شخصيت سان گڏ سفر ڪري ۽ سندس خدمت ڪري، مشهور شخص جي چوڌاري رهندڙ مددگار  صلاحڪار ۽ پيروڪار، اهي ساٿي جيڪي ڪنهن سان عام هنڌن تي گڏ هجن، اهي ماڻهو يا ماحول جيڪي ڪنهن سان ويجهو لاڳاپيل هجن
antonyms: Loner, Individual, Stranger, Outsider, Solitude, Isolation, Opponent
urduMeaning: لوگوں کا وہ گروہ جو کسی اہم شخصیت کے ساتھ سفر کرے اور اس کی خدمت کرے، مشہور شخص کے گرد رہنے والے معاون  مشیر اور پیروکار، وہ ساتھی جو کسی کے ساتھ عوامی مقامات پر ہوں، وہ لوگ یا ماحول جو کسی سے قریبی تعلق رکھتے ہوں

englishMeaning: To uproot a plant completely from the ground. To remove people from their native land or culture by force. To destroy or wipe out something entirely, including its roots. To separate someone from their familiar traditions and surroundings.
synonyms: Uproot, Eradicate, Displace, Dislodge, Extirpate, Remove, Expel, Banish, Destroy, Wipe out
urduMeaning: کسی پودے کو جڑ سمیت زمین سے اکھاڑنا، لوگوں کو زبردستی ان کے وطن یا ثقافت سے جدا کرنا، کسی چیز کو جڑ سے مکمل طور پر ختم کر دینا، کسی کو اس کی مانوس روایات اور ماحول سے الگ کر دینا
examples: The storm deracinated several old trees in the park. War can deracinate entire communities within days. The regime tried to deracinate the local language and customs. Migration had deracinated him from his village life.
antonyms: Plant, Root, Settle, Establish, Restore, Implant, Preserve, Anchor, Return
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ٻوٽي کي پاڙ سميت زمين مان ڪڍڻ، ماڻهن کي زور سان سندن وطن يا ثقافت کان جدا ڪرڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ کي پاڙ کان مڪمل طور ختم ڪرڻ، ڪنهن کي سندس ڄاتل سڃاتل روايتن ۽ ماحول کان الڳ ڪرڻ

examples: The deracinated trees lay across the flooded road. He felt deracinated after twenty years abroad. Deracinated families struggled to rebuild their lives. Their deracinated culture survived only in old songs.
synonyms: Uprooted, Displaced, Dispossessed, Rootless, Exiled, Alienated, Removed, Homeless, Detached
urduMeaning: جڑ سمیت مکمل طور پر اکھاڑا ہوا، اپنے وطن  ثقافت یا برادری سے جدا کیا گیا، اپنی روایات اور تعلق کے احساس سے کٹا ہوا، جڑ سے ختم یا مٹایا ہوا
englishMeaning: Pulled up completely by the roots. Removed from one's native land, culture, or community. Feeling cut off from familiar traditions and a sense of belonging. Destroyed or eliminated from the very root.
antonyms: Rooted, Settled, Established, Grounded, Native, Belonging, Planted, Anchored
sindhiMeaning: پاڙ سميت مڪمل طور ڪڍيل، پنهنجي وطن  ثقافت يا برادريءَ کان جدا ٿيل، پنهنجي روايتن ۽ تعلق جي احساس کان ڪٽيل محسوس ڪندڙ، پاڙ کان ختم ٿيل يا مٽايل

examples: The cost of private treatment is simply prohibitive. Prohibitive taxes discouraged people from importing cars. There are prohibitive rules against parking on this street. The champion started the match as a prohibitive favourite.
synonyms: Excessive, Exorbitant, Unaffordable, Restrictive, Forbidding, Preventive, Discouraging, Steep, Crippling, Suppressive
sindhiMeaning: ايترو مهانگو جو ڪا شيءِ ناممڪن يا سگهه کان ٻاهر ٿي وڃي، ڪنهن ڪم کي قانون يا ضابطي ذريعي روڪيندڙ، سخت مشڪل يا خرچ سبب ماڻهن کي ڪم ڪرڻ کان روڪيندڙ، اهڙو جنهن کي شڪست ڏيڻ يا حاصل ڪرڻ تمام ڏکيو هجي
antonyms: Affordable, Reasonable, Cheap, Permissive, Encouraging, Moderate, Accessible, Allowable, Nominal
urduMeaning: اتنا مہنگا کہ کوئی چیز ناممکن یا استطاعت سے باہر ہو جائے، کسی کام کو قانون یا ضابطے کے ذریعے روکنے والا، سخت مشکل یا خرچ کے باعث لوگوں کو کام سے باز رکھنے والا، ایسا جسے شکست دینا یا حاصل کرنا نہایت مشکل ہو
englishMeaning: So high in cost that something becomes impossible or unaffordable. Serving to forbid or prevent an action by rule or law. Discouraging people from doing something because of severe difficulty or expense. Very unlikely to be beaten or achieved, as of odds in a contest.

antonyms: Cheaply, Affordably, Reasonably, Moderately, Permissively, Accessibly, Slightly, Encouragingly
urduMeaning: اس حد تک کہ کوئی کام ہو نہ سکے یا استطاعت میں نہ رہے، اس طرح کہ کسی کام کو منع یا محدود کر دے، اتنے مہنگے طور پر کہ خریدنا یا کرنا ناممکن ہو جائے، اس انداز میں کہ لوگوں کی حوصلہ شکنی ہو
sindhiMeaning: ايتري حد تائين جو ڪو ڪم ٿي نه سگهي يا سگهه ۾ نه رهي، اهڙي طرح جو ڪنهن ڪم کي منع يا محدود ڪري، ايترو مهانگو نموني جو خريد ڪرڻ يا ڪرڻ ناممڪن ٿي وڃي، اهڙي طرح جو ماڻهن جي همت ٽوڙي ڇڏي
examples: Housing in the city centre is prohibitively expensive. The equipment proved prohibitively costly for small farms. Insurance premiums rose prohibitively after the accident. Travelling by air was prohibitively priced last summer.
englishMeaning: To an extent that prevents something from being done or afforded. In a way that forbids or restricts an action. So expensively that buying or doing something becomes impossible. In a manner that strongly discourages people.
synonyms: Excessively, Exorbitantly, Unaffordably, Restrictively, Impossibly, Steeply, Extremely, Forbiddingly

urduMeaning: کسی چیز کو قانون یا ضابطے کے ذریعے سرکاری طور پر منع کرنے کا عمل، وہ قانون  حکم یا ضابطہ جو کسی کام پر پابندی لگائے، امریکہ کا وہ دور جب شراب بنانے اور بیچنے پر پابندی تھی، باقاعدہ طور پر اجازت نہ ہونے کی حالت
examples: There is a strict prohibition on smoking inside the hospital. The new law placed a prohibition on plastic bags. Prohibition in America led to widespread illegal trade. Their religion imposes a prohibition against gambling.
synonyms: Ban, Embargo, Restriction, Veto, Interdiction, Injunction, Bar, Suppression, Forbiddance, Moratorium
antonyms: Permission, Approval, Allowance, Authorisation, Licence, Consent, Freedom, Sanction, Legalisation
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ کي قانون يا ضابطي ذريعي سرڪاري طور تي منع ڪرڻ جو عمل، اهو قانون  حڪم يا ضابطو جيڪو ڪنهن ڪم تي بندش وجهي، آمريڪا جو اهو دور جڏهن شراب ٺاهڻ ۽ وڪڻڻ تي پابندي هئي، رسمي طور تي اجازت نه هجڻ جي حالت
englishMeaning: The act of officially forbidding something by law or rule. A law, order, or rule that bans a particular activity. The period in the United States when making and selling alcohol was banned. The state of being formally not allowed.

urduMeaning: کسی چیز کو قانون  ضابطے یا اختیار کے ذریعے سرکاری طور پر منع کرنا، کسی شخص کو کوئی خاص کام کرنے سے روکنا، حالات کے باعث کسی کام کو ناممکن بنا دینا، کسی خاص جگہ یا وقت میں کسی کام پر پابندی لگانا
englishMeaning: To officially forbid something by law, rule, or authority. To prevent a person from doing a particular thing. To make an action impossible because of circumstances or conditions. To ban an activity within a specified place or time.
antonyms: Allow, Permit, Authorise, Approve, Sanction, Let, Enable, Legalise, Encourage
synonyms: Forbid, Ban, Bar, Outlaw, Veto, Disallow, Prevent, Restrict, Block, Proscribe
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ کي قانون  ضابطي يا اختيار ذريعي سرڪاري طور منع ڪرڻ، ڪنهن ماڻهوءَ کي ڪو خاص ڪم ڪرڻ کان روڪڻ، حالتن سبب ڪنهن ڪم کي ناممڪن بڻائڻ، ڪنهن خاص جاءِ يا وقت اندر ڪنهن ڪم تي پابندي وجهڻ
examples: The law prohibits the sale of tobacco to children. School rules prohibit the use of mobile phones in class. Heavy snow prohibited any travel through the mountain pass. The court prohibited him from contacting the witness.

antonyms: Allowed, Permitted, Legal, Lawful, Authorised, Approved, Acceptable, Licensed, Free
examples: Parking is strictly prohibited in front of the gate. The airline listed all prohibited items on its website. Smoking is prohibited in every public building. He was prohibited from entering the stadium for two years.
urduMeaning: قانون  ضابطے یا اختیار کے ذریعے سرکاری طور پر منع کیا گیا، جس کا استعمال  فروخت یا عمل جائز نہ ہو، وہ کام جس پر عمل کرنے سے سزا ملے، جسے ہونے سے روک دیا گیا ہو
sindhiMeaning: قانون  ضابطي يا اختيار ذريعي سرڪاري طور تي منع ٿيل، جنهن جو استعمال  وڪرو يا عمل جائز نه هجي، اهو ڪم جنهن تي عمل ڪرڻ سان سزا ملي، جنهن کي ٿيڻ کان روڪيو ويو هجي
synonyms: Banned, Forbidden, Illegal, Outlawed, Barred, Unlawful, Disallowed, Restricted, Taboo, Vetoed
englishMeaning: Officially forbidden by law, rule, or authority. Not allowed to be used, sold, or carried out. Describing an action that carries a penalty if performed. Prevented or blocked from happening.

urduMeaning: وہ سیاسی اور سماجی نظریہ جو اصلاحات اور معاشرے کی بتدریج بہتری کی حمایت کرے، سماجی انصاف  مساوات اور جدید اصلاحات کو حکومتی عمل کے ذریعے آگے بڑھانے کا عقیدہ، تعلیم کی وہ تحریک جو تجربے سے سیکھنے اور بچے کی ضروریات پر زور دے، روایت کے بجائے تبدیلی اور ترقی کی حمایت
englishMeaning: A political and social philosophy that supports reform and gradual improvement of society. Belief in advancing social justice, equality, and modern reform through government action. An educational movement that stresses learning by experience and the needs of the child. Support for change and progress rather than tradition.
antonyms: Conservatism, Traditionalism, Reactionism, Orthodoxy, Stagnation, Regression, Fundamentalism
sindhiMeaning: اهو سياسي ۽ سماجي نظريو جيڪو سڌارن ۽ سماج جي تدريجي بهتري جي حمايت ڪري، سماجي انصاف  برابري ۽ جديد سڌارن کي حڪومتي عمل ذريعي اڳتي وڌائڻ جو عقيدو، تعليم جي اها تحريڪ جيڪا تجربي ذريعي سکيا ۽ ٻار جي ضرورتن تي زور ڏئي، روايت جي بدران تبديلي ۽ ترقيءَ جي حمايت
synonyms: Reformism, Liberalism, Radicalism, Modernism, Social reform, Advancement, Enlightenment, Change
examples: Progressivism shaped many reforms of the early twentieth century. She defended progressivism in her weekly newspaper column. Critics argue that progressivism ignores traditional values. Progressivism in education encourages learning through activity.

antonyms: Suddenly, Abruptly, Immediately, Instantly, Regressively, Decreasingly, Erratically, At once
sindhiMeaning: اهڙي طرح جو وقت سان گڏ آهستي آهستي وڌي يا بهتر ٿئي، قدم به قدم ۽ لاڳيتي ترتيب سان، اهڙي انداز ۾ جيڪو سڌارن  جديد خيالن ۽ سماجي ترقيءَ جي حمايت ڪري، هر مرحلي تي پهرين کان وڌيڪ ٿيندي
synonyms: Gradually, Steadily, Increasingly, Step by step, Continuously, Successively, Slowly, Cumulatively
examples: His health improved progressively after the operation. The road becomes progressively narrower near the village. Taxes are charged progressively according to income. The company progressively adopted greener technologies.
englishMeaning: In a way that develops or increases gradually over time. Step by step, in a continuing sequence. In a manner that favours reform, modern ideas, or social progress. Increasingly, with each stage becoming greater than the last.
urduMeaning: اس طرح کہ وقت کے ساتھ آہستہ آہستہ بڑھے یا بہتر ہو، قدم بہ قدم اور مسلسل ترتیب سے، ایسے انداز میں جو اصلاحات  جدید خیالات اور سماجی ترقی کی حمایت کرے، ہر مرحلے پر پہلے سے زیادہ ہوتے ہوئے

englishMeaning: Favouring social reform, new ideas, and gradual improvement. Happening or developing steadily over a period of time. Relating to a tax system in which the rate rises as income rises. In grammar, a verb form that shows a continuing action, such as 'is running'.
antonyms: Conservative, Traditional, Backward, Reactionary, Static, Regressive, Declining, Old-fashioned
urduMeaning: سماجی اصلاحات  نئے خیالات اور بتدریج بہتری کی حمایت کرنے والا، وقت کے ساتھ مسلسل ہونے یا بڑھنے والا، وہ ٹیکس نظام جس میں آمدنی بڑھنے کے ساتھ شرح بھی بڑھے، گرامر میں فعل کی وہ صورت جو جاری عمل ظاہر کرے
examples: The party promised a progressive policy on education. Doctors described her illness as a progressive condition. Most countries use a progressive system of income tax. The progressive tense is formed with the verb to be.
sindhiMeaning: سماجي سڌارن  نون خيالن ۽ تدريجي بهتريءَ جي حمايت ڪندڙ، وقت سان گڏ لاڳيتو ٿيندڙ يا وڌندڙ، اهو ٽيڪس نظام جنهن ۾ آمدني وڌڻ سان شرح به وڌي، گرامر ۾ فعل جو اهو روپ جيڪو جاري عمل ڏيکاري
synonyms: Forward-looking, Reformist, Liberal, Modern, Advancing, Increasing, Developing, Enlightened, Gradual

urduMeaning: وہ حالت جس میں جسم یا ذہن کا کوئی حصہ پوری طرح کام نہ کرے، ایسا نقصان یا کمزوری جو کسی چیز کی طاقت  قدر یا معیار کم کر دے، سننے  دیکھنے یا چلنے کی صلاحیت کا نقصان، اکاؤنٹنگ میں کسی اثاثے کی قدر میں مستقل کمی
antonyms: Improvement, Enhancement, Recovery, Strengthening, Repair, Restoration, Health, Soundness, Growth
sindhiMeaning: اها حالت جنهن ۾ جسم يا ذهن جو ڪو حصو پوري طرح ڪم نه ڪري، اهڙو نقصان يا ڪمزوري جيڪا ڪنهن شيءِ جي طاقت  قدر يا معيار گهٽائي، ٻڌڻ  ڏسڻ يا هلڻ جي صلاحيت جو نقصان، حساب ڪتاب ۾ ڪنهن اثاثي جي قدر ۾ مستقل گهٽتائي
synonyms: Damage, Weakening, Disability, Deterioration, Injury, Defect, Dysfunction, Reduction, Harm, Handicap
examples: The accident left him with a serious hearing impairment. Schools must support children with learning impairments. Long working hours caused a clear impairment of his judgement. The company reported an impairment of its overseas assets.
englishMeaning: A condition in which a part of the body or mind does not work fully. Damage or weakening that reduces the strength, value, or quality of something. A loss of ability such as hearing, sight, or movement. In accounting, a permanent reduction in the recorded value of an asset.

synonyms: Stage, Dais, Podium, Rostrum, Stand, Terrace, System, Framework, Programme, Manifesto, Forum
examples: The speaker walked onto the platform and greeted the crowd. Our train leaves from platform four in ten minutes. The company launched a new online learning platform. The party fought the election on a platform of tax reform.
sindhiMeaning: مٿي کنيل هموار جاءِ جتي ماڻهو بيهن  تقرير ڪن يا فن پيش ڪن، ريلوي لائين جي ڀرسان اها جاءِ جتي مسافر گاڏي جو انتظار ڪن، اهو ڪمپيوٽر نظام  ويب سائيٽ يا سافٽ ويئر جنهن تي پروگرام ۽ خدمتون هلن، ڪنهن سياسي جماعت جا اعلان ڪيل اصول ۽ مقصد، وڏي عوام تائين پنهنجا رايا پهچائڻ جو موقعو
urduMeaning: اونچی ہموار جگہ جہاں لوگ کھڑے ہوں  تقریر کریں یا فن پیش کریں، ریلوے لائن کے ساتھ وہ جگہ جہاں مسافر گاڑی کا انتظار کرتے ہیں، وہ کمپیوٹر نظام  ویب سائٹ یا سافٹ ویئر جس پر پروگرام اور خدمات چلتی ہیں، کسی سیاسی جماعت کے اعلان کردہ اصول اور مقاصد، بڑے مجمع تک اپنی رائے پہنچانے کا موقع
englishMeaning: A raised flat surface on which people stand, speak, or perform. The area beside a railway line where passengers wait for a train. A computer system, website, or piece of software on which programs and services run. The stated policies and aims of a political party or group. An opportunity to express opinions to a wide audience.
antonyms: Pit, Hollow, Ground, Basement, Depression, Audience, Silence, Obscurity

examples: The new law protects visually impaired passengers. His memory was impaired after the long illness. Driving while impaired is a serious criminal offence. Heavy rain impaired visibility on the motorway.
synonyms: Damaged, Weakened, Diminished, Defective, Disabled, Reduced, Harmed, Faulty, Compromised, Injured
sindhiMeaning: ڪمزور يا خراب ٿيل جو صحيح ڪم نه ڪري، گهٽيل صلاحيت وارو جيئن ڪمزور نظر  ٻڌڻ يا هلڻ جي سگهه، شراب يا نشي کان متاثر جو فيصلو ڀروسي جوڳو نه هجي، معيار  طاقت يا قدر ۾ گهٽيل
antonyms: Healthy, Intact, Sound, Improved, Strengthened, Unimpaired, Perfect, Repaired, Enhanced
urduMeaning: کمزور یا خراب ہو جانے والا جو ٹھیک کام نہ کرے، کم صلاحیت والا جیسے کمزور نظر  سماعت یا حرکت، شراب یا نشے سے متاثر کہ فیصلہ قابلِ اعتماد نہ رہے، معیار  طاقت یا قدر میں کم ہو جانے والا
englishMeaning: Weakened or damaged so that it no longer works properly. Having a reduced ability such as poor sight, hearing, or movement. Affected by alcohol or drugs so that judgement is not reliable. Reduced in quality, strength, or value.

synonyms: Affected, Influenced, Struck, Hit, Shaken, Touched, Altered, Damaged, Compressed, Wedged, Jammed, Packed
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ کان سخت متاثر ٿيل، ڪنهن واقعي يا فيصلي جو اثر قبول ڪندڙ، زور سان ٽڪرايل يا لڳل، تنگ جاءِ ۾ سختيءَ سان ڦاٿل يا ڀريل، اهڙو ڏند جيڪو صحيح نموني ٻاهر نه نڪري سگهي، منفي طور تي متاثر ٿيل
examples: Thousands of families were impacted by the sudden floods. The new policy has impacted small businesses across the country. The dentist removed an impacted tooth from the back of his jaw. Soil that is heavily impacted makes it difficult for roots to grow.
urduMeaning: کسی چیز سے شدید متاثر ہونے والا، کسی واقعے یا فیصلے کا اثر قبول کرنے والا، زور سے ٹکرایا ہوا، تنگ جگہ میں سختی سے پھنسا یا بھرا ہوا، ایسا دانت جو ٹھیک طرح باہر نہ نکل سکے، منفی طور پر متاثر شدہ
antonyms: Unaffected, Untouched, Unchanged, Unharmed, Loose, Free, Unmoved, Ignored, Uninfluenced
englishMeaning: Strongly affected or influenced by something. Having been hit or struck with force. Firmly wedged, packed, or pressed tightly into a space. (Of a tooth) unable to grow out properly because it is wedged against another tooth or bone. Affected negatively by a situation, event, or decision.

examples: Her speech was short but incredibly impactful. The charity ran an impactful campaign that changed public opinion. We need a more impactful way to present these findings. His impactful leadership transformed the entire organisation.
urduMeaning: گہرا اثر ڈالنے والا، طاقتور اور یادگار تاثر پیدا کرنے والا، بامعنی تبدیلی لانے والا، مؤثر اور کارگر، دل پر گہرا اثر چھوڑنے والا
englishMeaning: Having a strong effect on someone or something. Producing a powerful and lasting impression. Capable of creating meaningful or noticeable change. Effective and memorable in the way it influences people.
synonyms: Effective, Powerful, Influential, Striking, Meaningful, Memorable, Compelling, Significant, Forceful, Telling
antonyms: Ineffective, Weak, Insignificant, Forgettable, Trivial, Bland, Powerless, Unimpressive, Minor
sindhiMeaning: وڏو اثر ڇڏيندڙ، طاقتور ۽ يادگار اثر پيدا ڪندڙ، بامعنيٰ تبديلي آڻيندڙ، اثرائتو ۽ ڪارگر، دل تي گهرو اثر ڪندڙ

antonyms: Neglect, Ignore, Abandon, Disregard, Forsake, Avoid, Overlook, Desert
sindhiMeaning: عام طور تي ڪنهن خاص طريقي سان ٿيڻ يا ڪرڻ جو رجحان رکڻ، ڪنهن جي سنڀال يا خدمت ڪرڻ، ڏانهن مائل ٿيڻ يا جهڪڻ، زمين  جانورن يا ڪاروبار جي ديک ڀال ڪرڻ، گراهڪن جي خدمت ڪرڻ
synonyms: Incline, Lean, Gravitate, Nurse, Care for, Look after, Attend, Nurture, Mind, Cultivate
examples: Prices tend to rise sharply just before the festival. She stayed up all night tending to her sick child. The discussion tended towards politics as the evening went on. He spent the morning tending the garden behind the house.
englishMeaning: To be likely to behave in a particular way or to happen often. To take care of, look after, or attend to someone or something. To move or lean in a particular direction. To manage or work on land, animals, or a business. To serve customers, especially at a bar or shop.
urduMeaning: عام طور پر کسی خاص انداز میں ہونے یا کرنے کا رجحان رکھنا، کسی کی دیکھ بھال یا تیمارداری کرنا، کسی طرف مائل یا جھکنا، زمین  جانوروں یا کاروبار کی نگہداشت کرنا، گاہکوں کی خدمت کرنا

englishMeaning: Extremely worried, upset, or emotionally troubled. So anxious or grief-stricken that one cannot think or behave normally. Deeply distressed because of fear, loss, or shock. Showing great agitation and confusion of mind.
synonyms: Distressed, Upset, Anguished, Frantic, Agitated, Troubled, Heartbroken, Overwrought, Grief-stricken, Beside oneself
examples: The distraught mother searched the streets for her missing son. He looked distraught when he heard about the accident. She was too distraught to answer any of the questions. Distraught passengers waited for news of the delayed flight.
urduMeaning: شدید پریشان اور دل گرفتہ، غم یا خوف کے باعث بے چین اور بے قرار، اتنا پریشان کہ سوچ یا سنبھل نہ سکے، ذہنی طور پر منتشر اور مضطرب، صدمے میں مبتلا
sindhiMeaning: انتهائي پريشان ۽ ڏکويل، غم يا خوف سبب بيچين ۽ بيقرار، ايترو پريشان جو سوچي يا سنڀالي نه سگهي، ذهني طور تي منتشر ۽ مضطرب، صدمي ۾ ورتل
antonyms: Calm, Composed, Relaxed, Untroubled, Serene, Collected, Content, Unruffled, Cheerful

sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن اهم واقعي جي سالياني تاريخ، هر سال ملهايو ويندڙ يادگار ڏينهن، شاديءَ جي سالگرهه، ڪنهن اداري جي قيام يا ڪنهن وفات جي ساليانه ياد، سالگرهه
examples: They celebrated their tenth wedding anniversary in the mountains. The school marked the fiftieth anniversary of its founding. A special ceremony was held on the anniversary of the disaster. She sends him flowers every year on their anniversary.
synonyms: Jubilee, Commemoration, Celebration, Remembrance, Birthday, Centenary, Memorial
englishMeaning: The yearly return of the date of an important past event. A celebration held on the date when something notable happened in an earlier year. The date on which a couple was married, marked each year. A yearly commemoration of a death, founding, or historic occasion.
antonyms: Ordinary day, Forgetting, Oblivion, Neglect
urduMeaning: کسی اہم واقعے کی سالانہ تاریخ، ہر سال منایا جانے والا یادگار دن، شادی کی سالگرہ، کسی ادارے کے قیام یا کسی وفات کی سالانہ یاد، برسی

synonyms: Manager, Director, Administrator, Officer, Leader, Boss, Chief, Managerial, Administrative, Governing
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن اداري جو وڏو عهديدار يا منتظم، حڪومت جو اهو حصو جيڪو قانون تي عمل ڪرائي، انتظام يا نظم و نسق سان تعلق رکندڙ، فيصلا ڪرڻ ۽ لاڳو ڪرڻ جو اختيار رکندڙ، اعليٰ درجي جو يا عهديدارن لاءِ مخصوص
examples: She was promoted to a senior executive at the age of thirty. The executive must implement the laws passed by parliament. He booked an executive suite for the two-day conference. The board gave the manager full executive authority over the project.
urduMeaning: کسی ادارے کا اعلیٰ عہدیدار یا منتظم، حکومت کا وہ شعبہ جو قوانین پر عمل درآمد کرائے، انتظام و انصرام سے متعلق، فیصلے کرنے اور نافذ کرنے کا اختیار رکھنے والا، اعلیٰ درجے کا یا افسران کے لیے مخصوص
englishMeaning: A senior person responsible for managing an organisation or part of it. The branch of government that puts laws into effect. Relating to the management or administration of an organisation. Having the power to make decisions and put plans into action. Designed for or suited to senior managers, often meaning high quality or expensive.
antonyms: Employee, Subordinate, Worker, Junior, Legislative, Judicial, Follower, Assistant

synonyms: Trustworthiness, Reliability, Believability, Integrity, Authority, Reputation, Plausibility, Dependability
examples: The scandal seriously damaged the minister's credibility. Independent research gave the report much-needed credibility. He has built up credibility over twenty years of honest work. Without evidence, the claim lacks credibility.
urduMeaning: قابلِ اعتبار یا قابلِ بھروسہ ہونے کی خوبی، لوگوں میں یقین پیدا کرنے کی صلاحیت، سچائی اور دیانت کی ساکھ، کسی بات کا قابلِ یقین ہونا، اعتماد و ساکھ
englishMeaning: The quality of being believed or trusted by other people. The degree to which something appears convincing or reliable. A reputation for honesty and dependability. The ability to inspire confidence through knowledge or evidence.
sindhiMeaning: اعتبار يا ڀروسي جي لائق هجڻ جي خاصيت، ماڻهن ۾ يقين پيدا ڪرڻ جي صلاحيت، سچائي ۽ ڀروسي واري ساک، ڪنهن ڳالهه جو قابل يقين هجڻ، ساک ۽ اعتبار
antonyms: Unreliability, Dishonesty, Implausibility, Doubt, Distrust, Disrepute, Falsehood

synonyms: Seriously, Severely, Critically, Solemnly, Sombrely, Dangerously, Earnestly, Badly
urduMeaning: نہایت سنجیدگی اور متانت کے ساتھ، خطرناک یا شدید حد تک، تشویش اور فکر کے انداز میں، اس طرح کہ خطرے کا احساس ہو، سخت طور پر
englishMeaning: In a very serious and solemn manner. To a dangerous or severe degree. In a way that shows deep concern or worry. Seriously enough to cause alarm about health, safety, or outcome.
examples: He was gravely injured in the road accident. The doctor spoke gravely about her condition. She nodded gravely as the news was announced. The country is gravely affected by the ongoing drought.
sindhiMeaning: تمام سنجيدگيءَ ۽ متانت سان، خطرناڪ يا شديد حد تائين، ڳڻتيءَ ۽ فڪر واري انداز ۾، اهڙي طرح جو خطري جو احساس ٿئي، سخت نموني
antonyms: Slightly, Mildly, Lightly, Cheerfully, Playfully, Harmlessly, Casually

urduMeaning: اعتبار نہ کرنے والا، کسی پر شک یا بے اعتمادی رکھنے والا، دوسروں پر بھروسہ کرنے سے گریزاں، محتاط اور شکی مزاج، بدگمان
antonyms: Trusting, Confident, Believing, Credulous, Assured, Faithful, Unsuspecting, Open
synonyms: Suspicious, Wary, Doubtful, Sceptical, Cautious, Guarded, Cynical, Uneasy, Mistrustful
sindhiMeaning: اعتبار نه ڪندڙ، ڪنهن تي شڪ يا بي اعتمادي رکندڙ، ٻين تي ڀروسو ڪرڻ کان لنوائيندڙ، محتاط ۽ شڪي مزاج، بدگمان
englishMeaning: Having no confidence or faith in someone or something. Feeling doubt or suspicion about a person's honesty or motives. Unwilling to believe or rely on others. Showing wariness and lack of trust.
examples: She remained distrustful of strangers after the incident. Years of broken promises made the villagers distrustful of officials. He gave the salesman a distrustful look. Voters are increasingly distrustful of political advertising.

antonyms: Neglect, Laxity, Non-enforcement, Disregard, Leniency, Abandonment, Exemption
englishMeaning: The act of making sure that a law, rule, or obligation is obeyed. The process of compelling observance of something by authority. The officials or agencies responsible for applying the law. The act of imposing something forcefully upon others.
urduMeaning: قانون یا ضابطے پر عمل درآمد کرانے کا عمل، اختیار کے ذریعے پابندی کرانا، قانون نافذ کرنے والے ادارے یا عملہ، زبردستی کسی چیز کا نفاذ، اطلاق
examples: Strict enforcement of traffic rules has reduced accidents. Law enforcement agencies are investigating the case. The new regulations will require careful enforcement. Weak enforcement of the ban made it almost meaningless.
sindhiMeaning: قانون يا قاعدي تي عمل ڪرائڻ جو عمل، اختيار ذريعي پابندي ڪرائڻ، قانون لاڳو ڪندڙ ادارا يا عملو، زور سان ڪا شيءِ نافذ ڪرڻ، نفاذ
synonyms: Implementation, Application, Imposition, Execution, Administration, Compulsion, Policing, Compliance

urduMeaning: ایسی صورتحال جس میں کوئی فریق دوسرے پر برتری حاصل نہ کر سکے، تنازعے میں کشیدہ تعطل، مذاکرات یا مقابلے میں برابری یا بند گلی کی کیفیت، مسلح تصادم کا رک جانا، تعطل
antonyms: Agreement, Resolution, Settlement, Compromise, Breakthrough, Progress, Accord
sindhiMeaning: اهڙي صورتحال جنهن ۾ ٻئي ڌريون هڪ ٻئي تي حاوي نه ٿي سگهن، تڪرار ۾ ڪشيده تعطل، ڳالهين يا مقابلي ۾ برابري يا بند ڳليءَ واري حالت، هٿياربند تصادم جو رڪجي وڃڻ، جمود
englishMeaning: A situation in which neither side in a dispute can gain an advantage. A tense pause in a conflict where both sides refuse to move or give in. A deadlock or draw in a contest or negotiation. A confrontation, especially an armed one, that has reached a halt.
examples: The two sides remained locked in a tense stand-off for hours. Police ended the armed stand-off without any casualties. The negotiations ended in a complete stand-off. A political stand-off delayed the passing of the budget.
synonyms: Deadlock, Stalemate, Impasse, Tie, Draw, Gridlock, Confrontation, Standstill
Division, Split, Separation, Segregation, Fragmentation, Opposition, Estrangement
examples: Social media has increased political polarization in many countries. The debate led to a sharp polarization of public opinion. Polarization of light is used in many camera filters. Economic inequality contributed to the polarization of society.
urduMeaning: کسی گروہ کا دو مخالف حصوں میں بٹ جانا، آراء یا نظریات کا انتہاؤں کی طرف چلے جانا، سماجی یا سیاسی تقسیم، روشنی کی لہروں کا ایک خاص سمت میں محدود ہونا، کسی شے میں مخالف برقی یا مقناطیسی خصوصیات کا پیدا ہونا
englishMeaning: The division of a group into two sharply opposed sets of opinions or beliefs. The process by which people or ideas move towards opposite extremes. The restriction of light or other waves to vibration in one direction. The development of opposite electrical or magnetic properties in an object.
antonyms: Unity, Agreement, Consensus, Harmony, Cohesion, Reconciliation, Convergence
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن گروهه جو ٻن مخالف حصن ۾ ورهائجي وڃڻ، رايا يا خيالن جو انتها پسنديءَ ڏانهن وڃڻ، سماجي يا سياسي ورهاست، روشنيءَ جي لهرن جو هڪ خاص رخ ۾ محدود ٿيڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ ۾ مخالف برقي يا مقناطيسي خاصيتن جو پيدا ٿيڻ

antonyms: Unity, Consensus, Harmony, Agreement, Cohesion, Reconciliation, Convergence
englishMeaning: The British spelling of polarization. The division of people or opinions into two directly opposing groups. The movement of ideas or attitudes towards opposite extremes. The confinement of light or other waves to a single plane of vibration. The creation of opposite electrical or magnetic poles.
examples: The report examines the growing polarisation of British politics. Media coverage deepened the polarisation between the two communities. Scientists measured the polarisation of the reflected light. Polarisation within the party made compromise impossible.
sindhiMeaning: پولرائيزيشن جو برطانوي هجي، ماڻهن يا راين جو ٻن مخالف گروهن ۾ ورهائجڻ، خيالن جو انتهائن ڏانهن مائل ٿيڻ، روشنيءَ جي لهرن جو هڪ رخ تائين محدود ٿيڻ، مخالف برقي يا مقناطيسي قطبن جو پيدا ٿيڻ
synonyms: Division, Split, Separation, Fragmentation, Opposition, Segregation, Estrangement
urduMeaning: پولرائزیشن کا برطانوی املا، لوگوں یا آراء کا دو مخالف گروہوں میں بٹ جانا، نظریات کا انتہاؤں کی طرف مائل ہونا، روشنی کی لہروں کا ایک رخ تک محدود ہونا، مخالف برقی یا مقناطیسی قطبین کا پیدا ہونا

synonyms: Kill oneself slowly, Ruin one's health, Shorten one's life, Court death, Self-destruct
word: Smoke oneself into an early grave
examples: If he keeps this up, he will smoke himself into an early grave. The doctor warned him that he was smoking himself into an early grave. Her father smoked himself into an early grave at just fifty. Many young people are smoking themselves into an early grave without realising it.
sindhiMeaning: ايترو سگريٽ ڇڪڻ جو صحت تباهه ٿي وڃي ۽ وقت کان اڳ موت اچي، تمباڪونوشي سان پنهنجي ڄمار گهٽائڻ، سگريٽ جي عادت سبب پاڻ کي مارڻ
urduMeaning: اتنا زیادہ سگریٹ پینا کہ صحت تباہ ہو جائے اور وقت سے پہلے موت آ جائے، تمباکو نوشی سے اپنی عمر گھٹا لینا، سگریٹ کی لت سے خود کو ہلاک کر لینا
englishMeaning: To damage one's health by smoking so heavily that it causes death before the normal lifespan. To shorten one's life through continuous heavy smoking. To ruin one's health steadily by refusing to stop smoking.
antonyms: Live healthily, Quit smoking, Preserve one's health, Prolong life, Recover
Abandon, Betray, Desert, Turn back, Forsake, Withdraw
urduMeaning: مرتے دم تک کسی کا وفادار رہنا، کسی مقصد کی پیروی زندگی کے آخری لمحے تک کرنا، جنازے کے ساتھ قبرستان تک جانا، ایسی راہ پر چلنا جو موت کی طرف لے جائے
englishMeaning: To remain devoted to someone or something until death. To follow a path or cause right up to the end of one's life. To accompany a dead person's coffin to the burial place. To continue on a course that inevitably leads to one's death.
sindhiMeaning: مرڻ تائين ڪنهن سان وفادار رهڻ، ڪنهن مقصد جي پيروي زندگيءَ جي آخر تائين ڪرڻ، ميت سان گڏ قبرستان تائين وڃڻ، اهڙي راهه تي هلڻ جيڪا موت ڏانهن وٺي وڃي
examples: He vowed to follow the grave rather than betray his friend. The whole village came to follow the grave of the old teacher. She was loyal enough to follow the grave with him. Some soldiers follow the grave for a cause they truly believe in.
synonyms: Stay loyal until death, Accompany to the end, Remain devoted, Attend a burial

word: Have one foot in the grave
englishMeaning: To be very old or so ill that death seems near. To be close to dying. To be in a very weak or failing condition. Used humorously to say that someone is getting old.
synonyms: At death's door, Dying, Failing, On one's last legs, Near the end, Ailing
urduMeaning: موت کے قریب ہونا، نہایت بوڑھا یا سخت بیمار ہونا، آخری وقت میں ہونا، بہت کمزور اور نحیف ہونا، مذاقاً کسی کو بوڑھا کہنا
examples: He is ninety and has one foot in the grave, yet he still gardens daily. The old man looked as if he had one foot in the grave. Stop teasing me about my age; I do not have one foot in the grave yet. After the illness, she seemed to have one foot in the grave.
sindhiMeaning: موت جي ويجهو هجڻ، ڏاڍو پوڙهو يا سخت بيمار هجڻ، آخري وقت ۾ هجڻ، تمام ڪمزور ۽ بيحال هجڻ، مذاق ۾ ڪنهن کي پوڙهو چوڻ
antonyms: In the prime of life, Healthy, Thriving, Robust, Full of life, Youthful

sindhiMeaning: پنهنجي تباهيءَ جو سامان پاڻ ڪرڻ، اهڙو ڪم ڪرڻ جيڪو پنهنجي لاءِ نقصانڪار ثابت ٿئي، پنهنجي هٿن سان پنهنجو نقصان ڪرڻ، پاڻ کي مصيبت ۾ وجهڻ
antonyms: Save oneself, Protect one's interests, Secure one's position, Prosper, Succeed
englishMeaning: To do something that will cause serious trouble or ruin for yourself. To bring about your own downfall through your own actions. To behave in a way that guarantees future failure or punishment. To create the conditions of your own destruction.
synonyms: Bring about one's downfall, Self-destruct, Ruin oneself, Shoot oneself in the foot, Court disaster
urduMeaning: اپنی تباہی کا سامان خود کرنا، ایسا کام کرنا جو اپنے ہی لیے نقصان دہ ثابت ہو، اپنے ہاتھوں اپنا نقصان کرنا، خود کو مصیبت میں ڈالنا
examples: By lying to the committee, he dug his own grave. If you keep missing deadlines, you are digging your own grave. The company dug its own grave by ignoring customer complaints. She warned him that arguing with the boss was digging his own grave.

antonyms: Temporarily, Briefly, Momentarily, Short-term, For a while
word: From the cradle to the grave
urduMeaning: پیدائش سے موت تک، ساری زندگی کے دوران، زندگی کے ہر مرحلے پر، پوری عمر کی دیکھ بھال یا سہولت
examples: The state promised welfare from the cradle to the grave. He lived in the same village from the cradle to the grave. The scheme offers health cover from the cradle to the grave. Their friendship lasted from the cradle to the grave.
synonyms: Lifelong, All one's life, Womb to tomb, Throughout life, Perpetually
sindhiMeaning: ڄمڻ کان وٺي مرڻ تائين، سڄي زندگيءَ جي عرصي ۾، حياتيءَ جي هر مرحلي تي، پوري عمر جي سنڀال يا سهولت
englishMeaning: For the whole of a person's life, from birth until death. Covering every stage of life without interruption. Describing care, support, or service provided throughout a lifetime.

sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن مري ويل شخص جو موجوده ڳالهه تي سخت ناراض ٿيڻ جو تصور، اهڙو ڪم جيڪو مرحوم کي ڏاڍو ڏک ڏئي ها، سخت ناپسنديدگي ظاهر ڪرڻ لاءِ چيو ويندڙ محاورو
englishMeaning: Said of a dead person who would be shocked or angry about something happening now. Used to express that an action would deeply offend someone who has died. To indicate strong disapproval by imagining a dead person's reaction.
antonyms: Rest in peace, Approve, Be pleased, Be satisfied, Rejoice
synonyms: Roll over in one's grave, Be appalled, Be scandalised, Be horrified, Disapprove strongly
urduMeaning: کسی مرحوم کا موجودہ بات پر سخت ناراض ہونے کا تصور، ایسا کام جو فوت شدہ شخص کو بہت ناگوار گزرتا، شدید ناپسندیدگی ظاہر کرنے کا محاورہ
examples: Their grandfather would turn in his grave if he saw the house today. He would turn in his grave to hear the party abandon its principles. The founder must be turning in his grave over these changes. If she knew how the money was spent, she would turn in her grave.

urduMeaning: محاورے ’ٹرن اِن ونس گریو‘ کی امریکی صورت، کسی مرحوم کا موجودہ بات پر ناراض ہونے کا تصور، ایسا عمل جو مرحوم کے اصولوں کے خلاف ہو، شدید ناپسندیدگی کا اظہار
antonyms: Rest in peace, Approve, Be pleased, Be content, Rejoice
synonyms: Turn in one's grave, Be appalled, Be horrified, Be scandalised, Strongly disapprove
englishMeaning: The American form of 'turn in one's grave'. Said of a dead person who would be shocked, upset, or angry at something happening now. Used to show that an action strongly violates the values of someone who has died.
sindhiMeaning: محاوري ’ٽرن اِن ونس گريو‘ جو آمريڪي روپ، ڪنهن مرحوم جو موجوده ڳالهه تي ناراض ٿيڻ جو تصور، اهڙو عمل جيڪو مرحوم جي اصولن جي خلاف هجي، سخت ناپسنديدگي جو اظهار
examples: My grandmother would roll over in her grave if she heard that language. The old coach would roll over in his grave watching this performance. He is probably rolling over in his grave right now. Selling the family land would make our father roll over in his grave.

englishMeaning: A sum of money given to someone for a service, in addition to the standard charge. A tip given to a waiter, driver, or other service worker. A payment made to an employee at the end of service or on retirement. A voluntary gift of money as a token of appreciation.
antonyms: Salary, Wage, Fixed charge, Fine, Penalty, Deduction
sindhiMeaning: خدمت جي عيوض ڏنل اضافي رقم، ويٽر يا ڊرائيور کي ڏنل انعام يا ٽِپ، نوڪري ختم ٿيڻ يا رٽائرمينٽ تي ملندڙ رقم، شڪرگذاريءَ طور ڏنل رضاڪارانه تحفو، گريجويٽي
synonyms: Tip, Bonus, Reward, Perquisite, Present, Baksheesh, Honorarium, Recompense
urduMeaning: خدمت کے عوض دی جانے والی اضافی رقم، ویٹر یا ڈرائیور کو دیا جانے والا انعام یا ٹِپ، ملازمت ختم ہونے یا ریٹائرمنٹ پر ملنے والی رقم، اظہارِ تشکر کے طور پر دیا گیا رضاکارانہ تحفہ، گریجویٹی
examples: A ten percent gratuity is included in the final bill. He received a generous gratuity after thirty years of service. Passengers often leave a small gratuity for the driver. The hotel staff are not permitted to ask for a gratuity.

antonyms: Necessarily, Justifiably, Reasonably, Deservedly, For payment, Purposefully
synonyms: Needlessly, Unnecessarily, Wantonly, Unjustifiably, Freely, Without charge, Uncalled-for
englishMeaning: Without any good reason or justification. In a way that is unnecessary and often offensive. Free of charge, without payment being required. In an uncalled-for or excessive manner.
sindhiMeaning: بنا ڪنهن مناسب سبب جي، اجايو ۽ غير ضروري نموني، مفت ۾ يا بنا معاوضي جي، حد کان وڌيڪ ۽ بي مقصد طريقي سان
urduMeaning: بغیر کسی معقول وجہ کے، بلاوجہ اور غیر ضروری طور پر، مفت میں یا بلا معاوضہ، حد سے زیادہ اور بے مقصد انداز میں
examples: The film was gratuitously violent from beginning to end. He gratuitously insulted a guest who had done nothing wrong. The lawyer offered her advice gratuitously to the poor family. Critics said the scene was gratuitously shocking.

antonyms: Gratitude, Thankfulness, Appreciation, Recognition, Acknowledgement, Indebtedness
urduMeaning: ناشکری، احسان فراموشی، بھلائی کا شکر ادا نہ کرنا، کسی کی مدد کی قدر نہ کرنا، احسان کا بدلہ برائی سے دینا
examples: He was hurt by his nephew's ingratitude after years of support. Such ingratitude towards a loyal friend is hard to forgive. The letter accused the committee of sheer ingratitude. She repaid their kindness with ingratitude.
sindhiMeaning: ناشڪري، احسان فراموشي، ڀلائيءَ جو شڪر ادا نه ڪرڻ، ڪنهن جي مدد جي قدر نه ڪرڻ، احسان جو بدلو خرابيءَ سان ڏيڻ
synonyms: Thanklessness, Ungratefulness, Unappreciation, Disregard, Selfishness
englishMeaning: The state of not being thankful for kindness received. A failure to show appreciation for help or favours. Unkind behaviour towards someone who has been generous to you. Lack of gratitude or thanklessness.

antonyms: Discontinuity, Interruption, Break, Disruption, Inconsistency, Gap, Cessation
urduMeaning: بغیر کسی رکاوٹ کے جاری رہنے کی حالت، تسلسل و ربط، کسی چیز کے حصوں میں منطقی اور یکساں ربط، فلم یا کہانی میں تفصیلات کی یکسانیت، واقعات کا مسلسل سلسلہ
sindhiMeaning: بنا ڪنهن رڪاوٽ جي جاري رهڻ جي حالت، تسلسل ۽ ربط، ڪنهن شيءِ جي حصن ۾ منطقي ۽ هڪجهڙائي وارو ڳانڍاپو، فلم يا ڪهاڻيءَ ۾ تفصيلن جي هڪجهڙائي، واقعن جو مسلسل سلسلو
examples: The new manager was appointed to ensure continuity of policy. There is little continuity between the first and second chapters. A continuity error was spotted in the final scene of the film. The family business has maintained continuity for four generations.
englishMeaning: The state of continuing without interruption over a period of time. A logical and consistent connection between the parts of something. The maintenance of consistency in details across scenes of a film or story. An unbroken succession or flow of events.
synonyms: Consistency, Persistence, Flow, Succession, Cohesion, Continuance, Uninterruptedness, Connection

englishMeaning: Kept going without stopping or being interrupted. Resumed after a pause or break. Ongoing and still in progress. Extended further in time, space, or amount.
sindhiMeaning: جاري رهيل، بنا رڪاوٽ هلندڙ، وقفي کان پوءِ ٻيهر شروع ٿيل، اڃا به جاري، وقت يا مقدار ۾ اڳتي وڌايل
antonyms: Stopped, Ended, Discontinued, Halted, Interrupted, Ceased, Abandoned
examples: We are grateful for your continued support during difficult times. The trial continued for another three weeks. The story is continued on page twelve. Continued rainfall has damaged crops across the province.
synonyms: Ongoing, Sustained, Persistent, Uninterrupted, Prolonged, Resumed, Maintained, Steady
urduMeaning: جاری رہنے والا، بغیر رکاوٹ چلنے والا، وقفے کے بعد دوبارہ شروع کیا گیا، تاحال جاری، وقت یا مقدار میں آگے بڑھایا گیا

englishMeaning: To keep doing something without stopping. To begin again after an interruption. To remain in a particular place, state, or condition. To carry on further in a stated direction. To extend or prolong something in time or space.
synonyms: Carry on, Proceed, Persist, Resume, Endure, Maintain, Keep on, Prolong, Last
examples: Please continue with your work while I make a call. The meeting will continue after a short break. She continued as chairperson for another two years. The road continues for another ten kilometres.
urduMeaning: کام کو بغیر رکاوٹ جاری رکھنا، وقفے کے بعد دوبارہ شروع کرنا، کسی حالت یا جگہ پر برقرار رہنا، کسی سمت میں آگے بڑھتے رہنا، کسی چیز کو بڑھانا یا طول دینا
sindhiMeaning: ڪم کي بنا رڪاوٽ جاري رکڻ، وقفي کان پوءِ وري شروع ڪرڻ، ڪنهن حالت يا جاءِ تي برقرار رهڻ، ڪنهن طرف اڳتي وڌندو رهڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ کي وڌائڻ يا ڊگهو ڪرڻ
antonyms: Stop, Cease, Quit, Discontinue, Halt, Abandon, Finish, Pause, End

urduMeaning: کسی کام کو جاری رکھنے کا عمل، پہلے سے شروع شدہ چیز کا آگے بڑھایا ہوا حصہ، وقفے کے بعد دوبارہ آغاز، تسلسل یا اضافہ
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ڪم کي جاري رکڻ جو عمل، اڳ شروع ٿيل شيءِ جو اڳتي وڌايل حصو، وقفي کان پوءِ ٻيهر شروع ڪرڻ، تسلسل يا اضافو
antonyms: Cessation, End, Termination, Discontinuation, Stoppage, Interruption, Conclusion
englishMeaning: The action of carrying something on without stopping. A part that follows and extends something already begun. The act of resuming after a break. Something added that makes a work or process longer.
synonyms: Extension, Prolongation, Resumption, Sequel, Persistence, Maintenance, Carrying on
examples: The novel is a continuation of the author's earlier work. They voted for the continuation of the aid programme. This meeting is a continuation of yesterday's discussion. The path is a continuation of the old railway line.

urduMeaning: ایسی آواز جو سانس رہنے تک جاری رکھی جا سکے، ایسی صوتی آواز جس میں منہ مکمل طور پر بند نہ ہو، جاری رہنے والی یا برقرار رہنے والی چیز، لسانیات میں مسلسل آواز
examples: The sound of 's' is a continuant in English phonetics. Students learned to distinguish continuants from stops. Nasal consonants are treated as continuants in this analysis. The teacher gave 'f' and 'v' as examples of continuant sounds.
sindhiMeaning: اهڙو آواز جيڪو ساهه هلڻ تائين جاري رکي سگهجي، اهڙو صوتي آواز جنهن ۾ وات مڪمل بند نه ٿئي، جاري رهندڙ يا برقرار رهندڙ شيءِ، لسانيات ۾ مسلسل آواز
synonyms: Fricative, Sustained sound, Persistent, Enduring, Ongoing
englishMeaning: A speech sound that can be held for as long as the breath lasts, such as a fricative or nasal. Relating to a sound produced with an incomplete closure of the vocal tract. Something that continues or persists.
antonyms: Stop, Plosive, Occlusive, Momentary, Transient

sindhiMeaning: بار بار ۽ وري وري، ننڍن وقفن سان مسلسل، گهڻي وقت تائين هر هر ٿيندڙ، اڪثر ۽ لڳاتار
englishMeaning: Repeatedly and frequently, with short breaks in between. Again and again over a long period. In a way that happens very often and seems never to end.
antonyms: Rarely, Seldom, Occasionally, Never, Once, Infrequently
synonyms: Repeatedly, Frequently, Regularly, Persistently, Time and again, Recurrently, Often
urduMeaning: بار بار اور مسلسل، مختصر وقفوں کے ساتھ لگاتار، طویل عرصے تک بار بار ہونے والا، اکثر و بیشتر
examples: He was continually interrupting the speaker with questions. The machine continually breaks down and needs repair. Prices have risen continually over the past decade. She continually reminded us about the deadline.

antonyms: Occasional, Rare, Infrequent, Sporadic, Intermittent, Momentary
englishMeaning: Happening repeatedly with short breaks in between. Frequent and recurring over a period of time. Constant enough to be annoying or noticeable.
urduMeaning: بار بار ہونے والا، مختصر وقفوں کے ساتھ لگاتار، طویل عرصے تک دہرایا جانے والا، مسلسل اور کوفت آمیز
sindhiMeaning: بار بار ٿيندڙ، ننڍن وقفن سان لڳاتار، ڊگهي عرصي تائين ورجندڙ، مسلسل ۽ ڪوفت ڏيندڙ
examples: His continual complaints annoyed the whole office. Continual power cuts have disrupted business in the city. She suffered continual pain in her left knee. The continual noise from the street made sleep impossible.
synonyms: Repeated, Frequent, Recurrent, Persistent, Regular, Habitual, Incessant

antonyms: Termination, End, Cessation, Discontinuance, Stoppage, Conclusion
examples: The continuance of the project depends on further funding. The judge granted a continuance until the following month. They prayed for the continuance of peace in the region. His continuance in office surprised many observers.
sindhiMeaning: جاري رهڻ يا قائم رهڻ جي حالت، ڪنهن شيءِ جي مدت يا عرصو، عدالتي ڪيس جي ٻي تاريخ تي ملتوي ٿيڻ، ڪنهن عهدي يا حالت ۾ برقرار رهڻ
urduMeaning: جاری رہنے یا قائم رہنے کی حالت، کسی چیز کی مدت یا دورانیہ، عدالتی مقدمے کا آئندہ تاریخ تک ملتوی ہونا، کسی عہدے یا حالت میں برقرار رہنا
englishMeaning: The state of continuing to exist or operate. The length of time something lasts. A postponement or adjournment of a court case to a later date. The act of remaining in a particular office or condition.
synonyms: Continuation, Persistence, Duration, Endurance, Maintenance, Postponement, Adjournment

englishMeaning: In a way that depends on something else happening. Only if certain conditions are met. By chance rather than by necessity. In a manner that is possible but not certain.
antonyms: Absolutely, Unconditionally, Certainly, Necessarily, Definitely, Independently
urduMeaning: کسی دوسری بات پر انحصار کرتے ہوئے، صرف اسی صورت میں جب شرائط پوری ہوں، اتفاقی طور پر نہ کہ لازمی طور پر، ممکنہ مگر غیر یقینی انداز میں
synonyms: Conditionally, Dependently, Provisionally, Incidentally, Accidentally, Tentatively
examples: The bonus will be paid contingently on meeting the sales target. Funding was approved contingently upon the committee's final review. Events that occur contingently cannot be predicted with certainty. The agreement applies contingently, depending on the outcome of the vote.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ٻي ڳالهه تي دارومدار رکندي، صرف تڏهن جڏهن ڪي شرط پوريون ٿين، اتفاقي طور تي نه ڪي لازمي طور، ممڪن پر يقيني نه هجڻ واري انداز ۾

englishMeaning: Going on without any interruption or break. Forming an unbroken whole in space or time. Steady and uninterrupted in flow or extent. (Grammar) Describing a verb form that shows an action in progress.
urduMeaning: بغیر کسی وقفے کے مسلسل جاری، وقت یا جگہ میں غیر منقطع، لگاتار اور یکساں، گرامر میں جاری فعل ظاہر کرنے والی صورت
antonyms: Intermittent, Broken, Interrupted, Sporadic, Occasional, Irregular, Discontinuous
synonyms: Constant, Unbroken, Uninterrupted, Nonstop, Steady, Perpetual, Endless, Unceasing
sindhiMeaning: بنا ڪنهن رڪاوٽ جي مسلسل هلندڙ، وقت يا جاءِ ۾ اڻ ٽٽل، لڳاتار ۽ هڪجهڙو، گرامر ۾ جاري فعل ظاهر ڪندڙ صورت
examples: The machine produces a continuous stream of plastic sheets. We heard a continuous humming from the generator. She has been in continuous employment since 2015. The present continuous tense describes actions happening now.

englishMeaning: A bass part that runs throughout a piece of Baroque music, providing harmonic support. The instruments, usually a keyboard and a bass instrument, that play this part. Short for basso continuo, the continuous accompaniment in early music.
urduMeaning: بیروک موسیقی میں پورے ٹکڑے کے دوران جاری رہنے والا بیس حصہ، ہم آہنگی فراہم کرنے والی مسلسل سنگت، وہ ساز جو یہ حصہ بجاتے ہیں، ’باسو کونٹینوو‘ کا مختصر نام
antonyms: Melody, Solo line, Treble part, Silence
sindhiMeaning: بيروڪ موسيقيءَ ۾ سڄي ٽڪري دوران هلندڙ بيس حصو، هارمونڪ سهارو ڏيندڙ مسلسل سنگت، اهي ساز جيڪي اهو حصو وڄائين، ’باسو ڪنٽينيو‘ جو مختصر نالو
synonyms: Basso continuo, Thoroughbass, Figured bass, Accompaniment, Bass line
examples: The harpsichord played the continuo throughout the concerto. A cello and organ provided the continuo for the choir. Baroque composers relied heavily on the continuo. She studied continuo playing at the conservatory.

Only credentialed teachers may apply for this position. The hospital employs fully credentialed nursing staff. She is a credentialed translator with fifteen years of experience. Credentialed journalists were allowed inside the hall.
sindhiMeaning: سرڪاري سند يا اهليت رکندڙ، ڪنهن اداري پاران باقاعده تسليم ٿيل، شناخت يا قابليت جا دستاويز رکندڙ، مستند
synonyms: Qualified, Certified, Licensed, Accredited, Authorised, Chartered, Recognised
antonyms: Unqualified, Uncertified, Unlicensed, Unaccredited, Amateur, Untrained
englishMeaning: Holding official qualifications or certificates for a particular role. Formally recognised as qualified by an authority. Provided with documents proving identity, status, or ability.
urduMeaning: سرکاری سند یا اہلیت رکھنے والا، کسی ادارے کی جانب سے باقاعدہ تسلیم شدہ، شناخت یا قابلیت کی دستاویز رکھنے والا، مستند

antonyms: Original word, Plain text, Literal form
urduMeaning: کسی لفظ کے حروف کو آگے پیچھے کر کے بنایا گیا نیا لفظ، حروف کی ترتیب بدل کر بنایا گیا فقرہ، حروف کی پہیلی یا معمہ
englishMeaning: A word or phrase formed by rearranging the letters of another word or phrase. A word puzzle based on rearranging letters. The result of shuffling letters to create a new meaningful word.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن لفظ جي اکرن کي اڳتي پوئتي ڪري ٺاهيل نئون لفظ، اکرن جي ترتيب بدلائي ٺاهيل جملو، اکرن واري پروڙ يا معما
examples: The word 'listen' is an anagram of 'silent'. He enjoys solving anagrams in the weekend newspaper. Her pen name is an anagram of her real name. The teacher used anagrams to make spelling practice fun.
synonyms: Word puzzle, Letter rearrangement, Wordplay, Transposition, Riddle

englishMeaning: A sentence that contains every letter of the alphabet at least once. A phrase used to display fonts or test typewriters because it uses all letters. A complete-alphabet sentence created as a linguistic exercise.
antonyms: Incomplete sentence, Ordinary sentence, Partial alphabet
urduMeaning: ایسا جملہ جس میں حروفِ تہجی کا ہر حرف کم از کم ایک بار آئے، فونٹ دکھانے یا ٹائپ رائٹر جانچنے کے لیے استعمال ہونے والا جملہ، مکمل حروفِ تہجی والا جملہ
examples: 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog' is a famous pangram. Designers use a pangram to show how a typeface looks. The students were asked to write their own pangram. A perfect pangram uses each letter only once.
sindhiMeaning: اهڙو جملو جنهن ۾ الف بي جو هر اکر گهٽ ۾ گهٽ هڪ ڀيرو اچي، فونٽ ڏيکارڻ يا ٽائيپ رائيٽر جانچڻ لاءِ استعمال ٿيندڙ جملو، مڪمل الف بي وارو جملو
synonyms: Holoalphabetic sentence, Alphabet sentence, Wordplay, Language puzzle

antonyms: Dull, Drab, Plain, Shabby, Unfashionable, Dowdy, Boring
englishMeaning: Stylish, smart, and attractive in an eye-catching way. Fashionable and impressively modern. Flashy and appealing in appearance. (Informal) Very smartly dressed or designed.
examples: He turned up at the party in a snazzy blue suit. They have designed a snazzy new website for the shop. She bought a snazzy pair of sunglasses for the trip. The café has a snazzy interior full of bright colours.
synonyms: Stylish, Smart, Chic, Fashionable, Flashy, Elegant, Dashing, Trendy
urduMeaning: دلکش اور نمایاں انداز میں خوبصورت، فیشن ایبل اور جدید، چمکدار اور آنکھوں کو بھانے والا، غیر رسمی زبان میں بنا ٹھنا یا شاندار
sindhiMeaning: دلڪش ۽ نمايان انداز ۾ خوبصورت، فيشن وارو ۽ جديد، چمڪدار ۽ اکين کي وڻندڙ، غير رسمي ٻوليءَ ۾ ٺاهوڪو يا شاندار

antonyms: Peace, Calm, Quiet, Harmony, Agreement, Order, Tranquillity
urduMeaning: شور شرابے والا جھگڑا یا ہنگامہ، کسی بات پر شدید احتجاج اور شور، اختلاف کے باعث پیدا ہونے والی ہلچل، لوگوں کی جانب سے اٹھائے گئے اعتراضات یا مصیبت
synonyms: Quarrel, Row, Uproar, Commotion, Disturbance, Fracas, Brawl, Rumpus, Squabble
sindhiMeaning: گوڙ وارو جهيڙو يا هنگامو، ڪنهن ڳالهه تي شديد احتجاج ۽ شور، اختلاف سبب پيدا ٿيل هلچل، ماڻهن پاران اٿاريل اعتراض يا مصيبت
examples: There was a terrible ruction in the street last night. The decision caused a ruction among the club members. If we cancel the trip, there will be ructions at home. A ruction broke out between the two neighbours over the boundary wall.
englishMeaning: A noisy quarrel, disturbance, or fight. An angry protest or uproar about something. A commotion caused by strong disagreement. (Often plural) Trouble or objections raised by people.

urduMeaning: پردہ پوشی, راز چھپانے کی کوشش, پردہ ڈالنے کا عمل
antonyms: Disclosure, Revelation, Exposure, Confession, Unmasking
englishMeaning: An attempt to prevent people from discovering the truth about a serious mistake or crime. An action or strategy intended to conceal a scandal or illegal activity.
sindhiMeaning: پردو پوشي, لڪاءُ, راز لڪائڻ جي ڪوشش
examples: The government was accused of a massive cover-up regarding the scandal. They tried to organize a cover-up, but the journalists exposed the truth. A thorough investigation revealed the corporate cover-up. She refused to participate in the cover-up of her colleague's error.
synonyms: Concealment, Suppression, Whitewash, Disguise, Masking

antonyms: Plateau, Plain, Valley, Surface, Safety
urduMeaning: عمودی چٹان, سخت ڈھالان, کھائی, خطرناک صورتحال
sindhiMeaning: تکو ڍالو, ڪرائيندڙ ڀٽ, ڳري جبل جي چوٽي, خطرناڪ حد
englishMeaning: A very steep cliff or mass of rock, the top of which overhangs the edge. A dangerous or precarious situation that could lead to catastrophe.
examples: They stood near the edge of the steep precipice looking down at the ocean. The economy was hanging on the edge of a financial precipice. A misstep near the precipice could lead to a fatal fall. The nation was brought to the precipice of war.
synonyms: Cliff, Crag, Bluff, Abyss, Brink, Steep

examples: She decided to tuck away her old journals in the attic. The cozy cabin was tucked away in the dense forest. He can tuck away a huge meal after a hard day of work. They managed to tuck away a bit of money for retirement.
englishMeaning: To store or hide something in a safe, convenient, or secret place. To eat a large amount of food with enthusiasm.
sindhiMeaning: لڪائي رکڻ, محفوظ جڳھ تي رکڻ, ماني خوب شوق سان کائڻ
synonyms: Hide, Store, Stash, Conceal, Consume, Devour
antonyms: Display, Expose, Reveal, Show, Discard
urduMeaning: سنبھال کر رکھنا, چھپا کر رکھنا, محفوظ جگہ پر رکھنا, پیٹ بھر کر کھانا

antonyms: Tear, Rip, Break, Damage, Divide
urduMeaning: پیوند, جوڑ, زمین کا قطعہ, سافٹ ویئر پیچ, مرمت کرنا

englishMeaning: A person who uses violence and fear to achieve political aims. Someone involved in acts of terrorism. Relating to terrorism or those who carry it out. Describing an attack, group, or activity connected with terror.

sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کي مسلسل خوفزده ڪرڻ، ڊيڄارڻ ۽ دهشت ۾ رکڻ، ماڻهن کي ڊيڄاري پنهنجي قبضي ۾ رکڻ، تشدد ذريعي ڪنهن علائقي کي خوف ۾ رکڻ، ڪنهن کي بار بار تنگ ڪرڻ

sindhiMeaning: اهڙي دستاويز تي ٻي صحيح ڪرڻ جيڪا اڳ ۾ ڪنهن ٻئي دستخط ڪئي هجي، تصديق يا منظوريءَ لاءِ ٻي صحيح وجهڻ، سپاهين يا پهريدارن جو ڳجهو جوابي لفظ، سڃاڻپ جي تصديق لاءِ استعمال ٿيندڙ ڳجهو لفظ
urduMeaning: ایسی دستاویز پر دوسرے دستخط کرنا جس پر پہلے کوئی اور دستخط کر چکا ہو، تصدیق یا منظوری کے لیے دوسرا دستخط ثبت کرنا، سپاہیوں یا پہرے داروں کا خفیہ جوابی لفظ، شناخت کی تصدیق کے لیے استعمال ہونے والا خفیہ لفظ

urduMeaning: مقررہ حصہ یا محدود مقدار، کسی مدت میں اجازت شدہ زیادہ سے زیادہ تعداد، وہ ہدف جو کسی فرد یا گروہ کو پورا کرنا ہو، کسی خاص طبقے کے لیے مخصوص کیا گیا حصہ

urduMeaning: ایسا جملہ جو دہرانے کے قابل ہو، یاد رکھنے لائق اور خوبصورت انداز میں کہا گیا، جس کا حوالہ دیا جا سکے، ایسا شخص جو یادگار باتیں کہتا ہو

examples: The project was largely funded by the government. His success is largely due to hard work. The town remains largely unchanged after fifty years. Their complaints were largely ignored by the management.

urduMeaning: شراب کا شوقین اور جاننے والا شخص، مختلف شرابوں کی پرکھ رکھنے والا، مے کا قدردان، شراب کا ماہر

synonyms: Gullet, Food pipe, Alimentary canal, Throat tube, Digestive tract

englishMeaning: An irrational and persistent belief that other people are trying to harm, cheat, or mistreat one. A psychological condition marked by constant feelings of being targeted or plotted against. Extreme suspicion of others without real evidence.
synonyms: Paranoia, Victim mentality, Delusion of persecution, Suspicion, Mistrust, Insecurity
examples: His persecution complex made him distrust his closest friends. She developed a persecution complex after years of bullying. A persecution complex can seriously damage relationships. He blamed everyone, showing a clear persecution complex.

synonyms: Oppressor, Tormentor, Tyrant, Bully, Abuser, Harasser, Aggressor, Villain

antonyms: Idleness, Laziness, Surrender, Weakness, Inconstancy, Hesitation, Giving up
urduMeaning: مشکلات کے باوجود کوشش جاری رکھنا، ثابت قدمی، استقلال، ہمت نہ ہارنا، مسلسل جدوجہد
englishMeaning: Continued effort to do or achieve something despite difficulties, failure, or opposition. Steady persistence in a course of action or purpose. The quality of not giving up easily.

sindhiMeaning: نفسيات ۾ ڌيءَ جي پيءُ ڏانهن لاشعوري ڪشش ۽ ماءُ سان رقابت، اوڊيپس ڪامپليڪس جو عورتاڻو روپ، يوناني ديومالائي ڪردار ايليڪٽرا جي نالي تي رکيل اصطلاح، ڪارل يُنگ جو بيان ڪيل مرحلو

Elector's vote, Ballot, Poll vote, Formal vote, College vote, Suffrage
