examples: The operation was completely successful. She is a successful businesswoman in the city. Their campaign was successful in raising funds. He made a successful attempt to break the record.
sindhiMeaning: ڪامياب، مقصد حاصل ڪندڙ، دولت، شهرت يا مرتبو ماڻيندڙ، سٺو نتيجو ڏيندڙ
englishMeaning: Achieving the aim or result that was wanted. Having gained wealth, fame, or a high position. Producing a good outcome or working effectively.
urduMeaning: کامیاب، مقصد حاصل کرنے والا، دولت، شہرت یا مقام حاصل کرنے والا، اچھا نتیجہ دینے والا
synonyms: Prosperous, Triumphant, Victorious, Thriving, Effective, Fruitful, Accomplished, Flourishing
antonyms: Unsuccessful, Failed, Unproductive, Fruitless, Ineffective, Losing

sindhiMeaning: ڪاميابيءَ سان، مقصد حاصل ڪندي، سٺي نتيجي سان، ڪامياب انداز ۾
antonyms: Unsuccessfully, Ineffectively, Fruitlessly, Vainly, Poorly
englishMeaning: In a way that achieves the desired aim or result. With a good and favourable outcome. In a manner marked by achievement or prosperity.
urduMeaning: کامیابی کے ساتھ، مقصد حاصل کرتے ہوئے، اچھے نتیجے کے ساتھ، کامیاب انداز میں
synonyms: Triumphantly, Effectively, Victoriously, Fruitfully, Prosperously, Satisfactorily
examples: She successfully completed her degree in three years. The team successfully defended their title. The medicine was used successfully in many patients. He successfully persuaded them to change the plan.

englishMeaning: The act or order of following one after another. A sequence or series. The process of inheriting a position, title, property, or right. In ecology, the gradual replacement of one plant or animal community by another.
antonyms: Interruption, Break, Discontinuity, Disorder, Failure to inherit, End
urduMeaning: سلسلہ، لگاتار آنا، جانشینی، وراثت یا عہدے پر آنا، ترتیب، ماحولیات میں ایک جاندار برادری کا دوسری سے آہستہ بدلنا
sindhiMeaning: سلسلو، لڳاتار اچڻ، جانشيني، وراثت يا عهدي تي اچڻ، ترتيب، ماحوليات ۾ هڪ جاندار برادري جي ٻي سان آهستي تبديلي
synonyms: Sequence, Series, Continuity, Inheritance, Order, Lineage, Replacement
examples: The company had a clear succession plan. A succession of storms damaged the coast. The king's death caused a dispute over succession. Forest succession can take many years. She answered a succession of difficult questions.

sindhiMeaning: رسيلو  نرم ۽ مزيدار، خاص ڪري کاڌي جي حوالي سان، پاڻي سان ڀرپور ۽ کائڻ ۾ وڻندڙ، اهڙو ٻوٽو جنهن جا ٿلها پن يا ڏانڊيون پاڻي جمع ڪن، ٿوهر جهڙو خشڪ ماحول ۾ ٿيندڙ ٻوٽو
antonyms: Dry, Tough, Withered, Stale, Tasteless, Parched, Shrivelled, Arid
urduMeaning: رسیلا  نرم اور لذیذ، خاص طور پر کھانے کے حوالے سے، نمی سے بھرپور اور کھانے میں خوشگوار، ایسا پودا جس کے موٹے پتے یا تنے پانی محفوظ رکھتے ہیں، ناگ پھنی جیسا خشک ماحول کا پودا
synonyms: Juicy, Luscious, Tender, Moist, Flavourful, Fleshy, Ripe, Mouth-watering
examples: We enjoyed a succulent roast chicken for dinner. The mangoes were sweet and succulent. Succulent plants need very little water. She keeps a shelf of small succulents by the window.
englishMeaning: Juicy, tender, and full of flavour, especially of food. Rich in moisture and pleasing to eat. Of a plant, having thick fleshy leaves or stems that store water. A plant such as a cactus that is adapted to dry conditions.

sindhiMeaning: عمر ۾ وڏو مالدار مرد جيڪو نوجوان ساٿيءَ تي پئسو خرچ ڪري، سنگت جي بدلي مالي مدد ڏيندڙ امير مرد، عام معنيٰ ۾ ڪنهن کي دل کولي پئسو ڏيندڙ سرپرست
synonyms: Benefactor, Patron, Financial backer, Provider, Sponsor, Keeper
examples: The tabloids claimed she had found a sugar daddy. He jokes that the company's investor is its sugar daddy. She refused to be seen as anyone's sugar daddy arrangement. Gossip about a sugar daddy followed the young actor everywhere.
englishMeaning: A wealthy older man who gives money or gifts to a much younger partner. A rich man who supports someone financially in return for companionship. Informally, any generous financial backer of a person or project.
urduMeaning: عمر رسیدہ دولت مند مرد جو نوجوان ساتھی پر پیسہ خرچ کرے، رفاقت کے بدلے مالی مدد دینے والا امیر شخص، عام معنی میں کھلے دل سے مالی سرپرستی کرنے والا
antonyms: Dependant, Beggar, Freeloader, Sponger, Pauper, Equal partner
Lunar eclipse, Full sunlight, Bright day
sindhiMeaning: فلڪياتي واقعو جيڪو تڏهن ٿئي ٿو جڏهن چنڊ ڌرتيءَ ۽ سج جي وچ ۾ گذري ٿو، سج جي سموري يا ڪجهه روشنيءَ کي بلاڪ ڪري ٿو، اهو واقعو جنهن ۾ سج اونداهو يا چنڊ جي ڇانوَ کان ڍڪيل نظر اچي ٿو، سج جي روشنيءَ جو عارضي طور تي بلاڪ ٿيڻ جڏهن چنڊ سج جي اڳيان لنگهي ٿو
englishMeaning: An astronomical event that occurs when the moon passes between the Earth and the sun, blocking all or part of the sun's light. A phenomenon where the sun appears darkened or obscured by the moon's shadow. The temporary blocking of sunlight as the moon crosses in front of the sun.
examples: The sun eclipse darkened the sky at midday. Scientists traveled to observe the total sun eclipse. Never look directly at a sun eclipse without protection. The sun eclipse lasted for three minutes.
urduMeaning: فلکیاتی واقعہ جو اس وقت ہوتا ہے جب چاند زمین اور سورج کے درمیان سے گزرتا ہے، سورج کی تمام یا کچھ روشنی کو بلاک کرتا ہے، وہ واقعہ جس میں سورج اندھیرا یا چاند کے سائے سے ڈھکا ہوا نظر آتا ہے، سورج کی روشنی کا عارضی طور پر بلاک ہونا جب چاند سورج کے سامنے سے گزرتا ہے
synonyms: Solar eclipse, Eclipse of the sun, Solar darkening

urduMeaning: ضرورت سے زیادہ، غیر ضروری، ایسا جو کوئی فائدہ نہ دے، فالتو اور بے مقصد، تحریر یا کام میں غیر ضروری اضافہ
synonyms: Unnecessary, Redundant, Excess, Surplus, Needless, Extra, Uncalled for
sindhiMeaning: ضرورت کان وڌيڪ، غير ضروري، اهڙو جيڪو ڪو فائدو نه ڏئي، فالتو ۽ بي مقصد، لکڻ يا ڪم ۾ غير ضروري اضافو
examples: The editor removed several superfluous paragraphs. Any further explanation would be superfluous. He packed a few superfluous items he never used. Superfluous detail can weaken a good argument.
englishMeaning: More than is needed or wanted. Unnecessary because it adds nothing useful. Extra and therefore serving no real purpose. Redundant in a piece of writing, work, or arrangement.
antonyms: Necessary, Essential, Vital, Required, Useful, Indispensable
Tax relief, Rebate, Exemption, Deduction, Refund, Allowance
urduMeaning: پہلے سے عائد ٹیکس کے اوپر لگایا جانے والا اضافی ٹیکس, ایک زائد محصول جو مقررہ حد سے زیادہ آمدنی پر لگے, اضافی ٹیکس عائد کرنا, زائد محصول
examples: The government introduced a surtax on very high incomes. A small surtax was added to imported luxury goods. Businesses protested against the new surtax. The council decided to surtax second properties in the city.
englishMeaning: An additional tax charged on top of an existing tax. An extra levy imposed on income or goods above a certain level. To impose such an additional tax on a person, company, or product.
sindhiMeaning: اڳ ۾ لڳل ٽيڪس مٿان وڌيڪ لڳايل ٽيڪس, هڪ اضافي محصول جيڪو خاص حد کان مٿي آمدني تي لڳي, اضافي ٽيڪس مڙهڻ, واڌو محصول
synonyms: Additional tax, Extra levy, Supertax, Surcharge, Excise, Duty

examples: The opera was performed in Italian with English surtitles. Surtitles helped the audience follow the complex plot. The theatre installed a new screen for surtitles. Without surtitles, many visitors would have missed the jokes.
synonyms: Captions, Subtitles, Supertitles, Translations, Screen text
sindhiMeaning: اسٽيج مٿان ڏيکاريل ترجمو ٿيل جملا, اوپيرا يا ڊرامي دوران مٿي ڏيکاريل عبارت, ٻولي سمجهڻ لاءِ ڏنل لکت, ناظرين جي سهولت لاءِ لکيل ترجمو
urduMeaning: اسٹیج کے اوپر دکھائے جانے والے ترجمہ شدہ جملے, اوپیرا یا ڈرامے کے دوران اوپر نمایاں کی گئی عبارت, زبان سمجھنے کے لیے دی گئی تحریر, ناظرین کی سہولت کے لیے لکھا گیا ترجمہ
antonyms: Untranslated dialogue, Original speech, Silence, Dubbing
englishMeaning: Translated words or captions projected above a stage during an opera or foreign-language play. On-screen text that helps an audience follow dialogue or lyrics in another language. A theatrical device used to make performances accessible to wider audiences.

examples: The company carried out a survey of customer satisfaction. Engineers will survey the site before construction begins. He stood on the hill and surveyed the valley below. According to the survey, most residents support the new park.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن علائقي جو جائزو وٺڻ يا ماپڻ, غور سان ڏسڻ ۽ پرکڻ, ماڻهن جي راءِ گڏ ڪرڻ وارو مطالعو, تفصيلي معائنو يا رپورٽ
synonyms: Examine, Inspect, Study, Review, Poll, Questionnaire, Assessment, Overview
antonyms: Ignore, Overlook, Neglect, Disregard, Guess
urduMeaning: کسی علاقے کا جائزہ لینا یا اس کی پیمائش کرنا, غور سے دیکھنا اور پرکھنا, لوگوں کی رائے جمع کرنے والا مطالعہ, تفصیلی معائنہ یا رپورٹ
englishMeaning: To examine and record the measurements, features, or condition of an area or building. To look carefully at something as a whole in order to form an opinion. A detailed study of people's opinions collected through questions. A general view, inspection, or written report of a subject.

examples: The surveyor marked the boundary of the new plot. A qualified surveyor inspected the house before the sale. The surveyor's report delayed the construction work. She works as a land surveyor for the city council.
englishMeaning: A person whose job is to measure and record the features and boundaries of land. A professional who examines the condition and value of buildings and property. An official who inspects and reports on structures, roads, or equipment.
urduMeaning: زمین کی پیمائش کرنے والا ماہر, عمارتوں کی حالت اور قیمت کا جائزہ لینے والا, حد بندی اور نقشہ سازی کرنے والا فرد, سرکاری معائنہ کرنے والا افسر
synonyms: Land measurer, Assessor, Inspector, Valuer, Examiner, Appraiser
antonyms: Owner, Builder, Buyer, Labourer, Client
sindhiMeaning: زمين ماپڻ وارو ماهر, عمارتن جي حالت ۽ قدر جو جائزو وٺندڙ, حد بندي ۽ نقشه سازي ڪندڙ فرد, سرڪاري معائنو ڪندڙ آفيسر

synonyms: Endurable, Bearable, Recoverable, Sustainable, Livable, Tolerable
sindhiMeaning: جنهن مان بچي سگهجي, اهڙو حادثو يا بيماري جنهن مان جان بچائي سگهجي, برداشت لائق, جيئرو رهڻ جي گنجائش رکندڙ
examples: Doctors said the injury was serious but survivable. Modern car design makes many crashes survivable. The disease is survivable if it is detected early. Engineers work to make aircraft accidents more survivable.
englishMeaning: Able to be survived or lived through. Describing an accident, illness, or condition that a person can come out of alive. Capable of being endured without causing death or total destruction.
antonyms: Fatal, Deadly, Lethal, Unsurvivable, Terminal, Mortal
urduMeaning: جس سے بچنا ممکن ہو, ایسا حادثہ یا بیماری جس سے زندہ بچا جا سکے, قابل برداشت, زندہ رہنے کی گنجائش رکھنے والا

synonyms: Self-reliance, Preparedness, Self-sufficiency, Prepping, Endurance philosophy
englishMeaning: The belief in and practice of preparing to survive a serious disaster or breakdown of society. A way of life focused on stockpiling supplies and learning skills needed to stay alive in emergencies. The philosophy that individuals must be ready to protect themselves when normal systems fail.
examples: Survivalism became popular after the widespread power failures. His interest in survivalism began with a wilderness course. Books on survivalism fill an entire shelf in his study. Critics argue that survivalism encourages unnecessary fear.
urduMeaning: آفت یا تباہی سے بچنے کی تیاری کا نظریہ, بقا کے لیے سامان اور مہارتیں جمع کرنے کا طریقہ, ہنگامی حالات میں زندہ رہنے کی تربیت کا رجحان, خود انحصاری کا فلسفہ
antonyms: Dependence, Complacency, Helplessness, Unpreparedness, Reliance
sindhiMeaning: آفت يا تباهي کان بچڻ جي تياري ڪرڻ جو نظريو, بقا لاءِ سامان ۽ هنر گڏ ڪرڻ جو طريقو, هنگامي حالتن ۾ جيئرو رهڻ جي تربيت وٺڻ جو رجحان, خود انحصاريءَ جو فلسفو

synonyms: Prepper, Self-reliant person, Outdoorsman, Doomsday prepper, Endurer
sindhiMeaning: اهو شخص جيڪو آفتن کان بچڻ جي اڳواٽ تياري ڪري, کاڌو ۽ سامان ذخيرو ڪندڙ ماڻهو, بقا جي هنر سکندڙ فرد, بقا پرستيءَ سان لاڳاپيل
urduMeaning: وہ شخص جو آفات سے بچنے کی پیشگی تیاری کرے, خوراک اور سامان ذخیرہ کرنے والا, بقا کی مہارتیں سیکھنے والا فرد, بقا پرستی سے متعلق
examples: The survivalist kept a year's supply of food in his cellar. She joined a survivalist group to learn first aid and navigation. His survivalist habits surprised his neighbours. The documentary followed a family living a survivalist lifestyle.
antonyms: Dependent, Unprepared person, Consumer, Idler
englishMeaning: A person who prepares in advance to survive a natural disaster, war, or collapse of society. Someone who stores food, water, and equipment and learns skills for emergencies. Relating to the beliefs or practices of such a person.

synonyms: Doubtful, Distrustful, Wary, Sceptical, Questionable, Dubious, Shady
sindhiMeaning: شڪي، ڪنهن تي اعتبار نه ڪندڙ، اهڙو جيڪو شڪ پيدا ڪري، مشڪوڪ رويو رکندڙ، محتاط ۽ جلد يقين نه ڪندڙ
englishMeaning: Feeling that something is wrong or that someone cannot be trusted. Causing a feeling of doubt or distrust. Behaving in a way that makes people think something is dishonest. Cautious and unwilling to believe easily.
examples: The police found a suspicious bag near the gate. She became suspicious when he changed his story. His suspicious behaviour attracted the guard's attention. I am suspicious of offers that sound too good.
urduMeaning: شکی، کسی پر اعتبار نہ کرنے والا، ایسا جو شبہ پیدا کرے، مشکوک رویہ رکھنے والا، محتاط اور جلدی یقین نہ کرنے والا
antonyms: Trusting, Confident, Certain, Unsuspecting, Credible, Innocent, Genuine

examples: A pair of swans glided across the quiet lake. The dancer moved with the grace of a swan. He swanned into the office an hour late. Swans are protected birds in many countries.
urduMeaning: ہنس، لمبی گردن والا بڑا سفید آبی پرندہ، حسن اور نفاست کی علامت، بے فکری سے گھومنا پھرنا
synonyms: Waterbird, Cygnet, Wander, Drift, Saunter, Roam
englishMeaning: A large waterbird with a long neck, usually white, known for its grace. A symbol of beauty, elegance, or purity. To move around in a relaxed and carefree manner, often in a way that annoys others.
antonyms: Hurry, Rush, Toil, Labour, Stay put
sindhiMeaning: هنج، ڊگهي ڳچيءَ وارو وڏو اڇو آبي پکي، حسن ۽ نفاست جي علامت، بي فڪر ٿي گهمڻ ڦرڻ

antonyms: Debut, Opening, Beginning, First appearance, Premiere
synonyms: Farewell, Finale, Last act, Final performance, Curtain call
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ماڻهوءَ جو آخري ڪم يا پرفارمنس، رٽائرمينٽ يا موت کان اڳ آخري ڪارنامو، ڪيريئر جي آخري ڪوشش، وڇوڙي جو آخري اظهار
examples: That concert proved to be the singer's swan song. He wrote the novel as a swan song to his long career. The match was the veteran captain's swan song. Her final lecture was a memorable swan song.
urduMeaning: کسی شخص کی آخری کارکردگی یا کارنامہ، ریٹائرمنٹ یا موت سے پہلے آخری کام، کیریئر کی آخری کوشش، الوداعی اظہار
englishMeaning: The final performance or achievement of a person before retirement or death. A last work, appearance, or effort in a career. A farewell gesture marking the end of something.

synonyms: Dressmaker, Garment maker, Seamstress, Adapt, Customise, Fit, Modify
examples: The tailor finished the suit two days before the wedding. We can tailor the course to suit your requirements. She asked the tailor to shorten the sleeves. The company tailors its services for small businesses.
urduMeaning: درزی، کپڑے سینے یا درست کرنے والا، کسی خاص مقصد کے لیے کوئی چیز بنانا یا ڈھالنا، ناپ کے مطابق کپڑے سینا
sindhiMeaning: درزي، ڪپڙا سبڻ يا سنوارڻ وارو، ڪنهن خاص مقصد لاءِ ڪا شيءِ ٺاهڻ يا ڍالڻ، ماپ مطابق ڪپڙا سبڻ
englishMeaning: A person who makes or alters clothes, especially for men. To make or adapt something for a particular purpose or person. To sew clothes to fit an individual's measurements. To adjust a plan or service to specific needs.
antonyms: Standardise, Mass-produce, Generalise, Leave unaltered
Ready-made, Off-the-peg, Standard, Generic, Loose, Ill-fitting
urduMeaning: ناپ کے مطابق سلا ہوا، کسی خاص مقصد کے لیے تیار کیا گیا، جسم پر ٹھیک بیٹھنے والا اور سلیقے سے سلا ہوا، مخصوص ضروریات کے مطابق بنایا گیا
sindhiMeaning: ماپ مطابق سبيل، ڪنهن خاص مقصد لاءِ تيار ڪيل، جسم سان ٺهڪندڙ ۽ سليقي سان سبيل، خاص ضرورتن مطابق ٺهيل
examples: He wore a beautifully tailored grey jacket. The bank offers tailored loans for farmers. She received a tailored training plan from her coach. The tailored curtains fitted the windows perfectly.
synonyms: Custom-made, Bespoke, Fitted, Personalised, Customised, Well-cut, Adapted
englishMeaning: Made or adapted for a particular person or purpose. Cut and sewn to fit closely and neatly. Specially designed to meet specific needs. Smart and well-fitted in appearance.

urduMeaning: کسی کو غلطی سے کوئی اور سمجھ لینا، کسی کو کسی خاص انداز میں خیال کرنا، ایک شخص کو دوسرا سمجھ بیٹھنا، بغیر تصدیق کے کوئی بات مان لینا
examples: I took him for the manager of the shop. Do not take me for a fool. She was often taken for her elder sister. They took his silence for agreement.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کي غلطيءَ سان ٻيو ڪو سمجهڻ، ڪنهن کي ڪنهن خاص نموني ۾ سمجهڻ يا ڀائڻ، هڪ ماڻهوءَ کي ٻئي سان مشابهه سمجهي وٺڻ، بنا پرکڻ جي ڪا ڳالهه مڃي وٺڻ
synonyms: Mistake for, Assume, Suppose, Regard as, Consider, Believe to be, Presume, Confuse with
englishMeaning: To wrongly believe that someone or something is a particular person or thing. To regard or consider in a certain way. To mistake one person for another. To assume something without checking.
antonyms: Recognise, Identify correctly, Know, Distinguish, Verify

examples: He took ill during the journey and had to return. She took ill soon after the wedding. Do not take it ill if I speak frankly. He took my advice ill and stopped talking to me.
synonyms: Fall sick, Become ill, Sicken, Be taken unwell, Resent, Be offended, Take offence
urduMeaning: اچانک بیمار ہو جانا، بیماری میں مبتلا ہونا، کسی بات پر ناراض ہونا، کسی کی بات کا برا مان جانا
englishMeaning: To become sick or unwell suddenly. To fall into illness. To be offended by something said or done. To receive a remark badly.
antonyms: Recover, Get well, Stay healthy, Be pleased, Appreciate, Take kindly
sindhiMeaning: اوچتو بيمار ٿي پوڻ، بيماريءَ ۾ مبتلا ٿيڻ، ڪنهن ڳالهه تي ناراض ٿيڻ، ڪنهن جي ڳالهه کي خراب نموني وٺڻ

examples: The divorce settlement took him to the cleaners. Those online scammers took her to the cleaners. Our team was taken to the cleaners in the final. Be careful with that contract or they will take you to the cleaners.
synonyms: Swindle, Fleece, Cheat, Defraud, Rip off, Con, Bankrupt, Trounce, Beat badly
urduMeaning: کسی سے سارے پیسے نکلوا لینا، دھوکہ دے کر بڑا نقصان پہنچانا، کسی کو مالی طور پر تباہ کر دینا، مقابلے میں بری طرح شکست دینا
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کان سڀ پئسا ڦٻائي وٺڻ، ٺڳي ڪري وڏو نقصان پهچائڻ، ڪنهن کي مالي طور تباهه ڪري ڇڏڻ، مقابلي ۾ بري طرح شڪست ڏيڻ
antonyms: Compensate, Reimburse, Enrich, Repay, Deal fairly, Reward, Lose to
englishMeaning: To take all or most of someone's money, often unfairly. To cheat or swindle a person out of a large sum. To defeat someone completely in a game, contest, or lawsuit. To cause someone heavy financial loss.

examples: The children took to their new teacher at once. After his retirement he took to gardening. The villagers took to the hills when the flood came. She has taken to walking every morning before work.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کي پسند ڪرڻ لڳڻ، ڪا ڳالهه عادت طور شروع ڪرڻ، بچاءَ لاءِ ڪنهن جاءِ ڏانهن وڃڻ، ڪو نئون طريقو يا زندگيءَ جو ڍنگ اختيار ڪرڻ
synonyms: Like, Grow fond of, Adopt, Begin, Resort to, Turn to, Take up, Warm to
antonyms: Dislike, Avoid, Abandon, Give up, Reject, Shun, Quit
englishMeaning: To begin to like someone or something. To start doing something as a habit. To go to a place for safety or escape. To adopt a new practice or way of life.
urduMeaning: کسی کو پسند کرنے لگنا، کوئی کام عادت کے طور پر شروع کر دینا، پناہ کے لیے کسی جگہ چلے جانا، کوئی نیا طریقہ یا طرزِ زندگی اپنانا

synonyms: Flee, Run away, Bolt, Escape, Dash off, Scamper, Take flight, Make off
englishMeaning: To run away quickly, especially to escape danger. To flee in a hurry. To escape by running rather than facing a situation.
examples: The thief took to his heels when the alarm rang. Seeing the police, the boys took to their heels. He took to his heels and disappeared into the crowd. The dog barked and the stranger took to his heels.
sindhiMeaning: تڪڙ ۾ ڀڄي وڃڻ، خاص ڪري خطري کان بچڻ لاءِ، جلدي ۾ فرار ٿيڻ، صورتحال کي منهن ڏيڻ بدران ڀڄي نڪرڻ
urduMeaning: تیزی سے بھاگ جانا، خاص طور پر خطرے سے بچنے کے لیے، جلدی میں فرار ہونا، صورتِ حال کا سامنا کرنے کے بجائے بھاگ نکلنا
antonyms: Stand firm, Stay, Face, Confront, Remain, Resist, Hold ground

urduMeaning: کسی کو غلطی پر ڈانٹنا یا سرزنش کرنا، کسی سے غلط کام کا جواب طلب کرنا، لاپروائی یا نامناسب رویّے پر سختی سے تنبیہ کرنا
synonyms: Reprimand, Scold, Rebuke, Reproach, Censure, Chide, Admonish, Berate, Upbraid
examples: The manager took him to task for arriving late. She was taken to task for the errors in the report. Parents should take their children to task politely. The editor took the writer to task over false figures.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کي غلطيءَ تي ڇنڊڇاڻ ڪرڻ يا جھڻڪڻ، ڪنهن کان ڪيل غلط ڪم جو حساب گهرڻ، لاپرواهي يا نامناسب رويي تي سختيءَ سان سرزنش ڪرڻ
englishMeaning: To criticise or scold someone for a fault. To call a person to account for wrongdoing. To reprimand firmly for careless or improper behaviour.
antonyms: Praise, Commend, Applaud, Compliment, Encourage, Excuse, Overlook
Believe fully, Trust completely, Accept, Rely on, Take at face value
examples: Take his account of the accident with a grain of salt. Online reviews should be taken with a pinch of salt. I take her promises with a grain of salt now. Take those figures with a pinch of salt until they are checked.
englishMeaning: To accept a statement with doubt or reserve. To believe something only partly, allowing for exaggeration. To treat information cautiously rather than as full truth.
word: Take with a grain or pinch of salt
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ڳالهه کي شڪ سان قبول ڪرڻ، ڪنهن ڳالهه تي پورو ڀروسو نه ڪرڻ ۽ وڌاءَ جو خيال رکڻ، معلومات کي احتياط سان وٺڻ نه ڪي مڪمل سچ
synonyms: Doubt, Question, Be sceptical, Distrust slightly, Treat cautiously, Not take literally
urduMeaning: کسی بات کو شک کے ساتھ قبول کرنا، کسی بات پر پورا یقین نہ کرنا اور مبالغے کا خیال رکھنا، معلومات کو مکمل سچ کے بجائے احتیاط سے لینا

englishMeaning: To talk to someone for a very long time, often tiring or boring them. To speak at excessive length without letting the other person contribute.
antonyms: Keep quiet, Be brief, Stay silent, Listen, Hush
urduMeaning: کسی سے اتنی زیادہ باتیں کرنا کہ وہ تھک جائے, دوسرے کو موقع نہ دیتے ہوئے بہت لمبی بات کرنا
synonyms: Chatter, Prattle, Ramble on, Jabber, Go on and on, Bore
examples: My neighbour talked my ear off about his garden. She will talk your ear off if you let her start. He talked the poor clerk's ear off over one form. Be ready; that driver talks everyone's ear off.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن سان ايترو گهڻو ڳالهائڻ جو هو ٿڪجي پوي, ٻئي کي موقعو نه ڏيندي حد کان وڌيڪ ڳالهائڻ

synonyms: Chatty, Garrulous, Loquacious, Communicative, Voluble, Gossipy, Conversational
examples: He becomes very talkative after a cup of tea. The talkative passenger kept everyone entertained. She is shy at first but soon grows talkative. A talkative child can be tiring at bedtime.
sindhiMeaning: گهڻو ڳالهائيندڙ, ڳالهائڻ جو شوقين, ٻڌ ٻڌ ڪندڙ, ڳالهڙيو
englishMeaning: Fond of talking a great deal. Inclined to speak more than is necessary. Chatty and communicative by nature.
antonyms: Quiet, Silent, Reserved, Taciturn, Reticent, Shy, Tight-lipped
urduMeaning: بہت باتیں کرنے والا, باتونی, گفتگو کا شوقین, بک بک کرنے والا

synonyms: Count, Total, Record, Score, Reckoning, Match, Correspond, Compute, Agree
examples: He kept a tally of the runs scored in the match. Please tally the votes and announce the result. Her account of the incident does not tally with his. The final tally showed a clear victory for the team.
urduMeaning: گنتی، حساب، پوائنٹس یا اشیاء کا ریکارڈ، گنتی کے لیے لگایا جانے والا نشان، شمار کرنا، دوسری چیز سے مطابقت رکھنا
sindhiMeaning: ڳاڻاٽو، حساب، پوائنٽن يا شين جو رڪارڊ، ڳڻپ لاءِ نشان، ڳڻڻ يا جوڙ ڪڍڻ، ٻي شيءِ سان ميل کائڻ يا برابر هجڻ
englishMeaning: A record or count of a number of items, points, or scores. A mark used in counting, usually a stroke in groups of five. To count or calculate a total. To match or correspond with something else exactly.
antonyms: Differ, Disagree, Conflict, Mismatch, Contradict
Secant, Chord, Relevant, On-topic, Perpendicular, Intersecting
sindhiMeaning: هڪ سڌي لڪير جيڪا وکر کي رڳو هڪ نقطي تي ڇهي پر ڪٽي نه، سوچ يا عمل جي بلڪل مختلف طريقي، مثلثاتي فنڪشن جيڪو سامهون واري رخ جو ڀرسان واري رخ سان تناسب برابر هجي، ڇهڻ وارو پر ڪٽڻ نه وارو
examples: Draw a tangent to the circle at point P. The professor went off on a tangent during the lecture. Calculate the tangent of 45 degrees. The two circles are tangent to each other.
englishMeaning: A straight line that touches a curve at a single point without crossing it. A completely different line of thought or action. The trigonometric function equal to the ratio of opposite to adjacent sides. Touching but not intersecting.
synonyms: Touching line, Contact line, Digression, Deviation, Tan (trigonometry)
urduMeaning: ایک سیدھی لکیر جو خم کو صرف ایک نقطے پر چھوئے لیکن کاٹے نہیں، سوچ یا عمل کی بالکل مختلف سمت، مثلثاتی فنکشن جو مخالف ضلع کا ملحقہ ضلع سے تناسب برابر ہو، چھونے والا لیکن کاٹنے نہ والا
دو یا زیادہ دائرے جو ایک دوسرے کو بالکل ایک نقطے پر چھوئیں لیکن کاٹیں نہیں، دائرے جن میں رابطے کا ایک واحد مشترکہ نقطہ ہو، دائرے جو ایک دوسرے سے باہر سے یا اندر سے مماس ہوں
antonyms: Intersecting circles, Overlapping circles, Separate circles, Non-touching circles
synonyms: Touching circles, Kissing circles, Osculating circles, Circles with single contact point
englishMeaning: Two or more circles that touch each other at exactly one point without crossing. Circles that have a single common point of contact. Circles that are externally or internally tangent to each other.
sindhiMeaning: ٻه يا وڌيڪ دائرا جيڪي هڪ ٻئي کي بلڪل هڪ نقطي تي ڇهن پر ڪٽن نه، دائرا جن ۾ رابطي جو هڪ واحد گڏيل نقطو هجي، دائرا جيڪي هڪ ٻئي سان ٻاهران يا اندران ڇهندڙ هجن
examples: Two tangent circles share only one point. The gears are designed as tangent circles. Tangent circles do not overlap or intersect. The diagram shows externally tangent circles.

antonyms: Central, Direct, Relevant, Main, Essential, Perpendicular, Core, Focused
sindhiMeaning: ڇهڻ واري لڪير سان لاڳاپيل، ڪنهن وکر يا مٿاڇري کي رڳو هڪ نقطي تي ڇهڻ وارو، بنيادي موضوع سان معمولي تعلق رکڻ وارو، مکيه نقطي کان ڀڄڻ وارو
urduMeaning: مماس سے متعلق، کسی خم یا سطح کو صرف ایک نقطے پر چھونے والا، بنیادی موضوع سے معمولی تعلق رکھنے والا، اصل نکتے سے ہٹنے والا
examples: The line is tangential to the circle at point A. His remarks were tangential to the main discussion. The professor made a tangential comment about history. The tangential velocity increases with distance from the center.
englishMeaning: Relating to or along a tangent. Touching a curve or surface at a single point without crossing it. Only slightly connected or related to the main subject. Diverging from a main point or course.
synonyms: Peripheral, Incidental, Divergent, Oblique, Irrelevant, Side, Digressive, Marginal

antonyms: Cyclic quadrilateral, Inscribed quadrilateral, Irregular quadrilateral
sindhiMeaning: اهو چوڪنڊو جنهن جا چارئي پاسا هڪ اندروني دائري کي ڇُهن ٿا, اهو چئن پاسن وارو شڪل جيڪو دائري کي گهيري ٿو, اهو چوڪنڊو جنهن ۾ سامهون وارن پاسن جي ٻن جوڙن جا مجموعا برابر هوندا آهن, جنهن کي محيطي يا مماسي چوڪنڊو به چيو ويندو آهي
urduMeaning: وہ رباعی جس کے چاروں اضلاع ایک اندرونی دائرے کو مس کرتے ہیں, وہ چار اضلاع والی شکل جو دائرے کو گھیرتی ہے, وہ رباعی جس میں مقابل اضلاع کے دو جوڑوں کے مجموعے برابر ہوتے ہیں, جسے محیطی یا مماسی رباعی بھی کہا جاتا ہے
englishMeaning: A quadrilateral whose four sides are all tangent to one inscribed circle. A four-sided figure that circumscribes a circle. A quadrilateral in which the sums of the two pairs of opposite sides are equal. Also known as a circumscribed or tangent quadrilateral.
examples: In a tangential quadrilateral the sums of opposite sides are equal. A rhombus is always a tangential quadrilateral. The circle inside a tangential quadrilateral is called the incircle. He constructed a tangential quadrilateral around a given circle.
synonyms: Circumscribed quadrilateral, Tangent quadrilateral, Circumscriptible quadrilateral

antonyms: Bright, Vivid, Bold, Colourful, White, Black
englishMeaning: A dark greyish brown colour. A neutral shade between grey and brown, often used in fashion and interiors. Of or having this muted brownish grey colour.
sindhiMeaning: گهرو خاڪي مائل ناسي رنگ، خاڪي ۽ ناسي جي وچ وارو غير جانبدار رنگ، اهڙي هلڪي ناسي خاڪي رنگ جو
urduMeaning: گہرا سرمئی مائل بھورا رنگ، سرمئی اور بھورے کے درمیان کا غیر جانبدار رنگ، ایسے دھیمے بھورے سرمئی رنگ کا
examples: She chose taupe paint for the hallway. The sofa was upholstered in a soft taupe fabric. Taupe shoes go well with almost any outfit. The room's taupe walls created a calm atmosphere.
synonyms: Greyish brown, Mushroom, Beige, Fawn, Stone, Neutral, Dun

sindhiMeaning: ڇڪيل يا تنگ، ڍرو نه، تڻاءُ يا پريشاني ظاهر ڪندڙ، سٺي ترتيب ۽ سخت ضابطي هيٺ، مختصر ۽ جامع نموني لکيل
antonyms: Slack, Loose, Relaxed, Limp, Flabby, Baggy
englishMeaning: Stretched or pulled tight, not slack. Showing tension, strain, or anxiety. Kept in good order and under firm control. Written or expressed concisely with no wasted words.
synonyms: Tight, Tense, Stretched, Rigid, Strained, Firm, Concise
urduMeaning: کھنچا ہوا یا تنا ہوا، ڈھیلا نہیں، تناؤ یا پریشانی ظاہر کرنے والا، مضبوط نظم و ضبط میں، مختصر اور جامع انداز میں لکھا ہوا
examples: Make sure the rope is taut before you climb. His face was taut with worry as he waited for the news. The captain runs a taut ship and expects discipline. The novel has a taut plot that never loses pace.

antonyms: Pale, Grey, White, Black, Colourless, Dark
sindhiMeaning: گرم واريءَ جهڙي يا نارنگي مائل ناسي رنگ جو، شينهن يا سڪل گاهه جهڙو سونهري ناسي رنگ رکندڙ، پيلاڻ مائل هلڪو ناسي رنگ
urduMeaning: گرم ریتلی یا نارنجی مائل بھورے رنگ کا، شیر یا خشک گھاس جیسا سنہری بھورا رنگ رکھنے والا، زردی مائل ہلکا بھورا رنگ
examples: The lion's tawny coat blended with the dry grass. She had tawny eyes that caught the light. A tawny owl called from the woods at dusk. The fields turned tawny in late summer.
englishMeaning: Of a warm sandy or orange-brown colour. Having the golden brown shade seen in lions, autumn grass, or certain owls. A light brown colour with a yellowish tinge.
synonyms: Golden brown, Fawn, Tan, Amber, Bronze, Sandy, Ochre

sindhiMeaning: اهڙا مطلب جيڪي وڏي تعداد ۾ موجود هجن، لفظ جا ڪيترائي ۽ ڀرپور مطلب، هڪ ئي جملي مان نڪرندڙ گهڻن مطلبن جي فراواني
antonyms: Single meaning, Literal sense, Plain meaning, Emptiness, Ambiguity-free sense
urduMeaning: ایسے معانی جو کثرت سے موجود ہوں، کسی لفظ کے متعدد اور بھرپور مفہوم، ایک ہی جملے سے نکلنے والے کئی مطالب کی فراوانی
examples: The poem is rich with teeming meanings. Sacred texts often carry teeming meanings for scholars. His short remark had teeming meanings for the family. Students explored the teeming meanings of the metaphor.
synonyms: Abundant meanings, Multiple senses, Rich significance, Manifold interpretations, Layered meanings
englishMeaning: Meanings that are present in great abundance. Senses of a word that are numerous and overflowing. A wealth of interpretations carried by a single expression.

antonyms: Slowness, Delay, Stagnation
examples: The conductor increased the tempo in the final movement. The tempo of city life can be exhausting. They played the song at a faster tempo. The team needs to pick up the tempo in the second half.
sindhiMeaning: رفتار يا رفتار جنهن تي موسيقي جو هڪ ٽڪرو وڄايو وڃي، حرڪت يا سرگرمي جي شرح يا رفتار، ڪنهن سرگرمي جي خاص تال يا نمونو، ڪنهن شيءِ جي عام رفتار يا وقت
englishMeaning: The speed or pace at which a piece of music is played. The rate or speed of motion or activity. The characteristic rhythm or pattern of an activity. The general pace or timing of something.
urduMeaning: رفتار یا رفتار جس پر موسیقی کا ایک ٹکڑا بجایا جائے، حرکت یا سرگرمی کی شرح یا رفتار، کسی سرگرمی کی خاص تال یا نمونہ، کسی چیز کی عام رفتار یا ٹائمنگ
synonyms: Pace, Speed, Rate, Rhythm, Beat, Cadence, Velocity, Time, Measure

sindhiMeaning: روحاني معاملن جي بجاءِ دنياوي معاملن سان لاڳاپيل، وقت سان ڳنڍيل يا محدود، مٿي جي مندرن سان لاڳاپيل، ابدي جي بجاءِ محدود وقت لاءِ رهندڙ، فطرت ۾ سيڪيولر يا غير مذهبي
synonyms: Worldly, Secular, Earthly, Material, Mundane, Transient, Temporary, Physical, Non-spiritual
examples: They were more concerned with temporal power than spiritual enlightenment. The temporal lobe of the brain processes auditory information. All temporal things must eventually pass away. Kings focused on temporal authority over their kingdoms.
englishMeaning: Relating to worldly rather than spiritual matters. Connected with or limited by time. Relating to the temples of the head. Lasting for a limited time rather than eternal. Secular or non-religious in nature.
antonyms: Spiritual, Eternal, Permanent, Everlasting, Sacred, Religious, Timeless, Immortal
urduMeaning: روحانی معاملات کی بجائے دنیاوی معاملات سے متعلق، وقت سے جڑا ہوا یا محدود، سر کے مندروں سے متعلق، ابدی کی بجائے محدود وقت کے لیے رہنے والا، فطرت میں سیکولر یا غیر مذہبی

examples: The road is temporarily closed for repairs. She is temporarily staying with her parents. The office will be temporarily relocated during renovations. His vision was temporarily blurred after the accident.
synonyms: Briefly, Momentarily, Short-term, Provisionally, For now, For the time being, Transiently
urduMeaning: محدود عرصے کے لیے، مستقل طور پر نہیں، ایسے طریقے سے جو صرف تھوڑے وقت کے لیے رہے، فی الوقت یا اس درمیان میں، جب تک کچھ زیادہ مستقل ترتیب نہ دیا جائے، نہ رہنے والا یا نامعلوم وقت تک رہنے کا ارادہ
sindhiMeaning: محدود عرصي لاءِ، مستقل طور تي نه، اهڙي طريقي سان جيڪو صرف ٿورڙي وقت لاءِ هلي، في الوقت يا ان وچ ۾، جيستائين ڪجهه وڌيڪ مستقل ترتيب نه ڏني وڃي، نه رهڻ وارو يا اڻڄاتل وقت تائين رهڻ جو ارادو
antonyms: Permanently, Forever, Indefinitely, Long-term, Continually, Constantly, Always
englishMeaning: For a limited period of time, not permanently. In a way that lasts for only a short time. For the time being or in the meantime. Until something more permanent is arranged. Not lasting or intended to last indefinitely.

examples: The temporariness of life makes every moment precious. She accepted the temporariness of her living situation. The temporariness of the job made him keep searching for something permanent. We must embrace the temporariness of all worldly things.
englishMeaning: The quality or state of being temporary or lasting for only a limited time. The characteristic of not being permanent. The condition of being transient or short-lived. The nature of existing for a brief period.
urduMeaning: عارضی ہونے یا صرف محدود وقت کے لیے رہنے کا معیار یا حالت، مستقل نہ ہونے کی خاصیت، عارضی یا قلیل المدتی ہونے کی حالت، مختصر عرصے کے لیے موجود ہونے کی نوعیت
synonyms: Impermanence, Transience, Brevity, Ephemerality, Fleetingness, Short-livedness, Instability
antonyms: Permanence, Durability, Stability, Longevity, Constancy, Endurance, Perpetuity
sindhiMeaning: عارضي هجڻ يا صرف محدود وقت لاءِ رهڻ جو معيار يا حالت، مستقل نه هجڻ جي خاصيت، عارضي يا مختصر عرصي واري هجڻ جي حالت، مختصر عرصي لاءِ موجود هجڻ جي طبيعت

englishMeaning: Using very few words; brief and to the point. Short in a way that seems rude or unfriendly. Expressed in a compact and economical style. Abrupt and lacking warmth in speech or writing.
urduMeaning: مختصر اور دو ٹوک، کم الفاظ میں بات کہنے والا، ایسا جواب جو مختصر ہونے کے باعث رُوکھا لگے، جامع اور غیر ضروری الفاظ سے پاک، سپاٹ اور بے مروت انداز
synonyms: Brief, Concise, Curt, Succinct, Laconic, Pithy, Blunt, Abrupt
examples: His reply was terse and left no room for discussion. She sent a terse message saying only that she was busy. The manager gave a terse account of the incident. I was surprised by his terse manner on the phone.
antonyms: Verbose, Lengthy, Wordy, Rambling, Long-winded, Polite, Elaborate

urduMeaning: معاملے کی تہہ میں کوئی خرابی ہے، کوئی چھپی یا مشکوک بات موجود ہے، اصل وجہ پوشیدہ ہے، بات میں کچھ گڑبڑ ہے
synonyms: Something fishy, A hidden catch, Foul play, A rat to smell, An underlying problem, Suspicious circumstances, A concealed motive

examples: The evidence was weak; therefore, the case was dismissed. He was ill and therefore could not attend the meeting. Prices have risen, and therefore sales have slowed. She trained hard and therefore deserved the win.
synonyms: Hence, Thus, Consequently, So, Accordingly, As a result, For this reason, Ergo
antonyms: Nevertheless, However, Nonetheless, Yet, Despite this, Regardless
englishMeaning: For that reason. As a consequence of what has been said. Used to introduce a logical conclusion drawn from evidence or reasoning.
urduMeaning: اس لیے، اسی وجہ سے، چنانچہ، نتیجتاً، مذکورہ بات کے نتیجے میں
sindhiMeaning: انهيءَ ڪري، ان سبب ڪري، تنهنڪري، ان جي نتيجي ۾، مٿين ڳالهه جي نتيجي طور

antonyms: Clever, Bright, Intelligent, Sharp, Astute, Quick-witted
urduMeaning: غیر رسمی انگریزی محاورہ جس کا مطلب انتہائی بے وقوف یا کم عقل, مذاق یا تنقید کے طور پر کسی کی بے عقلی کے لیے استعمال
examples: He is a kind man, but thick as two short planks. Don't ask him to fix the wiring; he's thick as two short planks. She joked that her cousin was thick as two short planks. Anyone who believed that rumour is thick as two short planks.
englishMeaning: An informal British expression meaning extremely stupid or slow to understand. Used humorously or critically about someone's lack of intelligence.
synonyms: Stupid, Dim, Dense, Slow-witted, Foolish, Brainless, Dull
sindhiMeaning: غير رسمي انگريزي چوڻي جنهن جو مطلب تمام گهڻو بيوقوف يا ڪم عقل, مذاق يا نقطي چينيءَ طور ڪنهن جي بي عقليءَ لاءِ استعمال

englishMeaning: To make someone feel confused, surprised, or uncertain. To disturb someone's physical balance so that they nearly fall. To upset someone's composure or plans unexpectedly.
antonyms: Stabilize, Steady, Calm, Reassure, Compose
urduMeaning: کسی کو حیران یا بے قرار کرنا، جسمانی توازن بگاڑنا کہ وہ گرنے والا ہو، اچانک کسی کے سکون یا منصوبے کو بگاڑنا
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کي حيران يا بي قرار ڪرڻ، جسمي توازن بگاڙڻ ته هو ڪرڻ وارو هجي، اچانڪ ڪنهن جي سکون يا منصوبي کي بگاڙڻ
synonyms: Disconcert, Unsettle, Confuse, Fluster, Upset, Disturb, Rattle
examples: The sudden change in schedule threw the whole team off balance. His unexpected arrival threw her off balance for a moment. The strong wave threw the surfer off balance. Difficult questions from the audience threw the speaker off balance.

englishMeaning: To shock, confuse, or surprise someone completely. To upset a person's plans or expectations suddenly. To leave someone unable to react because of astonishment. To disturb someone's composure with unexpected news or events.
antonyms: Calm, Reassure, Steady, Comfort, Prepare, Settle, Soothe
examples: The sudden resignation threw the whole team for a loop. Her question really threw me for a loop. The change in schedule threw us for a loop. News of the merger threw investors for a loop.
urduMeaning: کسی کو حیران یا پریشان کر دینا، اچانک خبر سے الجھا دینا، کسی کے منصوبے الٹ دینا، سکتے میں ڈال دینا
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کي حيران يا پريشان ڪري ڇڏڻ، اوچتي خبر سان منجهائي وجهڻ، ڪنهن جا رٿيل منصوبا اُبتا ڪري ڇڏڻ، سراسيمگي ۾ وجهڻ
synonyms: Stun, Bewilder, Astonish, Confuse, Startle, Rattle, Disconcert, Catch off guard

antonyms: Nevertheless, However, Yet, Nonetheless, Regardless, Notwithstanding
englishMeaning: In this way. In the manner just described. As a result of what has just been mentioned. Therefore; consequently. To this degree or extent, as in the phrase 'thus far'.
synonyms: Therefore, Hence, Consequently, So, Accordingly, In this way, Thereby, As a result, Ergo
urduMeaning: اس طرح، اسی طریقے سے، لہٰذا، اس کے نتیجے میں، اب تک یا اس حد تک، مذکورہ بالا طریقے کے مطابق
examples: He mixed the colours slowly, thus avoiding any streaks. The road was blocked, thus we had to take a longer route. Thus far, the project has stayed within budget. She spoke calmly and thus calmed the whole room.
sindhiMeaning: هن طرح، اهڙي طرح، ان ڪري، انهيءَ نتيجي طور، هيستائين يا هن حد تائين، مٿي بيان ڪيل طريقي مطابق
ڊپ يا هٻڪ، بزدلي، اعتماد جي کوٽ، ماڻهن سامهون شرم يا جھجڪ، خطرو کڻڻ کان لنوائڻ، ناڪامي جي ڊپ سبب محتاط رويو
englishMeaning: A lack of courage or confidence, especially in facing new situations. Shyness or nervousness in the presence of other people. An unwillingness to take risks or act boldly. Cautious behaviour caused by fear of failure or criticism.
antonyms: Boldness, Courage, Confidence, Bravery, Audacity, Assertiveness, Daring, Fearlessness
synonyms: Shyness, Fearfulness, Cowardice, Diffidence, Nervousness, Hesitancy, Bashfulness, Meekness, Apprehension
urduMeaning: جھجک یا بزدلی، اعتماد کی کمی، لوگوں کے سامنے شرمیلا پن، خطرہ مول لینے سے گریز، ناکامی کے خوف سے محتاط رویہ
examples: His timidity prevented him from speaking at the meeting. She overcame her timidity and joined the debate club. The government was criticised for its timidity in facing the crisis. Timidity in business can cost you valuable opportunities.

sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن وڏي لڪل مسئلي جو ننڍڙو ظاهر حصو، ڪنهن تمام وڏي ڳالهه جي پهرين نشاني، پوري معاملي جو صرف ٿورڙو حصو جيڪو خبر ۾ آيو هجي
examples: These complaints are just the tip of the iceberg. The arrests were only the tip of the iceberg in the fraud case. What we see on the surface is the tip of the iceberg. Officials fear the losses are the tip of the iceberg.
synonyms: Small part, Surface sign, Fraction, First hint, Visible portion, Beginning, Warning sign
urduMeaning: کسی بڑے چھپے ہوئے مسئلے کا چھوٹا سا ظاہری حصہ، کسی بہت بڑی بات کی پہلی نشانی، پورے معاملے کا صرف تھوڑا سا حصہ جو معلوم ہو
antonyms: Whole picture, Entire problem, Full extent, Complete story, Bulk, Totality
englishMeaning: A small visible part of a much larger hidden problem. The first sign of something far bigger. Only a fraction of the whole matter that is known so far.

examples: This legal document is all Greek to me. When he explains physics, it becomes Greek to the whole class. The instructions were Greek to anyone without technical training. Her accounts were Greek to me until the auditor explained them.
synonyms: Unintelligible, Incomprehensible, Obscure, Baffling, Confusing
antonyms: Clear, Plain, Simple, Understandable, Obvious
sindhiMeaning: بلڪل سمجهه ۾ نه اچڻ وارو، ڪا ڳالهه جيڪا ماڻهوءَ جي سمجهه کان ٻاهر هجي، مونجهاري ڀري يا اڻ ڄاتل ٻولي، پيچيده ۽ ڏکي ڳالهه
englishMeaning: To be completely unintelligible or beyond one's understanding, as in 'it is all Greek to me'. To speak or write in a way nobody can follow. Something confusing, obscure, or full of unfamiliar terms.
urduMeaning: بالکل سمجھ میں نہ آنے والا، ایسی بات جو فہم سے باہر ہو، الجھی ہوئی یا اجنبی زبان، پیچیدہ اور دشوار بات

antonyms: Finally, Lastly, In conclusion, At the end, Ultimately
englishMeaning: Used to introduce the first point or reason in a discussion or argument. At the start or in the first place. Initially or originally. As the first consideration or factor.
sindhiMeaning: بحث يا دليل ۾ پهرين نقطي يا سبب کي متعارف ڪرائڻ لاءِ استعمال ٿيل، شروعات ۾ يا پهرين جاءِ تي، شروعات ۾ يا اصل ۾، پهرين غور يا عنصر جي طور تي
examples: To begin with, we need to understand the problem clearly. The plan was flawed to begin with. To begin with, let me introduce the team members. She should never have accepted the offer to begin with.
urduMeaning: بحث یا دلیل میں پہلے نقطے یا سبب کو متعارف کرانے کے لیے استعمال، شروعات میں یا پہلی جگہ پر، ابتدائی طور پر یا اصل میں، پہلے غور یا عنصر کے طور پر
synonyms: First of all, Firstly, Initially, In the first place, Originally, At the outset, At first

word: To bring grist to the mill
urduMeaning: فائدہ مند چیز مہیا کرنا، کام آنے والا مواد فراہم کرنا، نفع پہنچانا، اپنے فائدے کے لیے کچھ لے آنا
antonyms: Be useless, Waste, Hinder, Bring loss, Be unprofitable
synonyms: Be profitable, Provide advantage, Add value, Be useful, Benefit
englishMeaning: To provide something useful or profitable. To supply material or experience that can be turned to advantage. To add to one's resources or benefit.
sindhiMeaning: فائديمند شيءِ مهيا ڪرڻ، ڪم اچڻ جهڙو مواد ڏيڻ، نفعو پهچائڻ، پنهنجي فائدي لاءِ استعمال ٿيندڙ شيءِ آڻڻ
examples: Every new client brings grist to the mill for the young firm. His travels brought grist to the mill for his next novel. Even small donations bring grist to the mill of the charity. Local gossip brings grist to the mill of the columnist.

synonyms: Procrastinate, Delay, Dawdle, Loiter, Waste time, Dither
examples: He never lets the grass grow under his feet when there is work to do. Do not let the grass grow under your feet; apply for the job today. She let the grass grow under her feet and lost the contract. Successful people rarely let the grass grow under their feet.
sindhiMeaning: وقت ضايع ڪرڻ، ڪم ۾ دير ڪرڻ، سستي ڪري موقعو وڃائڻ، هٿ تي هٿ رکي ويهڻ
urduMeaning: وقت ضائع کرنا، کام میں تاخیر کرنا، سستی کر کے موقع گنوا دینا، ہاتھ پر ہاتھ رکھ کر بیٹھنا
englishMeaning: To waste time or delay taking action. To be idle and miss opportunities through inactivity. To move slowly when prompt action is needed.
antonyms: Act promptly, Hurry, Seize the moment, Be prompt, Get moving
word: To let the grass grow under one’s feet

englishMeaning: To speak about something without knowing the facts. To talk nonsense or make claims that are not true. To speak foolishly or without proper understanding.
antonyms: Speak knowledgeably, Talk sense, Be accurate, Be informed
examples: He was talking through his hat about the new tax law. Do not believe him; he is simply talking through his hat. She talks through her hat whenever the subject is science. The critics were talking through their hats without reading the report.
urduMeaning: بغیر علم کے بات کرنا، بے تکی باتیں کرنا، بے بنیاد دعوے کرنا، بکواس کرنا
synonyms: Talk nonsense, Bluff, Waffle, Speak ignorantly, Rant
sindhiMeaning: بغير ڄاڻ جي ڳالهائڻ، بيوقوفيءَ واريون ڳالهيون ڪرڻ، بي بنياد دعوائون ڪرڻ، اجائي بڪواس ڪرڻ

نتيجن جي پرواهه ڪرڻ کان سواءِ خوشي يا خودمختياري جو تعاقب ڪرڻ، آسان يا خوشگوار رستي جي پيروي ڪرڻ جيڪو برباديءَ ڏانهن وڃي، آرام ۽ خوشي جي زندگي گذارڻ جيڪا آخرڪار تباهي ڏانهن وڃي، ڊگهي مدي جي ڀلائي تي فوري اطمينان چونڊڻ
synonyms: Live recklessly, Pursue pleasure, Self-indulge, Take the easy way, Live for the moment
urduMeaning: نتائج کی پرواہ کیے بغیر لذت یا خود مختاری کا تعاقب کرنا، آسان یا خوشگوار راستے کی پیروی کرنا جو بربادی کی طرف لے جائے، آرام اور لذت کی زندگی گزارنا جو بالآخر تباہی کی طرف لے جائے، طویل مدتی بہبود پر فوری اطمینان کا انتخاب کرنا
examples: He walked the primrose path of luxury and excess. Walking the primrose path often leads to regret. They warned him not to walk the primrose path. The novel's protagonist walked the primrose path to destruction.
englishMeaning: To pursue pleasure or self-indulgence without regard to consequences. To follow an easy or pleasant path that leads to ruin. To live a life of ease and pleasure that ultimately leads to disaster. To choose immediate gratification over long-term well-being.
antonyms: Live responsibly, Be prudent, Exercise self-control, Plan ahead, Be disciplined

synonyms: Air one's grievances, Reveal secrets, Make private matters public, Expose scandals
word: To wash one’s dirty linen in public
examples: They argued at the wedding and washed their dirty linen in public. He warned his brothers not to wash their dirty linen in public. The interview was an unfortunate case of washing dirty linen in public. Families should settle disputes at home rather than wash their dirty linen in public.
englishMeaning: To discuss private or embarrassing matters where others can hear. To reveal family or personal quarrels openly. To expose shameful secrets instead of settling them privately. To air private disputes in front of outsiders.
urduMeaning: اپنے ذاتی یا گھریلو معاملات لوگوں کے سامنے بیان کرنا، گھر کی بات باہر نکالنا، شرمناک راز عام کرنا، اندرونی جھگڑے دوسروں کے سامنے لانا
sindhiMeaning: پنهنجا ذاتي يا گهرو معاملا عام ماڻهن اڳيان بيان ڪرڻ، گهر جي ڳالهه ٻاهر ڪڍڻ، شرمناڪ راز کي عام ڪرڻ، اندروني جهيڙا ماڻهن سامهون آڻڻ
antonyms: Keep it private, Stay discreet, Settle privately, Maintain confidentiality

sindhiMeaning: قبر جي پٿر تي لکيل عبارت، مئل ماڻهوءَ جي ياد ۾ ڪنداري لکت، نالو ۽ تاريخون ڏيندڙ يادگار عبارت، قبر جي ڪتبي تي اُڪريل لفظ
urduMeaning: قبر کے پتھر پر کندہ عبارت، مرحوم کی یاد میں لکھی گئی تحریر، نام اور تاریخیں درج کرنے والی یادگاری عبارت، لوحِ مزار پر کندہ الفاظ
antonyms: Blank stone, Anonymity, Unmarked grave, Erasure, Silence
synonyms: Epitaph, Gravestone inscription, Memorial text, Headstone engraving, Monumental inscription
examples: The tomb stone inscription was worn away by centuries of rain. He read the tomb stone inscription aloud to his children. The tomb stone inscription simply said, 'Beloved teacher and friend'. Historians study old tomb stone inscriptions for family records.
englishMeaning: The words carved on a gravestone to commemorate a dead person. A memorial text giving the name, dates, and a short tribute to the deceased. An epitaph engraved on a monument marking a grave.

sindhiMeaning: سست ۽ بي همت، جسماني يا ذهني طور تي بي عمل، آهستي هلندڙ يا ڍرو، سياري ۾ ننڊ ۾ ويل جانور وانگر بي حرڪت، بي پرواهه ۽ جذبي کان خالي، ترقي يا عمل جي طاقت کان محروم
synonyms: Sluggish, Lethargic, Inactive, Dormant, Listless, Inert, Apathetic, Slow, Dull, Languid, Drowsy, Idle
examples: The summer heat left everyone feeling torpid by midday. Trade remained torpid throughout the winter months. The bear lay torpid in its den until spring. He gave a torpid reply that showed no real interest.
urduMeaning: سست اور بے حس، جسمانی یا ذہنی طور پر غیر فعال، دھیمی رفتار والا یا کاہل، سردیوں کی نیند میں پڑے جانور کی طرح بے حرکت، بے پروا اور جذبے سے خالی، عمل یا نمو کی قوت سے محروم
antonyms: Active, Energetic, Lively, Alert, Brisk, Vigorous, Animated, Dynamic, Spirited, Awake
englishMeaning: Mentally or physically inactive; lacking energy or alertness. Sluggish and slow-moving. Dormant, as an animal in hibernation. Apathetic and dull in feeling or response. Lacking the vigour needed to act or grow.

examples: After the heavy meal, a pleasant torpor settled over him. The bear remained in a state of torpor throughout the winter. The heat of the afternoon filled the town with torpor. She struggled to shake off the mental torpor of grief.
sindhiMeaning: جسماني يا ذهني بي عملي ۽ سستي جي حالت، کاڌل ٿڪل ۽ توانائي جي کوٽ جي حالت، ڪجهه جانورن ۾ غيرفعال ٿيڻ جي حالت، بي دلچسپي يا ڪنهن به شيءِ ۾ دلچسپي نه هجڻ
synonyms: Lethargy, Sluggishness, Inactivity, Drowsiness, Apathy, Dullness, Languor, Stupor, Inertia
urduMeaning: جسمانی یا ذہنی غیر فعالیت اور سستی کی حالت، کاہلی، سستی اور توانائی کی کمی کی حالت، کچھ جانوروں میں غیر فعال ہونے کی حالت، بے دلچسپی یا کسی بھی چیز میں دلچسپی نہ ہونا
englishMeaning: A state of physical or mental inactivity and sluggishness. A condition of lethargy, dullness, and lack of energy. A state of dormancy in some animals. Apathy or lack of interest in anything.
antonyms: Energy, Vigor, Activity, Alertness, Enthusiasm, Vitality, Liveliness, Zeal

englishMeaning: Very hot and dry, especially describing weather or climate. Full of intense passion or emotion, especially romantic. Rapid, energetic, or difficult, as in a torrid pace or time. Scorching and parched.
urduMeaning: بہت گرم اور خشک خاص طور پر موسم یا آب و ہوا، شدید جوش یا جذبات سے بھرپور خاص طور پر رومانوی، تیز، پرجوش یا مشکل جیسے تیز رفتار یا وقت، جھلسا دینے والا اور خشک
examples: They endured the torrid heat of the desert summer. The novel tells of a torrid love affair. The team had a torrid start to the season. Nothing grows in the torrid zone without irrigation.
synonyms: Scorching, Sweltering, Burning, Blazing, Sizzling, Passionate, Ardent, Sultry, Fiery
antonyms: Cold, Cool, Freezing, Frigid, Chilly, Passionless, Indifferent, Mild
sindhiMeaning: تمام گرم ۽ واري خاص ڪري موسم يا آب وهوا، شديد جوش يا جذبات سان ڀرپور خاص ڪري رومانوي، تيز جوشيلو يا ڏکيو جهڙي تيز رفتار يا وقت، جلائيندڙ ۽ واري

urduMeaning: پیچ دار، بل کھاتا ہوا اور ٹیڑھا راستہ، سیدھا نہ ہونا بلکہ مڑا ہوا ہونا، بہت طویل اور الجھا ہوا، پیچیدہ اور سمجھنے میں مشکل، غیر سیدھا یا چالاکی پر مبنی طریقہ
englishMeaning: Full of twists, turns, and bends; not straight. Winding or crooked in shape or path. Excessively lengthy, complex, and difficult to follow. Not direct or straightforward in expression or reasoning. Devious or deceitful in method or intention.
antonyms: Straight, Direct, Simple, Clear, Plain, Straightforward, Uncomplicated, Honest, Open, Concise
sindhiMeaning: وڪڙ کائيندڙ، ٽيڏو ۽ گھمڻ گھيرو ڪندڙ رستو، سڌو نه پر مروڙيل، ڏاڍو ڊگهو ۽ منجهيل، پيچيده ۽ سمجهڻ ۾ ڏکيو، سڌي سنئين نه پر ڪوڙو ۽ چالباز طريقو
examples: The bus climbed slowly along a tortuous mountain road. His tortuous explanation left everyone more confused than before. The company took a tortuous route to secure the contract. We followed a tortuous path through the narrow valley.
synonyms: Winding, Twisting, Meandering, Crooked, Serpentine, Zigzag, Convoluted, Complicated, Involved, Circuitous, Devious

examples: The prisoners endured torturous conditions for many months. Waiting for the results was a torturous experience for the family. He described the injury as a torturous, constant pain. The long march through the desert proved torturous for the soldiers.
englishMeaning: Causing or involving severe physical pain or suffering. Extremely unpleasant, painful, or hard to endure. Relating to torture or cruel treatment. Mentally distressing or agonizing over a long period.
urduMeaning: شدید جسمانی تکلیف یا اذیت دینے والا، عذاب اور دکھ سے بھرا ہوا، ناقابلِ برداشت حد تک تکلیف دہ، ظلم اور تشدد سے متعلق، ذہنی طور پر سخت اذیت ناک
synonyms: Painful, Agonizing, Excruciating, Unbearable, Punishing, Harrowing, Distressing, Grueling, Cruel, Tormenting
antonyms: Painless, Comfortable, Pleasant, Soothing, Easy, Enjoyable, Gentle, Relieving, Restful
sindhiMeaning: سخت جسماني ڏک ۽ تڪليف ڏيندڙ، ايذاءُ يا عذاب سان ڀريل، برداشت کان ٻاهر ڏکيو ۽ تڪليف ڏيندڙ، ظلم ۽ سختيءَ سان لاڳاپيل، ذهني طور تي ڏاڍو اذيتناڪ
سياحت، تفريح لاءِ سفر ڪرڻ جو عمل، سيرگاهن ۽ هوٽلن سان لاڳاپيل ڪاروبار، سياحن کي خدمتون ڏيڻ وارو شعبو
antonyms: Isolation, Seclusion, Home-staying, Non-travel, Local confinement
englishMeaning: The business of providing services for people who travel for pleasure. The activity of travelling to places for holidays and sightseeing. The industry connected with hotels, travel, and holiday attractions. Travel undertaken for recreation as an economic activity.
