sindhiMeaning: اهڙو ماڻهو جيڪو وفاقيت جي حمايت يا وڪالت ڪري، ڪو به جيڪو علائقائي اختيارين سان گڏ مضبوط مرڪزي حڪومت ۾ يقين رکي، وفاقي سياسي پارٽي يا تحريڪ جو ميمبر يا حامي، وفاقي حڪومتي جوڙجڪ سان لاڳاپيل يا حمايت ڪندڙ
antonyms: Anti-federalist, States' rights advocate, Decentralist, Confederalist, Separatist
urduMeaning: ایسا شخص جو وفاقیت کی حمایت یا وکالت کرے، کوئی بھی جو علاقائی اختیارات کے ساتھ مضبوط مرکزی حکومت میں یقین رکھے، وفاقی سیاسی پارٹی یا تحریک کا ممبر یا حامی، وفاقی حکومتی ڈھانچے سے متعلق یا حمایت کرنے والا

englishMeaning: Information or comments about how well someone is doing something, used as a basis for improvement. A reaction or response to a product, service, or performance. The return of part of a system's output to its input, affecting the process. The unpleasant noise produced when sound from a loudspeaker returns to a microphone.
synonyms: Response, Reaction, Comment, Criticism, Evaluation, Review, Opinion, Assessment, Input
antonyms: Silence, No response, Indifference, Disregard, Ignorance
examples: The teacher gave detailed feedback on my essay. We collect customer feedback to improve our service. Positive feedback from the team encouraged him to continue. The microphone produced loud feedback during the speech.
sindhiMeaning: راءِ يا تبصرو جيڪو ڪنهن جي ڪم بابت ڏنو وڃي، بهتري لاءِ ڏنل مشورو، ڪنهن شيءِ يا خدمت بابت ردعمل، نظام جي نتيجي جو واپس اثر ڪرڻ، لائوڊ اسپيڪر مان مائيڪ ۾ ايندڙ ناخوشگوار آواز
urduMeaning: کسی کے کام کے بارے میں رائے یا تبصرہ، بہتری کے لیے دیا گیا مشورہ، کسی چیز یا خدمت پر ردِعمل، نظام کے نتیجے کا واپس اثر انداز ہونا، اسپیکر سے مائیک میں آنے والی ناخوشگوار آواز

synonyms: Trick, Ruse, Bluff, Dodge, Pretence, Manoeuvre, Deception
antonyms: Honesty, Directness, Sincerity, Real attack, Frankness
sindhiMeaning: مخالف کي ڌوڪو ڏيڻ لاءِ ڪيل ٺلهي چال، ٺلهو حملو جيڪو گمراهه ڪرڻ لاءِ ڪجي، راند يا جنگ ۾ اهڙي دوکي واري حرڪت ڪرڻ، اصل ارادو لڪائڻ لاءِ ڪيل عمل
examples: The boxer made a feint with his left hand and struck with his right. Their advance on the bridge was only a feint. He feinted to the right and then slipped past the defender. The whole offer turned out to be a clever feint.
englishMeaning: A deceptive movement made to distract an opponent. A pretended attack or blow intended to mislead. To make such a misleading movement in sport or combat. Any action meant to conceal one's real intention.
urduMeaning: حریف کو دھوکہ دینے کے لیے کی گئی جھوٹی حرکت، گمراہ کرنے کے لیے دکھاوے کا حملہ، کھیل یا لڑائی میں ایسی چال چلنا، اصل ارادہ چھپانے کے لیے کیا گیا عمل
قیدی کے پاؤں میں ڈالی جانے والی زنجیر یا بیڑی، ایسی چیز جو آزادی کو روکے، کسی کو زنجیروں میں جکڑنا، کسی کی آزادی یا ترقی کو محدود کرنا، پابند کرنا
examples: The prisoner's fetters were removed before the trial. Old customs can act as fetters on progress. They fettered the captives and led them away. He felt fettered by endless family obligations.
antonyms: Free, Release, Liberate, Unshackle, Unchain, Emancipate, Loosen, Freedom
englishMeaning: A chain or shackle placed around a prisoner's ankles. Anything that restricts freedom of movement or action. To bind someone with chains or restraints. To restrain, hamper, or limit someone's liberty or development.
synonyms: Shackle, Chain, Bond, Manacle, Restraint, Hamper, Restrict, Confine, Curb
sindhiMeaning: قيديءَ جي پيرن ۾ وجهڻ واري زنجير يا ٻيڙي، اهڙي شيءِ جيڪا آزادي کي روڪي، ڪنهن کي زنجيرن سان جڪڙڻ، ڪنهن جي آزادي يا ترقي کي محدود ڪرڻ، پابند ڪرڻ

examples: Pulmonary fibrosis affects lung function. Liver fibrosis can progress to cirrhosis. Cystic fibrosis is a genetic disorder. The scarring caused fibrosis in the tissue.
urduMeaning: جوڑنے والے ٹشوز کا موٹا ہونا اور داغ پڑنا، ایک طبی حالت جس میں اضافی ریشے دار ٹشو کی تشکیل شامل ہے، اعضاء میں داغ ٹشو کی نشوونما جو کام کو خراب کرے، ایک عمل جہاں عام ٹشو ریشے دار داغ ٹشو سے بدل جائے
synonyms: Scarring, Tissue thickening, Scar tissue formation, Fibrous tissue buildup
englishMeaning: The thickening and scarring of connective tissue. A medical condition involving excess fibrous tissue formation. The development of scar tissue in organs that impairs function. A process where normal tissue is replaced by fibrous scar tissue.
sindhiMeaning: ڳنڍيندڙ بافتن جو ٿلهو ٿيڻ ۽ داغ پوڻ، هڪ طبي حالت جنهن ۾ اضافي ريشيدار بافت جي ٺهڻ شامل آهي، عضون ۾ داغ بافت جي ترقي جيڪا ڪم کي خراب ڪري، هڪ عمل جتي عام بافت ريشيدار داغ بافت سان تبديل ٿئي
antonyms: Normal tissue, Healthy tissue, Non-scarred, Soft tissue

synonyms: Burning, Blazing, Fiery, Glowing, Red-hot, Passionate, Fierce, Intense
antonyms: Cold, Cool, Dim, Dull, Calm, Gentle, Extinguished
examples: Firefighters rushed to the flaming building. She wore a flaming red scarf. His flaming temper got him into trouble. The flaming sunset lit up the whole sky.
englishMeaning: Burning with flames or on fire. Bright red or orange like fire. Very hot or glowing like flames. Passionate, intense, or violent in emotion. Used informally to express annoyance or emphasis.
sindhiMeaning: باهه سان ٻرندڙ يا باهه ۾، باهه وانگر چمڪدار ڳاڙهو يا نارنگي، تمام گرم يا باهه وانگر چمڪدار، جذبات ۾ پرجوش، تيز يا ڦرڪيل، غير رسمي طور تي ناراضگي يا زور ڏيڻ لاءِ استعمال
urduMeaning: آگ کے شعلوں سے جلتا ہوا یا آگ میں، آگ کی طرح چمکدار سرخ یا نارنگی، بہت گرم یا شعلوں کی طرح چمکتا ہوا، جذبات میں پرجوش، شدید یا طوفانی، غیر رسمی طور پر ناراضگی یا زور دینے کے لیے استعمال

sindhiMeaning: سَن جي ريشي وانگر هلڪي پيلي رنگ وارو، هلڪن پيلن يا سنهرن وارن وارو، سَن جو ٺهيل، نرم هلڪي سنهرن پيلي رنگ وارو
examples: The little girl had long flaxen hair. She braided her flaxen locks into two plaits. The field of ripe wheat looked flaxen in the sun. His flaxen beard was tied with a ribbon.
urduMeaning: سن کے ریشے جیسا ہلکا پیلا رنگ رکھنے والا، ہلکے پیلے یا سنہری بالوں والا، سن کا بنا ہوا، نرم ہلکے سنہرے پیلے رنگ کا
synonyms: Blonde, Pale yellow, Golden, Light-haired, Straw-colored, Fair
antonyms: Dark, Brunette, Black, Raven-haired
englishMeaning: Having a pale yellow color like flax fibers. Having light yellow or blonde hair. Made of flax. Of a soft, pale golden-yellow shade.

examples: Loggers used a wooden flume to move timber down the mountain. The stream rushed through a narrow flume between the rocks. The children queued for the water flume at the park. Water was flumed from the reservoir to the mill.
sindhiMeaning: پاڻي وهائڻ لاءِ ٺهيل سوڙهي نالي يا نار، ڪاٺيون لوڙهڻ لاءِ استعمال ٿيندڙ پاڻي جو رستو، اونهي ۽ سوڙهي وادي جنهن مان ندي وهي، پاڻي واري سلائيڊ جنهن تي ماڻهو لهن، اهڙي نالي ذريعي ڪا شيءِ نيڻ
synonyms: Channel, Chute, Conduit, Sluice, Aqueduct, Ravine, Gorge, Waterway, Millrace
urduMeaning: پانی بہانے کے لیے بنائی گئی تنگ نالی یا نہر، لکڑیاں بہانے کے لیے استعمال ہونے والا آبی راستہ، گہری اور تنگ گھاٹی جس میں ندی بہتی ہو، پانی والی پھسل گاڑی یا واٹر سلائیڈ، ایسی نالی کے ذریعے کوئی چیز منتقل کرنا
englishMeaning: A narrow, artificial channel built to carry water, often used for transporting logs. A deep, steep-sided ravine through which a stream flows. A water slide or ride in which people travel along a channel of flowing water. To transport something by means of such a channel.
antonyms: Dam, Barrier, Blockage, Embankment, Plateau, Obstruction

synonyms: Flapper, Fluttering bird, Wingbeater, Hoverer, Wanderer, Bettor
urduMeaning: ایسا شخص یا چیز جو پھڑپھڑائے یا لہرائے، تیز اور ہلکے پروں سے اڑنے والا پرندہ یا کیڑا، بے چینی سے ادھر ادھر پھرنے والا شخص، چھوٹی رقم پر شرط لگانے والا شخص
englishMeaning: A person or thing that flutters. A bird or insect that moves its wings quickly and lightly. Someone who moves about restlessly or in an unsettled manner. A person who bets small amounts casually, in informal British use.
antonyms: Glider, Soarer, Stayer, Settler, Motionless one
sindhiMeaning: اهڙو شخص يا شيءِ جيڪا ڦڙڪي يا لهرائي، تيز ۽ هلڪن پرن سان اڏامندڙ پکي يا حشرو، بيچينيءَ سان هيڏانهن هوڏانهن گهمندڙ شخص، ننڍي رقم تي شرط لڳائيندڙ ماڻهو
examples: The butterfly was a delicate flutterer among the roses. He is a restless flutterer who never settles in one job. Every flutterer in the aviary rose at once. She is an occasional flutterer on the horse races.

englishMeaning: A colourless, sharp-smelling acid found naturally in ant venom and nettles. A simple carboxylic acid with the chemical formula HCOOH. A chemical used in leather processing, textiles, and preservatives. A corrosive liquid used in industry and laboratories.
antonyms: Base, Alkali, Neutral solution, Hydroxide
synonyms: Methanoic acid, Carboxylic acid, Chemical acid, Industrial acid
sindhiMeaning: بي رنگ ۽ تيز بوءِ وارو تيزاب جيڪو ماڪوڙين جي زهر ۽ ٻوٽن ۾ ملي ٿو، سادو ڪاربوڪسيلڪ ايسڊ، چمڙي ۽ ڪپڙي جي صنعت ۾ استعمال ٿيندڙ ڪيميائي مادو، سنکندڙ مايع
examples: Ant stings burn because of formic acid. Formic acid is widely used in the leather industry. The students prepared formic acid in the laboratory. Formic acid can irritate the skin and eyes.
urduMeaning: بے رنگ اور تیز بو والا تیزاب جو چیونٹیوں کے زہر اور بچھو بوٹی میں پایا جاتا ہے، سادہ کاربوکسلک ایسڈ، چمڑے اور کپڑے کی صنعت میں استعمال ہونے والا کیمیائی مادہ، سنکنے والا مائع

examples: The kitchen counter was covered with white Formica. Formica surfaces are easy to clean and maintain. They replaced the old Formica table with a wooden one. Ants of the genus Formica are common in forests.
urduMeaning: سخت اور پائیدار پلاسٹک کی تہہ جو میز اور کاؤنٹر ڈھانپنے کے لیے استعمال ہوتی ہے، گرمی سے محفوظ لیمینیٹ شیٹ، سائنسی درجہ بندی میں چیونٹیوں کی ایک نسل، آسانی سے صاف ہونے والا سطحی مواد
englishMeaning: A hard, durable plastic laminate used for covering surfaces such as tables and counters. A trade name for a heat-resistant laminated sheet material. A genus of ants in scientific classification. A smooth, easy-to-clean surfacing material used in kitchens.
antonyms: Wood, Marble, Granite, Natural stone, Bare surface
synonyms: Laminate, Veneer, Surfacing material, Plastic sheet, Countertop material
sindhiMeaning: سخت ۽ مضبوط پلاسٽڪ جي پرت جيڪا ميز ۽ ڪائونٽر ڍڪڻ لاءِ استعمال ٿئي، گرمي کان محفوظ ليمينيٽ شيٽ، سائنسي درجه بندي ۾ ماڪوڙين جو هڪ قسم، صاف ڪرڻ ۾ آسان مٿاڇري وارو مواد

synonyms: Powerful, Intimidating, Daunting, Impressive, Redoubtable, Fearsome, Mighty
antonyms: Weak, Feeble, Harmless, Insignificant, Easy, Unimpressive
examples: They faced a formidable opponent in the final match. She has a formidable reputation as a lawyer. The mountain presented a formidable challenge to the climbers. He built a formidable collection of rare books.
englishMeaning: Inspiring fear, respect, or awe because of size, strength, or ability. Difficult to deal with, defeat, or overcome. Impressively powerful or capable. Causing worry because of seriousness or difficulty.
sindhiMeaning: خوف يا احترام پيدا ڪندڙ، طاقتور ۽ مضبوط، جنهن کي شڪست ڏيڻ ڏکيو هجي، متاثر ڪندڙ صلاحيت وارو، ڏکيو ۽ سنگين
urduMeaning: خوف یا احترام پیدا کرنے والا، طاقتور اور مضبوط، جسے شکست دینا مشکل ہو، متاثر کن صلاحیت والا، دشوار اور سنگین

synonyms: Impressively, Powerfully, Dauntingly, Intimidatingly, Strongly, Mightily
antonyms: Weakly, Feebly, Poorly, Mildly, Unimpressively
urduMeaning: خوف یا احترام پیدا کرنے والے انداز میں، متاثر کن حد تک، اس طرح کہ مقابلہ مشکل ہو جائے، طاقتور انداز سے
sindhiMeaning: خوف يا احترام پيدا ڪندڙ انداز ۾، متاثر ڪندڙ حد تائين، اهڙي طرح جو مقابلو ڪرڻ ڏکيو ٿي وڃي، طاقتور نموني سان
englishMeaning: In a way that inspires fear, respect, or awe. To an impressive or intimidating degree. In a manner that is difficult to overcome. Powerfully and strikingly.
examples: The team was formidably prepared for the tournament. She is formidably intelligent and hardworking. The fortress was formidably built on high rocks. He argued formidably against the proposal.

antonyms: Shaped, Defined, Structured, Organized, Distinct, Clear
urduMeaning: جس کی کوئی صورت یا شکل نہ ہو، بے شکل، بغیر ترتیب یا ساخت کے، مبہم اور غیر واضح، جس کی حدود متعین نہ ہوں
synonyms: Shapeless, Amorphous, Vague, Unstructured, Indefinite, Nebulous
englishMeaning: Having no clear shape, structure, or outline. Lacking definite form or organization. Vague and difficult to describe or define. Without a fixed physical or artistic form.
sindhiMeaning: جنهن جي ڪا صورت يا شڪل نه هجي، بي شڪل، بغير ترتيب يا بناوت جي، مبهم ۽ اڻ چٽو، جنهن جي حدون مقرر نه هجن
examples: A formless mist covered the valley at dawn. His fears were vague and formless. The clay was still a formless lump. The essay felt formless and hard to follow.

antonyms: Criticism, Condemnation, Censure, Rebuke, Disapproval, Insult, Denunciation, Reproach, Abuse, Blame
synonyms: Praise, Tribute, Eulogy, Panegyric, Commendation, Accolade, Compliment, Applause, Homage, Testimonial
sindhiMeaning: وڏي واکاڻ يا ساراهه، ڪنهن جي تعريف ۾ چيل يا لکيل رسمي تقرير، ڪنهن جي خوبين تي عام طور تي ڪيل خراج تحسين، پرجوش ساراهه جو اظهار، ڪنهن جي عزت ۾ چيل ساراهه ڀريا لفظ
urduMeaning: بلند تعریف، کسی کی مدح میں کی گئی رسمی تقریر یا تحریر، کسی کی خوبیوں پر عوامی خراج تحسین، پرجوش ستائش کا اظہار، کسی کے اعزاز میں کہے گئے تعریفی کلمات
englishMeaning: A formal expression of high praise, especially in speech or writing. A speech or piece of writing that warmly praises a person, thing, or achievement. A tribute paid publicly to honour someone's qualities or work. Enthusiastic admiration expressed openly. A eulogy delivered in honour of someone.
examples: The principal delivered a warm encomium at the retiring teacher's farewell. Critics wrote a glowing encomium for her debut novel. His encomium moved many people in the audience to tears. The article was less a review than an encomium to the young scientist.

sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ڏينهن يا فيصلي تي پڇتائڻ، ماضيءَ جي ڪنهن ڪم تي شديد افسوس ڪرڻ، پنهنجي چونڊ جا خراب نتيجا ڀوڳي پشيمان ٿيڻ، ڪنهن کي خبردار ڪرڻ ته هو پوءِ پڇتائيندو
examples: You will rue the day you trusted that man with your savings. He came to rue the day he left his steady job. She warned that they would rue the day they ignored her advice. Many investors now rue the day they entered the market so hastily.
antonyms: Rejoice, Celebrate, Welcome, Appreciate, Enjoy, Be glad, Delight in, Applaud
englishMeaning: To deeply regret the time when something happened. To feel bitter sorrow about a past decision or action. To suffer the unpleasant consequences of a choice and wish it had never been made. Used as a warning that someone will be sorry for what they are doing.
urduMeaning: کسی دن یا فیصلے پر پچھتانا، ماضی کے کسی کام پر شدید افسوس کرنا، اپنے انتخاب کے برے نتائج بھگت کر شرمندہ ہونا، کسی کو خبردار کرنا کہ وہ بعد میں پچھتائے گا
synonyms: Regret, Repent, Lament, Bemoan, Deplore, Mourn, Be sorry, Grieve over, Feel remorse

sindhiMeaning: سخت زهريلو ۽ تلخ، ڪڙي ۽ ظالماڻي تنقيد سان ڀريل، ڳالهائڻ يا لکڻ ۾ نهايت سخت ۽ نفرت ڀريو، گاريون ڏيندڙ ۽ دل ڏکائيندڙ، تيزاب جهڙو جلائيندڙ
urduMeaning: نہایت تلخ اور زہریلا، سخت اور ظالمانہ تنقید سے بھرپور، بولنے یا لکھنے میں نہایت کڑوا اور نفرت آمیز، دشنام آمیز اور دل آزار، تیزاب جیسا جلا دینے والا
examples: He launched a vitriolic attack on his former colleagues. The newspaper published a vitriolic review of the play. Their argument turned vitriolic within minutes. She received vitriolic messages after posting her opinion online.
englishMeaning: Filled with bitter criticism or cruel hostility. Extremely harsh, cutting, and full of hatred, especially in speech or writing. Savagely abusive in tone. Relating to or resembling vitriol, a corrosive acid.
antonyms: Kind, Gentle, Complimentary, Gracious, Mild, Praising, Pleasant, Sympathetic, Polite, Sweet
synonyms: Caustic, Scathing, Acerbic, Bitter, Venomous, Abusive, Harsh, Sarcastic, Withering, Malicious
Dummy, Teat, Comforter, Soother, Calmer, Peacemaker, Tranquilliser
antonyms: Irritant, Agitator, Provoker, Disturber, Stimulant, Troublemaker
examples: The baby fell asleep as soon as she was given her pacifier. He kept a spare soother in the nappy bag. Some parents avoid using a pacifier after the first year. The soft music acted as a soother for the restless child.
englishMeaning: A rubber or plastic teat given to a baby to suck on for comfort. A small device used to calm or quieten a crying infant. Something or someone that calms anger or restlessness. A person who restores peace between quarrelling parties.
urduMeaning: بچے کو چپ کرانے والی چُوسنی، ربڑ یا پلاسٹک کی نپل نما چیز جو بچے کو سکون دے، کوئی چیز جو غصہ یا بے چینی کم کرے، جھگڑا ختم کرانے والا شخص
sindhiMeaning: ٻار کي چپ ڪرائڻ لاءِ ڏنل چوسڻي، ربڙ يا پلاسٽڪ جي چوسڻي جيڪا ٻار کي آرام ڏي، ڪا شيءِ جيڪا ڪاوڙ يا بيچيني گهٽائي، جهيڙو ختم ڪرائيندڙ ماڻهو

synonyms: Until now, Up to now, Thus far, Hitherto, To date, Yet, As yet, Currently
sindhiMeaning: هينئر تائين، هن وقت تائين، هڪ حد تائين، هڪ خاص فاصلي يا حد تائين، اڃا تائين جيترو ٿيو آهي
urduMeaning: اب تک، اس وقت تک، ایک حد تک، ایک خاص فاصلے یا حد تک، اب تک جتنا ہوا ہے
antonyms: Never, Henceforth, In future, Afterwards, Later, From now on
examples: So far, we have collected half of the required funds. The weather has been pleasant so far this week. He has made no mistakes so far in the tournament. So far, nobody has been able to answer the question.
englishMeaning: Up to the present moment or point in time. To the extent or degree reached until now. Up to a certain distance or limit. Used to say that something has been true until now but may change.

examples: This is by far the best restaurant in the city. She is by far the strongest player on the team. The new model is by far more efficient than the old one. His speech was by far the most memorable of the evening.
sindhiMeaning: گهڻو وڌيڪ، تمام گهڻي فرق سان، ٻين جي ڀيٽ ۾ گهڻو بهتر يا وڏو، بنا ڪنهن شڪ جي سڀ کان مٿي
antonyms: Slightly, Marginally, Barely, Hardly, Somewhat, Equally
englishMeaning: By a great amount or margin. Used to emphasise that something is much greater or better than the rest. Very much, when comparing two or more things. Beyond any doubt or comparison.
urduMeaning: بہت زیادہ، نمایاں فرق سے، دوسروں کے مقابلے میں کہیں بہتر یا بڑا، بلا شبہ سب سے بڑھ کر
synonyms: Much, Considerably, Significantly, Easily, Decidedly, Overwhelmingly, Undoubtedly, Greatly
Pincers, Nippers, Tongs, Gripper, Clamp, Forceps
antonyms: Loosener, Release tool, Spreader
examples: He tightened the wire with a pair of pliers. The electrician reached for his pliers to cut the cable. Keep a plier and a screwdriver in the toolbox. She used pliers to pull out the bent nail.
englishMeaning: A hand tool with two hinged jaws, used for gripping, bending, or cutting wire (usually used in the plural, pliers). A gripping instrument commonly found in a toolbox. A person who plies a trade or works steadily at something.
sindhiMeaning: پلاس، تارون پڪڙڻ موڙڻ يا ڪٽڻ وارو اوزار، ٻن ڄاڙين وارو هٿ جو اوزار، ڪو ماڻهو جيڪو مسلسل ڪو ڪم يا هنر ڪري
urduMeaning: پلاس، تاریں پکڑنے موڑنے یا کاٹنے کا اوزار، دو جبڑوں والا ہاتھ کا آلہ، وہ شخص جو مسلسل کوئی کام یا ہنر کرے

examples: He used a hammer to drive the nails into the wood. The rain hammered against the windows all night. Our team hammered their opponents in the final. She hammered away at the problem until she solved it.
sindhiMeaning: هٿوڙو، ڪوڪا هڻڻ يا ڪا شيءِ ڀڃڻ وارو ڳرو اوزار، زور سان بار بار ڌڪ هڻڻ، ڪنهن کي بري طرح شڪست ڏيڻ، مسلسل محنت ڪري ڪم پورو ڪرڻ
synonyms: Mallet, Gavel, Strike, Pound, Beat, Bash, Batter, Thrash, Defeat
englishMeaning: A tool with a heavy metal head and a handle, used for driving nails or breaking things. To hit something repeatedly with a hammer or with force. To defeat someone decisively. To work at something persistently until it is finished. A heavy ball on a wire thrown in an athletic event.
urduMeaning: ہتھوڑا، کیلیں ٹھونکنے یا کوئی چیز توڑنے کا بھاری اوزار، زور سے بار بار ضرب لگانا، کسی کو بری طرح شکست دینا، مسلسل محنت کر کے کام مکمل کرنا
antonyms: Caress, Pat, Stroke, Protect, Lose, Surrender, Soothe

sindhiMeaning: پيچ ڪش، اسڪرو کولڻ يا ڪسڻ وارو اوزار، اهڙو هٿ جو اوزار جنهن جي نوڪ پيچ جي مٿي ۾ ويهي، وودڪا ۽ سنتري جي رس مان ٺهيل هڪ مشروب
urduMeaning: پیچ کش، اسکرو کھولنے یا کسنے کا اوزار، ایسا ہاتھ کا آلہ جس کی نوک پیچ کے سر میں فٹ ہو، ووڈکا اور مالٹے کے رس سے بنا ایک مشروب
examples: He tightened the hinge with a small screwdriver. Do you have a flat-head screwdriver in your toolbox? The screwdriver slipped and scratched the wooden panel. A magnetic screwdriver makes the job much easier.
antonyms: Wrench, Spanner, Hammer
synonyms: Turnscrew, Driver, Hand tool, Implement
englishMeaning: A tool with a shaped tip used for turning screws. A hand tool designed to fit into the head of a screw to tighten or loosen it. An alcoholic drink made from vodka and orange juice.

sindhiMeaning: ٺهراءُ وارو، پرسڪون ۽ نرم مزاج، جلدي ڪاوڙ ۾ نه اچڻ وارو، اوچتي يا شديد تبديليءَ کان آجو، معتدل ۽ هڪجهڙو موسم يا حالت
urduMeaning: پرسکون اور نرم مزاج، جلدی غصے میں نہ آنے والا، اچانک یا شدید تبدیلی سے پاک، معتدل اور یکساں موسم یا حالت، ٹھہراؤ والا
examples: He has an equable temperament that keeps the team calm. The island enjoys an equable climate throughout the year. She responded to the criticism in an equable tone. Their equable relationship has lasted for decades.
englishMeaning: Calm and even-tempered, not easily upset or annoyed. Free from sudden or extreme changes. Describing a climate that stays moderate and steady. Uniform and consistent in nature or quality.
antonyms: Excitable, Irritable, Volatile, Moody, Erratic, Temperamental, Unstable, Harsh, Extreme
synonyms: Calm, Serene, Composed, Placid, Even-tempered, Steady, Moderate, Tranquil, Unruffled, Consistent

sindhiMeaning: لهر، سمنڊ يا ڍنڍ جي پاڻيءَ جي لهر، هٿ لوڏي سلام يا اشارو ڪرڻ، ڪنهن جذبي يا سرگرميءَ ۾ اوچتو واڌ، وارن جو وٽ يا موڙ، آواز يا روشنيءَ جي موج
examples: A large wave knocked the child off his feet. She waved goodbye from the window of the train. A wave of relief passed through the waiting families. Heat waves are becoming more frequent every summer.
urduMeaning: لہر، سمندر یا جھیل کے پانی کی موج، ہاتھ ہلا کر سلام یا اشارہ کرنا، کسی جذبے یا سرگرمی میں اچانک اضافہ، بالوں کی لٹ یا خم، آواز یا روشنی کی موج
antonyms: Calm, Stillness, Trough, Lull, Ignore, Steadiness
englishMeaning: A moving ridge of water on the surface of the sea or a lake. To move your hand back and forth as a greeting or signal. A sudden increase or spread of a feeling, activity, or condition. A curving movement or shape, as in hair. A disturbance that transfers energy, such as sound or light.
synonyms: Ripple, Billow, Surge, Swell, Gesture, Signal, Flourish, Undulate, Flutter

englishMeaning: An image or statue worshipped as a god. A person who is greatly admired, loved, or revered by many. Something to which excessive devotion is given. A false god or object of misplaced worship.
sindhiMeaning: بت، اهڙي مورتي جنهن جي پوڄا ڪئي وڃي، اهو شخص جنهن کي ماڻهو تمام گهڻو پسند ۽ پوڄين، ڪا شيءِ جنهن سان حد کان وڌيڪ عقيدت هجي، ڪوڙو معبود
antonyms: Outcast, Villain, Nonentity, Reject, Unknown
synonyms: Statue, Effigy, Icon, Hero, Star, Favourite, Deity, Image, Figure
urduMeaning: بت، وہ مجسمہ جس کی پوجا کی جائے، وہ شخص جسے لوگ بے حد پسند اور عقیدت سے دیکھیں، ایسی چیز جس سے حد سے زیادہ لگاؤ ہو، جھوٹا معبود
examples: The ancient temple was filled with stone idols. That singer has been her idol since childhood. Money became the idol of his entire life. Young players often try to imitate their sporting idols.

sindhiMeaning: ننڍي چوري، ٿورين شين جي بار بار چوري، دڪان گودام يا مال مان ٿيندڙ ننڍي ڦر، اهڙي چوريءَ سبب مال جو نقصان، چوري ٿيل مال جي مقدار يا قيمت
synonyms: Petty theft, Stealing, Shoplifting, Filching, Thieving, Pinching, Larceny, Embezzlement
antonyms: Honesty, Integrity, Restitution, Return, Protection, Safekeeping
englishMeaning: The act of stealing small items, especially repeatedly. Petty theft of goods, often from a shop, warehouse, or cargo. The loss of goods caused by such small-scale stealing. The amount or value of goods stolen in this way.
examples: The company installed cameras to reduce pilferage in the warehouse. Pilferage of stationery had become a daily problem. Losses from pilferage were higher than expected this year. Strict checks at the gate cut pilferage by half.
urduMeaning: چھوٹی چوری، معمولی اشیاء کی بار بار چوری، دکان گودام یا مال سے ہونے والی چھوٹی چوری، ایسی چوری سے ہونے والا نقصان، چوری شدہ مال کی مقدار یا قیمت

englishMeaning: Something presented as a gift, especially to a god or in a religious ceremony. A product or service made available to the public. Money contributed during a religious service. The act of presenting something for acceptance or use.
urduMeaning: نذرانہ، کسی مذہبی رسم میں پیش کیا گیا تحفہ، عوام کے لیے پیش کی گئی چیز یا خدمت، عبادت کے دوران دیا گیا چندہ، کوئی چیز پیش کرنے کا عمل
antonyms: Refusal, Withholding, Denial, Retention, Withdrawal, Rejection
sindhiMeaning: نذرانو، ڪنهن ديوتا يا مذهبي رسم ۾ پيش ڪيل تحفو، عوام لاءِ پيش ڪيل شيءِ يا خدمت، عبادت دوران ڏنل چندو، ڪا شيءِ پيش ڪرڻ جو عمل
synonyms: Gift, Donation, Contribution, Sacrifice, Present, Oblation, Tribute, Product, Submission
examples: Villagers placed flowers and fruit as an offering at the shrine. The bakery's latest offering is a honey walnut loaf. The congregation made a generous offering for the flood victims. Their new offering includes both software and support.

synonyms: Intellect-attracted, Mind-oriented, Cerebral admirer, Brain-oriented
antonyms: Superficial, Looks-focused, Shallow, Appearance-driven
urduMeaning: وہ شخص جسے کسی کی ذہانت سب سے زیادہ پرکشش لگے، جسمانی خوبصورتی کے بجائے عقل و دانش کی طرف مائل، ذہنی صلاحیت کی بنیاد پر کشش محسوس کرنے والا
englishMeaning: A person who finds intelligence the most attractive quality in a partner. Sexually or romantically attracted to intelligence rather than physical appearance. Relating to attraction based primarily on the mind and intellect.
sindhiMeaning: اهو ماڻهو جنهن کي ڪنهن جي ذهانت سڀ کان وڌيڪ ڪشش ڏئي، جسماني حسن بجاءِ عقل ۽ سمجهه ڏانهن مائل، ذهني قابليت جي بنياد تي ڇڪ محسوس ڪندڙ
examples: She describes herself as a sapiosexual who values deep conversation. For a sapiosexual, wit matters more than looks. He wrote an article explaining what sapiosexual attraction means. Many sapiosexual people meet partners through book clubs.

sindhiMeaning: سببي، ڪنهن سبب سان لاڳاپيل، اهڙو تعلق جنهن ۾ هڪ ڳالهه ٻي کي جنم ڏئي، ڪنهن ڳالهه جو سبب ظاهر ڪندڙ، گرامر ۾ سبب ڏيکاريندڙ
examples: Researchers found no causal link between the two events. The study explains the causal factors behind the decline. A correlation does not always prove a causal relationship. 'Because' is a causal conjunction in English.
urduMeaning: سببی، کسی وجہ سے متعلق، ایسا تعلق جس میں ایک واقعہ دوسرے کو جنم دے، کسی بات کی وجہ ظاہر کرنے والا، گرامر میں سبب بتانے والا
englishMeaning: Relating to or acting as a cause. Describing a relationship in which one event produces another. Expressing the reason why something happens. In grammar, indicating cause, as with words like 'because'.
synonyms: Causative, Contributory, Originating, Responsible, Explanatory, Determining
antonyms: Unrelated, Incidental, Coincidental, Random, Resultant, Accidental

examples: The conspirators met secretly in an abandoned building. He was named as the chief conspirator in the plot. Police arrested three conspirators before the attack. Historians still debate who the real conspirators were.
urduMeaning: سازشی، خفیہ منصوبے میں شریک شخص، کسی کے خلاف چھپ کر منصوبہ بنانے والا، سازش کا رکن، خفیہ اسکیم میں ساتھی
sindhiMeaning: سازش ۾ شامل ماڻهو، ڳجهي منصوبي ۾ ڀائيوار، ڪنهن جي خلاف لڪ ڇپ ۾ منصوبو ٺاهيندڙ، سازش جو رڪن، ڳجهي رٿ ۾ ساٿي
antonyms: Loyalist, Supporter, Ally, Defender, Patriot, Whistle-blower
synonyms: Plotter, Schemer, Accomplice, Collaborator, Traitor, Intriguer, Confederate, Insurgent
englishMeaning: A person who takes part in a secret plan to do something harmful or unlawful. Someone who plots with others against a person, group, or government. A member of a conspiracy. An accomplice in a hidden scheme.

examples: He stood there with a gormless expression on his face. Don't be so gormless; read the instructions first. The film's hero is a gormless but likeable young man. She gave a gormless answer to a simple question.
sindhiMeaning: بيوقوف، عقل کان خالي، سمجهه ۾ سست، بيوقوفن وانگر بيٺل يا ڏسندڙ، ماحول کان بي خبر ۽ اڍنگو
synonyms: Foolish, Stupid, Dim, Clueless, Dense, Slow-witted, Vacant, Dull, Silly
englishMeaning: Lacking sense or intelligence; foolish. Looking or behaving in a stupid, vacant way. Slow to understand things. Clumsy and unaware of what is going on around one.
antonyms: Clever, Intelligent, Sharp, Bright, Astute, Quick-witted, Alert, Shrewd
urduMeaning: بے وقوف، عقل سے عاری، دیر سے سمجھنے والا، احمقوں کی طرح خالی نظروں سے دیکھنے والا، ماحول سے بے خبر اور بھونڈا

synonyms: Petty thief, Shoplifter, Filcher, Thief, Snatcher, Robber, Purloiner
sindhiMeaning: ننڍي چوري ڪندڙ، ٿورين شين جو چور، گهٽ قيمت واريون شيون چورائيندڙ، دڪان يا ڪم جي جاءِ تان مال چورائيندڙ
antonyms: Honest person, Owner, Guardian, Protector, Custodian, Donor
urduMeaning: چھوٹی چوری کرنے والا، معمولی اشیاء کا چور، کم قیمت چیزیں چرانے والا، دکان یا کام کی جگہ سے مال چرانے والا
examples: The pilferer was caught taking supplies from the store room. Security guards identified the pilferer on camera. A known pilferer had been visiting the market daily. The manager warned that any pilferer would be dismissed.
englishMeaning: A person who steals small things, especially repeatedly. A petty thief who takes items of little value. Someone who steals goods from a shop, workplace, or shipment.

sindhiMeaning: ننڍي چوري ڪرڻ، ٿورين ۽ سستيون شيون بار بار چورائڻ، بي ايماني سان ٿورو ٿورو مال کڻڻ، مالڪ يا دڪان تان معمولي چوري ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: چھوٹی چوری کرنا، معمولی اور سستی چیزیں بار بار چرانا، بے ایمانی سے تھوڑا تھوڑا مال لینا، مالک یا دکان سے معمولی چوری کرنا
examples: He was dismissed for pilfering from the stock room. Pilfering of office supplies costs the company thousands. She admitted pilfering coins from the till. Constant pilfering forced the owner to hire a guard.
englishMeaning: The act of stealing small or inexpensive items, usually repeatedly. Taking things dishonestly in small quantities. Petty stealing from an employer, shop, or store. Committing minor theft over a period of time.
synonyms: Stealing, Filching, Thieving, Shoplifting, Pinching, Purloining, Larceny
antonyms: Returning, Restoring, Giving, Honesty, Guarding, Protecting

examples: Thick fog caused a twenty-car pile-up on the motorway. There was a pile-up of dishes in the kitchen sink. A pile-up of unpaid bills worried the small business owner. Emergency crews cleared the pile-up within three hours.
sindhiMeaning: ڪيترن گاڏين جو پاڻ ۾ ٽڪرجڻ وارو حادثو، شين جو وڏو ڍير، ڪم يا مسئلن جو گڏ ٿي وڃڻ، وڏي مقدار ۾ جمع ٿيڻ
urduMeaning: کئی گاڑیوں کا آپس میں ٹکرانے کا حادثہ، چیزوں کا بڑا ڈھیر، کام یا مسائل کا جمع ہو جانا، بڑی مقدار میں اکٹھا ہونا
synonyms: Crash, Collision, Smash, Heap, Accumulation, Stack, Backlog, Mound
englishMeaning: A road accident involving several vehicles crashing into one another. A large accumulation of things gathered in a heap. A build-up of work, problems, or delays. To gather or accumulate in large amounts.
antonyms: Clearance, Dispersal, Reduction, Gap, Order, Emptiness

sindhiMeaning: جنسي تعلق جو شديد ۽ غير منطقي خوف، جسماني قربت جي خيال تي گهٻراهٽ، ساٿيءَ سان ويجهڙائپ بابت انتهائي پريشاني، هڪ نفسياتي ڊپ
englishMeaning: An intense and irrational fear of sexual intimacy. A phobia in which a person feels panic at the thought of sexual contact. Extreme anxiety related to physical closeness with a partner. Also known as coitophobia.
examples: Genophobia can seriously affect a person's relationships. Therapy helped her overcome her genophobia. The counsellor explained that genophobia is more common than people think. He avoided dating because of his genophobia.
urduMeaning: جنسی قربت کا شدید اور غیر منطقی خوف، جسمانی نزدیکی کے خیال پر گھبراہٹ، ساتھی سے قربت سے متعلق انتہائی بے چینی، ایک نفسیاتی خوف
antonyms: Confidence, Comfort, Intimacy, Attraction, Boldness, Ease
synonyms: Coitophobia, Erotophobia, Sexual anxiety, Intimacy fear, Phobia

examples: His ereuthophobia made public speaking almost impossible. People with ereuthophobia often avoid group meetings. She sought therapy for her ereuthophobia last year. Ereuthophobia can begin during the teenage years.
urduMeaning: دوسروں کے سامنے شرما کر سرخ ہو جانے کا غیر منطقی خوف، سماجی مواقع پر چہرہ سرخ ہونے کی شدید بے چینی، شرمندگی ظاہر ہونے کا ڈر، ایک نفسیاتی خوف
synonyms: Erythrophobia, Blushing fear, Social anxiety, Phobia, Shyness disorder
sindhiMeaning: ٻين اڳيان شرمائي ڳاڙهو ٿيڻ جو غير منطقي خوف، سماجي موقعن تي منهن ڳاڙهو ٿيڻ جي شديد پريشاني، شرمساري ظاهر ٿيڻ جو ڊپ، هڪ نفسياتي خوف
englishMeaning: An irrational fear of blushing in front of others. Extreme anxiety about turning red in the face in social situations. A phobia in which a person dreads visible embarrassment. Also spelled erythrophobia.
antonyms: Confidence, Poise, Self-assurance, Boldness, Composure, Calm

synonyms: Hemophobia, Blood fear, Phobia, Medical anxiety, Dread of blood
urduMeaning: خون کا شدید اور غیر منطقی خوف، خون دیکھ کر بے ہوش ہو جانے والا ڈر، زخم یا طبی عمل دیکھ کر شدید بے چینی، ایک نفسیاتی خوف
antonyms: Courage, Boldness, Fearlessness, Composure, Calmness, Confidence
examples: His haematophobia made blood tests very difficult. Children with haematophobia may faint during vaccinations. She could not watch the surgery because of haematophobia. Gradual exposure therapy is used to treat haematophobia.
sindhiMeaning: رت جو شديد ۽ غير منطقي خوف، رت ڏسي بيهوش ٿي وڃڻ وارو ڊپ، زخم يا طبي عمل ڏسي شديد پريشاني، هڪ نفسياتي خوف
englishMeaning: An intense and irrational fear of blood. A phobia that may cause fainting at the sight of blood. Severe anxiety triggered by injuries, wounds, or medical procedures. Also spelled hemophobia or hematophobia.

synonyms: Germophobia, Bacillophobia, Fear of germs, Contamination fear, Phobia
sindhiMeaning: گندگي جراثيم ۽ آلودگيءَ جو غير منطقي خوف، شين کي هٿ لائڻ سان بيمار ٿيڻ جي شديد پريشاني، بار بار هٿ ڌوئڻ سان جڙيل نفسياتي ڊپ، صفائيءَ جو حد کان وڌيڪ وسوسو
englishMeaning: An irrational fear of dirt, germs, and contamination. Excessive anxiety about becoming infected by touching things. A phobia often linked with compulsive washing or cleaning. Also called germophobia.
antonyms: Tolerance, Fearlessness, Indifference, Calmness, Confidence, Ease
examples: Her mysophobia made her wash her hands dozens of times a day. Mysophobia grew more common during the pandemic. He avoids public transport because of mysophobia. Treatment for mysophobia often includes cognitive therapy.
urduMeaning: گندگی جراثیم اور آلودگی کا غیر منطقی خوف، چیزوں کو چھونے سے بیمار ہونے کی شدید بے چینی، بار بار ہاتھ دھونے سے جڑا نفسیاتی خوف، صفائی کا حد سے زیادہ وسوسہ

examples: His ornithophobia began after a seagull attacked him as a child. She refuses to sit outdoors because of ornithophobia. Ornithophobia can be treated with gradual exposure. The pigeons in the square trigger his ornithophobia.
sindhiMeaning: پکين جو غير منطقي خوف، پکين کي ڏسي يا ٻڌي شديد گهٻراهٽ، اهڙو ڊپ جنهن سبب ماڻهو پارڪن ۽ کليل جاين کان پري رهي
antonyms: Fondness for birds, Courage, Calmness, Fearlessness, Comfort

The office, rank, or jurisdiction of a patriarch. The territory or church district governed by a patriarch. The official residence of a patriarch. The period during which a patriarch holds office. A system of society governed by a patriarch.

synonyms: Patriarchy, See, Bishopric, Diocese, Episcopate, Jurisdiction, Prelacy
urduMeaning: پیٹریارک (بڑے مذہبی پیشوا) کا عہدہ یا اختیار، وہ علاقہ جو پیٹریارک کے زیرِ انتظام ہو، پیٹریارک کی سرکاری رہائش گاہ، اس کے عہدے کی مدت، مردانہ سرداری کا نظام
examples: The patriarchate of Constantinople has a long history. He was appointed to the patriarchate in his sixties. The patriarchate issued a statement about the dispute. Records from the patriarchate date back centuries.
sindhiMeaning: پيٽريارڪ (وڏي مذهبي پيشوا) جو عهدو يا اختيار، اُهو علائقو جيڪو پيٽريارڪ جي ماتحت هجي، پيٽريارڪ جي سرڪاري رهائشگاهه، سندس عهدي جو عرصو، مرداڻي سرداري وارو نظام

antonyms: Inflame, Provoke, Aggravate, Worsen, Ignite, Intensify, Arm, Escalate
urduMeaning: بم سے فیوز نکالنا تاکہ وہ نہ پھٹے، کسی خطرناک یا کشیدہ صورتِ حال کو پُرسکون بنانا، غصہ یا تناؤ کم کرنا، خطرہ ٹالنا
sindhiMeaning: بم مان فيوز ڪڍڻ ته جيئن اهو ڦاٽي نه، ڪنهن خطرناڪ يا تڪراري صورتحال کي نرم ڪرڻ، ڪاوڙ يا ڇڪتاڻ گهٽائڻ، خطري کي ٽارڻ
synonyms: Calm, Ease, Settle, Soothe, Pacify, Disarm, Deactivate, Reduce, Neutralize
englishMeaning: To remove the fuse from a bomb so that it cannot explode. To make a dangerous or tense situation calmer and less harmful. To reduce anger, stress, or hostility in a conflict. To make something less likely to cause trouble.
examples: Experts were called to defuse the bomb safely. She managed to defuse the argument with a joke. The talks helped defuse tension between the two countries. A calm response can quickly defuse an angry customer.

urduMeaning: جو اب موجود نہ ہو، ختم شدہ، بند ہو چکا ادارہ یا کاروبار، ناکارہ یا بے کار، معدوم
antonyms: Active, Operating, Functioning, Alive, Existing, Working, Thriving
sindhiMeaning: جيڪو هاڻي موجود نه هجي، ختم ٿيل، بند ٿيل ادارو يا ڪاروبار، ناڪاره يا بيڪار، معدوم
englishMeaning: No longer existing, operating, or functioning. Having ceased to work or be used. Describing an organisation or business that has closed down. Dead or extinct.
examples: The company has been defunct for over a decade. He found an old map published by a defunct society. The defunct factory now stands empty. They revived a defunct tradition from the village.
synonyms: Extinct, Obsolete, Dead, Inoperative, Disused, Closed, Nonexistent, Expired

antonyms: Fund, Finance, Support, Subsidize, Sponsor, Bankroll, Invest
urduMeaning: کسی ادارے یا منصوبے کی مالی امداد بند کرنا، فنڈ روک دینا، بجٹ میں بڑی کٹوتی کرنا، رقم کی فراہمی ختم کرنا
englishMeaning: To stop providing money or financial support to an organisation or programme. To withdraw funding as a political or administrative decision. To reduce the budget of a public body significantly. To cut off the financial resources needed for something to continue.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن اداري يا منصوبي جي مالي مدد بند ڪرڻ، فنڊ روڪڻ، بجيٽ ۾ وڏي ڪٽ ڪرڻ، رقم جي فراهمي ختم ڪرڻ
examples: The government threatened to defund the programme. Activists campaigned to defund the project entirely. Schools suffered after the council decided to defund them. Lawmakers voted to defund the agency next year.
synonyms: Cut funding, Withdraw support, Discontinue, Starve of funds, Slash budget, Withhold money
Ruminated food, Regurgitated feed, Bolus, Chewed food, Rumen contents
urduMeaning: وہ نیم ہضم شدہ غذا جسے جگالی کرنے والے جانور دوبارہ چباتے ہیں، جگالی، پاگُر، دوبارہ چبانے کا عمل، کسی بات پر بار بار غور کرنا
examples: The cows lay in the field chewing the cud. Sheep chew the cud for hours after grazing. Farmers know that a healthy animal chews its cud regularly. He sat quietly, chewing the cud over the day's events.
englishMeaning: Food that a cow or similar animal brings back from its stomach to chew again. Partly digested food chewed a second time by ruminant animals. The act or process of such chewing. Figuratively, something reflected on slowly and repeatedly.
sindhiMeaning: اُهو اڌ هضم ٿيل کاڌو جيڪو ڍڳو ٻيهر چٻاڙي، ڳاڙ، جڳالي، ٻيهر چٻاڙڻ جو عمل، ڪنهن ڳالهه تي بار بار سوچڻ
antonyms: Fresh fodder, Undigested food, Waste, Dung, Unchewed grass

examples: A woodpecker was tapping loudly on the old oak tree. We watched a woodpecker searching for insects in the bark. The forest echoed with the drumming of a woodpecker. Children were excited to spot a woodpecker near the path.
synonyms: Picidae bird, Flicker, Sapsucker, Tree tapper, Wryneck, Bird
urduMeaning: وہ پرندہ جو مضبوط چونچ سے درخت میں سوراخ کر کے کیڑے تلاش کرتا ہے، لکڑ ٹھونگا، درخت پر بار بار ٹھک ٹھک کرنے والا پرندہ، مسلسل محنت کرنے والا شخص
sindhiMeaning: هڪ پکي جيڪو مضبوط چهنب سان وڻ ۾ سوراخ ڪري ڪيڙا ڳولهي، ڪاٺ ٺوڪيندڙ پکي، وڻ تي بار بار ٺڪ ٺڪ ڪندڙ پکي، لاڳيتو محنت ڪندڙ ماڻهو
antonyms: Songbird, Waterfowl, Bird of prey, Flightless bird, Silent bird
englishMeaning: A bird with a strong beak that pecks holes in tree trunks to find insects. Any bird of the family Picidae, known for drumming on wood. A bird that makes a rapid tapping sound on trees. Figuratively, a person who works persistently at the same task.

urduMeaning: ادب و احترام ظاہر کرنے والا، بڑوں کی رائے کے سامنے جھکنے والا، نیاز مندانہ، عاجزی اور احترام سے پیش آنے والا، تعظیم کرنے والا
englishMeaning: Showing polite respect towards someone, especially a senior person. Willing to yield to the opinions or wishes of others out of respect. Marked by courteous submission or humility. Behaving in a way that acknowledges another's higher status.
antonyms: Disrespectful, Rude, Arrogant, Insolent, Impolite, Defiant, Contemptuous
sindhiMeaning: ادب ۽ احترام ڏيکاريندڙ، وڏن جي راءِ اڳيان جهڪندڙ، نياز مندي وارو، عاجزي ۽ احترام سان پيش ايندڙ، تعظيم ڏيکاريندڙ
synonyms: Respectful, Polite, Courteous, Humble, Submissive, Reverent, Obliging, Civil
examples: He was polite and deferential towards his teachers. She spoke in a deferential tone to the elderly guests. The staff were unusually deferential to the visiting director. His deferential manner impressed the committee.

synonyms: Plush, Velour, Silk, Softness, Smoothness, Fabric, Textile
englishMeaning: A soft fabric with a thick, short pile on one side. Cloth made of silk, cotton, or nylon with a smooth, rich surface. The soft skin covering the growing antlers of a deer. Something extremely smooth, soft, or luxurious to touch. Made of or resembling this fabric.
sindhiMeaning: مخمل، هڪ نرم ۽ ملائم ڪپڙو جنهن جي مٿاڇري تي ننڍڙا وار هجن، ريشمي يا سوٽي مخملي ڪپڙو، هرڻ جي نئين سڱن مٿان نرم کل، تمام نرم ۽ ملائم شيءِ
examples: She wore a dark green velvet dress to the party. The chairs were covered in soft red velvet. His voice was as smooth as velvet. The deer's antlers were still covered in velvet.
urduMeaning: مخمل، ایک نرم اور ملائم کپڑا جس کی سطح پر باریک روئیں ہوں، ریشمی یا سوتی مخملی کپڑا، ہرن کے نئے سینگوں پر نرم کھال، نہایت نرم و ملائم چیز
antonyms: Coarse cloth, Burlap, Roughness, Sackcloth, Canvas, Harshness
Synthetic fabric, Polyester, Wool, Nylon, Plastic, Rough cloth
synonyms: Flax cloth, Textile, Fabric, Cambric, Bedding, Napery, Cloth
sindhiMeaning: ڪتان جي ٻوٽي مان ٺهيل مضبوط ڪپڙو، لينن، اهو ڪپڙو جيڪو ٿڌو ۽ پائيدار هوندو آهي، گهر ۾ استعمال ٿيندڙ چادرون ۽ ميز پوش، ڪتاني ڪپڙي جو ٺهيل

urduMeaning: کتان کے پودے کے ریشوں سے بنا مضبوط کپڑا، لینن، وہ کپڑا جو ٹھنڈا اور پائیدار ہوتا ہے، گھریلو چادریں، میز پوش اور تولیے، کتانی کپڑے سے بنا ہوا

englishMeaning: A heap of animal dung or farmyard manure. A pile of waste or refuse, especially near a farm. A dirty, squalid place or condition. Figuratively, a situation or position regarded as low and worthless.

urduMeaning: گوبر کا ڈھیر جو کھاد کے طور پر استعمال ہو، فضلے یا کوڑے کا انبار، نہایت گندی جگہ، بے کار یا حقیر چیز
synonyms: Dunghill, Manure pile, Midden, Muckheap, Compost heap, Refuse pile

antonyms: Ordinary, Unremarkable, Expected, Boring, Mediocre, Commonplace

urduMeaning: جوش پیدا کرنے والا، بجلی جیسا اثر رکھنے والا، نہایت سنسنی خیز اور پرجوش، سامعین کو جھنجھوڑ دینے والا، بجلی فراہم کرنے سے متعلق

urduMeaning: سنسنی خیز، بڑی دلچسپی یا ہلچل پیدا کرنے والا، نہایت شاندار، چونکا دینے والے انداز میں پیش کیا گیا، حواس سے متعلق
englishMeaning: Causing great public interest, excitement, or shock. Extremely good or impressive. Presented in a way designed to shock or excite people. Relating to the senses or physical sensation.

synonyms: Amazing, Thrilling, Spectacular, Startling, Marvellous, Exciting, Shocking
sindhiMeaning: سنسني خيز، وڏي دلچسپي يا هلچل پيدا ڪندڙ، تمام شاندار، حيرت ۾ وجهندڙ انداز ۾ پيش ڪيل، حواسن سان لاڳاپيل
examples: The team's comeback was nothing short of sensational. Newspapers published sensational reports about the scandal. She looked sensational in her wedding dress. The trial received sensational media coverage.

urduMeaning: غیر معمولی، حیرت انگیز حد تک شاندار، مقدار یا معیار میں بہت زیادہ، کسی مظہر سے متعلق، غیر معمولی صلاحیت والا
examples: She has a phenomenal memory for names and dates. The film enjoyed phenomenal success worldwide. His growth as a player has been phenomenal. The city experienced phenomenal economic development.
sindhiMeaning: غير معمولي، حيرت انگيز طور شاندار، مقدار يا معيار ۾ تمام گهڻو، ڪنهن مظهر سان لاڳاپيل، غير معمولي صلاحيت وارو
synonyms: Extraordinary, Remarkable, Exceptional, Outstanding, Incredible, Prodigious, Amazing
antonyms: Ordinary, Average, Mediocre, Unremarkable, Poor, Common, Modest
englishMeaning: Extraordinary and remarkable in a way that impresses people. Exceptionally great in amount, quality, or degree. Relating to a phenomenon or something perceived by the senses. Outstandingly successful or gifted.

antonyms: Minimalist, Trendsetter, Individualist, Nonconformist, Frugal person
englishMeaning: A person obsessed with buying trendy or hyped fashion items. Someone who follows streetwear trends mainly for status. A collector of limited-edition sneakers and branded clothing. Informally, a person who values brand hype over personal style.
examples: He spends his entire salary like a true hypebeast. The store was crowded with hypebeasts waiting for the new release. She calls her brother a hypebeast because of his sneaker collection. Being a hypebeast can be an expensive habit.
synonyms: Trend follower, Fashion victim, Sneakerhead, Style chaser, Brand lover, Follower
sindhiMeaning: اُهو شخص جيڪو مشهور ۽ مهانگي فيشن جي شين جو ديوانو هجي، برانڊ جي شوق ۾ مبتلا نوجوان، محدود ايڊيشن جوتن ۽ ڪپڙن جو گڏ ڪندڙ، صرف اسٽيٽس لاءِ فيشن ڪندڙ
urduMeaning: وہ شخص جو مشہور اور مہنگے فیشن آئٹمز کا دیوانہ ہو، برانڈ کے شوق میں مبتلا نوجوان، محدود ایڈیشن جوتوں اور کپڑوں کا کلیکٹر، صرف اسٹیٹس کے لیے فیشن کرنے والا

examples: The young firebrand challenged the party leadership. He was known as a political firebrand in his youth. She pulled a firebrand from the campfire. The firebrand preacher drew huge crowds.
synonyms: Agitator, Radical, Rabble-rouser, Instigator, Militant, Torch, Ember
antonyms: Peacemaker, Moderate, Conciliator, Pacifist, Conformist, Calmer
englishMeaning: A person who stirs up trouble or passionately supports a cause. An energetic and often rebellious agitator. A piece of burning wood. Someone whose fiery speech inspires or provokes others.
urduMeaning: جوش دلانے والا شخص، ہلچل یا بغاوت پیدا کرنے والا، جلتی ہوئی لکڑی کا ٹکڑا، جذباتی تقریر سے لوگوں کو ابھارنے والا
sindhiMeaning: جوش ڏياريندڙ شخص، بغاوت يا هلچل پيدا ڪندڙ، ٻرندڙ ڪاٺ جو ٽڪرو، جذباتي تقرير سان ماڻهن کي اڀاريندڙ

synonyms: News addict, Compulsive scroller, Pessimistic reader, Screen addict, Doomsurfer
englishMeaning: A person who keeps scrolling through negative or distressing news online. Someone who compulsively reads bad news on social media. A user who spends long periods consuming alarming content. Informally, a person trapped in a cycle of gloomy online reading.
urduMeaning: وہ شخص جو آن لائن مسلسل بری اور مایوس کن خبریں پڑھتا رہے، سوشل میڈیا پر منفی خبروں کا عادی، خوفناک مواد میں گم رہنے والا صارف، مایوس کن اسکرولنگ کرنے والا
examples: He became a doomscroller during the long lockdown. Every doomscroller should take regular breaks from the news. She admits she is a doomscroller late at night. Doomscrollers often report higher levels of anxiety.
sindhiMeaning: اُهو شخص جيڪو آن لائين لاڳيتو خراب ۽ مايوس ڪندڙ خبرون پڙهندو رهي، سوشل ميڊيا تي منفي خبرن جو عادي، ڊيڄاريندڙ مواد ۾ گم رهندڙ صارف، مايوسي واري اسڪرولنگ ڪندڙ
antonyms: Optimist, Digital minimalist, Offline person, News avoider, Mindful user

sindhiMeaning: خودپسند ۽ ٺاٺ باٺ وارو مرد، بانڪو، بيوقوف ۽ نمائشي شخص، مسخري جي ٽوپي جيڪا ڪڪڙ جي ڪلغي جهڙي هجي، ڪلغي جهڙي گل وارو ٻوٽو
examples: He dismissed the young man as a vain coxcomb. The play features a coxcomb who admires himself constantly. The jester's coxcomb was bright red and yellow. She planted coxcomb along the garden path.
synonyms: Dandy, Fop, Popinjay, Show-off, Peacock, Jester's cap, Celosia
urduMeaning: خود پسند اور بناؤ سنگھار کا شوقین مرد، بانکا، احمق اور نمائشی شخص، مسخرے کی ٹوپی جو مرغ کی کلغی جیسی ہو، کلغی نما پھول والا پودا
antonyms: Modest person, Humble man, Plain dresser, Unassuming person, Simpleton
englishMeaning: A vain and conceited man who is overly concerned with his appearance. A foolish, showy person. The cap worn by a court jester, resembling a cock's comb. A plant with a crested flower head, also called celosia.

A person who tells stories or anecdotes in a skillful and entertaining way. Someone who is good at narrating events with humour and vivid detail. A gifted and amusing storyteller who holds the attention of listeners. A person known socially for recounting interesting personal experiences.
sindhiMeaning: ڪهاڻيون دلچسپ انداز ۾ ٻڌائيندڙ ماڻهو، ماهر قصه گو، اهڙو شخص جيڪو واقعا مزيدار ۽ تفصيل سان بيان ڪري، محفل ۾ ڳالهه ٻڌائڻ جو ڀلوڙ ماهر
antonyms: Listener, Audience, Bore, Mute, Silent person
synonyms: Storyteller, Narrator, Anecdotalist, Talespinner, Chronicler, Entertainer, Conversationalist
examples: Her grandfather was a wonderful raconteur who kept everyone spellbound. The dinner guests laughed for hours at the raconteur's tales. As a raconteur, he could turn an ordinary journey into an adventure. The old sailor was a famous raconteur in the coastal town.
urduMeaning: دلچسپ انداز میں کہانیاں سنانے والا شخص، ماہر قصہ گو، ایسا شخص جو واقعات مزے دار اور تفصیل سے بیان کرے، محفل میں باتیں سنانے کا ماہر

antonyms: Sage, Thinker, Listener, Wisdom, Sense, Silence, Reticent person
englishMeaning: A person who talks at great length without making much sense. Someone who speaks foolish or nonsensical talk. Foolish, empty or long-winded talk itself. A babbling, boastful and tiresome talker.
sindhiMeaning: بيهوده ۽ اجائي ڊگهي ڳالهه ڪندڙ ماڻهو، بڪواس ڪندڙ، اجائي ۽ بي معنيٰ ڳالهه، وڏ ڦڙو ۽ ٿڪائيندڙ ڳالهائيندڙ
synonyms: Babbler, Windbag, Chatterbox, Blowhard, Prattler, Nonsense, Twaddle, Gibberish
examples: The old blatherskite talked for an hour without saying anything useful. Ignore that blatherskite; he never knows what he is talking about. The meeting was ruined by the blatherskite in the front row. His speech was pure blatherskite from beginning to end.
urduMeaning: بے تکی اور بے معنی لمبی باتیں کرنے والا شخص، بکواس کرنے والا، فضول اور لایعنی گفتگو، شیخی بگھارنے والا تھکا دینے والا مقرر

antonyms: Hero, Brave, Valiant, Courageous, Champion, Daredevil, Stalwart
sindhiMeaning: بزدل ۽ ڊڄڻو ماڻهو، همت کان خالي شخص، انتهائي ڪايرو، ڊڄڻي رويي وارو
englishMeaning: An utter coward who lacks courage in the face of danger. A contemptibly timid or spiritless person. Behaving in a cowardly or shamefully fearful manner. Describing someone marked by a complete lack of bravery.
examples: He called the deserter a poltroon in front of the whole regiment. Only a poltroon would abandon his friends in such danger. She refused to be a poltroon and spoke against the injustice. His poltroon behaviour cost the team its victory.
urduMeaning: انتہائی بزدل شخص، ہمت سے عاری آدمی، ڈرپوک اور کم ہمت، بزدلانہ رویہ رکھنے والا
synonyms: Coward, Craven, Dastard, Chicken, Recreant, Weakling, Faint-hearted

englishMeaning: A single flake or crystal of falling snow. A person considered overly sensitive or easily offended, used in an insulting way. Someone who believes they are uniquely special and deserving of attention. A shape or decorative pattern resembling a crystal of snow.
antonyms: Hailstone, Thick-skinned, Resilient, Tough, Hardy, Stoic
sindhiMeaning: برف جو ٿلهو ذرو يا گلو، تمام گهڻو حساس ۽ جلد ناراض ٿيندڙ ماڻهو (طنزيه)، پاڻ کي انوکو ۽ خاص سمجهندڙ شخص، برف جي گلي جهڙي شڪل يا نقش
urduMeaning: برف کا گالہ یا ذرہ، بہت زیادہ حساس اور جلد ناراض ہو جانے والا شخص (طنزاً)، خود کو منفرد اور خاص سمجھنے والا فرد، برف کے گالے جیسی شکل یا نقش
synonyms: Snow crystal, Flake, Ice crystal, Oversensitive person, Delicate soul
examples: Each snowflake that fell had a perfect six-sided pattern. Children pressed their faces to the glass to watch the snowflakes. He accused his critics of being snowflakes who cannot take a joke. She cut paper snowflakes to decorate the classroom windows.

As a misoneist, he refused to use a smartphone for years. The committee's misoneist members blocked every reform. She is no misoneist and welcomes fresh ideas. A misoneist rarely thrives in a fast-changing industry.
sindhiMeaning: نئين شيءِ يا تبديليءَ کان نفرت ڪندڙ ماڻهو، جدت مخالف، پراڻن طور طريقن سان چنبڙيل شخص، ترقي ۽ اصلاح جو مخالف
urduMeaning: نئی چیزوں اور تبدیلی سے نفرت کرنے والا شخص، جدت مخالف، پرانے طور طریقوں سے چمٹا رہنے والا فرد، ترقی اور اصلاح کا مخالف
synonyms: Conservative, Traditionalist, Reactionary, Luddite, Diehard, Old-fashioned person
antonyms: Innovator, Progressive, Reformer, Modernist, Pioneer, Trendsetter
englishMeaning: A person who hates or strongly dislikes change, novelty or new ideas. Someone deeply attached to old ways and suspicious of innovation. A hater of anything new, including modern technology or reform. One who resists progress out of principle or habit.

sindhiMeaning: ٺڳ ۽ فريبي ماڻهو، جعلي دوائون وڪڻندڙ، ڪوڙيون دعوائون ڪري ماڻهن کي بيوقوف بڻائيندڙ، ڏيکاءَ وارو ٺڳ
examples: The so-called healer turned out to be a mountebank. Do not trust that mountebank with your savings. In old markets, a mountebank would sell useless potions. Critics dismissed the speaker as a political mountebank.
synonyms: Charlatan, Fraud, Swindler, Quack, Impostor, Trickster, Con artist
urduMeaning: دھوکے باز اور فریبی شخص، جعلی دوائیں بیچنے والا، جھوٹے دعوے کر کے لوگوں کو بے وقوف بنانے والا، دکھاوے باز ٹھگ
antonyms: Honest person, Expert, Authority, Professional, Truth-teller, Specialist
englishMeaning: A person who deceives others in order to trick them out of money. A charlatan who makes false claims about skills or remedies. A showy speaker who attracts crowds with boastful and dishonest talk. Historically, a seller of fake medicines at fairs and markets.

synonyms: Optimist, Idealist, Dreamer, Hopeful, Panglossian
urduMeaning: حد سے زیادہ اور غیر حقیقی امید رکھنے والا شخص، ہر حال میں اچھائی ڈھونڈنے والا، مسائل کو نظر انداز کر کے خوش رہنے والا، سادہ لوح خوش فہم
examples: Do not be such a Pollyanna about the company's losses. Her Pollyanna outlook helped the team stay hopeful. A Pollyanna attitude will not solve these serious issues. He smiled like a Pollyanna even after the bad news.
englishMeaning: A person who is excessively or unrealistically optimistic. Someone who always finds something good in every situation. An attitude of blind cheerfulness that ignores real problems. Describing an outlook that is naively positive.
sindhiMeaning: حد کان وڌيڪ ۽ غير حقيقي اميد رکندڙ ماڻهو، هر حال ۾ چڱائي ڳوليندڙ، مسئلن کي نظرانداز ڪري خوش رهندڙ، سادو ۽ خوش فهم شخص
antonyms: Pessimist, Cynic, Realist, Doomsayer, Defeatist

examples: As a digital nomad, she writes code from a different city each month. Many digital nomads gather in cheap coastal towns. He became a digital nomad after his company allowed remote work. Reliable internet is essential for any digital nomad.
synonyms: Remote worker, Location-independent worker, Telecommuter, Freelancer, Global worker
urduMeaning: ٹیکنالوجی کی مدد سے سفر کرتے ہوئے کام کرنے والا شخص، آن لائن روزگار کمانے والا سیاح، کسی مقررہ دفتر کے بغیر کام کرنے والا، مقام سے آزاد پیشہ ور
antonyms: Office worker, Commuter, Resident employee, Settler, Nine-to-fiver
englishMeaning: A person who works remotely using technology while travelling from place to place. Someone with no fixed office who earns a living online. A worker who combines a mobile lifestyle with internet-based employment. A modern professional who chooses location independence.
sindhiMeaning: ٽيڪنالاجي جي مدد سان گهمندي ڦرندي ڪم ڪندڙ ماڻهو، آن لائين روزگار وارو سفر ڪندڙ، ڪنهن مقرر آفيس کان سواءِ ڪم ڪندڙ، جاءِ کان آزاد پيشيور

antonyms: Expert, Veteran, Master, Professional, Specialist, Adept
sindhiMeaning: نئون سکندڙ يا ابتدائي ماڻهو، ڪم ۾ نئون، نئون مذهب اختيار ڪندڙ، ڪنهن جماعت ۾ نئون شامل ٿيل فرد
synonyms: Beginner, Novice, Learner, Rookie, Apprentice, Newcomer, Trainee
examples: As a neophyte, he made several simple mistakes. The class is designed for neophytes rather than experts. The monastery welcomed three neophytes this spring. Even a neophyte can learn this software in a week.
urduMeaning: نیا سیکھنے والا یا ابتدائی شخص، کسی کام میں نو آموز، نیا مذہب اختیار کرنے والا، کسی گروہ میں نیا شامل ہونے والا فرد
englishMeaning: A person who is new to a subject, skill or activity. A beginner who is still learning the basics. A recent convert to a religion or belief. A newly admitted member of a group or order.

urduMeaning: مویشیوں کو کاٹنے والی مکھی، مسلسل تنقید کرنے والا شخص، حکام سے مشکل سوالات پوچھ کر پریشان کرنے والا، لوگوں کو جھنجھوڑنے والا ناقد
antonyms: Supporter, Flatterer, Conformist, Yes-man, Sycophant, Peacemaker
sindhiMeaning: مال کي چڪ هڻندڙ مک، مسلسل تنقيد ڪندڙ ماڻهو، اختيارين کان ڏکيا سوال پڇي پريشان ڪندڙ شخص، ماڻهن کي جاڳائيندڙ تنگ ڪندڙ نقاد
synonyms: Critic, Provocateur, Agitator, Irritant, Pest, Horsefly, Nuisance
englishMeaning: A fly that bites livestock, especially a horsefly. A person who persistently criticises or provokes others into action. Someone who annoys authorities by asking uncomfortable questions. An irritating but useful critic who stirs up complacent people.
examples: A gadfly settled on the horse's back in the summer heat. The journalist was a gadfly who exposed official corruption. Every council needs a gadfly to question lazy decisions. He enjoyed his role as the gadfly of the university board.

synonyms: Speaker, Rhetorician, Lecturer, Declaimer, Spokesperson, Preacher
urduMeaning: ماہر مقرر، عوام کے سامنے مؤثر تقریر کرنے والا، فصاحت سے سامعین کو متاثر کرنے والا، فنِ خطابت کا ماہر
examples: The orator held the crowd's attention for a full hour. She is a gifted orator who never uses notes. Ancient Rome produced many famous orators. The young orator won the national debate competition.
sindhiMeaning: ماهر مقرر، عوام اڳيان اثرائتي تقرير ڪندڙ، فصاحت سان ماڻهن کي متاثر ڪندڙ ڳالهائيندڙ، تقرير جي فن جو ڄاڻو
englishMeaning: A person who delivers speeches in public with skill and power. A speaker who can move an audience through eloquence. Someone formally trained or gifted in the art of public speaking. A leading spokesperson at a ceremony or debate.
antonyms: Listener, Audience, Mute, Stammerer, Silent observer

synonyms: Empty, Blank, Inane, Mindless, Shallow, Meaningless, Hollow, Unintelligent
urduMeaning: بے معنی اور خالی، سوچ سے عاری، بے مقصد اور بے مغز، خالی الذہن یا بے تاثر چہرے والا
examples: He gave a vacuous smile and said nothing. The interview was full of vacuous remarks. Her vacuous stare showed she was not listening. Critics called the film beautiful but vacuous.
englishMeaning: Showing a lack of thought or intelligence. Empty of meaning, content or substance. Having a blank or expressionless appearance. Devoid of ideas or serious purpose.
antonyms: Thoughtful, Intelligent, Profound, Meaningful, Substantial, Insightful
sindhiMeaning: بي معنيٰ ۽ خالي، سوچ کان خالي، بي مقصد ۽ بي مغز، بي تاثر شڪل وارو
مالدار ۽ غريب ماڻهو، سماج ۾ سکيا ستابا ۽ محروم طبقا، وسيلن وارا ۽ وسيلن کان خالي ماڻهو، معاشي ناهمواري جو اظهار
antonyms: Equality, Classless society, Egalitarianism, Equal distribution, Social parity
synonyms: Rich and poor, Wealthy and needy, Privileged and deprived, Upper and lower classes
examples: The gap between the haves and the have-nots keeps widening. Education can reduce the distance between the haves and the have-nots. The city clearly divides the haves and the have-nots. Politicians often promise to help the have-nots.
englishMeaning: The people who are wealthy and those who are poor. A phrase contrasting privileged groups with deprived groups in society. The division between those who own resources and those who lack them. A general expression for economic inequality.
urduMeaning: دولت مند اور غریب لوگ، معاشرے میں مراعات یافتہ اور محروم طبقات، وسائل رکھنے والے اور وسائل سے محروم افراد، معاشی ناہمواری کا اظہار
اچھے اور برے دونوں حالات میں، ہر حال میں ساتھ نبھانا، مشکل ہو یا آسانی، غیر متزلزل وفاداری
antonyms: Fair-weather, Only in good times, Disloyally, Inconsistently, Conditionally
synonyms: Through everything, In good times and bad, Come what may, Rain or shine, Steadfastly
englishMeaning: Good times and bad times alike. Under all circumstances, whatever difficulties arise. Used to describe unwavering loyalty or support. Every kind of condition, favourable or unfavourable.
examples: She stood by her brother through thick and thin. Good friends stay together through thick and thin. The team supported their captain through thick and thin. They have shared thick and thin for thirty years.
sindhiMeaning: سک ۽ ڏک ٻنهي حالتن ۾، هر حال ۾ ساٿ ڏيڻ، مشڪل توڙي آسان وقت ۾، مضبوط ۽ اٽل وفاداري
وڏائي ڪندڙ، پاڻ کي ٻين کان مٿانهون سمجهندڙ، مغرور ۽ خودپسند، وڏ ماڻهپي ڏيکاريندڙ
englishMeaning: Having far too much pride in oneself and one's abilities. Behaving as if one is better or more important than others. Showing vanity in speech, manner or appearance. Excessively self-satisfied.
antonyms: Humble, Modest, Unassuming, Self-effacing, Meek, Down-to-earth
synonyms: Arrogant, Vain, Boastful, Egotistical, Self-important, Haughty, Smug, Proud
urduMeaning: مغرور اور خود پسند، خود کو دوسروں سے برتر سمجھنے والا، گھمنڈی، اپنی تعریف پر نازاں
examples: He is too conceited to accept any advice. Winning one prize made her rather conceited. Nobody enjoys working with a conceited colleague. His conceited manner annoyed the whole class.

urduMeaning: تسلیم کر لیا، مان لیا، شکست قبول کی، ناچاہتے ہوئے کوئی بات یا رعایت دی، حریف کو گول یا پوائنٹ دے دیا
antonyms: Denied, Refused, Disputed, Contested, Withheld, Resisted
sindhiMeaning: مڃيو، تسليم ڪيو، شڪست قبول ڪئي، ناچاهيندي به ڪا شيءِ ڏني يا اجازت ڏني، مخالف کي پوائنٽ يا گول ڏنو
synonyms: Admitted, Acknowledged, Accepted, Yielded, Granted, Surrendered, Allowed
englishMeaning: Admitted that something is true after first denying it. Accepted defeat in a contest or argument. Granted or allowed something, often reluctantly. Gave away points, goals or ground to an opponent.
examples: He finally conceded that he had made a mistake. The candidate conceded the election that night. The company conceded a small pay rise. Our team conceded two goals in the last minutes.

englishMeaning: Impossible to erase, remove or rub out. Leaving a permanent mark or impression. Unable to be forgotten or wiped from memory. Lasting and indelible in effect.
sindhiMeaning: جيڪو مِٽجي نه سگهي، ناقابل مٽائڻ، هميشه رهندڙ نشان ڇڏيندڙ، ذهن مان نه نڪرندڙ
antonyms: Erasable, Removable, Temporary, Forgettable, Fleeting, Washable
synonyms: Indelible, Permanent, Unforgettable, Enduring, Lasting, Imperishable

antonyms: Unlucky, Unfortunate, Untimely, Disastrous, Ill-timed, Calamitous
sindhiMeaning: خوش قسمتيءَ وارو، خدا جي مهربانيءَ سان صحيح وقت تي ٿيندڙ، غيبي مدد وارو، اهڙو موقعو جيڪو اتفاق کان وڌيڪ لڳي، رباني رهنمائي يا حفاظت سان لاڳاپيل
synonyms: Fortunate, Lucky, Timely, Opportune, Heaven-sent, Auspicious, Fortuitous, Blessed
urduMeaning: خوش قسمت، عین وقت پر ہونے والا، خدا کی مہربانی سے آنے والا، غیبی مدد سے متعلق، ایسا اتفاق جو محض اتفاق نہ لگے، ربانی رہنمائی یا حفاظت سے متعلق

urduMeaning: بدنصیب، بدقسمت، قابلِ رحم، مسلسل مصیبت میں گھرا ہوا، لاچار اور بے بس، بغیر کسی قصور کے نقصان اٹھانے والا
englishMeaning: Unlucky and deserving of pity. Suffering repeated misfortune through no fault of one's own. Unfortunate in a way that often seems helpless or pitiful. Having bad luck in a situation one cannot control.
examples: The hapless traveller lost his passport on the first day. A hapless goalkeeper watched the ball slip through his hands. She felt sorry for the hapless victims of the flood. The hapless team lost every match of the season.
synonyms: Unlucky, Unfortunate, Ill-fated, Wretched, Luckless, Doomed, Pitiable, Miserable
sindhiMeaning: بدنصيب، بدقسمت، ترس جوڳو، مسلسل مصيبت ۾ ڦاٿل، لاچار ۽ بي وس شخص، بغير ڪنهن ڏوهه جي نقصان سهندڙ
antonyms: Lucky, Fortunate, Blessed, Successful, Prosperous, Favoured

examples: Sperm and egg cells are haploid. The haploid number in humans is twenty-three. Fertilisation joins two haploid cells to form a diploid one. Many fungi spend most of their life cycle in a haploid state.
urduMeaning: ایک سیٹ کروموسوم رکھنے والا خلیہ، معمول سے نصف کروموسوم والا، ایسا خلیہ جیسے مادۂ تولید یا بیضہ، جنسی خلیوں کی یک لڑی حالت سے متعلق
synonyms: Monoploid, Single-set, Gametic, One-chromosome-set
antonyms: Diploid, Polyploid, Triploid, Tetraploid
sindhiMeaning: هڪ سيٽ ڪروموزوم رکندڙ خليو، عام تعداد کان اڌ ڪروموزوم وارو، اهڙو خليو جهڙو نطفو يا انڊو، جنسي خليي جي هڪ هيري واري حالت سان لاڳاپيل
englishMeaning: Having a single set of unpaired chromosomes in a cell. Describing a cell or organism with half the usual number of chromosomes. A cell, such as a sperm or egg cell, that contains one set of chromosomes. Relating to the single chromosome condition found in gametes.

sindhiMeaning: ٻه سيٽ ڪروموزوم رکندڙ خليو، ماءُ ۽ پيءُ کان هڪ هڪ سيٽ حاصل ڪندڙ، جوڙيدار ڪروموزوم وارو، جسم جي عام خلين واري حالت
englishMeaning: Having two complete sets of chromosomes, one from each parent. Describing a cell or organism with paired chromosomes. A cell that contains the full number of chromosomes typical of a species. Relating to the normal chromosome condition of most body cells.
antonyms: Haploid, Monoploid, Gametic, Polyploid
synonyms: Double-set, Paired, Two-set, Somatic
urduMeaning: دو سیٹ کروموسوم رکھنے والا خلیہ، والدین میں سے ہر ایک سے ایک سیٹ حاصل کرنے والا، جوڑی دار کروموسوم والا، جسم کے عام خلیوں کی حالت سے متعلق

englishMeaning: An official document or certificate showing that a person has completed a course of study. A qualification awarded by a college, school, or training institution. antonyms: Modern creature, Innovator, Trendsetter, Progressive, Newcomer
sindhiMeaning: ڊائناسور، لکين سال اڳ رهندڙ وڏو ناپيد ٿي ويل ريڙهندڙ جانور، ميسوزوئڪ دور جي جانورن جو فرد، پراڻي سوچ وارو شخص يا شيءِ جيڪا هاڻ ڪم جي ناهي، تبديليءَ کي قبول نه ڪندڙ ماڻهو

urduMeaning: ڈائناسور، لاکھوں سال پہلے پایا جانے والا بہت بڑا معدوم رینگنے والا جانور، میسوزوئک دور کے جانوروں میں سے ایک، فرسودہ سوچ رکھنے والا شخص یا بے کار پرانی چیز، تبدیلی کو قبول نہ کرنے والا شخص

antonyms: Approving, Praising, Encouraging, Complimentary, Supportive, Admiring

synonyms: Disapprovingly, Reproachfully, Critically, Chidingly, Admonishingly, Sternly

examples: She shook her head reprovingly at the noise. He looked reprovingly at his younger brother. The manager spoke reprovingly about the late reports. My grandmother clicked her tongue reprovingly.
urduMeaning: ملامت آمیز انداز میں، سرزنش کے ساتھ، ناپسندیدگی ظاہر کرتے ہوئے، نرمی سے ٹوکتے ہوئے، اصلاح کی نیت سے تنبیہ کرتے ہوئے
