englishMeaning: Excessive or self-absorbed unhappiness about one's own troubles or misfortunes. A feeling of sorrow for oneself. An indulgent sense of being unfairly treated or especially unfortunate.
antonyms: Resilience, Fortitude, Self-confidence, Acceptance
sindhiMeaning: پاڻ تي ترس، خود رحمي، پنهنجي تڪليفن تي حد کان وڌيڪ ڏک، پاڻ کي مظلوم سمجهڻ، پنهنجي بدقسمتيءَ ۾ ٻڏل رهڻ

examples: His self-pitying tone made real comfort difficult. She wrote a self-pitying letter blaming everyone but herself. Stop being self-pitying and take responsibility for your choices. The character's self-pitying monologue dominated the second act.
synonyms: Maudlin, Mournful, Woeful, Self-absorbed, Complaining
urduMeaning: خود ترسی میں مبتلا، اپنے حال پر ترس کھانے والا، خود کو مظلوم سمجھنے والا، اپنی مصیبت کی شکایت سے ہمدردی لینے والا
antonyms: Resilient, Stoic, Upbeat, Self-assured, Uncomplaining
sindhiMeaning: پاڻ تي ترس کائيندڙ، خود رحمي ۾ مبتلا، پاڻ کي مظلوم سمجهندڙ، پنهنجي ڏکن جي شڪايت ڪري همدردي وٺندڙ
englishMeaning: Feeling or showing excessive sorrow for one's own troubles or misfortunes. Characterized by an indulgent belief that one is unfairly treated or especially unfortunate. Expressing complaints intended to attract sympathy.

examples: Poverty can become a self-perpetuating cycle. The bureaucracy seemed to be a self-perpetuating system resistant to reform. Prejudice becomes self-perpetuating when passed through generations. The committee's self-perpetuating structure made change difficult.
englishMeaning: Able to continue or renew itself indefinitely without outside intervention. Describing a process, system, or cycle that sustains or reproduces itself. Tending to reinforce the conditions that keep it operating.
synonyms: Self-sustaining, Self-renewing, Self-continuing, Self-reinforcing
sindhiMeaning: پاڻ کي جاري رکندڙ، پاڻمرادو برقرار رهندڙ، پنهنجو تسلسل پاڻ پيدا ڪندڙ، پنهنجي حالتن کي مضبوط ڪري هلندڙ
antonyms: Self-limiting, Temporary, Unsustainable, Finite
urduMeaning: خود کو جاری رکھنے والا، خودکار طور پر برقرار رہنے والا، اپنا تسلسل خود پیدا کرنے والا، اپنی موجودگی کی حالتوں کو مضبوط کرنے والا

examples: He is so self-obsessed that he never asks how anyone else is doing. She became increasingly self-obsessed after gaining fame. Self-obsessed people may struggle to maintain healthy relationships. His self-obsessed attitude annoyed everyone at the party.
urduMeaning: خود میں حد سے زیادہ مگن، خود پسند، اپنی ضرورتوں یا صورت ہی کے بارے میں سوچنے والا، دوسروں کے جذبات سے بے پروا
synonyms: Narcissistic, Self-centered, Egotistical, Vain, Self-absorbed
antonyms: Selfless, Altruistic, Considerate, Humble, Other-centered
sindhiMeaning: پاڻ سان حد کان وڌيڪ مشغول، خودپرست، پنهنجي ضرورتن يا ڏيک بابت ئي سوچيندڙ، ٻين جي احساسن کان بي پرواهه
englishMeaning: Excessively preoccupied with oneself, one's needs, achievements, or appearance. Focused on oneself to an unhealthy or unpleasant degree. Showing little interest in other people's feelings or needs.

The inner drive to pursue goals and take action without external pressure or encouragement. The ability to begin and sustain effort independently. Personal enthusiasm, discipline, and determination that direct behavior toward achievement.
antonyms: Apathy, Laziness, Indifference, Lethargy, Dependence
sindhiMeaning: اندروني اتساهه، پاڻ کي همٿائڻ جي صلاحيت، ٻاهرين دٻاءَ کانسواءِ ڪم ڪرڻ، مقصد لاءِ پنهنجي ڪوشش جاري رکڻ، ذاتي جوش ۽ ارادو
synonyms: Drive, Initiative, Ambition, Determination, Willpower
examples: Her self-motivation helped her complete the marathon training alone. Employers value self-motivation because it reduces the need for supervision. He found the self-motivation to study every night after work. Self-motivation is essential for independent entrepreneurs.
urduMeaning: اندرونی ترغیب، خود کو حوصلہ دینے کی صلاحیت، بیرونی دباؤ کے بغیر کام کرنا، مقصد کے لیے اپنی کوشش جاری رکھنا، ذاتی جوش اور عزم

sindhiMeaning: پنهنجي جسم کي ڄاڻي واڻي زخمي ڪرڻ، خود ايذا رساني، جذباتي تڪليف سبب پاڻ کي نقصان پهچائڻ، پنهنجي جسم جو حصو خراب يا ڪٽڻ
englishMeaning: The deliberate injury of one's own body, often as a response to severe emotional distress. Intentional self-harm, such as cutting or burning, that may occur without suicidal intent. The act of damaging or removing part of one's own body.
synonyms: Self-harm, Self-injury, Cutting, Self-inflicted Injury
urduMeaning: اپنے جسم کو جان بوجھ کر زخمی کرنا، خود ایذا رسانی، جذباتی تکلیف کے سبب خود کو نقصان پہنچانا، اپنے جسم کے حصے کو کاٹنا یا خراب کرنا
examples: The therapist helps teenagers who struggle with self-mutilation. Self-mutilation can be a sign of severe emotional pain. Doctors warned that repeated self-mutilation can cause serious injury. Compassionate support can help people resist urges toward self-mutilation.
antonyms: Self-care, Self-preservation, Self-protection, Self-nurturing

englishMeaning: Having an excessively high regard for one's own opinions. Stubbornly convinced that one's views are correct. Unwilling to listen to or consider other people's ideas.
examples: He is too self-opinionated to accept criticism of his plan. Her self-opinionated remarks often started arguments. Being self-opinionated can prevent a person from learning. The self-opinionated manager ignored his team's suggestions.
synonyms: Opinionated, Dogmatic, Obstinate, Headstrong, Arrogant
antonyms: Open-minded, Flexible, Receptive, Humble, Tolerant
urduMeaning: اپنی رائے کو حد سے زیادہ درست سمجھنے والا، اپنی بات پر اڑا رہنے والا، ہٹ دھرم، دوسروں کے خیالات نہ سننے والا
sindhiMeaning: پنهنجي راءِ کي حد کان وڌيڪ صحيح سمجهندڙ، پنهنجي ڳالهه تي اڙيل، ضدي راءِ رکندڙ، ٻين جا خيال نه ٻڌندڙ

antonyms: Lazy, Apathetic, Unmotivated, Indifferent, Passive
sindhiMeaning: اندروني اتساهه رکندڙ، خودجوش، ٻاهرين دٻاءَ کانسواءِ ڪم ڪندڙ، پاڻمرادو ڪوشش جاري رکندڙ، مقصد لاءِ پرعزم
synonyms: Driven, Ambitious, Proactive, Determined, Enterprising
urduMeaning: اندرونی ترغیب رکھنے والا، خود محرک، بیرونی دباؤ کے بغیر کام کرنے والا، خود کوشش جاری رکھنے والا، مقصد کے لیے پُرعزم
examples: She is a self-motivated employee who rarely needs reminders. Self-motivated students often achieve strong academic results. He remained self-motivated while working from home. Companies value self-motivated candidates for independent roles.
englishMeaning: Driven by internal desire, interest, or ambition rather than external pressure or reward. Able to begin tasks and sustain effort independently. Showing initiative, discipline, and determination in pursuing goals.

urduMeaning: سوراخ، جسم کا قدرتی کھلا حصہ، کسی ساخت یا پائپ میں کھلی جگہ، ہوا یا سیال کے گزرنے کا راستہ
englishMeaning: An opening or hole, especially one in the body. An aperture in the surface of a structure, vessel, pipe, or device. A passage through which air, liquid, or another substance can enter or leave.
antonyms: Closure, Seal, Blockage, Obstruction
examples: The surgeon carefully examined the orifice before the procedure. Water flowed through a small orifice in the pipe. Each nasal orifice allows air to enter the respiratory system. Engineers adjusted the orifice to control the flow rate.
sindhiMeaning: سوراخ، جسم جو قدرتي کليل حصو، ڪنهن بناوت يا پائيپ ۾ کليل جاءِ، هوا يا سيال جي اچ وڃ جو لنگهه
synonyms: Opening, Aperture, Hole, Vent, Mouth

urduMeaning: کسی سمت کے مطابق ترتیب دیا گیا، خاص مقصد یا گروہ کی طرف مرکوز، نئے ماحول یا طریقوں سے واقف کرایا گیا، مخصوص رجحان رکھنے والا
examples: The building is oriented to face the morning sun. New employees were oriented to company procedures. The course is oriented toward practical skills. Her career has always been oriented around helping others.
synonyms: Aligned, Directed, Focused, Positioned, Geared
antonyms: Disoriented, Misaligned, Unfocused, Undirected
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن رخ ڏانهن ترتيب ڏنل، خاص مقصد يا گروهه تي ڌيان ڏنل، نئين ماحول يا طريقي سان واقف ڪيل، مخصوص لاڙو رکندڙ
englishMeaning: Positioned or aligned in relation to a particular direction or reference point. Directed or organized toward a particular purpose, interest, or group. Familiarized with a new situation, environment, or set of procedures. Having a specified orientation or preference.

examples: Java is a widely used object-oriented programming language. The team redesigned the software using object-oriented principles. Object-oriented design can make code easier to reuse and maintain. Students learn object-oriented concepts such as inheritance and polymorphism.
urduMeaning: آبجیکٹس پر مبنی پروگرامنگ سے متعلق، ڈیٹا اور اس پر عمل کرنے والے طریقے ایک اکائی میں جمع کرنے والا، کلاس اور آبجیکٹ کے مطابق منظم، وراثت اور کثیر شکلی کے اصولوں والا
sindhiMeaning: آبجيڪٽن تي ٻڌل پروگرامنگ سان لاڳاپيل، ڊيٽا ۽ ان تي ڪم ڪندڙ طريقا هڪ يونٽ ۾ گڏ ڪندڙ، ڪلاس ۽ آبجيڪٽن مطابق ترتيب ڏنل، وراثت ۽ گهڻ روپيت جي اصولن وارو
synonyms: OOP-based, Class-based, Object-based, Modular
antonyms: Procedural, Non-object-oriented, Function-oriented
englishMeaning: Relating to a programming paradigm based on objects that combine data with the procedures that operate on that data. Organized around reusable classes and objects rather than only sequences of actions. Designed according to principles such as encapsulation, inheritance, abstraction, and polymorphism.

urduMeaning: اپنے لیے کام کرنے والا، کسی آجر کے ہاں ملازمت کے بجائے اپنا کاروبار یا آزادانہ کام کرنے والا، اپنی آمدنی اخراجات ٹیکس اور کاروباری خطرات کا خود ذمہ دار
englishMeaning: Working for oneself rather than for an employer. Earning income from one’s own business, profession, or freelance work. Employing oneself and taking responsibility for one’s own taxes, expenses, and business risks.
antonyms: Employed, Salaried, Wage-earning, On staff
synonyms: Independent, Freelance, In business for oneself, Sole-trading, Entrepreneurial
sindhiMeaning: پنهنجي لاءِ ڪم ڪندڙ، ڪنهن آجر وٽ نوڪري ڪرڻ بدران پنهنجو ڪاروبار يا آزاد ڪم ڪندڙ، پنهنجي آمدني خرچن ٽيڪسن ۽ ڪاروباري خطري جو پاڻ ذميوار
examples: She has been self-employed as a graphic designer for five years. Self-employed workers must manage their own taxes. He became self-employed after leaving the company. Many self-employed people work from home.

synonyms: Self-respect, Self-worth, Confidence, Dignity, Pride, Self-regard
examples: Positive feedback helped rebuild her self-esteem. Children need encouragement to develop healthy self-esteem. His self-esteem suffered after repeated criticism. She refused to let the mistake damage her self-esteem.
urduMeaning: اپنی قدر و صلاحیت پر اعتماد، اپنے بارے میں احترام پر مبنی رائے، ذاتی وقار اور اہمیت کا احساس، غرور کے بغیر صحت مند خود اعتمادی
englishMeaning: Confidence in one’s own worth or abilities. The opinion and respect a person has for oneself. A sense of personal value and dignity. Healthy pride in oneself without arrogance.
sindhiMeaning: پنهنجي قدر ۽ صلاحيتن تي اعتماد، پنهنجي باري ۾ عزت ڀريو خيال، ذاتي وقار ۽ اهميت جو احساس، بنا غرور جي صحتمند خود اعتمادي
antonyms: Self-doubt, Insecurity, Shame, Self-contempt, Inferiority

englishMeaning: Confidence in one’s own abilities, judgment, or character. A calm certainty when speaking or acting. Freedom from nervousness or self-doubt.
antonyms: Insecurity, Timidity, Nervousness, Self-doubt, Uncertainty
urduMeaning: اپنی صلاحیت فیصلے یا کردار پر اعتماد، بولتے یا عمل کرتے وقت پُرسکون یقین، گھبراہٹ یا خود شک سے آزادی
sindhiMeaning: پنهنجي صلاحيتن فيصلي يا ڪردار تي اعتماد، ڳالهائڻ يا عمل ڪرڻ وقت پرسڪون يقين، گهٻراهٽ يا خود شڪ کان آزادي
synonyms: Confidence, Poise, Composure, Certainty, Assertiveness, Self-confidence
examples: She answered the difficult questions with self-assurance. His quiet self-assurance impressed the interview panel. Experience gave her greater self-assurance on stage. The child approached the new class with surprising self-assurance.

antonyms: Selfless, Considerate, Altruistic, Generous, Thoughtful
synonyms: Egocentric, Selfish, Self-absorbed, Egotistical, Inconsiderate, Narcissistic
englishMeaning: Concerned mainly with one’s own needs, wishes, or interests. Giving little thought to other people’s feelings or needs. Viewing situations chiefly in relation to oneself.
urduMeaning: زیادہ تر اپنی ضروریات خواہشات یا مفادات کی فکر کرنے والا، دوسروں کے جذبات یا ضرورتوں کا کم خیال رکھنے والا، ہر صورتِ حال کو اپنے حوالے سے دیکھنے والا
sindhiMeaning: گهڻو ڪري پنهنجي ضرورتن خواهشن يا مفادن بابت سوچيندڙ، ٻين جي احساسن يا ضرورتن جو ٿورو خيال رکندڙ، هر حالت کي پنهنجي حوالي سان ڏسندڙ
examples: His self-centred behavior upset the rest of the team. She seemed self-centred because she never asked about anyone else. A self-centred manager may ignore employees’ concerns. He is becoming less self-centred as he grows older.

englishMeaning: To make someone lose their sense of direction. To make someone confused about where they are, what is happening, or what time it is. To disturb a person’s normal understanding or mental balance.
antonyms: Orient, Guide, Clarify, Steady, Reassure
synonyms: Disorient, Confuse, Bewilder, Baffle, Perplex, Unsettle
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کي رخ يا طرف جي سڃاڻپ وڃرائڻ، ڪنهن کي جاءِ وقت يا صورتحال بابت منجهائڻ، عام سمجهه يا ذهني توازن بگاڙڻ
examples: The maze was designed to disorientate visitors. Bright lights can disorientate a tired driver. The sudden change in routine may disorientate some patients. The spinning ride began to disorientate me.
urduMeaning: کسی کو سمت کا احساس کھو دینے پر مجبور کرنا، کسی کو جگہ وقت یا صورتِ حال کے بارے میں الجھانا، معمول کی سمجھ یا ذہنی توازن کو بگاڑنا

antonyms: Oriented, Alert, Clear-headed, Composed, Certain
synonyms: Confused, Bewildered, Lost, Dazed, Perplexed, Unsettled
urduMeaning: اپنی جگہ یا سمت پہچاننے سے قاصر، وقت مقام حالات یا شناخت کے بارے میں الجھا ہوا، ذہنی طور پر پریشان اور ردعمل کے بارے میں غیر یقینی
sindhiMeaning: پنهنجي جاءِ يا رخ سڃاڻڻ کان لاچار، وقت هنڌ حالت يا سڃاڻپ بابت منجهيل، ذهني طور پريشان ۽ ردعمل بابت اڻپڪ
englishMeaning: Unable to recognize one’s location or direction. Confused about time, place, circumstances, or identity. Mentally unsettled and unsure how to respond.
examples: I felt disorientated when I woke in the unfamiliar room. The injured hiker was cold and disorientated. She became disorientated after walking through the crowded station. Jet lag left him tired and disorientated.

englishMeaning: To cause someone to lose their sense of direction. To confuse someone about time, place, identity, or circumstances. To unsettle or disturb a person mentally.
antonyms: Orient, Direct, Guide, Clarify, Reassure
urduMeaning: کسی کا سمت پہچاننے کا احساس ختم کرنا، وقت مقام شناخت یا حالات کے بارے میں الجھانا، ذہنی طور پر پریشان یا بے چین کرنا
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن جو رخ سڃاڻڻ وارو احساس وڃائڻ، وقت هنڌ سڃاڻپ يا حالتن بابت منجهائڻ، ذهني طور پريشان يا بيقرار ڪرڻ
examples: The identical corridors can disorient new visitors. A loud explosion may temporarily disorient people nearby. The misleading signs disoriented the tourists. Waking suddenly in darkness can disorient anyone.
synonyms: Confuse, Bewilder, Daze, Perplex, Unsettle, Mislead

englishMeaning: A loss of the sense of direction. Confusion about time, place, identity, or circumstances. A temporary state of mental uncertainty or bewilderment. A disturbance of normal spatial awareness.
synonyms: Confusion, Bewilderment, Dizziness, Perplexity, Uncertainty, Daze
examples: The patient experienced brief disorientation after surgery. Thick fog caused disorientation among the hikers. He felt a sense of disorientation in the unfamiliar city. Memory loss and disorientation can require medical attention.
urduMeaning: سمت کے احساس کا کھو جانا، وقت مقام شناخت یا حالات کے بارے میں الجھن، ذہنی بے یقینی یا حیرانی کی عارضی حالت، مکانی شعور میں خلل
sindhiMeaning: رخ جي سڃاڻپ وڃائڻ، وقت هنڌ سڃاڻپ يا حالتن بابت مونجهارو، ذهني اڻپڪ يا حيراني جي عارضي حالت، جاءِ جي عام شعور ۾ خلل
antonyms: Orientation, Clarity, Awareness, Certainty, Composure

examples: Her disparagement of her colleagues damaged team morale. The article contained an unfair disparagement of local artists. He objected to the constant disparagement of his work. Constructive criticism should not become personal disparagement.
englishMeaning: The act of speaking about someone or something in a disrespectful or belittling way. A remark that lowers someone’s reputation or value. Unfair criticism that presents something as inferior or unimportant.
synonyms: Belittlement, Denigration, Depreciation, Slander, Insult, Criticism
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن يا ڪنهن شيءِ بابت بي عزتي يا گهٽتائي سان ڳالهائڻ، شهرت يا قدر گهٽائيندڙ ڳالهه، ڪنهن شيءِ کي گهٽ يا بي اهميت ڏيکاريندڙ ناجائز تنقيد
antonyms: Praise, Compliment, Approval, Admiration, Appreciation, Respect
urduMeaning: کسی شخص یا چیز کے بارے میں توہین آمیز یا حقیر انداز میں بات کرنا، شہرت یا قدر گھٹانے والی بات، کسی چیز کو کمتر یا غیر اہم دکھانے والی غیر منصفانہ تنقید

englishMeaning: In a way that shows little respect for someone or something. In a manner intended to belittle, criticize, or make something seem unimportant. Scornfully or contemptuously.
examples: She spoke disparagingly about her former employer. He referred disparagingly to the opposing team. The critic wrote disparagingly of the new exhibition. They should not speak disparagingly about people’s accents.
synonyms: Scornfully, Contemptuously, Derisively, Dismissively, Critically, Mockingly
urduMeaning: بے عزتی یا حقارت ظاہر کرنے والے انداز میں، کمتر یا غیر اہم دکھانے کے طریقے سے، تحقیر یا نفرت کے ساتھ
antonyms: Respectfully, Admiringly, Favorably, Appreciatively, Praisingly
sindhiMeaning: بي عزتي يا گهٽتائي ڏيکاريندڙ نمونو، گهٽ سمجهڻ يا بي اهميت بڻائڻ واري انداز ۾، حقارت يا نفرت سان

synonyms: Automatic-cleaning, Maintenance-free, Dirt-resistant, Easy-clean
englishMeaning: Able to remove dirt or unwanted material automatically. Designed so that it requires little or no manual cleaning. Capable of cleaning itself through a special surface, mechanism, or cycle.
examples: The oven has a self-cleaning cycle. We installed self-cleaning glass in the roof. This fabric has a self-cleaning coating. Self-cleaning filters reduce routine maintenance.
urduMeaning: خودکار طور پر میل یا غیر ضروری مادہ ہٹانے کے قابل، اس طرح تیار کیا گیا کہ ہاتھ سے بہت کم یا کوئی صفائی نہ چاہیے، خاص سطح نظام یا چکر کے ذریعے خود صاف ہونے والا
sindhiMeaning: پاڻمرادو گند يا اڻ گهربل مواد هٽائڻ جي قابل، اهڙي نموني ٺهيل جو هٿ سان ٿوري يا ڪا صفائي نه گهرجي، خاص سطح نظام يا چڪر سان پاڻ صاف ٿيندڙ
antonyms: Manually cleaned, High-maintenance, Dirt-retaining

examples: She is a Belizean writer living abroad. We enjoyed several Belizean dishes during our visit. The Belizean guide explained the history of the ruins. Many Belizeans speak more than one language.
englishMeaning: Relating to Belize, its people, culture, or language. A person who is a citizen or native of Belize.
urduMeaning: ملک بیلیز اس کے لوگوں ثقافت یا زبان سے متعلق، بیلیز کا شہری یا مقامی باشندہ
synonyms: Citizen of Belize, Native of Belize, Belizian
antonyms: No direct antonym
sindhiMeaning: بيلز ملڪ ان جي ماڻهن ثقافت يا ٻولي سان لاڳاپيل، بيلز جو شهري يا اصل رهواسي

synonyms: Fill the bases, Put runners on every base, Set the stage, Prepare the ground
englishMeaning: In baseball, to put a runner on first, second, and third base at the same time. To create a situation in which all three bases are occupied. Informally, to arrange several favorable conditions or resources before taking action.
examples: A walk in the eighth inning loaded the bases. The team managed to load the bases with only one out. The pitcher remained calm after the opponents loaded the bases. The campaign loaded the bases by securing money, volunteers, and endorsements.
urduMeaning: بیس بال میں پہلی دوسری اور تیسری بیس پر بیک وقت کھلاڑی موجود کرنا، تینوں بیس بھر دینا، غیر رسمی طور پر عمل سے پہلے کئی سازگار حالات یا وسائل تیار کرنا
sindhiMeaning: بيس بال ۾ پهرين ٻي ۽ ٽين بيس تي هڪ ئي وقت رانديگر بيهارڻ، ٽئي بيس ڀريل ڪرڻ، غير رسمي طور عمل کان اڳ گهڻيون سازگار حالتون يا وسيلا تيار ڪرڻ
antonyms: Clear the bases, Empty the bases, Leave the bases unoccupied

examples: An arborist inspected the damaged oak tree. We hired a certified arborist to prune the branches safely. The arborist diagnosed a fungal disease in the tree. She trained as an arborist after studying forestry.
urduMeaning: درختوں کی دیکھ بھال اور نگہداشت کا تربیت یافتہ ماہر، درخت لگانے تراشنے بیماری پہچاننے اور علاج کرنے والا پیشہ ور، درختوں کی حفاظت اور انتظام کا ماہر
synonyms: Tree surgeon, Tree-care specialist, Arboriculturist, Tree expert
antonyms: No direct antonym
englishMeaning: A specialist trained in the care and maintenance of trees. A professional who plants, prunes, diagnoses, and treats trees and woody plants. An expert in tree safety and management.
sindhiMeaning: وڻن جي سنڀال ۽ سار سنڀال جو تربيت يافته ماهر، وڻ پوکڻ ڇانگڻ بيماري سڃاڻڻ ۽ علاج ڪرڻ وارو پيشه ور، وڻن جي حفاظت ۽ انتظام جو ماهر

synonyms: Fan, Devotee, Aficionado, Admirer, Hobbyist, Supporter, Buff
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن سرگرمي يا موضوع ۾ تمام گهڻي دلچسپي رکندڙ ماڻهو، شوق ۽ خوشي سان دلچسپي جي پيروي ڪندڙ، ڪنهن شيءِ جو پرجوش مداح يا حمايتي
examples: He is a photography enthusiast who travels widely. Car enthusiasts gathered for the annual show. As a history enthusiast, she visits many museums. The club welcomes beginners as well as experienced enthusiasts.
urduMeaning: کسی سرگرمی یا موضوع میں بہت زیادہ دلچسپی رکھنے والا شخص، شوق اور خوشی سے دلچسپی کی پیروی کرنے والا، کسی چیز کا پُرجوش مداح یا حامی
englishMeaning: A person who is highly interested in a particular activity or subject. Someone who pursues an interest with strong excitement and enjoyment. An eager admirer or supporter of something.
antonyms: Critic, Opponent, Detractor, Skeptic, Indifferent person
Professional, Expert, Specialist, Practitioner
englishMeaning: A person who regularly does an activity for pleasure rather than as a profession. An amateur with a strong interest in a particular craft, subject, or pastime. Someone who practices a skill in their free time.
sindhiMeaning: پيشي بدران خوشي لاءِ باقاعده سرگرمي ڪندڙ ماڻهو، ڪنهن هنر موضوع يا وندر ۾ گهري دلچسپي رکندڙ شوقين، واندڪائي ۾ مهارت آزمائيندڙ
examples: The camera is affordable enough for a hobbyist. A local gardening hobbyist won the flower competition. The workshop attracts both professionals and hobbyists. He began as a hobbyist before becoming a full-time carpenter.
urduMeaning: پیشے کے بجائے خوشی کے لیے باقاعدگی سے سرگرمی کرنے والا شخص، کسی ہنر موضوع یا مشغلے میں گہری دلچسپی رکھنے والا شوقین، فارغ وقت میں مہارت آزمانے والا
synonyms: Amateur, Enthusiast, Dabbler, Fan, Aficionado, Nonprofessional
Hereditarily, Inheritedly, Genomically, Biologically
urduMeaning: جینس یا وراثت سے متعلق انداز میں، حیاتیاتی والدین یا آباؤ اجداد سے ورثے میں، جینیاتی مادے کی تبدیلی یا تجزیے کے ذریعے
examples: The twins are genetically identical. Some diseases are genetically inherited. The crops were genetically modified to resist pests. The two populations are genetically distinct.
sindhiMeaning: جينس يا وراثت سان لاڳاپيل نموني، حياتياتي والدين يا ابن ڏاڏن کان ورثي ۾، جينياتي مواد جي تبديلي يا جاچ ذريعي
englishMeaning: In a way that relates to genes or heredity. By inheritance from biological parents or ancestors. Through alteration or analysis of genetic material.
antonyms: Environmentally, Acquiredly, Nongenetically

synonyms: Pastime, Recreation, Leisure activity, Pursuit, Interest, Diversion
sindhiMeaning: واندڪائي ۾ خوشي لاءِ باقاعده ڪيل سرگرمي، پگهار واري ڪم بدران دلچسپي لاءِ ڪيل مشغلو، آرام يا ذاتي واڌ لاءِ وڻندڙ وندر
examples: Gardening is her favorite hobby. He turned his photography hobby into a career. A relaxing hobby can reduce stress. My hobbies include reading, cycling, and cooking.
antonyms: Work, Profession, Occupation, Chore, Duty
englishMeaning: An activity done regularly for pleasure during one’s free time. A subject or pursuit followed for interest rather than as paid work. An enjoyable pastime used for relaxation or personal development.
urduMeaning: فارغ وقت میں خوشی کے لیے باقاعدگی سے کی جانے والی سرگرمی، معاوضہ والے کام کے بجائے دلچسپی سے کیا جانے والا مشغلہ، آرام یا ذاتی ترقی کے لیے پسندیدہ سرگرمی

antonyms: Firm, Strong, Forceful, Decisive, Resolute
englishMeaning: Having a wrist that is bent, loose, or lacking firmness. Weak, indecisive, or lacking force. Sometimes used as an offensive stereotype about an effeminate man and therefore best avoided when referring to people.
sindhiMeaning: ڍري مڙيل يا بي طاقت ڪرائي وارو، ڪمزور اڻفيصلائتو يا زور کان خالي، ڪڏهن عورتاڻن مردن لاءِ توهين آميز تصور طور استعمال ٿيندڙ تنهنڪري ماڻهن لاءِ استعمال کان پاسو ڪرڻ گهرجي
examples: The dancer avoided a limp-wristed pose by holding her hands firmly. Critics described the response as limp-wristed and ineffective. His limp-wristed handshake suggested nervousness. The term can be offensive when used to describe a person’s manner.
synonyms: Weak, Feeble, Flaccid, Ineffectual, Indecisive, Spineless
urduMeaning: ڈھیلی مڑی ہوئی یا بے طاقت کلائی والا، کمزور غیر فیصلہ کن یا زور سے خالی، کبھی زنانہ انداز والے مرد کے لیے توہین آمیز دقیانوسی لفظ اس لیے لوگوں کے لیے استعمال سے گریز بہتر ہے
کمزور ڈھیلے یا بے جان انداز میں، مضبوطی توانائی یا مزاحمت کے بغیر، بے طاقت لٹکنے یا حرکت کرنے کے انداز میں
synonyms: Weakly, Slackly, Flaccidly, Feebly, Lifelessly, Listlessly
examples: His injured arm hung limply at his side. The wet flag drooped limply from the pole. She sank limply into the chair after the race. He shook my hand limply and looked away.
englishMeaning: In a weak, loose, or lifeless way. Without firmness, energy, or resistance. In a manner that hangs or moves without strength.
sindhiMeaning: ڪمزور ڍري يا بي جان نموني، مضبوطي توانائي يا مزاحمت کان سواءِ، بنا طاقت لڙڪندڙ يا هلندڙ انداز ۾
antonyms: Firmly, Strongly, Stiffly, Energetically, Vigorously

sindhiMeaning: هيٺاهين مخروطي خول وارو ننڍو سامونڊي جاندار جيڪو پٿرن سان مضبوطيءَ سان چنبڙي ٿو، ڪنهن سان سدائين لڳل ۽ جدا ڪرڻ ڏکيو ماڻهو، سطح سان مضبوط چنبڙندڙ شيءِ
examples: A limpet clung to the rock below the waterline. The child held on to her mother like a limpet. We found several limpets in the tidal pool. He became a limpet at social events and never left his friend’s side.
englishMeaning: A small marine mollusk with a low cone-shaped shell that clings tightly to rocks. A person who stays very close to someone and is difficult to detach. Something that attaches itself firmly to a surface.
synonyms: Shellfish, Marine mollusk, Clinger, Barnacle, Tagalong
antonyms: Detached person, Independent person, Free-moving creature
urduMeaning: نیچے مخروطی خول والا چھوٹا سمندری جانور جو چٹان سے مضبوطی سے چمٹتا ہے، کسی کے ساتھ مسلسل لگا رہنے اور جدا کرنا مشکل شخص، سطح سے مضبوطی سے چپکنے والی چیز

جہاز کے بیرونی حصے سے مقناطیسی یا دوسرے طریقے سے چپکانے کے لیے بنایا گیا دھماکہ خیز آلہ، غوطہ خور یا اہلکار کی جانب سے براہِ راست ہدف پر لگائی گئی بحری بارودی سرنگ، دھاتی سطح سے مضبوطی سے چپکنے والا پوشیدہ دھماکہ خیز مواد
sindhiMeaning: جهاز جي ٻاهرين حصي سان مقناطيسي يا ٻي نموني چنبڙائڻ لاءِ ٺهيل ڌماڪيدار اوزار، غوطه خور يا ڪارروائي ڪندڙ طرفان سڌو هدف تي لڳايل بحري بارودي سرنگ، ڌاتو جي سطح سان مضبوط لڳندڙ لڪل ڌماڪيدار مواد
antonyms: No direct antonym
synonyms: Naval mine, Magnetic mine, Attached charge, Underwater explosive
examples: The divers searched the hull for a suspected limpet mine. A limpet mine can be attached below a ship’s waterline. The navy trained crews to detect and remove limpet mines. Investigators found evidence of a limpet mine on the damaged vessel.
englishMeaning: An explosive device designed to attach magnetically or otherwise to the hull of a ship. A naval mine placed directly on a target by a diver or operative. A concealed charge that adheres firmly to a metal surface.

antonyms: Compact car, Economy car, Utility vehicle
sindhiMeaning: وڏي شاندار ڪار جيڪا اڪثر ڊرائيور هلائي، خاص موقعن يا اهم مسافرن لاءِ ڊگهي رسمي گاڏي، تاريخي طور ڊرائيور کان جدا بند مسافر خانو رکندڙ گاڏي
englishMeaning: A large luxurious car, often driven by a chauffeur. A long formal vehicle used for special events or important passengers. Historically, a closed passenger compartment separated from the driver.
examples: A limousine waited outside the hotel. They hired a limousine for the wedding. The actor arrived at the theater in a black limousine. A chauffeur opened the limousine door for the guests.
urduMeaning: بڑی پُرتعیش کار جسے اکثر ڈرائیور چلاتا ہے، خاص تقریبات یا اہم مسافروں کے لیے لمبی رسمی گاڑی، تاریخی طور پر ڈرائیور سے الگ بند مسافر خانہ رکھنے والی گاڑی
synonyms: Limo, Luxury car, Chauffeured car, Executive car, Formal car

examples: The wedding party arrived in a stretch limo. They rented a stretch limo for the school dance. A white stretch limo was parked outside the venue. The stretch limo had enough room for ten passengers.
synonyms: Stretched limousine, Extended limousine, Long limo, Luxury vehicle
sindhiMeaning: عام ڪار جو ڍانچو ڊگهو ڪري ٺاهيل تمام ڊگهي ليموزين، وڌيڪ مسافر جاءِ واري ڊرائيور هلائيندڙ شاندار گاڏي، جشنن ۽ رسمي موقعن لاءِ ڪرائي تي ورتل ڊگهي گاڏي
urduMeaning: عام کار کا ڈھانچا لمبا کر کے بنائی گئی بہت طویل لیموزین، زیادہ مسافر جگہ والی ڈرائیور کے ذریعے چلائی جانے والی پُرتعیش گاڑی، تقریبات اور رسمی مواقع کے لیے کرائے پر لی جانے والی لمبی گاڑی
englishMeaning: An extra-long limousine created by extending the body of a standard car. A chauffeur-driven luxury vehicle with additional passenger space. A long vehicle commonly hired for celebrations and formal events.
antonyms: Compact car, Standard car, Short-wheelbase vehicle

synonyms: Extend, Lengthen, Spread out, Lie down, Reach out, Unfold
urduMeaning: جسم یا اعضا پوری طرح پھیلانا عموماً آرام یا ورزش کے لیے، پوری لمبائی سے آرام دہ لیٹنا، کھینچ کر کسی چیز کو لمبا یا چوڑا کرنا، زیادہ فاصلے یا مدت تک جاری رہنا یا پھیلنا، ہاتھ یا بازو آگے بڑھانا
examples: Stretch out your legs after the long journey. She stretched out on the sofa and fell asleep. The road stretches out across the desert. He stretched out his hand to catch the ball.
sindhiMeaning: جسم يا عضوا پوريءَ طرح ڊگها ڪرڻ اڪثر آرام يا ورزش لاءِ، پوري ڊيگهه سان آرام سان ليٽڻ، ڇڪڻ سان شيءِ ڊگهي يا ويڪري ڪرڻ، وڌيڪ فاصلي يا مدت تائين جاري يا پکڙجڻ، هٿ يا ٻانهن اڳتي وڌائڻ
englishMeaning: To extend the body or limbs fully, often to relax or exercise. To lie down comfortably at full length. To make something longer or wider by pulling it. To continue or spread over a longer distance or period. To extend a hand or arm toward something.
antonyms: Contract, Shorten, Curl up, Fold, Retract

synonyms: Elastic, Flexible, Resilient, Supple, Expandable
examples: These stretchy trousers are comfortable for traveling. The bandage is soft and stretchy. Choose a stretchy fabric for the costume. That is a rather stretchy interpretation of the rule.
englishMeaning: Able to stretch easily and return toward its original shape. Made from flexible or elastic material. Informally, capable of being interpreted or extended beyond usual limits.
antonyms: Rigid, Stiff, Inelastic, Brittle, Unyielding
sindhiMeaning: آسانيءَ سان ڇڪجڻ ۽ وري اصل شڪل ڏانهن موٽڻ جي قابل، لچڪدار يا الاسٽڪ مواد مان ٺهيل، غير رسمي طور معمولي حدن کان وڌيڪ تشريح يا وڌاءَ جي قابل
urduMeaning: آسانی سے کھنچنے اور پھر اصل شکل کی طرف لوٹنے کے قابل، لچکدار یا الاسٹک مواد سے بنا ہوا، غیر رسمی طور پر عام حدود سے زیادہ تشریح یا توسیع کے قابل

synonyms: Striae, Skin streaks, Linear scars, Striae distensae
examples: She developed stretch marks during pregnancy. Rapid growth can cause stretch marks in teenagers. The lotion may soften the appearance of stretch marks. Stretch marks often fade gradually over time.
urduMeaning: جلد کے تیزی سے کھنچنے یا سکڑنے سے بننے والی لمبی باریک لکیریں، حمل نشوونما وزن کی تبدیلی یا پٹھے بڑھنے سے وابستہ داغ نما دھاریاں، جلد کے معاون بافت میں تبدیلی سے بننے والے نشان
englishMeaning: Long narrow lines that form on the skin when it stretches or shrinks quickly. Scar-like streaks commonly associated with pregnancy, growth, weight change, or muscle gain. Marks caused by changes in the skin’s supportive tissue.
sindhiMeaning: چمڙي تي تيزيءَ سان ڇڪجڻ يا سُڪڙجڻ سبب ٺهندڙ ڊگهيون سنهيون لڪيرون، حمل واڌ وزن جي تبديلي يا عضلا وڌڻ سان لاڳاپيل داغ جهڙيون پٽيون، چمڙي جي سهاري واري بافت ۾ تبديلي سبب نشان
antonyms: Unmarked skin, Smooth skin, Even skin

examples: Two stretcher-bearers carried the injured player off the field. He served as a stretcher-bearer during the war. The stretcher-bearers moved carefully through the narrow passage. A trained stretcher-bearer checked the straps before lifting.
synonyms: Medical orderly, Casualty carrier, Rescue worker, Litter bearer
sindhiMeaning: اسٽريچر جو هڪ پاسو کڻندڙ ماڻهو اڪثر جوڙي يا ٽيم جو حصو، زخمي يا بيمار ماڻهن کي اسٽريچر تي کڻندڙ طبي يا فوجي ڪارڪن، زخمين کي محفوظ نموني منتقل ڪرڻ لاءِ مقرر بچاءُ ڪندڙ
englishMeaning: A person who carries one end of a stretcher, usually as part of a pair or team. A medical or military worker who transports injured or sick people on a stretcher. A rescuer assigned to move casualties safely.
antonyms: No direct antonym
urduMeaning: اسٹریچر کا ایک سرا اٹھانے والا شخص عموماً جوڑی یا ٹیم کا حصہ، زخمی یا بیمار افراد کو اسٹریچر پر منتقل کرنے والا طبی یا فوجی کارکن، زخمیوں کو محفوظ انداز میں لے جانے والا امدادی کارکن

examples: The old cinema still retains a sense of glamour. Travel magazines often emphasize the glamour of distant cities. She brought elegance and glamour to the event. The job involves hard work despite its public glamour.
synonyms: Allure, Charm, Elegance, Sophistication, Enchantment, Appeal, Splendor
sindhiMeaning: حسن جوش دولت يا ڪاميابي سان لاڳاپيل پرڪشش خوبي، دلڪش ۽ اڪثر مثالي ڪشش جيڪا ماڻهو جاءِ يا سرگرمي کي خاص ڏيکاري، نفيس سونهن ۽ شان، تاريخي طور جادو يا طلسم
antonyms: Dullness, Plainness, Drabness, Ugliness, Ordinariness
urduMeaning: حسن جوش دولت یا کامیابی سے وابستہ پُرکشش خوبی، دلکش اور اکثر مثالی کشش جو کسی شخص مقام یا سرگرمی کو خاص دکھائے، نفیس خوبصورتی اور شان، تاریخی طور پر جادو یا طلسم
englishMeaning: An attractive quality associated with beauty, excitement, wealth, or success. A charming and often idealized appeal that makes a person, place, or activity seem special. Stylish beauty and sophistication. Historically, a magical enchantment or spell.

antonyms: No direct antonym
englishMeaning: A portable frame used to carry a sick, injured, or unconscious person. A device or frame used to stretch, support, or shape something. A wooden frame over which an artist’s canvas is stretched. A brick laid with its long side visible in a wall.
urduMeaning: بیمار زخمی یا بے ہوش شخص کو اٹھانے کے لیے قابلِ حمل چارپائی نما فریم، کسی چیز کو کھینچنے سہارا دینے یا شکل دینے والا آلہ یا چوکھٹا، مصور کا کینوس کھینچنے والا لکڑی کا فریم، دیوار میں لمبا رخ نمایاں رکھ کر لگائی گئی اینٹ
examples: Paramedics placed the injured cyclist on a stretcher. The canvas was secured to a wooden stretcher. The rescue team carried a folding stretcher. Each stretcher in the brick wall was carefully aligned.
sindhiMeaning: بيمار زخمي يا بيهوش ماڻهو کڻڻ لاءِ هلڪو کٽ جهڙو ڍانچو، ڪنهن شيءِ کي ڇڪڻ سهارو ڏيڻ يا شڪل ڏيڻ وارو اوزار يا فريم، مصور جي ڪينواس ڇڪڻ لاءِ ڪاٺ جو فريم، ڀت ۾ ڊگهو پاسو ظاهر ڪري رکيل سر
synonyms: Litter, Gurney, Carrying frame, Canvas frame, Stretcher brick

urduMeaning: کسی خاص جگہ نقطے مقدار یا وقت تک پھیلنا، مقرر مقصد یا مقدار کے لیے کافی ہونا، مشکل سطح تک پہنچنے یا حاصل کرنے کی کوشش کرنا، کسی اصول معنی یا وسیلے کو کچھ شامل کرنے کے لیے وسعت دینا
englishMeaning: To extend as far as a particular place, point, amount, or time. To be sufficient for a specified purpose or quantity. To make an effort to reach or achieve a demanding level. To broaden a rule, meaning, or resource to include something.
antonyms: Fall short of, Stop before, Contract from, Exclude
synonyms: Extend to, Reach, Run to, Suffice for, Expand to
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن خاص جاءِ نقطي مقدار يا وقت تائين پکڙجڻ، مقرر مقصد يا مقدار لاءِ ڪافي ٿيڻ، ڏکئي سطح تائين پهچڻ يا حاصل ڪرڻ جي ڪوشش ڪرڻ، ضابطي معنيٰ يا وسيلي کي ڪجهه شامل ڪرڻ لاءِ وڌائڻ
examples: The forest stretches to the edge of the lake. Our budget will not stretch to a luxury hotel. She had to stretch to reach the top shelf. That interpretation stretches the rule to its limit.

antonyms: Withdraw from, Recoil from, Give up on, Avoid
urduMeaning: کسی چیز کو پکڑنے یا چھونے کے لیے آگے ہاتھ بڑھانا، کسی چیز کے حصول کی کوشش میں جسم یا عضو کو پھیلانا، مشکل مقصد کے حصول کے لیے جدوجہد کرنا
englishMeaning: To reach out toward something one wants to take or touch. To extend the body or a limb in an attempt to obtain something. To strive for a goal that is difficult to achieve.
examples: The baby stretched for the bright toy. She stretched for the handle above the door. He stretched for the final note but missed it. The young athlete continues to stretch for excellence.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ کي وٺڻ يا ڇهڻ لاءِ اڳتي هٿ وڌائڻ، شيءِ حاصل ڪرڻ جي ڪوشش ۾ جسم يا عضوو ڊگهو ڪرڻ، حاصل ڪرڻ ڏکئي مقصد لاءِ جاکوڙڻ
synonyms: Reach for, Extend toward, Grasp for, Strive for, Aim for

sindhiMeaning: پري فاصلي تائين لڳاتار پکڙجڻ، هڪ نقطي کان وسيع علائقي ۾ ڦهلجڻ، نظر کان پري ٿيندي ڊگهو ۽ اڻٽٽ ڏسڻ ۾ اچڻ
examples: Green fields stretch away toward the mountains. The empty road stretched away into the mist. Sand dunes stretch away in every direction. From the tower, the city seemed to stretch away forever.
synonyms: Extend, Spread out, Reach into the distance, Run on, Continue
englishMeaning: To extend continuously into the distance. To spread from a point across a wide area. To appear long and uninterrupted as it recedes from view.
antonyms: End nearby, Stop abruptly, Contract, Shorten
urduMeaning: دور فاصلے تک مسلسل پھیلنا، ایک نقطے سے وسیع علاقے میں پھیل جانا، نظر سے دور ہوتے ہوئے لمبا اور بلا رکاوٹ دکھائی دینا

synonyms: Restrict to, Confine to, Cap at, Reduce to, Keep to
englishMeaning: To restrict someone or something to a particular amount, number, place, group, or activity. To allow only a specified range or choice. To confine the effect, discussion, or use of something to a stated boundary.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ماڻهو يا شيءِ کي خاص مقدار انگ جاءِ گروهه يا سرگرمي تائين محدود ڪرڻ، رڳو مقرر دائري يا چونڊ جي اجازت ڏيڻ، اثر بحث يا استعمال کي ڄاڻايل حد اندر رکڻ
examples: Please limit your answer to two paragraphs. The offer is limited to new customers. We should limit the discussion to relevant facts. Doctors advised him to limit himself to light exercise.
urduMeaning: کسی شخص یا چیز کو خاص مقدار تعداد جگہ گروہ یا سرگرمی تک محدود کرنا، صرف مقرر دائرے یا انتخاب کی اجازت دینا، اثر بحث یا استعمال کو بیان کردہ حد کے اندر رکھنا
antonyms: Expand to, Extend beyond, Broaden, Allow freely, Unrestrict

sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ کي خاص سبب ضابطي مقدار يا شرط موجب محدود ڪرڻ، ڪنهن سبب ڪري ماڻهو يا شيءِ جي آزادي دائري يا سگهه گهٽائڻ، مقرر پابندي ذريعي حد طئي ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: کسی چیز کو خاص عامل اصول مقدار یا شرط کے مطابق محدود کرنا، کسی سبب سے شخص یا چیز کی آزادی دائرہ یا صلاحیت کم کرنا، مقرر پابندی کے ذریعے حد متعین کرنا
examples: Production is limited by the available supply of water. The project was limited by a small budget. Our choices are limited by time and distance. Growth may be limited by poor soil conditions.
englishMeaning: To restrict something according to a particular factor, rule, amount, or condition. To cause a person or thing to have less freedom, scope, or capacity because of something. To determine a boundary through a specified constraint.
synonyms: Restrict by, Constrain by, Bound by, Cap through, Hamper by
antonyms: Enable by, Expand through, Free from, Unrestrict, Enhance by

synonyms: Charm, Allure, Appeal, Enchantment, Fascination, Elegance, Splendor, Mystique, Glitz, Romanticize
englishMeaning: An attractive or exciting quality that makes someone or something seem special or desirable. Charm created by beauty, luxury, fame, fashion, or mystery. A deceptively appealing appearance that can hide ordinary or unpleasant reality. To make something appear more attractive or romantic than it really is. An archaic enchantment or magic spell.
urduMeaning: دلکشی یا کشش، حسن شہرت یا آسائش سے پیدا ہونے والا سحر، کسی چیز کو حقیقت سے زیادہ خوبصورت یا پرکشش دکھانا، ظاہری چمک دمک جو حقیقت کو چھپا دے، قدیم جادو یا طلسم
examples: The glamor of the film industry attracts many young performers. Travel magazines often add glamor to ordinary destinations. The old theater retains the glamor of a bygone age. Advertisers glamor the product with elegant photography.
sindhiMeaning: دلڪشي يا ڪشش، حسن شهرت يا عيش سبب پيدا ٿيندڙ موهيندڙ اثر، ڪنهن شيءِ کي حقيقت کان وڌيڪ خوبصورت يا پرڪشش ڏيکارڻ، ظاهري چمڪ دمڪ جيڪا حقيقت لڪائي، پراڻو جادوي اثر يا منڊ
antonyms: Dullness, Plainness, Ugliness, Drabness, Reality, Ordinariness, Repulsiveness

examples: She wore a glamorous silver dress to the ceremony. The job sounds glamorous, but it involves long hours. They spent a glamorous weekend at a seaside resort. Old photographs show the glamorous side of city life.
sindhiMeaning: دلڪش ۽ حسين، شان شوڪت وارو، عيش ۽ شهرت سان لاڳاپيل، عام حقيقت کان وڌيڪ پرڪشش نظر ايندڙ، نفاست ۽ وقار سان ڀرپور
synonyms: Attractive, Alluring, Elegant, Chic, Dazzling, Luxurious, Stylish, Sophisticated, Prestigious
antonyms: Plain, Dull, Drab, Unattractive, Ordinary, Unfashionable, Shabby
urduMeaning: دلکش اور حسین، شان و شوکت والا، آسائش اور شہرت سے وابستہ، روزمرہ حقیقت سے زیادہ پرکشش نظر آنے والا، نفاست اور وقار سے بھرپور
englishMeaning: Possessing exciting beauty, charm, elegance, or attractiveness. Associated with luxury, fame, fashion, or a desirable lifestyle. Appearing more appealing or romantic than everyday reality. Full of sophistication, spectacle, or prestige.

urduMeaning: دلکش انداز میں، شان و شوکت اور نفاست کے ساتھ، آسائش یا فیشن والے طریقے سے، کسی چیز کو حقیقت سے زیادہ پرکشش انداز میں پیش کرتے ہوئے
englishMeaning: In an attractive, elegant, exciting, or sophisticated manner. In a way associated with luxury, fame, fashion, or prestige. In a manner that makes something seem more appealing or romantic than it really is.
antonyms: Plainly, Dully, Drably, Shabbily, Unattractively, Simply
synonyms: Elegantly, Stylishly, Attractively, Luxuriously, Dazzlingly, Sophisticatedly
examples: She dressed glamorously for the evening reception. The hotel was glamorously decorated for the awards night. The magazine portrayed city life glamorously. He arrived glamorously in a classic car.
sindhiMeaning: دلڪش نموني سان، شان شوڪت ۽ نفاست سان، عيش يا فيشن واري انداز ۾، ڪنهن شيءِ کي حقيقت کان وڌيڪ پرڪشش نموني پيش ڪندي

urduMeaning: کسی شخص کام یا حالت کو حقیقت سے زیادہ دلکش یا دلچسپ دکھانا، مثالی یا رومانوی انداز میں پیش کرنا، خطرات یا مشکلات چھپا کر صرف خوش نما پہلو نمایاں کرنا
synonyms: Idealize, Romanticize, Beautify, Embellish, Exalt, Adorn, Enhance, Glorify
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شخص ڪم يا حالت کي حقيقت کان وڌيڪ دلڪش يا دلچسپ ڏيکارڻ، مثالي يا رومانوي انداز ۾ پيش ڪرڻ، نقصانن يا ڏکيائين کي لڪائي رڳو وڻندڙ پهلو نمايان ڪرڻ
examples: Films should not glamorize violence. The campaign glamorized life in the armed forces. Social media can glamorize unrealistic lifestyles. The novel does not glamorize poverty or hardship.
englishMeaning: To make a person, activity, or situation seem more attractive, exciting, or desirable than it truly is. To present something in an idealized, romantic, or luxurious way. To conceal risks, hardships, or unpleasant facts by emphasizing appealing features.
antonyms: Depict realistically, Devalue, Disparage, Expose, Criticize, Demystify, Tarnish

examples: The book offers a useful demystification of modern economics. Demystification of the legal process helped the families. Her lecture began the demystification of genetic testing. Good science writing encourages demystification rather than confusion.
urduMeaning: مشکل یا پراسرار موضوع کو آسان اور قابل فہم بنانے کا عمل، غلط فہمیوں رازوں یا پیچیدگیوں کو واضح تشریح سے دور کرنا، خوفناک نظر آنے والی بات کی اصل حقیقت ظاہر ہونا
sindhiMeaning: ڏکئي يا پراسرار موضوع کي آسان ۽ سمجهڻ جهڙو بڻائڻ جو عمل، غلط فهمين رازن يا پيچيدگين کي صاف وضاحت سان ختم ڪرڻ، ڪنهن خوفناڪ لڳندڙ ڳالهه جي اصل حقيقت پڌري ٿيڻ
synonyms: Clarification, Explanation, Simplification, Elucidation, Illumination, Interpretation, Disclosure
antonyms: Mystification, Confusion, Obscurity, Complication, Concealment, Bewilderment
englishMeaning: The act or process of making something difficult, mysterious, or confusing easier to understand. A clear explanation that removes secrecy, misconceptions, or unnecessary complexity. The exposure of the ordinary reality behind an intimidating subject.

antonyms: Wisdom, Sense, Intelligence, Seriousness, Substance, Meaning, Profundity
urduMeaning: بے وقوف یا بے معنی ہونے کی حالت، بے مقصد اور کھوکھلی بات، احمقانہ یا معمولی قول عمل یا خیال، سنجیدہ سوچ اور قدر کی کمی
sindhiMeaning: بيوقوفي يا بي معنيٰ هجڻ جي حالت، بي مقصد ۽ خالي ڳالهه، احمقاڻو يا معمولي قول عمل يا خيال، سنجيده سوچ ۽ قدر جي کوٽ
englishMeaning: The quality of being silly, empty, pointless, or lacking sense. A foolish, trivial, or meaningless remark, action, or idea. Intellectual emptiness or a lack of serious thought or value.
synonyms: Foolishness, Silliness, Absurdity, Nonsense, Emptiness, Stupidity, Triviality, Vacuity
examples: She was tired of the inanity of the conversation. The article exposed the inanity of the proposal. Viewers complained about the program's endless inanity. His remark was an inanity that added nothing to the debate.

antonyms: Wisely, Sensibly, Intelligently, Meaningfully, Thoughtfully, Purposefully
sindhiMeaning: بيوقوفي سان، بي معنيٰ يا بي مقصد نموني، عقل سوچ يا وزن کان سواءِ، خالي ۽ بي خبر انداز ۾
urduMeaning: بے وقوفی سے، بے معنی یا بے مقصد انداز میں، عقل سوچ یا وزن کے بغیر، خالی اور بے خبری والے انداز میں
englishMeaning: In a silly, foolish, empty, or meaningless manner. In a way that lacks sense, purpose, substance, or intelligence. With a vacant or unthinking expression.
examples: He grinned inanely at the camera. They chatted inanely about nothing important. The character wandered inanely through the scene. She repeated the slogan inanely without questioning it.
synonyms: Foolishly, Silly, Senselessly, Mindlessly, Vacantly, Absurdly, Pointlessly

urduMeaning: احمقانہ یا بے عقل، بے معنی اور بے مقصد، اہمیت یا وزن سے خالی، سطحی معمولی اور اکتا دینے والا
antonyms: Sensible, Wise, Intelligent, Meaningful, Profound, Substantial, Thoughtful
englishMeaning: Silly, foolish, or lacking sense. Empty of meaning, purpose, substance, or value. Tediously trivial, superficial, or intellectually vacant.
examples: The meeting was delayed by several inane questions. I turned off the show because of its inane jokes. His inane response failed to address the problem. They spent an hour discussing an inane rumor.
sindhiMeaning: بيوقوفاڻو يا بي عقل، بي معنيٰ ۽ بي مقصد، اهميت يا وزن کان خالي، سطحي معمولي ۽ بور ڪندڙ
synonyms: Silly, Foolish, Senseless, Absurd, Vacuous, Empty, Trivial, Mindless, Pointless

examples: A stone is an inanimate object. The doll lay inanimate on the floor. The actor remained completely inanimate during the scene. Some languages distinguish animate nouns from inanimate nouns.
synonyms: Lifeless, Nonliving, Insentient, Motionless, Inert, Dead, Still, Unconscious
sindhiMeaning: بي جان يا غير جاندار، زندگي حرڪت يا شعور کان خالي، مئل يا مئل جهڙو، گرامر ۾ غير جاندار شين سان لاڳاپيل اسم جو درجو
urduMeaning: بے جان یا غیر جاندار، زندگی حرکت یا شعور سے خالی، مردہ یا مردہ سا، قواعد میں غیر جاندار چیزوں سے متعلق اسم کا درجہ
antonyms: Living, Animate, Alive, Sentient, Moving, Active, Conscious
englishMeaning: Not alive and having none of the qualities of living things. Showing no sign of movement, life, or consciousness. Lifeless or apparently dead. Grammatically, belonging to a noun class referring chiefly to nonliving things.

urduMeaning: محبوب عورت، وہ عورت جس سے کوئی محبت کرے، خاتون محبوبہ یا پیاری، رومانوی محبت کا مرکز بننے والی عورت خصوصاً ادبی انداز میں
synonyms: Beloved, Sweetheart, Lover, Girlfriend, Lady love, Paramour, Darling
examples: He dedicated the poem to his inamorata. The hero crossed the sea to find his inamorata. At dinner, he proudly introduced his inamorata. The old letters reveal how deeply he loved his inamorata.
englishMeaning: A woman with whom someone is in love. A female lover, sweetheart, or beloved woman. A woman who is the object of romantic affection, especially in literary or humorous use.
sindhiMeaning: محبوب عورت، اها عورت جنهن سان ڪو پيار ڪري، عورت عاشق يا پياري، رومانوي محبت جو مرڪز بڻيل عورت خاص ڪري ادبي انداز ۾
antonyms: Enemy, Rival, Adversary, Stranger, Foe

synonyms: Unwise, Imprudent, Ill-advised, Unsuitable, Risky, Inappropriate, Foolhardy
sindhiMeaning: نامناسب يا غير دانشمنداڻو، صلاح ڏيڻ جهڙو نه، خطري يا مسئلي سبب پاسو ڪرڻ لائق، حالتن موجب اڻ وڻندڙ يا غير موزون
examples: It is inadvisable to drive during the storm. Discussing private matters in public would be inadvisable. Doctors said that strenuous exercise was inadvisable for now. It may be legal, but it is still inadvisable.
urduMeaning: نامناسب یا غیر دانش مندانہ، مشورے کے قابل نہیں، خطرے یا مسئلے کی وجہ سے گریز کے لائق، حالات کے مطابق غیر موزوں
englishMeaning: Not recommended because it is unwise, unsafe, unsuitable, or likely to cause problems. Imprudent or inappropriate under the circumstances. Better avoided despite being possible or lawful.
antonyms: Advisable, Wise, Prudent, Sensible, Suitable, Recommended, Appropriate

synonyms: Accidental, Inadvertent, Unplanned, Unintended, Unwitting, Incidental, Unconscious
examples: The omission was unintentional. His unintentional joke made everyone laugh. An unintentional error changed the final total. The new rule had unintentional effects on small businesses.
urduMeaning: غیر ارادی یا انجانے میں، جان بوجھ کر نہ کیا گیا، اتفاقاً ہونے والا، بغیر منصوبے یا مقصد کے، ایسا نتیجہ جس کا ارادہ نہ ہو
sindhiMeaning: اڻ ڄاتل يا اڻ ارادي، ڄاڻي واڻي نه ڪيل، حادثاتي طور ٿيندڙ، بنا منصوبي يا مقصد جي، اهڙو نتيجو جيڪو پيدا ڪرڻ جو ارادو نه هجي
antonyms: Intentional, Deliberate, Planned, Purposeful, Willful, Conscious, Premeditated
englishMeaning: Not done deliberately or by conscious choice. Happening accidentally, inadvertently, or without a planned purpose. Causing an effect that the person did not mean to cause.

examples: The change was intentional, not a mistake. She made an intentional effort to listen carefully. Intentional practice helped him improve quickly. The novel's repetition is an intentional stylistic choice.
urduMeaning: جان بوجھ کر اور ارادے سے کیا گیا، واضح مقصد کے ساتھ منصوبہ بند، اتفاقی نہیں بلکہ سوچا سمجھا، شعوری ارادے یا فیصلے سے متعلق، فلسفے میں کسی شے کی طرف ذہنی رخ سے متعلق
synonyms: Deliberate, Purposeful, Planned, Conscious, Willful, Premeditated, Designed, Meant
sindhiMeaning: ڄاڻي واڻي ۽ ارادي سان ڪيل، واضح مقصد سان رٿيل، حادثاتي نه پر سوچيل، شعوري ارادي يا فيصلي سان لاڳاپيل، فلسفي ۾ ڪنهن شيءِ ڏانهن ذهن جي رخ سان لاڳاپيل
antonyms: Accidental, Unintentional, Inadvertent, Unplanned, Unconscious, Random
englishMeaning: Done deliberately and with a clear purpose. Planned or meant rather than accidental. Relating to a conscious aim, decision, or design. In philosophy, directed toward or representing an object.

examples: She intentionally left the final page blank. He did not intentionally hurt anyone. The designer intentionally used simple colors. They intentionally delayed the announcement until Friday.
sindhiMeaning: ڄاڻي واڻي، ارادي ۽ مقصد سان، اتفاق سان نه پر شعوري چونڊ سان، رٿيل يا قصدي نموني
synonyms: Deliberately, Purposely, Knowingly, Willfully, Consciously, Designedly, On purpose
antonyms: Accidentally, Unintentionally, Inadvertently, Unknowingly, Unconsciously, Randomly
urduMeaning: جان بوجھ کر، ارادے اور مقصد سے، اتفاقاً نہیں بلکہ شعوری انتخاب سے، منصوبہ بند یا قصداً
englishMeaning: Deliberately and with a particular aim or purpose. By conscious choice rather than by accident. In a planned, knowing, or willful manner.

antonyms: Casually, Inattentively, Distractedly, Indifferently, Carelessly, Absentmindedly
englishMeaning: With close, fixed, and concentrated attention. In an earnest, determined, or purposeful manner. With one's eyes or mind focused strongly on something.
synonyms: Attentively, Closely, Earnestly, Fixedly, Keenly, Concentratedly, Absorbedly
sindhiMeaning: گهري ڌيان سان، يڪسوئي ۽ سنجيدگي سان، اکين يا ذهن کي ڪنهن شيءِ تي مضبوط نموني مرڪوز ڪري، پڪي ارادي سان

englishMeaning: Planned, meant, or designed for a particular purpose or person. Expected or meant to happen. A person whom one plans to marry, chiefly in informal usage. Deliberately signified or implied.

synonyms: Accidentally, Inadvertently, Unwittingly, Unknowingly, Carelessly, Incidentally
examples: I unintentionally deleted the message. Her comment unintentionally embarrassed him. The policy unintentionally excluded some applicants. He unintentionally revealed the surprise.
englishMeaning: Without intending or planning to do something. Accidentally or inadvertently. In a way that produces an unforeseen or unwanted result.
antonyms: Intentionally, Deliberately, Purposely, Knowingly, Willfully, Consciously

sindhiMeaning: اڻ ڄاڻائي سان، بنا ارادي يا منصوبي جي، اتفاقي طور، اهڙي نموني جو اڻ ڏٺو يا اڻ وڻندڙ نتيجو نڪري

synonyms: Accidental, Unplanned, Unintentional, Inadvertent, Unforeseen, Unwanted, Incidental

urduMeaning: غیر منصوبہ بند یا غیر ارادی، ناپسندیدہ، اتفاقی یا غیر متوقع نتیجے کے طور پر ہونے والا، کسی اور کے لیے مقرر، ایسا مطلب جو بولنے والا ظاہر نہ کرنا چاہے
sindhiMeaning: اڻ رٿيل يا اڻ ارادي، اڻ گهربل، اتفاقي يا اڻ ڏٺل نتيجي طور ٿيندڙ، ڪنهن ٻئي لاءِ مقرر ڪيل، اهڙو مطلب جيڪو چوڻ وارو ظاهر ڪرڻ نه چاهي

antonyms: Interested, Curious, Engaged, Enthusiastic, Concerned, Attentive, Biased
englishMeaning: Not interested in or concerned about something. Showing no curiosity, attention, enthusiasm, or desire to participate. Impartial or free from personal interest, though disinterested is often preferred for this meaning.

antonyms: Boldly, Brazenly, Loudly, Immodestly, Confidently, Shamelessly, Flamboyantly
englishMeaning: In a quiet, modest, reserved, or shy manner. With a composed and decorous appearance. In an affectedly modest or coy way.
sindhiMeaning: شرميلي ۽ حيا واري انداز ۾، خاموشي ۽ سنجيدگي سان، شائستگي ۽ وقار سان، بناوٽي لڄ يا ناز سان
examples: She smiled demurely at the compliment. He sat demurely beside his grandmother. The actor lowered her eyes demurely. She answered demurely but confidently.

englishMeaning: A medium-sized nocturnal mammal native to North America, with grayish fur, a black facial mask, and a ringed tail. An adaptable animal known for dexterous front paws and scavenging near human settlements. The fur or pelt of this animal.
synonyms: Procyon, Ringtail, Coon, Masked mammal, Scavenger
examples: A raccoon searched the trash bins at midnight. We saw a raccoon beside the forest trail. The raccoon washed its food in the stream. Secure the lid so a raccoon cannot open the container.

urduMeaning: انتہائی دلچسپ اور مسحور کن، توجہ کو مضبوطی سے تھامنے والا، حسن پیچیدگی نیا پن یا راز کی وجہ سے پرکشش، طاقتور سحر یا اثر رکھنے والا
englishMeaning: Extremely interesting, attractive, or captivating. Holding attention through unusual beauty, complexity, novelty, or mystery. Exercising a powerful charm or irresistible influence.
synonyms: Captivating, Engrossing, Intriguing, Compelling, Absorbing, Enchanting, Riveting, Interesting
examples: The museum contains a fascinating collection of maps. We had a fascinating conversation about memory. It is fascinating to watch bees communicate. Her research offers a fascinating view of ancient life.
sindhiMeaning: تمام دلچسپ ۽ موهيندڙ، ڌيان کي مضبوطي سان جهلي رکندڙ، حسن پيچيدگي نواڻ يا راز سبب ڪشش وارو، طاقتور سحر يا اثر رکندڙ
گهڻو متاثر ۽ دلچسپي ورتل، ڪنهن شخص يا شيءِ ڏانهن سخت ڪشش رکندڙ، تجسس حسن يا راز سبب مڪمل ڌيان ۾ ٻڏل، ڄڻ جادو هيٺ آيل
antonyms: Bored, Uninterested, Indifferent, Repelled, Disenchanted, Unimpressed
englishMeaning: Strongly interested, attracted, or captivated by someone or something. Having one's attention completely held by curiosity, admiration, beauty, or mystery. Historically, enchanted or held as if by a spell.
examples: The children were fascinated by the magician. I am fascinated with how languages change. She watched, fascinated, as the sculpture took shape. He became fascinated by local history.
urduMeaning: بہت متاثر اور دلچسپی رکھنے والا، کسی شخص یا چیز کی طرف شدید کشش والا، تجسس حسن یا راز کے باعث پوری توجہ میں ڈوبا ہوا، گویا جادو کے زیر اثر
synonyms: Captivated, Entranced, Absorbed, Enthralled, Mesmerized, Intrigued, Spellbound, Engrossed

synonyms: Captivatingly, Intriguingly, Engagingly, Compellingly, Absorbingly, Remarkably
urduMeaning: انتہائی دلچسپ اور مسحور کن انداز میں، اس طرح کہ توجہ مضبوطی سے کھنچے، تجسس پیدا کرنے والے طریقے سے، حیرت انگیز طور پر
examples: The documentary fascinatingly connects art with science. She spoke fascinatingly about desert wildlife. The two languages are fascinatingly similar. The author fascinatingly reconstructs the lost city.
sindhiMeaning: تمام دلچسپ ۽ موهيندڙ انداز ۾، اهڙي نموني جو ڌيان مضبوطي سان ڇڪجي، تجسس پيدا ڪندڙ طريقي سان، حيرت انگيز نموني
englishMeaning: In an extremely interesting, attractive, or captivating way. In a manner that strongly holds attention or arouses curiosity. Remarkably or intriguingly.

antonyms: Healthy fascia, Absence of inflammation, Normal tissue
englishMeaning: Inflammation of fascia, the connective tissue surrounding muscles, blood vessels, nerves, and other structures. A painful inflammatory condition that may result from strain, injury, infection, or disease. A general medical term used in specific conditions such as plantar fasciitis.
sindhiMeaning: فاشيا يعني عضلن رڳن ۽ اعصاب کي ڍڪيندڙ ڳنڍيندڙ ٽشو جي سوزش، ڇڪ زخم انفيڪشن يا بيماري سبب ٿيندڙ تڪليف ڏيندڙ حالت، پلانٽر فاشيائٽس جهڙين حالتن لاءِ طبي اصطلاح
examples: The runner developed fasciitis after months of overtraining. Rest and stretching may help some forms of fasciitis. The doctor examined her foot for signs of fasciitis. Severe fasciitis requires prompt medical assessment.
synonyms: Fascial inflammation, Inflammation of fascia, Plantar fasciitis, Connective-tissue inflammation
urduMeaning: فاشیا یعنی پٹھوں رگوں اور اعصاب کو ڈھانپنے والے جوڑنے والے ٹشو کی سوزش، کھنچاؤ چوٹ انفیکشن یا بیماری سے ہونے والی دردناک حالت، پلانٹر فیشیائٹس جیسی حالتوں کے لیے طبی اصطلاح

synonyms: Flesh-eating disease, Necrotizing soft-tissue infection, NSTI, Fascial necrosis
examples: Doctors diagnosed necrotizing fasciitis and began emergency treatment. Severe pain and rapidly spreading swelling can signal necrotizing fasciitis. Surgery is often necessary to control necrotizing fasciitis. Early recognition of necrotizing fasciitis can save a patient's life.

sindhiMeaning: تيزي سان پکڙجندڙ ناياب بيڪٽيريائي انفيڪشن جيڪا فاشيا ۽ ڀرپاسي جي نرم ٽشو کي تباهه ڪري، جان لاءِ خطري واري هنگامي بيماري جنهن کي گوشت کائيندڙ بيماري به چوندا آھن، فوري اسپتال علاج اينٽي بايوٽڪ ۽ اڪثر آپريشن گهرجندڙ حالت

englishMeaning: A rare, rapidly spreading bacterial infection that destroys fascia and nearby soft tissue. A life-threatening medical emergency sometimes called flesh-eating disease. A condition requiring immediate hospital treatment, antibiotics, and often surgery.

urduMeaning: پھولوں سے نکلنے والا میٹھا رس جو زیرہ افشانی کرنے والے جانوروں کو کھینچے، شہد کی مکھیوں کا جمع کیا ہوا رس جس سے شہد بنتا ہے، پھل کا رس یا گاڑھا مشروب، قدیم دیومالا میں دیوتاؤں کا مشروب، نہایت لذیذ یا زندگی بخش مشروب

antonyms: Poison, Bitterness, Brine, Toxin, Bile

englishMeaning: The death of cells or tissue in a living body because of injury, infection, disease, toxins, or loss of blood supply. A pathological process in which damaged tissue dies prematurely. Localized tissue death, often accompanied by inflammation and loss of function.
antonyms: Viability, Regeneration, Healing, Healthy tissue, Cell survival
urduMeaning: زندہ جسم میں چوٹ انفیکشن بیماری زہر یا خون کی کمی سے خلیوں یا بافت کی موت، خراب بافت کے وقت سے پہلے مرنے کا مرضیاتی عمل، کسی خاص جگہ بافت کی موت کے ساتھ سوزش اور کام کی کمی
sindhiMeaning: جيئري جسم ۾ زخم انفيڪشن بيماري زهر يا رت جي کوٽ سبب خلين يا ٽشو جو مرڻ، خراب ٿيل ٽشو جي وقت کان اڳ موت جو بيماري وارو عمل، ڪنهن خاص هنڌ ٽشو جي موت سان گڏ سوزش ۽ ڪم جي کوٽ
examples: Poor blood flow caused necrosis in the damaged tissue. The scan revealed a small area of bone necrosis. Doctors removed the tissue affected by necrosis. Untreated infection can sometimes lead to necrosis.
synonyms: Tissue death, Cell death, Mortification, Gangrene, Devitalization, Tissue decay

antonyms: City of the living, Settlement, Habitation, Birthplace

sindhiMeaning: مئل جسمن ڏانهن جنسي ڪشش، لاش بابت جنسي دلچسپي خيال يا عمل، هڪ ناياب غيرمعمولي جنسي لاڙو جيڪو تڪليف نقصان يا جرم جو سبب بڻجي سگهي

synonyms: Necrophile, Thanatophile, Person with necrophilia

sindhiMeaning: جانور جي موت جو سبب يا بيماري معلوم ڪرڻ لاءِ مرڻ کان پوءِ جاچ، مئل جانور جي جسم جي چير ڦاڙ ۽ معائنو، انسان جي آٽوپسي جي جانورن واري برابر جاچ، گهٽ استعمال ۾ مئل انسان جي جسم جو معائنو
antonyms: Ante-mortem examination, Living examination, External observation
englishMeaning: A postmortem examination of an animal to determine the cause of death or study disease. The dissection and inspection of an animal body after death. A veterinary equivalent of a human autopsy. Less commonly, an examination of a human body after death.
synonyms: Animal autopsy, Postmortem examination, Postmortem, Dissection, Pathological examination
examples: The veterinarian performed a necropsy on the dead bird. A necropsy revealed that the whale had swallowed plastic. Tissue samples were collected during the necropsy. The zoo requested a necropsy to determine the cause of death.

antonyms: Isolation, Individual, Division, Separation
synonyms: Society, Neighborhood, Group, Population, Fellowship, Collective
urduMeaning: ایک جگہ رہنے والے یا مشترک دلچسپی شناخت یا حالات رکھنے والے لوگ، مشترک اقدار یا مقاصد والا سماجی گروہ، علاقہ اور اس کے باشندے، باہم رہنے والے پودوں اور جانوروں کا مجموعہ، بھائی چارے اور تعاون کا احساس
examples: The community raised money for the new library. She found support in the local artistic community. Scientists studied the insect community in the wetland. The festival created a strong sense of community.

The staff handled every request efficiently. This engine uses fuel more efficiently than the old one. She organized the files quickly and efficiently. The new system allows orders to be processed efficiently.

sindhiMeaning: وقت محنت توانائي يا پئسي جي گهٽ ضايع سان نتيجو حاصل ڪندي، منظم ۽ قابل انداز ۾، موجود وسيلن مان وڌ ۾ وڌ فائدو وٺندي

englishMeaning: In a way that achieves results with little waste of time, effort, energy, or money. In an organized and competent manner. With maximum useful output from available resources.

englishMeaning: Achieving a result with minimal waste of time, effort, energy, or money. Working in a well-organized and competent way. Producing a high useful output relative to input.
urduMeaning: وقت محنت توانائی یا رقم کے کم ضیاع کے ساتھ نتیجہ دینے والا، منظم اور قابل طریقے سے کام کرنے والا، کم وسائل سے زیادہ مفید پیداوار دینے والا
examples: The new heating system is highly efficient. She is an efficient and dependable manager. We need a more efficient way to deliver supplies. Efficient appliances can reduce electricity costs.

sindhiMeaning: وقت محنت توانائي يا پئسي جي گهٽ ضايع سان نتيجو ڏيندڙ، منظم ۽ قابل طريقي سان ڪم ڪندڙ، گهٽ وسيلن مان وڌيڪ فائدو پيدا ڪندڙ

urduMeaning: پھول آنے یا کھلنے کا عمل، فن ثقافت یا خیالات کے عروج کی حالت، دیوار یا سطح پر نمودار ہونے والی سفید قلمی تہہ، جلد کی سرخی یا دانے
examples: Spring brought an efflorescence of wildflowers. The period saw an efflorescence of music and poetry. White efflorescence appeared on the damp brick wall. The doctor examined the sudden efflorescence on her skin.

sindhiMeaning: گلجڻ يا گلن ۾ اچڻ جو عمل، فن ثقافت يا خيالن جي عروج واري حالت، ڀتين يا سطح تي نمودار ٿيندڙ سفيد قلمی تهه، چمڙي جي ڳاڙهاڻ يا داڻا
englishMeaning: The process or period of flowering. A flourishing or full development of art, culture, or ideas. A powdery crystalline deposit appearing on masonry or other surfaces. Redness or a skin eruption.
