sindhiMeaning: اوچتو شروع ڪرڻ، جوش سان لڳي وڃڻ، فرض بڻجڻ
englishMeaning: To begin doing something eagerly or immediately, often after a delay. To start doing something actively, especially work or eating, often with enthusiasm.
examples: After the speech, they fell to eating dinner. As soon as the teacher entered, the students fell to their books. After the signal, the workers fell to repairing the road. Everyone fell to eating as soon as dinner was served. She fell to crying when she heard the sad news.

urduMeaning: دونوں ہاتھوں سے یکساں مہارت سے کام کرنے والا، ایسا شخص جو دائیں اور بائیں دونوں ہاتھوں سے لکھنے یا کام کرنے کی صلاحیت رکھتا ہو، یہ لفظ ایسے شخص کے لیے بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے جو مختلف طریقوں کو مہارت سے استعمال کر سکے، کئی طریقوں سے کام کرنے کی قابلیت رکھنے والا شخص
antonyms: One handed, Inflexible, Clumsy, Unskilled with the left hand or right hand
englishMeaning: A person who can perform tasks such as writing, throwing, or using tools with both the right hand and the left hand with equal skill. It can also describe someone who adapts easily in different situations or uses different methods effectively.
examples: She is ambidextrous and can write with either hand. The surgeon is ambidextrous, which helps during complex operations. Being ambidextrous allowed the athlete to throw from both sides. His ambidextrous skills made him very efficient at many manual tasks.
sindhiMeaning: ٻنهي هٿن سان هڪجهڙو ڪم ڪرڻ وارو، اهڙو ماڻهو جيڪو ساڄي ۽ کاٻي ٻنهي هٿن سان برابر مهارت سان ڪم ڪري سگهي، اهو لفظ اهڙي شخص لاءِ به استعمال ٿيندو آهي جيڪو مختلف حالتن ۾ آساني سان طريقا بدلائي سگهي، گهڻ رخي صلاحيت رکندڙ ماڻهو، حالتن مطابق آساني سان طريقو بدلائڻ وارو
synonyms: Versatile, Adaptable, Dexterous, Skillful with both hands, Flexible

englishMeaning: To break or come apart physically. To lose control emotionally or mentally. To stop functioning properly or completely fail. To become weak, disorganized, or destroyed.
antonyms: Hold together, Remain strong, Stay calm, Endure, Persevere
urduMeaning: ٹکڑے ٹکڑے ہو جانا، بکھر جانا، حوصلہ یا قابو کھو دینا، مکمل طور پر ناکام ہو جانا، تباو ہوجانا
synonyms: Break down, Collapse, Fall apart, Crumble, Disintegrate, Shatter, Lose control
examples: After hearing the sad news, she completely fell to pieces. The old bridge fell to pieces after years of neglect. When the company lost its main investor, the whole project fell to pieces. He tried to stay strong, but during the speech he fell to pieces.
sindhiMeaning: ٽڪرا ٽڪرا ٿي وڃڻ، ڪمزور ٿي وڃڻ، قابو وڃائي ڇڏڻ، مڪمل طور ناڪام ٿي وڃڻ

urduMeaning: کسی خاص زمرے قانون یا ضابطے کے تحت آنا، کسی کے اثر و اختیار میں آ جانا
antonyms: Exclude, Escape
englishMeaning: To be included within a particular category, group, or classification. To belong to or be classified as part of a specific group, law, rule, or category. To come under the influence or control of something or someone.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن درجي، قانون، قاعدي يا ضابطي ۾ شامل ٿيڻ يا ڪنهن جي اثر، ڪنٽرول يا اثر هيٺ اچڻ
synonyms: Belong to, Be classified
examples: This case falls under the category of fraud. This topic falls under the subject of psychology. His actions fall under criminal behavior. The city falls under federal jurisdiction. Many young people fall under the influence of social media.

englishMeaning: Capable of making mistakes. Describes a person, system, or belief that is not perfect and can be wrong or make errors
antonyms: Infallible, Perfect, Flawless, Unerring
synonyms: Imperfect, Error prone, Mistaken, Unreliable
urduMeaning: غلطی کرنے والا، ایسا شخص یا چیز جو کامل نہ ہو اور اس سے غلطی ہو سکتی ہو
sindhiMeaning: غلطي ڪرڻ جي صلاحيت رکڻ وارو، اهڙو شخص يا شيءِ جيڪا مڪمل نه هجي ۽ ان مان غلطي ٿيڻ جو امڪان هجي
examples: Even experienced doctors are fallible and can make mistakes. Humans are fallible, which is why learning never stops. The plan failed because it was designed by fallible judgment. He admitted that his memory is fallible under pressure.

The political scandal caused widespread fallout within the party. Many people were affected by the economic fallout of the pandemic. Scientists measured the radioactive fallout after the test. The decision had serious fallout for the local community.
englishMeaning: The negative results or consequences of an event or action. The side effects, aftereffects, or repercussions following an event, especially one that is harmful or controversial. It can also literally mean radioactive particles that settle after a nuclear explosion.
urduMeaning: نتیجہ، اثر، کسی واقعے یا کارروائی کے بعد پیدا ہونے والے منفی نتائج یا اثرات خاص طور پر نقصان دہ یا متنازعہ اثرات، نیوکلیئر دھماکے کے بعد موجود ریڈیائی ذرات

sindhiMeaning: نتيجا، اثر، ڪنهن واقعي يا ڪارروائي کان پوءِ ٿيندڙ منفي اثر يا نقصان خاص ڪري ته اهو ڪاوڙ يا نقصان پهچائيندڙ هجي، ريڊيو ايڪٽو ذرات جو ڇنڊڇاڻ پڻ چئبو آهي
antonyms: Benefit, Advantage, Gain, Success, Blessing

synonyms: Deception, Frame-up, Set-up, Hoax operation, Disinformation tactic, Cover operation, Staged attack
sindhiMeaning: اهڙو عمل جيڪو ماڻهن کي ڌوڪي ۾ رکڻ لاءِ ڪنهن ٻئي جي نالي سان ڪيو وڃي، اهڙو فريب وارو عمل جنهن ۾ ڪو ماڻهو ٽولو يا ملڪ پاڻ ڪو ڪم ڪري ٿو پر اهڙو ڏيک ڏئي ٿو ڄڻ اهو ڪنهن ٻئي ڪيو هجي، هي لفظ گهڻو ڪري سياست جنگ جاسوسي سلامتي ۽ ميڊيا جي بحثن ۾ استعمال ٿيندو آهي، ان جو مقصد عام طور ماڻهن کي گمراهه ڪرڻ الزام ڪنهن ٻئي تي وجهڻ بدلي يا ڪارروائي لاءِ جواز پيدا ڪرڻ يا ڪنهن خاص مقصد لاءِ حمايت حاصل ڪرڻ هوندو آهي
examples: The analyst warned that the attack might be a false flag intended to blame a rival group. Some historians study whether certain incidents were planned as false flag operations. The report found no evidence that the event was a false flag. Spreading unverified claims about a false flag can create confusion and fear.
urduMeaning: ایسا عمل جو دھوکا دینے کے لیے اس طرح کیا جائے کہ لگے یہ کسی اور نے کیا ہے، ایک فریب پر مبنی عمل جس میں کوئی شخص گروہ یا ملک خود کوئی کارروائی کرتا ہے لیکن ایسا ظاہر کرتا ہے جیسے یہ کسی اور نے کی ہو، یہ اصطلاح زیادہ تر سیاست جنگ خفیہ کارروائیوں سلامتی اور میڈیا کی بحث میں استعمال ہوتی ہے، اس کا مقصد عموماً لوگوں کو گمراہ کرنا الزام کسی اور پر ڈالنا جوابی کارروائی کے لیے جواز پیدا کرنا یا کسی خاص مقصد کے لیے حمایت حاصل کرنا ہوتا ہے
englishMeaning: An act that is done to mislead people by making it appear that someone else did it. A deceptive action in which a person, group, or country carries out an act but makes it look as if another person, group, or country is responsible. This term is often used in politics, war, intelligence, media discussion, and security matters. Its purpose is usually to confuse people, create blame, justify retaliation, or gain support for a certain action.
antonyms: Truth, Honesty, Open action, Direct responsibility, Transparency, Genuine act

examples: He tried to falsify his academic records to get the job. The company was accused of falsifying financial statements. She falsified her signature on the contract. Politicians sometimes falsify data to support their claims.
synonyms: Forge, Fabricate, Misrepresent, Doctor, Alter
sindhiMeaning: ڪوڙو ڪرڻ، ڪوڙو ثابت ڪرڻ، ڪوڙ ٺاھڻ يا غلط ثابت ڪرڻ، ڪنهن شيءَ کي غلط يا جهل ڪندڙ بڻائڻ، ڄاڻ يا دستاويز ۾ ڌوڪو ڏيڻ، حقيقت کي غلط ظاهر ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: جعل بنانا ، جھوٹا بنانا یا غلط ظاہر کرنا، کسی چیز یا دستاویز کو جان بوجھ کر غلط یا جھوٹا ظاہر کرنا، حقیقت کو مسخ کرنا یا غلط بیانی کرنا
antonyms: Verify, Confirm, Authenticate, Validate, Prove true
englishMeaning: To make false or incorrect. To lie about or alter information. To deliberately alter information, documents, or facts to make them untrue or misleading. It can also mean misrepresenting the truth in statements, records, or evidence.

antonyms: Abundance, Plenty, Sufficiency, Surplus
synonyms: Starvation, Hunger, Scarcity, Food shortage, Dearth
englishMeaning: A severe shortage of food that causes widespread hunger and suffering among people, often due to drought, war, crop failure, or economic crisis.
urduMeaning: قحط، ایسی حالت جب کھانے پینے کی اشیاء کی شدید کمی ہو جائے اور لوگ بھوک و افلاس کا شکار ہوں
sindhiMeaning: قحط، ڏڪار، اهڙي حالت، جڏهن کاڌي پيتي جي شيئن جي سخت کوٽ هجي، ۽ ماڻهو بک، بيمارين ۽ بدحالي جو شڪار ٿين
examples: The country faced a terrible famine after years of drought. Thousands of people migrated to the city to escape the famine. Relief organizations provided food aid to famine-affected areas. Famine not only destroys lives but also weakens the economy.

antonyms: Chaos, Disorder, Confusion, Disturbance, Uproar
urduMeaning: ماحول، فضا، کسی جگہ کا ماحول یا ماحول کی کیفیت، کسی واقعے کے اردگرد کے حالات یا ماحول، ماحول کا اثر
synonyms: Atmosphere, Environment, Mood, Aura, Setting, Tone
englishMeaning: The character, feeling, or mood of a place or environment. The atmosphere or overall feeling of a place, including its surroundings, lighting, sound, and general mood that affect people’s experiences or emotions.
examples: The restaurant's soft music and candlelight gave it a romantic ambience. The restaurant has a cozy ambience that makes you feel at home. The peaceful ambience of the library helped me concentrate. Soft music added to the romantic ambience of the evening. The hotel lobby’s elegant ambience impressed the guests.
sindhiMeaning: ماحول جو مزاج، جڳھ جي فضا، ڪنهن جاءِ جو احساس، ڪا شيءِ يا واقعي جو ماحول، ماحول جو اثر، جاءِ جو ماحول

antonyms: Scatter, Spread out, Disperse
englishMeaning: To move or spread inward toward a central point. In computer science or electronics: the number of input signals or connections going into a single component (like a logic gate). To gather people, things, or energy toward one point or area.
examples: After the performance ended, the audience began to fan in toward the exit. The soldiers fanned in to secure the central area. In this circuit, the logic gate has a high fan-in capacity. As the rain started, the tourists fanned in under the shelter.
sindhiMeaning: اندر جي طرف گڏ ٿيڻ، هڪ مرڪزي هنڌ ڏانهن وڌڻ، ڪنهن مرڪزي نقطي تي سڀ شيون يا ماڻهو گڏ ٿيڻ، (اليڪٽرانڪس ۾) هڪ ڊيوائس ۾ داخل ٿيندڙ سگنلن جي تعداد
urduMeaning: اندر کی طرف پھیلنا یا جمع ہونا، کسی مرکزی نقطے کی طرف حرکت کرنا، (الیکٹرانکس میں) کسی ایک حصے میں داخل ہونے والے سگنلز یا روابط کی تعداد
synonyms: Gather in, Close in

examples: The police officers fanned out across the field to search for clues. The crowd fanned out as the concert ended. He fanned out the cards on the table for everyone to see. The rescue teams fanned out in different directions after the earthquake.
englishMeaning: To spread out or move in different directions from a single point, similar to how the ribs of a fan open outward.
synonyms: Disperse, Scatter
urduMeaning: پھیل جانا، مختلف سمتوں میں منتشر ہو جانا، پنکھے کی طرح کھل جانا، الگ الگ سمتوں میں جانا
antonyms: Gather, Assemble
sindhiMeaning: پکڙجڻ، ڦهلجڻ، منتشر ٿيڻ، هڪ هنڌ کان مختلف طرفن ۾ پکڙجي وڃڻ

englishMeaning: A type of comedy that uses exaggeration, ridiculous situations, and absurd characters to make people laugh. It can also mean something that is so badly organized, false, or ridiculous that it seems like a joke.

antonyms: Believer in free will, Non fatalist, Optimist, In some contexts, Activist, In some contexts, Self determined person, Free thinker, In some contexts, Person who believes in personal choice

The law contains ambiguous language that lawyers interpret in different ways. Her facial expression was ambiguous, so it was hard to tell if she was happy or upset.
sindhiMeaning: غير واضح، ٻٽي معنيٰ وارو، شڪي يا اڻ پڪ، غيريقيني، ذو معنيٰ، منجهيل، پيچدار، ڳجهو، مبهم، سڃاڻپ ۾ مشڪل، اهڙو جنهن جي تشريح مختلف نموني ٿي سگهي
ايجاد ڪرڻ، خيال ڪرڻ، مڪر ڪرڻ، پنهنجو ٺاهڻ، بهانو ڪرڻ، ٻيائي يا ٺڳي ڪرڻ، مڪر عُذر يا حيلي بهاني کان ڪم وٺڻ، ڍونگ ڪرڻ

sindhiMeaning: ڏار/ شگاف، ڦاٽ يا دراڙ جيڪا پٿر زمين يا جسم ۾ دٻاءُ يا حرڪت سبب پيدا ٿئي، ڪنهن شيءِ کي ڦاڙڻ يا ان ۾ دراڙ پوڻ

It can occur due to pressure, movement, drying, or damage.

sindhiMeaning: تمام صحتمند ۽ تندرست، ڀرپور توانائي سان، اهڙي حالت جتي ماڻهو مڪمل طور تي صحتمند طاقتور ۽ سرگرم هجي، ڪنهن به بيماري يا ڪمزوري کان پاڪ

examples: After a few weeks of rest, he felt as fit as a fiddle again. Even at seventy, she is as fit as a fiddle and walks every day. He recovered quickly from the illness and is now fit as a fiddle. With regular exercise and a healthy diet, you can stay fit as a fiddle.

sindhiMeaning: فيصلو نه ڪري سگهڻ واري حالت، مختلف خيالن ۽ احساسن ۾ ڦاٿل هجڻ، ذهن ۾ تڪراري جذبا هئڻ، ماڻهو ڪنهن شيءِ يا شخص بابت هڪ ئي وقت ۾ خوشي ۽ ناپسنديدگي ٻنهي احساسن ۾ هجي (اهڙي حالت ۾ فيصلو ڪرڻ مشڪل ٿي ويندو آهي)، ڪنهن شيءِ يا ماڻهو بابت هڪ ئي وقت ۾ ٻه الڳ يا مخالف احساس رکڻ
synonyms: Uncertain, Undecided, Conflicted, Torn, Hesitant, Mixed feelings

He was ambivalent about the proposal, unsure whether it was a good opportunity or a risk. Many people feel ambivalent about technology, appreciating its benefits but worrying about its impact. I am ambivalent about the movie; some parts were great, but others were boring.
urduMeaning: غیر یقینی کیفیت، دو متضاد خیالات یا جذبات کا ہونا، کسی بات پر واضح رائے نہ رکھنا، کسی چیز یا شخص کے بارے میں ایک ساتھ مثبت اور منفی دونوں احساسات رکھنا، کوئی شخص کسی چیز یا فرد کے بارے میں ایک ہی وقت میں مثبت اور منفی دونوں جذبات رکھتا ہو (جس کی وجہ سے واضح فیصلہ کرنا مشکل ہو جاتا ہے)
اچانک بھڑک اٹھنا، شدت اختیار کرنا، کسی مرض یا جھگڑے کا دوبارہ بڑھ جانا یا شروع ہو جانا، اچانک غصہ جھگڑا یا سرگرمی بڑھ جانا، وقتی طور پر پہلے سے سکونت کے بعد دوبارہ بڑھ جانا

sindhiMeaning: اوچتو ڀڙڪڻ، اوچتو تپڻ يا وڌي وڃڻ، ڪنهن جذبي بيماري يا جهڳڙي جو اوچتو ٻيهر شروع ٿيڻ، ٿوري وقت خاموشي بعد ٻيهر شدت وٺڻ، اوچتو زور وٺڻ

urduMeaning: اچانک غصے میں آ جانا، کسی پر بھڑک اُٹھنا، تیز ردعمل ظاہر کرنا

englishMeaning: A market where second-hand goods are sold. An open-air market or a large indoor venue where people sell used, old, or second-hand items such as clothes, furniture, books, antiques, and collectibles. It is often informal and may operate on weekends or special occasions.

synonyms: Second-hand market, Swap meet, Bazaar, Car boot sale
urduMeaning: کباڑی مَنڈی، ایسی منڈی یا بازار جہاں پرانی استعمال شدہ یا کم قیمت اشیاء فروخت کی جاتی ہیں، ایک کھلا یا اندرونی بازار جہاں لوگ پرانی یا استعمال شدہ اشیاء جیسے کپڑے فرنیچر کتابیں اینٹیک اشیاء اور کلیکٹیبلز فروخت کرتے ہیں، عام طور پر یہ بازار ہفتہ وار یا کسی خاص موقع پر لگتی ہے

englishMeaning: To develop feathers or to grow enough feathers to fly; also to leave the nest after becoming able to fly. To “fledge” means when a young bird grows feathers that are large and strong enough for flight. It also means the stage when the bird leaves its nest for the first time. In broader use, it can also mean becoming fully developed or ready for independence.
antonyms: Hatch, Nest, Remain, Stay, Be immature
urduMeaning: پرندے کا پروں سے مکمل ہونا یا گھونسلہ چھوڑ کر اڑنے کے قابل ہونا، جب کوئی چھوٹا پرندہ بڑے اور مضبوط پر حاصل کر لیتا ہے اور اڑنے کے قابل ہو جاتا ہے یا پہلی بار گھونسلہ چھوڑ دیتا ہے تو اسے فلیج کرنا کہتے ہیں، بعض اوقات یہ لفظ مکمل طور پر تیار ہونے کے معنی میں بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے

examples: The baby sparrow finally fledged and left the nest. These chicks will fledge in about three weeks. The bird was too weak to fledge properly after the storm. Once they fledge, they start learning to fly on their own.

englishMeaning: Perfectly done or looking great. Used to describe something that is perfectly done, flawless, stylish, or looking extremely good.
antonyms: Messy, Imperfect, Dull, Sloppy, Untidy

Human nature related to physical desires and weaknesses. Skin or body in a general sense. To add more detail or substance. To develop or expand something by adding more details. To make an idea, plan, or story clearer and more complete. To train or encourage someone or an animal to enjoy something.
synonyms: Expand, Develop, Elaborate, Enrich, Detail

antonyms: Honesty, Truth, Sincerity, Integrity, Fairness
urduMeaning: فریب، مکاری، دھوکہ دہی، جھوٹا بہانہ، لغو گفتگو، فریب یا فضول باتیں، دھوکہ یا فریب جس کے ذریعے کسی کو بے وقوف بنایا جائے، یہ فضول یا گمراہ کن باتوں کے لیے بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے جو حقیقت کو چھپانے کے لیے کی جاتی ہیں
sindhiMeaning: فريب، مڪاري، ٺڳي، ڪوڙو بهانو، اجائي ڳالهيون، دوکو يا بي معنيٰ ڳالهيون، ٺڳي يا اهڙو دوکو جنهن سان ڪنهن کي بيوقوف بڻايو وڃي، اهو بي معنيٰ يا گمراه ڪندڙ ڳالهيون به ٿي سگهن ٿيون جيڪي سچ کي لڪائڻ لاءِ ڪيون وڃن

examples: Please flip off the lights when you leave. He flipped off the machine after work. The driver flipped off another car in anger. She quickly flipped off her laptop.

synonyms: Switch on, Turn on, Activate, Target, Aim at

antonyms: Calm, Relaxed, Leisurely, Peaceful, Controlled
sindhiMeaning: انتهائي تيز ۽ سرگرم، تمام گهڻي تيزيءَ سان، وڌيڪ سرگرميءَ سان ۽ بي قاعدگيءَ سان ڪم ڪرڻ يا هلڻ
وچ ۾، چوڌاري گهيريل حالت ۾، ڪنهن حالتن يا واقعن جي وچ ۾، حالتن واقعن يا شور شرابي جي وچ ۾، ڪنهن ماحول جي اندر
synonyms: Among, Amongst, In the middle of, Surrounded by, During
englishMeaning: In the middle of something. Surrounded by something. Used to show that something happens in the center of a situation, place, or group of things. It often describes being surrounded by events, people, noise, problems, or conditions.
examples: The village remained calm amid heavy rainfall. She found her friend amid a large crowd at the market. The meeting continued amid loud protests outside the building. The flowers grew beautifully amid the green grass.
urduMeaning: درمیان میں، بیچ میں، کسی صورتحال یا حالات کے درمیان، حالات یا واقعات کے بیچ، کسی ماحول یا ہجوم کے درمیان
antonyms: Outside, Beyond, Apart from, Away from

synonyms: Tissue fold, Connecting band, Ligament (in some contexts)
englishMeaning: A small fold of tissue that secures or restricts the motion of a mobile organ in the body. A narrow band of tissue that connects two parts of the body, commonly found in the mouth (under the tongue or upper lip) or other areas. It limits movement and helps in proper function. Examples include the lingual frenulum (under the tongue) and labial frenulum (inside the upper or lower lip).
urduMeaning: جسم کے دو حصوں کو جوڑنے والا چھوٹا نرم ٹشو، ایک پتلا نرم ٹشو جو جسم کے دو حصوں کو جوڑتا ہے اور حرکت کو محدود کرتا ہے، عام طور پر زبان کے نیچے یا اوپر کے ہونٹ کے اندر پایا جاتا ہے
examples: The dentist checked the baby’s lingual frenulum to ensure it wasn’t too tight. A torn frenulum can cause bleeding after an accident. Some people need minor surgery to release a tight frenulum under the tongue. The upper lip frenulum can affect how the teeth align.
sindhiMeaning: جسم جي ٻن حصن کي ڳنڍڻ وارو ننڍڙو نرم ٽشو، هڪ نرم ۽ سنھو ٽشو جيڪو جسم جي ٻن حصن کي ڳنڍي ۽ انهن جي حرڪت کي محدود ڪري، عام طور تي زبان جي هيٺان يا اُپري لب جي اندر ڏٺو وڃي ٿو
antonyms: Freedom of movement, Loose tissue, Unrestricted tissue

englishMeaning: Wild or uncontrolled. Showing extreme, uncontrolled excitement, activity, or emotion; behaving in a chaotic or frantic way
synonyms: Agitated, Frantic, Wild, Hectic, Delirious
sindhiMeaning: بي ترتيب جذباتي، انتهائي جذباتي يا بي ترتيب حرڪت، جيڪو ڪنٽرول کان ٻاهر هجي
urduMeaning: جوش و خروش میں بے قابو، انتہائی جذباتی یا بے ترتیب حرکت یا حالت؛ جس پر قابو نہ پایا جا سکے
examples: The crowd became frenzied when the singer appeared. She made a frenzied attempt to finish the work on time. The stock market saw frenzied trading today. Children ran in frenzied joy during the festival.
antonyms: Calm, Relaxed, Composed, Peaceful, Orderly
Calmly, Slowly, Steadily, Peacefully
sindhiMeaning: جلدي ۾، ڀاڙيل، ڪنٽرول کان ٻاهر، انتهائي جوش يا پريشاني سان ڪم ڪرڻ، جنون سان، انتهائي جوش ۾، بي قابو، ڀاڙيل، پريشان، ذهني يا جسماني شدت سان
englishMeaning: In a very excited or uncontrolled way. Performing an action with intense, wild, or uncontrolled energy or emotion; acting in a state of frenzy.
urduMeaning: جنونی انداز میں، بے قابو، شدت، جوش یا اضطراب کے ساتھ کسی عمل کو انجام دینا؛ غیر قابو شدہ حالت میں عمل کرنا
synonyms: Wildly, Madly, Violently, Frantically
examples: She typed frenziedly to finish the report on time. Fans waved flags frenziedly at the concert. He searched frenziedly for his lost passport. The children played frenziedly in the garden.

synonyms: Hysteria, Mania, Rage, Excitement, Agitation, Delirium
englishMeaning: A state of extreme excitement, anger, or wild behavior. A temporary state of uncontrolled emotion or activity, often characterized by intense excitement, agitation, or violent behavior. It can describe both positive excitement and negative emotional outbursts.
examples: The crowd went into a frenzy when the singer appeared on stage. She worked in a frenzy to finish the project on time. News of the victory sent the city into a frenzy of celebration. The dog chased the cat in a frenzy.
urduMeaning: جنون، شور و غل، پاگل پن، شدت جذبات، شدت جذبات یا بے قابو کیفیت، جوش و خروش، دیوانگی، بہت زیادہ خوشی یا غصہ، اضطراب یا بے قابو حرکت، شدت سے جذبات کا اظہار
sindhiMeaning: جوش، ڀڄڪ، ڏاڍو جذبو، جنون، ڏاڍو جوش، پاگل پن، ٿڌو نه رهڻ، بي قابو عمل يا حرڪت، عارضي پر انتهاپسند جذبات، هنگامي مايوسي يا خوشي ۾ ڀڄڪ
antonyms: Calm, Composure, Serenity, Peace, Tranquility

englishMeaning: To waste or squander. To break or tear into small pieces, shred. To waste (money, time, etc) bit by bit on petty things usually with away. To separate or break into fragments. Round pieces of fruit, vegetables, or meat that are dipped in batter and fried. A small cake of fried batter, usually containing corn, fruit, or other filling. A small piece, fragment, or shred.
synonyms: Spend carelessly, Throw away, Misuse, Fried snack, Fried patty
examples: I fritter my time away at coffee mornings. The fritters should be golden brown and sizzling. When both sides are golden brown, transfer the fritters to a serving platter. She served apple fritters with tea. He frittered away his savings on expensive gadgets. Do not fritter your time on meaningless arguments.
urduMeaning: پکوڑے ، تکہ ، پارچہ ، ٹکڑا ، بوٹی ، بَرباد کر دينا ، خَرچ کر دينا ، بے کار کر دينا ، ضائع کر دينا ، لُٹا دينا ،اَنڈّہ آٹا اور دُودھ کو مِلا کر گھی ميں خَستَہ کر کے بَنايا ہُوا
sindhiMeaning: ٿورو ٿورو ڪري وقت يا پئسا ضايع ڪرڻ، پڪوڙو، بيٽر ۾ ٻوڙي تريل کاڌي جو ننڍو ٽڪرو، پڪل گوشت جو ٽڪر، اهڙي کاڌي جي ننڍڙي حصي کي چوندا آهن جيڪو ميون ڀاڄين يا گوشت مان ٺهيل هجي بيٽر ۾ ٻوڙي تريو وڃي، اهو ٻاهران ڪرسپي ۽ اندر نرم هوندو آهي
antonyms: Save, Conserve, Preserve, Raw food, Steamed food

synonyms: Lighthearted, Superficial, Unimportant
examples: He spent money on frivolous things. She spent her money on frivolous things instead of saving it. His frivolous remarks annoyed the teacher. The court dismissed the case as frivolous. He has a frivolous attitude towards his responsibilities.
englishMeaning: Not serious or important, silly or trivial. Describes something that lacks seriousness, value, or sense. Often refers to actions, behavior, or things that are unworthy of attention or overly playful when seriousness is expected.
urduMeaning: غیر سنجیدہ، فضول، بیکار، ہلکی پھلکی یا غیر ضروری کام، بے وقوفانہ رویہ یا گفتگو
antonyms: Serious, Important
sindhiMeaning: سنجيدگي کان خالي، فضول، بيمعني، غير ضروري سرگرميون، بيوقوفيءَ وارا عمل يا ڳالهيون
بي فڪري سان يا سنجيدگي کانسواءِ، ڪنهن ڳالهه کي بغير سنجيدگي، ذميواري يا سوچ ويچار جي وٺڻ يا ڪرڻ عام طور تي اهڙي رويي لاءِ استعمال ٿئي ٿو جيڪو اهم معاملن ۾ غير ذميوار هجي
synonyms: Carelessly, Lightheartedly, Thoughtlessly, Trivially
examples: He laughed frivolously during the serious meeting. The issue of climate change should not be discussed frivolously. She spent money frivolously without thinking about the future. The lawyer argued that the case was not filed frivolously.
urduMeaning: لاپرواہی سے يا غير سنجيدگی کے ساتھ، کسی کام يا بات کو بغیر سنجیدگی، ذمہ داری یا غور و فکر کے کرنا ، یہ لفظ اکثر ایسے رویے کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے جو اہم معاملات میں غیر محتاط یا غیر ذمہ دار ہو
englishMeaning: In a light, careless, or unserious way. Doing or treating something in a way that shows a lack of seriousness, responsibility, or careful thought. It is often used to criticize behavior, speech, or decisions that should have been taken more seriously.
antonyms: Seriously, Carefully, Thoughtfully, Responsibly
Seriousness, Gravity, Solemnity, Responsibility, Thoughtfulness
sindhiMeaning: هلڪڙائپ، غير سنجيدگي، فضول رويو، اهڙي حالت يا رويو جنهن ۾ ماڻهو اهم ڳالهين کي سنجيدگي سان نه وٺي ۽ بي پرواهه انداز اختيار ڪري
urduMeaning: غیر سنجیدگی، سطحی پن، لاپرواہی، ایسا رویہ جس میں سنجیدہ یا اہم معاملات کو ہلکا سمجھا جائے اور ذمہ داری کا احساس نہ ہو
englishMeaning: Lack of seriousness or importance. Light and careless behavior. An attitude or behavior that treats serious matters as unimportant. It shows a lack of responsibility, depth, or thoughtful concern, especially in situations that require seriousness or careful judgment.
examples: His frivolousness during the meeting annoyed the senior staff. The judge criticized the lawyer for the frivolousness of his arguments. Frivolousness has no place in matters of public safety. Her tone showed a level of frivolousness that weakened her message.
synonyms: Carelessness, Lightheartedness, Triviality, Playfulness, Irresponsibility

antonyms: Without
englishMeaning: In the midst or middle of, surrounded or encompassed by
sindhiMeaning: وچ ۾، منجھ، شامل، (جو) جي وچ ۾، درميان، سلسلي دوران، وچون
synonyms: Amongst
examples: The Trump administration is formulating its North Korea policy amidst accelerating threats and deteriorating relations in the region.
urduMeaning: گھرا ہوا، کے درمیان میں، بیچ میں، دوران میں، گھرا ہوا

synonyms: Scowl, Glare, Grimace, Glower, Pout
urduMeaning: تیوری چڑھانا ، ناراضگی کا اظہار کرنا، غم یا فکر کی حالت میں چہرے کا بگڑ جانا، غصے یا الجھن کا اظہار چہرے سے کرنا
sindhiMeaning: ڀرون چڙهائڻ، چهري تي ناراضگي ڏيکارڻ، پريشاني يا غصي جو اظهار ڪرڻ، فڪر يا خفگيءَ جو تاثر، ناراضگيءَ جو اظهار چهري تي، پريشاني يا نفرت جو چهرو
examples: She frowned when she heard the bad news. The teacher frowned at the noisy students. He looked at me with a deep frown on his face. People usually frown when they are confused or upset.
englishMeaning: To bring your eyebrows together and wrinkle your forehead, usually when you are angry, worried, or thinking hard. The expression on your face that shows disapproval or worry.
antonyms: Smile, Grin, Beam, Laugh

englishMeaning: Careful with money or resources; not wasteful. Someone who spends money and resources wisely, avoids unnecessary expenses, and prefers simplicity. It reflects prudence and careful management rather than stinginess.
urduMeaning: کفایت شعار، محتاط، فضول خرچی سے بچنے والا، غَير مُسرِف ، سادہ اور معتدل طرز زندگی اپنائے
antonyms: Wasteful, Extravagant, Lavish, Profligate, Careless
sindhiMeaning: پئسا ۽ وسيلن ۾ محتاط، فضول خرچي کان بچڻ وارو، ڪم خرچائو، ڪفايتي، بچت ڪرڻ وارو، سادي زندگي گذارڻ ڪرڻ وارو
synonyms: Economical, Thrifty, Prudent, Sparing, Careful
examples: She lives a frugal life and saves most of her income. He made frugal choices when furnishing his new apartment. The company adopted frugal measures to cut costs. Even though he was wealthy, he remained frugal in his daily habits.

antonyms: Glutton, Indulgent Eater, Extravagant Eater, Lavish Eater
englishMeaning: A person who eats modestly or economically. Someone who is careful about the quantity and cost of food they consume, preferring simple meals and avoiding waste or extravagance.
urduMeaning: سادہ کھانے والا، وہ شخص جو کھانے میں سادگی اور کفایت رکھتا ہے، زیادہ نہیں کھاتا اور ضائع ہونے سے بچاتا ہے
examples: John is a frugal eater and prefers simple home-cooked meals. Despite his wealth, he remains a frugal eater. She became a frugal eater after moving to a small apartment. Being a frugal eater helped him save money for his travels.
sindhiMeaning: سادو ۽ محتاط کائيندڙ، اهو ماڻهو جيڪو کائڻ ۾ سادگي ۽ بچت رکندو آهي، گهڻو نه کائيندو ۽ ضايع ٿيڻ کان بچائيندو آهي
synonyms: Economical Eater, Thrifty Eater, Modest Eater, Simple Eater

sindhiMeaning: ڪفايت شعاري، بچت ڪرڻ جو طريقو، پئسن يا وسيلن جو محتاط استعمال، فضول خرچي کان پاسو ڪرڻ
examples: Her frugality allowed her to save enough money for a house. He is known for his frugality and rarely spends on luxuries. Frugality in cooking can help reduce household expenses. Practicing frugality does not mean living poorly but managing resources wisely.
urduMeaning: کفایت شعاری، بچت، غیر ضروری خرچ سے گریز، وسائل کا محتاط استعمال
englishMeaning: Careful use of money or resources, avoiding waste. The quality of being economical with resources, especially money. It involves avoiding unnecessary expenses, using what you have wisely, and prioritizing needs over wants.
synonyms: Thrift, Economy, Prudence, Saving, Sparingness
antonyms: Extravagance, Wastefulness, Lavishness, Prodigality
Wastefully, Extravagantly, Lavishly, Prodigally, Recklessly
urduMeaning: کفایت شعاری سے ، کم خرچ میں، وسائل، پیسہ یا چیزوں کو فضول خرچی سے بچاتے ہوئے محتاط اور سادہ انداز میں استعمال کرنا
examples: She lived frugally to save enough money for her children’s education. They furnished their home frugally, using mostly second-hand items. He ate frugally during his travels to avoid spending too much. The company managed its resources frugally to survive the recession.
sindhiMeaning: بچت سان، گهٽ خرچ ڪرڻ جي طريقي سان، وسيلن، پئسن يا شيون کي فضول خرچي کان بچائيندي محتاط ۽ سادي انداز ۾ استعمال ڪرڻ
englishMeaning: In a careful way to avoid waste or spending too much. Acting with economy, prudence, or simplicity in the use of resources, money, or materials; avoiding extravagance while still meeting needs
synonyms: Economically, Thriftily, Prudently, Sparingly, Conservatively

antonyms: Raw, Boil
englishMeaning: To cook food (usually quickly) by frying, often used for breakfast or leftovers.
urduMeaning: تل کر پکانا
examples: She fried up some eggs for breakfast. Let’s fry up the leftovers. He fried up the fish for dinner. They fried up some vegetables.
sindhiMeaning: تيل ۾ پچائڻ
synonyms: Cook, Sauté
Traditionalist, Conservative, Stick-in-the-mud, Old fogey
sindhiMeaning: پراڻن خيالن وارو ماڻهو، اهڙو ماڻهو جيڪو نون خيالن، جديد طريقن يا تبديلي کي پسند نٿو ڪري ۽ هميشه پراڻين روايتن سان جڙيل رهي ٿو
examples: He refuses to use a smartphone and prefers handwritten letters like a true fuddy-duddy. The young staff think their manager is a fuddy-duddy because he dislikes flexible work hours. She called him a fuddy-duddy for opposing modern teaching methods. Not everyone who likes tradition is a fuddy-duddy, but he clearly resists all change.
urduMeaning: قدامت پسند اور پرانے خیالات رکھنے والا شخص، ایسا شخص جو نئی سوچ، جدید طریقوں یا تبدیلی کو ناپسند کرے اور ہمیشہ پرانی روایات پر قائم رہے
englishMeaning: A person who is old-fashioned and resists change. Someone who strongly prefers traditional ways of thinking or behaving and often dislikes new ideas, modern styles, or changes in society. Such a person may criticize trends simply because they are new.
antonyms: Progressive, Modernist, Forward-thinking, Trendsetter

examples: I was starting to realize that Grandpa's tales about when he was a boy were a lot of fudge.
synonyms: Nonsense, Waffle, Rubbish
englishMeaning: Language, behavior, or ideas that are absurd and contrary to good sense. To avoid giving a definite answer or position. To use dishonest methods to achieve a goal. A soft sweet made from sugar, butter, and milk. To change so much as to create a wrong impression or alter the meaning of.
urduMeaning: پیوند لگانا، جھوٹی کہانی کہنا
sindhiMeaning: بيوقوفي، نفرت جو اظهار، کير کنڊ ۽ مکڻ مان ٺاهيل ٽافيءَ برفي، جھڙو مٺاڻ، بڪواس، واهيات، دوکو، بي ايماني، جعلي ڪم، نااهلي سا منهن ڏيڻ، ستياناس ڪرڻ، غير ذميواري ڪرڻ، ندا نه مڃڻ، نااهلي يا دوکي جو ڪم ڪرڻ
antonyms: Clarify, Common sense, Rationality
Law-abiding person, Citizen, Resident, Permanent
englishMeaning: A person who is running away, especially from the law. A person who escapes or is in hiding, often to avoid arrest or danger. Something that is fleeting, temporary, or hard to capture.
examples: The fugitive was finally caught after hiding for months. Police are searching for a fugitive who escaped last night. His fame was fugitive and disappeared quickly. She had only a fugitive glimpse of the rare bird.
sindhiMeaning: مفرور، ڀڄندڙ/ ڀڳوڙو/ ڀڳل، فرار ٿيل، پناه ڳولهيندڙ، قانون کان ڀڄندڙ ماڻهو، اهو ماڻهو جيڪو قانون يا خطري کان بچڻ لاءِ لڪي وڃي يا ڀڄي وڃي، عارضي/ جلدي ختم ٿيندڙ يا پڪڙ ۾ نه ايندڙ
synonyms: Escapee, Runaway, Absconder, Outlaw, Transient
urduMeaning: مفرور، قانون سے بھاگنے والا شخص، قید سے فرار ہونے والا، وہ شخص جو گرفتاری یا خطرے سے بچنے کے لیے فرار ہو جائے، عارضی/ جلد ختم ہونے والا یا قابو میں نہ آنے والا

antonyms: Hostility, Enmity, Conflict, Hatred, Discord
sindhiMeaning: ميل ميلاپ، هم آهنگي، ڀائپي، سٺا لاڳاپا، دوستي يا ڀائيچارو، ماڻهن گروهن يا ملڪن وچ ۾ اهڙو سٺو ۽ پرامن لاڳاپو جنهن ۾ محبت ڀائيچارو اعتماد ۽ گڏيل هم آهنگي هجي
urduMeaning: میل جول، باہمی ہم آہنگی، خیر سگالی، دوستانہ تعلقات، میل جول، خیر سگالی، دوستانہ تعلقات، افراد گروہوں یا ممالک کے درمیان ایسا پرامن اور دوستانہ تعلق جس میں خیر سگالی ہم آہنگی اور باہمی احترام موجود ہو
englishMeaning: Friendly relationship. A peaceful and friendly relationship between people, groups, or countries where there is goodwill, harmony, and mutual respect. It often describes cooperation and absence of conflict.
examples: The two countries signed a treaty to promote amity and cooperation. The community festival helped build amity among people from different cultures. Years of honest dialogue created amity between the neighboring villages. Leaders encouraged amity so that social tensions could be reduced.
synonyms: Friendship, Harmony, Goodwill, Cordiality, Peacefulness, Fellowship
Mishandle, Drop, Bungle, Stumble, Botch
urduMeaning: گھبرا کر غلطی کرنا یا چیز ہاتھ سے گر جانا، کسی کام کو بے ڈھنگے انداز میں کرنا، ہاتھوں سے چیز ٹھیک طرح نہ سنبھال پانا، گھبراہٹ کی وجہ سے غلطی کر بیٹھنا، بات کرتے ہوئے الفاظ میں اٹک جانا، کارکردگی میں ہونے والی چھوٹی مگر اثرانداز غلطی
sindhiMeaning: اونداهي يا بي ڌياني ۾ هٿ هلائي شيءِ ڳولڻ، گهٻراهٽ سبب ڪم اڻ سڌي نموني ڪرڻ، ڳالهائڻ وقت لفظن ۾ اٽڪڻ، مهارت جي کوٽ سبب ڪم خراب ڪرڻ، راند دوران بال تي ڪنٽرول وڃائڻ، سماجي يا عوامي غلطي، ڪارڪردگي ۾ ٿيندڙ معمولي پر اثرائتي غلطي
englishMeaning: To handle something clumsily or fail due to lack of control. She threatened to get the goods on her boss if he treated her unfairly. The lawyer got the goods on the company and proved the case in court.

The term can also describe vehicles or objects capable of operating on both land and water.

examples: We decided to head for the airport early in the morning. After work, she headed for home to rest. The hikers are heading for the mountain trail. Without planning, the project may head for failure.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن هنڌ ڏانهن وڃڻ، رخ ڪرڻ، ستو وٺڻ، تڪليف يا مصيبت ۾ پئجي وڃڻ، طرف وڃڻ
synonyms: Go towards, Move to, Make for, Be bound for, Approach, Go to, Travel toward, Proceed
englishMeaning: To go toward a place or move in a particular direction. To start moving toward a destination or goal, either physically or figuratively. It can describe traveling to a place or moving toward a situation, result, or future outcome.
urduMeaning: کسی طرف روانہ ہونا ، رخ کرنا، سمت پکڑنا، مصیبت میں پڑنا

تجزیاتی، منطقی سوچ رکھنے والا، باریک بینی سے جائزہ لینے والا، تحقیقاتی انداز رکھنے والا، ایسا انداز فکر یا طریقہ جس میں مسئلہ معلومات یا خیال کو مختلف حصوں میں تقسیم کر کے منظم اور منطقی انداز میں اس کا جائزہ لیا جائے تاکہ درست نتیجہ حاصل ہو
synonyms: Logical, Critical, Systematic, Rational, Investigative, Reasoning
examples: She has an analytical mind and solves complex problems quickly. The researcher used an analytical approach to study climate data. His analytical skills helped the team understand the cause of the failure. Teachers encourage students to develop analytical thinking in science classes.
sindhiMeaning: تجزياتي، منطقي سوچ وارو، جاچ ڪندڙ، حقيقتن جو جائزو وٺندڙ، اهڙو طريقو يا سوچ جنهن ۾ مسئلي خيال يا معلومات کي ننڍن حصن ۾ ورهائي تفصيلي جائزو وٺي صحيح نتيجو ڪڍيو وڃي
englishMeaning: Relating to careful examination of something by breaking it into parts. A person or method that studies facts, data, ideas, or problems step by step in order to understand how they work and to reach logical conclusions.
antonyms: Emotional, Illogical, Unsystematic, Unthinking, Superficial

sindhiMeaning: حقيقت کان پري سوچڻ، اهڙي حالت جڏهن ماڻهو خيالن يا خوابن ۾ ايترو گم هجي جو عملي حالتن تي ڌيان نه ڏئي
antonyms: Practical, Realistic, Focused, Attentive, Down to earth
urduMeaning: حقیقت سے دور، ایسی حالت جب کوئی شخص خیالی دنیا میں گم ہو اور عملی یا حقیقی باتوں پر توجہ نہ دے
englishMeaning: Not paying attention to reality. A person who is dreamy, unrealistic, distracted, or lost in thoughts and imagination instead of focusing on what is happening around them.
examples: He walked into the meeting with his head in the clouds and missed the main point. She often has her head in the clouds, dreaming about travel and adventure. If you keep your head in the clouds, you will miss important details. The teacher warned him to stop having his head in the clouds and focus on his studies.
synonyms: Daydreaming, Unrealistic, Absent minded, Lost in thought, Dreamy
Prevent, Stop, Avert
examples: The manager acted quickly to head off the crisis. She headed off early to avoid traffic. Police were able to head off the protest. We should head off before it gets dark.
englishMeaning: To prevent something from happening or to leave for a place before others. It is often used for stopping trouble early or starting a journey.
sindhiMeaning: روڪڻ يا اڳواٽ نڪري پوڻ، ڪنهن هنڌ ڏانهن روانو ٿيڻ يا ڪنهن مسئلي يا تڪرار کي اڳواٽ روڪي ڇڏڻ
urduMeaning: روک دینا یا روانہ ہو جانا، کسی جگہ کے لیے روانہ ہونا یا کسی مسئلے کو پیدا ہونے سے پہلے ہی روک دینا
antonyms: Allow, Encourage, Delay
Avoid, Ignore, Evade
englishMeaning: To deal with a problem directly and bravely without avoiding it. To face a situation, problem, or opponent directly with courage and honesty, without delay or evasion.
sindhiMeaning: سڌو سنئون مقابلو ڪرڻ، نا ڊڄڻ جي ڪنهن مسئلي يا حالتن کي سامهون کان منهن ڏيڻ
urduMeaning: براہ راست مقابلہ کرنا، بغیر ٹال مٹول کے کسی مسئلے یا صورتحال کا سامنا کرنا
examples: She decided to head on the challenge. He faced the issue head on. The team tackled the problem head on. You must meet your fears head on.
synonyms: Confront, Face, Tackle

englishMeaning: Completely, deeply, or totally, especially in love. To be completely in love with someone. To be fully involved or absorbed in something. Sometimes used to describe a chaotic or disordered situation.
antonyms: Slightly, Partially, Indifferent, Uninvolved
sindhiMeaning: مڪمل طور، ڪنهن سان انتهائي پيار ڪرڻ، پيار ۾ مڪمل طور غرق ٿيڻ، ڪنهن ڪم ۾ مڪمل طور شامل يا مصروف ٿيڻ، افراتفري يا الٽي حالت ۾ هجڻ
urduMeaning: مکمل طور پر، کسی کے ساتھ شدید محبت میں مبتلا ہونا، کسی کام میں مکمل طور پر مشغول یا ملوث ہونا، انتشار یا الٹی حالت میں ہونا
synonyms: Deeply in love, Madly in love, Completely, Totally, Entirely
examples: She fell head over heels in love with her classmate. He is head over heels involved in his new business project. They turned the house head over heels while searching for the keys. After hearing the news, his life went head over heels.

sindhiMeaning: ترقي يا اڳتي وڌڻ، ڪم يا منصوبي ۾ اڳڀرائي، ڏکيائي باوجود ڪجهه اڳتي وڌڻ، اڳتي وڌڻ يا اڳڀرائي جيڪا ڪا محنت يا ڪوشش ڪرڻ بعد حاصل ٿئي، هي ترقي يا بهتري ڏانهن سفر جي نشاندهي ڪري ٿي
antonyms: Setback, Delay, Stagnation, Stop, Reverse, Hindrance
urduMeaning: ترقی یا آگے بڑھنے کی پیش رفت، کسی منصوبے یا کام میں پیش رفت، مشکل کے باوجود آگے بڑھنے کی کوشش کا نتیجہ، آگے بڑھنے کی پیش رفت جو کسی محنت یا کوشش کے بعد حاصل ہو، یہ بہتری یا ترقی کی طرف آگے بڑھنے کو ظاہر کرتا ہے
synonyms: Progress, Advance, Improvement, Development, Gain, Movement forward
englishMeaning: Progress or movement forward in work, plans or travel. Gradual improvement in a long and difficult process. Any positive change after effort. The progress you make when moving forward in a task, project, goal or journey. It shows improvement or advancement after effort.
examples: We are finally making some headway on the report. The team made little headway because of the bad weather. She worked all night but could not make much headway. The project is slow but we are starting to see headway.

My grandfather always says, “Health is wealth,” so he walks every morning. After falling sick, Ali realized that health is wealth. Eating healthy food proves that health is wealth. People who exercise regularly understand that health is wealth.
synonyms: Good health is priceless, Health comes first, A sound mind in a sound body, Well-being is true wealth
englishMeaning: Good health is the greatest blessing and more valuable than money or material things. Good health is better than riches. A healthy life brings happiness and success. Physical and mental fitness are priceless. Taking care of health is the key to a better life.
sindhiMeaning: تندرستي هزار نعمت آهي، صحت سڀ کان وڏي دولت آهي، سٺو صحتمند هجڻ هر دولت کان وڌيڪ اهم آهي
antonyms: Wealth without health, Sickness is misery, Poor health ruins happiness
urduMeaning: تندرستی ہزار نعمت ہے، صحت سب سے بڑی دولت ہے، اچھی صحت دولت اور مال سے زیادہ قیمتی ہوتی ہے

examples: She worked heart and soul to make the project a success. The teacher puts her heart and soul into helping he students. He is heart and soul devoted to his family. The musicians played with heart and soul, moving everyone to tear
synonyms: Devotedly
sindhiMeaning: سڄي دل سان، دل ۽ جان سان، پوري محبت ۽ لڳاءَ سان، سچي جذبي ۽ ايمانداري سان ڪم ڪرڻ
englishMeaning: With complete enthusiasm, energy, and devotion. To do something with full passion, sincerity, and involvement. Refers to the deepest emotions, dedication, or true essence of a person or thing.
antonyms: Carelessly
urduMeaning: دل و جان سے، پوری لگن اور محبت سے، پورے اخلاص اور جذبے کے ساتھ کام کرنا

examples: The landlord had a heart of stone and refused to help the poor family. Anyone with a heart of stone could ignore the cries of hungry children. She thinks her boss has a heart of stone because he never listens to employees’ problems. Despite the tragedy, the criminal showed a heart of stone and felt no regret.
synonyms: Cruel person, Cold hearted person, Merciless person, Unfeeling person, Hard hearted person, Ruthless person
antonyms: Kind hearted person, Compassionate person, Merciful person, Sympathetic person, Caring person, Soft hearted person
sindhiMeaning: پٿر دل، بي رحم ماڻهو، اهڙو ماڻهو جنهن ۾ همدردي نه هجي، سخت دل ماڻهو، احساس کان خالي ماڻهو، رحم نه ڪندڙ ماڻهو، بي حس انسان
urduMeaning: سنگ دل، بے رحم انسان، ایسا شخص جس میں ہمدردی نہ ہو، سخت دل انسان، احساس سے خالی شخص، رحم نہ کرنے والا، بے حس انسان
englishMeaning: A hard and unkind person with no sympathy. Someone who appears emotionally hard and uncaring. Such a person may ignore the suffering, feelings, or needs of others. The phrase compares the human heart with stone to show absence of warmth, love, mercy, or emotional softness.

antonyms: Emotionally, Subjectively, Impulsively, Randomly
sindhiMeaning: تجزياتي طور تي، تجزياتي طريقي سان، پرک سان، غور سان حصن ۾ ورهائي سمجهڻ جي طريقي سان، تجزيي واري طريقي سان، منطقي ۽ تفصيلي تجزيي ذريعي سمجهڻ يا جاچڻ واري طريقي سان
urduMeaning: تَحليلی طَور پَر ، تَجزِيَہ کارانَہ طَريقے سے ، تَجزِيے کے انداز ميں، تجزیاتی طور پر، غور و فکر اور منطقی تجزیے کے ذریعے سمجھنے یا جانچنے کے طریقے سے
examples: Equations of motion for the water atoms were solved analytically. Tests that measure children’s ability to think analytically are being introduced in a number of schools. The research is analytically rigorous sloppy. Some people are better than others at thinking analytically.
englishMeaning: In a way that relates to analysis or logical examination. Doing something by carefully examining the components, understanding the structure, and evaluating relationships to reach a logical conclusion. Often used in thinking, problem-solving, or studying data.
synonyms: Logically, Critically, Methodically, Systematically

sindhiMeaning: اهو ماڻهو جيڪو خوشي ۽ لطف کي زندگي جو اهم مقصد سمجهي، اهو ماڻهو آهي جيڪو زندگي ۾ خوشي آرام ۽ لطف کي سڀ کان اهم سمجهي ، اهو شخص اهڙين شين جي ڳولا ۾ رهي ٿو جيڪي کيس خوشي ۽ سڪون ڏين (جهڙوڪ کاڌو تفريح يا آرامده زندگي)
urduMeaning: وہ شخص جو زندگی کا اصل مقصد خوشی اور لذت کو سمجھتا ہے، جو خوشی آرام اور لذت کو زندگی کا سب سے بڑا مقصد سمجھتا ہے، ایسا شخص ان چیزوں کو ترجیح دیتا ہے جو اسے خوشی اور تسکین فراہم کریں چاہے وہ جسمانی ہوں یا ذہنی
antonyms: Ascetic, Stoic, Self-denying person, Puritan, Disciplined individual
synonyms: Pleasure seeker, Epicurean, Sensualist, Indulgent person, Bon vivant
englishMeaning: A person who seeks pleasure as the main goal of life. Someone who believes that pleasure, enjoyment, and comfort are the most important things in life. Such a person focuses on experiences that bring happiness, whether physical, emotional, or sensory.
examples: He lived like a true hedonist, always chasing pleasure and luxury. Some people think a hedonist cannot live a disciplined life. She is not a hedonist, she values hard work more than comfort. The character in the novel is a hedonist who avoids responsibility.

antonyms: Ignore, Neglect, Disregard, Overlook
urduMeaning: لحاظ کرنا، النفات کرنا، توجہ دینا، پرواہ کرنا، خیال رکھنا، غور کرنا، سنجیدگی سے لینا، توجہ یا خیال
englishMeaning: To pay attention to something or take notice. To listen carefully, consider advice, warnings, or instructions, and act accordingly. Careful attention or notice given to something.
sindhiMeaning: ٻڌڻ، ڌيان ڏيڻ، توجھ ڪرڻ، خيال ڪرڻ، غور ڪرڻ، نصيحت يا خبرداري کي سنجيدگي سان وٺڻ ۽ ان تي عمل ڪرڻ، پرواهه ڪرڻ، ڌيان يا توجهه
examples: You should heed your teacher’s advice. He did not heed the warning and got into trouble. Please heed the instructions before using the machine. She heeded her doctor and took rest.
synonyms: Listen, Notice, Observe, Consider, Mind

englishMeaning: Control, dominance or strong influence of one group, country or leader over others. Dominant leadership or influence by one group over others, especially in politics or international relations. A situation where one state, group, institution or ideology holds leading power or influence over others, often shaping their decisions, culture or direction.
antonyms: Equality, Balance, Inferiority, Submission, Weakness, Powerlessness
synonyms: Dominance, Supremacy, Control, Influence, Leadership, Authority, Ascendancy
sindhiMeaning: بالادستي، حاڪميت، حڪمراني، غلبو، اختيار، سربراهي، هڪ گروهه يا ملڪ جو ٻين تي قبضو برتري يا اثر رسوخ رکڻ (سياسي معاشي يا ثقافتي اثر جي صورت ۾)، ڪنهن ميدان ۾ اڳواڻي يا بالادستي، ثقافتي غلبو جنهن ۾ هڪ سوچ کي سڀ قبول ڪن، ضابطن يا معيارن کي طئي ڪرڻ جي طاقت
urduMeaning: بالادستی، غلبہ، حکمرانی، اقتدار (کسی طاقتور کا دوسروں پر سیاسی یا ثقافتی غلبہ)، تسلط، کسی گروہ یا ملک کی دوسروں پر غلبہ برتری یا اثر و رسوخ (سیاسی معاشی یا ثقافتی اثر کی شکل میں)، کسی میدان میں نمایاں قیادت، ثقافتی غلبہ جس میں ایک سوچ کو وسیع طور پر قبول کیا جائے، قواعد اور معیار طے کرنے کی طاقت
examples: The country's economic hegemony shaped trade policies across the region. Cultural hegemony can influence how people think, behave and consume media. The alliance was formed to resist the military hegemony of a powerful neighbor. Some scholars argue that global hegemony shifts from one superpower to another over time.

urduMeaning: وہ رویہ یا رجحان جس میں کوئی جاندار سورج کی روشنی کو ترجیح دیتا ہے اس میں وقت گزارتا ہے یا اس سے توانائی حاصل کرتا ہے، انسانی تناظر میں یہ اُن لوگوں کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے جو دھوپ میں وقت گزارنا پسند کرتے ہیں اور اس سے صحت یا خوشی محسوس کرتے ہیں
sindhiMeaning: سج سان محبت يا سج جي روشنيءَ سان لڳاءُ، سج جي روشني ۾ وقت گذارڻ يا ان مان توانائي حاصل ڪرڻ سان ظاهر ٿئي ٿو، انساني لحاظ سان اهو انهن ماڻهن لاءِ استعمال ٿئي ٿو جيڪي سورج جي روشني ۾ رهڻ پسند ڪن ٿا يا ان مان صحت ۽ خوشي محسوس ڪن ٿا
antonyms: Shade-loving, Photophobic, Sun-averse, Light-avoiding
synonyms: Sun-loving, Light-loving, Photophilic, Sun-seeking
englishMeaning: Love or preference for sunlight, tendency to seek or thrive in sunlight. The condition or inclination of organisms, especially plants and animals, to seek out sunlight for growth, energy, or comfort. It can also refer to humans who enjoy spending time in sunlight for health or pleasure.
examples: Sunflowers exhibit heliophilia by turning their heads toward the sun. The cat showed heliophilia, lounging in the warm sunlight all afternoon. People with heliophilia often go outside to enjoy sunny days. Certain plants display heliophilia to maximize photosynthesis.

englishMeaning: A person, animal, or organism that avoids sunlight, either due to fear, sensitivity, or discomfort. It is often used in psychology for humans or in biology for plants and animals sensitive to bright light.
antonyms: Helio friendly, Sun-loving, Sun-tolerant, Light-loving
sindhiMeaning: سج جي روشنيءَ کان ڊڄندڙ يا بچڻ وارو، جيڪو ماڻهو يا جاندار سج جي روشنيءَ کان ڊڄي يا ان کان پاسو ڪري، سج جي روشنيءَ کان بچڻ لاءِ سرگرميون بدلائي
examples: The heliophobic cat stayed indoors all day to avoid the sun. Some plants are heliophobic and grow better in shaded areas. His heliophobic tendencies made him prefer evening walks over daytime outings. The researcher studied heliophobic behaviors in certain desert animals.
urduMeaning: سورج کی روشنی سے خوف رکھنے والا یا بچنے والا، وہ شخص یا جاندار جو سورج کی روشنی سے ڈرتا ہو یا اس سے بچنے کی کوشش کرتا ہو روشنی کے سامنے آنے سے گریز کرتا ہو
synonyms: Sun-averse, Light-sensitive, Photophobic, Sun-shy

englishMeaning: A swelling or collection of blood outside blood vessels, usually caused by an injury. A localized collection of blood in tissues, organs, or under the skin due to the rupture of blood vessels. It often results from trauma, surgery, or medical conditions affecting blood clotting. The swelling may be painful, discolored, and can vary in size.
synonyms: Bruise, Contusion, Blood clot, Swelling
examples: The patient developed a large hematoma on his thigh after the fall. The doctor drained the hematoma to relieve the pressure. She noticed a small hematoma forming on her arm after the injection. Hematomas can sometimes resolve on their own without treatment.
urduMeaning: خون کا جماؤ، جسم کے اندر یا جلد کے نیچے خون کا ذخیرہ جو عموماً چوٹ یا خون جمنے کی بیماری کی وجہ سے ہوتا ہے، خون کی نالیوں کے پھٹنے کی وجہ سے جسم کے کسی حصے میں سوجن یا خون جمع ہونا
sindhiMeaning: رت جي ڳانڍاپي، رت جو ڳانڍاپو جيڪو زخمي ٿيڻ يا رت جي نالي سبب جسم ۾ جمع ٿئي، رت جي نالن جي ٽٽڻ سبب جسم جي ڪنهن حصي ۾ رت جو ڍڳ ٺهڻ
antonyms: Healing, Recovery, Normal tissue, Uninjured area

sindhiMeaning: هڪ طبي حالت جنهن ۾ رت صحيح نموني جمندو نه آهي، جنهن سبب ننڍن زخم کان به گهڻو رت وهندو آهي
antonyms: Normal clotting, Hemostasis, Blood clotting ability
englishMeaning: A genetic disorder in which a person’s blood lacks sufficient clotting factors. This results in prolonged bleeding after injuries, cuts, or surgery. Internal bleeding in joints and muscles is common in severe cases.
examples: He was diagnosed with hemophilia as a child and must avoid injuries. People with hemophilia need careful medical attention during surgeries. Severe hemophilia can cause spontaneous bleeding in joints. Advances in treatment have improved the life expectancy of those with hemophilia.
urduMeaning: ایک طبی حالت جس میں خون صحیح طریقے سے جم نہیں پاتا، جس کی وجہ سے معمولی چوٹ سے بھی زیادہ خون بہتا ہے
synonyms: Blood clotting disorder, Coagulopathy, Bleeding disorder

examples: The doctor applied pressure to achieve hemostasis after the surgery. Platelets play a crucial role in hemostasis. Hemostasis is vital to prevent excessive blood loss after an injury. The nurse monitored the patient to ensure proper hemostasis.
englishMeaning: The process that stops bleeding by clotting blood. Physiological process through which the body stops bleeding at the site of an injury. It involves blood vessel constriction, platelet aggregation, and the formation of a blood clot to prevent excessive blood loss.
synonyms: Blood clotting, Coagulation, Arrest of bleeding, Thrombostasis
urduMeaning: خون بہنے کو روکنے کا عمل، خون بہنے کو روکنے کا جسمانی عمل جس میں خون کی نالیوں کا سکڑنا پلیٹلیٹس کا جمع ہونا اور خون کا جمنے کے عمل شامل ہیں تاکہ خون زیادہ نہ بہے
antonyms: Hemorrhage, Bleeding, Blood loss, Exsanguination
sindhiMeaning: رت کي روڪڻ جو عمل، رت کي روڪڻ جو قدرتي عمل جنهن ۾ رت جون رڳون سکڙجن ٿيون پليٽليٽ گڏ ٿين ٿا ۽ رت جي ٿلهي جوڙجڪ ٿئي ٿي ته جيئن رت وهڻ بند ٿئي

sindhiMeaning: بيوقوفي سان کيڏڻ يا شرارت ڪرڻ، غير سنجيده رويو رکڻ، ڪو ماڻهو غير سنجيده شرارتي يا بيوقوفاڻو رويو اختيار ڪري، اڪثر اهو اهڙي وقت ٿيندو آهي جڏهن سنجيدگي ضروري هجي پر ماڻهو مذاق يا کل ڀوڳ ۾ لڳل هجي
examples: The teacher told the students to stop horsing around and focus on their work. They were horsing around in the playground and accidentally broke a window. Stop horsing around and listen carefully to the instructions. The kids love to horse around when no one is watching.
synonyms: Fool around, Mess around, Play around, Joke around, Act silly
englishMeaning: To behave in a silly, noisy, or playful way, often when you should be serious. Acting in a playful, careless, or foolish manner. It often involves joking, teasing, or rough play, especially in situations where such behavior is inappropriate, like in school, workplace, or during serious tasks.

synonyms: Encouraging, Persuasive, Advisory, Exhorting, Motivational
urduMeaning: نصیحت آمیز یا ترغیب دینے والا، ایسا اندازِ گفتگو یا تحریر جو لوگوں کو کسی کام کے لیے زور دے کر ابھارے یا اخلاقی رہنمائی دے
examples: The teacher gave a hortatory speech encouraging students to work honestly. His writing has a hortatory tone that urges social reform. The leader’s hortatory message inspired people to help the poor. The article was hortatory rather than informative.
englishMeaning: Giving strong encouragement or advice. Used for speech or writing that urges, advises, or encourages people to act in a particular moral or practical way. It often sounds persuasive and motivational rather than neutral.
sindhiMeaning: نصيحت ڪندڙ يا همٿائيندڙ، اهڙي ڳالهه يا لهجو جيڪو ماڻهن کي ڪنهن عمل لاءِ زور سان همٿائي يا اخلاقي طور رهنمائي ڪري
antonyms: Discouraging, Neutral, Critical, Dismissive, Indifferent

urduMeaning: کوئی شخص جسے مطالبات پورے کرنے یا دباؤ ڈالنے کے لیے قید کیا جائے
synonyms: Captive, Prisoner, Detainee, Pawn
examples: Three children were taken hostage during bank robbery. He was held hostage for almost a year. The rebels took several villagers as hostages. Negotiators worked to secure the hostage’s release. He was held hostage until the ransom was paid. The children were used as hostages during the conflict.
englishMeaning: A person who is captured and held prisoner by a person or group, and who may be injured or killed if people do not do what the person or group is asking.
sindhiMeaning: اغوا، يرغمال، باندي، مخصوص شرطن پورائي تائين قيد ڪيل شخص
antonyms: Free person, Liberated, Released

urduMeaning: سخت غصے میں آ جاتا یا کسی موقع پر شرمندگی محسوس کرتا
antonyms: Relaxed
sindhiMeaning: تمام گهڻو غصي ۾ اچي وڃڻ، شرمندگي سبب پريشاني محسوس ڪرڻ
examples: He got hot under the collar when his friend made fun of him. She was hot under the collar after being blamed for something she didn’t do. The manager became hot under the collar during the heated meeting. Don’t get hot under the collar; it was just a joke.
synonyms: Provoked
englishMeaning: Feeling very angry, annoyed, or embarrassed, especially because of something unfair, insulting, or frustrating.

sindhiMeaning: لامارا ڏيڻ، هوا ۾ هڪ هنڌ تي بيهڻ يا آهستي ويجهو گهمڻ، هوا ۾ بيحرڪ رهڻ يا اڏامندي هڪ هنڌ تي بيهڻ، ڪنهن جي ويجهو گهمڻ يا انتظار ڪرڻ، غير يقيني حالت ۾ رهڻ، ڪنهن سطح يا حالت تي قائم رهڻ، هوا ۾ هڪ هنڌ تي بيهڻ جو عمل، شڪ يا غير يقيني حالت
antonyms: Land, Settle, Drop, Depart, Move away, Movement, Action, Progress, Decision
examples: A hawk hovered over the hill. He hovered nervously in the doorway. Temperature hovered around freezing. A smile hovered on her lips. He hovered on the edge of consciousness. The bird remained in a hover above the lake. The drone held a steady hover for several minutes. His career is in a hover due to uncertainty.
synonyms: Float, Drift, Linger, Hang, Loiter, Suspension, Pause, Stillness, Hesitation
urduMeaning: ہوا میں ایک جگہ ٹھہرنا یا آس پاس منڈلانا، ہوا میں بغیر آگے بڑھے معلق رہنا، کسی کے قریب منڈلاتے رہنا یا انتظار کرنا، غیر یقینی حالت میں ہونا، کسی سطح یا حالت پر برقرار رہنا، ہوا میں ایک جگہ ٹھہرنے کا عمل، تذبذب یا غیر یقینی کی حالت
englishMeaning: To stay in one place in the air or move around slowly nearby. To remain floating in the air without moving forward. To stay close to a place or person, often waiting. To be uncertain or undecided. To remain at a particular level or position. The act of staying in one place in the air.

antonyms: Silence, Calm, Quiet, Peace, Stillness
sindhiMeaning: شور شرابو، افراتفري، هَنگامو، ڪيترائي ماڻهو هڪ ئي وقت ڳالهائين يا شور مچائين جنهن سان افراتفري يا هَنگامو پيدا ٿئي
examples: The marketplace was full of hubbub as vendors shouted to attract customers. She could hardly hear him over the hubbub of the party. The sudden hubbub in the street made everyone look outside. There was a hubbub of voices in the courtroom as the verdict was announced.
urduMeaning: ہلچل، شور، افرا تفری، بہت سے لوگ ایک ساتھ باتیں کر رہے ہوں یا شور مچا رہے ہوں، جس سے ایک افراتفری یا ہنگامہ پیدا ہو
synonyms: Commotion, Uproar, Clamor, Din, Racket, Turmoil
englishMeaning: A loud, confused noise; a commotion or uproar. A situation where many people are talking, shouting, or making noise at the same time, creating confusion or excitement. It can describe the noise in a busy place, a public event, or general clamor.

antonyms: Reject, Ignore
urduMeaning: چال سے حاصل کرنے کی کوشش کرنا، چالاکی سے کچھ حاصل کرنے کی کوشش کرنا، بالواسطہ طور پر کسی چیز کا طلبگار ہونا
synonyms: Scheme, Maneuver
englishMeaning: To try to get something by hinting, scheming, or using indirect methods, not asking directly, but trying to get it cleverly.
examples: He was angling for a promotion by praising the boss all the time. She kept asking about the project, clearly angling for more information. The journalist was angling for an exclusive interview. I think he’s angling for an invitation to the party. The politician was clearly angling for public sympathy.
sindhiMeaning: چال سان حاصل ڪرڻ، اشاري سان گهرڻ، ڪن ڳالهين يا فائدن کي سڌو نه پر چالاڪي سان يا اشارن ۾ حاصل ڪرڻ جي ڪوشش ڪرڻ

examples: There was a hue and cry when the government increased the taxes. The villagers raised a hue and cry after the robbery. A hue and cry was raised against the unfair treatment of workers. The media created a hue and cry over the environmental issues.
synonyms: Turmoil, Outburst
urduMeaning: شور و غوغا، واویلا، احتجاج، چیخ و پکار
englishMeaning: Loud protest. A loud public outcry. A strong protest or noisy reaction by many people often against something wrong, unfair, or alarming. It also refers to a public alarm or commotion raised to catch attention or draw action.
antonyms: Silence, Calm, Peace, Harmony
sindhiMeaning: احتجاجي شور، شديد احتجاج، واويلا، شور شرابو، آواز اٿارڻ

examples: After running up the stairs, he was huffing and puffing. She huffed and puffed at the meeting, complaining about the new rules. The old man huffed and puffed as he carried the heavy bag. Don’t just huff and puff; explain what the problem is.
englishMeaning: To breathe heavily or express anger, frustration, or effort. A person showing strong effort, often physically (like running or lifting something heavy), or expressing annoyance or impatience vocally. It often conveys exaggerated or noisy action.
urduMeaning: تھک کر ہانپنا، غصے میں شور مچانا، جسماني مشقت يا محنت بعد زور سے سانس لینا، کسی پر ناراضگی یا جھنجھلاہٹ ظاہر کرنا
synonyms: Pant, Gasp, Blow, Puff, Moan, Complain
antonyms: Relax, Calm down, Rest, Soothe
sindhiMeaning: ٿڪجي ۽ سسڪڻ، ڳڻتيءَ ۾ ڳڻڳڻ ڪرڻ، ناراضگي ظاهر ڪرڻ يا گهڻو شورو ڪرڻ، ڪنهن ڳالهه تي ڪاوڙ يا مايوسي ڏيکارڻ، زور زور سان شڪايت ڪرڻ
انسان دوستي، انساني همدردي، انساني ڀلائي جو نطريو، خلق جو خادم
urduMeaning: مذہب انسانیت کا پیرو
englishMeaning: Connected with helping people who are suffering and improving the conditions. A person who tries to help people who are suffering and improve the conditions that they are living in. Having or showing a concern for the welfare of others.
antonyms: Inhumane, Self-centered, Self-concerned, Selfish
synonyms: Compassionate, Beneficent, Benevolent, Charitable, Humane
examples: We will also do everything in our power to improve delivery of food, medicine, water, incredibly essential humanitarian needs. The actor and humanitarian took to the platform Friday to share a picture of a handwritten letter from a teenage girl in Afghanistan, according to the post's caption.

urduMeaning: مذہب انسانیت کا پیرو، انسانی بھلائی، ہمدردی یا انسانی حقوق کی بنیاد پر کیے جانے والے اقدامات یا فیصلے، یہ ایسے حالات میں استعمال ہوتا ہے جہاں انسانوں کی زندگی مدد یا فلاح و بہبود کو ترجیح دی جاتی ہے
sindhiMeaning: انسان دوست، انساني ڀلائيءَ متعلق، انساني ھمدرديءَ جي بنياد تي، اهو بنياد جيڪو انسانيت رحم يا انسانن جي ڀلائي تي ٻڌل هجي، اهو اهڙن فيصلن يا عملن لاءِ استعمال ٿئي ٿو جيڪي انساني زندگي کي بچائڻ مدد ڪرڻ يا سٺائي وڌائڻ جي مقصد سان ڪيا وڃن
antonyms: Legal ground, Political reason, Self-interest, Strict rule
englishMeaning: A reason or justification based on human welfare, compassion, or the need to help people. Refers to actions, decisions, or considerations made to protect, aid, or improve the wellbeing of humans, often in emergencies, conflicts, or situations of suffering. It emphasizes moral responsibility and human rights.
synonyms: Legal ground, Political reason, Self-interest, Strict rule
examples: They are calling for release of hostages on Humanitarian Grounds. The refugees were allowed to enter the country on humanitarian ground. She appealed to the court on humanitarian ground for the prisoner’s early release. Aid workers provide food and medical help on humanitarian ground during disasters. The government granted special permits on humanitarian ground to the injured victims.

englishMeaning: Boring, dull, routine, Lacking excitement, variety, or interest. Repetitive and boring due to routine. Dull and ordinary with nothing special. Monotonous in nature, especially daily life or work.
antonyms: Exciting, Interesting, Thrilling, Lively, Engaging
urduMeaning: بور/ پھیکا/ معمولی، بور کرنے والا جس میں کوئی دلچسپی نہ ہو، روزمرہ اور ایک ہی طرح کا، پھیکا اور غیر دلچسپ، یکسانیت کی وجہ سے اکتاہٹ پیدا کرنے والا، قابلِ پیش گوئی اور بغیر تبدیلی، تھکا دینے والا، بے جان اور بے اثر
sindhiMeaning: بيزار/ سستو/ هڪجهڙو، بيزار ڪندڙ جنهن ۾ ڪا دلچسپي نه هجي، روزمره جهڙو ۽ ورجاءُ وارو، سادو ۽ بي رنگ، هڪجهڙائي سبب بي مزو، اڳڪٿي لائق ۽ بنا تبديلي، ٿڪائيندڙ يا اوٻاڻو، بي جان يا بي روح
examples: His job became humdrum after doing the same tasks every day. She wanted to escape her humdrum routine and travel the world. The movie started well but turned humdrum in the middle. Life in the small town felt humdrum to him.
synonyms: Boring, Dull, Monotonous, Tedious, Routine

antonyms: Arrogance, Pride, Vanity, Conceit, Overconfidence
sindhiMeaning: نوڙت علم جي نشاني آهي، سچو عالم هميشه عاجز هوندو آهي، علم انسان کي نرم دل بڻائي ٿو، دانائي سان ادب ۽ نوڙت پيدا ٿيندي آهي، وڏائي اڻڄاڻائي جي نشاني ٿي سگهي ٿي
examples: The professor spoke kindly to every student because humility reflects knowledge. Despite his success, he remained polite and calm, proving that humility reflects knowledge. Great scientists often listen carefully to others because humility reflects knowledge. A wise leader understands mistakes and learns from them because humility reflects knowledge.
urduMeaning: عاجزی علم کی عکاسی کرتی ہے، حقیقی علم انسان کو جھکنا سکھاتا ہے، دانا انسان تکبر نہیں کرتا، علم کے ساتھ شائستگی آتی ہے، عاجزی سمجھدار انسان کی پہچان ہے
synonyms: Modesty shows wisdom, Wisdom brings humility, Knowledge creates modesty, True learning removes arrogance, Humble wisdom
englishMeaning: Wise people stay humble. Real education teaches respect. Knowledgeable people avoid arrogance. Learning develops modest behavior. Intelligence with humility earns respect.

sindhiMeaning: هڪ نرم ۽ ڪريمي کاڌو جيڪو چڻن تل جي پيسٽ زيتون جي تيل ليمون ۽ ٿوم مان ٺاهيو ويندو آهي، اهو عام طور تي ڊِپ يا اسپريڊ طور کائبو آهي
examples: I ate hummus with warm pita bread for lunch. She spreads hummus on her sandwich instead of butter. Hummus is a healthy snack rich in protein and fiber. They served hummus with fresh vegetables at the party.
englishMeaning: A smooth, creamy food made mainly from mashed chickpeas blended with tahini, olive oil, lemon juice, and garlic. It is commonly eaten as a dip or spread.
synonyms: Chickpea dip, Chickpea spread, Garbanzo bean paste, Middle Eastern dip
urduMeaning: ایک نرم اور کریمی غذا جو چنے تل کے پیسٹ زیتون کے تیل لیموں اور لہسن سے تیار کی جاتی ہے، یہ عموماً ڈِپ یا اسپریڈ کے طور پر استعمال ہوتی ہے
antonyms: There is no direct antonym

urduMeaning: روحانی اذیت یا تکلیف، شَديد دَرد يا بے چينی، عذاب ، بُری طَرَح اذيَت ميں ہونا، صدمہ، اچھا نہ لگنا ، بُرا لگنا
synonyms: Torture, Agony
examples: Tears of anguish filled her eyes. He suffered the anguish of watching his son go to prison.
englishMeaning: Extreme pain, distress, or anxiety. Severe physical or mental pain, difficulty or unhappiness.
antonyms: Apathy, Assurance, Pleasure
sindhiMeaning: سخت ڏک، سور، عذاب، ايذاءُ محسوس ڪرڻ يا ڪرائڻ، درد، سخت ذهني يا جسماني تڪليف

englishMeaning: Funny or amusing; causing laughter. Having or showing a sense of humor, able to make others laugh, playful in nature, amusing in a lighthearted way.
sindhiMeaning: خوش مزاجي، چرچائي، مزي جھڙو، کلائيندڙ، مذاق جي حِس رکندڙ
antonyms: Humorless, Unamusing, Uncomic
synonyms: Amusing, Funny, Cerebral
examples: She has a humorous way of telling stories that always makes us laugh. His humorous comments lightened the tense meeting. The movie was full of humorous scenes that kept everyone entertained. A humorous personality often helps in making friends easily.
urduMeaning: خوش طبع، مزاحیہ، ہنسی مذاق والا

sindhiMeaning: نباتياتي مٽي، نامياتي ڀاڻ، مٽي جو نامياتي زرخيز عنصر، زمين ۾ ڳريل نباتاتي مواد، مٽيءَ جو اهو زرخيز ۽ ڪارو نامياتي حصو جيڪو ٻوٽن پنن ۽ جاندارن جي گرڻ سڙڻ سان ٺهي ٿو، اهو مٽيءَ جي زرخيزي وڌائي ٿو پاڻي کي محفوظ رکي ٿو فائديمند جراثيمن جي واڌ ويجهه ۾ مدد ڪري ٿو ۽ ٻوٽن کي صحتمند وڌڻ ۾ سهارو ڏئي ٿو
antonyms: Mineral soil, Sand, Clay without organic content, Barren soil
englishMeaning: The rich, dark organic matter in soil that forms when plants, leaves, and animals decompose. It improves soil fertility, increases moisture retention, supports beneficial microorganisms, and helps plants grow stronger. Humus plays a key role in agriculture, forestry, and environmental sustainability.
examples: Farmers add compost to increase the humus content of the soil. Humus helps the soil retain water during dry seasons. Forest floors are rich in humus due to fallen leaves. The presence of humus improves soil structure and fertility.
synonyms: Organic matter, Compost, Leaf mold, Soil organic material
urduMeaning: تُراب، نباتی مٹی، نباتی کھاد، مٹی کا وہ زرخیز اور سیاہ نامیاتی حصہ جو پودوں پتوں اور جانداروں کے گلنے سڑنے سے بنتا ہے، یہ مٹی کی زرخیزی بڑھاتا ہےنمی کو محفوظ رکھتا ہے مفید جراثیم کی افزائش میں مدد دیتا ہے اور پودوں کی بہتر نشوونما میں اہم کردار ادا کرتا ہے

antonyms: Straighten, Stand upright, Extend, Certainty, Fact, Knowledge, Proof
sindhiMeaning: جسم اڳتي جھڪائڻ (خاص ڪري پٺ ۽ ڪلهن کي)، ٿوھو يا ڪُٻ ڪڍڻ، احساس جي بنياد تي فيصلو ڪرڻ، هڪ اڻڄاتل احساس يا اندازو بغير ڪنهن ثبوت جي، دٻاءُ يا پريشانيءَ ۾ جسم جي جھڪاءُ جي وضاحت ڪرڻ لاءِ استعمال ٿيندو آهي
examples: It seemed that the doctor's hunch had been right. I have a hunch that Jane likes me. My hunch is that the burglars are still in the area. Her hunches were confirmed the next day. I had a hunch that you might be here. We hunched round the fire to keep warm. She leaned forward, hunching over the desk. He hunched his shoulders and thrust his hands deep into his pockets.
urduMeaning: جسم کو آگے جھکانا (خاص طور پر کمر یا کندھوں کو)، جسم کا اوپری حصہ جھکانا، کسی چیز کے بارے میں بغیر ثبوت کے اندیشہ یا حدس، جسمانی جھکاؤ یا کمر کے موڑ کو دباؤ یا پریشانی کے اظہار کے لیے استعمال کیا جاتا ہے
synonyms: Bend, Stoop, Crouch, Lean forward, Intuition, Suspicion, Feeling, Guess, Inkling
englishMeaning: To bend your body forward, especially your back or shoulders. To make a decision based on instinct rather than facts. An intuitive feeling, guess, or suspicion without concrete evidence. The act of bending forward, often with shoulders or back rounded. Someone who looks worried or tense because of posture.

Everything is fine, satisfactory, or going well. A situation, condition, or state of affairs that is completely satisfactory, without problems, or proceeding smoothly. Often informal and conversational.
antonyms: Awry, Problematic, Bad, Troublesome, Off
sindhiMeaning: هر شيءَ ٺيڪ آهي، سڀ حالتون خوشگوار آهن، ڪابه پريشاني ناهي، ڪم يا زندگي سٺي ۽ آسان حالت ۾ آهي، سڀ ڪجهه ٺيڪ ۽ مطمئن ڪندڙ آهي
urduMeaning: سب کچھ بالکل ٹھیک ہے، کوئی مسئلہ نہیں، حالات خوشگوار ہیں، سب کچھ آسان اور مطمئن کن صورت میں ہے، ہر کام بغیر کسی رکاوٹ کے بہتر چل رہا ہے
examples: After fixing the car, everything was hunky dory. He thought the meeting went well and that everything was hunky dory. After a short argument, things were hunky dory between them. The project started with a few delays, but now it’s hunky dory.
synonyms: Fine, Okay, All right, Smooth, Satisfactory

urduMeaning: طوفانی آندھی، ہوا کا تیز چھکڑ، طوفان بادوباراں، تیز و تند ہوا، ہنگامہ برپا کر دینا، آندھی
sindhiMeaning: طوفان، واچوڙو، سامونڊي طوفان، وڏو سامونڊي واچوڙو
antonyms: Calm, Hush, Peace, Quiet, Quietude
englishMeaning: A violent storm with very strong winds, especially in the western Atlantic Ocean. A tropical cyclone with winds of 74 miles (119 kilometers) per hour or greater that is usually accompanied by rain, thunder, and lightning, and that sometimes moves into temperate latitudes. A state of noisy, confused activity.
synonyms: Cyclone, Tornado, Typhoon, Storm

examples: Child 1: You can’t run fast!, Child 2: I am rubber, you are glue. Your words stick to you, not me.
