examples: Great ideas often imperish even after centuries. His love for knowledge will imperish in every stage of life. Ancient traditions can imperish despite social changes. True friendships sometimes imperish through the hardest times.
synonyms: Endure, Last, Survive, Persist, Remain, Stay intact, Never fade

sindhiMeaning: پيوند ڪاري، پوکڻ، ڄمائڻ، ڪا شيءِ جڙڻ يا جسم ۾ لڳائڻ جو عمل، حياتيات ۾ ايمبريو جو رحم جي ڀتين سان ڳنڍجڻ
englishMeaning: The process of placing or embedding something in a fixed position. In medical and biological contexts, it often describes the stage in early pregnancy when the fertilized egg attaches to the lining of the uterus. It can also refer to inserting devices or objects into a body or system.
antonyms: Removal, Extraction, Detachment, Dislodgment
synonyms: Insertion, Embedding, Establishment, Fixation, Embedding
examples: The doctor explained the implantation of the pacemaker. Implantation of the embryo occurs a few days after fertilization. The company focused on the implantation of new safety protocols. Dental implantation can restore missing teeth effectively.
urduMeaning: اثر پذیری، دل نشینی، کسی چیز کو جسم یا کسی جگہ میں لگانے یا جڑنے کا عمل، حیاتیات میں بچہ دانی کی دیوار سے ایمبریو کا جڑنا

synonyms: Indicator, Sign, Suggestion, Implication source, Hint
englishMeaning: Something that indicates or suggests a meaning, conclusion, or relation without stating it directly. In logic and mathematics it can also mean a condition or expression that guarantees another statement is true.
examples: The statement acted as an implicant of a deeper political intention. In Boolean algebra, each implicant represents a condition that makes the function true. His silence became an implicant that something was wrong. The evidence served as an implicant of the larger theory.
sindhiMeaning: اهڙي شيءِ يا اظهار جيڪو ڪنهن ٻي ڳالهه ڏانهن اشارو ڪري، منطق ۾ اهڙو بيان جيڪو ڪنهن ٻئي بيان کي ظاهر ڪري، بولين الجبرا يا رياضي ۾ اهڙو اصطلاح جيڪو ڪنهن فنڪشن کي ظاهر ڪري، عام استعمال ۾ اهڙو اشارو يا سبب جيڪو لڪل مطلب ڏيکاري
urduMeaning: کوئی ایسی چیز یا اظہار جو کسی دوسری بات کی طرف اشارہ کرے، منطق میں ایسا بیان جو کسی دوسرے بیان کو ظاہر کرے، بولین الجبرا یا ریاضی میں ایسا جزو جو کسی فنکشن کو ظاہر کرے، عام زبان میں ایسا اشارہ یا عنصر جو کسی پوشیدہ مطلب کی طرف رہنمائی کرے
antonyms: Explicit statement, Direct expression, Clear declaration, Open explanation

englishMeaning: To indicate that a person is involved in a crime, fault, or harmful act. It can also mean that one thing is connected with or affected by another situation or problem. Sometimes it is used when evidence or statements suggest involvement even if it is not proven yet.
antonyms: Exonerate, Clear, Acquit, Disassociate, Defend
sindhiMeaning: ڦاسائڻ، ملوث ڪرڻ، شامل ڪرڻ، لاڳاپو ظاهر ڪرڻ، قصوروار ڏيکارڻ، ڪنھن شخص کي ڏوھ غلطي يا نقصان ڏيندڙ عمل سان لاڳاپيل ظاهر ڪرڻ، ڪنھن شيء جو ڪنھن مسئلي يا صورتحال سان تعلق يا اثر ڏيکارڻ ڀلي مڪمل ثبوت موجود نه هجي
urduMeaning: پھانسنا، ملوث کرنا، شامل کرنا، تعلق ظاہر کرنا، قصوروار ٹھہرانا ، کسی شخص کو جرم غلطی یا نقصان دہ عمل میں ملوث ظاہر کرنا، کسی چیز کا کسی مسئلے یا صورتحال سے گہرا تعلق ظاہر کیا جائے چاہے مکمل ثبوت ابھی موجود نہ ہو
examples: The evidence may implicate several officials in the corruption case. He refused to say anything that might implicate his friend. The report implicates poor planning in the failure of the project. Her statement seemed to implicate the manager in the mistake.
synonyms: Incriminate, Involve, Connect, Associate, Link

examples: The implication was obvious. This rule has major implications. He understood the implication of the decision. The statement carried a serious implication.
synonyms: Consequence, Suggestion, Indication
sindhiMeaning: اشارو، پوشيده مطلب، نتيجو، شموليت، اثر، ڪو مطلب يا خيال سڌي طرح بيان نه ڪيو وڃي پر ڳالهه مان اشارو ملي، اهو ڪنهن عمل جو ممڪن نتيجو يا اثر به ٿي سگهي ٿو يا ڪنهن معاملي ۾ شامل ٿيڻ جو مطلب به ڏيکاري سگهي ٿو
englishMeaning: Something suggested indirectly rather than stated clearly. It can also mean a possible result or effect of an action, or involvement in a situation especially something negative such as a crime or problem.
antonyms: Clarity, Certainty
urduMeaning: اشارہ، پوشیدہ مطلب، نتیجہ، شمولیت، اثر، وہ مطلب جو براہ راست نہ کہا جائے بلکہ بات کے انداز سے ظاہر ہو، یہ کسی عمل کا ممکنہ نتیجہ یا اثر بھی ہو سکتا ہے یا کسی معاملے میں شمولیت کو بھی ظاہر کرتا ہے

synonyms: Facelessness, Namelessness, Nowhere, Nowheresville, Obscurity
examples: Names of people in the book were changed to preserve anonymity. The anonymity of the city (= where people do not know each other). The person donating the money insisted on complete anonymity. Some people prefer the anonymity of life in a big city.
sindhiMeaning: گمنامي، بي نالي هجڻ يا لڪيل سڃاڻپ جي حالت، اهڙي حالت جنهن ۾ ڪنهن جو نالو يا سڃاڻپ ظاهر نه ڪئي وڃي ته جيئن رازداري يا حفاظت برقرار رهي
urduMeaning: گمنامی، بے نام ہونے کی حالَت یا صُورَت، بے نامی، گُمنام باشی، جس کی کوئی پہچان نہ ہو
antonyms: Celebrity, Fame, Notoriety, Renown
englishMeaning: The state of remaining unknown to most other people. The quality or state of being mostly or completely unknown.

examples: The old submarine imploded under the pressure of deep water. The company began to implode after years of internal conflict. His plans imploded when the funding was suddenly withdrawn. The building was designed to implode safely during demolition.
synonyms: Collapse, Cave in, Fall in, Crash, Break down
englishMeaning: To collapse inward with force, often suddenly. To fail suddenly (figurative, for example ideas or organizations). To self-destruct (common in technical or mechanical context). To shrink violently inward (physical). To experience a sudden loss of stability or structure (emotional or social).
urduMeaning: ذہنی یا جذباتی طور اندر ہی اندر ٹوٹ جانا، ذہنی یا جذباتی طور اندر ہی اندر ٹوٹ جانا، اندرونی اختلاف کی وجہ سے اچانک ناکام ہو جانا، کسی چیز کو اندر کی طرف گرا کر تباہ کرنا، اندر پھٹنا، اچانک ناکامی، اندر سے ٹوٹ جانا، خود کو تباہ کرنا، غیر متوقع نقصان
antonyms: Explode, Expand, Rise, Succeed, Strengthen
sindhiMeaning: ذهني يا جذباتي طور اندر ئي اندر ٽٽي وڃڻ، دٻاءَ سبب اندر طرف ويهي وڃڻ، اندروني اختلاف يا ڪمزوري سبب اوچتو ختم ٿي وڃڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ کي اندر طرف ڀڃي تباهه ڪرڻ، اندر ڌوٻڻ، ڀڃڻ، ٽٽڻ، اندر کان ڦاٽڻ، اڻڄاتل تباهي، اوچتو ناڪامي

englishMeaning: Persistent, sometimes annoying, requests or demands, the quality of asking again and again with urgency.
antonyms: Reluctance, Hesitation, Indifference, Shyness, Modesty
sindhiMeaning: بار بار ضد ڪرڻ، زور ڀرڻ، اصرار سان گهرڻ، زور لائڻ، اصرار ڪرڻ، ليلائڻ
examples: I finally took what he offered me to save myself from his importunities. Despite his importunity, she refused to change her decision. The beggar’s importunity made the passerby uncomfortable. With increasing importunity, they demanded political power to match their economic power. Finally, she rose and opened the door to her sister's importunities.
urduMeaning: بار بار ضد کرنا، اصرار، ہٹ دھرمی سے مانگنا، تقاضا ، ضِد ، اڑ ، ابرام ، اِصرار آمیز معروضات، چڑچڑا پن
synonyms: Persistence, Insistence, Pleading, Urging, Demanding, Solicitation

sindhiMeaning: رکڻ، مٿان مڙهڻ يا وجهڻ، لاڳو ڪرڻ، عائد ڪرڻ، تي مڙهڻ، ڍل ٻڌڻ، مُسلط ڪرڻ، تعميل تي اصرار ڪرڻ، محصول، فرض، الزام يا ذميداري مُڙهڻ
urduMeaning: ذمے کرنا، مجبور کرنا، عائد کرنا ، نافَذ کرنا ، لگانا ، اِختیّار کے ذریعے مُقرر کرنا، تھوپنا، لاگو کرنا ، لازم کرنا
antonyms: Diminish, Remit
synonyms: Assess, Charge
englishMeaning: To introduce a new law, rule, tax, etc To order that a rule, punishment, etc be used. To force somebody, something to have to deal with something that is difficult or unpleasant. To establish or apply as a charge or penalty.
examples: A new tax was imposed on fuel. The time limits are imposed on us by factors outside our control.

englishMeaning: Someone who forces rules, taxes, duties, or authority on others. A person who imposes something on others, often in an authoritative or burdensome way. This could include laws, taxes, rules, or personal demands, usually without consent.
urduMeaning: تھوپنے والا، وہ شخص جو دوسروں پر قواعد، ٹیکس، ذمہ داریاں یا مطالبات زبردستی عائد کرتا ہے
antonyms: Liberator, Reliever, Helper, Permitter
sindhiMeaning: لاڳو ڪندڙ، اهو شخص جيڪو ٻين تي پابنديون، قانون، ٽيڪس يا ذميواريون زور زبردستي لاڳو ڪري ٿو
synonyms: Enforcer, Dictator, Controller, Taxer, Authoritarian
examples: The government acted as an imposer of new taxes. He felt like an imposer when he forced his opinions on everyone. History remembers him as an imposer of strict rules. No one likes an imposer who controls every little detail.

synonyms: Confiscate, Seize, Detain, Take over
urduMeaning: قانونی اختیار کے تحت کسی چیز کو ضبط کرنا، قانون یا سرکاری اختیار کے تحت کسی چیز جیسے گاڑی، سامان یا جانور کو اپنے قبضے میں لے لینا ہے، عموماً قانون کی خلاف ورزی کی وجہ سے
examples: The police decided to impound the car due to unpaid fines. The city can impound animals that are found wandering on the streets. His bike was impound after repeated traffic violations. Authorities may impound illegal goods at the border.
englishMeaning: To officially take and keep something, usually by authority. To take possession of property, vehicles, documents, or animals by legal or official authority, often because of a rule violation or for safety reasons.
sindhiMeaning: اختيار سان ڪا شيءِ ضبط ڪرڻ، قانوني يا سرڪاري اختيار هيٺ ڪنهن شيءِ جهڙوڪ گاڏي، سامان يا جانور کي پنهنجي قبضي ۾ وٺڻ، عام طور تي ضابطن جي ڀڃڪڙي سبب
antonyms: Release, Return, Free, Hand back

examples: The long war impoverished the country and destroyed its economy. Heavy taxes can impoverish small businesses. Cutting down forests impoverishes the soil. Corruption has impoverished the nation’s resources.
englishMeaning: To make someone poor. To make something weaker or less rich (in quality, strength, or resources).
synonyms: Drain, Exhaust, Bankrupt, Deplete, Weaken
antonyms: Enrich, Strengthen, Empower
sindhiMeaning: بي وسيلو ڪرڻ، غريب ڪرڻ، ڪمزور ڪرڻ، مال دولت يا وسيلن کان محروم ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: غریب کرنا ، مفلس بنانا ، کمزور کرنا، مال و دولت یا وسا ئل سے محروم کر نا
ناقابلِ تسخیر، جسے فتح یا توڑا نہ جا سکے، ایسا قلعہ مقام یا خیال جسے دشمن فتح نہ کر سکے یا جسے توڑنا ناممکن ہو، صرف قلعوں تک محدود نہیں بلکہ مضبوط دلائل نظریات یا پوزیشن کے لیے بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے
antonyms: Vulnerable, Defenceless, Weak, Breakable, Exposed, Assailable
synonyms: Unassailable, Invincible, Fortified, Secure, Unbreakable, Unconquerable
sindhiMeaning: ناقابلِ تسخير، جيڪو فتح يا ٽوڙڻ ناممڪن هجي، اهڙو مضبوط قلعو جاءِ يا خيال جيڪو دشمن لاءِ فتح ڪرڻ يا نقصان پهچائڻ ناممڪن هجي، صرف فوجي يا جسماني حفاظت تائين محدود ناهي پر مضبوط خيالن ۽ دليلن لاءِ به استعمال ٿئي ٿو
englishMeaning: Impossible to defeat, capture, or enter; very strongly defended. Something, especially a fortress, position, or argument, that is so strong or well protected that it cannot be attacked, entered, or defeated successfully. Often used figuratively for ideas, beliefs, or arguments that cannot be disproved. Can describe emotional or mental strength that cannot be easily broken.
examples: The castle was built on a mountain, making it impregnable to enemy attacks. He presented an impregnable argument that no one could refute. The army believed their base was impregnable, but it was eventually breached. Her logic was so strong that her position remained impregnable in the debate.

antonyms: Realism, Naturalism, Academic art, Detailed classical painting
sindhiMeaning: هڪ اهڙي فن تحريڪ جنهن ۾ ڪنهن منظر جي تفصيل بدران روشني ۽ رنگن جا تاثر ڏيکاريا ويندا آهن، اڻويهين صدي ۾ فرانس ۾ شروع ٿيل هڪ فن تحريڪ آهي، هن ۾ مصور منظر کي ان لمحي جيئن نظر اچي ٿو تيئن ڏيکارڻ جي ڪوشش ڪندا آهن خاص طور تي روشني ۽ قدرتي رنگن تي ڌيان ڏنو ويندو آهي
englishMeaning: An art movement that focuses on capturing the visual impression of a moment, especially the effects of light and color, rather than detailed realism. A style of painting developed in the 19th century, mainly in France. Artists try to capture how a scene looks at a particular moment, especially how light changes its appearance. The focus is on quick brush strokes, natural light, and everyday scenes instead of precise details.
synonyms: Impressionist art, Impressionistic style, Modern art movement, Real-time painting style (contextual)
urduMeaning: ایک فنِ مصوری کی تحریک ہے جس میں کسی منظر کی اصل تفصیل کے بجائے روشنی اور رنگوں کے اثر کو دکھایا جاتا ہے، انیسویں صدی میں فرانس میں شروع ہونے والی ایک فنِ مصوری کی تحریک ہے، اس میں فنکار کسی منظر کو اس وقت جیسا نظر آتا ہے ویسا دکھانے کی کوشش کرتے ہیں خاص طور پر روشنی کے اثرات کو، اس میں باریک تفصیلات کے بجائے تیز برش اسٹروکس اور قدرتی مناظر دکھائے جاتے ہیں
examples: Impressionism changed the way artists painted light and shadow. Monet is famous for his contribution to Impressionism. The museum has a large collection of Impressionism artworks. Impressionism focuses more on feeling than on fine detail.

synonyms: Spontaneous, Extemporaneous, Unplanned, Offhand, Ad-lib
englishMeaning: Unplanned or spontaneous. Done without being planned, prepared, or rehearsed. Spontaneous or improvised action or speech. Occurring suddenly, often unexpectedly.
examples: She gave an impromptu speech at the ceremony. We had an impromptu meeting to discuss the urgent issue. The musician played an impromptu melody for the audience. His impromptu jokes kept everyone laughing all evening.
urduMeaning: فوری یا بغیر تیاری کے کیا گیا، اچانک انجام دیا گیا، بغیر منصوبہ بندی کے
sindhiMeaning: اوچتوبنا تياريءَ جي، ڪنهن ڪم کي فوري طور تي تيار نه ٿيڻ باوجود انجام ڏيڻ، فوري طور تي ڪيل ڪارڪردگي، بنا تياريءَ جي، اچانڪ ڪيو ويو، اچانڪ طور تي
antonyms: Planned, Rehearsed, Prepared, Deliberate

examples: She had to improvise a speech when the projector failed. During the power outage, we improvised by using candles. The musician improvised a beautiful melody on the piano. He improvised a solution using the tools he had on hand.
englishMeaning: To make or perform something spontaneously without preparation. To create, arrange, or perform something on the spot, using available resources rather than following a plan or script. Often used in music, speech, acting, or problem-solving.
sindhiMeaning: عارضي حل ڪڍڻ، موجوده وسيلن سان ڪم کي فوري طور تي حل ڪرڻ، اڳواٽ منصوبابندي کان سواءِ ڪم ڪرڻ، فوري طور تي تخليقي طريقو اختيار ڪرڻ
synonyms: Ad-lib, Extemporize, Invent, Make do
antonyms: Plan, Prepare, Design, Rehearse
urduMeaning: عارضی حل نکالنا، موجود وسائل سے فوری طور پر کسی کام کو انجام دینا، غیر منصوبہ بندی کے تحت کسی کام کو سنبھالنا، فوری طور پر تخلیقی طریقہ اختیار کرنا

englishMeaning: The act of making something anonymous by removing identifying information. The process of removing or changing personal information from data so that an individual cannot be identified. It is commonly used to protect privacy in research, medical records, surveys, and digital platforms.
urduMeaning: کسی کی شناخت چھپا دینا یا ختم کرنا، کسی شخص کی ذاتی معلومات جیسے نام پتہ شناختی نمبر وغیرہ کو ریکارڈ یا ڈیٹا سے ہٹا دینا یا تبدیل کرنا تاکہ اس کی شناخت ظاہر نہ ہو سکے، یہ عمل رازداری اور پرائیویسی کی حفاظت کے لیے کیا جاتا ہے
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن جي سڃاڻپ لڪائڻ يا ختم ڪرڻ، ڪنهن ماڻهو جي ذاتي ڄاڻ جهڙوڪ نالو پتو سڃاڻپ نمبر وغيره کي ڊيٽا مان هٽائڻ يا تبديل ڪرڻ ته جيئن ان جي سڃاڻپ ظاهر نه ٿئي، هي عمل رازداري جي حفاظت لاءِ ڪيو ويندو آهي
antonyms: Identification, Disclosure, Revelation, Exposure, Personalisation
synonyms: Data masking, Identity concealment, Privacy protection, Obscuring identity
examples: The hospital uses anonymization to protect patient records. Social media platforms often perform anonymization on user data before sharing with advertisers. Researchers applied anonymization to the survey results to ensure participants’ privacy. Anonymization of emails prevented tracing back to the original sender.

urduMeaning: ذہنی طور پر اچانک ابھرنے والی تحریک جو انسان کو فوراً عمل کرنے پر مجبور کرے، مختصر وقت کے لیے لگنے والی قوت جو کسی جسم کی حرکت کو بدل دے، برقی توانائی کا مختصر سگنل یا جھٹکا، بغیر منصوبہ بندی کیا گیا اچانک فیصلہ
englishMeaning: A sudden mental urge that pushes a person to act quickly, often without logical thinking. A spontaneous decision made without planning. A force applied over a short time that changes the motion of an object. A short electrical signal or burst of energy.
antonyms: Restraint, Control, Caution, Hesitation, Deliberation
synonyms: Urge, Instinct, Desire, Drive, Motivation
examples: He struggled to control his aggressive impulses. It was just an impulse trip to the beach. The impulse from the bat sent the ball flying. The device sends an impulse to activate the motor. His first impulse was to run away from the problem. Acting on impulse can sometimes lead to regret. The sudden impulse of wind closed the door loudly.
sindhiMeaning: اوچتو ذهني اُڀار جيڪو ماڻهو کي فوري عمل ڪرڻ تي مجبور ڪري، ٿوري وقت لاءِ لڳندڙ زور جيڪو شيءِ جي حرڪت بدلائي ڇڏي، بجليءَ جو مختصر سگنل يا توانائيءَ جو جھٽڪو، بنا منصوبابندي ڪيل اوچتو فيصلو

englishMeaning: Something that makes a substance or situation not pure or clean. Any foreign, harmful, or unwanted element mixed into something that reduces its purity, quality, or moral goodness.
urduMeaning: ناپاکی، کوئی بھی غیر ضروری یا نقصان دہ چیز جو کسی چیز کی پاکیزگی یا خلوص کو خراب کرے
antonyms: Purity, Cleanliness, Innocence, Wholesomeness, Refinement
synonyms: Contamination, Pollution, Adulteration, Defilement, Taint
sindhiMeaning: ناپاڪ شيءِ، ڪا به اهڙي شيءِ يا مادو جيڪو پاڪ صاف يا خالص حالت کي خراب ڪري
examples: The water contained chemical impurities that made it unsafe to drink. Gold is valuable, but its price drops when impurities are present. Moral impurity is often discussed in religious and ethical teachings. The factory was fined for releasing impurities into the air.

synonyms: In short, Briefly, To sum up, In summary, In essence
urduMeaning: مختصر اور سادہ انداز میں اصل بات بیان کرنا، یہ روزمرہ گفتگو اور تحریر میں استعمال ہوتا ہے جب کسی بات کا خلاصہ پیش کرنا ہو، کسی لمبی یا تفصیلی بات کو بہت کم اور آسان الفاظ میں بیان کر نا، اصل بات کو مختصر کر دینا
englishMeaning: In a very short and simple way; summarizing the main point. It is often used in spoken and written English to quickly summarize arguments, reports, stories, or ideas. Used when someone wants to express the main idea of something using very few words, leaving out extra details. It is often used when summarizing long explanations.
examples: In a nutshell, the meeting was about budget cuts. She explained the whole story in a nutshell. In a nutshell, we need more time to finish the project. The movie, in a nutshell, is about friendship and sacrifice.
sindhiMeaning: مختصر طور تي يا ٿورن لفظن ۾ سموري ڳالهه بيان ڪرڻ، روزمره ڳالهه ٻولهه ۽ لکڻين ۾ استعمال ٿيندو آهي جڏهن ڪنهن ڳالهه جو نچوڙ ٻڌائڻو هجي، ڪنھن ڊگهي ڳالهه يا تفصيل کي ٿورن ۽ سادن لفظن ۾ بيان ڪرڻ، اصل مطلب کي مختصر طور پيش ڪرڻ
antonyms: In detail, At length, Thoroughly, In full explanation, Expanded form

sindhiMeaning: تمام سٺي صحت ۾، بهترين حالت ۾، مڪمل صحت ۾ هجڻ، بهترين حالت ۾ هجڻ يا جسماني ۽ ذهني طور بهترين حالت ۾ هجڻ، اهو ڪنهن شيءِ جي اعليٰ معيار يا مڪمل حالت لاءِ به استعمال ٿيندو آهي
examples: After regular exercise, he felt in a pink of health. The athlete was in a pink before the final match. She looked in a pink after recovering from illness. The garden is in a pink during the spring season.
synonyms: In good health, Fit as a fiddle, In top form, In excellent condition
urduMeaning: بہت اچھی صحت میں، بہترین حالت میں، بہترین صحت میں ہونا، مکمل طور پر ٹھیک حالت میں ہونا یا جسمانی اور ذہنی طور پر اعلیٰ حالت میں ہونا، یہ کسی چیز کے بہترین معیار کے لیے بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے
antonyms: In poor health, Sick, Weak, Unwell
englishMeaning: In excellent health or perfect condition. An old-fashioned idiom that means being in very good health, excellent condition, or at one’s best state physically or mentally. It can also refer to something being in perfect form or top quality.

examples: She keeps popping in and out. People kept drifting in and out of the meeting. He kept going in and out of the room during the meeting. After years of work, she knows the ins and outs of the business. The patient has been in and out of the hospital this year. I’ll just be in and out, it won’t take long.
englishMeaning: To go inside and outside often, or to know something completely. Moving or going inside and outside a place repeatedly or quickly. Being familiar with all details of something (when used as “the ins and outs”). Describing something done quickly and efficiently. Sometimes used to mean changing status frequently
synonyms: Back and forth, To and fro, Coming and going, Familiar with, Aware of
sindhiMeaning: پوري حقيقت، پوري ڪهاڻي، اندر ٻاهر اچڻ وڃڻ يا ڪنهن شيءِ جي مڪمل ڄاڻ رکڻ، (ڪڏهن ڪڏهن حالت بدلجڻ لاءِ پڻ استعمال ٿيندو آهي)
antonyms: Steady, Stationary, Unfamiliar, Fixed
urduMeaning: اندر باہر آنا جانا یا مکمل واقفیت ہونا، کسی چیز یا معاملے کے تمام پہلوؤں کو جاننا (بعض اوقات حالت یا کیفیت کے بدلنے کے لیے بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے)

antonyms: Reveal, Disclose, Expose, Identify, Uncover
englishMeaning: To remove personal or identifying details from something such as data, documents, or records so that the person it refers to cannot be recognized or identified. To make something anonymous.
sindhiMeaning: گمنام ڪرڻ، سڃاڻپ لڪائڻ، نالو لڪائڻ، اهو عام طور تي رازداري يا حفاظت لاءِ ڪيو ويندو آهي
synonyms: Conceal, Disguise, Obscure, Hide, Mask, De-identify
examples: We anonymize the data so researchers cannot identify any individual subjects. The company anonymized all customer records before sharing them for research. Journalists often anonymize their sources to protect their identities. The survey data was anonymized to ensure participants' ants’ privacy. He anonymized the file so no one could trace it back to him.
urduMeaning: شناخت مٹانا ، گمنام بنانا، یہ عام طور پر رازداری برقرار رکھنے کے لیے کیا جاتا ہے

antonyms: Mercifully, in hot blood, passionately, emotionally, impulsively, kindly
urduMeaning: ایسا عمل جو پوری سوچ سمجھ کے، بغیر کسی جذبے یا رحم کے کیا جائے
sindhiMeaning: اهڙو عمل جيڪو سوچي سمجهي، بي احساسيءَ ۽ بي رحميءَ سان ڪيو ويو هجي
examples: The murderer killed the victim in cold blood. The soldiers attacked the village in cold blood. He betrayed his best friend in cold blood. The crime was committed in cold blood, showing no sign of mercy.
englishMeaning: To act without emotion, pity, or mercy, especially when doing something cruel or violent. It describes doing something calmly and deliberately, not out of passion or anger.
synonyms: Cruelly, deliberately, cruelly, callously, heartlessly

sindhiMeaning: مشڪل ۾ هجڻ، مصيبت ۾ پئجي وڃڻ، تڪليف يا ڏکي صورتحال ۾ هجڻ، مصيبت ۾ پئجي وڃڻ
antonyms: Safety, Ease
urduMeaning: مشکل میں ہونا ، مصیبت میں پھنس جانا، دقت میں
synonyms: Trouble, Difficulty
englishMeaning: To be in trouble, difficulty, or a problematic situation, often because of something you have done wrong.
examples: He forgot his wedding anniversary, and now he’s in hot water with his wife. The student is in hot water for cheating on the exam. She got in hot water at work for missing an important meeting. The company found itself in hot water after breaking environmental laws.

After a good year, the company is in the black. After years of hard work, the company is finally in the black. His business stayed in the black even during the recession. They worked hard to get out of debt and back in the black. By cutting unnecessary expenses, the organization remained in the black.
urduMeaning: مالی طور پر مستحکم، منافع میں ہونا، قرض سے آزاد ہونا
sindhiMeaning: مالي طور تي بهتر، منافعو حاصل ڪرڻ وارو، قرض کان آزاد
synonyms: Profitable, Solvent
antonyms: Bankrupt, Insolvent, In debt, In the red
englishMeaning: Being financially sound, profitable, or not in debt. To be financially stable or making a profit.

sindhiMeaning: وقت جي پوري ٿيڻ تي، مناسب وقت تي، جڏهن وقت پورو ٿيندو، هر ڪم پنهنجي وقت تي ٿيندو آهي جلدبازيءَ ۾ نه
urduMeaning: وقت کے پورا ہونے پر ، مناسب وقت پر ، جب وقت آجائے گا، ہر کام اپنے وقت پر ہوتا ہے جلدی کی ضرورت نہیں
englishMeaning: Something will happen eventually, when circumstances are ready, not immediately. An event will occur at the proper time, in due course, or as things naturally develop, often with patience or destiny involved. After a suitable or natural amount of time has passed, or when the right or destined time comes.
antonyms: Immediately, Right away, Instantly, At once, Without delay
synonyms: In due course, Eventually, Sooner or later, At the right time, When the time is ripe, In the long run
examples: In the fullness of time, they realized that the decision had been the right one. The truth will come out in the fullness of time. In the fullness of time, she achieved everything she had dreamed of. You will understand the reason for this change in the fullness of time.

urduMeaning: نقصان میں ہونا،قرض میں ہونا
examples: The shop is in the red and may close soon. The company has been in the red for three years due to poor sales. After paying all the bills, I realized my account was in the red. The shop went in the red during the off-season. He borrowed money to keep his business from going in the red.
synonyms: Losing money, Insolvent, Overdrawn
englishMeaning: To owe money or be in financial loss. Being in debt or having spent more money than you have. It is often used for people, businesses, or organizations whose expenses are greater than their income.
antonyms: Financially stable, In the black
sindhiMeaning: نقصان ۾ هئڻ، قرض ۾ هئڻ، مالي ڏک ۾ هئڻ

synonyms: In the same situation, Sharing the same fate, Facing the same problem
englishMeaning: To be in the same difficult situation as someone else; sharing the same problem, risk, or challenge.
examples: We’re all in the same boat here. Since the company is losing money, all employees are in the same boat. Don’t worry, you’re not alone, we’re all in the same boat. Both students failed the test, so they’re in the same boat now. During the flood, the whole village was in the same boat, struggling for food and shelter.
urduMeaning: ایک ہی مسئلے میں پھنسے ہونا، ایک ہی کشتی میں ہونا، یک ہی جیسی مشکل یا پریشانی میں مبتلا ہونا
antonyms: In a different position, Unaffected, Safe from the problem
sindhiMeaning: ساڳئي مشڪل ۾ هجڻ، ساڳئي ٻيڙيءَ ۾ هجڻ، هڪجهڙي تڪليف، خطري يا حالتن ۾ هجڻ

بي عملي، بي حرڪتي، خاموشي، لاپرواهي، ڪو به قدم نه کڻڻ، حرڪت نه ڪرڻ، ڪنهن معاملي ۾ خاموش ۽ بي عملي اختيار ڪرڻ جتي عمل ڪرڻ ضروري هجي، اهو لفظ اڪثر انهن حالتن لاءِ استعمال ٿيندو آهي جتي ڪنهن جي بي عملي سان نقصان يا مسئلو وڌي وڃي
antonyms: Action, Activity, Effort, Movement, Diligence, Initiative, Responsiveness
synonyms: Idleness, Passivity, Inactivity, Negligence, Apathy, Indifference, Dormancy
urduMeaning: غیر فعالیت ، سستی ، بے عملی ، عدم حرکت، کوئی عمل نہ کرنا، خاموش یا غیر متحرک رہنا، خاص طور پر جب کسی عمل کی ضرورت ہو، یہ لفظ اُن حالات کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے جہاں کسی کی بے عملی نقصان کا سبب بنتی ہے
englishMeaning: Lack of action. A state of doing nothing when action is needed. It refers to failure to act, idleness, or absence of effort, especially when action could prevent a problem.
examples: The manager’s inaction during the crisis caused serious losses. Environmental problems are getting worse because of public inaction. His inaction showed that he was afraid to take responsibility. The country suffered due to the leaders’ inaction on important reforms.
The money was donated by an anonymous benefactor. Police said an anonymous caller warned that a bomb was about to go off. I'm not prepared to give credence to anonymous complaints.
sindhiMeaning: گمنام، نامعلوم، مجهول، بي نام، اڻ ڄاتل، مجهول، اڻ سڃاتل، غير معروف
urduMeaning: گمنام، نا معلوم، خفیہ، بے پہچان، بغیر شناخت
synonyms: Unidentified, Obscure, Unknown, Unnamed, Unspecified
antonyms: Known, Identified, Famous, Recognized, Named
englishMeaning: A person whose name is not known or not made public. Something done without revealing the identity of the doer. A work such as a book or letter published without the writer’s name. Lacking unique features, ordinary or not distinctive.

antonyms: Sufficiency, Adequacy, Competence, Completeness, Capability
sindhiMeaning: ڪمي، نامڪمل هجڻ، ڪنهن ڪم يا معيار کي پورو ڪرڻ ۾ ناڪامي، ڪافي نه هجڻ، ڪمي محسوس ڪرڻ جو حال
englishMeaning: Lack of the quality or quantity needed; insufficiency. A state of being insufficient, incomplete, or not good enough to meet a requirement, expectation, or standard.
examples: The inadequacy of the public transport system makes commuting difficult. She felt a sense of inadequacy when comparing herself to her peers. The report highlighted the inadequacy of the safety measures in the factory. His inadequacy in handling finances led to serious problems.
urduMeaning: کمی، ناکافی ہونا، کسی کام معیار یا ضرورت کو پورا کرنے میں ناکامی یا غیر کافی ہونا
synonyms: Insufficiency, Deficiency, Shortcoming, Lack, Weakness, Incompleteness

englishMeaning: Not focusing the mind on a matter. Done by accident, without being intended.
urduMeaning: غافل، بے پروا، غیر ارادی، حادثاتی، بغیر قصد کے
antonyms: Deliberate, Intended, Intentional, Planned
synonyms: Unintentional, Fortuitous, Incidental, Unintended
sindhiMeaning: غافل، بي پرواه، بي خيالو، بي فڪر، بي ڌيانو، غير ارادي، اتفاقي، بي ارادي ٿيل
examples: All authors need to be wary of inadvertent copying of other people's ideas. He made an inadvertent mistake on the report. The email was sent inadvertently to the wrong person. Her comment caused inadvertent offense. They inadvertently revealed the secret.

sindhiMeaning: بي خياليءَ سان، غفلت سان، غفلت وچان، نادانيءَ ۾، غلطي سان، بي ڌياني ۾، اڻ ارادي طور، اڻ ڄاڻائيءَ ۾، بي ڌيانيءَ سان، ڪو ڪم بنا ارادي يا بغير ڌيان جي ٿي وڃڻ
englishMeaning: By accident, without intention. Doing something without planning or without realizing it. Unintentionally, accidentally, unknowingly, carelessly.
antonyms: Deliberately, Intentionally, Purposely, Knowingly
synonyms: Accidentally, Unintentionally, Unknowingly, Mistakenly, Carelessly
urduMeaning: غلفت سے، غیر ارادی طور پر، انجانے میں، نادانستہ طور پر، غلطی سے، بے دھیانی میں، کسی کام کا غیر ارادی طور پر یا بغیر سوچے سمجھے ہو جانا
examples: He inadvertently deleted the important file. She inadvertently revealed the secret during conversation. I inadvertently left my keys at home. The teacher inadvertently skipped one question.

The authorities decided to incarcerate the criminal for ten years. Many activists were incarcerated during the political unrest. He felt that the strict rules incarcerated his creativity. The government promised not to incarcerate minor offenders unnecessarily.
synonyms: Imprison, Detain, Jail, Confine, Intern
urduMeaning: کسی شخص کو قانونی سزا کے طور پر جیل یا بندش میں رکھنا، آزادی سے محروم کرنا، کسی کو محدود یا قید میں رکھنا، خیالات یا جذبات کو قید کرنا جیسے ذہنی یا جذباتی پابندی

englishMeaning: To put someone in prison or confine them. To confine a person, typically as a punishment for a crime, by placing them in prison or another form of detention. It implies legal or enforced restriction of freedom.
antonyms: Release, Free, Liberate, Emancipate

sindhiMeaning: آغاز، شروعات، ابتدا، منڍ، تمھيد، شروع ٿيڻ جو عمل، ڪنهن شيءِ جي شروع ٿيڻ جو مرحلو، ڪنهن خيال منصوبي يا اداري جي بنياد رکڻ يا ابتدا ٿيڻ
englishMeaning: Beginning or start of something. The point at which something begins or originates. It refers to the establishment, founding, or first stage of an idea, project, organization, or process.
antonyms: End, Conclusion, Finish, Termination, Closure
synonyms: Beginning, Start, Origin, Commencement, Initiation, Foundation
urduMeaning: شروع، آغاز، شروعات، ابتد، نقطہ آغاز، کسی چیز کے شروع ہونے کا مرحلہ، کسی خیال منصوبے یا ادارے کی بنیاد یا ابتدا
examples: The company has grown rapidly since its inception. From the inception of the project, she was involved. The idea was successful from its inception. The school has improved a lot since its inception in 2010.

The plan was still inchoate and needed more discussion. His ideas about climate policy were inchoate but promising. The movement remained inchoate due to lack of leadership. She expressed an inchoate feeling of concern she could not explain.

urduMeaning: نامکمل، ایسی چیز جو شروع ہو چکی ہو مگر ابھی مکمل، واضح یا پوری طرح تیار نہ ہوئی ہو
synonyms: Incomplete, Immature, Unformed, Rudimentary, Incipient
antonyms: Complete, Finished, Fully developed, Mature, Perfected
sindhiMeaning: اڻپورو، ڪا اهڙي شيءِ جيڪا شروع ته ٿي آهي پر اڃا مڪمل يا واضح نه ٿي آهي

englishMeaning: To burn something completely until it turns into ashes. To destroy something, especially waste or unwanted material, by burning it at a very high temperature so that nothing remains except ash
examples: The city built a new plant to incinerate hospital waste safely. The rebels incinerated the captured documents before retreating. The spacecraft was incinerated as it entered the Earth’s atmosphere. All infected material was carefully incinerated to prevent the spread of disease. The fire incinerated everything in its path, leaving only ashes.
synonyms: Cremate, Destroy, Annihilate
antonyms: Extinguish
urduMeaning: کسی چیز کو مکمل طور پر جلا دینا تاکہ وہ راکھ بن جائے (جیسے فضلہ یا پرانے کاغذات کو جلانا)
sindhiMeaning: مڪمل طور تي ساڙڻ، راک ۾ تبديل ڪرڻ (مثلاً: ڪا شيءِ مڪمل طور تي باهه سان ختم ٿي وڃي)

englishMeaning: The act of including or being included within a group or structure. The practice or state of ensuring that people, ideas, or elements are accepted, valued, and integrated within a group, organization, or society. It emphasizes participation, belonging, and equality.
synonyms: Integration, Incorporation, Acceptance, Involvement, Participation
sindhiMeaning: شموليت، شامل ڪرڻ جو عمل، ڪنهن گروپ يا سرگرمي ۾ حصو وٺڻ
examples: The school promotes inclusion of students from all backgrounds. Inclusion of everyone in decision-making leads to better outcomes. The policy focuses on inclusion of disabled employees in the workforce. Cultural inclusion helps build a more tolerant society.
antonyms: Exclusion, Rejection, Segregation, Omission
urduMeaning: شمولیت، کسی گروپ یا نظام میں شامل ہونا، سب کو برابر طور پر شامل کرنا

examples: The school has an inclusive curriculum that caters to students with different learning needs. The conference was inclusive, welcoming participants from all countries. Their vacation package is inclusive of meals, travel, and accommodation. The policy aims to create an inclusive workplace where everyone feels valued.
englishMeaning: Including all parts, groups, or elements. Not excluding anything. Something that is comprehensive and takes everything or everyone into account. Often used in social, financial, or organizational contexts to indicate openness, acceptance, or coverage.
synonyms: Comprehensive, All-encompassing, Embracing, Open, Broad, Universal
sindhiMeaning: سڀني کي شامل ڪرڻ وارو، ڪنهن شيءِ يا گروهه ۾ سڀني حصن ماڻهن يا عنصرن کي شامل ڪرڻ، جيڪو ڪنهن کي به خارج نه ڪري
antonyms: Exclusive, Limited, Restrictive, Selective
urduMeaning: شامل کرنے والا، ایسا جو ہر فرد گروہ یا جزو کو شامل کرے اور کسی کو خارج نہ کرے، استعمال عام طور پر سماجی تعلیمی یا مالی سیاق میں ہوتا ہے

examples: The package is priced inclusively, covering all meals and activities. The school plans its curriculum inclusively to accommodate students with different needs. She spoke inclusively, making sure everyone felt welcome in the discussion. The report was written inclusively, considering all relevant data points.
englishMeaning: In a way that includes everything or everyone. Actions, policies, or approaches that incorporate all members, elements, or aspects without excluding anyone or anything.
synonyms: Comprehensively, Entirely, Wholly, Collectively
urduMeaning: شامل طور پر، سب کچھ شامل کرتے ہوئے، اس طرح سے جو سب افراد چیزیں یا پہلو شامل کرے، کسی کو خارج نہ کرے
sindhiMeaning: سڀني کي شامل ڪندي، گڏيل طور تي، اهڙي انداز ۾ جيڪو سڀني ماڻهن شين يا پهلوئن کي شامل ڪري، ڪنهن کي الڳ نه ڪري
antonyms: Exclusively, Partially, Selectively, Narrowly

englishMeaning: The quality of being impossible or very difficult to understand. Something too complex for the mind to process easily. Lack of clarity in speech, writing, or ideas. antonyms: Comprehensibility, Clarity, Understandability, Simplicity, Transparency, Intelligibility
synonyms: Unintelligibility, Obscurity, Confusion, Complexity, Unclear nature, Opacity
urduMeaning: ناقابل فہم ہونے کی حالت، یعنی جسے سمجھنا بہت مشکل ہو، ایسی کیفیت جس میں کوئی بات یا چیز سمجھ میں نہ آئے یا بہت زیادہ پیچیدہ اور الجھی ہوئی ہو
examples: The incomprehensibility of the ancient text made translation very difficult. Scientists discussed the incomprehensibility of quantum behavior to the general public. A person who secretly enters a place or group to gather information or cause harm. Someone who deliberately and quietly gains access to an organization, area, or system without permission, often pretending to belong there, usually for spying, sabotage, or criminal purposes.
examples: The army captured an infiltrator near the border late at night. The infiltrator pretended to be an employee to access confidential files. Security cameras revealed the movements of an infiltrator inside the building. The novel revolves around an infiltrator working within the enemy camp.

examples: The teacher gave us an anthology of modern English poetry. I enjoy reading a short story anthology before sleeping. The library has a new anthology of African writers. She published an anthology of her favorite essays.

urduMeaning: مختلف مصنفین کی منتخب کردہ نظمیں کہانیاں یا تحریریں جو ایک کتاب میں جمع ہوں، ایک ایسی کتاب یا مجموعہ جس میں مختلف مصنفین کی منتخب شدہ نظمیں کہانیاں یا تحریریں شامل کی جاتی ہیں جو کسی خاص موضوع یا انداز کے تحت مرتب کی جاتی ہیں

synonyms: Creativity, Inventiveness, Cleverness, Resourcefulness, Originality
examples: The engineer showed great ingenuity in designing a low-cost water filter. Her ingenuity helped the team overcome unexpected challenges. The child's ingenuity turned old boxes into a makeshift playhouse. Scientists rely on ingenuity to develop new technologies.
englishMeaning: The quality of being clever, original, and inventive. The ability to think creatively, solve problems in clever ways, and come up with original solutions. It highlights mental skill and inventiveness.
sindhiMeaning: ذهانت، نواڻ، تخليقيت، عقل ۽ سمجھداري سان مسئلا حل ڪرڻ جي صلاحيت، تخليقي سوچ ۽ جدت وارو دماغ
urduMeaning: ذہانت، اختراع، جدت، کسی مسئلے کا سمجھداری سے حل نکالنے کی صلاحیت، تخلیقی سوچ اور نیا پن
antonyms: Stupidity, Dullness, Ineptitude, Unoriginality, Ignorance

englishMeaning: To firmly establish or embed something, especially an idea, habit, or belief. To cause something to become deeply fixed or rooted so that it is difficult to change. It can refer to habits, beliefs, skills, or qualities that are deeply embedded in a person or system.

sindhiMeaning: ڳنڍيل، ڄميل، ڪنهن شيءِ کي گهرو يا مضبوط طريقي سان انساني يا ذهني طريقي ۾ وجھڻ جيئن عادتون راءِ يا قدرون
synonyms: Embed, Implant, Instill, Root, Establish
examples: Good manners were ingrained in her from childhood. These beliefs are deeply ingrained in the culture. The training aims to ingrain safety habits in employees. Fear of failure was ingrained in him after repeated setbacks.

antonyms: Grateful person, Thankful person, Appreciative person, Obliged person
sindhiMeaning: احسان نه مڃيندڙ ماڻهو، ناشڪرگذار، احسان فراموش، ناشڪرو، بي شناسو، نمڪ حرام، اڻ وڻندڙ، نا شڪرو، ڳڻ جوڙ، بي قدر ماڻهو
englishMeaning: A person who is not thankful for kindness or help received. Someone who fails to show gratitude after receiving support, favor, kindness, or generosity. Such a person may ignore, deny, or even resent the help given to them. The word is usually used in a negative sense to criticize someone's ungrateful behavior.
examples: After all the support she gave him, he proved to be an ingrate. The teacher felt hurt when the student behaved like an ingrate. Only an ingrate would complain after receiving so much help. He was called an ingrate for ignoring his parents' sacrifices.
synonyms: Ungrateful person, Thankless person, Inappreciative person, Ungrateful individual
urduMeaning: نمک حرام، ناشکر گزار، ناشُکرا ، ناسپاس، بے قدر انسان، احسان فراموش فرد، شکر ادا نہ کرنے والا شخص

synonyms: Flatter, Charm, Court, Please, Win over
urduMeaning: کسی کے دل میں اپنی جگہ بنانے کے لیے خوشامد کرنا یا پسندیدہ بننا، کوشِش کر کے دُوسروں کی خُوشنودی حاصِل کرنا ، دل میں گھر کرنا

She ingratiated herself with the new boss by offering help on every project. He quickly ingratiated himself into the social circle by telling jokes and compliments.
sindhiMeaning: پاڻ کي ڪنهن جي دل ۾ خوش ڪرڻ لاءِ محبت يا تعريف ڏيکارڻ، دل ۾ جاءِ حاصل ڪرڻ، مقبول ۽ منظور ٿيڻ
englishMeaning: To try to gain someone's favor by flattering or pleasing them. To deliberately try to make oneself liked or accepted by someone, often through flattery or by doing things to please them
antonyms: Alienate, Offend, Repel, Insult
Whole, Entirety, Complete, Finished product
englishMeaning: A component or element that is part of a mixture, recipe, or combination. Any substance or element that is combined with others to form a whole, such as in cooking, chemical mixtures, or abstract compositions like plans or ideas. It can refer to both tangible items like food and intangible aspects like qualities or factors. A contributing factor in a situation. Part of a formula or mixture. A feature that helps produce a result.
sindhiMeaning: جزو، مواد، عنصر، سامان جو حصو جيڪو گڏيل شيءَ ۾ شامل ھجي، اهڙو عنصر جيڪو نتيجو پيدا ڪري، فارمولي يا مرکب جو جزو، صورتحال جو حصو
examples: Sugar is an essential ingredient in making cakes. Honesty is a key ingredient for a strong friendship. This medicine contains natural ingredients. Creativity is an important ingredient in successful marketing.
urduMeaning: جزو، مواد، عنصر، کسی مرکب یا نسخے میں شامل چیز، ایسا عنصر جو نتیجہ پیدا کرے، نسخہ یا مرکب میں استعمال ہونے والا جزو، کسی حالت یا نتیجے میں شامل حصہ
synonyms: Component, Element, Constituent, Part, Factor
Restraint, Control, Suppression, Shyness, Constraint
examples: Fear can create inhibition and stop people from speaking openly. Alcohol lowered his inhibition and made him talk more freely. Social inhibition often affects people in large gatherings. The drug works by inhibition of harmful enzymes.

englishMeaning: A feeling or condition that prevents someone from doing or expressing something freely. An internal or external restraint that limits behavior, emotions, thoughts, or actions. It can be psychological, social, emotional, or biological. In psychology, it often means the ability to control impulses. In science, it refers to a process that slows down or prevents a reaction or activity.
sindhiMeaning: اهڙو احساس يا رڪاوٽ جيڪا ماڻهو کي کلي طرح ڪم ڪرڻ يا ڳالهائڻ کان روڪي، سماجي يا جذباتي رڪاوٽ جيڪا انسان جي روين جذبن يا عملن کي محدود ڪري، نفسيات ۾ هي خود ضابطو ظاهر ڪري ٿي جڏهن ته سائنس ۾ ڪنهن عمل کي سست يا روڪڻ واري عمل لاءِ استعمال ٿيندي آهي

urduMeaning: مخالف، دشمنانہ، نقصان دہ،
sindhiMeaning: دشمناڻو، نقصانڪار، غير دوستاڻو يا مخالف رويي وارو
examples: His actions were inimical to progress. His inimical attitude towards change slowed down the progress of the project. Too much heat is inimical to the growth of delicate plants. They faced an inimical environment full of hostility and resistance. Lack of sleep is inimical to good health.

antonyms: End, Stop, Conclude, Terminate, Close

examples: She showed great initiative by organizing the meeting herself. Employees who take initiative often succeed in their careers. The government launched a new initiative to improve education. Taking initiative can help you stand out from others.
urduMeaning: خود سے قدم اٹھانے یا پہل کرنے کی صلاحیت، کسی عمل یا مقابلے میں پہلا قدم یا ابتدائی کارروائی، پیش قدمی ، پہلا قدم

sindhiMeaning: پاڻ مرادو قدم کڻڻ يا اڳواڻي ڪرڻ جي صلاحيت، ڪنهن عمل يا مقابلي ۾ پهريون قدم يا شروعاتي ڪارروائي، شروع ڪرڻ جو اختيار، اڳڀرائي
antonyms: Inactivity, Passiveness, Laziness, Hesitation, Dependence

synonyms: Vaccinate, Immunize, Inject, Protect, Infuse
sindhiMeaning: ٽيڪو هڻڻ، جسم ۾ ويڪسين يا جراثيم جي ٿوري مقدار داخل ڪرڻ ته جيئن مدافعتي نظام مضبوط ٿئي ۽ بيماري کان بچاءُ ملي، ڪنهن کي خراب اثرن کان بچائڻ لاءِ اڳواٽ ٿورو آگاهه ڪرڻ يا ذهن ۾ خيال ويهارڻ، زمين يا ٻوٽن ۾ خاص جراثيم داخل ڪرڻ ته جيئن سٺو نتيجو حاصل ٿئي
examples: The nurse inoculated the child against measles. Farmers inoculate seeds with beneficial bacteria before planting. The teacher tried to inoculate students against false information. Scientists inoculated the plants to study disease resistance.

To protect someone from harmful ideas or influences by exposing them to a mild form of them. Also to plant a belief or idea in someone’s mind. To introduce microorganisms into soil, plants, or laboratory cultures to produce a specific effect.
urduMeaning: ٹیکا لگانا ، جسم میں ویکسین یا جراثیم کی تھوڑی مقدار داخل کرنا تاکہ مدافعتی نظام مضبوط ہو جائے اور بیماری سے بچاؤ حاصل ہو، کسی کو نقصان دہ اثرات سے بچانے کے لیے پہلے سے آگاہ کرنا یا ذہن میں کوئی خیال بٹھانا، زمین یا پودوں میں مخصوص جراثیم شامل کرنا تاکہ مطلوبہ نتیجہ حاصل ہو
antonyms: Infect, Contaminate, Expose, Harm

The eagerly anticipated movie will be released next month. We need someone who can anticipate and respond to changes in the fashion industry. We eagerly anticipated the day we would leave school. When Scott reached the South Pole he found that Amundsen had anticipated him.

The child received inoculation against polio at the clinic. Farmers use seed inoculation to improve crop yield. Early inoculation can prevent serious infections. The teacher used logical arguments as an inoculation against misinformation.
urduMeaning: بیماری سے بچاؤ کے لیے جسم میں ویکسین یا مادہ داخل کرنے کا عمل، مٹی پودوں یا لیبارٹری کلچر میں جراثیم شامل کرنا تاکہ نشوونما یا سائنسی تحقیق کی جا سکے، کسی کو نقصان دہ خیالات سے بچانے کے لیے ان کا ہلکا اظہار پہلے کر دینا

sindhiMeaning: بيماري کان بچاءَ لاءِ جسم ۾ ويڪسين يا دوا داخل ڪرڻ جو عمل، مٽي ٻوٽن يا ليبارٽري ڪلچر ۾ جراثيم شامل ڪرڻ ته جيئن واڌ ويجهه يا سائنسي جاچ ڪئي وڃي، ڪنهن کي نقصانڪار خيالن کان بچائڻ لاءِ انهن جو هلڪو روپ اڳ ۾ ڏيکارڻ

Protecting someone from harmful ideas by exposing them to a weaker form of those ideas.
