urduMeaning: کسی چیز کے ہونے کی پیشگی امید یا انتظار کی کیفیت، آنے والے واقعے کے بارے میں جذباتی انتظار، مستقبل کی ضرورت کے لیے پہلے سے انتظام کرنا، مقررہ وقت سے پہلے رقم حاصل کرنا یا بندوبست کرنا
antonyms: Surprise, Unawareness, Indifference, Doubt

examples: The mistake seemed insignificant, but it later caused serious problems. He felt insignificant in a crowd of famous scientists. The cost increase was so insignificant that most customers did not notice it. A small and insignificant detail helped the detective solve the case.
urduMeaning: حقیر، معمولی، کم اہم، ناچیز، غیر اہم یا بہت معمولی، کسی ایسی چیز شخص واقعہ یا مقدار کے لئے بولا جاتا ہے جس کی اہمیت اثر یا قدر بہت کم ہو اور جسے زیادہ توجہ نہ دی جائے
sindhiMeaning: حقير، معمولي، ننڍڙي اهميت وارو، نظرانداز لائق، غير اهم يا تمام ننڍڙي اهميت وارو، اهڙي شيء شخص واقعي يا مقدار لاءِ استعمال ٿئي ٿو جنهن جي ڪا خاص اهميت اثر يا قدر نه هجي ۽ جنهن کي عام طور نظرانداز ڪيو وڃي
synonyms: Trivial, Minor, Negligible, Petty, Unimportant, Inconsequential
antonyms: Significant, Important, Major, Meaningful, Influential
englishMeaning: Something very small, unimportant, or not worthy of attention. Used for a person, thing, event, or amount that has little value, influence, effect, or importance. It may refer to something too minor to be noticed or considered meaningful.

urduMeaning: اہمیت کو کم کرنا، بے معنی بنانا، کسی چیز کی اہمیت یا قدر کو گھٹانے کا عمل جس سے وہ معمولی یا غیر اہم محسوس ہو جائے
englishMeaning: The act of making something seem unimportant or meaningless. The process or action of diminishing the importance, value, or significance of something. It often implies rendering something trivial or without weight in a particular context.
antonyms: Significance, Importance, Value, Weight
synonyms: Trivialization, Belittlement, Depreciation, Diminishment
examples: The constant criticism led to the insignification of his achievements. Social media can cause the insignification of serious issues through trivialization. The teacher’s harsh words resulted in the insignification of her student’s efforts. Bureaucracy often causes the insignification of citizens’ complaints.
sindhiMeaning: اھميت گهٽائڻ، بي معنيٰ بڻائڻ، ڪنھن کي اھميت قيمت يا اثر کان خالي ڪرڻ اھڙي طريقي سان جيڪو ان کي معمولي يا غير اهم محسوس ڪرائي

urduMeaning: بے ذائقہ، پھیکا، بے لطف، ایسی چیز جس میں ذائقہ یا دلچسپی نہ ہو
antonyms: Flavorful, Exciting, Interesting, Lively
englishMeaning: Lacking taste, interest, or excitement. Describes food, speech, writing, or behavior that is dull, bland, or without strong flavor or emotion
synonyms: Bland, Dull, Tasteless, Uninteresting
sindhiMeaning: بي ذائقو، بي مزو، ڦڪو، اهڙي شيءِ جنهن ۾ ذائقو يا دلچسپي نه هجي
examples: The soup was insipid and needed more spices. His speech sounded insipid and failed to impress the audience. She found the movie insipid despite its strong cast. An insipid conversation can quickly drain interest.

The student gave an insolent reply to the teacher. His insolent tone angered everyone in the meeting. She was punished for her insolent behavior at work. The guard did not tolerate insolent remarks from visitors.
sindhiMeaning: بدتميزي ۽ بي ادبي سان ڀرپور، اهڙو رويو يا ڳالھ ٻولھ جيڪا بي ادبي، غرور يا وڏائي سان ڪئي وڃي، خاص ڪري وڏن يا اختيار وارن ماڻهن سان
englishMeaning: Rude and disrespectful in speech or behavior. Showing a lack of respect, often in a bold or arrogant way, especially toward someone older or in authority.
synonyms: Rude, Impolite, Disrespectful, Arrogant, Cheeky
antonyms: Polite, Respectful, Courteous, Humble, Well mannered
urduMeaning: بدتمیز اور بے ادب، ایسا رویہ یا اندازِ گفتگو جس میں گستاخی، تکبر یا بے ادبی ہو، خاص طور پر بڑوں یا اختیار رکھنے والوں کے ساتھ

synonyms: Provoke, Incite, Encourage, Trigger, Spark, Stir up
urduMeaning: اکسانا، آمادہ کرنا، تحریک کرنا، کسی عمل جھگڑے یا ردعمل کو شروع یا بھڑکانا، کسی ردعمل یا واقعے کو جنم دینا، لوگوں کو کسی کام پر اکسانا، فساد یا تنازع پیدا کرنا، کسی کو اکسانا یا کسی عمل فساد جھگڑے یا ردعمل کو شروع کروانا
examples: The leader tried to instigate the crowd to protest. He was accused of instigating violence during the rally. Don’t instigate arguments between friends. Someone instigated the fight outside the school. The were accused of instigating racial violence. The govt has instigated a program of economic reform.
sindhiMeaning: ورغلائڻ، ڀرکائڻ، ڪن ڀرڻ، چورڻ، ڇيڙڻ، ڪنهن عمل يا جهيڙي کي شروع ڪرڻ يا ڀڙڪائڻ، ڪنهن ردعمل يا واقعي کي شروع ڪرڻ، ماڻهن کي ڪنهن ڪم لاءِ اڀارڻ، فساد يا اختلاف پيدا ڪرائڻ، ڪنهن کي اڀارڻ يا ڪنهن عمل جهيڙي يا مسئلي کي شروع ڪرائڻ لاءِ اثرانداز ٿيڻ
englishMeaning: To start, encourage, or provoke something, especially something negative like conflict or action. To deliberately cause something to happen, especially by provoking, urging, or encouraging others to take action. It is often used in situations involving conflict, protest, violence, or strong reactions.
antonyms: Calm, Deter, Prevent, Suppress, Discourage

urduMeaning: فطری عمل، جِبَلّی، خُود بخُود ، صلاحیت یا ردعمل جو انسان یا جانور میں پیدائشی طور پر موجود ہو یہ سیکھنے یا مشق کا نتیجہ نہیں ہوتا بلکہ قدرتی طور پر ظاہر ہوتا ہے، جیسے خطرہ محسوس ہوتے ہی فوراً پیچھے ہٹ جانا
antonyms: Learned, Acquired, Deliberate, Planned, Intentional
englishMeaning: Something done because of an inner feeling, not logic. A natural ability to do something well without formal learning. A quick reaction driven by feelings rather than careful thought. Actions that living beings perform because they are born with the tendency to do so.
sindhiMeaning: فطري، ذاتي، سڀاويڪ، طبعي، خاصيت يا عمل جيڪو انسان يا جانور جي اندر ڄمڻ سان گڏ موجود هوندو آهي اهو سکڻ يا تجربو ڪرڻ سان پيدا نه ٿيندو پر قدرتي طور تي ظاهر ٿيندو آهي، جيئن خطري وقت فوراً بچاءَ ڪرڻ
examples: His instinctive reaction was to protect his younger sister. Birds have an instinctive ability to build nests. She made an instinctive decision to trust him. The goalkeeper made an instinctive save during the match.
synonyms: Inborn, Natural, Innate, Automatic, Intuitive

examples: The mountain was insurmountable without proper equipment. She thought the problem was insurmountable, but she solved it. The team faced an insurmountable challenge during the match. Poverty can sometimes seem insurmountable.
englishMeaning: Impossible to overcome or solve. A problem, difficulty, obstacle, or challenge that cannot be overcome, defeated, or solved, even with effort. It suggests something extremely hard or impossible to manage.
synonyms: Unbeatable, Impossible, Overwhelming, Unconquerable, Unmanageable, Formidable
urduMeaning: جسے عبور کرنا یا حل کرنا ناممکن ہو، بہت بڑی یا سخت مشکل، قابو سے باہر مسئلہ، ناقابل حل رکاوٹ، ایسی مشکل رکاوٹ یا مسئلہ ہوتا ہے جس پر قابو پانا یا اسے حل کرنا ممکن نہ ہو
antonyms: Surmountable, Possible, Easy, Solvable, Manageable, Conquerable
sindhiMeaning: جنهن کي پار يا حل ڪرڻ ناممڪن هجي، تمام وڏو يا سخت مسئلو، جيڪو ڪنٽرول کان ٻاهر هجي، جنهن کي ختم ڪرڻ ڏکيو هجي، ان حالتن لاءِ استعمال ٿئي ٿو جتي ڪا رڪاوٽ مسئلو يا مشڪل ايتري وڏي هجي جو ان کي ختم ڪرڻ يا پار ڪرڻ ممڪن نه هجي

اهڙو جيڪو هٿ سان ڇهي يا ڏسي نه سگهجي، جيڪي مادي صورت ۾ نه هجن، اهي هٿ سان ڇهي يا اکين سان ڏسي نٿا سگهجن، انهن جو اثر محسوس ڪري سگهجي ٿو، واضح طور بيان نه ٿي سگهندڙ جهڙوڪ محبت عزت ڀروسو آزادي ۽ شهرت، ماپڻ يا ڳڻڻ ۾ ڏکيو، جذباتي يا خيالي نوعيت جو
englishMeaning: Something that cannot be touched, seen, or physically measured. Things that have no physical form. These can be ideas, feelings, qualities, rights, or values. Although they cannot be physically touched, they can strongly influence people and situations. Examples include love, reputation, trust, and freedom.
examples: Trust is an intangible asset in any relationship. Happiness is intangible but deeply important in life. The company values intangible qualities like honesty and loyalty. Cultural heritage includes many intangible traditions and beliefs.
synonyms: Abstract, Immaterial, Invisible, Spiritual, Nonphysical, Ethereal
antonyms: Tangible, Physical, Concrete, Visible, Material
urduMeaning: ایسا جو چھوا یا دیکھا نہ جا سکے، جن کی مادی شکل نہ ہو، انہیں نہ چھوا جا سکتا ہے اور نہ آنکھوں سے دیکھا جا سکتا ہے، ان کا اثر محسوس کیا جا سکتا ہے جیسے محبت عزت اعتماد آزادی اور شہرت، واضح طور پر بیان نہ کیا جا سکے، ناپنا یا گننا مشکل، جذباتی یا تصوراتی نوعیت کا

antonyms: Derivative, Extrinsic, Fractional
urduMeaning: تمام، کامل، پورا، جُزو تکمیلی ، جُزو لازِم، عدد صحیح
englishMeaning: Being an essential part of something. Included as part of something, rather than supplied separately. Having all the parts that are necessary for something to be complete. Constituting a whole together with other parts or factors, not omittable or removable.
examples: Music is an integral part of the school's curriculum. The unit comes complete with integral pump and heater. He's an integral part of the team and we can't do without him.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ڪُل جو جُزو يا لازمي جز، ڪامل، سالم، سڄو، پورو، صحيح، ڪامل، عدد، مجموعي، جملي، ڪل عدد، لازمي، ضروري، مڪمل
synonyms: Necessary, Immanent, Inherent

sindhiMeaning: دانشور، فڪر ڪندڙ شخص، علم وارو ماڻهو، ذهني، فڪري، عقلي، سوچ ۽ علم سان واسطو رکندڙ
urduMeaning: دانشور، مفکر، علم و فکر رکھنے والا شخص، ذہنی، فکری، عقلی، سوچنے سمجھنے اور علم سے تعلق رکھنے والا
synonyms: Rational, Logical, Analytical, Brainy, Educated, Scholarly, Thoughtful
examples: She is known for her intellectual discussions about politics and society. Reading books regularly helps develop intellectual skills. The conference brought together many intellectuals from around the world. His intellectual approach to problem-solving impressed everyone.
antonyms: Uneducated, Ignorant, Illogical, Emotional, Simple-minded
englishMeaning: A person who uses their mind for study, reflection, and analysis, often interested in ideas, culture, and knowledge. Related to the ability to think deeply, understand ideas, and use reasoning rather than emotion.

antonyms: Ignore, Neglect, Forget, Disregard, Hesitate
synonyms: Plan, Aim, Mean, Purpose, Decide, Resolve, Design, Propose
urduMeaning: ارادہ کرنا، نیت کرنا، منصوبہ بنانا، کسی کام کے لیے پہلے سے ارادہ یا نیت رکھنا، کسی مقصد یا انجام تک پہنچنے کے لیے سوچنا
englishMeaning: To have a plan, purpose, or aim. To mean or want to do something. To have a clear purpose or decision in your mind to do it, even if you haven’t done it yet.
sindhiMeaning: ارادو رکڻ، نيت ڪرڻ، منصوبو ٺاهڻ، سوچڻ ته ڪجهه ڪرڻو آهي، ڪنهن ڪم لاءِ ذهن ۾ ارادو رکڻ، اڳواٽ فيصلي سان ڪجهه ڪرڻ جي نيت رکڻ
examples: I intend to finish my homework tonight. She intends to become a doctor. They didn’t intend to hurt your feelings. We intend to travel next summer.

englishMeaning: Existing in an extreme degree. Having or showing a characteristic in extreme degree. Exhibiting strong feeling or earnestness of purpose.
synonyms: Anxious, Ardent
examples: The president is under intense pressure to resign. He is very intense about every thing. She dislikes him intensely. She is prepared to carry out her threat to resign. She had an intent look on her face.
sindhiMeaning: سخت، تمام گهڻو، بي حد، تکو، گهڻو شوخ
antonyms: Dull, Mild,
urduMeaning: تیز، شدید، سخت، زیادہ، بہت، گرم، حساس

synonyms: Aim, Purpose, Goal, Plan, Objective, Motive, Design
examples: Her intention was to help the poor, not to gain fame. He went there with the intention of meeting his old friend. I had no intention of hurting your feelings. Good intentions are not enough without actions.
urduMeaning: ارادہ ، نیت ، مقصد، کسی کام کو کرنے کا ذہنی فیصلہ
englishMeaning: A plan, aim, or purpose that shows what someone wants to do or achieve. It refers to the state of mind directing one’s actions.
antonyms: Accident, Chance, Neglect, Aimlessness
sindhiMeaning: ارادو، نيت، مقصد، ذهن ۾ ڪيو ويو ارادو يا سوچ جنهن تحت ڪو ڪم ڪرڻ جو فيصلو ڪيو وڃي

examples: Students interact with teachers during class. Social media helps people interact easily. Children interact while playing games. The two chemicals interact with each other. Teachers encourage students to interact more. Apps allow users to interact in real time.
sindhiMeaning: رابطو ڪرڻ يا گڏجي اثر انداز ٿيڻ، ڳالهه ٻولهه ڪرڻ، گڏجي ڪم ڪرڻ، هڪ ٻئي سان لاڳاپو رکڻ، اثر انداز ٿيڻ، ميل جول ڪرڻ، هڪ ٻئي سان ڳالهائڻ گڏ ڪم ڪرڻ يا هڪ ٻئي تي اثر وجهڻ
synonyms: Communicate, Connect, Engage, Cooperate, Associate, Socialize
antonyms: Ignore, Avoid, Isolate, Disconnect, Separate
urduMeaning: باہمی رابطہ کرنا یا ایک دوسرے پر اثر ڈالنا، بات چیت کرنا، مل جل کر کام کرنا، رابطہ رکھنا، ایک دوسرے پر اثر ڈالنا، میل جول کرنا، ایک دوسرے کے ساتھ بات چیت کرنا مل کر کام کرنا یا ایک دوسرے پر اثر انداز ہونا
englishMeaning: To communicate or work with someone or something. To act together, communicate, influence each other, or respond mutually in a situation

examples: Interaction between students improves learning. There was little interaction during the online class. Social media increases human interaction. The interaction between teacher and students was friendly.
sindhiMeaning: لهه وچڙ يا هڪ ٻئي سان رابطو، باهمي رابطو، ميل جول، ڳالهه ٻولهه اثر ۽ ردعمل، گڏجي ڪم ڪرڻ، ماڻهن شين يا گروهن جو هڪ ٻئي سان ڳالهائڻ رابطو ڪرڻ اثرانداز ٿيڻ يا گڏجي ڪم ڪرڻ
englishMeaning: Communication or action between two or more people or things. The process where people, groups, or objects communicate, influence, or work with each other. It can be social, physical, verbal, or digital.
synonyms: Communication, Contact, Connection, Cooperation, Exchange, Relationship
antonyms: Isolation, Separation, Disconnection, Silence, Noncommunication
urduMeaning: باہمی رابطہ یا میل جول، اثر و ردعمل، گفتگو کا تبادلہ، باہمی عمل، دو یا زیادہ افراد یا چیزوں کے درمیان رابطہ گفتگو اثر یا باہمی عمل

sindhiMeaning: اهڙو جيڪو ماڻهن يا سسٽم جي وچ ۾ سڌي ريت ڳالهه ٻولهه يا حصو وٺڻ سان لاڳاپيل هجي، اهڙي شيءِ جيڪا صرف ڏسڻ يا پڙهڻ تائين محدود نه هجي پر استعمال ڪندڙ کي جواب ڏيڻ چونڊ ڪرڻ يا ڪنٽرول ڪرڻ جي سهولت ڏئي، اهو لفظ خاص طور تي ايپس ويب سائيٽس سکيا جي اوزارن ۽ پريزينٽيشن لاءِ استعمال ٿئي ٿو
synonyms: Engaging, Responsive, Participatory, Dynamic, Communicative
examples: The app has an interactive learning module for students. The website is interactive and allows users to customize themes. The teacher used an interactive presentation in class. This game is highly interactive and keeps players engaged.
urduMeaning: ایسا جس میں لوگوں یا نظام کے درمیان براہ راست رابطہ یا شرکت ہو، اس چیزجس میں صارف صرف دیکھتا نہیں بلکہ جواب دیتا ہے کلک کرتا ہے یا کنٹرول کرتا ہے، یہ لفظ خاص طور پر ایپس ویب سائٹس تعلیمی ٹولز اور پریزنٹیشن کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے
englishMeaning: Involving active participation or communication between people, systems, or devices. Something that allows two way communication. The user does not just watch or read but also responds, clicks, types, or controls what happens. It is commonly used for software, apps, websites, learning tools, and presentations.
antonyms: Passive, Static, Noninteractive, One sided, Inactive

urduMeaning: روکنا، راستے میں پکڑنا، عبور میں رکاوٹ ڈالنا، کسی چیز کو اس کی منزل تک پہنچنے سے پہلے روکنا یا قبضہ کرنا، روکنے کا عمل، روک لی گئی چیز، منزل تک پہنچنے سے پہلے روکنے کا واقعہ یا چیز
examples: The defender intercepted the pass and ran towards the goal. Police intercepted the smuggled goods at the border. She intercepted the letter before it reached him. The missile was intercepted mid-air by the defense system. His intercept of the football changed the game. The spy's intercept of the secret letter prevented a disaster. The missile intercept saved the city.
sindhiMeaning: روڪڻ، وچ ۾ پکڙڻ، حاصلات ۾ رڪاوٽ وجهڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ کي منزل تائين پهچڻ کان اڳ روڪڻ يا قبضو ڪرڻ، روڪڻ جو عمل، وچ ۾ روڪيل شيءِ، منزل تائين پهچڻ کان اڳ روڪڻ جو عمل يا وچ ۾ پکڙيل شيءِ
synonyms: Seize, Catch, Block, Stop, Obstruct
englishMeaning: To take control of or prevent something (like a message, object, or person) from reaching its intended target. The event, instance, or object that is caught, blocked, or stopped. Often used in communication, sports, and military contexts.
antonyms: Deliver, Send, Release, Pass, Allow

urduMeaning: براہِ راست مخالف، دو چیزوں یا خیالات کے درمیان واضح تضاد، کسی خیال یا صفت کا مکمل مخالف
examples: Love is the antithesis of hate. His calm demeanor was the antithesis of her fiery temperament. The new policy is the antithesis of fairness. Freedom is the antithesis of oppression.
synonyms: Opposite, Contrary, Inverse, Reverse
sindhiMeaning: سڌو مخالف، ٻه شيون يا خيالن جي وچ ۾ واضح تضاد، ڪنهن خيال يا خاصيت جو مڪمل مخالف
antonyms: Similarity, Likeness, Same, Equivalent
englishMeaning: Direct opposite. A contrast or opposition between two things, the exact opposite of an idea, concept, or quality. It is often used in literature or speech to highlight differences.

antonyms: Sectarian, Intolerant, Divisive
englishMeaning: Involving or relating to people of different religions or faiths. Activities, relationships, or dialogue between people or groups belonging to different religions. It emphasizes mutual respect, understanding, and cooperation among followers of various faiths. Interfaith efforts aim to promote peace, tolerance, and harmony in diverse societies.
examples: The city organized an interfaith conference to promote peace. Interfaith dialogue encourages respect among communities. Many schools hold interfaith prayers to foster unity. She joined an interfaith group supporting social justice. The school’s interfaith program teaches students about respect for all religions.
sindhiMeaning: مختلف مذهبن يا عقيدن جي وچ ۾ لاڳاپو، مختلف مذهبن وچڪار، مذهبي هم آهنگي يا لاڳاپي سان لاڳاپيل، اهڙا لاڳاپا يا سرگرميون جيڪي مختلف مذهبن يا عقيدن وارن ماڻهن جي وچ ۾ ٿين
synonyms: Multireligious, Ecumenical, Cross-religious
urduMeaning: مختلف مذاہب کے درمیان تعلق یا ہم آہنگی سے متعلق، وہ تعلقات یا سرگرمیاں جو مختلف مذاہب کے ماننے والوں کے درمیان ہوتی ہیں، اس کا مقصد مختلف عقائد رکھنے والے لوگوں میں برداشت احترام اور ہم آہنگی کو فروغ دینا ہوتا ہے

englishMeaning: To place something between layers. To put one material, object, or layer between other layers. It is often used in construction, textile work, printing, design, or technical processes where different materials are combined in layers.
examples: The process involves interlaying very thin layers of silicon. Three slices of toasted bread were interlaid with pieces of chicken. The workers interlay insulation between the wooden panels. She interlaid soft cotton between the fabric layers. The artist interlays colored sheets to create texture. Engineers interlay protective material to strengthen the structure.
urduMeaning: تہوں کے درمیان کوئی چیز رکھنا، درمیان میں مواد رکھنا، کسی چیز میں مختلف عناصر شامل کرنا
synonyms: Insert, Interpose, Place between, Embed, Sandwich
antonyms: Remove, Extract, Separate, Detach, Unlayer
sindhiMeaning: پرتَن جي وچ ۾ ڪا شيءِ رکڻ، وچ ۾ مواد رکڻ، ٻن سطحن جي وچ ۾ پرت رکڻ، وچ ۾ بچاءَ وارو مواد رکڻ، وچ ۾ عنصر رکڻ

urduMeaning: زیرِ تربیت ملازم یا طالب علم جو عملی تجربے کے لیے کام کرے، وہ طالب علم یا تازہ فارغ التحصیل شخص جو کسی ادارے کمپنی یا اسپتال میں عارضی طور پر عملی تجربہ حاصل کرنے کے لیے کام کرتا ہے
antonyms: Expert, Professional, Specialist, Supervisor, Mentor
englishMeaning: To work as a trainee in an organization for practical training. A trainee working in a professional setting to gain experience. A person, usually a student or recent graduate, who temporarily works in an organization such as a company, hospital, or office to gain practical knowledge and job experience. Internships are often part-time or short-term and may be paid or unpaid.
examples: She joined the hospital as a medical intern after graduation. The company hired five interns for the summer program. He worked as an intern at a software house to gain experience. Interns are often supervised by senior professionals.
synonyms: Trainee, Apprentice, Learner, Probationer, Resident (medical context)
sindhiMeaning: تربيتي ملازم يا شاگرد جيڪو عملي سکيا لاءِ اداري ۾ ڪم ڪري، اهو شاگرد يا تازو فارغ ٿيل ماڻهو جيڪو ڪنهن اداري ڪمپني يا اسپتال ۾ عارضي طور تي عملي تجربو حاصل ڪرڻ لاءِ ڪم ڪندو آهي

examples: The party collapsed due to internecine fighting among its leaders. Years of internecine conflict weakened the country’s economy. Internecine disputes within the family destroyed their unity. The company suffered because of internecine rivalry between departments.
sindhiMeaning: ساڳئي ٽولي اندر تڪرار، اهڙي ويڙهه يا تڪرار جيڪو ساڳئي خاندان جماعت يا قوم جي ماڻهن جي وچ ۾ ٿئي ۽ سڀني کي نقصان پهچائي
englishMeaning: Describes conflict within the same group. Internecine refers to violence, struggle, or conflict between members of the same group, family, organization, or nation, often causing serious damage to all sides involved.
synonyms: Internal, Civil, Factional, Mutual, In-house
antonyms: External, Foreign, United, Peaceful, Harmonious
urduMeaning: آپسی لڑائی ، ایک ہی گروہ خاندان یا قوم کے افراد کے درمیان شدید اور نقصان دہ لڑائی یا تنازع

چیزوں کے درمیان موجود خالی جگہ سے متعلق، طب: خلیات یا بافتوں کے درمیان جگہ، اشتہارات: مواد کے درمیان دکھائے جانے والے اشتہارات، عام: درمیانی خلا یا وقفے سے متعلق، اُن چیز یا حالت کو کہتے ہیں جو مختلف اشیاء یا حصوں کے درمیان موجود خالی جگہ میں ہو
antonyms: External, Outer, Surface, Peripheral
synonyms: Intermediate, Intervening, Internal, Medial, Gap-related
englishMeaning: Something that exists in the small spaces between things. Anything located in or relating to the spaces between structures, objects, or parts. It is commonly used in medicine, biology, construction, and digital media. For example, in healthcare it describes spaces between tissues, and in advertising it refers to ads that appear between content.
examples: The doctor diagnosed an interstitial lung disease. Interstitial fluid surrounds the cells in the body. The app shows interstitial ads between levels. The interstitial spaces in the wall help with insulation.
sindhiMeaning: شيئن جي وچ ۾ خالي جڳهه سان لاڳاپيل، طب: سيلن يا عضون جي وچ واري جاءِ، ٽيڪنالاجي: ايپ يا ويب ۾ وچ ۾ ڏيکاريل اشتهار، عام: وچ واري خالي جڳهه سان لاڳاپيل، اُن حالتن يا شين لاءِ استعمال ٿئي ٿو جيڪي ٻين شين جي وچ واري خالي جڳهه ۾ موجود هجن

synonyms: Frighten, Threaten, Cow, Bully, Overawe, Scare, Oppress
englishMeaning: To frighten or threaten someone so they do what you want or stop them from doing something. To make a person feel scared, nervous, or less confident, often by using threats, strong behavior, or pressure. It can be physical, verbal, or psychological. When someone is intimidated, they feel weak, unsafe, or unable to respond freely.
urduMeaning: ڈرانا، دھمکانا، خوف زدہ کرنا، دھمکی دینا، دہشت بٹھانا، مرعوب کرنا، کسی شخص کو ڈرا دھمکا کر اس پر اثر ڈالنا یا اسے کسی کام سے روک دینا
examples: The manager tried to intimidate the workers into accepting lower wages. Big dogs sometimes intimidate small children. He was intimidated by the strict teacher and stayed quiet. She refused to be intimidated by their threats.
antonyms: Encourage, Comfort, Reassure, Support, Calm, Strengthen
sindhiMeaning: ڌمڪائڻ، هيسائڻ، خوف پيدا ڪرڻ، دٻاءُ وجهي قابو ڪرڻ، دل ۾ خوف ويهارڻ، ڊيڄارڻ، مرعوب ڪرڻ، ڪنهن کي خوف ۾ وجهي کيس ڪنٽرول ڪرڻ يا ڪم کان روڪڻ

englishMeaning: A substance that affects the mind or body and causes drunkenness, loss of control, or altered mental state. Any chemical substance, especially alcohol or drugs, that temporarily changes how the brain works. It can reduce awareness, slow reactions, and affect judgment. It may cause a feeling of pleasure at first, but it can also lead to confusion, addiction, or harmful behavior.
synonyms: Drug, Narcotic, Alcohol, Stimulant (context dependent), Substance, Mind-altering substance
examples: Alcohol is a common intoxicant used in many countries. The doctor warned him about the harmful effects of intoxicants. Some plants contain natural intoxicants that affect the nervous system. Driving under the influence of any intoxicant is illegal.
sindhiMeaning: نشو آڻيندڙ شي، شراب، نشيدار شيء، اهڙو مادو جيڪو دماغ تي اثر ڪري انسان کي هوش وڃائڻ يا نشي واري حالت ۾ آڻي، هر اهڙو مادو جيڪو نشي يا هوش ۾ خرابي پيدا ڪري
urduMeaning: نشے دار، مخمور کرنے والی، نشہ آور چیز، ایسا مادہ جو دماغی کیفیت کو بدل دے اور انسان کو مدہوش یا بے قابو کر دے جیسے شراب یا منشیات
antonyms: Sobriety, Sobering agent, Clear-minded substance (contextual), Non-alcoholic substance

synonyms: Drunk, Tipsy, Inebriated, Stoned (informal), Buzzed (informal), High (context dependent)
sindhiMeaning: شراب يا نشي جي اثر هيٺ هجڻ، جذباتي طور تي حد کان وڌيڪ متاثر ٿيڻ، ماڻهو شراب يا نشي جي اثر ۾ هجي جنهن سبب هو صحيح طرح سوچ يا عمل نه ڪري سگهي، ڪڏهن ڪڏهن اهو لفظ جذباتي حالت لاءِ به استعمال ٿيندو آهي جهڙوڪ خوشي يا محبت ۾ بيحد متاثر ٿيڻ
englishMeaning: Under the influence of alcohol or drugs, or strongly excited by emotion or joy. A person is affected by alcohol or drugs so that normal thinking, movement, and behavior are disturbed. It can also be used figuratively for strong emotional states like love, joy, or excitement.
urduMeaning: شراب یا نشے کے اثر میں ہونا، کسی جذبات یا خوشی سے بہت زیادہ متاثر ہونا، کوئی شخص شراب یا نشے کے زیر اثر ہو جس سے اس کی سوچ اور رویہ متاثر ہو جائے، یہ لفظ جذباتی کیفیت جیسے شدید خوشی یا محبت کے لیے بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے
examples: He was intoxicated after drinking too much wine at the party. The driver was arrested because he was intoxicated while driving. She felt intoxicated with happiness after hearing the good news. They were intoxicated by the beauty of the mountain view.
antonyms: Sober, Clear-headed, Alert, Conscious, Straight

examples: His intoxication made him unable to walk properly. She felt an intoxication of success after winning the competition. Driving under intoxication is dangerous and illegal. The crowd was in intoxication of excitement during the concert.
synonyms: Drunkenness, Inebriation, Euphoria, High, Elation, Stimulation
sindhiMeaning: نشي جي حالت يا شديد جذبي جي حالت، ان حالت کي چيو وڃي ٿو جنهن ۾ ماڻهو شراب منشيات يا شديد احساسن سبب پنهنجي معمولي ڪنٽرول وڃائي ويهي ٿو
englishMeaning: State of being affected by alcohol, drugs, or strong emotion. A condition in which a person loses normal control because of alcohol, drugs, or overwhelming emotions such as happiness, love, or anger.
antonyms: Sobriety, Clarity, Calmness, Awareness, Self control
urduMeaning: نشے یا شدید جذبے کی حالت، اس حالت کو کہتے ہیں جب انسان شراب منشیات یا شدید جذبات کی وجہ سے اپنے معمول کے کنٹرول سے باہر ہو جائے

englishMeaning: To be restless or unable to sit still due to excitement or nervousness. Very excited.
synonyms: Restless, Excited
sindhiMeaning: بي چين، بي قرار، ويهڻ ۾ آرام نه هجڻ، ڪنهن ڳالهه جي انتظار يا جوش ۾ هجڻ
examples: The kids had ants in their pants before the trip. He had ants in his pants before his first flight. The children had ants in their pants waiting for the party to start. She can’t sit still, must have ants in her pants today!. He had ants in his pants during the meeting, thinking about the big game.
urduMeaning: بے چین، بے قرار، سکون میں نہ رہنے والا، کسی بات کے جوش یا گھبراہٹ میں ہونا
antonyms: Calm, Relaxed

urduMeaning: سازش،منصوبہ بازی، فریب، دغا، جنسی تعلق، دغا کرنا، پوشیدہ تعلق پیدا کرنا، مسحور کرنا، حیرت زدہ کرنا، تجسس پیدا کرنا، چال چلنا
antonyms: Sincerity, Bore, Repel, Disinterest, Discourage, Expose
synonyms: Fascinate, Captivate, Interest, Scheme, Plot, Conspire, Conspiracy
examples: Throughout history, people have been intrigued by the question of whether there is intelligent life elsewhere in the universe. It intrigues me that no one appears to have thought of this before. The young heroine steps into a web of intrigue in the academic world.
sindhiMeaning: سازش، منصوبو، عشق بازي، شرارت، اٽڪل، ڳجھي سازش ڪرڻ، ڳجھي نموني اثررسوخ هلائڻ، لُڀائڻ، تجسس اڀارڻ، وڻڻ، ڪشش ڪرڻ، دلچسپي پيدا ڪرڻ، سازش ڪرڻ
englishMeaning: The activity of making secret plans. The practice of engaging in secret schemes. To secretly plan with other people to harm somebody. To make somebody very interested and want to know more about something.

sindhiMeaning: غيرقانوني طور تي داخل ٿيندڙ ماڻهو، ٻئي جي معاملن يا رازداري ۾ مداخلت ڪندڙ، ڪمپيوٽر يا نظام ۾ بغير اجازت داخل ٿيندڙ، اهڙو ماڻهو جيڪو اڻ سڏيل طور ڪنهن ميڙ يا ڳالهه ۾ شامل ٿئي
urduMeaning: غیر قانونی طور پر کسی جگہ داخل ہونے والا شخص، دوسروں کے معاملات یا نجی زندگی میں مداخلت کرنے والا، کمپیوٹر یا نظام میں بغیر اجازت داخل ہونے والا شخص، ایسا فرد جو کسی گروہ یا سرگرمی میں بلا اجازت شامل ہو جائے
antonyms: Clergy, Priesthood, Religious leaders, Experts, Professionals
englishMeaning: A person who enters a place, property, group, or system without invitation, permission, or legal right. A trespasser who enters private property. A person who interferes in others’ affairs or privacy. Someone who enters a computer system without authorization. A person who joins a group or activity where they are not welcome.
synonyms: Laypeople, Laypersons, Congregation, Common people, Nonprofessionals
examples: The security guard caught an intruder inside the office building at night. The alarm system warned the family about an intruder in the house. The hacker acted like an intruder in the company’s computer network. She felt like an intruder when she accidentally joined their private meeting.

urduMeaning: بلا اجازت مداخلت کرنے والا، حد سے بڑھ کر دخل دینے والا، بہت ذاتی سوال کرنے والا، اچانک مداخلت کرنے والا، ناپسندیدہ طور پر موجودگی تھوپنے والا، نفسیات میں غیر مطلوب بار بار آنے والے خیالات
sindhiMeaning: بنا اجازت دخل ڏيندڙ، بيجا مداخلت ڪندڙ، حد کان وڌيڪ ذاتي سوال ڪندڙ، اوچتو خلل وجھندڙ، اڻ وڻندڙ موجودگي مسلط ڪندڙ، نفسيات ۾ اڻ گهريل ورجندڙ خيال
antonyms: Respectful, Unobtrusive, Considerate, Nonintrusive, Polite
englishMeaning: Unwanted and entering someone’s space, thoughts, or life without permission. Describes something or someone that interferes in a way that feels unwelcome, invades privacy, or interrupts normal flow.
synonyms: Invasive, Interfering, Meddlesome, Obtrusive, Pushy
examples: His intrusive questions made everyone uncomfortable. She found the pop up ads intrusive while reading. The reporter’s intrusive behavior annoyed the actor. He tried to stop intrusive thoughts before sleeping.

She had an intuitive sense that something was wrong. The app has an intuitive interface that is easy to navigate. His intuitive decision-making often leads to success. Artists often rely on their intuitive feelings to create.
sindhiMeaning: فطري طور تي سمجھندڙ يا سمجھڻ جي قدرت رکندڙ
synonyms: Instinctive, Perceptive, Natural, Insightful
antonyms: Logical, Reasoned, Analytical, Deliberate
urduMeaning: فطری طور پر سمجھنے والا، باطن کی سمجھ رکھنے والا
englishMeaning: Having the ability to understand or know something immediately, without conscious reasoning. Something that feels natural or easy to grasp because it aligns with instinct or perception.
In a way that is based on instinct or immediate understanding rather than conscious reasoning. By using your feelings rather than by considering the facts.
examples: She intuitively knew something was wrong. He solved the problem intuitively without checking the manual. The design feels intuitively easy to use. Children often learn language intuitively.
urduMeaning: فطری طور پر، بغیر سوچے سمجھے یا وجدانی طور پر سمجھنا یا محسوس کرنا
synonyms: Instinctively, Naturally, Innately, By intuition
antonyms: Analytically, Logically, Deliberately, Methodically
sindhiMeaning: فطرتي طور تي، انساني حس يا ڄاڻ سان بنا سوچ ويچار

synonyms: Overwhelm, Swamp, Overflow, Submerge, Beflood
sindhiMeaning: ٻوڙڻ، غرق ڪرڻ، ڪناتار ڪرڻ، ڀرجَڻ، وهڻ، ٻوڏ ڪرڻ، بوڇاڙ ڪرڻ
examples: We have been inundated with offers of help. She's inundated with work at the moment. Flood waters inundate the river plain each spring. Many sheep were lost in the floods and the city was inundated. The agency was inundated with phone calls.
englishMeaning: To give or send somebody so many things that they cannot deal with them all. To cover an area of land with a large amount of water. To bring to a place or person too much of something, so that it cannot be dealt with.
antonyms: Inundate, Drain, Unseal, Break, Abstain, Underwhelm
urduMeaning: غرقاب کرنا، سیلاب میں غرق کردینا، ضبط ہو جانا، غرق کرنا، سیلاب میں ڈبونا، کِناروں سے باہِر بہنا، کِسی چیز کی فراوانی سے مغلوب کرنا

حملہ کرنا، مداخلت کرنا، تجاوز کرنا، زبردستی داخل ہونا یا قبضہ کرنا، کسی ملک یا علاقے میں فوجی طاقت کے ساتھ داخل ہونا، بغیر اجازت کسی جگہ میں داخل ہونا، کسی نقصان دہ چیز کا پھیل جانا، کسی کی ذاتی زندگی یا جگہ میں مداخلت کرنا
antonyms: Defend, Protect, Withdraw, Leave, Retreat
englishMeaning: To enter a place by force or without permission. To enter a country or area using military force. To spread into something harmful or unwanted. To interrupt or disturb someone’s privacy or space. To overrun or overwhelm. To intrude physically or emotionally. To spread like disease, insects, or unwanted thoughts.
examples: The army planned to invade the neighboring country. It is wrong to invade someone’s privacy without permission. Ants invaded the kitchen after the rain. Negative thoughts can invade your mind if you are not careful.
sindhiMeaning: حملو ڪرڻ، ڪنهن ملڪ تي چڙهائي ڪرڻ، بيماري يا جذباتن تي حملو ڪرڻ، حقن وغيرھ تي حملو ڪرڻ، ڪاهه ڪرڻ، زبردستي داخل ٿيڻ يا قبضي ڪرڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ ۾ نقصانڪار نموني پکڙجڻ، ڪنهن جي ذاتي زندگي يا جاءِ ۾ مداخلت ڪرڻ
synonyms: Attack, Enter, Occupy, Intrude, Overrun, Encroach

englishMeaning: The opening at the end of the digestive system through which solid waste (feces) leaves the body. It is a part of human and animal anatomy, located at the end of the rectum.
antonyms: There are no antonyms
sindhiMeaning: اها جاءِ جتان انساني جسم مان فضلو يا گند ٻاهر نڪري ٿو، اهو هاضمي واري نظام جو آخري حصو آهي
examples: The doctor examined the anus for any signs of infection. Waste leaves the body through the anus. The anus is an essential part of the digestive system. Pain near the anus can be a symptom of a medical condition.
synonyms: Rectal opening, Back passage, Anal opening, Terminal opening of the digestive tract
urduMeaning: جسم کا وہ حصہ جہاں سے فضلہ خارج ہوتا ہے، آنتوں کا آخری سرا

antonyms: Nonintrusive, Contained, Limited, Harmless, Reserved
sindhiMeaning: زبردستي داخل ٿيندڙ، ڦهلجندڙ ۽ نقصانڪار، ذاتي حدن ۾ مداخلت ڪندڙ، جسم اندر داخل ٿيندڙ طبي عمل سان لاڳاپيل، جتي نه گهرجي اتي داخل يا ڦهلجندڙ، حد کان وڌيڪ ذاتي سوال ڪرڻ
examples: The doctor recommended a less invasive treatment. This invasive plant is damaging local crops. His questions felt invasive and uncomfortable. The species became invasive in the new environment.
urduMeaning: جہاں ضرورت نہ ہو وہاں داخل ہونے والا یا مداخلت کرنے والا، زبردستی داخل ہونے والا، زبردستی داخل ہونے والا، زبردستی داخل ہونے والا، جسم کے اندر داخل ہونے والا طبی طریقہ، حد سے زیادہ ذاتی سوال کرنا
englishMeaning: Something that enters, spreads, or intrudes where it is not welcome. Entering or spreading into an area where it is not wanted. Involving medical procedures that enter the body. Intruding into someone's privacy or personal space. Spreading rapidly and harming the environment, especially plants or species.
synonyms: Intrusive, Encroaching, Spreading, Penetrating, Meddlesome

examples: The champion looked invincible throughout the tournament. Her courage made her seem invincible in difficult times. The army believed its strong walls were invincible. After several victories, the team felt invincible.
synonyms: Unbeatable, Unconquerable, Undefeated, Indomitable, Invulnerable, Overpowering
sindhiMeaning: اَجِيتو، ناقابلِ شڪست، اڻهارائتو، زبردست، جنهن تي غالب نه پئجي سگهجي، جنهن کي شڪست نه ڏئي سگهجي، جنهن کي هارائي نه سگهجي، ڪمزور نه بڻائي سگهجي، اهو لفظ حقيقي طاقت لاءِ ايندو آهي ۽ ڪڏهن مضبوط حوصلي يا اعتماد لاءِ پڻ استعمال ٿيندو آهي
englishMeaning: Impossible to defeat, overcome, or destroy. A person, group, spirit, or thing that cannot be defeated, conquered, or broken. It may refer to real strength, great power, or strong confidence. Sometimes it is also used figuratively for someone who feels unbeatable.
urduMeaning: ناقابلِ شکست، ناقابلِ تسخیر، اَجے، جس پر غلبہ نہ پایا جا سکے، جسے مغلوب نہ کیا جا سکے، جسے ہرایا نہ جا سکے، کمزور نہ بنایا جا سکے، یہ لفظ حقیقی طاقت کے لیے بھی آتا ہے اور کبھی مضبوط حوصلے یا اعتماد کے لیے بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے
antonyms: Vulnerable, Defeatable, Weak, Conquerable, Beatable, Fragile

synonyms: Sacred, Untouchable, Protected, Absolute
examples: Freedom of religion is considered inviolable in many constitutions. The sanctity of human life should remain inviolable at all times. The agreement stated that national borders are inviolable. Medical confidentiality is an inviolable ethical principle.
englishMeaning: Something that must not be broken, harmed, or violated. A rule, right, place, or principle that is protected by law, morals, or strong belief and should never be broken, attacked, or ignored.
antonyms: Violable, Breakable, Vulnerable, Open to violation
urduMeaning: ناقابلِ خلاف ورزی، جسے توڑا یا پامال نہ کیا جا سکے، لازوال ، واثق ، ناقابلِ انفساخ، واجِب العمل، واثق ، ناقابلِ انفساخ، ناقابِل فسخ ، ناقابِل تخَلُّف
sindhiMeaning: مختل نه ٿيڻ وارو، ٽوڙڻ يا ڀڃڪڙي کان محفوظ، ناقابل تلافي، نه ڀڃڻ جهڙو، پاڪ، بي زوال، بي حرمتي کان محفوظ، قانون يا اخلاق موجب محفوظ ڪيل، اهڙو حق يا اصول جيڪو ڪنهن به حالت ۾ ختم نه ٿي سگهي

englishMeaning: To call upon something, especially a higher power, authority, or law, for help, support, or inspiration. To cite or appeal to something as a justification. To cause something to happen or bring something into effect. To call on a higher power or deity for assistance. To call a function, method, or procedure in programming. To cite or refer to as evidence or justification. To summon someone or something formally.
antonyms: Ignore, Reject, Dismiss, Neglect
urduMeaning: کسی کی مدد یا رہنمائی کے لیے پکارنا، کسی اصول قانون یا دلیل کا حوالہ دینا، کسی کام کو شروع کرنا یا اثرانداز کرنا، مدد یا رہنمائی کے لیے کسی اعلیٰ طاقت یا ہستی کو پکارنا، کسی قانون اصول یا حق کا حوالہ دینا، کسی اثر یا ردعمل کو جنم دینا، پروگرامنگ میں کسی فنکشن یا طریقہ کو چلانا، کسی دلیل یا ثبوت کے طور پر ذکر کرنا
synonyms: Appeal, Call upon, Summon, Cite, Request, Activate
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ کي مدد لاءِ طلب ڪرڻ، ڪنهن قانون يا اصول جو حوالو ڏيڻ، اثر پيدا ڪرڻ يا شيءِ کي لاڳو ڪرڻ، اثر پيدا ڪرڻ يا ڪنهن عمل کي شروع ڪرڻ، ڪم يا پروگرام کي فعال ڪرڻ، دليل يا ثبوت طور حوالو ڏيڻ، التجا ڪرڻ، خدا کان دعا گهرڻ، منتر پڙهي روحن کي حاضر ڪرڻ، درخواست ڪرڻ
examples: The priest invoked blessings upon the congregation. She invoked her right to remain silent during the trial. The programmer invoked the function to run the application. The manager invoked company policy to resolve the dispute. The villagers invoked the rain god during the drought. The app invoked the login API to authenticate the user. The teacher invoked previous research to support her argument.

synonyms: Unbreakable, Indestructible, Impervious, Impenetrable, Bulletproof
sindhiMeaning: جيڪو نقصان زخم يا حملي کان محفوظ هجي ۽ جنهن کي ڪو به نقصان نه پهچائي سگهي، هي لفظ جذباتي طور تي به استعمال ٿئي ٿو جڏهن ڪو ماڻهو تنقيد يا ذهني دٻاءَ کان متاثر نه ٿئي
examples: The fortress was considered invulnerable to enemy attacks. He felt invulnerable after wearing the protective armor. No one is truly invulnerable to criticism. The superhero seemed invulnerable to all weapons.
urduMeaning: جسے نقصان چوٹ یا شکست نہ دی جا سکے یعنی مکمل طور پر محفوظ ہونا، یہ لفظ جذباتی یا ذہنی طور پر بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے جب کوئی شخص تنقید خوف یا ذہنی دباؤ سے متاثر نہ ہو
englishMeaning: Someone or something that cannot be harmed, damaged, or defeated. It refers to being completely safe from attack, injury, criticism, or danger. Also used in emotional or abstract sense, meaning someone who is not affected by criticism, fear, or emotional harm.
antonyms: Vulnerable, Weak, Defenseless, Exposed, Fragile

sindhiMeaning: جلد غصي ۾ اچڻ وارو، جلدي ڪاوڙجڻ وارو، اهڙو شخص جيڪو ٿوري ڳالهه تي به جلدي ڪاوڙ ۾ اچي وڃي
synonyms: Irritable, Hot tempered, Testy, Short tempered
urduMeaning: جلد غصہ ہونے والا، ایسا شخص جو معمولی بات پر بھی فوراً غصے میں آ جائے، چڑچڑا
examples: The irascible teacher shouted when the class became noisy. His irascible nature made it hard for others to work with him. She avoided arguments because her boss was irascible. Age and stress had made him more irascible than before. He has an irascible temperament.
englishMeaning: Easily angered or irritated. A person who becomes angry very quickly, often over small or unimportant matters.
antonyms: Calm, Patient, Mild
Literal, Expected, Straightforward, Obvious, Direct
sindhiMeaning: اها ڳالهه جيڪا اميد جي ابتڙ ٿئي، اميد ۽ حقيقت ۾ فرق، حيرت انگيز يا مزاحيه صورتحال، لفظن جو الٽو مطلب کڻڻ، اهڙي حالت يا ڳالهه جنهن ۾ نتيجو اميد جي ابتڙ هجي يا حيرت انگيز انداز ۾ الٽو ٿي وڃي
englishMeaning: Something that happens in an opposite or unexpected way. A situation where the outcome is opposite to what is expected, or when something happens in a surprising and often funny or sad way. It can also mean using words to express something different from their literal meaning, usually for humor or criticism.
examples: It was ironic that the fire station burned down. She found it ironic that the health coach was always unhealthy. It is ironic that he failed the safety test. The weather was ironic because it rained on the day they planned a beach picnic.
urduMeaning: ایسی بات جو توقع کے خلاف ہو، توقع اور حقیقت میں فرق، غیر متوقع اور عجیب صورتحال، طنزیہ انداز میں الٹا مطلب، صورتحال جس میں نتیجہ توقع کے خلاف ہو یا کوئی بات الٹے یا طنزیہ انداز میں ظاہر ہو
synonyms: Sarcastic, Paradoxical, Contradictory, Wry, Unexpected
Guess, Speculation
englishMeaning: An attempt made without knowledge or certainty. A guess. Something you do without knowing what the result will be.
examples: His answer was just a stab in the dark. The figure he came up with was really just a shot in the dark. It was only a stab in the dark, but I hoped I could learn something. I didn’t know the answer, so my guess was just a stab in the dark.
sindhiMeaning: اوچتو اندازو، پڪ کان سواءِ اندازو، انڌو اندازو
urduMeaning: اندھیرے میں تیر، بغیر کسی معلومات یا شواہد کے صرف اندازے یا قسمت پر بھروسہ کرتے ہوئے کوئی فیصلہ کرنا
antonyms: Certain decision, Surety

englishMeaning: The state of feeling nervous or worried that something bad is going to happen. A mental health problem that causes somebody to worry so much that it has a very negative effect on their daily life. A worry or fear about something.
urduMeaning: فکر، تشویش، پریشانی، اندیشہ ، خطرہ ، خوف زدہ، خَوف یا ڈَر کا احساس،تَجَسُّس، فِکَر مَندی، اُلجھَن، بے چینی، فکر، گھبراہٹ
antonyms: Calm, Peace, Relaxation, Confidence, Contentment
synonyms: Worry, Concern, Nervousness, Apprehension, Uneasiness, Stress
examples: She felt anxiety before her final exam. His anxiety about the interview kept him awake all night. Parents often experience anxiety when their children are sick. Too much anxiety can affect both mental and physical health.
sindhiMeaning: انديشو، پريشاني، فڪر، تشويش، ڳڻتي، خيال، اضطراب، دڪ دڪو، جکڻي، بيچيني، آنڌ مانڌ، هُرکُر، سوئنچو

synonyms: Surprisingly, Unexpectedly, Contradictorily, Paradoxically, In an ironic way
sindhiMeaning: اهڙي طريقي سان جيڪو اميد جي ابتڙ هجي يا حيرت انگيز هجي، ان صورتحال لاءِ استعمال ٿئي ٿو جتي ڪا ڳالهه اميد جي ابتڙ ٿئي يا نتيجو بلڪل مختلف ۽ حيرت انگيز نڪري
examples: Ironically, the fire station burned down during a fire. He studied hard for the exam but, ironically, he failed it. Ironically, the doctor who advised healthy eating died of a heart attack. She was afraid of water, but ironically became a swimming coach.
urduMeaning: اس انداز میں جو توقع کے خلاف ہو یا الٹ نتیجہ ظاہر کرے، اس صورت حال کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے جب کوئی بات توقع کے بالکل الٹ ہو جائے یا نتیجہ حیران کن طور پر مختلف نکلے
antonyms: Predictably, Expectedly, Naturally, Obviously, Normally
englishMeaning: In a way that is opposite to what is expected or intended, often in a surprising or funny way. Used when something happens in a way that is unexpected, opposite, or contradictory to what was intended or believed. It often highlights a situation where reality is very different from expectation, sometimes in a humorous or sad way.

sindhiMeaning: غير عقلي، بي سبب سوچ وارو، جذبات جي اثر هيٺ اچي عقل وڃائي ويهڻ وارو، اهڙو عدد جيڪو سادي ڪسر جي صورت ۾ نه لکي سگهجي ۽ جنهن جو ڏھائي وارو حصو نه ختم ٿئي ۽ نه ورجائي، اهڙي ڳالهه جيڪا عقل کان ٻاهر هجي يا منطقي وضاحت نه رکي
antonyms: Rational, Logical, Reasonable, Sensible, Wise
urduMeaning: غیر عقلی، بے دلیل، جذبات کے زیر اثر آ کر عقل سے کام نہ لینا، وہ عدد جو سادہ کسر کی شکل میں نہ لکھا جا سکے اور جس کا اعشاریہ نہ ختم ہو نہ دہرایا جائے، ایسی بات جو عقل سے بالاتر ہو یا جس کی منطقی وضاحت نہ ہو
englishMeaning: Not based on reason or clear thinking. A person, action, belief, or feeling that is not guided by logic, reason, or sound judgment. It may involve emotions that overpower sensible thinking or ideas that do not make practical sense. number that cannot be written as a simple fraction and has a non repeating, non ending decimal form.
examples: His fear of harmless insects is completely irrational. She made an irrational decision when she refused medical help. The market sometimes reacts in irrational ways during a crisis. He became irrational with anger and shouted at everyone. It is irrational to expect success without hard work. Pi is an irrational number.
synonyms: Illogical, Unreasonable, Senseless, Absurd, Foolish

antonyms: Peninsula, Island
urduMeaning: ایک تنگ زمین کا ٹکڑا جو دو بڑے زمینی علاقوں کو جوڑتا ہے اور دو پانی کے حصوں کو الگ کرتا ہے
englishMeaning: A narrow strip of land connecting two larger land areas, usually with water on either side. A thin land bridge that connects two larger landmasses while separating two bodies of water. It is important in geography and often serves as a route for transportation, trade, or strategic purposes.
synonyms: Land bridge, Neck of land, Strip of land, Connection
examples: The Isthmus of Panama connects North and South America. Ancient civilizations often built cities along an isthmus for trade advantages. The soldiers defended the narrow isthmus against enemy forces. Ships pass through the canal that cuts across the isthmus.
sindhiMeaning: هڪ تنگ زميني پٽي جيڪا ٻن وڏن زمينن کي ڳنڍي ٿي ۽ ٻن پاڻيءَ وارن حصن کي الڳ ڪري ٿي

examples: Ahmed and Ali kept insulting each other in class because it takes two to make a quarrel. My teacher advised us to stay calm during arguments because it takes two to make a quarrel. The neighbors finally realized that it takes two to make a quarrel and decided to solve the issue peacefully. Sara ignored the rude comments, proving that it takes two to make a quarrel.
urduMeaning: تالی ایک ہاتھہ سے نہیں بجتی، لڑائی یا جھگڑا ہونے کے لیے دونوں فریقوں کا شامل ہونا ضروری ہوتا ہے، جھگڑا دونوں کے ردعمل سے بڑھتا ہے، اگر ایک شخص خاموش رہے تو لڑائی رک سکتی ہے، غصے کا جواب غصے سے دینے سے تنازع بڑھتا ہے، صبر اور برداشت امن پیدا کرتے ہیں
synonyms: Both sides are responsible, It takes two to tango, Conflict needs participation from both sides, Mutual disagreement, Shared responsibility in conflict
antonyms: One-sided blame, Innocent party, Peaceful understanding, Mutual harmony, Silent patience
sindhiMeaning: تاڙي هڪ هٿ سان نه وڄندي آهي، جهيڙو ٿيڻ لاءِ ٻن ماڻهن جو شامل هجڻ ضروري هوندو آهي، جهيڙو ٻنهي ڌرين جي ردعمل سبب وڌندو آهي، جيڪڏهن هڪ ماڻهو خاموش رهي ته تڪرار گهٽجي سگهي ٿو، ڪاوڙ جو جواب ڪاوڙ سان ڏيڻ جهيڙي کي وڌائيندو آهي، صبر ۽ برداشت سان امن قائم رهي سگهي ٿو
englishMeaning: A quarrel or fight usually happens because both sides contribute to the disagreement. One person alone cannot continue an argument if the other refuses to participate. Arguments grow when both people react emotionally. Disagreements need participation from both sides. Peace can be maintained if one person stays calm. Shared anger often creates conflict.
word: It takes two to make a quarrel

urduMeaning: کسی بھی تنازعہ تعلق یا مسئلے میں دونوں افراد برابر ذمہ دار ہوتے ہیں، ایک اکیلا ذمہ دار نہیں ہوتا، یہ کہاوت اکثر رشتوں اور جھگڑوں میں استعمال ہوتی ہے تاکہ یہ واضح کیا جا سکے کہ دونو افراد کی شراکت ہوتی ہے
synonyms: Both sides are responsible, It needs cooperation from both sides, Shared responsibility, Two-way involvement
examples: The couple keeps blaming each other, but it takes two to tango. If the project failed, remember it takes two to tango between manager and worker. Don’t blame only him for the fight; it takes two to tango. In every argument, it takes two to tango, so both should reflect on their actions.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن به تڪرار يا تعلق ۾ ٻه ماڻهو شامل هوندا آهن ۽ ٻئي برابر ذميوار هوندا آهن، هڪ ماڻهو اڪيلو ذميوار نه هوندو آهي، هي اصطلاح عام طور تي رشتن يا تڪرارن ۾ استعمال ٿيندي آهي ته ٻنهي ڌرين جو حصو هوندو آهي
englishMeaning: A situation or conflict usually involves two people, and both are responsible for it. Many actions, arguments, relationships, or problems cannot happen because of just one person. Both sides contribute, so both share responsibility. It is often used when blaming or explaining a disagreement or situation involving two people.
antonyms: One-sided responsibility, Only one person is guilty, Single-handed effort, One-way action

examples: I tried reading the report but the technical terms made it all Greek to me. When he explained the math formula, it was all Greek to me. The computer code looks Greek to me because I have never learned programming. She talked about astronomy and to me it was all Greek.
synonyms: I cannot make sense of it, I do not get it, It makes no sense to me, It is confusing
urduMeaning: بالکل سمجھ نہ آئے، کسی بات کو نہ سمجھنے پر حیرت یا بے بسی ظاہر کرنا، جب کوئی مشکل یا علمی لفظ بولے اور بات سمجھ نہ آئے، کسی غیر مانوس موضوع کو بیان کرنے کے لئے بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے، جب کوئی بات بہت الجھی ہوئی ہو یا سمجھ میں نہ آئے تو یوں لگتا ہے جیسے یہ کسی اجنبی زبان میں ہو
sindhiMeaning: سمجهڻ ۾ نہ اچڻ، ڪنهن به اڻڄاتل ڳالهه بابت حيرانگي ظاهر ڪرڻ، جڏهن ڪو ماڻهو پيچيده لفظ استعمال ڪري ۽ ڳالهه سمجهه ۾ نه اچي، ڪنهن پرڏيهي يا ڏکي موضوع کي بيان ڪرڻ، جڏهن ڪا ڳالهه بلڪل اڻڄاتل هجي ڏکي هجي يا سمجهڻ کان ٻاهر لڳي ته اها ڳالهه يوناني وانگر لڳي ٿي
englishMeaning: I do not understand it at all. Used when something is confusing, unclear or impossible to understand because it feels like a foreign language. Used to express total lack of understanding. Sometimes said jokingly when someone uses big or complicated words. Can refer to any unfamiliar subject or skill.
antonyms: I understand it clearly, It makes perfect sense, I get it, I follow it

sindhiMeaning: دهرائڻ، ڪنهن شيءَ کي ٻيهر ورجائڻ، عمل کي بهتر بڻائڻ لاءِ ٻيهر انجام ڏيڻ
antonyms: Cease, Stop, Halt, Discontinue
englishMeaning: To repeat. To say or do something repeatedly. To repeat a process or action, often to improve or refine it.
synonyms: Repeat, Recapitulate, Reiterate, Redo, Reproduce
examples: The designer iterated the app interface until it looked perfect. Software developers iterate their code to fix bugs and improve performance. The teacher iterated the instructions to ensure every student understood. During the meeting, she iterated her key points several times.
urduMeaning: کسی کام یا عمل کو بار بار دہرانا خاص طور پر بہتری یا درستگی کے لیے

englishMeaning: The process of repeating something, usually to improve it or reach a desired outcome. A single repetition or version in a sequence of attempts. In computing, a step in a loop or repeated process. An instance of doing something again in a systematic way.
antonyms: Original, First attempt, Single instance, Unique
sindhiMeaning: ورجائڻ يا ٻيهر عمل ڪرڻ جو عمل، هڪ مرحلو يا ورجن جيڪو ورجائڻ سان پيدا ٿئي، ڪمپيوٽنگ ۾ هڪ لوپ جو هڪ قدم، ڪنهن ڪم کي منظم طريقي سان ٻيهر ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: کسی عمل یا کام کو دہرانے کا عمل، ہر ایک بار دہرایا جانے والا مرحلہ یا صورت، کمپیوٹر پروگرامنگ میں کسی لوپ یا دہرائی جانے والی کارروائی کا ایک مرحلہ، کسی عمل کو منظم طریقے سے دوبارہ کرنا
synonyms: Repetition, Version, Cycle, Revision, Loop
examples: The software went through several iterations before the final version was released. Each iteration of the design improved user experience. The teacher asked the student to review his essay after the first iteration. In programming, an iteration refers to one complete cycle of a loop.

synonyms: Nomadic, Wandering, Roaming, Traveling, Migratory
urduMeaning: جگہ جگہ گھومنے والا، سفر کرنے والا، گھومنے والا مزدور، آوارہ مسافر، خانہ بدوش پیشہ ور، سفر کرنے والا استاد یا مبلغ، ایسا شخص جو مستقل ایک جگہ نہ رہے بلکہ کام یا دیگر مقاصد کے لیے مختلف مقامات پر سفر کرتا رہے

A lively musical composition used for dancing. A device to guide or hold workpieces for precise cutting, drilling, or shaping. A type of lure or weighted hook that moves up and down to attract fish.
antonyms: Sit still, Remain, Stop, Stand

synonyms: Marriage settlement, Dower provision, Widow’s provision, Property settlement
sindhiMeaning: جائداد، مهر، زوجيت جو حق، زال لاءِ ملڪيت يا آمدني جيڪا شادي وقت يا مڙس جي وفات کان پوءِ مقرر ڪئي وڃي (اهو بندوبست زال جي مالي تحفظ لاءِ ڪيو ويندو آهي ته جيئن هوءَ مڙس کان پوءِ ڪنهن تي ڀاڙڻ کانسواءِ عزت سان زندگي گذاري سگهي)
examples: The jointure ensured that she would not face financial hardship after her husband’s death. Under the marriage contract, a jointure was settled in her name. urduMeaning: وہ جائيداد جو شوہَر بيوی کے نام لِکھ دے، بیوی کے لیے مقرر کی گئی جائیداد یا آمدنی (شوہر کی وفات کے بعد، تاکہ وہ کسی دوسرے پر انحصار کیے بغیر باعزت زندگی گزار سکے)
englishMeaning: A legal provision made for a wife, usually giving her income or property after marriage or after her husband’s death. جھٽڪو، ڌڪ هڻڻ، ڌڪو، ڌڪو ڏيڻ، ڌڪڻ، ٺونٺ هڻڻ، اوچتو يا اڍنگو ڌڪو ڏيڻ، ماڻهن جي ميڙ ۾ ڌِڪ ڌڪان، سخت هڻ هڻان ڪرڻ، ٽَڪر، ٽَڪراءُ

urduMeaning: ظاہری شکل پر فیصلہ نہ کرو، کسی کے ظاہری انداز سے اس کی حقیقت کا اندازہ لگانا غلط ہے، کسی کے کپڑوں یا حالت کو دیکھ کر فیصلہ مت کرو ، ظاہر دھوکہ دے سکتا ہے
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن جي ڪپڙن کي ڏسي اهو نه سمجهو ته هو غريب آهي، رڳو ظاهر تي فيصلو نه ڪريو، انسان يا شيءِ جي قيمت ۽ سچائي ظاهر سان نه پر اندر سان ماپي وڃي

word: Judge a book by its cover

synonyms: Wise, Prudent, Rational, Thoughtful

urduMeaning: دانشمند، عاقلانہ، سمجھدار، وہ شخص یا عمل جو عقل سمجھ بوجھ اور احتیاط کے ساتھ کیا گیا ہو
antonyms: Foolish, Reckless, Imprudent, Thoughtless, Unwise

examples: Everyone is jumping on the bandwagon of social media trends. After the team started winning, many new fans jumped on the bandwagon. When online business became profitable, everyone jumped on the bandwagon and started their own stores. Politicians often jump on the bandwagon of popular movements to gain votes. He didn’t believe in the cause at first, but he jumped on the bandwagon when it became popular.
antonyms: Resist trend, Oppose
