englishMeaning: To become extremely angry, excited, or out of control.
sindhiMeaning: بي قابو، ڏمر ۾ اچي وڃڻ، جوش ۾ اچي وڃڻ
synonyms: Furious, Enraged, Hysterical, Crazy, Wild, Ecstatic
Survive, Make ends meet, Sustain oneself
sindhiMeaning: بمشڪل گذر بسر ڪرڻ، زنده رهڻ لاءِ جدوجهد ڪرڻ، تنگي يا مشڪلات ۾ صرف زندگي گذارڻ لاءِ جدوجهد ڪرڻ يعني ٿورو کاڌو ڪم يا وسيلو هجي پر پوءِ به زندگي جاري رکي
examples: He worked hard to keep body and soul together. After losing his job, he could hardly keep body and soul together. The poor old man sells fruits just to keep body and soul together. In the desert, the travelers struggled to keep body and soul together until help arrived. During the famine, many families barely managed to keep body and soul together.
urduMeaning: بمشکل گزارا کرنا، بمشکل گزر بسر کرنا، زندگی کا سلسلہ جاری رکھنا، بڑی مشکل میں صرف زندہ رہنے کے لیے جدوجہد کرنا یعنی بس اتنا ہی کما یا کھا رہا ہو کہ زندگی کا سلسلہ چلتا رہے
englishMeaning: To survive or manage to stay alive, especially when one has very little money, food, or resources. It means doing just enough to sustain life, maintaining basic needs like food, shelter, or health.
antonyms: Die, Perish, Starve, Give up

englishMeaning: To prevent something from increasing or to stay in a low position. To control or limit something so it does not rise or grow. It can refer to costs, noise, emotions, or numbers. It also means to stay low or not be seen or noticed, especially to avoid trouble or danger.
sindhiMeaning: دٻائڻ، وڌڻ کان روڪڻ يا هيٺ رکڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ کي ڪنٽرول ۾ رکڻ جيئن اها وڌي نه وڃي جهڙوڪ خرچ شور يا ڪاوڙ، اهو مطلب به ڏئي سگهي ٿو پاڻ کي لڪائي رکڻ يا هيٺ رهڻ ته جيئن مسئلو پيدا نه ٿئي
antonyms: Encourage, Release
urduMeaning: دبانا، بڑھنے سے روکنا یا نیچے رکھنا، کسی چیز کو قابو میں رکھنا تاکہ وہ زیادہ نہ ہو جیسے خرچ شور یا جذبات، اس کا مطلب یہ بھی ہو سکتا ہے کہ خود کو نمایاں ہونے سے بچانا یا خطرے سے بچنے کے لیے نیچے رہنا
synonyms: Suppress, Control, Restrain
examples: Keep your voice down. The medicine keeps the fever down. Prices were kept down by the government. Try to keep down your anger.

antonyms: Drop the subject, Let go, Ignore, Overlook, Move on
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ڳالهه کي بار بار ورجائڻ ۽ ان تي زور ڏيندو رهڻ، ڪنهن کي مسلسل ٽوڪيندو رهڻ، ڪنهن جي غلطي ياد ڏياريندو رهڻ، هڪ ئي نقطي تي زور ڏيندو رهڻ، ساڳئي ڳالهه ۾ ڦاٿل رهڻ
examples: He keeps harping on about my late arrival. Stop harping on the same issue and let us move forward. She was harping on about the budget cuts during the entire meeting. My brother keeps harping on about healthy eating habits.
englishMeaning: To talk about something repeatedly in an annoying way. To nag about something continuously. To keep reminding someone of a mistake or issue. To repeatedly stress the same point. To dwell on a topic without moving forward
synonyms: Nag about, Go on about, Dwell on, Repeat constantly, Keep talking about
urduMeaning: کسی بات کو بار بار دہرانا اور اسی پر زور دیتے رہنا، مسلسل ٹوکتے رہنا، کسی کی غلطی یاد دلاتے رہنا، ایک ہی نکتے پر اصرار کرتے رہنا، ایک ہی موضوع پر اٹکے رہنا

examples: The teacher kept the students in after class. I kept in my anger. Keep the cat in during the night. He kept in his feelings. Please keep in touch while you are abroad. The news was kept in to avoid panic.
synonyms: Contain, Confine, Retain
englishMeaning: To remain inside or to continue having something such as contact, control, or possession. To hold back feelings or speech. To include or keep something in mind. To not share information.
urduMeaning: اندر رکھنا، باہر نہ جانے دینا، اندر رہنا، رابطہ برقرار رکھنا، جذبات یا باتوں کو قابو میں رکھنا، ذہن میں رکھنا یا شامل کرنا، راز میں رکھنا
antonyms: Release, Free
sindhiMeaning: اندر رکڻ، ٻاهر نه وڃڻ ڏيڻ، اندر رهڻ، لاڳاپو برقرار رکڻ، راز ۾ رکڻ، ذهن ۾ رکڻ يا شامل ڪرڻ، احساسن يا ڳالهين کي قابو ۾ رکڻ

antonyms: Approach, Indulge
englishMeaning: To stay away from something or not touch or step on it. (Used especially on warning signs to protect property, plants, or unsafe areas.)
urduMeaning: دور رہنا، ہاتھ نہ لگانا، نہ چلنا یا نہ چھونا، پرہیز کرنا، استعمال نہ کرنا، دخل نہ دینا
sindhiMeaning: پري رهڻ، هٿ نه لڳائڻ، نه هلڻ يا نه ڇهڻ، لاڳاپو نه رکڻ، پاسو ڪرڻ
examples: Keep off the grass. Please keep off spicy food. He kept off the subject of politics. Keep your hands off my things.
synonyms: Avoid, Stay away, Abstain

englishMeaning: To stay confident and hopeful despite challenges or sadness. To remain positive, confident, or courageous in difficult or challenging situations, without showing fear or discouragement.
antonyms: Lose Courage, Give Up, Be Discouraged, Despair
sindhiMeaning: حوصلي سان رهڻ، همٿ نه وڃائڻ، دل نه هارڻ
examples: Despite losing the match, he kept his head up. She kept her head up while dealing with workplace stress. Keep your head up; better days are coming. He kept his head up even when everyone doubted him.
urduMeaning: حوصلہ بلند رکھنا، حوصلہ بلند رکھنا، خود اعتمادی برقرار رکھنا
synonyms: Stay Strong, Be Confident, Remain Positive, Persevere

sindhiMeaning: پاڻ کي صاف رکڻ، پريشانين کان پاسو ڪرڻ، مصيبتن يا تڪليفن کان پاڻ کي بچائڻ، غلط ڪم يا قانون جي ڀڃڪڙي کان پاسو ڪرڻ، سٺي روَيي ۽ ذميواري سان رهڻ
englishMeaning: To stay out of trouble. To avoid doing anything illegal, wrong, or morally questionable. To behave properly so no one can blame you.
antonyms: Misbehave
urduMeaning: صاف رہنا، مشکلات سے بچنا
synonyms: Behave, Stay out of trouble
examples: He tries to keep his nose clean and avoid trouble. He just got out of prison, so he’s trying to keep his nose clean. If you want to succeed in this job, keep your nose clean and work hard.

englishMeaning: A short, wise saying that expresses a general truth. A concise statement that conveys a deep idea, moral lesson, or universal truth. It is often memorable and thought provoking, commonly used in literature, philosophy, and everyday speech.
examples: "Actions speak louder than words" is a well known aphorism. His speech was filled with aphorisms about life and success. "Time is money" is a classic aphorism used in business. The book contains many aphorisms that teach valuable lessons.
synonyms: Maxim, Adage, Proverb, Saying, Epigram, Truism
antonyms: Rambling statement, Long explanation, Wordy expression, Confusing statement
sindhiMeaning: مختصر دانائي ڀريو قول، اهڙو ننڍو ۽ جامع جملو جيڪو ڪنهن وڏي سچائي دانائي يا تجربي کي ظاهر ڪري، اهو عام طور تي ياد رهڻ جهڙو ۽ سبق ڏيندڙ هوندو آهي
urduMeaning: مختصر حکیمانہ قول، ایک مختصر مگر جامع جملہ جو کسی بڑی حقیقت دانائی یا تجربے کو بیان کرتا ہے، یہ اکثر یاد رکھنے کے قابل اور سبق آموز ہوتا ہے

examples: Even after losing his job, he tried to keep his pecker up. Life can be tough sometimes, but you must keep your pecker up. She told her friend to keep his pecker up during the exam stress. Though the team lost several matches, their coach told them to keep their peckers up.
englishMeaning: To remain cheerful, brave, and confident, especially in a difficult or challenging situation.
urduMeaning: جب حالات خراب ہوں تو بھی امید اور ہمت قائم رکھنا، مایوسی سے بچنا اور اعتماد کے ساتھ مشکل وقت کا سامنا کرنا
synonyms: Stay strong
antonyms: Become hopeless
sindhiMeaning: مشڪل يا ڏکئي حالتن ۾ به پنهنجو حوصلو ۽ همت برقرار رکڻ، جڏهن حالتون خراب هجن تڏهن به دل کي مضبوط رکڻ ۽ نااميد نه ٿيڻ
پابند رهڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ تي قائم رهڻ، پيروي ڪرڻ، ڪنهن ڪم رستي قانون يا شيءَ سان مستقل طور تي لڳل رهڻ يا ان جي پيروي ڪرڻ
englishMeaning: To follow, stick with, or stay on something. To continue doing something consistently, follow a rule, plan, schedule, or path, or to restrict oneself to a particular topic, route, or routine.
antonyms: Ignore, Disobey
synonyms: Follow, Adhere, Abide
urduMeaning: پابند رہنا، کسی چیز پر قائم رہنا، عمل کرنا، کسی کام قانون منصوبہ یا راستے پر مستقل طور پر عمل کرنا یا اس کے پابند رہنا
examples: Keep to the path. Try to keep to your budget. He kept to the topic. Please keep to your word.

urduMeaning: جاری رکھنا، ایک ہی رفتار پر چلنا، برقرار رکھنا، کسی کام یا معیار کو قائم رکھنا یا کسی معلومات میں پیچھے نہ رہنا
englishMeaning: To maintain or continue at the same level. To continue doing something at the same rate, pace, or standard; to remain informed about something. To not fall behind.
antonyms: Fall behind, Stop
examples: Keep up the good work!. She can’t keep up with the others. Keep up your studies. Prices are kept up by demand.
sindhiMeaning: جاري رکڻ، ساڳئي رفتار سان هلڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ کي جاري رکڻ يا رفتار، معيار يا ڄاڻ ۾ پوئتي نه رهڻ
synonyms: Maintain, Continue, Match pace

antonyms: Lose focus, Get distracted, Ignore the task, Be careless, Lose track
englishMeaning: To stay focused on the main task or goal and not get distracted. It means maintaining attention, awareness, and consistency, especially during important work or situations.
examples: If you want to succeed in your exams, you must keep your eye on the ball. The manager told his team to keep their eye on the ball during the project. Even under pressure, she kept her eye on the ball and completed the task on time. It is easy to lose progress if you do not keep your eye on the ball.
sindhiMeaning: ڌيان برقرار رکڻ، پنهنجو ڌيان اصل ڪم يا مقصد تي رکو ۽ ڌيان نه هٽايو، ڪنهن به اهم ڪم دوران توجهه برقرار رکڻ
word: Keep your eye on the ball
urduMeaning: توجہ برقرار رکھنا، اپنی توجہ اصل کام یا مقصد پر رکھنا اور ادھر ادھر دھیان نہ دینا، اہم کام کے دوران مکمل توجہ برقرار رکھنا
synonyms: Stay focused, Pay attention, Stay on track, Keep focused, Concentrate

antonyms: Give up, Despair
urduMeaning: حوصلہ بلند رکھنا، حوصلہ رکھو، ہمت نہ ہارو، مشکل حالات میں مثبت رہو
englishMeaning: To stay confident and hopeful despite challenges or sadness. To remain positive, brave, or confident in difficult situations and not let problems or failures make you feel defeated.
examples: Keep your head up; things will get better. Even in tough times, she keeps her head up. Keep your head up—you’ve done your best. He told his friend to keep his head up after the loss.
sindhiMeaning: حوصلي سان رهڻ، همت رکو، حوصلو نه وڃايو، مشڪلات ۾ به پختو رهو
synonyms: Stay positive, Persevere
Astraphobia, Brontophobia, Fear of storms, Lightning fear, Thunder anxiety
sindhiMeaning: گوڙ ۽ بجليءَ کان حد کان وڌيڪ يا غير معقول خوف، هي هڪ نفسياتي خوف آهي جنهن ۾ ماڻهو گوڙ واري موسم يا بجليءَ جي چمڪ کان شديد ڊپ محسوس ڪري ٿو ۽ پريشاني ۾ مبتلا ٿي سگهي ٿو
examples: She suffers from keraunophobia and hides in a closed room during thunderstorms. His keraunophobia became worse after he experienced a severe lightning strike as a child. People with keraunophobia often check weather reports frequently to avoid storms. Despite his keraunophobia, he tries to stay calm when thunder starts at night.
urduMeaning: گرج چمک اور بجلی (آسمانی بجلی اور گرج) سے حد سے زیادہ اور غیر ضروری خوف، یہ ایک نفسیاتی کیفیت ہے جس میں فرد بادلوں کی گرج یا بجلی کی چمک سے شدید خوف محسوس کرتا ہے حتیٰ کہ موسم کا اندازہ ہوتے ہی گھبراہٹ شروع ہو سکتی ہے
antonyms: Fearlessness, Courage, Calmness during storms, Bravery, Composure
englishMeaning: The extreme or irrational fear of thunder and lightning. A specific phobia in which a person experiences intense fear, anxiety, or panic when they hear thunder or see lightning. The fear may occur during storms or even at the thought of stormy weather. It can lead to avoidance behavior, stress, and physical symptoms like sweating or trembling.

examples: The book offers a vision of the future in which there is a great nuclear apocalypse. Nobody was artistically better prepared to deal with the watery apocalypse that followed Hurricane Katrina than this 75-year-old man. A large part of this secret literature was the apocalypses. Apocalypse's blood can heal other mutants, but is fatal for humans.
synonyms: Destruction, Holocaust, Havoc, Devastation, Catastrophe, Armageddon, Cataclysm, End times
sindhiMeaning: وحي، الهام، آسماني ڪتاب، الهامي ڪتاب، خاص طور تي جيڪو جان سان پيٽموس جي ٻيٽ تي ٿيو
antonyms: Happiness, Miracle, Wonder, Good Fortune
englishMeaning: The destruction of the world. The end of the world, as described in the Bible. The final book of the Bible, also known as Revelation, which describes events leading up to the final destruction of the world. A situation causing very serious damage and destruction.
urduMeaning: کَشَف ، آسمانی کِتاب ، الہامی کِتاب ، الہام بالخصوص وہ جو یوحنا کو جزیرہ پتموس میں ہوا
کسی راز، مسئلے یا پہیلی کا حل یا وضاحت، کسی جگہ یا موقع تک رسائی حاصل کرنے کا ذریعہ، قشے یا چارٹ میں علامتوں کی وضاحت کرنے والی فہرست
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن راز، مسئلي يا ڳجهارت جو حل يا وضاحت، ڪنهن جاءِ يا موقعي تائين پهچ حاصل ڪرڻ جو ذريعو، نقشو يا چارٽ ۾ نشانين جي وضاحت ڪندڙ فهرست
antonyms: Irrelevant to, Unimportant to, Insignificant to, Minor to
synonyms: Vital to, Fundamental to, Central to
englishMeaning: The correct explanation or solution to a mystery, problem, or puzzle. Something that allows entry, control, or access to a place, system, or opportunity. A guide that explains symbols, signs, or codes in a chart, map, or text.
examples: The witness gave the key to the mystery. Communication is the key to a healthy relationship. Education is the key to a better future. Practice is the key to mastering any skill. Confidence is the key to public speaking. Use the key to understand the map symbols.

sindhiMeaning: جوش ۾ آڻڻ، تيار ڪرڻ، چست ڪرڻ، جذبات يا ڪشش وڌائڻ، معلومات يا ڊيٽا داخل ڪرڻ (ڪمپيوٽر ۾)، گروپ يا فرد ۾ جوش يا جذبو پيدا ڪرڻ
englishMeaning: To make someone more alert, focused, or energetic. To increase tension or anticipation in a situation. To enter data or information into a system (less common, in computing context). To stimulate emotions or reactions in a group or individual.
urduMeaning: جوش دلانا، تیار کرنا، چوکنا کرنا، جذبات یا تناو بڑھانا، معلومات یا ڈیٹا داخل کرنا (کمپیوٹر میں)، گروپ یا فرد میں جوش یا ردعمل پیدا کرنا
antonyms: Calm, Relax, Soothe, Depress, Dull
examples: The speaker keyed up the audience with an inspiring story. The tension in the courtroom keyed up as the verdict was announced. He keyed up all the customer orders into the system before lunch. The trainer keyed up the athletes before the championship.
synonyms: Stimulate, Excite, Energize, Provoke, Intensify, Alert

examples: We kicked about the idea of moving abroad. They kicked about some business plans. The topic was just kicked about at lunch. Let’s not just kick about, let’s decide.
urduMeaning: کسی خیال یا منصوبے پر غیر رسمی گفتگو کرنا، بغیر مقصد کے اِدھر اُدھر گھومنا یا وقت گزارنا
synonyms: Discuss, Debate
englishMeaning: To discuss or talk about an idea informally before making a decision. To move or travel from one place to another without a clear purpose. (British informal) To spend time aimlessly or casually.
antonyms: Ignore, Avoid
sindhiMeaning: ڳالهائڻ، بحث ڪرڻ، ڪنهن ڳالهه تي غير رسمي طرح بحث يا صلاح ڪرڻ، ڪنهن جاءِ تي بي مقصد يا بي رخ گهمڻ

urduMeaning: مخالفت کرنا یا بغاوت کرنا، احتجاج یا مزاحمت کرنا
antonyms: Accept, Obey, Comply, Agree
synonyms: Resist, Oppose, Defy, Rebel
sindhiMeaning: مخالفت ڪرڻ يا بغاوت ڪرڻ، مزاحمت ڪرڻ
englishMeaning: To resist or protest something. Relax after hard work. To react strongly or forcefully. Can also mean to return money illegally (bribe).
examples: He always kicks against authority. They kicked against the unfair decision. Children often kick against strict rules. She kicked against her parents’ expectations.

antonyms: Work, Strain, Calm down, Freeze
englishMeaning: To sit comfortably and rest without stress. Money given secretly in return for favor or business. To react suddenly or violently (machine/gun). To respond strongly or aggressively.
urduMeaning: سکون سے بیٹھنا اور آرام کرنا، خفیہ طور پر فائدہ کے بدلے پیسے دینا، مشین یا ہتھیار کا پیچھے کی طرف زور سے جانا، سخت ردعمل دینا
synonyms: Relax, Rest, React, Recline
sindhiMeaning: سڪون سان ويهڻ ۽ آرام ڪرڻ، لڪ ۾ فائدي لاءِ پئسا ڏيڻ، مشين يا اوزار جو اوچتو پٺتي وڃڻ، سخت ردعمل ڏيکارڻ
examples: After work, I just want to kick back and watch TV. The horse kicked back when someone touched it. The manager was accused of kicking back money to suppliers. Let’s kick back and enjoy the weekend.

englishMeaning: To begin to take effect or start working (often used for medicines, plans, systems, or reactions). To contribute or add something, especially money or effort.
antonyms: Cease, End
examples: The painkillers kicked in after ten minutes. The law will kick in next month. The new system kicked in smoothly. His training kicked in during the emergency.
urduMeaning: کسی چیز کا اثر ظاہر ہونا، جیسے دوا یا نظام کا عمل میں آنا، کسی کام میں پیسے یا مدد کے طور پر حصہ ڈالنا
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ جو اثر شروع ٿيڻ (جهڙوڪ دوائن، قانونن يا نظام جو)، ڪنهن ڪم ۾ مدد يا حصو ڏيڻ (پئسن يا ڪوشش جي صورت ۾)
synonyms: Begin, Start

antonyms: End, Finish, Conclude, Terminate, Close
urduMeaning: شروع ہونا، آغاز کرنا، شروع کر دینا، کسی کام تقریب یا سرگرمی کا آغاز کرنا، کبھی کبھار کسی چیز کو لات مار کر ہٹانے یا غصہ ظاہر کرنے کے لیے بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے
englishMeaning: To begin or start something. To indicate the start of an event, activity, process, or action. It can also mean to remove something by kicking, or in informal contexts, to get angry.
examples: The football match will kick off at 7 PM. Let’s kick off the meeting with a quick introduction. He kicked off his shoes as soon as he got home. She kicked off when she heard the unfair decision.
synonyms: Launch, Commence, Initiate, Open
sindhiMeaning: شروع ٿيڻ، آغاز ڪرڻ، شروع ڪرڻ، ڪنهن ڪم تقريب يا سرگرمي کي شروعات ڪرڻ، ان جو مطلب ڪنهن شيءِ کي ڪِڪ ڪري هٽائڻ يا غصو ڏيکارڻ به ٿي سگهي ٿو

examples: He was kicked out of school. They kicked out the rude customer. The tenant was kicked out for not paying rent. She kicked him out of the car. The teacher kicked the noisy students out of the class.
synonyms: Expel, Dismiss
englishMeaning: To expel someone or something from a place or organization.
antonyms: Admit, Welcome
sindhiMeaning: زبردستي ڪنهن جڳهه نوڪري يا تنظيم مان ڪڍي ڇڏڻ، خارج ڪرڻ، ڌڪ سان ٻاهر ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: زبردستی جگہ نوکری یا ادارے سے نکال دیناا، خارج کرنا،باہر نکالنا

antonyms: Set upright, Lift, Balance
englishMeaning: To overturn or knock something down accidentally. En relax after hard work. To react strongly or forcefully. Can also mean to return money illegally (bribe).
examples: He kicked over the bucket of paint by mistake. The child kicked over his toys. The engine kicked over but didn’t start. She kicked over the stool while dancing.
urduMeaning: لات مار کر کسی چیز کو گرا دینا یا مشین کو چلانا، شروع ہونا، اچانک ردِعمل دینا یا بغاوت کرنا
sindhiMeaning: مشين يا انجڻ جو هلڻ شروع ٿيڻ يا ڪنهن شيءِ کي ٽنگ سان ڪيرائڻ يا ڌڪ ڏئي اڇلائڻ، اوچتو ردعمل ڏيکارڻ يا بغاوت ڪرڻ
synonyms: Overturn, Knock down, Tip over
Provoke trouble, Stir up anger, Invite conflict, Create chaos
examples: When he criticized the management during the meeting, he really kicked the hornet’s nest. The new policy kicked the hornet’s nest among the employees. By questioning the leader’s decision, she kicked the hornet’s nest. Posting that controversial comment online was like kicking the hornet’s nest.
urduMeaning: ایسا عمل یا بات کرنا جس سے لوگوں میں غصہ، ہنگامہ یا تنازعہ پیدا ہو جائے، کسی خطرناک یا حساس مسئلے کو چھیڑ کر حالات کو بگاڑ دینا
englishMeaning: To cause trouble or anger by doing or saying something that upsets many people. To create a situation full of problems, anger, or conflict that is difficult to control afterward.
sindhiMeaning: اهڙو ڪم ڪرڻ يا ڳالهه چوڻ جنهن سان ماڻهن ۾ غصو، جهيڙو يا تڪرار پيدا ٿئي، ڪنهن حساس يا خطرناڪ معاملي کي چھيڙڻ ۽ ان سان تڪليف يا ڏکيائي پيدا ڪرڻ
antonyms: Calm the situation, Restore peace, Avoid conflict, Settle issues

synonyms: Complain, Protest, Agitate, Rise
sindhiMeaning: شور شرابو ڪرڻ يا تڪرار پيدا ڪرڻ، ڪنهن مسئلي کي وڏو ڪري پيش ڪرڻ، احتجاج ڪرڻ
englishMeaning: To cause trouble or start a disturbance. Du relax after hard work. To react strongly or forcefully. Can also mean to return money illegally (bribe).
examples: The students kicked up a fuss about the new rules. The wind kicked up a lot of dust. The kids kicked up when asked to go to bed early. Prices kicked up after the announcement.
urduMeaning: شور مچانا یا مسئلہ کھڑا کرنا، جھگڑا کھڑا کرنا، تنازع یا فساد پیدا کرنا، سخت احتجاج کرنا
antonyms: Calm down, Settle, Soothe, Lower

synonyms: Initiate, Energize, Launch, Activate, Jump-start, Stimulate
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ڪم يا منصوبي کي زور سان شروع ڪرڻ، جيئن اهو جلدي اڳتي وڌي يا مؤثر طور تي ڪم ڪرڻ لڳي
urduMeaning: کسی کام، منصوبے یا سرگرمی کو طاقت یا توانائی کے ساتھ شروع کرنا تاکہ وہ تیزی سے آگے بڑھے یا مؤثر طور پر کام کرے
examples: The manager tried to kick-start the new marketing campaign with a big launch event. I need a strong cup of coffee to kick-start my day. The government launched a program to kick-start economic growth in rural areas. A short motivational speech helped kick-start the team’s energy before the match.
englishMeaning: To give a strong or energetic start to a process, activity, or project, often to overcome inertia or delay. It can also mean jump-starting something to make it function efficiently.
antonyms: Stop, Halt, Delay, Slow, Postpone

urduMeaning: ایک تیر سے دو شکار، ایک ہی کوشش سے دو فائدے حاصل کرنا
examples: He killed two birds with one stone by shopping and visiting friends. By driving my friend to the airport and doing some shopping on the way back, I killed two birds with one stone. She improved her English and made new friends at the same time, killing two birds with one stone. Walking to work helps me exercise and save money on transport, it’s like killing two birds with one stone.
synonyms: Do double work, Be efficient
antonyms: Waste effort
word: Kill two birds with one stone
englishMeaning: To achieve two goals or solve two problems with a single action or effort. Doing one thing that brings double benefit.
sindhiMeaning: هڪ ئي ڪم سان ٻه فائدا حاصل ڪرڻ، هڪ ئي ڪوشش سان ٻه مقصد پورا ڪرڻ، ھڪڙي تير سان ٻہ شڪار

englishMeaning: A person who has the same ideas, feelings, interests, or nature as another person. A person who feels very similar to you in thoughts, emotions, values, interests, or attitude. It is used for someone with whom you feel a natural connection, understanding, or closeness because both of you think or feel in much the same way.
antonyms: Opposite, Unlike person, Stranger, Rival, Opponent, Enemy, Misfit, Incompatible person
urduMeaning: ایسا شخص جس کے خیالات جذبات یا دلچسپیاں آپ سے ملتی جلتی ہوں، ہم خیال شخص، ہم مزاج انسان، دل کے قریب شخص، یکساں فطرت والا، مشترک دلچسپیوں والا دوست
examples: When I met Sara, I felt I had found a kindred spirit because we both loved books and quiet places. He saw his grandfather as a kindred spirit who shared his respect for honesty and hard work. The two artists became kindred spirits after discovering their similar views on beauty and life. In a new city, finding a kindred spirit made her feel less lonely and more understood.
sindhiMeaning: اهڙو ماڻهو جيڪو اوهان جهڙا خيال احساس يا دلچسپيون رکي، هم خيال ماڻهو، هم مزاج شخص، دل سان ويجهو ماڻهو، ساڳي طبيعت وارو، ساڳين دلچسپين وارو دوست
synonyms: Like minded person, Soulmate, Kindred soul, Kindred mind, Kindred heart, Kindred being, Kindred companion, Kindred friend, Bosom friend, Kindred one
Moving, Dynamic, Active, Motional
examples: A moving car has kinetic energy. The ball gains kinetic force as it rolls downhill. Wind turbines convert kinetic energy into electricity. The dancer performance was full of kinetic motion.
sindhiMeaning: حرڪت سان لاڳاپيل، اُن شيءِ يا توانائي کي چيو وڃي ٿو جيڪا حرڪت سبب پيدا ٿئي، هي لفظ خاص طور تي فزڪس ۾ استعمال ٿيندو آهي جتي هلندڙ شيءِ وٽ حرڪتي توانائي هوندي آهي
urduMeaning: حرکت سے متعلق، اس چیز یا توانائی کو کہتے ہیں جو حرکت کی وجہ سے پیدا ہو، یہ لفظ زیادہ تر طبیعیات میں استعمال ہوتا ہے جہاں چلتی ہوئی چیز میں حرکی توانائی ہوتی ہے
antonyms: Static, Still, Stationary, Motionless
englishMeaning: Related to motion or movement. Something that is produced by movement or is connected with physical motion. It is commonly used in science, especially physics, to describe energy that an object has because it is moving.

A small booth or stand used to sell items or provide information. A small, separate structure or booth, often found in public places such as streets, malls, airports, or parks. It is used to sell newspapers, food, tickets, or to provide digital services and information through screens.
urduMeaning: چھوٹا سا اسٹال یا دکان جہاں چیزیں بیچی جائیں یا معلومات دی جائے، ایک چھوٹی اور الگ بنی ہوئی جگہ جو عام طور پر بازاروں ہوائی اڈوں یا پارکوں میں ہوتی ہے، یہ اخبارات کھانا ٹکٹ فروخت کرنے یا ڈیجیٹل معلومات فراہم کرنے کے لیے استعمال ہوتی ہے
antonyms: Supermarket, Department store, Large shop, Mall
sindhiMeaning: ننڍو دڪان يا اسٽال جتان شيون وڪرو ڪيون وڃن يا ڄاڻ ڏني وڃي، هڪ ننڍي ۽ الڳ ٺهيل جڳهه جيڪا عام هنڌن جهڙوڪ مارڪيٽن هوائي اڏن يا پارڪن ۾ هوندي آهي، اها اخبارون کاڌو ٽڪيٽون وڪڻڻ يا ڪمپيوٽر ذريعي ڄاڻ مهيا ڪرڻ لاءِ استعمال ٿيندي آهي
synonyms: Booth, Stall, Stand, Counter
examples: He bought a newspaper from the kiosk near the bus stop. A digital kiosk helps visitors find their way in the mall. The food kiosk sells snacks and cold drinks. Tickets can be printed from the self service kiosk at the airport.

He invited all his kith and kin to the wedding ceremony. During the festival, people love to celebrate with their kith and kin. She moved to the city, leaving her kith and kin behind in the village. In times of trouble, your kith and kin are the ones who stand by you.
urduMeaning: رشتہ دار، وہ سب لوگ جو خون یا تعلقات کی بنیاد پر آپ کے قریب ہوں، خاندان کے افراد اور دوست احباب
synonyms: Loved ones, Family members
sindhiMeaning: مٽ مائٽ ۽ دوست احباب، جيڪي لاڳاپن يا محبت جي لحاظ سان ويجها هجن
englishMeaning: Friends and family; all your relatives and close acquaintances. People you are closely connected to by blood or friendship.
antonyms: Strangers, Outsiders

sindhiMeaning: آخر ۾ تڪليف ڏيندڙ ڳالهه، ڪنهن ڳالهه واقعي يا فيصلي جي پڇاڙي ۾ اهڙو نقصان يا مسئلو جيڪو شروع ۾ ظاهر نه هجي ۽ بعد ۾ تڪليف ڏئي
urduMeaning: آخر میں ناگوار نتیجہ، کسی بات واقعے یا فیصلے کے اختتام پر آنے والا ایسا منفی یا تکلیف دہ پہلو جو پہلے نظر نہ آئے مگر بعد میں مسئلہ بن جائے
antonyms: Pleasant ending, Happy surprise, Benefit, Advantage, Positive outcome
englishMeaning: An unpleasant ending. A surprising and often unpleasant detail or consequence that appears at the end of a situation, story, decision, or event, reducing its overall positive effect
examples: The movie was entertaining, but there was a sting in the tail when the hero betrayed his friend. The job offer looked perfect, but the long unpaid probation was a sting in the tail. His speech was inspiring, with a sting in the tail that criticized the audience sharply. The agreement seemed fair, yet the hidden fee at the end was a real sting in the tail.
synonyms: Hidden drawback, Nasty surprise, Unpleasant twist, Catch, Downside

englishMeaning: A natural ability to do something well. A special skill or talent that someone has, often learned easily or done naturally without much effort. It usually describes practical abilities rather than academic knowledge.
antonyms: Inability, Weakness, Clumsiness, Incompetence
synonyms: Talent, Skill, Ability, Flair, Aptitude
sindhiMeaning: قدرتي صلاحيت، خاص مهارت، ڪنهن ڪم کي آساني سان ڪرڻ جي خوبي
urduMeaning: فطری مہارت، کسی کام کو آسانی سے اچھی طرح کرنے کی صلاحیت
examples: She has a knack for explaining difficult ideas clearly. He has a natural knack for fixing machines. Teaching requires more than knowledge, it needs a knack for communication. Some people have a knack for making others feel comfortable.

antonyms: Caretaker, Breeder, Farmer, Energetic Person
sindhiMeaning: اوڳاڙ يا ٿڪل جانورن جو واپار ڪندڙ ماڻهو، ڪڏهن ڪڏهن ٿڪجي پيل يا بيڪار شخص لاءِ پڻ استعمال ٿيندو آهي
englishMeaning: Someone who buys old, worn-out animals (especially horses) for slaughter or disposal. A person who deals in old or worn-out animals, typically buying them to kill for meat or to sell parts like hides, bones, or other materials. Informally, it can also mean someone who is tired out or worn down.
examples: The farmer sold his old horse to the knacker. After years of hard work, he felt like a complete knacker. Knackers often supply leather to tanneries. The village knacker bought the worn-out ox for a small price.
synonyms: Slaughterer, Dealer in old animals, Tanner, Worn-out person
urduMeaning: پرانے یا تھکے ہوئے جانور خرید کر بیچنے والا شخص، کبھی کبھار تھکا ہوا یا کمزور شخص بھی مراد ہو سکتا ہے

antonyms: Thoughtful response, Deliberate action, Considered reaction, Rational response
sindhiMeaning: اوچتو ردعمل، سوچڻ کان سواءِ تڪڙو ردعمل، تجزئي کان سواءُ فوري ردعمل، عادت مطابق ٿيندڙ پيشگوئيءَ جهڙو عمل، اڪثر منفي اثر سان جڙيل، اهو ردعمل جيڪو بنا سوچ ويچار جي ڏنو وڃي، عام طور تي جذبات جي بنياد تي ٿيندو آهي ۽ ماڻهو حالتن کي سمجهي يا جائزو وٺڻ کان اڳ جواب ڏئي ڇڏيندو آهي
urduMeaning: فوری ردعمل، سوچے بغیر دیا گیا فوری ردعمل، بغیر غور و فکر کے فوری ردعمل، عادت یا معمول کے مطابق ظاہر ہونے والا ردعمل، اکثر منفی یا غیر مناسب ردعمل کے مفہوم میں استعمال، ایسا ردعمل جو انسان بہت جلدی اور جذبات میں آ کر دے دیتا ہے ، اس میں حالات کو سمجھنے اور نتائج پر غور کرنے کا موقع نہیں ہوتا
englishMeaning: An automatic or reflexive response. A response that is automatic, instinctive, or done without careful thought. It is usually a quick reaction triggered by emotion, habit, or impulse rather than reason. A response made without analysis or reflection. A habitual or predictable reaction. Often carries a negative connotation implying lack of control.
examples: His criticism was just a knee-jerk reaction to the new policy. She had a knee-jerk reaction of anger when she saw the mistake. Politicians often give knee-jerk responses to public outrage. Don’t let a knee-jerk reaction ruin a thoughtful discussion.
synonyms: Reflex response, Automatic reaction, Instinctive reply, Impulsive response
Hero, Savior
examples: He was her knight in shining armour. She waited for a knight in shining armour. Don’t expect a knight in shining armour to fix things. He became the knight in shining armour for his family.
englishMeaning: A person who appears at the right moment to help, save, or rescue someone. Often used for someone who protects or supports another in a difficult situation.
sindhiMeaning: هيرو، مددگار ماڻهو جيڪو وقت سر اچي ڪنهن کي بچائي يا مدد ڪري، اهڙي شخص لاءِ استعمال ٿيندو آهي جيڪو مشڪل وقت ۾ سهارو بڻجي
antonyms: Villain, Oppressor
urduMeaning: بہادر، وہ شخص جو مشکل وقت میں آکر مدد کرے یا بچائے، عام طور پر کسی محافظ یا مددگار شخصیت کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے

antonyms: Start, Begin, Raise, Create, Preserve, Maintain, Add
urduMeaning: قیمت کم کرنا، رعایت دینا،نقل کرنا یا سستا نقل تیار کرنا، مارنا اور چیز کو ہٹانا، قتل کرنا (عام بول چال میں)، کسی کام کو آسانی سے مکمل کرنا، فہرست سے ہٹانا یا اہمیت کم کرنا
englishMeaning: To end work temporarily or permanently. To lower the cost of something. To produce something in imitation, usually cheaply. To strike something and make it fall. To eliminate someone. To quickly or easily complete a task. To take something off a list or reduce its importance.
examples: Let's knock off work early today. The store knocked off 20% from all electronics. That handbag is a knock-off of a designer brand. He accidentally knocked off the vase from the shelf. The mafia threatened to knock him off.
sindhiMeaning: ڪم ختم ڪرڻ، ڪم بند ڪرڻ، قيمت گھٽائڻ، رعايت ڏيڻ، نقل ڪرڻ يا سستو ٺاهڻ، ڌڪ هڻڻ ۽ شيءَ کي هٽائڻ، قتل ڪرڻ (غير رسمي)، آسان سان ڪم مڪمل ڪرڻ، لسٽ مان هٽائڻ يا اهميت گهٽائڻ
synonyms: Finish, Stop, Reduce, Copy, Imitate, Topple, Eliminate, Complete, Remove

sindhiMeaning: نظر نه لڳي، ماشاءللھ، بد نظر کان بچاءُ، اميد آهي ائين ئي رهي، سٺي ڳالهه کان پوءِ بدقسمتي کان بچڻ لاءِ چيو ويندو آهي، جڏهن ڪو ماڻهو پنهنجي خوش نصيبي يا سٺي حالت جو ذڪر ڪري ته هو ھي محارو چوي ٿو ته جيئن اها حالت خراب نه ٿئي، هي هڪ وهم تي ٻڌل اظهار آهي
synonyms: Hope for the best, Pray for good luck, Touch wood
englishMeaning: An expression people use after mentioning something good or lucky, to avoid bad luck. Expressing hope that your good luck continues and that no misfortune follows.
examples: I’ve never failed an exam, knock on wood. We’ve had great weather all week, knock on wood it stays this way. My car has never broken down, knock on wood. Everything is going smoothly, knock on wood. He’s never had an accident while driving, knock on wood. Everything in our family is fine, knock on wood.
urduMeaning: ماشاءاللہ، نظر نہ لگے، اللہ کرے ایسا ہی رہے، اچھی بات کے بعد بدقسمتی سے بچنے کے لئے کہا جاتا ہے، یہ جملہ اس وقت کہا جاتا ہے جب کوئی شخص اپنی اچھی قسمت کامیابی یا خوش قسمتی کا ذکر کرے اور بدقسمتی سے بچنے کے لیے اللہ سے خیر مانگے
antonyms: Invite bad luck

englishMeaning: To have sexual intercourse with someone. This phrase originates from the Bible, where "to know" someone sometimes refers to a sexual relationship rather than simply being acquainted. It implies intimacy in a sexual or marital context.
synonyms: Sleep with, Have relations with, Be intimate with, Make love to
urduMeaning: کسی کے ساتھ جنسی تعلق رکھنا، یہ محاورہ بائبل سے آیا ہے جس میں "کسی کو جاننا" کا مطلب محض واقفیت نہیں بلکہ جنسی یا ازدواجی تعلق رکھنے کے معنی میں استعمال ہوتا ہے
examples: The old text said he knew her in the biblical sense, implying a private relationship. Some passages in the Bible say Adam knew Eve in the biblical sense. The phrase is often misunderstood by those unfamiliar with biblical language. He avoided using that expression because it explicitly refers to sexual intimacy.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن سان جنسي تعلق رکڻ، هيءَ اصطلاح بائبل مان آئي آهي جتي "ڪڏهن ڪنهن کي ڄاڻڻ" مطلب صرف ملاقات نه پر جنسي يا ازدواجي تعلق رکڻ جي معنيٰ هوندي آهي
antonyms: Acquaint with, Meet, Recognize, Know casually
word: Know somebody in the biblical sense

examples: He knowingly broke the rules despite the warning. She knowingly shared false information online. The company knowingly ignored safety standards. He walked into the deal knowingly, accepting all risks.
synonyms: Intentionally, Deliberately, Consciously, Purposefully, Willfully
sindhiMeaning: ڄاڻي واڻي، سمجهه سان، ڪو ڪم پوري ڄاڻ شعور يا ارادي سان ڪرڻ، اهڙي حالت ۾ ماڻهو کي خبر هوندي آهي ته هو ڇا ڪري رهيو آهي ۽ ان جا نتيجا ڪهڙا ٿي سگهن ٿا
urduMeaning: جان بوجھ کر، دانستہ طور پر، کسی کام کو پوری سمجھ بوجھ شعور اور ارادے کے ساتھ کرنا، اس میں انسان کو معلوم ہوتا ہے کہ وہ کیا کر رہا ہے اور اس کے نتائج کیا ہو سکتے ہیں
englishMeaning: With awareness or intention. Doing something with full awareness, understanding, or intention. The person is conscious of what they are doing and understands the consequences or facts involved.
antonyms: Unknowingly, Accidentally, Unintentionally, Innocently

englishMeaning: To yield or submit under pressure. To push or strike using knuckles. To submit or apply pressure. The joint in a finger where it bends. A cut of meat from the leg joint. Mechanical joint or hinge part.
synonyms: Joint, Finger joint, Yield, Submit, Bend
examples: He cracked his knuckles before starting to type. She injured a knuckle while playing basketball. The boxer’s knuckles were bleeding after the match. She knocked on the door with her knuckles. The manager refused to knuckle under pressure.
sindhiMeaning: دٻاءُ هيٺ مڃڻ، ڳنڍ سان هڻڻ، هٿ جي ڳنڍن سان زور ڏيڻ، آڱريون سختي سان موڙڻ، آڱر جو ڳنڍ، گوشت جو ڳنڍ وارو حصو، مشيني ڳنڍ، دٻاءُ ڏيڻ يا مڃڻ، جانور جي ٽنگ جو ڳنڍ، پائپ يا ڍانچي جو موڙ، دروازي جي قبضي جو گول ڳنڍ وارو حصو، سخت محنت ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: دباؤ میں آ کر مان لینا، مکے سے مارنا، دباؤ ڈالنا یا جھک جانا، انگلی کا جوڑ، گوشت کا ایک حصہ، مشینی جوڑ، قبضے کا گول حصہ، جانور کی ٹانگ کا جوڑ، پائپ یا ڈھانچے کا موڑ، انگلیوں کو سختی سے موڑنا، ہاتھ کے جوڑوں سے زور لگانا، سخت محنت کرنا

synonyms: Get serious, Focus, Work hard

sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کي رسيءَ سان قابو ۾ رکڻ يا محدود ڪرڻ، رسي پٽي يا زنجير جيڪو جانور کي قابو ڪرڻ لاءِ استعمال ٿئي
urduMeaning: کسی کو پٹے یا رسی کے ذریعے قابو میں رکھنا یا محدود کرنا، جانور کو قابو کرنے کے لیے پٹہ یا رسی
englishMeaning: To control, restrain, or guide an animal (or figuratively, a person or thing) by using a leash. A strap, cord, or chain used to control, guide, or restrain an animal, usually a dog.
antonyms: Unleash, Free, Release, Freedom, Release, Unchain

examples: Let’s leave aside our differences and focus on work. Let’s leave aside our personal differences and work together for the project. Leave aside the cost for now; first, we need to check if the plan is practical. Let’s leave aside this discussion until we have more information.
synonyms: Put aside, Ignore
urduMeaning: وقتی طور پر نظر انداز کرنا، کسی بات یا چیز کو وقتی طور پر نظر انداز کر دینا تاکہ کسی اور اہم بات پر توجہ دی جا سکے
antonyms: Focus, Consider
sindhiMeaning: عارضي طور نظرانداز ڪرڻ، ڪنهن ڳالهه يا شيءَ کي عارضي طور نظرانداز ڪرڻ يا هڪ طرف رکڻ، جيئن ڪنهن وڌيڪ اهم ڳالهه تي ڌيان ڏئي سگهجي
englishMeaning: To ignore or not consider something for the moment. To set something aside in order to focus on something more important.

sindhiMeaning: پٺ تي ڇڏڻ، ڇڏي وڃڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ يا شخص کي پاڻ سان گڏ نه وٺي وڃڻ، پاڻ کان پوءِ ڪجھه باقي ڇڏڻ (جهڙوڪ ياد اثر يا ملڪيت)، ٻين کان اڳتي نڪري وڃڻ
urduMeaning: پیچھے چھوڑ دینا، کسی چیز یا شخص کو ساتھ نہ لے جانا، کچھ اپنے بعد باقی چھوڑ جانا (جیسے یادیں اثرات یا جائیداد)، دوسروں سے آگے نکل جانا
antonyms: Carry, Take along
englishMeaning: To forget or fail to take something/someone along. To cause something to remain after departing. To surpass or outdo others. To create a lasting impact, memory, or legacy.
synonyms: Abandon, Forget
examples: He left his bag behind on the train. The poet left behind a treasure of beautiful verses. The young athlete left all his competitors behind. We should not leave anyone behind when we move. He left his phone behind on the bus.

urduMeaning: کوئی کسر نہ چھوڑنا، ہر ممکن کوشش کرنا، کسی مقصد کو حاصل کرنے کے لیے ہر ممکن کوشش کرنا، ہر راستہ اختیار کرنا
antonyms: Neglect
englishMeaning: Try every possibility. To try every possible way or make every possible effort to achieve something or find something. It means to do everything you can, not giving up until the goal is reached.
examples: The police left no stone unturned in searching for the missing child. She left no stone unturned to get the scholarship. Our team left no stone unturned to win the competition. He left no stone unturned to make his parents proud.
sindhiMeaning: هر ممڪن ڪوشش ڪرڻ، ڪا به ڪسر نه ڇڏڻ، مڪمل جدوجهد ڪرڻ، ڪنهن مقصد تائين پهچڻ لاءِ سڀ رستا آزمائڻ، سڀ ڪوششون ڪرڻ، ڪا به ڪوتاهي نه ڇڏڻ
synonyms: Try everything

urduMeaning: کسی کو مشکل یا مصیبت کے وقت میں اکیلا چھوڑ دینا
antonyms: Support, Assist, Stand by, Help, Back up, Stay with
englishMeaning: To abandon someone in a difficult or dangerous situation, especially when they need help or support the most.
examples: When his friend was arrested, he left him in the lurch instead of helping him. The company left its workers in the lurch by closing down without notice. She promised to help but left me in the lurch at the last moment. A true friend will never leave you in the lurch when you are in trouble.
sindhiMeaning: مشڪل وقت ۾ ڪنهن کي اڪيلو ڇڏڻ، مدد کان محروم ڪرڻ يا بي يارو مددگار ڇڏي ڏيڻ
synonyms: Betray, Leave helpless, Let down

englishMeaning: Something valuable or influential that is passed from one generation to another. The achievements or reputation someone leaves behind. A software or system that is old but still in use. Long lasting cultural or historical influence. Anything handed down from the past. It can be property, money, achievements, traditions, values or the lasting impact a person leaves behind. It often highlights long term influence.
antonyms: Loss, Dispossession, Forfeit, Neglect
urduMeaning: کوئی چیز یا اثر جو نسل در نسل منتقل ہو، کسی شخص کا چھوڑا ہوا اثر یا نام، پرانا نظام یا طریقہ جو اب بھی استعمال ہو رہا ہو، تاریخی یا ثقافتی ورثہ، وہ چیز جو ماضی سے آگے منتقل ہو یہ دولت جائیداد روایات قدریں یا کسی شخص کا چھوڑا ہوا اثر بھی ہو سکتا ہے
sindhiMeaning: شي يا اثر جيڪو نسلن کان نسلن تائين منتقل ٿئي، ڪنهن جو ڇڏي ويل اثر يا نالو، پراڻو نظام يا طريقو جيڪو اڃا هلي رهيو آهي، تاريخي يا ثقافتي ورثو، ڪا به شي جيڪا پوئين دور يا ماڻهن کان اڳتي منتقل ٿئي اها دولت ملڪيت روايتون قدرون يا ڪنهن شخص جو ڇڏي ويل اثر ٿي سگهي ٿي
synonyms: Heritage, Inheritance, Tradition, Bequest, Endowment, Birthright
examples: Her kindness is the greatest legacy she left for her children. The cultural legacy of this region is rich and unique. He wants to build a legacy that future generations will admire. The scientist’s research became a lasting legacy for the medical field.

antonyms: History of failure, Pattern of loss, Trail of mistakes, Legacy of defeat
englishMeaning: A lasting impact or influence created by a history of achievements. The enduring results, reputation, or benefits that come from consistent achievements, excellence, or accomplishments over time. It often implies something valuable passed down to others, such as lessons, practices, or reputation.
synonyms: Heritage of achievement, Record of accomplishment, Tradition of excellence, Mark of distinction
sindhiMeaning: نسل در نسل، ڪاميابيءَ جو ورثو، ڪاميابيءَ جي يادگار، اهو اثر يا اهميت جيڪا مسلسل ڪاميابين ۽ ڪوششن جي نتيجي ۾ رهجي وڃي، اهو اڪثر ڪجھ مفيد يا قيمتي شي ٻين لاءِ ڇڏي وڃڻ کي ظاهر ڪري ٿو
examples: The company has built a legacy of success through innovation and hard work. Her leadership left behind a legacy of success that inspires others. The founder left a legacy of success that the company still benefits from today. Education can build a legacy of success in communities.
urduMeaning: نسل در نسل، کامیابی کی وراثت ، کامیابی کا ورثہ، مسلسل کامیابیوں اور کارکردگی کے نتیجے میں جو اثر یا وقار باقی رہتا ہے، یہ اکثر دوسروں کے لیے قیمتی سبق یا اثر چھوڑنے کو ظاہر کرتا ہے

antonyms: Certainty
urduMeaning: کہانی، قومی روایتی افسانے، داستان
sindhiMeaning: روايت، داستان، اڪريل عبارت، قصو، ڪهاڻي، ڏند ڪٿا، سرخي، نقشي تي لکيل لفظ
examples: Legend has it that the lake was formed by tears of a god.
englishMeaning: A story from ancient times about people and events, that may or may not be true, this type of story. An explanatory list of the symbols on a map or chart. A traditional but unfounded story that gives the reason for a current custom, belief, or fact of nature.
synonyms: Fable

antonyms: Respondent, Defendant, Appellee
sindhiMeaning: درخواست ڏيندڙ، اهو شخص جيڪو عدالت يا ڪنهن اختيار وارن جي فيصلي خلاف اپيل ڪري ٿو ۽ اُها فيصلي ٻي مٿين عدالت کان نظرثاني ڪرائڻ لاءِ پيش ڪري ٿو
urduMeaning: اپیل کرنے والا، وہ شخص جو کسی عدالت یا مجاز اتھارٹی کے فیصلے سے متفق نہ ہو اور اس فیصلے کو اعلیٰ عدالت یا اتھارٹی کے سامنے دوبارہ جانچنے کے لیے اپیل کرتا ہے
synonyms: Petitioner, Claimant, Challenger, Complainant

englishMeaning: A person who makes an appeal to a higher court against a decision made by a lower court. Someone who disagrees with a judgment or decision made by a court, tribunal, or authority and formally requests a higher authority or court to review and change that decision.

synonyms: Lawfulness, Validity, Authenticity, Justifiability, Rightfulness
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ جو جائز يا صحيح هئڻ، سماجي طور قبوليل هئڻ، قانوني حق جي بنياد تي اختيار، ڪنهن ڳالهه جي صحيح ۽ معتبر هجڻ جي حيثيت، ڪنهن ڪم يا فيصلي جو قانوني طور صحيح هئڻ يا سماج پاران درست ۽ جائز سمجهيو وڃڻ
examples: The new policy gained legitimacy after public approval. People questioned the legitimacy of the election results. The court confirmed the legitimacy of the company’s ownership. The leadership struggled to maintain its legitimacy during the crisis.
urduMeaning: کسی چیز کا جائز یا قانونی ہونا، سماجی طور پر قبول کیے جانے کی کیفیت، قانونی حق یا جواز کی بنیاد پر اختیار، کسی بات کا معتبر یا صحیح تسلیم کیا جانا، کسی عمل یا فیصلے کا قانونی طور پر درست ہونا یا معاشرے کے نزدیک جائز اور قابل قبول ہونا ہے
englishMeaning: The state of being lawful, accepted or rightful. The quality of something being accepted as correct, lawful, rightful or valid by law, society or moral standards. Social acceptance or moral justification. Authority based on trust or legal right. Recognition of something as proper or genuine.
antonyms: Illegitimacy, Unlawfulness, Invalidity, Wrongfulness, Unacceptability

urduMeaning: شرعی، قانونی، حلال، مناسب، مستند، حقیقی، درست، جائز، ایسا کام دعویٰ یا حق جو قانون اصول یا سماجی طور پر درست اور تسلیم شدہ ہو، پرانے مفہوم میں ایسا بچہ جو قانونی شادی سے پیدا ہوا ہو
antonyms: Illegal, Illegitimate, Unlawful, Invalid, Fake
englishMeaning: Lawful, valid, or accepted as proper according to law, rules, or social standards. It can describe something genuine, reasonable, or officially recognized. In older usage it also refers to a child born to parents who are legally married.
synonyms: Lawful, Valid, Legal, Genuine, Authentic, Justified
examples: Her complaint about the poor service was legitimate. The company proved that its business activities were legitimate. Citizens have a legitimate right to demand transparency from the government. The court confirmed that the contract was legitimate and legally binding. She raised some legitimate concerns.
sindhiMeaning: حلال، مناسب، درست، اصلي، حق وارو، جائز قانوني يا صحيح، اهڙو ڪم يا دعويٰ جيڪو قانون ضابطن يا سماجي اصولن مطابق درست هجي، پراڻي استعمال ۾ اهو لفظ اهڙي ٻار لاءِ به ايندو آهي جيڪو قانوني شادي مان پيدا ٿيو هجي

sindhiMeaning: فرصت، واندڪائي، مھلت، غير مصروف، فارغ، تفريح، فرست، فراغت
examples: I suggest you take the forms way & read them at your leisure.

urduMeaning: فرصت، مہلت

sindhiMeaning: مدد ڪرڻ، هٿ ونجهڻ، سهارو ڏيڻ، ساٿ ڏيڻ، خدمت پيش ڪرڻ
synonyms: Support, Aid, Give a hand, Pitch in, Cooperate
examples: Could you lend a hand with the bags? Could you lend a hand with these boxes? They’re too heavy for me. The teacher asked the students to lend a hand in cleaning the classroom. When my neighbor was sick, I lent a hand by cooking for her family. Volunteers lent a hand to rebuild houses after the flood.

antonyms: Hinder, Ignore, Refuse, Oppose

synonyms: Pulse, Legume, Dal, Split pea
urduMeaning: دال، ایک چھوٹا گول یا چپٹا بیج ہے جو دال کے پودے سے حاصل ہوتا ہے، یہ عام طور پر سوپ سالن اور کری میں استعمال ہوتا ہے، یہ پروٹین اور فائبر سے بھرپور ہوتا ہے
examples: She cooked lentils for dinner. Lentils are healthy and full of protein. I added lentils to the soup. Many people eat lentils every day

englishMeaning: A woman who is emotionally, romantically, or sexually attracted to other women. The word can also describe anything related to such attraction or identity.
urduMeaning: ہم جنس پرست عورت، وہ عورت جو دوسری عورتوں کی طرف جذباتی رومانوی یا جنسی کشش رکھتی ہو
sindhiMeaning: هم جنس پرست عورت، عورت جو عورت سان همبستري ٿيڻ، هم جنس يا شهوت پرستي، اها عورت جيڪا عورتن ڏانهن جذباتي رومانوي يا جنسي ڪشش رکي
antonyms: Heterosexual woman, Straight woman
synonyms: Gay woman, Homosexual woman, Sapphic woman, Woman attracted to women
examples: She openly identifies as a lesbian and supports equal rights for all people. The novel tells the story of a lesbian couple living in a small town. Many communities organize events to celebrate lesbian culture and identity. She joined a support group for lesbian women in her city.

synonyms: Disappoint, Fail
urduMeaning: کسی کی توقعات پر پورا نہ اترنا، کسی کو مایوس کرنا، جسمانی طور پر نیچے کرنا یا چھوڑنا، رفتار کم کرنا
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کي اميدن تي پورو نه لهڻ، مايوس ڪرڻ، جسماني طور تي هيٺ ڪرڻ يا ڇڏڻ، رفتار گهٽ ڪرڻ
examples: He promised to help, but he let me down. The team was let down by their captain’s absence. I felt let down when the package arrived late. Don’t let me down on this project.

antonyms: Support, Encourage

examples: I let him in through the back door. She let in the cat after it meowed. Don’t let negative thoughts in. He finally let her in on the secret.
urduMeaning: اندر آنے دینا، جذبات یا احساسات کو دل میں جگہ دینا، شریک کرنا، موقعہ یا اثر کو اپنی زندگی میں داخل ہونے دینا
sindhiMeaning: اندر اچڻ جي اجازت ڏيڻ، پنهنجا جذبا يا احساس ڪنهن شيءِ لاءِ کولڻ، شامل ڪرڻ، موقعو يا اثر پنهنجي زندگيءَ ۾ آڻڻ
synonyms: Admit, Allow
antonyms: Refuse, Exclude
englishMeaning: To allow someone or something to enter. To allow feelings, emotions, or thoughts to affect oneself. To share secret or private information; to include someone in knowledge. To allow opportunities, influences, or changes to enter one’s life.

antonyms: Punish, Penalize
englishMeaning: To excuse someone from punishment or responsibility. To allow something to explode or release (like fireworks). To release someone from a duty or obligation. To let something happen without interference.
examples: The teacher let him off for being late this time. The police let off the driver with a warning. They let off fireworks on New Year’s Eve. She was let off from her duty because of illness.
sindhiMeaning: سزا کان آزاد ڪرڻ، معاف ڪرڻ، فرض يا ذميداري کان آزاد ڪرڻ، ڪا شيءِ بنا روڪ ٽوڪ ٿيڻ ڏيڻ، ڪا شيءِ ڌماڪي يا ڇڏڻ
urduMeaning: سزا معاف کرنا، گولی چلانا، آزاد کرنا، بغیر مداخلت کے ہونے دینا، سزا یا ذمہ داری سے بری کرنا
synonyms: Excuse, Release

englishMeaning: To add something at the end. To attach, add, or join something to the end of a document, list, text, or other item.
antonyms: Remove, Detach, Delete, Subtract, Separate
synonyms: Add, Attach, Affix, Annex, Supplement, Join, Include
sindhiMeaning: آخر ۾ شامل ڪرڻ، ڳنڍڻ، وڌائڻ، شامل ڪرڻ، پڇاڙي ۾ لڳائڻ، ڪنهن به لسٽ دستاويز يا لکت جي آخر ۾ ڪا شيءِ وڌائڻ يا شامل ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: آخر میں شامل کرنا، منسلک کرنا، اضافہ کرنا، ساتھ لگانا، آخر میں جوڑنا، کسی دستاویز فہرست یا متن کے آخر میں کوئی چیز جوڑنا یا شامل کرنا
examples: Please append your signature to the document. The report was incomplete, so he appended extra data. She appended a note at the end of the email. The program appends new records automatically.

urduMeaning: اہر جانے کی اجازت دینا، جذبات آواز یا کسی چیز کو خارج کرنا، کپڑوں یا جگہ کو بڑا کرنا، راز یا معلومات ظاہر کرنا
antonyms: Confine, Detain
synonyms: Release, Free
englishMeaning: To allow a person, animal, or object to exit or leave a place. To release something contained, such as air, sound, or emotion. To enlarge a piece of clothing or extend space. To reveal or disclose information.
examples: She let out the cat before leaving the house. He let out a sigh of relief when the exam was over. I need to let out this dress; it’s too tight now. He accidentally let out the secret about the surprise party.
sindhiMeaning: ٻاهر وڃڻ جي اجازت ڏيڻ، جذبات آواز يا مواد کي ڇڏڻ، ڪپڙن کي ڦهلائڻ يا وڏو ڪرڻ، راز يا معلومات ظاهر ڪرڻ

antonyms: Hide, Conceal
englishMeaning: To reveal a secret or tell something that was supposed to be kept hidden, often by mistake. When someone “lets the cat out of the bag,” they tell others a secret that was not meant to be shared.
sindhiMeaning: راز ظاهر ڪرڻ، راز فاش ڪرڻ، لڪيل ڳالهه ظاهر ڪرڻ، ساهه ۾ اچي وڃڻ، جڏهن ڪو ماڻهو ڪا اهڙي ڳالهه ٻڌائي ڇڏي جيڪا لڪل هجڻ گهرجي ها
word: Let the cat out of the bag
examples: He let the cat out of the bag about the surprise. John let the cat out of the bag about Mary’s surprise birthday party. Don’t let the cat out of the bag; it’s supposed to be a secret!. She let the cat out of the bag and everyone knew about the new project. When he mentioned the promotion, he realized he had let the cat out of the bag.
synonyms: Disclose, Expose
urduMeaning: راز کھول دینا، راز افشا کرنا، چھپی ہوئی بات بتا دینا، بھید کھول دینا، جب کوئی شخص غلطی سے یا جان بوجھ کر کوئی راز ظاہر کر دیتا ہے
آئیے اصل بات کرتے ہیں، چلیے سیدھی بات کرتے ہیں، اب کام کی بات کرتے ہیں
antonyms: Beat around the bush, Talk nonsense, Avoid the main issue, Make small talk
sindhiMeaning: اچو سڌي ڳالهه ڪيون، اصل ڳالهه تي اچون، اچو، ڪم واري ڳالهه ڪيون، اچو، اصلي ڳالهه ڪيون
synonyms: Get to the point, Be direct, Cut to the chase, Discuss seriously
englishMeaning: To talk seriously and directly about a practical matter, especially about business, money, or final decisions, without wasting time on small talk. To get straight to the point or start a serious discussion about an important issue.
examples: We’ve discussed enough background, now let’s talk turkey and finalize the deal. They sat down after dinner and talked turkey about the project budget. Enough small talk, let’s talk turkey about your salary expectations. Before signing the contract, the partners talked turkey about the risks involved.

The snake has a lethal bite that can kill within minutes. The chemical gas was lethal when inhaled in large amounts. A lethal disease spread quickly in the remote village. The soldier was trained to handle lethal weapons safely.
englishMeaning: Something that is capable of causing death or is deadly. Anything that can cause death, either instantly or over time. It is often used for poisons, weapons, diseases, or dangerous conditions.

antonyms: Harmless, Safe, Nonlethal, Benign, Inoffensive

urduMeaning: کسی لفظ یا نام کو عارضی طور یاد نہ کر پانا حالانکہ وہ ذہن میں موجود ہو، لفظ یاد کرنے میں وقتی رکاوٹ، ذہنی تلاش میں تاخیر، ایسی کیفیت جس میں جانا پہچانا لفظ فوراً یاد نہ آئے

englishMeaning: A situation where everyone has equal opportunities, rights, and conditions. A level playing field refers to fairness in a system where no individual or group has an unfair advantage. examples: The government aims to create a level playing field for all businesses. Scholarships help provide a level playing field for students from poor backgrounds. englishMeaning: To use something (resources, skills, influence, or connections) to gain a strategic advantage or achieve a desired result. antonyms: Addition, Extra, Supplement, Bonus

Dull person, Introvert, Quiet person, Boring, Lifeless
synonyms: Entertainer, Cheerful person, Lively person

examples: He is the life and soul of the party. Ali is the life and soul of every party, everyone feels happy when he’s around. Without her, the meeting felt dull; she’s truly the life and soul of our team. His jokes and laughter make him the life and soul of any gathering. Even in difficult times, she remains the life and soul of her family.

The anterior cruciate ligament in the knee is commonly injured in athletes. She tore a ligament in her ankle while playing football. Proper warm-up exercises help protect ligaments from damage. Ligaments are less elastic than tendons but equally important for joint stability.

antonyms: Joint instability, Disconnection
englishMeaning: A strong band of fibrous tissue that connects bones to other bones, stabilizing and supporting joints. It helps limit movement to prevent injury. Ligaments are flexible but not elastic; they maintain joint stability. Injuries to ligaments include sprains and tears.
urduMeaning: ہڈیوں کو جوڑنے والا ٹشو، ایک مضبوط ریشے دار ٹشو جو ہڈیوں کو ایک دوسرے سے جوڑتا ہے اور جوڑوں کو مستحکم رکھتا ہے، یہ حرکت کو محدود کرتا ہے تاکہ چوٹ سے بچا جا سکے، جوڑوں کو سہارا دیتے ہیں اور ہڈیوں کے درمیان حرکت کی حد کو کنٹرول کرتے ہیں

antonyms: History repeats itself, It can happen again, Recurring event, Patterns repeat
englishMeaning: A rare or unusual event is unlikely to happen again in the same way. Rare events do not usually repeat. Bad luck is unlikely to happen again. Extraordinary success is hard to repeat. Situations rarely occur exactly the same way twice.
examples: After failing the exam once, she stayed calm because lightning never strikes twice. He lost his wallet last week, but he believes lightning never strikes twice. The team lost badly in the first match, but they are confident lightning never strikes twice. She got a rare opportunity and doubts she will get the same chance again, since lightning never strikes twice.
synonyms: Once in a blue moon, A rare occurrence, History does not repeat itself exactly, Unlikely to happen again
sindhiMeaning: ڪو ناياب يا غير معمولي واقعو ٻيهر ساڳي طرح ٿيڻ جو امڪان گهٽ هوندو آهي، ناياب واقعا عام طور ٻيهر نٿا ٿين، خراب قسمت ٻيهر اچڻ جو امڪان گهٽ هوندو، غير معمولي ڪاميابي ٻيهر حاصل ڪرڻ مشڪل هوندي، حالتون ساڳي نموني ٻيهر نٿيون ورجائن
urduMeaning: کوئی نایاب یا غیر معمولی واقعہ دوبارہ اسی طرح ہونے کا امکان کم ہوتا ہے، نایاب واقعات عام طور پر دوبارہ نہیں ہوتے، بدقسمتی دوبارہ آنے کا امکان کم ہوتا ہے، غیر معمولی کامیابی کو دہرانا مشکل ہوتا ہے، حالات بالکل ایک جیسے دوبارہ پیش نہیں آتے

examples: Ahmed is a brilliant carpenter just like his father, Like father, like son. His father was very generous, and he helps everyone too, Like father, like son. Both the father and son love cricket and play professionally, Like father, like son. The boy became a successful teacher, following his father’s path, Like father, like son.
sindhiMeaning: جهڙا ڪانگ تهڙا ٻچا، جهڙو پيءُ تهڙو پٽ، هيءَ چوڻي تڏهن استعمال ٿيندي آهي جڏهن پٽ پنهنجي پيءُ جهڙيون عادتون صلاحيتون اخلاق يا ڪم ڏيکاري، اها سٺين يا خراب ٻنهي عادتن لاءِ استعمال ٿي سگهي ٿي
urduMeaning: جیسے کوے ویسے بچے، جیسا باپ ویسا بیٹا، یہ کہاوت اس وقت استعمال ہوتی ہے جب بیٹا اپنے والد جیسی عادتیں صلاحیتیں طبیعت یا کردار ظاہر کرے، یہ اچھی یا بری دونوں قسم کی خصوصیات کے لیے استعمال ہو سکتی ہے
synonyms: A chip off the old block, The apple does not fall far from the tree, Following in his father’s footsteps, Two peas in a pod
antonyms: Different as night and day, Nothing like his father, Opposites in nature
englishMeaning: A son often behaves, thinks, or has qualities similar to his father. Used when a boy or man shows behavior, talents, habits, personality, or character similar to his father. It may be used positively for good qualities or negatively for bad habits.

antonyms: Compatible, Harmonious, Well-matched, Agreeable
englishMeaning: Two people or things that do not mix or get along well together. Completely different in nature.
synonyms: Incompatible, Mismatched, Conflicting, Opposite
urduMeaning: دو لوگ یا چیزیں جو کبھی ایک ساتھ نہیں چل سکتیں، فطرت یا مزاج میں بالکل مختلف ہوں
sindhiMeaning: ٻه ماڻهو يا شيون جيڪي ڪڏهن به گڏ نه هلن، مزاج يا فطرت ۾ بلڪل مختلف هجن
examples: My brother and I are like oil and water; we never agree on anything. Politics and honesty often seem like oil and water. She and her coworker are like oil and water; they can’t work together peacefully. Their ideas are like oil and water, so cooperation is difficult.

sindhiMeaning: اهڙو ماڻهو يا جاندار جيڪو ڍنڍن ۽ ساکن مٺي پاڻي وارن هنڌن کي پسند ڪري
antonyms: Riverine organism, Marine organism, Ocean dweller, Terrestrial organism
englishMeaning: A person or organism that loves or prefers lakes and calm freshwater environments
synonyms: Lake lover, Freshwater organism, Still water species, Lake dwelling organism
urduMeaning: ایسا شخص یا جاندار جو جھیلوں اور پرسکون میٹھے پانی کے ماحول کو پسند کرے
examples: The scientist studied several limnophile species living in the lake. As a limnophile, she enjoys spending weekends near quiet lakes. Many aquatic plants in the region are limnophile and grow well in still water. The park attracts limnophile visitors who appreciate lake ecosystems.

antonyms: Scatter, Disperse
urduMeaning: لوگوں یا اشیاء کو سیدھی قطار میں لگانا، سرگرمیاں یا واقعات ترتیب دینا، کسی چیز کے لیے تیار ہونا، کسی چیز سے ہم آہنگ ہونا یا میل کھانا
englishMeaning: To place people or objects in a row or order. To schedule or organize activities or events. To be ready or prepared for something. To match or correspond with something.
sindhiMeaning: ماڻهن يا شين کي سڌي قطار ۾ رکڻ، سرگرمين يا منصوبن کي ترتيب ڏيڻ، ڪنهن ڪم لاءِ تيار ٿيڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ سان هم آهنگ يا ملائڻ
examples: Students lined up outside the classroom before the assembly. We need to line up the chairs for the meeting. He lined up several interviews for next week. The planets line up perfectly during the eclipse.
synonyms: Arrange, Organize

sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ کي ٻي شيءِ سان اهڙي ريت ڳنڍڻ جو اهي گڏجي ڪم ڪن يا ڪنهن وڏي نظام جو حصو بڻجن، هي لفظ جسماني ڳانڍاپي لاءِ به استعمال ٿئي ٿو ۽ خيالن يا منصوبن جي ڳانڍاپي لاءِ به
englishMeaning: To connect one thing with another so that they work together or become part of a larger system. It can be used for physical connections like machines and cables, or for abstract ideas such as linking a plan with a strategy or linking people with an organization.
antonyms: Disconnect, Separate, Detach, Isolate, Unlink
examples: The new software will link in with the existing database. The community project is designed to link in with local schools. Please link in the new device before starting the system. His research links in closely with climate policy discussions.
urduMeaning: کسی چیز کو دوسری چیز کے ساتھ اس طرح جوڑنا کہ وہ مل کر کام کریں یا کسی بڑے نظام کا حصہ بن جائیں، یہ جسمانی تعلق کے لیے بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے اور خیالات یا منصوبوں کے تعلق کے لیے بھی
synonyms: Connect, Join, Attach, Integrate, Tie in

antonyms: Disapproval, Criticism
examples: The boss gave the project a thumbs up. He gave me a thumbs up before the presentation. Everyone gave a thumbs up to the new policy. That’s a thumbs up from the team.
urduMeaning: منظور یا تعریف کا اشارہ، منظوری یا حوصلہ افزائی کا اشارہ
synonyms: Approval, Praise
sindhiMeaning: پسنديدگي جو اشارو، سٺائي يا حمايت جو اشارو
englishMeaning: A sign of approval or agreement, to express that something is good or accepted.

urduMeaning: بھوک بڑھانے کے لیے کھانے سے پہلے کھائی جانے والی چیز، ابتدائی کھانا، ہلکا ناشتہ، دلچسپی بڑھانے والی چیز، کسی بڑی چیز کا تعارف، ایسی خوراک جو مرکزی کھانے سے پہلے پیش کی جاتی ہے تاکہ بھوک بڑھے، یہ کسی ایسی چیز کے لیے بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے جو دلچسپی یا خواہش پیدا کرے
synonyms: Starter, Snack, Hors d'oeuvre, First course, Light bite
englishMeaning: A small dish or something that stimulates appetite before the main meal. A starter dish. A light snack before meals. Something that increases desire or interest. An introduction to something larger. A small portion of food served before the main course to stimulate the appetite. Anything that creates interest or desire for something more.
examples: She ordered a soup as an appetizer before the main course. These small snacks work well as appetizers at parties. The trailer served as an appetizer for the upcoming movie. Fresh salad can be a healthy appetizer.
sindhiMeaning: بک وڌائڻ لاءِ کاڌي کان اڳ کائڻ واري شيءِ، شروعاتي کاڌو، هلڪو سنئڪ، دلچسپي وڌائڻ واري شيءِ ڪنهن وڏي شيءِ جو تعارف، اها شيءِ جيڪا مکيه کاڌي کان اڳ پيش ڪئي وڃي ته جيئن بک وڌي وڃي، اهو لفظ اهڙي شيءِ لاءِ به استعمال ٿئي ٿو جيڪا ڪنهن شئي ۾ دلچسپي يا خواهش پيدا ڪري
antonyms: Main course, Dessert, Full meal

examples: Researchers link air pollution to respiratory diseases. This button links to the company’s official website. The report links poor planning to project failure. He linked his success to hard work and discipline.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ کي ٻي شيءِ سان لاڳاپيل ڪرڻ يا ڳنڍڻ، اهو جسماني شين خيالن سببن يا انٽرنيٽ صفحن لاءِ استعمال ٿيندو آهي
synonyms: Connect to, Relate to, Associate with, Attach to
antonyms: Separate from, Disconnect from, Detach from, Isolate from
englishMeaning: To connect, relate, or associate one thing with another. It can be used in physical, digital, or abstract contexts. For example, connecting two ideas, attaching a webpage to another webpage, or relating a problem to a specific cause.
urduMeaning: کسی چیز کو کسی دوسری چیز سے متعلق یا منسلک کرنا، یہ لفظ خیالات وجوہات ویب سائٹس یا اشیاء کے تعلق کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے
لوگوں یا چیزوں کو آپس میں جوڑنا تاکہ وہ ساتھ کام کریں، کسی مقصد کے لیے کسی کے ساتھ شامل ہونا، طے شدہ جگہ پر کسی سے ملنا، رابطہ قائم کرنا یا تعلق بنانا
antonyms: Separate, Disconnect, Divide, Detach, Split
englishMeaning: To connect people, systems, or things so they work together. To join with someone for a shared purpose such as work, travel, or partnership. To meet someone at a planned place. To establish communication between groups, devices, or individuals.
sindhiMeaning: ماڻهن يا شين کي پاڻ ۾ ڳنڍڻ ته جيئن گڏ ڪم ڪن، ڪنهن مقصد لاءِ گڏ ٿيڻ يا شامل ٿيڻ، طئي ٿيل هنڌ تي ڪنهن سان ملي وڃڻ، رابطي يا لاڳاپي قائم ڪرڻ
examples: The two companies decided to link up for a new project. We will link up with the research team tomorrow morning. The railway lines link up several major cities. She linked up with her old friends after many years.
synonyms: Connect, Join, Unite, Associate, Collaborate

antonyms: Separate from, Disconnect from, Break away from, Split from, Part from
englishMeaning: To connect, join, or cooperate with a person, group, or organization. It can refer to meeting someone, forming a partnership, or establishing communication for work, travel, or shared goals.
examples: We will link up with our partners to complete the project. She linked up with her old classmates during the reunion. The two companies linked up with each other for a new business venture. The hikers planned to link up with the rest of the group at the campsite.
urduMeaning: کسی فرد گروہ یا ادارے سے رابطہ قائم کرنا، مل کر کام کرنا یا کسی مقصد کے لیے شمولیت اختیار کرنا، یہ ملاقات کرنے یا تعاون کرنے کے معنی میں بھی آتا ہے
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ماڻهو گروپ يا اداري سان رابطو قائم ڪرڻ، گڏ ٿيڻ يا ڪنهن مقصد لاءِ سهڪار ڪرڻ، اهو ملاقات ڪرڻ يا ڀائيواري ڪرڻ لاءِ به استعمال ٿيندو آهي
synonyms: Connect with, Join, Team up with, Associate with, Collaborate with

antonyms: Criticize, Ignore, Disregard, Insult
englishMeaning: To treat someone as very important or famous. To give someone a lot of public attention, admiration, or praise, often like they are a celebrity or a hero
sindhiMeaning: وڏي اهميت ڏيڻ يا مشهور ڪرڻ، ڪنهن کي اهم شخص يا مشهور شخص وانگر مڃڻ، وڏي عزت ۽ توجه ڏيڻ
urduMeaning: کسی کو اہم یا مشہور سمجھنا، کسی شخص کو بہت زیادہ توجہ، عزت یا شہرت دینا، گویا وہ کسی ہیرو یا مشہور شخصیت ہو
examples: The media lionized the young scientist for her groundbreaking research. After the championship, the team was lionized by their fans. Critics often lionize actors for their latest performances. The author was lionized at the book festival for her new novel.
synonyms: Glorify, Celebrate, Honor, Praise, Admire
Majority, The bulk
urduMeaning: سب سے بڑا حصہ، اہم حصہ جو دوسروں سے زیادہ ہو
examples: He took the lion’s share of the profit. The manager took the lion’s share of the credit for the project. When profits were divided, the owner received the lion’s share. In most families, the mother does the lion’s share of the household work. The city spends the lion’s share of its budget on education.
englishMeaning: The largest portion or most important share of something. To get or take most of something, often leaving little for others.
sindhiMeaning: سڀني کان وڏو حصو، اهم حصو جيڪو ٻين جي ڀيٽ ۾ تمام گهڻو هجي
antonyms: Minority, Least part, Small portion

sindhiMeaning: ملڪيت يا ڪاروباري اثاثا وڪڻي انهن کي نقد رقم ۾ تبديل ڪرڻ ته جيئن قرض ادا ڪري سگهجن يا ڪاروبار ختم ڪيو وڃي، ڪڏهن ڪڏهن ڪنهن شيءِ کي مڪمل طور ختم ڪرڻ لاءِ به استعمال ٿيندو آهي
antonyms: Establish, Build, Invest, Preserve, Expand
englishMeaning: To sell property or business assets in order to obtain cash, usually to pay debts. It can also mean to close or dissolve a business, organization, or financial position. In some contexts it means to eliminate or completely remove something.
synonyms: Dissolve, Settle, Cash out, Wind up, Convert to cash
urduMeaning: کاروبار یا جائیداد کے اثاثے فروخت کر کے انہیں نقد رقم میں تبدیل کرنا تاکہ قرض ادا کیے جائیں یا کمپنی بند کی جائے، بعض اوقات کسی چیز کو مکمل طور پر ختم کرنے کے معنی میں بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے
examples: The company decided to liquidate its assets to pay off outstanding debts. After years of losses, the owners chose to liquidate the business. He had to liquidate some investments to cover his medical expenses. The court ordered the firm to liquidate its properties and distribute the money to creditors. The Govt tried to liquidate the rebel movement and failed.

urduMeaning: کاروبار کا خاتمہ، اثاثوں کو نقد میں تبدیل کرنا، قرضوں کی ادائیگی کے لئے جائیداد فروخت کرنا، کسی چیز کو مکمل طور پر ختم کرنا
antonyms: Establishment, Formation, Expansion, Continuation, Growth
synonyms: Bankruptcy, Dissolution, Winding up, Asset sale, Closure, Settlement
englishMeaning: The process of closing a business by selling its assets to pay debts. It can also mean converting assets into cash or eliminating something.
sindhiMeaning: ڪاروبار جو خاتمو، اثاثن کي نقد رقم ۾ بدلائڻ، قرض ادا ڪرڻ لاءِ ملڪيت وڪڻڻ، ڪنهن شي کي مڪمل ختم ڪرڻ، ڏيوالو نڪرڻ
examples: The company went into liquidation after suffering heavy financial losses. During liquidation, the firm's assets were sold to repay creditors. The court ordered the liquidation of the bankrupt corporation. Investors agreed to the liquidation of the failing project.

synonyms: List based article, Enumerated article, Numbered article
sindhiMeaning: فهرست جي صورت ۾ لکيل مضمون، اهڙو مضمون جيڪو نقطن يا نمبرن جي فهرست ۾ لکيل هوندو آهي، هر نقطو الڳ خيال يا ڄاڻ بيان ڪندو آهي، اهڙا مضمون آن لائن پڙهڻ ۾ آسان هوندا آهن
examples: She shared a listicle about healthy eating habits. The website published a listicle on top travel destinations. Readers like listicles because they save time. He wrote a listicle explaining climate change facts.
antonyms: Essay, Narrative article, Continuous prose
englishMeaning: An article written in the form of a list. A type of article that presents information as a numbered or bullet list. Each point usually explains one idea. Listicles are common in blogs, news websites, and social media because they are easy to read and quick to understand.
urduMeaning: فہرست کی شکل میں لکھا گیا مضمون، ایسا مضمون جو نکات یا نمبروں کی فہرست میں لکھا جاتا ہے، ہر نکتہ ایک الگ خیال یا معلومات پیش کرتا ہے، یہ انداز آن لائن پڑھنے میں آسان ہوتا ہے

englishMeaning: Using the real or original meaning of a word or phrase. In a literal, true, or accurate way. Used to emphasize the truth and accuracy of a statement or description.
urduMeaning: لغوی معنی میں، حرف بہ حرف ، لفظ بہ لفظ، حقیقی معنی میں، لَفظی طَور پَر ،لَفظاً، واقعی سچ مچ
antonyms: Figuratively, Virtually, Metaphorically, Carelessly, Freely, Imprecisely, Inaccurately
sindhiMeaning: لفظي طور، لفظي، حقيقتا، سچي پچي
examples: They were responsible for literally millions of deaths. The word ‘planet’ literally means ‘wandering body’. She refused food and literally starved herself to death. The event literally stopped the traffic.
synonyms: Accurately, Precisely, Really, Exactly, Verbatim

englishMeaning: Trash or rubbish left lying around. Waste scattered in public places. Babies born to an animal in one birth. Objects lying in a messy way. A seat or bed carried by people. To drop trash carelessly. To spread around. To give birth to young animals.
examples: Please do not throw litter in the park. The beach was covered with litter after the picnic. The cat had a litter of five kittens. Clothes littered the floor. The injured man was carried on a litter. The king traveled in a litter. People should not litter the streets. Books littered the table. The rabbit littered last night.
synonyms: Trash, Rubbish, Garbage, Waste, Debris, Mess
sindhiMeaning: گندگي يا ڪچرو جيڪو هتي اُتي پکڙيل هجي، هڪ ئي وقت ڄاول جانورن جا ٻچا، پکڙيل شيون، ماڻهو کڻي هلندڙ پالڪي يا کٽ، ڪچرو اڇلائڻ، پکڙائڻ، جانورن جا ٻچا ڄڻڻ، پکڙيل ڪچرو بي ترتيب شيون يا جانورن جا ٻچا
antonyms: Cleanliness, Order, Neatness, Tidiness
urduMeaning: کچرا جو اِدھر اُدھر پھیلا ہوا ہو، ایک ہی وقت میں پیدا ہونے والے جانوروں کے بچے، بکھری ہوئی چیزیں، اٹھا کر لے جانے والی پالکی یا اسٹریچر، کچرا پھینکنا، بکھیر دینا، جانور کا بچے دینا، بکھرا ہوا کچرا پھیلی ہوئی چیزیں یا جانوروں کے بچے
غلطیوں سے سیکھنا، زندگی میں تجربے سے سیکھنا
sindhiMeaning: غلطي مان سکڻ، زندگي ۾ تجربن مان سکڻ، خاص طور جڏهن ڪو ماڻهو غلطي يا نئين ڳالهه مان سبق وٺي ٿو
antonyms: Repeat mistakes, Remain ignorant
synonyms: Gain wisdom, Realize, Discover, Become wiser
englishMeaning: Used when you learn something new through experience, often after making a mistake or being surprised.
examples: I thought the shop was open on Sundays, but it was closed, Well, live and learn. He trusted the wrong person and lost money, but he said, “You live and learn”. I never knew mango skin is edible; live and learn!. We made a few mistakes in the project, but that’s how we live and learn.
After the crash, he’s living on borrowed time. The patient is living on borrowed time. Some say the company is living on borrowed time. We are all living on borrowed time.
