urduMeaning: بلاوجہ آہستہ چلنا، مفت میں کچھ لینا، مانگنا، بغیر پیسے کے حاصل کرنا، آوارہ گردی کرنا، اِدھر اُدھر پھرنا
examples: He's happy to mooch around the house all day. We had coffee then mooched down to the beach. He's always mooching off his friends. He always mooches cigarettes.
englishMeaning: To get money, food, etc from somebody else instead of paying for it yourself. To walk slowly with no particular purpose. To be somewhere not doing very much.

Someone who takes advantage of others’ generosity without offering anything back. A person who always depends on others for money, food, or favors without giving anything in return. It’s often used negatively for someone lazy or freeloading. One who exploits the generosity of others. A person who mooches off others.
examples: Don’t be such a moocher; pay for your own meal. He lost many friends because he was known as a moocher. One of my brothers was a moocher and drug addict.
antonyms: Independent, Self-reliant, Hard-working, Contributor, Giver, Supporter
sindhiMeaning: مُفت خور، ڀاڙو کائيندڙ، ٻين تي ڀاڙيندڙ ماڻهو، اهو ماڻهو جيڪو پاڻ ڪم نه ڪري ۽ ٻين تي گذارو ڪري
urduMeaning: مفت خور ، پرجیوی، بھکاری
synonyms: Parasite, Sponger, Beggar, Scrounger, Leech
Propose, Put forward, Argue
englishMeaning: Unlikely to happen & therefore not worth considering. A matter of disagreement or uncertainty. To suggest an idea for people to discuss. To bring up for discussion.
urduMeaning: اجتماع، بحث طلب، بحث کرنا
antonyms: Irrefutable, Censor
examples: He argued that the issue had become moot since the board had changed its policy. The plan was first mooted at last week’s meeting.
sindhiMeaning: قابل بحث،صلح جوڳو، زير بحث، تڪراري، تقرير ڪرڻ، بحث ڪرڻ، تڪرار ڪرڻ

englishMeaning: A place where dead bodies are kept, especially for identification or before burial. A room or building, usually in a hospital or forensic department, where dead bodies are stored for examination, identification, or postmortem analysis before burial or cremation.
examples: The police took the unidentified body to the morgue for examination. She works night shifts at the city morgue. After the accident, the victims were transferred to the hospital morgue. The journalist searched the newspaper morgue for old photographs.
sindhiMeaning: مرده خانو، اهو ڪمرو يا عمارت (عام طور اسپتال يا فارنزڪ اداري ۾) جتي فوت ٿيل ماڻهن جون لاشون جاچ سڃاڻپ يا پوسٽ مارٽم لاءِ تدفين يا ساڙڻ کان اڳ رکبيون آهن
synonyms: Mortuary, Dead house, Autopsy room, Funeral home storage
urduMeaning: مردہ خانہ،ایک کمرہ یا عمارت (جو عموماً اسپتال یا فرانزک ادارے میں ہوتی ہے) جہاں مرنے والوں کی لاشیں جانچ شناخت یا پوسٹ مارٹم کے لیے دفن یا جلانے سے پہلے رکھی جاتی ہیں
antonyms: Maternity ward, Nursery, Birth center

synonyms: Human, Earthly, Perishable, Fatal, Deadly, Severe
sindhiMeaning: جيڪو مرڻ وارو هجي يا هميشه لاءِ نه رهي سگهي، جيڪو موت جو سبب بڻجي سگهي، عام انسان جيڪو خدا يا ديوتا نه هجي، انتهائي شديد يا سخت، هر اها شي يا انسان جنھن کي مرڻو يا ختم ٿيڻو آھي (فنا/فاني)، اهو لفظ انساني ڪمزوري يا سخت خطري لاءِ به استعمال ٿئي ٿو
englishMeaning: Something that will die or cannot live forever. Anything living that is subject to death. Causing death or capable of causing death. A human, especially in contrast to a divine being. Very strong or extreme (mortal fear, mortal hatred). It can also describe something severe, extreme, or related to human weakness and limitations.
antonyms: Immortal, Eternal, Undying, Imperishable
examples: All humans are mortal, so life should be valued. The hero received a mortal wound during the battle. She felt a mortal fear when the earthquake started. The story reminds us that even kings are mortal.
urduMeaning: جو مرنے والا ہو یا ہمیشہ نہ رہ سکے، جو موت کا سبب بن سکتا ہو،عام انسان جو خدا یا دیوتا نہیں ہوتا، بہت شدید یا سخت، ہر وہ چیز یا انسان جو فنا پذیر ہو، یہ لفظ انسانی کمزوری یا شدید خطرے کے لئے بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے

examples: Doctors are studying the rise in mortality among young adults. The story reminds us of human mortality. Better healthcare has reduced child mortality in many countries. The flood caused a high mortality rate in the affected villages.
urduMeaning: فانی ہونا، آبادی میں اموات کی شرح، انسانی کمزوری یا ناپائیداری، زندگی کے عارضی ہونے کا احساس، مرنے کی حالت، یہ حقیقت کہ ہر جاندار ایک دن مر جاتا ہے، یہ لفظ آبادی میں اموات کی شرح یا کسی عرصے میں ہونے والی اموات کی تعداد کے لیے بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے
englishMeaning: The state of being mortal or subject to death. The number of deaths in a given population. Human weakness or vulnerability. A reminder that life is temporary. The fact that all living beings must eventually die. It can also mean the rate at which deaths occur in a particular population or period. The word is used in general life, philosophy, medicine, and population studies.
synonyms: Death, Fatality, End of life, Extinction (in population context), Demise
sindhiMeaning: آبادي ۾ موتن جي شرح، انساني ڪمزوري يا ناپائيداري، زندگي جي عارضي هجڻ جي ياد ڏيارڻ، مرڻيون حالت، مرڻ جي لائق ٿيڻ، هر جاندار کي آخرڪار مرڻو پوي ٿو، اهو لفظ آبادي ۾ موت جي شرح يا ڪنهن دور ۾ مرڻ جي تعداد لاءِ به استعمال ٿيندو آهي
antonyms: Immortality, Eternal life, Survival
Loose material, Separation, Detacher, Disconnector
synonyms: Bowl for grinding, Grinder bowl, Cannon, Launcher, Cement mixture, Binding material
urduMeaning: ادویات یا مصالحے پیسنے کا وزنی برتن، ایک چھوٹا توپ نما ہتھیار جو گولہ بلند زاویے سے داغتا ہے، اینٹوں اور پتھروں کو جوڑنے والا سیمنٹ اور ریت کا مسالہ، اینٹوں کو مسالے سے جوڑنا، گریجوئیشن والی ٹوپی
englishMeaning: A bowl-shaped tool used for crushing or grinding substances. A type of explosive weapon that fires shells at a high angle. A mixture used in building to bind bricks or stones. To apply mortar in order to join, fix or secure bricks, stones or tiles. It refers to spreading or using the masonry mixture to bind construction materials. A square academic cap worn at graduation ceremonies.
examples: She crushed the spices in a stone mortar. The soldiers fired a mortar during the night attack. The mason mixed sand and cement to make fresh mortar. They mortared the bricks to build a strong wall.
sindhiMeaning: مسالا پيسڻ لاءِ ڳرو کڙو، ننڍو توپ نما هٿيار جيڪو مٿانهين زاويي سان گولو فائر ڪري، سرن يا پٿرن کي ٻڌڻ لاءِ ريت ۽ سيمينٽ جو مسالو، مسالو لڳائي سرن کي ٻڌڻ، گريجوئيشن واري ٽوپي

examples: The aristocrate lived in a grand mansion outside the city. Many aristocrates played key roles in early European politics. Despite being an aristocrate, he supported social reforms. The novel describes the life of an aristocrate during wartime.
englishMeaning: A person belonging to the highest social class. A member of the aristocracy, usually someone from a noble family who traditionally holds social, political, or economic power. The status is often inherited and linked with wealth, land ownership, or royal connections.
synonyms: Noble, Elite, Blue blood, Patrician
sindhiMeaning: امير يا نواب طبقو جو فرد، اهو جيڪو امير، نوابي يا اعليٰ سماجي طبقي سان تعلق رکي، اهڙي حيثيت گهڻو ڪري وراثت ۾ ملندي آهي ۽ دولت يا اثر رسوخ سان لاڳاپيل هوندي آهي
urduMeaning: اشرافیہ کا فرد، وہ شخص جو اعلیٰ اور بااثر طبقے سے تعلق رکھتا ہو، عام طور پر یہ حیثیت خاندانی وراثت، دولت یا سیاسی طاقت کی بنیاد پر ہوتی ہے
antonyms: Commoner, Peasant, Ordinary citizen, Proletarian

englishMeaning: To use property as security for a loan. A loan taken to buy property, where the property itself is used as security until the loan is fully paid. A legal agreement in which a bank or financial institution lends money to a person to buy a house or land. The borrower agrees to repay the loan in installments. If they fail to repay, the lender has the right to take the property.
examples: He took a mortgage to buy his first house. The bank approved her mortgage application last week. They are still paying off their mortgage after ten years. She mortgaged her property to start a business.
synonyms: Loan, Home loan, Pledge, Lien, Hypothecation (formal)
antonyms: Release, Freehold, Discharge, Redeem, Unencumbered ownership
sindhiMeaning: ملڪيت کي گروي رکڻ، مقرر مدي لاءِ اوڌر وٺي ضمانت طور ڏنل ملڪيت، گروي نامو، گهر يا زمين کي قرض جي ضمانت طور رکڻ; جيستائين قرض ادا نه ٿئي ملڪيت بئنڪ يا قرض ڏيندڙ وٽ رهندي آهي
urduMeaning: جائیداد کو رہن رکھنا، جائیداد (گھر یا زمین) کو قرض کے بدلے ضمانت کے طور پر رکھنا، جب تک قرض ادا نہ ہو جائے جائیداد بینک کے پاس رہتی ہے
ذلیل کرنا، شرمندہ کرنا، شدید شرمندگی یا رسوائی میں ڈالنا، نفسیاتی یا جذباتی تکلیف دینا، شدید دکھ یا پریشانی محسوس کروانا، نفس کُشی کرنا، جذبات کو مجروح کرنا ، جذبات کو ٹھیس پہچانا
examples: She was mortified to discover her phone was on speaker during the meeting. The king mortified his soldiers with strict discipline. He mortified himself by admitting his failure publicly. The frost mortified the crops before the harvest.
englishMeaning: To make someone feel extremely embarrassed, ashamed, or humiliated. To check or curb one’s natural inclinations. To cause someone to feel self-conscious or humbled. To suppress or put an end to something unpleasant.
synonyms: Humiliate, Embarrass, Shame, Abash, Disgrace
sindhiMeaning: سخت شرمندگي يا نفرت محسوس ڪرائڻ، جذبات کي دٻائڻ، ذهني طور پريشان ڪرڻ يا شرمندگي ۾ وجھڻ، سماجي طور يا ذاتي طور پريشان ڪرڻ، من مارڻ، ذليل ڪرڻ
antonyms: Praise, Honor, Compliment, Encourage

sindhiMeaning: مڇ، مڇون، ڇاپر، شھپر، مٿين چپ تي وار، عزت يا مردانگي جي نشاني
synonyms: Whiskers, Facial hair, Mustachio
antonyms: Clean shaven, Smooth faced
examples: His thick moustache made him look older. He trimmed his moustache before the wedding. The police officer had a long, curved moustache. My grandfather’s moustache was his pride.
englishMeaning: Hair grown on the upper lip of a man. Facial hair on the upper lip.
urduMeaning: موُچھ، اوپر والے ہونٹ پر بال، عزت یا مردانگی کی علامت

synonyms: Revenue village, Administrative unit, Land record area, Territorial division
sindhiMeaning: سرڪاري زمين جي رڪارڊ ۾ درج علائقو، محصول ۽ بندوبست لاءِ استعمال ٿيندڙ يونٽ، عام طور تي ان ۾ هڪ يا وڌيڪ ڳوٺ شامل هوندا آهن ۽ اهو زرعي زمين جو حصو هوندو آهي
englishMeaning: A revenue or land record unit with defined boundaries, used for administrative and taxation purposes, typically containing agricultural land and one or more villages.
urduMeaning: یہ انتظامی اور مالیاتی (ریونیو) مقاصد کے لیے استعمال ہونے والا ایک یونٹ ہے، جس میں ایک یا زیادہ دیہات شامل ہو سکتے ہیں
antonyms: City, Urban area
examples: The land is located in Mouza Qasimabad, as recorded in the revenue documents. Each Mouza has its own map and boundary description maintained by the revenue department. The property dispute arose due to unclear boundaries between two Mouzas. Census data is often collected based on Mouza-level administrative divisions.

She moved heaven and earth to get her son into that school. I will move heaven and earth to make your dream come true. They moved heaven and earth to rescue the trapped miners. The team moved heaven and earth to finish the project on time.
sindhiMeaning: سڀ ڪوششون ڪرڻ يا پوري طاقت سان جدوجهد ڪرڻ، تمام گهڻي ڪوشش ڪرڻ، هر ممڪن طريقي سان ڪا شيءِ حاصل ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: کسی کام کو کرنے کے لیے ہر ممکن کوشش کرنا یا اپنی پوری طاقت لگا دینا
synonyms: Try one’s best, Go to any length, Make every effort, Do everything possible, Work tirelessly
englishMeaning: To try very hard to do something. To make every possible effort to achieve something, help someone, or make something happen, no matter how difficult it is. It shows strong determination, commitment, and hard work.
antonyms: Do nothing, Give up easily, Make no effort, Stay idle

synonyms: Numerophobia, Math anxiety, Fear of numbers, Calculation phobia
sindhiMeaning: انگن ۽ رياضي سان واسطو رکڻ جي خوف جو جذبو، جيڪو پريشاني يا بچاءُ جو سبب بڻجي سگهي ٿو
antonyms: Numeracy, Math confidence, Comfort with numbers, Mathematical aptitude
englishMeaning: Fear of numbers or mathematics. A strong and persistent fear of numbers, calculations, or dealing with mathematics, which may cause anxiety, avoidance, or distress.
examples: His arithmophobia made it hard for him to manage his finances. She avoids math classes due to her arithmophobia. Arithmophobia can interfere with everyday tasks like shopping or budgeting. Therapy helped him gradually overcome his arithmophobia.
urduMeaning: اعداد و شمار یا ریاضی سے شدید خوف یا اضطراب کی حالت، جو ذہنی دباؤ یا کسی کام سے گریز پیدا کر سکتی ہے
کسی نئے مقام، جگہ یا حالت میں داخل ہونا
examples: They moved into a new apartment. The company moved into the tech industry. She moved into her office last week. We’re moving into a bigger house soon.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن نئين جاءِ يا صورتحال ۾ داخل ٿيڻ
antonyms: Move out
synonyms: Settle, Occupy
englishMeaning: To go into a new house, apartment, or building to live or work. To begin to take on a new position, responsibility, or role. To start to involve oneself in a new activity, topic, or field. To gradually become absorbed in a situation or state of mind.
To depart. To start moving / to begin a journey. To leave a place / go away. To change topic / to stop discussing something.
synonyms: Leave, Depart
antonyms: Stay, Arrive
urduMeaning: روانہ ہونا، چلنا شروع کرنا ، حرکت میں آنا، جگہ چھوڑ دینا ، ہٹ جانا، موضوع بدل دینا
examples: The bus moved off slowly. The bus moved off after picking up passengers. The crowd slowly moved off after the speech. Let’s move off this subject and talk about something else.
sindhiMeaning: روانو ٿيڻ، حرڪت شروع ڪرڻ، اڳتي وڌڻ، جڳهه ڇڏڻ، وڃڻ، موضوع بدلائڻ

englishMeaning: To progress. To leave a place and continue forward. To stop focusing on something (often the past) and direct attention to the future. To continue with the next topic or activity.
examples: It’s time to move on from the past. The police told the crowd to move on. After the breakup, she decided to move on with her life. Let’s move on to the next chapter.
antonyms: Stay, Linger, Hold on
urduMeaning: آگے بڑھنا، اگلے موضوع کی طرف بڑھنا، گزری ہوئی بات کو بھلا دینا اور زندگی میں آگے بڑھنا
sindhiMeaning: اڳتي وڌڻ، گذريل ڳالهه وساري اڳتي وڌڻ، نئين موضوع يا ڪم ڏانهن وڃڻ
synonyms: Progress, Continue, Advance

sindhiMeaning: ترقي ڪرڻ، اڳتي وڌڻ، مٿي وڃڻ، اُچائي تي وڃڻ، اڳ ۾ آڻڻ
examples: He moved up to manager. Students move up a grade each year. She quickly moved up in the company. Prices have moved up again.
antonyms: Move down, Demote, Decline, Drop, Regress
urduMeaning: ترقی کرنا، اوپر جانا، آگے بڑھانا یا وقت کو پہلے کرنا
synonyms: Advance, Promote, Rise, Escalate, Elevate, Progress
englishMeaning: To advance, rise in position, or change to a higher level or rank.

examples: I had to mug up all the formulas before the math exam. She mugged up the history dates just one night before the test. Don’t just mug up the answers, try to understand the concepts. He always mugs up notes at the last moment.
sindhiMeaning: رٽو هڻڻ، امتحان لاءِ جلد پڙهڻ، زبردستي ياد ڪرڻ، مختصر وقت ۾ سبق ياد ڪرڻ
englishMeaning: To study something quickly and try to memorize it, usually just before an exam or test, without deep understanding. It often implies short-term memorization rather than real learning.
synonyms: Cram, Memorize, Rote learn, Swot up, Brush up (contextual), Learn by heart (informal)
antonyms: Understand deeply, Comprehend, Forget, Ignore, Neglect study
urduMeaning: رٹنا، امتحان کے لیے جلدی یاد کرنا، زبانی یاد کرنا، وقتی طور پر یاد کرنا

synonyms: Cram, Memorize, Revise, Study, Learn quickly, Prepare
antonyms: Forget, Ignore, Neglect, Misunderstand, Overlook
urduMeaning: رٹا لگانا، جلدی یاد کرنا، امتحان کے لیے تیزی سے پڑھنا، کسی موضوع کے بارے میں جلدی معلومات حاصل کرنا ، جلدی سبق یاد کرنا
englishMeaning: To study something quickly and carefully, especially to memorize facts for an exam, test, interview, or discussion. To learn or revise something in a short time by memorizing important facts, details, or information. It is often used when someone prepares at the last moment before an exam or important event.
examples: I need to mug up on history before tomorrow’s exam. She mugged up on English grammar before the interview. He spent the whole night mugging up on science formulas. We should mug up on current affairs for the quiz competition.
sindhiMeaning: رٽو هڻڻ، جلدي ياد ڪرڻ، امتحان لاءِ تيزي سان پڙهڻ، ڪنهن موضوع بابت جلدي معلومات حاصل ڪرڻ، تيزي سان سبق ياد ڪرڻ

antonyms: Wizard, Magician, Expert, Insider
urduMeaning: عام انسان، وہ شخص جس کے پاس جادوی صلاحیتیں نہیں ہوتیں اور وہ جادوی دنیا سے ناواقف ہوتا ہے، عام طور پر، یہ کسی خاص شعبے میں تجربہ نہ رکھنے والے شخص کے لیے بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے
englishMeaning: A non-magical person. Someone who does not have magical powers and is unaware of the magical world. More generally, it can refer to someone who is inexperienced in a particular field.
sindhiMeaning: عام ماڻهو، اهڙو ماڻهو جيڪو جادوي طاقت نه رکي ٿو ۽ جادوي دنيا کان واقف نه آهي، عام ڳالهه ۾، اهو ڪنهن به شعبي ۾ اڻڄاتل يا ناپوھ جو ماڻهو ٿي سگهي ٿو
synonyms: Non-magical person, Ordinary person, Outsider, Novice
examples: Harry explained to the Muggle world that magic exists. He felt like a Muggle among all the scientists. The Muggle parents were confused by their child’s strange stories. Don’t be a Muggle in the tech world; learn coding.

urduMeaning: خچر ایک جانور جو گھوڑی اور گدھے سے پیدا ہوتا ہے، خچر ایک طاقتور اور محنتی جانور جو وزن اٹھانے کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے، مجازی طور پر ضدی انسان کو بھی خچر کہا جاتا ہے، یہ لفظ غیر قانونی سامان لے جانے والے شخص کے لیے بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے
synonyms: Animal, Stubborn person, Smuggler
antonyms: Flexible person, Agreeable person, Law enforcer, Officer
englishMeaning: A mule is an animal born from a male donkey and a female horse. It can also mean a stubborn person or someone who illegally carries goods.
examples: The mule carried heavy loads across the mountains. Farmers prefer mules because they are strong and patient. He is as stubborn as a mule when making decisions. The police arrested a mule at the airport for smuggling drugs.
sindhiMeaning: هڪ جانور جيڪو گهوڙي ۽ گڏهه مان پيدا ٿئي ٿو، هڪ مضبوط ۽ محنتي جانور جيڪو بار کڻڻ لاءِ استعمال ٿيندو آهي، مجازي طور ضدّي ماڻهو کي به چيو ويندو آهي، غير قانوني شيون کڻندڙ ماڻهو لاءِ به لفظ استعمال ٿئي ٿو

sindhiMeaning: رستي ڳولڻ، هدايت ڪرڻ، هلائڻ، سنڀالڻ، سمجھڻ ۽ قابو پائڻ، جهاز يا ٻيڙي هلائڻ، مشڪل حالتن مان نڪرڻ، قدم بہ قدم رهنمائي ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: راستہ تلاش کرنا، ہدایت دینا، سفر کرنا، قابو پانا، سمجھنا اور نپٹنا، جہاز یا کشتی چلانا، مشکل حالات سے نمٹنا، مرحلہ وار رہنمائی دینا
examples: He navigated the ship through the storm safely. She had to navigate a complex legal system. I am learning to navigate the new software interface. The hikers navigated through the dense forest using a map.

examples: The captain used a compass for navigation across the sea. Modern cars have GPS systems to help with navigation. Website navigation should be simple for users to find information. Pilots undergo extensive training in air navigation before flying commercial planes.

urduMeaning: ارمینین ازم پروٹسٹنٹ عیسائیت کے اندر ایک مذہبی نظریہ ہے جو جیکبس آرمینیس کی تعلیمات پر مبنی ہے، اس نظریے کے مطابق انسان کو خدا کے فضل کو قبول یا رد کرنے کی آزاد مرضی حاصل ہے، یہ غیر مشروط انتخاب کے عقیدے کو رد کرتا ہے، اس میں مشروط انتخاب سب کے لیے کفارہ اور ایمان کے بعد گمراہ ہونے کا امکان شامل ہے
englishMeaning: A theological system within Protestant Christianity based on the teachings of Jacobus Arminius. It teaches that human beings have free will to respond to God's grace. It rejects the idea that God has unconditionally chosen certain people for salvation. It supports conditional election, universal atonement, and the possibility that believers may fall from grace.
examples: Arminianism teaches that people have the freedom to choose salvation. Many Methodists follow Arminianism in their theology. Arminianism opposes the idea of unconditional predestination. The debate between Arminianism and Calvinism shaped Protestant history.
antonyms: Calvinism, Predestinarianism, Determinism
sindhiMeaning: ارمينينزم پروٽيسٽنٽ عيسائيت اندر هڪ مذهبي نظريو آهي جيڪو جيڪبس آرمينيوس جي تعليمات تي ٻڌل آهي، هن نظريي مطابق انسان وٽ آزاد ارادو آهي ته هو خدا جي فضل کي قبول ڪري يا رد ڪري، هي نظريو غير مشروط چونڊ جي مخالفت ڪري ٿو هن ۾ شرط سان چونڊ سڀني لاءِ ڪفارو ۽ ايمان کان پوءِ به گمراه ٿيڻ جو امڪان شامل آهي
synonyms: In theological context, Free will theology, Remonstrant theology, Wesleyan theology

examples: During the pandemic, people invented better online learning systems because schools were closed, Necessity is the mother of invention. Farmers created simple water-saving tools during droughts, Necessity is the mother of invention. When people needed faster communication, smartphones and messaging apps became popular, Necessity is the mother of invention. A student made a homemade lamp during a power outage to continue studying, Necessity is the mother of invention.
antonyms: Comfort prevents innovation, Satisfaction stops creativity, Laziness avoids invention
word: Necessity is the mother of invention
synonyms: Need inspires creativity, Difficulties lead to innovation, Need creates solutions, Problems encourage invention

Problems, shortages, or difficult situations force people to think differently and invent useful things. Many inventions in history were created because people needed easier, faster, or better ways to solve problems.

examples: The government will not negotiate with terrorists. We successfully negotiated the release of the hostages. The climbers had to negotiate a steep rock face.

examples: Many people call him a nepo baby because his father is a famous actor. She worked hard, but critics still label her a nepo baby due to her family background. The debate about nepo babies in the film industry is growing louder. Not every nepo baby lacks talent, but they often get easier access to opportunities.
urduMeaning: خاندانی تعلقات کی وجہ سے فائدہ پانے والا شخص، اس شخص کو کہا جاتا ہے جو اپنی محنت یا صلاحیت کے بجائے اپنے والدین یا خاندان کی طاقت، شہرت یا اثر و رسوخ کی وجہ سے ترقی یا مواقع حاصل کرتا ہے، خاص طور پر فلم، سیاست یا کاروبار میں
اقربا پروری، سفارش اور تعلقات کی بنیاد پر فیصلے کرنا، ایسا عمل جس میں کسی ادارے یا حکومت میں رشتہ داروں کو قابلیت کے بغیر عہدے یا فائدے دیے جائیں
examples: The company was accused of nepotism after the manager hired his own brother. Nepotism in politics prevents talented people from getting leadership roles. همت وارو، بهادري ڏيکاريندڙ، بي باڪ، گستاخ، پريشان يا گھٻرائيندڙ، خطري وارو، رسڪ وٺڻ وارو، اعتماد وارو، بي خوف

englishMeaning: The branch of medicine that deals with the nervous system and its disorders. Medical science concerned with the study, diagnosis, and treatment of disorders affecting the brain, spinal cord, nerves, and muscles. It includes conditions like epilepsy, Parkinson’s disease, multiple sclerosis, and strokes.
examples: She decided to specialize in neurology after completing her medical degree. Neurology research has advanced treatments for Alzheimer’s disease. The patient was referred to the neurology department for severe headaches. Neurology requires detailed understanding of both the brain and spinal cord.

urduMeaning: عددی مہارت رکھنے والا، اعداد و شمار کو سمجھنے اور استعمال کرنے کی صلاحیت والا، بنیادی ریاضی میں ماہر، منطقی اور تجزیاتی ذہن رکھنے والا جو عددی ڈیٹا سے کام لے سکتا ہے
examples: She is highly numerate and quickly analyzes financial data. A numerate workforce is essential for the success of this project. He is numerate enough to calculate discounts without a calculator. Being numerate helps students manage their personal budgets effectively.
sindhiMeaning: انگن کي سمجهڻ ۽ استعمال ڪرڻ جي قابليت وارو، رياضي جي بنيادي ڄاڻ رکندڙ، منطقي ۽ تجزيي واري سوچ وارو جيڪو انگن سان ڪم ڪري سگهي ٿو
englishMeaning: Able to understand and work with numbers. A person who has the ability to reason and apply simple mathematical concepts in everyday life. This includes skills like interpreting graphs, calculating percentages, or estimating quantities.
antonyms: Innumerate, Innumerate, Unskilled in mathematics, Unquantitative
synonyms: Mathematical, Skilled with numbers, Quantitative, Arithmetical

sindhiMeaning: ڳڻپ ڪندڙ، شمار ڪندڙ، اَنس، ڀاڱي جو مٿيون انگ، ڪنهن واقع جي تعداد يا ڪامياب نتيجن جو انگ، ڪل نتيجي ۾ حصو وٺندڙ انگ يا تعداد

antonyms: Denominator, Bottom number, Lower figure
urduMeaning: گنتی کرنے والا ، نمبر لگانے والا، شمار کرنے والا، شُمار کُنِندہ ، وہ عدد جو حِسابی ترقیم میں خط کے اُوپر لِکھا جاۓ
englishMeaning: The number above the line in a fraction. The part of a fraction that is above the line and signifies the number to be divided by the denominator. A person or thing that numbers. The part that counts toward a whole or goal. The quantity compared against another.

examples: Numismatics helps historians understand ancient trade systems. He developed an interest in numismatics at a young age. The museum has a department dedicated to numismatics. Numismatics can be both a hobby and an academic discipline.
englishMeaning: Study or collection of coins, paper money, and medals. The academic study and collection of coins, currency, tokens, medals, and other related objects. It includes researching their history, design, production, and economic significance.
urduMeaning: سکوں نوٹوں اور تمغوں کے مطالعے یا جمع کرنے کا علم، سکے جمع کرنے کا شوق، کرنسی کی تاریخ کا مطالعہ، تمغوں اور ٹوکنز کا تجزیہ، مالیاتی نظام سے متعلق تحقیق
synonyms: Coin collecting, Coin study, Currency study, Medal collecting

antonyms: Spending money, Currency use, Monetary exchange

synonyms: Healthy, Strong
antonyms: Weak, Sick
englishMeaning: Very healthy, strong, and full of energy. In perfect physical condition.
urduMeaning: بالکل صحت مند، تندرست و توانا، مکمل طور پر ٹھیک، تندرست اور توانائی سے بھرپور
examples: At 70, he is still as fit as a fiddle. After a week of rest, he is now as fit as a fiddle and ready to work again. Even at the age of seventy, my grandfather is as fit as a fiddle. She exercises every day, eats healthy food, and stays as fit as a fiddle. Don’t worry about me, I’m as fit as a fiddle after the check-up.
sindhiMeaning: مڪمل صحتمند، سڄو سٺو ۽ صحتمند، بلڪل ٺيڪ، طاقت ۽ توانائي سان ڀرپو، بيماري کان آزاد

urduMeaning: شادی یا جوڑوں کے ملاپ کا عمل، شادی بیاہ سے متعلق، شادی کا ، عروسی کا ، عروسی ، شادی یا اتحاد کی علامتی تعبیر کے طور پر
examples: She has tied the nuptial knot with a businessman. The poet described the forest as a nuptial union of earth and sky. Many birds perform elaborate nuptial displays before mating. synonyms: Wedlock, Matrimonial, Wedding, Marital, Conjugal
sindhiMeaning: شادي يا جوڙي ٺاهڻ وارو عمل، شاديءَ متعلق، ازدواجي، عروسي، وهانءٌ، نڪاح، شاديءَ سان لاڳاپيل، شاديءَ جي تقريب سان تعلق رکڻ وارو، شاديءَ سان گڏ ٿيندڙ ذميوارين يا فرضن سان لاڳاپيل

synonyms: Seed, Kernel, Enthusiast, Fanatic
urduMeaning: گری، بادام، اخروٹ، گری یا پیچ، سر یا دماغ، کسی شے کا شوقین یا جنونی شخص
sindhiMeaning: کاجو، بادام، اخروٽ، ڳنڍڻ واري ڌاتو جي شي، دماغ يا سر، ڪنهن شيءِ ۾ شدت سان دلچسپي رکڻ وارو ماڻهو، چريو، پاگل، اڌ مغزي، سوپاڙي
examples: I ate a handful of almonds, a healthy nut. He tightened the nut on the bolt. She is a computer nut, always trying new software. The squirrel stored nuts for winter.

sindhiMeaning: مختصر وضاحت يا خلاصو، ٿورن لفظن ۾، ميون جي سخت ٻاهري خول، ڪنهن ڳالهه جو ننڍو بيان، سادي انداز ۾ بيان ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: مختصر ترین لفظوں میں ، مختصر ، اخروٹ کا چھلکا ،بوست جوز ، کھانے والے اخروٹ کے اوپر والا سخت چھلکا یا جھلی

synonyms: Ace, Dab, Dash, Driblet, Drop, Fraction
examples: To put it in a nutshell, we're bankrupt. Well, to put it in a nutshell, we're lost. Give it to me in a nutshell. In a nutshell, the owners thought they knew best.
englishMeaning: In a very clear way, using few words. Using as few words as possible. Something small in size, amount, or range. In a very brief statement. The hard external covering in which the kernel of a nut is enclosed. The shell around the kernel of a nut.

examples: Her nyctophobia made her sleep with a night light on every night. The boy’s nyctophobia prevented him from camping outdoors. He avoided basements and dark alleys because of his nyctophobia. Therapy helped reduce her nyctophobia over several months.
sindhiMeaning: اونداهيءَ جو خوف، اونداهيءَ يا رات جو شديد ۽ غير معقول خوف جيڪو ڊڄڻ پريشاني يا اونداهي هنڌن کان پاسو ڪرڻ جو سبب بڻجي سگهي ٿو

antonyms: Fearlessness, Bravery, Courage, Comfort in darkness
synonyms: Fear of darkness, Scotophobia, Night phobia

urduMeaning: دیومالائی کہانیوں میں فطرت سے وابستہ ایک نوجوان نسوانی روح، یونانی اور رومی دیومالائی روایات میں ایک خوبصورت نسوانی فطری روح ہوتی ہے جو جنگلات دریاؤں یا پہاڑوں سے منسوب ہوتی ہے، حیاتیات میں بعض کیڑوں کی ابتدائی بالغ حالت کو کہتے ہیں
examples: The story describes a forest nymph dancing near the river. Ancient poets often wrote about nymphs living in nature. The insect is still a nymph and cannot fly yet. In mythology, a nymph is usually gentle and graceful.
sindhiMeaning: ديو مالا ۾ فطرت سان لاڳاپيل نوجوان عورت جهڙو روح، يوناني ۽ رومي ديو مالا موجب هڪ خوبصورت عورت جهڙو فطرتي روح جيڪو جهنگلن دريائن يا جبلن سان لاڳاپيل هوندو آهي، حياتيات ۾ ڪي حشرن جي اڻپوري بالغ حالت کي چيو ويندو آهي
englishMeaning: A beautiful female nature spirit connected with forests, rivers, mountains, or seas. In biology, a nymph is the immature form of certain insects that looks like a small adult but has not fully developed.
synonyms: Fairy, Dryad, Nature spirit, Sprite
antonyms: Monster, Ogre, Adult insect, Human

englishMeaning: Very overweight, having excessive body fat. A person or animal whose body weight is significantly higher than what is considered healthy for their height, often due to excessive accumulation of fat.
antonyms: Slim, Thin, Lean, Underweight
synonyms: Overweight, Fat, Corpulent, Heavy
sindhiMeaning: وڌيڪ وزن وارو، موٽو، ٿلھو، اهڙو شخص جنهن جو وزن عام کان گهڻو وڌيڪ هجي، جسم ۾ چرٻي جي مقدار وڌيڪ هجي، اهو صحت تي منفي اثر رکي سگهي ٿو
examples: The doctor advised him to reduce weight because he was obese. Obese children are at higher risk of diabetes. She became obese after years of unhealthy eating habits. Obese pets need special care and diet.
urduMeaning: موٹا، بہت زیادہ وزن والا، ایسا شخص جس کا جسمانی وزن عام سے زیادہ ہو اور جسم میں چربی کی مقدار بہت زیادہ ہو، جو صحت کے مسائل پیدا کر سکتا ہے

sindhiMeaning: موٽاپو، ٿولهه، ٿلھائپ، جسم ۾ گهڻي چرٻي هجڻ، هڪ طبي حالت جنهن ۾ ماڻهو جي جسم ۾ صحتمند حد کان وڌيڪ چرٻي جمع ٿي وڃي، اها حالت دل شگر ۽ بلڊ پريشر جي بيمارين جو خطرو وڌائي ٿي، سببن ۾ وڌيڪ کاڌو ورزش جي گهٽتائي يا جينياتي عنصر شامل ٿي سگهن ٿا
urduMeaning: موٹاپا، جسم میں زائد چربی، ایک طبی حالت جس میں جسم میں غیر صحت مند مقدار میں چربی جمع ہو جاتی ہے، جو ذیابیطس دل کی بیماری اور بلند فشار خون کے خطرات کو بڑھاتی ہے، اس کی وجہ زیادہ کھانا ورزش کی کمی یا جینیاتی عوامل ہو سکتے ہیں
examples: Obesity can lead to serious health problems if not controlled. Childhood obesity is becoming a global concern. A balanced diet helps prevent obesity. Doctors recommend exercise to reduce obesity.
antonyms: Thinness, Slimness, Leanness, Underweight
englishMeaning: Excessive body fat that may harm health. A medical condition where a person accumulates an unhealthy amount of body fat, which increases the risk of various diseases, including diabetes, heart disease, and high blood pressure. It usually results from overeating, lack of exercise, or genetic factors.
synonyms: Overweight, Fatness, Corpulence, Heaviness

examples: As God is my witness, I never told anyone your secret. As God is my witness, I will always stand by you. As God is my witness, I didn’t take that money. As God is my witness, I’ll make sure justice is done.
urduMeaning: خدا گواہ ہے،خدا کی قسم ، میں سچ کہہ رہا ہوں، خدا کو گواہ بنا کر کہتا ہوں، یقیناً یہ بات درست ہے، میں پوری سچائی سے کہتا ہوں
englishMeaning: Used to strongly affirm that something is true. The speaker calls God as proof of honesty. I swear it is true. I am completely honest. I promise sincerely. I strongly affirm the truth. I truly mean what I say.
synonyms: I swear, I promise, Honestly, Truly, I give you my word, On my honor, I solemnly swear
sindhiMeaning: الله جو قسم، خدا شاهد آهي، مان سچ پيو چوان، خدا کي شاهد ڪري چوان ٿو، هي ڳالھ بلڪل سچي آهي، مان مڪمل سچائي سان چوان ٿو
antonyms: I doubt it, Maybe, I am not sure, Possibly, I guess

urduMeaning: حواس باختہ کر دینا ، بد حواسی ، ابہام پیدا کرنا، بات کو الجھا دینا، کسی بات کو جان بوجھ کر یا غیر ارادی طور پر اس طرح پیچیدہ بنانا ہے کہ اصل مطلب سمجھنا مشکل ہو جائے
englishMeaning: The act of making something unclear or confusing. Refers to deliberately or unintentionally making information difficult to understand by using complex language, vague explanations, or unnecessary details. It is often used to hide the real meaning or to confuse the audience.
examples: The legal document was full of obfuscation, making it hard for ordinary people to understand. His technical explanation caused more obfuscation than clarity. Obfuscation in official statements often hides the real issue. The teacher avoided obfuscation and explained the concept in simple words.
antonyms: Clarity, Simplicity, Transparency, Plainness, Directness
sindhiMeaning: بدحواسي، مونجهه، وايون بتال، گنجلڪ ڪرڻ، ڳالهه کي اڻ واضح يا مشڪل بڻائڻ، ڪنهن ڳالهه کي ڄاڻي واڻي يا اڻ ڄاڻائي سان اهڙو پيچيده بڻائڻ جو ماڻهو ان کي آساني سان سمجهي نه سگهن
synonyms: Confusion, Obscurity, Ambiguity, Complexity, Vagueness

englishMeaning: A notice published in a newspaper or online announcing a person's death, usually with a short biography. A written announcement that informs the public about someone’s death. It often includes the person's name, age, date of death, achievements, and details about funeral services. It may also highlight the person's life story and contributions.
antonyms: Birth announcement, Welcome notice, Congratulations message

examples: The newspaper published an obituary for the famous writer. Her obituary described her achievements in education and social work. I read my grandfather’s obituary in the local newspaper. The online obituary included details about the funeral service.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شخص جي وفات جي خبر ۽ سندس زندگي بابت مختصر تعارف جيڪو اخبار يا آن لائن شايع ڪيو وڃي، هڪ لکيل اعلان جيڪو ڪنهن شخص جي وفات جي خبر ڏئي، ان ۾ عام طور تي نالو عمر وفات جي تاريخ اهم ڪم ۽ جنازي بابت تفصيل شامل هوندا آهن، ڪڏهن ڪڏهن ان ۾ زندگي جو خلاصو به ڏنو ويندو آهي

englishMeaning: To require someone to do something or to bind by duty or law. Something essential or necessary. To put someone in a position where they must act because of a rule, duty, promise or circumstance. Something that cannot exist or function without something else, or something that is essential.
examples: The contract obligates both parties to follow the agreed rules. Her kindness obligates me to help her whenever she needs support. The company is obligated to provide safety equipment to all workers. Some animals are obligate predators that survive only by hunting.
synonyms: Require, Compel, Bind, Duty bound, Force, Necessitate
antonyms: Free, Release, Excuse, Liberate, Allow
urduMeaning: پابند کرنا، لازم بنانا، مجبور کرنا، مکمل انحصار کرنا، ایسی چیز جو کسی دوسرے عنصر کے بغیر موجود نہ رہ سکے یا ضروری ہو
sindhiMeaning: مجبور ٿيڻ، پابند ڪرڻ، لازمي بڻائڻ، ڪنهن شخص يا شيء کي ذميواري يا فرض هيٺ آڻڻ، ڪا شيء ڪنهن ٻي شيء کان بغير نه هلي سگهي يا لازمي هجي، ڪنهن شيء تي مڪمل دارومدار رکڻ

synonyms: Duty, Responsibility, Commitment, Requirement, Burden, Pledge
urduMeaning: ضروری، فرض یا ذمہ داری جو کسی پر قانونی اخلاقی یا وعدے کی وجہ سے لازم ہو، پابندی، احسان، مہربانی، امر واجب، احساس، وہ حق جو کسی کو دینا لازم ہو جیسے قرض کی ادائیگی
examples: She felt an obligation to help her friend during the crisis. Paying taxes is a legal obligation for every citizen. Parents have an obligation to care for their children. He completed the project out of a sense of obligation, not interest.
englishMeaning: A duty or responsibility that a person is expected or required to do. Something you must do because it is your duty, responsibility, or because a rule, law, promise or moral principle requires it. It can be legal, moral, social, or personal.
sindhiMeaning: شرط، مجبوري احسان، فرض، ٿورو، مهرباني، ذميواري، پابندي، اخلاقي فرض جو ٻين سان نيڪي ۽ مدد ڪرڻ تي مجبور ڪرڻ، اهو حق جيڪو ڪنهن کي ملڻو هجي ۽ پورو ڪرڻ واجب هجي
antonyms: Freedom, Choice, Option, Liberty, Exemption

sindhiMeaning: اهو شخص جيڪو ڪنهن ذميواري يا فرض کي پورو ڪرڻ جو پابند هجي
englishMeaning: A person who is bound by a duty or obligation. Someone who is legally or morally required to do something. A person who is responsible for fulfilling an obligation or duty. It is used for a person who owes a duty, promise, service or payment to another party. The term appears mostly in legal or formal contexts.
antonyms: Non-responsible party, Free agent, Exempt person, Unbound party
synonyms: Responsible party, Debtor, Duty bearer, Obligee, Bound person
urduMeaning: وہ شخص جو کسی ذمہ داری یا فرض کو پورا کرنے کا پابند ہو
examples: The obligator must submit the documents before the deadline. In this agreement, the company acts as the obligator. An obligator who fails to perform the duty may face penalties. Each member became an obligator after signing the pact.

Wearing a helmet is obligatory for all motorcycle riders. Attendance at the meeting is obligatory for senior staff. It is obligatory to follow safety instructions in the lab. In many cultures, it is obligatory to show respect to elders.
sindhiMeaning: ضروري، لازمي، اهو ڪم جيڪو قاعدي يا ذميواري سبب ڪرڻ لازمي هجي، رواج موجب لازمي ڪم، سماجي طور تي لازم سمجهيو ويندڙ عمل
synonyms: Required, Compulsory, Mandatory, Necessary, Binding
antonyms: Optional, Voluntary, Unnecessary, Nonessential
urduMeaning: لازمی ، ضروری ، وہ کام جو قانون اصول یا ذمہ داری کے تحت کرنا پڑے، رواج کے مطابق لازم سمجھا جانے والا عمل، سماجی توقع کے تحت ضروری خیال کیا جانے والا کام
englishMeaning: Required or expected because of a rule, duty, law or custom. Something that must be done because it is demanded by rules, duty, law or social expectations. It leaves no choice and is not optional.

examples: You eventually become oblivious to the noise. He drove off oblivious of the damage he had caused.
englishMeaning: Not aware of something. Lacking remembrance, memory, or mindful attention. Lacking active conscious knowledge or awareness.
synonyms: Clueless
sindhiMeaning: بيخبر، غافل، ويسر کاڌو، نيسان، ويس، کاڌو، فراموش ڪندڙ
antonyms: Acquainted
urduMeaning: بھولنے والا، فراموش کنندہ

جیسا راجا، ویسی پرجا، جیسا بادشاہ ویسی رعایا، رہنما کا کردار عوام پر اثر انداز ہوتا ہے، اچھی قیادت اچھی قوم بناتی ہے، لوگ اپنے بڑوں اور حکمرانوں کی نقل کرتے ہیں، معاشرے کی حالت اکثر اس کے لیڈروں سے ظاہر ہوتی ہے
englishMeaning: People usually follow the behavior, character, and habits of their leader. Good leaders create good followers, while bad leaders influence people negatively. Leadership influences society. Example is stronger than words. People imitate authority figures. Moral behavior spreads from the top. Culture of a group depends on its leader

englishMeaning: To go up or rise to a higher place or position. To gain a higher position in society, career, authority, or importance. To grow stronger, louder, or more intense. Often used for sounds, emotions, prices, or temperature. To rise to a higher spiritual, moral, or emotional state. To move upward in numerical order or increase in value.
examples: They slowly ascended the steep path up the mountain. He eventually ascended to the position of chief executive. A long flight of steps ascends (= leads up) to the door of the museum. She ascended the throne when her mother abdicated. The hikers plan to ascend the mountain early in the morning. Smoke began to ascend into the sky after the fire started.

sindhiMeaning: ويجهي ايندڙ شيءِ، ڪا شيءِ جلد ٿيڻ واري هجي يا سمنڊ جو اهو حصو جيڪو ڪناري کان ٿورو پري نظر اچي
urduMeaning: قریب آنے والی چیز، جلد ہونے والی ہو یا سمندر کا وہ حصہ جو ساحل سے کچھ فاصلے پر نظر آئے

antonyms: Increase, Worsen, Intensify, Aggravate, Drawback
englishMeaning: To balance or counter the effect of something. To reduce or neutralize the effect of a cost, loss, or negative impact by an equal or opposite action. To make something stand out by contrasting it with another element. To move or position something slightly away from a main line or center Something that compensates for a loss, disadvantage, or negative effect (A balancing factor). A small distance or shift from a main position. A credit used to reduce a debt or cost. A printing method where ink is transferred from a plate to a surface.
sindhiMeaning: توازن ڪرڻ، ڪنهن نقصان، خرچ يا منفي اثر کي برابر يا گهٽ ڪرڻ لاءِ ٻيو قدم کڻڻ، تلافي ڪندڙ شيءِ، اهڙي شيءِ يا فائدو جيڪو نقصان يا گهٽتائي کي برابر ڪري، ٿوري هٽ يا فرق، مالي ترتيب يا ڪٽوتي، ڇپائي جو طريقو جنهن ۾ مس سڌي ڪاغذ تي نه لڳي، مقابلي ۾ آڻي نمايان ڪرڻ
examples: Higher profits offset the increase in production costs. Overtime pay helped offset monthly expenses. Salary benefits are an offset to long working hours. The discount served as an offset to the delay. There is a slight offset between the two lines. Tax offsets reduced the payable amount. The book was produced using offset printing. Job security is an offset to lower pay. Higher income can offset rising living costs. The designer offset the image to the left. Dark walls offset the bright furniture.
synonyms: Compensate, Counteract, Neutralize, Make up, Adjustment
Overseas, Seaward, Foreign based, External
examples: The company moved its customer service to an offshore location. Offshore drilling plays a major role in energy production. Many firms use offshore banking for financial management. The government approved a new offshore wind project.
englishMeaning: Located at sea or outside the main land area, often used for activities done abroad. Something situated away from the coast or outside a country, especially across the sea. It is commonly used for oil drilling, wind farms, banking, companies, or jobs that are based in another country to reduce costs or manage operations internationally.
urduMeaning: ساحل سے دور یا ملک سے باہر واقع، اُن چیزوں یا سرگرمیوں کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے جو ساحل سے دور سمندر میں ہوں یا کسی دوسرے ملک میں قائم کی گئی ہوں، جیسے تیل کی تنصیبات، بینک یا بیرون ملک کمپنیاں

antonyms: Onshore, Inland, Domestic, Local

englishMeaning: A very rich and powerful person who is part of a small group controlling a country or organization.
urduMeaning: وہ شخص جو چند امیر اور بااثر لوگوں کے گروہ میں شامل ہو جو کسی ملک یا ادارے پر قابض ہوں

synonyms: Aristocracy, Plutocracy, Elite rule, Ruling class

englishMeaning: A symbol or action showing a desire for peace or reconciliation. sindhiMeaning: مڪمل طور شامل هجڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ ۾ مڪمل طرح سان مشغول يا دلچسپي هجڻ، ڪنهن ڪم پيار ڏکيائي يا قرض ۾ پوري طرح ڦاٿل هجڻ ايترو جو ٻاهر نڪري نه سگهجي

To go beyond control, limit, or capacity. Excess beyond limit or budget. An amount or situation in which something exceeds its expected limit, time, or cost.
sindhiMeaning: بي قابو ٿي وڃڻ، قبضي ۾ وٺڻ، حد کان وڌي وڃڻ، اضافو، وڌيڪ خرچ

sindhiMeaning: الٽو ڪرڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ کي الٽو ڪري ڇڏڻ، مٿان هيٺ ڪري ڇڏڻ، عدالت يا اختيار واري اداري جي فيصلي کي رد ڪرڻ، سياست ۾ حڪومت يا نظام کي ختم ڪرڻ، حالت کي مڪمل طور بدلائڻ، الٽو ٿيڻ يا ڪنهن فيصلي جي رد ٿيڻ جو عمل

Wegener's theory led to a paradigm shift in the earth sciences. I could convince only a few of my colleagues of the need for a revolution, a paradigm shift.
synonyms: Transformation, Revolution, Radical change, Reorientation
urduMeaning: کسی نظام، سوچ یا طریقہ کار میں بنیادی اور انقلابی تبدیلی، بُنیادی تبدیلی ، کایا پلٹ ، نئی انقلابی فِکر

englishMeaning: Seemingly contradictory, Seemingly absurd, self-contradictory, or against common sense, but may contain a hidden truth. Something that has two opposite features that exist together.
sindhiMeaning: تضاد وارو، ابتڙ لڳندڙ، ظاهري تضاد پر حقيقت سان لاڳاپيل
antonyms: Logical, Reasonable
synonyms: Contradictory, Absurd
examples: It is paradoxical but true. It is paradoxical that the poorest people often give the most in charity. His paradoxical statement confused everyone in the meeting. The paradoxical nature of technology is that it connects us but also isolates us. The silence of the leader at a time of crisis was paradoxical.
urduMeaning: تضاد نما، متضاد، خلافِ قیاس، بظاہر متضاد مگر حقیقت رکھنے والا

sindhiMeaning: سُڪائي ڇڏڻ، ڪنهن شيءَ کي تمام گهڻو خشڪ ڪرڻ (جهڙوڪ زمين ٻوٽي يا کاڌي کي سج يا گرميءَ سان سُڪل ڪرڻ)
antonyms: Moisten, Hydrate, Soak, Drench
urduMeaning: خشک کرنا، پیاسا کرنا، کسی چیز کو مکمل طور پر خشک کر دینا (جیسے زمین پودا یا خوراک کو سورج یا گرمی سے خشک کرنا)
examples: The summer sun parched the fields, leaving them cracked. After hours of walking in the desert, he felt parched and needed water. The heat parched the fruit, making it shriveled and tough. His curiosity parched for knowledge could not be satisfied by books alone.
englishMeaning: To dry out completely or cause to become very thirsty or dry. Often used for crops, soil, or figuratively for thirst or desire.
synonyms: Dry, Dehydrate, Scorch, Desiccate

urduMeaning: ایک مضبوط مواد جو بھیڑ بکری یا دیگر جانوروں کی کھال سے تیار کیا جاتا تھا اور قدیم زمانے میں اہم دستاویزات مذہبی کتابوں اور مخطوطات کے لیے استعمال ہوتا تھا، آج کل یہ لفظ ایسے کاغذ کے لیے بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے جو شکل یا بناوٹ میں اس سے مشابہ ہو، کوئی چیز جو خشک، پیلی یا سکڑی ہوئی معلوم ہو، سرکاری سند یا ڈگری
antonyms: Digital document, Electronic file, Modern paper
englishMeaning: A durable material prepared from the skin of animals such as sheep or goats, used in ancient and medieval times for writing important documents, manuscripts, and religious texts. It can also refer to a formal certificate or document written on such material. In modern usage, it may describe paper that resembles this material in texture or color. Something dry, pale, or shriveled in appearance. An official document such as a diploma or legal certificate.
examples: The ancient manuscript was written on parchment. The king signed the treaty on fine parchment. Her face looked pale like old parchment. The diploma was printed on thick parchment paper. She proudly framed her university parchment. His skin looked like parchment after days in the sun.
sindhiMeaning: هڪ مضبوط مواد جيڪو رڍ ٻڪري يا ٻين جانورن جي کل مان ٺاهيو ويندو هو ۽ قديم دور ۾ اهم دستاويزن مذهبي ڪتابن ۽ تحريرن لاءِ استعمال ٿيندو هو، اڄڪلهه اهو لفظ اهڙي ڪاغذ لاءِ به استعمال ٿيندو آهي جيڪو ظاهر يا بناوت ۾ اهڙو لڳي، ڪا شيءِ جيڪا سڪي ڦڪي يا سڙيل جهڙي لڳي، سرڪاري سند يا ڊگري
synonyms: Vellum, Manuscript paper, Sheepskin document, Diploma, Certificate

englishMeaning: To reduce, trim, or cut something down. To remove a small amount from something, often slowly and carefully. It is commonly used for cutting the skin of fruits or vegetables, and also for reducing costs, numbers, or limits step by step.
antonyms: Increase, Add, Expand, Enlarge
urduMeaning: کم کرنا یا تھوڑا تھوڑا کاٹنا، کسی چیز کو آہستہ آہستہ کم کرنا یا اس کا غیر ضروری حصہ کاٹ دینا، جیسے پھل کا چھلکا اتارنا یا اخراجات کم کرنا
synonyms: Trim, Reduce, Cut, Peel, Lessen
sindhiMeaning: گهٽائڻ يا ٿورو ٿورو ڪٽڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ مان ٿورو ٿورو حصو ڪٽڻ يا گهٽ ڪرڻ، جيئن ميوي جي کل لاھڻ يا خرچ گھٽائڻ
examples: She pared the apple before giving it to the child. The company plans to pare its expenses next year. He tried to pare down the long report to a short summary. The chef carefully pared the vegetables for the soup.

urduMeaning: اضافی یا غیر ضروری حصہ آہستہ آہستہ کاٹنا یا ہٹانا
antonyms: Attach, Add, Build, Join
synonyms: Remove, Shave off, Strip, Cut away
sindhiMeaning: اضافي حصو يا ٻاهرين تہه کي آهستي آهستي ڪٽڻ يا هٽائڻ
englishMeaning: To remove small parts. To gradually remove or cut away parts of something, often little by little
examples: She pared away the rough edges of the wooden sculpture. The chef pared away the skin of the fruit before serving. Over time, he pared away unnecessary expenses from his budget. They pared away the extra material to fit the fabric perfectly.

The company plans to pare back unnecessary expenses next quarter. She pared back her wardrobe to just the essentials. The government is paring back subsidies for certain industries. He decided to pare back his commitments to focus on family.
sindhiMeaning: آهستي آهستي ڪنهن شيءِ کي گهٽائڻ يا ڪٽڻ، خاص طور تي خرچ يا سائيز کي منظم طريقي سان گهٽائڻ
englishMeaning: To cut back gradually. To cut down or reduce something carefully and systematically. Often used in financial or organizational contexts to indicate trimming excess.
synonyms: Scale back, Reduce, Cut, Decrease
antonyms: Boost, Expand, Raise, Build up
urduMeaning: بتدریج کم کرنا، کسی چیز کو آہستہ آہستہ کم کرنا یا چھانٹنا، خاص طور پر خرچ یا سائز کو منظم طریقے سے کم کرنا

examples: The company decided to pare down its workforce to save costs. She pared down her wardrobe before moving to a smaller apartment. The editor asked the writer to pare down the article to 1,000 words. They are trying to pare down unnecessary expenses this month.
synonyms: Reduce, Cut back, Trim, Lessen
sindhiMeaning: گهٽائڻ، غير ضروري شيون ڪڍي گهٽ ڪرڻ (مثال طور خرچ ڪم يا سامان ۾ گهٽتائي ڪرڻ)
antonyms: Expand, Increase, Enlarge, Add
urduMeaning: کم کرنا، غیر ضروری چیزیں نکال کر محدود کرنا (مثلاً بجٹ کام یا سامان میں کمی کرنا)
englishMeaning: To reduce size, number, or amount. To make something smaller or simpler by removing unnecessary parts, costs, or details.

antonyms: Optional part, Separate element, Unnecessary addition, Nonessential
sindhiMeaning: ضروري حصو، حصو ۽ جزو، لازمي حصو، جدا نه ٿي سگهندڙ حصو
urduMeaning: لازمی حصہ، مستقل حصہ، جزوِ لازم، الگ نہ ہونے والا حصہ
examples: Hard work is part and parcel of success. Stress is part and parcel of modern life. Learning from failure is part and parcel of growing up. Communication is part and parcel of a healthy relationship.
synonyms: Inseparable part, Fundamental aspect, Core component
englishMeaning: An essential or necessary part of something. Something that cannot be separated from the whole. It refers to something that is a natural, basic, or integral element of a situation, activity, or system.

antonyms: Refuse, Reject
urduMeaning: کسی کو اپنے گھر بلانا، دعوت دینا، کئی لوگوں سے کسی بات کے متعلق پوچھنا
examples: I’ll ask some friends round for dinner tonight. She asked round to see if anyone had seen her lost dog. They asked their neighbors round for tea last weekend. If you need advice, ask round, someone might know the answer.
englishMeaning: To invite someone to visit your home. To ask several people for information or help.
sindhiMeaning: مهمان طور گهر تي سڏڻ دعوت ڏيڻ، ڪنهن ڳالهه جي ڄاڻ لاءِ ماڻهن کان پڇڻ
synonyms: Call over, Host

examples: He is a real party animal and never misses a weekend celebration. My cousin became a party animal after joining university. She was known as a party animal during her college days. Don’t invite him if you want a quiet evening, he is a party animal.
sindhiMeaning: اهڙو ماڻهو جيڪو گهڻيون پارٽيون ڪري، خوش مزاج پرجوش ۽ سماجي ميل جول پسند ڪري، جيڪو وندر محفلن ۽ گڏجاڻين کي پسند ڪري، جيڪو گهڻو وقت دوستن سان ميل جول ۽ پارٽين ۾ گذاري
urduMeaning: ایسا شخص جو اکثر پارٹیوں میں جاتا ہے اور بہت زیادہ خوش مزاج پرجوش اور سماجی ہوتا ہے، جو تفریح محفلوں اور میل جول کو ترجیح دیتا ہے، جو زیادہ وقت گھروں سے باہر پارٹیوں میں گزارتا ہے
englishMeaning: A person who enjoys going to parties often and behaves in a very energetic, lively, and social way at social gatherings. Someone who loves nightlife, celebrations, music, dancing, and social events. Such a person usually enjoys staying out late, meeting new people, and having fun in crowded or festive environments. The phrase is informal and often used in a friendly or humorous way.
synonyms: Social butterfly, Life of the party, Extrovert, Night owl (contextual), Celebrator
antonyms: Introvert, Homebody, Reserved person, Quiet person, Stay-at-home type

englishMeaning: To give or share something to each person in a group. To distribute something among a group of people, either physically or by sharing information. It can also mean to circulate something widely, sometimes gossip or news.
antonyms: Withhold, Keep, Retain, Hold back
urduMeaning: کسی چیز کو گروپ میں ہر شخص تک پہنچانا یا بانٹنا،معلومات یا افواہیں پھیلانا
synonyms: Distribute, Share, Circulate, Hand out, Give out
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ کي گروپ ۾ هر هڪ ڏانهن ورهائڻ يا موڪلڻ، معلومات يا خبر کي وڏي پيماني تي ڦهلائڻ
examples: Please pass around the papers so everyone can read them. They passed around a birthday cake at the party. Rumors started passing around the office. She passed around the photos from her vacation.

sindhiMeaning: فوت ٿيڻ، دنيا مان لاڏاڻو ڪري وڃڻ (اهو لفظ عزت ۽ ادب سان استعمال ڪيو ويندو آهي)، تڪليف جو آهستي آهستي ختم ٿيڻ، بيهوش ٿيڻ، آهستي آهستي ختم ٿي وڃڻ يا مٽجي وڃڻ، وقت گذارڻ
synonyms: Die, Perish, Expire, Depart, Leave this world
englishMeaning: To die (a polite and gentle way to say someone has died). To slowly disappear or come to an end. To let time go by. To become unconscious
examples: His grandfather passed away last night. She passed away after a long illness. Many heroes passed away in the war. He passed away quietly in his sleep. The storm clouds passed away after sunset. The pain will pass away soon. They told stories to pass away the long night. He passed away from exhaustion. They played games to pass away the evening.
urduMeaning: وفات پانا، انتقال کر جانا (یہ لفظ ادب اور احترام کے ساتھ استعمال ہوتا ہے)، تکلیف آہستہ آہستہ ختم ہونا، ہوش ہونا، وقت گزارنا، آہستہ آہستہ ختم ہو جانا یا مٹ جانا
antonyms: Be born, Live, Survive, Exist

englishMeaning: To give something back to someone or return it. Also used for throwing or kicking a ball backward to a teammate. In communication, to send information back to someone. To move something backward in a line or group.
urduMeaning: واپس دینا، پیچھے کی طرف بھیجنا، اطلاع یا پیغام واپس بھیجنا، قطار میں کسی چیز کو پیچھے منتقل کرنا
antonyms: Pass forward, Keep, Hold, Receive, Take
synonyms: Return, Give back, Hand back, Send back, Throw back
sindhiMeaning: واپس ڏيڻ، پوئتي موڪلڻ، اطلاع يا پيغام واپس موڪلڻ، قطار ۾ پوئتي طرف شيءِ يا پيغام هلائڻ
examples: Please pass the paper back to me. He passed the ball back to the goalkeeper. She passed back the document after signing. The teacher asked the students to pass the books back.

sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شخص يا شيءِ جي ڀرسان لنگهي وڃڻ بغير بيهڻ جي، ڪنهن هنڌ يا شخص جي ويجهو ٿي اڳتي نڪري وڃڻ، نظرانداز ڪرڻ يا ڌيان نه ڏيڻ، وقت جو گذري وڃڻ بغير ڪنهن عمل جي، موقعي يا آڇ کي رد ڪرڻ، رسمي طور ڪنهن جي وفات جو ذڪر ڪرڻ لاءِ
examples: I saw him pass by my house yesterday. She passed by me without saying hello. The opportunity passed by because we were not ready. Many years have passed by since we met. His grandfather passed by peacefully in his sleep.
synonyms: Go past, Move past, Overlook, Ignore, Bypass
antonyms: Stop, Notice, Accept, Stay, Approach
urduMeaning: کسی شخص یا چیز کے پاس سے بغیر رکے گزر جانا، کسی جگہ یا شخص کے قریب سے آگے نکل جانا، نظر انداز کرنا یا توجہ نہ دینا، وقت کا بغیر کسی عمل کے گزر جانا، موقع یا پیشکش کو مسترد کرنا، رسمی انداز میں کسی کے انتقال کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے
englishMeaning: To go past someone or something without stopping. To go near or beyond a person, place, or object. To not notice or deliberately ignore someone or something. To let time go (when time moves without action being taken). To refuse an opportunity or offer. In formal language, sometimes used to mean someone has died.

examples: He tried to pass off the fake painting as an original. The meeting passed off without any problems. She passed off her old homework as new. The exam passed off smoothly for all students. He tried to pass off cheap wine as expensive.
synonyms: Pretend, Represent, Present, Occur, Happen, Carry out
urduMeaning: جعلی چیز کو اصلی ظاہر کرنا، کسی چیز کو کچھ اور ظاہر کرنا یا جھوٹا ثابت کرنا، واقعہ یا کام کا پیش آنا، کسی کام کو مکمل کرنا یا ختم کرنا، کسی چیز کو اصلی ظاہر کرنا، واقعہ یا کام پیش آنا، قبول کرانا، آہستہ آہستہ ختم ہونا، کام دوسروں پر سونپنا، توجہ سے بچانا
sindhiMeaning: غلط يا نقلي شيءِ کي صحيح ظاهر ڪرڻ، ڪنهن شيءَ کي ڪجهه ٻيو ڏيکارڻ، واقعو يا حالت پيش ٿيڻ، ڪجهه مڪمل يا ختم ڪرڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ کي اصل ظاهر ڪرڻ، واقعو يا ڪاروائي ٿيڻ، قبول ڪرائڻ، منظور ڪرائڻ، آهستي آهستي ختم ٿيڻ، ڪم ٻين تي سونپڻ، ڪوڙو ظاهر ڪرڻ، ڌيان کان بچائڻ
englishMeaning: To represent or present something or someone as something else, often deceptively. To happen, occur, or take place (often used for events). To successfully complete or get rid of something (informal).
antonyms: Fail, Expose, Reveal, Stop, Interrupt

examples: She passed on her knowledge to her students. He passed on after years of illness. Please pass on the message. The ring was passed on through generations. I will pass on this question. He passed on commenting about it.
englishMeaning: To transfer or hand over something to another person. To transmit information, knowledge, or a message. To decline an opportunity. To die (informal). To skip or refuse something. To not use, answer, or deal with something. To give as a legacy or inheritance.
synonyms: Transfer, Give, Relay, Communicate, Hand over, Decline (contextual), Die (informal context)
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کي شيءَ ڏيڻ يا منتقل ڪرڻ، ڄاڻ يا پيغام پهچائڻ، موقعو رد ڪرڻ، وفات ٿيڻ (عام ڳالهه ٻولهه ۾)، ڪنهن شيءَ کي ڇڏڻ يا نظرانداز ڪرڻ
antonyms: Keep, Retain, Withhold, Accept, Survive (contextual)
urduMeaning: کسی کو چیز دینا یا منتقل کرنا، علم یا پیغام پہنچانا، کسی موقع کو قبول نہ کرنا، وفات پا جانا (عام بول چال میں)، کسی چیز کو رد کرنا یا چھوڑنا، کسی چیز کو چھوڑ دینا یا نظرانداز کرنا، جائیداد یا چیز کو وراثت میں دینا

بیہوش ہونا، وش کھو دینا، تعلیم یا تربیت مکمل کر کے فارغ التحصیل ہونا، بانٹنا ، تقسیم کرنا، فوجی تربیت مکمل کرنا ، پاس آؤٹ پریڈ میں شرکت کرنا، زیادہ تھکن یا دباؤ کی وجہ سے گر جانا، عارضی طور پر بے قابو ہونا یا سوچنے میں مشکل
antonyms: Recover, Regain consciousness, Drop out, Withhold
englishMeaning: To faint or lose consciousness temporarily due to exhaustion, heat, shock, or illness. To successfully complete a course or training and receive a certificate, diploma, or degree. To distribute something to a group of people (less common).
sindhiMeaning: بيهوش ٿي وڃڻ، هوش وڃائڻ، تعليم مڪمل ڪرڻ، ڪورس مڪمل ڪرڻ بعد سند حاصل ڪرڻ، ورهائڻ، تقسيم ڪرڻ، عارضي طور تي ڪمزور ٿيڻ، سوچڻ ۾ دير ڪرڻ، فوجي تربيت مڪمل ڪرڻ، فارغ التحصيل ٿيڻ
examples: She passed out after standing in the sun for too long. He passed out from medical school last year. The teacher passed out the exam papers to the students. During the concert, one fan passed out from excitement. He joked that he nearly passed out when he saw the bill. The volunteers passed out food to flood victims. In military contexts, pass out parade means the formal graduation ceremony for cadets.
synonyms: Faint, Blackout, Collapse, Graduate, Complete, Distribute

urduMeaning: نظر انداز کرنا، چھوڑ دینا یا چھوڑنا، ذمہ داری یا حق منتقل کرنا، اوپر سے گزرنا یا عبور کرنا، فوقیت نہ دینا
antonyms: Notice, Consider, Acknowledge, Attend to, Include
sindhiMeaning: نظرانداز ڪرڻ، ترڪ ڪرڻ، اهميت نه ڏيڻ، ڇڏڻ، ذميواري منتقل ڪرڻ، مٿان گذرڻ يا پار ڪرڻ
examples: The manager decided to pass over the junior employee for promotion. Please don’t pass over any important details in the report. The king passed over the crown to his eldest son. The plane passed over the mountains at sunrise.
synonyms: Ignore, Overlook, Skip, Omit, Bypass, Disregard
englishMeaning: To deliberately ignore or not give attention to someone. To skip or omit something. To transfer or hand over responsibility. To ascend or move above something.

A specific part, feature, angle, or characteristic of a situation, object, or idea. The way something appears or is viewed. Shows how an action relates to time, such as completed or ongoing. The way something looks or appears. The position or relationship of planets.
antonyms: Whole, Total, Entirety, Complete
urduMeaning: کسی چیز کا پہلو یا رخ، کسی چیز صورت حال یا خیال کا خاص پہلو زاویہ یا خصوصیت جسے الگ انداز سے دیکھا یا سمجھا جائے، ظاہری شکل، گرامر میں فعل کی حالت جیسے جاری یا مکمل، سیاروں کی پوزیشن یا تعلق
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ جو پهلو يا رخ، ڪنهن شيءِ حالت يا خيال جو خاص پهلو رخ يا خاصيت جنهن کي الڳ طرح سان ڏٺو يا سمجهيو وڃي، ظاهري صورت، گرامر ۾ عمل جي حالت (جهڙو جاري يا مڪمل)، سيارن جي جڳهه يا لاڳاپو
synonyms: Feature, Element, Part, Angle, Facet, Side
examples: One important aspect of education is critical thinking. The financial aspect of the project needs careful planning. She considered every aspect of the problem before deciding. The cultural aspect of the festival attracts many tourists.

synonyms: Decline, Refuse, Reject, Ignore
urduMeaning: موقع چھوڑ دینا، موقع ہاتھ سے جانے دینا یا انکار کرنا
sindhiMeaning: موقعو وڃائڻ، رد يا نظرانداز ڪرڻ، پيشڪش کي قبول نه ڪرڻ
examples: I can’t believe she passed up the chance to study abroad. Don’t pass up this opportunity to meet the CEO. He passed up the free tickets for the concert. She always passes up dessert, even when it looks delicious.
englishMeaning: To decline or refuse an opportunity or offer. Choosing not to take advantage of an opportunity, offer, or chance, often one that could be beneficial. It can also mean letting something go or ignoring it.
antonyms: Accept, Take, Seize, Grab

examples: Everyone could see the passion in his approach to the work. Her performance is full of passion and originality. The crime was committed in a fit of passion.
synonyms: Desire, Fervency
englishMeaning: A very strong feeling of love, anger, hatred, enthusiasm, excitement, A very strong feeling of sexual love,
antonyms: Abomination
sindhiMeaning: جوش، جذبو، حاوي جذبات، اڪسائيندڙ، اڀاريندڙ، ڪاوڙ جي حالت، خواهش، حرص، خفت، بيچين ڪندڙ اتساه
urduMeaning: جوش، جزبہ، ولولہ، جنون

synonyms: Enthusiastic, Emotional, Zealous, Devoted, Eager, Intense
englishMeaning: Having strong feelings, enthusiasm, or deep interest. Full of strong emotion. Showing deep love. Very enthusiastic about something. Having intense belief or commitment.
examples: She is passionate about teaching children. He gave a passionate speech about education. They are passionate football fans. I am passionate about learning languages.
urduMeaning: پُرجوش، شدید جذبہ رکھنے والا، گہری محبت رکھنے والا، کسی چیز کے لیے بہت پُرجوش، مضبوط یقین رکھنے والا، شدید جذبات والا
sindhiMeaning: تمام گهڻي جذبي وارو، ڏاڍي دلچسپي رکندڙ، جذبات سان ڀريل، گهري محبت وارو، ڏاڍي شوق سان ڪم ڪندڙ، مضبوط عقيدي وارو
antonyms: Indifferent, Uninterested, Apathetic, Cold, Calm

synonyms: Connect, Link, Integrate, Include, Join, Attach, Insert
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ماڻهو يا نظام کي ڳنڍڻ، گڏ ڪرڻ يا ڪنهن ڳالهه ۾ شامل ڪرڻ، خاص طور تي فون، ڪمپيوٽر يا ڳالهه ٻولهه ۾، اڳ ۾ هلندڙ ڪم، ڳالهه يا نظام سان شامل ڪرڻ، ملائڻ، رابطو ڪرائڻ
examples: The technician patched me in so I could join the conference call. Can you patch her in on the video meeting? They patched the new software in without shutting down the system. The manager patched in the marketing team to discuss the new strategy.
englishMeaning: To connect someone or something into a communication system, discussion, or electronic network, especially by phone or computer. To add or include a person or piece of information into an ongoing situation or system.
urduMeaning: کسی شخص یا نظام کو کسی گفتگو یا نیٹ ورک سے جوڑنا یا شامل کرنا، خاص طور پر فون یا کمپیوٹر کے ذریعے، جوڑنا، شامل کرنا، رابطہ قائم کرنا، ملا دینا
antonyms: Disconnect, Remove, Exclude, Detach, Separate

englishMeaning: To fix or cover up a problem, disagreement, or mistake temporarily instead of solving it completely. It can also mean to make peace or smooth out differences in a situation.
antonyms: Expose, Worsen, Reveal, Destroy, Aggravate, Deepen
sindhiMeaning: عارضي طور تي مسئلي يا غلطي کي لڪائڻ يا ٺيڪ ڪرڻ، اهڙو قدم جنهن سان مسئلو ڪجهه وقت لاءِ ختم لڳي پر اصل ۾ مڪمل حل نه ٿئي
urduMeaning: کسی مسئلے یا غلطی کو عارضی طور پر چھپانا یا ٹھیک کرنا، اختلاف یا خرابی کو وقتی طور پر ختم کرنے کی کوشش کرنا
synonyms: Cover up, Smooth over, Repair, Fix temporarily, Gloss over, Mend, Reconcile
examples: They tried to patch over their argument, but the tension remained. The manager patched over the mistake by giving a quick explanation. The committee patched over the budget issues instead of addressing them properly. A thin layer of paint cannot patch over structural problems in the building.

sindhiMeaning: گڏ ڪرڻ، گڏيل ٺاهڻ، ٽڪرا گڏ ڪرڻ، جلدي تيار ڪرڻ، عارضي مرمت ڪرڻ (عام طور تي نتيجو عارضي ۽ مڪمل نه هوندو آهي پر ڪم هلائي سگهجي ٿو)
urduMeaning: جلدی میں جوڑنا، عارضی طور پر تیار کرنا، مختلف حصوں کو ملا کر بنانا، عارضی مرمت کرنا، وقتی انتظام کرنا
englishMeaning: To put or join different parts, ideas, or things together quickly or roughly, often in an imperfect or temporary way. It is usually used when something is made or arranged without proper planning or resources.
antonyms: Destroy, Dismantle, Break apart, Ruin, Separate
synonyms: Assemble, Put together, Improvise, Repair, Fix, Mend, Cobble together
examples: They managed to patch together a temporary shelter before the storm started. She patched together an old computer from spare parts. The team patched together a plan at the last minute. After the argument, they tried to patch together their friendship.

antonyms: Break up, Damage, Ruin, Separate, Worsen
urduMeaning: مرمت کرنا یا جھگڑا ختم کر کے تعلق دوبارہ قائم کرنا، کسی چیز کو عارضی یا سادہ طریقے سے ٹھیک کرنا، جھگڑے کے بعد دوبارہ صلح کر لینا، زخمی شخص کا علاج کرنا یا پٹی باندھنا، کسی چیز کو جلدی میں تیار یا ترتیب دینا
englishMeaning: To fix something quickly, often in a simple or temporary way. To become friends again after a disagreement or conflict. To give medical care to an injured person, especially by covering or stitching a wound. To put something together in a hurried or improvised way.
examples: After years of silence, the two brothers finally patched up their differences. She patched up the torn dress before the party. The doctor patched him up after the accident. They tried to patch up a quick agreement before the meeting ended.
synonyms: Reconcile, Make up, Repair, Fix, Mend, Heal
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ کي عارضي يا سادي طريقي سان ٺيڪ ڪرڻ، جهيڙي کان پوءِ ٻيهر صلح ڪري دوستي قائم ڪرڻ، زخمي شخص جو علاج ڪرڻ يا پٽي ٻڌڻ، ڪا شيءِ جلدي ۾ تيار يا ترتيب ڏيڻ

antonyms: Even, Uniform, Consistent, Steady, Regular, Smooth
urduMeaning: غیر یکساں، ٹکڑوں میں، غیر مسلسل، غیر مکمل یا ادھورا، جگہ جگہ سے کمزور یا خراب، بکھرا ہوا یا غیر ہموار، جو مکمل یا یکساں نہ ہو بلکہ ٹکڑوں میں ہو یا غیر مسلسل ہو، یہ موسم کارکردگی علم یا کسی سطح کی حالت کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے
synonyms: Uneven, Irregular, Inconsistent, Spotty, Broken, Unevenly distributed
sindhiMeaning: اڻ برابر، ٽڪرن ۾، غير مسلسل، اڻ پورو يا اڌورو، جڳهن تي خراب يا ڪمزور، غير برابر يا ٽٽل حالت، اهڙي شيءِ جيڪا برابر يا مڪمل نه هجي پر ٽڪرن ۾ يا غير مسلسل هجي، اهو موسم ڄاڻ يا ڪنهن حالت لاءِ استعمال ٿيندو آهي
examples: The internet connection was patchy during the storm. His knowledge of the subject is patchy. The paint on the wall looks patchy. Rainfall will be patchy across the region today.
englishMeaning: Uneven, inconsistent, or not continuous. Something that is not uniform or complete. It can refer to physical things like grass, paint, or weather coverage, and also to performance, knowledge, or information that is irregular or unreliable.
The ability to stay calm, accept delays, problems, or suffering without getting angry or upset. It means waiting or dealing with difficulties in a peaceful and controlled way.
antonyms: Impatience, Anger, Frustration, Restlessness, Irritation
urduMeaning: صبر اور برداشت، تحمل اور ضبط نفس، انتظار کرنے کی صلاحیت، غصے پر قابو رکھنا، مشکل حالات میں خاموش اور پرسکون رہنا، جلد بازی سے بچنا
sindhiMeaning: صبر ۽ تحمل، برداشت ڪرڻ جي صلاحيت، ڏکين حالتن ۾ پرسڪون رهڻ، انتظار ڪرڻ جي همت، غصي تي ضابطو رکڻ، سهپ/ ثابت قدمي/ استقلال
synonyms: Tolerance, Endurance, Calmness, Self-control, Forbearance, Perseverance
examples: She showed great patience while teaching the children. Patience is important when learning a new language. He lost his patience after waiting for two hours. With patience, you can solve even the hardest problems.

englishMeaning: Harshness or severity, especially in tone, manner, or conditions. Roughness, sharpness, or severity in behavior, speech, or environment. It can describe difficult circumstances or the sharpness of a surface.
antonyms: Gentleness, Softness, Mildness, leniency, Smoothness
sindhiMeaning: سختي، کڙڪ، تيز رويي يا صورتحال جو سخت ۽ ڪٽيل انداز
examples: The teacher addressed the students with unexpected asperity. Life in the desert is known for its asperity. His speech was full of asperity and criticism. The mountain trail tested their patience with its asperity.
synonyms: Harshness, Severity, Rigor, Roughness, Sternness
urduMeaning: سختی، تلخی، کڑواہٹ، کسی بات یا رویے کی سخت نوعیت

sindhiMeaning: خاندان يا قبيلي جو بزرگ مرد، خاندان قبيلو يا گروپ جو مٿين ۽ معزز مرد جنهن وٽ فيصلا ڪرڻ جو اختيار ۽ احترام هوندو آهي
synonyms: Elder, Father figure, Leader, Founder, Chief
englishMeaning: The male head of a family, tribe, or group. A senior male figure who holds authority in a family, community, or organization. This term often implies respect, leadership, and wisdom. Historically, it also refers to founding fathers of religious or social communities.
examples: Abraham is considered the patriarch of the Jewish people. The family patriarch made the final decision on the property. In many tribes, the patriarch holds the power to resolve disputes. The company founder is regarded as the patriarch of the business.
antonyms: Junior, Subordinate, Dependent, Follower
urduMeaning: خاندان یا قبیلے کا بزرگ مرد، وہ مرد جو خاندان قبیلہ یا گروپ میں سب سے بڑا اور معزز ہوتا ہے اور جس کے فیصلے اور رائے کو اہمیت دی جاتی ہے

englishMeaning: Property or money inherited from one’s father or ancestors. The inheritance of property, wealth, or rights passed down from previous generations, usually from parents or ancestors. It can also refer to cultural heritage or legacy received from forefathers.
antonyms: Loss, Deprivation, Forfeiture, Disinheritance
sindhiMeaning: اھو وسيلو يا ملڪيت جيڪو والدين يا آباواجداد کان حاصل ٿئي، شيون ملڪيت يا حق جيڪي ڪنهن جي والدين يا اڳوڻن کان وراثت طور ملن، هي لفظ ثقافتي يا تاريخي ورثي لاءِ پڻ استعمال ٿي سگهي ٿو
synonyms: Heritage, Inheritance, Legacy, Birthright
urduMeaning: وہ جائداد یا مال جو والد یا آبا و اجداد سے وراثت میں ملا ہو ، وہ ملکیت دولت یا حقوق جو والد یا آبا و اجداد سے وراثت میں منتقل ہوتے ہیں، یہ ثقافتی یا تاریخی ورثہ کے لیے بھی استعمال ہو سکتا ہے
examples: He proudly inherited his family’s patrimony. The ancient castle is part of the nation’s patrimony. She safeguarded the patrimony left by her grandfather. Cultural patrimony is essential for understanding history.

sindhiMeaning: ملڪ سان محبت رکڻ ۽ ان جي حفاظت ڪرڻ، قومي ثقافت، رواجن ۽ تاريخ جو احترام ڪرڻ وارو، ملڪ لاءِ قرباني ڏيڻ وارو ۽ ذاتي مفاد کي پوئتي رکڻ وارو
englishMeaning: Showing love, support, and devotion to one’s country. Feeling or expressing strong attachment, loyalty, and pride toward one’s nation.
antonyms: Unpatriotic, Disloyal, Treacherous, Anti-national
synonyms: Nationalistic, Loyal, Devoted, Devoted to one’s country, Flag-waving
urduMeaning: وطن سے محبت اور اس کے دفاع والا، قومی اقدار، ثقافت اور تاریخ کی عزت کرنے والا، ملک کے لیے قربانی دینے والا اور ذاتی مفاد کو پیچھے رکھنے والا
examples: The patriotic citizens celebrated Independence Day with great enthusiasm. She wrote a patriotic poem about her homeland. His patriotic actions inspired others to volunteer for the community. Patriotic songs were played during the national ceremony.

antonyms: Opponent, Critic, Rival, Enemy
sindhiMeaning: ساراهيندڙ، مددگار، سرپرست، حامي، پٺڀرائي ڪندڙ، اهو شخص جيڪو ڪنهن ڪم تنظيم فن يا ماڻهوءَ جي مالي يا اخلاقي مدد ڪري، ڪنهن ادارو يا فنڪار جو سرپرست يا مددگار
englishMeaning: A person who supports, sponsors, or protects someone, an organization, an activity (especially the arts, education, or charity). It can also mean a regular customer of a shop or restaurant.
urduMeaning: سرپرست، حامی، مددگار، کفیل، معاون، وہ شخص جو کسی فن، ادارے یا شخص کی مالی یا اخلاقی مدد کرے، کسی تنظیم یا کام کی حوصلہ افزائی کرنے والا
examples: The artist found a wealthy patron who supported his work. She is a patron of the local charity organization. The restaurant’s patrons were very satisfied with the service. The king acted as a patron for poets and scholars.
synonyms: Supporter, Sponsor, Backer, Benefactor, Guardian, Customer

examples: He always tries to patronize his juniors by giving unnecessary advice. The organization was patronized by several famous philanthropists. We often patronize the restaurant near our office. Don’t patronize me, I know what I’m doing!.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شخص، اداري يا ڪم جي حمايت يا مدد ڪرڻ، مغرور طريقي سان رويو رکڻ، ڪنهن سان اهڙي مهرباني ڏيکارڻ جيڪا اصل ۾ حقارت يا وڏائي ظاهر ڪري، گراهڪ ٿيڻ، ڪنهن دڪان يا هوٽل تي باقاعده وڃڻ
urduMeaning: سرپرستی کرنا ، کسی فرد، ادارے یا کام کی حمایت یا مدد کرنا، احسان جتانا ، تحقیر آمیز انداز میں پیش آنا – ایسا برتاؤ جو بظاہر مہربان لگے مگر دراصل برتری ظاہر کرے، کسی دکان یا ہوٹل کا مستقل گاہک ہونا
synonyms: Support, Sponsor, Aid, Favor, Condescend, Demean
antonyms: Oppose, Ignore, Neglect, Humiliate, Disrespect
englishMeaning: To support or sponsor someone or something (like an organization, shop, or artist). To behave in a way that seems kind but actually shows a sense of superiority (talking down to someone). To frequent a business as a customer.
A very poor person. A person destitute of means except such as are derived from charity. A very poor person who has no money to pay for food, clothing, etc.
antonyms: Millionaire
urduMeaning: محتاج، مفلس، نادار، کنگال، مسکین ، گداگر، غریب، نادر
examples: There is not much difference between a greedy person and a pauper. Eat breakfast like a king, lunch like a prince, and dinner like a pauper.
sindhiMeaning: ضرورت مند، سُڃو، کُٽل، ڪنگال، محتاج، مسڪين، مفلس، غريب، پينو
synonyms: Mendicant

englishMeaning: A person who strongly desires or tries to achieve a particular position, goal, or honor. Having ambitions to achieve something, especially a high position or distinction. Someone who hopes or works hard to become something, for example, a job seeker, a student aiming for success, or a candidate for a position.
synonyms: Candidate, Contender, Applicant, Seeker, Hopeful, Striver, Ambitious person
urduMeaning: امیدوار ، خواہشمند ، طلبگار، وہ شخص جو کسی منصب کامیابی یا عہدے کے حصول کی خواہش اور کوشش رکھتا ہو
examples: Many aspirants applied for the position of manager. He is an aspirant for the national football team. Every aspirant must work hard to achieve success. The scholarship attracted hundreds of young aspirants. It is to inform that all aspirant candidates of forthcoming MDCAT must bring their original CNIC.
sindhiMeaning: اميدوار، خواهشمند، تمنا رکندڙ، اهو ماڻهو جيڪو ڪنهن وڏي مقصد يا مقام تائين پهچڻ لاءِ محنت ڪري رهيو هجي
antonyms: Noncompetitor, Indifferent person, Unmotivated person, Uninterested

examples: She decided to pave her own road by starting a business instead of joining a corporate job. He paved his own road in music despite his family wanting him to become a doctor. Many successful entrepreneurs pave their own road by taking risks others avoid.
synonyms: Forge one’s path, Carve out one’s destiny, Go one’s own way, Break new ground
sindhiMeaning: پنهنجو رستو پاڻ ٺاهڻ، ٻين جي پيروي ڪرڻ بدران پنهنجي سوچ ۽ فيصلي سان زندگي گذارڻ
urduMeaning: اپنی زندگی کا راستہ خود بنانا، دوسروں کی پیروی کرنے کے بجائے اپنی سوچ اور فیصلوں کے مطابق آگے بڑھنا
antonyms: Copy others, Depend on others, Conform to society, Stick to tradition
englishMeaning: To create your own path in life by making independent decisions instead of following others. It refers to originality, self-reliance, and choosing a unique direction even if it is difficult or unconventional.

examples: He had to sacrifice another pawn. The hostages are being used as political pawns. The prince became a pawn in the game of power politics.
synonyms: Pledge, Impignorate
antonyms: Ransom, Redeem
sindhiMeaning: گروي، وَٿُ، ڍڪيل، دالان، پيادو(شطرنج)، مُهرو، ڪَٽ پُتلي، شرط رکڻ، داءُ رکڻ، گروي رکڻ، ضمانت طور، ٻين جي مقصدن لاءِ استعمال ٿيندڙ شخص، (پنهنجي عزت ۽ آبرو تي) پڪو واعدو ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: شطرنج کا پیادہ، وہ شخص جسے کوئی دوسرا اپنے مقصد کیلئے استعمال کرے، گروی، رہناڑنا، بیذق، پیادہ، گروی رکھی ہوئی چیز، گروہ ، بطور ضمانت
englishMeaning: A person used by another to gain an end. Borrowing and leaving an article as security for repayment of the loan. Leave as a guarantee in return for money. To pledge for the fulfillment of a promise, to stake, to risk, to wager, to hazard.

urduMeaning: واپس دینا، بدلہ لینا، قرض یا رقم واپس کرنا، عمل کا نتیجہ ظاہر ہونا، ویسا ہی برتاؤ کرنا جیسا اس نے آپ کے ساتھ کیا، بدلہ چکانا، معاوضہ دینا
examples: I will pay back the money next week. She paid him back for the loan within a month. He plans to pay back his brother for the prank. She paid her parents back by supporting them in old age.
synonyms: Repay, Reimburse, Refund, Return, Avenge, Retaliate, Get even
antonyms: Borrow, Lend, Forgive, Pardon, Ignore
englishMeaning: To return borrowed money. To take revenge. To reward or return a favor. To cause a result later because of an earlier action. To respond equally to someone’s behavior. To settle a debt of gratitude. To compensate for damage or loss
sindhiMeaning: واپس ڏيڻ، بدلو وٺڻ، قرض يا پيسا واپس ڪرڻ، عمل جو اثر يا نتيجو بعد ۾ ظاهر ٿيڻ، ڪنهن سان ساڳي ريت پيش اچڻ جيئن هن اوهان سان ڪيو، عملي جواب ڏيڻ، معاوضو ڏيڻ

antonyms: Receive, Earn, Gain, Get for free, Save
sindhiMeaning: قيمت ڀرڻ، سزا ڀوڳڻ، تلافي ڪرڻ يا رقم ڀرڻ، خرچ يا محنت جي لائق هجڻ، نقصان يا تڪليف برداشت ڪرڻ
examples: I paid for the groceries with my debit card. He will pay for his careless mistake. The company paid for the repairs after the accident. The training course paid for itself within a year.
englishMeaning: To give money to buy something. To accept punishment or negative result. To compensate for damage. To be worth the cost or effort
urduMeaning: قیمت چکانا، سزا پانا، نقصان یا تکلیف اٹھانا، معاوضہ ادا کرنا، خرچ یا محنت کے قابل ہونا
synonyms: Purchase, Compensate, Repay, Settle, Suffer

urduMeaning: قرض اتارنا، کامیاب ہونا، رشوت دینا، انعام دینا یا فائدہ پہنچانا، آخری ادائیگی، فائدو يا منافع
antonyms: Borrow, Owe, Lose, Fail, Ignore, Default
synonyms: Repay, Settle, Clear, Reward, Bribe, Succeed, Profit
englishMeaning: To repay money that is owed. To bring a good result after effort. To bribe someone. To reward someone. Final payment. Profit or benefit.
sindhiMeaning: قرض لاهڻ، ڪامياب ٿيڻ، رشوت ڏيڻ، انعام ڏيڻ يا فائدو پهچائڻ، آخري ادائيگي، فائدو يا منافع
examples: She worked extra hours to pay off her student loan. His patience finally paid off when he got promoted. The criminal tried to pay off the officer. Their long term investment paid off with huge profits.

sindhiMeaning: بي حساب رقم ادا ڪرڻ، تمام گهڻي رقم ڏيڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ لاءِ قيمت کان وڌيڪ ادا ڪرڻ، ناجائز طور تي وڌيڪ پئسا ڏيڻ، اهڙي شيءِ لاءِ گهڻو وڌيڪ ڏيڻ جنهن جي قيمت ايتري نه هجي

synonyms: Strive, Yearn, Hope, Long for, Dream
urduMeaning: خواہش رکھنا ، آرزو کرنا، بلند مقام یا درجہ پانے کی کوشش کرنا، کسی عظیم مقصد کے لیے جدوجہد کرنا
antonyms: Neglect, Ignore, Dismiss, Give up, Despair
englishMeaning: To have a strong desire or ambition to achieve something high or great. To aim for success, excellence, or a particular goal in life.

antonyms: Carefree, Cheerful, Unthinking, Lighthearted

sindhiMeaning: انتهائي غريب هجڻ، بنيادي ضرورتن جي کوٽ ۾ هجڻ، جهڙوڪ کاڌو، ڪپڙا ۽ رهائش حاصل نه ڪرڻ
