synonyms: Overtake, Get ahead, Move ahead, Take the lead, Surge ahead, Outpace
urduMeaning: آگے نکل جانا، سبقت لے جانا، کسی میدان میں دوسروں سے بہتر کارکردگی دکھا کر آگے ہو جانا، معمولی برتری کو بڑھا دینا اور واضح برتری حاصل کرنا
sindhiMeaning: اڳتي وڌڻ، اڳتي نڪري وڃڻ، مقابلي يا ڊوڙ ۾ سڀني کان اڳتي ٿي وڃڻ، ڪنهن شعبي ۾ ٻين کان وڌيڪ ڪامياب ٿي وڃڻ، ٿورو اڳتي هئڻ کان پوءِ وڌيڪ فاصلو پيدا ڪرڻ
examples: The red car pulled ahead in the final lap. Our team pulled ahead in the second half. She pulled ahead of her competitors. The company pulled ahead in sales this year.

antonyms: Join, Unite
englishMeaning: To separate people or animals that are fighting. To separate something into pieces by pulling different parts of it in different directions. To say that something, usually a piece of work, is very bad.
synonyms: Separate, Dismantle
sindhiMeaning: ٽوڙڻ، جدا ڪرڻ، وڙهندڙ ماڻهن يا جانورن کي الڳ ڪرڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ کي مختلف طرفن کان ڌار ڪري ٽڪر ٽڪر ڪرڻ، چوڻ لاءِ ته ڪا شيءِ، عام طور تي ڪم جو هڪ ٽڪرو، تمام خراب آهي
urduMeaning: زبردستی الگ کرنا ، توڑ کے ٹکڑے ٹکڑے کر دینا، نافدانہ انداز سے جانچنا ، الگ کرنا
examples: Customers stepped in and pulled the two men apart. The rolls pull apart easily. She pulled the rolls apart with her hands. His gambling problem is pulling the family apart. The last essay I gave him he completely pulled apart. They pulled apart the old machine. The crowd was pulled apart by police.

antonyms: Stop, Halt, Brazen, Breast, Confront,
urduMeaning: پیچھے ڈھکیلنا ،کسی کو پیچھے کر دینا، آگے بڑھنا
synonyms: Detach, Flee, Leave, Depart, Move off
sindhiMeaning: اڳتي وڌڻ، هٿ کڻڻ، اڳتي نڪري وڃڻ، اڳ وٺڻ، جدا ٿي وڃڻ، هٿ کڻي وڃڻ، الڳ ٿيڻ
examples: They waved as the bus pulled away. There was a roar and a cloud of smoke as the car pulled away from the traffic lights. She pulled away just as he was about to kiss her. The Cowboys hit five shots in a row to pull away from Marquette.
englishMeaning: To start moving, especially a vehicle. To increase a score or improve a rank. To draw oneself back or away.

sindhiMeaning: چوڻ جي آزادي هئڻ، چوڻ جي آزادي رکڻ، بيان ڪرڻ جي اجازت رکڻ، اظهار ڪرڻ لاءِ آزاد
englishMeaning: Allowed or free to reveal information. Someone has permission, freedom, or the right to express an opinion, make a statement, or share information without restriction. It often implies that the speaker is not bound by secrecy or authority in this context.
examples: I’m not at liberty to say anything yet. She was at liberty to share the news. The officer isn’t at liberty to comment. Are you at liberty to discuss it now?
antonyms: Restricted, Forbidden
urduMeaning: کہنے کی اجازت ہونا، کہنے کی آزادی رکھنا؛ اظہار کرنے کی اجازت ہونا، رائے دینے کی آزادی ہونا
synonyms: Free, Allowed

examples: Their sponsors pulled back at the last minute. They pulled back a goal just before half-time. He leaned forward to kiss her but she pulled back. Michelle pulled back from her mother and wiped the tears from her eyes. Businesses have already pulled back on corporate travel.
sindhiMeaning: پوئتي هٽڻ يا هٽائڻ، موٽڻ، روڪ، رنڊڪ، واپس وڃڻ، پوئتي هٽڻ
urduMeaning: روکنا،پیچھے ہٹنا
antonyms: Advance, Attack
englishMeaning: To move backwards or away from someone. To decide not to do something that you were intending to do, because of possible problems. To make an army move back from a place. To improve a team’s position in a game. To retreat or withdraw.
synonyms: Withdraw, Retreat, Pullout

englishMeaning: To make somebody less happy, healthy or successful. To destroy a building completely. To earn the large amount of money mentioned.
sindhiMeaning: ڊاهڻ، بي عزت ڪرڻ، شرمندو ڪرڻ، خوار ڪرڻ، ڳاري ڇڏڻ، گھٽ ڪرڻ، ڪيرائڻ گهٽائڻ، عمارت يا شيءِ کي ڊاهڻ
examples: I reckon she's pulling down over £200 000. A powerful storm pulled down the old fishing shack, which had been immortalized in countless paintings. An ugly billboard that was eventually pulled down. He's pulling down six figures at that job.
antonyms: Repair, Mend, Construct
urduMeaning: تباہ کرنا، مسمار کرنا، ڈھانا، جڑ سے اکھیڑنا، گرانا، ادا کیا جانا یا وصول کرنا، صحت خراب ہونا ، عمارت گرا دینا
synonyms: Demolish, Make, Devastate

antonyms: Lose, Leave
sindhiMeaning: اسٽيشن ۾ داخل ٿيڻ ۽ روڪڻ، رستي جي پاسي يا ذڪر ڪيل جاءِ ڏانهن وڃڻ ۽ روڪڻ، ڪنهن منزل تي پهچڻ يا بيهي وڃڻ، گاڏي جو رڪجڻ، آمدني حاصل ڪرڻ
synonyms: Arrive, Earn, Bridle, Check, Constrain, Contain
englishMeaning: To enter a station and stop. To move to the side of the road or to the place mentioned and stop. To arrive at a destination or come to a stop. To earn money.
urduMeaning: کھینچنا ، نقشہ کشی کرنا ، گھوڑے کو باگ سے قابو میں رکھنا ، گاڑی کا رکنا، آمدنی حاصل کرنا
examples: A company that cannot manage to pull in costs will not be in business for very long. The police car signalled to us to pull in. He was pulled in after a random traffic stop turned up drugs in his car.

urduMeaning: اُتارنا ، نکالنا ، کامیابی کے ساتھ انجام پہنچانا ، مشکل کام میں کامیاب ہونا
examples: The team pulled off an upset. The rebel forces pulled off a surprisingly successful offensive against the better equipped government troops. We pulled off the deal. I never thought you'd pull it off. The car pulled off and sped up the road. He pulled off a surprise victory. She pulled off the deal successfully.
synonyms: Execute, Accomplish, Achieve
sindhiMeaning: ڏکيو ڪم ڪاميابي سان ڪرڻ، ڇڪي ڌار ڪرڻ، ٽوڙڻ، کڻڻ يا حاصل ڪرڻ ۾ ڪامياب ٿيڻ، لاهڻ، پٽڻ، لنگهي پار پوڻ، لڪ لنگهڻ يا لنگهائڻ
antonyms: Fail Skimp, Slight, Slur
englishMeaning: To carry through (as a process) to completion. To leave the road in order to stop for a short time. To succeed in doing something difficult. To carry out despite difficulties. To accomplish successfully against odds.

antonyms: Take off, Push away, Release, Discourage, Drop
urduMeaning: جلدی سے کپڑے پہننا، کسی چیز کو اپنی طرف کھینچنا، حوصلہ دینا یا آگے بڑھانا، گاڑی کو کنارے لگا کر روکنا، زور لگا کر چلنا شروع کرنا
sindhiMeaning: جلدي ڪپڙا پائڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ کي پاڻ ڏانهن ڇڪڻ، همٿ افزائي ڪرڻ يا اڳتي وڌائڻ، گاڏي کي ڪناري تي روڪڻ، زور لڳائي هلڻ شروع ڪرڻ
synonyms: Wear, Put on, Drag, Tug, Draw, Encourage, Motivate
englishMeaning: To put on clothing quickly. To draw or tug something toward yourself. To encourage or motivate someone. To move a vehicle to the side and stop. To start moving with effort.
examples: She pulled on her jacket before going outside. He pulled on the rope to lift the bucket. The coach pulled on the team to win the match. The driver pulled on to the side of the road.

urduMeaning: کسی کام کو کامیاب بنانے کے لیے ہر ممکن کوشش کرنا، کسی مقصد کو حاصل کرنے کے لیے اپنی پوری طاقت وسائل اور صلاحیتیں استعمال کرنا
examples: The company pulled out all the stops to launch the new product successfully. She pulled out all the stops to prepare for her final exams. The wedding planners pulled out all the stops to make the event unforgettable. Our team pulled out all the stops and won the championship.
antonyms: Give up, Hold back, Do little, Neglect effort, Take it easy
synonyms: Do one's best, Go all out, Spare no effort, Give it everything, Leave no stone unturned, Try every possible way, Put in maximum effort
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ڪم کي ڪامياب بڻائڻ لاءِ هر ممڪن ڪوشش ڪرڻ، ڪنهن مقصد حاصل ڪرڻ لاءِ مڪمل طاقت وسيلا صلاحيتون ۽ ڪوششون استعمال ڪرڻ
englishMeaning: To use every possible effort, skill, or resource to achieve something. To do everything possible in order to succeed, impress someone, solve a problem, or achieve a goal. It refers to giving maximum effort without holding anything back.

examples: She saw the ambulance coming up behind her and pulled over. Just pull over here, and I'll get out and walk the rest of the way. The police asked him to pull over. She pulled over to answer the call.
urduMeaning: ایک طرف سے دوسری طرف کھینچنے، گاڑی سڑک کے کنارے روکنا
sindhiMeaning: گاڏي جو اچي لڳڻ، روڊ جي ڪناري گاڏي بيهارڻ

englishMeaning: To move to the side of the road in order to stop or let something pass. To make a driver or vehicle move to the side of the road. To move a vehicle to the side of the road and stop.
antonyms: Drive on, Continue

synonyms: Play a prank on, Have fun with
urduMeaning: مذاق کرنا، مذاق اڑانا، کسی کو مذاق میں چھیڑنا، کسی کے ساتھ مذاق کرنا، جھوٹ موٹ بات کہنا تاکہ وہ ہنسنے لگے یا لمحے بھر کے لیے دھوکے میں آجائے
antonyms: Be serious, Be sincere
sindhiMeaning: مذاق ڪرڻ، ڪنهن کي خوش طبع طريقي سان بيوقوف بڻائڻ، مزاحيه انداز ۾ ڪو ڪوڙو ڳالهه چئي کلائڻ
examples: Don’t take it seriously, I was just pulling your leg. She said she met a movie star, but she was pulling our legs. I thought he really bought a new car, but he was pulling my leg. Whenever he says something unbelievable, I know he’s pulling my leg again.
englishMeaning: To tease, joke, or make fun of someone in a friendly way, not to insult, but to playfully mislead them for amusement.

antonyms: Tavern, Marketplace, City hall, Public house, Secular building

sindhiMeaning: عبادت گاهه، خانقاهه، راھبن جو مندر، هيءَ جڳهه اڪثر ڪري چرچ ۽ رهائشگاهه ٻنهي تي مشتمل هوندي آهي
synonyms: Convent, Cloister, Priory
examples: The monks have lived in the old abbey for over five centuries. Tourists visited the ancient abbey to admire its beautiful architecture. The abbey was surrounded by peaceful gardens and tall trees. He donated a large amount of money to restore the damaged abbey.
englishMeaning: A large church or monastery where monks or nuns live, work, and worship. It usually includes a church, living quarters, and other buildings used by members of a religious community.

To be in strong disagreement or serious conflict with someone. It means two people or groups are arguing strongly and cannot agree on something. It shows a state of serious conflict where both sides hold opposite opinions and refuse to compromise. Often used in politics, workplaces, or personal relationships where disagreement becomes intense and ongoing. It suggests not just a small argument, but a deep and persistent conflict.
antonyms: To agree, To be in harmony, To get along, To cooperate, To reconcile
synonyms: To be in conflict, To disagree strongly, To be at odds, To clash, To quarrel
urduMeaning: کسی سے سخت اختلاف یا جھگڑے میں ہونا، دو افراد یا گروہ کسی معاملے پر سخت اختلاف میں ہوں اور کسی بھی بات پر متفق نہ ہوں بلکہ جھگڑے یا تنازع میں ہوں، عام طور پر سیاست دفتر یا ذاتی زندگی میں استعمال ہوتی ہے جہاں اختلاف شدید اور طویل ہو جائے
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن سان سخت اختلاف يا جهڳڙي ۾ هئڻ، ٻه ماڻهو يا گروهه ڪنهن معاملي تي سخت اختلاف ۾ هجن ۽ ڪنهن به ڳالهه تي متفق نه ٿين بلڪه هڪ ٻئي سان جهڳڙو يا تڪرار ۾ هجن، عام طور تي سياست ڪم جي جڳهن يا ذاتي زندگي ۾ استعمال ٿئي ٿي جتي اختلاف گهڻو وڌي وڃي ۽ ڊگهي وقت تائين جاري رهي
examples: The two departments are at loggerheads over the new budget plan. The teacher and student were at loggerheads about the assignment deadline. The neighbors have been at loggerheads for years over the property wall. The company owners are at loggerheads regarding future investments.

englishMeaning: To intentionally stop an activity, project, or operation, often because it is no longer useful, successful, or desired. The phrase comes from the literal act of unplugging an electrical device, causing it to stop working.
examples: The company decided to pull the plug on the failing project. They pulled the plug on the TV series after two seasons. Investors pulled the plug when the startup showed losses. He pulled the plug on his plans to move abroad.
urduMeaning: کسی کام منصوبے یا سرگرمی کو مکمل طور پر ختم کرنا یا روکنا، خاص طور پر جب وہ کام ناکام ہو یا ضرورت نہ ہو
antonyms: Continue, Maintain, Proceed, Start, Launch
synonyms: Stop, Terminate, End, Discontinue, Abandon
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ڪم منصوبي يا سرگرمي کي مڪمل طور تي بند ڪرڻ يا روڪڻ، خاص طور تي جڏهن اهو ڪم ناڪام هجي يا ضرورت نه رهي

urduMeaning: مشکل سے نکلنا، صحت یاب ہونا، کسی مشکل یا خطرناک صورت حال یا کیفیت سے عہدہ بر آ ہونا ، کسی عمل جراحی یا شدید بیماری سے صحت یاب ہونا، مشکل پر قابو پانا
sindhiMeaning: مشڪل مان نڪرڻ، صحتياب ٿيڻ، بيماري مان نڪرڻ، ڏکي صورتحال يا ذميواري مان پار پوڻ، ڪنهن کي مشڪل مان ڪڍڻ، لنگھي پار پوڻ
antonyms: Succumb, Fail, Pass out, Decease, Depart
englishMeaning: To recover from a difficult situation or illness. To get better after a serious illness, operation, etc. To succeed in doing something very difficult. To help somebody get better after a serious illness, operation, etc. To help somebody succeed in doing something very difficult.
synonyms: Rally, Recover, Endure, Prosper, Survive
examples: The doctors think she will pull through. It's going to be tough but we'll pull through it together. I relied on my instincts to pull me through. We pulled through most of the victims of the bomb attack. She pulled through the surgery. They pulled through the crisis.

sindhiMeaning: پنهنجي محنت يا ڪارڪردگي بهتر ڪرڻ، هي محاورو ان حالتن ۾ استعمال ٿئي ٿو جڏهن ڪنهن کي چيو وڃي ته هو پنهنجي ڪم ۾ وڌيڪ ڌيان ڏئي محنت وڌائي ۽ بهتر ڪارڪردگي ڏيکاري
urduMeaning: اپنی کارکردگی بہتر کرنا یا زیادہ محنت کرنا، جب کسی کو کہا جائے کہ وہ اپنی کارکردگی بہتر کرے زیادہ محنت کرے اور سنجیدگی سے کام کرے خاص طور پر جب وہ پہلے اچھا کام نہ کر رہا ہو
antonyms: Give up, Perform poorly, Slack off, Be lazy, Underperform
synonyms: Improve yourself, Shape up, Work harder, Buckle down, Step up your game
englishMeaning: To improve your effort, performance, or behavior. To start doing something in a better, more serious, and more focused way. It is often used when someone is not performing well and needs to improve quickly in studies, work, sports, or life.
examples: You are failing in math; you need to pull up your socks. If you want promotion, you must pull up your socks at work. The coach told the team to pull up their socks before the final match. She needs to pull up her socks if she wants better grades.

sindhiMeaning: ڦڦڙن ۽ ساهه جي نالن جي بيمارين جي سڃاڻپ، علاج ۽ روڪٿام جو علم ۽ طب جو شعبو جنهن ۾ تنفس جي خرابي ننڊ جي دوران ساھ جي مسئلا ۽ انتقالي نگہداشت شامل آهن
examples: She consulted a pulmonologist for her persistent cough. Pulmonology focuses on conditions like asthma and bronchitis. Advances in pulmonology have improved treatment for lung cancer. He specialized in pulmonology to help patients with chronic respiratory diseases.
urduMeaning: پھیپھڑوں اور سانس کی نالیوں کی بیماریوں کی تشخیص، علاج اور روک تھام کا شعبہ جس میں سانس کے مسائل نیند کے دوران سانس کی خرابی اور انتہائی نگہداشت کے انتظامات شامل ہیں
englishMeaning: The branch of medicine that deals with the lungs and respiratory system. Pulmonology is the medical specialty focused on diagnosing, treating, and preventing diseases and disorders of the respiratory system, including the lungs, bronchi, trachea, and associated structures. Pulmonologists handle conditions such as asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), pneumonia, tuberculosis, and lung cancer.
antonyms: Cardiology (heart), Nephrology (kidneys), Gastroenterology (digestive system)
synonyms: Respiratory medicine, Lung medicine, Chest medicine

sindhiMeaning: دل جي ڌڙڪڻ جيڪا شريانن ۾ محسوس ٿئي ٿي، برقي يا مشيني سگنل يا لهر، دالون جهڙوڪ مٽر مسور وغيره، ڪنهن به ڪم يا طاقت جو مختصر زور، ڌڙڪڻ يا لهر وانگر هلڻ، مسلسل يا وقفن سان سگنل موڪلڻ
synonyms: Heartbeat, Beat, Rhythm, Throb, Signal (technical sense), Legumes (for food sense)
englishMeaning: The regular beating of the heart felt in arteries. A regular vibration or signal, like electrical pulses. Edible seeds of leguminous plants such as lentils, beans, and peas. A brief burst of energy or activity. To beat, throb, or move in a regular rhythmic way. To send out waves, signals, or energy in bursts.
antonyms: Stillness, Silence, Pause, Flatline (medical context), Inactivity
urduMeaning: دل کی دھڑکن جو شریانوں میں محسوس ہوتی ہے، برقی یا مشینی سگنل یا ارتعاش، دالیں جیسے مسور چنا وغیرہ، کسی بھی کام یا توانائی کا مختصر زور، دھڑکنا یا مسلسل وقفوں سے حرکت کرنا، وقفے وقفے سے سگنل یا لہریں بھیجنا
examples: The doctor checked my pulse to measure my heartbeat. The machine sends electrical pulses to the device. Lentils are a rich source of protein and belong to pulses. The city had a sudden pulse of activity during the festival. Her heart pulsed faster during the exam. Light pulsed through the dark tunnel.

urduMeaning: زندگی کی دھڑکن، زندگی کی روانی، حیات کی اصل طاقت، زندہ رہنے کی توانائی
synonyms: Vitality, Life force, Energy, Spirit, Essence of life, Heartbeat, Dynamism
antonyms: Death, Lifelessness, Weakness, Stillness, Inactivity, Emptiness
sindhiMeaning: زندگيءَ جي ڌڙڪن، زندگيءَ جي رواني، حياتي طاقت، جيئڻ جي اصل توانائي
examples: Music is the pulse of life for many people around the world. The busy market showed the true pulse of life in the city. Nature gives us the pulse of life through fresh air and green trees. Hope and love are often called the pulse of life during difficult times.
englishMeaning: The main energy, activity, or living force that keeps a person, place, or thing alive and active. It can also mean the rhythm, excitement, and movement of life.

antonyms: Stillness, Silence, Calm, Inactivity, Rest
synonyms: Lentils, Beans, Heartbeat, Throb, Beat, Vibration
englishMeaning: Edible seeds of plants such as lentils, beans and peas. Regular beating of the heart. Short burst or wave of energy, light, or sound. To beat or throb rhythmically. Electrical signal burst. Vibration or rhythmic movement. Sudden increase of activity.
urduMeaning: دالیں/ خشک پھلیاں، دل کی دھڑکن، توانائی یا روشنی کی لہر، دھڑکنا یا زور سے چلنا
sindhiMeaning: دالون سڪل اناج جهڙوڪ مسور چڻا، دل جي ڌڙڪن، توانائي يا روشني جي لهر، ڌڙڪڻ يا زور سان هلڻ
examples: Pulses are an important source of protein. The doctor checked his pulses carefully. Bright pulses of light came from the machine. Music pulses through the crowded hall.

antonyms: Protect, Defend, Shield, Comfort, Spare
synonyms: Beat, Strike, Batter, Pound, Thrash
englishMeaning: To hit someone or something repeatedly with force. To strike again and again, usually with fists or heavy blows. It can describe physical attacks, harsh weather effects, or strong criticism that overwhelms someone.
examples: The boxer pummeled his opponent until the referee stopped the match. Heavy rain pummeled the coastal villages for hours. The politician was pummeled by criticism from the media. Waves pummeled the boat during the storm.
urduMeaning: زور زور سے بار بار مارنا، کسی کو مکے یا سخت ضربیں مسلسل لگانا ، یہ لفظ شدید تنقید یا قدرتی آفات کے اثرات کے لیے بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے
sindhiMeaning: زور سان بار بار هڻڻ، ڪنهن ماڻهو يا شيءِ کي مسلسل ۽ زور سان هڻڻ جنهن ۾ رحم يا وقفو نه هجي، اهو لفظ تنقيد يا سخت حالتن لاءِ به استعمال ٿئي ٿو

englishMeaning: To continue pumping or working hard, especially with energy or persistence.
examples: The firefighters pumped away to clear the water. He kept pumping away at the handle. The team pumped away until the job was done. The old machine was still pumping away after hours.
antonyms: Stop, Rest
urduMeaning: کسی چیز کو مسلسل پمپ کرنا یا مسلسل کوشش کرنا
synonyms: Persist, Operate, Work hard
sindhiMeaning: لڳاتار ڪم ڪرڻ، محنت سان پمپ هلائڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ کي مسلسل پمپ ڪرڻ يا زور سان ڪوشش ڪرڻ

urduMeaning: ہر وقت کسی کے حکم پر تیار رہنا، تابع ہونا، خدمت کے لیے ہمیشہ تیار رہنا، کسی کے کہنے پر فوراً حاضر ہو جانا
synonyms: At one’s disposal, Subservient, Obedient, Ready to serve
antonyms: Independent, Unavailable, Free-willed
examples: The servants were always at the king’s beck and call. He keeps his employees at his beck and call. The manager expects his staff to be at his beck and call even after office hours. She doesn’t want to be at anyone’s beck and call; she values her independence.
englishMeaning: Always available to follow requests. Always ready to obey someone’s orders or requests immediately.
sindhiMeaning: هميشه ڪنهن جي حڪم تي تيار رهڻ، تابع ٿيڻ، حڪم مڃڻ لاءِ هميشه تيار رهڻ، خدمت لاءِ هميشه موجود، حڪم هيٺ رهڻ

urduMeaning: واپس پمپ کرنا، مائع یا گیس کو اس کے ماخذ میں واپس پمپ کرنا
antonyms: Draw out, Extract
sindhiMeaning: واپس پمپ ڪرڻ، مائع يا گئس کي واپس ان جي ماخذ ۾ دٻائڻ
synonyms: Return, Revert, Send back
examples: The system pumps back the excess water. The oil was pumped back to the refinery. They had to pump back the coolant. The machine pumps back unused fuel into the tank.
englishMeaning: To send or push a liquid or substance back to its original source.

synonyms: Invest, Pour, Inject
englishMeaning: To put a large amount of energy, effort, or money into something, also to physically inject liquid or gas into something.
antonyms: Withdraw, Deplete
examples: The company pumped millions into new research. He pumped all his savings into the project. They pumped fuel into the generator. She pumped energy into the campaign.
sindhiMeaning: ڪوشش، توانائي يا پئسا گهڻو مقدار ۾ ڪنهن ڪم ۾ لڳائڻ
urduMeaning: کسی کام میں بہت زیادہ محنت، توانائی یا پیسہ ڈالنا

synonyms: Transfer, Shift, Move
antonyms: Retain, Keep
examples: The fuel was pumped over to the storage tank. They pumped over the water to another section. The system automatically pumps oil over when full. The engineer pumped over the solution for testing.
englishMeaning: To transfer or move liquid, gas, or other substances from one place to another using a pump
sindhiMeaning: پمپ ذريعي هڪ جڳهه کان ٻي جڳهه تي منتقل ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: پمپ کے ذریعے منتقل کرنا
پائپ کے ذریعے گزارنا، جلدی سے منظور کرانا، کسی چیز کو پمپ کے ذریعے یا زور سے گزرنا
examples: The heart pumps blood through the body. The new law was pumped through Parliament. Water is pumped through the irrigation system. The air conditioner pumps cool air through the vents.
antonyms: Block, Stop
englishMeaning: To force liquid, gas, or another substance to move through a pipe, system, or network using a pump or mechanical pressure. It can also be used metaphorically to describe sending something through a system quickly.
synonyms: Circulate, Channel, Push through
sindhiMeaning: وهڪري ۾ هلائڻ، تڪڙو عمل ڪرائڻ، ڪنھن شيءَ کي پائيپ يا نظام ذريعي زور سان گذارڻ

englishMeaning: To fill something (like a tire or ball) with air or gas. To increase something, make it stronger, more intense, or more exciting. It can also mean to make someone feel more enthusiastic or energetic.
urduMeaning: ہوا بھرنا، جوش دلانا، کسی چیز کو بڑھانا، زور دینا یا جوش و ولولہ پیدا کرنا
examples: He pumped up the football before the game. The coach pumped up the team before the final. Pump up the tires or we can’t drive. The music really pumped up the crowd.
antonyms: Deflate, Discourage
synonyms: Inflate, Excite, Energize
sindhiMeaning: هوا ڀرڻ، توانائي، جوش يا اعتماد وڌائڻ، ڪجهه وڌائڻ، زور ڏيڻ

examples: Pump up the pressure to 100 PSI. The speaker pumped up to full volume. She pumped up to maximum effort before the race. They pumped up to get the crowd’s energy high.
englishMeaning: To raise or increase something (like pressure, volume, or enthusiasm) to a higher level.
sindhiMeaning: وڌائڻ، تيز ڪرڻ، وڌ ۾ وڌ جذبات يا توانائي ڏيڻ
antonyms: Lower, Reduce
urduMeaning: کسی چیز کی مقدار یا توانائی بڑھانا، کسی کو جوش دلانا
synonyms: Boost, Heighten, Increase

examples: The punk spray-painted the walls of the building. He acted like a punk when confronted. Punk rock music became popular in the 1970s. Don’t be fooled by that punk; he can be dangerous.
englishMeaning: Small-time troublemaker; worthless person; rebellious youth. A young person who behaves in a rebellious or defiant way, often associated with a particular subculture of music, fashion, and attitude. A person considered worthless or insignificant. Slang for a young criminal or troublemaker.
sindhiMeaning: ننڍڙو تڪرار ڪندڙ / گهٽ اهميت وارو شخص، نوجوان جيڪو انقلابي يا بغاوت ڪندڙ رويي وارو هجي
urduMeaning: چھوٹا شرارتی / کم قدر شخص، نوجوان جو بغاوت یا نافرمانی کے رویے والا ہو
antonyms: Gentleman, Nobleman, Respected Person, Responsible Citizen
synonyms: Troublemaker, Delinquent, Hoodlum, Rebel, Misfit

antonyms: Binding
sindhiMeaning: جلاب، دست ڏيندڙ، جُلاب آڻيندڙ
synonyms: Evacuant, Laxative, Enema
urduMeaning: جلاب، مسہل، دست آور
englishMeaning: A substance, medicine that causes your bowels to empty, Cathartic
examples: I took some purgative medicine. In some febrile and plethoric cases it is difficult to obtain the full action of a purgative.

sindhiMeaning: صاف ڪرڻ، ختم ڪرڻ، صفائي ڪرڻ، غير ضروري يا نقصانڪار شيون هٽائڻ، نجاست صاف ڪرڻ، غير مناسب ميمبر هٽائڻ، زهر يا فضلات ڪڍڻ، جذبات کي ڪڍڻ، صفائي جو عمل، غير ضروري شيون هٽائڻ جو عمل
examples: The company decided to purge outdated records from its database. She felt relieved after purging her anger on paper. The dictator purged the government of opposition members. Drinking plenty of water helps the body purge toxins naturally. The country went through a political purge. He underwent a detox purge to cleanse his system.
antonyms: Retain, Keep, Preserve, Accumulate, Retention
urduMeaning: صاف کرنا، ختم کرنا، صفائی کرنا، غیر ضروری یا نقصان دہ چیزیں ہٹانا، نجاست صاف کرنا، غیر مناسب اراکین کو نکالنا، زہریلے مواد یا فضلات خارج کرنا، جذبات کو خارج کرنا، صفائی کا عمل، غیر ضروری یا نقصان دہ چیزوں کو ہٹانے کا عمل
englishMeaning: To remove something unwanted, harmful, or impure. To cleanse or purify. To remove political opponents or undesirable members. To expel bodily substances. To release emotions or stress. To cleanse or rid someone or something of unwanted elements. An act of removal or cleansing.
synonyms: Cleanse, Eliminate, Expel, Remove, Clear, Cleansing

sindhiMeaning: ذهن جي حد تائين پهچڻ، پريشان يا مايوس ٿيڻ، جتي ماڻهو سمجهڻ نه ڄاڻي ته ڇا ڪرڻو آهي
examples: After trying everything to fix the computer, she was at her wits’ end. He was at his wits’ end trying to quiet the crying baby. They were at their wits’ end when the negotiations failed. I am at my wits’ end with this complicated paperwork.
englishMeaning: Extremely worried, confused, or frustrated; not knowing what to do. When someone is at a point where they have exhausted all their ideas, patience, or resources and do not know what action to take next. It describes a state of desperation or mental strain.
antonyms: Calm, Confident, Relaxed, Composed, In control
synonyms: Desperate, Frustrated, Perplexed, Troubled, At one’s limit
urduMeaning: عقل یا صبر کے آخر میں پہنچنا، پریشان یا مایوس ہونا، جس میں سمجھ نہ آ رہی ہو کہ کیا کرنا چاہیے
تعاقب، حاصل کرنے کی کوشش، مقصد کے پیچھے لگنا، کوشش کے ساتھ تلاش
antonyms: Neglect, Abandonment, Avoidance, Idleness
englishMeaning: The act of pursuing something. Effort to achieve or obtain something. The process of following a goal, person, or activity. Attempt to accomplish a purpose.
synonyms: Pursuit, Chase, Striving, Quest, Search
examples: His pursual of knowledge made him successful. She continued her pursual of a better job. The pursual of happiness is important in life. Their pursual of excellence inspired others.
sindhiMeaning: پٺيان لڳڻ، ڪوشش سان حاصل ڪرڻ، مقصد جي تلاش، ڪنهن شيءِ جي حاصلات لاءِ جدوجهد

examples: The committee acted in pursuance of the new policy. He worked in pursuance of his dream to become a doctor. The police took action in pursuance of the court order. She continued her studies in pursuance of higher education.
englishMeaning: The act of following or carrying out something. Continuation of an action. In accordance with something. Following a rule or instruction. Doing something in accordance with a plan, rule, order, or intention. It means continuing or carrying out an action to achieve a goal.
sindhiMeaning: تعميل يا پيروي ڪرڻ، حڪم جي تعميل، منصوبي جي پيروي، عمل جاري رکڻ، قانون موجب ڪم ڪرڻ، ڪنهن حڪم منصوبي يا ارادي مطابق عمل ڪرڻ يا ڪنهن ڪم کي جاري رکڻ
antonyms: Neglect, Abandonment, Violation, Disobedience, Ignoring
synonyms: Compliance, Execution, Pursuit, Following, Enforcement, Continuation
urduMeaning: تعمیل یا پیروی کرنا، حکم کی تعمیل، منصوبے کی پیروی، عمل جاری رکھنا، قانون کے مطابق کام کرنا، کسی حکم منصوبے یا ارادے کے مطابق عمل کرنا یا کسی مقصد کے لیے کام جاری رکھنا

englishMeaning: To follow, try to achieve, continue doing something. To chase or go after. To work toward something desired. To carry on an activity. To explore or examine further.
synonyms: Follow, Chase, Seek, Strive, Continue, Aim for
antonyms: Abandon, Stop, Ignore, Quit, Give up
sindhiMeaning: پٺيان لڳڻ، حاصل ڪرڻ جي ڪوشش ڪرڻ، جاري رکڻ، ڪنهن جي پٺيان وڃڻ يا تعاقب ڪرڻ، مقصد حاصل ڪرڻ لاءِ ڪوشش ڪرڻ، ڪنهن ڪم کي جاري رکڻ، تحقيق ڪرڻ يا وڌيڪ ڄاڻ حاصل ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: پیچھا کرنا، حاصل کرنے کی کوشش کرنا، جاری رکھنا، کسی کا پیچھا کرنا یا تعاقب کرنا، کسی مقصد کو حاصل کرنے کی کوشش کرنا، کسی کام کو جاری رکھنا، تحقیق کرنا یا مزید جانچ کرنا
examples: She decided to pursue a career in medicine. The police pursued the thief through the streets. He wants to pursue higher education abroad. They continue to pursue their dreams despite difficulties.
The police were in hot pursuit of the thief. She dedicated her life to the pursuit of knowledge. Happiness is not a destination, but a pursuit. In his free time, painting became his favorite pursuit.
englishMeaning: The act of chasing or following something/someone. An effort to achieve or attain something (goal, ambition). An activity or interest that one spends time doing.
synonyms: Chase, Quest, Search, Striving, Endeavor
sindhiMeaning: پٺيان، پيڇو، ڳولا، ڪوشش، ڪاميابيءَ جي جستجو، مقصد حاصل ڪرڻ جي جدوجهد، مشغلو، شوق
urduMeaning: پیچھا ، جستجو، تلاش، مقصد یا ہدف کے حصول کی کوشش، مشغلہ یا دلچسپی، کامیابی کی جستجو
antonyms: Retreat, Surrender, Idleness, Neglect

urduMeaning: دھکے دینا یا برا سلوک کرنا، کسی کو بار بار دھکے دینا یا تنگ کرنا، چیزوں کو اِدھر اُدھر زور سے ہلانا، بے عزتی یا تنگ کرنا
synonyms: Bully, Harass
antonyms: Respect, Protect
englishMeaning: To treat someone roughly or without respect. To bully or harass. To move things around roughly or without care.
examples: He was pushed about by the bullies at school. The older boys used to push the younger ones about in the playground. Example:
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن سان خراب سلوڪ ڪرڻ، ڌڪا ڏيڻ، تنگ ڪرڻ، ڪنهن کي زور سان ڌڪا ڏئي ستائڻ، شيون زور سان ھيڏاھن اوڌاھن ڪرڻ

antonyms: Quit, Retreat
sindhiMeaning: مشڪل باوجود اڳتي وڌڻ، ثابت قدم رهڻ، حوصل سان اڳتي وڌڻ
urduMeaning: مشکلات کے باوجود آگے بڑھنا، ڈٹے رہنا، حوصلے سے جاری رکھنا
synonyms: Persevere, Advance
englishMeaning: To continue with determination despite difficulties. To make progress with an activity, plan, or work. To move forward with effort and persistence.
examples: They pushed ahead with the project despite obstacles. The government decided to push ahead with the project. Despite challenges, she kept pushing ahead to fulfill her dream.
He was tired of being pushed around by his boss. The manager always pushes his junior staff around. She was tired of being pushed around by her elder brother.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کي قابو ڪرڻ يا ستائڻ، زبردستي حڪم هلائڻ، ماڻهن کي دٻاءُ ۾ رکي تنگ ڪرڻ يا حڪم هلائڻ، ڏاڍائي سان هدايتون ڏيڻ يا بي عزتي ڪرڻ
englishMeaning: To treat someone badly by dominating, bossing, or bullying them. To order someone about in a rough or unfair way.
synonyms: Dominate, Oppress
antonyms: Support, Respect
urduMeaning: کسی پر ظلم یا جبر کرنا، دوسروں کو دباؤ میں رکھنا ، دھونس جماتے ہوئے قابو پانا، کسی کو دھمکا کر یا زبردستی قابو میں رکھنا، غلط طریقے سے حکم چلانا یا تنگ کرنا

synonyms: Ignore, Reject
urduMeaning: نظر انداز کرنا، اہمیت نہ دینا، کسی چیز یا شخص کو ایک طرف دھکیل دینا
antonyms: Accept, Consider
examples: She pushed aside her doubts and went ahead. He pushed aside the chair to make space. She pushed aside her fears and spoke confidently.
sindhiMeaning: نظرانداز ڪرڻ، اهميت نه ڏيڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ يا ماڻهوءَ کي پاسيرو ڪرڻ لاءِ ڌڪڻ
englishMeaning: To move something or someone to the side by pushing. To ignore, reject, or dismiss something/someone as unimportant.

examples: They are pushing for better wages. The students are pushing for better facilities in their college. She is pushing for a promotion at work. The organization is pushing for stronger climate change policies.
englishMeaning: To strongly try to achieve something. To demand, request, or insist on something with determination.
synonyms: Advocate, Demand
sindhiMeaning: زور سان مطالبو ڪرڻ، زور ڀرڻ، زور ڏيڻ، ضد ڪرڻ، سخت ڪوشش ڪرڻ، اصرار ڪرڻ
antonyms: Oppose, Resist
urduMeaning: زور دے کر مطالبہ کرنا، زور دینا ، دباؤ ڈالنا، کوشش کرنا ، اصرار کرنا

englishMeaning: To be extremely happy, joyful, or delighted. (as in a perfect or heavenly state of joy).
examples: She was at seventh heaven when she received her job offer. After the birth of his daughter, he felt at seventh heaven. When the team won the final match, everyone was at seventh heaven. He was at seventh heaven after hearing the good news about his promotion.

فالتو ، غیر ضروری ، بیکار ، اعادہ کثیر ، زیادتی ، کثرت ، کام نہ ہونے کی وجہ سے نوکری کا خاتمہ ، فضول ہونا ، زائد ہونا
englishMeaning: A situation where something is repeated, excessive, or not required. A worker losing a job because the position is no longer needed. In technology or systems, it may also mean extra components added to increase reliability.
antonyms: Necessity, Need, Essentiality, Importance, Requirement
sindhiMeaning: اهڙي حالت جتي ڪا شيءِ ورجائي وڃي ضرورت کان وڌيڪ هجي يا ڪم لاءِ گهربل نه هجي، نوڪري جي حوالي سان جڏهن اداري کي ڪنهن عهدي جي ضرورت نه رهي ته ملازم کي فارغ ڪيو وڃي
synonyms: Excess, Surplus, Superfluity, Repetition, Duplication
examples: The editor removed several sentences because they created redundancy in the paragraph. Many workers faced redundancy when the company automated its production line. The aircraft system includes redundancy to ensure safety if one component fails. Good writing avoids redundancy and keeps ideas clear and concise.

englishMeaning: Something that is unnecessary, extra, or not needed. Describes a word, idea, worker, or thing that is no longer useful, needed, or required because there is too much of it or it repeats what is already present.
urduMeaning: غیر ضروری، زائد، فالتو، ضرورت سے زیادہ، ایسی چیز یا شخص جو ضرورت سے زیادہ ہو یا جس کی ضرورت باقی نہ رہی ہو
sindhiMeaning: فالتو، غير ضروري، وڌيڪ، بيڪار ٿي ويل، اهڙي شيءِ يا ماڻهو جيڪو هاڻي ضرورت کان وڌيڪ هجي يا جنهن جي ضرورت باقي نه رهي هجي
examples: The report contained several redundant sentences that repeated the same idea. Many workers became redundant after the company installed automated machines. Adding more details here would be redundant because the point is already clear. The editor removed redundant words to make the paragraph concise.
synonyms: Unnecessary, Superfluous, Excessive, Surplus, Repetitive
antonyms: Necessary, Essential, Required, Useful, Important

examples: Data are redundantly stored in multiple different locations. The report was written redundantly, repeating the same facts in several paragraphs. He explained the rule redundantly, even though everyone already understood it. Some speakers talk redundantly when they are nervous. The instructions were redundantly detailed and made the process harder to follow.
synonyms: Repetitively, Needlessly, Excessively, Superfluously, Unnecessarily
sindhiMeaning: غير ضروري طور يا ورجاءَ سان، اهڙي طريقي سان ڳالهائڻ يا لکڻ جنهن ۾ ساڳي ڳالهه ٻيهر ٻيهر چئي وڃي جيتوڻيڪ اها اڳ ۾ ئي واضح هجي، ڪڏهن ڪڏهن ضرورت کان وڌيڪ يا اضافي انداز سان ڪم ڪرڻ لاءِ به استعمال ٿيندو آهي
englishMeaning: In a repetitive or unnecessary way. It describes something said or written again even though the information is already clear. It can also refer to something done with extra duplication or excess beyond what is needed.
urduMeaning: غیر ضروری طور پر یا تکرار کے ساتھ، ایسی حالت جس میں کوئی بات بلا ضرورت بار بار دہرائی جائے جبکہ مطلب پہلے ہی واضح ہو، یہ لفظ اس وقت بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے جب کسی چیز میں ضرورت سے زیادہ اضافی پن موجود ہو
antonyms: Concisely, Briefly, Efficiently, Succinctly
Steady, Balance, Stabilize, Flat, Board, Slab
englishMeaning: To lose balance or feel dizzy. To stagger, sway, or spin, often due to shock, surprise, injury, or intoxication. A round object used to wind rope, film, thread, or fishing line. Can also refer to a lively dance or sequence of events.
sindhiMeaning: ڌچڪو ڏيڻ، ڊگهو ٿيڻ، ڦري وڃڻ، حيران ٿيڻ، ليڪ يا ڌاڳي کي ڦرائڻ، ڦرندڙ رول، ڪپڙي يا مڇيءَ جي ليڪ لاءِ اسپول، روايتي ناچ جو هڪ قسم، ڌاڳي يا فلم لاءِ رول، وڊيو يا آڊيو ڪلپس جو سلسلو، احساسن يا واقعن جو تيز سلسلو
synonyms: Stagger, Sway, Spin, Stumble, Spool, Coil, Cylinder
examples: He reeled after hearing the shocking news. She reeled from the punch. He bought a new fishing reel. The movie reel was damaged.
urduMeaning: دھکیلنا یا ہلانا، کنڈلی میں لپیٹنا، صدمہ پہنچانا، گھومنا، پھیرنا، لڑکھڑانا، چکرانا، حیران ہونا، ریل، کوئل، کنڈلی، روایتی رقص کا ایک انداز، ویڈیو یا آڈیو کلپس کی جھلکیاں
اصلاح کرنا یا خرابی کو درست کرنا، بہتری لانا، قانونی یا سماجی اصلاح، عادتوں کی درستگی، اخلاقی بہتری، کسی نظام قانون ادارے یا عادت میں بہتری لانا، خرابیوں کو دور کرنا اور اسے بہتر بنانا
antonyms: Worsen, Damage, Corrupt, Deteriorate, Ruin
englishMeaning: To improve something by removing faults or correcting mistakes. Making changes to improve a system, law, organization, or behavior by correcting what is wrong or unfair. It can refer to social, political, educational, or personal improvement.
sindhiMeaning: سڌارو ڪرڻ يا بگاڙيل شيءِ کي درست ڪرڻ، بهتري آڻڻ، قانوني يا سماجي سڌارا، عادتن جي درستگي، اخلاقي سڌارو، ڪنهن نظام قانون اداري يا عادتن ۾ سڌارو آڻڻ، غلطين کي درست ڪرڻ ۽ بهتر بڻائڻ
synonyms: Improve, Correct, Amend, Fix, Revise, Upgrade
examples: The government plans to reform the education system. He worked hard to reform his bad habits. Social reform is necessary for a better society. The new law aims to reform the justice system.

sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کي خاص نموني لباس پارائڻ، لباس پارائڻ، ڪپڙا پارائڻ، سينگارڻ، تيار ڪرڻ، لباس، ڪپڙا، پوشاڪ، وڳا، جوڙو، روايتي لباس، رسمي لباس
antonyms: Undress, Strip, Uncover, Disrobe
englishMeaning: To dress or clothe someone in a particular way. To dress, clothe, or decorate someone in particular clothes, especially formal, elegant, traditional, or special clothing. Clothing, dress, or what a person is wearing, especially when speaking in a formal, elegant, traditional, or noticeable way.
urduMeaning: کسی کو خاص انداز میں لباس پہنانا، لباس پہنانا، کپڑے پہنانا، آراستہ کرنا، تیار کرنا، لباس، کپڑے، پوشاک، ملبوسات، جوڑا، پہناؤا، رسمی لباس، روایتی لباس
synonyms: Dress, Clothe, Outfit, Garb, Array
examples: She arrived at the wedding in elegant traditional attire. Office attire should be neat and professional. The dancers wore colorful attire during the cultural show. The bride was attired in a beautiful red gown. The actor was attired as a king for the play. The children were attired in warm clothes for winter. She was richly attired for the royal event.

synonyms: Avoid, Abstain, Withhold, Resist, Hold back, Chorus, Repetition, Burden, Recurring line
englishMeaning: To stop yourself from doing something. To consciously avoid or hold oneself back from doing something, especially something tempting or habitual. To pause deliberately. A line or group of lines that is repeated regularly in a poem or song.
examples: She tried to refrain from laughing during the serious meeting. Please refrain from using your phone in the classroom. He could not refrain from expressing his opinion. The song’s refrain was catchy and easy to remember.
sindhiMeaning: پاسو ڪرڻ، پاڻ کي روڪڻ يا باز رهڻ، گيت يا شاعري ۾ ورجائجندڙ سٽ، ڪنهن ڪم کان ڄاڻي واڻي پاڻ کي روڪڻ يا پرهيز ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: پرہیز کرنا، اجتناب کرنا، خود کو روکنا، گانے یا نظم میں بار بار آنے والا مصرع، کسی کام سے جان بوجھ کر خود کو روکنا یا باز رہنا
antonyms: Indulge, Continue, Engage, Persist, Variation, Change

sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ کي صاف مرمت يا بھتر بڻائڻ لاءِ نئين سر ٺاھڻ، جيئن پهرين جي حالت ۾ آڻڻ يا وڌيڪ دلڪش ٿي وڃي، پراڻي شيءِ کي نئين جهڙو ڪرڻ، استعمال ٿيل شين کي مرمت ڪري ٻيهر وڪرو لاءِ تيار ڪيو
antonyms: Damage, Neglect, Ruin, Destroy, Deteriorate
urduMeaning: کسی چیز کو صاف ستھرا مرمت یا بہتر بنا کر اسے دوبارہ نیا یا خوبصورت بنانا، عام طور پر یہ ظاہری اور عملی بہتری دونوں کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے، استعمال شدہ سامان کو درست کر کے دوبارہ فروخت کے قابل بنانا
synonyms: Renovate, Restore, Redecorate, Overhaul, Repair, Revamp
examples: They decided to refurbish the old library before reopening it. The hotel was refurbished to attract more tourists. She refurbished her living room with new furniture and curtains. The company refurbished used laptops and sold them at a lower price.
englishMeaning: To restore an object, building, or space by cleaning, repairing, or improving it so that it regains its original condition or becomes more attractive. It often involves both cosmetic and functional improvements.

antonyms: Confirm, Accept, Support, Validate
englishMeaning: To prove that something is false. To deny a statement, claim, or argument by giving clear evidence, logic, or facts that show it is incorrect or untrue.
urduMeaning: غلط ثابت کرنا، کسی دعوے یا الزام کو مضبوط دلائل یا شواہد سے غلط ثابت کرنا
sindhiMeaning: غلط ثابت ڪرڻ، ڪنهن دعويٰ يا الزام کي ثبوت يا دليل سان غلط ثابت ڪرڻ
examples: The lawyer refuted the accusation with strong evidence. Scientists refuted the theory after new research. He refuted the rumor during the press conference. The data clearly refuted their claims.
synonyms: Disprove, Deny, Contradict, Debunk

sindhiMeaning: حڪومت يا حڪمراني جو نظام، اقتدار ۾ ويٺل حڪمرانن جو طريقو، ڪنهن ڪم کي هلائڻ لاءِ مقرر ڪيل منظم طريقو، ڪنٽرول ڪيل نظام يا حالتون، حڪومتي دور، راڄ، حڪمراني
synonyms: Government, Administration, Rule, Authority, System, Order
examples: The country experienced economic changes under the new regime. She follows a strict fitness regime to stay healthy. The new tax regime was introduced to improve revenue collection. Many people protested against the military regime.
urduMeaning: حکومت یا حکمرانی کا نظام، اقتدار میں موجود حکمرانوں کا طریقہ کار، کسی کام کو منظم انداز میں چلانے کا طریقہ، حکمران حکومت یا اقتدار کا نظام، انتظامی طریقہ کار، کنٹرول شدہ نظام یا حالات
antonyms: Disorder, Anarchy, Chaos, Lawlessness
englishMeaning: A system of government, a ruling authority, or an organized method used to manage something such as health, diet, or policies. It may describe political power or a structured plan followed over time.

antonyms: Enjoy, Relish, Revel, Impenitence, Welcome, Hail, Approve
sindhiMeaning: افسوس، افسوس ڪرڻ، پچتائڻ، ڏڪ جو اظھار ڪرڻ، ڏک ڪرڻ، ارمان ڪرڻ
englishMeaning: To be very sorry for. To mourn the loss or death of. Sorrow aroused by circumstances beyond one's control or power to repair. To feel sorry about something you have done or about something that you have not been able to do. Used to say in a polite or formal way that you are sorry or sad about a situation.
examples: I you don’t do it now you'll only regret. It is with great regret that I accept you resignation. The president said that his country deeply regretted the incident. The United States regrets the loss of innocent civilian lives.
urduMeaning: افسوس، افسوس کرنا، پچھتانا، ملول کرنا، اداس ہونا، ملال، ندامت، شرمندگی، شرمساری
synonyms: Apologize, Deplore, Repent, Penitence, Distress, Grief

examples: The doctor helped rehabilitate the injured athlete after surgery. The government built programs to rehabilitate drug addicts. The old building was rehabilitated into a modern library. After serving his sentence, he was rehabilitated into society.
synonyms: Restore, Recover, Reconstruct, Reintegrate, Rebuild, Mend, Reform
antonyms: Damage, Destroy, Harm, Ruin, Corrupt, Break, Worsen
sindhiMeaning: ٻيهر آباد ڪرڻ، ٻيهر سٺي حالت ۾ آڻڻ، ڪنهن شخص جڳهه يا نظام کي نقصان بيماري يا خرابي کان پوءِ ٻيهر صحيح ۽ بهتر حالت ۾ آڻڻ
englishMeaning: To restore someone or something to a normal or better condition after damage, illness, addiction, or trouble. To help a person, place, or system recover after physical injury, illness, addiction, crime punishment, or damage, so they can function normally again.
urduMeaning: بحال کرنا، سابقہ حالت پر لانا، پھر آباد کرنا، کسی شخص عمارت یا نظام کو نقصان بیماری نشے یا سزا کے بعد دوبارہ بہتر اور نارمل حالت میں لانا

examples: The patient is undergoing rehabilitation after surgery. The government started a rehabilitation program for flood victims. Physical rehabilitation helped him walk again. The athlete needed months of rehabilitation after the injury.
sindhiMeaning: بحالي، ٻيهر سٺي حالت ۾ آڻڻ، بيماري يا زخمي ٿيڻ کان پوءِ بحالي، ساک بحال ڪرڻ، تباهه ٿيل هنڌن جي ٻيهر تعمير، سماجي ٻيهر شامل ٿيڻ، ڪنهن ماڻهو يا شيءِ کي علاج تربيت يا مدد ذريعي ٻيهر سٺي حالت ۾ آڻڻ، اهو ماڻهن عمارتن يا ماحول لاءِ استعمال ٿيندو آهي
englishMeaning: The process of restoring someone or something to good condition. Medical recovery after illness or injury. Restoring reputation. Rebuilding damaged areas. Social reintegration of offenders. Restoring health, ability, reputation, or normal life through training, therapy, or support. It can apply to people, buildings, systems, or environments.
synonyms: Restoration, Recovery, Rebuilding, Renewal, Reinstatement
antonyms: Deterioration, Damage, Decline, Worsening, Destruction
urduMeaning: بحالی، دوبارہ بہتر حالت میں لانا، بیماری یا چوٹ کے بعد بحالی، ساک کی بحالی، تباہ شدہ علاقوں کی تعمیر نو، معاشرے میں دوبارہ شامل کرنا، کسی شخص یا چیز کو علاج تربیت یا مدد کے ذریعے دوبارہ بہتر حالت میں لانا ہے، یہ افراد عمارتوں یا ماحول کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے

englishMeaning: To practice or make people practice a play, piece of music, etc in preparation for a public performance. To prepare in your mind or practice privately what you are going to do or say to somebody. To repeat ideas or opinions that have often been expressed before. To do over and over so as to become skilled.
antonyms: Generalize, Forget, Halt
sindhiMeaning: وري وري چوڻ، دور ڪرڻ، ذڪر ڪرڻ، زبان تي آڻڻ، ريهرسل ڪرڻ، ورجائڻ، زبان تي آڻڻ، ماڻهن جي سامهون پڙهڻ، مشق ڪرڻ، مشقي داڪاري ڪرڻ، ماڻهن کي ڏيکارڻ کان اڳ (ڊرامي وغيره جي) مشق ڪرڻ
examples: We were given only two weeks to rehearse. We're rehearsing for the show. She walked along rehearsing her excuse for being late. He had his speech well rehearsed.
urduMeaning: دہرانا، دوبارہ سنانا، دوبارہ کہنا، بار بار مشق کرنا، بیان کرنا ، سُنانا
synonyms: Exercise, Run over, Reiterate,

antonyms: Charge, Withhold, Collect, Demand payment, Confiscate
englishMeaning: To pay back money that someone has spent or lost. To repay someone the money they have spent on your behalf or to compensate them for a loss or expense. It is commonly used in travel, office expenses, insurance claims, and business payments.
urduMeaning: خرچ کیا گیا پیسہ واپس دینا یا ادا کرنا، کسی شخص کو وہ رقم واپس دینا جو اس نے کسی کام سفر یا خرچ کے لیے اپنی جیب سے ادا کی ہو، یہ لفظ عام طور پر دفتر کاروبار اور انشورنس میں استعمال ہوتا ہے
examples: The company will reimburse your travel expenses. She was reimbursed for the damaged goods. The hospital reimbursed him for the extra medical costs. You can be reimbursed after submitting the receipts.
sindhiMeaning: خرچ ڪيل پئسو واپس ڏيڻ يا ادا ڪرڻ، ڪنهن ماڻهو کي اهو پئسو واپس ڏيڻ جيڪو هن ڪنهن ڪم سفر يا خرچ لاءِ پنهنجي کيسي مان ڏنو هجي، هي لفظ اڪثر نوڪري آفيس يا بيمه جي ادائگي ۾ استعمال ٿيندو آهي
synonyms: Repay, Refund, Compensate, Pay back, Return

antonyms: Withdraw, Cancel, Ignore, Neglect, Suppress
urduMeaning: کسی بات کو مزید واضح کرنے کے لیے دوبارہ کہنا، کسی خیال کو زور دینے کے لیے بار بار دہرانا، ایک ہی بات کو مختلف الفاظ میں دوبارہ بیان کرنا، کسی ہدایت یا پیغام کو پختہ کرنے کے لیے دوبارہ کہنا، غلط فہمی سے بچانے کے لیے بات کو دہرانا
englishMeaning: To say or do something again, usually for emphasis or clarity. To repeat a statement, idea, or action more than once in order to make it clearer, stronger, or better understood. It is often used in formal speech, meetings, teaching, and communication when someone wants to emphasize an important point.
synonyms: Repeat, Restate, Emphasize, Reaffirm, Recap
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ڳالهه کي وڌيڪ واضح ڪرڻ لاءِ ٻيهر ورجائڻ، ڪنهن خيال کي زور ڏيڻ لاءِ بار بار چوڻ، هڪ ئي ڳالهه کي مختلف لفظن ۾ ٻيهر بيان ڪرڻ، ڪنهن هدايت يا پيغام کي پڪ سان سمجهائڻ لاءِ ورجائڻ، ڳالهه کي غلط فهمي کان بچائڻ لاءِ ٻيهر چوڻ
examples: The teacher reiterated the instructions before the exam started. The manager reiterated the importance of punctuality. I want to reiterate that safety is our top priority. She reiterated her request for additional support.

englishMeaning: To say or believe that something is the result of a particular thing. To say or believe that somebody is responsible for doing something, especially for saying, writing or painting something. To regard a quality or feature as belonging to somebody, something. A quality or feature of somebody, something.
urduMeaning: منسوب کرنا، سبب قرار دینا ، خصوصیت قرار دینا، کِسی کے سَر ڈالنا ، نِسبَت دينا ، سَبَب بَنانا، خاصِيَت يا خَصُوصِيَت جِسے کِسی شَخَص يا چيز سے مَنسُوب کِيا جا سَکے ، وَصف ،خاصَہ
sindhiMeaning: منسوب ڪرڻ، باعث ٺهرائڻ، لاڳاپو ڏيکارڻ، صفت يا لاڳاپو ڏيکاريندڙ، ارپڻ، کان ڀانئڻ، جو نتيجو سمجهڻ، جو گُڻ سمجهڻ، سبب سمجهڻ، جو حاصل ھئڻ، خاصيت، گُڻ، وصف، امتياز، سڃاڻپ
antonyms: Deny, Disconnect, Dissociate, Separate, Sever, Sunder
synonyms: Accredit, Ascribe, Chalk up, Credit, Impute, Lay, Put down, Rationalize, Account (for), Affection, Characteristic
examples: She attributes her success to hard work and a little luck. The power failure was attributed to the recent storms and high winds. This play is usually attributed to Shakespeare. The committee refused to attribute blame without further information. Patience is one of the most important attributes in a teacher. The most basic attribute of all animals is consciousness.

urduMeaning: دوبارہ جوان اور تازہ دم کرنا، توانائی اور طاقت بحال کرنا، تازگی اور نیا جوش پیدا کرنا
synonyms: Refresh, Revitalize, Renew, Restore, Recharge, Invigorate
examples: A short vacation helped him rejuvenate after months of hard work. The spa treatments rejuvenate the skin and improve its glow. Green parks help rejuvenate the city environment. The new manager rejuvenated the company with fresh ideas.
englishMeaning: To make someone or something feel or look young, fresh, or energetic again. To restore strength, energy, spirit, or appearance after tiredness, damage, or decline. It is used for people, nature, organizations, skin, or systems when they are renewed or refreshed.
antonyms: Exhaust, Drain, Weaken, Tire, Deplete, Age
sindhiMeaning: وري جوان يا تازو ڪرڻ، طاقت ۽ توانائي بحال ڪرڻ، ٿڪاوٽ ختم ڪري نئون احساس ڏيڻ

englishMeaning: The process of making someone or something feel, look, or become young, fresh, or stronger again. It refers to restoring energy, vitality, or freshness to a person, place, system, or object. It can describe physical renewal, mental refreshment, or even the improvement and redevelopment of environments, organizations, or nature. It often implies bringing back lost strength, beauty, or effectiveness.
