urduMeaning: طے شدہ جگہ اور وقت پر کسی سے ملنا، مقرر وقت اور جگہ پر ملاقات، عاشقوں کی خفیہ ملاقات، فوج یا جہازوں کے جمع ہونے کی جگہ، پہلے سے طے شدہ سماجی یا سرکاری ملاقات
antonyms: Separation, Parting, Farewell, Avoidance, Departure
sindhiMeaning: طئي ڪيل هنڌ ۽ وقت تي ڪنهن سان ملڻ، اهڙي ملاقات جيڪا اڳواٽ طئي ڪيل وقت ۽ هنڌ تي ٿئي، عاشقن جي ڳجهي ملاقات، فوج يا جهازن جو گڏ ٿيڻ وارو هنڌ، اڳواٽ مقرر ڪيل سماجي يا سرڪاري ملاقات

synonyms: Break a promise, Back out, Default, Withdraw, Go back on one’s word
englishMeaning: To go back on a promise, agreement or commitment. To fail to do what you promised or agreed to do. It is used when someone withdraws from a commitment, breaks their word, or refuses to carry out an obligation they previously accepted.
sindhiMeaning: واعدي تان ڦرڻ، ڪيل معاهدي تان هٿ کڻڻ، ڪنهن ذميواري کي نه نڀائڻ، انجام کان مُڪرڻ، اصولن جي ڀڃڪڙي ڪرڻ
examples: He promised to support the project, but later he reneged on his commitment. The company reneged on the agreement after facing financial issues. She felt disappointed when her friend reneged on their plan. In the card game, he was penalized because he reneged by not following suit.
urduMeaning: وعدہ توڑ دینا، کسی معاہدے یا وعدے سے پیچھے ہٹ جانا، کسی ذمہ داری کو پورا نہ کرنا، مکر جانا، معاہدے کی خلاف ورزی کرنا، اصول کی خلاف ورزی کرنا
antonyms: Keep a promise, Honor, Fulfill, Uphold, Commit

sindhiMeaning: مشهور، شهرت، مشهوري، نالو،عزت ۽ مان، مشهور ڪرڻ، نامور بڻائڻ، ڪاميابيءَ جي ڪري حاصل ٿيل شهرت، عوامي سڃاڻپ، وڏائي يا مرتبو، وڏي پيماني تي سڃاڻپ يا شهرت حاصل ڪرڻ خاص ڪري ڪنهن جي قابليت ڪاميابين يا سٺين خوبين جي ڪري، اهو لفظ عام طور تي انهن ماڻهن جڳهن يا شين لاءِ استعمال ٿيندو آهي جيڪي عزت ۽ شهرت حاصل ڪن ٿا
examples: The scientist gained international renown for his groundbreaking research. She is a writer of great renown in modern literature. The city achieved renown as a center of culture and art. His bravery brought him lasting renown among his people. Great achievements can renown a person for generations. The victory renown the kingdom far and wide.
synonyms: Fame, Reputation, Prestige, Glory, Recognition, Distinction
urduMeaning: شہرت، ناموری، معروفیت، نامی گرامی، مشہور، عزت و وقار، مشہور کرنا، نامور بنانا، کامیابی سے حاصل ہونے والی شہرت، عوامی تعریف، بلند مرتبہ یا مقام، وسیع پیمانے پر شہرت اور پہچان جو عموماً کسی کی کامیابیوں صلاحیتوں یا اچھی خصوصیات کی وجہ سے حاصل ہوتی ہے، یہ لفظ زیادہ تر ان افراد مقامات یا چیزوں کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے جو عزت اور شہرت رکھتے ہیں
antonyms: Obscurity, Unknown, Anonymity, Disrepute
englishMeaning: Fame, wide recognition, or a strong reputation for something good. The state of being widely known and respected, usually because of achievements, talent, or good qualities. It is often used for people, places, or things that have gained lasting fame. To make someone or something famous or well-known.

synonyms: Compensation, Restitution, Amends, Redress, Indemnity, Repayment, Reimbursement, Atonement
examples: The company paid reparation to the families affected by the accident. The country was forced to provide reparation after the war. He offered money as reparation for the damage he had caused. Many people believe historical wrongs should be addressed through reparation.
englishMeaning: Compensation or payment made for a wrong, loss, or damage. Something done to repair a wrong or make up for damage, injury, loss, or injustice. It often refers to compensation, repayment, or an effort to correct harm caused to a person, group, or country.
urduMeaning: کسی نقصان زیادتی یا غلطی کے بدلے دیا جانے والا معاوضہ یا تلافی، ازالہ، ہرجانہ، نقصان کی بھرپائی، غلطی کا ازالہ، ناانصافی کا مداوا، حق کی واپسی یا بحالی، یہ کسی فرد گروہ یا ملک کے ساتھ ہونے والی زیادتی کے بدلے بھی بولا جاتا ہے
antonyms: Injury, Damage, Harm, Loss, Injustice, Punishment, Wrongdoing
sindhiMeaning: نقصان ظلم يا غلطي جي بدلي ۾ ڏنل تلافي يا معاوضو، ازالو، بدلو طور ڏنل ادائيگي، نقصان جي پورائي، غلطي جو ازالو، ناانصافي جي سڌاري لاءِ قدم، حق جي واپسي يا بحالي، اهو فرد جماعت يا ملڪ سان ٿيل ظلم يا نقصان جي پورائي لاءِ به استعمال ٿيندو آهي

antonyms: Loss, Misplacement
englishMeaning: The act of making something full again by replacing what has been used. Filling again by supplying what has been used up.
urduMeaning: بھرا ہوا ہونا، بھرائی، ذخیرہ کاری ،خالی ہونے پر پھِر سے بھر دینا
examples: Computerization has enabled the automatic replenishment of stock. Bone marrow plays an important role in the constant replenishment of red blood cells. A recent sand replenishment project widened the beach by hundreds of feet.
synonyms: Recovery, Repossession, Retrieval Redemption
sindhiMeaning: ڀرتي، معموري، ڀرپوري، سامان، توشو، ڀرائي، مقرري

englishMeaning: Fully filled, abundant. Completely filled or well-supplied with something. Fully satisfied (especially with food). Abundantly provided, overflowing.
antonyms: Empty, Lacking
urduMeaning: مملو، بھرا ہوا، کثرت سے موجود، کسی چیز سے لبریز
sindhiMeaning: ڀريل، ڪثرت سان موجود، مڪمل طور تي ڀريل، هر طرف کان مالا مال
examples: The book is replete with examples. The book is replete with historical details. After the meal, he felt replete and happy.
synonyms: Full, Abundant

sindhiMeaning: صاف ٻڌڻ جوڳو آواز، اهڙو آواز جيڪو رڪاوٽ کان سواءِ ٻڌجي، ڳالهائڻ يا آواز جي وضاحت لاءِ استعمال ٿيندو آهي
antonyms: Inaudible, Silent, Muffled, Unheard
synonyms: Hearable, Perceptible, Detectable, Clear, Louder
urduMeaning: واضح اور سنائی دینے والا آواز، کمزور یا دبے ہوئے نہ ہونے والا آواز، آواز کی وضاحت یا سننے کی صلاحیت کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے
examples: The teacher spoke in an audible voice so all students could hear. His heartbeat was barely audible in the silent room. The alarm became audible after the door was closed. She made sure her instructions were audible to everyone in the hall.
englishMeaning: Able to be heard. That can be heard clearly by the ear. It is used when a sound is strong enough to be detected or understood by listening.

A place or container where things are stored safely. A person or thing regarded as a store of knowledge, information, or skill. A central location in which data or resources are collected and maintained. A storage place for valuable or important items.
sindhiMeaning: اها جڳھه جتي شيون ڄاڻ يا مواد گڏ ڪيو وڃي ۽ محفوظ رکيو وڃي، اهڙو مرڪز جتي ڄاڻ معلومات يا دستاويز گڏ ڪيا وڃن ۽ ضرورت وقت استعمال ڪيا وڃن، ذخيرو، مرڪز
urduMeaning: ذخیرہ، مرکز، وہ جگہ جہاں چیزیں معلومات یا دستاویزات جمع اور محفوظ کی جائیں، ایسا مقام جہاں قیمتی اشیاء یا علم کو سنبھال کر رکھا جائے
antonyms: Disposal, Wasteland, Emptiness, Scatter, Dispersal
synonyms: Storehouse, Archive, Warehouse, Depository, Storage, Collection, Data bank
examples: The library is a vast repository of human knowledge. This museum serves as a repository for ancient artifacts. Our company uses an online repository to store research documents. She became a repository of family traditions and stories.

antonyms: Express, Release, Encourage, Allow, Liberate
englishMeaning: To control, hold back, or stop feelings, thoughts, or actions. To push painful or unwanted thoughts, memories, or feelings into the unconscious mind so that a person is not fully aware of them. To control or suppress a group, protest, or movement by force or authority.
urduMeaning: دبانا یا روک دینا، تکلیف دہ خیالات احساسات یا یادوں کو شعور سے نیچے دبا دینا تاکہ انسان ان سے مکمل طور پر آگاہ نہ رہے، کسی تحریک احتجاج یا گروہ کو طاقت یا اختیار کے ذریعے دبا دینا، کسی جذبے یا ردعمل کو قابو میں رکھنا یا روکنا
sindhiMeaning: دٻائڻ يا روڪڻ، تڪليف ڏيندڙ خيالن احساسن يا يادگيرين کي شعور کان هيٺ لڪائڻ يا دٻائڻ، ڪنهن تحريڪ احتجاج يا گروهه کي طاقت يا اختيار سان دٻائڻ، ڪنهن احساس يا ردعمل کي روڪڻ يا قابو ۾ رکڻ
examples: She tried to repress her anger during the meeting. The government repressed the protest quickly. He repressed painful childhood memories for many years. She repressed a smile when she heard the joke.
synonyms: Suppress, Restrain, Inhibit, Control, Subdue

examples: The teacher reprimanded the student for being late. He received a strong reprimand from his manager for missing the deadline. The police officer was reprimanded for misconduct. She reprimanded her son for lying.
synonyms: Scold, Rebuke, Blame, Criticize, Admonish, Reproach, Chastise
sindhiMeaning: ملامت ڪرڻ، ڇيڙڻ، ڦٽڪارڻ، سختي سان ڇيڙڻ يا ڌڪارڻ، سزا ڏيڻ يا نصيحت ڪرڻ، ناراضگي جو اظهار، تنقيد يا تنبيهه ڪرڻ جو عمل
englishMeaning: To express sharp disapproval or criticism of someone’s behavior, especially by a person in authority. An official expression of disapproval or scolding.
antonyms: Praise, Compliment, Approve, Reward, Commend
urduMeaning: سرزنش کرنا، ڈانٹنا، ملامت کرنا، سخت لہجے میں تنبیہ یا ڈانٹ، سختی سے ڈانٹنے کا عمل

examples: The manager reproached the staff for poor performance. They reproached her for ignoring the warning. The mistake brought reproach on the whole team. There was no reproach in her tone, only sadness.
sindhiMeaning: ملامت ڪرڻ يا ڏوهه ڏيڻ، ڪنهن کي سندس غلطي تي ملامت ڪرڻ يا ناراضگي ظاهر ڪرڻ، ملامت يا الزام، ناراضگي جي اظهار، ڏوراپو، مهڻو، الزام مڙهڻ، بدنام ڪرڻ، شرمندگي جو سبب، اخلاقي تنقيد
synonyms: Blame, Criticism, Disapproval, Rebuke, Censure, Condemnation
englishMeaning: To blame or express disappointment toward someone. To criticize someone for a mistake or wrong action, often with a tone of disappointment rather than anger. A blame or criticism for a fault. The act or expression of blame, or a feeling of disappointment caused by someone's actions.
antonyms: Praise, Approval, Compliment, Appreciation, Commendation
urduMeaning: ملامت کرنا یا الزام دینا، کسی کو اس کی غلطی پر ملامت کرنا یا ناراضی ظاہر کرنا، ملامت یا الزام، الزام یا ناراضی کے اظہار، شرمندگی کا باعث، اخلاقی تنقید
کسی عمل یا خیال کو سختی سے ناپسند کرنا یا اخلاقی طور پر غلط سمجھنا، وہ شخص جو اخلاقی اقدار کو نظرانداز کرتا ہے اور برے اعمال پر کوئی ندامت محسوس نہیں کرتا، اخلاقی طور پر بگڑا ہوا شخص
antonyms: Virtuous person, Moral individual, Upright citizen, Righteous person
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن عمل يا خيال کي سختي سان رد ڪرڻ يا ان کي غلط قرار ڏيڻ، اهڙو ماڻهو جيڪو اخلاق ۽ سماجي قدرن کي نظرانداز ڪري خراب عمل ڪندو آهي ۽ ان تي شرمندگي محسوس نه ڪندو آهي، اخلاقي طور خراب يا بگڙيل ماڻهو
examples: He was known as a reprobate who ignored all moral rules. Society often isolates a reprobate because of repeated bad behavior. The judge openly reprobated corruption in public offices. The community reprobated the dishonest practices of the company.
synonyms: Degenerate, Rogue, Villain, Scoundrel, Corrupt person
englishMeaning: To strongly disapprove of something or to reject it as morally wrong. A person who behaves in a morally corrupt way and shows no regret for bad actions. Such a person often ignores social and ethical values.

synonyms: Disgusting, Offensive, Revolting, Loathsome, Abhorrent
urduMeaning: انتہائی ناپسندیدہ يا نفرت انگیز، جو شدید نفرت کراہت یا اخلاقی ناپسندیدگی پیدا کرے، یہ اکثر غیر اخلاقی یا ظالمانہ عمل کے لیے بولا جاتا ہے
sindhiMeaning: تمام گهڻو ناپسنديده يا نفرت انگيز، جيڪو شديد نفرت ڪراهت يا اخلاقي طور غلط محسوس ٿئي، اڪثر غير انساني يا غير اخلاقي روين لاءِ استعمال ٿيندو آهي
examples: The cruel treatment of animals is repugnant to any civilized society. He found the corrupt practices of the company repugnant. Racism is a repugnant ideology that harms communities. The smell coming from the garbage was absolutely repugnant.
englishMeaning: Extremely unpleasant or morally offensive. Something that causes strong dislike, disgust, or moral rejection. It is often used for actions, ideas, behavior, or things that deeply offend one’s values or senses.
antonyms: Pleasant, Agreeable, Acceptable, Delightful, Appealing

sindhiMeaning: ضروري يا لازمي شيء جيڪا ڪنهن ڪم يا مقصد لاءِ لازمي هجي
antonyms: Optional, Unnecessary, Unrequired, Extra, Superfluous
synonyms: Necessary, Essential, Required, Mandatory, Fundamental, Indispensable
urduMeaning: ضروری یا لازمی چیز جو کسی کام یا مقصد کے لیے درکار ہو
englishMeaning: Something that is necessary or required. Something that is required as a condition for success. A necessary qualification or item. Essential element for completion of a task. Mandatory requirement in rules or systems.
examples: She lacks a requisite experience for the job. A passport is a requisite for international travel. Discipline is a requisite for success in life. Education is a requisite for most jobs today. Proper tools are requisite for completing this project. They were not able to start the meeting until the requisite number of members were present.

antonyms: Absolve, Pardon
sindhiMeaning: بدلو ڏيڻ، پلاند وٺڻ، عيوضو ڏيڻ، سزا ڏيڻ، صلو ڏيڻ، پارڻ، جوابي الزام هڻڻ، بدلو وٺڻ، تلافي ڪرڻ، زخمي ڪرڻ، جزا ڏيڻ، وير پاڙڻ، احسان لاهڻ، ادلي جو بدلو ڏيڻ
examples: Requited love is not enough to sustain a long-term relationship. We never can requite the women for what they have done in this war. The company requited the employee who had fallen on the ice while leaving work by promptly paying all his medical bills, hoping that would stave off a lawsuit.
englishMeaning: To give or do something in return for something given to you or done for you. To repay or to retaliate, to punish or to reward, may be to make some return very inadequate to the benefit or injury received, or the right or wrong done.
urduMeaning: بدلہ دینا، عوض دینا، صلہ دینا، معاوضہ دینا، تلافی کرنا، جزا دینا، بدلے میں کچھ دینا یا کرنا
synonyms: Avenge, Repay

sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کي خطري يا تڪليف مان بچائڻ، ڪنهن ماڻهو جانور يا شيءِ کي خطري نقصان يا ڏکي صورتحال مان محفوظ طريقي سان ڪڍڻ يا بچائڻ، بچائڻ جو عمل يا ڪنهن کي خطري مان ڪڍڻ، صرف جسماني خطري تائين محدود ناهي پر ڪنهن کي مالي يا ذهني مشڪلاتن مان به ٻاهر ڪڍڻ لاءِ استعمال ٿيندو آهي
antonyms: Abandon, Endanger, Harm, Trap, Neglect, Surrender
synonyms: Save, Recover, Free, Deliver, Retrieve, Liberate
englishMeaning: To save someone or something from danger or harm. To free or save a person, animal, or thing from a dangerous, harmful, or difficult situation. It is often used in emergencies like accidents, floods, fire, or kidnapping cases. To bring someone out of a bad condition or difficult situation, not only physical danger. For example, rescuing someone from financial problems or emotional stress. The act of saving someone or something from danger or harm.
urduMeaning: کسی کو خطرے یا مشکل سے بچانا، کسی شخص جانور یا چیز کو خطرناک مشکل یا ہنگامی حالت سے محفوظ طریقے سے نکالنا یا بچانا، بچانے کا عمل، صرف جسمانی خطرے تک محدود نہیں بلکہ کسی کو مالی یا ذہنی مشکلات سے نکالنے کے لیے بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے
examples: The firefighters rescued the family from the burning house. The coast guard rescued the fishermen during the storm. Volunteers rescued the injured dog from the road. The army rescued people trapped in the flood area.

The aim is to find the cause of the child's aberrant behavior. It reflects the aberrant personality of some American politicians hostile to China's development and becoming powerful. Now, this tree is aberrant in that it has two trunks.
synonyms: Abnormal, Deviant, Bizarre, Odd, Nonstandard, Exceptional, Anomalous, Atypical
englishMeaning: Not usual or not socially acceptable. Being or becoming different from the normal type. Different from what is typical or usual, especially in an unacceptable way.
antonyms: Normal, Regular, Usual, Same, True, Common, Unexceptional, Ordinary
sindhiMeaning: گمراه، قاعدي خلاف، خلاف معمول، ابتر، عام رواجي کان مختلف، معمول کا ھٽيل، ڀٽڪيل، تسليم ٿيل معيار کان ھٽيل
urduMeaning: خِلافِ مَعمُول ، بھَٹکا ہُوا ، گُمراہ ، تَسلیم شُدہ معیار سے مُختَلِف ، عام سے مُختَلِف

examples: He augmented his income with a part-time job. The company plans to augment its staff during the busy season. He augmented his income by doing freelance work. The teacher used videos to augment the lesson. Regular exercise can augment your overall health.
synonyms: Increase, Expand, Enhance, Boost, Enlarge, Amplify, Extend
urduMeaning: بڑھانا، اضافہ کرنا، تقویت دینا، زیادہ کرنا
englishMeaning: To make something greater by adding to it. To increase, enlarge, or improve something in size, value, strength, or amount by adding more to it. It is often used when something already exists and is being enhanced further.
sindhiMeaning: وڌائڻ، اضافو ڪرڻ، وڌيڪ مضبوط يا وڏو ڪرڻ، واڌارو آڻڻ
antonyms: Reduce, Decrease, Diminish, Lessen, Cut, Shrink

synonyms: Feel bitter, Be offended, Begrudge, Feel aggrieved, Take offense
sindhiMeaning: چڙ لڳڻ، ناراض ٿيڻ، خفا ٿيڻ، ڪاوڙ يا رنج محسوس ڪرڻ، ڳالهه کي دل تي وٺڻ، ڪنهن ناانصافي تڪليف يا بي عزتي واري ڳالهه تي اندروني ڪاوڙ يا رنج رکڻ، اهو احساس گهڻو وقت تائين دل ۾ رهندو آهي
englishMeaning: To feel anger or bitterness about something unfair. To feel upset, offended, or bitter because of something perceived as unfair, insulting, or hurtful. It often involves holding negative feelings over time.
examples: The children resented the new woman in their father’s life. He bitterly resents being treated like a child. She resented him making all the decisions. She resented being told what to do. He resented his boss for making him work late.
urduMeaning: بُرا ماننا، ناراض ہونا، خفا ہونا، غصہ میں آنا، ناراضگی یا دل میں رنج رکھنا، کسی ناانصافی توہین یا تکلیف دہ بات پر دل میں غصہ یا رنج رکھنا اور اسے بھلانا مشکل ہونا
antonyms: Forgive, Accept, Tolerate, Overlook, Appreciate

examples: She felt deep resentment after being ignored by her team. His resentment grew when he was treated unfairly at work. Years of resentment affected their friendship. He tried to hide his resentment, but it was clear in his voice.
synonyms: Bitterness, Anger, Grudge, Indignation, Irritation
sindhiMeaning: ناراضگي يا دل ۾ ويٺل ڪاوڙ، اندروني ڏک، رنجش، ناانصافي جو احساس، اهو احساس جيڪو تڏهن پيدا ٿئي ٿو جڏهن ڪنهن سان ناانصافي ٿئي يا کيس تڪليف پهچي، اهو دل ۾ رهندڙ ڪاوڙ ۽ رنجش آهي جيڪا گهڻي وقت تائين ختم نه ٿئي
antonyms: Forgiveness, Contentment, Happiness, Acceptance, Peace
urduMeaning: دل کی ناراضی یا چھپی ہوئی ناراضگی، رنجش، دل کی کڑواہٹ، ناانصافی کا احساس، دل کا دکھ، ایسا احساس جو اس وقت پیدا ہوتا ہے جب کسی کے ساتھ ناانصافی ہو یا اسے تکلیف پہنچے، یہ دل میں چھپی ہوئی ناراضگی اور رنجش ہوتی ہے جو دیر تک برقرار رہتی ہے
englishMeaning: A feeling of anger or bitterness because of unfair treatment. A deep feeling of anger, hurt, or bitterness that develops when a person believes they have been treated unfairly, insulted, or wronged. It often lasts for a long time and may remain hidden inside the heart.
Left at the end of a process. Remaining after most of something has gone.
antonyms: Main, Whole
urduMeaning: باقی، پسماندہ، بقیہ
synonyms: Outstanding, Left over, Balance, Unconsumed
examples: There are still a few residual problems with the computer program. They tested for chemical residuals in the water. I still felt some residual bitterness ten years after my divorce. They clearly have some residual guilt about their treatment of their son.
sindhiMeaning: باقي، پاڇي، پڇاڙيءَ جو، رھيل، پچاڙيڪو، باقي بچيل، پاڇي، بچت، بقاي، پڇاڙيءَ جو، اڃا ليکي ۾ نہ آيل

urduMeaning: باقی، بچا ہوا، فضلہ
synonyms: Balance, Leavings, Leftovers, Odds and ends, Remainder, Remains
examples: The residue of the estate was divided equally among his children. She cut off the best meat and threw away the residue. The white residue is on the kettle is a result of minerals in the water. The residue (of the estate) went to her granddaughter.
englishMeaning: A small amount of something that remains at the end of a process. The part of the money, property, etc of a person who has died that remains after all the debts, gifts, etc have been paid. The part that is left after the main part has gone or been taken away, or a substance that remains after a chemical process such as evaporation.
sindhiMeaning: بچت، باقيات، رھيل، بچيل، پاڇي، باقي، رھت، صافي ترڪو، رسوب، تلچٽ، ڇاڻو، فضلو، گيرٺ
antonyms: Body, Bulk, Main, Mass, Most, Weight
Weakness, Fragility, Vulnerability, Inflexibility, Sensitivity
synonyms: Strength, Toughness, Endurance, Flexibility, Adaptability, Recovery
sindhiMeaning: تڪليفن يا مشڪلاتن کان جلدي سنڀالڻ جي صلاحيت، ذهني يا جذباتي مضبوطي، حالتن سان هم آهنگ ٿيڻ جي صلاحيت، ڪنهن شيءِ جو ٻيهر پنهنجي اصل شڪل ۾ اچڻ، آفتن کان پوءِ سماج جي بحالي جي صلاحيت، اهڙي صلاحيت جنهن سان ڪو ماڻهو نظام يا شيءِ مشڪلاتن دٻاءُ يا تڪليفن کي برداشت ڪري انهن سان مطابقت پيدا ڪري ۽ وري پنهنجي اصل حالت ڏانهن موٽي اچي
englishMeaning: Ability to recover quickly from difficulties. Emotional strength during tough times. Ability to adapt to change. Flexibility of a material to return to its original shape. Capacity of communities to recover after disasters. The capacity of a person, system, or material to withstand challenges, adapt to change, and recover from setbacks, stress, or adversity while maintaining normal functioning.
urduMeaning: مشکلات سے جلد سنبھلنے یا واپس آنے کی صلاحیت، ذہنی اور جذباتی مضبوطی، حالات کے مطابق ڈھلنے کی صلاحیت، کسی چیز کا دوبارہ اپنی اصل شکل میں آ جانا، آفات کے بعد معاشرے کی بحالی کی صلاحیت، وہ صلاحیت جس کے ذریعے کوئی انسان نظام یا چیز مشکلات دباؤ یا صدموں کو برداشت کر کے ان کے ساتھ خود کو ہم آہنگ کرے اور دوبارہ اپنی اصل حالت میں آ جائے
examples: She showed great resilience after losing her job. Children often have remarkable resilience in difficult situations. The city's resilience helped it recover after the flood. This material is valued for its strength and resilience.

antonyms: Weak, Fragile, Vulnerable, Delicate, Sensitive
englishMeaning: Able to recover quickly from difficulties. Mentally strong and emotionally stable. Able to adapt to change. Capable of withstanding pressure. Flexible and tough. A person, system, or material that can face problems, stress, or shock and return to normal condition quickly. It also refers to emotional strength and flexibility.
sindhiMeaning: جلدي سنڀلجڻ وارو، ذهني طور مضبوط، حالتن سان ٺهڪي ايندڙ، دٻاءُ برداشت ڪندڙ، لچڪدار ۽ مضبوط، اهڙو شخص نظام يا شيءِ جيڪو مشڪلاتن دٻاءُ يا صدمو اچڻ باوجود جلدي ٻيهر پنهنجي حالت ۾ واپس اچي وڃي، اهو ذهني مضبوطي ۽ لچڪ کي به ظاهر ڪري ٿو
synonyms: Strong, Tough, Flexible, Hardy, Adaptable, Durable
examples: She is a resilient woman who never gives up. Children are often more resilient than adults in tough situations. The city remained resilient after the flood. A resilient mindset helps people succeed in life.
urduMeaning: جلد سنبھل جانے والا، ذہنی طور پر مضبوط، حالات کے مطابق خود کو ڈھالنے والا، دباؤ برداشت کرنے والا، لچکدار اور مضبوط، ایسا شخص نظام یا چیز جو مشکلات دباؤ یا صدمے کے بعد جلد اپنی اصل حالت میں واپس آ جائے، یہ ذہنی مضبوطی اور لچک کو بھی ظاہر کرتا ہے

sindhiMeaning: پڪو ارادو رکندڙ، مضبوط ارادي وارو، اهڙو شخص جيڪو پنهنجي فيصلي تي مضبوط رهي، ڏکين حالتن ۾ به پوئتي نه هٽي
antonyms: Indecisive, Weak, Hesitant, Uncertain, Flexible
englishMeaning: Very firm and determined. Not willing to change one’s decision. A person who is strong in purpose and determination. A resolute person stays focused on their decision or goal, even when facing difficulty, pressure, or opposition. It reflects mental strength, confidence, and persistence.
examples: She remained resolute despite strong criticism. The leader was resolute in protecting national interests. He made a resolute effort to complete the task on time. Her resolute attitude inspired the entire team.
synonyms: Determined, Firm, Steadfast, Unwavering, Strong minded
urduMeaning: پُرعزم، مضبوط ارادے والا، ایسا شخص جو اپنے فیصلے پر قائم رہے اور مشکلات کے باوجود پیچھے نہ ہٹے

examples: Her voice had a strange and thrilling resonance. His words will have resonance for many musicians. The movie had a special emotional resonance for me. This poem has many resonances for me.
synonyms: Reverberation, Echo, Vibration, Timbre, Impact
urduMeaning: گونج، ہم آہنگی، جذباتی اثر، وہ حالت جب کوئی شے کسی دوسری شے کے ساتھ ہم آہنگ ارتعاش کرتی ہے، آواز یا موسیقی میں گہرائی اور وضاحت،کسی بات یا تجربے کے جذباتی اثر کو بڑھانا، دیرپا اثر، معنوی گہرائی، توانائی کی بازگشت
sindhiMeaning: آواز جي گونج، هم وقتي ۾ ارتعاش، جذباتي اثر، پڙاڏو، لرزشي جسم جو ڪنھن ٻئي جسم ۾ پيدا ڪيل ساڳئي قسم جو ارتعاش، ماليڪيول جي ھڪ کان وڌيڪ شڪلين ۾ ظاھر ٿيڻ جي خاصيت، بي بقا نيم جوھري ذرو، اصل ۾ قائم ذري جي اڀاريل صورت، اثر پذيري، يادگاري اثر، ڌن جي شدت
antonyms: Dullness, Silence, Flatness, Lifelessness
englishMeaning: In physics, resonance is the reinforcement or prolongation of sound by reflection or by synchronous vibration. In a figurative sense, it describes the capacity of something to evoke a strong emotional response or connection with people. The quality in music, speech, or any sound that enriches the tone.

examples: The orator's resonant voice filled the hall. His voice sounded oddly resonant in the empty room. The voice was metallic and resonant. It has risen to a high, resonant pitch, emerging from his nose.
sindhiMeaning: اهڙو آواز جيڪو ڳوڙهو صاف ۽ گونجدار هجي، اهڙو جيڪو لهرن ذريعي آواز کي وڌائي يا ڊگهو ڪري، دل تي اثر ڪندڙ يا گهري معنيٰ رکندڙ، ڪنهن خاص خيال يا احساس سان مضبوط لاڳاپو رکندڙ
synonyms: Echoing, Deep, Sonorous, Vibrant, Meaningful, Powerful
urduMeaning: ایسا جو گہری واضح اور گونجدار آواز رکھتا ہو، جو ارتعاش کے ذریعے آواز کو بڑھائے یا دیر تک قائم رکھے، جذباتی طور پر اثر انگیز یا بامعنی، کسی خیال یا جذبے سے مضبوط تعلق رکھنے والا
antonyms: Dull, Flat, Weak, Insignificant, Muffled
englishMeaning: Producing a deep, clear, and rich sound (also emotionally powerful or meaningful). Having a strong, deep, and echoing sound. Capable of increasing or prolonging sound through vibration. Emotionally powerful or meaningful, leaving a lasting impression. Symbolically significant or strongly associated with something.

sindhiMeaning: گونجڻ، گونج يا پڙاڏو پيدا ڪرڻ، ارتعاش ٿيڻ،
synonyms: Resound, Echo, Eeecho, Reverberate
examples: Her voice resonated through the theatre. The body of the violin acts as a resonating chamber and makes the sound louder. The room resonated with the chatter of 100 people. These issues resonated with the voters. His speech resonated with the fears and suspicions of his audience.
englishMeaning: To continue or be repeated in a series of reflected sound waves. (Of a voice, an instrument, etc) to make a deep, clear sound that continues for a long time. (Of a place) to be filled with sound, to make a sound continue longer. To remind somebody of something, to be similar to what somebody thinks or believes.
antonyms: Damp, Dampen, Deaden, Dull, Quiet
urduMeaning: گونجنا ، گمک پیدا ہونا ، گونج پیدا کرنے والے کے طور پر کام کرنا، لمبی گونجنلہ

englishMeaning: An invisible quality or energy that seems to surround someone or something and strongly influences how others feel about it. It can suggest mood, character, or presence.
antonyms: Dullness, Plainness, Insignificance, Ordinary feeling
synonyms: Presence, Atmosphere, Vibe, Charisma
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شخص يا شيءِ جي چوڌاري محسوس ٿيندڙ اثر يا احساس، اهو غير نظر ايندڙ اثر يا توانائي جيڪا ڪنهن انسان، هنڌ يا شيءِ جي چوڌاري هجي ۽ ٻين تي گهرو اثر ڇڏي
urduMeaning: کسی شخص یا چیز کے گرد موجود خاص تاثر یا فضا، وہ غیر مرئی کیفیت یا توانائی جو کسی انسان، جگہ یا شے کے ارد گرد محسوس ہو اور دوسروں پر گہرا اثر ڈالے
examples: The teacher had an aura of confidence that calmed the students. The old library carried an aura of mystery and wisdom. Her kindness gave her an aura that people trusted instantly. The leader entered the room with an aura of authority.

synonyms: Turn to, Rely on, Fall back on, Use, Holiday spot, Retreat, Getaway, Vacation place
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن حل يا ذريعي ڏانهن آخري طور رجوع ڪرڻ، اهڙو هنڌ جتي ماڻهو موڪلن يا آرام لاءِ وڃن، غير مناسب حل يا طريقو استعمال ڪرڻ جڏهن ٻيو رستو نه هجي
englishMeaning: To turn to something, especially as a solution when nothing else works. A place where people go for holidays or relaxation. A holiday destination with facilities like hotels, beaches, or recreation. To use or depend on something as a last option. The act of repeatedly using something, especially something not ideal.
examples: They spent a month at a fashionable ski resort in Switzerland. There are hopes that the conflict can be resolved without resort to violence. Strike action should be regarded as a last resort, when all attempts to negotiate have failed. He got hold of the money legally, without resort to violence.
urduMeaning: کسی مشکل میں آخری حل کے طور پر کسی چیز کا سہارا لینا، ایسی جگہ جہاں لوگ سیر و تفریح یا آرام کے لیے جائیں، کسی غیر مناسب یا آخری حل کا سہارا لینا
antonyms: Avoid, Reject, Abandon, Home, Workplace, Local area
Answer, Avoid, Escape, Dissuade, Give, Refuse, Disclaim
sindhiMeaning: آسرو ڪرڻ، آخر ۾ ڪرڻ، مجبوريءَ ۾ ڪنهن شيءَ جو سهارو وٺڻ، ڪنهن مشڪل حالتن ۾، جڏهن ٻيو ڪو رستو نه هجي، تڏهن ڪنهن ڪم، طريقي يا عمل کي اختيار ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: سہارا لینا، رجوع کرنا، کسی طریقے یا عمل کو اپنانا، خاص طور پر مجبوری میں یا آخری حل کے طور پر
examples: They felt obliged to resort to violence. They achieved their demands without having to resort to force. We had to resort to another loan from the bank. We may have to resort to using untrained staff.
synonyms: Recourse, Visit, Address, Submit, Apply, Petition, Sue, Go (to), Refer (to), Consult, Turn (to)
englishMeaning: To make use of something, especially something bad, as a means of achieving something, often because there is no other possible solution.

synonyms: Turned to, Fell back on, Used, Adopted
sindhiMeaning: آخري حل طور اختيار ڪرڻ، جڏهن ٻيا سڀ طريقا ناڪام ٿي وڃن ته ڪنهن عمل يا وسيلي کي مجبوراً اختيار ڪرڻ
examples: He resorted to borrowing money after losing his job. The villagers resorted to using river water during the drought. She resorted to silence when words failed her. The team resorted to defensive tactics in the final minutes.
urduMeaning: مجبوری میں اختیار کرنا، جب تمام راستے ناکام ہو جائیں تو کسی عمل یا طریقے کو آخری حل کے طور پر اپنانا
englishMeaning: To turn to a particular action, method, or person when other options have failed or are not available. It often implies necessity rather than preference and is commonly used with the word to.
antonyms: Avoided, Rejected, Abandoned, Gave up

englishMeaning: A short period of rest or relief from something difficult, tiring, or unpleasant such as work, pain, stress, or trouble. Temporary relief from difficulty or stress. To grant a delay, relief, or temporary suspension from something difficult, especially punishment, duty, or pressure.
antonyms: Stress, Strain, Burden, Hardship, Continuation, Exhaustion, Pressure
urduMeaning: کسی مشکل تکلیف یا تھکا دینے والی حالت سے عارضی آرام یا وقفہ، کسی مشکل سزا یا ذمہ داری کو عارضی طور روک دینا یا مہلت دینا
examples: The workers welcomed a brief respite from the hot sun. After hours of studying, she took a short respite to relax. The rain offered a respite from the extreme heat. There was no respite from his busy schedule all week. The judge respited the execution for a week. The king respited the prisoner’s punishment.
synonyms: Break, Rest, Pause, Relief, Pause in activity, Intermission, Breather, Pause for recovery
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ڏکي يا ٿڪائيندڙ حالت مان عارضي آرام يا سڪون جو وقت، ڪنهن ڏکي ڪم سزا يا ذميواري کي عارضي طور روڪڻ يا وقفو ڏيڻ

examples: She tried to restrain her anger during the meeting. The police restrained the suspect from escaping. He could not restrain himself from laughing. Parents should restrain children from bad habits.
englishMeaning: To hold back or control. To stop someone or something from acting freely, to control emotions, actions, or movement, or to keep something within limits.
synonyms: Control, Limit, Prevent, Hold back, Suppress
urduMeaning: روکنا، قابو میں رکھنا، روک تھام کرنا، محدود کرنا، دبا دینا، قابو رکھنا، لگام دینا، کسی کو یا کسی چیز کو آزادانہ عمل کرنے سے روکنا، جذبات یا حرکات پر قابو رکھنا یا حدود میں رکھنا
antonyms: Encourage, Release, Allow, Free, Promote
sindhiMeaning: روڪڻ، قابو ۾ رکڻ، بندش ڪرڻ، محدود ڪرڻ، جهلي رکڻ، ڪنٽرول ڪرڻ، روڪ لڳائڻ، ڪنهن کي يا ڪنهن شيءِ کي آزادي سان عمل ڪرڻ کان روڪڻ، جذبن يا عملن کي ڪنٽرول ڪرڻ يا حدن اندر رکڻ
ضابطو، پاڻ تي ڪنٽرول، پابندي يا روڪ، اعتدال، عمل کان روڪ، پنهنجي احساسن ڳالهين يا عملن کي سنڀالڻ، اهو ڪنهن شيءِ تي پابندي يا حد به ظاهر ڪري سگهي ٿو ته جيئن نقصان کان بچي سگهجي
synonyms: Self-control, Discipline, Moderation, Constraint, Inhibition
urduMeaning: ضبط، قابو، خود پر قابو، پابندی، اعتدال، روک تھام، اپنے جذبات رویے یا اعمال پر قابو رکھنا ہے خاص طور پر مشکل حالات میں، یہ کسی چیز پر پابندی یا روک ٹوک کے معنی میں بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے
englishMeaning: Control over actions, emotions, or behavior. The ability to control your feelings, actions, or behavior, especially in difficult situations. It can also mean a limitation or restriction placed on someone or something to prevent excess or harm.
examples: He showed great restraint during the argument. Parents should teach children restraint in their behavior. The government imposed restraint on spending. She exercised restraint and did not respond angrily.
antonyms: Excess, Indulgence, Freedom, Lack of control, Impulsiveness

urduMeaning: کی وجہ سے ہونا، کسی چیز کا نتیجہ ہونا، کسی وجہ سے پیدا ہونا
sindhiMeaning: سبب ٿيڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ جو نتيجو ٿيڻ، ڪنهن سبب جي ڪري پيدا ٿيڻ
synonyms: Arise from, Stem from, Be caused by, Originate from
examples: The flooding resulted from heavy rainfall in the area. Her success results from years of hard work. Health problems can result from poor nutrition. The accident resulted from a mechanical failure.
englishMeaning: To happen or exist because of a particular action, event, or situation, to be caused by something. Caused by, originate from.
antonyms: Lead to, Cause, Bring about, Produce

englishMeaning: To cause or bring about a specific outcome, to be the reason something happens.
synonyms: Lead to, Cause, Bring about, Produce, Give rise to
examples: The new policy resulted in increased employee satisfaction. Ignoring safety rules can result in serious accidents. The merger resulted in higher operational efficiency. Poor nutrition during childhood may result in developmental delays.
urduMeaning: کا سبب بننا، کسی عمل یا واقعے کے نتیجے میں کچھ ہونا، کسی نتیجے تک پہنچنا
sindhiMeaning: نتيجو ڏيڻ، ڪنهن عمل يا واقعن جي ڪري ڪنهن نتيجي تي پهچڻ يا سبب بڻجڻ
antonyms: Prevent, Avoid, Stop, Hinder

synonyms: Revival, Comeback, Renewal, Reappearance, Rebirth, Recovery, Return
urduMeaning: زوال کے بعد دوبارہ ابھرنا یا بڑھ جانا، دوبارہ بحالی یا واپسی، نئی سر سے بڑھوتری یا سرگرمی، غائب ہونے کے بعد دوبارہ ظاہر ہونا، دوبارہ طاقت یا مقبولیت میں اضافہ، اس عمل کو کہتے ہیں جب کوئی چیز کمی زوال یا غیر فعالیت کے بعد دوبارہ طاقت اہمیت یا مقبولیت حاصل کرے
sindhiMeaning: ٻيهر اڀار يا گهٽتائي کان پوءِ ٻيهر واڌ، ٻيهر جيئرو ٿيڻ يا واپسي، نئين سر واڌ يا سرگرمي، غائب ٿيڻ کان پوءِ ٻيهر ظاهر ٿيڻ، ٻيهر طاقت يا مقبوليت ۾ واڌ، ان حالت کي چوندا آهن جڏهن ڪا شيءِ گهٽجڻ ختم ٿيڻ يا ڪمزور ٿيڻ کان پوءِ ٻيهر زور وٺي وڌي يا مقبول ٿئي
englishMeaning: A return or increase after a period of decline. Revival or comeback. Revival or comeback. Reappearance after disappearance. Increase in strength or popularity again. The act of rising again, becoming active again, or increasing in strength, popularity, or importance after a period of decline or inactivity.
examples: There was a resurgence of interest in classical music. The city saw a resurgence in tourism after the pandemic. His career experienced a resurgence after the new film. Scientists noticed a resurgence of the disease in winter.
antonyms: Decline, Decrease, Fall, Drop, Collapse, Disappearance

examples: The gang threatened to rough up on anyone who entered their area. He was roughed up on his way home by unknown attackers. The guards roughed up on the prisoner during the arrest. The coach warned the players not to rough up on the weaker team.
urduMeaning: کسی کو مارنا یا سختی سے پیش آنا، زبردستی مارنا پیٹنا، سخت یا ظالمانہ سلوک کرنا، طاقت کے زور پر کسی کو قابو میں کرنا
synonyms: Criticize, Scold, Berate
antonyms: Praise, Compliment, Support
englishMeaning: To attack or treat someone roughly. To use physical force against someone or to handle a person or thing in a violent, aggressive, or careless way. It often implies intimidation, beating, or causing harm rather than a serious fight. In daily English, speakers usually say rough up without on.

sindhiMeaning: گڏ ڪرڻ يا گڏ ڪرڻ لاءِ ڪو عمل، جيئن جانورن، ماڻهن يا شين کي گڏ ڪرڻ، ڪا ڳالهه ختم ڪرڻ يا مڪمل ڪرڻ، انگ کي ويجهڙائي واري وڏي انگ تي آڻڻ، گرفتار ڪرڻ
antonyms: Disperse, Scatter, Release, Separate, Divide
urduMeaning: اکٹھا کرنا یا جمع کرنا، کسی کام کو مکمل کرنا یا اختتام تک پہنچانا، عدد کو اوپر والے عدد تک بڑھانا، مجرموں یا لوگوں کو گرفتار کرنا
examples: The teacher rounded up all the students after the trip. The police rounded up the thieves last night. Let’s round up the meeting with some final thoughts. Please round up the bill to the nearest dollar.
englishMeaning: To gather people, animals, or things together in one place. To bring to a conclusion or complete an activity. To increase a number to the nearest whole or higher figure (in mathematics or estimation). To arrest or capture a group of people.
synonyms: Organize, Arrest, Capture, Conclude, Finish

antonyms: Victory, Triumph, Win, Success
urduMeaning: کسی کو مکمل شکست دے کر بھگا دینا، بری طرح شکست دینا، دشمنوں کو منتشر کرنا، زبرد، ست فتح، ایسی شدید شکست ہے جس میں مخالف مکمل طور پر بکھر جائے یا بھاگ جائے
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کي مڪمل طور هارائڻ ۽ ڀڄائي ڇڏڻ، دشمنن کي ڀڄائي ڇڏڻ، افراتفري ۾ ڀڄڻ، زبردست فتح، اهڙي سخت شڪست جنهن ۾ مخالف مڪمل طور تي هارائي وڃي يا ڀڄي وڃي
englishMeaning: To defeat someone completely and force them to flee or withdraw. A complete and overwhelming defeat in a battle, game, election, or competition. It can also mean a chaotic retreat or disorderly escape.
examples: The army suffered a terrible rout in the battle. Our team routed the opponents by ten goals. The frightened crowd fled in rout after the explosion. The king’s soldiers routed the enemy forces quickly.
synonyms: Defeat, Crush, Overthrow, Beat, Scatter, Vanquish

examples: The rowdy crowd cheered loudly at the match. Some rowdy students were sent out of the classroom. He is known for his rowdy behavior at parties. The rowdy dogs chased each other around the yard.
sindhiMeaning: فساد ڪندڙ شخص، گوڙ ڪندڙ، وڳوڙ وجهندڙ، اهڙو ماڻهو جيڪو شور مچائيندو ۽ ترتيب نه ڏيندو ھجي، شور ڪندڙ
synonyms: Boisterous, Unruly, Disruptive, Wild
englishMeaning: Someone or something that is loud, disruptive, and difficult to control, often causing trouble in a group or gathering. Noisy and disorderly
antonyms: Calm, Quiet, Orderly, Peaceful
urduMeaning: اودھم مچانے والا، جھگڑالو، فسادی، ہنگامہ خیز، وہ شخص یا چیز جو شور مچائے اور قابو پانے میں مشکل ہو، اکثر پریشانی پیدا کرے

examples: After the long run, he asked someone to rub down his legs. She rubbed down the wooden table until it shined. The mechanic rubbed down the car with oil to prevent rust. He tried to rub down the tension in the room with a joke.
sindhiMeaning: مساج ڪرڻ (جسم جي عضون کي رگڙڻ لاءِ)، صاف ڪرڻ يا صافي لاءِ رگڙڻ، مٿاڇري تي تيل يا لوڻ لڳائڻ لاءِ رگڙڻ
synonyms: Massage, Polish, Wipe, Scrub, Anoint
englishMeaning: To apply pressure with hands or a cloth to massage, soothe, or relax muscles. To clean or polish a surface by rubbing. To apply something over a surface by rubbing (like oil or lotion). Sometimes, to reduce tension or calm a situation through a figurative "rubbing down".
antonyms: Neglect, Ignore, Scratch roughly, Scratch off
urduMeaning: مالش کرنا (جسم کے عضلات کو رگڑنا)، کسی چیز کو رگڑ کر صاف کرنا، کسی سطح پر تیل یا کریم لگانا

synonyms: Irritate someone, Annoy someone, Rub up the wrong way, Get on someone’s nerves, Bother someone
examples: His sarcastic jokes always rub me the wrong way. She didn’t mean to be rude, but her tone rubbed him the wrong way. The new manager rubs many employees the wrong way with strict rules. I think I rubbed her the wrong way when I interrupted her speech.
urduMeaning: کسی کو نادانستہ طور پر ناراض یا چِڑانا، جب کسی شخص کا انداز رویہ یا بات چیت دوسرے شخص کو نادانستہ طور پر ناگوار یا چِڑچڑا بنا دے، یہ جملہ اکثر روزمرہ گفتگو میں استعمال ہوتا ہے جب کسی کا رویہ یا بات دوسروں کو ناگوار گزرے
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کي بنا ارادي ناراض يا تنگ ڪرڻ، جڏهن ڪنهن جو رويو ڳالهائڻ جو انداز يا عمل ڪنهن ٻئي ماڻهو کي بغير ارادي جي تنگ يا ناراض ڪري ڇڏي، هي محاورو عام طور تي روزمره ڳالهه ٻولهه ۾ استعمال ٿئي ٿو جڏهن ڪنهن جو انداز ٻين کي پسند نه اچي
englishMeaning: To annoy or irritate someone, often without intending to. To irritate or annoy a person through behavior, tone, or actions, even if no harm was intended. It often happens due to personality clashes or communication style differences.
antonyms: Please someone, Impress someone, Calm someone, Soothe someone, Delight someone

synonyms: Massage, Wipe, Clean, Polish, Rub
englishMeaning: The act of massaging or rubbing someone’s body, often after exercise to relax muscles. It can also mean wiping or cleaning a surface thoroughly. In sports, it’s a post-workout massage. In mechanical or cleaning contexts, it means rubbing a surface to remove dirt, grease, or polish.
examples: After the match, the players received a quick rub-down. She gave the table a good rub-down with a cloth. The massage therapist performed a thorough rub-down of his back. Mechanics gave the engine a rub-down before assembling it.
urduMeaning: ایسا عمل جس میں کسی کے جسم کو مالش دی جاتی ہے یا کسی سطح کو صاف یا رگڑ کر صاف کیا جاتا ہے، کھیلوں میں ورزش کے بعد پٹھوں کو آرام دینے کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے، صفائی یا میکینیکل کام میں مٹی یا گریس ہٹانے کے لیے بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے
sindhiMeaning: اهڙو عمل جنهن ۾ جسم کي مالش ڪئي وڃي يا ڪنهن شيءِ کي چڱي طرح صاف يا رگڙيو وڃي، راندن ۾ ورزش کان پوءِ عضون کي آرام ڏيڻ لاءِ استعمال ٿئي ٿو، صفائي يا مشيني ڪم ۾ مٽي يا گريز هٽائڻ لاءِ رگڙڻ جو مطلب
antonyms: Neglect, Ignore, Dirty, Scratch

urduMeaning: زمین پر بکھرا ہوا ٹوٹا ہوا ملبہ، ٹوٹے ہوئے اینٹ پتھر، ٹوٹا ہوا حصہ، کھلے پتھر یا اینٹیں جو زمین پر بکھری ہوں
antonyms: Whole, Intact, Structure, Order
englishMeaning: Broken pieces of stone, brick, or concrete from a destroyed building or structure. Fragments of rock, stone, bricks, or concrete that remain after the destruction of a building, wall, or other structure. It can also describe loose debris from a demolished area or natural disaster.
synonyms: Debris, Wreckage, Fragments, Ruins
examples: The bomb reduced the houses to rubble. After the earthquake, the streets were filled with rubble. The demolition left a heap of rubble behind. Workers cleared the rubble from the collapsed bridge. Rubble from the old castle was used in building the new road.
sindhiMeaning: پٿر جا ڀڳل ٽٽل ٽڪرا، پٿرن جي روڙي، ملبو، ٽٽل پٿر يا سِرن جو مجموعو، ڪنهن صورتحال ۾ بکھريل شيون، ٽٽل پٿر يا سِرن جا ٽڪرا جيڪي زمين تي ڦهليل هجن

antonyms: Silence, Calm, Peace, Order, Quiet
urduMeaning: شور و غل، ہنگامہ، لڑائی جھگڑا، شور شرابا، ہنگامہ آرائی، افراتفری غل غپاڑا ، ایسی صورتحال جس میں بہت شو ر بحث یا ہنگامہ ہو
sindhiMeaning: شور شرابو، هُلڙبازي، هنگامو/ گوڙ، جهيڙو، اُفرا تفري، اهو حالتون جتي ماڻهو شور ڪن بحث مباحثو ڪن يا ڪنهن ڳالهه تي جهيڙو ڪن،
synonyms: Uproar, Commotion, Chaos, Tumult, Hubbub
englishMeaning: A loud noise, disturbance, or chaotic commotion. A situation where there is a lot of noise, confusion, or disorder, often caused by people arguing, shouting, or reacting strongly. It is commonly used when something attracts sudden attention due to chaos or protest.
examples: The children created a ruckus in the classroom when the teacher left. A ruckus broke out in the market after the accident. Don’t make a ruckus over small issues. The loud music caused a ruckus in the neighborhood. His sudden complaint created a ruckus in the meeting. The neighbors made a ruckus late at night, disturbing everyone.

sindhiMeaning: لاش جو طبي معائنو جنهن سان موت جو سبب معلوم ڪيو وڃي، پوسٽ مارٽم معائنو، موت کان پوءِ جاچ، ڪنهن واقعي يا ناڪاميءَ جي گهري جاچ
urduMeaning: مردہ جسم کا طبی معائنہ جس سے موت کی وجہ معلوم کی جائے، پوسٹ مارٹم، موت کے بعد طبی جانچ، کسی واقعہ یا ناکامی کا گہرا تجزیہ
antonyms: Birth examination, Medical treatment, Revival, Resuscitation
examples: The doctor performed an autopsy to determine the exact cause of death. The police ordered an autopsy in the suspicious case. The autopsy report revealed no signs of poisoning. After the project failed, the team conducted an autopsy of their mistakes.
englishMeaning: A medical examination of a dead body to find the cause of death. Postmortem examination. Medical investigation after death. A detailed analysis of a failure or event to understand what went wrong.
synonyms: Necropsy, Medical examination after death

antonyms: Joyful, Cheerful, Delightful, Hopeful
englishMeaning: Causing sorrow, regret, or deep sadness. Something that makes a person feel remorse or emotional pain. An event, situation, or memory that causes emotional pain, sorrow, or a feeling of regret. It is often used for actions or outcomes that are deeply unfortunate and leave a lasting sense of remorse.
examples: The accident was a ruesome reminder of careless driving. He spoke about his past mistakes in a ruesome tone. Losing the village to floods was a ruesome experience for the community. The story ends on a ruesome note of regret and loss.
sindhiMeaning: ڏکائيندڙ يا افسوس پيدا ڪندڙ، اهڙي شيءِ جيڪا غم يا پڇتاءُ جو احساس پيدا ڪري
synonyms: Sorrowful, Regretful, Mournful, Sad
urduMeaning: افسوسناک یا غم انگیز، ایسی چیز جو دکھ یا پچھتاوے کا احساس پیدا کرے

englishMeaning: A violent or cruel person, A person who behaves in a rough, aggressive, and lawless way. Such a person often uses force, threats, or intimidation and shows no respect for others or social rules.
synonyms: Thug, Bully, Brute, Hoodlum, Gangster
examples: The ruffian attacked the shopkeeper without any reason. The police arrested the ruffian who was terrorizing the neighborhood. He was once a street ruffian but later changed his life. The movie portrayed the villain as a ruthless ruffian.
urduMeaning: غنڈا یا بدمعاش شخص، وہ شخص جو سخت مزاج تشدد پسند اور بدتمیز ہو، وہ اکثر طاقت یا دھمکی کے ذریعے دوسروں کو نقصان پہنچاتا ہے
antonyms: Gentleman, Law abiding person, Peacemaker, Civilian
sindhiMeaning: بدتميز ۽ ظالم ماڻهو، اهڙو ماڻهو جيڪو سخت جهيڙو ڪندڙ ۽ ظالم رويو رکي، هو اڪثر ٻين کي نقصان پهچائيندو يا ڊيڄاريندو آهي

urduMeaning: تباہی، تباہ کرنا ویران کرنا، زندگی برباد کرنا، افلاس، ویرانے، کھنڈر، زوال، بربادی
sindhiMeaning: اجاڙ، خانہ خرابي، زوال يا خاتمو، تباهي، بربادي، ستياناس، برباد ڪرڻ، تباهه ڪرڻ، ڦٽائڻ، ناس ڪرڻ، حُليو بگاڙڻ، کنڊر ڪري ڇڏڻ
antonyms: Recondition, Recover, Restore, Build, Construct, Construction
synonyms: Destroy, Devastate, Ravage, Scourge, Demolishment
examples: That one mistake ruined his chances of getting the job. The crops were ruined by the late frost. e ruined his new white slacks by accidentally spilling oil on them. The house went to rack and ruin. Drinking was his ruin.
englishMeaning: To damage something so badly that it loses all its value, pleasure, etc. To spoil or destroy something completely. To cause a person or company to lose all their money or their good reputation. The state or process of being destroyed or severely damaged.
Causing or likely to cause great damage, destruction, or loss. Extremely harmful to success, wealth, or health. Something that brings ruin (complete destruction or downfall)
antonyms: Beneficial, Helpful, Constructive, Profitable, Favorable, Productive
examples: The flood had a ruinous effect on the village. He suffered ruinous losses in the stock market. Their constant arguments had a ruinous impact on their marriage. The company went bankrupt after a ruinous decision by its management.
synonyms: Devastating, Destructive, Disastrous, Damaging, Catastrophic, Harmful, Fatal
urduMeaning: تباہ کن ، برباد کن ، نقصان دہ، خطرناک نتائج لانے والا
sindhiMeaning: تباه ڪندڙ، برباد ڪندڙ، نقصانڪار، ختم ڪندڙ، تباهي آڻيندڙ

antonyms: Rule out, Dismiss, Ignore, Exclude
sindhiMeaning: شامل ڪرڻ، قبول ڪرڻ، غور هيٺ آڻڻ
urduMeaning: شامل کرنا، ممکن سمجھنا، غور میں لینا
examples: The police ruled in theft as a motive. Doctors have ruled in infection as the cause of his illness. We cannot rule in John’s involvement until we have more evidence. The company has ruled in remote work for certain employees.
synonyms: Include, Consider, Take into account
englishMeaning: To include something or someone as a possibility or consideration. To decide that something should be considered as part of the explanation or decision.

antonyms: Join, Unite
englishMeaning: To end or conclude something. To draw a line to separate or end something. To mark off or close a section of writing, accounts, or a page.
sindhiMeaning: لڪير ڪڍي ڌار ڪرڻ (تحرير يا صفحي ۾ حصو ختم ڪرڻ لاءِ)، ڪنهن حصي کي ختم يا الڳ ڪرڻ، حساب يا تحرير کي بند ڪرڻ
examples: The teacher ruled off the section for notes. Please rule off the page before starting the next question. The accountant ruled off the account book at the end of the month. Let’s rule off this discussion and move to the next topic.
synonyms: Divide, Separate
urduMeaning: لکیر کھینچ کر الگ کرنا، لکیر کھینچنا، صفحہ بند کرنا، حساب مکمل کرنا
آئین باہر، زير غَور لانے سے اِنکار کَر دينا، خارِج کَر دينا ، نامَنظُور کَر دينا، رد کرنا، ممکنات سے نکال دینا
englishMeaning: To eliminate or exclude something as a possibility. To decide that something cannot happen, or is not suitable. To dismiss or reject an option, explanation, or person.
antonyms: Admit, Consider, Include, Allow
synonyms: Reject, Dismiss, Eliminate, Disregard
sindhiMeaning: بي قاعدي ٺهرائڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ کي امڪان مان ڪڍي ڇڏڻ، ڪنهن سبب يا اختيار کي رد ڪرڻ، ڪنهن ڳالهه کي ناممڪن قرار ڏيڻ، خارج ڪرڻ، رد ڪرڻ
examples: Police have not rule out the possibility that man was murdered. The proposed solution was ruled out as too expensive. A shoulder injury ruled him out for most of the season. We cannot rule out the chance of rain tomorrow. His lack of experience rules him out as a candidate for this job.

englishMeaning: To eliminate, exclude, or consider something as impossible. To decide that something cannot happen or someone cannot be chosen.
examples: His injury ruled him out of the game. The doctor ruled out cancer after seeing the test reports. His injury ruled him out of the final match.
synonyms: Exclude, Eliminate
antonyms: Include, Allow
sindhiMeaning: امڪان مان ٻاهر ڪرڻ، خارج ڪرڻ، رد ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: خارج کرنا ، رد کرنا ، امکان ختم کرنا

antonyms: Silence, Whisper, Quiet, Hide, Conceal, Cover
englishMeaning: To make a deep, low, continuous sound. To move while making such a sound. To discover or expose a secret plan. To fight or argue loudly. A deep rolling sound. A noisy fight or quarrel.
urduMeaning: بھاری اور مسلسل آواز پیدا کرنا، ایسے آواز کے ساتھ حرکت کرنا، کسی خفیہ بات یا منصوبے کو بے نقاب کرنا، زور دار جھگڑا کرنا، گونج دار گہرا آواز، شور والا جھگڑا
examples: Thunder began to rumble in the distance. The trucks rumbled along the rough road. The police finally rumbled the criminal gang. A rumble broke out between the two groups.
sindhiMeaning: ڳرو ۽ لڳاتار آواز ڪرڻ، اهڙي آواز سان هلڻ يا حرڪت ڪرڻ، ڪنهن لڪل ڳالهه يا راز کي پتو لڳائڻ، زور سان جهيڙو ڪرڻ، ڳرو گونجدار آواز، شور وارو جهيڙو
synonyms: Roar, Growl, Grumble, Boom, Detect, Expose, Uncover, Reveal

urduMeaning: اضافی، معاون، مددگار، امدادی ، ذيلی ، سود مند ، کار آمد، مرکزی کام یا عمل میں مدد یا تعاون فراہم کرنے والا، گرائمر میں معاون فعل مرکزی فعل کی صیغہ وقت یا انداز بنانے میں مدد دیتا ہے
examples: The hospital has an auxiliary power generator in case of outages. She works as an auxiliary nurse in the community clinic. In the sentence "She has gone," "has" is an auxiliary verb. The army called in auxiliary forces to support the main battalion.
sindhiMeaning: اضافي، مددگار، معاون، هٿ ونڊائيندڙ، سپورٽ ڪندڙ، مکيه ڪم کي مدد يا سپورٽ ڏيندڙ، اضافي يا سپليمنٽري ڪردار ۾ هجڻ، گرامر ۾مددگار فعل مکيه فعل جي وقت انداز يا صفت ٺاهڻ ۾ مدد ڪندو آهي
synonyms: Supportive, Supplementary, Backup, Subordinate
antonyms: Primary, Main, Principal, Independent
englishMeaning: Providing additional help or support. Something or someone that functions in a supportive or supplementary role, assisting the main function or operation. In grammar, an auxiliary verb helps the main verb to form tenses, moods, or voices.

antonyms: Non-ruminant, Carnivore, Meat-eating animal
englishMeaning: An animal that chews cud, such as cows and goats. A herbivorous animal that digests plant food in two steps. It first swallows the food, then brings it back to the mouth (cud) to chew it again for better digestion. Common examples include cows, buffaloes, sheep, and goats.
examples: A cow is a ruminant animal that chews cud. Sheep and goats are common ruminants found on farms. The farmer raised several ruminant animals for milk production. Ruminant digestion helps animals extract more nutrients from grass.
urduMeaning: جُگالی کَرنے والا جانوَر ، نِگلی ہُوئی غِذا خوراک کو دوبارَہ چَبانے کی صِفت سے مُتَصَّف ، ایسا جانور جو کھانا واپس منہ میں لا کر دوبارہ چباتا ہے، مثال کے طور پر گائے بکری اور بھیڑ، کبھی کبھی یہ لفظ ایسے شخص کے لیے بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے جو کسی بات پر بار بار غور کرتا رہے

urduMeaning: کسی چیز کی طرف تیزی سے جانا، اخراجات یا بل بڑھا لینا، کسی چیز کو جلدی بنانا یا تیار کرنا، جھنڈا یا علامت بلند کرنا
examples: He ran up the stairs to catch the train. They ran up a large phone bill last month. She ran up a beautiful dress for the party in one day. They ran up the national flag during the ceremony.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ کي تيزي سان ڪرڻ يا وڌائڻ، خرچ بل يا رقم کي وڌائڻ، ڪا شيءِ تيزي سان ٺاهڻ يا تيار ڪرڻ، جهنڊو يا نشاني مٿي ڪرڻ
synonyms: Increase, Furry, Raise, Accumulate, Prepare, Ascend

antonyms: Reject, Abandon, Neglect, Dismiss
synonyms: Continue, Act on
examples: She liked my idea and decided to run with it. Once you get a good plan, you should run with it immediately. The coach told the players to run with the new strategy. He got a small opportunity and really ran with it to build his career.
urduMeaning: ساتھ چلنا یا کسی خیال، منصوبے یا موقعے کو آگے بڑھانا، (کسی بات یا خیال کو قبول کرکے عمل میں لانا)
sindhiMeaning: يا ڪنهن ڳالهه کي اڳتي وڌائڻ، گڏ هلڻ يا ڪنهن خيال يا موقعي کي اڳتي وڌائڻ، ڪنهن خيال، تجويز يا موقعو کي اڳتي وڌائڻ

antonyms: Aftermath, Decline, Fall, Decrease, Drop, Slowdown
urduMeaning: تیاری کا عرصہ، پیشگی دور، دوڑ کا فاصلہ، اچانک اضافہ
sindhiMeaning: تياريءَ جو دور، اڳواٽ جو وقت، وڌڻ يا تيزيءَ سان وڌندڙ حالت، ڊوڙ لاءِ وٺايل فاصلو
englishMeaning: The time before an event or an increase in something.
synonyms: Preparation period, Buildup, Approach, Increase, Advance, Rise
examples: The company worked hard in the run-up to the product launch. The cricketer took a long run-up before bowling. There was a sharp run-up in fuel prices last month. Students were busy studying in the run-up to their exams.

synonyms: Break, Tear, Burst, Split, Fracture, Sever
urduMeaning: اچانک پھٹنا یا ٹوٹنا، کسی چیز یا جسم کے حصے کا زور سے پھٹ جانا، لوگوں یا گروہوں کے درمیان تعلقات کا ٹوٹ جانا، عضو کا اندرونی پھٹ جانا، معمول کے تسلسل میں اچانک خلل، دھماکے کی طرح پھٹ جانا، جذباتی ٹوٹ پھوٹ
sindhiMeaning: اوچتو ڦاٽڻ يا ٽٽڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ يا جسم جي حصي جو زور سان ڦاٽڻ، ماڻهن يا ڌرين وچ ۾ لاڳاپن جو ختم ٿيڻ، عضوي جي اندروني ڦاٽ، عام وهڪري يا تسلسل ۾ اوچتو خلل، ڌماڪي جهڙو ڦاٽڻ، جذباتي ٽٽڻ
examples: The pipe ruptured after the pressure increased. A rupture developed between the two business partners. The athlete suffered a muscle rupture during training. The earthquake caused a rupture in the ground.
englishMeaning: To break or burst suddenly. Sudden break, tear, or failure. A forceful split in an object or body tissue. Serious ending of relations between people or groups. Interruption in normal flow or continuity. Explosion like burst. Emotional breakdown.
antonyms: Repair, Join, Mend, Fix, Heal, Connect

sindhiMeaning: تڪڙو نڪري وڃڻ، فوري طور ٻئي هنڌ وڃڻ، ڪم پورو ڪرڻ کان اڳ جلدي هلي وڃڻ، هنگامي حالت سبب تڪڙو وڃڻ، اهم ڪم لاءِ جلدي ٻاهر وڃڻ
antonyms: Stay, Remain, Linger, Wait, Delay
synonyms: Hurry away, Dash off, Run off, Leave quickly, Bolt, Speed away
urduMeaning: جلدی میں نکل جانا، فوراً کسی اور جگہ چلے جانا، کام مکمل کیے بغیر جلدی روانہ ہونا، ہنگامی صورتحال میں فوراً نکل جانا، اہم کام کے لیے جلدی نکلنا
englishMeaning: To leave quickly or suddenly because of urgency. To depart in a hurry without delay. To go somewhere immediately after finishing something. To leave before proper completion due to urgency. o suddenly move away because of an emergency.
examples: She had to rush off to catch the bus. He rushed off after receiving an urgent call. They rushed off without saying goodbye. I must rush off now because my meeting is starting.

synonyms: Corrosion, Oxidation, Tarnish, Corrode, Decay, Deteriorate
examples: Brass doesn't rust. Water had got in & rusted the engine. Pipes covered with rust. The old gate was covered in rust. Iron tools rust quickly in humid weather. His skills began to rust after years without practice. The bike chain will rust if you leave it in the rain.
englishMeaning: To decay due to oxidation. A reddish-brown coating that forms on iron due to moisture and air. A chemical reaction that happens when iron or steel is exposed to water and oxygen. It forms a flaky reddish-brown substance that weakens the metal.
sindhiMeaning: زنگ لڳڻ يا زنگ سبب خراب ٿيڻ، لوھ تي لڳندڙ ڳاڙهو زنگ، وقت سان بگاڙ يا زوال، مهارت ۾ گهٽتائي، ڪيميائي عمل جيڪو لوھ يا اسٽيل تي پاڻي ۽ هوا جي اثر سبب پيدا ٿئي ٿو، اهو ڳاڙهو ڀورو مادو بڻجي ٿو جيڪو ڌاتو کي ڪمزور ڪري ٿو
antonyms: Polish, Protect, Preserve, Maintain, Strengthen
urduMeaning: زنگ لگ جانا یا زنگ کی وجہ سے خراب ہونا، زنگ، کیمیائی عمل جو لوہے یا اسٹیل پر پانی اور ہوا کے اثر سے پیدا ہوتا ہے، یہ سرخی مائل بھورا مادہ بنتا ہے جو دھات کو کمزور کر دیتا ہے، وقت کے ساتھ بگاڑ یا زوال، مہارت میں کمی

examples: Because of her aviophobia, she always chooses to travel by train instead of plane. His aviophobia became worse after experiencing severe turbulence. Therapy helped her manage aviophobia and fly again with confidence. Many people with aviophobia feel anxious days before their flight.
synonyms: Fear of flying, Aerophobia
urduMeaning: ہوائی سفر یا پرواز کا شدید خوف، ایک نفسیاتی خوف جس میں انسان کو جہاز میں سفر کرنے یا اس کے بارے میں سوچنے سے بھی شدید گھبراہٹ محسوس ہوتی ہے، یہ خوف بے چینی یا ماضی کے منفی تجربات کی وجہ سے ہو سکتا ہے
antonyms: Love of flying, Aviophilia
englishMeaning: Fear of flying in an aircraft. An anxiety disorder in which a person experiences intense fear or panic when flying or even thinking about air travel. This fear may be linked to heights, loss of control, turbulence, or past negative experiences.
sindhiMeaning: هوائي سفر جو شديد خوف يا اُڏام کان ڊپ، اهڙو خوف جنهن ۾ ماڻهو جهاز ۾ سفر ڪرڻ يا اڏام بابت سوچي به گهٻرائجي وڃي ٿو، هي خوف گهڻو ڪري ذهني پريشاني يا خراب تجربي سبب ٿيندو آهي

synonyms: Sword, Cutlass, Scimitar, Blade
examples: The soldier drew his saber and charged forward. In the museum, we saw an ancient saber used by Mughal warriors. The general’s saber was decorated with gold and precious stones. The two officers crossed sabers in a duel. The soldier tried to saber his opponent in battle.
antonyms: Shield, Peace, Dagger
englishMeaning: To strike or wound someone with a sword. It refers to attacking using a curved sword. A type of sword with a curved blade, usually used by soldiers or in cavalry combat. It is designed for cutting and slashing rather than stabbing.
sindhiMeaning: تلوار سان وار ڪرڻ يا زخمي ڪرڻ، تلوار، تڙڦندڙ تلوار، مڙيل ڌار واري تلوار، شمشير، ڌاريدار تلوار
urduMeaning: تلوار سے وار کرنا ،تلوار چلانا، شمشیر تلوار، خم دار تلوار
توڑ پھوڑ، کلوں اور دوسرے سامان کو خراب کرنا، شرارت سے کام خراب کرنا، تخریب کاری، خفیہ طور پر نظام کو کمزور کرنا، کسی کی کوششوں کو جان بوجھ کر ناکام بنانا، ترقی میں نقصان دہ رکاوٹ ڈالنا
synonyms: Damage, Destroy, Undermine, Disrupt, Ruin, Obstruct
englishMeaning: To secretly weaken or disrupt operations. To ruin someone’s efforts intentionally. To interfere with progress in a harmful way. Deliberate damage or obstruction to something. Intentionally damaging, destroying, or interfering with something such as work, plans, systems, or equipment, often for personal, political, or strategic reasons.
examples: The main electricity supply had been sabotaged by the rebels. Police investigating the train derailment have not rules out sabotage. Someone tried to sabotage the company’s project by leaking confidential information. The mechanic was accused of sabotaging the engine. He sabotaged his own success by not preparing for the interview. During the conflict, bridges were sabotaged to stop enemy movement.
sindhiMeaning: توڙ ڦوڙ، تخريبڪاري، تباهڪاري، ڀڃڻ ڊاهڻ، تباھ ڪرڻ، بگاڙڻ، بيڪار ڪرڻ، ڪم کان وڃائڻ، ڄاڻي واڻي نقصان يا رڪاوٽ پيدا ڪرڻ، لڪي ڪمزور ڪرڻ يا بگاڙڻ، ڄاڻي واڻي خراب ڪرڻ، ترقي ۾ نقصانڪار رڪاوٽ وجهڻ
antonyms: Support, Help, Assist, Protect, Promote, Strengthen

synonyms: Sword, Cutlass, Scimitar, Blade
examples: The cavalry charged forward, their sabres shining in the sunlight. He wore a sabre as part of his ceremonial uniform. The soldier drew his sabre to defend himself. In the museum, we saw an ancient sabre used in the 18th century. His face was seamed with sabre cuts.
sindhiMeaning: تلوار سان وار ڪرڻ يا زخمي ڪرڻ، تلوار، تڙڦندڙ تلوار، مڙيل ڌار واري تلوار، شمشير، ڌاريدار تلوار
urduMeaning: تلوار سے وار کرنا، تلوار چلانا، شمشیر تلوار، خم دار تلوار
englishMeaning: To strike or wound someone with a sword. It refers to attacking using a curved sword. A type of sword with a curved blade, usually used by soldiers or in cavalry combat. It is designed for cutting and slashing rather than stabbing.
antonyms: Shield, Peace, Dagger

synonyms: Dismiss, Bag, Fire, Terminate, Plunder, Looting
sindhiMeaning: ٻوري، ڳوڻ، ٿيلهي، ڳوٿري، ٻورو، سامان رکڻ لاءِ وڏو ٿيلهو، نوڪري مان ڪڍڻ، برطرفي، برخاستگي، لٽ مار، شهر جي تباهي، ڦرلٽ، ڌاڙو هڻڻ، لُٽڻ ڦرڻ
examples: The farmer carried a sack of wheat. She feared the sack after the mistake. Many workers received the sack. The manager sacked two employees. The sack caused great damage. The army carried out the sack of the city.
urduMeaning: بورا، بڑا تھیلا جس میں سامان رکھا جائے، ملازمت سے نکالنا، برطرفی، تباہ کرنا، لوٹ مار کرنا، شہر کی تباہی
englishMeaning: To dismiss someone from a job. A large bag made of strong material used for storing or carrying goods. Removal from a job. Plundering of a place.
antonyms: Spare, Indemnify, Protect, Hire, Appoint, Employ, Container

sindhiMeaning: پاڪ، مقدس، مذهب سان واسطو رڪندڙ، واجب الاحترام، تعظيم لائق، حرمت وارو، پاڪيزه، تقدس وارو، عزت لائق، وڏي عزت ۽ حفاظت جو حقدار، تمام اهم يا قيمتي
englishMeaning: Holy, religiously important, deserving respect. Connected with religion or spiritual beliefs, considered holy. Deserving great respect and protection. Dedicated to a divine being or religious purpose. Deeply valued or important in a personal sense.
antonyms: Profane, Unholy, Secular, Ordinary, Impure
synonyms: Holy, Divine, Blessed, Consecrated, Revered, Hallowed
urduMeaning: پاک، مقدس، متبرک، واجب التعظیم، معظم، حرمت والا، پاکیزہ، قابلِ تعظیم، قابلِ احترام، ہت زیادہ احترام اور حفاظت کے قابل، نہایت اہم یا قیمتی
examples: The temple is a sacred place for worship. Many people consider the river sacred. He kept the book in a sacred space in his home. Trust between friends is sacred.

antonyms: Reverence, Respect, Devotion, Veneration
urduMeaning: مقدس چیز کی بے حرمتی، کسی مقدس چیز جگہ عقیدہ یا رسم کی بے حرمتی کرنا یا اسے ناحق استعمال کرنا
englishMeaning: Disrespect or violation of something sacred or holy. An act that shows disrespect toward a sacred object, place, or belief. It can involve desecration, misuse, or offensive treatment of something regarded as holy.
sindhiMeaning: مقدس شيء جو بي حرمتي يا توهين، ڪنهن مقدس شيءَ جڳھه يا ريت کي بي عزتي ڪرڻ يا کيس غلط طريقي سان استعمال ڪرڻ
examples: Stealing from the church is considered a sacrilege. Many saw the vandalism of the ancient temple as a sacrilege. It would be a sacrilege to disrespect the traditions of the ceremony. Painting over the historic mural was viewed as sacrilege by the community.
synonyms: Desecration, Profanation, Blasphemy, Violation, Irreverence

englishMeaning: Treated as extremely important and not to be questioned or changed. Something regarded as holy, inviolable, or beyond criticism because of tradition, belief, law, or deep respect.
urduMeaning: نہایت مقدس اور ناقابلِ سوال، ایسی چیز جسے بہت زیادہ احترام حاصل ہو اور جس پر تنقید یا تبدیلی کو ناجائز سمجھا جائے
antonyms: Profane, Ordinary, Changeable, Disregarded, Violable
synonyms: Sacred, Holy, Inviolable, Untouchable, Revered
sindhiMeaning: تمام گهڻو مقدس ۽ ناقابلِ تبديلي، اهڙي شيءِ جنهن کي مقدس سمجهيو وڃي ۽ جنهن تي اعتراض يا تبديلي قبول نه هجي
examples: Freedom of speech is considered sacrosanct in many democratic societies. The judge treated the confidentiality of the jury as sacrosanct. For the community, the ancient shrine was sacrosanct and untouchable. He believed that family traditions were sacrosanct and must be preserved.

urduMeaning: دوسروں کو تکلیف یا درد دینے میں خوشی محسوس کرنا، ایک نفسیاتی کیفیت یا رویہ جس میں انسان دوسروں کو جسمانی یا ذہنی تکلیف دینے سے خوشی یا تسکین حاصل کرتا ہے، یہ کبھی ہلکی چھیڑ چھاڑ کی شکل میں اور کبھی شدید ظلم یا تشدد کی صورت میں ظاہر ہوتا ہے
englishMeaning: Enjoying causing pain, suffering, or humiliation to others. A psychological condition or behavior in which a person derives pleasure, satisfaction, or excitement from causing physical or emotional pain to others. It can appear in mild forms like teasing or controlling behavior, or in severe cases as cruelty or abuse.
antonyms: Kindness, Compassion, Mercy, Sympathy, Humanity, Gentleness
synonyms: Cruelty, Brutality, Viciousness, Harshness, Inhumanity, Callousness
sindhiMeaning: ايذا پسندي، ايذائيندڙ، ٻين کي تڪليف يا درد ڏيڻ مان خوشي حاصل ڪرڻ، اهڙو رويو يا نفسياتي حالت جنهن ۾ ماڻهو ٻين کي جسماني يا ذهني تڪليف ڏيڻ مان خوشي يا اطمينان حاصل ڪري، ڪڏهن ڪڏهن اهو هلڪي مذاق يا تنگ ڪرڻ جي صورت ۾ هوندو آهي ۽ ڪڏهن سخت ظلم يا تشدد جي صورت ۾
examples: His sadism made him enjoy seeing others suffer in games. The villain showed sadism in the way he treated prisoners. She was shocked by his sadism toward animals. The report described the guard’s sadism during the interrogation.

antonyms: Kind person, Compassionate person, Empathetic person, Humanitarian, Gentle person
englishMeaning: A person who enjoys causing pain, suffering, or humiliation to others. Someone who gains pleasure, excitement, or satisfaction from inflicting physical or emotional pain on others. It can be psychological (emotional cruelty) or physical harm. The term is often used in psychology or to describe extremely cruel behavior.
examples: The sadist enjoyed watching others suffer. He was labeled a sadist because of his cruel behavior toward animals. In the story, the villain behaves like a sadist. No one wanted to work under such a sadist manager.
urduMeaning: اذیت پسند، وہ شخص جو دوسروں کو درد یا تکلیف پہنچانے میں خوشی محسوس کرے، وہ شخص جو دوسروں کو جسمانی یا ذہنی تکلیف دے کر خوشی حاصل کرتا ہے، یہ رویہ نفسیاتی طور پر غیر صحت مند سمجھا جاتا ہے
synonyms: Cruel person, Tormentor, Abuser, Oppressor, Tyrant (in behavioral sense)
sindhiMeaning: ايذا پسند، رنج تڪليف ڏيندڙ، اهڙو شخص جيڪو ٻين کي تڪليف يا اذيت ڏيڻ مان مزو وٺي، اهو ماڻهو جيڪو ٻين کي جسماني يا ذهني تڪليف ڏئي خوشي محسوس ڪري، اهڙو رويو نفسياتي طور تي غير صحتمند سمجهيو ويندو آهي

urduMeaning: چَچا، مامُوں، پھُوپھَا، وستانہ اور مہربان رویہ رکھنے والا، مددگار اور دوستانہ، شفقت اور مدد فراہم کرنے والا، نوجوانوں کے لیے رہنمائی کرنے والا اور نرم دل، دوستانہ معاون اور قابل اعتماد رویہ رکھنے والا
examples: His avuncular smile made the new students feel instantly at ease. The professor had an avuncular approach, always encouraging students to ask questions. She enjoyed the avuncular advice of her elder colleague. His avuncular gestures made everyone in the office trust him naturally.
synonyms: Uncle-like, Friendly, Kind, Supportive, Warm, Affectionate
sindhiMeaning: ماما، چاچا، پيار ڪندڙ، مهربان، هدايت ڏيندڙ، دوستاڻو ۽ مددگار، پيار ۽ همدردي ڏيکارڻ وارو، نوجوانن سان مهربان، مددگار ۽ مشوري ڏيندڙ، نرم دل، ڀروسو جوڳو ۽ دوستاڻو رويو
antonyms: Hostile, Cold, Unfriendly, Indifferent, Harsh
englishMeaning: Showing kindness, friendliness, or generosity in a way that resembles a caring uncle. Often implies a supportive, warm, and guiding demeanor. Characteristic of an uncle; kind and indulgent. Supportive, mentoring, and protective behavior toward younger people. Gentle, approachable, and trustworthy in demeanor.

antonyms: Kind, Compassionate, Gentle, Humane, Caring, Sympathetic, Merciful
urduMeaning: دوسروں کو تکلیف یا اذیت دے کر خوشی حاصل کرنا، وہ شخص جو دوسروں کو جسمانی یا ذہنی تکلیف دے کر خوشی محسوس کرے یا ان کی تکلیف دیکھ کر مزہ لے، ظلم اور سختی سے لطف اندوز ہونا، دوسروں کو ذلیل یا خوفزدہ کرنے میں خوشی محسوس کرنا
sindhiMeaning: ٻين کي تڪليف يا ڏک ڏئي خوشي حاصل ڪرڻ، اهو ماڻهو جيڪو ٻين کي جسماني يا ذهني تڪليف ڏئي خوشي محسوس ڪري، ظلم ۽ سختي مان مزو وٺڻ، ٻين کي هيٺ ڏيکارڻ يا تڪليف ڏيڻ مان خوشي حاصل ڪرڻ
englishMeaning: Getting pleasure from causing pain, suffering, or humiliation to others. A person who enjoys hurting others physically or emotionally, or who takes pleasure in seeing others suffer or be controlled harshly.
synonyms: Cruel, Brutal, Vicious, Heartless, Inhuman, Ruthless, Harsh, Abusive
examples: The sadistic guard enjoyed punishing the prisoners harshly. He showed sadistic behavior when he laughed at others’ pain. The villain in the story was portrayed as sadistic and cruel. No teacher should ever act in a sadistic way toward students.

antonyms: Foolish, Ignorant, Naive, Thoughtless, Unwise
urduMeaning: دانشمند، عقلمند، ہوشیار، ایسا شخص جو عقل فہم اور تجربے کے ساتھ دانشمندی سے فیصلے کرتا ہے
englishMeaning: Having or showing good judgment and keen mental insight. Wise, intelligent, and able to make sensible decisions. Someone who understands situations deeply and acts wisely.
sindhiMeaning: دانشمند، عقل مند، سمجھدار، اهڙو ماڻهو جيڪو گهري سوچ تجربي ۽ دانشمندي سان فيصلا ڪري، سگھڙو، هوشيار، اهڙو شخص جنهن وٽ حالتن کي سمجهڻ ۽ صحيح فيصلو ڪرڻ جي صلاحيت هجي

examples: He sarcastically thanked her for being late again. She sarcastically said, "What a perfect day," when it started raining. He smiled sarcastically after hearing the unfair decision. "Great job," he said sarcastically when the computer crashed.
