urduMeaning: طنزیہ انداز میں، مذاق یا تضحیک کے ساتھ، یہ لفظ اس وقت استعمال ہوتا ہے جب کوئی شخص ظاہری طور پر کچھ کہے لیکن اس کا اصل مطلب اس کے برعکس ہو، عام طور پر مذاق تنقید یا ناراضی ظاہر کرنے کے لئے

examples: She gave a sassy reply to the teacher’s question. The little girl wore a sassy hat that caught everyone’s attention. He walked into the room with a sassy grin. Her sassy attitude makes her very popular among friends.
urduMeaning: جرات مند، چالاک، پرکشش اور کبھی کبھی تھوڑا گستاخ یا شرارتی
synonyms: Bold, Cheeky, Lively, Spirited, Saucy
antonyms: Shy, Timid, Reserved, Modest, Quiet
englishMeaning: Bold, lively, and cheeky in a confident way. Showing a lively, confident, and sometimes slightly disrespectful attitude; often playful and spirited.
sindhiMeaning: چُست ۽ ڀرپور خوداعتمادي سان، ٿورو شرارتي ۽ بي باڪ

مذاقي تنقيد، سماجي مسئلن تي طنزيه حملو، اڻسڌي اخلاقي يا سياسي اظهار، طنزيه انداز يا لکڻ جو طريقو جنهن ۾ مذاق يا تنقيد ذريعي خاميون ظاهر ڪيون وڃن، اهڙو ادبي يا فني انداز جنهن ۾ مزاح طنز يا مبالغو استعمال ڪري ماڻهن سماج يا ادارن جي ڪمزورين بيوقوفي يا برائين کي ظاهر ڪيو ويندو آهي، اهو سڌي تنقيد بدران اڻسڌي نموني سان پيغام ڏئي ٿو
englishMeaning: A style of writing or expression that uses humor, irony, or exaggeration to criticize people, society, or ideas. A literary or artistic form used to expose and criticize foolishness, corruption, or weaknesses in individuals, institutions, or society. It often uses humor, irony, sarcasm, or exaggeration to make serious points in an indirect way.
antonyms: Praise, Flattery, Compliment
synonyms: Parody, Irony, Lampoon, Mockery, Ridicule
urduMeaning: تمسخر آمیز تنقید، معاشرتی مسائل پر طنزیہ حملہ، بالواسطہ اخلاقی یا سیاسی تبصرہ، طنزیہ انداز یا تحریر جس میں مزاح طنز یا مبالغہ کے ذریعے معاشرے یا افراد کی برائیوں کو ظاہر کیا جائے، ایک ادبی یا فنی انداز جس میں مزاح طنز یا مبالغہ کے ذریعے افراد معاشرے یا اداروں کی کمزوریوں حماقتوں یا برائیوں کو ظاہر کیا جاتا ہے، یہ براہ راست تنقید کے بجائے بالواسطہ انداز میں پیغام دیتا ہے
examples: The novel Animal Farm is a satire on totalitarian regimes. His speech was full of satire about political corruption. The cartoonist used satire to comment on social inequality. Satire can make serious issues more approachable through humor.

antonyms: Sincere, Serious, Literal, Respectful, Straightforward
englishMeaning: A style or approach that exposes human vices, follies, or social issues through wit, irony, ridicule, or sarcasm. Often found in literature, cartoons, speeches, and media.
urduMeaning: خامیوں یا برائیوں پر طنز، مزاح یا مبالغہ آرائی کے ذریعے روشنی ڈالنا، سیاست یا روایات کی نقاد کرنا، لوگوں یا اداروں کی منافقت یا بی معنی رویوں کو ظاہر کرنا، مزاحیہ انداز میں سنجیدہ پیغام پہنچانا
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن جي غلطي يا نقص کي طنز يا مذاق سان ظاهر ڪرڻ، رياستي پاليسين يا رواجن تي طنزيه تبصرو ڪرڻ، ماڻهن يا ادارن جي منافقت يا بي معنيٰ عملن کي نمايان ڪرڻ، مذاق سان گڏ اهم پيغام پهچائڻ
examples: The cartoonist’s satirical drawings criticized political leaders. His satirical novel exposed the absurdities of society. The comedian made a satirical remark about the government’s new policy. Satirical articles often provoke thought as well as laughter.
synonyms: Ironical, Mocking, Sarcastic, Ridiculing, Witty

englishMeaning: To soak something thoroughly with liquid until no more can be absorbed. To fill something completely with a substance, feeling, color, sound, or influence. To supply a market or place with so much of something that it cannot take any more. In chemistry, to combine a substance with the maximum amount of another substance. To fill completely so that it is impossible or useless to add any more.
synonyms: Soak, Drench, Flood, Permeate, Fill, Impregnate
examples: Heavy rain saturated the soil within a few hours. The room was saturated with the smell of perfume. The company saturated the market with its new product. His speech was saturated with emotion.
urduMeaning: سيراب کَرنا، کسی چیز کو اس قدر بھگو دینا کہ وہ مزید پانی جذب نہ کر سکے، کسی جگہ یا ماحول کو کسی چیز سے مکمل طور پر بھر دینا، مارکیٹ میں کسی شے کو اتنی زیادہ مقدار میں فراہم کرنا کہ مزید ضرورت نہ رہے، کیمیا میں کسی مادے کو دوسرے مادے کے ساتھ مکمل طور پر ملا دینا
antonyms: Dry, Dehydrate, Drain, Empty, Reduce
sindhiMeaning: شاداب ڪرڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ کي ايترو ڀڄائڻ جو اها وڌيڪ پاڻي يا مايع جذب نه ڪري سگهي، ڪنهن جاءِ يا ماحول کي مڪمل طور ڪنهن شيءِ سان ڀري ڇڏڻ، بازار ۾ ڪا شيءِ ايتري مقدار ۾ آڻڻ جو وڌيڪ گنجائش نه رهي، ڪيميا ۾ ڪنهن مادّي کي ٻي مادّي سان مڪمل طور ملائڻ

englishMeaning: A condition in which no more of something can be added, absorbed, or accepted. It is used in different fields such as chemistry, physics, marketing, photography, medicine, and everyday language. It may describe physical absorption, emotional overload, color intensity, or market supply reaching its limit.
antonyms: Dryness, Emptiness, Scarcity, Deficiency, Depletion
urduMeaning: وہ حالت جب کوئی چیز مزید جذب یا قبول نہ کر سکے اور مکمل طور پر بھر جائے، یہ لفظ کیمیا طبیعیات مارکیٹنگ فوٹوگرافی طب اور عام زندگی میں استعمال ہوتا ہے، یہ جسمانی جذب جذباتی دباؤ رنگ کی شدت یا مارکیٹ میں حد سے زیادہ فراہمی کو ظاہر کر سکتا ہے
synonyms: Fullness, Soaking, Immersion, Supersaturation, Overload, Intensity
examples: After hours of heavy rain, the soil reached saturation. The market showed signs of saturation due to too many similar products. Increase the color saturation to make the image look brighter. The doctor checked the patient’s oxygen saturation level.
sindhiMeaning: اُھا حالت جڏهن ڪا شيءِ وڌيڪ جذب يا قبول نه ٿي سگهي ۽ مڪمل ڀرجي وڃي، هي لفظ ڪيمسٽري طبعيات مارڪيٽنگ فوٽوگرافي طب ۽ عام زندگي ۾ استعمال ٿيندو آهي، اهو جسماني جذب ٿيڻ احساسن جي گهڻائي رنگن جي تيزي يا مارڪيٽ ۾ سامان جي گهڻائي کي ظاهر ڪري سگهي ٿو

examples: I relaxed in the sauna after exercise. The hotel has a sauna and swimming pool. Doctors say sauna helps reduce stress. He spent ten minutes inside the sauna.
urduMeaning: گرم بھاپ والا کمرہ جہاں پسینہ نکالنے کے لیے بیٹھتے ہیں، ایک چھوٹا گرم کمرہ جس میں خشک یا بھاپ والی گرمی پیدا کی جاتی ہے، لوگ اس میں بیٹھ کر پسینہ نکالتے ہیں آرام کرتے ہیں اور صحت بہتر کرتے ہیں
synonyms: Steam bath, Hot room, Sweat bath, Bathhouse
antonyms: Cold room, Ice bath, Cooling room, Cold shower
englishMeaning: A small heated room used for relaxation and sweating. A small room or building designed to produce dry or wet heat. People sit inside to sweat, relax muscles, and improve circulation.
sindhiMeaning: گرم ٻاڦ وارو ڪمرو جتي ماڻهو پسڻ لاءِ ويهندا آهن، هڪ ننڍڙو گرم ڪمرو جنهن ۾ خشڪ يا ٻاڦ واري گرمي پيدا ڪئي ويندي آهي، ماڻهو ان ۾ ويهي پسڻ آرام ڪرڻ ۽ صحت بهتر ڪرڻ لاءِ استعمال ڪندا آهن

examples: I had a grilled sausage for breakfast. The butcher made fresh sausages this morning. Sausages are often served with bread or mustard. She prefers chicken sausage over pork sausage.
englishMeaning: A food made from ground meat, often mixed with spices, and usually enclosed in a skin or casing. A preparation of ground meat such as pork, beef, or chicken, combined with fat, salt, spices, and sometimes fillers like breadcrumbs. It is typically stuffed into a casing made of intestine or synthetic material and can be cooked by frying, grilling, or boiling. Sausages can be fresh, cured, smoked, or cooked.
urduMeaning: گوشت سے تیار کردہ کھاناعام طور پر مصالحہ کے ساتھ اور خول میں بند، ایک قسم کا کھانا ہے جو قیمہ کیا ہوا گوشت جیسے سور گائے یا مرغی سے تیار کیا جاتا ہے اس میں چربی نمک مصالحہ اور کبھی کبھار فلرز شامل کیے جاتے ہیں اسے عام طور پر آنت یا مصنوعی خول میں بھرا جاتا ہے اور تل کر، گرل کر کے یا اُبال کر پکایا جا سکتا ہے ساسج تازہ، خشک یا دھواں دار بھی ہو سکتا ہے
sindhiMeaning: گوشت جو ٺهيل کاڌو عام طور تي ٿورو مصالحو سان ڀريل ۽ ڦرڻ ۾ رکيل، هڪ قسم جو کاڌو جيڪو ڪٽيل گوشت جهڙوڪ سور گئون يا ڪڪڙ مان تيار ڪيو ويندو آهي ان ۾ چرٻي لوڻ مصالحا ۽ ڪڏهن ڪڏهن بغير مصالحو جي اضافو ڪيو ويندو آهي، ان کي عام طور تي ڦرڻ يا ڪيسنگ ۾ ڀريو ويندو آهي ۽ تلڻ گرل ڪرڻ يا اُبالڻ سان تيار ڪيو ويندو آهي ساسج تازو، خشڪ يا دُھيمو ڪري تيار ڪري سگهجي ٿو
synonyms: Frankfurter, Wiener, Bratwurst, Banger
antonyms: Vegetarian patty
Adult
sindhiMeaning: ٻار، تجربو کان خالي، سادو ماڻهو، ننڍڙو ٻار جيڪو اڃا ڳچ ۾ کڻبو هجي
urduMeaning: شیر خوار بچہ، گود کا بچہ، نابالغ یا کم عمر بچہ، ناتجربہ کار، معصوم شخص
examples: When he joined the company, he was just a babe in arms compared to the senior managers. She’s no babe in arms when it comes to politics, she knows exactly what she’s doing. The young mother looked tired while holding her babe in arms.
englishMeaning: An infant, A very young baby who is still carried in the arms. A person who is very inexperienced, immature, or naïve.
synonyms: Infant, Baby

englishMeaning: A highly knowledgeable or learned person, especially in a specific field. A person with deep and exceptional knowledge in a particular subject. It can also refer to someone with a condition known as savant syndrome, where a person has remarkable abilities in areas like mathematics, music, or memory despite developmental differences.
antonyms: Ignorant person, Novice, Beginner, Amateur
urduMeaning: کسی خاص علم یا فن میں ماہر یا بہت زیادہ علم رکھنے والا شخص، ایساشخص جو کسی خاص شعبے میں غیر معمولی علم یا مہارت رکھتا ہو، یہ لفظ ان افراد کے لیے بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے جن میں خاص ذہنی حالت کے باوجود غیر معمولی صلاحیتیں ہوتی ہیں جیسے یادداشت یا ریاضی میں مہارت
examples: He is considered a savant in the field of mathematics. The young boy amazed everyone as a musical savant. She became a savant in environmental science after years of research. The documentary featured a savant with incredible memory skills.
synonyms: Scholar, Expert, Genius, Intellectual, Specialist
sindhiMeaning: وڏو عالم يا ڪنهن خاص علم ۾ ماهر ماڻهو، اهڙو شخص جيڪو ڪنهن خاص شعبي ۾ تمام گهڻو ڄاڻو ۽ ماهر هجي، ڪڏهن ڪڏهن اهو لفظ اهڙن ماڻهن لاءِ به استعمال ٿيندو آهي جن وٽ غيرمعمولي صلاحيتون هونديون آهن جهڙوڪ يادگيري يا حساب ۾ مهارت

synonyms: Keep in reserve, Put aside, Store up, Set aside, Save up
englishMeaning: To keep money, resources, or something valuable for future use in times of trouble or need. It means being prepared for unexpected difficulties or hard times.
examples: You should save some money for a rainy day in case you lose your job. She always saves a part of her salary for a rainy day. My parents taught me to save for a rainy day because life is unpredictable. He invested wisely to have funds saved for a rainy day.
urduMeaning: مشکل وقت کے لئے بچانا، کسی مشکل یا ضرورت کے وقت کے لیے پیسے یا چیزیں سنبھال کر رکھنا
sindhiMeaning: مشڪل لاءِ بچت ڪرڻ، مشڪل وقت يا تڪليف واري حالت لاءِ ڪجهه شيون يا پيسا بچائڻ
antonyms: Spend freely, Waste, Squander, Misuse

englishMeaning: To form a crust over a wound. To become rough or covered with patches. To work in place of striking workers. A hard dry layer that forms over a cut or wound during healing. A person who refuses to join a strike or who works during a strike. A skin disease causing rough crusty patches. Dirt, rust, or rough patch on a surface.
antonyms: Smooth skin, Healed skin, Union supporter, Clean surface
urduMeaning: زخم پر تہہ بن جانا، سطح کا کھردرا ہونا، ہڑتال کرنے والوں کی جگہ کام کرنا، زخم پر بننے والی خشک تہہ، ہڑتال کے دوران کام کرنے والا شخص، جلد کی بیماری جس میں کھردرے دھبے ہوں، سطح پر زنگ یا کھردرا نشان
synonyms: Crust, Scale, Flake, Scar layer, Strikebreaker, Rough patch
sindhiMeaning: زخم تي ٺهندڙ سڪل تهه، هڙتال دوران ڪم ڪندڙ ماڻهو، چمڙي جي بيماري جنهن ۾ خشڪ داغ ٿين، مٿاڇري تي خشڪ يا کُردرو نشان، زخم تي تهه ٺهڻ، مٿاڇري جو کُردرو ٿيڻ، هڙتال ڪندڙن جي جاءِ تي ڪم ڪرڻ
examples: The scab on his knee fell off after a week. Do not pick the scab or the wound will bleed again. Workers were angry at the scabs who crossed the picket line. The metal pipe had scabs of rust on it.

englishMeaning: Covered with scabs, dirty, or mean. Having scabs on the skin because of healing wounds or disease. Untidy, filthy, or poorly maintained. Mean, stingy, or contemptible person. A worker who refuses to join a strike or replaces striking workers
synonyms: Crusty, Dirty, Shabby, Rough, Filthy, Mean
examples: The boy had scabby knees after falling on the road. He lived in a scabby old house near the market. The dog looked scabby and needed treatment. People disliked his scabby behavior at the meeting.
sindhiMeaning: خارش وارو، ميلو، گھٽ درجي جو، چمڙي تي زخم جا سڪا ٿيل تهه هئڻ، گندو بي ترتيب خراب حالت وارو، گھٽ درجي جو يا ڪنجوس ماڻهو، هڙتال ٽوڙيندڙ مزدور
antonyms: Clean, Smooth, Healthy, Neat, Generous
urduMeaning: خارش زدہ، میل کچیل والا، گھٹیا، جلد پر زخم کے خشک چھلکوں کا ہونا، گندا بوسیدہ خراب حالت میں، گھٹیا یا کنجوس شخص، ہڑتال توڑنے والا مزدور

synonyms: Itch, Mange, Skin infestation, Sarcoptic mange
sindhiMeaning: خارش جي بيماري جيڪا چمڙي ۾ گهڻي کجلي پيدا ڪري ٿي، هڪ چمڙي جي بيماري جيڪا ننڍڙن جاندارن سبب ٿيندي آهي جيڪي چمڙي ۾ گهڙي وڃن ٿا، هن سان سخت خارش ڳاڙهاڻ ۽ ننڍڙا داڻا ٿين ٿا هي ويجهي رابطي يا ڪپڙا ۽ بسترو گڏ استعمال ڪرڻ سان پکڙجي ٿي
urduMeaning: جلد کی ایک متعدی بیماری جس میں شدید خارش ہوتی ہے، جلد کی بیماری جو ننھے کیڑوں کی وجہ سے ہوتی ہے جو جلد میں گھس جاتے ہیں، اس سے شدید خارش لالی اور چھوٹے دانے پیدا ہوتے ہیں، یہ قریبی رابطے یا کپڑے اور بستر مشترک استعمال کرنے سے پھیلتی ہے
examples: The child was treated for scabies at the hospital. Scabies spreads quickly in crowded living conditions. The doctor confirmed that the itching was caused by scabies. Proper hygiene helps prevent scabies infection.
englishMeaning: A contagious skin disease causing intense itching and rash. A skin infestation caused by tiny mites that burrow into the skin. It leads to severe itching, redness, and small bumps. It spreads through close physical contact or sharing clothes and bedding.
antonyms: There are no antonyms

examples: The company decided to scale back its operations in Europe. Due to budget cuts, we need to scale back our project plans. They scaled back the party after realizing it was too expensive. The government scaled back its promises during the economic downturn.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ جي مقدار وسيلن يا ڪارڪردگي کي گهٽائڻ يا محدود ڪرڻ جيئن خرچ گھٽائڻ يا ڪم آسان ڪرڻ
englishMeaning: To reduce the size, amount, or extent of something. To decrease or cut down on activities, spending, plans, or operations, usually for efficiency, cost-saving, or practical reasons.
synonyms: Reduce, Cut down, Lessen, Decrease, Trim
antonyms: Expand, Increase, Enlarge, Boost, Amplify
urduMeaning: کسی منصوبے سرگرمی یا عمل کی مقدار دائرہ یا وسائل کو کم کرنا تاکہ اخراجات کم ہوں یا کام آسان ہو جائے

antonyms: Expand, Increase, Enlarge, Scale up, Boost
urduMeaning: کم کرنا، محدود کرنا، پیمانہ گھٹانا، دائرہ محدود کرنا، منصوبہ چھوٹا کرنا، پیداوار میں کمی کرنا، حجم گھٹانا
englishMeaning: To reduce the size, amount, level, or importance of something. To make something smaller, less intense, or less extensive than before. It is commonly used for reducing budgets, plans, operations, production, expectations, or physical size while keeping the core purpose intact.
examples: The company decided to scale down its operations due to financial losses. We need to scale down the project to meet the available budget. The factory scaled down production during the off season. He scaled down his expectations after hearing the final results.
sindhiMeaning: گھٽ ڪرڻ، ماپ يا سطح گهٽائڻ، منصوبو ننڍو ڪرڻ، وسعت گهٽ ڪرڻ، ڪم يا پيداوار گهٽائڻ
synonyms: Reduce, Cut back, Decrease, Downsize, Limit

sindhiMeaning: نفرت ڪرڻ، ڌڪارڻ، ڪرڀ اچڻ، ڪراهت اچڻ، گھڻي بيزاري محسوس ڪرڻ
examples: Most decent people abhor corruption in government. She abhors any form of cruelty towards animals. I abhor cruelty to animals. Many people abhor the idea of war. He abhors eating spicy food.
synonyms: Loathe, Detest
englishMeaning: To hate something, for example a way of behaving or thinking, especially for moral reasons. To regard with extreme repugnance, disgust, or aversion.
antonyms: Admire, Approve, Esteem
urduMeaning: نفرت کرنا، مُتنَفَّر ہونا ، کَراہَت کَرنا ، گھِن کھانا، سَخت ناگَواری محسُوس کَرنا ، حَقارَت سے دیکھنا

urduMeaning: جھلسا ہوا، جلا ہوا، خشک

antonyms: Preserve, Build, Protect

urduMeaning: سزا سے بچ جانا، کسی جرم غلطی یا نقصان کے بعد بھی بغیر کسی سزا، نقصان یا گرفت کے آزاد ہو جانا
englishMeaning: To escape without punishment or harm. Escaping a difficult situation, crime, mistake, or responsibility without receiving any punishment, damage, or negative consequence, even when punishment was expected.

synonyms: Unpunished, Free
sindhiMeaning: سزا کان بچي وڃڻ، ڪنهن ڏوهه غلطي يا نقصان کان پوءِ به بغير سزا، ڏنڊ يا نقصان جي آزاد ٿي وڃڻ

antonyms: Ignorer, Neglector, Follower
englishMeaning: To explore or examine an area. To search for information or opportunities. To look for talent or resources. sindhiMeaning: جاچ ڪرڻ/ ڳولا ڪرڻ/ جاچ پڙتال ڪرڻ، معلومات يا موقعن جي تلاش ڪرڻ، اهو ماڻهو جيڪو ڪنهن علائقي حالت يا دشمن بابت ڄاڻ گڏ ڪري، اسڪائوٽ تنظيم جو ميمبر، اهو ماڻهو جيڪو موقعا ماڻهن يا جڳهن جي ڳولا ڪري
examples: The scout went ahead of the team to check the route. She works as a talent scout for a sports company. The soldiers were sent to scout the area before the mission. He scouted several locations before choosing the perfect one.

antonyms: Fat, Chubby, Plump, Strong, Muscular

urduMeaning: بہت دُبلا پتلا، کمزور جسم والا، ہڈیوں والا کمزور جسم، غیر صحت مند حد تک پتلا، طاقت سے محروم، جو حد سے زیادہ دبلا پتلا ہو، جس کے جسم میں طاقت یا گوشت نہ ہو، جو کمزور یا غیر صحت مند نظر آئے
sindhiMeaning: تمام گهڻو ڏٻرو، ڪمزور جسم وارو، هڏن جهڙو ۽ ڪمزور، غير صحتمند نموني ڏٻرو، طاقت کان خالي، جنهن جي جسم ۾ طاقت يا گوشت گهٽ هجي، جيڪو ڪمزور يا غير صحتمند لڳي
examples: The scrawny cat wandered through the streets looking for food. He was a scrawny child but very intelligent. The dog looked scrawny after being lost for weeks. She adopted a scrawny kitten and cared for it until it became healthy.

Reverse into, Retreat into, Bump into, Return to

examples: He prefers to BACK his car INTO the garage. He accidentally backed into a parked car. She backed into the garage slowly. He backed into his old job after leaving the company. She backed into her old habits after some time.
sindhiMeaning: پويان هٽي ڪري ٽڪرائجي وڃڻ، پويان هٽي ڪنهن جاءِ ۾ وڃڻ، ٻيهر ڪنهن حالت يا ڪم ۾ موٽي وڃڻ
urduMeaning: پیچھے ہٹ کر ٹکرانا، پیچھے ہو کر کسی جگہ جانا، دوبارہ کسی حالت یا کام میں آ جانا
antonyms: Move forward, Advance into, Avoid, Stay away from
Whisper, Murmur, Silence, Calm speech
sindhiMeaning: رڙ ڪرڻ، دانهن ڪرڻ، چيخ ڪرڻ، ڪيڪ ڪرڻ، رڙ، ڪيڪ، دانهه، اوچتو ۽ تمام زور سان نڪرندڙ آواز جيڪو گهڻو ڪري ڊپ تڪليف حيرانگي ڪاوڙ يا خوشي جي شدت سبب نڪري ٿو، اهو عام طور تي تيز آواز سان سڏ ڪرڻ يا جذبات جو اظهار ڪرڻ لاءِ به استعمال ٿيندو آهي
examples: She let out a loud scream when she saw the snake. The baby screamed all night due to discomfort. He screamed for help when he got lost in the forest. The audience screamed with excitement at the concert.
urduMeaning: چلانا، چیخنا، چلا کر اٹھنا، کوک مارنا، اچانک اور بہت اونچی آواز میں چیخنا جو عموماً خوف درد حیرت غصہ یا خوشی کے شدید جذبات کی وجہ سے نکلتی ہے، یہ زور سے پکارنے یا شدید انداز میں اظہار کرنے کے لیے بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے
synonyms: Shout, Yell, Shriek, Cry, Howl
englishMeaning: To shout very loudly. To express strong emotion vocally. To make a loud, piercing sound. A sharp, loud cry produced suddenly, often due to strong emotions such as fear, surprise, pain, anger, or even excitement. It can also mean shouting loudly in general speech or expressing something in a very intense way.

synonyms: Writer, Copyist, Clerk, Recorder, Secretary, Notetaker
examples: The scribe carefully copied the ancient manuscript. During the meeting, she acted as a scribe and noted every detail. In ancient Egypt, a scribe held an important position in society. He was asked to scribe the professor’s lecture for the absent students.
sindhiMeaning: لکندڙ/ ليکڪ، قلمڪار/ خط نويس، مصنف/ ڪاتب/ نقل نويس، پراڻن وقتن ۾ اهو ماڻهو جيڪو ڪتاب يا دستاويز هٿ سان لکي نقل ڪندو هو، اهو شخص جيڪو ڪنهن جي ڳالهه لکي، پڙهيل لکيل ماڻهو جيڪو رڪارڊ سنڀالي، لکت ڪرڻ يا نقل ڪرڻ
englishMeaning: To write, record, or copy something. A person who writes or copies documents, especially in earlier times. A professional writer who copied manuscripts before printing was common. A person who writes down what someone else says, such as in a meeting or examination. In ancient contexts, an educated person skilled in reading and writing, often keeping records.
urduMeaning: لکھنے والا / کاتب، خوش نویس، قدیم زمانے میں وہ شخص جو کتابیں یا دستاویزات نقل کرتا تھا، کسی کے کہنے پر لکھنے والا شخص، تعلیم یافتہ فرد جو ریکارڈ محفوظ کرتا ہو، لکھنا یا نقل کرنا
antonyms: Reader, Listener, Speaker, Ignorant person

urduMeaning: لکھنے کا خوف، لکھنے کے عمل یا تحریر سے متعلق غیر منطقی یا شدید خوف، اس سے شخص کو تحریری کام کرنے میں مشکل یا خوف محسوس ہوتا ہے
englishMeaning: Fear of writing. An extreme or irrational fear of writing, including fear of putting thoughts on paper or creating written documents. This can affect personal, academic, or professional tasks that involve writing.
antonyms: Writing confidence, Ease in writing, Literary comfort
sindhiMeaning: لکڻ کان ڊڄڻ، لکڻ جي عمل يا تحرير ڪرڻ سان لاڳاپيل غير منطقي يا شديد خوف، ماڻهو تحرير ڪرڻ کان پاسو ڪن ٿا يا جذبات لکڻ ۾ ظاهر ڪرڻ ۾ پريشاني محسوس ڪن ٿا
examples: Her scriptophobia made it difficult for her to complete the report on time. Despite being talented, he struggled with scriptophobia and avoided journals. Therapy helped him overcome his scriptophobia and start writing letters again. Scriptophobia can hinder academic performance if students are afraid to take notes.
synonyms: Graphophobia, Fear of writing, Penophobia

antonyms: Neglect, Ignore, Overlook, Glance, Skim
englishMeaning: To examine something very carefully. To look at or inspect something closely and thoroughly in order to understand it or find any problems.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءَ کي غور سان ۽ تفصيل سان ڏسڻ يا جاچڻ، ڄاڻڻ يا مسئلا ڳولڻ لاءِ جانچڻ
examples: The lawyer scrutinized every clause in the agreement before advising his client. The teacher scrutinized the students’ essays for plagiarism. Investigators scrutinized the security footage to find clues. She scrutinized the painting, noting every brushstroke and color choice.
urduMeaning: کسی چیز کو باریک بینی سے جانچنا، غور سے دیکھنا یا تجزیہ کرنا تاکہ غلطیاں یا مسائل سامنے آئیں
synonyms: Examine, Inspect, Analyze, Review, Study

antonyms: Oversight
sindhiMeaning: ڇنڊ ڇاڻ، جاچ پڙتال، تحقيقات، چڪاس، تفتيش، پڙتال
urduMeaning: تلاش، جانچ پڑتال، تلاش، آزمائش
englishMeaning: Careful and complete examination. A close look at or over someone or something in order to judge condition.
examples: The documents should be available for public scrutiny. Her arguments doesn’t really stand up to scrutiny. Foreign policy has come under close scrutiny recently.
synonyms: Inspection
Fight, Clash, Brawl, Tussle
sindhiMeaning: اوچتو ۽ ٿوري وقت لاءِ هٿاپائي يا جهڳڙو ڪرڻ، ڌڪا ڏيڻ يا هڪ ٻئي سان جهيڙڻ، ڪشمڪش، ڪشتي، ننڍڙو جهڳڙو يا هٿاپائي، اوچتو شروع ٿيندڙ ننڍو جهڳڙو يا هٿاپائي جنهن ۾ ڌڪ لڳن يا ماڻهو هڪ ٻئي سان جهيڙي پون، اهو گهڻو وقت نه هلندو آهي
examples: A scuffle broke out between two students after the match. Police quickly stopped the scuffle before it became serious. He got injured during a scuffle at the market. The players scuffled over the ball for a few seconds.
urduMeaning: گَتھَم گَتھا ہونا ، دھينگا مُشتی کَرنا ، اندھا دھُند لَڑنا ،دھکم دھکا کرنا ، لپٹ جانا، کشا کشی جھگڑا ہاتھاپائی، کشا کشی جھگڑا ہاتھاپائی
englishMeaning: To fight or struggle briefly in a rough way. To engage in a short and usually sudden physical struggle. It often involves pushing, grabbing, or hitting and is not a long or planned fight. A short and sudden physical fight or struggle. antonyms: Peace, Harmony, Agreement, Truce

englishMeaning: To create a work of art by carving, molding, or shaping materials like stone, wood, clay, or metal. It can also mean shaping something carefully, such as the body, a hairstyle, landscape, or even ideas and skills.
antonyms: Destroy, Break, Ruin, Damage, Demolish
examples: The artist will sculpt a statue from marble. She sculpted the clay into a beautiful bowl. Regular exercise helps sculpt the body. The designer sculpted the garden into a peaceful space.

englishMeaning: A person who makes statues or artistic forms by carving, shaping, or modeling materials like stone, wood, clay, or metal. A person who shapes or builds something carefully, such as ideas, careers, or policies. A digital artist who designs 3D models using software.

examples: The sculptor spent months carving the marble statue. She is a talented sculptor known for her abstract art. The sculptor displayed his work in the city gallery. A skilled sculptor can turn a simple block of stone into a masterpiece.

synonyms: Statue, Figure, Carving, Effigy, Model, Bust, Monument

Any object shaped artistically in solid form. A decorative or symbolic three dimensional structure. To create or shape something as a sculpture by carving or modeling material.

synonyms: Retreat, Withdraw, Step aside, Pull back, Recede
englishMeaning: Retreat, make space. To move away from someone or something. To stop criticizing, interfering, or being aggressive. To reduce pressure or intensity in an argument or situation.

examples: You better back off a little if you want me to start serving this crown again. The dog barked, so he quickly backed off. You should back off and let her handle the problem herself. The manager told the staff to back off when the client got angry. He refused to back off even when he knew he was wrong.
sindhiMeaning: پري هٽي وڃڻ، مداخلت بند ڪرڻ، هٿ کڻڻ
antonyms: Confront, Advance, Interfere, Attack, Persist

synonyms: Smooth, Perfect, Flawless, Continuous, Unified
examples: The team delivered a seamless presentation that impressed everyone. The transition from one scene to the next was seamless. We want the customer experience to feel seamless from start to finish. The software update made the system run in a seamless way.

urduMeaning: درزن ، سلائی کرنے والی، کپڑے سینے والی عورت، ہ عورت جو پیشہ ورانہ طور پر کپڑے سیتی، مرمت کرتی یا لباس تیار کرتی ہے
sindhiMeaning: درزياڻي، عورت جيڪا ڪپڙا سِئي، اها جيڪا پيشه ورانه طور ڪپڙا سِئي، مرمت ڪري يا ماپ مطابق تيار ڪري
antonyms: Client, Customer, Buyer

synonyms: Dressmaker, Tailoress, Needlewoman, Garment worker
examples: The seamstress stitched the wedding dress with great care. She works as a seamstress in a local tailoring shop. The seamstress repaired my torn jacket quickly. A skilled seamstress can turn simple fabric into elegant clothing.

englishMeaning: To keep yourself, somebody away from contact with other people. To set or keep apart from others.
sindhiMeaning: جدا ڪرڻ، الڳ ڪرڻ، ڪنڊائتو ڪرڻ، مجمع کان الڳ ڪرڻ، علحدو يا الڳ ٿلڳ رکڻ
antonyms: Assimilate, Associate, Connect, Join, Link, Unite

examples: The monks secluded themselves from the rest of society. She secludes herself in her study to work. You can't seclude yourself from the world.
synonyms: Cut off, Insulate, Isolate, Segregate, Separate, Sequester

urduMeaning: اعتکاف، تنہائی یا لوگوں سے الگ رہنے کی حالت، خلوت ، گوشہ نشینی ، علیحدگی، کنارہ کش
examples: The writer lived in seclusion in a small mountain village. After the incident, he chose seclusion to recover peacefully. The monk spent years in seclusion for spiritual growth. The celebrity escaped to an island for seclusion and privacy.
sindhiMeaning: اعتڪاف، اڪيلائي يا ماڻهن کان الڳ رهڻ جي حالت، ڪناره ڪشي، گوشه نشيني، خلوت، علحدگي، جدائي
englishMeaning: The state of being private and away from other people. A condition in which a person lives or stays away from others, often in a quiet, private, or isolated place. It may be chosen for peace, safety, religious practice, reflection, or rest. It can also sometimes mean being kept apart for protection or medical reasons.
antonyms: Society, Company
Socialite, Extrovert, Gregarious person, Communalist
englishMeaning: A person who prefers to be alone or secluded. A person who prefers to live in isolation, away from society, or avoids social contact.
urduMeaning: تنہائی پسند، علیحدگی پسند ، علیحدہ رہنے والا ، گوشہ نشین، تنہا پسند، تنہائی اختیار کرنے والا
examples: The writer was known as a seclusionist, preferring to live far from society in his mountain cabin. As a seclusionist, she avoided social gatherings and valued her privacy above all else. The village considered him a seclusionist because he rarely interacted with others.
sindhiMeaning: اڪيلائي پسند شخص، گوشہ نشين شخص، ڪنڊ نشين، سماج کان الڳ رهندڙ
synonyms: Recluse, Hermit, Loner, Introvert, Isolationist

sindhiMeaning: دنياوي يا سماجي معاملن سان واسطو رکندڙ، اهڙي حڪومت يا رياست جيڪا ڪنهن خاص مذهب جي پيروي نه ڪري، تعليم يا ادارا جيڪي مذهبي ڪنٽرول کان آزاد هجن، ڊگهي عرصي تائين هلندڙ يا صدين تائين جاري رهندڙ
antonyms: Religious, Sacred, Spiritual, Ecclesiastical
englishMeaning: Related to non religious life or worldly affairs. Government or state that does not support any specific religion. Education or institutions not controlled by religious groups. In historical usage, something lasting for a very long time or many centuries.
synonyms: Nonreligious, Worldly, Temporal, Civil, Lay
examples: The country follows a secular constitution that treats all religions equally. Many public schools provide secular education rather than religious instruction. The organization focuses on secular social services such as health and education. Some historians study secular trends in society instead of religious movements.
urduMeaning: دنیاوی یا معاشرتی معاملات سے متعلق، ایسی ریاست جو کسی خاص مذہب کی سرپرستی نہ کرے، ایسا تعلیمی نظام جو مذہبی اداروں کے کنٹرول میں نہ ہو، طویل مدت تک قائم رہنے والی چیز کے لیے بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے

antonyms: Active, Energetic, Mobile, Dynamic

examples: A sedentary lifestyle can lead to health problems. Office jobs often require long hours of sedentary work. He became overweight due to his sedentary habits. Yoga helps counteract the effects of a sedentary life.
sindhiMeaning: ويهڻ وارو، بيڪارو، غير فعال (ڪم يا زندگي جو انداز جيڪو گھڻو ويهڻ ۽ گهٽ سرگرمي تي ٻڌل هجي)

synonyms: Inactive, Stationary, Desk-bound, Seated
Residue, Deposit, Dregs, Silt, Sludge
urduMeaning: تہہ میں جمع ہونے والے ذرات، مٹی ریت معدنیات یا دیگر باریک ذرات جو پانی یا کسی مائع میں تیرنے کے بعد نیچے بیٹھ کر تہہ بنا لیتے ہیں
examples: The river carried sediment that slowly settled at the bottom of the lake. Scientists studied the ocean sediment to learn about ancient climate conditions. After boiling the herbal mixture, a thick sediment remained in the pot. Over centuries, layers of sediment formed the rocks seen in the canyon.

examples: After months of treatment, she is finally back on her feet. The small business was back on its feet after the crisis. He struggled for years but is now back on his feet financially. With support from friends, she got back on her feet again.
urduMeaning: دوبارہ سنبھل جانا، مشکل یا بیماری کے بعد پھر سے ٹھیک ہو جانا، بیماری سے صحت یاب ہونا، مالی نقصان کے بعد بحالی، ذہنی یا جذباتی بہتری، دوبارہ خودمختار ہونا
synonyms: Recovered, Restored, Rehabilitated, Stable again, Revived
antonyms: Struggling, Collapsing, Unstable, Sick, Defeated
sindhiMeaning: ٻيهر سنڀالي بيهڻ، ڏکيائي يا بيماري کانپوءِ ٻيهر بهتر ٿيڻ، بيماري کان صحتيابي، مالي نقصان کان پوءِ بحالي، ذهني يا جذباتي بحالي، خودمختياري ٻيهر حاصل ڪرڻ
englishMeaning: Recovered from a problem, illness, or difficulty and functioning normally again. A situation where a person has gone through hardship such as illness, financial trouble, emotional stress, or failure, and has now recovered enough to return to normal life or activity. It often implies strength, resilience, and improvement after a setback.

urduMeaning: کسی کو اپنی طرف مائل یا قائل کرنے کا عمل، جو دلکشی، جاذبیت یا کشش کے ذریعے ہو، یہ رومانوی یا جنسی سیاق میں استعمال ہوسکتا ہے لیکن کسی کو غلط فیصلے کی طرف لے جانے کے لیے بھی ہو سکتا ہے
synonyms: Temptation, Allure, Enticement, Charm, Attraction
examples: The movie explored the theme of seduction and desire. He fell victim to her seduction and made a risky decision. The advertisement used seduction to attract customers. Ancient stories often warn of the dangers of seduction.
englishMeaning: The process of enticing someone to do something, often by appealing to desire or attraction. It can involve persuasion, charm, or allure. It is sometimes used in a romantic or sexual context but can also apply to convincing someone to act against their better judgment.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کي پنهنجي طرف راغب ڪرڻ يا قائل ڪرڻ جو عمل، جيڪو ڪشش، دلڪشي يا جاذبيت ذريعي ٿئي ٿو، اهو رومانوي يا جنسي صورتحال ۾ ٿي سگهي ٿو، پر ڪنهن کي پنهنجي بهتر فيصلي جي خلاف عمل ڪرڻ لاءِ به ٿي سگهي ٿو
antonyms: Repulsion, Discouragement, Deterrence, Dissuasion

englishMeaning: Attractive in a way that tempts or entices. Having the quality of tempting or attracting someone often in a way that is hard to resist. Can refer to charm, appearance, or behavior that draws interest or desire.
urduMeaning: دلکش، پرکشش، لبھانے والا، جو کسی کو اپنی طرف متوجہ کرے یا دلچسپی پیدا کرے، ظاہری حسن یا رویے کی وجہ سے دلکشی پیدا کرنے والا
antonyms: Repulsive, Unattractive, Unappealing, Off-putting
synonyms: Alluring, Attractive, Tempting, Charming, Captivating
sindhiMeaning: پرڪشش، دلڪش، راغب ڪندڙ، جيڪو ڪنهن کي پنهنجي طرف ڇڪي يا راغب ڪري، دلڪش يا پرڪشش هجڻ، عام طور تي ظاهري يا رويي ۾ متاثر ڪرڻ وارو
examples: Her smile was extremely seductive. The advertisement used seductive colors to attract customers. He found her voice seductive. The movie had a seductive plot that kept everyone engaged.

synonyms: Allure, Charm, Attractiveness, Appeal, Magnetism
examples: Her seductiveness made everyone at the party notice her. The seductiveness of the city drew tourists from all over the world. He admired the seductiveness of her writing style. Seductiveness in marketing can influence people’s choices.
englishMeaning: The quality of being attractive or charming in a way that tempts or entices someone.
urduMeaning: دلکشی، کشش، کسی کو اپنی طرف مائل کرنے کی صفت
antonyms: Repulsiveness, Unattractiveness, Dullness, Plainness
sindhiMeaning: دلڪشي، پرڪشش هجڻ جو خاصيت، ڪنهن کي متوجه ڪرڻ جي صلاحيت
هڪ عورت جيڪا حسن، دلڪشي يا دلپسندي سان ڪنهن جي جذبات يا محبت کي راغب ڪرڻ يا متاثر ڪرڻ لاءِ ڪوشش ڪري ٿي
antonyms: Chaste woman, Virtuous woman, Modest woman, Innocent woman
urduMeaning: ایک عورت جو حسن، دلکشی یا جاذبیت کے ذریعے کسی کو جذباتی یا رومانوی طور پر متاثر یا قابو پانے کی کوشش کرتی ہے
synonyms: Enchantress, Temptress, Charmer, Siren
examples: The novel portrayed her as a cunning seductress. He fell for the charms of a seductress at the party. The movie featured a seductress who led men into trouble. Legends often speak of a seductress whose beauty was irresistible.
englishMeaning: A woman who deliberately attracts someone, often using charm, beauty, or allure to influence or manipulate them emotionally or romantically. A woman who entices or tempts someone, especially in a sexual way

sindhiMeaning: محنتي، ڌيان سان ڪم ڪندڙ، لگن وارو، جيڪو ماڻهو ڪنهن ڪم ۾ محنت ۽ مستقل مزاجي ڏيکاري، ڌيان سان ڪم ڪري، ۽ هر ڪم کي مڪمل ڪري ٿو
antonyms: Negligent, Lazy, Careless, Indifferent, Idle
urduMeaning: محنتی، کوشاں، لگن والا، جو شخص کسی کام میں مستقل محنت کرے، بار بار کوشش کرے اور ہر کام کو احتیاط کے ساتھ مکمل کرے
examples: She was sedulous in her studies, reviewing notes every evening. The researcher conducted sedulous experiments to ensure accuracy. His sedulous efforts at work earned him a promotion. Sedulous planning made the event run smoothly.
synonyms: Diligent, Industrious, Assiduous, Persistent, Hardworking
englishMeaning: Showing dedication and careful attention to work or duty. Someone who is persistent, diligent, and meticulous in completing tasks. It conveys consistent effort and attention to detail over time.

antonyms: Carelessly, Negligently, Lazily, Haphazardly
englishMeaning: Diligently, with careful and persistent effort. Performing a task with constant, careful, and attentive effort, showing dedication and persistence in completing work.
examples: She sedulously prepared for the final exams to ensure top marks. The researcher sedulously gathered data for the study. He sedulously maintained his garden every morning. They sedulously followed the instructions to complete the project perfectly.
sindhiMeaning: محنت سان، توجهه سان، ڪنهن ڪم کي لڳاتار، ڌيان سان ۽ پوري محنت سان ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: محنت و لگن سے، کسی کام کو مسلسل، باریک بینی اور لگن کے ساتھ کرنے کا عمل
synonyms: Diligently, Industriously, Assiduously, Carefully, Meticulously

antonyms: Ignore, Neglect, Overlook, Avoid
englishMeaning: To arrange, deal with, or take responsibility for something. To look into a matter, make arrangements, or take steps to solve a problem or fulfill a request. It often implies future action rather than immediate completion.
examples: I will see about booking the meeting room tomorrow. The manager said she would see about the complaint. Can you see about repairing the broken chair? He promised to see about the travel arrangements.

sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن مسئلي يا ڪم تي ڌيان ڏيڻ، ان بابت جاچ ڪرڻ يا ان کي مڪمل ڪرڻ لاءِ قدم کڻڻ، اڪثر اهو مستقبل جي عمل کي ظاهر ڪري ٿو
synonyms: Arrange, Look into, Take care of, Deal with, Attend to

antonyms: Front onto, Open away from, Separated from
urduMeaning: پیچھے کی طرف کھلنا ، پیچھے واقع ہونا
examples: The vehicle backed onto my father’s toe. Our house backs onto a beautiful park. The school playground backs onto a busy road. The restaurant backs onto the river, giving it a lovely view. The library backs onto the main street, so it can get noisy sometimes.

sindhiMeaning: پٺيان لڳڻ، پٺيان کُلڻ، پٺيان ڏسڻ، پٺيان وارو حصو ڪنهن جاءَ سان ملڻ، پٺيان پاسي موجود هجڻ

englishMeaning: To agree fully or have the same opinion with someone; to think in the same way about something. It is often used when two people share the same views, ideas, or understanding.
examples: We see eye to eye on this issue. My brother and I don’t always see eye to eye on politics. The manager and the staff finally saw eye to eye about the new plan. They rarely see eye to eye, but they respect each other’s opinions. After a long discussion, we began to see eye to eye on the solution.
sindhiMeaning: هڪجهڙا خيال رکڻ، ساڳي ڳالهه تي متفق ٿيڻ، هڪ نظر سان ڏسڻ، ڪنهن ڳالهه فيصلي يا خيال تي مڪمل طور متفق هجڻ ۽ ساڳي سوچ هجڻ
synonyms: Agree, Have the same opinion, Be in harmony, Be of one mind, Concur
urduMeaning: کسی سے مکمل اتفاق کرنا، ہم خیال ہونا، متفق ہونا، ایک رائے ہونا، کسی بات پر پوری طرح اتفاقِ رائے رکھنا
antonyms: Disagree, Differ, Clash, Conflict, Dispute

sindhiMeaning: غور سان جاچ ڪرڻ، ڪنهن معاملي يا مسئلي کي ڌيان سان پرکڻ، حقيقتون معلوم ڪرڻ يا لڪل سببن کي سمجهڻ
antonyms: Ignore, Overlook, Neglect, Dismiss
synonyms: Investigate, Examine, Look into, Inquire into, Probe
urduMeaning: غور سے جانچ کرنا، کسی معاملے کی گہرائی میں جا کر تحقیق کرنا، حقیقت معلوم کرنا یا پوشیدہ پہلوؤں کو سمجھنا
examples: The committee promised to see into the complaints made by the workers. I will see into the reason for the delay tomorrow. The manager saw into the issue and found the real cause. Police are seeing into the matter seriously.
englishMeaning: To investigate or understand something carefully. To examine a matter closely in order to discover facts, causes, problems, or hidden intentions. It can also mean to perceive beyond what is obvious.

antonyms: Leave early, Abandon, Quit, Desert
synonyms: Stay until the end, Continue, Finish, Escort

englishMeaning: To remain until the end of a period, event, or situation. To continue with someone or something until it finishes. It can be used for a time period, a task, or a person until the end of a particular event or situation. It sometimes also means to escort someone to the door at the end of a visit.
sindhiMeaning: پورو ٿيڻ تائين گڏ رهڻ، آخري تائين جاري رکڻ يا ڪنهن کي ٻاهر وڃڻ تائين ساڻس گڏ وڃڻ
examples: She decided to see out the meeting even though she was tired. The old manager promised to see out the project before retiring. We stayed to see out the concert until the final song. He saw me out to the car after the party.

antonyms: Be deceived, Overlook, Misunderstand
urduMeaning: حقیقت جاننا، کسی کی اصلیت یا چھپی ہوئی نیت کو پہچاننا، خاص طور پر جب وہ دھوکہ دینے کی کوشش کر رہا ہو
sindhiMeaning: سچ معلوم ڪرڻ، ڪنهن جي اصل حقيقت يا ڪوشش جو پتو لڳائڻ، خاص ڪري جڏهن ڪو ڌوڪو ڏيڻ جي ڪوشش ڪري
synonyms: Discern, Detect, Perceive, Understand
englishMeaning: Understand the truth. To recognize the true nature of someone or something, especially when they are trying to hide it or deceive you.
examples: I could see through his excuses. She saw through their plan immediately. Don’t try to lie to me; I can see through you. He saw through the tricky situation and acted wisely.

urduMeaning: خیال رکھنا یا انتظام کرنا، کسی کام یا ذمہ داری پر توجہ دینا اس کا خیال رکھنا یا اس بات کو یقینی بنانا کہ وہ کام مکمل ہو
antonyms: Ignore, Neglect, Overlook, Abandon
synonyms: Take care of, Attend to, Handle, Manage, Ensure
englishMeaning: To take care of something or make sure it is done. To give attention to a task, responsibility, or person, to manage it properly, or to ensure that something happens as required.
examples: Please see to the arrangements before the guests arrive. The manager will see to the customer complaints. She asked him to see to the documents immediately. I will see to it that the report is submitted on time.
sindhiMeaning: خيال رکڻ يا بندوبست ڪرڻ، ڪنهن ڪم ذميواري يا معاملي جو خيال رکڻ ان کي سنڀالڻ يا پڪ ڪرڻ ته اهو صحيح نموني مڪمل ٿئي

examples: The school decided to segregate students by age for the science classes. Factories segregate waste materials for recycling. During the event, volunteers segregated the donations into clothes, food, and books. Some societies historically segregated communities based on social status.
synonyms: Separate, Isolate, Divide, Partition, Set apart
sindhiMeaning: جدا ڪرڻ، الڳ ڪرڻ، ڌار ڌار ڪرڻ، درجه بندي ڪرڻ، قانوني يا ضابطي جي ذريعي الڳ رکڻ
urduMeaning: جدا کرنا، الگ کرنا، بندی کرنا، کسی قانون یا ضابطے کے تحت علیحدہ رکھنا
englishMeaning: To separate or set apart from others. To keep people, things, or groups apart from each other, often based on differences such as race, religion, gender, or type. It can refer to both physical separation and social exclusion.
antonyms: Integrate, Combine, Unite, Mix, Join

sindhiMeaning: علحدگي، جدائي، تفريق
urduMeaning: تفریق، علیحدہ رکھنا
antonyms: Company
englishMeaning: The state of being alone or kept apart from others. The act or policy of separating people from different groups, for example people of different races, religions or sexes, and treating them in a different way.
examples: The report recommends segregation of cyclists from both cars and pedestrians. They objected to the college's strict segregation of men and women.
synonyms: Isolation

antonyms: Miss the opportunity, Hesitate, Delay action, Procrastinate, Ignore the chance
sindhiMeaning: موقعي کي هٿ ۾ وٺڻ، وقت کي ضايع نه ڪرڻ ۽ فوري فائدو وٺڻ، موجوده موقعي مان مڪمل فائدو حاصل ڪرڻ، موقعي کي وڃائڻ کان اڳ استعمال ڪرڻ، جلدي فيصلو ڪري عمل ڪرڻ، وقت جي اهميت کي سمجهي قدم کڻڻ
examples: You should seize the moment and apply for the scholarship today. He seized the moment and started his own business when the opportunity came. She decided to seize the moment and express her true feelings. They seized the moment to invest in the market at the right time.
synonyms: Take advantage of the opportunity, Act now, Make the most of it, Grab the chance, Carpe diem
urduMeaning: موقع سے فائدہ اٹھانا، وقت کو ضائع کیے بغیر فوراً عمل کرنا، موجودہ موقع کو بہترین طریقے سے استعمال کرنا، موقع ہاتھ سے جانے نہ دینا، بروقت قدم اٹھانا، تاخیر کے بغیر فیصلہ کرنا
englishMeaning: Act now and do not miss the opportunity. To take immediate advantage of an opportunity without delay. It suggests acting quickly before the chance disappears and making the most of the present time.

antonyms: Commit, Proceed, Fulfill, Agree, Carry out
sindhiMeaning: واعدي تان موٽي وڃڻ، پٺتي هٽي وڃڻ، انڪار ڪري ڇڏڻ
synonyms: Withdraw, Renege, Retreat, Pull out, Abandon
urduMeaning: وعدہ توڑ دینا، پیچھے ہٹ جانا، معاہدے سے انکار کر دینا
examples: He backed out two days before the holiday so we gave the ticket to his sister. He promised to help me with the project, but he backed out at the last minute. They agreed to sign the contract, but later backed out. She never backs out of her commitments. The company backed out of the deal after reviewing the risks.

sindhiMeaning: موقعي جو فائدو وٺڻ، موقع وڃڻ کان اڳ عمل ڪرڻ، ڪاميابي لاءِ موقعو استعمال ڪرڻ، حالت کي پنهنجي حق ۾ ڪرڻ، موقعي کي سڃاڻي فوراً ان مان فائدو حاصل ڪرڻ، اهو اهڙي حالت ۾ استعمال ٿئي ٿو جتي دير ڪرڻ سان موقعو هٿ مان نڪري سگهي ٿو
synonyms: Take advantage, Grab the chance, Make use of the opportunity, Capitalize on, Act on
urduMeaning: موقع سے فائدہ اٹھانا، موقع ضائع ہونے سے پہلے قدم اٹھانا، کامیابی کے لیے موقع حاصل کرنا، حالات کو اپنے حق میں کرنا، کسی اچھے موقع کو پہچان کر فوراً اس سے فائدہ اٹھانا، اس میں سمجھداری اور بروقت فیصلہ شامل ہوتا ہے تاکہ موقع ضائع نہ ہو
englishMeaning: Act quickly to take advantage of a chance. To recognize a favorable situation and act on it without delay. It implies courage, readiness, and smart decision-making to benefit from a moment that may not come again.
examples: She seized the opportunity to study abroad and changed her life. He seized the opportunity to start his own business during the crisis. If you seize the opportunity now, you can achieve great success. They seized the opportunity to learn new skills during their free time.
antonyms: Miss the opportunity, Ignore the chance, Waste the chance, Let it pass, Hesitate

examples: We seldom go to the theater downtown because its prices are so high. Two dogs over one bone seldom agree. I seldom drive my car into the city. He had seldom seen a child with so much talent. They seldom watch television these days.
synonyms: Rarely, Scarcely, Rarely, Barely, Hardly, Infrequently, Occasionally, Inconstantly,
englishMeaning: Not often. Almost never. Sometimes. As few times. In few instances.
antonyms: Often, Frequently, Commonly, Uniformly, Habitually, Regularly
sindhiMeaning: ورلي، ڪڏھن ڪڏھن، اڻ لڀ، قضائي، بعض، اوقات، ٿورڙو
urduMeaning: بہت کم، شاذ و نادر، کبھی کبھار

englishMeaning: Someone who thinks mainly about himself. A person who focuses on his own needs, feelings, and interests while giving little or no attention to others.
antonyms: Selfless, Caring, Considerate, Altruistic
urduMeaning: خود غرض، ایسا شخص جو صرف اپنی ذات فائدے اور احساسات کے بارے میں سوچے اور دوسروں کو نظرانداز کرے
sindhiMeaning: پاڻ تي ڌيان ڏيندڙ، اهو ماڻهو جيڪو صرف پنهنجي فائدي احساسن ۽ خواهشن بابت سوچي ۽ ٻين جي پرواهه نه ڪري
synonyms: Selfish, Egocentric, Narcissistic, Self absorbed
examples: He became self centered after gaining success. A self centered attitude can damage relationships. She was so self centered that she ignored her team’s efforts. Self centered people often struggle to maintain friendships.

englishMeaning: Achieving success through one’s own effort. Describes a person who becomes successful through personal hard work, determination, and skill, without significant help, wealth, or status inherited from family or others.
antonyms: Privileged, Inherited, Dependent, Born wealthy
examples: He is a self made businessman who started with nothing. She is proud to be self made and independent. The company was built by a self made entrepreneur. Many self made leaders inspire young people.
sindhiMeaning: پاڻ ڪمايل ڪامياب، اهڙو شخص جنهن پنهنجي محنت، جدوجهد ۽ صلاحيت سان ڪاميابي حاصل ڪئي هجي، بغير خانداني دولت يا سهائتا جي،
urduMeaning: خود محنت سے کامیاب، ایسا شخص جس نے اپنی محنت، قابلیت اور لگن سے کامیابی حاصل کی ہو، نہ کہ وراثت یا دوسروں کی مدد سے، خود پرداختہ اپنی ذاتی جدوجہد سے کامیابی حاصل کرنے والا خودساختہ
synonyms: Self achieved, Independent, Self reliant, Hard working

antonyms: Insecure, Doubtful, Timid, Uncertain
urduMeaning: خود پر اعتماد، ایسا شخص جو اپنی صلاحیتوں فیصلوں اور قابلیت پر یقین رکھتا ہو اور بغیر جھجک کے کام کر سکے
examples: She is self-confident enough to speak in front of a large audience. A self-confident leader inspires trust in the team. He became more self-confident after gaining work experience. Self-confident students participate actively in class discussions.
englishMeaning: Feeling sure about your own abilities, qualities, or judgment. Certain that you can manage any situation by yourself. Such a person is comfortable making decisions, expressing opinions, and taking responsibility without excessive fear or doubt.
synonyms: Confident, Self-assured, Positive, Sure of oneself
sindhiMeaning: خود اعتماد، پنهنجي صلاحيتن تي ڀروسو ڪندڙ، اهڙو ماڻهو جيڪو پنهنجي قابليت فيصلي ۽ صلاحيتن تي مڪمل اعتماد رکي ٿو ۽ بغير ڊپ جي ڪم ڪري ٿو

antonyms: Indulgence, Acceptance, Self-indulgence, Adoption
sindhiMeaning: خود انڪار، پاڻ تي پابندي، ذاتي خواهشن کي رد ڪرڻ، اخلاقي قابو، سادي زندگي اپنائڻ، پاڻ تي ضبط
examples: She practiced self-denial by fasting during the holy month. His self-denial helped him save money for his education. Athletes often show self-denial to maintain peak performance. The monk’s life was full of self-denial and meditation.
englishMeaning: The act of refusing oneself something, especially for moral, religious, or personal reasons. The practice of intentionally giving up personal desires, pleasures, or comforts, often to achieve higher goals, moral discipline, or spiritual growth. It involves restraint and self-control over one’s impulses.
urduMeaning: اِنکارِ ذات ، تَرکِ خَواہِشات ، نَفس کُشی ، خود انکار، ذاتی خواہشات کو ترک کرنا، اخلاقی ضبط، سادہ زندگی، خود پر قابو پانا
synonyms: Abstinence, Abnegation, Renunciation, Refusal, Renouncement

urduMeaning: اپنے فیصلے خود کرنے کا حق، خود ارادیت ، اپنی زندگی، نظام اور مستقبل کے بارے میں آزادانہ طور پر فیصلے کرنا بغیر کسی بیرونی مداخلت کے
antonyms: Dependence, Subjugation, Oppression, Domination
englishMeaning: The right or ability to make one’s own choices. The freedom and power of a person, group, or nation to decide their own goals, actions, and future without external control or force.
sindhiMeaning: پنهنجا فيصلا پاڻ ڪرڻ جو حق، خود اراديت، اهو اختيار ته پنهنجا سياسي، سماجي يا ذاتي فيصلا پاڻ ڪري بغير ٻاهرين دٻاءَ جي
examples: Education helps students develop self determination and confidence. Many nations fought for self determination after colonial rule. Self determination allows individuals to choose their own career paths. The movement demanded political self determination for the region.
synonyms: Independence, Autonomy, Self rule, Freedom of choice

urduMeaning: سب بیچ دینا، دغا دینا، اصولوں کا سودا کرنا، ضمیر فروشی، اپنے اصولوں یا وفاداری کو ذاتی مفاد کے لیے بیچ دینا
synonyms: Compromise, Exhaust, Run out
examples: The concert tickets sold out within an hour. All the books were sold out by the end of the day. Many fans felt he sold out when he started promoting products he didn’t believe in She promised never to sell out her friends for money.
englishMeaning: To sell all available items (nothing left in stock). To betray one’s principles or supporters for personal gain (especially money or fame).
sindhiMeaning: سڄو وڪامي وڃڻ، دغا ڏيڻ، اصولن جو سودو ڪرڻ، پاڻ وڪڻڻ، پنهنجي ايمان، اصول يا وفاداري کي مفاد يا پئسن خاطر ڇڏي ڏيڻ
antonyms: Keep, Stay loyal

examples: She backed out of the agreement at the last minute. He backed out of the deal at the last minute. She promised to help us, but then she backed out of her commitment. The company backed out of the contract due to financial problems.
synonyms: Withdraw from, Renege on, Retreat from, Pull out of, Abandon
sindhiMeaning: واپس هٽي وڃڻ، قول تان ڦري وڃڻ، ذميواري نه نڀائڻ
englishMeaning: Fail to keep an agreement, arrangement. To withdraw from an agreement, promise, or responsibility that one had previously accepted. To fail to keep a commitment or plan.
antonyms: Commit to, Stick wit, Fulfill, Carry out, Go through with
urduMeaning: پیچھے ہٹ جانا، وعدہ توڑ دینا ، ذمہ داری سے انکار کرنا
ایک تعلیمی ادارہ جہاں پادری علما یا مذہبی رہنما مذہبی تعلیم اور تربیت حاصل کرتے ہیں، ا یسا مدرسہ جہاں الٰہیات اور مذہبی علوم پڑھائے جاتے ہیں
sindhiMeaning: تعليمي ادارو يا درسگاه جتي مذهبي اڳواڻ پادرين يا علمائن کي تربيت ۽ تعليم ڏني ويندي آهي، اهو ادارو جتي ماڻهن کي روحانيت مذهب ۽ اخلاقيات جي باري ۾ سکيا ڏني وڃي
antonyms: Secular school, Public university, Non-religious institution
examples: He joined a seminary to study theology and become a priest. The seminary offers courses in philosophy, ethics, and church history. Many famous leaders received their moral education from a seminary. The town built a new seminary to train future religious scholars.
synonyms: Theological, Religious school, Academy, Monastery (contextually), Training institute
englishMeaning: A place of learning or a training ground for future leaders or professionals in a certain field. A school, college, or educational institution where people, especially those preparing to become priests, ministers, or religious scholars are trained in theology, religion, and philosophy.

urduMeaning: علامات سے متعلق، اس تصور سے تعلق رکھتا ہے جو علامات اور نشانات کے ذریعے پیغام پہنچانے اور اس کے معنی سمجھنے کے بارے میں ہوتا ہے
antonyms: Literal, Non-symbolic, Denotative
englishMeaning: Related to signs, symbols, and their meanings. Anything concerning signs and symbols, and how they are used to communicate meaning. It often applies to language, art, media, and cultural symbols to interpret or analyze messages.
sindhiMeaning: نشانين يا علامتن سان لاڳاپيل، اُن مفهوم سان لاڳاپيل آهي جيڪو نشانين ۽ علامتن جي ذريعي پيغام پهچائڻ ۽ انهن جي معنيٰ کي سمجهڻ ۾ مدد ڪري
examples: The semiotic analysis of advertisements reveals hidden cultural messages. Colors in the painting carry semiotic significance about emotions. Semiotic theory helps decode language beyond literal meaning. Traffic signs are a basic example of semiotic communication.
synonyms: Symbolic, Sign-related, Emblematic, Representational

sindhiMeaning: مقابلي ۾ آخري مقابلي کان اڳ جو مرحلو، جنهن کي اڌ آخري مرحلو چيو وڃي ٿو، ڪا شيءِ جيڪا اڌ مڪمل هجي يا جزوي هجي
synonyms: Semi-finals, Partials, Incompletes, Halves
englishMeaning: Short for semi-finals (plural form of semi). Something partial or incomplete. Refers to the round in a competition just before the final, often called semi-finals. Can describe objects, items, or conditions that are partial, incomplete, or halfway.
examples: The team won their semis and advanced to the final. She was nervous before the semis of the tennis tournament. They offered semis of chocolates for tasting. The building’s semis construction looks impressive.
urduMeaning: مقابلے میں آخری مرحلے سے پہلے کا مرحلہ، جسے نصف فائنل کہا جاتا ہے، کوئی چیز جو جزوی یا مکمل نہ ہو
antonyms: Finals, Complete, Whole, Full

urduMeaning: عیاشی، حواس خمسہ کے متعلق، نفسانی، شہوانی
sindhiMeaning: حِسن تي ٻڌل، نفس پرست، عياش، حواس کي خوش ڪندڙ، حسي، سراسري
examples: She is amazingly flirty and sensual. He is elegant, sensual, conscious of his body. He kissed her full sensual lips. Sensual pleasure had been swirling around her.
synonyms: Carnal, Fleshly, Luscious, Lush
antonyms: Harsh, Painful, Uncomfortable
englishMeaning: Connected with your physical feelings, giving pleasure to your physical senses, especially sexual pleasure. Relating to or consisting in the gratification of the senses or the indulgence of appetite.

antonyms: Acquittal, Fragment, Acquit, Release
englishMeaning: To officially declare punishment in court. To declare a legal punishment for someone who has been found guilty of a crime. A punishment given by a court. A group of words that expresses a complete thought.
sindhiMeaning: عدالت طرفان سزا ٻڌائڻ، عدالت طرفان ڏوهاري لاءِ مقرر ڪيل سزا، لفظن جو اهڙو مجموعو جيڪو مڪمل خيال ظاهر ڪري، جملو
examples: The judge will sentence him next week. The court sentenced the criminal to five years. He was sentenced after the trial. They plan to sentence the accused soon. She wrote a long sentence in her essay. This sentence is easy to understand. The judge announced the sentence today. He received a ten year sentence.
urduMeaning: عدالت کی طرف سے سزا سنانا، عدالت کی طرف سے دی گئی سزا، الفاظ کا ایسا مجموعہ جو مکمل خیال ظاہر کرے، جملہ
synonyms: Judgment, Phrase, Punish, Penalize

examples: Humans are sentient beings capable of empathy. The philosopher argued that animals are sentient and deserve moral consideration. AI may simulate intelligence, but it is not truly sentient. She felt a sentient presence in the room, as if someone was watching.
urduMeaning: حساس، شعور رکھنے والا، محسوس کرنے کی صلاحیت رکھنے والا، خود آگاہ، جذباتی طور پر جاگا ہوا
synonyms: Conscious, Aware, Perceptive, Responsive, Cognizant
englishMeaning: Able to perceive or feel things; conscious. Having the capacity for sensation, perception, and awareness. A sentient being can experience feelings, emotions, or consciousness.
sindhiMeaning: شعور رکندڙ، محسوس ڪرڻ جي صلاحيت رکندڙ، جذباتي، سچيت، جاڳيل وجود
antonyms: Insentient, Unconscious, Unaware, Inanimate, Unfeeling
Mix everything together, Confuse good with bad, Fail to distinguish, Ignore differences
urduMeaning: اچھی اور بیکار چیز میں فرق کرنا، دانائی سے فیصلہ کرنا ، غیر ضروری معلومات میں سے مفید معلومات نکالنا، سچ کو جھوٹ سے الگ کرنا، زیادہ چیزوں میں سے بہترین کا انتخاب کرنا
englishMeaning: To distinguish what is valuable or true from what is useless or false. To judge wisely. To filter useful information from noise. To recognize truth among lies. To pick the best from many options.
synonyms: Distinguish the good from the bad, Sort out the useful from the useless, Filter the best, Identify what matters
sindhiMeaning: سٺي ۽ بيڪار شيءِ ۾ فرق ڪرڻ، دانائي سان فيصلو ڪرڻ، غير ضروري معلومات مان اهم معلومات چونڊڻ، سچ کي ڪوڙ کان الڳ ڪرڻ، گهڻين شين مان بهترين چونڊڻ
examples: The interview process helps the company separate the wheat from the chaff. A good teacher can separate the wheat from the chaff in students abilities. In the age of social media, it is hard to separate the wheat from the chaff. The competition was tough, but the judges managed to separate the wheat from the chaff.

englishMeaning: A person or group that wants to break away from a larger country or organization. Someone who supports or promotes the idea that a region, group, or community should become independent from an existing state, government, or authority. It describes ideas, movements, or actions aimed at separation.
urduMeaning: علیحدگی پسند، وہ شخص یا گروہ جو کسی ریاست یا نظام سے الگ ہونا چاہے، شخص یا گروہ جو سیاسی، سماجی ثقافتی یا مذہبی بنیاد پر کسی بڑی ریاست، نظام یا جماعت سے الگ ہونا چاہتا ہو، یہ لفظ خود مختاری یا شناخت کے تحفظ کے لیے بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے
antonyms: Unionist, Nationalist, Loyalist
synonyms: Secessionist, Dissenter, Rebel
sindhiMeaning: الڳ ٿيڻ جو حامي، جدا ٿيڻ وارو شخص يا گروهه، شخص يا گروهه کي جيڪو سياسي سماجي ثقافتي يا مذهبي سببن جي ڪري پاڻ کي وڏي نظام يا رياست کان الڳ ڪرڻ چاهي، ڪڏهن ڪڏهن اهو لفظ سڃاڻپ بچائڻ يا خودمختياري حاصل ڪرڻ لاءِ به استعمال ٿيندو آهي
examples: The government held talks with separatist leaders to reduce tensions. Separatist movements often arise due to political or cultural differences. He was accused of supporting separatist activities in the region. The separatist group demanded full independence from the country.

sindhiMeaning: محبت يا عزت جو اظهار ڪرڻ لاءِ ڪنهن کي راڳ يا دُهن سان خوش ڪرڻ، ڪنهن جي عزت محبت يا تعريف ۾ ڳايل مٺڙو راڳ يا موسيقي (گهڻو ڪري رات جو)
antonyms: Silence, Cacophony, Dissonance, Neglect
synonyms: Melody, Musical tribute, Ballad
examples: He serenaded her under the stars with his guitar. The singer serenaded the crowd with a soulful melody. He played a beautiful serenade for his beloved under the moonlight. The violinist performed a serenade in honor of the guests. The soldiers were serenaded by the villagers as they returned home. She was serenaded by the band during her birthday celebration.
englishMeaning: To sing or play music for someone, especially to show love or admiration. A piece of music or song performed, especially in the open air, typically by a man at night under the window of the person he loves. A musical performance given to honor or express affection for someone.
urduMeaning: محبت کا گیت گانا،نغمہ سنانا، محبت بھرا گیت رات کے وقت محبوب کے لیے گایا جانے والا نغمہ

examples: After months of planning, the project was rejected, so we are back to square one. He failed the exam, which means he is back to square one with his studies. When the negotiations collapsed, both sides were back to square one. We lost all our data in the system crash, and now we are back to square one.
englishMeaning: To be forced to start again from the very beginning after a failure or setback. When all the effort is wasted, and you must return to the starting point.
synonyms: Restart, Begin again
antonyms: Progress, Finish
sindhiMeaning: ٻيهر شروعات ڪرڻ، واپس شروعات کان شروع ڪرڻ، ٻيهر پهرين هنڌ تي اچڻ
urduMeaning: شروع سے دوبارہ، پھر سے ابتدا پر آ جانا، دوبارہ شروعات کرنا

antonyms: Silence, Listening, Praise without advice, Entertainment talk
sindhiMeaning: ديني نصيحت، واعظ، خطبو، وعظ، مذهبي يا اخلاقي موضوع تي آسماني ڪتابن جو حوالا ڏيئي ڪيل خطاب، مذهبي يا اخلاقي نصيحت وارو خطاب
synonyms: Lecture, Homily, Address, Discourse, Moral instruction
urduMeaning: وعظ، نصیحت، خطبہ، درس، مذہبی یا اخلاقی نصیحت پر مبنی خطاب، اخلاقی سبق دینے والی گفتگو
examples: The priest delivered a powerful sermon about kindness and forgiveness. Every Friday the imam gives a sermon to guide the community. My father gave me a long sermon about honesty and responsibility. The pastor's sermon inspired many people to help the poor.
englishMeaning: A religious speech that teaches moral or spiritual lessons. A talk or lecture given by a religious leader, usually in a place of worship, to explain religious teachings, guide people toward moral behavior, or interpret sacred texts.

sindhiMeaning: نانگ، خاص طور تي وڏو يا خطرناڪ سانپ، ڪڏهن ڪڏهن فريبڪار شخص لاءِ به استعمال ٿيندو
englishMeaning: A snake; often used for a large, dangerous or symbolic snake. Also used for a treacherous or deceitful person.
antonyms: Dove, Innocent, Honest person
urduMeaning: سانپ، خاص طور پر بڑا یا زہریلا سانپ، کبھی کبھی دھوکے باز شخص کیلئے بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے
synonyms: Snake, Viper, Reptile, Deceiver
examples: A serpent crawled through the grass. The serpent in the story guarded the treasure. He called the traitor a serpent. The ancient symbol showed a coiled serpent.

synonyms: Ophidiophobia, Snake phobia
urduMeaning: سانپ سے خوف ، سانپ دیکھنے یا سوچنے پر شدید ڈر یا بےچینی محسوس کرنا
examples: His serpentophobia made it impossible for him to visit the reptile house at the zoo. She refuses to go hiking because of her serpentophobia. Even a picture of a snake triggers his serpentophobia. The therapist helped him manage his serpentophobia through gradual exposure.
englishMeaning: An extreme or irrational fear of snakes. It goes beyond simple dislike and can cause anxiety or panic at the sight or thought of snakes.
sindhiMeaning: نانگ کان تمام گهرو يا شديد خوف، جيڪو صرف ناپسند ڪرڻ کان وڌيڪ آهي، نانگن کان تمام گهڻي گهبراھٽ
antonyms: Snake appreciation, Snake fascination

urduMeaning: ایک چھوٹا کپڑا یا کاغذ کا ٹکڑا جو کھانے کے دوران ہاتھ اور منہ صاف کرنے کے لیے استعمال کیا جاتا ہے اور بعض اوقات میز کی سجاوٹ کے لیے بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے
antonyms: Cloth-free, Bare, Uncovered (in context of table setting)
sindhiMeaning: هڪ ننڍڙو ڪپڙو يا ڪاغذي ٽڪرو جيڪو ماني کائڻ وقت هٿن ۽ وات کي صاف ڪرڻ لاءِ استعمال ٿيندو آهي ۽ ڪڏهن ڪڏهن ميز کي سينگارڻ لاءِ به استعمال ٿئي ٿو
examples: She placed a serviette on her lap before starting dinner. The waiter folded the serviette into a fancy shape. He wiped his hands with a serviette after eating the messy sandwich. Always keep a serviette handy during meals.
englishMeaning: A piece of cloth or paper used at meals to wipe the mouth or hands. A small piece of fabric or disposable paper placed at a dining table to protect clothes from spills or to clean fingers and lips while eating. It can also be folded decoratively for table settings.
synonyms: Napkin, Handkerchief (in some contexts), Tissue, Towel

sindhiMeaning: ڊگها ۽ ڏکيا لفظ استعمال ڪرڻ جي عادت، اها عادت يا انداز جنهن ۾ ماڻهو ڳالهائڻ يا لکڻ دوران تمام ڊگها ۽ مشڪل لفظ استعمال ڪري ٿو، ڪڏهن اهو علم ۽ سٺي لفظن جي ڄاڻ ڏيکاري ٿو پر ڪڏهن سمجهڻ ۾ ڏکيائي به پيدا ڪري ٿو
synonyms: Verbosity, Grandiloquence, Pomposity, Wordiness, Pretentiousness
englishMeaning: The habit of using very long, complex words, often to sound intelligent. A style of speaking or writing that uses long, often complicated words. It can be used positively for rich vocabulary, or negatively when it makes communication unclear or overly showy.
examples: His sesquipedalianism made his speech hard to understand. The professor was known for his sesquipedalianism in lectures. Avoid sesquipedalianism if you want your writing to be clear. Her essay was full of sesquipedalianism, which confused the readers.
urduMeaning: بہت لمبے اور مشکل الفاظ استعمال کرنے کی عادت، ایک ایسا انداز جس میں کوئی شخص بولتے یا لکھتے وقت بہت لمبے اور پیچیدہ الفاظ استعمال کرتا ہے، یہ بعض اوقات علم اور وسیع ذخیرہ الفاظ ظاہر کرتا ہے لیکن بعض صورتوں میں بات کو سمجھنا مشکل بنا دیتا ہے
antonyms: Simplicity, Conciseness, Brevity, Plainness
Finish, Stop, Halt
sindhiMeaning: شروع ڪرڻ، لڳي وڃڻ، ڪم ۾ مشغول ٿيڻ
urduMeaning: شروع کرنا، لگ جانا، کسی کام میں مصروف ہونا
englishMeaning: To begin doing something with purpose, energy, or determination, especially a task, work, or activity.
synonyms: Commence, Start
examples: After breakfast, she set about cleaning the house. He set about learning a new language. The workers set about repairing the road after the storm. The teacher set about preparing the exam papers.

urduMeaning: الگ رکھنا، محفوظ رکھنا، منسوخ کرنا، نظر انداز کرنا، کسی بات یا فیصلے کو وقتی طور پر نظرانداز کرنا
examples: He set aside some money for his children’s education. Let’s set aside our differences and work together. The court set aside the previous judgment. You should set aside some time each day for reading.
synonyms: Dismiss, Disregard, Allocate

englishMeaning: To raise your shoulders slightly to show that you do not know, do not care, or think something is not important. The act or movement of raising the shoulders to express uncertainty or indifference.
antonyms: Care, Show concern, React strongly, Acknowledge seriously
synonyms: Gesture, Indicate indifference, Show uncertainty, Be unconcerned
sindhiMeaning: ڪلهن کي ٿوري دير لاءِ مٿي کڻڻ ۽ پوءِ هيٺ ڪرڻ، هي عمل اڪثر تڏهن ڪيو ويندو آهي جڏهن ماڻهو کي ڳالهه جي ڄاڻ نه هجي، هو لاپرواهه هجي يا ڳالهه کي اهم نه سمجهي
examples: He shrugged when asked about the missing files. She just shrugged and walked away. I shrugged my shoulders because I did not know the answer. The teacher shrugged at the mistake and continued the lesson. He replied with a shrug. Her shrug showed she did not care. I got only a shrug in response.

She shrugged aside his advice and continued with her plan. The manager shrugged aside the complaints from customers. He shrugged aside the risks and invested all his money. Do not shrug aside criticism if you want to improve.
synonyms: Ignore, Dismiss, Brush off, Overlook, Play down
antonyms: Consider, Acknowledge, Take seriously, Accept, Address
sindhiMeaning: نظرانداز ڪرڻ، اهميت نه ڏيڻ، لاپرواهي سان رد ڪرڻ، ڪنهن ڳالهه، مسئلي يا صلاح کي بغير سنجيدگي جي رد ڪرڻ يا ان کي اهم نه سمجهڻ
urduMeaning: نظر انداز کرنا، اہمیت نہ دینا، لاپرواہی سے ٹال دینا، کسی بات، مسئلے یا مشورے کو سنجیدگی کے بغیر رد کر دینا یا اسے غیر اہم سمجھنا
englishMeaning: To dismiss or ignore something as unimportant. To treat a problem, suggestion, warning, or comment as not worth attention. It often suggests a casual or careless attitude, as if the matter does not deserve concern or serious thought.

To show indifference, doubt, or lack of concern by raising your shoulders. To express that they do not care about something, are unsure about it, or consider it unimportant. It is often accompanied by a physical gesture of raising the shoulders.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ جي اهميت نه ڏيڻ، بي پرواهي يا لاچاري ڏيکارڻ لاءِ ڪلهن کي مٿي ڪرڻ، ڪڏهن ڪڏهن اهو حيرانگي يا شڪ ظاهر ڪرڻ لاءِ به استعمال ٿئي ٿو
antonyms: Acknowledge, Notice, Care, Consider
urduMeaning: کسی بات، صورتحال یا شخص کی طرف بے توجہی یا بے پروائی ظاہر کرنے کے لیے کاندھے اُٹھانا، یہ عمل اکثر اس بات کا اظہار کرتا ہے کہ آپ کو معاملے کی پرواہ نہیں یا آپ اس سے حیران یا مشکوک ہیں
synonyms: Dismiss, Disregard, Ignore, Overlook
examples: She just shrugged at the news, showing she didn’t care. He shrugged at my suggestion, not taking it seriously. When asked about the mistake, he only shrugged at it. I shrugged at the rumors, ignoring them completely.

She shrugged off the criticism and continued her work confidently. He tried to shrug off the pain and finish the match. The team shrugged off early setbacks and won the game. Do not shrug off health warnings, they can be serious.
sindhiMeaning: ڪجهه ڳالهه کي نظرانداز ڪرڻ، ڪابه تڪليف، تنقيد، ڊپ يا مسئلو پاڻ تي اثر انداز ٿيڻ کان روڪڻ يا ان کي سنجيدگي سان نه وٺڻ
synonyms: Ignore, Dismiss, Brush aside, Shake off, Overlook
antonyms: Take seriously, Worry about, Dwell on, Accept, Acknowledge
englishMeaning: To ignore or dismiss something unpleasant or unimportant. To deliberately refuse to let something affect you. It is often used when someone ignores criticism, stress, blame, illness, fear, or a problem and continues as normal. It suggests emotional or mental strength, or sometimes carelessness, depending on context.
urduMeaning: کسی بات کو نظرانداز کرنا، کسی پریشانی، تنقید، الزام یا مسئلے کو اہمیت نہ دینا اور اس سے متاثر نہ ہونا

antonyms: Nonrelative

sindhiMeaning: شديد ردعمل، جوابي ڪاروائي، سخت ردِعمل، منفي ردِعمل، مخالفت ۾ اوچتو اُٿل

The mayor foresaw no political backlash against his proposal. There was swift backlash to the senator's controversial comments.

sindhiMeaning: ڇنڊڻ، فلٽر ڪرڻ، ڇاڻڻ، ڌار ڪرڻ، گنديون شيون هٽائڻ، ڇڪڻ لاءِ جال، ڇنڊڻ وارو اوزار، مکڻ يا اٽو ڇاڻڻ لاءِ اوزار، کير يا پاڻيءَ مان گندي شيون ڌار ڪرڻ جو اوزار، ڇاڻي، پرڻ، پروڻ
urduMeaning: چھاننا، چھلنا، الگ کرنا، فلٹر کرنا، ریزہ ریزہ کرنا، چھلنی، چھاننے کا برتن، ریت یا آٹے کو چھاننے والا برتن

englishMeaning: To strain or filter out unwanted elements. To sift, sort, or purify material or information. To examine or scrutinize carefully, filtering out the unnecessary (figurative). A utensil with a mesh or perforated bottom used for separating coarse particles from fine ones. A tool for straining liquids to remove solids. A device used in cooking, construction, or laboratory work to separate materials by size.
synonyms: Strain, Filter, Sift, Refine, Strainer, Colander, Mesh, Filter
examples: She sieved the flour before baking the cake. He sieved the water to remove impurities. The editor sieved through hundreds of submissions. The baker poured the flour through a fine sieve. The sand was run through a sieve to remove pebbles. His mind is like a sieve; he forgets everything.

englishMeaning: To put a substance (like flour or sand) through a sieve to remove lumps or larger pieces. To examine information, evidence, or ideas thoroughly to find what is important or useful.
examples: She sifted the flour before baking the cake. The detective sifted through the files for clues. We need to sift the facts from the rumors. The teacher sifted through the essays to find the best ones.
sindhiMeaning: ڇاڻڻ، فلٽر ڪرڻ، جانچڻ، تحقيق، ٿورو ٿورو ورهائڻ، ڇنڊڻ، آڪارڻ، صفائي، جاچڻ، چڪاسڻ، اٽو يا ريتي وغيرھ ڇاڻڻ
synonyms: Filter, Strain, Screen, Examine, Inspect, Analyze

examples: After walking all day in the desert, the river was a sight for sore eyes. When I saw my family waiting for me at the airport, it was a sight for sore eyes. The green valley after miles of barren land was truly a sight for sore eyes. Her smiling face early in the morning is always a sight for sore eyes.

englishMeaning: A welcome or pleasant sight. Something or someone that you are very pleased or happy to see, especially after a long time or in an unpleasant situation.
To officially receive something by writing your signature. Also to agree formally to take responsibility for something.
antonyms: Refuse, Reject, Decline, Return
synonyms: Acknowledge receipt, Accept, Receive officially, Endorse, Contract

urduMeaning: دستخط کر کے کوئی چیز وصول کرنا یا ذمہ داری قبول کرنا
examples: I had to sign for the courier package this morning. She signed for the registered letter at the post office. The company signed for new office equipment last week. The football club signed for a young striker before the season started.

antonyms: Sign out, Log out, Exit, Leave
sindhiMeaning: سسٽم ۾ داخل ٿيڻ يا لاگ ان ٿيڻ، ڪنهن تقريب يا جڳهه تي موجودگي کي سرڪاري طور تي داخل ڪرڻ
examples: I need to sign in to my email before checking messages. Please sign in at the reception desk when you arrive. You can sign in using your Google account. He forgot to sign in, so his visit was not recorded.
englishMeaning: To log into a system, website, or account by providing credentials. To officially record your attendance or presence at an event or place.

synonyms: Log in, Enter, Access, Register

englishMeaning: To formally approve or authorize something, such as a document, plan, or message. To conclude a broadcast, message, or correspondence, indicating completion. To leave work or log out from a system. To end participation or withdraw from an activity.
urduMeaning: باضابطہ طور پر منظوری دینا یا حتمی تصدیق کرنا، بات چیت یا پیغام کو ختم کرنا، کام سے رخصت ہونا یا سسٹم سے لاگ آؤٹ ہونا
antonyms: Reject, Disapprove, Deny, Continue, Start

synonyms: Approve, Authorize, Endorse, Conclude, Log out, Finish

urduMeaning: شامل ہونا یا دستخط کرنا، بے روزگاری کے فوائد کے لیے رجسٹر ہونا، کسی پروجیکٹ یا ٹیم میں کام شروع کرنا، کسی سسٹم میں لاگ ان کرنا

sindhiMeaning: شامل ٿيڻ يا شروعات ڪرڻ، بيروزگاري جي فائدي لاءِ رجسٽر ٿيڻ، ڪنهن منصوبي ۾ ڪم شروع ڪرڻ، سسٽم ۾ لاگ ان ٿيڻ
englishMeaning: To agree to join or participate in something, often a job or contract. To officially register for unemployment benefits. To start working on a new project or team. To log into a digital system or platform.

urduMeaning: سسٹم یا اکاؤنٹ سے باہر نکلنا، کسی اکاؤنٹ ایپلیکیشن یا سسٹم سے اپنی نشست ختم کرنا تاکہ دوسروں کو بغیر اجازت رسائی نہ ہو
