englishMeaning: To prevent or delay something unwanted. To keep something from happening for a period of time, often temporarily.
urduMeaning: کسی ناپسندیدہ چیز کو عارضی طور پر روکنا یا ٹالنا
antonyms: Face, Confront, Allow
synonyms: Avoid, Defer, Delay
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن اڻ وڻندڙ ڳالهه کي عارضي طور روڪڻ يا ٽارڻ
examples: He tried to stall off criticism. The government stalled off protests for weeks. She stalled off the decision until Monday. They stalled off the issue with excuses.

antonyms: Continue, Proceed, Function
englishMeaning: To stop suddenly or fail to continue. Used when a machine, vehicle, process, or plan suddenly stops working or loses momentum.
sindhiMeaning: اوچتو بند ٿي وڃڻ يا ناڪام ٿي وڃڻ، ڪنهن ڪم يا مشين جو اڳتي نه هلي سگهڻ
examples: The car stalled out in heavy traffic. The project stalled out due to lack of funds. Negotiations stalled out after disagreements. The engine stalled out on the highway.
synonyms: Stop, Fail, Break down
urduMeaning: اچانک رک جانا یا ناکام ہو جانا، کسی عمل یا مشین کا آگے نہ چل پانا

englishMeaning: To pile up, heap, or build up something together, often in a protective or supportive way (materials, fuel, snow). To increase the amount of something gradually or to fortify. Commonly used for fires, snow, earth, or resources.
antonyms: Scatter, Reduce
sindhiMeaning: وڌائڻ، وڌ ۾ وڌ ڪرڻ، تحفظ يا مدد لاءِ گڏ ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: اوپر بڑھانا، ذخیرہ کرنا، اکٹھا کرنا، ڈھیر لگانا،
examples: They banked up the sandbags before the storm. She banked up the fire to keep warm. The snow was banked up along the road. Farmers bank up soil around crops
synonyms: Heap, Pile, Accumulate

antonyms: Decide, Proceed, Act, Finalize
englishMeaning: To delay a decision or action intentionally. To avoid moving forward by wasting time, making excuses, or postponing action until a later moment
urduMeaning: جان بوجھ کر فیصلہ یا عمل مؤخر کرنا، کسی کام یا فیصلے سے بچنے کے لیے وقت ضائع کرنا یا بہانے بنانا
examples: He stalled over signing the contract because he was unsure. The manager stalled over the issue until more information arrived. She stalled over answering the question to gain time. They stalled over the plan hoping the problem would resolve itself.
synonyms: Stop, Fail, Break down
sindhiMeaning: ڄاڻي واڻي فيصلي يا ڪم ۾ دير ڪرڻ، ڪنهن ڪم يا فيصلي کان بچڻ لاءِ وقت ضايع ڪرڻ يا بهانا ٺاهڻ

synonyms: Loyal, Steadfast, Reliable, Strong, Faithful
examples: She is a stalwart supporter of community education. The doctor remained stalwart during the health crisis. He proved to be a stalwart friend in times of trouble. The team relied on its stalwart members to stay focused.
sindhiMeaning: مضبوط، وفادار ۽ قابلِ ڀروسو، اهڙو شخص يا صفت جيڪا مشڪل حالتن ۾ به وفاداري، همت ۽ مضبوط ڪردار ڏيکاري
urduMeaning: مضبوط، وفادار اور قابلِ اعتماد، ایسا شخص یا وصف جو مشکل حالات میں بھی وفاداری، ثابت قدمی اور مضبوط کردار دکھائے
antonyms: Weak, Unreliable, Disloyal, Unsteady, Fickle
englishMeaning: Very loyal, strong, and dependable. A person or quality that shows firm loyalty, strength of character, and reliability, especially in difficult situations

examples: What is newspaper stance on war. He is known for his anti-abortion stance. The government clarified its stance on climate policy. Her stance on education reform gained public support. The boxer adjusted his stance before the fight started. The teacher appreciated the student's clear stance during the debate.
englishMeaning: Position or opinion about an issue. Way of standing or posture. Attitude toward something. Stand taken in debate or politics.
synonyms: Position, Attitude, Stand, Viewpoint, Opinion, Posture
antonyms: Indifference, Neutrality, Uncertainty, Hesitation
urduMeaning: مؤقف، کھڑے ہونے کا انداز، رویہ، بحث یا سیاست میں اختیار کیا گیا مؤقف، کسی مسئلے خیال یا بحث کے بارے میں کسی شخص کا مؤقف یا رائے
sindhiMeaning: موقف، سمجھ، رايو، راءِ، بيھڻ جو طريقو، سلوڪ، ڪنھنجي باري ۾ مخصوص جذباتي يا ذھني ھلت، ڪنهن مسئلي خيال يا بحث بابت ڪنهن ماڻهو جو موقف يا راءِ

examples: I will stand by you no matter what happens. The team is standing by for further instructions. She stood by her friend during the entire crisis. We cannot stand by and watch this injustice continue.
synonyms: Support, Help, Back, Assist
englishMeaning: To support someone. To stay ready. To do nothing while something happens. To remain loyal in difficult times.
antonyms: Abandon, Ignore, Neglect, Desert
urduMeaning: سہارا دینا یا تیار رہنا، ساتھ دینا اور مشکل میں حمایت کرنا، کچھ ہوتے دیکھ کر خاموش رہنا، کارروائی کے لیے تیار کھڑا رہنا
sindhiMeaning: سپورٽ ڪرڻ يا تيار رهڻ، ڪنهن جي مدد ڪرڻ يا ساڻس وفادار رهڻ، ڪنهن به وقت عمل لاءِ تيار رهڻ، ڪجهه ٿيندي ڏسي خاموش بيٺو رهڻ

synonyms: Withdraw, Resign, Retire, Step aside
sindhiMeaning: واپس هٽجڻ، ڪنهن عمل کي روڪڻ، ذميواري کان پاسو وٺڻ، ٿورڙو آرام ڪرڻ بعد تياري جي حالت ختم ڪرڻ
examples: The police were told to stand down after the situation was under control. The CEO decided to stand down after ten years in charge. Soldiers were ordered to stand down when the threat ended. The manager asked his team to stand down and wait for further instructions.
urduMeaning: پیچھے ہٹ جانا، کسی کارروائی کو روکنا، ذمہ داری سے دستبردار ہونا یا دباؤ یا خطرہ ختم ہونے کے بعد سکون اختیار کرنا
englishMeaning: To withdraw, relax, or step aside from a position or action. To stop an action, withdraw from a position of responsibility, or relax after a period of tension or readiness. It is often used in military, official, or conflict-related contexts but can apply generally.
antonyms: Continue, Persist, Remain, Stay

englishMeaning: To become independent and self-reliant without depending on others for financial, emotional, or practical support.
examples: After finishing his studies, he decided to stand on his own feet and find a job. She works hard to stand on her own feet without asking her parents for money. Many young people want to stand on their own feet as soon as possible. Losing his job forced him to learn how to stand on his own feet quickly.
urduMeaning: اپنے پاؤں پر کھڑا ہونا، خود مختار ہونا، اپنی زندگی کے فیصلے اور اخراجات خود سنبھالنا بغیر کسی پر انحصار کیے
synonyms: Be independent, Self-reliant, Self-sufficient, Stand alone
antonyms: Depend on others, Rely on others, Be dependent, Lean on others
sindhiMeaning: پنهنجي پيرن تي بيهڻ، پاڻ تي ڀروسو ڪرڻ ۽ ڪنهن جي مدد کان سواءِ پنهنجي زندگي ۽ ضرورتون پوريون ڪرڻ

examples: Her creative ideas always make her stand out from the crowd in meetings. He worked hard to stand out from the crowd in his class. The bright red dress helped her stand out from the crowd at the event. Good communication skills help a candidate stand out from the crowd in interviews.
sindhiMeaning: ٻين ماڻهن کان الڳ ۽ نمايان هجڻ (يعني اهڙو ڪم يا شخص جيڪو عام ماڻهن ۾ خاص نظر اچي)، جتي ڪو ماڻهو يا شيءِ ٻين جي مقابلي ۾ وڌيڪ خوبصورت ذهين يا منفرد هجي ۽ هر ڪنهن جي نظر ۾ اچي وڃي
synonyms: Be unique, Be outstanding, Be exceptional, Shine out, Rise above others, Be noticeable, Be different from the rest
englishMeaning: To be noticeably different and better or more interesting than others. To be unique among others. To attract attention because of difference. To be more impressive than the rest. To not blend in with the group. To be exceptional in a competitive situation.
antonyms: Blend in, Fit in, Conform, Be ordinary, Go unnoticed, Be average, Follow the crowd
urduMeaning: دوسروں کے مقابلے میں نمایاں اور مختلف ہونا (یعنی بھیڑ میں سب سے الگ اور خاص نظر آنا)، جب کوئی شخص چیز یا خیال دوسروں کے درمیان اپنی منفرد بہتر یا خاص خصوصیات کی وجہ سے واضح طور پر نمایاں ہو جائے

antonyms: Sit down, Give up, Abandon, Fail,
sindhiMeaning: بيهي وڃڻ يا دفاع ڪرڻ، بيهڻ، ڪنهن جي حمايت ڪرڻ، وعدي مطابق نه اچڻ
urduMeaning: کھڑا ہونا یا مضبوطی سے دفاع کرنا، کھڑا ہونا، کسی کا ساتھ دینا، وعدہ کر کے نہ آنا
englishMeaning: To rise to a standing position. To rise to your feet. Also to defend someone or fail to meet someone as promised. To physically get up from a sitting or lying position. It can also mean supporting someone or something in a situation that requires courage. Another meaning is when someone does not arrive for a planned meeting or appointment.
examples: She asked him to stand up when the judge entered the room. You should stand up for your friend when he is treated unfairly. He stood up after sitting for a long time. She felt hurt because he stood her up on their meeting.
synonyms: Rise, Get up, Support, Defend

urduMeaning: دعوت دینا یا ضیافت کرنا، ضیافت ، ایک بڑا رسمی دعوتی کھانا جو کسی خاص موقع پر بہت سے لوگوں کے لیے دیا جائے، ایک بڑا اور رسمی کھانا جو کسی خاص موقع جیسے شادی تقریب یا کامیابی کے جشن کے لیے منعقد کیا جائے، اس میں بہت سے مہمان شامل ہوتے ہیں اور مختلف قسم کے کھانے پیش کیے جاتے ہیں
examples: The wedding banquet was held at a five-star hotel. They invited all the guests to a grand banquet after the ceremony. The king hosted a banquet for foreign diplomats. After winning the award, she attended a celebratory banquet. The company banqueted its employees after completing the project.
synonyms: Feast, Feast meal, Reception, Spread, Gala dinner, Celebration meal
sindhiMeaning: دعوت يا ضيافت ڪرڻ، کاڌي جي وڏي مجلس، وڏو رسمي دعوتي کاڌو جيڪو ڪنهن خاص موقعي تي ڪيترن ماڻهن لاءِ ڏنو وڃي، وڏو ۽ رسمي دعوتي کاڌو جيڪو شادي ڪاميابي يا ڪنهن اهم تقريب لاءِ ڪيو ويندو آهي، ان ۾ ڪيترائي مهمان شامل هوندا آهن ۽ مختلف قسم جا طعام پيش ڪيا ويندا آهن
englishMeaning: To entertain with a feast. A large formal meal or feast for many people, usually to celebrate an event. A grand and formal meal where many guests are invited. It is usually arranged to celebrate weddings, achievements, ceremonies, or official events. Banquets often include multiple courses of food and organized seating.
antonyms: Fast, Starvation, Hunger, Famine, Abstinence
Surrender, Submit, Give in, Back down, Yield
englishMeaning: To confront someone powerful or threatening without fear. To defend yourself or others against pressure or attack. To resist something such as criticism, force, or difficulty. To remain strong and not give in to intimidation. To tolerate or endure something difficult or unpleasant. To be strong enough to deal with a situation or challenge
examples: She stood up to the bully and refused to be afraid. He finally stood up to his boss about the unfair treatment. This material can stand up to extreme weather conditions. You must stand up to pressure if you want to succeed.
urduMeaning: مقابلہ کرنا، ڈٹ کر کھڑا ہونا، مزاحمت کرنا، ہمت سے سامنا کرنا، برداشت کرنا
sindhiMeaning: مقابلو ڪرڻ، ڊٽڻ يا سامهون بيهڻ، مزاحمت ڪرڻ، همت سان منهن ڏيڻ، برداشت ڪرڻ
synonyms: Confront, Resist, Oppose, Defend against, Face boldly, Withstand

sindhiMeaning: پنهنجي موقف تي قائم رهڻ، ڪنهن جي مخالفت يا دٻاءَ جي باوجود پنهنجي سوچ موقف يا حقن کي مضبوط طور تي برقرار رکڻ، هن ۾ همت ۽ ثابت قدمي شامل آهي
antonyms: Yield, Back down, Surrender, Give in, Compromise
examples: Despite the criticism, she stood her ground on the project. The soldier stood his ground during the attack. He stood his ground when everyone doubted his decision. Parents sometimes need to stand their ground with teenagers.
urduMeaning: اپنی پوزیشن پر قائم رہنا، مخالفت تنقید یا دباؤ کے باوجود اپنے موقف رائے یا حقوق کو مضبوطی سے برقرار رکھنا، اس میں حوصلہ اور استقلال شامل ہے
englishMeaning: To refuse to change your opinion or position, to defend your stance. To maintain your position, opinion, or rights firmly, even when facing opposition, criticism, or threat. It implies courage, determination, and assertiveness.
synonyms: Hold firm, Maintain position, Be resolute, Persist, Resist
Halt, Stop, Deadlock, Stalemate, Impasse, Gridlock
examples: The heavy rain brought traffic to a standstill. The factory came to a standstill during the strike. Negotiations reached a standstill after hours of discussion. The project is at a standstill due to lack of funds.
englishMeaning: A complete stop or situation where no progress happens. Complete halt of movement. A situation where trade or business activity stops. Talks stop because no agreement is reached. Progress in a plan or project stops. A condition in which movement, activity, discussion, or progress stops completely. It can describe physical stopping, such as traffic, or non physical situations like business, negotiations, or development coming to a halt.
urduMeaning: مکمل رکاوٹ یا ایسی حالت جہاں کوئی پیش رفت نہ ہو، حرکت کا مکمل رک جانا، کاروبار یا تجارت کا رک جانا، مذاکرات کا تعطل کیونکہ کوئی سمجھوتا نہ ہو سکا، کسی منصوبے یا ترقی کا عمل رک جانا
antonyms: Movement, Progress, Advance, Development, Flow
sindhiMeaning: مڪمل بيهڪ يا اهڙي حالت جتي ڪا اڳڀرائي نه ٿئي، حرڪت جو مڪمل بند ٿيڻ، واپار يا ڪاروبار جو بيهجي وڃڻ، ڳالهين جو رڪجي وڃڻ ڇو ته ڪو فيصلو نه ٿيو، منصوبي يا ترقي جو عمل بند ٿي وڃڻ

examples: We started off on the right foot by planning everything carefully. Try to start off on the right foot with your new colleagues. The meeting started off on the right foot with a warm welcome from the manager. Their friendship started off on the right foot and grew stronger over time.
synonyms: Start positively
urduMeaning: اچھا آغاز کرنا، خوشگوار شروعات کرنا، صحیح طریقے سے ابتدا کرنا
antonyms: Start off on the wrong foot
word: Start off on the right foot
sindhiMeaning: سٺي نموني سان شروعات ڪرڻ، سٺو آغاز ڪرڻ
englishMeaning: To begin well or correctly. To begin something in a good, positive, or successful way, especially when starting a relationship, job, project, or activity.
To have a bad beginning. To begin something in a bad, unpleasant, or unsuccessful way, especially a relationship, job, or situation that starts with misunderstanding, mistake, or tension.
word: Start off on the wrong foot
antonyms: Start off on the right foot, Start smoothly
sindhiMeaning: خراب شروعات ڪرڻ، غلط طريقي سان شروع ڪرڻ، ڪنهن ڪم رشتو يا حالتن کي خراب طريقي سان شروع ڪرڻ، جڏهن شروعات ۾ ڪا غلطي تڪرار يا ناڪامي ٿي وڃي
synonyms: Make a poor start, Get off track
examples: They started off on the wrong foot in business. I started off on the wrong foot with my new boss by arriving late on my first day. Their friendship started off on the wrong foot because of a silly argument. The project started off on the wrong foot due to poor planning. She felt they started off on the wrong foot when she forgot his name.
urduMeaning: بری شروعات کرنا، غلط آغاز کرنا، کسی کام رشتے یا صورتحال کی شروعات غلط انداز میں کرنا، جب ابتدا میں ہی کوئی غلط فہمی یا مسئلہ پیدا ہو جائے

examples: The enemy tried to starve the city into surrender by blocking all food supplies. The workers refused to be starved into submission by the unfair company policies. During the war, thousands were starved into leaving their homes. The government cannot allow its citizens to be starved into desperation.
synonyms: Coerce, Force
urduMeaning: بھوک سے مجبور کرنا ، بھوکا رکھ کر کچھ کرنے پر مجبور کرنا، کسی کو بھوک یا فاقے کے ذریعے کسی عمل پر مجبور کرنا
antonyms: Persuade, Convince
sindhiMeaning: بک جي ذريعي مجبور ڪرڻ، بک رکي ڪنهن ڪم تي مجبور ڪرڻ، ڪنهن کي بک يا کوک سبب ڪو ڪم ڪرائڻ تي مجبور ڪرڻ
englishMeaning: To force someone (or a group) to do something by depriving them of food or basic needs. It’s often used in war, sieges, or extreme hardship, meaning compelling by hunger.

urduMeaning: کسی چیز کی کمی سے پریشان ہونا، سے محروم ہونا ، کمی ہونا، کسی چیز کی شدید کمی یا محرومی کا شکار ہونا
examples: The area is starved of water. The students are starved of opportunities. The students were starved of proper facilities in their school. Children starved of love often struggle with relationships later in life. The village was starved of clean drinking water during the drought. He felt starved of opportunities to prove his talent.
sindhiMeaning: کاڌي سان گڏ ٻين ضرورتن جي کوٽ سبب تڪليف، کان محروم ٿيڻ، گھٽ هجڻ، ڪابه اهم شيءِ نه ملڻ يا ان جي کوٽ ٿيڻ
synonyms: Lack, Deprive
englishMeaning: To suffer because of a lack of something necessary (not only food). To be deprived of something essential, such as love, attention, money, or opportunities.
antonyms: Provide, Supply

sindhiMeaning: سامان بند ڪري مجبور ڪرڻ، کاڌي کان محروم ڪري مجبور ڪرڻ، بک سان شڪست ڏيڻ، ڪنهن کي کاڌي پيتي کان محروم ڪري قلعو يا هنڌ ڇڏڻ تي مجبور ڪرڻ
antonyms: Invite, Welcome
englishMeaning: To force someone to surrender, leave, or give up by cutting off their food supply. To weaken someone by deliberately depriving them of necessities (especially food).
urduMeaning: رسد بند کرکے نکال دینا، بھوک سے جھکانا ، بھوکا رکھ کر مجبور کرنا، کسی کو کھانے پینے کی چیزوں سے محروم کرکے ہتھیار ڈالنے یا کسی جگہ سے نکلنے پر مجبور کرنا
examples: The army tried to starve out the rebels. They were starved out of the town. The army tried to starve out the rebels by blocking all food supplies to the valley. The landlord cut off water and electricity to starve out the tenants. During the war, the city was besieged in an attempt to starve out its people. The company reduced resources to starve out the workers on strike.
synonyms: Drive out, Expel

englishMeaning: Not moving or not changing. Something that does not move, grow, or develop. It stays the same over time. A situation where there is no progress, improvement, or decline. A state where a person feels stuck and does not grow or improve.
synonyms: Still, Motionless, Unchanging, Fixed, Inactive
examples: The old system has remained static for years. The picture on the screen looked static and lifeless. Static electricity made the clothes stick together. His career became static after he stopped learning new skills. The economy stayed static despite new policies.
urduMeaning: غیر متحرک، جامد، بے حرکت، ساکن، لا حرکت، کوئی چیز جو نہ آگے بڑھے نہ بدلے اور ایک ہی حالت میں رہے، کوئی ترقی یا تبدیلی نہ ہو، ذہنی یا ذاتي جمود جہاں انسان آگے نہ بڑھ سکے
sindhiMeaning: نه بدلجندڙ، سڪون ۾، ساڪن، بيٺل، سڪوني، بي حرڪت، ماٺيڻو، جامد، شيءِ جيڪا نه هلي نه وڌي ۽ نه ئي وقت سان تبديل ٿئي، اهڙي حالت جتي ترقي يا تبديلي نه ٿئي، اهڙي ذهني حالت جتي انسان اڳتي نه وڌي
antonyms: Dynamic, Moving, Changing, Active, Flexible

examples: The soldiers were shocked by the barbarity of the attack. History is full of stories about the barbarity of ancient wars. The victims suffered great pain because of such barbarity. Acts of barbarity against innocent people must never be tolerated.
sindhiMeaning: اهو عمل يا رويو جيڪو انتهائي ظالماڻو بي رحم ۽ انساني همدردي کان خالي هجي (جنهن ۾ ڪنهن به قسم جي رحم يا انساني احساس جو اظهار نه هجي)
urduMeaning: انتہا ئی ظلم و ستم، درندگی یا غیر انسانی سلوک (جس میں کسی قسم کی نرمی یا رحم نہ ہو)
synonyms: Cruelty, Savagery, Brutality, Inhumanity, Ruthlessness
englishMeaning: Cruel and violent behavior. Extreme cruelty, savageness, or inhuman behavior. It refers to actions that show a lack of compassion, mercy, or civilization.
antonyms: Kindness, Compassion, Humanity, Mercy, Gentleness
Moving, Mobile, Shifting
synonyms: Fixed, Still, Immobile
urduMeaning: غیر متحرک، ایک جگہ پر رکنے یا حرکت نہ کرنے والا، نہ ہلنے والا، ایک جگہ پر رکا ہوا یا ساکن
sindhiMeaning: بي حرڪت، هڪ جاءِ تي ثابت يا غير متحرڪ، نه هلندڙ، بيهڪ تي رهندڙ، هڪ هنڌ تي بيٺل شيءِ
englishMeaning: Not moving, fixed in one place. It describes something that doesn't change position and remains still.
examples: The car remained stationary at the light. She kept the vase stationary. Stationary objects are easier to paint. The train stayed stationary for hours.

englishMeaning: Materials used for writing, such as paper, envelopes, pens, notebooks, files, and other office or school supplies. It includes all items used for writing, printing, and organizing documents.
examples: She bought new stationery. Office stationery includes pens and files. The shop sells stationery items. I need stationery for school.
antonyms: Electronics, Furniture, Tools
sindhiMeaning: لکت پڙهت جا سامان جيئن ڪاغذ لفافا قلم نوٽ بڪ فائلون ۽ ٻيا دفتري يا اسڪولي شيون، اهي سموريون شيون جيڪي لکڻ ڇپائي يا دستاويزن کي ترتيب ڏيڻ لاءِ استعمال ٿين ٿيون
synonyms: Writing materials, Supplies, Paper goods
urduMeaning: تحریری سامان، لکھنے پڑھنے کا سامان جیسے کاغذ لفافے قلم نوٹ بکس فائلیں اور دیگر دفتری یا تعلیمی چیزیں، وہ تمام اشیا جو لکھائی پرنٹنگ یا دستاویزات کی ترتیب میں استعمال ہوتی ہیں

sindhiMeaning: هاڻوڪي صورتحال، موجوده حالت، جيئن حالتون آهن، موجوده حالتن کي جيئن جو تيئن برقرار رکڻ، يعني ڪا تبديلي نه آڻڻ
urduMeaning: موجودہ حالت، موجودہ حالت جس میں کوئی تبدیلی نہ کی گئی ہو، سیاسی معاشرتی یا معاشی حالات کے تسلسل کو ظاہر کرنے کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے
examples: The government decided to maintain the status quo instead of introducing new laws. Many people resist change because they prefer the status quo. The peace agreement was designed to preserve the status quo between the two countries. The company’s management wanted to challenge the status quo and bring innovation.
synonyms: Current state, Existing condition, Present situation, Existing order, Equilibrium
englishMeaning: The existing state or condition of affairs, especially regarding social, political, or economic situations. It refers to keeping things as they currently are, without change.
antonyms: Change, Innovation, Reform, Transformation, Revolution
Use, Approach
urduMeaning: بچنا، دور رہنا، استعمال نہ کرنا، ہاتھ نہ لگانا، الگ رہنا
synonyms: Avoid, Keep away
examples: Stay off the grass because it has just been planted and needs time to grow. The doctor advised him to stay off junk food to improve his health. Please stay off social media until the issue is resolved. He was told to stay off the construction site for his own safety.
englishMeaning: To avoid stepping on, touching, using, or getting involved with something. It is often used as a warning or instruction.
sindhiMeaning: پاسو ڪرڻ، پري رهڻ، استعمال نه ڪرڻ، هٿ نه لڳائڻ، ڌار رهڻ

examples: Stay put until I come back. The doctor told him to stay put after the surgery. During the storm, residents were advised to stay put indoors. If you get lost, stay put and wait for help.
englishMeaning: Remain in the same place. Do not move. To remain where you are, especially when you are told or expected not to move. It is often used in situations involving safety, instructions, or waiting.
sindhiMeaning: ساڳي هنڌ تي رهڻ، نه هلڻ، پنهنجي جاءِ تي قائم رهڻ بغير حرڪت ڪرڻ جي، عام طور تي اهو تڏهن استعمال ٿيندو آهي جڏهن ڪنهن کي هدايت ڏني وڃي ته هو نه هلي يا ساڳي جاءِ تي انتظار ڪري
urduMeaning: وہیں رہنا، اپنی جگہ سے نہ ہلنا، اپنی جگہ پر قائم رہنا اور حرکت نہ کرنا، یہ اکثر اس وقت استعمال ہوتا ہے جب کسی کو ہدایت دی جائے کہ وہ وہیں رہے یا انتظار کرے
synonyms: Remain, Stay, Wait, Hold position, Not move
antonyms: Move, Leave, Go away, Relocate

englishMeaning: Not changing in your attitudes or aims. Staying the same for a long time and not changing quickly or unexpectedly. Firmly fixed in place. Not subject to change.
synonyms: Constant, Firm, Fixed,
antonyms: Unreliable, Infirm, Weak
examples: The group remained steadfast in its support for the new system, even when it was criticized in the newspapers. He remained steadfast in his determination to bring the killers to justice.
urduMeaning: ثابت قدم، پکا، استوار
sindhiMeaning: ثابت قدم، پڪو، مستحڪم، مضبوط، قائم، مستقل مزاج

examples: She stole my thunder by announcing the project before I could. He stole the manager’s thunder by presenting the idea first. Don’t steal her thunder; let her share the news herself. The guest speaker stole the host’s thunder with his surprise speech.
englishMeaning: To take attention, credit, or praise away from someone by doing or saying something similar before they do. To spoil or reduce the effect of another person’s success, idea, announcement, or performance by introducing it first or by attracting attention away from them. It often implies taking credit or recognition that was meant for someone else, sometimes unintentionally and sometimes deliberately.
synonyms: Upstage someone, Overshadow someone, Outshine someone, Take credit, Draw attention away
urduMeaning: کسی کی کامیابی، بات یا اعلان کی اہمیت یا توجہ خود لے لینا، کسی کے کام یا بات کا اثر کم کر دینا، کسی کے اعلان سے پہلے خود بات کر دینا، کسی کی توجہ اپنی طرف لے لینا، کسی کی محنت کی اہمیت کم کر دینا
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن جي ڪاميابي خيال يا اعلان جي اهميت يا ڌيان پاڻ ڏانهن کڻي وڃڻ، ڪنهن جي ڳالهه يا ڪم جي اثر کي گهٽائي ڇڏڻ، ڪنهن ٻئي جي ڪاميابي جو اثر گهٽ ڪرڻ، ڪنهن جي اعلان کان اڳ پاڻ ڳالهه ظاهر ڪرڻ، ڪنهن جي ڌيان کي پنهنجي طرف موڙڻ، ڪنهن جي محنت جي اهميت گهٽائڻ
antonyms: Support someone, Highlight someone, Give credit, Praise openly, Acknowledge someone
Aroma, Fragrance, Perfume
englishMeaning: A strong unpleasant smell. A bad effect that follows an unpleasant event or situation and is noticeable for a long time.
synonyms: Stink, Pong, Unpleasant smell
sindhiMeaning: بدبوءِ، ڌپ، سڙائد، بانسَ
urduMeaning: بدبو، سڑاند، عفونت
examples: I caught the stench of fear from the duke and his men. The stench of rotting fish filled the hut. We finally discovered the dead rat that was causing the stench in the basement

Please step aside so others can pass. The manager stepped aside to let his deputy take charge. She stepped aside from the project temporarily. When the argument heated up, he stepped aside to avoid conflict.
antonyms: Stand firm, Block, Resist, Hold position
englishMeaning: Physically move sideways to allow passage. Give up a position, role, or responsibility temporarily or permanently to let someone else take over. To allow someone else to take the lead or handle a situation.
urduMeaning: جسمانی طور پر ایک طرف ہٹنا تاکہ کوئی گزر سکے، وقتی یا مستقل طور پر اپنی ذمہ داری کردار یا عہدہ چھوڑنا تاکہ دوسرا سنبھال سکے، کسی کو قیادت یا معاملہ سنبھالنے کی اجازت دینا
sindhiMeaning: پاسي هٽڻ ته جيئن ڪنهن کي گذرڻ جو موقعو ملي، عارضي يا مستقل طور تي پنهنجو ڪردار عهده يا ذميواري ڇڏڻ ته جيئن ٻيو ماڻهو ان کي سنڀالي، ڪنهن کي اڳواڻي ڪرڻ يا صورتحال کي منهن ڏيڻ جي اجازت ڏيڻ
synonyms: Move aside, Make way, Yield, Give way

sindhiMeaning: منسوخ ڪرڻ، ڪنهن ڪم منصوبي يا عمل کي مڪمل ٿيڻ کان اڳ بند ڪرڻ يا ختم ڪرڻ خاص طور تي جڏهن ان کي جاري رکڻ مناسب نه هجي يا ممڪن نه هجي، طبي طور تي حمل ختم ڪرڻ، ڪچو ٻار ڪيرائڻ
examples: The pilot decided to abort the landing due to bad weather. The system will abort the process if an error is detected. They had to abort the mission after technical failure. The doctor may abort the procedure if complications arise.
antonyms: Continue, Proceed, Start, Begin, Resume, Carry on
urduMeaning: روک دینا یا ختم کر دینا، منسوخ کرنا، حمل کو ختم کرنا یا روک دینا، کسی کام منصوبے یا عمل کو مکمل ہونے سے پہلے روک دینا یا ختم کر دینا
englishMeaning: To end a process, mission, task, or action before it is completed, usually because continuing is unsafe, unnecessary, or not possible. Medical: to terminate a pregnancy (formal/clinical use)
synonyms: Cancel, Stop, Terminate, Halt, Discontinue, End, Call off

urduMeaning: کسی چیز کی قیمت کم کروانا، بیچنے والے کو راضی کرنا کہ وہ اصل قیمت سے کم پر بیچے
synonyms: Haggle, Negotiate, Talk down, Cut the price
antonyms: Overpay, Pay full price, Agree without negotiation
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ جي قيمت گهٽائڻ لاءِ ڳالهه ٻولهه ڪرڻ، وڪڻندڙ کي راضي ڪرڻ ته هو شيءِ اصل ڀيٽ ۾ سستي ڏئي
englishMeaning: To persuade a seller to reduce the price of something. To negotiate for a lower price than originally asked.
examples: She managed to bargain down the price of the carpet from $200 to $150. He always tries to bargain down the shopkeepers in the market. We bargained down the rent before signing the agreement. They couldn’t bargain down the cost because the item was already discounted.

She stepped back to get a better view of the painting. I need to step back and think before making a decision. He stepped back when he saw the dog growling. Sometimes it helps to step back from your work and rest your mind.
englishMeaning: To physically moving a step backward, creating space or distance. Figuratively, it can mean taking a pause to reflect, reassess, or gain perspective before acting.
antonyms: Advance, Move forward, Approach, Rush in
sindhiMeaning: پوئتي قدم کڻڻ، ڪنهن ڪم کان پاڻ کي هٽائڻ، صورتحال کي آرام سان ڏسڻ يا سوچڻ لاءِ فاصلو وٺڻ
urduMeaning: پیچھے ہٹنا، کسی کام سے خود کو الگ کرنا، صورتحال پر غور کرنے کے لیے وقتی طور پر پیچھے ہٹنا
synonyms: Retreat, Withdraw, Pull back, Pause, Reconsider

antonyms: Take office, Assume, Continue, Remain
synonyms: Resign, Retire, Relinquish, Bow out
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن اهم عهدي تان رضاڪارانه طور تي وڃڻ، طاقت، اهميت يا شدت گهٽائڻ
englishMeaning: To leave a position of authority voluntarily. To decrease in power, importance, or intensity.
examples: The CEO decided to step down after ten years in the company. He stepped down from the committee due to health issues. The government stepped down some regulations to ease business. She stepped down to let a younger manager take charge.
urduMeaning: کسی اہم عہدے سے خود سے استعفیٰ دینا، طاقت، اہمیت یا شدت میں کمی لانا

examples: The teacher had to step in when the students started arguing. She stepped in to manage the office while her boss was on leave. The police stepped in to control the crowd. He stepped in quickly to prevent a serious mistake.
englishMeaning: To intervene in a situation to help, control, or stop something. To enter a place suddenly or briefly. To take over someone’s role or responsibility temporarily. To become involved when action is needed.
sindhiMeaning: وچ ۾ اچڻ، مداخلت ڪرڻ، اندر داخل ٿيڻ، ڪنهن جي غير موجودگي ۾ ان جي ذميواري سنڀالڻ، ضرورت پوڻ تي اڳتي اچي ڪارروائي ڪرڻ
synonyms: Intervene, Interfere, Enter, Take over, Get involved
urduMeaning: مداخلت کرنا، درمیان میں آنا، اندر داخل ہونا، کسی کی غیر موجودگی میں اس کی ذمہ داری سنبھالنا، ضرورت کے وقت آگے بڑھ کر کارروائی کرنا
antonyms: Withdraw, Ignore, Stay out, Step aside, Avoid involvement

urduMeaning: کسی جگہ میں قدم رکھنا، ذمہ داری سنبھالنا
examples: She stepped into the room quietly. After the manager resigned, he stepped into the leadership role. I stepped into the shoes of my predecessor to continue the project. The firefighter stepped into the burning building without hesitation.
englishMeaning: To physically enter a space or area. To take on a role, responsibility, or situation, often replacing someone else.
antonyms: Exit, Leave, Withdraw, Step out
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن جاءِ ۾ داخل ٿيڻ، ذميواري سنڀالڻ
synonyms: Enter, Assume, Take on, Move into

antonyms: Avoid, Lift, Withdraw
englishMeaning: To place your foot onto or over something, often accidentally or intentionally. To tread on someone’s feelings or rights, to act in a domineering or aggressive way. To accelerate, especially a vehicle, by pressing the pedal.
urduMeaning: پیڈل دبانے سے رفتار بڑھانا، دبانا یا روکنا، اختیار سے تجاوز کرنا، دباؤ بڑھانا، جلدی کرنا، دخل دینا، پاؤں کے نشانات چھوڑنا، ذبات یا حقوق کو ٹھیس پہنچانا، پیر پر حادثتاً پیر رکھنا
synonyms: Tread on, Trample, Press, Crush
sindhiMeaning: گاڏي جي پيڊل تي زور ڏيڻ سان رفتار وڌائڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ کي دٻائڻ يا روڪڻ، اختيار کان وڌ ڪم ڪرڻ، زور وڌائڻ، جلدي ڪرڻ، مداخلت ڪرڻ، ڪنهن جي پير تي غلطِي سان پير رکڻ، پير جا نشان ڇڏڻ
examples: She stepped on a nail in the backyard. Don’t step on his pride by criticizing him publicly. Step on the accelerator to reach on time. The government stepped on protests to maintain order. Step on it! We are late for the meeting.

englishMeaning: To leave a room, building, or place for a short period. To go outside. To attend an event or social gathering. To act boldly or assertively in a situation.
sindhiMeaning: ٻاهر وڃڻ، ٻاهر نڪرڻ، ڪنهن تقريب يا سماجي ملاقات ۾ شرڪت ڪرڻ، بهادري سان قدم رکڻ يا عمل ڪرڻ
examples: I need to step out for a moment to take a call. She stepped out to get some fresh air. He stepped out to attend the meeting downtown. The young manager stepped out confidently to present his ideas.
urduMeaning: باہر جانا، باہر نکلنا، سی تقریب یا اجتماع میں شرکت کرنا، جرأت کے ساتھ قدم اٹھانا یا عمل کرنا
antonyms: Stay in, Remain, Linger, Withhold, Hesitate
synonyms: Leave briefly, Go out, Exit, Attend, Venture
Increase, Intensify, Enhance, Accelerate, Rise, Take charge, Advance
sindhiMeaning: مقدار، شدت يا سطح وڌائڻ، عمل يا ذميواري سنڀالڻ، اڳتي اچڻ يا ويجهو ٿيڻ
urduMeaning: مقدار، شدت یا معیار بڑھانا، کام کرنا یا ذمہ داری قبول کرنا، آگے بڑھنا یا قریب آنا
englishMeaning: To increase the level, amount, or intensity of something. To take action or responsibility, especially when needed. To move closer or forward physically.
antonyms: Decrease, Reduce, Lower, Step back, Retreat
examples: The company decided to step up production to meet demand. She stepped up and took responsibility for the project. Volunteers stepped up during the flood crisis. He stepped up to the microphone and gave his speech.

sindhiMeaning: ذميواري قبول ڪري اڳتي وڌڻ، ڪنهن اهم يا ڏکئي موقعي تي اڳتي وڌي ذميواري کڻڻ ۽ عمل ڪرڻ
englishMeaning: To accept responsibility and take action. To willingly take responsibility in a difficult or important situation and act with courage or initiative
examples: When the team leader resigned, she stepped up to the plate and managed the project. It is time for the government to step up to the plate and address climate risks. He stepped up to the plate during the crisis and helped the community. A good manager knows when to step up to the plate and make tough decisions.
urduMeaning: ذمہ داری قبول کر کے آگے آنا، کسی مشکل یا اہم موقع پر آگے بڑھ کر ذمہ داری لینا اور عملی قدم اٹھانا
antonyms: Avoid responsibility, Back away, Shrink from duty, Refuse to act
synonyms: Take responsibility, Rise to the occasion, Take charge, Accept the challenge

urduMeaning: اپنی کارکردگی محنت یا مہارت کو بہتر بنانا تاکہ بہتر نتیجہ حاصل کیا جا سکے یا مقابلے میں آگے بڑھا جا سکے، جب کسی کو اپنی محنت صلاحیت یا کارکردگی کو بہتر کرنے کی ضرورت ہو تاکہ وہ بہتر نتائج حاصل کر سکے یا دوسروں کے برابر یا ان سے آگے نکل سکے
sindhiMeaning: پنهنجي ڪارڪردگي محنت يا مهارت کي بهتر بڻائڻ ته جيئن بهتر نتيجا حاصل ٿين يا مقابلي ۾ اڳتي وڌجي، جڏهن ڪنهن کي پنهنجي محنت صلاحيت يا ڪارڪردگي کي وڌائڻ جي ضرورت هجي ته جيئن هو بهتر نتيجا حاصل ڪري سگهي يا مقابلي ۾ اڳتي نڪري سگهي
antonyms: Perform poorly, Slack off, Underperform, Decline in effort, Give up
synonyms: Improve performance, Raise your standards, Work harder, Upgrade your skills, Level up
englishMeaning: To improve your performance, effort, or skills in order to do better than before or compete at a higher level. To start performing better than you currently are. It is used when someone needs to increase effort, improve skills, or raise the quality of work or behavior in order to succeed or compete.
examples: If you want to get promoted, you need to step up your game. The team must step up their game to win the final match. She stepped up her game and passed the exam with top marks. You need to step up your game if you want to compete in this industry.

synonyms: Label, Generalize, Categorize, Prejudge
urduMeaning: لکیر کا فقیر، کسی گروہ کے بارے میں عام رائے یا خیال، کسی گروہ یا شخص کے بارے میں قائم شدہ اور سادہ خیال جو حقیقت کی عکاسی نہیں کرتا، یہ نسل جنس عمر پیشہ یا دیگر خصوصیات پر مبنی ہو سکتا ہے اور اکثر غیر منصفانہ رویوں کی وجہ بنتا ہے، کسی کو عام خیال کے مطابق پرکھنا یا دیکھنا
englishMeaning: To form a fixed idea about a person or thing which may not really be true. A fixed idea or image that many people have of a particular type of person or thing, but which is often not true in reality and may cause hurt and offence. A generalized belief or assumption about a group of people or things that may not accurately reflect reality. It can be based on race, gender, age, profession, or other characteristics and often leads to unfair judgments.
antonyms: Treat individually, Recognize uniqueness, Judge fairly
examples: You shouldn’t stereotype people based on their accent. Teachers often stereotype students by their grades. Media tends to stereotype minorities. She was stereotyped as a shy person just because she was quiet.
sindhiMeaning: لڪير جو فقير، ڪنهن گروپ يا ماڻهو بابت هڪ مقرر ڪيل خيال جيڪو حقيقت سان مطابقت نه رکي اڪثر غير منصفانه سوچ يا فيصلن جو سبب بڻجي ٿو، ڪنهن کي اڳڀرو خيال مطابق جانچڻ يا ڏسڻ، ڪنهن شخص يا گروپ کي هڪ مقرر ٿيل سادي خيال تحت رکڻ، حقيقتن جي بدران مفروضن تي ٻڌل، اڪثر غير منصفانه نتيجا پيدا ڪري ٿو

antonyms: Fertile, Productive, Fruitful, Contaminated (opposite of sterile in hygienic sense)
urduMeaning: بانجھ، بے ثمر، صاف ستھرا ، بے اثر، بےثمر، بے جان، خالی، جراثيم سے پاک، غَیر زَرخَیز
englishMeaning: Unable to produce offspring or lacking the ability to grow or develop. Not producing anything of value; unproductive, barren. Completely clean, free from bacteria or germs.
synonyms: Infertile, Barren, Unproductive, Clean, Disinfected
sindhiMeaning: غير مؤثر، بنا پھل، ناپيد، بانجھ، جراثيم کان پاڪ، صاف، بي اثر، غيرآباد، بنجر، بي ڦل، نامرد، خصي
examples: The couple discovered they were sterile and could not have children. The desert soil is sterile and cannot support crops. The surgeon used sterile gloves during the operation. His arguments were sterile and did not convince anyone.

If you stick at your studies, you will improve your results. She stuck at the project despite many problems. Learning a new language is hard, but you must stick at it. He advised his team to stick at the plan until the end.
sindhiMeaning: ڪم کي مشڪل هوندي به جاري رکڻ، ڪنهن ڪم کي مشڪل هوندي به ثابت قدمي سان جاري رکڻ ۽ هار نه مڃڻ
englishMeaning: To continue doing something with effort, even when it is difficult. To keep working on a task or activity without giving up, especially when it becomes hard or frustrating. It shows determination and persistence.
urduMeaning: مشکل ہونے کے باوجود کسی کام میں لگے رہنا، کسی کام کو مشکلات کے باوجود جاری رکھنا اور ہمت نہ ہارنا
antonyms: Give up, Quit, Abandon, Drop, Leave off
synonyms: Persevere, Persist, Keep at, Continue, Carry on

antonyms: Abandon, Desert, Leave, Reject, Turn against
sindhiMeaning: ساٿ ڏيڻ، وفادار رهڻ، ڏکئي وقت ۾ به گڏ رهڻ، يعني ڪنهن ماڻهو، فيصلي يا ڳالهه سان مشڪل حالتن ۾ به گڏ رهڻ ۽ ان کي نه ڇڏڻ
urduMeaning: ساتھ دینا، وفادار رہنا، مشکل وقت میں بھی حمایت کرنا، کسی شخص، فیصلے یا مؤقف کے ساتھ حالات خراب ہونے کے باوجود کھڑے رہنا
englishMeaning: To remain faithful, loyal, or supportive, especially during difficult times. It is often used when someone does not abandon a person, opinion, or promise even when there is pressure to change or leave. To support someone or something consistently and not leave or abandon them.
synonyms: Support, Stand by, Remain loyal to, Stay with, Back
examples: She promised to stick by her friend during tough times. The lawyer decided to stick by his original argument. Good leaders stick by their teams even under pressure. He stuck by his values despite criticism.

urduMeaning: کسی بات پر اَڑے رہنا، کسی خاص چیز یا حق کا مطالبہ کرتے رہنا، کسی چیز یا حق پر اَڑے رہنا، اپنی شرط یا مطالبے پر زور دینا، سمجھوتہ نہ کرنا، کسی خاص چیز یا فائدے کے لیے مطالبہ جاری رکھنا
sindhiMeaning: پنهنجي ڳالھ تي اَٽل رهڻ، ڪنهن خاص شيءِ يا حق لاءِ ضد ڪرڻ، جنهن تي راضي نه ٿيڻ، پنهنجي حق يا ضرورت لاءِ زور ڀرڻ، ڪنهن شرط يا مطالبو تي زور ڏيڻ
examples: He stuck out for a higher salary despite pressure from the company. The workers are sticking out for better safety conditions. She stuck out for her original plan and refused to change it. They decided to stick out for a written agreement before signing anything.
englishMeaning: To insist on having or getting something and refuse to accept less. To firmly demand a specific condition, amount, right, or benefit. A person who sticks out for something does not compromise easily and continues to insist until their demand is met. It is often used in negotiations, requests, or disagreements.
antonyms: Give in, Compromise, Settle for, Yield
synonyms: Insist on, Demand, Hold out for, Press for
Adhere to, Follow, Persist with, Remain with, Continue
antonyms: Abandon, Leave, Quit, Deviate from, Give up
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ڪم، منصوبي، اصول يا شخص سان وفادار رهڻ، مقرر ڪيل رستي، قانون يا حڪم تي عمل ڪرڻ، ڪنهن فيصل يا رويي تي ثابت قدم رهڻ
examples: She decided to stick to her diet despite the party. If you stick to the plan, you will finish on time. He sticks to his principles no matter what. I will stick to this book until I finish reading it.
urduMeaning: کسی کام، منصوبے یا عادت پر قائم رہنا، کسی شخص یا چیز کے ساتھ وفادار یا مستحکم رہنا، کسی اصول، منصوبے یا راہ کی پابندی کرنا،کسی رائے یا فیصلہ پر ثابت قدم رہنا
englishMeaning: To continue doing something, to follow or remain with something. To stay with a particular plan, task, rule, or person without changing or giving up. It emphasizes persistence, loyalty, or adherence.

synonyms: Interrupt, Intrude, Burst in
sindhiMeaning: اوچتوبنا اجازت اندر اچڻ يا ڳالهه ۾ ٽپ ڏيڻ، بنا اجازت اچڻ يا ٽوڪڻ، بي ادبي سان مداخلت ڪرڻ
antonyms: Wait, Respect, Refrain, Stay out
urduMeaning: بے ادبی سے داخل ہونا یا بات میں مداخلت کرنا، اجازت کے کسی جگہ داخل ہونا
examples: He barged in without knocking. Don’t barge in when someone else is speaking. She barged in on our private meeting. The kids barged into the kitchen shouting loudly. He barged in while we were having a serious discussion.
englishMeaning: To enter rudely or interrupt suddenly. On relax after hard work. To react strongly or forcefully. Can also mean to return money illegally (bribe). To suddenly enter a place or conversation without permission, often in a noisy or impolite way, ignoring others.

sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن جي حمايت ڪرڻ، ڪنهن شخص يا ڳالهه جي حق ۾ ڳالهائڻ يا ان جو بچاءُ ڪرڻ، خاص طور تي جڏهن ان سان ناانصافي ٿي رهي هجي يا ماڻهو ان تي الزام هڻي رهيا هجن
examples: She stuck up for her colleague when he was blamed unfairly. A good teacher should always stick up for their students. He decided to stick up for his beliefs despite strong opposition. Friends are expected to stick up for each other in difficult times.
englishMeaning: To defend or support someone or something, especially when they are criticized or treated unfairly. To protect, defend, or speak in favor of a person, idea, or right when others oppose it or treat it unjustly.
urduMeaning: کسی کی حمایت کرنا، کسی شخص خیال یا حق کا دفاع کرنا یا اس کے حق میں کھڑا ہونا، خاص طور پر اس وقت جب اس پر تنقید ہو رہی ہو یا اس کے ساتھ ناانصافی ہو رہی ہو
synonyms: Defend, Support, Stand up for, Back, Protect
antonyms: Abandon, Oppose, Betray, Neglect, Turn against
Abandon, Leave, Give up on, Quit
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن سان يا ڪنهن ڪم سان لڳاتار گڏ رهڻ، فيصلي، منصوبي يا ڪم ۾ ثابت قدم رهڻ، ڪنهن جي مدد يا ساٿ ڏيڻ، ساڻ گڏ هلڻ، مضبوط وابستگي ڏيکارڻ، ڪنهن سان وفادار رهڻ
synonyms: Stay with, Continue, Persist with, Remain loyal to
urduMeaning: کسی کے ساتھ یا کسی کام کے ساتھ قائم رہنا، کسی فیصلے یا منصوبے پر مستقل مزاجی سے قائم رہنا، کسی کی مدد یا حمایت جاری رکھنا، وفادار رہنا، کسی شخص، ٹیم یا منصوبے کے ساتھ وابستگی رکھنا
englishMeaning: To continue with someone or something; to remain loyal or committed. To stay involved with a person, plan, activity, or idea despite difficulties or challenges. It implies persistence, loyalty, or ongoing support. It can be used in professional, personal, or casual contexts.
examples: I will stick with this project until it’s finished. Stick with me, and I’ll show you the best route. She decided to stick with her old team despite the offers from others. If you stick with a healthy routine, you will feel better soon.

He'll come to a sticky end one of these days if he carries on like that. He met a sticky end after getting involved with the gang. Ignoring safety rules can lead to a sticky end. The villain in the story faced a sticky end. Many pirates in history met a sticky end at sea.
urduMeaning: برا انجام، ایسی صورتحال جس میں کسی کو نقصان، خطرہ یا موت کا سامنا ہو، عام طور پر خطرناک یا مجرمانہ حالات کے تناظر میں
sindhiMeaning: خراب انجام، ڪنهن کي خطري، نقصان يا موت واري انجام تائين پهچڻ، خاص طور تي خطري يا ڏوهن واري صورتحال ۾
englishMeaning: A bad or unpleasant outcome, often referring to death or serious trouble. A situation where someone meets a disastrous, harmful, or fatal outcome. It is often used in contexts of danger, crime, or risky situations.
synonyms: Disastrous outcome, Fatal end, Ruin, Demise
antonyms: Safe outcome, Happy ending, Successful outcome, Survival

urduMeaning: کڑا، سخت، ضدی، بے لچک
synonyms: Firm, Rigid
antonyms: Flexible, Elastic
examples: The windows were stiff & she couldn’t get them open. The company faces stiff competition from its rivals.
sindhiMeaning: سخت، موڙي نه سگڻ، رسمي، بي لچڪ، سگھارو، ڏکيو، ڏاڍو، ضدي، سرڪش، تيز، پڪو پُختو، مستحڪم
englishMeaning: Difficult to bend or move. The body of a dead person. To cheat somebody or not pay them what you owe them, especially by not leaving any money as a tip. Very much, to an extreme degree. Incapable of or highly resistant to bending.

sindhiMeaning: هٺيلو، ضدي، وڏائي خور، مغرور
synonyms: Arrogant
antonyms: Humble
englishMeaning: Proud & refusing to change. Stubborn. Having a feeling of superiority that shows itself in an overbearing attitude. Sticking to an opinion, purpose, or course of action in spite of reason, arguments, or persuasion.
examples: Four of his friends are stiff necked. He was too stiff-necked to admit that "underlings" might have useful ideas
urduMeaning: کڑا، سخت، ضدی، بے لچک

englishMeaning: To prevent something from happening, to prevent a feeling from being expressed. To withhold from circulation or expression. To cut off (the voice, the breath, etc). To kill by depriving of oxygen.
antonyms: Ventilate, Stimulate, Excite
sindhiMeaning: لِڪائڻ، ظاھر نه ڪرڻ، گهو گهو ڏيڻ، گلو گهٽڻ، ٻوساٽڻ، داٻڻ، گل ڪرڻ، گھٽو ڏيئي مارڻ، ٻوساٽڻ، دٻي ڇڏڻ، وساٽڻ، نڙي گھٽڻ
synonyms: Suffocate, Suppress, Choke (back)
urduMeaning: دم روک دینا، سانس رک جانا، دَم گھونٹ کر مار دینا، چھُپا دینا ، دم گھُٹنا
examples: She managed to stifle a yawn. They hope the new rules will not stifle creativity. The government failed to stifle the unrest. The army stifled the rebellion. Stifling her impatience, she waited another half an hour. I felt I was stifling in the airless room.

sindhiMeaning: خاموش ۽ سادن ماڻهن جي اندر گهري سوچ عقل يا لڪل صلاحيتون هونديون آهن، جيڪو ماڻهو گهٽ ڳالهائيندو آهي يا تمام خاموش هوندو آهي اهو اندر ۾ گهري سوچ وڏي سمجهه علم يا لڪل قابليت رکي سگهي ٿو، جيئن سڪون وارو پاڻي گهرو هوندو آهي تيئن خاموش ماڻهو به گهري شخصيت وارا هوندا آهن
synonyms: Quiet people often think deeply, Silent people may be wise, Depth beneath calmness, Actions speak louder than words, Wise men speak little
urduMeaning: خاموش اور پُرسکون لوگ اکثر گہری سوچ سمجھ یا چھپی ہوئی صلاحیت رکھتے ہیں، خاموش یا کم بولنے والے لوگ اکثر اندر سے بہت سمجھدار ذہین حساس یا باصلاحیت ہوتے ہیں، جیسے پرسکون پانی گہرا ہو سکتا ہے ویسے ہی خاموش انسان کی شخصیت بھی گہری ہو سکتی ہے
antonyms: Empty vessels make the most noise, Loud people are not always wise, Shallow minds talk too much, All bark and no bite
englishMeaning: Quiet or calm people often have deep thoughts, strong feelings, great intelligence, or hidden abilities. A person who does not talk much or show off may actually be very wise, emotional, intelligent, or powerful inside. Just like calm water may be very deep, quiet people may have deep knowledge, strong character, or hidden talents.
examples: Ahmed rarely speaks in meetings, but his ideas are always brilliant, Still waters run deep. She looks quiet and shy, yet she writes amazing poetry, Still waters run deep. Many students ignored the silent boy in class, but he became the top scorer, Still waters run deep. My grandfather speaks very little, but his advice is always wise, Still waters run deep.

urduMeaning: لمبا ڈنڈا جن پر کھڑے ہو کر چلا جاتا ہے، عمارت کو زمین سے اونچا رکھنے کے لیے ستون، بات چیت یا تحریر کا مصنوعی انداز ، عمارت کو زمین سے اونچا رکھنے والا ستون، میلوں یا کھیلوں میں استعمال ہونے والے لمبے ڈنڈے، بناوٹی یا غیر فطری انداز گفتگو
examples: A circus performance on stilts. The workers walked on stilts to paint the tall wall. Many houses near rivers are built on stilts to avoid flood water. The festival performer entertained the crowd while walking on stilts. His speech sounded formal and stilted, which made the conversation uncomfortable.
sindhiMeaning: لٺ، ٽيڪ ڏيندڙ ٿنبو، ڊگهو ٿنڀو يا ڪاٺي جنهن سان ماڻهو مٿي هلن يا عمارت کي زمين کان مٿي رکيو وڃي، ڳالھائڻ يا لکڻ جو غير فطري انداز، عمارت کي مٿي کڻندڙ ٿنڀو، ميلن يا ڪم ۾ استعمال ٿيندڙ ڊگهي ڪاٺي پير، غير فطري گفتگو يا لکڻ
antonyms: Natural style, Simple speech, Ground level support, Informal expression
synonyms: Pole, Support, Post, Raised support, Artificial style (figurative sense)
englishMeaning: A long pole used to raise a person or structure above the ground. Also refers to stiff or unnatural style in speech or writing. Support post that lifts buildings above ground. Long poles used by performers or workers. Figurative use for artificial language or behavior.
To touch skin or make a small hole to feel sharp pain, To make feel angry, upset, The sharp pointed part of insect that goes into skin leaving poisonous wound.
examples: The scorpion has a sting in its tail. A wasp or bee sting is painful but not necessarily serious. Be careful of nettles they sting.
antonyms: Comfort, Undercharge
sindhiMeaning: زهر، ڏنگڻ، ڏاڍو سور ٿيڻ، ڏنگ، گهائڻ
urduMeaning: ڈنک، کاٹنا، ڈسنا
synonyms: Tingle, Venom
Force into, Rush into, Invade
urduMeaning: زبردستی کسی جگہ یا بات میں گھس جانا، کسی جگہ کمرے یا گفتگو میں اچانک بدتمیزی یا لاپرواہی کے ساتھ بغیر اجازت داخل ہونا، یہ رویہ عموماً دوسروں کی نجی حدود کی خلاف ورزی سمجھا جاتا ہے
englishMeaning: To forcefully enter a place or topic. To enter a room, situation, or discussion suddenly and aggressively, often causing disruption or discomfort to others.
antonyms: Avoid, Withdraw, Leave
examples: The manager barged into the meeting unexpectedly. He barged into the room full of anger. She barged into their conversation without thinking. The police barged into the house at midnight.
sindhiMeaning: زبردستي اوچتو ڪنهن جاءِ يا ڳالهه ۾ گهڙڻ، ڪنهن هنڌ ڪمري يا ڳالهه ٻولهه ۾ اوچتو بي ادبانه نموني سان ۽ بغير اجازت جي داخل ٿيڻ، اهو عمل عام طور ٻين جي بي آرامي يا ناراضگي جو سبب بڻجي ٿو

examples: His stinginess made it difficult for him to maintain friendships. She was criticized for her stinginess despite having a high income. Stinginess can sometimes lead to missed opportunities in life. The old man's stinginess became a topic of discussion in the village.
englishMeaning: The quality of being unwilling to spend or give money. The habit or attitude of being extremely careful with money or resources, often to the point of not wanting to share or spend even when it is reasonable or necessary. A stingy person avoids generosity and prefers to keep everything for themselves.
urduMeaning: کنجوسی کرنے کی عادت یا حالت، ایسی عادت یا رویہ جس میں انسان پیسہ یا وسائل خرچ کرنے یا دوسروں کے ساتھ بانٹنے سے گریز کرتا ہے چاہے ضرورت ہی کیوں نہ ہو، ایسا شخص فیاضی سے دور ہوتا ہے
synonyms: Miserliness, Parsimony, Tightfistedness, Meanness, Penny pinching
sindhiMeaning: ڪنجوسي ڪرڻ جي عادت يا حالت، اهڙي عادت يا رويو جنهن ۾ ماڻهو پئسا يا وسيلا خرچ ڪرڻ يا ٻين سان ورهائڻ کان گهڻو پاسو ڪري جيتوڻيڪ ضرورت هجي، اهڙو ماڻهو سخاوت کان پري هوندو آهي
antonyms: Generosity, Charity, Liberality, Kindness, Open handedness
Generous, Liberal, Charitable, Openhanded, Giving
sindhiMeaning: ڪنجوس، لالچي، لوڀي، تنگ دل(مالي معاملي ۾)، خرچ ۾ سخت، بخيل، خرچ نه ڪندڙ، جيڪو پئسا خرچ ڪرڻ کان گهڻو ڪيٻائيندو آهي ٻين سان شيئر ڪرڻ پسند نه ڪندو آهي ۽ تمام گهڻو ڪنجوس هوندو آهي
urduMeaning: کنجوس، بخیل، خرچ نہ کرنے والا، تنگ دل، خرچ میں سخت، جو پیسے خرچ کرنے سے کتراتا ہے دوسروں کے ساتھ چیزیں بانٹنے سے گریز کرتا ہے اور حد سے زیادہ کنجوس ہوتا ہے
synonyms: Miserly, Parsimonious, Cheap, Ungenerous, Tightfisted
englishMeaning: Not willing to spend money; very miserly. A person who is unwilling to spend money, share resources, or give help, even when it is reasonable or necessary. Such a person is excessively careful about spending and avoids generosity.
examples: He is too stingy to buy gifts even for his family. The boss is stingy and never gives bonuses to employees. She saved money, but she was not stingy with her friends. Being stingy can damage relationships over time.

synonyms: Smell bad, Reek, Foul odor, Stench, Odor
urduMeaning: بہت زیادہ بدبو آنا یا بہت بری بو، کسی چیز کا خراب ہونا یا مشکوک ہونا، بدنامی یا شک ہونا (غیر رسمی استعمال)
antonyms: Fragrance, Perfume, Fresh smell, Aroma, Scent
examples: The garbage in the street began to stink after two days. His socks really stink after football practice. The fish started to stink in the hot weather. The whole room stinks because of the rotten eggs.
sindhiMeaning: تيز ۽ خراب بو اچڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ جو خراب يا مشڪوڪ هجڻ، بدنامي يا شڪ وارو حال
englishMeaning: To produce a very bad smell. A strong and unpleasant smell. It is often used for rotten food, dirty places, or anything that smells extremely bad. To have a very bad reputation (informal use): The deal stinks (means it is suspicious or bad).

examples: The university gives a monthly stipend to research students. She received a stipend during her internship. The organization provided a small stipend to volunteers. His scholarship includes a living stipend.
sindhiMeaning: اهڙي مقرر رقم جيڪا باقاعدي طور تي ڪنهن شاگرد تربيت حاصل ڪندڙ انٽرن محقق يا مذهبي خدمت ڪندڙ کي ڏني ويندي آهي، هي عام طور تي مڪمل پگهار کان گهٽ هوندي آهي ۽ بنيادي خرچن کي پورو ڪرڻ لاءِ ڏني ويندي آهي
synonyms: Allowance, Grant, Scholarship, Payment, Honorarium, Fellowship
urduMeaning: ایک مقرر رقم جو باقاعدگی سے طالب علم تربیت یافتہ فرد انٹرن محقق یا مذہبی خدمت انجام دینے والے کو دی جاتی ہے، یہ عام طور پر مکمل تنخواہ سے کم ہوتی ہے اور بنیادی اخراجات پورے کرنے کے لیے دی جاتی ہے
antonyms: Deduction, Fine, Penalty, Loss, Unpaid work
englishMeaning: A fixed amount of money paid regularly for services, study, or support. A set payment given at regular intervals to support someone, often a student, trainee, intern, researcher, religious worker, or employee in a training position. It is usually smaller than a salary and is meant to cover basic living or study expenses rather than full employment compensation.

To clearly state a condition or requirement. To insist on a specific condition. To make something necessary in an agreement. To require something formally. To specify or demand something as a condition in an agreement, law, or arrangement. It is often used in formal or legal contexts where rules or requirements must be clearly defined.
sindhiMeaning: شرط مقرر ڪرڻ، شرط لاڳو ڪرڻ، واضع طور شرط بيان ڪرڻ، ڪنهن ڳالهه کي لازمي قرار ڏيڻ، ڪنهن معاهدي قانون يا ڳالهه ۾ ڪنهن شرط کي صاف لفظن ۾ بيان ڪرڻ يا مقرر ڪرڻ،
examples: The contract stipulates that payment must be made within 30 days. She stipulated that no one should enter the room without permission. The rules stipulate wearing a uniform at all times. He stipulated several conditions before accepting the job.
antonyms: Ignore, Waive, Allow freely, Overlook, Neglect
urduMeaning: شرط مقرر کرنا، شرط عائد کرنا، واضح شرط رکھنا، کسی چیز کو لازم قرار دینا، کسی معاہدے قانون یا معاملے میں کسی شرط کو واضح طور پر بیان کرنا یا لازمی قرار دینا
synonyms: Specify, Require, Demand, Prescribe, Lay down, Insist

examples: She stirred around the soup. Stir around the mixture. He stirred around the paint. Stir around the ingredients gently.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ڪم ۾ سرگرميءَ سان هليو وڃڻ، گهمايو يا هلايو، برتن ۾ شيء کي چمچي سان گهمايو يا هلڪو ملائڻ
englishMeaning: To move or mix something around. To use a spoon or tool to move contents of a container in circles or random motion.
synonyms: Swirl, Rotate, Mix, Move
urduMeaning: ادھر ادھر ہلانا، چمچ سے کسی چیز کو حرکت دینا یا گھمانا (کبھی کبھار کسی کام میں سرگرمی کے لیے بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے)
antonyms: Hold still, Stop, Leave untouched, Stay still

synonyms: Random, Probabilistic, Chance based, Unpredictable, Variable
sindhiMeaning: اتفاقي يا امڪاني، بي ترتيب طئي ٿيل، اتفاقي متغيرن جي تابع، اتفاقي متغيرن جي تابع، اڳڪٿي نه ٿي سگهي پر شمارياتي طور ماپي سگهجي، اهڙو عمل يا نظام جيڪو مڪمل طور اڳڪٿي نه ڪري سگهجي ۽ جنهن ۾ امڪان يا اتفاق شامل هجي پر ان کي امڪان جي حساب سان سمجهي سگهجي
antonyms: Deterministic, Predictable, Certain, Fixed, Definite
englishMeaning: Involving randomness or probability. Describes processes, systems, or events that are random and cannot be predicted exactly, but can be analyzed using probability
urduMeaning: احتمالی یا اتفاقی، بے ترتیب طور پر طے شدہ، اتفاقي متغيرن جي تابع، احتمالی نوعیت کا، غیر متوقع مگر شماریاتی طور قابل پیمائش، ایسا عمل یا نظام جس میں غیر یقینی اور اتفاق شامل ہو جس کی درست پیش گوئی ممکن نہ ہو مگر احتمال کے ذریعے تجزیہ کیا جا سکے
examples: The weather follows a stochastic pattern during the monsoon Stock market prices are often modeled using stochastic processes The scientist used a stochastic method to simulate population growth Random noise in the signal created a stochastic variation

If you think I broke your phone, you are barking up the wrong tree. The police were barking up the wrong tree during the investigation. She accused her colleague, but she was barking up the wrong tree. If you believe he cheated, you are barking up the wrong tree.
sindhiMeaning: غلط ماڻهو يا شيءِ تي شڪ ڪرڻ يا الزام لڳائڻ، جيڪڏهن توهان غلط وڻ وٽ ڀونڪيو پيا وڃو ته توهان غلط هنڌ تي جواب ڳولي رهيا آهيو، هيءُ محاورو تڏهن استعمال ٿيندو آهي جڏهن ڪو ماڻهو غلط فهمي ۾ هجي ۽ پنهنجي ڪوشش يا الزام ڪنهن غلط طرف موڙي
englishMeaning: To make a wrong assumption or accuse the wrong person. Wasting effort on something that will not give the desired result. This idiom is used when someone believes something that is not true or directs their effort or blame toward the wrong target. It often suggests misunderstanding or misjudgment of a situation.

antonyms: Overt, Conscious, Explicit, Noticeable
sindhiMeaning: لاشعوري طور تي اثرانداز ٿيندڙ، اهڙو اثر جيڪو شعور کان هيٺ هجي پر ذهن تي اثرانداز ٿئي، غير محسوس يا نرم اثر ڏيڻ وارو، ذهن جي هيٺئين سطح تي ڪم ڪندڙ، لڪل، ڳجھو يا پوشيده پيغام يا نشاني، اهي سگنل جيڪي تمام ڪمزور هجن پر ذهن انهن کي پروسيس ڪري

sindhiMeaning: پاڻيءَ ۾ لاهڻ يا ٻڏي وڃڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ کي پاڻيءَ يا مائع جي سطح هيٺ رکڻ، جذبات يا ڪم جي لحاظ کان مڪمل طور تي ڍڪڻ يا دٻائڻ، احساسن يا يادن کي عارضي طور دٻائڻ، ڪم يا سوچ ۾ مڪمل طور مشغول ٿيڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ سان مڪمل طور ڍڪڻ، ڏسڻ کان لڪائڻ يا پوشيده رکڻ

The street was submerged under floodwater after the storm. His past memories were submerged deep in his mind.
englishMeaning: To put under water or cover completely. To cause something to go below the surface of water or any liquid. To overwhelm or cover completely in a figurative sense, like emotions or tasks. To suppress or put aside temporarily (for example feelings or memories). To be completely absorbed or involved in something (for example work or thoughts). To hide or obscure from view.

examples: The lawyer was accused of suborning a witness to lie in court. He tried to suborn the official with money to change the report. The investigation revealed that several people were suborned to give false statements. Attempting to suborn a juror is a serious criminal offense.

examples: The major has succumbed to his injuries and passed away. The town succumbed after a short siege. Thousands of cows have succumbed to the disease in the past few months. urduMeaning: ہمت ہار دینا یا مزاحمت نہ کر پانا، بیماری کی وجہ سے جان کھو بیٹھنا، طاقتور قوت کے سامنے شکست کھانا، خواہش یا لالچ کے سامنے جھک جانا، کسی دباؤ طاقت بیماری یا لالچ کے سامنے آخرکار جھک جانا یا مزاحمت نہ کر پانا

examples: He said that such and such happened yesterday. You must complete such and such tasks before leaving. She met such and such a person at the event. The teacher explained such and such rules in class.
englishMeaning: Used to refer to a person, thing, or number without naming it exactly. It is used when the speaker does not want to specify details. antonyms: Blow, Spit, Release, Expel
synonyms: Sip, Draw, Absorb, Slurp

englishMeaning: To drink or swallow something quickly and eagerly. To drink something fast, often in large amounts or with enjoyment. It can also be used casually for food that is eaten very quickly. The phrase often suggests speed rather than politeness or manners.
sindhiMeaning: تيزي سان پيئڻ يا نگلڻ، ڪنهن مشروب يا شيءِ کي جلدي ۽ شوق سان پيئڻ يا نگلڻ، عام طور تي هي لفظ غير رسمي گفتگو ۾ استعمال ٿيندو آهي
examples: He sucked down a glass of water after the long run. She sucked down her juice before leaving for work. The kids sucked down their milk in a hurry. He sat quietly and sucked down his coffee.
antonyms: Sip, Nurse, Savor, Take slowly
urduMeaning: جلدی سے پینا یا نگلنا، کسی مشروب یا چیز کو تیزی اور شوق سے پینا یا نگل لینا، یہ لفظ زیادہ تر غیر رسمی گفتگو میں استعمال ہوتا ہے
synonyms: Drink up, Gulp down, Swallow, Chug

englishMeaning: To pull something in with force or attraction. To draw someone or something inside suddenly or strongly, either physically like air or water, or mentally by involving someone deeply in an activity or situation. Expel, throw out.
antonyms: Push out, Release from, Keep out, Exclude from, Detach from
synonyms: Pull into, Draw in, Absorb into, Drag into, Involve deeply
urduMeaning: زور سے اندر کھینچ لینا، کسی چیز یا شخص کو طاقت کے ساتھ اندر لے جانا، کسی سرگرمی یا مسئلے میں پوری طرح شامل کر لینا
sindhiMeaning: زبردستي اندر ڇڪڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ يا ماڻهو کي زور سان اندر وٺي وڃڻ، ڪنهن ڪم يا حالت ۾ مڪمل طور شامل ڪري ڇڏڻ
examples: The powerful machine sucked the dust into its filter. She was sucked into the online debate and forgot about time. The whirlpool sucked the boat into the center. He got sucked into unnecessary office politics.

englishMeaning: To build, develop, or form an idea, decision, plan, or action using certain facts, evidence, or principles as the foundation. It shows that one thing depends on or is derived from another.
examples: The committee will base its decision on scientific evidence. This movie is based on a true story. We should base our policies on reliable data. His opinion is based on personal experience.
urduMeaning: کسی خیال فیصلے یا منصوبے کو کسی حقیقت ثبوت یا اصول کی بنیاد پر تیار کرنا، یعنی ایک چیز دوسری چیز پر انحصار کرتی ہے
sindhiMeaning: ڪنھن خيال فيصلي يا منصوبي کي ڪنھن حقيقت شاهدي يا اصول تي تيار ڪرڻ يا ان کي بنياد بڻائڻ، يعني هڪ شيءِ ٻي شيءِ تي دارومدار رکي ٿي
antonyms: Ignore, Disregard, Reject, Overlook
synonyms: Rely on, Build on, Establish on, Found on, Derive from

sindhiMeaning: چوس ڪري ٻاهر ڪڍڻ، چوسڻ يا ڇڪڻ جي ذريعي ڪنهن شيءِ کي اندر مان ٻاهر ڪڍڻ جيئن رت زهر پاڻي يا طاقت
synonyms: Extract, Remove, Draw out, Drain, Pull out
antonyms: Put in, Fill, Insert, Pour in, Add
examples: The doctor used a pump to suck out the poison. The machine can suck out excess water from the ground. He tried to suck out the venom from the wound. Long working hours suck out all his energy.
englishMeaning: To remove something by sucking, often liquid, air, poison, or strength. To pull or remove something from inside another thing using suction or strong pulling force. It is commonly used for liquids, air, toxins, venom, or even energy in a figurative sense. It can describe physical removal as well as emotional or financial draining.
urduMeaning: چوس کر باہر نکالنا، کسی چیز کو چوسنے کے ذریعے اندر سے باہر نکالنا جیسے زہر خون پانی یا طاقت کو نکالنا

examples: He keeps sucking up to the boss to get a promotion. She hates people who suck up instead of working honestly. You will not succeed by sucking up to teachers. He tried to suck up by praising every decision the manager made.
sindhiMeaning: چاٽو ڪرڻ، خوشامد ڪرڻ، ڪنهن بااثر ماڻهو کي خوش ڪرڻ لاءِ وڌ کان وڌ تعريف يا چاپلوسي ڪرڻ، خاص طور ذاتي فائدي لاءِ
antonyms: Ignore, Disrespect, Criticize, Speak frankly
urduMeaning: خوشامد کرنا، چاپلوسی کرنا، کسی بااثر شخص کو خوش کرنے کے لیے حد سے زیادہ تعریف یا خوشامدانہ رویہ اختیار کرنا، عموماً ذاتی مفاد کے لیے
englishMeaning: To flatter someone in order to gain favor or advantage. To behave in an overly polite or flattering way toward someone, especially a person in authority, with the intention of gaining approval, benefits, or special treatment. It usually carries a negative sense because the behavior is seen as insincere.
synonyms: Flatter, Butter up, Curry favor, Sweet talk

sindhiMeaning: خوشامد ڪرڻ، ڪنهن کي راضي ڪرڻ لاءِ ڪرڻ، ڪنهن جي توجه يا راضي ڪرڻ لاءِ ضرورت کان وڌيڪ مهرباني يا تعريف ڏيکارڻ، خاص طور تي اٿارٽي وارن ماڻهن سان، خود فائدي لاءِ
examples: He is always sucking up to the boss to get a promotion. Stop sucking up to your teacher; it won’t help you cheat on the exam. She’s really good at sucking up to influential people to get contracts. Employees disliked him because he constantly sucked up to the manager.
synonyms: Flatter, Brown-nose, Fawn, Grovel, Kowtow
englishMeaning: To try to gain favor by flattering or pleasing someone, often insincerely. To behave in an overly flattering way toward someone, usually a person in authority, in order to get something you want. It implies insincerity and self-interest. Ingratiate yourself with someone.
urduMeaning: چاپلوسی کرنا، کسی کو خوش کرنے کی کوشش کرنا، کسی سے پسندیدگی یا مفاد حاصل کرنے کے لیے ضرورت سے زیادہ تعریف یا خوشامد کرنا، اکثر کسی اختیار رکھنے والے شخص کے سامنے، خود کے فائدے کے لیے
antonyms: Criticize, Oppose, Challenge, Defy, Ignore

englishMeaning: To make a claim against a person or an organization in court about something that they have said or done to harm you. To take legal proceedings in court. To make a request or application.
sindhiMeaning: منٿ ڪرڻ، درخواست پيش ڪرڻ، دعويٰ داخل ڪرڻ، شاديءَ جو پيغام موڪلڻ، حق ۽ انصاف لاءِ ڪورٽ ۾ دانهن، پيڇو ڪرڻ، عرض ڪرڻ، دانهن ڪرڻ، دعويٰ ڪرڻ
antonyms: Absolve
synonyms: Litigate
urduMeaning: کیس کرنا، دعوی کرنا، درخواست کرنا
examples: To sue damages. They threatened to sue if the work was not completed. To sue for divorce. The rebels were forced to sue for peace. George sues for peace after Russian blitz.

synonyms: Pout, Brood, Mope, Frown, Grumble, Stay silent
englishMeaning: To be silently moody or gloomy, often because of being upset or disappointed. To remain silent, withdrawn, or silently resentful due to anger, disappointment, or unhappiness. Can refer to a temporary mood or a pattern of behavior.
urduMeaning: روٹھ جانا ، منہ پھلانا ، خاموشی اختیار کرنا ناراضگی میں، جب کوئی شخص ناراض ہو کر خاموش ہو جائے یا چہرے پر ناراضگی ظاہر کرے مگر کچھ نہ کہے، چپ رہ کر ناراضی کا اظہار کرنا
antonyms: Cheer up, Smile, Rejoice, Forgive, Engage
examples: He went to his room to sulk after losing the game. She is still sulking because her friends didn’t invite her. Children often sulk when they don’t get what they want. Instead of sulking, talk about what’s bothering you.
sindhiMeaning: موڙجي ويهڻ، ناراض ٿي چپ رهڻ، خفا ٿي ويهڻ، ناراض ٿيڻ ۽ بغير ڳالهائڻ جي پنهنجي غصي يا ڏک جو اظهار ڪرڻ، مايوس يا ناراض ٿي خاموشي اختيار ڪرڻ، پنهنجي اندر جذبات رکڻ

urduMeaning: روٹھا ہوا شخص ، منہ پھولانے والا شخص، ایسا شخص جو ذرا سی بات پر ناراض ہو جاتا ہے خاموش رہتا ہے یا منہ بنا کر اپنی ناراضی ظاہر کرتا ہے، اکثر لوگ “سولک پاٹ” اس شخص کے لیے کہتے ہیں جو بار بار روٹھتا ہے
englishMeaning: Someone who, instead of expressing anger or disappointment openly, stays quiet and moody, often to get sympathy or attention. A person who often sulks, pouts, or becomes silent and unhappy when things don’t go their way. It describes someone who easily gets offended and shows it by withdrawing or refusing to talk.
examples: Don’t be such a sulk-pot; it was only a joke!. He’s a real sulk-pot when things don’t go his way. She turned into a sulk-pot after losing the game. Nobody likes a sulk-pot; it’s better to talk about your feelings.
sindhiMeaning: روٺل ماڻهو، موڏي ماڻهو، خاموش ناراض ماڻهو، اهڙو ماڻهو جيڪو ڪنهن ڳالهه تي ناراض ٿي وڃي ۽ ڳالهائڻ ڇڏي ڏئي، خاموش ٿي وڃي يا پنهنجو ناراضگي بغير ڳالهائڻ جي ظاهر ڪري، عام طور تي اهڙو ماڻهو پنهنجي ناراضگي يا مايوسي ڏيکارڻ لاءِ روٺل رهندو آهي
antonyms: Optimist, Lively person, Cheerful person
synonyms: Pessimist, Moody person, Grumbler

antonyms: Bottom, Nadir, Depth, Base, Foot
urduMeaning: چوٹی، انتہائی بلند، آخری مقام، سربراہی اجلاس، انتہائی بلندی، نُقطہ عروج، اِنتہا ، اُونچا مُقام، اُونچی جگہ، سربراہوں کی کانفرنس چوٹی انتہا حد
sindhiMeaning: اجلاس، چوٽيءَ سرو، اوج، بلند، جبل جي چوٽي، مٿاھون درجو، بلندي، مٿاهين، اعليٰ ترين عزم يا ارادو، مختلف ملڪن جڳ سربراهن جڳ ملاقات
synonyms: Acme, Apex, Peak, Apogee, Capstone, Climax, Zenith, Meeting, Conference
englishMeaning: The highest point of something, especially the top of a mountain. An official meeting or series of meetings between the leaders of two or more governments at which they discuss important matters. The highest, most successful, or most important point in something.
examples: I intend to work hard to reach the summit of my career. We reached the summit at noon. This path leads to the summit World leaders will meet next week for their annual economic summit.

englishMeaning: To order somebody to appear in court. To order someone to come to or be present at a particular place, or to officially arrange a meeting of people. To call upon for specified action. To notify to come to appear.
examples: He was summoned to appear before the magistrates. She summoned the waiter. He was summoned before the board of directors. The president summoned an emergency meeting of his advisers. I have been summoned to appear in court.
synonyms: Ask, Invite, Convene, Gather, Arouse, Assemble, Beckon, Beep
antonyms: Answer, Calm, Cancel, Dismiss, Disperse
sindhiMeaning: سڏڻ، طلب ڪرڻ، ڪوٺائڻ، گهُرائِڻُ، مطيع ٿيڻ لاءِ چوائي موڪلڻ، ڪوٺڻ، عدالت ۾ حاضر ٿيڻ جو حڪم ڏيڻ، گڏجاڻي ۾ گھرائڻ
urduMeaning: بلانا، طلب کرنا، عدالت میں حاضرہونے کا حکم دینا، پروانہ طلبی، حاضری بھیجنا، عدالت میں طلب کرنا، ہمت دلانا
سورج، آفتاب، خورشید، دھوپ یا تیز روشنی، توانائی کا ذریعہ، امید اور زندگی کی علامت، خوشی اور گرمی لانے والا
synonyms: Star, Daystar, Sunshine, Light, Radiance
antonyms: Moon, Darkness, Shade, Night
sindhiMeaning: اُس، تڙڪو، سج جي روشني، ڌوپ، سج، سورج، آفتاب، شمس، تيز روشني، خوشي يا گرمي آڻيندڙ، توانائي جو ذريعو، اميد يا زندگي جي علامت
examples: She closed her eyes and felt the sun on her face. The sun gives us natural light during the day. They enjoyed a warm day under the summer sun. The snow sparkled in the sun. Without the sun, life on Earth would not exist.
englishMeaning: The star at the center of our solar system that gives light and heat to the Earth. A huge, hot ball of gases located at the center of our solar system. It provides light, heat, and energy that make life possible on Earth. The Earth and other planets move around it. The word sun can also mean sunlight or a place that receives strong sunlight.

examples: His dealings are always above board. His business dealings are completely above board. The company promised that the selection process would be above board. She is an above board employee who always tells the truth. We want our work to be above board so no one can question our integrity.
synonyms: Transparent
englishMeaning: Honest and open, without cheating or deception. To being straightforward and free from any kind of dishonesty or hidden motives.
antonyms: Deceptive
urduMeaning: صاف گو، صاف و شفاف، ایماندار، بے فریب، جس میں کوئی دھوکہ یا چھپاؤ نہ ہو
sindhiMeaning: صاف ۽ ايماندار، بي دغا، بي عيب، جنهن ۾ ڪو به دوکو يا لڪاءُ نه هجي

englishMeaning: To build an idea, decision, belief, plan, or action on a particular fact, principle, evidence, or assumption. It shows that something depends on or is formed from something else.
examples: The argument is based upon scientific proof. The rule is based upon precedent. The plan is based upon feedback. The estimate is based upon past trends.
antonyms: Ignore, Disregard, Overlook, Reject, Contradict
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن فيصلي، خيال، راءِ يا منصوبي کي ڪنهن حقيقت، ثبوت يا اصول تي قائم ڪرڻ، يعني ڪا ڳالهه ٻي ڳالهه تي دارومدار رکي ٿي
urduMeaning: کسی فیصلے، خیال، منصوبے یا عقیدے کو کسی حقیقت، ثبوت یا اصول پر قائم کرنا یعنی ایک چیز دوسری چیز پر منحصر ہو
synonyms: Rely on, Depend on, Build on, Be founded on, Rest on

urduMeaning: از خود، خود ہی کارروائی کرنا، خود سے اقدام کرنا، بغیر درخواست کارروائی، از خود نوٹس لینا، عدالت یا کوئی ادارہ خود سے بغیر کسی درخواست کے کارروائی شروع کرے، عام طور پر جج خود نوٹس لیتا ہے
examples: The court took suo motu notice of the environmental issue. The judge acted suo motu to prevent further injustice. The Supreme Court initiated a suo motu case on public safety. Authorities started an investigation suo motu after the incident.
englishMeaning: On its own motion or initiative, especially by a court or authority without a formal request. An action taken by a court or authority on its own initiative, without a formal request or petition from any party. Commonly used when a judge starts proceedings independently.
sindhiMeaning: پاڻمرادو، پنهنجي مرضي سان ڪارروائي ڪرڻ، پاڻ ئي قدم کڻڻ، بغير درخواست جي ڪارروائي، خودمختيار فيصلي سان عمل، عدالت يا ڪو اختيار پاڻمرادو بغير ڪنهن درخواست جي ڪارروائي شروع ڪري، عام طور تي جج پاڻ فيصلو ڪري ڪيس کولي ٿو
antonyms: On request, By application, Petition based, Externally initiated, Upon complaint
synonyms: On its own initiative, Self initiated, Independently, Voluntarily, Without prompting

antonyms: Terrible, Awful, Poor, Bad, Disappointing
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ جي انتهائي سٺائي خوبصورتي يا شاندار هجڻ کي زور سان ظاهر ڪرڻ لاءِ استعمال ٿيندو آهي، عام گفتگو ۾ وڌيڪ استعمال ٿيندو آهي
urduMeaning: کسی چیز کے بہت زیادہ اچھا متاثر کن یا مزے دار ہونے کو زور دے کر بیان کرنے کے لیے ، یہ عام طور پر روزمرہ گفتگو میں استعمال ہوتی ہے
synonyms: Excellent, Fantastic, Amazing, Outstanding, Wonderful
englishMeaning: Very good or excellent. Used to strongly emphasize that something is extremely good, impressive, or enjoyable. It is often used in casual speech and writing to show excitement or approval.
examples: She did a super-duper job on the presentation. We had a super-duper time at the picnic. This phone has super-duper features for its price. The movie was super-duper fun to watch.

sindhiMeaning: تمام گھڻو شاندار حيرت انگيز يا لفظن کان ٻاهر خوبصورت ۽ بهترين، هڪ مذاقي ۽ ٺاهيل لفظ جيڪو تمام سٺي شيءِ لاءِ استعمال ٿئي ٿو، جڏهن ڪا شيءِ ايتري سٺي هجي جو ان لاءِ عام لفظ نه ملن
englishMeaning: A playful, made-up word used to describe something that is extremely good, wonderful, amazing, or extraordinary. It is often used humorously when you cannot find a real word strong enough to express excitement or admiration. This word is not found in normal dictionaries as a real word. It is a coined, humorous term that expresses extreme delight, excellence, or amazement. It is often used in songs, movies, or casual speech to sound fun and dramatic rather than serious.
examples: The view from the mountain was supercalifragilisticexpialidocious. Her performance in the play was supercalifragilisticexpialidocious. We had a supercalifragilisticexpialidocious day at the beach. The celebration was supercalifragilisticexpialidocious and full of joy.
urduMeaning: انتہائی شاندار بہت ہی زبردست یا ناقابلِ بیان حد تک خوبصورت یا اچھا، ایک مزاحیہ اور فرضی لفظ جو کسی بہت زیادہ اچھی چیز کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے، جب کوئی چیز عام الفاظ سے بہت زیادہ اچھی ہو اور اس کی تعریف کرنا مشکل ہو
antonyms: Terrible, Bad, Ordinary, Boring, Unimpressive
synonyms: Amazing, Wonderful, Fantastic, Incredible, Extraordinary, Marvelous

examples: His knowledge of history is superficial. She gave a superficial glance at the report. The doctor noted only superficial cuts. Their friendship seemed superficial, lacking real trust.
sindhiMeaning: سطحي، ظاهري، فقط ظاهر تي ڌيان ڏيڻ، گهرو نه هجڻ، سچي ڄاڻ کان ٻاهر، گهري ڄاڻ کان خالي، مٿاڇري سوچ يا عمل
synonyms: Shallow, Cursory, Exterior, Surface
urduMeaning: سطحی، ظاہری، بظاہر، صرف باہر سے متعلق، گہرائی میں نہ جانا، ظاہری یا وقتی، صرف بیرونی پہلو یا شکل دیکھنا، گہرائی یا حقیقت میں نہ جانا
englishMeaning: Concerned only with the surface or appearance. Lacking depth or thoroughness; relating to the obvious or external aspects rather than underlying realities or details.

antonyms: Reason, Logic, Rationality
examples: Breaking a mirror is considered bad luck in superstition. Superstition guided their rituals. Many avoid walking under ladders due to superstition. Superstitions can affect behavior.
englishMeaning: A widely held but irrational belief in supernatural influence, luck, or omens, beliefs that have no scientific basis but affect behavior or decisions. A belief in supernatural causes of good or bad luck. A custom or belief passed from one generation to another without scientific proof. A belief that performing or avoiding a particular action can change the outcome of an event. A belief that certain signs or omens predict something good or bad.
urduMeaning: خرافات/ توہم/ وہم، بدشگونی کا عقیدہ، بے بنیاد عقیدہ، ایسا عقیدہ جو غیر منطقی ہو مگر لوگوں کے رویے یا فیصلوں پر اثر ڈالے
sindhiMeaning: خرافات/ توهم/ وهم، بدشگونيءَ جو عقيدو، بي بنياد عقيدو، اهڙو عقيدو جيڪو منطقي نه هجي پر ماڻهن جي وچ ۾ مشهور هجي ۽ ماڻهن جي روين تي اثر انداز ٿئي

antonyms: Encourage, Release, Express, Allow, Promote, Inspire, Provoke
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ڳالهه احساس يا تحريڪ کي روڪڻ يا دٻائڻ، طاقت يا اختيار سان ڪنهن عمل يا ڳالهه کي بند ڪرڻ، دل اندر واري ڳالهه يا جذبي کي ظاهر نه ڪرڻ
synonyms: Restrain, Subdue, Stifle, Silence, Repress, Curb, Contain
urduMeaning: کسی جذبے عمل یا بات کو ظاہر ہونے سے روک دینا، طاقت کے ذریعے کسی تحریک یا آواز کو ختم کر دینا، دل کی کیفیت یا احساس کو اندر ہی رکھنا
examples: He tried to suppress his anger during the meeting. The government suppressed the protest before it could spread. She couldn’t suppress her laughter when she heard the joke. The doctor gave medicine to suppress the patient’s cough.
englishMeaning: To stop, control, or put an end to something, especially a feeling, action, or expression. To prevent something from being seen, known, or expressed.
