examples: Walking through the dusty bookstore filled her with vellichor. The library’s silence and old pages created a strong sense of vellichor. He felt vellichor while browsing forgotten novels from another century. Vellichor settled in her heart as she touched books once read by strangers.
urduMeaning: پرانے کتابوں سے بھرے مقامات میں موجودگی کے دوران پیدا ہونے والا ایک خاموش اور اداس مگر خوشگوار احساس، جس میں ماضی کی جھلک محسوس ہو

synonyms: Cover, Disguise, Mask, Coating, Covering,
englishMeaning: To cover or disguise something’s real appearance. A thin covering or outward show that hides the real thing underneath.
antonyms: Uncover, Expose, Authenticity, Reality
examples: The veneer of false love has gone. The veneer of civility has gone. The company veneered its poor service with flashy advertising. He veneered his selfishness with kind words. The table was made of cheap wood covered with a veneer of oak. His kindness was only a veneer hiding his selfish motives.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ کي ظاهري طور خوبصورت يا سٺو ڏيکارڻ، اهڙو ظاهري پرت جيڪو حقيقت کي لڪائي
urduMeaning: کسی چیز کو خوبصورت یا جھوٹی شکل دینا، ظاہری خوبصورتی یا پردہ جو حقیقت کو چھپائے

antonyms: Ordinary, Average, Unimpressive, Below standard, Mediocre
synonyms: Extraordinary, Outstanding, Phenomenal, Incredible, Unbelievable
sindhiMeaning: بي حد، حد کان وڌ، تمام اعليٰ
urduMeaning: حد سے زیادہ،بے مثال،نہایت شاندار
examples: Her confidence level was off the charts during the presentation. The team’s performance was off the charts, they broke every record!. The movie’s popularity is off the charts this year. His energy and enthusiasm were absolutely off the charts.
englishMeaning: To be much better, higher, stronger, or more impressive than expected or than anything measured before. Used when something or someone performs exceptionally well or is extremely intense (in a positive or negative way).

synonyms: Revenge, Retaliation, Reprisal, Retribution, Payback
urduMeaning: انتقام، کسی کے نقصان یا ظلم کا بدلہ لینا، کسی کو سزا دینا جو نقصان یا تکلیف پہنچانے کا سبب بنا ہو
antonyms: Forgiveness, Mercy, Pardon, Clemency, Leniency
examples: He sought vengeance for the betrayal of his friend. The villain planned his vengeance carefully. She vowed vengeance after the injustice she suffered. History shows that acts of vengeance often escalate conflicts.
englishMeaning: Punishment inflicted in return for an injury or offense. The act of taking revenge or seeking retribution against someone who has caused harm, injury, or insult. It often implies a strong emotional desire to punish the wrongdoer.
sindhiMeaning: انتقام، ڪنهن نقصان يا ظلم جو بدلو وٺڻ، ڪنهن کي سزا ڏيڻ جو عمل جيڪو هن نقصان جو سبب بڻيو آهي

examples: She found it helpful to vent her anger in a journal. The mechanic checked the vent to see why the gas was escaping. He needed someone to vent his frustrations to after a tough day. The bathroom has a small vent to let out steam.
englishMeaning: To release feelings, emotions, or pressure. To express emotions, frustrations, or thoughts openly, especially to relieve stress or tension. A passage, hole, or outlet through which something flows or escapes. Used in physical contexts like vents in walls, pipes, or machines.
urduMeaning: جذبات کا اظہار کرنا، دکھ یا غصہ نکالنا، سوراخ، راستہ، جس سے ہوا یا گیس خارج ہو
synonyms: Outlet, Opening, Exhaust, Release, Express, Discharge
antonyms: Blockage, Closure, Suppression, Restrain, Contain
sindhiMeaning: جذبات ظاهر ڪرڻ، ڏک، ڪاوڙ يا خوشي جو اظهار ڪرڻ، سوراخ، راه يا فتوح، جتان هوا يا گئس نڪري سگهي

antonyms: Avoid, Stay back, Withdraw, Hesitate, Retreat, Decline
synonyms: Risk, Attempt, Dare, Undertake, Enterprise, Project, Endeavor, Speculation, Pursuit
englishMeaning: To take a risky step or action. To express something carefully or cautiously. To travel into unknown areas. A speculative investment. A joint business or partnership (as in joint venture). A business project that involves risk. To move forward or do something that involves risk, uncertainty or possible loss. A risky journey, activity or business investment started with the hope of gain.
examples: They decided to venture into online business despite the risks. No one wanted to venture out after the storm warnings. His new venture in software development turned out to be successful. She ventured a guess about the results even though she was not sure. They ventured nervously into the water. The project is joint venture between public & private sectors.
sindhiMeaning: خطري وارو قدم کڻڻ يا ڪا نئين ڪوشش ڪرڻ، ڪاروباري يا خطري وارو منصوو، محتاط طريقي سان راءِ ڏيڻ، اڻڄاتل هنڌن ڏانهن سفر ڪرڻ، سيڙپڪاري جنهن ۾ خطرو هجي، گڏيل ڪاروباري منصوو، ڪنهن اڻڄاتل يا خطري واري حالتن ۾ قدم وڌائڻ يا ڪا ڳالهه ڪرڻ جنهن ۾ نقصان يا ناڪامي جو امڪان هجي، اهڙي مهم يا ڪاروباري منصوبي لاءِ استعمال ٿيندو آهي جنهن ۾ منافعو به سگهي ٿو ۽ نقصان جو خطرو به هجي
urduMeaning: خطرے کے ساتھ قدم اٹھانا یا کوئی کام شروع کرنا، خطرے والا کاروباری منصوبہ، کسی بات کا محتاط انداز میں اندازہ لگانا یا کہنا، نامعلوم جگہوں کا سفر کرنا، ایسی سرمایہ کاری جس میں خطرہ ہو، مشترکہ کاروباری منصوبہ، کسی نامعلوم یا غیر یقینی صورتحال میں قدم رکھنا یا کچھ ایسا کرنا جس میں نقصان یا ناکامی کا امکان ہو، ایسے سفر کام یا کاروباری منصوبے کے لیے آتا ہے جس میں نفع کی امید اور خطرہ دونوں شامل ہوں

sindhiMeaning: لفظ بہ لفظ، بلڪل ساڳي طرح، ساڳين لفظن ۾، بغير ڪنهن تبديلي جي نقل ڪرڻ يا ورجائڻ، سڌي نقل، بنا تبديلي ورجاءُ
examples: The witness repeated the statement verbatim in court. Please copy the paragraph verbatim from the book. The teacher asked students to write the definition verbatim. His speech was recorded verbatim for accuracy.
synonyms: Exactly, Precisely, Word-for-word, Literally, Directly
englishMeaning: Word for word; exactly as spoken or written. Repeating or copying something in exactly the same words without any change, omission, or interpretation. It is commonly used in writing, reporting, legal documents, and academic work when accuracy is essential.
antonyms: Paraphrased, Summarized, Altered, Interpreted
urduMeaning: لفظ بہ لفظ، جوں کا توں، عین الفاظ میں نقل، براہ راست اقتباس، بغیر تبدیلی دہرانا، انہی الفاظ میں دہرانا یا نقل کرنا، بغیر کسی تبدیلی یا تشریح کے

antonyms: Concise, Succinct, Laconic
synonyms: Loquacious, Talkative, Voluble, Turgid, Inflated, Wordy, Tedious, Prolix, Long-winded
englishMeaning: Using or containing more words than are needed. Containing more words than necessary. Characterized by the use of many or too many words.
sindhiMeaning: طول ڪلام، ڪثير الفاظي، گهڻ اکرو، لفظي، گهڻو ڳالهائيندڙ، ضرورت کان وڌيڪ لفظ استعمال ڪندڙ، ڊگهو چوڙو بيان ڪندڙ
examples: Much academic language is obscure and verbose. The editors received streams of verbose articles from young hopeful journalists. The man was smartly dressed, verbose, and seriously agitated. He was a notoriously verbose after-dinner speaker. Not that he was verbose: most often when he made any comments on such matters he addressed them to himself. For once, his usually verbose wife was content to listen. His writing is difficult and often verbose.
urduMeaning: طول طویل ، لفاظی کا ، طوالت پسند ، طول کلام، کثیر الفاظ استعمال کرنے والا ، اطناب پسند ، لفّاظ

sindhiMeaning: وڌيڪ لفظن جو استعمال ڪرڻ، غير ضروري طور تي گهڻا لفظ استعمال ڪرڻ جنهن ڪري ڳالهه ڊگهي ۽ سمجهڻ ۾ ڏکي ٿي وڃي
englishMeaning: Using more words than necessary. A style of speaking or writing that uses too many words, often making the message unclear or unnecessarily long. It usually has a negative sense, suggesting lack of clarity or conciseness.
examples: His verbosity made the presentation difficult to follow. The teacher advised students to avoid verbosity in their essays. Due to her verbosity, the meeting lasted longer than expected. Clear writing requires reducing verbosity and focusing on key points.
antonyms: Brevity, Conciseness, Clarity, Succinctness
urduMeaning: ضرورت سے زیادہ الفاظ استعمال کرنا، بلا ضرورت زیادہ الفاظ استعمال کرنا جس سے بات لمبی اور غیر واضح ہو جاتی ہے
synonyms: Wordiness, Loquacity, Garrulity, Prolixity, Redundancy

examples: The jury reached a guilty verdict after two hours of discussion. The doctor’s verdict was that he needed more rest. The final verdict surprised everyone in the courtroom. Public verdict on the new policy was mostly positive.
sindhiMeaning: عدالت جو حڪم يا آخري فيصلو، غور بعد آخري راءِ، نتيجو يا انجام، اهو سرڪاري فيصلو جيڪو جج يا جوري سڀ حقيقتون ٻڌڻ بعد ڏئي، اهو ڪنهن معاملي بابت آخري راءِ يا نتيجو به ظاهر ڪري سگهي ٿو
urduMeaning: حتمی فیصلہ، عدالت کا فیصلہ، غور کے بعد حتمی رائے، نتیجہ یا انجام، وہ سرکاری فیصلہ جو جج یا جیوری تمام حقائق سننے کے بعد دیتی ہے، یہ کسی معاملے کے بارے میں حتمی رائے یا نتیجہ بھی ظاہر کرتا ہے
synonyms: Decision, Judgment, Ruling, Conclusion, Finding, Determination
antonyms: Question, Doubt, Uncertainty, Indecision, Hesitation
englishMeaning: Final decision or judgment, especially by a court. The official decision made by a judge or jury after hearing all the facts in a case. It can also mean a final opinion or conclusion about something.

examples: The bride applied vermilion on her forehead as a symbol of marriage. The artist mixed vermilion with white to create a soft pink hue. Autumn leaves glowed like vermilion under the evening sun. The temple walls were painted in bright vermilion.
englishMeaning: A bright red or scarlet color. A vivid reddish-orange pigment traditionally made from powdered cinnabar or artificially synthesized. It is often used in painting, decoration, and ceremonial markings.
urduMeaning: سندور، ایک چمکدار سرخ یا نارنجی سرخ رنگ جو عام طور پر پینٹنگ آرائش اور مذہبی رسموں میں استعمال ہوتا ہے

antonyms: Pale, Faded, White, Ash, Colorless

englishMeaning: To be the person that an action is directed at, especially an unpleasant one. To be the person who experiences something, often something unpleasant. to be the one who receives the effect of an action, treatment, criticism, blame, violence or punishment rather than causing it. It is often used when the experience is negative or unwanted, but it can also be neutral or positive depending on context.
synonyms: Experience, face, suffer, be subjected to
urduMeaning: کسی عمل یا رویے کا نشانہ بننا، وہ شخص ہونا جو کسی بات، تنقید، سزا یا بدسلوکی کا سامنا کرے، نہ کہ وہ جو یہ عمل کرے
antonyms: Cause, give, deliver, impose
examples: She found herself on the receiving end of a great deal of criticism. He was on the receiving end of harsh criticism from his manager. Villages near the border are often on the receiving end of violence. As a junior officer, she was frequently on the receiving end of blame. The team was on the receiving end of unexpected praise after the project.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن عمل يا روَيّي جو شڪار ٿيڻ، اهو ماڻهو ٿيڻ جنهن تي ڪا ڳالهه، تنقيد، سزا يا خراب رويو ڪيو وڃي، يعني عمل ڪندڙ نه پر برداشت ڪندڙ هجڻ
ڳاڙهي ڇانوَ وارو رنگ، جيڪو سينگار يا رنگ سازي ۾ استعمال ٿيندو آهي، جيڪو ڳاڙهي يا نارنگي ڇانوَ وارو هجي
examples: The artist mixed vermilion with gold to create a royal shade. A streak of vermilion adorned her forehead. She wore a vermilion sari during the ceremony. The sunset bathed the sky in vermilion light. He painted the door in a vermilion shade.
englishMeaning: A bright red pigment or color with an orange tint. Having the color of bright red or scarlet.
synonyms: Scarlet, Crimson, Ruby, Carmine, Red
urduMeaning: چمکدار سرخ یا نارنجی مائل رنگ جو عموماً سنگھار اور مصوری میں استعمال ہوتا ہے، جو شوخ سرخ یا نارنجی مائل رنگ کا ہو
antonyms: Pale, Faded, White, Dull, Colorless

englishMeaning: Animals or insects that are harmful, dirty, or destructive, especially those that spread disease or damage crops or property. The word is often used for rats, mice, cockroaches, lice, and similar pests. It can also be used insultingly for people considered harmful or morally bad.
examples: The warehouse was infested with vermin such as rats and cockroaches. Farmers try to protect their crops from vermin. The city launched a campaign to control vermin in crowded areas. He used the word vermin to insult his enemies.
synonyms: Pests, Rodents, Parasites, Insects
sindhiMeaning: نقصان پهچائيندڙ ۽ گندا جانور يا حشرات جهڙوڪ چوها ڇپريون يا جونڪون جيڪي بيماريون ڦهلائين يا فصلن ۽ ملڪيت کي نقصان ڏين، ڪڏهن ڪڏهن ماڻهن لاءِ به نفرت واري معنى ۾ استعمال ٿيندو آهي
urduMeaning: نقصان دہ اور گندے جانور یا کیڑے مکوڑے جیسے چوہے کاکروچ یا جوئیں جو بیماریاں پھیلاتے یا فصلوں اور املاک کو نقصان پہنچاتے ہیں، بعض اوقات نفرت یا حقارت کے اظہار کے لیے انسانوں کے لیے بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے
antonyms: Pets, Animals, Wildlife, Helpers

synonyms: Native language, Dialect, Mother tongue, Local language, Colloquial speech
antonyms: Formal language, Standard language, Literary language, Official language
urduMeaning: وہ مقامی زبان یا لہجہ جو عام لوگ روزمرہ زندگی میں بولتے ہیں، یہ سرکاری یا تعلیمی زبان سے مختلف ہوتی ہے اور زیادہ سادہ اور عام فہم ہوتی ہے
sindhiMeaning: اها مقامي ٻولي يا لهجو جيڪو عام ماڻهو روزمره جي زندگي ۾ ڳالهائين ٿا، هي رسمي يا سرڪاري زبان کان مختلف هوندي آهي
examples: The teacher explained the lesson in the vernacular so students could understand easily. Many ancient texts were written in Latin, not in the local vernacular. The novel uses the vernacular of rural communities. He prefers writing speeches in the vernacular instead of formal English.
englishMeaning: The language or dialect spoken by ordinary people in a particular region or country. The native language or dialect that is commonly spoken by people in a specific area. It is different from formal or official language used in writing, education, or government. It can also describe something expressed in a plain, everyday style.

Able to do many different things or serve many functions. Someone or something that is versatile has many skills or can adapt to different tasks, situations, or purposes easily. It implies flexibility, adaptability, and usefulness in multiple contexts.
examples: She is a versatile artist who can paint, sculpt, and design clothes. This smartphone is versatile; it works as a camera, gaming device, and personal assistant. His versatile skills make him valuable to any team. The versatile actor can play both comedy and serious roles convincingly.
sindhiMeaning: گهڻ رُخو، هر فن مولا، ڦرڻ يا مڙڻ جي قابل، ڦرڻو گهرڻو، مختلف ڪم ڪرڻ جي صلاحيت رکندڙ، جيڪو ماڻهو يا شيءِ مختلف ڪم يا حالتن ۾ آساني سان ڪم اچي سگهي، گهڻ رُخو ۽ لچڪدار هجڻ وارو
antonyms: Inflexible, Limited, Specialized, Unskilled, Rigid
synonyms: Adaptable, Flexible, Multi-talented, All-round, Resourceful
urduMeaning: ہمہ جہت، ہمہ گیر، ہر فن مولا، وسیع النظر،کئی کام انجام دینے کی صلاحیت رکھنے والا، ایسا شخص یا چیز جو مختلف کاموں یا حالات میں آسانی سے اپنا کردار ادا کر سکے، لچکدار اور قابلِ استعمال

examples: He was well versed in employment law. I'm not sufficiently versed in XML to understand what you're saying. He was well versed in all branches of the field and published extensively. He is well versed in history. She was so poorly versed in the emotions that she failed to comprehend its true nature.
englishMeaning: Having a lot of knowledge about something, or skill at something. Having knowledge gained by close association, study, or experience.
sindhiMeaning: واقف، بلڪل چڱيءَ طرح ڄاڻو، ماهر، تجربيڪار، سٺو واقف
synonyms: Expert, Skilled, Acquainted, Experienced, Qualified, Competent, Proficient, Trained Practiced, Knowledgeable
urduMeaning: منجھا ہوا ، مشّاق ، ماہر، واقف ، سیکھا ہوا ، تربیت یافتہ ، تجربہ کار
antonyms: Green, Ignorant, Immature, Incompetent, Inept, Inexperienced, Unable, Unskilled

urduMeaning: برتن یا جہاز، سمندر یا دریا میں چلنے والا جہاز یا کشتی، جسم میں خون یا سیال لے جانے والی نالیاں، ایسا شخص جو خیالات یا جذبات کا ذریعہ ہو، ایسا برتن جس میں پانی یا کوئی مائع رکھا جائے
englishMeaning: A container used to hold liquids such as water, oil, or medicine. A ship or large boat used for transport on water. In biology, a tube that carries blood or fluid in the body such as blood vessels A person seen as a carrier of qualities, emotions, or ideas. Sacred container used in religious practices. Any hollow structure designed to contain something.
examples: She poured water into a clay vessel. The fishing vessel returned safely after the storm. Blood vessels carry oxygen throughout the body. He became a vessel of hope for his community.
antonyms: Contents, Solid mass, Empty space
sindhiMeaning: برتن يا ٻيڙو، سمنڊ يا درياهه ۾ هلندڙ ٻيڙو يا جهاز، جسم ۾ رت يا رطوبت کڻندڙ نليون، اهڙو ماڻهو جيڪو احساسن يا خيالن جو ذريعو هجي، برتن جيڪو پاڻي يا ٻيو مائع رکڻ لاءِ استعمال ٿئي
synonyms: Container, Ship, Boat, Receptacle, Tank

antonyms: Remove, Revoke, Take away, Withdraw
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کي حق يا اختيار ڏيڻ، قانوني يا سرڪاري طور ڪنهن کي حق، ملڪيت يا اختيار سونپڻ، بغير ٻانهن وارو ڪپڙو، بنيان، گنجي
synonyms: Grant, Confer, Assign, Endow, Waistcoat, Undershirt, Jacket
urduMeaning: کسی کو قانونی حق یا اختیار دینا، کسی کو قانون یا معاہدے کے تحت اختیار، حق یا ملکیت دینا، بنیان یا بغیر بازو کا لباس، بنیان
examples: He wore a black vest with his formal suit. The safety vest made the workers visible at night. The constitution vests power in the parliament. Ownership of the land will vest in the heirs next year.
englishMeaning: To give someone legal rights, power, or authority. A sleeveless garment worn on the upper body.

examples: The priest’s vestiture reflected centuries old traditions. Royal vestiture was prepared for the coronation ceremony. The document discussed the vestiture of authority to the new council. His academic vestiture marked his graduation day.
englishMeaning: Clothing or the act of dressing. Garments or clothing, especially ceremonial or formal dress. It can also mean the act of putting on clothes or being clothed. In legal or formal contexts, it may describe the granting or endowment of rights or authority.
urduMeaning: لباس یا کپڑے خاص طور پر رسمی یا مذہبی لباس، قانونی یا رسمی زبان میں یہ اختیار یا حق دیے جانے کے عمل کو بھی ظاہر کرتا ہے
sindhiMeaning: لباس يا ڪپڙا، پوشاڪ خاص طور مذهبي يا رسمي لباس، قانوني معنيٰ ۾ اهو اختيار يا حق ڏيڻ جي عمل لاءِ به استعمال ٿئي ٿو
synonyms: Clothing, Attire, Garment, Dress, Regalia
antonyms: Undress, Nakedness, Bareness, Disrobing
Apprentice, Newbie, Ignore, Overlook, Neglect
sindhiMeaning: جائزو وٺڻ يا ڇنڊڇاڻ ڪرڻ ڪنهن شيءَ جي درستگي يا قابليت لاءِ، جانورن جو ڊاڪٽر

examples: The workers demanded higher wages due to rising prices. He earns his wage by working at a construction site. The country decided to wage a war against corruption. They are waging a campaign to protect the environment.

examples: You still think the company will never change. Wake up and smell the coffee. He believes he can pass the exam without studying, but he needs to wake up and smell the coffee. sindhiMeaning: حقيقت کي سمجهو، سچائي کي قبول ڪرڻ، اصل حالتن کي سمجهڻ، بي خبري ڇڏڻ، هوشيار ٿيڻ، حقيقت کي سڃاڻڻ، هي محاورو ڪنهن کي سجاڳ ڪرڻ يا حقيقت جو احساس ڏيارڻ لاءِ استعمال ٿيندو آهي، ان جو مطلب آهي ته ماڻهو وهم يا بي خبري ڇڏِي اصل حالت کي سمجهي

englishMeaning: To understand someone’s feelings, experiences, or situation by imagining yourself in their position. It teaches empathy and compassion.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن جي حالت يا احساسن کي سمجهڻ لاءِ پاڻ کي سندس جڳهه تي تصور ڪرڻ، ڪنهن جي جڳهه تي پاڻ کي رکي سمجهڻ
synonyms: Empathize, Understand, Relate to, Feel for, Sympathize

urduMeaning: کسی کے حالات اور احساسات کو سمجھنے کے لیے خود کو اس کی جگہ پر رکھنا

englishMeaning: To produce a successful or desired result. To show positive outcomes after effort or hard work. Literally, it means “to produce fruit,” but figuratively it means “to achieve results.”
sindhiMeaning: ڪاميابي حاصل ڪرڻ، ساراهه جو نتيجو ڏيکارڻ، سٺو نتيجو ڏيڻ، نتيجو خيز ٿيڻ، اثر ڏيکارڻ، پھل ڏيڻ
examples: After years of hard work, their business finally bore fruit. The government’s education reforms are beginning to bear fruit. His continuous training and patience bore fruit when he won the gold medal. Her kindness and generosity will surely bear fruit someday.

synonyms: Succeed

urduMeaning: کہی ہوئی بات کو عمل میں لانا، اپنی باتوں وعدوں یا دعووں کو اپنے اعمال کے ذریعے ثابت کرنا، بات اور عمل میں مطابقت دکھانا
synonyms: Practice what you preach, Back up your words, Live up to your word, Act on your promises
sindhiMeaning: پنهنجو چيو عمل ۾ آڻڻ، جيڪو ڪو چوي ٿو اهو پنهنجي عملن سان ثابت ڪرڻ، قول ۽ عمل ۾ هم آهنگي ڏيکارڻ
antonyms: Talk without action, Hypocrisy, Empty promises, Fail to follow through
examples: If you want people to respect your leadership, you need to walk the talk. Politicians must walk the talk on climate change, not just make speeches. englishMeaning: To act according to what one says; to follow through on promises or statements. Demonstrating through actions that one’s words, commitments, or claims are genuine. It emphasizes integrity and consistency between what someone says and what they do.

urduMeaning: کسی چیز کو حاصل کرنے کے لیے ہوشیاری یا چالاکی سے تدبیریں اختیار کرنا، حالات کو اپنے فائدے کے لیے قابو پانا، کسی مشکل یا رکاوٹ سے بچنے کے لیے چالاکی سے راستہ نکالنا
examples: She managed to wangle an invitation to the exclusive party. He wangled his way out of trouble by lying. I wangle a few extra days off work every year. They wangle the best seats at the theater through connections.

synonyms: Feel extremely embarrassed, Want to disappear, Feel ashamed, Be mortified, Feel humiliated
urduMeaning: شدید شرمندگی محسوس کرنا اور غائب ہو جانے کی خواہش کرنا، جب کوئی شخص کسی غلطی شرمندگی یا بے عزتی کی وجہ سے اتنا پریشان ہو جائے کہ وہ چاہے کہ وہ فوراً وہاں سے غائب ہو جائے یا زمین اسے نگل لے، اکثر روزمرہ گفتگو میں شرمندگی کے شدید احساس کو ظاہر کرنے کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے
word: Want the ground to swallow you up
examples: When I slipped and fell in front of everyone, I wanted the ground to swallow me up. He forgot his speech on stage and wished the ground would swallow him up. She felt so embarrassed by her mistake that she wanted the ground to swallow her up. I called my teacher “mom” by accident and wanted the ground to swallow me up.

examples: Many citizens protested against the leader because they believed he was a warmonger. Historians often debate whether certain rulers were defenders of their country or warmongers. The journalist criticized politicians who acted like warmongers during the crisis. Peace activists try to challenge the ideas spread by warmongers.

examples: The mud washed off easily. he tried to wash off the paint from her hands. The rain will wash off the dust from the leaves. I need to wash off the mud before entering the house. The ink stain is hard to wash off from the fabric.

examples: The cricket match was washed out by rain. The heavy rain washed out the cricket match. (canceled). The flood washed out the bridge. (carried away). His old jeans are completely washed out. (faded). He tried to become a pilot, but he washed out during training. (failed)

examples: His story was borne out by witnesses. The data bear out our hypothesis. Experience bears out his claims. The facts bore out the theory.

englishMeaning: Doing something useless or pointless that gives no real result. Effort that is wasted because the activity cannot produce any real benefit. englishMeaning: To habitually engage in relationships with multiple women, often in a flirtatious or exploitative way. It refers to a man who is fond of women in a way that is often considered morally questionable.
examples: He tends to womanize whenever he travels to new cities. The movie portrays a man who womanizes but never commits to anyone. People criticized him for trying to womanize his colleague. Despite being married, he continued to womanize.
synonyms: Philander, Flirt, Playboy, Casanova
antonyms: Monogamous, Faithful, Loyal, Devoted
sindhiMeaning: گهڻين عورتن سان محبت يا لاڳاپا رکڻ (بنا سنجيدگي جي)، بار بار مختلف عورتن سان رومانوي يا جسماني لاڳاپا رکڻ عام طور تي بغير سچائي يا سنجيدگي جي، هي لفظ اڪثر منفي معنيٰ ۾ استعمال ٿيندو آهي جيڪو عورتن سان غير ذميوارانه رويو ڏيکاري ٿو

englishMeaning: The organ in a woman’s body where a baby develops before birth. The uterus, a hollow muscular organ in female mammals where the embryo develops and grows until birth. It also metaphorically refers to a place where something originates or is nurtured.
antonyms: Outside, Exterior, Open air, Outer world
synonyms: Uterus, Matrix, Birthplace, Origin
urduMeaning: بچہ رکھنے والا عضو، رحم، کسی چیز کے جنم لینے یا پروان چڑھنے کی جگہ
sindhiMeaning: ٻار جي حمل رکڻ وارو عضوو، رحم، ڪا شيءِ پيدا ٿيڻ يا پروان چڙهڻ جو هنڌ
examples: The baby grew safely in her mother’s womb. The artist said his studio was like the womb of creativity. Scientists study how cells develop in the womb. The story was born in the womb of history.

urduMeaning: غیر یَقینی طَور پَر ، اُلجھے ہُوئے طَور پَر، چکرا کر، بے دھیانی سے، گھبراہٹ کے ساتھ
antonyms: Steadily, Firmly, Clearly, Alertly, Consciously, Strongly, Confidently
englishMeaning: In a way that shows you feel weak or ill and unable to think clearly. In a dizzy, unsteady, or slightly faint manner.
sindhiMeaning: چڪرائي، بيهوشيءَ جهڙو، غير مستحڪم طريقي سان
synonyms: Dizzy, Confused, Rocky, Bemused, Shakily, Reeling, Staggeringly, Giddily
examples: His eyes opened woozily. She emerged from the rollercoaster somewhat woozily. He lay motionless for about 30 seconds before standing up and woozily walking off the field. Michelle stumbles woozily out of bed to be sick in the bathroom. I looked woozily around for Mr and Mrs Gould.

synonyms: Hearsay, Talk, Buzz, Speculation
sindhiMeaning: عوام ۾ مشهور خيال افواھ يا ڳالهه جيڪا ماڻهن ۾ ڦهلجي وئي آهي جيڪو ماڻهو غير رسمي طور تي ٻڌائي رهيا هجن
antonyms: Fact, Truth, Reality, Certainty
examples: Word on the street is that the company is planning to hire more staff soon. Word on the street says that the new cafe in town is amazing. I haven’t confirmed it, but word on the street is that she’s moving abroad. Word on the street is that the football team will win the championship this year.
englishMeaning: The general opinion, rumor, or gossip circulating among people. What people are saying informally, often in public.
urduMeaning: عوام میں گردش کرنے والا خیال افواہ یا بات لوگ جو غیر رسمی طور پر کہہ رہے ہوں

examples: She is a true wordsmith, crafting stories that captivate readers. The poet proved to be a wordsmith, blending emotion and rhythm seamlessly. As a wordsmith, he could turn simple sentences into powerful messages. Every article she writes shows her skill as a wordsmith.
sindhiMeaning: لکڻ جو ماهر، الفاظ جو ماهر، جيڪو لکڻ ۾ مهارت رکي ۽ زبان کي خوبصورت انداز ۾ پيش ڪري
urduMeaning: لکھاری کا ماہر، الفاظ کا ماہر، جو لکھائی میں مہارت رکھتا ہو اور زبان کو بہترین انداز میں استعمال کرے
synonyms: Author, Writer, Scribe, Poet, Linguist, Essayist, Novelist, Storyteller
antonyms: Illiterate, Novice, Unskilled writer, Non-writer
englishMeaning: A skilled writer or expert in words. A person who is skilled in using words, especially in writing. Someone who crafts language with precision and artistry.

examples: His lack of experience worked against him in the interview. Poor weather conditions worked against the rescue efforts. Her own fear started to work against her progress. Rising prices are working against small businesses.
sindhiMeaning: ڪاميابي گهٽائڻ يا نتيجي کي منفي بڻائڻ، ڪنهن جي مخالفت ڪرڻ، نقصانڪار نتيجو پيدا ڪرڻ، فطرت يا صلاحيت جي ابتڙ هئڻ، نقصان يا پوئتي پيل حالت پيدا ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: کامیابی کو کم کرنا، کسی کی مخالفت کرنا، منفی نتیجہ پیدا کرنا، فطرت یا صلاحیت کے خلاف ہونا، نقصان یا کمزور پوزیشن پیدا کرنا
englishMeaning: To have a negative effect on something or to oppose someone or something. To create difficulties, reduce chances of success, or act in opposition to a goal, plan, person, or idea.
synonyms: Oppose, Hinder, Go against, Obstruct, Undermine
antonyms: Support, Help, Aid, Work for, Promote

urduMeaning: کسی مسئلے یا رکاوٹ کو براہِ راست حل کرنے کے بجائے متبادل طریقہ اختیار کرنا
antonyms: Confront, Tackle, Address, Solve, Face
synonyms: Bypass, Circumvent, Avoid, Navigate, Manage
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن مسئلي يا رڪاوٽ کي سڌو سنئون حل ڪرڻ بجاءِ متبادل طريقي سان حل ڪرڻ
englishMeaning: To find a way to deal with a problem or obstacle without directly confronting it. To handle an issue, limitation, or obstacle by finding an alternative method, solution, or route instead of trying to remove or solve the problem directly.
examples: We had to work around the broken printer by sending documents digitally. She worked around her tight schedule to attend the meeting. The developers found a way to work around the software bug. They worked around the traffic by leaving earlier than usual.

antonyms: Remove
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن خيال منصوبي ڳالهه ٻولهه يا ڪم ۾ ڪنهن شيءِ کي ٿوري ٿوري ڪري شامل ڪرڻ، اهو مهارت يا عادت کي وقت سان گڏ محنت ذريعي پيدا ڪرڻ لاءِ به استعمال ٿيندو آهي
englishMeaning: To include or introduce something gradually. To develop something slowly through effort. To gradually add something into a plan, system, conversation, or physical object.
synonyms: Incorporate
urduMeaning: کسی خیال منصوبے گفتگو یا کام میں کسی چیز کو آہستہ آہستہ شامل کرنا، یہ کسی مہارت یا عادت کو وقت کے ساتھ محنت سے پیدا کرنے کے لیے بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے
examples: She worked the idea into her proposal. He worked jokes into the presentation. They worked new data into the report. I worked your suggestion into the plan.

antonyms: Gently, Politely, Kindly, Softly, Smoothly
sindhiMeaning: سخت لهجي سان، بي ادبي سان، اباڻڻ سان، اهڙي طريقي سان ڳالهائڻ يا عمل ڪرڻ جيڪو سخت بي ادبي وارو يا دل آزاري ڪندڙ هجي
synonyms: Harshly, Rudely, Roughly, Unkindly, Bluntly, Sharply
urduMeaning: سخت لہجے میں، بے ادبی سے، کھرچنے سے، ایسے انداز میں بات کرنا یا برتاؤ کرنا جو سخت درشت یا غیر شائستہ ہو اور جس سے دوسروں کے جذبات مجروح ہوں
examples: She is abrasively critical of her opponents. Why not?" he asked abrasively. He is often seen as abrasively sure of himself. He spoke abrasively to his coworkers during the meeting. The teacher corrected the students abrasively, which hurt their confidence. The manager’s abrasively honest remarks offended some employees. She handled the situation less tactfully and rather abrasively.
englishMeaning: In a manner that is harsh, rough, or rude in speech, behavior, or action. Showing little concern for the feelings of others.
To beat someone very badly so that the body is covered with bruises. To physically assault someone with great force, causing severe injuries and dark bruises on the skin.
urduMeaning: کسی کو بری طرح مارنا، کسی شخص کو اتنا زیادہ مارنا کہ اس کے جسم پر نیل اور گہرے زخم پڑ جائیں
examples: The thieves beat him black and blue before running away. He was beaten black and blue during the street fight. The report said the prisoner was beaten black and blue. She was afraid he would beat her black and blue if she spoke out.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کي تمام گهڻو مارڻ، ڪنهن ماڻهو کي سخت نموني سان مارڻ جنهن سبب سندس جسم تي نيرا ۽ ڪارا نشان پئجي وڃن
antonyms: Protect, Defend, Spare, Comfort, Shield
synonyms: Beat Badly, Assault Brutally, Batter, Thrash, Pummel

urduMeaning: کسی چیز کو محنت عمل یا کوشش کے ذریعے ختم کرنا، دور کرنا یا قابو پانا، قرض یا ذمہ داری کو محنت کے ذریعے ادا کرنا یا کم کرنا
examples: She went for a long run to work off her stress. He worked off his debt by doing extra shifts at the office. I need to work off the calories I ate at lunch. They worked off their frustration by cleaning the house.
antonyms: Accumulate, Retain, Store, Add, Gain
englishMeaning: To eliminate or reduce something by physical or mental effort, effort at work, or other activity. To get rid of something, often a feeling, energy, or debt, through action.
synonyms: Eliminate, Burn off, Get rid of, Pay off, Reduce
sindhiMeaning: ختم ڪرڻ، دور ڪرڻ، محنت ذريعي قابو پائڻ، ڪنهن ڪم محنت يا سرگرمي ذريعي ڪنهن جذبي يا مسئلي کي ختم ڪرڻ يا گھٽائڻ (جهڙوڪ: دٻاءُ غصو ٿڪاوٽ)

examples: I am working on my report. She is working on her skills. We are working on the plan. He needs to work on communication.
urduMeaning: کسی چیز کو بہتر بنانے پر کام کرنا، کسی کام منصوبے مسئلے یا مہارت پر توجہ اور مسلسل کوشش کرنا تاکہ اسے بہتر بنایا جا سکے یا مکمل کیا جا سکے
antonyms: Neglect
englishMeaning: To spend time and effort to improve, develop, fix, or complete something. To actively deal with a task, problem, project, skill, or situation in order to make progress or bring improvement. It can refer to physical work, mental effort, planning, learning, or repairing.
synonyms: Develop, Improve
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ڪم تي محنت ڪرڻ يا ان کي بهتر بڻائڻ، ڪنهن ڪم منصوبي مسئلي يا صلاحيت تي ڌيان سان محنت ڪرڻ ته جيئن ان ۾ بهتري اچي يا اهو مڪمل ٿي سگهي

urduMeaning: آہستہ آہستہ مہارت میں اضافہ کرنا، وقت کے ساتھ عزت یا پہچان حاصل کرنا، قدم بہ قدم کامیابی حاصل کرنا، جب کوئی شخص نچلے درجے سے شروع کر کے محنت تجربے اور وقت کے ساتھ آہستہ آہستہ اوپر کی سطح تک پہنچے خاص طور پر ملازمت یا مقام میں ترقی کے لیے
antonyms: Fall behind, Drop down, Decline, Regress, Lose position
sindhiMeaning: آهستي آهستي مهارت وڌائڻ، وقت سان عزت يا سڃاڻپ حاصل ڪرڻ، قدم بہ قدم ڪاميابي حاصل ڪرڻ، جڏهن ڪو ماڻهو هيٺين سطح کان آهستي آهستي محنت ۽ تجربي سان مٿي پهچي خاص طور تي نوڪري يا حيثيت ۾ ترقي ڪرڻ لاءِ
synonyms: Climb the ladder, Rise gradually, Progress, Advance, Move up
englishMeaning: To gradually achieve higher status, position, or success through effort and time. To start from a lower level and progress step by step to a higher level through hard work, experience, and persistence. It often refers to career growth, social status, or skill development.
examples: She started as an intern and worked her way up to manager. He worked his way up in the company through dedication and honesty. They worked their way up from a small business to a large enterprise. She worked her way up to the top of her profession.

antonyms: Fail, Break down
englishMeaning: To exercise physically, to find a solution, or to develop successfully. Exercise or solve a problem. Work out means doing physical exercise to stay fit. It also means thinking carefully to find an answer or solution to a problem. In relationships or plans, it can mean ending successfully or being resolved in a good way.
urduMeaning: حل کرنا یا ورزش کرنا، حل نکالنا، کامیاب ہونا، مشق کرنا، کسی مسئلے کا حل تلاش کرنا، کسی منصوبے یا تعلق کا کامیاب ہونا ہے
synonyms: Resolve, Exercise
examples: I work out at the gym every morning. We need to work out a solution to this issue. She worked out the answer after some thinking. Their plan worked out better than expected.
sindhiMeaning: حل ڪرڻ يا مشق ڪرڻ، ورزش ڪرڻ، حل ڳولڻ، ٺيڪ طرح سان مڪمل ٿيڻ، ڪنهن مسئلي جو حل ڳولڻ، ڪو منصوبو يا تعلق ڪاميابي سان هلڻ
مرحليوار حل ڪرڻ، ڪنهن مسئلي ڪم يا حالت کي صبر سان قدم بہ قدم سمجهڻ يا حل ڪرڻ جيستائين نتيجو حاصل ٿئي
synonyms: Resolve, Process
antonyms: Ignore
examples: We need to work through these calculations carefully. She worked through her fear with the help of a counselor. The team worked through the report before submitting it. He stayed calm and worked through the problem step by step.
englishMeaning: To deal with a problem or task step by step until it is finished or understood. To carefully handle, solve, or process something by giving it time and effort.
urduMeaning: مرحلہ وار حل کرنا، کسی مسئلے جذبات یا کام کو وقت اور محنت کے ساتھ آہستہ آہستہ سمجھنا یا مکمل کرنا

examples: The team is working towards improving disaster preparedness. She is working towards a master’s degree in climate studies. The government is working towards reducing poverty. We must work towards long term solutions for climate risks.
englishMeaning: To make efforts to achieve a goal or result. To take planned and continuous actions in order to reach a particular aim, objective, or outcome.
urduMeaning: مقصد کی طرف بڑھنا، کسی خاص مقصد یا نتیجے کے حصول کے لیے مسلسل اور منظم کوشش کرنا، اس میں وقت اور محنت شامل ہوتی ہے
synonyms: Strive for, Aim for, Pursue, Make efforts toward, Work for
sindhiMeaning: مقصد ڏانهن وڌڻ، ڪنهن خاص مقصد نتيجي يا هدف تائين پهچڻ لاءِ باقاعده ۽ مسلسل ڪوششون ڪرڻ، اها ڪوشش وقت ۽ محنت گهري ٿي
antonyms: Give up on, Abandon, Neglect, Ignore, Stop pursuing

englishMeaning: To gradually develop or produce something such as emotion, energy, courage, or effort. To build something slowly through effort or time. It can also mean preparing something step by step.
examples: He worked up the courage to speak in the meeting. She worked up a sweat during her morning exercise. The story worked up excitement among the audience. It took him time to work up an appetite after the illness.
urduMeaning: آہستہ آہستہ کسی جذبے طاقت یا ہمت کو پیدا کرنا یا بڑھانا
antonyms: Reduce, Suppress, Calm, Lessen, Diminish
sindhiMeaning: آهستي آهستي ڪنهن احساس طاقت يا همت کي پيدا ڪرڻ يا وڌائڻ
synonyms: Develop, Build up, Generate, Create, Increase

urduMeaning: کسی شخص ادارے یا چیز کے ساتھ تعاون کرنا، مل جل کر کام کرنا، کسی مقصد کے حصول کے لیے مشترکہ کوشش کرنا
synonyms: Collaborate with, Cooperate with, Team up with, Partner with, Coordinate with
antonyms: Work against, Oppose, Resist, Compete with, Act independently
englishMeaning: To cooperate, collaborate, or engage jointly with a person, group, organization, or system to achieve a shared goal.
examples: She works with local communities to improve education. I enjoy working with people who are honest and skilled. The engineer is working with new software tools. Our team worked with the government on disaster planning.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ماڻهو اداري يا شيءِ سان گڏجي سهڪار سان ڪم ڪرڻ، ڪنهن مقصد حاصل ڪرڻ لاءِ گڏيل ڪوشش ڪرڻ

examples: Sarah is a workaholic and often misses family gatherings because of her job. He became a workaholic after getting promoted to manager. Despite being exhausted, the workaholic stayed late at the office to finish the project. John’s friends worry about him because he is turning into a workaholic.
sindhiMeaning: ڪو ماڻهو جيڪو تمام گهڻو ڪم ۾ مصروف رهي ٿو ۽ آرام ڪرڻ يا ڪم ڇڏڻ ۾ مشڪل محسوس ڪري ٿو، جيڪو شخص ڪم ڪرڻ جي عادت ۾ تمام گهڻو آهي، جيڪو ڪم ۾ پنهنجو سڃاڻپ ۽ اهميت ڏسي ٿو، گهڻو ڪري ذاتي زندگي ۽ صحت تي اثرانداز ٿيندڙ
synonyms: Overworker, Busybody (in some contexts), Labor enthusiast, Work addict
urduMeaning: ایسا شخص جو بہت زیادہ کام میں مصروف رہتا ہے اور آرام کرنے یا کام چھوڑنے میں دشواری محسوس کرتا ہے، ایسا شخص جسے کام کرنے کی عادت بہت زیادہ ہو، جو اپنے کام سے اپنی پہچان اور اہمیت حاصل کرتا ہے، اکثر ذاتی زندگی اور صحت پر منفی اثر ڈالنے والا
englishMeaning: Someone who works too much. A person who is excessively devoted to work and finds it difficult to relax or stop working. Often prioritizes work over personal life, relationships, or health. Someone with an obsessive need to work. A person who derives identity and self-worth from working. Can have negative connotations due to work-life imbalance.
antonyms: Lazy, Relaxed, Idle, Leisurely
Shade, Raise
englishMeaning: To strike or fall with force, or to make someone accept a lower price or position. (Weather-related: When rain or sunlight falls very strongly).
sindhiMeaning: زور سان مارڻ، تيز سج ڪرڻ، زور سان ڪرڻ يا ڪنھن تي دٻاءُ وجھي ان کي مڃائڻ، زور سان ڪرڻ، قيمت گھٽ ڪرائڻ، ڪنھن کي زبردستي مڃائڻ
synonyms: Blaze, Force
urduMeaning: قیمت کم کرانا، زور سے مارنا، دھوپ یا بارش کا تیز پڑنا
examples: The sun beat down on the desert. The rain beat down on the roof. The police beat down the door. The sun was beating down all day. He beat the seller down to a fair price. Heavy rain beat down on the rooftops during the storm.

englishMeaning: Something that causes worry or concern. A situation, behavior, or condition that makes people feel anxious, uneasy, or concerned about possible problems or danger.
synonyms: Concerning, Troubling, Alarming, Disturbing, Worrying, Uneasy
antonyms: Reassuring, Comforting, Calming, Encouraging, Relieving
examples: The dark clouds were worrisome before the flight. His sudden silence is worrisome to his family. The doctor said the test results looked worrisome. Rising prices are becoming worrisome for many people.
urduMeaning: پریشان کن، فکرمند کرنے والا، تشویش ناک، خطرناک معلوم ہونے والا، تشویش پیدا کرنے والا
sindhiMeaning: پريشان ڪندڙ، ڳڻتي وارو، فڪر پيدا ڪندڙ، ڏڪاءُ پيدا ڪندڙ، خطرناڪ لڳندڙ، ڳڻتي وڌائيندڙ
ڪنهن شيءِ کي سخت نقصان پهچائڻ يا ذهني تڪليف ۾ وجھڻ، سخت نقصان، تباهي يا شديد ذهني يا جسماني تڪليف کي ظاهر ڪري ٿو
synonyms: Ruin, Destruction, Devastation, Wreck
urduMeaning: کسی چیز کو بری طرح نقصان پہنچانا یا شدید ذہنی اذیت دینا، شدید تباہی، بربادی یا انتہائی تکلیف کو ظاہر کرتا ہے
englishMeaning: To seriously damage something or to cause intense mental or physical suffering. Great destruction, collapse, or extreme physical or mental suffering.
antonyms: Repair, Restoration, Relief, Improvement
examples: The storm wracked the coastline. The illness wracked his body for years. She was wracked with anxiety before the exam. The war left the city in utter wrack. The building was reduced to wrack after the earthquake. The floods caused widespread wrack across the region.

urduMeaning: مرے ہوئے انسان کی روح یا بھوت،دھندلی سایہ نما شکل، بہت دبلا اور کمزور انسان، ایسی چیز جو غیر حقیقی یا عارضی محسوس ہو، بہت دبلا یا سایہ نما انسان
synonyms: Tropical cyclone, Hurricane, Cyclone, Windstorm, Tempest
sindhiMeaning: مئل انسان جو روح يا ڀوت، پاڇي وانگر نظر ايندڙ ڌندلو وجود، تمام ڪمزور يا ڏٻرو ماڻهو، اهڙي شيءِ جيڪا حقيقي نه لڳي، تمام ڪمزور يا پاڇي جهڙو ماڻهو
antonyms: Calm, Breeze, Stillness, Mild weather, Clear sky
examples: The old castle was said to be haunted by the wraith of a forgotten king. After weeks of illness, he looked like a wraith, pale and weak. A pale wraith seemed to move silently through the dark hallway. In the mist, the distant figure appeared like a wraith floating above the ground.
englishMeaning: The spirit or ghost of a dead person that appears as a faint shadowy figure. In literature and folklore it is often seen as a supernatural appearance connected with death. The word is also used metaphorically for a person who looks extremely thin, weak, pale, or ghost like. Sometimes it describes something that seems unreal, fleeting, or barely visible.

examples: Wrap the bandage firmly around the injured limb. He spent the evening wrapping up the Christmas presents. Each apple was wrapped in paper. She wrapped the present and tied it with ribbon. She wrapped the baby in a blanket. We stock a wide range of cards and gift wrap.

Stay still, Freeze, Remain

sindhiMeaning: اهڙي شيءِ يا ڳالهه جيڪا خاص تعريف يا ذڪر جي لائق هجي يا نه هجي، عام طور تي اهو اصطلاح منفي معنيٰ ۾ استعمال ٿيندو آهي جڏهن ڪا شيءِ معمولي هجي
examples: The food was nothing to write home about. The movie was fine, but nothing to write home about. The meal was not bad, yet nothing to write home about. His performance was something to write home about; everyone praised him. The hotel was clean but not worth writing home about.

synonyms: Hospitable, Welcoming, Friendly, Cordial, Gracious, Accommodating
englishMeaning: Showing hospitality and kindness to guests, strangers, or foreigners. Being friendly and generous to visitors.
urduMeaning: مہمان نواز، خوش اخلاق، مہمانوں یا اجنبیوں کے ساتھ خلوص نرمی اور عزت سے پیش آنا
sindhiMeaning: مهمان نواز، خوش خلق، مهمانن يا اجنبي ماڻهن سان محبت خلوص ۽ احترام سان پيش اچڻ
examples: The villagers were xenial, welcoming every traveler with food and shelter. She has a xenial nature and always makes visitors feel at home. Their xenial traditions are rooted in their culture of hospitality. Being xenial is an important trait for anyone working in tourism.

englishMeaning: Friendly and welcoming to strangers or guests. A person who is warm, hospitable, and kind toward strangers. It is often used to highlight generosity and openness in social behavior.
examples: The village is known for its xenodochial people who warmly greet visitors. She has a xenodochial nature, always making newcomers feel comfortable. The host was extremely xenodochial, offering food and shelter to everyone. His xenodochial attitude helped him make friends wherever he traveled.
urduMeaning: اجنبی لوگوں کے ساتھ خوش اخلاق اور مہمان نواز، جو اجنبی لوگوں کے ساتھ بھی خوش اخلاقی نرمی اور مہمان نوازی سے پیش آئے، یہ کشادہ دل اور مہمان نواز رویے کو ظاہر کرتا ہے
synonyms: Hospitable, Welcoming, Friendly, Warm, Cordial, Generous
sindhiMeaning: اجنبي ماڻهن سان مهربان ۽ مهمان نواز، جيڪو اجنبي ماڻهن سان به محبت عزت ۽ مهمان نوازي سان پيش اچي، اهڙو ماڻهو دل جو کليل ۽ مهمان نواز هوندو آهي
antonyms: Hostile, Unfriendly, Cold, Unwelcoming, Rude

examples: The ancient xenodochium offered refuge to weary travelers crossing the desert. Monks managed the xenodochium and ensured every guest received food and rest. In medieval times, a xenodochium served both pilgrims and the poor. The ruins of the old xenodochium still stand near the historic church.
sindhiMeaning: مسافرن يا پرديسين لاءِ رهائش ۽ مهمان نوازي جي جاءِ، خيراتي مهمان خانو، مذهبي دور جو مسافر خانو، مسافرن لاءِ پناهه جي جاءِ، هڪ پراڻو يا تاريخي مهمان خانو جتي اجنبي مسافر يا زائرين کي رهائش کاڌو ۽ سار سنڀال مهيا ڪئي ويندي هئي، هي مهمان نوازي ۽ انسانيت جي جذبي کي ظاهر ڪري ٿو
englishMeaning: A place or institution that provides lodging for strangers, especially pilgrims or travelers. A charitable shelter for strangers, A religious guesthouse in early Christian times, A hospice-like place for travelers. An ancient or historical type of guest house, often run by religious communities, where strangers, travelers, or pilgrims were welcomed and given shelter, food, and care. It reflects the idea of hospitality toward unknown guests.
synonyms: Guesthouse, Hostel, Inn, Shelter, Hospice
antonyms: Private residence, Restricted facility, Exclusive hotel, Closed shelter
urduMeaning: مسافروں اور اجنبیوں کے لیے قیام اور مہمان نوازی کی جگہ، خیراتی مہمان خانہ، ابتدائی عیسائی دور کا مسافر خانہ، مسافروں کے لیے پناہ گاہ، ایک قدیم یا تاریخی مہمان خانہ جہاں اجنبیوں مسافروں یا زائرین کو رہائش کھانا اور دیکھ بھال فراہم کی جاتی تھی، یہ مہمان نوازی اور انسانیت کے جذبے کی علامت ہے

examples: She played a cheerful tune on the xylophone. The child learned basic music using a colorful xylophone. The xylophone added a bright sound to the orchestra. He tapped the xylophone gently with two mallets.
englishMeaning: A musical instrument made of wooden bars that are struck with mallets to produce sound. A teaching tool used in early music education. A melodic percussion instrument. Sometimes used in children’s toys for learning sound and rhythm. A percussion instrument consisting of a series of wooden bars of different lengths. Each bar produces a different pitch when struck with a mallet. It is commonly used in orchestras, bands, and music education.
sindhiMeaning: ڪاٺ جي ٺهيل موسيقي وارو ساز جنهن جا ٽڪرا هٿوڙين سان وڄايا وڃن ٿا، ٻارن کي موسيقي سيکارڻ لاءِ استعمال ٿيندڙ اوزار، سريلي ڌڪ وارو ساز، رانديڪن ۾ به استعمال ٿيندو آهي، هڪ ڌڪ سان وڄائڻ وارو ساز جنهن ۾ مختلف ڊيگهه وارا ڪاٺ جا ٽڪرا لڳل هوندا آهن، هر ٽڪرو الڳ آواز پيدا ڪندو آهي جڏهن ان کي هٿوڙي سان وڄايو وڃي، اهو ساز موسيقي جي اسڪولن بينڊن ۽ آرڪسٽرا ۾ استعمال ٿيندو آهي

urduMeaning: لکڑی کے سلاخوں پر مشتمل ایک موسیقی کا آلہ جسے چھڑیوں سے بجایا جاتا ہے، بچوں کو موسیقی سکھانے کے لیے استعمال ہونے والا آلہ، سر پیدا کرنے والا ضربی ساز، کھلونوں میں بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے، یک ضربی موسیقی کا آلہ جس میں مختلف لمبائی کی لکڑی کی تختیاں ہوتی ہیں، ہر تختی کو چھڑی سے مارنے پر مختلف آواز پیدا ہوتا ہے، یہ آلہ آرکسٹرا بینڈز اور تعلیمی مقاصد کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے
synonyms: Percussion instrument, Marimba (similar instrument), Glockenspiel (metal version, Slightly different)

examples: He stood up, stretched and yawned. I can't stop yawning - I must be tired. She managed to stifle a yawn. He covered his mouth to hide his yawn. The film was a total yawn.

examples: He arrived home late yestreen after a long journey. The storm that began yestreen damaged several houses. She spoke of events that happened yestreen with sadness. Yestreen was colder than any night this week.

examples: She beat the odds and recovered from a serious illness. Despite financial problems, he beat the odds and built a successful business. The team beat the odds and won the championship. He came from a poor background but beat the odds to become a doctor.

synonyms: Overcome difficulties, Defy the odds, Succeed against all odds, Triumph, Prevail

englishMeaning: A rude, aggressive, or hooligan-like young person. A young man who behaves in a noisy, violent, or antisocial way, often involved in petty crime or troublemaking. The term is mostly British slang.
examples: The yob smashed the shop window during the protest. Local authorities are trying to stop yobs from vandalizing the park. A group of yobs were causing trouble outside the stadium. The police caught a yob trying to steal a bicycle.

examples: You blew it when you forgot to submit your job application on time. She blew it by arguing with the manager during the interview. We had a great chance to win the match, but we blew it. He knows he blew it when he lied to his best friend.

word: You look like a million bucks
englishMeaning: You look extremely attractive, elegant, stylish, or impressive. This idiom is used to compliment someone’s appearance, meaning.

examples: Wow, you look like a million bucks in that dress!. After his makeover, he looked like a million bucks. You must be going to a party, you look like a million bucks today!. She felt like a million bucks after winning the award.

englishMeaning: To move from side to side in sharp, quick turns instead of going straight. It describes a repeated change of direction. A shape or line made of sharp turns going left and right. antonyms: Straight, Direct, Linear, Even, Smooth
examples: The cyclist had to zig zag through the crowd. The snake left a zig zag on the sand. The zig zag road slowed the cars. We watched the kite move in a zig zag across the sky.

sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءَ تي مڪمل ڌيان ڏيڻ، ڌيان سان سوچڻ يا نظر مرڪوز ڪرڻ، پنهنجو ڌيان سڀني شين کان هٽائي رڳو هڪ ڪم يا ڳالهه تي مرڪوز ڪرڻ

urduMeaning: کسی چیز پر مکمل توجہ مرکوز کرنا، گہرائی سے دھیان دینا، خیالات اور توجہ کو ہٹا کر صرف ایک کام یا بات پر فوکس کرنا
synonyms: Focus on, Concentrate on, Pay attention to, Direct attention, Fixate on
englishMeaning: To give your complete attention or focus to a particular task, subject, or person. It means concentrating deeply on something and ignoring distractions.
examples: During the exam, I zoned in on the most difficult questions first. He zoned in on her voice even in the noisy room. You need to zone in on your goals if you want to succeed. The teacher asked the students to zone in on the main idea of the passage.

He zoned on the speaker’s words and forgot about his phone. She zoned on the music and started dancing with full energy. During the exam, I zoned on my paper and didn’t notice the time. The photographer zoned on the perfect angle for the picture.
englishMeaning: To focus all your attention or concentration on a particular person, thing, or activity while ignoring everything else. It often refers to becoming deeply absorbed or mentally locked in.
synonyms: Concentrate on, Focus on, Pay attention to, Be absorbed in, Fixate on
urduMeaning: توجہ مرکوز کرنا، مکمل توجہ دینا، ذہنی طور پر کسی کام میں ڈوب جانا، ساری توجہ ایک ہی چیز پر لگانا
antonyms: Ignore, Overlook, Neglect, Be distracted, Disregard
sindhiMeaning: ڌيان لڳائڻ، مڪمل ڌيان ڏيڻ يا ذهن کي اُن تي مرڪوز ڪرڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ ۾ ايترو محو ٿي وڃڻ جو باقي سڀ وسري وڃي

urduMeaning: ذہنی طور پر غیر حاضر ہو جانا، خیالات میں گم ہو جانا، دھیان ہٹ جانا، اپنی ہی دنیا میں کھو جانا
englishMeaning: To stop paying attention or become unaware of what is happening around you, often because you are tired, bored, or lost in thought.
examples: I often zone out during long meetings. She zoned out while watching the lecture video. He was so tired that he completely zoned out on the bus. When I zone out, I don’t even notice people talking to me.
sindhiMeaning: ذهني طور غير حاضر ٿيڻ يا ڌيان وڃائجي وڃڻ، ڌيان هٽجي وڃڻ، پنهنجي دنيا ۾ وڃائجي وڃڻ، سوچن ۾ وڃائجي وڃڻ
antonyms: Concentrate, Focus, Pay attention, Stay alert
synonyms: Daydream, Drift off, Space out, Lose focus, Wander off, Tune out

antonyms: Ignore, Neglect, Overlook, Avoid, Disregard
englishMeaning: To focus attention closely on something or someone, to concentrate deeply, or to give full mental attention.
urduMeaning: توجہ مرکوز کرنا، غور سے دیکھنا، کسی بات پر دھیان دینا
synonyms: Focus on, Concentrate on, Pay attention to, Fix one’s eyes on, Observe closely, Zero in on
sindhiMeaning: مرڪوز ٿيڻ، ڌيان ڏيڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ تي توجهه ڏيڻ
examples: The teacher zoned upon the student who was not paying attention. During the meeting, he zoned upon the main issue that needed to be solved. The scientist zoned upon the smallest details of the experiment. She zoned upon her goals and ignored all distractions.

sindhiMeaning: ويجھو ڏسڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ کي ويجھو آڻڻ يا ڌيان ڏيڻ، جيئن ڪئميرا يا نگاهه کي ويجھو ڪرڻ
synonyms: Focus on, Magnify, Concentrate on, Center on
antonyms: Zoom out, Expand, Overlook, Ignore
urduMeaning: قریب سے دیکھنا، کسی چیز کو قریب سے دیکھنا یا کسی خاص پہلو پر توجہ دینا، جیسے کیمرے یا نظریں کسی چیز کے قریب لے آئیں
examples: The photographer zoomed in on the bird sitting on the branch. Let’s zoom in on the financial report to understand the trends. During the video call, I zoomed in to see the text on her screen. The detective zoomed in on the suspect’s movements.
englishMeaning: Focus closely. To adjust a camera, lens, or view to make a subject appear larger or closer; also used metaphorically to mean focusing on a particular detail

examples: She avoids parks because her zoophobia makes her afraid of dogs. Zoophobia can interfere with daily life if not treated. His zoophobia began after a traumatic childhood experience with animals. Therapy helped her manage her zoophobia and regain confidence.
sindhiMeaning: جانورن کان غيرمعمولي يا شديد ڊپ، اهڙي ذهني حالت جنهن ۾ ماڻهو جانورن کان غير منطقي خوف محسوس ڪري ٿو، جيڪو روزمره زندگي تي اثر وجهي سگهي ٿو
englishMeaning: An extreme fear of animals. An intense and irrational fear of animals. A person with this fear may panic, feel anxiety, or avoid places where animals are present, even if the animals are harmless.
synonyms: Fear of animals, Animal phobia, Specific phobia related to animals
urduMeaning: جانوروں کا شدید خوف، ایک نفسیاتی حالت جس میں انسان کو جانوروں سے غیر معمولی اور بلا وجہ خوف ہوتا ہے، یہ خوف گھبراہٹ بے چینی یا جانوروں سے دور رہنے کی صورت میں ظاہر ہوتا ہے
antonyms: Love of animals, Zoolatry, Comfort with animals

examples: She developed zoosadismophobia after seeing a documentary on animal abuse. His zoosadismophobia prevented him from visiting the circus. Talking about hunting triggers his zoosadismophobia. Zoosadismophobia can cause extreme anxiety in people sensitive to animal suffering.
englishMeaning: Fear of cruelty to animals or fear of seeing animals being harmed. A psychological condition in which a person experiences intense fear, anxiety, or distress at the thought, sight, or discussion of cruelty or abuse towards animals. This can include witnessing abuse, hearing about it, or even imagining such situations.
urduMeaning: ایک نفسیاتی حالت جس میں کسی شخص کو جانوروں پر ظلم دیکھنے سننے یا سوچنے سے شدید خوف یا اضطراب محسوس ہوتا ہے
synonyms: Animal cruelty phobia, Zoophobia related to cruelty, Bestiality fear
sindhiMeaning: هڪ نفسياتي حالت جنهن ۾ ماڻهو کي جانورن سان ظلم يا انهن کي نقصان پهچائڻ جي خيال تي شديد خوف يا پريشاني ٿيندي آهي (اهو ڏسڻ ٻڌڻ يا تصور ڪرڻ سان ٿي سگهي ٿو)
antonyms: Fearlessness of animal harm, Animal cruelty tolerance

englishMeaning: Someone or something that is extremely attractive, pleasing to the eyes, or delightful in appearance, often used in a poetic or literary sense.
examples: The beauteous landscape took everyone’s breath away. She wore a beauteous dress that sparkled in the sunlight. The poet described the moon as beauteous and calm. Visitors admired the beauteous architecture of the old palace.
antonyms: Ugly, Unattractive, Plain, Hideous
urduMeaning: کسی شخص یا چیز کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے جو غیر معمولی طور پر حسین دلکش اور آنکھوں کو بھانے والی ہو
sindhiMeaning: اهڙو شيءِ يا شخص جيڪو ڏاڍو حسين هجي ڏسڻ ۾ وڻندڙ هجي ۽ دل کي خوش ڪري
synonyms: Beautiful, Lovely, Gorgeous, Attractive, Charming

sindhiMeaning: خوبصورتي ڏسندڙ جي اک ۾ هوندي آهي
word: Beauty is in the eye of the beholder
examples: She may not be a model, but to him, she’s the most beautiful woman, beauty is in the eye of the beholder. Some people love modern art, others don’t; beauty is in the eye of the beholder. He admires old buildings, while others call them ugly, beauty is in the eye of the beholder. To a mother, her child is always beautiful, proving that beauty is in the eye of the beholder.
antonyms: Beauty has a universal standard
synonyms: Everyone has their own taste
englishMeaning: Everyone sees beauty in their own way. Different people see things differently based on personal taste or opinion.
urduMeaning: خوبصورتی دیکھنے والے کی آنکھ میں ہوتی ہے

examples: Life is not all beer and skittles; you must work hard. He thought moving abroad would be beer and skittles, but it was challenging. Success isn’t beer and skittles; it requires effort. Retirement isn’t always beer and skittles if health issues arise.
sindhiMeaning: سولو ۽ مزيدار زندگي، اهڙي زندگي جيڪا خوشگوار ۽ آرامده هجي، بغير ڪنهن پريشانيءَ جي
urduMeaning: آسان اور خوشگوار زندگی، وہ زندگی جو لطف اور آرام سے بھری ہو، بغیر کسی مشکل یا رکاوٹ کے
synonyms: Comfort, Pleasure, Ease
englishMeaning: Easy and enjoyable life. Refers to a life of pleasure and comfort without troubles, often suggesting things are not always easy in reality
antonyms: Hardship, Struggle, Difficulty

examples: The abrasiveness of the diamonds made them particularly useful for industrial use. His abrasiveness frequently annoyed his teammates. He is candid to the point of abrasiveness. She never displayed the big ego or abrasiveness that others have shown. Some people are put off by his abrasiveness.
urduMeaning: ریگ مال، سخت مزاجی، بے ادبی، کھردرا پن، سخت یا کھردرا برتاؤ یا رویہ

synonyms: Harshness, Roughness, Rudeness, Sharpness, Coarseness
antonyms: Gentleness, Softness, Mildness, Smoothness, Politeness
englishMeaning: A rough quality in a substance that can be used to clean a surface or make it smooth. The fact of being rude and unkind in a way that may hurt other people’s feelings. A rude and unfriendly way of talking or behaving.

examples: Abraham begetteth Isaac, and Isaac begetteth Jacob. Hatred begetteth more hatred among enemies. The king begetteth many heirs to the throne. Laziness begetteth poverty in the long run.
sindhiMeaning: ڄمائي ٿو، پيدا ڪري ٿو، ڪنهن کي ڄمائڻ يا پيدا ڪرڻ، ڪنهن نتيجي يا اثر جو سبب بڻجڻ، عام طور تي قديم انگريزي ادب ۾ استعمال ٿيندو آهي

synonyms: Generate, Produce, Father, Create, Cause
englishMeaning: To father or produce offspring, to cause or bring about. An archaic form of “begets,” typically found in older English texts like the King James Bible. It means to generate, create, or produce something, especially offspring, but it can also mean causing a particular effect or result.
antonyms: Destroy, Prevent, End, Stop

examples: He is the only begotten son of his parents. From these efforts, new opportunities were begotten. The poem speaks of the begotten love between two souls. In theology, Jesus is referred to as the begotten Son of God.
urduMeaning: آفریدہ ، پیدا کیا ہوا ، مخلوق، پیدا کیا گیا، جنم دیا ہوا
sindhiMeaning: پيدا ٿيل، جنم ڏنل، (اولاد جو) پيدائشي عمل، پيءُ ٿيڻ، پيدا ڪيل، ٺاهيل
englishMeaning: The past participle of “beget,” which means to father or produce a child, or more broadly to cause something to exist. It often appears in religious, literary, or formal contexts. Example: “Only begotten son” refers to a child uniquely born from a parent. Produced or brought into existence; generated.
synonyms: Generated, Produced, Fathered, Created
antonyms: Unborn, Nonexistent, Childless

synonyms: Conduct-related, Actions-based, Interactive, Responsive
antonyms: Non-behavioural, Indifferent, Inactive, Unresponsive
sindhiMeaning: ورتاءُ سان تعلق رکندڙ ، برتاءُ وارو يا ان عمل سان واسطو رکندڙ
englishMeaning: Related to the way someone acts or behaves. Concerning or describing patterns, tendencies, or characteristics of a person's actions, reactions, or conduct. Often used in psychology, education, or organizational studies to describe observable actions.
examples: The teacher focused on the students’ behavioural changes after the new program. Behavioural therapy can help patients manage anxiety. Companies analyze behavioural patterns to improve customer experience. His behavioural issues at work were addressed by the HR department.
urduMeaning: رویے سے متعلق، عمل یا طرز عمل سے تعلق رکھنے والا

examples: The committee acted at the chairman's behest. She donated the books at her teacher's behest. The investigation started at the minister's behest. He traveled abroad at his company's behest.
sindhiMeaning: حڪم، هدايت، فرمان، حڪم، فرمائش، ڪنهن جي چوڻ تي ڪيل ڪم
urduMeaning: امر، حکم، ہدایت، فرمائش، کسی کے کہنے پر کیا گیا عمل
synonyms: Command, Request, Order, Instruction, Directive
antonyms: Refusal, Disobedience, Defiance, Rejection
englishMeaning: A command, request, or order given by someone who has authority. Something done because a person with influence, power, or respect asked or ordered it. It often shows that the action happened because someone important wanted it.
In private, secretly, or away from the public eye. When something happens without others knowing or without public discussion. Often used for private meetings, decisions, or personal matters.
examples: The peace talks were held behind closed doors to avoid media pressure. Many important business deals are made behind closed doors. The committee discussed the issue behind closed doors before announcing the decision. What happens behind closed doors should stay private.
sindhiMeaning: بند دروازن جي پٺيان، ڳجهيءَ طرح، خفيه طور، جڏهن ڪو فيصلو يا ڳالهه بند ڪمري ۾ ماڻهن جي موجودگي کان سواءِ ڪئي وڃي

synonyms: In confidence

englishMeaning: Old-fashioned; not modern; not aware of current ideas or developments. A person, idea, system, or practice that is outdated and does not keep up with modern trends, technology, or thinking. It often suggests resistance to change or lack of awareness of current developments.
examples: His teaching methods are behind the times and need improvement. That company is behind the times because it still uses outdated technology. Wearing such clothes makes him look behind the times. Some people think printed newspapers are behind the times in the digital age.
antonyms: Modern, Up-to-date, Current, Advanced, Progressive
sindhiMeaning: وقت کان پوئتي پيل، پراڻو خيال رکندڙ، پراڻو، فرسوده، ماڻهو خيال يا نظام جيڪو جديد دور سان هم آهنگ نه هجي، پراڻن طريقن يا سوچن تي هلندو هجي ۽ نون تبديلين کي قبول نه ڪري
urduMeaning: فرسودہ، پرانا، غیر جدید، وقت سے پیچھے، پرانے خیالات رکھنے والا ، خیال یا نظام جو جدید دور کے مطابق نہ ہو، پرانے طریقوں یا سوچ پر قائم ہو اور نئی تبدیلیوں کو قبول نہ کرے
synonyms: Outdated, Old-fashioned, Antiquated, Obsolete, Outmoded

synonyms: Unpunctual, Slow
urduMeaning: دیر سے، وقت سے پیچھے،تاخیر سے ، مقررہ وقت پر مکمل نہ ہونا
sindhiMeaning: دير سان، وقت تي نه پهچڻ يا دير ٿيڻ
examples: The train arrived behind time because of the heavy rain. He reached the office behind time and missed the meeting. Our project is running behind time due to technical issues. She apologized for being behind time for the class.

sindhiMeaning: گهيرو ڪرڻ، روڪڻ، محاصرو ڪرڻ، ناڪابندي ڪرڻ، تنگ ڪرڻ، پريشان ڪرڻ
examples: They were beleaguered by enemy armies. The lack of funds that beleaguers schools. At the same time, the public believed they were beleaguered by crime.

urduMeaning: محاصرہ کرنا، ناکہ بندی کرنا، تنگ پریشان کرنا ، پابند کرنا

synonyms: Side by side, Alongside, Up to date, Informed, Level, Equal
sindhiMeaning: لڳو لڳ، برابر برابر، ڪلهوڪلهي سان، آمهون سامهون، ترقي يا واڌ جي ساڳئي مرحلي تي هجڻ، هڪ ئي قطار ۾ گڏ گڏ هجڻ، ساڳئي سطح تي يا گڏ گڏ
antonyms: Behind, Outdated, Uninformed, Separated, Unequal
examples: A police car drew abreast of us and signalled us to stop. Young people always keep abreast of the times. The two cyclists rode abreast along the road. She keeps abreast of current affairs by reading newspapers daily. The company stayed abreast with new technology to remain competitive. The students walked abreast into the hall.
englishMeaning: Up to date with information. Side by side and facing the same direction. At the same stage of development or progress. When two or more people or things move or stand next to each other in the same line.

synonyms: Aggressive, Hostile
sindhiMeaning: جنگ ۾ شامل ڌر، ڪنهن تڪرار يا مقابلي ۾ شرڪت ڪندڙ، جهڳڙالو، وڙهڻ لاءِ تيار، دشمني وارو، جنگي رويي وارو، بحث يا ڳالهين ۾ وڙهڻ وارو، شديد مخالفت ڪندڙ، آساني سان غصو ڪندڙ، جارحاڻو يا مقابلي وارو

englishMeaning: A person, group, or country engaged in war or conflict. Aggressive and ready to fight. Showing hostility, aggression, or a willingness to fight. It can refer to physical fighting, verbal arguments, or an aggressive attitude in general.

examples: The treaty was signed by both belligerents. Each belligerent blamed the other for starting the war. The organization called for talks between the belligerents. Aid was sent to civilians affected by the belligerents. He gave a belligerent reply during the meeting. The belligerent crowd refused to calm down. Her belligerent attitude caused tension in the office.

To become round or swollen outward like a stomach because of air, wind, or pressure.
synonyms: Stomach, Abdomen, Tummy, Midsection
urduMeaning: پیٹ ، شکم ، جسم کا درمیانی نرم حصہ ، کسی چیز کا نچلا حصہ، ابھرنا، پھول جانا
antonyms: Back, Spine area, Upper chest

synonyms: Fit in, Suit
sindhiMeaning: مناسب جاءِ تي هجڻ، پنهنجي جاءِ تي هجڻ، لاڳو ٿيڻ، صحيح جاءِ تي هجڻ

examples: The cups belong in the cupboard. You belong in this company. That word doesn’t belong in this sentence. Such items belong in a museum. That painting belongs in a museum.
urduMeaning: کسی جگہ مناسب ہونا، صحیح جگہ پر ہونا، اپنی جگہ پر ہونا، موزوں ہونا

synonyms: Own, Relate to
englishMeaning: To show possession, relationship, or connection. To be the property of, to be part of or associated with a group, place, or person.
sindhiMeaning: تعلق رکڻ، حصو ٿيڻ، واسطو رکڻ، ملڪيت ۾ هجڻ
antonyms: Separate, Disassociate
urduMeaning: تعلق رکھنا، کسی کا ہونا، وابستہ ہونا، ملکیت میں ہونا
examples: This book belongs to Ali. I feel I belong to this team. Who does this car belong to? The islands belong to the country.

antonyms: Unclassify, Misplace
synonyms: Categorize, Classify
sindhiMeaning: ھڪ خاص درجي ۾ اچڻ، ڪنھن عنوان ھيٺ شمار ٿيڻ، ڪنھن گروپ سان لاڳاپيل ھجڻ
englishMeaning: To be classified or placed in a particular category, group, or section.
urduMeaning: کسی زمرے یا عنوان کے تحت آنا، اس میں شمار ہونا
examples: This law belongs under criminal justice. These files belong under archives. That topic belongs under biology. The data belongs under confidential records.

antonyms: Clash, Mismatch, Contradict
sindhiMeaning: ٺهڪندڙ هجڻ، مل رکڻ، مناسب هجڻ، گڏ ٿيڻ جي لائق هجڻ، ڏ ٿيڻ جو اهل هجڻ، ميل رکڻ، هڪ ٻئي لاءِ ٺهيل هجڻ
synonyms: Fit with, Go with, Be part of
urduMeaning: میل کھانا، مناسب ہونا، ایک ساتھ ہونا، ایک دوسرے کے لیے ٹھیک ہونا، تعلق رکھنا، ساتھ جچنا، ایک دوسرے کے لیے بنے ہونا
examples: This color belongs with that shade perfectly. He really belongs with this team. These books belong with the classics. She feels she belongs with her friends here. These files belong with the documents in the finance folder. This color belongs with the warm tones of the room’s design.
englishMeaning: To be in the right place or to match well with someone or something. To fit emotionally, socially, or logically with another person or thing. To be meant to stay together or exist together. To form a natural pair or set.

synonyms: Yardstick, Reference point
antonyms: Aberration, Guess
urduMeaning: سروے کرنے والے کا بنایا ہوا نِشان کِسی دیوار ، ستون یا عمارت وغیرہ پر جو اونچائی کو ناپنے کے لیے بطور نُقطہ حوالہ ڈالا جاتا ہے
examples: Tests at the age of seven provide a benchmark against which the child's progress at school can be measured. Her outstanding performances set a new benchmark for singers throughout the world. Projects are assessed and benchmarked against the targets. The journal was recently benchmarked against other IT journals.
englishMeaning: Something that can be measured and used as a standard that other things can be compared with. To judge the quality of something in relation to that of other similar things.
sindhiMeaning: حوالي جو نشان، حوالي طور ڪم، معيار ماپڻ، پرکڻ وغيرھ ۾ ڪو معيار

antonyms: Neglect, Hold back, Do nothing
sindhiMeaning: سڀ ڪجهه ڪرڻ جي ڪوشش ڪرڻ، تمام گهڻي ڪوشش ڪرڻ، ڪنهن کي خوش ڪرڻ لاءِ حد کان وڌيڪ ڪرڻ، ڪنهن جي مدد يا خوشي لاءِ پاڻ کي تڪليف ۾ وجهڻ
synonyms: Help, Strive hard, Make every effort
englishMeaning: To make a great effort to help someone, often going beyond what is necessary. To try extremely hard to please or accommodate others.
urduMeaning: ہر ممکن کوشش کرنا، کسی کی مدد یا خوشی کے لیے اپنی جان پر کھیل جانا، بہت زیادہ کوشش کرنا، کسی کو خوش کرنے کے لیے حد سے بڑھ جانا
examples: She bent over backwards to help. The teacher bent over backwards to help the weak students pass the exam. She bent over backwards to make her guests feel comfortable.
