urduMeaning: بے معقولیت، کوئی ایسی چیز یا صورت حال جو غیر منطقی بے معنی یا مضحکہ خیز ہو، اس کا اطلاق خیالات اعمال یا حالات پر ہوتا ہے جو عقل کے خلاف ہوں، کبھی کبھی مضحکہ خیز یا طنزیہ معنی بھی رکھتا ہے، متضاد رویہ یا دعویٰ
antonyms: Reason, Logic, Sense, Rationality, Sanity
sindhiMeaning: بي معنيٰ يا بي وقوفي، اهڙي ڳالهه يا عمل جيڪو عقل منطق يا وجدان جي خلاف هجي، ڪنهن صورتحال يا خيال جو بي معنيٰ يا بي وقوفي هجڻ، جيڪو سمجھ کان پري ۽ مزاحيه هجي، تضاد يا متضاد خيال
examples: The idea that humans can live forever is pure absurdity. It is an absurdity to think money can buy happiness. His claim that the earth is flat is full of absurdity. The novel explores the absurdity of war through dark humor.
Police blocked off the main street. The road was blocked off due to flooding. They blocked off the entrance for repairs. Workers blocked off the tunnel.
sindhiMeaning: رستو بند ڪرڻ، بند ڪري ڇڏڻ، رستو روڪڻ، داخل ٿيڻ کان منع ڪرڻ
synonyms: Barricade, Close
urduMeaning: راستہ بند کرنا، بند کرنا، راستہ روکنا، داخلہ ممنوع کرنا
englishMeaning: To close or seal a road, path, or area so that people cannot enter.
antonyms: Open, Unblock
Flop, Failure, Disappointment
sindhiMeaning: تمام گهڻي ڪامياب فلم، گهڻو وڪرو ٿيندڙ ڪتاب يا راند، وڏي اثر يا سائيز واري شيءِ، ڪاروبار ۾ وڏي ڪاميابي، ڪنهن به مشهور يا دلچسپ شيءِ لاءِ، اصل ۾ وڏي بم لاءِ استعمال ٿيندو هو جيڪو پوري علائقي کي تباهه ڪري سگهي، هاڻي اهو لفظ اهڙي فلم ڪتاب يا شيءِ لاءِ استعمال ٿئي ٿو جيڪا تمام گهڻي مقبوليت وڪرو ۽ ڪاميابي حاصل ڪري، اهو ڪنهن به وڏي اثر واري شيءِ لاءِ به استعمال ٿئي ٿو
synonyms: Hit, Smash hit, Mega hit, Best-seller, Sensation, Success
urduMeaning: بہت کامیاب فلم، زیادہ فروخت ہونے والی کتاب یا گیم، بڑی اثر والی چیز، کاروبار میں بڑی کامیابی، کسی بھی بہت مشہور یا دلچسپ چیز کے لیے، اصل مطلب ایک بہت بڑا بم تھا جو پورے علاقے کو تباہ کر سکتا تھا، اب یہ لفظ ایسی فلم کتاب یا چیز کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے جو بہت زیادہ کامیابی شہرت اور منافع حاصل کرے، یہ کسی بھی بڑی اور متاثر کن چیز کے لیے بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے
englishMeaning: Something extremely successful, especially a movie, book, or product that earns huge popularity and profit. A very large bomb capable of destroying an entire city block. Today, it is commonly used to describe highly successful movies, books, or products that achieve massive sales, attention, or impact. It can also describe anything big, powerful, or highly impressive.
examples: The new action movie became a blockbuster within a week of its release. Her novel turned into a blockbuster and sold millions of copies worldwide. The company launched a blockbuster product that changed the market. The summer season is full of blockbuster films in cinemas.

englishMeaning: Family bonds are stronger and more important than other relationships. It means that loyalty to family members comes before loyalty to friends or others.
examples: He helped his brother instead of his friend because blood is thicker than water. Even after many fights, she supported her parents; blood is thicker than water. Though they disagreed, he stood by his cousin in trouble because blood is thicker than water. You can always depend on your family, as blood is thicker than water.
urduMeaning: خاندانی رشتے دوستی یا دیگر تعلقات سے زیادہ مضبوط اور اہم ہوتے ہیں، انسان ہمیشہ اپنے خاندان کے ساتھ زیادہ وفادار رہتا ہے
synonyms: Family comes first
antonyms: Betrayal of family, Weak family bond
sindhiMeaning: خانداني رشتا ٻين سڀني لاڳاپن کان وڌيڪ مضبوط ۽ اهم هوندا آهن

urduMeaning: ہوا میں اُڑ جانا، بہت متاثر کرنا، آسانی سے شکست دینا
synonyms: Amaze, Kill
englishMeaning: To impress someone greatly, or to move something by the force of wind.
antonyms: Bore, Spare
examples: The performance blew me away. The wind blew the papers away. That movie really blew everyone away. The storm blew away the roof.
sindhiMeaning: ھوا سان اڏامي وڃڻ، تمام حيران يا متاثر ڪرڻ، آسانيءَ سان شڪست ڏيڻ

urduMeaning: تیز ہوا یا طوفان کے زور سے کسی چیز کا گر جانا، جیسے درخت یا دیوار
synonyms: Knock over
sindhiMeaning: زور واري ھوا يا طوفان سبب ڪا شيءِ جهڙوڪ وڻ، ديوار يا ڇت ڪري پوڻ، طوفان ۾ ڪري پوڻ
antonyms: Stand firm
examples: The old tree was blown down in the storm. Several signs blew down last night. The wind blew down the fence. The hurricane blew down many houses.
englishMeaning: To be knocked over or destroyed by the wind. To make something fall by the force of the wind or air.

synonyms: Ignore, Cancel
antonyms: Attend, Respect
sindhiMeaning: نظرانداز ڪرڻ، اهميت نه ڏيڻ، غصو ڪڍڻ، هوا ڇڏڻ
examples: He blew off the meeting. Don’t blow off your homework. She blew off some steam at the gym. The valve blew off due to pressure.
urduMeaning: نظر انداز کرنا، پروا نہ کرنا، غصہ نکالنا، ہوا خارج کرنا
englishMeaning: To ignore, avoid, or dismiss someone or something, or to release air, gas, or pressure suddenly.
To release anger, stress, or frustration by doing something active or relaxing so that you can feel calmer afterward. To relax or get rid of built-up emotions.
examples: He played football to blow off some steam. After a long day at work, I went jogging to blow off some steam. He shouted just to blow off some steam, he didn’t mean to be rude. Let’s play a game to blow off some steam after the exam. She went out with her friends to blow off some steam after the argument.
urduMeaning: غصہ نکالنا، غصہ یا تناؤ کم کرنے کے لیے کچھ کرنا، یعنی دل کا بوجھ ہلکا کرنے یا سکون حاصل کرنے کے لیے کوئی سرگرمی اختیار کرنا جیسے کھیلنا، چلنا یا کسی سے بات کرنا
sindhiMeaning: ڪاوڙ ڪڍڻ، بي چيني، غصي يا تڪليف کي گهٽائڻ لاءِ ڪجهه ڪرڻ، يعني پاڻ کي آرام ڏيڻ يا دل جو بوجھ گهٽائڻ لاءِ ڪا سرگرمي ڪرڻ، جيئن ته ورزش، گهمڻ يا ڳالهائڻ
synonyms: Relax, Vent
antonyms: Bottle up

synonyms: Exaggerate, Overreact, Magnify, Overstate, Make a mountain out of a molehill, Dramatize, Inflate the issue
englishMeaning: To make a problem, event, or situation seem much bigger, worse, or more serious than it really is. Make a mountain out of a molehill. Overdramatize a situation. Stretch the truth. Overemphasize a problem. Turn a small issue into a big one.
antonyms: Understate, Minimize, Downplay, Stay realistic, Remain calm
examples: Don’t blow things out of proportion; it was only a small mistake. The media sometimes blows things out of proportion to attract attention. She blew the argument out of proportion and stopped talking to everyone. Parents should stay calm and not blow minor problems out of proportion.
urduMeaning: کسی بات یا مسئلے کو حقیقت سے زیادہ بڑھا چڑھا کر پیش کرنا، چھوٹی بات پر بڑا ہنگامہ کھڑا کرنا، معمولی مسئلے کو سنگین بنا دینا، حقیقت سے زیادہ بڑھا چڑھا کر بیان کرنا، کسی چھوٹی بات کو بہت بڑا بنا کر پیش کرنا، غیر ضروری طور پر بڑھا چڑھا کر بیان کرنا یا حد سے زیادہ ردعمل ظاہر کرنا
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ڳالهه کي حقيقت کان وڌيڪ وڏو يا اهم بڻائي پيش ڪرڻ، ننڍڙي ڳالهه تي وڏو شور مچائڻ، ڳالهه کي وڌائي ماڻهن ۾ پريشاني پيدا ڪرڻ، معمولي مسئلي کي وڏو ڏيکارڻ، ننڍڙي ڳالهه کي تمام وڏي خطرناڪ يا اهم بڻائي پيش ڪرڻ، اهو وڌاءُ ڪرڻ غير ضروري پريشاني پيدا ڪرڻ يا حد کان وڌيڪ ردعمل ڏيکارڻ لاءِ چيو ويندو آهي

synonyms: Plentiful, Ample, Copious, Overflowing, Rich
sindhiMeaning: تمام گهڻو، جهجهو، جام، وافر، جالارو، ڪنھن شيء جو ڪثرت ۾ ھجڻ، وڌيڪ، وڏي مقدار ۾، ڀرپور، ڪافي کان وڌيڪ
antonyms: Scarce, Rare, Insufficient, Limited, Meager
examples: Fish are abundant in the lake. We have abundant evidence to prove his guilt. The region has abundant natural resources. Fresh water is abundant in this valley. She has abundant energy even after a long day. The garden produced abundant vegetables this year.
urduMeaning: زیادہ، بہت سا، کثیر، وافر، زیادہ مقدار میں، ضرورت سے زیادہ، بھرپور
englishMeaning: Existing in large quantities, more than enough. Existing or occurring in large amounts. It refers to more than what is needed or expected. It can be used for food, resources, opportunities, happiness, knowledge, or anything available in plenty.

examples: The bomb blew up in the field. He blew up at his friend. They blew up the balloons. The conflict blew up into a major issue.
englishMeaning: To explode. To destroy with explosives. To become very angry. To inflate
sindhiMeaning: ڦاٽڻ، غصي ۾ اچڻ، ڌماڪو ڪرڻ، اڏائي ڇڏڻ، ڪاوڙجي وڃڻ، هوا ڀرڻ
synonyms: Explode, Erupt
urduMeaning: پھٹنا ، غصہ کرنا، پھٹ جانا، اڑانا، غصہ کرنا، ہوا بھرنا
antonyms: Calm down, Defuse

sindhiMeaning: اوچتو سخت ڪاوڙجي وڃڻ، ڪاوڙ ۾ ڦاٽ پئڻ، غصي ۾ ڪنٽرول وڃائڻ، اوچتو تيز ردعمل ڏيکارڻ، اوچتو پنهنجي ڪاوڙ تي ڪنٽرول وڃائي ويهڻ ۽ زور سان ردعمل ڏيکارڻ جهڙوڪ رڙ ڪرڻ يا تڪرار ڪرڻ
examples: He blew his top when he saw the broken laptop. She tends to blow her top over small mistakes. The manager blew his top during the meeting. Don’t blow your top, we can fix the problem calmly.
urduMeaning: اچانک بہت غصے میں آ جانا، غصے سے پھٹ پڑنا، قابو کھو دینا، شدید جذباتی ردعمل دینا، اچانک اپنا غصہ کھو دینا اور شدت سے ردعمل دینا، جیسے چیخنا لڑنا یا سخت ناراضگی ظاہر کرنا
antonyms: Stay calm, Keep your cool, Remain composed, Control yourself, Stay relaxed
englishMeaning: To suddenly become very angry and lose control. To lose your temper quickly and express anger in a strong or uncontrolled way. It often involves shouting, arguing, or reacting emotionally without thinking.
synonyms: Lose your temper, Fly into a rage, Hit the roof, Go ballistic, Explode
Aristocrat, Noble, Elite, High-born, Patrician
urduMeaning: اعلیٰ خاندان یا اشرافیہ سے تعلق رکھنے والا شخص، اشرافیہ کا فرد، اعلیٰ نسل سے تعلق رکھنے والا، معزز خاندانی پس منظر رکھنے والا، جو کسی اعلیٰ معزز یا شاہی خاندان سے تعلق رکھتا ہو، یہ خاندانی وقار اور سماجی حیثیت کو ظاہر کرتا ہے
antonyms: Commoner, Peasant, Low-born, Ordinary person
sindhiMeaning: شريف يا امير خاندان سان تعلق رکندڙ ماڻهو، امير نسل جو ماڻهو، وڏيري يا رئيس خاندان سان تعلق، اعليٰ سماجي حيثيت وارو فرد، جيڪو ڪنهن امير بااثر يا شريف خاندان سان واسطو رکي ٿو، اهو نسب عزت ۽ سماجي حيثيت ڏيکاري ٿو
examples: She comes from a blue blood family with a long history of influence. Despite his blue blood background, he lived a simple life. The event was attended by many blue blood members of society. He may not be blue blood, but he earned respect through hard work.
englishMeaning: A person of noble birth or high social status. Someone who comes from an aristocratic, royal, or highly respected family. It suggests inherited status, prestige, and social influence rather than personal achievement alone.

synonyms: Favorite, Golden Boy, Pet, Chosen One
sindhiMeaning: پسنديده ماڻهو، اهڙو ماڻهو جيڪو ڪنهن طاقتور يا اختيار واري شخص جو خاص پسنديده هجي ۽ جنهن کي ٻين کان وڌيڪ سهولتون يا فائدا ملن
englishMeaning: Someone who is favored. A person who receives special treatment, approval, or preference from someone in authority. The favor may be unfair or based on personal liking rather than merit.
urduMeaning: خاص منظورِ نظر شخص، ایسا شخص جو کسی بااختیار فرد کا پسندیدہ ہو اور جسے دوسروں کے مقابلے میں خاص رعایت یا ترجیح دی جائے
antonyms: Outsider, Neglected person, disfavored Employee
examples: He is the boss’s blue eyes, so his mistakes are often ignored. She became the manager’s blue eyes after completing the project successfully. The team complained that only the blue eyes get promotions. Being the teacher’s blue eyes can create jealousy among students.

She tried to bluff her way through the interview. He was bluffing about having more money. The player called his opponent’s bluff. We stood on the bluff overlooking the river. She bluffed the doorman into thinking that she was a reporter. I don't think he'll shoot, I think he's just bluffing.
antonyms: Be honest, Reveal, Confess, Tell the truth, Polite, Gentle, Indirect
englishMeaning: To mislead someone by false confidence, threats, or claims so they believe something that is not true. Often used in games, negotiations, or arguments. An act of deception in which someone pretends to have more strength, knowledge, or advantage than they truly have. A steep cliff or high bank, especially near a river or the sea. Speaking in a direct and honest way, sometimes in a slightly rough manner.
urduMeaning: دھوکا دینا، جھوٹی جرات دکھانا، جھوٹا دعویٰ کرنا، جھوٹی دھمکی دینا، جھوٹی خود اعتمادی ظاہر کر کے کسی کو غلط یقین دلانا، گمراہ کرنا، دھونس جمانا، جھوٹی یقین دہانی کرانا، دھوکا دہی کے لیے طاقت اور اعتماد کا مظاہرہ کرنا، صاف گو، خالی دھمکی، اونچا عمودی کنارہ
sindhiMeaning: ڌوڪو ڏيڻ، ڪوڙي همت ڏيکارڻ، ڪوڙي دعويٰ ڪرڻ، گمراهه ڪرڻ، ٺڳڻ، پنهنجي گُتي پوري ڪرڻ لاءِ آڪڙ ڏيکارڻ، دوکيباز تي بي اعتباري جو اظهار ڪرڻ، ڪوڙي کي للڪارڻ، کهرو، رکو، ڊيٺ، ڌونس، چرچ، دوکو، ٽڪري يا جھاز جيڪو سامهون کا ويڪرو ۽ اڀو هجي، کرو سچو ۽ حجائتو(ماڻهو يا انداز)، درياهه يا سمنڊ جو اُڀريل ڪنارو
synonyms: Deceive, Trick, Mislead, Pretend, Feign, Cliff, Crag, Bank, Escarpment
Unsharpened, Flat, Frank, Straightforward, Outspoken
urduMeaning: تیزی ختم کرنا، جس کا کنارہ یا نوک تیز نہ ہو، صاف گو، بے باک، سیدھا جو بناوٹ کے بغیر بات کرے
sindhiMeaning: مُڏو ڪرڻ، تيزي گهٽائڻ، جيڪو ڪٽڻ يا ڇڪڻ لاءِ تيز نه هجي، مُڏو، سڌو، بي باڪ، صاف گو(جيڪو ڳالهيون بنا ڪنهن بناوت جي سڌي طرح چوي)
englishMeaning: To make something less sharp or less strong. Not sharp or having a dull edge (used for objects like knives or pencils). (Of a person or speech) speaking in a direct, plain, and sometimes rude way, not trying to be polite.
antonyms: Sharp, Pointed, Polite, Tactful, Subtle, Gentle
examples: The knife is too blunt to cut the fruit. He is a blunt person who always speaks his mind. Her blunt reply hurt his feelings. Years of use have blunted the edge of the scissors.

urduMeaning: شیخی مارنا، فخر کرنا، اپنی بڑائی بیان کرنا، شیخی بگھارنا، خود تعریف کرنا، فخر سے بیان کرنا
antonyms: Humble, Modest, Understate, Conceal
sindhiMeaning: فخر ڪرڻ، وڏائي ڪرڻ، پاڻ جي تعريف ڪرڻ، پاڻ ساراهڻ، شيخي هڻڻ، پاڻ کي وڏو ڏيکارڻ
synonyms: Brag, Show off, Crow, Glory, Swagger, Vaunt
englishMeaning: To speak proudly about oneself, achievements, possessions, or abilities. It can also mean something worthy of pride.
examples: He always boasts about his expensive car. She boasted that she could finish the work alone. The city boasts beautiful historical buildings. They boasted of their team's victory for weeks.

He sounded boastful when he kept talking about his expensive car. The player gave a boastful speech after winning the match. Her boastful attitude annoyed her colleagues. The boy became boastful after scoring the highest marks in class.
urduMeaning: دکھاوے والا فخر کرنے والا، اپنی تعریف کرنے والا، بڑھا چڑھا کر بات کرنے والا، لا فزن، مُتَکَبَّر ، پُر غَرُور، شیخی خوار، مغرور
sindhiMeaning: ڏيکاءَ وارو فخر ڪندڙ، پاڻ جي واکاڻ ڪندڙ، وڌائي ڪري ڳالهائڻ وارو، مغرور، ٻٽاڪي، وات ڦاٽو، ڊاڙِي، لٻاڙِي، ٺرڙو، هٺيلو
synonyms: Proud, Bragging, Arrogant, Self praising, Vainglorious, Egotistical
englishMeaning: A person who frequently praises himself or herself and speaks proudly about achievements, wealth, strength, or abilities. Such a person often exaggerates personal success to impress others.
antonyms: Humble, Modest, Quiet, Unassuming, Reserved

examples: The office was abuzz with news of the promotion. Social media is abuzz after the movie trailer was released. The market was abuzz with shoppers before the festival. The classroom became abuzz when the teacher announced a surprise test.
urduMeaning: جوش اور چرچا میں، ایسی حالت جہاں لوگ کسی خبر، واقعے یا افواہ کی وجہ سے سرگرم اور پرجوش ہوں
sindhiMeaning: جوش يا چرچو ۾، اهڙي حالت جتي ماڻهو گهڻو ڳالهائي رهيا هجن يا ڪنهن خبر يا واقعي سبب جوش ۾ هجن
antonyms: Quiet, Calm, Silent, Dull, Inactive
synonyms: Excited, Lively, Animated, Active
englishMeaning: Describes a situation, place, or group where people are actively talking, reacting, or feeling excited, often because of news, an event, or anticipation. Full of excitement, activity, or talk.

sindhiMeaning: رڪاوٽ ۾ ڦاٿل، جسماني طور تي مٽي يا پاڻي ۾ ڦاٿل ٿيڻ، ڪم يا منصوبو ڪنهن رڪاوٽ يا پيچيدگي سبب اڳتي نه وڌڻ، ڳالهه ٻولهه يا عمل ۾ رڪاوٽ اچڻ
urduMeaning: پھنس جانا یا رک جانا، گاڑی یا شخص مٹی یا پانی میں پھنس جانا، کام، منصوبہ یا بات چیت کسی رکاوٹ یا پیچیدگی کی وجہ سے آگے نہ بڑھنا، باریکیوں یا مسائل کی وجہ سے عمل یا کوشش سست ہونا
examples: The car bogged down in the swamp. The negotiations bogged down due to disagreements. She bogged down in paperwork and missed the deadline. The team bogged down in minor technical issues. The project bogged down because of lack of funds. He bogged down in unnecessary details.
antonyms: Progress, Advance, Speed up, Move forward, Accelerate
synonyms: Stuck, Trapped, Hindered, Entangled, Delayed, Obstructed
englishMeaning: To get stuck, delayed, or hindered. To physically get trapped in mud, water, or difficult terrain. To become overwhelmed or slowed by difficulties, obstacles, or excessive details. To impede progress in work, discussion, or process. To lose focus or energy because of complications.
To reduce a complex situation to a simple core idea. When something can be explained by one essential idea or cause.
examples: It all boils down to trust. The issue boils down to money. Their argument boils down to a misunderstanding. Success boils down to hard work.
urduMeaning: ایک بنیادی بات تک محدود ہونا، اصل بات، کسی پیچیدہ بات کو سادہ شکل میں لا کر اس کی بنیادی وجہ یا نکتہ بیان کرنا
sindhiMeaning: هڪ اهم ڳالهه تائين محدود ٿيڻ، اصل ڳالهه، ڪنهن پيچيده ڳالهه جو خلاصو جنهن ۾ صرف اهم نقطو بچي وڃي
synonyms: Reduce, Summarize, Result in
antonyms: Expand, Complicate

examples: After hours of discussion, he finally acceded to their request. The government acceded to the demands of the protesters. She acceded to the position of chairperson last year. He was reluctant at first but later acceded to the plan.
sindhiMeaning: مڃڻ، قبول ڪرڻ، راضپو ڏيڻ، سرڪاري طور قبول ڪرڻ، گهرج يا درخواست کي مڃڻ، عهدو سنڀالڻ، ڪنهن ڳالهه کي سوچ ويچار کان پوءِ مڃڻ يا قبول ڪرڻ، اهو لفظ عام طور تي رسمي حالتن ۾ استعمال ٿيندو آهي جهڙوڪ ڪنهن درخواست معاهدي يا اختيار کي قبول ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: مان لینا، قبول کرنا، رضامند ہونا، باضابطہ طور پر قبول کرنا، کسی مطالبے کو مان لینا، عہدہ سنبھالنا، کسی بات کو غور کرنے کے بعد مان لینا یا قبول کر لینا، یہ لفظ عموماً رسمی مواقع پر استعمال ہوتا ہے جیسے کسی درخواست معاہدے یا اختیار کو قبول کرنا
antonyms: Refuse, Reject, Deny, Oppose, Resist
synonyms: Agree, Consent, Accept, Approve, Comply, Assent
englishMeaning: To agree, to give consent, or to accept a request or demand. To agree to something after initially resisting or considering it. It is often used in formal situations such as accepting a proposal, request, treaty, or authority. It can also mean to take on a position or office.

antonyms: Weaken, Undermine, Discourage, Damage, Hinder, Reduce
sindhiMeaning: سهارو ڏيڻ، طاقت يا مضبوطي وڌائڻ، حمايت ڪرڻ، مضبوط ڪرڻ، حوصلا وڌائڻ، ساک وڌائڻ، نظام کي طاقت ڏيڻ، ڪنهن خيال دليل اداري يا شخص کي وڌيڪ مضبوط بڻائڻ، اهو لفظ ڪڏهن جسماني سهاري لاءِ به استعمال ٿيندو آهي جهڙوڪ تڪيو يا گدي جهڙو سهارو
synonyms: Support, Strengthen, Reinforce, Encourage, Back, Fortify, Promote
englishMeaning: To support, strengthen, or increase the strength, confidence, or effectiveness of something such as an argument, system, organization, or person. It can also mean providing physical support like a cushion or pad.
urduMeaning: سہارا دینا، مضبوط کرنا، طاقت اور اعتماد میں اضافہ کرنا، حوصلہ بڑھانا، ساک بہتر بنانا، نظام کو تقویت دینا، یہ لفظ کسی دلیل منصوبے ادارے یا شخص کی حمایت کے لیے بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے،کبھی کبھی جسمانی سہارا دینے والی چیز جیسے لمبا تکیہ
examples: The government introduced new policies to bolster the economy. Good evidence can bolster your argument in a debate. The teacher tried to bolster the student's confidence. Community support helped bolster the relief program after the flood. She placed a bolster behind her back while sitting on the bed. The sofa had a decorative bolster on each side.

synonyms: Complete surprise, Sudden shock, Unexpected event, Out of nowhere
sindhiMeaning: اهڙي واقعي، خبر يا صورتحال کي چيو ويندو آهي جيڪا اوچتو پيش اچي، جنهن جي ڪنهن کي به اڳڪٿي نه هجي، ۽ جيڪا ٻڌندڙ يا ڏسندڙ کي حيران، پريشان يا صدمو پهچائي ڇڏي
antonyms: Expected event, Foreseen situation, Planned occurrence, Predictable outcome
englishMeaning: A sudden and completely unexpected event or piece of news. Something shocking that happens without any warning. It is used when an event or news surprises people because there were no signs or expectations beforehand. The phrase comes from the idea of lightning striking from a clear blue sky.
urduMeaning: ایسے واقعے یا خبر کو کہا جاتا ہے جو اچانک سامنے آئے، جس کا کوئی اندازہ نہ ہو، اور جو سننے یا دیکھنے والوں کو شدید حیرت، پریشانی یا صدمے میں مبتلا کر دے
examples: His sudden resignation was a bolt from the blue for the entire team. The announcement of early elections came like a bolt from the blue. Her illness was a bolt from the blue to her family. The company’s closure was a complete bolt from the blue.

urduMeaning: حیران کن یا صدمہ دینے والا واقعہ، اچانک خبر، خوبصورت یا دلکش عورت
englishMeaning: A shocking or surprising event or person. Something that causes sudden shock, surprise, or excitement. Can also refer to a very attractive person, especially a woman.
examples: The news of her resignation was a real bombshell. He dropped a bombshell during the meeting about the budget cuts. She appeared at the party looking like a bombshell. The celebrity’s sudden engagement was a bombshell for fans.
antonyms: Calm, Expected event, Ordinary person
sindhiMeaning: ڇڪتاڻ وارو واقعو يا حيرت انگيز خبر، دلڪش عورت
synonyms: Surprise, Shock, Revelation, Stunner

urduMeaning: بہتر طرزِ زندگی اور لذیذ کھانوں مشروبات اور محفلوں سے لطف اندوز ہونے والا شخص
synonyms: Epicure, Gourmet, Sybarite, Pleasure-seeker, Connoisseur, Gastronomist
sindhiMeaning: اهڙو ماڻهو جيڪو سٺي خوراڪ مشروبات ۽ سماجي ميل جول مان مزو وٺي ۽ آرامده زندگي گذارڻ پسند ڪري
antonyms: Ascetic, Hermit, Minimalist, Abstainer, Stoic
examples: He is known as a bon vivant who always attends the finest dinner parties in the city. The bon vivant spent his weekends exploring new restaurants and wine tastings. As a bon vivant, she enjoyed traveling to places famous for their cuisine and culture. The magazine described him as a charming bon vivant with expensive tastes.
englishMeaning: A person who enjoys good food, good drink, and a comfortable social life. Someone who loves to live well and enjoys luxury, especially fine dining, social gatherings, and entertainment. A person with refined tastes who actively seeks pleasure in social and cultural experiences.

antonyms: Agreement, Harmony, Consensus
sindhiMeaning: تڪراهو سبب جيڪو ماڻهن يا گروهن ۾ اختلاف يا بحث پيدا ڪريار جو سبب
synonyms: Dispute, Disagreement, Conflict, Argument, Controversy
urduMeaning: جھگڑے یا اختلاف کی وجہ، وہ چیز جو لوگوں یا گروپوں کے درمیان تنازعہ یا بحث پیدا کرے
englishMeaning: A cause of dispute. Something that causes disagreement or argument between people or groups
examples: The property line became a bone of contention between neighbors. Funding for the project has been a bone of contention for months. The new law is likely to become a bone of contention among politicians. His refusal to attend the meeting was a bone of contention in the office.

antonyms: Neglect
synonyms: Study, Revise
urduMeaning: خوب پڑھنا، کسی موضوع پر جلدی سے اچھی طرح مطالعہ کرنا یا تیاری کرنا
sindhiMeaning: سخت محنت سان پڙهڻ، تيزي سان پڙهڻ يا ياد ڪرڻ، ڪنهن موضوع تي ڌيان سان تياري ڪرڻ
examples: I need to bone up on my English grammar. She boned up on company policies before the interview. He’s boning up on history for his test. You should bone up on driving laws before your exam.
englishMeaning: To study or revise something intensively, especially before an exam or event, to refresh one’s knowledge quickly.

synonyms: Campfire, Fire, Blaze, Pyre, Outdoor fire
urduMeaning: خوشی کا آلاؤ، غلاظت جالانے والی آگ یا خوشی کے موقع پر روشن کی جانے والی آگ، تہوار کی آگ، بڑی کھلی آگ، رسم یا تقریب کی آگ، چیزوں کو جلانے کے لیے بنائی گئی آگ
antonyms: Ice, Cold, Frost, Snow
englishMeaning: A large open fire built outdoors for celebration, warmth, or burning things. A ceremonial fire during traditional festivals. A large controlled fire for disposing of materials. A symbolic fire representing celebration or protest. A social gathering centered around a large outdoor fire.
examples: The villagers gathered around the bonfire to celebrate the harvest festival. We sat near the bonfire to keep warm during the cold night. They built a bonfire on the beach and sang songs together. The old furniture was thrown into the bonfire.
sindhiMeaning: جشن وقت باهه جو مچ، ڀَڀَڙُ، هڪ وڏي باهه جيڪا کليل جڳهه ۾ ٻاري ويندي آهي عام طور تي خوشي ميلن سردي کان بچاءُ يا رسم لاءِ، ميلي يا تہوار جي باهه، کليل ميدان ۾ ٻاريل وڏي باهه، رسم يا جشن لاءِ باهه، ساڙڻ لاءِ تيار ڪيل باهه

examples: We booked in at the hotel before dinner. She booked in at the clinic for her appointment. They booked in early to get a good seat. Guests must book in before 9 pm.
sindhiMeaning: داخلا ڪرائڻ، داخل ٿيڻ يا پنهنجو نالو درج ڪرائڻ
synonyms: Check in
englishMeaning: To register or check in at a place such as a hotel, hospital, or event, to make a booking officially.
antonyms: Check out
urduMeaning: داخلہ کرانا، اندراج کروانا یا چیک اِن کرنا

examples: The new hospital is a boon for the local community. For farmers, good rainfall is always a great boon. Mobile phones can be a boon if used wisely. The scholarship proved to be a real boon for poor students.
synonyms: Blessing, Benefit, Advantage, Gift
englishMeaning: A blessing or something that is very helpful. A timely blessing or benefit. Something very helpful, useful, or advantageous.
sindhiMeaning: نعمت، رحمت، برڪت، ڪا اهڙي شيءِ جيڪا تمام مددگار ۽ فائدي واري هجي، ڪا اهڙي شي يا حالت جيڪا زندگي کي آسان يا بهتر بڻائي
urduMeaning: کوئی بڑی نعمت یا رحمت جو انسان کے لیے فائدہ مند ہو، کوئی ایسی چیز یا موقع جو مددگار یا مفید ثابت ہو
antonyms: Curse, Disadvantage, Bane, Misfortune

examples: His boorish comments ruined the friendly atmosphere. She found his boorish behavior embarrassing at the dinner party. The manager criticized the boorish attitude of the staff member. Avoid being boorish when meeting new people; first impressions matter.
urduMeaning: بے تہذیب، بدتمیز، ایسا رویہ جو سنجیدہ، مہذب یا دوسروں کے جذبات کا احترام نہ کرے، سخت یا بے مزاجی سے بھرا ہوا ہو
englishMeaning: Rude, crude, or insensitive in behavior or manner. Showing a lack of refinement, good manners, or consideration for others; behaving in a rough, insensitive, or socially awkward way
synonyms: Rude, Crude, Uncouth, Coarse, Insensitive
antonyms: Polite, Refined, Courteous, Cultured, Considerate
sindhiMeaning: بي ادب، ڳنوار، دهقاني، ڄٽ، جهنگلي، بدتميز، اهڙو رويو جيڪو غير مهذب بديهن يا ٻئي جي جذبات جو خيال نه رکندو هجي
اڳتي وڌائڻ، تيزي سان اڳتي وڌڻ ۾ مدد ڏيڻ، ڪنهن ڪم کي اڳتي وڌائڻ لاءِ حوصلہ افزائي ڪرڻ يا مدد فراهم ڪرڻ، جيئن منصوبي يا عمل کي تيزي سان اڳتي وڌڻ ۾ مدد ملي
examples: The manager boosted the team along with additional resources to finish the project on time. A good mentor can boost a young professional along in their career. The new marketing strategy helped boost sales along faster than expected. Technological innovations can boost economic growth along significantly.
synonyms: Accelerate, Advance, Encourage, Promote, Facilitate
antonyms: Hinder, Obstruct, Delay, Slow down, Impede
urduMeaning: آگے بڑھانا، تیزی سے آگے بڑھانے میں مدد کرنا، کسی کام یا منصوبے کی ترقی میں مدد دینا یا اسے تیز رفتاری سے آگے بڑھانے کے لیے سہولت یا حوصلہ افزائی فراہم کرنا
englishMeaning: To help something progress or move forward more quickly. To encourage, support, or accelerate the progress of something, such as a project, process, or idea. It often implies providing help, resources, or motivation so that advancement happens more smoothly or faster.

synonyms: Restore, Revive, Uplift, Rejuvenate, Encourage
antonyms: Weaken, Depress, Demoralize, Reduce, Discourage
examples: The coach’s advice helped boost back the team’s morale after the loss. A good night’s sleep can boost back your energy levels. The government launched a program to boost back small businesses affected by floods. Positive feedback from her manager boosted back her confidence.
urduMeaning: واپس بہتر حالت میں لانا، حوصلہ افزائی کرنا، دوبارہ بڑھانا
englishMeaning: To help someone or something recover or return to a better state. To giving support, encouragement, or assistance to restore someone or something to a previous level of performance, confidence, or strength. It implies a return to a positive condition after a decline or setback.
sindhiMeaning: واپسي مضبوط ڪرڻ، حوصلا ڏيڻ، ٻيهر وڌائڻ
ڪنهن کي جاءِ، صورتحال يا عهدي مان ٻاهر ڪڍڻ ۾ مدد ڏيڻ، جسماني يا ذهني طور
antonyms: Pull in, Bring in, Retain, Keep
urduMeaning: کسی کو کسی جگہ، حالت یا عہدے سے باہر نکالنے میں مدد دینا، جسمانی یا معنوی طور پر
synonyms: Push out, Lift out, Help Exit, Remove
englishMeaning: To help someone leave or exit, often by giving physical or metaphorical assistance. To push or lift someone or something out of a place, situation, or position. It can be literal, such as helping someone climb out of a window, or figurative, like helping someone leave a role or situation.
examples: He boosted me out of the car after it got stuck in mud. The manager boosted out the lazy employee from the project. She boosted the child out of the tree carefully. They boosted out the old furniture to make space for new items.

I need to boost up my confidence before the interview. The company plans to boost up sales by offering discounts. Exercise can boost up your energy levels. New policies were introduced to boost up student performance.
englishMeaning: To increase, improve, or raise something. To enhance or lift the level, amount, or quality of something. It can refer to physical, emotional, or abstract things like energy, morale, performance, or numbers.
sindhiMeaning: وڌائڻ، بهتر ڪرڻ، مضبوط ڪرڻ، حوصلو وڌائڻ، ڪارڪردگي وڌائڻ، توانائي وڌائڻ
synonyms: Increase, Raise, Enhance, Improve, Strengthen, Uplift
antonyms: Reduce, Lower, Weaken, Decrease, Diminish
urduMeaning: بڑھانا، مضبوط کرنا، بہتری لانا، حوصلہ بڑھانا، کارکردگی بڑھانا، توانائی بڑھانا

englishMeaning: Military forces physically deployed in an area. Field staff working directly in communities. Personnel carrying out operations instead of planning from headquarters. Ground level workers who collect data or implement programs.
sindhiMeaning: جنگي علائقي ۾ موجود فوجي دستا، ميدان ۾ ڪم ڪندڙ عملو يا رضاڪار، هيڊ آفيس بدران سڌو ڪم ڪندڙ ماڻهو، مقامي سطح تي منصوبا لاڳو ڪندڙ يا ڊيٽا گڏ ڪندڙ عملو
urduMeaning: کسی علاقے میں موجود فوجی دستے، میدان میں کام کرنے والا عملہ یا رضاکار، ہیڈکوارٹر کے بجائے عملی کام کرنے والی ٹیم، مقامی سطح پر پروگرام نافذ کرنے یا معلومات جمع کرنے والے کارکن
antonyms: Remote staff, Headquarters personnel, Desk workers, Off site management, Back office staff
synonyms: Field personnel, Ground forces, On site staff, Deployed troops, Frontline workers, Field team
examples: The government decided to send boots on the ground to help control the wildfire. The aid organization deployed boots on the ground after the flood to assist local communities. Good planning is important, but real progress happens when there are boots on the ground. The company sent boots on the ground to understand the market conditions directly.
He botched the repair and made the problem worse. The plan was botched due to poor coordination. She apologized for botching the presentation. The company botched the product launch.
englishMeaning: To do something badly or carelessly. To spoil a task or job by doing it in a careless, clumsy, or unskilled way. It can also refer to a job that has been done very badly and needs fixing.
sindhiMeaning: ڪم خراب ڪرڻ، ڪنهن ڪم کي بي ڌياني يا نااهلي سان ڪرڻ جنهن سبب نتيجو خراب نڪري
urduMeaning: کام خراب کرنا، کسی کام کو لاپرواہی یا ناتجربہ کاری سے اس طرح کرنا کہ وہ خراب ہو جائے
synonyms: Mess up, Spoil, Bungle, Mishandle
antonyms: Fix, Perfect, Manage, Execute properly

urduMeaning: زور دینا، نمایاں کرنا، اہمیت بڑھانا، واضح طور پر اجاگر کرنا، کسی خاص خوبی فرق احساس یا بات کو اس طرح نمایاں کرنا کہ وہ زیادہ واضح اہم یا نمایاں محسوس ہو
synonyms: Emphasize, Highlight, Stress, Intensify, Underline, Reinforce
englishMeaning: To make something more noticeable, stronger, or clearer. To emphasize or highlight a feature, quality, feeling, or difference so that it becomes more noticeable or important. It often refers to making something stand out clearly in speech, writing, appearance, or behavior.
antonyms: Minimize, Downplay, Reduce, Conceal, Weaken
examples: The designer used bright colors to accentuate the beauty of the dress. Good lighting can accentuate the details of a painting. His speech accentuated the importance of education in society. The makeup was applied carefully to accentuate her eyes.
sindhiMeaning: زور ڏيڻ، نمايان ڪرڻ، اهميت وڌائڻ، خاص طرح اجاگر ڪرڻ، ڪنهن خاص ڳالهه خوبي فرق يا احساس کي وڌيڪ نمايان ڪرڻ ته جيئن اها ٻين جي ڀيٽ ۾ صاف ۽ واضح نظر اچي يا وڌيڪ اهم محسوس ٿئي
نڪـ ۾ دم ڪرڻ، تنگ ڪرڻ، تڪليف ۾ وجھڻ، پريشان ڪرڻ، مسئلو پيدا ڪرڻ، بيزار ڪرڻ، حيران ڪرڻ، ڪڪ ڪرڻ، دق ڪرڻ، پريشاني، تڪليف، بيزاري
englishMeaning: To take the trouble to do something; to annoy or cause worry. To give effort or concern for something, often reluctantly. To disturb, worry, or annoy someone. A source of trouble, annoyance, or inconvenience. Something that causes difficulty or annoyance.
examples: Tell the children to stop bothering their father. Don’t bother me with foolish question. The man is always bothering me to lend him money. Don’t put yourself to any bothering. His lazy son is quite a bother to him. This drawer won't shut isn't it a bother.
synonyms: Annoy, Disturb, Trouble, Worry, Fret, Agitate
antonyms: Calm, Comfort, Please, Satisfy, Relax
urduMeaning: مسئلہ پیدا کرنا، پریشان ہونا، زحمت، دق کرنا، جان کھانا، تکلیف، ناک میں دم کرنا، زحمت اُٹھانا، پریشانی، جان کھانا ، مغز کھانا

examples: He bottled out at the last moment. He was going to ask for a promotion, but he bottled out at the last minute. The player bottled out of taking the final penalty She wanted to speak on stage but bottled out when she saw the crowd. They were supposed to confront the manager, but they bottled out.
synonyms: Lose nerve, Back out
antonyms: Persist, Continue
sindhiMeaning: همت وڃائڻ، ڊڄي يا گھبرائي ڪري ڪم نه ڪرڻ، ڊڄي پوئتي هٽڻ
englishMeaning: To lose courage at the last moment and fail to do something because of fear or nervousness.
urduMeaning: ہمت ہار دینا، ڈر یا گھبراہٹ کی وجہ سے کوئی کام نہ کرنا، ڈر کر پیچھے ہٹ جانا

synonyms: Hindrance, Barrier, Jam, Blockage, Congestion, Obstruction, Tie-up
antonyms: Broad, Fat, Thick, Wide, Opening
englishMeaning: A narrow or busy section of road where the traffic often gets slower and stops. Anything that delays development or progress, particularly in business or industry. A crowded mass (as of cars) that impedes or blocks movement. A narrow route.
examples: He drove around the outside of the town to avoid the bottleneck in the center. Opponents argue that the traffic lights would cause a bottleneck at the junction. Understaffing has caused a real bottleneck. Computer buffs call this a bottleneck.
sindhiMeaning: رڪاوٽ، رڪاوٽ، تنگ جاءِ، ڪم ۾ دير جو سبب
urduMeaning: وہ مرحلہ جہاں ٹریفک ، پیداوار وغیرہ آگے نہ بڑھ سکے ، تنگ جگہ جہاں حرکت کرنا مُشکِل ہو ، آہستہ ہونا یا رک جانا

examples: After failure, he bounced back better. They bounced back better after the loss. She always bounces back better from setbacks. Our team will bounce back better next season.
synonyms: Recover, Rebuild

examples: My car broke down on the way. She broke down in tears. The talks broke down after hours. The machine broke down again.

examples: After six months of business, the company finally managed to break even. We sold enough tickets to break even on the event costs. Despite hard work, the farmer could only break even this season. Our goal this year is at least to break even before making profits next year.

examples: Someone broke into my house. The burglars broke into the bank. She broke into a smile. The crowd broke into laughter.

englishMeaning: To do something innovative or original, to start something that has not been done before. To innovate or pioneer something new. To explore unknown areas or ideas. To achieve something for the first time.
To bring something to an abrupt end, such as a conversation, relationship, or agreement.

examples: Fire broke out last night. War broke out between two nations. She broke out in a rash. Prisoners broke out of jail.

examples: The manager brushed aside all the complaints from the workers. She brushed aside his apology and walked away. The government brushed aside the criticism from the media. He brushed aside my advice and did what he wanted.
urduMeaning: کسی بات، رائے یا تجویز کو اہمیت نہ دینا یا اسے رد کر دینا، نظرانداز کرنا یا توجہ نہ دینا
antonyms: Accept, Acknowledge
synonyms: Reject, Disregard
englishMeaning: To ignore, reject, or dismiss someone’s opinion, suggestion, or concern as unimportant or not worth considering. To pay no attention to something or someone.

synonyms: Phonophobia, Sound phobia, Fear of noise
sindhiMeaning: آوازن جو خوف، خوف جيڪو خاص آواز يا شور کان پيدا ٿئي ٿو، جنهن ۾ ماڻهو پريشان گھبرايل يا ڪنڌ ڍڪڻ وارن عملن ۾ مبتلا ٿي سگهي ٿو

englishMeaning: Fear of sounds or noises. An extreme or irrational fear of certain sounds or noises. People with this phobia may experience anxiety, panic attacks, or avoidance behavior when exposed to loud, unexpected, or particular types of sounds.
urduMeaning: آواز کا خوف ، شدید یا غیر معقول خوف جو مخصوص آوازوں یا شور سے پیدا ہوتا ہے، اس سے مبتلا شخص کو اضطراب گھبراہٹ یا اس آواز سے بچنے کے رویے کا سامنا ہو سکتا ہے

examples: She brushed away the dust from the old photograph. He brushed away his tears and smiled again. The teacher brushed away the student’s excuses. They brushed away all doubts and started the project.
urduMeaning: ہلکی حرکت سے مٹی آنسو یا کسی چیز کو ہٹانا، کسی بات یا احساس کو اہمیت نہ دینا

urduMeaning: کسی چیز یا کپڑے سے برش کے ذریعے مٹی یا گرد صاف کرنا

synonyms: Wipe, Scrub

examples: He tried to talk to her, but she brushed him off. The manager brushed off their complaints about the salary. She brushed off the criticism and continued working confidently. The government brushed off the report as unimportant.

urduMeaning: برش سے صاف کرنا،کنگھی کر کے سنوارنا، کسی چیز کو برش سے صاف کرنا یا بالوں کو کنگھی سے سنوارنا، زیادہ تر بالوں کپڑوں یا قالین وغیرہ کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے
englishMeaning: To clean, remove, or smooth something by using a brush. To clean something (such as hair, fabric, carpet, or an object) by brushing it to remove dust, dirt, or tangles.

antonyms: Tangle, Dirty, Mess Up, Soil, Wrinkle
sindhiMeaning: برش يا ڪنگهي سان ڪنهن شيءِ کي صاف ڪرڻ، مٽي يا ڌوڙ ڪڍڻ يا وارن کي سنوارڻ، اهو لفظ گهڻو ڪري وارن ڪپڙن يا قالين لاءِ استعمال ٿيندو آهي

sindhiMeaning: مسئلي کي لڪائڻ يا نظرانداز ڪرڻ، ظاهر نه ڪرڻ، ڏکيو يا شرمناڪ معاملو لڪائي ڇڏڻ، ڪنهن غلطي، مسئلي يا شرمناڪ ڳالهه کي ظاهر ڪرڻ بدران ان کي لڪائڻ يا ان تي ڳالهائڻ کان پاسو ڪرڻ تہ جيئن ٻين کي علم نہ ٿئي

sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ کي شامل ڪرڻ، اندر جوڙڻ، ٺاهڻ، عادتن شامل ڪرڻ، فطري طور شامل ڪرڻ، عادتن شامل ڪرڻ

synonyms: Knot, Lump, Bounce, Node, Nodule, Swelling, Collision, Concussion, Crash, Bang, Bash, Collide

examples: The morning sun will burn off the fog soon. He goes jogging every day to burn off extra calories. The fire burned off the dry grass around the field. She tried to burn off her frustration by exercising.

antonyms: Keep options open, Maintain relations, Preserve ties, Stay connected, Leave the door open

englishMeaning: Referring to a sudden, violent, and disastrous event that causes great destruction or change. Something extremely significant and life-altering, often used for natural disasters, social upheavals, or major crises.
examples: The cataclysmic earthquake destroyed the entire city within minutes. Climate change could lead to cataclysmic floods and droughts in the future. The war had cataclysmic effects on the nation’s economy and people. The fall of the empire was a cataclysmic event that reshaped history.

englishMeaning: Something that causes a change or speeds up a process without itself being affected. A substance or an agent that accelerates a chemical reaction or brings about significant change in a situation or process without undergoing permanent change itself. It can be literal, in chemistry, or metaphorical, in social, economic, or personal contexts.
urduMeaning: محرک یا تیز کرنے والا عنصر، کوئی ایسا عنصر یا چیز جو کسی عمل یا ردعمل کو تیز کرتا ہے یا کسی صورتحال میں تبدیلی لاتا ہے بغیر خود مستقل تبدیلی کے
examples: The new manager was a catalyst for positive changes in the company. Enzymes act as catalysts in many biological reactions. The invention of the internet was a catalyst for global communication. Her speech served as a catalyst for social reform.

synonyms: Stimulus, Impetus, Spark, Accelerator, Trigger, Motivator

synonyms: Disaster theory, Catastrophic theory, Sudden change theory
englishMeaning: The belief that the Earth has been shaped by sudden, violent events such as floods, earthquakes, or volcanic eruptions. A scientific theory in geology which states that major changes in the Earth's surface were caused by sudden natural disasters rather than slow and gradual processes. It suggests that events like massive floods, volcanic eruptions, earthquakes, or asteroid impacts played a key role in shaping landscapes and causing extinction of species.
examples: Catastrophism explains mass extinction as the result of sudden natural disasters. Early geologists supported catastrophism to describe changes in Earth's history. examples: The colorful painting caught her fancy immediately. That new phone model caught his fancy at the store. Traveling abroad caught their fancy after watching the documentary. The music band caught the audience’s fancy with their performance.

englishMeaning: An irrational fear of the sky, outer space, celestial bodies (such as stars, planets, and the moon), or anything related to the vastness of the universe. A person with this phobia may feel intense anxiety, panic, or discomfort when looking at the sky or thinking about space.

englishMeaning: In ancient times, a citadel was the strongest part of a city, often surrounded by walls. It served as the last defense point in case of invasion. Figuratively, it can describe something that protects important values or ideas.
sindhiMeaning: قلعو، مضبوط قلعو، حفاظت جو هنڌ، شهر يا علائقي ۾ ٺهيل اهڙو مضبوط قلعو جيڪو دشمن کان بچاءَ لاءِ ٺاهيو ويندو آهي، مجازي طور تي، ڪو به مضبوط ادارو يا جڳهه جيڪا ڪنهن قدر يا علم جي حفاظت ڪري ٿي
urduMeaning: قلعہ ، مضبوط قلعہ ، حفاظت گاہ، شہر کے اندر یا قریب بنایا گیا ایک مضبوط قلعہ جو حملے کے وقت پناہ کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے، مجازی طور پر کسی مضبوط ادارے یا نظریے کا مرکز
examples: The soldiers took refuge in the citadel when the enemy attacked. The citadel stood proudly on the hill overlooking the city. The university is regarded as a citadel of learning and wisdom. During the war, people sought safety within the walls of the citadel.
synonyms: Fortress, Stronghold, Castle, Bastion, Fort, Keep

sindhiMeaning: ڪو به ماخذ ڪتاب يا بيان جيڪو حوالو طور ڏنو وڃي، بهادري يا سٺي ڪم تي ڏنل سرڪاري ساراه، عدالت ۾ پيش ٿيڻ لاءِ ڏنل نوٽيس، لکيل حوالو، ڪتاب مان نقل ڪيل جملي جو ٽڪرو، سرڪاري واکاڻ جو دستخطي بيان، عدالتي سڏ نامه
antonyms: Plagiarism, Concealment, Omission
synonyms: Reference, Quotation, Source, Mention, Acknowledgment
urduMeaning: کسی معلومات کے ماخذ کا حوالہ، بہادری یا کارکردگی پر دیا جانے والا سرکاری اعزاز، عدالت میں پیش ہونے کا باضابطہ نوٹس، تحریری حوالہ، کسی کتاب سے لیا گیا اقتباس، سرکاری تعریفی نوٹ، عدالت کا سمن
englishMeaning: A reference to a source of information, or an official notice given for recognition or for a legal matter. Reference to a source used in writing or speech. An official award for bravery or achievement. A formal notice to appear in court. Formal praise recorded in writing.
examples: The report included a citation for every statistic. She received a citation from the governor for her service. The police issued a citation for parking in a restricted area. Always provide a citation when you use someone else's ideas.

urduMeaning: حوالہ دینا یا مثال کے طور پر ذکر کرنا، کسی شخص کو عدالت یا حکام کے سامنے پیش ہونے کا نوٹس دینا، کسی کی تعریف یا سرکاری سطح پر تحسین کرنا، کسی بات کو مثال یا ثبوت کے طور پر پیش کرنا، کسی دلیل بات یا وضاحت کو مضبوط بنانے کے لیے کسی کتاب شخص واقعے قانون یا مواد کا حوالہ دینا یا اس کا ذکر کرنا
englishMeaning: To mention something as evidence or support. To quote, refer to, or mention a source, example, rule, case, or fact in order to explain a point or support an argument. To officially call someone to appear in court or before authorities. To praise someone formally, especially for bravery or good work. To point out or list something as an example. It is often used in academic writing, legal discussions, speeches, and reports.
examples: She cited three research papers to support her argument. The teacher asked the students to cite reliable sources in their essays. Lawyers often cite previous court cases during trials. He cited his busy schedule as the reason for not attending the meeting.
synonyms: Quote, Refer to, Mention, Name, Invoke
antonyms: Ignore, Overlook, Discount, Drop, Omit
sindhiMeaning: حوالو ڏيڻ يا مثال طور ذڪر ڪرڻ، ڪنهن شخص کي عدالت ۾ طلب ڪرڻ جو حڪم ڏيڻ، ڪنهن جي ساراهه ڪرڻ يا شاباشي ڏيڻ، ڪنهن ڳالهه کي مثال طور بيان ڪرڻ، ڪنهن ڳالهه کي ثابت ڪرڻ يا وضاحت ڪرڻ لاءِ ڪتاب شخص واقعو قانون يا ڪنهن به مواد مان حوالو ڏيڻ يا مثال بيان ڪرڻ

synonyms: Municipal, Public, Community, Civil, Local, Social
urduMeaning: شہر شہریت یا شہری ذمہ داریوں سے متعلق، بلدیاتی عوامی شہری معاشرتی ذمہ داری سے متعلق، کمیونٹی سے متعلق، شہر سے وابستہ
sindhiMeaning: شهر شهريت يا شهري ذميوارين سان لاڳاپيل، بلدياتي عوامي شهري سماجي ذميواري سان لاڳاپيل، ڪميونٽي سان لاڳاپيل، شهر سان واسطيدار
examples: Civic responsibility includes obeying laws and helping the community. The mayor spoke about improving civic services in the city. Schools should teach students about civic duties and voting rights. Her civic engagement helped bring positive change to the neighborhood.
englishMeaning: Related to a city, town, citizenship, or the duties of citizens. Something connected with a city, town, community life, public affairs, or the responsibilities and rights of citizens. It is often used for public duties, social participation, local government, and community welfare.
antonyms: Private, Personal, Individual, Nonpublic, Domestic

sindhiMeaning: چپ ٿي وڃڻ، ڳالهائڻ بند ڪرڻ، اڪثر شرم، ڊپ يا پريشاني جي ڪري اوچتو خاموش ٿي وڃڻ
englishMeaning: To suddenly stop talking, usually due to fear, shyness, or secrecy.
antonyms: Speak, Talk, Confess
synonyms: Silence, Shut up, Stop talking
urduMeaning: خاموش ہو جانا، چپ لگ جانا، کثر شرمندگی، خوف یا گھبراہٹ کی وجہ سے اچانک خاموش ہو جانا
examples: When asked about his plans, he clammed up. He clammed up in front of the police. She clammed up when the topic came up. They all clammed up after the accident.

englishMeaning: Unpleasantly damp, sticky, or cold to the touch. Something that feels slightly wet, cold, and sticky, often causing discomfort. It can describe skin, hands, weather, or an atmosphere that is damp and chilling.
synonyms: Moist, Damp, Sticky, Wet, Cold, Sweaty
sindhiMeaning: نمي وارو، چپچپو، ٿڌو، ڪجھه اهڙو جيڪو ٿورو نمي وارو چپچپو ۽ ٿڌو محسوس ٿئي، جيئن هٿ يا هوا ۾ نمي ۽ ٿڌ ڏسي سگهجي
urduMeaning: نم دار، چپچپا، سرد، وہ چیز جو چھونے میں تھوڑی گیلی چپچپی اور سرد لگے، جیسے ہاتھ جلد یا ماحول میں نمی اور سردی ہو
examples: His clammy hands made me nervous during the handshake. The room felt clammy after the rainstorm. She wiped the clammy sweat off her forehead. The old walls of the basement were cold and clammy.
antonyms: Dry, Warm, Comfortable, Pleasant

urduMeaning: زور سے آواز کرنا، احتجاج کرنا، شور، ہنگامہ، زور دار مسلسل اور بلند آواز میں مطالبہ یا احتجاج
sindhiMeaning: زور سان آواز ڪرڻ، ڌيان طلب ڪرڻ، شديد مسلسل ۽ زور شور سان آواز يا احتجاج، وڏي تڪليف يا توجهه جو اظهار
examples: Citizens clamored for justice after the incident. The students clamored to meet the speaker. Fans clamored for autographs at the event. The clamor of the crowd could be heard from blocks away. The clamor for change grew louder every day. There was a clamor of voices in the market.
synonyms: Shout, Demand, Yell, Protest, Uproar, Outcry, Hubbub, Racket
antonyms: Whisper, Murmur, Remain silent, Comply quietly, Silence, Calm, Quiet, Stillness
englishMeaning: To make a loud noise or demand loudly. To shout, protest, or insist loudly. To demand something publicly and with force.

synonyms: Crack down on, Enforce, Control, Restrict
englishMeaning: To take strict measures to prevent or control something considered undesirable or illegal
urduMeaning: کسی غیر قانونی یا نقصان دہ عمل کو روکنے یا کنٹرول کرنے کے لیے سخت اقدامات کرنا
examples: The government clamped down on illegal mining. Authorities clamped down on fake products. Schools clamped down on cheating during exams. Police clamped down on street racing
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن غير قانوني يا نقصانڪار عمل کي روڪڻ لاءِ سخت قدم کڻڻ
antonyms: Allow, Tolerate, Overlook, Ignore
Unskilled, Inexperienced, Inept, Clumsy, Incompetent
urduMeaning: مہارت رکھنے والا، ہنر مند، ماہر، مشتاق ، فاضل، کاريگَر، تَربِيَت يافتَہ، استاد، ذہین اور قابل فرد
examples: She is adept at solving complex problems quickly. The teacher is adept in explaining difficult ideas in simple words. He became adept at using computer software after years of practice. The diplomat was adept at handling sensitive negotiations.
englishMeaning: Highly skilled or very good at something. A person who has strong ability, practice, or expertise in a particular activity, task, or field. Someone who performs an action with great competence and confidence.
sindhiMeaning: مهارت رکندڙ، قابليت رکندڙ، هوشيار ۽ قابل ماڻهو، فاضل، ڪاريگر، استاد، ڪامل، لائق، قابل، ماھر، تجربي وارو
synonyms: Skilled, Expert, Proficient, Capable, Masterful, Competent

urduMeaning: سخت کارروائی کرنا، کسی شے یا سرگرمی پر سخت کنٹرول کرنا، خاص طور پر غیر قانونی یا غلط عمل کو روکنے کے لیے
englishMeaning: To take strict action. To enforce strict control or restrictions on something, usually to stop unwanted behavior or illegal activities
antonyms: Allow, Tolerate, Ignore
synonyms: Enforce, Control, Restrict, Regulate
examples: The government clamped down on tax evasion. Authorities clamped down on illegal street vendors. Schools clamped down on cheating during exams. Police clamped down on public drinking
sindhiMeaning: سخت ڪنٽرول ڪرڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ يا سرگرمي تي سخت ڪنٽرول ڪرڻ، خاص طور تي غير قانوني يا خراب عمل کي روڪڻ لاءِ

synonyms: Secret, Hidden, Covert, Undercover, Sneaky, Confidential
sindhiMeaning: ڳجھو، لڪل، لڪي ڪري ٿيل، ڳجهي نموني، پوشيده، رازدارانه، اهڙو ڪم جيڪو ڄاڻي واڻي لڪائي ڪيو وڃي ته جيئن ماڻهن يا اختيارين کي خبر نه پوي
urduMeaning: خفیہ، پوشیدہ، چھپ کر کیا گیا، رازدارانہ، چھپا ہوا، خفیہ طریقے سے، ایسا کام جو جان بوجھ کر خفیہ رکھا جائے تاکہ لوگوں یا حکام کو معلوم نہ ہو
examples: They held a clandestine meeting late at night. The journalist uncovered a clandestine operation. He made clandestine plans to start his own company. The group carried out a clandestine mission.
englishMeaning: Covert, undercover, concealed, confidential. Secret, hidden, done privately. Something kept secret, often to avoid attention, rules, or authority.
antonyms: Open, Public, Overt, Transparent, Known
Release, Let go, Loose, Free, Unfasten
englishMeaning: A device or action used to hold things tightly together. A small object or fastener used to hold two things together, such as parts of a bag, necklace, or clothing. To grip or hold something tightly with hands or fingers. To embrace someone tightly in arms (hold closely).
sindhiMeaning: مضبوطي سان پڪڙڻ يا ڳنڍڻ جو اوزار يا عمل، ننڍڙو اوزار جيڪو ٻه شيون مضبوطي سان گڏ رکي جهڙوڪ زيور ڪپڙا يا ٿيلهو، هٿن سان مضبوطي سان پڪڙڻ يا جهلي رکڻ، ڪنهن کي ڀاڪر ۾ مضبوطي سان وٺڻ
examples: She fastened the necklace with a golden clasp. The bag has a broken clasp. He clasped her hand before she left. The soldier clasped the weapon tightly in his hands.
urduMeaning: مضبوطی سے پکڑنے یا جوڑنے کا آلہ یا عمل، چھوٹا سا آلہ جو دو چیزوں کو مضبوطی سے جوڑ کر رکھتا ہے جیسے زیورات کپڑے یا بیگ، ہاتھوں سے مضبوطی سے پکڑنا یا تھامنا، کسی کو مضبوطی سے گلے لگانا
synonyms: Grip, Hold, Fastener, Clamp, Grasp, Embrace

englishMeaning: A group of words with a subject and verb, or a section of a legal document. A group of words that usually contains a subject and a verb and forms part of a sentence. In legal or formal writing, a clause is a specific section of a contract, law, or agreement that explains a rule, condition, or obligation.
antonyms: Whole, Entire document, Main sentence
urduMeaning: جملے کا حصہ یا معاہدے کی شق، الفاظ کا وہ مجموع جس میں فاعل اور فعل شامل ہوں اور جو جملے کا حصہ بنے، قانونی یا رسمی تحریر میں معاہدے یا قانون کا ایک مخصوص حصہ جو شرط ذمہ داری یا قاعدہ بیان کرتا ہے
examples: The contract includes a clause about payment terms. This sentence has a dependent clause. Every clause in the agreement must be followed. The lawyer explained the meaning of each clause clearly.
sindhiMeaning: جملو يا معاهدي جو حصو، لفظن جو اهڙو مجمعو جنهن ۾ عام طور فاعل ۽ فعل هوندا آهن ۽ اهو جملي جو حصو هوندو آهي، قانوني يا سرڪاري لکڻ ۾معاهدي يا قانون جو هڪ مخصوص حصو جيڪو شرط يا قاعدو بيان ڪري
synonyms: Provision, Section, Condition, Term

examples: She could not ride in the small elevator because of her claustrophobia. His claustrophobia made it hard for him to travel on crowded trains. The doctor explained techniques to manage claustrophobia during MRI scans. Visiting the narrow cave triggered his claustrophobia.
synonyms: Confinement fear, Enclosed-space phobia, Small-space anxiety, Enclosure fear
englishMeaning: Fear of small or enclosed spaces. An anxiety disorder in which a person experiences intense fear or panic when in confined, crowded, or enclosed spaces. It can trigger physical symptoms like sweating, rapid heartbeat, or shortness of breath.
sindhiMeaning: بند جڳهن جو ڊپ، هڪ نفسياتي حالت جنهن ۾ ماڻهو تنگ يا بند جڳهن ۾ وڃڻ تي شديد ڊپ يا پريشاني محسوس ڪري ٿو (جهڙوڪ ايلويٽر ننڍا ڪمرا يا مصروف جڳهيون)، جسماني علامتون جهڙوڪ پسينو دل جي ڌڙڪن تيز ٿيڻ يا ساهه کڻڻ ۾ مشڪل پڻ ٿي سگهن ٿيون
antonyms: Spaciousness comfort, Openness, Agoraphobia (opposite type of phobia: fear of open spaces)
urduMeaning: بند جگہوں کا خوف، ایک نفسیاتی حالت جس میں فرد چھوٹے یا بند مقامات میں جانے پر شدید خوف یا اضطراب محسوس کرتا ہے، اس کے جسمانی علامات میں پسینہ آنا دل کی دھڑکن تیز ہونا یا سانس لینے میں مشکل شامل ہو سکتی ہے

synonyms: Hygiene is important, Purity leads to goodness, Neatness reflects character, Clean habits show discipline, Tidiness is a virtue
sindhiMeaning: صفائي ايمان جو حصو آهي، صفائي نصف ايمان آهي، صفائي سٺي عادت جي نشاني آهي، پاڪيزگي عزت ۽ اخلاق ڏيکاري ٿي، صاف ماحول صحت لاءِ فائديمند آهي، صفائي مهذب شخصيت ظاهر ڪري ٿي، صفائي سٺي تربيت ۽ نظم جي علامت آهي
englishMeaning: Clean living shows good character. Hygiene brings health and respect. A clean environment creates positivity. Purity and neatness reflect morality. Clean habits are signs of discipline
examples: Our teacher always reminds us that cleanliness is next to godliness, so we should keep our classroom neat and tidy. My mother believes that cleanliness is next to godliness and makes us clean the house every weekend. Hospitals must follow the rule that cleanliness is next to godliness to protect patients from diseases. He keeps his clothes and workplace clean because he thinks cleanliness is next to godliness.
antonyms: Dirtiness, Untidiness, Filthiness, Uncleanliness, Negligence
urduMeaning: صفائی نصف ایمان ہے، صفائی اچھی عادت کی علامت ہے، پاکیزگی انسان کو باوقار بناتی ہے، صاف ستھرا ماحول صحت کے لیے ضروری ہے، صفائی مہذب شخصیت کو ظاہر کرتی ہے، اچھی صفائی اچھی تربیت کی نشانی ہے
صاف کرنا، کسی چیز سے میل نجاست یا نقصان دہ چیز ہٹانا، جسمانی ذہنی یا روحانی طور پر پاک کرنا
synonyms: Purify, Wash, Sanitize, Detoxify, Scrub
englishMeaning: To make clean. To remove dirt, impurities, or harmful substances from something; to purify physically, mentally, or spiritually.
examples: She cleansed her hands before dinner. The ritual cleanses the soul of negativity. The doctor recommended a detox to cleanse the body. They cleansed the wound with antiseptic.
sindhiMeaning: صاف ڪرڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ مان مٽي آلودگي يا نقصانڪار جز هٽائڻ، جسماني يا ذهني طور پاڪ ڪرڻ
antonyms: Pollute, Soil, Dirty, Contaminate
